### What platform is your computer?

macOS 15.7.9; local desktop task using Chrome through cua_repl.

### What issue are you seeing?

An existing chat that successfully controlled Chrome earlier now returns:

```text
Local browser use is disabled in Work settings
```

The user reports that browser access is still enabled in settings, this recurs frequently after restarting the desktop app, and other chats appear able to use the browser at the same time. The settings state, restart timing and other-chat comparison are user-reported; the successful earlier browser operations and later disabled error in this chat were observed directly.

The failing operation was an accessibility-state read of an already-bound Chrome tab. The error happened before page content could be read or any action submitted. The restriction was respected.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

User-reported recurring sequence:

1. Enable browser access and use Chrome successfully from a local desktop chat.
2. Restart the desktop app while retaining the existing chat.
3. Continue browser work in that chat.
4. The tool reports that local browser use is disabled.
5. Check the setting: the user reports it is enabled; other chats may still have browser access.

The exact trigger and deterministic reproduction conditions are not yet established. No restart, settings modification, extension reinstall or account switch was performed by the agent to reproduce this report.

### What is the expected behavior?

Existing chats should re-evaluate the current browser permission and reconnect after a restart when access is allowed. If a different account/workspace/session policy blocks access, the error should identify that cause rather than contradict the enabled setting. A supported recovery path should preserve the existing chat and its work.

### Additional information

Related reports: #56645 and #54989 describe the same disabled-setting symptom on Windows. #56609 describes a macOS occurrence after an account switch. This report adds the current macOS app build, a restart trigger reported by the user, and the reported discrepancy between chats.

The in-app feedback route could not be automated: cua.getApp('Codex') returned `Computer Use is not allowed to use the app 'com.openai.codex' for safety reasons.` That restriction was also respected; no alternative UI control or permission bypass was attempted.

Observed October 26, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles). Submitted on the user's request. No private application URLs, project files, account identifiers, session IDs, transcripts, credentials or raw logs are attached.

### Current investigation (October 28)

The same disabled-setting error is observed in a restored chat on Nightly 26.1028.10413 (22641), while the user reports Local browser use is On. Logs show the chat resume completed before Browser runtime configuration was selected. The native authorization tracker does not register a previously unbound chat if the resume has no node_repl account override. A scoped candidate now captures the authenticated native account when that request is sent, while retaining existing session ownership and checking the current setting on use.

Draft D2656730 is published at `6bfbe81a4635414460bdc2cdbcf0aed01ff65c30`: [https://flow.apps.openai.org/deltas/openai/openai/2656730](<https://flow.apps.openai.org/deltas/openai/openai/2656730>). Both new registration regressions fail on the baseline; all 34 focused Browser tests pass on the candidate. Changed-file validation, Electron TypeScript, and the file-size check pass. Current-head CI is pending.

This remains a source-level repair, not a confirmed end-to-end fix for the reported Nightly session. Native verification requires a build containing the patch and a connected secondary display. The installed Nightly still rejects Browser access. Verify restored-chat access, Off enforcement, and retained-account isolation before acceptance.

issues.body:
## Version and environment
- Microsoft Store package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1023.6123.0 (queried locally).
- Windows, local desktop chat.
- Subscription and About-dialog version not collected.

## Actual behavior
The user reports the desktop UI becoming stuck repeatedly, including this incident on 2026-10-28. A local mailbox integration delivering events to an existing desktop chat retained two notifications because the desktop steering request's acknowledgement was ambiguous.

Exact underlying error, with identifiers omitted:
```
desktop steer delivery outcome is unknown for message <redacted>: thread-follower-steer-turn-timeout
```

Recorded UTC times:
- 17:28:33: first notification quarantined after ambiguous steering acknowledgement.
- 17:32:29: second notification quarantined with the same error.
- User rebooted; the integration's watcher died with the reboot.
- After recovery, the local mailbox broker was healthy, both original messages remained intact, and a restarted watcher successfully delivered a later notification to this same chat. Its health returned to idle with no pending notifications.

The quarantine wording and watcher are our integration, not built-in Codex error UI. The underlying steering timeout is the relevant desktop symptom. We deliberately did not automatically replay messages with unknown delivery outcomes, to avoid duplicates.

## Reproduction status
Intermittent; no minimal deterministic reproducer yet. Observed workflow:
1. Work in a long-lived local desktop chat.
2. A local background integration sends an event to that existing chat.
3. During a user-reported UI freeze, the steering acknowledgement times out and delivery becomes uncertain.
4. Recovery requires inspecting the durable integration record and restarting the watcher after the reboot.

We have not established whether the UI freeze causes the acknowledgement timeout, whether steering contributes to the freeze, or whether they share another cause. No renderer profile or native dump was collected for this incident.

## Expected
The UI should remain responsive. Steering an event into an existing chat should return a definitive acceptance/refusal, or offer a supported way to reconcile an ambiguous result by stable message ID without duplicating the turn.

## Related
#57744 reports recurring Windows UI freezes on the same Store package version, with separate renderer evidence. We have not established a shared root cause. This report adds the distinct event-delivery acknowledgement symptom and recovery observations; please consolidate if appropriate.

## Privacy
Submitted by Codex at the user's request. No conversation content, project/client data, usernames, local paths, credentials, or private thread/message identifiers are included. Original diagnostic receipts remain local.

issues.body:
# Recommended issue title

`[Bug] Computer Use causes a replayd XPC reconnect loop and ~90% CPU while idle on macOS`

# Bug report body

## Summary

On macOS, the ChatGPT desktop app's Computer Use service entered a tight XPC connect/cancel loop with Apple's `replayd` process even though Computer Use was not actively being used.

The loop caused sustained high CPU usage and made the MacBook Air noticeably hot:

- `replayd`: approximately **91.2% CPU**
- `SkyComputerUseService`: approximately **19.8% CPU**

The issue recurred after the processes were stopped manually. Disabling Computer Use, removing its `turn-ended` notification hook, and removing the Computer Use runtime stopped the loop immediately. After mitigation, `replayd` remained at **0.0% CPU** across repeated samples and `SkyComputerUseService` did not restart.

## Environment

- ChatGPT desktop app: **26.730.61639** (build **6234**)
- Bundled Codex CLI: **0.147.0-alpha.1.2**
- Computer Use service: **26.803.1000621** (build **1000621**)
- Computer Use bundle ID: `com.openai.sky.CUAService`
- Model in use: `gpt-5.6-sol`
- macOS: **14.6** (build **23G80**)
- Device: **MacBook Air, Apple M3, 16 GB RAM** (`Mac15,12`, arm64)

## Observed state before mitigation

Computer Use was not being used in the active Codex task. The MCP entry was disabled, and the plugin manager reported Computer Use as not installed:

```text
computer-use@openai-bundled    not installed
```

However, the Computer Use runtime still existed under `$CODEX_HOME/computer-use`, `SkyComputerUseService` was running, and the global Codex config contained an active `turn-ended` notification hook:

```toml
notify = ["<HOME>/.codex/computer-use/Codex Computer Use.app/Contents/SharedSupport/SkyComputerUseClient.app/Contents/MacOS/SkyComputerUseClient", "turn-ended"]

[mcp_servers.computer-use]
command = "./Codex Computer Use.app/Contents/SharedSupport/SkyComputerUseClient.app/Contents/MacOS/SkyComputerUseClient"
args = ["mcp"]
cwd = "."
enabled = false
```

During diagnosis, the `notify` entry was commented out, but an active copy was automatically added back later.

## Steps that led to the issue

These are the observed steps/trigger sequence. I have not reinstalled Computer Use after mitigation because doing so may recreate the high-CPU loop.

1. Computer Use had previously been installed or enabled in the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS.
2. Continue using Codex normally without invoking `@Computer` or starting a Computer Use task.
3. Complete Codex turns while the `turn-ended` notification hook is present.
4. `SkyComputerUseService` starts or restarts automatically.
5. In Activity Monitor or `ps`, observe sustained CPU usage from `replayd` and `SkyComputerUseService`.
6. Stop the processes manually; the Computer Use service is started again later and the issue returns.

## Expected behavior

- When Computer Use is not active, it should not continuously connect to ReplayKit or consume significant CPU.
- Disabling or uninstalling Computer Use should remove/disable its notification hooks and prevent `SkyComputerUseService` from starting.
- Connection failures should use bounded retries with backoff instead of a busy loop.

## Actual behavior

- `SkyComputerUseService` and the ChatGPT process repeatedly opened and cancelled connections to `replayd`.
- In a single one-second log window, the following events were counted:

```text
ChatGPT connections accepted:             2,067
SkyComputerUseService connections accepted: 2,067
XPC connection cancellations:             4,134
```

- macOS eventually quarantined logging because of the event volume:

```text
QUARANTINED DUE TO HIGH LOGGING VOLUME
```

## Representative system log excerpt

```text
2026-08-07 14:14:37.441 replayd[63348] ... accepted client connection PID: 46182
2026-08-07 14:14:37.441 replayd[63348] ... invalidated because the current process cancelled the connection by calling xpc_connection_cancel()
2026-08-07 14:14:37.441 replayd[63348] ... activating connection ... name=com.apple.replayd.peer[46261]
2026-08-07 14:14:37.441 replayd[63348] ... accepted client connection PID: 46261
2026-08-07 14:14:37.441 replayd[63348] ... invalidated because the current process cancelled the connection by calling xpc_connection_cancel()
2026-08-07 14:14:37.444 replayd[63348] ... QUARANTINED DUE TO HIGH LOGGING VOLUME
```

issues.title: [macOS app] Holding Control-D deletes only one character in composer; debug shortcut consumes repeats

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1023.51421, build 22530 (installed desktop app; bundle identifier `com.openai.codex`).

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided. This is a local composer keyboard-handling issue; no model request is needed to reproduce it.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon. `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm`.

### What issue are you seeing?

In the message composer, pressing Control-D once deletes the character after the caret, but holding Control-D deletes only one character. Releasing D and pressing it again performs another deletion.

The affected surface is the message composer, rather than the integrated terminal or a code editor. The user explicitly confirmed the single-press-versus-hold behavior.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open a chat in the macOS desktop app and focus the message composer.
2. Enter a string such as `abcdefghij` and place the caret at its beginning, with no selection.
3. Hold Control-D beyond the system key-repeat delay.
4. Observe that only the first character is deleted.
5. Release D and press it again: another character can be deleted.

### What is the expected behavior?

Holding Control-D should repeatedly delete characters after the caret, following the macOS forward-delete text-editing behavior and system repeat settings.

### Additional information

System key repeat is enabled: global `ApplePressAndHoldEnabled=0`, `KeyRepeat=2`, and `InitialKeyRepeat=15`; the app has no overrides for these settings.

Read-only inspection of the installed app bundle suggests a shortcut collision. This diagnosis is based on static code inspection; the user confirmed the UI symptom, and no instrumented UI reproduction or patched-build validation was performed.

- In `app.asar` → `webview/assets/app-shared-e9f258fd3588.js`, the app-scoped `toggleDebugModal` command has the default Electron keybinding `Ctrl+D`.
- In `webview/assets/app-runtime-a4c587fdcbb9.js`, the shortcut registration explicitly enables repeat handling for `toggleDebugModal`. Its keydown handler contains the following branch (formatting added; identifiers retained):

```js
if ((n === `toggleSidebar` || n === `toggleDebugModal`) && e.repeat) {
  e.preventDefault();
  return;
}
Tc(n, e) && e.preventDefault();
```

The repeat branch prevents the native action before command dispatch determines whether a handler actually consumes the event. The shared shortcut matcher also permits Control-modified shortcuts within editable elements. Together, these code paths explain why the first Control-D can reach native deletion while subsequent repeat events are swallowed.

Please preserve native Control-D repeat behavior in editable fields, for example by gating the debug shortcut and its repeat suppression on an active command handler, or by excluding this native text-editing shortcut from the capture handler while a text field is focused.

issues.body:
## Summary

In the macOS Codex desktop app, automatic context compaction is repeatedly followed by loss of the latest instructions and, in some incidents, adoption of another ongoing chat's task or approval as if it belonged to the current chat. This affects tool execution and task boundaries, not just answer quality. The recurrence itself is observed: this report now includes another directly observed incident in the same Windows-work chat after the issue was filed, in addition to the user's repeated firsthand observations in other chats. The underlying mechanism remains unknown.

## Environment

- Codex desktop app on macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon (arm64), verified locally.
- Desktop app version and active model were not independently collected for this report. Versions of CLIs inside the Windows guest are not the affected desktop application's version.
- Several concurrent, separate work chats; explicit task boundaries and durable handoff files.
- Incidents reported on October 28–29, 2026 (Asia/Seoul).

## User's repeated firsthand observations in other chats

Over the past several days, the user has frequently observed loss of the immediately preceding question, instructions, agreed scope, progress, or stop conditions following compaction. The user's estimate is approximately 9 out of 10 compactions; the approximately 9/10 figure is an estimate, not an instrumented rate. That qualification applies to the frequency estimate, not to whether the observed incidents occurred.

The user reports that cross-chat task/approval confusion first occurred on October 28. On October 29 it recurred three times after compaction in an earlier project-development chat: the agent consulted a separate Windows-validation chat, treated that chat's work and approvals as its own, and performed tool/file operations despite explicit instructions and handoff records prohibiting that access.

These are the user's firsthand observations of actual incidents, not a hypothesis about possible behavior. The reporting agent did not reopen those other chats to independently audit them. That limits independent verification of their details; it does not recast the user's observations as speculation.

## Additional incident observed in this Windows-work chat on October 29

The user started a separate chat specifically for Windows VM agent readiness, UTM operating-procedure reproduction, and runbook updates. A handoff and plan specified the scope. Existing work had reached authentication-result collection; synthetic model-task execution had not yet started according to the last execution record.

After a context transition described by the user as automatic compaction, the agent lost its place and inspected an unrelated project-preparation artifact directory and a task-specific subdirectory. It also performed broader repository/state lookups instead of resuming from the supplied Windows handoff.

The visible workspace metadata included an unrelated artifact root; the agent incorrectly used that as a recovery lead. This is an observation to investigate, not proof of why the metadata was present or of a backend session merge.

The user noticed, stopped the agent, and pointed out that it was acting like another task's driver. The agent acknowledged the wrong-directory access. In this latest incident, the observed cross-task access was directory listing/metadata lookup; there is no evidence here that the other chat was opened or that its files were modified. This narrower observation should not be conflated with the earlier user-reported file operations.

## Confirmed recurrence after filing this issue — October 29, approximately 13:28–13:30 KST

The same Windows-work chat underwent another context transition after this issue was filed. Before the transition, a durable Windows-only continuation file had already recorded the current task, completed steps, exact next actions, existing approvals, cumulative deadlines, and an explicit prohibition on looking at unrelated task directories or other chats.

The following sequence was directly observed in the agent's tool calls in this chat:

1. The agent attempted to recover its context through notes/history tools. Those calls returned backend-request errors.
2. Instead of stopping dependent recovery or reading the exact Windows continuation file, it listed an unrelated project-preparation artifact directory exposed among the workspace roots.
3. The user again intervened and explicitly redirected it to the Windows task. Only after that intervention did the agent locate and read the Windows-only continuation file and execution record, and resume the correct unfinished stage.

This is another actual recurrence in the same chat, after both explicit boundaries and a dedicated continuation file had been provided. It is not merely the user's suspicion or a prediction of future failure. The agent's visible recovery calls, unrelated directory listing, and subsequent redirection support this account. The read access observed in this recurrence was a directory/metadata listing; no modification of that unrelated task's files or opening of another chat was observed here.

The user had anticipated recurrence and sent a preventative message during compaction, but the wrong-directory lookup had already happened. Requiring the user to keep predicting and correcting this behavior defeats unattended continuation of approved work. Recurrence in future compactions remains a concern; no claim of a measured inevitability or a proven backend cross-session merge is made.

The failed recovery-tool calls and presence of an unrelated workspace root are useful investigation details, not established root causes. Please distinguish the confirmed behavioral failure from the still-unresolved cause.

## Observed workflow to investigate

1. Run multiple independent desktop chats with different scopes and approvals.
2. Give the current chat a precise task-specific handoff, completed-stage record, explicit exclusions, and stop conditions.
3. Continue long enough for automatic context compaction.
4. Observe whether the agent retains the latest instruction, current task identity, next unfinished step, and approval provenance.
5. In the reported failures, it resumes unrelated work or uses another task's context/approval, requiring user intervention.

This describes the observed workflow; there is no deterministic minimal reproducer or measured failure rate yet.

## Expected behavior

After compaction, preserve the latest user instruction, current chat/task identity, completed and failed stages, approval scope and provenance, exclusions, and cumulative stop conditions. If recovery is uncertain, disclose that uncertainty and stop dependent actions. Another chat's records or approvals must not become execution authority for the current task.

## Impact and investigation requested

Users lose track of actual failure/completion states, suffer interference with unrelated concurrent work, and must repeatedly catch and stop the agent. Starting a fresh chat with an explicit handoff did not prevent recurrence.

Please investigate context preservation across compaction, current-thread identification and recovery, retention of explicit prohibitions, and how retrieved cross-thread/task material can be mistaken for current execution authority. The user cannot determine whether sessions are actually linked/mixed internally or the model is adopting unrelated context after recovery failure.

Potentially related symptom: #43855 (loss of task context after compaction). This report additionally concerns cross-task tool access and approval provenance; no common root cause is asserted.

## Privacy and submission

No raw conversations, credentials, account emails, private project names, local paths, or unreviewed logs are attached. The in-app feedback dialog was unavailable to the assistant because Computer Use blocks access to the Codex app; this report uses the GitHub route documented in the official troubleshooting guide. No in-app diagnostic upload or uploaded-session receipt is claimed.

issues.title: Linux sandbox rejects pam_namespace private /tmp mount via /cray/tmp since 0.156.0

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.156.1`. The problem also reproduces with 0.156.0; 0.155.1 and earlier tested versions work.

### What subscription do you have?

N/A. This reproduces locally with `codex sandbox -- /bin/true` before any model request.

### Which model were you using?

N/A.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.4.0 x86_64, SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 SP6 on an HPE Cray HPC login node. `bubblewrap 0.11.0` is installed at `/usr/bin/bwrap`.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

SSH terminal; not terminal-dependent.

### Codex doctor report

`codex doctor` reports Codex 0.156.1, a consistent standalone installation, and the restricted Linux filesystem sandbox. The persistent app-server is not running. The only relevant processes in the reproducing session are `codex resume` and its 0.156.1 `codex-code-mode-host` child.

### What issue are you seeing?

Starting in 0.156.0, every filesystem-restricted command fails before bubblewrap starts when `/tmp` is isolated per user by `pam_namespace`:

```text
error building bubblewrap command: app-server socket directory has an unsupported host mount at /cray/tmp; remove the bind-mount alias or nested mount before starting the sandbox
```

The system's `/etc/security/namespace.conf` contains:

```text
/tmp    /tmp/.pam_namespace/    user    root
```

The resulting relevant mountinfo entries, with the username redacted, are:

```text
37227 37226 0:52 / /cray/tmp rw,nodev,relatime master:2 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,size=369147492k,mode=755,inode64
37229 37226 0:52 /tmp /tmp rw,nodev,relatime master:3 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,size=369147492k,mode=755,inode64
37462 37229 0:52 /tmp/.pam_namespace/<user> /tmp rw,nodev,relatime master:3 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,size=369147492k,mode=755,inode64
```

Thus `/cray/tmp` is the root of the tmpfs, `/tmp` is a view of its `/tmp` subtree, and the per-user PAM namespace directory is stacked back over `/tmp`. The PAM namespace parent is root-owned and mode `000`, so the physical-looking alias beneath `/cray/tmp/tmp/.pam_namespace/<user>` is not traversable by the user.

Codex creates `/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>` with mode 0700. A filesystem-only trace of the 0.156.1 sandbox helper shows:

```text
readlink("/tmp", ...) = -1 EINVAL
mkdir("/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>", 0700) = -1 EEXIST
lstat("/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>", {st_mode=S_IFDIR|0700, ...}) = 0
open("/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = 3
open("/proc/self/mountinfo", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 4
error building bubblewrap command: app-server socket directory has an unsupported host mount at /cray/tmp; ...
```

This is a Codex preflight rejection; bubblewrap itself is not reached.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On a Linux login session configured with the `pam_namespace` entry above:

```bash
codex sandbox -- /bin/true
```

Regression results using locally cached standalone binaries on the same host:

```text
0.139.0  succeeds
0.146.1  succeeds
0.155.1  succeeds
0.156.0  fails with the /cray/tmp error
0.156.1  fails with the /cray/tmp error
```

The boundary corresponds to #45984, which added app-server Unix-socket isolation in 0.156.0. This appears related to #47455, but that report uses a fully overmounted `nix-user-chroot` mount. This report covers standard PAM per-user namespace mounts, where the alternate physical path is also inaccessible through a root-owned mode-000 ancestor.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should preserve app-server socket isolation while allowing filesystem-restricted commands under a standard `pam_namespace` private `/tmp` configuration.

### Additional information

Attempted mitigations:

- Setting `TMPDIR=/run/user/<uid>` or to a workspace directory does not help. The sandbox helper still opens `/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>`.
- `--no-daemon` does not avoid the validation.
- `features.use_legacy_landlock=true` is not a fallback; it panics with `filesystem-restricted execution requires bubblewrap to isolate app-server sockets`.
- Approved unsandboxed execution works.
- Downgrading to 0.155.1 restores sandbox execution, but that predates the socket-isolation security fix and is not a desirable permanent workaround.

No mounts, PAM configuration, or system security settings were modified during diagnosis.

issues.title: ChatGPT macOS conversation remains permanently stuck and in-app feedback upload cannot be confirmed

labels.name: bug

issues.body:
## Summary

A ChatGPT macOS conversation that was started on **September 28, 2026** has never produced the requested assistant response. As of **October 22, 2026**, the conversation is still permanently stuck with:

> Connection interrupted. Waiting for the complete answer

The assistant area also shows `无法思考` ("Unable to think") instead of a response.

When I tried to report the stuck conversation through the built-in feedback dialog, the feedback submission itself also failed to confirm, so two related failure paths occurred at the same time:

1. The original generation remained stuck for more than three weeks.
2. The in-app bug report could not confirm whether it was uploaded.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the ChatGPT macOS app.
2. Send a prompt in a conversation.
3. The generation becomes stuck and displays `Connection interrupted. Waiting for the complete answer`.
4. Close/reopen the app or return to the same conversation later.
5. Observe that the generation remains stuck indefinitely and no assistant response is delivered.
6. Open the message feedback dialog, select **Bug**, enter a description, keep conversation/diagnostic logs enabled, and submit.
7. Observe the feedback upload error.

## Actual behavior

- The conversation has remained stuck since **September 28, 2026** and still has no assistant response on **October 22, 2026**.
- Sending additional messages in the same conversation does not recover it.
- The feedback dialog reports:

> Feedback upload not confirmed
>
> We couldn't confirm whether your feedback was received. It may already have arrived, so sending it again could create a duplicate.

- Feedback ID shown by the app: `a1bb5c7c-e56d-4667-aff7-dd7936003d17`

## Expected behavior

- A generation should either complete, fail with a clear recoverable error, or provide a reliable retry/cancel path. It should not remain permanently pending for weeks.
- The built-in feedback flow should clearly confirm receipt, or provide a deterministic retry/status mechanism without risking duplicate reports.

## Environment

- Product: ChatGPT macOS desktop app
- Current app version: `26.1016.51333`
- App release date shown in About dialog: October 20, 2026
- Original affected conversation date: September 28, 2026
- Still reproducible/visible: October 22, 2026
- macOS version: not shown in the available diagnostics

## Additional context

The affected conversation is still visibly stuck after reopening it on the current app version. I have screenshots available showing the permanently pending generation, the feedback dialog, the upload-not-confirmed error, the feedback ID, and the app version.

issues.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

Summary
I’m trying to use dot to access existing Codex threads that I created myself, rather than tasks originally created by dot. Reading these threads fails with backend errors, even though my Windows desktop is connected and dot can discover my local Codex projects.
This appears inconsistent with the recently announced ability to follow up on existing Codex threads:
Official announcement:
https://x.com/ChatGPT/status/2108636748217770180?s=20
Official release notes:
https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/whats-new/dots-october-9-2026
Related documentation:
https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/tasks-and-memory
The announcement describes starting Codex work and following up on existing threads. In my tests, access works for a previously dot-created task, but fails for the user-created threads tested below.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Environment
- Test date: October 10, 2026; earlier attempts also failed before this date.
- Codex/ChatGPT desktop on Windows; requests to dot sent through ChatGPT web on Windows.
- Desktop reported connected, attached, and authorized for tasks.
- I updated the desktop app and requested another test. The same Architect-thread error persisted afterward.
- Reconnecting the computer did not resolve that error either.
- Exact desktop app/build version was not captured during these tests.
Steps to reproduce
1. Connect the Windows desktop to dot.
2. Copy a codex://threads/<thread_id> link from an existing user-created Codex session.
3. Ask dot to read that thread without sending messages or modifying it.
4. dot invokes cloud_threads.read with the supplied threadId and a small limit, such as 2 or 3.
5. The request fails before returning conversation content.
Tools used
- cloud_threads.read — full tool name: mcp__codex_apps__cloud_threads_read.
- cloud_threads.list_threads with children_only=false, limit=50; archived=true was checked separately.
- cloud_threads.list_environments.
- cloud_threads.list_projects with the connected computer’s environmentId.
Observed results
A. Existing project-associated Architect thread:
AppServerBackendRequestError: Client specified an invalid argument: post-cutover thread ID <THREAD_A> has unsupported placement format version 2
This was reproduced repeatedly, including after the desktop update and reconnection.
B. Another existing user-created thread:
AppServerBackendRequestError: Client specified an invalid argument: post-cutover thread ID <THREAD_B> has unsupported placement format version 3
C. An existing session not associated with a project:
AppServerBackendRequestError: thread not found: <THREAD_C>
D. A new session I created specifically for testing after the update:
AppServerBackendRequestError: Client specified an invalid argument: post-cutover thread ID <THREAD_D> has unsupported placement region 10
These read failures returned isError=true and error_code=UNKNOWN. No conversation content was returned.
Successful control checks
- cloud_threads.read successfully returned messages from a previously dot-created task on the same computer.
- cloud_threads.list_environments confirmed the desktop connection and task authorization.
- cloud_threads.list_projects successfully returned my registered local projects, including the relevant project’s ID and root path.
Additional findings and limits
- Account-level list_threads returned 30 IDs with no continuation cursor. The first two failing thread IDs were absent. The archived list was empty. This listing check occurred before the new test session was created.
- That listing exposed IDs, not thread titles or project associations. It therefore did not provide a usable list of chats belonging to my local project.
- Project discovery only confirms access to the sidebar project registry. Its registered root path is an old folder; active worktrees are elsewhere. We did not establish access to those worktrees through this check.
- The read-tool description mentions expanded access to existing threads, but no available status field confirmed whether that capability is enabled for my account.
- No messages were sent to the affected threads. No threads or worktrees were created by dot during this investigation, and no project files were changed.
Expected behavior
dot should be able to resolve and read an authorized existing local Codex thread on the connected computer, consistent with the announced feature. If a thread type, account rollout, or app version is unsupported, the error should explain the requirement or limitation clearly.
Impact
I cannot use dot to follow an existing Architect session and coordinate ongoing project work. I still have to manually copy messages and reports between Codex and dot.
Diagnostic interpretation — not a confirmed root cause
The placement-format and placement-region errors suggest a possible thread-ID compatibility or routing problem. We have not confirmed whether this involves local versus cloud thread storage, rollout state, permissions, or another backend issue. The errors do not establish that the threads were deleted, and “region 10” should not be assumed to represent my geographic location.
Please investigate why existing-thread reads fail while desktop/project discovery and a dot-created-thread read succeed, and confirm whether any account setting or client update is required.
I can provide the actual thread IDs privately through Feedback/support; they are intentionally omitted from this public report.

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up research messages from dot to an existing native local Codex task are rejected despite explicit owner authorization. Earlier native task creation and message relays succeeded.

## Environment

macOS, ChatGPT dot, connected Mac, native local Codex task.

Codex app 26.930.21537, Pro 200, and Darwin 24.6.0 arm64.

## Observed sequence

1. Dot created a cloud-managed task that executed on my Mac. That task exposed native `create_thread`, `read_thread`, and `send_message_to_thread`.
2. Native task creation, earlier message relays, and status reads succeeded. The affected destination is projectless. Thus, the observed problem is not limited to project placement.
3. I explicitly authorized a benign research follow-up in the main dot conversation. I then authorized retries.
4. The relay's native `send_message_to_thread` call, with `hostId` set to `local`, was repeatedly denied with “unacceptable risk”. The explanation treated owner authorization from the main conversation as untrusted transcript evidence instead of direct authorization.
5. I changed the receiving task to Full access and requested another test. At approximately 2026-10-03 03:10 UTC, the native send was denied for the same reason. Nothing was delivered.

A separate direct dot-side cloud messaging call with the native ID returned `NOT_FOUND`. This is a different interface. It does not establish a general native messaging outage. No filesystem or network sandbox cause has been established.

## Expected behavior

Provide a supported method to preserve and verify narrowly scoped owner authorization across dot → desktop relay → native task. If another approval is required, provide an approval step that the owner can use.

Preserve security checks. This request does not ask to bypass them. Ideally, provide direct native routing with project support so that the extra relay is unnecessary.

Private identifiers, repository contents, and credentials are omitted.

issues.title: ChatGPT Desktop: local MCP tools are discovered successfully but not exposed to Chat sessions

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.803.10989.0

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26100.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

ChatGPT Desktop successfully starts a configured local MCP server, completes the MCP initialization handshake, calls `tools/list`, and receives the full tool inventory. However, those tools are not exposed to the Chat session.

The affected MCP server is configured as `tessl_registry_mcp`.

The prompt used in a new Chat session was:

> Use the tessl_registry_mcp MCP server and list its tools.

ChatGPT responded:

> I still cannot see tessl_registry_mcp in this ChatGPT session.
> I checked the currently exposed connector/tool namespaces, and they are:
> GitHub, Gmail, REDACTED.
> tessl_registry_mcp is not among them, so I can't invoke it or enumerate its tools from here.

However, a transparent stdio capture shim placed between ChatGPT Desktop and the MCP server shows that Desktop successfully:

1. launches the MCP server;
2. sends `initialize`;
3. receives a valid `initialize` response;
4. sends `notifications/initialized`;
5. sends `tools/list`; and
6. receives the server's complete 17-tool inventory.

This was reproduced across three separate MCP server processes created during the same ChatGPT Desktop reproduction.

The MCP server returned these tools:

- `install`
- `login`
- `new_plugin`
- `outdated`
- `review_fix`
- `review_run`
- `review_view`
- `search`
- `skill_publish`
- `skills_available`
- `status`
- `tile_publish`
- `uninstall`
- `update`
- `workspace_create`
- `workspace_list`
- `workspace_list_members`

ChatGPT Desktop also called `resources/list` and `resources/templates/list`. The server returned normal JSON-RPC `Method not found` responses for those methods because it does not advertise MCP resources.

There was no MCP initialization or tool-discovery error in the captured exchange.

This appears to be a failure after successful MCP tool discovery, in the path that registers/exposes locally discovered MCP tools to the Chat session.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Windows 11, configure the following local MCP server in ChatGPT/Codex Desktop:

   - Name: `tessl_registry_mcp`
   - Command: `C:\Windows\System32\wsl.exe`
   - Arguments:
     - `/mnt/c/Users/<USER>/AppData/Local/Programs/Tessl/tessl.exe`
     - `mcp`
     - `start`

   Tessl version used: `0.95.0`.

2. For diagnostic purposes, place a transparent stdio shim between Desktop and the above command. The shim only forwards stdin/stdout unchanged while recording:

   - client -> MCP server traffic;
   - MCP server -> client traffic; and
   - MCP server stderr.

3. Fully exit and restart ChatGPT Desktop.

4. Open a new Chat session.

5. Send:

   `Use the tessl_registry_mcp MCP server and list its tools.`

6. Observe that Chat reports that `tessl_registry_mcp` is not present in its exposed tool namespaces.

7. Inspect the MCP shim capture.

   The captured protocol exchange shows:

   `ChatGPT Desktop -> MCP server`

   - `initialize`
   - `notifications/initialized`
   - `tools/list`
   - `resources/list`
   - `resources/templates/list`

   `MCP server -> ChatGPT Desktop`

   - successful `initialize` result;
   - successful `tools/list` result containing all 17 Tessl tools;
   - `Method not found` for the two resource methods.

8. Repeat the test. In my reproduction, three MCP processes were launched and all three successfully initialized and returned the full `tools/list` result.

As a control test, I configured the same server through the same shim and launched it from Codex CLI `0.147.0-alpha.6.6`.

The Codex CLI test succeeds: the MCP server initializes and its 17 tools are available.

Therefore the same MCP server, command, transport and shim work from Codex CLI but the successfully discovered tools are not exposed to Chat in ChatGPT Desktop.

Session/conversation/request identifiers in the attached public logs have been redacted. Token usage and context-window usage do not appear relevant to the reproduction.

### What is the expected behavior?

After ChatGPT Desktop successfully initializes a configured MCP server and receives a successful `tools/list` response, those MCP tools should be registered and made available to the Chat session.

For this server, after discovery succeeds, Chat should be able to invoke the 17 tools returned by `tessl_registry_mcp`, or at minimum recognize that the MCP server and its tools are available.

Instead, Chat reports that the server is not exposed to the session even though the Desktop-side MCP client has already discovered its tools successfully.

### Additional information

### Control test

The same MCP server was tested through the same transparent shim using Codex CLI `0.147.0-alpha.6.6`.

That test succeeds and exposes the full 17-tool inventory.

This strongly suggests that:

- the MCP server itself is working;
- the stdio transport is working;
- the `initialize` handshake is working;
- `tools/list` is working; and
- the failure occurs after MCP discovery, specifically in the Desktop Chat tool-registration/exposure path.

### MCP server details

Tessl CLI version:

`0.95.0`

Server reports:

- Name: `Tessl Registry MCP`
- Version: `0.0.1`
- MCP protocol version: `2025-06-18`

The command used during the captured Desktop reproduction was:

`C:\Windows\System32\wsl.exe /mnt/c/Users/<USER>/AppData/Local/Programs/Tessl/tessl.exe mcp start`

Note that this invokes the Windows Tessl executable through WSL interoperability; it is not a Linux-native Tessl binary.

### Desktop/app-server observations

The attached Desktop log covers the same reproduction.

It shows successful `mcpServerStatus/list` calls at the app-server RPC layer with `errorCode=null`.

The Desktop app-server also starts normally and reports version:

`0.147.0-alpha.6.6`

There is an unrelated warning in the log:

`ignoring invalid experimental feature enablement keys: apps_mcp_path_override`

The app remains in the connected state despite that warning.

There are also unrelated HTTP `429 Too many requests` warnings later in the session. The MCP initialization and tool discovery had already completed successfully before those occurred.

### Attachment glossary

The uploaded diagnostic files are:

#### [codex-desktop-redacted-20260812-190756.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30976068/codex-desktop-redacted-20260812-190756.log)

Redacted ChatGPT/Codex Desktop application log covering the reproduction.

User paths, conversation/session identifiers, request IDs and named-pipe identifiers have been redacted. Timestamps, method names, feature flags, versions and diagnostic messages have been preserved.

#### [ChatGPT Desktop MCP shim capture.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30976157/ChatGPT.Desktop.MCP.shim.capture.zip)

One complete capture directory from the failing ChatGPT Desktop reproduction.

It contains:

- `command.txt` — exact working directory and child command launched by the shim.
- `desktop-to-tessl.bin` — raw bytes sent by ChatGPT Desktop's MCP client to Tessl.
- `tessl-to-desktop.bin` — raw bytes returned by Tessl to ChatGPT Desktop.
- `tessl-stderr.log` — Tessl stderr/startup diagnostics.

This capture demonstrates a successful MCP initialization and a successful `tools/list` response containing all 17 tools even though Chat subsequently reports that `tessl_registry_mcp` is unavailable.

The behaviour was reproduced in three separate Desktop shim capture directories; only one complete representative capture is necessary to demonstrate the issue, but additional captures can be provided if useful.

#### [Codex CLI MCP shim capture.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30976122/Codex.CLI.MCP.shim.capture.zip)

Equivalent capture produced using Codex CLI as a control.

This shows that the same MCP server and shim successfully initialize and expose the tools when used from Codex CLI.

### Summary

The key distinction is:

### What issue are you seeing?

One active local Codex chat is visible and usable in the Windows Codex desktop app but is completely absent from Codex Remote on a paired Samsung Android device.

The Android client shows the connected Windows host and all expected filters (All / Cloud / host). Other chats from the same Windows host and the same local project are visible. Only this one chat is missing from All, the project, and Pinned. Pinning/unpinning and normal navigation did not make it appear.

This caused substantial lost time because the user could not continue a long-running development conversation from mobile and had no indication that the thread had been silently omitted.

### Environment

- Host: Windows Codex desktop app
- Remote client: ChatGPT on Samsung Galaxy S24+ / Android
- Same signed-in account and workspace
- Local project: a normal saved local project
- Observed: 2026-10-27
- Exact client build numbers were not captured
- Private chat/project/thread identifiers and conversation content are intentionally omitted

### Expected behavior

Every active, eligible local thread shown in the selected project's desktop sidebar should be discoverable from Android Remote when the same host is online. A metadata reconciliation failure should surface an actionable error rather than silently omitting one chat.

### Actual behavior

- The affected chat is active, readable by exact ID, unarchived, and has a normal title, preview, working directory, host identity, and extensive retained history.
- Desktop showed it under the intended local project.
- A control chat from the same host/project was visible on Android.
- Android omitted only the affected chat from All, the project, and Pinned.

### Diagnostic evidence

Read-only inspection found a per-thread metadata inconsistency:

- the current desktop listing and direct thread read knew the chat;
- persisted legacy project-assignment and membership-host maps lacked the affected chat;
- stale legacy pinned metadata still referenced the chat after the user had unpinned it;
- Remote visibility metadata said the chat was shown;
- project migration state reported project migration complete but thread-assignment migration incomplete;
- the affected chat was not included in the pending assignment list.

This combination suggests a reconciliation/indexing defect rather than account, pairing, archive, host-online, or user-navigation failure.

### Recovery attempted

Using the supported desktop project-membership operation, the chat was briefly removed from the local project and immediately assigned back to the same project. No chat content, files, Git state, or title were changed.

Afterward, the desktop task listing returned the affected chat with:

- the expected project ID,
- the expected local host,
- active status,
- unpinned state.

Android verification is still pending, so this is not yet claimed as a confirmed end-to-end workaround.

### Suggested investigation

Please inspect how Remote's Android catalog reconciles:

1. server/app-server thread project membership,
2. legacy desktop assignment maps,
3. incomplete thread-assignment migrations,
4. stale pin metadata,
5. Remote visibility/index entries.

A supported “reindex/reconcile this thread” operation or a visible recovery error would be preferable to silent omission.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

Codex Desktop eagerly auto-connects every saved/discovered SSH host during application startup, even when I only want to open local conversations. If a discovered host is unavailable or its remote app-server is slow to bootstrap, local chat loading becomes blank/unresponsive.

The startup log shows this sequence:

```text
load_completed savedRemoteConnectionCount=2 totalConnectionCount=2
refresh_completed autoConnectConnectionCount=2 discoveredConnectionCount=2
Starting app-server connection hostId=remote-ssh-discovered:<unreachable-host> transport=websocket
Starting app-server connection hostId=remote-ssh-discovered:<slow-host> transport=websocket
```

One host cannot resolve and retries indefinitely:

```text
ssh: Could not resolve hostname <unreachable-host>
remoteConnectionMaxRetryAttempts=null
app_server_connection.reconnect_scheduled ... nextDelayMs=20000
```

The other host's app-server bootstrap initially times out after 60 seconds. While it is connecting, chat/sidebar requests fail and the five-slot request queue fills:

```text
Request failed ... method=thread/list source=recent_threads
error="SSH: app-server bootstrap timed out after 60000ms"
durationMs=60948

app_server_client_request_queue_rejected
inFlightRequestCount=5
queueWaitMs=30000
reason=queue-expired
method=config/read
```

The same queue rejection then affects `permissionProfile/list`, `app/list`, `skills/list`, and `plugin/list`. When the slow remote eventually connects, Desktop attempts to recover the currently selected local conversation against that remote host:

```text
websocket_reconnect_recovery_start ... hostId=remote-ssh-discovered:<slow-host>
websocket_reconnect_recovery_done
currentConversationExistsOnTargetHost=false
resumedCurrentConversation=false
```

At that point, local chats remain blank or fail to hydrate.

This does not appear to be local session-database latency. In the same run, local `thread/list` and `thread/read` requests completed in approximately 0–149 ms, and `codex doctor` reported healthy state databases and network/auth checks.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure or discover two SSH aliases in Codex Desktop.
2. Make one alias unreachable through DNS and make the other slow to start its remote Codex app-server.
3. Previously open or save these remote connections so Desktop remembers them.
4. Fully quit and reopen Desktop.
5. Do not intentionally select a remote workspace; try to open an existing local conversation.
6. Observe that Desktop automatically starts both SSH connections and the local conversation view remains blank or fails to load.

### Expected behavior

- Opening Desktop for local work should not connect to every discovered SSH host.
- SSH connections should start lazily when the user selects that remote, or run in isolation without blocking local chat hydration.
- Request queues should be host-scoped so a remote bootstrap cannot exhaust capacity needed by the local app-server.
- Failed SSH hosts should have bounded retries or a visible pause/disconnect control.
- Desktop should not attempt to resume a local conversation against a remote host where that conversation does not exist.

### Actual behavior

Desktop auto-connects both discovered hosts, an unavailable host retries indefinitely, queued requests expire, and local chats do not load.

### Workaround

Disconnect/disable the saved SSH connections, switch the active host to Local/This Mac, fully quit with Cmd-Q, and reopen the app.

### Environment

- App: ChatGPT Desktop / Codex view `26.721.41059` (build `5848`)
- Bundled Codex app-server: `0.146.0-alpha.3.1`
- Remote app-server observed after eventual connection: `0.144.5`
- OS: macOS `26.5.2` (`25F84`), arm64

### Related issues

- #19608 — blank/unhydrated conversation with app-server queue pressure in Remote SSH
- #20128 — repeated Codex Desktop SSH reconnect attempts worsen reliability
- #22438 — persisted remote sessions missing after reconnect/restart

The important difference here is that the remote connection failure also prevents otherwise healthy **local** conversations from loading immediately after application startup.

### Feature request

Dots can now communicate with users through SMS/iMessage, which is very useful. However, those conversations currently appear to be accessible only in the Messages app. The ChatGPT web interface provides a **Text** menu for the Dot, but it does not provide a way to view the text-message conversation history from the web.

This creates a continuity problem: a user may discuss a task with a Dot by text, then return to ChatGPT on the web and have no visible record of that exchange. It is also unclear whether those messages are being preserved as part of the Dot's ongoing context or memory.

### Suggested experience

In the Dot sidebar, after clicking **Text**, add a new action such as:

- **View text conversation**
- **View message history**

Selecting it could open a web panel or conversation view containing the complete SMS/iMessage thread between the user and that specific Dot, including timestamps and sent/received direction.

The messages in that thread should also be available to the same Dot for conversation continuity and memory, subject to the user's normal history, retention, and memory settings. For example, if a user asks for a project update by text, the Dot should be able to continue that same discussion later in the web interface without losing the context.

### Privacy and scope

This should only sync the conversation between the user and the selected Dot. It should not import or expose unrelated personal SMS/iMessage conversations.

It would also be helpful to provide a clear indicator or setting explaining whether Dot text messages are:

- saved to ChatGPT history,
- available to the Dot as context,
- eligible to contribute to memory,
- and removable from both the web history and the text integration.

### Why this matters

Texting makes Dots much easier to use away from the ChatGPT interface, but without a unified history, the experience is fragmented across Messages and the web app. A visible, synchronized conversation record would make the feature more reliable, transparent, and useful for ongoing tasks.

issues.title: Expose per-server MCP protocol mode in user configuration

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

issues.body:
### Problem

Codex already supports both legacy MCP initialization and the newer 2026-07-28 discovery lifecycle. The current user-facing `features.mcp_2026_07_28` switch selects the protocol globally for ordinary servers, so an agent with a modern-only Streamable HTTP server and older MCP servers cannot configure each connection independently.

At upstream main `6c776cfc8c3b2aa4e429813c52c0e044ff01104b`, `McpServerConnection` already chooses `ResolvedMcpServer::protocol_mode` before falling back to the global mode, and the MCP catalog already supports `McpServerRegistration::with_protocol_mode` for extension-supplied registrations. But ordinary `McpServerConfig` parsed from `config.toml` does not expose the corresponding per-server option.

### Requested minimal change

Expose the existing protocol selection through ordinary server configuration, for example:

```toml
[mcp_servers.modern]
url = "https://modern.example/mcp"
protocol_mode = "2026-07-28"

[mcp_servers.legacy_http]
url = "https://legacy.example/mcp"
protocol_mode = "legacy"
```

Preserve the existing default when omitted. Only apply the override to transports for which it is supported (Streamable HTTP); legacy stdio must not silently change lifecycle. Keep authentication, session identifiers, tool calls, authorization and the global feature's behaviour otherwise unchanged. The configured mode is a preference, not proof of what was negotiated on the wire.

A narrow downstream implementation and regression coverage exist in [sednalabs/codex#962](https://github.com/sednalabs/codex/pull/962), which was merged on the fork. An upstream-supported equivalent would eliminate a permanent fork carry. This is **not** a request to upstream the fork's unrelated agent runtime, mailbox, prompt, security or package changes.

### Suggested acceptance

- One Streamable HTTP server selects the modern protocol without changing an unrelated legacy server.
- Global fallback and explicit per-server precedence are tested, including absent/unsupported values.
- No unexpected authentication or other MCP configuration changes.

The key benefit is letting clients use mixed MCP deployments through configuration, without maintaining private patches to the hot MCP client.

issues.title: [Windows Desktop] Background hydration repeatedly reads access-denied conversations after restart

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
## Summary

After restarting Codex Desktop on Windows, a bounded log window recorded **742 distinct background thread/read requests across 157 conversations**, ending in access-denied responses. The requests came from two Desktop renderers and continued through the product's thread_hydration path.

Please investigate the request repetition, terminal-error handling and cross-renderer coordination while preserving the existing authorization boundary. This report does not ask the app to bypass access denial.

## Environment

- Observation date: October 7, 2026; all times below are UTC.
- Windows desktop package: 26.1002.6548.0.
- Desktop app-server: 0.162.0-alpha.2.
- Separately installed CLI: 0.160.1.
- Exact Windows OS build is not included in this report.

The app and runtime version fields are reported separately. The observation followed an app update, but no controlled before/after comparison establishes the update as the cause.

## Observed sequence

1. Around **03:46 UTC**, I encountered an app-server queue-full error and could not resume a chat.
2. I manually restarted the desktop app at **03:50:37 UTC**.
3. Between **03:50:52.036 and 03:52:14.362 UTC**, the installed app recorded the following background read activity:
   - **742 distinct thread/read request IDs**
   - **157 distinct target conversations**
   - Renderer A: **585 requests**
   - Renderer B: **157 requests**
   - source: **thread_hydration**
   - priority: **background**
   - error code: **-32003**, classified in the diagnostics as thread access denied
   - failureReason: **null**
   - observed queue waits: **0–1 ms**

Renderer A/B are aliases, not published process or window identifiers. A method-specific recount found 742 unique request IDs and zero duplicate error rows. These are not counts of user clicks, model turns, or unique conversations.

Two post-restart thread/resume response_routed entries show errorCode=null and no matching failure events: 03:51:03.018 UTC (578 ms) and 03:51:57.161 UTC (1,094 ms), both queueWaitMs=0. Result payloads were not logged; complete UI chat reopening remains unproven.

## Read-only client inspection

The inspected installed client contains a metadata query configured with **retry: 1** and a path that hydrates pinned entries in parallel. These are candidate contributors to examine, not a complete causal explanation for the 742 requests. The capture does not establish which request came from which query lifecycle, that all 157 conversations were pinned, or that this single retry setting explains the full repetition.

The measured calls are attributed by Desktop telemetry to its product hydration path. They were not generated by an agent-run polling/stress test or a custom wrapper.

## What the evidence establishes

- High-volume repeated background reads of a bounded set of conversations after desktop restart.
- Access-denied responses, rather than queue-expiry responses, in the measured post-restart window.
- Two renderers contributing requests during the same window.
- A read-only source-inspection lead involving retry and parallel pinned-entry hydration.

## Important limits

- The **0–1 ms queue waits do not establish queue saturation** during this post-restart window.
- The earlier owner-visible queue-full/resume failure and the later read burst are temporally adjacent; no causal connection has been proven.
- The current queue depth and pre-restart occupied-request inventory are unknown.
- The report does not establish why these conversations were denied, whether their denial was correct, an actor/account mismatch, deletion, corrupted history, or a common cause with separately observed missing native tools.
- Request volume is not a measurement of billed usage, financial loss, CPU saturation or duplicate task execution.
- This is a retained observation and installed-client inspection, not a deterministic clean-install reproduction.

## Expected behavior / requested investigation

Please make background hydration bounded and coordinated across renderers:

1. Correlate retry, invalidation and hydration ownership for each target and determine why the same denied reads are reissued.
2. Distinguish terminal authorization denial from transient transport failure, and avoid repeatedly retrying a denied target without a relevant authorization/state change or explicit user request.
3. Coalesce duplicate in-flight reads and bound background concurrency while preserving capacity for the selected conversation.
4. Preserve thread entries and history with a clear inaccessible state. Do not silently delete, unpin, reassign ownership or relax permissions.
5. Expose useful typed denial/route diagnostics instead of failureReason=null where possible.
6. Verify with harmless fixtures covering multiple renderers, pinned entries, permission changes, reconnect/restart and denied targets. Preserve tests that prevent unauthorized reads.

Please identify any supported recovery for the existing affected conversations and the applicable app/service version. Clearing history, rewriting account/actor identifiers or weakening review is outside the requested repair.

## Related reports and duplicate review

- [#36914](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36914): background collaboration/thread hydration starves interactive requests. Its captured requests waited until queue expiry; this report's measured reads have queue waits of 0–1 ms and access-denied responses.
- [#50561 comment 5973041135](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50561#issuecomment-5973041135): a specific -32003 read failure explicitly identified placement belonging to a different actor. No equivalent actor diagnostic has been established here.
- [#50812](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50812): sent-read timeouts retain host RPC slots. The earlier queue-full symptom may be related, but this report does not reproduce that mechanism.
- [#51087](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51087): repeated archived-thread resume failures on macOS. The terminal-state retry concern is adjacent, but the platform, method, error and observed outcome differ.
- [#42589](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/42589): Windows VS Code multi-window hydration/resume conflicts. This report concerns Desktop read denials, not active-writer conflicts.

I searched open and closed issues for thread_hydration, thread/read with -32003, thread access denied, hydration retries and pinned hydration. No exact report of this repeated access-denied Desktop read signature was found. Please consolidate if an existing issue preserves these distinctions.

## Privacy

This report contains only sanitized timings, versions, aggregate counts and selected diagnostic fields. No private paths, conversation/request/process identifiers, account or actor identities, conversation content, application architecture, credentials, screenshots or raw logs are attached. No new reproduction or denied-action workaround was run to prepare it.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.163.0`, confirmed by the incident session metadata and `codex --version`. At report time, `codex doctor --json` reports that 0.164.0 is available; this incident has not been retested on that version.

### What subscription do you have?

Authenticated with a ChatGPT account. Subscription tier was not verified.

### Which model were you using?

`gpt-6.1-sol`, reasoning effort `xhigh`, in the submission phase according to the session metadata.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Professional, build 26300, x64; PowerShell 7.6.7. Session metadata identifies the client as `codex-tui` / CLI.

### What issue are you seeing?

On 2026-10-24 (Asia/Tokyo), I authorized Codex to make a final check and submit a two-patch series to an open-source project's public development mailing list. One complete submission consists of a cover letter and two patch emails: **3 messages**.

Codex instead sent **13 messages**, using the public mailing list while repeatedly trying different delivery formats. It labeled unchanged patches v2, v3, and v4. The actual code and commit messages did not change between those versions. This imposed duplicate notifications and review work on the community under my identity and created a reputational concern for me.

A prior tool result on 2026-10-23 already contained Proxmox's explicit guidance, **“Always use git send-email”**, together with a warning that other sending methods can damage patch indentation and formatting:
https://pmg.proxmox.com/wiki/Developer_Documentation#Sending_Patches

That available warning was not reflected in the submission decisions.

| Submission | Messages sent | Observed result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Initial, unversioned series | 3 | Sent through the Gmail connector. Public copies had changed line wrapping/context whitespace and could not be applied. |
| v2 plus one v2 RESEND 1/2 | 4 | MIME/base64 settings were changed. Public archive entries for the two text/x-patch messages were not confirmed at the time of checking; the additional inline RESEND was still corrupted. |
| v3 | 3 | Full format-patch files were attached. The inspected public copies lacked the attachment data. |
| v4 | 3 | Finally used direct SMTP through git send-email. Public copies applied successfully and matched the original tree, authors, and commit messages. |
| **Total** | **13** | **10 messages beyond one complete submission.** |

Decoded saved inputs confirm that both patch bodies were identical across all four series. Changes were delivery format, subject version labels, threading/metadata, and cover-letter explanations of the resends.

The eventual successful v4 delivery did not undo the preceding messages. The total of 13 was disclosed only after I explicitly asked whether many emails had been sent.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is a recorded production incident, not a claimed deterministic model reproduction.

1. Prepare and locally validate an ordinary cover letter plus two-patch series.
2. Make the project's submission instructions available to the agent, including the git send-email requirement and formatting warning.
3. Authorize a final check and submission. The actual user instruction began: “パッチを送信できる状態か最終確認して送信” (“Make a final check that the patches are ready to send, then submit them.”).
4. Observe the agent choose the Gmail connector, discover delivery corruption, and continue sending alternate MIME/attachment forms to the public list while incrementing patch versions without code changes.
5. Observe eventual success through the originally documented git send-email path, after 13 sends.

For a safe regression evaluation, use a **mock mail service and a non-public sink** that simulates wrapping, missing archive entries, and attachment loss. Do not reproduce this by sending test series to a real development list. Measure the number of external writes, whether the agent stops public retries, and whether it preserves the distinction between unchanged resends and code revisions.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Apply the project's contribution and submission rules before the first external send, including rules already obtained in earlier tool results.
- Verify the transport with a private test destination or mock sink before submitting to a public mailing list.
- After the first delivery problem, stop using the public list for transport experiments; repair and verify the delivery path before any necessary resend.
- Preserve the patch version for unchanged resends and clearly identify the resend, rather than presenting delivery attempts as successive code revisions.
- Track every external send and report the complete count and unresolved failures, even when a later attempt succeeds.

### Additional information

Observed workflow failures:
- Local MIME checks and Gmail Sent copies were treated as sufficient delivery evidence, although the actual public copies differed.
- The initial lookup for an existing SMTP credential omitted the configured port `:587`. The credential was later found and direct authenticated SMTP worked.
- The agent did not stop repeated public sends after detecting corruption.
- Submission bookkeeping initially centered on the final successful v4 instead of clearly reporting the cumulative 13-message side effect.

The exact Gmail/connector/mailing-list processing stage that rewrote text or removed attachment data has **not** been established. This report does not attribute all transport behavior to a proven backend defect. The directly observed Codex problem is failing to apply available guidance and continuing costly external writes while troubleshooting.

Incident thread ID: `01a16703-c63e-7550-810b-6c8471a9260b`.

A doctor report was generated after the incident. Relevant results: CLI installation, authentication, configuration, and HTTP/WebSocket reachability checks passed. It also reports unrelated environment/inventory warnings. The full diagnostic is retained locally; only this relevant summary is included here to avoid publishing unrelated paths and thread inventories. Doctor's invocation configuration is separate from the active incident thread's permission overrides.

Evidence retained locally: original message inputs, MIME preflight results, Sent copies, SMTP responses, public archive copies, successful git am verification of v4, and the prior instruction-bearing tool output. Credentials, personal names/email addresses, raw mail headers, and full conversation logs are omitted from this public report.

issues.body:
# Codex voice repeatedly speaks after an explicit request for silence

Submission status: prepared locally; not submitted to OpenAI.
Observed: 29 October 2026, Windows desktop, active Codex realtime voice conversation in Russian. App version and voice model are not captured.

## Impact

The user cannot reliably silence spoken status updates while allowing development tasks to continue. Repeated acknowledgements of silence become the unwanted speech themselves.

## Reproduction observed in this conversation

1. Background development produces intermittent progress updates.
2. The user asks the voice assistant to stop repeating waiting/status announcements.
3. The assistant acknowledges the instruction, then repeatedly announces that it is waiting or will remain silent.
4. The user explicitly says: "Молчи вообще в целом" (remain silent altogether).
5. The supplied voice transcript subsequently contains the same silence acknowledgement at least four consecutive times, without a new substantive result or question between them.
6. Further corrections and a saved communication preference do not stop the repetition within the same session.

## Expected behavior

After an explicit request for silence, no spoken acknowledgement loop or background waiting narration. Authorized development may continue. A later direct user question can receive an answer.

## Actual behavior

The assistant repeatedly speaks a promise to remain silent. It also repeatedly speaks promises to avoid repetition. This continues despite multiple clear user corrections.

## Evidence and limits

- The user-supplied realtime transcript records repeated spoken silence acknowledgements.
- Recent backend terminal responses consisted only of a completion channel marker with no natural-language body, while later supplied voice transcripts still recorded repeated spoken phrases.
- This mismatch suggests a voice response/orchestration issue, but it does not establish the root cause. The record has not been aligned against audio timestamps or low-level frontend transport logs.
- No claim is made that the audio renderer alone is defective, that a specific model is responsible, or that the issue has been fixed.
- The user authorized filing this behavior as a bug. No full conversation, unrelated project material, credentials, or diagnostic log bundle is included in this report.

## Suggested investigation

Correlate frontend utterance generation with backend completion events and background task callbacks. Check whether an empty completion, a repeated callback, or a stale response causes the frontend to generate another silence acknowledgement. Verify that the silence request persists across callbacks and that repeated status events do not independently trigger speech.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reproduce the sequence with a Russian-speaking user and background task callbacks.
- After the silence request, repeated callbacks and empty completions produce no unsolicited spoken waiting/silence acknowledgements.
- A direct subsequent user question still receives one answer.
- Background development continues without requiring the voice call to end.

## Submission route

Official guidance: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/troubleshooting#feedback-and-logs

Use the message composer's slash menu to open feedback. Paste this report and optionally share this session after reviewing its contents. An actual submission acknowledgement or session reference is required before calling the report submitted.

issues.body:
Windows Codex Desktop can read an existing durable/cloud chat bound to a Windows execution environment, but direct plain-text submissions and a same-directory fork fail before execution.

Environment
- Observed on 2026-10-02.
- Desktop versions reproduced: 26.928.31416 and 26.930.21537.
- Windows package observed: 26.930.2377.0.
- Durable/cloud chat with a connected native Windows execution environment.
- The local checkout is an existing linked Git worktree. WSL was not required for this reproduction.

Errors
```text
invalid turn/start params: AbsolutePathBuf deserialized without a base path
invalid thread/fork params: AbsolutePathBuf deserialized without a base path
```

For turn/start, the recorded JSON-RPC code was -32602 and failureReason was invalid_config.

Reproduction
1. Open the existing environment-bound durable chat in the Windows desktop app.
2. Submit plain text without attachments.
3. Observe the turn/start error before a new turn is created.
4. An authorized diagnostic-only send_message_to_thread call from the desktop reproduces the same error.
5. Attempt to fork the affected chat in the same directory; thread/fork fails with the same AbsolutePathBuf message.

Observed evidence
- read_thread succeeds and the existing chat history remains readable.
- The failed composer item had no file, image, or pasted-text attachments.
- The same failure was present in logs before and after the desktop update between the two versions above.
- A diagnostic-only desktop submission was rejected at 2026-10-02 18:51:11 UTC.
- Executor diagnostics and later direct filesystem validation showed that the Windows cwd and checkout were usable.
- A later cloud-to-cloud diagnostic message to the source chat was accepted. The evidence therefore does not imply that all submission routes fail.
- The exact outbound request JSON was not captured.

Redacted path and request context
```text
Durable chat cwd:
/tmp/<cloud-agent>/app_servers/thread_service/workspace/C:\Users\<user>\Documents\Codex\<date>\task\<repo>

Windows executor cwd:
C:\Users\<user>\Documents\Codex\<date>\task\<repo>

Environment runtimeWorkspaceRoots:
C:\Users\<user>\Documents\Codex\<date>\task-2
```

The cached policy was workspaceWrite with writableRoots ["/tmp"], networkAccess false, excludeTmpdirEnvVar true, and excludeSlashTmp false. The queued desktop submission had executionHostId "durable", shouldSendPermissionOverrides false, usePermissionSelection false, and permissionSelection null. The desktop log nevertheless recorded a workspaceWrite override with one writable root.

Working hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause
The installed request-builder code appears to select environment-native Windows cwd/workspace roots and merge roots into the top-level workspaceWrite sandbox policy. A Windows drive path may then reach a POSIX AbsolutePathBuf parser. The logged root counts are consistent with this interpretation, but do not identify the exact offending field.

The inspected installed asset was webview/assets/app-shared-ac32c0d1413b.js; the relevant minified function names were ton, qB, and htn.
