issues.title: [macOS] Pages entry missing and Page references unavailable after restart; feature bootstrap times out

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1023.50603, build 22391, production distribution. Verified from the installed app bundle metadata, rather than the About dialog. Bundle identifier: `com.openai.codex`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this report.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 14.7, Apple Silicon.

```text
Darwin 23.6.0 arm64 arm
```

### What issue are you seeing?

The native **Pages entry has disappeared from the desktop navigation/overflow menu**, and existing Page references in chats display **“不可用的页面” (“Unavailable Page”)**. Fully quitting with Cmd+Q and relaunching does not restore either the entry or the Page references.

The documents themselves are still accessible: authorized Pages tool reads successfully returned the full content of two affected documents, with `deleted_at=null` and `can_read=true`. Their IDs, titles and contents are omitted here.

In a fresh startup on **2026-10-29**, main-window account lookup succeeded, but user-settings/profile requests failed and post-login feature-configuration bootstrap timed out. This is a correlation, not a confirmed causal diagnosis.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On this affected installation:

1. Launch the desktop app and open the navigation overflow menu. Pages is absent.
2. Open a chat that contains a previously saved Page reference. The reference shows “Unavailable Page”.
3. Completely quit the app with Cmd+Q, relaunch it, and repeat steps 1–2.
4. The problem persists after startup. The fresh-startup logs below show successful account lookup followed by request failures and feature-bootstrap timeout.

This describes reproduction on an already affected installation; the initial trigger has not been isolated, and a clean-install reproduction is not established. The user previously moved the computer between networks, which explains some older network-change events but does not establish the cause of the current failure.

### What is the expected behavior?

Previously accessible Pages should remain reachable through the native desktop navigation and Page references. If a temporary initialization or request failure prevents access, the app should offer an actionable error/retry state instead of leaving the entry absent and existing references generically unavailable.

### Additional information

#### Sanitized log evidence

The following contains **selected fields extracted from local desktop logs**, not complete raw lines. Timestamps are **UTC**; add eight hours for Asia/Shanghai. Local paths, user/account/document/session identifiers, request headers and stack traces have been omitted.

```text
2026-10-29T02:44:29.111Z event=startup
2026-10-29T02:44:37.590Z event=account_lookup rendererWindowAppearance="primary" result="succeeded" authenticatedAccountPresent=true hasEverErrored=false authMethod="chatgpt"
2026-10-29T02:45:09.092Z event=request_failure rendererWindowAppearance="primary" routePattern="/settings/user" status=500 errorCode="undefined" errorMessage="fail to touch upstream"
2026-10-29T02:45:38.274Z event=bootstrap_failure rendererWindowAppearance="primary" errorMessage="Timed out while fetching post-login Statsig bootstrap" attemptNumber=6
2026-10-29T02:45:55.050Z event=account_lookup rendererWindowAppearance="avatarOverlay" result="succeeded" authenticatedAccountPresent=true hasEverErrored=false authMethod="chatgpt"
2026-10-29T02:46:18.672Z event=request_failure rendererWindowAppearance="primary" routePattern="/profiles/me" status=500 errorCode="undefined" errorMessage="fail to touch upstream"
2026-10-29T02:46:57.569Z event=bootstrap_failure rendererWindowAppearance="avatarOverlay" errorMessage="Timed out while fetching post-login Statsig bootstrap" attemptNumber=6
```

The main-window post-login bootstrap also timed out on the preceding startup on October 28. In the inspected fresh-startup log interval, **02:44:29–03:07:50 UTC on October 29**, there were no `routePattern=/pages...` records. That absence does not prove either successful Pages requests or the precise reason they are unavailable.

Historical Pages failures from October 27:

```text
2026-10-27T01:31:03.866Z routePattern="/pages/{page_id}" status=403 errorCode="cloudflare_challenge" rendererWindowAppearance="primary"
2026-10-27T01:51:37.847Z routePattern="/pages/{page_id}" status=403 errorCode="cloudflare_challenge" rendererWindowAppearance="primary"
```

These historical 403s were **not observed in the fresh-startup interval above**. They should not be treated as proof that the current startup has the same failure.

#### Read-only investigation findings

Inspection of the installed JavaScript bundle found:

- Native Pages functionality is still present in this build.
- Pages availability depends on capability and feature-gate state. There are branches that return disabled on capability errors, as well as a special earlier branch; this is not an assertion about the actual runtime state.
- The Page-reference metadata resolver can return null immediately when Pages is not enabled or account context is missing. The localized `codex.space.reference.unavailableTitle` message includes the observed “不可用的页面” text. Thus this label alone does not establish document deletion.
- Post-login bootstrap failure has a fallback initialization path, so a timeout alone does not establish the final gate value.

Relevant bundle for the availability/reference observations: `app-initial-b539f0af92f3.js`. Bootstrap handling was inspected in `initialize-app-host-services-3253d49270fb.js`. These were read only; no app files or feature flags were modified.

#### What remains unconfirmed

- The actual runtime Pages capability/gate values, and which condition hides the entry.
- Whether the bootstrap failure is caused by the client, the network/request path, or an upstream service.
- Whether the settings/profile failures and bootstrap timeout share a cause.
- Whether fallback initialization recovers usable Pages configuration.

`status=500` above is preserved as a **client log field**; the originating layer of the “fail to touch upstream” response is not established. Successful Page tool reads also do not prove that the desktop's separate request/initialization path is healthy.

No logout, cache deletion, data reset, application patching or forced feature flags were performed. A complete user-initiated restart was tried and did not restore Pages.

#### Related reports

- #49372 — desktop Pages/Space requests receiving Cloudflare 403 challenges.
- #53901 — a different desktop navigation symptom involving Pages prewarm and availability handling.

These are related evidence, **not confirmed duplicates or an established shared root cause**. This report focuses on the missing native Pages entry plus unavailable Page references after restart, with successful account lookup and repeated post-login bootstrap timeout.

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, the desktop app's bundled marketplace sync repeatedly fails with `copyfile UNKNOWN`, leaving the installed Browser plugin older than the version shipped with the application. Updating the Browser package to the exact app-bundled version repairs the package mismatch, but the in-app browser is still absent from the supported Browser discovery API after a full application restart.

This blocks browser-assisted work. Related browser routing/permission symptoms are tracked in #48670; this report adds a reproducible bundled-package copy failure and the subsequent discovery behavior.

## Environment

- Desktop installedVersion: `26.1013.40934`, build `20770`, release channel `prod`.
- Windows app package version: `26.1013.4894.0` (a different version field).
- Browser plugin initially registered/cached: `26.924.22138`.
- Browser plugin shipped with the current application: `26.1013.40934`.
- UI language: Simplified Chinese.
- The default user configuration directory is a Windows junction to another local drive.
- Interactive approval was enabled for the final tests.
- Observed on 2026-10-21. The exact Windows OS build was not collected.

## Reproduction and observed results

### 1. Bundled marketplace sync fails

Normal app startup repeatedly records:

```text
[BundledPluginsMarketplace] plugin_marketplace_folder_write_failed
[BundledPluginsMarketplace] bundled_plugins_marketplace_resolve_failed
UNKNOWN: unknown error, copyfile
'<WindowsApps package>/app/resources/plugins/openai-bundled/plugins/<plugin>/.codex-plugin/plugin.json'
-> '<user configuration>/.tmp/bundled-marketplaces/openai-bundled.staging-<redacted>/plugins/<plugin>/.codex-plugin/plugin.json'
```

Failures were logged for codex-app-tools, Browser, unified-computer-use, and Chrome at different attempts.

A controlled copy of the official codex-app-tools plugin manifest into a disposable workspace reproduced the failure with Node's `fs.copyFileSync`. Reading the same file with `fs.readFileSync` and writing those exact bytes with `fs.writeFileSync` succeeded. The package alias and physical installation paths both reproduced it; their source SHA256 values matched.

### 2. Package mismatch was isolated and repaired, but this did not resolve browser use

Only the Browser software directory in the existing registered marketplace was backed up and restored byte-for-byte from the current app's bundled package. The marketplace registration, catalog, permission records, credentials, and browser profile were left untouched.

The app-bundled CLI command `codex plugin add browser@openai-bundled --json` then returned version `26.1013.40934`. A subsequent plugin list confirmed installed/enabled at that version. All 384 installed Browser files matched the official package's SHA256 inventory.

The running CLI executable also matched the current application's bundled CLI executable by SHA256. No security-check code was altered.

### 3. After fully restarting the app, IAB still cannot be selected

A fresh runtime was initialized from the newly installed Browser client using the documented API:

```js
const agent = await setupBrowserRuntime();
await agent.browsers.get("iab");
// Browser is not available: iab

await agent.browsers.list();
// Only a "Codex MCP Apps" entry with type "mcpapps"; no "iab" entry.
```

Native application navigation to the current chat reports success. Opening a browser tab through the native application tool reports `queued`; desktop logs nevertheless record creation of the browser sidebar tab.

Each observed discovery batch contains both:
- an IAB `getInfo` failure: `No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session <redacted>`; and
- a successful `getInfo` completion whose session metadata matches the current chat.

The created sidebar tab is logged under a temporary `client-new-thread:<redacted>` identifier while its owner route points at the current real chat. This is a diagnostic observation, not a confirmed root cause.

Before the package refresh/restart, content reads failed with `saved browser permissions could not be verified`. Switching from noninteractive to interactive approval did not resolve that failure.

## Expected result / requested investigation

1. Bundled plugin synchronization should reliably install the application-shipped versions, or expose an actionable recovery error.
2. A successfully registered, approved in-app browser should be discoverable.
3. Discovery diagnostics should distinguish routing failure, post-handshake capability-check failure, and session/build/backend filtering instead of silently omitting the candidate.
4. Please provide a supported recovery procedure that preserves browser sessions and security checks.

No alternative browser, raw CDP, private permission-store modification, or security-check bypass was used. This public report intentionally excludes account details, private domains, local usernames, full paths, chat/session identifiers, raw logs, credentials, and business data.

issues.title: [Windows] Capacity errors across Desktop, CLI (WebSocket disabled), and ChatGPT Work despite available allowance

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## Summary

Persistent `Selected model is at capacity` failures across Codex Desktop and standalone Codex CLI, alongside repeated failures in browser-based ChatGPT Work, during **October 27–29, 2026 (UTC+8)**. Ordinary ChatGPT conversations still work in Edge, Chrome, and Android.

Crucially, OpenAI Support reviewed two failed turns and stated that they were **server-overload errors while both the five-hour and weekly Codex allowances still had available capacity**. This is a reported support finding, not an independently verified root-cause diagnosis.

## Environment

- ChatGPT Plus subscription
- Windows; Codex Desktop package version `26.1023.6123.0` (Oct 29)
- Standalone CLI `codex-cli 0.165.0-alpha.1.2`
- Selected model in CLI test: `gpt-6-astra`, reasoning effort `high`
- Local HTTP proxy configured, US network egress; other proxy/TUN tests did not reliably resolve failures
- Model provider configuration uses OpenAI authentication, `wire_api="responses"`

## Minimal CLI reproduction

1. Launch the current standalone Codex CLI with the **invocation-only** override:
   ```powershell
   & $codex -c 'model_providers.custom.supports_websockets=false'
   ```
2. In a new interactive session, ask in Chinese: `Please report the current working directory and list up to five filenames. Read only; do not modify files.`
3. The request fails with:
   ```
   Selected model is at capacity.
   Please try a different model.
   ```

This occurs for a minimal read-only request without needing the original research project's long context. The override does not by itself prove which transport the server used, but the failure persists after turning off the provider WebSocket option.

## Desktop / Work symptoms

- Desktop occasionally handles a simple greeting, but existing long-running research threads and new multi-step work often fail, sometimes *after* starting tool calls.
- Repeated `Reconnecting 1/5 … 5/5`, then failure.
- Browser-based ChatGPT Work also encounters capacity errors.
- Ordinary ChatGPT conversations in browsers and Android function normally.

## Relevant client log signatures

- `WebSocket was closed before the connection was established`
- `closeCode=1006`
- `Unexpected server response: 401`
- `ECONNRESET`
- `stream disconnected - retrying sampling request`
- `stream disconnected before completion`
- Windows socket error `10054`

These signatures span more than one failure type; the logs do **not** establish that every issue has a single cause.

## Troubleshooting already performed

- Restarted the app and reauthenticated; checked proxy environment and connectivity.
- Tested TUN/network adapter mode; no reliable improvement.
- Restored the original TOML config after a separate configuration-edit attempt.
- Tested the current standalone CLI separately from Desktop, including the per-run WebSocket setting override.
- Verified ordinary ChatGPT works on multiple platforms.

## Expected / actual

**Expected:** Authorized tasks can complete with allowance available, and recover gracefully from transient backend/streaming errors.

**Actual:** Capacity errors prevent trivial as well as substantial work, sometimes following partial execution, with no useful recovery path.

## Engineering investigation requested

Please examine whether capacity admission/model routing, server-overload retries, session/authentication recovery, and streaming/tool-handoff failures are connected; identify a reproducible fix or mitigation, or identify the appropriate service-side owner if this is not a Codex client bug.

Similar reports: #53569, #56324, #57748. This issue adds a recent standalone-CLI reproduction with WebSocket disabled and the reported support confirmation of available allowance.

Sanitized logs and screenshots can be provided privately on request. Raw logs, personal account identifiers, support ticket IDs, and research files are intentionally omitted from this public issue.

**Separate private support concern:** disputed allowance consumption during failed/retried requests and three days of interrupted academic work; this requires a private account-level investigation and is not being requested through this public repository.

## Summary
Computer Use in the ChatGPT desktop app on Windows can discover/open Notepad, read its accessibility tree, and update its editor via `set_value`, but screenshot capture consistently times out.

## Environment
- Windows 10 Home Single Language 22H2, build 19045
- Intel HD Graphics 5500; driver 20.19.15.5063, WDDM 2.0

- Desktop app updated before retesting; exact app version not recorded

1. Enable Computer Use and allow Notepad.
2. Open Notepad and select its returned window.
3. Activate the window.
4. Call `get_window_state` with `include_screenshot: true`.
5. Refresh window discovery and retry.

Repeated errors:
```text
FrameArrived timed out: timed out waiting on channel
window capture timed out: timed out waiting on channel
```
An earlier click attempt returned:
```text
coordinate input geometry is unavailable
```
Accessibility-only reads succeed. `set_value` successfully updated the editor, verified by a subsequent accessibility read.

## Expected result
Capture the selected window and support screenshot-based interaction.

## Troubleshooting attempted
- Updated the desktop app
- Restarted the computer
- Used Windows app Repair
- Reset the JavaScript session and reinitialized the library
- Refreshed window discovery and retried capture

The errors persist. Windows display diagnostics reported no device problem; root cause remains unknown. Chrome extension browser control was separately observed working.

## Feedback reference
In-app feedback ID: `01a10427-af85-7ed1-9053-6a3c818d0037`

Please advise on a fix or additional diagnostics needed to determine why Windows Graphics Capture is not delivering a frame.

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

## English summary

Codex repeatedly failed to edit an Arabic academic Word research document according to explicit and repeated instructions. It altered the original text, changed paragraphs that were outside the requested scope, failed to implement Word comments item by item, did not build the requested model and structure, mishandled Arabic RTL formatting and footnotes, and then claimed that the document had been carefully reviewed even though the delivered file did not match the requirements.

## التفاصيل بالعربية

كانت تجربتي مع الخدمة في تحرير بحث عربي أكاديمي تجربة سيئة ومهدرة للوقت. لم تكن المشكلة خطأً عابرًا، بل تكررت إخفاقات جوهرية، منها:

- العبث بالنص الأصلي بدل المحافظة عليه.
- تعديل فقرات لم أطلب تعديلها.
- عدم تنفيذ تعليقات ملف Word بندًا بندًا.
- عدم بناء النموذج وفق الهيكل المطلوب.
- ضعف التعامل مع تنسيق العربية والحواشي واتجاه النص.
- تسليم ملفات مع الادعاء بأنها روجعت بدقة، مع أنها لا تطابق المطلوب.
- إجبار الباحث على إعادة شرح التعليمات وتصحيح أخطاء الأداة مرارًا.

هذه الخدمة بصورتها الحالية لا تراعي حساسية العمل البحثي؛ فالباحث يحتاج إلى أداة تحفظ نصه، وتفرّق بين التعليمات والمادة العلمية، وتنفذ التعديلات المحددة دون اجتهادات مفسدة.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Feedback ID: 01a177e3-d5c0-7cf1-b44a-698966be6021

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should preserve the source document and its structure, apply only explicitly requested changes comment by comment, maintain correct Arabic RTL layout and true Word footnotes, provide a reliable comparison with the original, and never claim that verification is complete unless the delivered file actually matches the instructions.

### Additional information

I am a paid ChatGPT Pro subscriber and expected a professional service proportionate to the subscription cost. I did not receive the requested service or the promised level of accuracy. Presenting the work as complete and carefully reviewed despite its clear noncompliance is, in my view, contrary to quality, precision, professional integrity, and transparency. It creates a feeling of having paid for a service that was not actually delivered.

I request a serious investigation of this experience, an explanation of the failure, safeguards for preserving researchers' original documents, and consideration of appropriate compensation for the time and money lost.

prs.title: Build V8 from source by default in Bazel
prs.body:
Build V8 from source by default in Bazel

## Why

Source-built V8 archives and generated Rust bindings must agree on their ABI, including in debug builds. Linux platform selection must also distinguish GNU and musl when using LLVM platforms.

## What changed

- Always select source-built V8 archives and matching bindings for Bazel consumers, removing the `rusty_v8_from_source` flag.

- Keep `V8_ENABLE_CHECKS` undefined in debug builds to match Rust's `HandleScope` layout, and set `V8_LOGGING_LEVEL=2` for debug verification.
- Include compiler-rt builtins in the ARM64 GNU/Linux archive to provide `__clear_cache`.
- Set the Intel macOS minimum version for `codex-code-mode-host` releases to 10.13 for V8's aligned allocation support.

## Testing

Always include the existing ignored CppGC ABI checks in Bazel `v8-poc` unit tests and remove their exclusion from Bazel CI.

Waiting for the event channel to close after `ShutdownComplete` retains the thread runtime because the thread owns its event sender. Remaining subscribers still need late notifications after shutdown.

- Close the status watch when removing a thread so a later load gets a fresh watch.

issues.body:
This EPIC tracks a series of investigations as to whether there is value in AST aware file read, search, or codebase mapping.

AST aware tools can be used to 1) more precisely read method bounds with a single tool call, reducing turns from misaligned reads, and reducing noise in tokens, 2) navigate to usages and definitions of syntax elements via syntax aware search (AST grep), and 3) compress high level context about the codebase, such as the location of specific classes and their members by collapsing code down to just top level classes and types and their children's signatures.

```
 1. tilth (Rust)
  tilth is built specifically to generate a structural outline of a codebase. It uses Tree-sitter under the hood but ships as a single binary. It gives you an
  immediate map of the repository's symbols.
   * Installation: cargo install tilth (or download the binary from their releases)
   * Usage:
       * tilth map . (Prints a tree-like overview of the whole codebase structure)
       * tilth read <file> (Prints the structural outline of a specific file)


  2. glyph (Go)
  glyph is another single-binary tool designed to generate clean, multi-file symbol maps. It's excellent if you want to quickly see the skeleton of a
  directory of source code.
   * Installation: go install github.com/benmyles/glyph@latest
   * Usage: glyph cli './**/*.go' (Prints a tree of functions, structs, and methods)


  3. ast-grep (sg) (Rust)
  While primarily known as a structural search-and-replace tool, ast-grep is the industry standard for distributing Tree-sitter as a fast, single binary. You
  can use it to extract landmarks via the command line.
   * Installation: brew install ast-grep or cargo install ast-grep
   * Usage: You can write quick one-liners to extract specific symbols (like all function declarations) and format the output.


  4. The Classic: Universal Ctags (C)
  If you truly want zero modern dependencies, u-ctags is the classic UNIX approach. It uses a hybrid regex/parser approach rather than full AST generation, so
  it's incredibly fast and supports over 100 languages out of the box.
   * Installation: brew install universal-ctags
   * Usage: ctags -R --output-format=json .
   * Note: It outputs a flat list of symbols (or JSON) rather than a visual tree, but it is the most robust and portable way to extract codebase landmarks.
```

issues.title: Subagent recovery after MAX_TURNS is reported as GOAL success, hiding interruption

labels.name: priority/p1
labels.description: Important and should be addressed in the near term.

labels.name: area/agent
labels.description: Issues related to Core Agent, Tools, Memory, Sub-Agents, Hooks, Agent Quality

labels.name: 🔒 maintainer only
labels.description: ⛔ Do not contribute. Internal roadmap item.

labels.name: workstream-rollup
labels.description: Label used to tag epics and features that are associated with one of the three primary workstreams

issues.body:
### What happened?

**Summary**: `codebase_investigator` subagent reports `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"` even though its own result says it hit the maximum turn limit before doing any analysis.

While using Gemini CLI to investigate two local repositories (`t3code` and `superset`), the agent invoked the `codebase_investigator` subagent and it failed immediately without doing any analysis.

I ran the Gemini CLI on these two local repositories with an objective asking it to understand their architectures and AI agent integrations. The saved session log shows:

- The main agent called `codebase_investigator` with a valid, concrete objective.
- The tool result was reported with `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.
- The embedded result text simultaneously says the investigation was interrupted because the "maximum number of turns was exceeded" before any specific task was identified or initiated.
- `RelevantLocations` was empty and no actual codebase analysis was performed.

This looks incorrect because:

1. The subagent appears to have exhausted its turn budget before performing any actual analysis.
2. The termination metadata is internally inconsistent: the parent tool call is surfaced as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`, but the embedded payload describes a limit-induced early termination with no findings.

Relevant evidence from the session log:

```text
session file: session-2026-03-09T18-34-10479ef5.json

line 50: "name": "codebase_investigator"
line 53: objective: "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset..."
line 61: "Termination Reason: GOAL"
line 61: "The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded)..."
line 61: "\"RelevantLocations\": []"
line 66: "status": "success"
line 79: "The `codebase_investigator` was unable to complete its analysis due to a turn limit..."
```

Full snippet from the saved session:

```json
{
  "id": "codebase_investigator_1773081420202_0",
  "name": "codebase_investigator",
  "args": {
    "objective": "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset, focusing on AI agent integrations.\nSpecifically:\n1. In t3code, how is 'Codex' integrated? Where is the core logic for agent interaction?\n2. In superset, what are the different agent/harness integrations (e.g., Mastra, MCP, Claude, etc.) and how are they implemented?\n3. What are the common patterns or interfaces used in superset that could be adapted for t3code to support multiple harnesses?\n\nIdentify key files, symbols, and architectural patterns in both repositories."
  },
  "result": [
    {
      "functionResponse": {
        "response": {
          "output": "Subagent 'codebase_investigator' finished.\nTermination Reason: GOAL\nResult:\n{\n  \"SummaryOfFindings\": \"The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded) before any specific task could be identified or initiated. As a result, no codebase analysis was performed, and no relevant locations or insights could be gathered.\",\n  \"ExplorationTrace\": [\n    \"Received system notification that the maximum number of turns was exceeded.\",\n    \"Followed emergency termination protocol as instructed.\"\n  ],\n  \"RelevantLocations\": []\n}"
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "status": "success"
}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected one of these outcomes:

- `codebase_investigator` should actually explore the repositories and return findings.
- If it truly hits a turn limit, it should do so after some visible work, and the tool invocation should be surfaced as a failure or explicit limit condition, not as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.

At minimum, the CLI should not report a contradictory success state for a subagent that says it exceeded its turn budget before beginning analysis. If the subagent hits a system-imposed turn limit before doing useful work, the tool result should be reported as a failure or explicit limit condition (e.g. `status: "error"` with a clear error code), not as a successful `GOAL` completion.


### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Run `gemini` to enter the interactive CLI, then run the `/about` command.

```console
> /about
Gemini CLI package version: 0.32.1
Platform: Windows
OS: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
Node.js: v20.20.0
PowerShell: 5.1.26100.7920
```

</details>

### Login information

Google Account, Pro tier from students promotion

### Anything else we need to know?

- After the failed `codebase_investigator` call, the main agent continued with manual file exploration and eventually produced an implementation plan. So the overall conversation did not fully crash, but the specialized investigator tool clearly failed.
- My current inference is that this may be either:
  - turn-budget state leaking into a fresh subagent invocation, or
  - an incorrect mapping of a subagent limit/error state into a successful `GOAL` termination in the parent session.
- If useful, I can provide the full saved session JSON or a redacted version of it.

labels.name: priority/p2

issues.body:
# [BUG] Browser Agent ignores `settings.json` overrides (e.g., `maxTurns`)

## What happened?
The Browser Agent completely ignores any configuration overrides provided in the global or project-level `settings.json`. While the `AgentRegistry` correctly reads and merges these settings during initialization, the `BrowserAgentInvocation` and its factory (`browserAgentFactory.ts`) skips the registry and recreate the agent definition from scratch with hardcoded defaults.

## What did you expect to happen?
The Browser Agent should respect settings overrides like `maxTurns`, `maxTimeMinutes`, etc., just like other sub-agents (e.g., `codebase_investigator`). For example, setting `maxTurns: 0` in `settings.json` should cause the agent to terminate immediately upon invocation.

## Client information
<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Platform: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)
Gemini CLI Version: 0.35.0-nightly.20260311.657f19c1f

</details>

## Login information
Google Account (OAuth)

## Anything else we need to know?
### Root Cause
The Browser Agent's unique invocation flow skips the `AgentRegistry` where settings overrides are maintained. Instead of using the pre-merged definition from the registry, it re-instantiates a fresh definition using hardcoded defaults.

**Relevant Files & Code Snippets:**

1.  **`packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts`**
    The Browser Agent is explicitly branched out of the standard flow that uses `LocalSubagentInvocation`:
    ```typescript
    if (definition.name === BROWSER_AGENT_NAME) {
      return new BrowserAgentInvocation(this.config, ...);
    }
    ```

2.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentInvocation.ts`**
    The `execute` method calls `createBrowserAgentDefinition`, passing the `config` object but omitting the merged definition from the registry.

3.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentFactory.ts`**
    The factory re-runs the `BrowserAgentDefinition` constructor, which returns hardcoded defaults (e.g., `maxTurns: 50`):
    ```typescript
    const baseDefinition = BrowserAgentDefinition(config, !visionDisabledReason);
    ```

### Suggested Fix
Update `browserAgentFactory.ts` to attempt to retrieve the existing definition from the `AgentRegistry` before falling back to creating a fresh one.

type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

The `browser_agent` (specifically `BrowserManager.ts`) currently employs a restrictive "fail-fast" strategy when encountering a locked browser profile (e.g., when `sessionMode: 'persistent'` is used and an existing instance or orphaned process is active):


```json
{
  "success": false,
  "summary": "The task could not be completed because the browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile.",
  "fullErrorMessage": "The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use --isolated to run multiple browser instances.\nCause: The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use a different userDataDir or stop the running browser first."
}
```

I propose to make it more resilient with the following capabilities:

1.  **Automatic Session Takeover:** If `persistent` mode fails due to a profile lock, the agent should automatically attempt to connect to the existing instance (as if `sessionMode: 'existing'` were specified). This requires a graceful "fallback-and-probe" mechanism in `BrowserManager.connectMcp()`.
2.  **Orphaned Process Recovery:** If an `existing` connection is not feasible but the profile remains locked, the `BrowserManager` should proactively detect orphaned `chrome` or `chrome-devtools-mcp` processes associated with the Gemini CLI profile and offer (or automatically execute) a "Self-Healing" routine (process termination + lock file removal).
3.  **Intelligent Error Remediation:** Replace the current static error messages with an interactive recovery flow. Utilizing the `ask_user` tool, the agent should present the user with a "Choice" menu featuring numbered options to resolve the lock (e.g., **1. Attempt Session Takeover**, **2. Force Termination & Reset**, or **3. Launch Isolated Session**). 
### Why is this needed?

Forcing the user to manually `pkill` processes or close browser windows is a friction point that degrades the autonomous agent experience. The agent has sufficient context (profile path, PIDs) to resolve this internally without user intervention.


### Additional context

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

## Objective
Ensure the Gemini CLI understands its own mechanics well enough to act as its own expert guide. The agent must be able to provide users with accurate facts about how it works, its hotkeys, and the exact CLI flags needed to run itself for specific workflows.

## The Problem
Users rely on the CLI to learn how to use the CLI. If the agent hallucinates flags (like suggesting the deprecated `--yolo` instead of `--approval-mode=yolo`) or forgets UI hotkeys (like `Double Esc` for `/rewind`), it blocks progress and creates friction. The agent needs strict grounding in its own documentation to accurately guide users.

### Why is this needed?

1. **Accurate Internal Facts:** The agent (specifically the `cli_help` subagent) must have flawless recall of its own UI keyboard shortcuts, slash commands, and settings hierarchy.
2. **Flag Construction:** It must be able to tell users exactly how to run it from the terminal for various use cases (e.g., suggesting `gemini -i "prompt" --sandbox --output-format json` for safe, headless scripting).
3. **Self-Execution & Guidance:** It should be able to write the exact commands needed to run itself, restart itself, or execute sub-tasks with the correct environment variables and flags.

issues.title: /compress command is not persistent across session resume

labels.name: priority/p2
labels.description: Important but can be addressed in a future release.

labels.name: area/agent
labels.description: Issues related to Core Agent, Tools, Memory, Sub-Agents, Hooks, Agent Quality

labels.name: 🔒 maintainer only
labels.description: ⛔ Do not contribute. Internal roadmap item.

labels.name: workstream-rollup
labels.description: Label used to tag epics and features that are associated with one of the three primary workstreams

labels.name: effort/small
labels.description: 1 day or less: trivial logic, UI adjustments, docs

issues.body:
### What happened?

The `/compress` command, which summarizes chat history to save tokens, is not persistent across session exits and resumes. When a user runs `/compress`, the in-memory chat history is correctly replaced by a summary, but this change is not written back to the session file on disk. Consequently, when the session is resumed later (using `--resume` or `/resume`), the CLI loads the original, uncompressed history from the session file, effectively losing the compression.

**Repro Steps:**
1. Start a chat with `gemini`.
2. Build up some history with several messages.
3. Run `/compress` and wait for completion.
4. Exit the CLI.
5. Resume the session with `gemini --resume latest`.
6. Observe that the history has reverted to its uncompressed state.

### What did you expect to happen?

Running `/compress` should persist the compressed history (the summary) to the session file on disk so that subsequent resumes of the same session correctly load the compressed state.

### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

OS: darwin (macOS)
Version: Current (detected in local development)

</details>

### Login information

N/A (General bug in persistence logic)

### Anything else we need to know?

Investigation shows that in `packages/core/src/core/client.ts`, the `tryCompressChat` method correctly replaces the `this.chat` object with a new `GeminiChat` initialized with the compressed history:
```typescript
this.chat = await this.startChat(newHistory, resumedData);
```
However, the `ChatRecordingService` (which manages the session file) is initialized with `resumedData` (which points to the existing session file) but is not explicitly instructed to overwrite the file's message history with the new `newHistory`. The `initialize` method in `ChatRecordingService` merely points to the existing file without clearing or updating its messages.

type.description: Related Changes across multiple feature sets

issues.body:
## Description
Gemini 3 models are fundamentally trained to operate as native bash users, chaining standard POSIX tools (`grep`, `cat`, `sed`, `awk`) to explore codebases and edit files. To make full use of the model's native and preferred capabilities without compromising user security or UX, we need to allow the model to use these tools directly to interact and make changes.

## Prior Art
Historically, we have attempted to force models to use custom tools (such as `replace`, `grep_search`, `write_file`, etc.). However, these methods fight the model's core training. Malicious prompts or complex scripts are inherently hard to control and catch via parsing, and forcing custom tools creates significant downstream UX and security issues.

## The Challenge & Value Proposition
Because the model strongly favors raw bash calls even when nudged towards custom tools, it frequently outputs large, complex bash scripts to accomplish tasks. Under our current security model, these scripts require explicit user confirmation. 

This creates a critical point of failure: users are frequently presented with dense, hard-to-read bash messages to evaluate. This leads to severe prompt fatigue, causing users to either blindly confirm the execution or enter "yolo mode" (auto-approving all actions). This behavior is highly detrimental to security and degrades the overall user experience. 

**Value Proposition:** By safely embracing the model's native bash tendencies, we can eliminate confirmation fatigue, prevent unsafe "yolo mode" habits, and drastically improve both the UX and our underlying security posture. 

## Proposed Solution
A highly viable solution is to utilize a secure sandbox. ALL standard shell commands will execute within a zero-dependency, kernel-enforced sandbox. Instead of trying to predict intent before execution (which led to the parsing challenges described above), we can safely observe and handle the results *after* execution.

### Method
By running commands in a sandboxed replica of the workspace, we achieve three distinct UX lanes:
1. **Reads:** Commands that do not mutate the filesystem (e.g., `ls`, `grep`) are auto-approved. We must ensure this does not read from protected spaces or outside our trusted workspaces.
2. **Edits:** Commands that mutate the sandboxed filesystem (e.g., `sed -i`, `>`) trigger a post-execution Diff UI before the changes are synced back to the host, allowing for a seamless "Edit" tool experience using the model's preferred mechanisms. 
3. **Side-Effects:** A dynamic command router will handle commands requiring host credentials or network access (e.g., `git`, `gh`), completely bypassing the sandbox but requiring strict upfront user confirmation (i.e., stays the same as today, utilizing the policy engine to execute or ask for user confirmation).

## Architectural Mandates
In order to support this properly, we must explore, investigate, and implement the proper sandboxing for all major platforms: Linux, macOS, and Windows.

## Epic
This is an epic that tracks this investigation and implementation. It will contain subtasks used to track progress towards its overall completion. After initial investigation, if this is not a feasible route, the epic can be marked as closed.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Current context baseline is approximately 36.6k tokens per turn. Large file reads often 'firehose' the context, leading to bloat (previously observed at +15k tokens/turn). 

The goal of 'Tactful Extraction' is to establish a surgical code-discovery hierarchy:
1. **grep_search**: Primary scout for locating symbols.
2. **shell/sed**: scalpel for semantic block extraction (preferred for specific line ranges).
3. **read_file**: surgical range-reading (migrated to 1-based start/end lines).

Telemetry indicates that making ~2.1% more targeted tool calls results in a ~6.9% reduction in total input tokens.

## Changes

- **read_file migration**: Switched from 0-based 'offset'/'limit' to 1-based 'start_line'/'end_line' for better model alignment.
- **Surgical Guidance**: Updated tool descriptions and system prompts to mandate 'token-frugal' behavior.
- **Tool Hierarchy**: Emphasized the use of 'grep_search' and 'sed' via 'run_shell_command' for efficient context management.

## Status

This work is temporarily sidelined in favor of other priorities but remains a key architectural goal for efficiency.

issues.body:
The current WriteToDo tool relies on "in-context" task tracking, which maintains the todo list solely within the LLM's conversation history (prompt context). This creates issues with "context rot," high token costs, and total memory loss between sessions.

This issue proposes deprecating WriteToDo in favor of a persistent task tracking system (e.g., a local tasks.json) that allows the agent to maintain state across restarts and manage complex dependencies.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a new set of tools backed by a persistent local file (e.g., .gemini/tasks.json) to replace WriteToDo.

1. New Tool Definitions
The agent should have access to specific CRUD tools rather than just "writing" a list:
task_add(description: str, priority: str, dependency_id: int)
task_list(filter: str) (e.g., "show only 'ready' tasks")
task_update(id: int, status: str)
task_complete(id: int)

2. Storage Backend
Tasks should be serialized to a local file  in the working directory.

Benefits
1. Persistence: The agent can pick up exactly where it left off after a restart.
2. Efficiency: We stop burning tokens passing the entire completed history back and forth. The agent only queries task_list when it needs to know what to do next.
3. Complexity: Enables multi-step reasoning where the agent can plan out 20 steps and execute them over several days.

Address concerns and suggestions in https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/17035 
Doc [go/tracker-gemini-cli](http://goto.google.com/tracker-gemini-cli)

prs.title: fix(core): use PowerShell CIM fallback for Windows IDE process lookup
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the Windows IDE process detection fallback in `packages/core/src/ide/process-utils.ts`, which previously called the Unix-only `ps` utility whenever the PowerShell process-table snapshot failed or omitted the current PID, silently returning an empty `command: '' `without logging any warning and degrading IDE detection.
    

## Details

 - **Windows single-PID CIM fallback (`getProcessInfoWindows`)**: Added a Windows-compatible single-process lookup using PowerShell (`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process
    -Filter 'ProcessId=${pid}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object ProcessId,ParentProcessId,Name,CommandLine | ConvertTo-Json -Compress`) with integer PID
    validation, a 3s timeout, and safe JSON normalization (handling single object, array, `null`, and nullable `Name`/`CommandLine` fields).
    - **Replaced broken `ps` fallback**: Updated `getIdeProcessInfoForWindows()` to invoke `getProcessInfoWindows(myPid)` when `myPid` is missing from
    `getProcessTableWindows()`, avoiding any `ps` execution on `win32`.
    - **`GEMINI_CLI_IDE_PID` resilience on Windows**: Added a fallback to `getProcessInfoWindows(idePid)` when `GEMINI_CLI_IDE_PID` is set on Windows and the full
    process-table snapshot fails or omits `idePid`.
    - **Observability**: Added `debugLogger.warn` diagnostics when Windows snapshot retrieval/JSON parsing fails, when `myPid` is missing from the snapshot, and when
    the single-PID CIM fallback fails.
    - **Unit & Integration Tests**: Added unit tests in `process-utils.test.ts` and real `child_process.exec` + `IdeClient` integration tests in
    `process-utils.integration.test.ts`.
    

## Related Issues

 Fixes #28998

## How to Validate

    1. Run the unit and integration tests for IDE process detection and client connection:
       ```bash
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/ide/process-utils.test.ts src/ide/process-utils.integration.test.ts src/ide/detect-ide.test.ts
       src/ide/ide-client.test.ts src/ide/ide-client.sandbox.test.ts src/ide/ide-connection-utils.test.ts
  2. Run typecheck and lint:
    npm run typecheck
    npm run lint -w @google/gemini-cli-core
  3. Verify edge cases covered by the test suites:
      • Windows process-table snapshot timeout/error or malformed JSON recovers process command via Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter 'ProcessId=<pid>' and
      accurately detects VS Code forks (vscodefork) and specific JetBrains IDEs (e.g., intellijidea).
      • Snapshot omitting the current PID or GEMINI_CLI_IDE_PID falls back to single-PID CIM lookup.
      • Total PowerShell/CIM failure (both snapshot and single-PID query failing) logs via debugLogger.warn, never invokes ps, and degrades gracefully to { pid,
      command: '' }.

prs.title: fix(core): drop tool calls streamed by failed attempts on retry
prs.body:
## Summary

On a mid-stream retry, `GeminiChat` has already yielded the failed attempt's chunks, while only the successful attempt's model turn is written to history. Every front end collected `ToolCallRequest` events from both attempts, executed both calls and answered both. A side-effecting command therefore ran twice, and the extra `functionResponse` no longer matched the model turn, so the next request failed with `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` and every later request in the session was rejected too.

This implements the existing `RETRY` contract ("The UI should discard any partial content from the attempt that just failed") for tool calls in every consumer.

## Details

- `core/Turn`: reset `pendingToolCalls` when a retry is signalled, so calls that never entered history are not reported as pending.
- ACP (`acpSession`), interactive UI (`useGeminiStream`, including `pendingToolCallRequestsRef`), headless (`nonInteractiveCli`), a2a-server (`executor`) and the subagent `LocalAgentExecutor`: drop the collected tool call requests on `Retry`.
- No behavior change when a turn is not retried; clearing only happens when the backend signals a retry.
- Out of scope (unchanged): partial text from a failed attempt is still displayed, and headless stream-json may still emit a `tool_use` event for a call that is dropped.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30014

## How to Validate

Each new test streams a tool call, then `Retry`, then a second call, and asserts that exactly one call is executed and answered. All of them fail without the source change.

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/turn.test.ts src/agents/local-executor.test.ts
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp/acpSession.test.ts src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx
cd packages/a2a-server && npx vitest run src/agent/executor.test.ts
```

Additional checks:

- `tsc --noEmit` (core/cli/a2a), `eslint --max-warnings 0` and `prettier --check` pass.
- Full `@google/gemini-cli-core` suite: 8555 passed. The single failure is the pre-existing macOS-only `/dev/ttys001` test from #30008.
- Full a2a-server suite: 183 passed.
- Affected suites also pass in a Linux Docker container (`node:22-bookworm`, linux/arm64) after a clean `npm ci` + `npm run build`.

## 中文说明

修复 #30014。流式中途重试时，失败 attempt 的 tool call 已经发给前端但不会进入 history，导致同一命令被执行两次，且多余的 functionResponse 与 history 不匹配，后续请求持续 400。现在各前端在收到 `Retry` 时丢弃失败 attempt 收集到的调用，并清空 `Turn.pendingToolCalls`；无重试时行为不变。

prs.title: fix(core): preserve session history during tool output masking
prs.body:
## Summary

Preserve the user's first prompt when resuming sessions whose tool outputs were masked.

## Details

`getHistory()` is prepared for API requests: for modern Gemini models it coalesces adjacent user turns and removes durable IDs. Writing this view back after masking merges the first prompt into the `<session_context>` message, which is skipped on resume.

Mask the stored history contents and reattach each original turn ID before updating the recording. This preserves turn boundaries and thought parts while allowing the recording service to update the masked tool response.

The masking service replaces contents at their original indices without filtering or reordering turns.

The regression test exercises `sendMessageStream`, real masking and recording, and `convertSessionToClientHistory`, with masking enabled and disabled. Existing chat mocks now include their durable history.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30015

## How to Validate

- With Node 20.19.0, run:
  ```sh
  npx vitest run --root packages/core src/core/client.test.ts src/context/toolOutputMaskingService.test.ts src/utils/sessionUtils.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1
  ```
  Result: 106 passed, 1 skipped. The new masking case fails on the original implementation because the first prompt is absent from resumed history; the no-masking control passes.
- `npm run preflight` was attempted on Linux with Node 20.19.0. Build, full lint and all workspace typechecks pass. The full run is not green in this managed root container: CLI reports 7,558 passed / 27 failed / 4 skipped (startup trust, extension-registry private-IP checks, IDE-bridge timeouts, and the `/work` prefix matching npm's `/workspace` PATH entries). Core's native sandbox integration stalls, so that run was interrupted. prs.title: fix(core): fix detectPowerShellSubstitution quote tracking and false positives
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes false positive command substitution detection in `detectPowerShellSubstitution` on Windows.
When quotes or escaped characters were present within double-quoted strings (such as `\"`, `""`, or nested single quotes), the parser's `inDoubleQuote` state tracking desynchronized, causing legitimate commands with parentheses (like `git log --format="%h \" (%an)"` or `git commit -m "fix(core): \"quoted\" (detail)"`) to be falsely blocked with a command injection warning.

## Details
1. **Quote State Machine Tracking**:
   - Inside single quotes: In PowerShell, `''` escapes a single quote; handle doubled single quotes `''` without exiting single quote mode.
   - Inside double quotes: In PowerShell, `""` escapes a double quote; handle doubled double quotes `""` without exiting double quote mode.
   - Backslash escape handling: Windows executables and wrappers frequently escape quotes as `\"`. In double quotes, consume backslash escape sequences `['$', '`', '"', '\\', '(', ')', "'"]` via `i += 2` so `\"` does not prematurely toggle `inDoubleQuote` to `false`.
   - Outside quotes: Handle general escape sequences (`\` and `` ` ``) so escaped parens like `\(` are not flagged as unquoted subexpressions.
2. **Regression Testing**:
   - Added unit test suite in `packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts` testing escaped double quotes with parens, doubled quotes, escaped substitution syntax, and verifying that actual malicious subexpressions (`$()`, `@()`, bare `()`) remain strictly blocked.
   - Added regression test in `packages/core/src/tools/shell.test.ts` verifying end-to-end execution of PowerShell commands with nested/escaped quotes and parentheses.

## Related Issues
Fixes #29738

## How to Validate
1. Run PowerShell with nested quotes and parentheses:
   ```powershell
   git commit -m "fix(core): \"quoted\" (detail)"
   git log --format="%h \" (%an)"
   echo "a \" b (c)"
   ```
   **Expected**: Commands execute cleanly without being blocked by command injection detection.
2. Run command injection attempts:
   ```powershell
   echo (whoami)
   echo $(whoami)
   echo @(whoami)
   ```
   **Expected**: Blocked with command injection warning.
3. Run test suites:
   - `packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts`
   - `packages/core/src/tools/shell.test.ts`

prs.title: feat(core): make API request headers and body timeouts configurable
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds two settings, `general.requestHeadersTimeoutMs` and `general.requestBodyTimeoutMs`, so users can raise the model API request timeouts under **every auth type**. Today long-thinking turns that stream nothing for more than 5 minutes are aborted with `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` and replayed from scratch (billed again), up to `maxAttempts` times. API-key users have no way to change this.

## Details

**Root cause:** `packages/core/src/utils/fetch.ts` hardcoded `defaultBodyTimeout = 300000` and `defaultHeadersTimeout = 60000`. The only override was `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts()`, driven by the `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` experiment flag. API-key auth never receives that flag, and even when it is present it only changed the headers timeout.

**Changes:**

- **`fetch.ts`**
  - `defaultBodyTimeout` is now mutable.
  - `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts(headersTimeoutMs, bodyTimeoutMs?)` accepts an optional body timeout and validates both values. It applies them to the global dispatcher, the proxy dispatcher (`setGlobalProxy`) and the safe agent.
  - Adds a small `getGlobalFetchTimeouts()` getter.
  - Existing callers are unaffected.
- **`Config` (core)**
  - New `requestHeadersTimeoutMs` / `requestBodyTimeoutMs` params. Non-positive or non-finite values are ignored with a `debugLogger.warn`.
  - `getRequestTimeoutMs()` now prefers the user setting over the experiment flag.
  - New `getRequestBodyTimeoutMs()`.
  - `refreshAuth()` applies whichever timeouts are configured. If only the body timeout is set, the current headers timeout is kept.
- **Settings schema (CLI):** two new `general.*` number settings (`requiresRestart: true`, not shown in the dialog), wired through `loadCliConfig`.
- **Small related fix:** a `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` flag value of `0` was accepted by `getRequestTimeoutMs()` and then made `updateGlobalFetchTimeouts()` throw a `RangeError` during `refreshAuth()`. It is now ignored.
- **Generated files:** regenerated `schemas/settings.schema.json` and `docs/reference/configuration.md` with `npm run schema:settings` and `npm run docs:settings`.

Behavior is unchanged when neither setting is configured.

Example `settings.json` (15 min, per the Gemini latest-model migration checklist):

```json
{
  "general": {
    "requestHeadersTimeoutMs": 900000,
    "requestBodyTimeoutMs": 900000
  }
}
```

Since `settings.json` already supports `${VAR}` expansion, containerized and headless users can drive these from environment variables without a separate env var.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29747
Related to #29693 (the headers-timeout half of the same problem)

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm run build --workspace @google/gemini-cli-core
   cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/utils/fetch.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts
   cd ../cli && npx vitest run src/config/settingsSchema.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts src/config/settings.test.ts
   ```
   New tests cover:
   - setting precedence over the experiment flag
   - invalid value handling
   - applying timeouts on `refreshAuth` with API-key auth
   - body-only configuration
   - propagation to the proxy dispatcher and safe agent
   - the flag value `0` edge case
2. Manual check: set `general.requestBodyTimeoutMs` to a small value (e.g. `5000`), run `gemini -p` with a prompt that makes the model think for a long time, and confirm the request is aborted after ~5 s instead of 300 s. Then set a large value and confirm a long silent turn is no longer aborted at 5 minutes.
3. `npm run schema:settings` and `npm run docs:settings` produce no further diff.

Fixes #29825.

When an MCP server exposes more tools than fit in a single page, `discoverTools` in `packages/core/src/tools/mcp-client.ts` only requested the first page and silently dropped the rest, because the `nextCursor` token returned by `tools/list` was ignored.

Local full `preflight` could not be executed on the development machine (1.8 GB RAM — `tsc --build` and repo-wide `eslint` are OOM-killed), so validation relied on targeted lint plus CI.

prs.title: fix(core,cli): fix instances of incorrect \n escape behavior
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes multiple instances of naive `\n` escaping/unescaping across `@google/gemini-cli-core` and `@google/gemini-cli` that corrupted valid `\n` escape sequences inside string literals, regular expressions, and inline/fenced code spans during file edits and UI/tool text normalization.

## Details

1. **Model family detection for `aggressiveUnescape` in `write_file` (`packages/core/src/config/models.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/write-file.ts`)**:
   - When `experimentalDynamicModelConfiguration` is enabled, `isGemini3Model` previously only checked `modelConfigService.getModelDefinition(resolved)?.family === "gemini-3"`. For Gemini 3 models without an explicit entry in `modelDefinitions` (such as `gemini-3-flash` or `gemini-3.0-pro`), it returned `false`, causing `aggressiveUnescape` to become `true` in `write_file` and stripping valid `\n` escape sequences inside string literals via `unescapeStringForGeminiBug`. `isGemini3Model` now falls back to `/^gemini-3(\.|-|$)/` when no model definition family is present.
   - Updated `isGemini2Model` to accept `config?: ModelCapabilityContext`, resolve model aliases (such as `auto-gemini-2.5`), and match hyphenated Gemini 2 model names (`/^gemini-2(\.|-|$)/`).
2. **File content correction & LLM escaping prompt (`packages/core/src/utils/editCorrector.ts`)**:
   - Short-circuit `ensureCorrectFileContent` before running `unescapeStringForGeminiBug` when `disableLLMCorrection && !aggressiveUnescape`.
   - Fixed template literal escaping in `correctStringEscaping` where `\\n` vs `\n` was unescaped in the prompt template, which previously instructed the LLM to replace `"bar\nbaz"` with a multi-line string containing a literal newline and referenced `corrected_new_string_escaping` instead of `corrected_string_escaping`.
3. **Context-aware newline normalization (`packages/core/src/utils/textUtils.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/ask-user.ts`, `packages/cli/src/ui/utils/textUtils.ts`, `packages/cli/src/ui/components/Banner.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useBanner.ts`)**:
   - Replaced naive `.replace(/\\r\\n/g, "\n").replace(/\\n/g, "\n")` calls with `normalizeEscapedNewlines`, which converts unescaped `\n` and `\r\n` sequences to actual newlines while preserving double-escaped backslashes (`\\n`), inline/fenced markdown code spans (e.g. `` `\n` ``), and standalone quoted escape tokens (`"\n"`, `'\n'`).

## Related Issues

Fixes #22466

1. Run unit tests for `@google/gemini-cli-core` and `@google/gemini-cli`:

prs.title: fix(core): normalize leading slashes in file search query for @ autocomplete
prs.body:
## Summary

Normalize leading slashes and dot-slashes (`/`, `./`, `\`, `.\`) in `@` file search patterns to enable path autocompletion when typing `@/` or root-relative paths in the CLI input prompt.

## Details

- **Problem:** When users type `@/`, `@/src`, or `@./package.json` to mention files/directories from the project root, the extracted query previously included the leading slashes (e.g. `'/'`, `'/src'`). Because file search indexes workspace files as relative paths without leading slashes (e.g. `package.json`, `src/`), the fuzzy search engine (`AsyncFzf` / picomatch) treated the leading slash as a literal match requirement. This caused 0 matches to be returned for root-level files and top-level directories, which suppressed the autocomplete dropdown and disabled Tab completion.
- **Solution:** In `RecursiveFileSearch.search` and `DirectoryFileSearch.search` (`packages/core/src/utils/filesearch/fileSearch.ts`), normalize the incoming search query by stripping leading `./`, `.\`, `/`, or `\` path prefixes before querying `fzf` or picomatch.
- **Completion Replacement:** In `useCommandCompletion`, accepting a suggestion replaces the range immediately after `@`, cleanly replacing `@/` or `@/src` with `@<completed_path>` without duplicating slashes.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `fileSearch.test.ts`, `useAtCompletion.test.ts`, and `useCommandCompletion.test.tsx` verifying recursive, non-recursive, async initialization, and text buffer replacement behaviors.

## Related Issues

Closes #29453

## How to Validate

1. Run unit test suites:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/filesearch/fileSearch.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useAtCompletion.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useCommandCompletion.test.tsx

2. Interactive test:
   - Start the CLI: `npm start`
   - In the prompt, type `@/`. Verify the dropdown opens displaying root-level files (`package.json`, `README.md`) and top-level folders (`src/`).
   - Type `@/pack` and press Tab. Verify it autocompletes to `@package.json `.
   - Type `@/src` and press Tab. Verify it autocompletes to `@src/`.

of `.git` anywhere in the name rather than only a trailing suffix. As a result,
repository names with an internal `.git` substring were parsed incorrectly (for
example, `blog.github.io` was parsed as `bloghub.io`), and a non-lowercase
extension such as `.GIT` was not removed. This change strips only a trailing
`.git` suffix, case-insensitively.

## Details

- **Solution:** Replaced the substring replacement in
  `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.ts` with a regular expression
  anchored to the end of the string: `parts[1].replace(/\.git$/i, '')`.
- **Impact:** Callers of `tryParseGithubUrl`, such as GitHub release lookup and
  `getExtensionId()`, now receive the correct repository name. Only names with
  an internal `.git` substring or a non-lowercase `.git` suffix parse
  differently than before.
- **Tests:** Added a unit test matrix to
  `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.test.ts` that covers internal
  `.git` substrings, a trailing `.git` suffix, and case handling:

| Input repository     | Parsed name      |
| -------------------- | ---------------- |
| `blog.github.io`     | `blog.github.io` |
| `my.git.repo`        | `my.git.repo`    |
| `tool.git`           | `tool`           |
| `tool.GIT`           | `tool`           |
| `blog.github.io.git` | `blog.github.io` |

## Related Issues

Fixes #29037

## How to Validate

1. Run the GitHub extension unit tests:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extensions/github.test.ts
   ```

   Expected: all tests pass, including the five new
   `should strip only a trailing .git suffix` cases.

2. Optional: revert the one-line change in
   `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/github.ts` and rerun the command above.
   Four of the five new cases fail; `tool.git` passes either way because its
   only `.git` is the trailing suffix.

prs.title: fix(cli): surface 429 rate limit cool-down and countdown in loading indicator
prs.body:
## Summary

Improves the terminal user experience during HTTP 429 (Rate Limit / Quota Exceeded) events by immediately surfacing a cool-down notice on Attempt 1 and rendering an active, second-by-second visual countdown ticker in the loading indicator.

## Details

- **Early Visibility for Rate Limits:** In default `low` error verbosity mode, generic retries are suppressed on Attempt 1 until later retries. For rate limits (`429` status code, `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`), this suppression caused perceived "silent hangs". We now detect rate limit errors via `isRateLimitRetry()` and surface them immediately on Attempt 1.
- **Active Countdown Ticker:** `useLoadingIndicator` now manages an active 1-second countdown interval while `isTimerActive` is true, decrementing remaining seconds (`delayMs / 1000` down to `1s`) to give continuous visual feedback:
  `Rate limit reached. Cooling down... Retrying in 12s (Attempt 1/3)`
- **Multi-Attempt Clean Reset:** When subsequent retry attempts arrive, the countdown cleanly resets to the new backoff duration.
- **Status Code Propagation:** Enriched `RetryAttemptPayload` in `packages/core` with optional `status?: number`, and forwarded `status: getErrorStatus(error)` from `geminiChat.ts`, `baseLlmClient.ts`, and `client.ts`.
- **Zero Regression / Full Backward Compatibility:** Generic network retries (e.g., 500s) maintain their exact existing behavior and strings. No new `eslint-disable` rules introduced.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29357

## How to Validate

1. Run the dedicated 429 countdown unit test suite:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useLoadingIndicator_429.test.tsx
   ```
2. Run related UI and loading indicator suites:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useLoadingIndicator.test.tsx src/ui/components/LoadingIndicator.test.tsx src/ui/components/StatusRow.test.tsx
   ```
3. Run core retry tests:
   ```bash

   ```

prs.title: fix(vscode-ide-companion): register all extension disposables in context.subscriptions
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->

In `packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.ts`, two pairs of adjacent `vscode.Disposable` registrations inside `activate(context)` were enclosed in redundant outer parentheses (`(reg1, reg2)`), causing them to be evaluated as comma expressions (`SequenceExpression`) where only the second `Disposable` in each pair was appended to `context.subscriptions`. This PR removes the redundant parentheses so all registered `Disposable` instances—including the `gemini.diff.accept` command and `vscode.workspace.onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` listener—are tracked in `context.subscriptions` and deterministically disposed upon extension deactivation.

Additionally, this PR enables the ESLint `no-sequences` rule (`{ allowInParentheses: false }`) across the monorepo to prevent unintended comma operator expressions in argument lists and statements.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->

1. **Extension subscription registration
   (`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.ts`)**:
   - Removed the redundant outer parentheses around the `gemini.diff.accept` and `gemini.diff.cancel` command registrations in the first `context.subscriptions.push(...)` call so both `Disposable` objects are passed as separate arguments.
   - Removed the redundant outer parentheses around the `vscode.workspace.onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` and      `vscode.workspace.onDidGrantWorkspaceTrust` listener registrations in the second `context.subscriptions.push(...)` call so both `Disposable` objects are passed as separate arguments.
2. **Unit test coverage and mock fidelity (`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/utils/vscode-mock.ts`,    `packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.test.ts`)**:
   - Updated `vscodeMock.workspace.registerTextDocumentContentProvider` and      `vscodeMock.commands.registerCommand` to return `{ dispose: vi.fn() }` objects matching the `vscode.Disposable` interface.
   - Added a unit test in `extension.test.ts` verifying that all 16 disposables registered during `activate(context)` (specifically including `gemini.diff.accept` and `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders`) are added to `context.subscriptions` and disposed when `context.subscriptions` is cleaned up.
3. **ESLint `no-sequences` enforcement (`eslint.config.js`, `packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.test.ts`)**:
   - Enabled `'no-sequences': ['error', { allowInParentheses: false }]` in `eslint.config.js` to catch parenthesized comma expressions inside function call arguments.

prs.title: fix(core): recognize dotted Gemini 3 models in supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse
prs.body:
When Gemini CLI runs without dynamic model configuration (`experimental.dynamicModelConfiguration` unset or `false`), `supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse()` (`packages/core/src/config/models.ts`) determined Gemini 3 support via `model.startsWith('gemini-3-')`. Because modern dotted Gemini 3 model names (such as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, and `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) do not match the prefix `gemini-3-`, `supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse` returned `false`. As a consequence, binary image data returned from tools like `read_file` was emitted as a separate sibling `inlineData` part adjacent to `functionResponse` instead of being nested within `functionResponse.parts`.

This change updates `supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse()` to use the regex `/^gemini-3(\.|-|$)/` (matching the pattern used by `isGemini3Model`), correctly enabling multimodal function responses for all Gemini 3 model variants. In addition, tests verify that `stripToolCallIdPrefixes` preserves nested `parts` within `functionResponse`.

## Details

- **`supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse` (`packages/core/src/config/models.ts`)**:
  - Updates the fallback check from `model.startsWith('gemini-3-')` to `/^gemini-3(\.|-|$)/.test(model)` so that dotted Gemini 3 models (e.g. `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.8-flash`) are recognized as supporting multimodal function responses.
- **Test Coverage**:
  - `packages/core/src/config/models.test.ts`: verifies `supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse` returns `true` for dotted Gemini 3 models (`gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`).
  - `packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.test.ts`: verifies that `stripToolCallIdPrefixes` preserves nested `parts` on `functionResponse` objects when normalizing tool call identifiers.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29589

## How to Validate

1. **Automated Unit Tests**:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/config/models.test.ts src/core/geminiChat.test.ts
   ```
2. **Full Preflight**:
   ```bash
   npm run preflight
   ```
3. **Interactive CLI Validation**:
   1. Place a sample image (e.g. `pic.png`) in the workspace.
   2. Build and run the interactive CLI with a Gemini 3 model (e.g. `gemini-3.8-flash` or `gemini-3.5-flash`):
      ```bash
      npm run build
      node packages/cli/dist/index.js -m gemini-3.8-flash
      ```
   3. Instruct the model to inspect the image:
      ```text
      Use read_file on pic.png and tell me what is depicted in the image.
      ```
   4. **Expected**:
      - The tool execution embeds the image in `functionResponse.parts`.
      - The model describes the actual image content accurately rather than hallucinating an image description from an empty placeholder.

prs.title: fix(core): make isWithinRoot case-insensitive on Windows
prs.body:
## Summary

Make `isWithinRoot()` and `getNormalizedRelativePath()` case-insensitive on Windows (`win32`) while keeping path comparisons case-sensitive on Linux and macOS.

On Windows, drive letters and directory segments frequently differ in casing across tools and APIs (for example, `c:\Users\...` from VS Code / IDE URIs vs `C:\Users\...` from `process.cwd()` or `os.homedir()`). Previously, `isWithinRoot()` compared resolved paths with case-sensitive `===` and `.startsWith()`, causing valid in-root Windows paths to be rejected:
- `AcpFileSystemService` fell back to native disk reads/writes instead of routing in-project files through the IDE ACP connection (or failed to protect global `~/.gemini` files when `os.homedir()` casing differed).
- `GitIgnoreParser` and `IgnoreFileParser` received `null` from `getNormalizedRelativePath()`, bypassing `.gitignore` and `.geminiignore` rules for paths with mismatched casing.
- `AcpSession` treated in-workspace `@`-attached paths with mismatched casing as outside-workspace paths.

## Details

- **`packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.ts` (`isWithinRoot`)**: Resolve paths using `path.win32` when `process.platform === 'win32'` and normalize both resolved paths with `.toLowerCase()` on Windows only before comparing equality and separator-terminated prefixes. Preserves existing Linux case-sensitivity and macOS `/private` canonicalization.
- **`packages/core/src/utils/ignorePathUtils.ts` (`getNormalizedRelativePath`)**: Use `path.win32` on `win32` for `resolve()` and `relative()` so relative ignore paths normalize consistently on Windows and can be unit-tested across platforms.
- **Unit tests**: Added Windows casing coverage in `fileUtils.test.ts`, `ignorePathUtils.test.ts`, and `acpFileSystemService.test.ts`, plus a Linux case-sensitivity check.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29000

1. Run targeted unit tests:

   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/fileUtils.test.ts src/utils/ignorePathUtils.test.ts

prs.title: fix(ui): handle surrogate pairs when truncating in sanitizeForDisplay
prs.body:
## Summary

`sanitizeForDisplay` truncated strings by UTF-16 code units
(`sanitized.length` and `sanitized.substring()`). When the truncation boundary
fell between the high and low surrogate of an astral character such as an emoji,
the result contained an unpaired surrogate, and the character was dropped when
the text was rendered in the terminal UI.

The function now measures and truncates by code points using the existing
`cpLen` and `cpSlice` helpers, so surrogate pairs are kept intact ahead of the
`...` marker. This applies to every call site that passes a `maxLength`:
suggestion descriptions (`SuggestionsDisplay`), help text (`Help`), file command
descriptions (`FileCommandLoader`), and terminal notification
title/subtitle/body (`terminalNotifications`).

## Details

- **Truncation** (`packages/cli/src/ui/utils/textUtils.ts`):

  ```ts
  if (maxLength && cpLen(sanitized) > maxLength) {
    sanitized = cpSlice(sanitized, 0, Math.max(0, maxLength - 3)) + '...';
  }
  ```

- **Boundary clamp**: `substring()` treats a negative end index as `0`, whereas
  `cpSlice()` follows `slice()` semantics and counts a negative end back from
  the end of the string. `Math.max(0, maxLength - 3)` keeps the existing `'...'`
  result when `maxLength` is smaller than 3; without it,
  `sanitizeForDisplay('abcdef', 2)` would return `'abcde...'`. No current caller
  passes a value below 3 (they use 48, 64, 100 and 180).
- **Behavior**: `maxLength` now counts code points. Output is unchanged for
  strings without astral characters. For strings that contain them, the UTF-16
  `length` of the result can exceed `maxLength` (e.g. 101 code units / 100 code
  points for the first test case below).
- **Tests** (`packages/cli/src/ui/utils/textUtils.test.ts`), three new cases:
  1. `'a'.repeat(96) + '😀' + 'b'.repeat(50)` truncated at 100 returns
     `'a'.repeat(96) + '😀' + '...'` with no unpaired surrogates.
  2. `'😀'.repeat(50)` truncated at 20 returns `'😀'.repeat(17) + '...'`
     (code-point counting).
  3. `maxLength` values below the ellipsis length return `'...'` for both ASCII
     and non-ASCII input (lower-bound clamp; covers both `cpSlice` code paths).

  The unpaired-surrogate assertion uses `/[\uD800-\uDFFF]/u`. The `u` flag is
  required: without it, the character class also matches both halves of a
  correctly paired emoji.

- **Not in this PR**: grapheme clusters made of several code points (ZWJ
  sequences, flags, skin-tone modifiers) can still be cut between code points.
  The output remains well-formed UTF-16, but a partial sequence may be shown;
  grapheme-aware truncation would require `Intl.Segmenter`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29301

## How to Validate

1. Run the unit tests for the changed module:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/utils/textUtils.test.ts
   ```

   Expected: all 88 tests pass.

2. All `packages/cli` test suites (7537 tests) pass locally, along with lint and
   typecheck.

3. Full workspace validation runs through the upstream GitHub Actions CI
   workflows.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

<!-- Check all that apply before requesting review or merging. -->

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed) — not needed;
      internal helper with no documented behavior change

### Description
When `telemetry.logPrompts` is disabled (the default recommended setting in enterprise/corporate environments to prevent collecting code, secrets, and PII), all `function_args` in `gemini_cli.tool_call` are omitted and metadata keys are strictly filtered against `TOOL_CALL_METADATA_SAFE_KEYS`.

As a result, organizations cannot audit which Agent Skills are being adopted or executed. Unlike user prompts or shell arguments, a skill's name is an enum identifier defined in the skill catalog that contains no private data.

This PR:
1. Adds `skill_name` to `TOOL_CALL_METADATA_SAFE_KEYS` in `packages/core/src/telemetry/types.ts`.
2. Emits `data: { skill_name: skillName }` from `ActivateSkillToolInvocation.execute()` in `packages/core/src/tools/activate-skill.ts`.
3. Adds unit tests verifying that `skill_name` is preserved in telemetry metadata even when `logPrompts` is `false`.
