prs.title: fix(cli): bound inline history re-render after terminal width changes
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->
Bounds the work performed by the inline renderer (`ui.useAlternateBuffer: false`, `ui.terminalBuffer: false`) when the terminal width changes, and reduces the repeated output that resize refreshes leave in the terminal scrollback. 

The change is split into two commits so each concern can be reviewed on its own:

1. **`fix(cli): bound inline history re-render after terminal width changes`** (the change requested in #21924). Each debounced static refresh remounted Ink `<Static>` with the entire chat history, so the cost of a width change (React reconciliation, Yoga layout, and the stdout payload) grew linearly with session length. A remount that follows a width change now re-prints the newest history until it exceeds 1,000 characters and covers at least one screen, always including the newest item. Message content is never altered, and the items that are not re-printed are those that had already scrolled into the terminal's native scrollback.
2. **`fix(cli): reduce repeated inline output after terminal resizes`** (additional fixes found while validating the first commit manually). Three sources of repeated output were independent of how much history is re-printed: the viewport erase sequence, refreshes triggered by pauses during a drag, and Ink's full-terminal redraw. Static refreshes now erase the viewport in place, width changes are debounced by 300 ms, and the inline layout stays one row shorter than the terminal while output height is  constrained.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->
### Commit 1: bounded resize refresh (issue goal)

- **Resize refresh window (`useStaticHistoryStartIndex.ts`, new)**:
  - `countHistoryItemChars` counts the content characters an item prints (text, tool descriptions, and string, diff, or ANSI tool output), uses a fixed size for non-text content, and stops counting at a limit so large tool output is not scanned in full.
  - `countHistoryItemMinRows` returns a conservative estimate of the rows an item occupies at a given width (wrapped non-empty text lines and one row per tool call, without blank lines, margins, borders, or tool output), so the window errs toward covering more than one screen.
  - `getResizeRefreshHistoryStartIndex` accumulates items from the newest backwards and keeps including older items while they fit in `RESIZE_REFRESH_MAX_HISTORY_CHARS = 1000` or while the window is shorter than the terminal height. The newest item is always included and no item is truncated, including within a long single response.
  - `useStaticHistoryStartIndex` keeps the start index fixed for each `historyRemountKey`, preserving the append-only `items.slice(index)` contract of `<Static>`, and computes it during render so the remounted `<Static>` never prints an intermediate full-history frame. The window is applied only when the remount follows a terminal width change and the history is an append-only continuation of the items already printed; any other remount (theme or Markdown toggles, Ctrl+O, `/clear`, session resume, `/chat` load, rewind) prints the full history as before.
- **Inline static list (`MainContent.tsx`)**:
  - Passes `historyItems.slice(startIndex)` to `<Static>` and includes `AppHeader` only when the full history is printed.
  - Provides the terminal height and main area width used to size the window.
  - Removes the `staticHistoryItems` and `lastResponseHistoryItems` memos, whose concatenation was identical to `historyItems`.
  - The alternate buffer and terminal buffer renderers are unchanged.
- **Design notes**:
  - The 1,000-character figure from the #21924 discussion is used as a budget for how much older history is re-printed, not as a truncation limit, so no message content is dropped.
  - The one-screen minimum guarantees that everything visible before the refresh is drawn again; without it, older items still on screen but outside the character budget would be erased and not re-printed.

### Commit 2: repeated output after resizes (additional fixes)

With the bounded refresh in place, manual runs still showed earlier output repeated in the scrollback. Each of the following causes produced copies regardless of how much history a refresh re-prints, so they are fixed together in a separate commit:

- **Viewport erase (`AppContainer.tsx`)**:
  - Change: `CLEAR_VIEWPORT` moves the cursor home and erases down (`CSI H`, `CSI J`) instead of using `CSI 2 J`.
  - Reason: VTE-based terminals implement `CSI 2 J` by moving the visible screen into scrollback, so every refresh left the previous screen, including the composer and footer, above the re-printed history. `CSI 3 J` is still never emitted, so the scrollback preserved since #29792 is kept.
- **Resize debounce (`AppContainer.tsx`)**:
  - Change: `RESIZE_DEBOUNCE_MS` is raised from 100 ms to 300 ms.
  - Reason: terminal emulators re-wrap previously printed rows while the window is resized and can push them into scrollback. With 100 ms, every pause in a quick back-and-forth drag triggered a refresh whose output was re-wrapped by     the next movement (seven partial copies of a short history after one drag). A delay that spans those pauses produces a single refresh once resizing settles.
- **Inline layout height (`DefaultAppLayout.tsx`)**:
  - Change: in inline mode, while output height is constrained, an always-rendered wrapper caps the dynamic UI at one row shorter than the terminal, hides overflow, and anchors content to the bottom so the input stays visible.
  - Reason: Ink's legacy renderer appends every `<Static>` print to an internal buffer that is never reset, and when the previous dynamic output was at least as tall as the terminal it switches to a full-terminal redraw that writes `CSI 3 J` and replays that whole buffer, including one copy per `refreshStatic()` remount (eleven copies of the header in one run, with the earlier scrollback erased). Pending output is budgeted against the composer height measured on the previous render, so the dynamic UI could reach the terminal height for a frame.
  - Scope: the cap is not applied while Ctrl+O expands output or in the alternate buffer and terminal buffer renderers. The inner root keeps its natural height for `useFlickerDetector`, and the wrapper is always rendered so toggling the cap never remounts `<Static>`.

## Related Issues

<!-- Use keywords to auto-close issues (Closes #123, Fixes #456). If this PR is
only related to an issue or is a partial fix, simply reference the issue number
without a keyword (Related to #123). -->

fixes: [#21924](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21924)

## How to Validate

<!-- List exact steps for reviewers to validate the change. Include commands,
expected results, and edge cases. -->

1. **Automated Unit Tests**:

   ```bash
   # Commit 1: bounded resize refresh
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/hooks/useStaticHistoryStartIndex.test.ts src/ui/components/MainContent.test.tsx
   # Commit 2: viewport erase, resize debounce, and inline layout height
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/AppContainer.test.tsx src/ui/layouts/DefaultAppLayout.test.tsx
   ```

   - Verify all tests pass, including:
     - Re-rendering only the newest history (and never the oldest item) when `<Static>` remounts after a terminal width change.
     - Re-rendering only the newest part of a long single response, without the prompt or the start of the response.
     - Re-rendering the full history when `<Static>` remounts without a width change, and printing items appended after a bounded refresh.
     - Erasing the viewport in place without `CSI 2 J` or `CSI 3 J`, and refreshing once 300 ms after the last width change.
     - Keeping the inline layout shorter than the terminal unless output is expanded with Ctrl+O.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

prs.title: fix(core): honor cancellation in read_background_output
prs.body:
## Summary

`read_background_output` ignored its abort signal. With `delay_ms` set, a cancelled call kept sleeping for the whole delay and then read the log anyway, and an already-aborted call with no delay read the log too.

## Details

- reject with an `AbortError` up front when the signal is already aborted
- wait through the existing `delay(ms, signal)` helper in `utils/delay.ts`, which clears the timer and rejects as soon as the signal fires
- successful delayed reads behave as before

## Related Issues

Fixes #29945

## How to Validate

```
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/tools/shellBackgroundTools.test.ts
```

New tests: cancelling during a 60s `delay_ms` rejects right away without touching the process list, and an already-aborted signal rejects with no delay, a zero delay and a 60s delay. Against main's source 4 of them fail; with this change the file passes 14/14 (macOS, Node 25). I didn't run the CLI end to end.

issues.title: 1.0.103: main process grows to 37 GiB; 133M malloc allocations and 10.7 GiB fragmentation during long parallel-agent session

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

A long-running, resumed Copilot CLI 1.0.103 session on a 32 GiB Apple Silicon Mac grows beyond physical RAM and becomes intermittently unresponsive. The main process reached **37.3 GiB physical footprint (37.6 GiB peak)** after approximately 6h19m. System-wide swap usage reached 21.6 GiB.

The strongest evidence is allocator accounting: an earlier `vmmap -summary` snapshot shows **132,788,706 allocations, 19.9 GiB allocated, and 10.7 GiB dirty+swap fragmentation (35%) in DefaultMallocZone**. Small malloc regions dominate. This is a suspected allocation-retention / fragmentation problem, not a proven unreachable-object leak; allocation ownership and root cause remain unknown.

The session is still completing work. Fresh 10-second event-flush warnings and 5-second background task-refresh timeouts accompany the slowdown. No recurrence of the session-lock-unavailable error from #5253 was found in this process's retained log. Filing separately because this report has substantial memory/allocator evidence and does not require the original lock failure to occur.

## Affected version and environment

- GitHub Copilot CLI **1.0.103**, verified by CLI output and loaded native runtime path.
- macOS **27.0.1 (26A434)**, ARM64, **32 GiB RAM**.
- Interactive CLI in tmux; launched from zsh.
- Native runtime: `prebuilds/darwin-arm64/runtime.node`, Mach-O UUID `9682A140-3161-362B-86DB-F14BE11B8017`.
- Runtime SHA-256: `70280452e26d03c3b6bd77b47510460b70416e0e421eac336c134a397a964fc8`.
- Long session with multiple parallel background agents, mixed models, repeated tool calls, and compactions. Eight custom extension child processes and MCP integrations are present; this has **not** been reproduced with a clean profile or extensions disabled.
- The measured footprint belongs to the main Copilot process; it is not a sum of child-process RSS.

## Observed workload / reproduction outline

This is an observed workload, not yet a minimal deterministic reproducer:

1. Resume a large existing session: `copilot --resume=<existing-session> --mode interactive`.
2. Run sustained parallel repository review/edit work with background agents, continued follow-ups, tool output and compactions for several hours.
3. Observe main-process memory growth, system swapping and intermittent UI/task-refresh delays.

At resume, the persisted transcript was approximately 5.864 GB. By 22:24 UTC it was approximately 7.607 GB. Since the resume observation boundary, the transcript contains **24,719 tool completions, 64 subagent-start events and 57 completed compactions**. These are persisted-event counts, not a claim that 64 agents were simultaneously active. Agents have also been resumed/reused. Transcript bytes do not establish what is retained in RAM.

## Measured memory timeline

All times below are UTC on 2026-10-25; native tool output uses UTC+01:00. G values from macOS tools are reported here as GiB.

| Time | Diagnostic | Main-process footprint | Peak |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 20:56:36 | `sample`, 2 seconds | 31.1 GiB | 32.3 GiB |
| 21:05:32 | `vmmap -summary` | 32.7 GiB | 32.9 GiB |
| 21:07:03 | `sample`, 1 second | 32.6 GiB | 32.9 GiB |
| 22:24:41 | `sample`, 1 second | 37.3 GiB | 37.6 GiB |

Growth is observed under active workload, not after an idle/GC experiment. A monotonically increasing leak is not established by these four points.

### Allocation breakdown at 21:05 UTC

| Category | Accounting |
|---|---|
| DefaultMallocZone allocations | 132,788,706 blocks; 19.9 GiB allocated |
| DefaultMallocZone dirty+swap fragmentation | 10.7 GiB, 35% |
| Malloc Small | 34.6 GiB virtual; 29.7 GiB in vmmap's SWAPPED column |
| Malloc Large | 766.6 MiB virtual; 672 MiB SWAPPED |
| App-Specific Tag 16 | 9.2 GiB virtual; 565.2 MiB SWAPPED |
| Mapped files | 133.4 MiB virtual; 512 KiB resident |
| Thread stacks | 229.2 MiB virtual; about 4.7 MiB SWAPPED |

The 385 GiB guard region is reserved address space, **not** RAM consumption. The vmmap SWAPPED column is process VM accounting, not a statement that the swap file contains that many physical bytes; system-wide swap was measured separately. RSS alone substantially understates this process's footprint under compression/swapping.

`footprint -p` independently attributes approximately 30 GiB to Malloc Small, 870 MiB to Malloc Large and 565 MiB to App-Specific Tag 16. This narrows the dominant category to malloc-managed allocations, but **does not distinguish Rust-owned data from native buffers owned by JavaScript or another allocator client**. No claim that a specific cache, event store or module is the leak is made.

## Correlated warnings

Sanitized message-only excerpts (IDs, paths and payloads omitted):

```text
20:49:44Z ordered native subagent bridge flush failed; falling back to durable progress
           error: subagent event bridge flush timed out
20:55:57Z Native session event flush exceeded 10000ms; dispatching the host event copy without the ordering barrier
20:55:57Z SessionClient background task refresh failed (continuing): timed out after 5000ms; continuing event dispatch with the previous task cache
20:56:07Z Native session event flush exceeded 10000ms; dispatching the host event copy without the ordering barrier
```

At a later observation around 22:24 UTC, the retained process log contained:

- 0 `session lock unavailable` messages;
- 13 native-session slow-flush warnings;
- 4 background task-refresh failures;
- 11,249 `dropping OTel` warnings;
- 12,568 `Ignoring subagent usage without an active matching invocation` warnings;
- 14,409 uncached Git-root lookup warnings, often on nonexistent or malformed paths.

These counts are correlations, not proof that telemetry or Git lookup owns the retained memory. Git itself remains executable. At the 20:56 check there were 18 established TCP sockets and 3 closed sockets, so the earlier large closed-socket accumulation is not needed for this memory symptom.

## Expected behavior

Memory usage should remain bounded for long-lived sessions, including completed/resumed subagents, retained tool events and telemetry. Repeated compactions and agent completions should not leave the main process larger than physical RAM, with tens of GiB of small allocations and fragmentation and recurrent dispatch/task-refresh delays.

## Diagnostic limits / requested maintainer guidance

- Only process accounting, short stack samples, log counts and streaming transcript aggregates were collected. No raw conversation, source code, prompts, credentials or heap contents are included here.
- `vmmap` took roughly a minute and may have temporarily perturbed responsiveness; the symptoms and earlier 31.1 GiB footprint predate it. Later tool completions were verified.
- No forced GC, debugger attachment, heap dump, malloc stack logging, leak reachability scan or restart was performed for this memory investigation. A full walk of 133 million allocations on an active 32 GiB machine could be disruptive.
- Stack samples contain mostly stripped `runtime.node` offsets; a CPU stack sample is not an allocation backtrace.
- Useful next steps from maintainers: a supported way to collect native allocation owners and V8 heap/external/ArrayBuffer statistics with bounded overhead; counters for completed-subagent retention, event/task caches and pending telemetry; instructions for a controlled reproduction with allocation stack logging.
- Related: #5253 (same session's earlier lock incident). #4306 reports subtask freezing but lacks this allocator evidence. #4807 is a different idle FileWatch storm; shared cause is not established.

<details><summary>Sanitized vmmap allocation tables</summary>

```text
ReadOnly portion of Libraries: Total=3.1G resident=367.3M(12%) swapped_out_or_unallocated=2.7G(88%)
Writable regions: Total=38.3G written=22.9G(60%) resident=87.4M(0%) swapped_out=31.3G(82%) unallocated=7.0G(18%)

                                VIRTUAL RESIDENT    DIRTY  SWAPPED VOLATILE   NONVOL    EMPTY   REGION 
REGION TYPE                        SIZE     SIZE     SIZE     SIZE     SIZE     SIZE     SIZE    COUNT (non-coalesced) 
===========                     ======= ========    =====  ======= ========   ======    =====  ======= 
Activity Tracing                   256K      32K       0K      32K       0K      32K       0K        1

issues.title: MCP OAuth: expired dynamic client registration is reused forever (invalid_client), no re-registration
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

For remote HTTP MCP servers that use OAuth dynamic client registration (DCR), Copilot stores the registered client in `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/<hash>.json` and reuses it indefinitely. It ignores the registration's expiry and does not register again when the authorization server rejects the client.

GitBook-hosted docs MCP servers (`https://<site>/~gitbook/mcp`, authorization server `https://sites.gitbook.com/oauth2/v1/<site_id>`) issue registrations that expire after 7 days. The `/register` response includes `client_id_issued_at` and `client_secret_expires_at`, and the difference is exactly 604800 seconds. The cached JSON only stores `issuedAt`, not `client_secret_expires_at`. After 7 days, every sign-in attempt fails at `/authorize` (and `/token`) with:

```
{"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Client authentication failed- Invalid client <client_id>"}
```

Clicking **Sign in** again (in the Copilot app: Customize → Installed → Sign in) gets the same error, because the expired client is reused. The only way to recover is to delete or move the cached `<hash>.json` and `<hash>.verifier` files by hand and restart. A new registration then works immediately.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.102-0.unstable.r40141230562.g130d689 (via the GitHub Copilot app)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure a GitBook-hosted docs MCP server, for example:
   ```json
   { "mcpServers": { "traksys-docs": { "type": "http", "url": "https://docs.parsec-corp.com/~gitbook/mcp" } } }
   ```
2. Sign in. Copilot registers a client via DCR and caches it in `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/`.
3. Wait more than 7 days (or check the registration's `client_secret_expires_at`).
4. Sign in again. Authorization fails with `invalid_client` / `Client authentication failed- Invalid client …`, and retrying never recovers.
5. Move the cached `<hash>.json` / `<hash>.verifier` aside and restart. Sign-in succeeds with a newly registered client.

To show that a new registration works while the cached one doesn't:

```sh
curl -s -X POST https://sites.gitbook.com/oauth2/v1/<site_id>/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"client_name":"test","redirect_uris":["http://127.0.0.1:33418/callback"],"grant_types":["authorization_code","refresh_token"],"response_types":["code"],"token_endpoint_auth_method":"none"}'
# -> client_secret_expires_at - client_id_issued_at == 604800
```

### Expected behavior

- Store `client_secret_expires_at` from the DCR response (RFC 7591 §3.2.1) and register again before using a client that has expired.
- If the authorization or token endpoint returns `invalid_client` for a dynamically registered (non-static) client, discard the cached registration, register again, and retry sign-in automatically.
- At minimum, provide a way to clear one server's cached OAuth registration (for example, a "Reset sign-in" action in the app or a CLI command) so users don't have to find hash-named files by hand.

### Additional context

- OS: Windows 11 (x64); GitHub Copilot app
- The cached file contains `serverUrl`, `authorizationServerUrl`, `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `redirectUri`, `resourceUrl`, `issuedAt`, `isStatic: false`, `httpsRedirect`. There's no expiry field.
- Possibly related to the other MCP OAuth caching issues, but distinct: #4695 (duplicate cache keys), #3973 (cached redirect port), #5229 (refresh token not used).
- We've added a workaround script for our users that moves only the affected server's cache entries aside.

issues.title: macOS: keychain prompts on every launch when GitHub-signed and Microsoft-signed copilot binaries share login-keychain items (XARA partition mismatch)

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On macOS, `copilot` stores credentials in legacy login-keychain items (`copilot-cli`, `copilot-mcp-oauth`). macOS XARA protection scopes each item's ACL to a *partition list* containing the Team ID of whoever last wrote it.

The same CLI ships under two different Developer ID Team IDs:

| Path | `Identifier` | Team ID |
|---|---|---|
| `~/Library/Caches/github-copilot-sdk/cli/<ver>/copilot` | `copilot` | `VEKTX9H2N7` (GitHub, Inc.) |
| `/Applications/Microsoft Scout.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar.unpacked/node_modules/@github/copilot-darwin-arm64/copilot.app` | `com.microsoft.clawpilot.copilot` | `UBF8T346G9` (Microsoft) |

Both read and write the same items, so each one invalidates the other's approval. "Always Allow" never sticks and the user is prompted forever.

From `log show --predicate 'process == "securityd"'`:

```
09:08:23  ACL partition mismatch: client teamid:VEKTX9H2N7  ACL ("teamid:UBF8T346G9")
09:08:23  asking user about XARA partition for 'teamid:VEKTX9H2N7'
09:08:23  displaying keychain prompt for .../github-copilot-sdk/cli/1.0.73/copilot
09:08:30  user approved 'always allow' -> adding XARA partition 'teamid:VEKTX9H2N7'
09:08:41  ACL partition mismatch: client teamid:UBF8T346G9  ACL ("teamid:VEKTX9H2N7")
09:08:41  displaying keychain prompt for /Applications/Microsoft Scout.app/.../copilot.app
09:47:18  ACL partition mismatch: client teamid:UBF8T346G9  ACL ("teamid:VEKTX9H2N7")
10:03:28  ACL partition mismatch: client teamid:VEKTX9H2N7  ACL ("teamid:UBF8T346G9")
```

Signature confirmation:

```
$ codesign -dv --verbose=2 ~/Library/Caches/github-copilot-sdk/cli/1.0.73/copilot
Identifier=copilot
Authority=Developer ID Application: GitHub (VEKTX9H2N7)
TeamIdentifier=VEKTX9H2N7

$ codesign -dv --verbose=2 "/Applications/Microsoft Scout.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar.unpacked/node_modules/@github/copilot-darwin-arm64/copilot.app"
Identifier=com.microsoft.clawpilot.copilot
Authority=Developer ID Application: Microsoft Corporation (UBF8T346G9)
TeamIdentifier=UBF8T346G9
```

**Amplified by an orphaned-item leak.** My login keychain held **765** `copilot-mcp-oauth` items against **8** files in `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/`, so **757 were orphans**. Creation timestamps show a new batch on every launch:

| Month | Items created |
|---|---|
| Feb-Apr 2026 | 10 |
| May 2026 | 138 |
| Jun 2026 | 364 |
| Jul 2026 (27 days) | 253 |

Three launches on 2026-07-27 produced 10 new items (6 at `15:47:43Z`, 3 at `16:08:35Z`, 1 at `17:03:34Z`), none of which matched a config file -- orphaned on creation. Each orphan is born with a single-Team-ID partition list, so each is a latent prompt.

This overlaps #2112, which diagnoses the stale-entry half on Windows/keytar. The macOS partition-list collision looks separate and unfiled.

### Affected version

`GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.75` (Scout-embedded) and `1.0.73` (SDK cache).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On macOS, use a host that embeds the GitHub-signed CLI (e.g. the Copilot app, via `github-copilot-sdk`).
2. Also use a host that embeds a Microsoft-signed copy (Microsoft Scout).
3. Sign in and configure at least one OAuth-based MCP server.
4. Launch each app in turn. Approve "Always Allow" when prompted.
5. Prompts return on the next launch of the other app, indefinitely.

### Expected behavior

Approving "Always Allow" once should be durable. Concretely:

1. When creating keychain items, set a partition list trusting every Team ID the CLI ships under (`teamid:VEKTX9H2N7,teamid:UBF8T346G9`) rather than letting macOS default to the writing binary's own Team ID.
2. Reuse the existing `copilot-mcp-oauth` item for a given server instead of writing a freshly-hashed one per launch, and delete the entry it supersedes.
3. Consider the data-protection keychain (`kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain` plus a shared access group) instead of the legacy file keychain, which sidesteps XARA partition lists entirely.

### Additional context

- **OS:** macOS 26.5.2 (25F84)
- **CPU:** arm64 (Apple silicon)
- **Shell:** zsh

Manual workaround -- trust both Team IDs. This is one-time and resets whenever an item is recreated:

```bash
security set-generic-password-partition-list \
  -S teamid:VEKTX9H2N7,teamid:UBF8T346G9,apple-tool:,apple: \
  -s copilot-cli ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db

security set-generic-password-partition-list \
  -S teamid:VEKTX9H2N7,teamid:UBF8T346G9,apple-tool:,apple: \
  -s copilot-mcp-oauth ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db
```

Orphans can be identified by diffing keychain account names against `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/*.json` basenames:

```bash
security dump-keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db | awk '
  /^keychain:/ { acct="" }
  /"acct"<blob>=/ { l=$0; sub(/^.*"acct"<blob>="/,"",l); sub(/".*$/,"",l); acct=l }
  /"svce"<blob>="copilot-mcp-oauth"/ { print acct }' | sort -u
```

Deleting the 757 orphans is safe and requires no keychain authorization (deletion does not decrypt the item, so it produces no prompt).

issues.title: Windows: Entra broker token cache stays 0 bytes after MCP sign-in, so every new process re-prompts

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

After I sign in through the Microsoft Entra account broker for an HTTP MCP server, the token cache file stays empty. Every new process shows the account picker again. A `/restart` in the same process does not prompt.

`~\.copilot\entra-broker-accounts\<id>.bin` is written (1,974 bytes) when I pick the account. `~\.copilot\entra-broker-cache\<id>.bin` stays at 0 bytes. I did not read the file contents.

### Affected version

1.0.103

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add an HTTP MCP server that uses Entra sign-in to `~\.copilot\mcp-config.json`: `{"mcpServers": {"EngHub": {"type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.eng.ms", "tools": ["*"]}}}`
2. Start a session. The CLI shows `Authenticating: EngHub` and the Windows "Pick an account" dialog.
3. Pick the signed-in account. Authentication succeeds.
4. Check the file sizes in `~\.copilot\entra-broker-cache\` and `~\.copilot\entra-broker-accounts\`. The cache file is 0 bytes.
5. Exit and start a new session. The account picker shows again.
6. Run `/restart` in a running session. No prompt shows.

### Expected behavior

The token is saved in `entra-broker-cache`. A new process signs in silently without the account picker.

### Additional context

- OS: Windows, x64
- Shell: PowerShell
- Launched with `agency copilot` (Agency 2026.10.20.6)
- I deleted the empty cache file and signed in again. It was recreated at 0 bytes.
- Related but different: #4464 (repeated interactive sign-in from refresh scope errors), #5068 and #5088 (Windows account broker failures).

issues.title: [Bug] Interactive mode activates 0 plugin custom agents while --prompt activates 4

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

Copilot CLI interactive mode discovers installed plugins but activates zero plugin-contributed custom agents. The same installation and working directory successfully activate four custom agents in non-interactive `--prompt` mode.

When started interactively with a selected plugin agent, the UI briefly shows the selected agent, then clears it and reports:

```text
Custom agent "<plugin>:<agent>" not found. Available agents: none
```

`/agent` then displays:

```text
No custom agents found in this workspace yet.
```

The session continues as the default agent.

This has a secondary MCP impact: because the selected agent never loads, its `mcp-servers:` scoping block never applies. All user-global MCP servers start instead of the two bundled by the agent. In the reproduced environment this changed startup from 2 scoped servers to 20 enabled servers, producing authentication prompts and unrelated server failures.

## Affected version

Reproduced on:

- `1.0.81-6`
- `1.0.81-7`
- `1.0.81-8`
- `1.0.81-9`

Primary evidence below is from `1.0.81-9` on Windows 11, x86_64, Windows Terminal, PowerShell 7.

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Install or load a Copilot CLI plugin that contributes a custom agent.
2. Confirm the agent works in prompt mode:

   ```powershell
   copilot --allow-all --agent <plugin>:<agent> --model claude-opus-5 --prompt "Reply OK"
   ```

3. Start the same agent interactively from the same working directory:

   ```powershell
   copilot --allow-all --agent <plugin>:<agent> --model claude-opus-5
   ```

4. Observe that the agent is initially shown as selected, then clears within about one second.
5. Run `/agent`. It reports no custom agents.
6. Run `/mcp`. User-global MCP servers are active rather than the selected agent's scoped MCP bundle.

### Deterministic A/B from debug logs

Successful non-interactive process:

```text
20:09:45.892 [INFO] Starting Copilot CLI: 1.0.81-9
20:09:46.658 [DEBUG] Plugin activation [agents]: ... plugins=6, loaded=4
```

Failed interactive process:

```text
20:15:53.416 [INFO] Starting Copilot CLI: 1.0.81-9
20:15:53.628 [DEBUG] ... cli_ready
20:15:53.633 [INFO] Login status unknown
20:15:53.827 [DEBUG] Plugin activation [agents]: ... plugins=6, loaded=0
```

The interactive process declares ready and activates agents about 0.4 seconds after process start. The prompt process activates agents about 0.8 seconds after process start and loads all four.

Repeated interactive launches consistently produced:

```text
Plugin activation [agents]: ... plugins=6, loaded=0
```

Repeated `--prompt` launches consistently produced:

```text
Plugin activation [agents]: ... plugins=6, loaded=4
```

## Expected behavior

Interactive and `--prompt` modes should activate the same installed plugin custom agents. `--agent <plugin>:<agent>` should remain selected in interactive mode, and the agent's `mcp-servers:` scoping should apply before MCP startup.

If agent activation must wait for model/backend initialization, interactive mode should delay activation or retry after initialization rather than permanently caching an empty agent list.

## Additional context

The following variables were tested and did not change interactive `loaded=0`:

- Trusted versus untrusted working directory
- Main repository versus linked Git worktree
- Existing credential versus `copilot login --with-token` refresh
- `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` present before child-process launch
- `--plugin-dir <plugin-root>`
- Repository-local `.github/agents/<agent>.agent.md`
- `--add-dir <repository>`
- Removing the `enabledPlugins` setting
- CLI versions `1.0.81-6` through `1.0.81-9`

A repository-local agent and `--add-dir` still hit the same early log line and then loaded no agents:

```text
No model backend (auth, legacy provider, or BYOK registry) available, skipping custom agents load
Plugin activation [agents]: ... plugins=6, loaded=0
```

Refreshing the supported Copilot credential succeeded:

```text
Signed in successfully as <user>
```

but the next interactive launch still emitted `Login status unknown` and `loaded=0`.

This does not appear to be the filename/frontmatter mismatch described in #2475. In this case the filename and frontmatter name match, and `/agent` lists zero custom agents rather than retaining filename-based entries.

issues.title: Context window rollover fails: "checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
# Context window rollover fails: "checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

### Describe the bug
Long-running agent sessions crash when the context window fills and the runtime attempts a rollover:

```
Execution failed: Failed to start a fresh context window: checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover
```

The turn ends and the session (or sub-agent) is effectively dead; it recurs on subsequent turns in the same session.

### What we observed
- The agent **had** written a `checkpoint.md` to the session's `files/` folder (via a normal file write / patch) ~7 minutes before the first failure, yet the runtime still reported it as absent "for this agent".
- The native runtime contains related errors ("Replacing checkpoint.md requires expected_revision; read or stat it first, or use append", "Stale checkpoint writer…"), which suggests checkpoints must be written through a runtime-managed store/tool rather than a plain file write. In our sessions the model did not appear to have any tool exposed for that store, so it could never satisfy the precondition.
- Seen repeatedly across multiple sessions/sub-agents (custom agents and the main agent), mostly in long tool-heavy sessions (builds, test runs, large tool outputs).

### Expected behavior
Either the runtime writes/derives the checkpoint itself before rollover, or the agent is given (and prompted to use) the tool needed to create it. Failing that, it should fall back to normal compaction instead of terminating the turn.

### Environment
- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.100 (also seen on 1.0.98)
- Windows 11 x64, PowerShell
- Models: GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 sessions

### Workaround
Manual `/compact` before the context fills avoids it.

issues.title: includeCoAuthoredBy: false is not inherited by task subagents; their commits still get the Co-authored-by trailer
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`includeCoAuthoredBy: false` in `~/.copilot/settings.json` is respected by the interactive session, but **is not inherited by `task`-tool subagents**. Commits created by subagents still get the `Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>` trailer.

This is a follow-up to #3181, which added the opt-out. The setting works for the main session — it just doesn't reach spawned subagents.

Beyond silently ignoring the setting, subagents appear to be *told* the trailer is mandatory. During a plan-execution run, one subagent amended an otherwise-finished commit purely to add it, and logged:

> `note: amended cleanup commit to <sha> to add the required Co-authored-by trailer; no file changes.`

That "required" wording suggests the subagent's system prompt carries the coauthor instruction unconditionally, rather than gated on `coauthorEnabled`.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Set the opt-out in `~/.copilot/settings.json`:
   ```json
   { "includeCoAuthoredBy": false }
   ```
2. Start an interactive session in a git repo.
3. Ask the main session to make a commit directly (e.g. via a shell `git commit`). ✅ No trailer — setting respected.
4. Now delegate committing work to a subagent, e.g. via the `task` tool with `agent_type: "general-purpose"`, instructing it to implement a change, commit it, and stop.
5. Inspect the resulting commit:
   ```
   git log -1 --format='%b'
   ```
6. ❌ The message contains `Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>`.

In my case 8/8 commits created by subagents carried the trailer, while every commit made directly from the main session had none. Stripping them across the branch required:

```
git rebase <base> --exec "git log -1 --pretty=%B | grep -v '^Co-authored-by:' | git commit --amend --quiet -F -"
```

### Expected behavior

`includeCoAuthoredBy: false` should apply to **all** commits produced by the CLI, including those created by subagents — the setting reads as global, not session-scoped.

### Additional context

- The setting key itself is correct and current: `app.js` computes `coauthorEnabled: T.includeCoAuthoredBy !== false`, and `includeCoAuthoredBy?: boolean` is declared in `sdk/index.d.ts`. (The changelog entry for #3181 calls it `include_coauthor`, which no longer matches the settings.json key — minor doc drift, possibly worth fixing too.)
- Ruled out as causes in my repo: no git hooks, `core.hooksPath` unset, and `commit.template` pointed at an empty file. Raw `git commit` from the main session never adds the trailer.
- `settings.json` had `includeCoAuthoredBy: false` for ~2 weeks before the affected session, so this isn't a case of the setting being applied late.
- Environment: macOS 26.5.2, arm64, zsh, iTerm2/agterm.

issues.title: Remote MCP (OAuth): active session keeps resending an expired access token instead of refreshing or prompting sign-in

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A Copilot CLI session connected to a remote OAuth-protected MCP server keeps sending the same expired access token after its first HTTP 401. The client makes no request to the token endpoint and does not prompt the user to sign in again. The rejected requests repeat about every four minutes for hours.

We run the MCP server at `https://api.plori.ai/mcp` and observed this from the server side:

- Session A (`copilot-cli/1.0.99-2`): the server rejected one bearer token (same fingerprint on every request) 581 times as expired, from 2026-10-19 00:56 UTC to 2026-10-21 06:50 UTC.
- Session B (`copilot-cli`): successful MCP pings until 2026-10-20 19:38 UTC, which is one hour after the token was issued (our access tokens live one hour). From 19:42 UTC the server rejected the same expired bearer 82 times, about four minutes apart, until 2026-10-21 05:55 UTC. Between 19:30 and 20:00 UTC our authorization server received no token-endpoint request.

Every rejection is HTTP 401 with:

```http
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", resource_metadata="https://api.plori.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"
```

The authorization server advertises `grant_types_supported: ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"]` and issues rotating refresh tokens when `offline_access` is requested. The token response sizes we logged before each session match a response that contains a refresh token, so we believe the client held one. We cannot inspect the client's credential store, so this is an inference.

### Affected version

`copilot-cli/1.0.99-2` (session A). Session B's user agent was `copilot-cli` without a version.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add a remote MCP server whose authorization server issues one-hour access tokens and rotating refresh tokens (`offline_access` advertised).
2. Sign in through the CLI's OAuth flow.
3. Keep the session open past the access token's expiry, with the server connected (background pings or subscriptions running).
4. Watch the server logs: requests continue with the expired bearer and receive 401 `invalid_token`; no `refresh_token` grant reaches the token endpoint.

### Expected behavior

On a 401 with `error="invalid_token"`, the client uses its refresh token (RFC 6749 §6), stores the rotated credentials, and retries with the new access token on the active transport. If refresh is not possible, the client tells the user that the server needs authentication again, instead of resending the rejected token.

### Additional context

This looks related to #4203, which describes an expired access token at session start forcing interactive sign-in instead of a refresh. Here the token expires during an active session, and the client neither refreshes nor asks for sign-in; it keeps retrying the same token. We are happy to provide more server-side detail (timestamps, request counts) if it helps.

— Plori AI team

issues.title: SDK: unbounded concurrency in listSessions() exhausts file descriptors with a large session-state
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`LocalSessionManager.listSessions()` in `@github/copilot/sdk` fans out over every directory in `~/.copilot/session-state` with an unbounded `Promise.all`, and per session reads `workspace.yaml`, reads `events.jsonl` for the first user message (summary), and reads `events.jsonl` again for detached-status detection. With N sessions the calling process briefly holds N to 2N open file handles.

Observed with 42,329 sessions (19 GB, created by `copilot -p` batch runs at roughly 470 per day; nothing prunes the store): a single `listSessions()` call from a VS Code extension host was captured via `lsof` with 19,985 `events.jsonl` files open at the same instant (20,043 of the process's 20,086 descriptors). Each call took 92 to 137 s. With 449 sessions it still takes 7 to 12 s.

Two consequences:

- Per process: on macOS `uv_spawn` returns `EBADF` once the child's stdio pipe descriptors are numbered above 10239, whatever the process limit is (libuv/libuv#5204, attributed to Apple libc). While `listSessions()` holds more than ~10k handles the host cannot spawn or fork at all. In VS Code this killed the ESLint language server (microsoft/vscode-eslint#2136), ripgrep and Copilot's own workspace indexer with `spawn EBADF` in the window that was listing.
- System wide: five VS Code windows calling it in parallel at startup drove `kern.num_files` to 122,477 (limit 122,880) and unrelated processes got `ENFILE`; `git rev-parse` took 1.5 to 3.4 s instead of ~50 ms.

De-minified shape of the code (`sdk/index.js`):

```js
async listSessions(e){
  let n=await _t.directoryFilesWithMetadata(this.settings), r=e?.metadataLimit, s=e?.includeDetached??!0,
  o = s ? n : r===void 0
      ? (await Promise.all(n.map(async l=>({file:l,isDetached:await this.isDetachedSession(l.file,l.mtime.getTime())})))).filter(...)
      : await this.getVisibleSessionEntriesWithBoundedDetachedDetection(n,r),
  a=(await Promise.all(o.map(async(l,c)=>{ ...
    let p = s ? await this.isDetachedSession(u, ...) : !1;      // opens events.jsonl (readDetachedStatusFromSessionStart)
    let m = await GI(u,this.settings);                           // reads workspace.yaml
    if(!f){ let b=await qI(y); f=b.summary; h=b.isEmpty }        // opens events.jsonl again (sessionExtractFirstUserMessage)
```

Notes: the bounded helper `getVisibleSessionEntriesWithBoundedDetachedDetection` is only used when `metadataLimit` is set and `includeDetached` is false, so the default path has no bound; the detached cache only helps on later calls in the same process; nothing is cached across processes, so every client pays the full cost.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

```bash
cd ~/.copilot/session-state
for i in $(seq 1 20000); do d=$(uuidgen | tr A-Z a-z); mkdir "$d"
  printf 'id: %s\ncwd: /tmp\ncreated_at: 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z\nupdated_at: 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z\n' "$d" > "$d/workspace.yaml"
  printf '{"type":"session.start","data":{"sessionId":"%s"}}\n{"type":"user.message","data":{"content":"hello"}}\n' "$d" > "$d/events.jsonl"
done
# same construction the VS Code extension uses
node -e 'import("@github/copilot/sdk").then(async m=>{const sm=new m.internal.LocalSessionManager({createFeatureFlagService:m.createLocalFeatureFlagServiceCreator()(),telemetryService:new m.internal.NoopTelemetryService,autoModeManager:new m.AutoModeSessionManager},{}); console.time("list"); await sm.listSessions(); console.timeEnd("list")})' &
while kill -0 $! 2>/dev/null; do lsof -p $! 2>/dev/null | grep -c events.jsonl; sleep 0.5; done
```

On macOS the open count climbs toward N; on a default `ulimit -n 256` shell it fails with `EMFILE`. Adding a `child_process.spawn` inside the script while the listing runs yields `spawn EBADF` past ~10k open files.


### Expected behavior

- Concurrency in `listSessions` is bounded (a `p-limit` style pool of 16 to 64), including the detached-detection pass, so the caller never holds more than a few dozen handles.
- `events.jsonl` is read once per session; detached status and the first user message come from the same prefix read.
- `metadataLimit` is effective on the default `includeDetached: true` path, with entries sorted by mtime first so the limit covers the most recent sessions.
- The derived summary is persisted (in `workspace.yaml` or in the existing `session-store.db`) so later listings do not open `events.jsonl` at all.
- A prune or retention option exists for `~/.copilot/session-state` (`copilot sessions` currently has only `import`).

### Additional context

- macOS (Darwin 27.2.0, arm64), zsh. `kern.maxfiles` 122,880, `kern.maxfilesperproc` 61,440.
- VS Code side: microsoft/vscode#327021 (slow repeated re-walks) and a separate new issue for the descriptor exhaustion in the extension.

Shell command runner does not inherit environment variables from PowerShell
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

Environment variables available in the PowerShell process that launches Copilot are not visible to Copilot's shell command runner. This prevents commands and integrations launched by the runner from using user-configured environment variables such as `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

## Affected version

Copilot CLI 1.0.105

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On Windows, store `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` in the User environment-variable scope.
2. Open a new PowerShell 7 prompt.
3. Load the User-scope value into the current process and verify it without printing the secret:

   ```powershell
   $env:GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN', 'User')
   $env:GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN -ne $null
   ```

   This returns `True`.

4. Launch Copilot CLI from that same PowerShell prompt.
5. In the Copilot session, run:

   ```text
   ! $env:GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN -ne $null
   ```

   This returns `False`.

6. The runner reports the following scope state without exposing the secret value:

   ```text
   Process: False
   User:    True
   Machine: False
   ```

The behavior reproduces in a newly opened PowerShell prompt and a newly launched Copilot session. No token value was printed or included in this report.

## Expected behavior

The shell command runner should inherit the environment of the Copilot process that was launched from PowerShell, or the behavior should be clearly documented if credential variables are intentionally filtered.

## Additional context

- Operating system: Windows
- Shell: PowerShell 7
- The runner and launcher are running under the same Windows account; account/domain details are intentionally omitted.
- The issue appears specific to the Copilot command-runner process boundary. It may be intentional credential sanitization, but this is not documented and prevents expected environment-based authentication for child commands.

issues.body:
Describe the bug
In the GitHub Copilot Desktop app, remote MCP servers configured with "type": "http" that are non-first-party (e.g. Atlassian, incident.io) fail to authenticate. Toggling the server off/on in Settings produces no browser popup and no visible error — the server simply never connects.

Affected version
Desktop app shell: v1.0.15 (latest, confirmed via in-app update check)
Bundled Copilot CLI engine: v1.0.69-0 (AppData\Local\github-copilot-sdk\cli\1.0.69-0\copilot.exe)

Steps to reproduce
Add a non-first-party remote MCP server with "type": "http" and a url in mcp-config.json (e.g. https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2)
Enable it via Settings → MCP servers in the Desktop app
Toggle it off, then on again
Observe: no browser window ever opens; the server stays disconnected with no user-facing error

Expected behavior
A browser window should open for OAuth consent, as it does for the raw copilot CLI and for local-type servers wrapped in npx mcp-remote.

Actual behavior
~/.copilot/logs/github-app.<pid>.log shows this single log line and nothing further:

github_app::session::manager::mcp_status: MCP OAuth non-first-party server; cancelling host-token so runtime browser flow runs server_name=<server>
```

This line repeats on every toggle attempt (confirmed 43 occurrences across multiple sessions for both atlassian and incident.io), but there is no subsequent log entry anywhere indicating the "runtime browser flow" it defers to is ever actually invoked — no browser-launch attempt, no OAuth URL, no error surfaced to the user.

## Root cause hypothesis
This behavior appears tied to the MCP host token-injection OAuth rework shipped in copilot-cli v1.0.66 (2026-06-30 changelog entry: "Added runtime telemetry for the MCP host token-injection OAuth flow, recording when an OAuth broadcast is emitted to the host and how the host responds (token or cancelled)"). For non-first-party servers, the host correctly identifies it should defer to a client-side browser flow and cancels its own token injection — but that deferred browser flow is never triggered inside the Desktop app shell.

## Workaround
Reconfiguring the server as a local type wrapping npx mcp-remote bypasses the broken Desktop-app host/browser-flow handoff entirely, since mcp-remote runs its own independent OAuth implementation:

```json
"atlassian": {
  "type": "local",
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["--yes", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp"]
}
```

This works reliably. Native "type": "http" does not, for any non-first-party server, in the Desktop app.

## Additional context
Possibly related to #2536, but distinct: that issue is about the raw copilot CLI's "Opening browser for X authentication..." log line firing and a browser genuinely opening, just re-registering (DCR) on every launch. In this Desktop-app case, the browser-flow deferral log line fires but no browser-launch attempt is ever logged afterward — a different failure point entirely (host→client handoff, not CLI OAuth caching).

issues.title: [Feature request] Authoritative foreground-session change hook for terminal integrations, including warm resume
issues.body:
### Problem

Terminal integrations need to associate a pane with the **currently foreground**
root conversation, rather than the last conversation that submitted a prompt.
Command `sessionStart` hooks do not appear to provide a complete foreground-change
stream when switching between already-loaded sessions.

### Isolated observation

Tested Copilot CLI **1.0.105 on Linux**, using an empty disposable project, separate
`HOME`/`COPILOT_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, user-level command hooks for `sessionStart`,
`sessionEnd` and `userPromptSubmitted`, normal folder consent and Manual Approval.
No auto-approval, production hooks or existing conversations were used.

1. Start the interactive CLI and submit a synthetic prompt in session A.
   Observe `sessionStart(A, source=new)` and `userPromptSubmitted(A)`.
2. Run `/new` and submit another synthetic prompt in B.
   Observe `sessionStart(B, source=new)` and `userPromptSubmitted(B)`.
3. Run `/resume <A-id>`, then `/session id` to independently confirm A is foreground.
4. Repeat `/resume <B-id>`, `/session id`, then `/resume <A-id>`, `/session id`.

Across these warm A-B-A switches, there were **no additional Start, End or
Prompt hook invocations** within the bounded 5-8 second observation windows.
A file written only by Start hooks would still identify B while A is displayed.
New idle conversations likewise produced no Start until the first submitted
prompt in this run.

A same-version `/restart` changed the observed CLI owner PID/start identity.
After restart, the first submitted prompt emitted Start with `source=resume`.
This was not a cross-version handoff test.

**Limitation:** model requests were rejected by account billing-entity
configuration, so this observation does not establish successful-completion,
subagent, background-model or all-platform behavior. The foreground switches,
session IDs and hook events were nevertheless observed independently. Please
confirm whether this limitation affects the intended lifecycle contract.

### Requested capability

Please provide or document one supported identity-only integration surface:

- A complete, causally serialized **foreground-session-changed** event covering
  warm switches, startup, new/clear/no-current transitions, with ordering and
  failure/supersession semantics; or
- A read-only authenticated accessor for current root identity (or no-current),
  resolved session-store location and an activation revision/conditional-current
  operation suitable for safely publishing asynchronous identity records.

An equivalent supported in-process integration would also work. Explicit revision
fields are not essential if the API guarantees complete serialized publication.
Session-only snapshots or hook-arrival counters alone do not establish that
delayed work still belongs to the current activation, particularly A-B-A.

This is not a request for tool approval, busy/idle authority, a heartbeat service,
or access to transcript contents. The goal is to stop relying on diagnostic log
registration lines to identify the displayed conversation.

Related but different: #4365 discusses prompt-hook/new/clear behavior; this request
concerns **command-hook coverage of warm foreground switches**.

issues.title: Windows/Edge: native Computer Use state lacks verified URL and web accessibility tree (fail-closed)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Native Computer Use on Windows discovered an Edge window, but a subsequent text-only, depth-limited state request could not establish its URL or web accessibility tree. Browser content was withheld. Please route this report to the native Computer Use Windows maintainers for prerequisite/diagnostic guidance or a verification-preserving fix.

**Prior observed result, not newly reproduced for this report:**

- `url: (missing - fail-closed)`
- The tool reported that the window exposed neither a web accessibility tree nor a verified URL and that browser pixels were withheld.
- Its instruction was: "Stop this attempt instead of inferring page identity or content from an unverified screenshot."

The attempt stopped. No screenshot retry, navigation, alternate content-extraction path, or configuration change followed. This report is not a request to weaken the fail-closed behavior.

### Affected version / environment

Installed executable version metadata checked on 2026-10-28:

- GitHub Copilot CLI: **1.0.105**.
- Microsoft Edge: **155.0.4283.62**.
- Windows 11: OS version **10.0.26300.0**, 64-bit operating system.

These are installed-file/OS observations, not fresh `copilot --version` output or verification of the running browser version. The native Computer Use backend/plugin version, exact launch transport/arguments, terminal/shell, and browser window mode are **unverified**. No new Copilot or browser session was started to collect these details.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

**Historical operation sequence only; not a verified minimal reproduction:**

1. In a local Windows Copilot CLI session exposing native `computer-use` MCP tools, window discovery succeeded.
2. A text-only, depth-limited state request targeted an Edge window.
3. The native tool returned the missing-URL/accessibility result above and withheld content.

The exact state-tool name, parameter payload, and depth value have not been verified. Reproduction frequency and behavior on other browser windows/versions are unknown. No claim is made that an arbitrary Edge page reproduces this issue.

### Expected behavior / clarification requested

Preserve URL verification before exposing browser content. If a supported prerequisite is missing, provide an actionable, non-content-bearing diagnostic rather than requiring users to guess or broaden permissions.

Could maintainers identify:

1. Supported Windows/Edge prerequisites for obtaining a verified URL and web accessibility tree, including any browser/window-mode limitations?
2. Metadata-only diagnostics for identifying the native backend/plugin version and the verification stage that failed, without capturing URLs, page content, screenshots, credentials, or raw session logs?
3. A documented correction or fixed version that preserves fail-closed verification, if this is a known defect?

### Additional context

The reviewed [native Computer Use setup/troubleshooting documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/computer-use) establishes Windows availability but did not establish an Edge compatibility matrix or a missing-URL remedy. The [CLI URL-permission documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/configure-copilot-cli) does not establish that URL allowlisting repairs native browser identity verification.

A setup prerequisite, browser accessibility integration problem, and backend defect remain hypotheses, not findings. The error does not establish that a particular destination is prohibited.

Open/closed issue searches found no matching report. The closest inspected reports concern different failures: #5049 (plugin unavailable in ACP), #4265 (browser-tool iframe traversal), and #4536 (MCP image delivery).

issues.title: BYOK Azure Foundry: no quota warning and /compact cannot recover a long session
issues.body:
### Description of the bug

With a BYOK model deployed in Microsoft Foundry, a long Copilot CLI session becomes unusable because requests exceed the deployment's token rate limit, even though the displayed model context window is far from full. Ordinary messages fail, and `/compact` also fails, leaving no working in-session recovery through compaction.

The CLI did not give me an actionable warning about the deployment's TPM limit before the session reached this state. Its context display still shows substantial free space.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.104.

### Environment

- Operating system: Windows.
- Provider: BYOK using a Microsoft Foundry deployment.
- Model: `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Region: `eastus`.
- Deployment token rate limit: 250,000 TPM (user-reported configuration).
- CLI-displayed context capacity: 922k tokens.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure Copilot CLI to use a Foundry BYOK deployment with a large model context window but a substantially lower TPM allocation.
2. Continue a long conversation until `/context` shows approximately 257k/922k tokens.
3. Send an ordinary message. It fails to obtain a model response.
4. Run `/compact` to reduce the history and continue the session.
5. Compaction also fails with the deployment token-rate-limit error below.

### Actual behavior

Exact user-visible compaction error:

```text
Compaction Failed: Error: Failed to get response from the AI model; retried 5 times (total retry wait time: 5.00 seconds) Last error: Your requests to gpt-6.1-sol for gpt-6.1-sol in eastus have exceeded token rate limit.
```

Relevant `/context` output:

```text
gpt-6.1-sol: 257k/922k tokens (28%)
Messages:   239.5k (26%)
Free Space: 618.7k (67%)
Buffer:      46.1k (5%)
```

The error identifies a token-rate-limit failure, not exhaustion of the advertised 922k model context window. The displayed accumulated context is already greater than the deployment's reported 250k TPM allocation.

### Expected behavior

- Distinguish model context capacity from deployment throughput limits in BYOK diagnostics. Explain that a large context window does not guarantee the deployment can accept the corresponding request under its current rate limit.
- Provide proactive, actionable warnings using provider rate-limit headers when available, and/or support a user-configured effective request budget for BYOK deployments. Account for prompt overhead and the provider's output-token reservation/estimation where applicable.
- Trigger compaction early enough to remain within that effective budget.
- Provide a recovery path when the session is already too large for a normal compaction request, such as bounded/chunked compaction or export of a handover that can be used in a fresh session. Preserve the original conversation rather than silently discarding history.
- Respect provider retry timing for temporary throttling, but do not rely only on resubmitting an unchanged request if its estimated token cost exceeds the deployment's entire available rate budget.

### Additional context

This report distinguishes observed behavior from the suspected mechanism: the exact error confirms token-rate-limit rejection, but I have not captured the HTTP status, rate-limit headers, actual compaction request size, or concurrent deployment traffic. The context display alone does not prove the exact provider-side token estimate or that the compaction request resubmits the entire history.

Related reports:

- #3679: BYOK Azure OpenAI throttling retries/backoff. This report additionally concerns missing quota-aware warning and inability to recover using `/compact`; the observed retry wait here is 5.00 seconds.
- #4950: BYOK context-overflow/compaction hangs with another provider. This report concerns a Foundry token rate limit while model context usage is only 28%, not the sampling regression described there.

No API keys, endpoint URLs, client data, conversation contents, or private logs are included.

issues.body:
## Problem

`/rename` (added in #1776) works in the terminal CLI, but not for Copilot CLI sessions hosted in VS Code's Agents window:

- Typing `/rename` in an agent session's chat has no effect there — renaming is only available through the VS Code UI (verified 2026-07-23).
- There is no way for the **agent itself** to rename its session — no tool, and no slash-command it can run.

## Proposal

1. **Honor `/rename NEW_NAME` in VS Code agent sessions**, matching the terminal CLI behavior.
2. **Expose rename to the agent** (a tool, or agent-invocable `/rename`), so workflows can set titles programmatically.

## Use case

Session-hygiene rituals: I keep many long-running agent sessions and prefix titles with a status word as threads settle — `DONE …`, `PARKED …`, `CONT'D …` — so the session picker doubles as a work board. Today every close-out ends with manual rename homework; an agent-invocable rename would let the close-out workflow set the title itself (and lower-stakes: agents could title sessions descriptively from the start, cf. #3365 on auto-naming).

## Notes from poking at the internals

- A UI rename syncs into `~/.copilot/session-state/UUID/workspace.yaml` (`name:` + `user_named:`), so agents can already *read* current titles (verified 2026-07-24).
- Writing `workspace.yaml` directly doesn't work as a workaround: VS Code caches session labels elsewhere (workspace `state.vscdb`, `agentSessions.model.cache`) and doesn't notice the change.

## Related

- #1776 — added `/rename` (terminal CLI)
- #3365 — auto-generated session names not working
- #3415 — show session name at all times
- #2966 — broader session-management tooling

issues.title: Cloud agent: "Registry only" MCP policy blocks all repo-configured MCP servers — proxy-bridged configs can't be fingerprinted ("unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration")

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Describe the bug

With the org MCP policy set to **Registry only**, the Copilot **cloud agent** silently drops every repo-configured MCP server, even when the server is present in the configured registry with a matching package identity. Only the platform defaults (`github-mcp-server`, `playwright`) reach the session.

The CLI log inside the session (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`) shows:

```
[DEBUG] Registry <org-registry>: servers will be verified against this registry
[ERROR] MCP server "mcp-server-A" filtered: Could not verify server "mcp-server-A" against registry <org-registry>: unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration
[ERROR] MCP server "mcp-server-B" filtered: Could not verify server "mcp-server-B" against registry <org-registry>: unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration
```

With the policy switched to **Allow all**, the same servers mount and their tools work.

## Root cause (from reading the shipped runtime)

In the cloud agent, the CLI never sees the repo's MCP config. cca-engine (`dist-cca-v3/index.js`) replaces every proxy-discovered server with a bridge config:

```js
// ~line 80361
discoveredServers[name] = toBridgedMcpServerConfig(name, void 0, mcpProxyUrl);
```

```js
// ~line 79716
function toBridgedMcpServerConfig(serverName, serverConfig, mcpProxyUrl, customAgentName, customAgentVersion) {
  const args = [BRIDGE_SCRIPT_PATH, `--proxy-url=${mcpProxyUrl}`, `--server-name=${serverName}`];
  if (serverConfig) {
    args.push(`--config=${Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(serverConfig)).toString("base64")}`);
  }
  ...
  return { type: "local", command: process.execPath, args, ..., tools: ["*"] };
}
```

So for every third-party server the CLI receives `node <bridge-script> --proxy-url=… --server-name=…`. The CLI derives a stdio server's identity from its command (`npx`→npm, `uvx`→pypi, `dotnet`→nuget, `docker`, `mcpb`; see the explanation in mindovermachine-dev/product-cli#20). `node` maps to nothing, so no fingerprint can be computed and the server is filtered.

- At line 80361 `serverConfig` is `void 0`, so even the base64 `--config` arg is omitted. The original config is not available to the CLI at all.
- Built-in servers pass only because they are marked runtime-authored (`markRuntimeAuthoredServer`, gated by `copilot_swe_agent_mcp_builtin_provenance`) and are exempt from third-party policy.
- From code reading (not tested end-to-end): remote/HTTP configs are bridged the same way when `mcpProxyUrl` is set (`toSdkMcpServerConfig`, ~line 79741), so switching to an `http` server does not avoid this in the cloud agent.

**Net effect:** under "Registry only", no repo-configured (or custom-agent) MCP server can ever pass verification in the cloud agent.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Org settings → Copilot → Policies: **MCP servers in Copilot** = Enabled; **MCP registry URL** = a spec-compliant registry; registry access = **Registry only**.
2. Registry entry named `mcp-server-A`:
```json
   {
     "name": "mcp-server-A",
     "version": "0.0.2",
     "packages": [{
       "registryType": "oci",
       "identifier": "<registry-host>/<path>/mcp-server-A",
       "version": "0.0.2",
       "transport": { "type": "stdio" }
     }]
   }
```
   Verified: `GET <org-registry>/v0.1/servers/mcp-server-A/versions/latest` returns 200 with `server.name == "mcp-server-A"`.
3. Repo → Settings → Copilot → coding agent → MCP configuration:
```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "mcp-server-A": {
         "type": "local",
         "command": "docker",
         "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "<registry-host>/<path>/mcp-server-A:0.0.2"],
         "tools": ["*"]
       }
     }
   }
```
4. Assign a task to the cloud agent.
5. Observe:
   - cca-engine logs `Discovered MCP server: mcp-server-A` and `MCP servers configured for session: …, mcp-server-A, …`.
   - No `MCP server 'mcp-server-A': pending` / `connected` lifecycle events appear.
   - The CLI log shows the `unable to compute fingerprint` error above.

## What we ruled out

- **Registry reachability/auth:** Cloud Run access logs show 200s for the CLI's requests during the session.
- **Name lookup:** before aliasing, the error was `Not found in registry`. After making the registry resolve the config key, the error moved to the fingerprint stage.
- **Local config shape:** `type: local` vs `stdio`, `-e VAR` vs `--env=VAR`, and minimal args all gave the identical error.
- **Package type:** `registryType` `oci` vs `docker` gave the identical error.
- **Policy fetch:** succeeds (`servers will be verified against this registry`). This is not the fail-closed family in #4378 / #2498 / #4346.

## Expected behavior

Repo-configured servers that match a registry entry should be verified against their **original** configuration. Options include passing `serverConfig` into the bridge and fingerprinting from it, or running the registry check in cca-engine/the MCP proxy before bridging. Registry-matching servers should then mount under "Registry only".

## Affected version

- Surface: Copilot cloud agent (Copilot Business, `api.business.githubcopilot.com`)
- Runtime: `runtime-cca-vendored-06412f43e9f392ebb48daa02136895268f688937` (also seen on `47b2e066…`)
- Feature flags present: `copilot_swe_agent_new_out_proc_mcp`, `copilot_swe_agent_mcp_builtin_provenance`
- Date observed: 2026-10-15

## Related

- mindovermachine-dev/product-cli#20: same error in the local CLI; documents the command→identity mapping.
- #4378: cloud agent silently dropping user-configured MCP servers (different trigger: policy fetch 401/403).
- Separate but adjacent: the registry lookup uses the config key as the server name, but config keys can't contain `.`. Spec-style reverse-DNS registry names (e.g. `io.example/server`) are therefore unmatchable from repo config without registry-side aliasing. Happy to file this separately.
