issues.title: Support default-deny tool permissions with explicit allowlist in non-interactive mode

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Non-interactive mode cannot enforce a strict tool allowlist because `--deny-tool` always overrides `--allow-tool` and some tools are allowed by default.

Currently, GitHub Copilot CLI does not provide a straightforward way to enforce a strict tool allowlist in non-interactive mode.
Some tool invocations, such as read-only shell commands, are allowed by default. Since `--deny-tool` rules always take precedence over `--allow-tool` rules, it is not possible to deny a tool broadly while explicitly allowing specific invocations.

For example, the following configuration does not work as intended:

```bash
copilot --deny-tool='shell' --allow-tool='shell(path/to/script)'
```

This limits the ability to enforce least-privilege execution policies in automated workflows, such as CI/CD pipelines, where tool execution must be restricted without relying on interactive approval.

### Proposed solution

Introduce a **default-deny permission mode for non-interactive execution**, in which all tool invocations are denied unless explicitly permitted through allow rules, including tools and commands normally allowed by default.

Ideally, this should integrate with the existing permission mechanisms and apply consistently across subagents.

This would make unattended runs more secure and predictable, remove the need for custom hooks, and make it easier to adopt Copilot CLI in CI/CD and security-sensitive environments.

### Example prompts or workflows

A CI/CD pipeline runs Copilot CLI in non-interactive mode. Copilot should be permitted to execute a specific validation script (`path/to/script`) while all other shell commands, including read-only commands, are denied.

### Additional context

A workaround for this feature is possible using `preToolUse` hooks, but this requires custom permission-checking logic and additional safeguards against bypasses, such as modifying hook scripts or configurations, or delegating execution to subagents.

Native support would simplify configuration and provide a more reliable way to enforce least-privilege policies in unattended environments.

issues.title: Model "auto" always runs with reasoning effort disabled (reasoningEffort: null), and rejects any attempt to configure one

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

labels.name: area:configuration
labels.description: Config files, instruction files, settings, and environment variables

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When the model is set to `auto`, every request is sent **without any reasoning effort**:

1. Selecting `auto` sets the session's `reasoningEffort` to `null` (visible in the session's `events.jsonl` as `session.model_change → "reasoningEffort": null`).
2. The auto router (`auto_v2`) picks a model per prompt (`session.auto_mode_resolved`) but **never assigns a reasoning effort** to it — the request goes out with none, confirmed by `reasoning_effort = NULL` and `reasoning_tokens = 0` in `~/.copilot/session-store.db` (`assistant_usage_events`).
3. Trying to set one explicitly is rejected: `copilot --model auto --effort xhigh` fails with `Error: Model "auto" does not support reasoning effort configuration (requested: "xhigh").`

So with `auto` there is **no way at all** to run with reasoning enabled. The degradation is silent — no error, no indication in the UI — and the impact on agentic work is severe: on a large agentic prompt (spec generation with mandatory file reads), the routed model (`gpt-5.3-codex`) ends its turn **without making a single tool call**, replying that it "could not perform the investigation". The exact same prompt, on the exact same routed model, works flawlessly when a reasoning effort is set (see "Same model, only effort differs" below).

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

```bash
# 1) auto → no reasoning (silent)
copilot --model auto --allow-all-tools -p "Reply with exactly: ok"

# 2) control: explicit model → reasoning works
copilot --model gpt-5.4 --allow-all-tools -p "Reply with exactly: ok"

# 3) auto + explicit effort → hard error
copilot --model auto --effort xhigh --allow-all-tools -p "Reply with exactly: ok"
```

Then inspect what was actually sent (replace the session ids printed in the `Resume` line):

```bash
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.copilot/session-store.db \
  "SELECT session_id, model, reasoning_effort, reasoning_tokens
   FROM assistant_usage_events ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;"
```

Observed results:

| Run | Routed/used model | `reasoning_effort` | `reasoning_tokens` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — `--model auto` | `gpt-5.4-mini` (via `auto_v2`) | **NULL** | **0** |
| 2 — `--model gpt-5.4` | `gpt-5.4` | `xhigh` | 21 |
| 3 — `--model auto --effort xhigh` | — | — | `Error: Model "auto" does not support reasoning effort configuration (requested: "xhigh").` |

The same happens in interactive mode: switching to `auto` logs
`session.model_change ... "previousReasoningEffort": "xhigh", "reasoningEffort": null`
in `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl`, and every subsequent `session.auto_mode_resolved` runs the chosen model with no effort.

### Same model, only effort differs — night and day

Real-world case that led us here (a large spec-generation prompt, ~19.6k input tokens, requiring file reads and skill loading):

- `auto` → routed to `gpt-5.3-codex`, `reasoning_effort = NULL`: the model ends the turn after **158 output tokens, 0 reasoning tokens, 0 tool calls**, claiming it could not perform the investigation. Reproduced consistently across several sessions.
- Same prompt, same `gpt-5.3-codex`, with `reasoning_effort = xhigh`: normal agentic behavior — tool calls, thousands of reasoning tokens, task completed.

The only variable is the reasoning effort. `auto` mode currently guarantees the degraded path.

### Expected behavior

`auto` should never silently disable reasoning. Either:

- the auto router assigns an appropriate reasoning effort for the routed model on each request (clamping to what that model supports), and/or
- a user-provided effort (`--effort`, settings `effortLevel`, session config) is honored under `auto` and clamped per routed model — instead of being cleared on switch and rejected on the CLI flag.

### Additional context

- This looks like an overcorrection of #2870: there, switching to `auto` **kept** the previous effort and caused loud `400` errors on models that don't support it; the fix apparently clears the effort entirely, trading a loud error for a silent, permanent degradation. #4459 and #4445 show the invalid-combination side of this is still not fully solved either — both symptoms share the same root: the auto router does not manage effort per routed model.
- The ACP server mode (`copilot --acp`) is affected identically, with no workaround at all: `session/set_config_option` with `model=auto` clears the effort and removes the reasoning-effort config option from the session, so ACP clients cannot restore it.

issues.title: Cannot search enterprise MCP registry, shows only public catalog results

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Copilot CLI does not show servers from our configured enterprise MCP registry in `/mcp` search. From a non-Git working directory, the **Online** tab loads public MCP results, but searching for `example-mcp-server` does not return our internal server. `/mcp search example` likewise does not show it.

A few releases ago, I was able to query the enterprise registry via the CLI. After some time of not trying it, I noticed it stopped working. 

The enterprise registry policy is fetched successfully and identifies our registry with `registry_access: allow_all`. The registry responds to `GET https://mcp-registry.example.com/v0.1/servers?limit=30` with HTTP 200 and 23 servers, including an active, latest `example-mcp-server`. VS Code can read the same registry.

GitHub's [MCP private registry enforcement documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/enterprise-administrators/mcp-private-registry-enforcement) lists **Registry display** as supported in Copilot CLI. A maintainer also described `/mcp search <query>` as showing servers available in the configured registry in #3436. Is the CLI expected to include enterprise-registry results when the policy is `allow_all`? If not, how should users browse their configured registry without changing the enterprise-wide access policy?

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.89 on Windows 11

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure an enterprise MCP Registry URL pointing to a working v0.1 registry. 
2. In GitHub policy, set **Restrict MCP access to registry servers** to **Allow all**.
3. Start a fresh Copilot CLI process outside any Git repository, for example, from `$HOME`.
4. Run `/mcp`, select **Online** tab, and search for an internal-only server like `example-mcp-server`.
5. Also try `/mcp search example`.

**Current behavior:**  The Online view shows public MCP catalog results but not `example-mcp-server`. `/mcp search example` also does not find the server (that is on the internal registry).

### Expected behavior

From the Copilot CLI, the internal `example-mcp-server` appears in search results and can be inspected or installed from the configured enterprise registry. Public results may also appear if **Allow all** is intended to include both sources.

### Additional context

- `GET https://api.github.com/copilot/mcp_registry` returns HTTP 200 and the expected registry URL with `registry_access: allow_all`. CLI startup logs independently report that the registry “permits all servers (allow_all).”
- In a local TLS pass-through test recording **destination hostnames only**, the search connected to `api.mcp.github.com`; no connection to `mcp-registry.example.com` was observed through the proxy. This does not rule out a GitHub backend fetching the registry or a request bypassing the proxy.
- This is separate from #4374: starting CLI inside our Azure DevOps Git repositories causes a **400** while loading registry policy. Starting outside a directory with Git avoids that error but does **not** make internal servers appear in search.
- Our enterprise also uses server-managed `allowedMcpServers` (#4989). This report concerns **discovery/search**, not whether an installed server is permitted to start.
- We have not changed the policy to **Registry only** as a test because that changes server-use permissions enterprise-wide, not just the search view.

issues.title: OTel execute_tool bash span does not expose nonzero process exit outcome
issues.body:
### Describe the observability gap

When the shell tool successfully launches the synthetic command `false`, the resulting `execute_tool bash` span has status code 0 and no exit-code, error, result, or outcome attribute. Consumers cannot distinguish exit 0 from a nonzero command outcome in metadata-only telemetry.

This is distinct from a tool invocation failure: reading a guaranteed nonexistent synthetic path correctly produced an `execute_tool view` span with error status, `error.type=failure`, and an exception event.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.83 on macOS.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable metadata-only OTel file export.
2. Run a synthetic prompt that directs the shell tool to execute exactly `false` once.
3. Inspect the `execute_tool bash` span.

The tool execution output reports completion, while the span contains no metadata representing the subprocess's nonzero exit.

### Expected behavior

It is reasonable for the tool invocation itself to be considered operationally successful, but metadata-only telemetry should expose a bounded, content-free command outcome such as `process.exit.code=1` and/or a Copilot tool outcome attribute. The span status policy can remain separate from the subprocess exit status.

### Privacy

The command is synthetic and harmless. Content capture was disabled; no command output, paths, repository data, or credentials are included.

issues.title: Gemini Flash: one malformed MCP array enum breaks all prompts with HTTP 400
MCP OAuth "Sign in" fails with "MCP server probe returned HTTP 400" for stateful servers (Atlassian /v2/mcp) when a valid token is already stored

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Summary

Since runtime **1.0.90-0** (GitHub Copilot desktop app 1.1.24, Windows 11), the Atlassian MCP server shows **Sign in** in the MCP panel, and clicking it fails with:

```
Authentication failed
atlassian: RPC error -32603: Request session.mcp.oauth.login failed with message: MCP request failed: MCP server probe returned HTTP 400 Bad Request
```

The server itself works: regular sessions connect (`server/discover returned an unusable JSON response; retrying with legacy initialize` → `Service initialized ... atlassian-mcp-server`) and Jira/Confluence tools run fine with the stored token.

### Config

```json
"atlassian": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp", "tools": ["*"] }
```

OAuth via dynamic client registration; a valid access + refresh token is stored in `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/`.

### Root cause (reproduced by hand)

The OAuth probe (`remote_probe.rs`) sends a JSON-RPC `ping` without an `Mcp-Session-Id`. Atlassian's endpoint is a stateful Streamable HTTP server:

| POST to `https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp` | Response |
|---|---|
| `ping`, no token | `401` + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v2/mcp"` |
| `ping`, **valid** token (`MCP-Protocol-Version` 2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, or omitted) | `400` `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Request must be an initialize request if no session ID is provided."}}` |
| `initialize`, valid token | `200` + `Mcp-Session-Id` |

So sign-in fails **only when the user is already authenticated**: the probe passes auth and then hits the server's session check, and the 400 is treated as fatal instead of "authenticated".

```sh
curl -i -X POST https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" -H "MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping","params":{}}'
```

### Why "Sign in" is shown in the first place

The app's MCP status session (global scope) never re-attaches the stored token for this third-party server. Its first connect gets 401, the host logs `MCP OAuth non-first-party server; cancelling host-token and kicking daemon-owned reconnect so the status badge can resolve`, and the reconnect gets 401 again, so the status stays "needs auth". Regular sessions in the same app handle the same initial 401 internally and connect. On 1.0.87-0 the same kick was followed by `MCP refresh generation bumped` and a token refresh within seconds.

### Expected

- The probe treats a `400` with JSON-RPC `-32600` "initialize required / no session ID" (or any non-401/403 reply to an authenticated request) as `authenticated`, or probes with `initialize` and then `DELETE`s the session, matching the connector's `server/discover` → legacy `initialize` fallback.
- The MCP status session reuses stored third-party OAuth tokens the way regular sessions do, so the badge doesn't ask for a sign-in that isn't needed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Atlassian server as above and sign in once, so tokens are stored.
2. Restart the app and open the MCP servers panel. Atlassian shows "Sign in", although tools work in sessions.
3. Click **Sign in**. The error above appears.

issues.title: grep tool silently ignores `n`, so models that drop the dash from `-n` get no line numbers

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The built-in grep tool shows line numbers only when it gets `"-n": true`. An argument named `n`, without the dash, is accepted without an error and ignored, so the matches come back without line numbers.

Models do drop the dash. In 664 headless benchmark runs on 1.0.90, claude-haiku-4.5 passed `"n": true` in 920 of its 1,949 grep calls and `"-n": true` in 22. claude-sonnet-5 passed `-n` in 508 of 571 calls and claude-opus-5.5 in all 53. Without line numbers haiku counted lines in files it opened with `view`, which also returns no line numbers, and was off by a few: 78 of its 79 wrong answers to "which line…" questions were a wrong line number.

### Affected version

1.0.91 (also 1.0.90)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

In a git repository with `notes.txt` containing `alpha`, `beta`, `needle here`, `gamma` on four lines:

```
copilot -p 'Call the grep tool twice and nothing else. First call: {"pattern": "needle", "paths": "notes.txt", "output_mode": "content", "n": true}. Second call: {"pattern": "needle", "paths": "notes.txt", "output_mode": "content", "-n": true}. Then reply with the two raw tool results.' --model claude-haiku-4.5 --allow-all-tools --available-tools grep --output-format json -s
```

With `"n": true` the tool returns `notes.txt:needle here`. With `"-n": true` it returns `notes.txt:3:needle here`.

### Expected behavior

Either accept `n` as an alias for `-n`, or reject unknown arguments with an error the model can see and correct.

### Additional context

The counts come from the session logs of a public benchmark: https://github.com/nefayran/code-graph-vs-grep

issues.title: WSL: clipboard write via clip.exe fails (quoted path in cmd /c), mouse selection copies nothing

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

issues.body:
**Version:** 1.0.105 (also seen on 1.0.104)
**Environment:** WSL2 (Ubuntu 26.04) + WSLg, GNOME Console (VTE, no OSC 52 support)

**Problem**
Selecting text with the mouse and copying leaves the clipboard empty. `/copy` works.

**Logs**
`writeToClipboard: clip.exe failed; relied on OSC 52: Error: clip.exe exited with code 1`

**Root cause**
On WSL the CLI spawns `cmd.exe /d /c 'chcp 65001 >nul & "<path>\clip.exe"'`. The quotes around the path get escaped when launched from WSL, and cmd reports:
`'\"C:\Windows\System32\clip.exe\"' is not recognized as an internal or external command`
so it exits with code 1. The CLI then falls back to OSC 52, which VTE terminals ignore, so nothing reaches the clipboard.

**Verification**
Running the same command without the quotes around the clip.exe path exits 0 and the text lands on the Windows clipboard.

**Workaround**
Remove the quotes around `${n}` in the `chcp 65001 >nul & "${n}"` template in `cli-main.js`.

**Suggested fix**
Don't quote the path (or escape it correctly for WSL interop), or invoke `clip.exe` directly instead of via `cmd /c`.

issues.title: ACP: plugin skills aren't available in ACP sessions, though the plugin's agents are

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp --stdio`), skills from enabled plugins aren't available in a session. The plugin itself loads, since the `agent` config option offers its agents. But none of its skills:

- are in `available_commands_update`, so an ACP client can't offer them as slash commands;
- show in `/skills list` sent over ACP, which lists only project and personal skills;
- reach the model: asked to list its skills, it names only the personal one.

Outside ACP, with the same `COPILOT_HOME` and folder, the skills are there: `copilot skill list` lists them under "Plugin skills", and in `copilot -p` the model lists them.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.104 (also seen on 1.0.92)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Enable plugins that have skills, and add one personal skill as a control. Here, two plugins from local marketplace directories, which `copilot plugin list` shows under "Live Plugins". Between them they have 12 agents and 36 skills.
2. `copilot skill list` lists the 36 under "Plugin skills".
3. Start `copilot --acp --stdio`, `initialize`, and call `session/new` with a `cwd`.
4. The `agent` config option offers the 12 plugin agents (`<plugin>:<agent>`).
5. `available_commands_update` has 33 commands: the 32 built-in commands and the personal skill. None of the plugin skills are there.
6. Send `/skills list` as a `session/prompt`. It lists only the personal skill ("Found 1 skill").
7. Send `Without using any tools, list the names of all the skills in your available skills list, comma-separated, and nothing else.` The reply names only the personal skill.
8. In the same folder, run `copilot -p` with the same text. The model lists the personal skill and the plugin skills.

### Expected behavior

An ACP session has the same skills as the interactive CLI and prompt mode, plugin skills included:

- they're offered in `available_commands_update`, as 1.0.40 did for skills ("Skills are available as slash commands in ACP clients, matching the CLI experience");
- `/skills list` lists them;
- the model can use them.

### Additional context

- Windows 11, x86_64, driven from a Node ACP client, in a scratch `COPILOT_HOME` with no extensions installed.
- Project and personal skills work over ACP. `/skills reload` picks up new ones and sends `available_commands_update`.
- Related: #2753 (plugin skills missing from `<available_skills>` in interactive sessions). There, a comment ties it to extensions that call `joinSession()`. Here no extension is installed, and prompt mode isn't affected.

issues.title: ACP: /session delete, cleanup and prune fail with "sessionsApi ... is unavailable for this session"

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp --stdio`), Copilot advertises `/session` in `available_commands_update`, but its `delete`, `cleanup` and `prune` subcommands fail over ACP. Sent as a `session/prompt`, each ends with `end_turn` in about 1 ms, without a model call, and replies with an error:

| Prompt | Reply |
|---|---|
| `/session delete <id>` | `Failed to run /session: Error: slash command effect sessionsApi.list is unavailable for this session` |
| `/session cleanup` | `Failed to run /session: Error: slash command effect sessionsApi.list is unavailable for this session` |
| `/session prune --older-than 1 --dry-run --include-named` | `Failed to run /session: Error: slash command effect sessionsApi.pruneOld is unavailable for this session` |

Nothing is deleted: the sessions' folders stay in `session-state`.

An ACP client has no other way to delete Copilot sessions. `initialize` offers `sessionCapabilities` `list` and `close` only, without ACP's stable [`session/delete`](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/session-delete).

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.104

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start `copilot --acp --stdio` and `initialize`.
2. Call `session/new` twice, for sessions A and B.
3. Send session A a `session/prompt` with the text `/session delete <B's sessionId>`.
4. The reply is the `sessionsApi.list` error above, with `stopReason: end_turn`. Session B's folder is still in `session-state`.
5. Send `/session cleanup`, then `/session prune --older-than 1 --dry-run --include-named`. Each gets its error above.

### Expected behavior

These subcommands work over ACP as they do in the interactive CLI:

- `/session delete <id>` deletes the session.
- `/session cleanup` removes empty or abandoned sessions.
- `/session prune --older-than <days>` deletes old sessions, or lists them with `--dry-run`.

Each replies with what it did.

Better still for ACP clients: advertise `sessionCapabilities.delete` and support `session/delete`. Then a client can delete a session without sending a prompt through another one.

### Additional context

- Windows 11, x86_64, driven from a Node ACP client, in a scratch `COPILOT_HOME`.
- `prune` checks its arguments before it fails. Without `--older-than` it replies with its usage, and `--older-than 0` gets `Invalid number of days: 0`. It fails once it needs the sessions API.
- This is like #5115. There, `/rename` over ACP replies that it renamed the session but saves nothing. In both cases the command is advertised over ACP, but the ACP session lacks what it needs.
- Related: #2555 (advertising every slash command over ACP) and #1451 (`/cleanup`).

issues.title: Org custom models on /chat/completions always fail with 400: CLI sends frequency_penalty/presence_penalty that providers reject (Google AI Studio, OpenAI-compatible)

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

Organization **custom models** (configured in the GitHub Copilot org settings) that are served over `/chat/completions` fail on every request in Copilot CLI with HTTP 400. Custom models served over `/responses` work fine in the same session.

The CLI sends OpenAI-specific sampling fields in every Chat Completions request to a custom model, and GitHub's proxy forwards them unchanged to the third-party provider, which rejects them:

```json
"temperature": 0,
"top_p": 0.95,
"frequency_penalty": 0,
"presence_penalty": 0,
"snippy": { "enabled": false },
"stream": true,
"stream_options": { "include_usage": true }
```

Google AI Studio's response names the field explicitly:

```text
Execution failed: 400 [{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name \"frequency_penalty\": Cannot find field.",
    "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT"
  }
}]
```

Xiaomi MiMo (provider type `openaicompatible`) returns a generic `400 Invalid request parameters` (81-byte JSON body), which is very likely the same cause.

This looks like the same sampling-parameter regression reported for local BYOK in #4950 (introduced in 1.0.81), but here it is a hard failure that makes `/chat/completions` org custom models completely unusable from the CLI.

## Results by provider

| Custom model provider (catalog `custom_model.provider`) | `supported_endpoints` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `azureai` (Azure AI Foundry, gpt-6-luna / gpt-6.1-sol / gpt-6.1-terra) | `/responses` | Works |
| `googleaistudio` (gemini-flash-latest, gemini-4-argon, ...) | `/chat/completions` | 400 `Unknown name "frequency_penalty"` |
| `openaicompatible` (Xiaomi MiMo mimo-v2.6-flash, mimo-v2.6-pro) | `/chat/completions` | 400 `Invalid request parameters` |

All models appear correctly in the `/model` picker and in the CAPI catalog (`capabilities.supports: {streaming: true, tool_calls: true}`, `family: "custom"`).

## Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.104 (Windows 11). Copilot Business, org custom models, requests go to `api.business.githubcopilot.com`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. As an org owner, add a custom model from Google AI Studio (or any OpenAI-compatible provider) in the org's Copilot custom models settings.
2. In Copilot CLI, select it via `/model`, or run:
   `copilot -p "say hi" --model "<org>/<key-name>/gemini-flash-latest" --log-level all`
3. Observe the 400. The debug log shows the `Wire request` body containing the fields above, followed by:
   `Upstream model error response shape (body content omitted) {"status":400,...}` and
   `Model provider request failed {"stage":"inference","api_endpoint":"/chat/completions","http_status":400,"failure_kind":"http_error"}`
4. Switch to an Azure Foundry custom model on `/responses` in the same session: it answers normally.

Side note: on the first attempt the CLI also logs `Model HTTP request with a compressed body was rejected; resending it uncompressed {"status":400,"content_encoding":"zstd"}`, and the uncompressed retry fails with the same 400, so compression is not the cause.

## Request IDs (for server-side correlation)

- Gemini (googleaistudio): `04C1:5294A:2E6DEC6:309B2BF:6AE102C3`, `04C1:2DF905:17A52BF:1A3B26D:6AE10A9B`
- MiMo (openaicompatible): `04C0:2A654E:2678A92:28B3279:6AE1026C`, `04C1:2DF905:179D61C:1A326DB:6AE10A7E`, `04C3:2FE0EC:24A422F:26C2232:6AE0FF00` (serviceRequestId `fb5768cd-4895-4282-b3c8-98a8fe123d7e`)

## Expected behavior

For custom models, the CLI (or the CAPI proxy) should not send sampling parameters the provider has not declared support for. Options:

- Omit `temperature` / `top_p` / `frequency_penalty` / `presence_penalty` for `family: "custom"` models (CLI 1.0.80 sent none), or send only non-default values.
- Have the proxy strip non-standard / unsupported fields (`snippy`, penalties) per provider type, e.g. drop penalties for `googleaistudio`.
- Expose a per-model capability flag in the catalog so the client knows which sampling fields are accepted.

## Additional context

- Related: #4950 (same sampling fields forced since 1.0.81, local BYOK), #3448 (control extra request params for BYOK models).
- There is no CLI setting to disable these fields, so there is currently no workaround inside the CLI for `/chat/completions` custom models.

issues.title: Input history (command-history-state.json) is last-writer-wins across concurrent copilot processes; prompts typed in one session are erased

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`~/.copilot/command-history-state.json` is shared by every interactive `copilot` process, and the last process to write it wins. Each process loads the file once at startup and keeps the list in memory. Each time it saves a prompt, it writes the whole list back to the file, without re-reading or merging. When two or more `copilot` processes are open, whichever one writes last erases every entry the others added after it started. Those prompts then disappear from Up arrow and Ctrl+R in every later session.

**Evidence (one machine, 2026-10-27, UTC):** three interactive processes were running at once.

- Process A (1.0.103) had been running since 23:34 the previous day.
- Process C (1.0.103) started at 02:57.
- Process B (1.0.104) started at 03:01, so it loaded the history file at that point.
- The final history file has 50 entries, newest first. B last wrote it at 14:29:54, when B submitted a prompt. It contains:
  - B's prompts from 14:19 to 14:29.
  - C's prompts from 02:58 and 03:00, which were before B started.
  - A's prompts up to 02:43, also before B started.
- **It's missing C's 14:15:13 prompt.** That prompt was submitted normally while the session was idle, with no error, so C's success path should have saved it. B's next write at 14:19:47 erased it.
- A's later prompts (03:00:55, 04:58, 05:00 and 14:12) are also missing. Each came right after a `Submission failed`, so they don't prove this bug either way. If the 04:58, 05:00 and 14:12 messages were late deliveries of "failed" prompts, the CLI never saved them (#5264). If they were retypes, B's later writes would have erased them anyway, because B started at 03:01. The 03:00:55 message came before B started, and #5264 explains why the history file indicates it was most likely never saved.

**Code (shipped `cli-main.js`, 1.0.103 and 1.0.104):** the history manager's `initialize()` loads the file once. `addCommand()` puts the new entry at the front of the in-memory array, then `saveHistory()` writes the whole array through `cliCommandHistoryWrite`. Nothing re-reads or merges the file before writing.

### Affected version

1.0.103 and 1.0.104. The code is the same in both.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

The steps below follow from the code. I haven't run this minimal version yet; the evidence above comes from normal use.

1. Open terminal 1 and run `copilot`. Open terminal 2 and run `copilot`.
2. In terminal 1, submit `alpha`.
3. In terminal 2, submit `beta`.
4. Without exiting the first two, start a third `copilot` and press Up. `beta` is there, but `alpha` is missing.

### Expected behavior

Concurrent sessions shouldn't erase each other's history. Either option would work:

- Under a file lock, re-read the file, merge the new entry by recency, remove duplicates, trim to `commandHistoryMaxSize`, then write.
- Store history as an append-only log and compact it when reading.

### Additional context

- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), arm64. Ghostty, zsh.
- Several interactive `copilot` processes usually run at the same time on this machine.
- We found this while trying to recover a prompt that the CLI had discarded (#5264). Because of this bug, input history can't be relied on as a safety net for lost prompts.

issues.title: Prompt is discarded after 'Submission failed' (host-ack timeout): composer cleared, not saved to history, delivered late or never

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When `session.send` fails because the session host stopped acknowledging events (the #5100 state), the CLI clears the prompt the user just submitted and keeps no copy of it. What happens to the prompt afterwards is unpredictable: sometimes it's delivered later anyway, and sometimes it's never delivered. The CLI shows:

```
Submission failed: Error: Request session.send failed with message: session event delivery failed: session host did not acknowledge the assistant.reasoning_delta event within 120s
```

After that, the composer is empty and the text is not put back. Up arrow and Ctrl+R don't find it, and there is no resend option. In the case below:

- **One "failed" prompt was most likely delivered 73 seconds later, after the user had been told it failed.** Input history points to a late delivery rather than a retype (see the timeline).
- **A later multi-paragraph prompt was never delivered.** The user had to rewrite it from memory.

**Why this happens (from reading the shipped `cli-main.js` in 1.0.103 and 1.0.104):** in the interactive submit path, the prompt is added to input history only in the success branch after `session.send` resolves. The error branch only emits `Submission failed`. The pending-submission tracker retires the draft when the send throws, and nothing restores the text to the composer. This means any `session.send` rejection leaves the user with no copy of the prompt, not only the 120s acknowledgement timeout. Whether the prompt still reaches the agent later is decided out of the user's sight.

**How often:** since October 23, this machine's retained session data has **20 `Submission failed` errors across 5 sessions, all with this host-acknowledgement error (the event named varies)**. #5100 notes that the agent's own output keeps being saved to `events.jsonl` after delivery fails. The user's input is the one thing nobody keeps a copy of.

### Affected version

1.0.103 (`copilotVersion` in `session.start`). The same submit and history code is in 1.0.104.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

This isn't deterministic, because it depends on first reaching the #5100 state.

1. Run a long interactive session. Ours was launched through a wrapper that loads several extensions. It used autopilot, many subagents, and a recurring scheduled prompt every 30 minutes. It ran 15 hours with 13 auto-compactions and no resume.
2. Wait until the host stops acknowledging events (#5100). The first visible sign is `Submission failed: ... did not acknowledge ... within 120s`.
3. Keep working. Submit prompts while the agent is busy.
4. Some submissions show `Submission failed`, and each one clears the composer. In our case, after the CLI logged `queue drain abandoned`, the next failed prompt (14:19:03) was never delivered before the user exited 11 minutes later, and no copy of it remained.

Timeline of the affected session (UTC, 2026-10-27):

| Time | What happened |
|---|---|
| 02:59:42 | First `Submission failed ... assistant.reasoning_delta ... within 120s`. The session was about 3.5 hours old. |
| 03:00–13:48 | The session stays partly usable. The agent keeps running turns. Two more `Submission failed` errors appear, at 04:56 and 04:59. Each of the three failures is followed 71–73 seconds later by a typed message arriving as a steering message. The first of these (03:00:55) was most likely the "failed" 02:59:42 prompt delivered late, not a retype. Successful submits write input history, and the history file suggests this one never did (see the explanation below the table). We can't tell whether the 04:58 and 05:00 messages were retypes or late deliveries. All 22 runs of the 30-minute scheduled prompt in this period log a `schedule_delivery_failed` warning ("Scheduled prompt #1 ... failed"), yet each run arrives 3 seconds to 4 minutes later. |
| 14:11:40 | `Submission failed`. A typed steering message arrives 21 seconds later. Like the 04:56 and 04:59 cases, we can't tell whether it was a retype or a late delivery. |
| 14:17:15 | The scheduled run fails again. This time it is not delivered. |
| 14:17:26 | `Scheduled queue processing failed after retry; queue drain abandoned` |
| 14:19:03 | `Submission failed` for a long multi-paragraph prompt. At the same moment the log shows two `Scheduled queue processing failed; retrying once` lines, and no later line reports the retry's outcome. **This prompt was never delivered and no copy of it remains.** |
| 14:29:52 | The user exits. Shutdown also fails with the same cached delivery error. |

Evidence that the 14:19:03 prompt was lost:

- `events.jsonl` has no user-typed `user.message` after 14:12:01. The only later `user.message` is a subagent prompt at 14:14:46.
- The text wasn't restored to the composer.
- It isn't in input history. That file also has a separate overwrite problem (#5265), so the code path above is the stronger evidence here.

Why the 03:00:55 message was most likely a late delivery and not a retype:

1. A second process (call it C) saved two prompts to history at 02:58 and 03:00:13. That process started after this session did, so this session's in-memory history list didn't include those two entries.
2. A third process loaded the history file when it started at 03:01:34, and it wrote the final version of the file at 14:29:54. The final file still contains the 02:58 and 03:00:13 entries.
3. If this session had saved a history entry at 03:00:55, it would have written its own list, which lacked those two entries, over the file before 03:01:34. They survived, so this session saved nothing between 03:00:55 and 03:01:34. Process C didn't write again in that window, because no later C entry from that window appears in the file.
4. In the shipped code, every interactive submit path saves to history when the send call returns. For steering submissions, the submit tracker resolves `true` once the send returns, and history is skipped only if an internal `skipHistory` option is set. No `Submission failed` appeared near 03:00:55, so a retyped prompt's send didn't fail. If it succeeded, it would have saved to history, unless its send took more than 39 seconds to return. The 03:00:55 message was therefore most likely the 02:59:42 prompt, delivered late. Either way, the user was told the 02:59:42 prompt failed and had no copy of it.

### Expected behavior

- Save the draft before sending it (for example, in session state), and clear it only after the session confirms it has the prompt.
- If the send fails, put the text and attachments back in the composer, or keep the prompt visibly marked as failed with a resend option.
- Add the prompt to input history whether or not the send succeeds. History records what the user typed.
- Report delivery honestly. If a "failed" prompt is still queued and will run later, don't say it failed. If it's dropped (for example, after `queue drain abandoned`), say so explicitly.
- If the session is in the permanent failed state from #5100, say so. Carry unsent drafts across `--resume` or `/restart` so they can be resent.

### Additional context

- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), arm64, 96 GiB RAM
- Ghostty, zsh
- Launched through a wrapper that adds several native extensions. Several other interactive `copilot` processes were running on the same machine.
- `events.jsonl` for the affected session was 444 MB.
- Related: #5100 (the root failure state), #5253, and #5018 (same family). #1780 asks to recover queued prompts after a crash. #4477 covers a prompt lost on stop.

The full logs contain private content and can't be shared publicly. I can provide filtered excerpts on request.

issues.title: SessionClient poll loop keeps retrying after session disposal ("Cannot invoke native session after disposal has started"), leaking memory until heap OOM

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A long-running interactive session gets slower and eventually crashes with `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`. On my machine this happens about once a week.

The cause appears to be an orphaned `SessionClient` poll loop. If a session is closed (for example, on `/resume` or when switching sessions) while an MCP server's OAuth flow is still running, the native session gets disposed. The JS-side poll loop does not stop, though. It keeps retrying forever, about once per second for each leaked loop:

```
[ERROR] SessionClient poll loop error (will retry): Error: Cannot invoke native session after disposal has started
```

Each leaked loop adds another stream of these errors, and heap usage climbs until V8 aborts at the ~4 GB limit.

### Affected version

1.0.100 and 1.0.102 (both crashes happened on these builds)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure remote HTTP MCP servers that need OAuth (in my case Confluence and Datadog) and start an interactive session while their tokens are expired or invalid. Both servers return `401`, which triggers the OAuth flow.
2. Close or switch the session (e.g. `/resume` another session) while the OAuth/MCP reload is still in progress.
3. Keep the CLI process running. The log fills with `SessionClient poll loop error` about once per second for each leaked loop, and the process OOMs after a few days.

Here is the log sequence at the moment the loop starts:

```
[INFO] Closing session <id>
[ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { ... status_code: 401 ... })
[WARNING] [rust:mcp_engine::agent_host] HTTP 401 challenge (...) {"server":"confluence","error":"MCP authorization was cancelled"}
[WARNING] [rust:mcp_engine::agent_host] HTTP 401 challenge (...) {"server":"datadog","error":"MCP authorization was cancelled"}
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::mcp::session_host] MCP reload lock still held at disposal; draining the graph without it
[ERROR] [rust:copilot_runtime::shared_api::event_log] Failed to retry MCP servers after OAuth listener registration: {"error":"MCP session host is disposed"}
[ERROR] SessionClient poll loop error (will retry): Error: Cannot invoke native session after disposal has started
... (repeats forever)
```

### Expected behavior

Disposing a session should stop its `SessionClient` poll loop, or the loop should exit on this error instead of retrying. Leaked loops should not pile up and exhaust the heap.

### Additional context

- macOS 26.7.1 (Apple Silicon, arm64), iTerm2, zsh; installed via Homebrew cask `copilot-cli`; Node v24.x embedded
- **Crash 1 (Oct 21):** one process OOM'd after the loop had run for about a day.
- **Crash 2 (Oct 27):** two processes launched Oct 21 died within ~10 ms of each other after ~6 days of uptime.
  - One was a V8 OOM (`node::OOMErrorHandler` → `abort`, last GC: `Mark-Compact 3871.5 (4102.0) -> 3851.3 (4086.0) MB`).
  - The other was a SIGABRT raised from `uv_kill`.
  - The OOM'd process had the error loop running continuously for 4+ days.
- **Log volume:**
  - One process rotated through 5 × 10 MB log files containing ~72–75k of these error lines each.
  - Another logged 3 identical errors per second, which suggests 3 leaked loops.
- **Possibly related:** #4699, #4725, #4686 (all OOM reports), but none of them identify this poll loop.
- **Workaround:** restart the CLI periodically.

---
🤖 *This issue was posted on behalf of Caleb Tenberge by GitHub Copilot CLI (Claude Opus 5.5/Anthropic).*

issues.title: Hooks: include the tool call id in preToolUse, postToolUse and postToolUseFailure input

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Tool hook input has no tool call id, so a hook can't tell which preToolUse a postToolUse or postToolUseFailure belongs to.

### Proposed solution

Add the call's id to the preToolUse, postToolUse and postToolUseFailure input (and permissionRequest, where there is one):
`toolCallId` in the camelCase format and `tool_use_id` in the VS Code compatible format.

The hooks reference lists `sessionId`, `timestamp`, `cwd`, `toolName`, `toolArgs` (plus `toolResult` or `error`)
for these events, and nothing that names the call. VS Code's own agent hooks send `tool_use_id` on PreToolUse and
PostToolUse (VS Code docs, agents/reference/hooks-reference), and the CLI's PascalCase format is described as matching
the VS Code extension's format, so a hook written against VS Code that reads `tool_use_id` gets nothing from the CLI.
Claude Code's hooks carry the same field.

Without it, two calls of the same tool with the same arguments (the same file viewed twice, a retried command, calls
dispatched in parallel) can't be told apart, and a hook has to pair pre and post events by tool and arguments in
arrival order, which is wrong when they finish in another order.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. An audit hook writes one record per call: the decision at preToolUse, the outcome at postToolUse or postToolUseFailure, joined by id.
2. A policy hook holds a call for a person's approval in another system, then attaches the result to that approval.
3. A telemetry hook measures each call's duration while calls run in parallel.
4. A hook links its record to the same call in the session's event log or an OpenTelemetry span.

### Additional context

prs.title: fix: add trap to clean up temp directory on unexpected exit
prs.body:
### Problem

`install.sh` uses `set -e` which terminates the script on any command failure. When this happens (e.g., download 404, network error), the temp directory created by `mktemp -d` is never cleaned up — it's leaked in `/tmp`.

The existing `rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"` calls only cover manually handled error paths, but `set -e` implicit exits bypass all of them.

**Repro:**
```bash
VERSION=v99.99.99 curl -fsSL https://gh.io/copilot-install | bash
# curl fails with 404, set -e kills script, /tmp/tmp.XXXXX left behind
```

### Fix

Add `trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"' EXIT` immediately after `mktemp -d`. This ensures cleanup on **all** exit paths — normal, error, and `set -e` implicit exits.

The 4 redundant manual `rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"` calls are removed since the trap handles them.

### Changes
- **+1 line**: `trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"' EXIT` after `mktemp -d`
- **-4 lines**: Removed manual `rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"` calls (now redundant)

prs.title: install: guard against duplicate PATH entries on reinstall
prs.body:
Running the installer twice without restarting the shell causes the PATH configuration line to be appended to the shell profile a second time. This happens because the script checks `command -v copilot` to decide whether to prompt for PATH setup, but that check requires a shell restart to reflect the previous install's RC_FILE changes.

**Repro:**
```bash
curl -fsSL https://gh.io/copilot-install | bash   # say y to PATH prompt
curl -fsSL https://gh.io/copilot-install | bash   # say y again → duplicate line
```

**Result:** `~/.bash_profile` (or equivalent) contains the same `export PATH=...` line twice.

This adds a `grep -qF` check for the exact `PATH_LINE` in `RC_FILE` before appending, making the write idempotent. On reinstall, the script reports that the configuration is already present instead of duplicating it.

**Before (reinstall):**
```
✓ Added PATH configuration to /home/user/.bash_profile   ← duplicate appended
```

**After (reinstall):**
```
✓ PATH configuration already in /home/user/.bash_profile
```

Works for all shells (bash, zsh, fish, POSIX fallback) since it matches the exact `PATH_LINE` string.

prs.title: install: verify the checksum entry matching the downloaded tarball
prs.body:
## Problem

The install script's checksum verification can report success without actually verifying the downloaded tarball, in two ways:

**1. Vacuous verification via `--ignore-missing`**

The script validates the whole `SHA256SUMS.txt` with:

```sh
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS.txt
```

`--ignore-missing` makes the checker skip every listed file that isn't present in the temp directory — and only `copilot-<platform>-<arch>.tar.gz` is ever present. If the checksums file exists but contains **no entry for the downloaded tarball** (stale/cached/mismatched file, release asset renamed, mirrored content tampering), GNU `sha256sum` ignores every line and **exits 0**, so the script prints `✓ Checksum validated` even though nothing was verified.

Repro (GNU sha256sum; the Darwin `sha256sum` behaves the same):

```console
$ echo hello > foo.txt
$ printf '%s  %s\n' "$(shasum -a 256 foo.txt | cut -d' ' -f1)" bar.txt > SHA256SUMS.txt
$ sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS.txt   # no entry for any present file
$ echo $?
0
```

Running the current `install.sh` end-to-end (stubbed download) against a `SHA256SUMS.txt` that only lists other platforms:

```
Downloading from: .../copilot-darwin-arm64.tar.gz
✓ Checksum validated          <- nothing was actually checked
✓ GitHub Copilot CLI installed to ...
```

(Perl `shasum` happens to fail closed here with "no file was verified", so behavior is also inconsistent across platforms.)

**2. Silent skip when the checksums file can't be downloaded**

If `SHA256SUMS.txt` fails to download, `CHECKSUMS_AVAILABLE` stays false and installation proceeds with **no message at all** — integrity verification is silently skipped.

## Fix

- Extract the checksum entry matching the downloaded tarball's file name and verify exactly that entry (`sha256sum -c checksum.txt` / `shasum -a 256 -c checksum.txt`), so a successful check always means *this* tarball was verified.
- Fail with a clear error if the checksums file contains no entry for the tarball (consistent with the existing hard failure on checksum mismatch, and with `shasum`'s current behavior).
- Print a warning when the checksums file cannot be downloaded, instead of silently skipping verification.

## Testing

Sandboxed the script with a stubbed `curl` serving local release assets; all cases pass on macOS (both the `sha256sum` and `shasum` code paths):

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Valid checksum | ✓ validates, installs | ✓ validates, installs |
| Tampered tarball | hard error | hard error (unchanged) |
| Checksums file lacks entry for tarball | **false `✓ Checksum validated`, installs** | hard error: `does not contain an entry for copilot-darwin-arm64.tar.gz` |
| Checksums file download fails | **silently skips verification** | warning, then continues |
| No `sha256sum`/`shasum` available | warning | warning (unchanged) |

issues.title: "Unknown identifier query" in Code Mode with MCP tools
issues.body:
## Bug Description

When calling MCP tools with a `query` parameter (e.g., `search_nodes`, `search_memory_facts`) from within OpenCode Code Mode, the JS interpreter throws:

```
Unknown identifier 'query'. (line 1, col 30)
```

## Environment

- **OpenCode version:** 2.0.3
- **MCP server:** Graphiti MCP (running in Docker)
- **MCP tools:** `search_nodes`, `search_memory_facts` (both have `query` as required `str` parameter)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Graphiti MCP server in `opencode.json`
2. Start OpenCode TUI/CLI with Code Mode
3. Use a tool call referencing `search_nodes` or `search_memory_facts`
4. JS interpreter fails with "Unknown identifier 'query'"

## Expected Behavior

The `query` parameter should be available as a JS variable in the Code Mode sandbox.

## Actual Behavior

JS interpreter throws `Unknown identifier 'query'. (line 1, col 30)` — the parameter is not declared in the JS scope before code execution.

## Related Issues

- **#48910** — Same version (2.0.3), same class of bug: MCP tool parameters not properly handled in Code Mode sandbox
- **#48912** — `search()` discovery function unregistered
- **#45521** — `search()` documented 3 ways, only bare `search(input)` works
- **#41389** — Catalog-listed MCP tools fail `Unknown tool` outside `execute`
- **#46628** — MCP schemas bypass `tool.definition` hook

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The Code Mode JS executor wraps LLM-generated code in an async function but doesn't declare MCP tool parameters (like `query`) as JS variables before execution. The LLM generates code referencing `query` but the variable doesn't exist in scope, causing the "Unknown identifier" error from acorn parser.

This is likely the same class of bug as #48910 — sandbox scope injection for MCP parameters is incomplete.

issues.title: [Go] Kimi Code receives 400 MissingSessionID — consider a fallback session signal for non-OpenCode clients
issues.body:
### Description

Requests from Kimi Code (CLI 2.3.1 / Desktop 1.1.2) to OpenCode Go fail on every inference call:

```json
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"MissingSessionID","message":"Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently. Please see https://opencode.ai/docs/go/#where-can-i-use-it"}}
```

Kimi Code already sends `prompt_cache_key` (a stable per-conversation value) in the Chat Completions body, but it does not send the `x-opencode-session` header. The Go docs already list Kimi Code under "Known problematic clients" and cite kimi-code#3506, which was closed as not planned, so today there is no supported path for these users.

### Why this matters

- Per kimi-code#3506, 836 organizations were calling Go through Kimi Code.
- Kimi Code supports only a static `custom_headers` entry for this, which cannot provide the per-conversation ID the gateway asks for; the desktop provider form exposes no header field at all.
- The same header requirement has already surfaced for other third-party clients (see #47763 for the generic MissingSessionID report).

### Ask

Would you consider accepting `prompt_cache_key` (or another documented body field) as a fallback session signal for non-OpenCode clients? Alternatively, documenting a supported workaround for clients that cannot set a per-conversation header — similar to the Qwen Code example requested in #48288 — would unblock affected users.

### References

- kimi-code#3506 — header request, closed as not planned
- kimi-code#3600 — same 400 error
- kimi-code#4376 — open bug report
- kimi-code#4238 — open PR that adds the header
- #47763 — same MissingSessionID error in other clients

### Environment

- API: OpenCode Go (`opencode.ai`)
- Client: Kimi Code 2.3.1 (CLI), Kimi Code Desktop 1.1.2

issues.title: feature(desktop): system tray icon with clean shutdown of the background opencode-cli service (Windows)
issues.body:
## Summary

OpenCode Desktop spawns a persistent background service (`opencode-cli.exe`) that outlives the app window. When the desktop is closed normally (or crashes), the CLI service keeps running and loads a **stale config** (providers, `disabled_providers`, etc.) until killed — but on Windows there is no clean, first-class way to stop it:

- Closing the window does not reliably stop the service (it lingers).
- Reopening the desktop does not reload config if the stale service is still alive.
- The only workarounds are Task ManagerKill or a terminal one-liner (`Get-Process opencode-cli | Stop-Process -Name opencode-cli -Force`), which are hostile to non-developer users and risk losing nothing but being invisible.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.13 (OpenCode Desktop, latest channel)
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200, win32 x64)
- Shell: PowerShell 5.1

## Real-world consequences observed today

1. Updated `disabled_providers` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` **didn't take effect after restarting the app window** because a lingering `opencode-cli.exe` (started earlier, PID kept-alive) still served `/api/provider` and `models` from its in-memory snapshot.
2. Provider list ("connect state") shown in Desktop was served by that stale process, causing confusion ("I disabled this provider, why is it still here?").
3. Full restart requires knowing that you must quit from the tray *if there were one*, then also verify/kill `opencode-cli.exe` manually — cannot be discovered from the UI.

## Requested feature

Add a **system tray icon** for OpenCode Desktop, with:

- `Quit OpenCode` — graceful shutdown that also terminates the background `opencode-cli` service (wait for exit, then fall back to terminate), so "restart Desktop to apply config" actually works;
- Optionally a status tooltip / menu showing the background service PID + version, and a "Restart background service" action;
- Windows: also consider exiting remaining child `opencode-cli` processes on app quit (or exposing the documented cleanup command in Settings).

Alternatively (lighter option): a "Cleanly quit Desktop incl. background service" button/setting in the Desktop UI. But the tray is where Windows users expect this behavior.

## Additional Context

- Related pain point (same lifecycle): after killing the CLI, next launch performs recovery/legacy-log cleanup; a tray-managed shutdown would avoid leaving half-torn-down state and stale locks (`*.bundle.lock`-style residue we've seen for long-running tools).
- Happy to test; desktop build reports 2.0.13.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Desktop: window/taskbar title should show the current project (and session) name

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

**Context**

issues.title: Free tier issues: read this first, then post your report here

labels.name: zen
labels.description: Relates to Zen

issues.body:
This is the **main issue for free tier problems**. If you see any of these, you're in the right place:

- `Free usage exceeded, subscribe to Go`
- `Free usage limit reached`
- `You've used today's free messages. They reset at ...` and the reset never happens
- `This version of OpenCode Desktop no longer supports free models`
- `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`
- `OpenCode 1.18.0 or newer is required to use the free tier`

**Please comment here instead of opening a new issue.** We're closing duplicates and pointing them here so everything is in one place.

## 1. Make sure you're on the latest OpenCode v2

Most free tier reports come from **OpenCode v1** (versions `0.x` and `1.x`, for example Desktop or CLI `1.19.4`). v1 no longer supports free models and only gets fixes for critical bugs. Updating to v2 has fixed this for many people.

Check your version:

- **Terminal:** `opencode --version`
- **Desktop:** Settings → About

The latest v2 release is **2.1.4**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The v1 Desktop app's built-in updater keeps you on `1.x`. Download v2 manually from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**.

### Desktop

Download v2 Desktop for macOS, Windows or Linux from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**, or on macOS:

```sh
brew install --cask opencode-desktop
```

### Terminal (TUI / CLI)

All install options are listed at **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**. The quickest on macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

Or use a package manager:

```sh
npm install -g @opencode/cli
bun install -g --trust @opencode/cli
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
paru -S opencode-beta
```

v1 and v2 both use the `opencode` command. If you installed v1 with a package manager, remove it first, for example `npm uninstall -g opencode-ai`. Windows package managers (Chocolatey, Scoop) don't support v2. On Windows, use the Desktop app, npm, or a [standalone binary](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/).

### Useful docs

- [Install OpenCode v2](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)
- [Migrate from v1](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/)
- [Free models, limits and privacy](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/models/#free-models)
- [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/)
- [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting/)

## 2. Other things to check

- **Free models only work inside OpenCode.** Other clients, proxies and direct API calls can't use them. Use a paid model or [Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/) there instead.
- **Subscribed to Go but still seeing free limits?** Run `/connect`, choose **OpenCode Go**, paste your Go API key, then pick a Go model (`opencode-go/...`) with `/models` rather than a free model (`opencode/...-free`).
- **Hit the real daily limit?** Wait for the reset time shown, subscribe to [Go](https://opencode.ai/go), or connect another provider with `/connect`.

## 3. Still broken on the latest v2? Comment with:

- OpenCode version, and whether you use Desktop, TUI, CLI or web
- Operating system
- The free model you used
- The exact error message (a screenshot is fine)
- When it started and the reset time you were shown
- Whether you have Go or Console credits

> [!WARNING]
> Don't post email addresses, payment details or other account information here. This issue is public.

## 4. Still don't know what's going on?

If you're on the latest v2 and none of the above helps, or the problem is about your account, billing or Go subscription, email **help@anoma.ly** with the details from step 3. Billing and account issues can't be fixed in GitHub issues.

issues.title: opencode2: user-defined local provider models never enter the model catalog
issues.body:
### Description

## Summary

I downloaded opencode2 beta.

My user-defined local OpenAI-compatible provider (per the documented "Local models" config) is not visible, while it is working with opencode.

According to the model which investigated, it is parsed by the service but its model is never exposed in the catalog. `opencode2 run -m <provider>/<model>` fails with `Model unavailable` and the provider is absent from `/api/provider`.

### Plugins

none

### OpenCode version

opencode2 v0.0.0-next-17444 (channel: next)

### Steps to reproduce

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (also reproducible as a real file, non-symlink):
   ```jsonc
   {
     "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
     "providers": {
       "local-llama-cpp": {
         "name": "Local llama.cpp",
         "package": "aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
         "settings": { "baseURL": "http://localhost:11434/v1" },
         "models": {
           "local-llm": {
             "modelID": "local-llm",
             "capabilities": { "tools": true, "input": ["text"], "output": ["text"] },
             "limit": { "context": 114588, "output": 32768 }
           }
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. `opencode2 service restart`
3. `opencode2 api get /api/provider` — only the built-in `opencode` provider is listed; `local-llama-cpp` is absent.
4. `opencode2 api get /api/model` — only the 7 built-in `opencode` models are present.
5. `opencode2 run -m local-llama-cpp/local-llm "hi"` → `Error: Model unavailable: local-llama-cpp/local-llm`

## Expected Behavior

Per the Local models documentation, the `local-llama-cpp/local-llm` model should appear in the model picker and be runnable.

## Actual Behavior

The provider is parsed and held by the service (confirmed via `/api/config`), but it never enters the model catalog: absent from `/api/provider` and `/api/model`, and `run` reports `Model unavailable`.

### Screenshot and/or share link

_No response_

### Operating System

Linux z390v2 7.1.8-arch1-3 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Terminal

Konsole / tmux

## Additional Context

- Distinct from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/36834 (closed):
  - There the model resolves but the request hangs / sends to `undefined/chat/completions`; here the model never enters the catalog, so the failure is earlier (catalog build / model resolution).
  - Also its repro used the V1 `npm`/`options` shape, whereas this report uses the documented native `package: "aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"` + `settings.baseURL` shape.

- The provider uses `aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` — the exact package the built-in `opencode` provider uses, so the package resolves.
- The config is confirmed loaded by the service: `opencode2 api get /api/config` returns the document with `providers.local-llama-cpp` and the model. No normalization warnings are emitted for the native V2 config.
- Reproduced with:
  - Minimal native V2 config (above) as a symlink AND as a real file — identical failure, so the dotfiles symlink is not the cause.
  - V1 `provider`/`npm`/`options` syntax (converted per the migration guide) — same failure.
- The OpenAI-compatible endpoint itself works: `curl localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions` returns a valid completion.

issues.title: Desktop `plugin.list()` with no location builds a permanent `$HOME` location in the shared service, booting every global plugin there
issues.body:
**Version:** OpenCode 2.2.0 (`1097e26`), desktop app, macOS
**Introduced with:** the experimental desktop plugins work (#55246, #59469, #59489)

## Summary

The desktop's shared background server runs with `$HOME` as its cwd. The desktop main process calls `client.plugin.list()` without a location, so the server resolves the request to `process.cwd()` and builds a full location for `$HOME`. Locations never expire, so every global plugin is set up for the home directory and stays live for the life of the process. A plugin that does real work at setup (indexing, watching) then works over the whole home directory.

In my case this caused a restart loop. A global indexing plugin blocked the event loop, three 2-second `/api/info` probes timed out, and the client sent SIGTERM and spawned a replacement. The replacement emitted `server.connected`, which made the desktop call `plugin.list()` again and rebuild the `$HOME` location. Restarting can never clear it.

## The chain (v2.2.0)

1. **The service runs from `$HOME`.** [`packages/cli/src/server-process.ts#L62-L66`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1097e26/packages/cli/src/server-process.ts#L62-L66): in `service` mode, `process.chdir(global.home)`.
2. **A request with no location falls back to cwd.** [`packages/server/src/location.ts#L75`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1097e26/packages/server/src/location.ts#L75): if there's no `location[directory]` query and no `x-opencode-directory` header, the server uses `process.cwd()`.
3. **The desktop sends exactly that request.** [`packages/desktop/src/main/plugin/host.ts#L440`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1097e26/packages/desktop/src/main/plugin/host.ts#L440): `listPlugins()` calls `client.plugin.list()` without a location. It is re-run on every `server.connected` and `plugin.updated` event ([L429](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1097e26/packages/desktop/src/main/plugin/host.ts#L429)).
4. **The location is never evicted.** [`packages/core/src/location-services.ts#L56`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1097e26/packages/core/src/location-services.ts#L56): `idleTimeToLive: Duration.infinity`. Building it runs the setup of every plugin in global config.
5. **The restart re-triggers it.** [`packages/client/src/service-timing.ts#L18`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1097e26/packages/client/src/service-timing.ts#L18) sets `requestTimeout: 2_000`. After repeated probe timeouts, [`packages/client/src/promise/service.ts#L156`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1097e26/packages/client/src/promise/service.ts#L156) sends SIGTERM and spawns a new server, which emits `server.connected` and goes back to step 3.

`config.get()` in [`packages/app/src/settings/general/controllers.ts#L37`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1097e26/packages/app/src/settings/general/controllers.ts#L37) is another request without a location. It only fires when Settings › General is opened.

## Evidence

- The plugin's index for `/Users/<me>` reached **658 MB / 11,446 files** (`~/Library`, `~/go/pkg/mod`, `~/.nvm`, `~/.npm`, …), written continuously from the day I upgraded. I never opened `$HOME` as a project. Only repos were open.
- Which repo was open made no difference, because the `$HOME` location runs alongside the real one in the same process.
- A/B, 10 minutes per phase, 30-second samples, same machine and project:

  | | Plugin on, unguarded | Plugin off | Plugin on, skips `$HOME` |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Server PIDs seen | 5 (4 restarts) | 1 | 1 |
  | `/api/info` timeouts | 8 | 0 | 0 |
  | Median RSS | 2603 MB (peak 4440) | 729 MB | 598 MB |
  | Median CPU | 68.6 % | 0.5 % | 0.6 % |

- During the guarded run the server still built the `$HOME` location (the log shows requests with `directory=/Users/<me>`), but the plugin skipped it. The `$HOME` index was not recreated, and the plugin kept working in the open repo. So the location is still created upstream, and only a plugin-side workaround makes it harmless.

## Suggested fixes

1. `listPlugins()` in the desktop main process should pass a location, or `plugin.list` should be answerable without booting a location.
2. In service mode, location-scoped routes should reject requests that carry no location, instead of silently resolving them to the service's cwd (`$HOME`).
3. Consider not keeping locations alive forever, or at least not one that was created implicitly.

Related but secondary, since they amplify the problem rather than cause it: three 2-second probes is a tight threshold for a server whose plugins may be busy, and a restart that re-creates the same conditions has no backoff.

*Reported on behalf of the user by an AI agent (OpenCode); symptom confirmed by the user.*

## Description

In the desktop app, `$$` display-math blocks in an assistant reply sometimes stay as raw text, while inline math (`\(...\)`) in the same message renders fine. It happens only for replies watched while streaming, is intermittent (same syntax renders correctly in other sessions), and reloading the session fixes it — so the stored text is correct.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In the desktop app, watch an assistant reply stream that contains `$$\n…\n$$` display blocks plus `\(...\)` inline math.
2. In some sessions the display blocks show as raw text while the inline math renders.
3. Close and reopen the session: the display math renders correctly.

## System Information

- OpenCode version: 2.0.18 (desktop app)
- OS: macOS 26 (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64)
- Terminal: desktop app (Electron)
- Plugins: none

## Notes

Differs from #38030 / #51432 (always-raw): here rendering depends on streaming timing, and a reload fixes it. Suspect the streaming "projection" path falls back to raw text when the async worker parse for a math-containing block is superseded. Can share extracted failing/working transcripts and a Node repro against the bundled markdown worker on request.

issues.body:
### Description

ZCode 3.14.3 and Codex CLI both hit the same Go endpoint (zen/go/v1, deepseek-v4.1-flash) on my machine. Counting per-request cache hits from logs (Sep 25–27):

- Codex: 2 misses / 657 requests (0.30%)
- ZCode (opencode-go-chat channel): 23 / 685 (3.36%)

Miss = cache_read < 5% of input, input > 10k. On the ZCode side a miss is a single request between ~99% hits: cache_read drops to 0/1024/1152 (always multiples of 128) while input is 90k–520k, then recovers on the next request. ZCode sends a stable x-opencode-session (verified: 1225 requests, 22 sessions, no drift), but its body has no cache routing key — only model/messages/max_tokens/reasoning_effort. Codex sends prompt_cache_key (per OpenAI's prompt caching docs).

So it looks like the session header alone isn't enough for sticky cache routing. Does Go use prompt_cache_key when present? If yes, could it be documented next to x-opencode-session in the Go guide? Raw per-request tables available if needed.

N/A

N/A (not the opencode CLI) — ZCode 3.14.3 and Codex CLI v0.157.1

1. Point both clients at zen/go/v1 on the same machine.

issues.title: permissions: parallel Code Mode asks for the same tool orphan the second request
issues.body:
## Summary

When two parallel Code Mode (`execute`) calls in the same assistant turn both invoke the same ask-gated MCP tool, resolving/approving one permission ask orphans the second: it never resolves, even after the permission is fully granted, and the second call hangs until the user interrupts it.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.16
- OS: Linux 7.2.6-1-omarchy-rc3 (x64, Arch-based Omarchy)
- Terminal: ghostty (TERM=xterm-ghostty, COLORTERM=truecolor)
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest (v2.0.16, background service via `opencode serve --service`)
- Active plugins: superpowers (git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git)
- MCP: local stdio server with a tool gated by `{ "action": "hyprland_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }`

## Reproduction

1. Gate an MCP tool with `ask` (see above).
2. Produce an assistant turn with two parallel `execute` calls that both invoke the same tool, e.g. both run `await tools.hyprland.clipboard_copy({ text: "x" })`.
3. Observe: one call completes (after the ask is granted), the other hangs indefinitely.

## Expected Behavior

Either one ask covers both pending calls, or each ask is independently surfaced and resolved. Granting the permission (`allow` rule / saved approval) should release every pending call gated on it.

## Actual Behavior

From session data (all times UTC):

- 18:24:15 — both parallel calls start (`execute` #1 and #2, both calling `hyprland.clipboard_copy`).
- 18:28:53 — an `hyprland_clipboard_copy` allow grant is persisted; call #1 completes at that moment (blocked 278 s on the ask).
- Call #2 never resolves despite the permission now being granted; it stays pending 1462 s until 18:48:39, when the user's next message aborts it with `{"type":"aborted","message":"Tool execution interrupted"}`.

So the second (duplicate) ask appears to be superseded/orphaned by the first and is not re-evaluated when the permission state changes.

## Additional Context

Possibly related to the same permission-ask pipeline as the Code Mode asks that never surface in the TUI (filed separately). Workaround: never issue parallel `execute` calls to the same ask-gated tool; issue them sequentially, or pre-`allow` the tool in config. Full investigation report with timeline available on request.

issues.title: permissions: asks from MCP tools inside Code Mode never surface in the TUI, execute hangs until user interrupt
issues.body:
## Summary

Permission asks raised by MCP tools invoked from inside Code Mode (`execute`) never render in the TUI. The `execute` call blocks indefinitely on the invisible ask, and the next user message (or Esc) aborts it with `{"type":"aborted","message":"Tool execution interrupted"}`. This silently deadlocks agent↔user workflows. Direct (non-Code-Mode) tool calls show their permission dialogs normally.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.16
- OS: Linux 7.2.6-1-omarchy-rc3 (x64, Arch-based Omarchy)
- Terminal: ghostty (TERM=xterm-ghostty, COLORTERM=truecolor)
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest (v2.0.16, background service via `opencode serve --service`)
- Active plugins: superpowers (git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git)
- MCP: two local stdio servers (a custom FastMCP Python server, desktop-commander)

## Reproduction

1. Configure an MCP tool to require an ask, e.g. in `opencode.json`:
   `{ "permissions": [ { "action": "hyprland_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" } ] }`
2. In a session, call that tool from Code Mode:
   `await tools.hyprland.clipboard_copy({ text: "hello" })`
3. No permission dialog appears anywhere in the TUI.
4. The `execute` call hangs indefinitely (observed 5–44 minutes).
5. Type any new message (or press Esc) → the tool result becomes:
   `{"error":{"type":"aborted","message":"Tool execution interrupted"}}`

## Expected Behavior

The permission ask renders in the TUI like asks for direct tool calls, so the user can approve/deny and the Code Mode call proceeds.

## Actual Behavior

- No ask is ever displayed; the model believes the tool call is running while the user sees nothing. Both sides wait on each other.
- A pending ask eventually exceeds the MCP request timeout in some cases: on v1.18.32→v2 era data we also captured `MCP error -32001: Request timed out` (~60 s) for an unanswered ask.
- Additional quirks observed in the same timeline (may be the same root cause):
  - Editing `opencode.json` permissions mid-session fires `config.updated` (seen in the log), but the running session still hangs the newly-allowed tool — permission rules are only effective for sessions started after the change.
  - An "Allow always" answer is stored project-scoped (row in the `permission` table with the project id). A long-running session that belongs to the legacy `global` project never receives that grant, so its Code Mode calls keep asking (and hanging) forever.

## Additional Context

Evidence that the hang is the invisible ask (not the MCP server):

- A config-`allow`ed tool called via Code Mode returns in 31 ms (`tools.hyprland.list_windows()`), so Code Mode → MCP plumbing and permission allow-rules work.
- A hung call completed at 18:28:53 — the exact timestamp an `hyprland_clipboard_copy` allow row was written to the `permission` table — i.e. it had been blocked on the ask for 278 s and was released by the grant.
- Reproduced twice in one session after a config change was confirmed applied (`config.updated` in the server log 4 s before the second hang).
- The server log shows `message=asking` entries for direct tool-call asks (which users answer normally), but no asking entries for the Code Mode hangs.

Full investigation report with timeline available on request.
