issues.title: [FEATURE]: Add android to v2 npm package supported OS for Termux compatibility
issues.body:
## Description

OpenCode v2 beta (`@opencode-ai/cli@beta`) works on Termux/Android aarch64 using the existing musl loader, but npm rejects the install because `android` is not in the package supported OS list.

> [!NOTE]
> This issue does not exist in v1 — v1 requires a proxy/libresolvefix workaround because of Bun io_uring. v2 replaces Bun with Node.js, eliminating that problem entirely.

## Test results

- **Device**: Pixel 10 (Android 17, Termux 0.119, aarch64)
- **Package**: `@opencode-ai/cli-linux-arm64-musl@0.0.0-beta-19192`

| Command | Result |
|---------|--------|
| `opencode2 --version` | `opencode2 v0.0.0-beta-19192` ✅ |
| `opencode2 --help` | Works ✅ |

<details>
<summary>Binary dependencies (click to expand)</summary>

The v2 musl binary only depends on:
- `libstdc++.so.6`
- `libc.musl-aarch64.so.1`

No Bun, no JSC, no WebKit — significantly simpler than v1.

</details>

## Current behavior

```
npm error code EBADPLATFORM
npm error notsup Unsupported platform for @opencode-ai/cli: wanted {"os":"darwin,linux,win32"} (current: {"os":"android"})
```

> [!TIP]
> **Workaround**:
> ```sh
> npm install -g @opencode-ai/cli@beta --force
> curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DEAD1nsane/opencode-termux-musl/master/scripts/fix-opencode2-wrapper.sh | sh
> ```
>
> The `--force` flag bypasses the OS check. The fix script is required because the npm postinstall generates a broken wrapper that execs itself instead of `opencode2.exe`, causing infinite recursion.

<details>
<summary>Full install output (click to expand)</summary>

```
$ npm install -g @opencode-ai/cli@beta
npm error code EBADPLATFORM
npm error notsup Unsupported platform for @opencode-ai/cli@0.0.0-beta-19192: wanted {"os":"darwin,linux,win32","cpu":"arm64,x64"} (current: {"os":"android","cpu":"arm64"})
npm error notsup Valid os:   darwin,linux,win32
npm error notsup Actual os:  android
```

</details>

## Request

Add `android` to the supported OS list in the v2 npm package, plus android prebuilds for the two native dependencies that still lack them (details below).

> [!WARNING]
> Without this change, Termux users must use `--force` to install, which bypasses all platform safety checks. The generated wrapper also has a recursive self-call bug that requires a separate fix script. Both are not discoverable and give a poor first impression.

<details>
<summary>Why this should be straightforward (click to expand)</summary>

1. The v2 binary is already compiled as `linux-arm64-musl` — it runs on Android without modification
2. The `postinstall.mjs` already handles platform detection via `os.platform()` which returns `"android"` on Termux
3. Adding `"android"` to the `os` field in `package.json` is a one-line change
4. No code changes needed for the CLI binary itself — it works as-is

</details>

> [!NOTE]
> The `os` field fix is necessary but not sufficient: without android prebuilds for the native dependencies, install succeeds and TUI/pty break at runtime. Blocker list first raised by @Hope2333 [in this comment](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/47612#issuecomment-5770432864); registry status re-checked 2026-09-24:
> - `@parcel/watcher@2.6.0` — **already ships** `@parcel/watcher-android-arm64`. Resolved.
> - `@opentui/core@0.5.12` — 8 platform targets, **zero android**. Needs an NDK CI build.
> - `@opencode-ai/pty@0.1.13` — darwin + linux gnu/musl only, no android (`linux-arm64-musl` won't `dlopen` on Bionic). Needs an android target.
>
> Actual remaining work: the `os` field + those two prebuilds.

<details>
<summary>Wrapper bug details (click to expand)</summary>

The npm postinstall generates a shell wrapper at `$PREFIX/bin/opencode2` that contains:

```sh
exec "$PREFIX/lib/node_modules/@opencode-ai/cli/bin/opencode2" "$@"
```

This execs the wrapper script itself (infinite recursion), not the actual binary (`opencode2.exe`). Additionally, the wrapper:
- Unnecessarily starts the Python HTTP proxy (v2 is Node.js-based, doesn't need it)
- Sets `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` which v2 doesn't need

The fix script (`fix-opencode2-wrapper.sh`) patches the ELF interpreter (binary expects `/lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1` but Termux installs at `$PREFIX/lib/`) and creates a correct wrapper.

If this issue is resolved (adding `android` to supported OS), the postinstall.mjs should also be updated to generate a correct wrapper on Android.

</details>

## Related

- #11689 — v1 feature request for Android binary (closed)
- #12515 — v1 postinstall fails with missing `opencode-android-arm64` (closed)
- [guysoft/opencode-termux](https://github.com/guysoft/opencode-termux) — community v1 cross-compile project
- [DEAD1nsane/opencode-termux-musl](https://github.com/DEAD1nsane/opencode-termux-musl) — musl loader approach for v1 + v2 wrapper fix

issues.body:
## Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

## Describe the enhancement you want to request

Plugins have no way to prevent the agent loop from stopping. When the loop is about to break, there is no hook that fires — so a plugin cannot inspect session state and inject a follow-up message to keep the agent working.

**Why `session.idle` is not sufficient:**

`session.idle` fires after the loop has already broken. A plugin receiving it can call `client.session.chat` to re-prompt, but this has two problems:

1. In `opencode run` mode, process teardown races against the re-prompt (#15267). The continuation turn can arrive after disposal has begun.
2. The injected message appears as a visible user message in the conversation. For use cases like workflow phase gates — where the intent is a silent "you're not done yet, keep working" — this is the wrong UX.

A hook that fires before the `break` avoids both problems. The re-entry happens inside the existing loop iteration with no new HTTP call, no disposal race, and the injected message uses the same internal path as a normal user turn.

**Proposed solution:** add a `session.stopping` hook to the plugin `Hooks` interface. A plugin sets `output.stop = false` and provides `output.message` to inject a user message and continue the loop. If no plugin modifies the output, behaviour is unchanged.

**Known limitation:** if a plugin unconditionally returns `stop=false`, the loop will run forever. Plugins are responsible for their own termination condition (e.g. a marker file, a state flag, a counter). This is consistent with how other re-entry patterns work in the plugin API.

**Example use case:** a workflow plugin that gates on phase completion. If the agent decides it is done but the workflow state machine says an active phase is incomplete, the plugin injects a silent continuation message. This is the same mechanism Claude Code's Stop hooks use (#12472) — if a Stop hook exits with code 2, its stderr is injected as a prompt and the agent resumes.

issues.title: tui: delayed OSC 10/11 replies leak into prompt as ":ffff/ffff/ffff"
issues.body:
## Summary

On opencode 2.1.0, starting the TUI over SSH can leave the tail of the terminal's OSC 11 color reply in the prompt as `:ffff/ffff/ffff`. The TUI sends OSC 10/11 color probes at startup; when the reply is fragmented (here: `ESC ]11;rgb` arrives first, the rest arrives about 2s later), the incomplete prefix is discarded and the late tail is treated as typed input. It is cosmetic, but it pollutes the first input and can be submitted accidentally.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.1.0
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, Linux 6.8.0-147-generic x86_64
- Terminal: Windows Terminal (PowerShell 7) over SSH; remote `TERM=xterm-256color`, `TERM_PROGRAM`/`COLORTERM`/`VTE_VERSION` unset
- Shell: remote `/bin/bash`; local PowerShell 7
- Install/channel: release standalone binary at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`, latest channel
- Active plugins: none found
- Multiplexer: none (`$TMUX` unset)

## Reproduction

Real-world:

1. SSH into a Linux host from a terminal that delivers OSC 10/11 replies in fragments.
2. Run `opencode` 2.1.0.
3. Before typing anything, the prompt contains `:ffff/ffff/ffff` (sometimes the preceding `]10;rgb:...]11;rgb:...` is visible too). It reproduces on every startup.

Deterministic local PTY reproduction:

1. Start `opencode` 2.1.0 under a PTY.
2. Wait until the `ESC ]11;?` query is written.
3. Write `ESC ]10;rgb:2e2e/3434/3434 BEL` and `ESC ]11;rgb` (stop in the middle of the OSC 11 reply).
4. Wait 2 seconds, then write `:ffff/ffff/ffff BEL`.
5. The rendered prompt contains exactly `:ffff/ffff/ffff`.

Control results with the same harness:

- Whole reply in one write: no leak.
- Split at `ESC ]11;rgb` with a 50 ms gap: no leak.
- Split at `ESC ]11;rgb` with a 2 s gap: leaks the exact string.

This points to the escape-sequence timeout in the stdin parser discarding the incomplete OSC prefix, after which the late tail is parsed as ordinary text.

## Expected Behavior

Terminal query replies, including fragmented or delayed ones, should be consumed as terminal responses and must never appear in the prompt. Late bytes belonging to an already-abandoned reply should be drained/discarded.

## Actual Behavior

The tail of the reply is rendered into the prompt. It is stable on every startup on the affected SSH terminal. It is not persisted in the session database, so it appears to be a startup input-parser race.

## Additional Context

- PTY capture of 2.1.0 startup shows unconditional `ESC ]10;?`, `ESC ]11;?`, palette and capability queries.
- No environment/config switch tested stops the OSC 10/11 probes: `COLORFGBG`, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb`, pinning the theme, and `OTUI_USE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=false` all still send them.
- Potential workaround: run opencode under tmux so the outer terminal's fragmented reply does not reach the TUI directly. `Ctrl+U` clears the leaked line.
- Related reports (same family, some auto-closed): #40035 (tmux startup replies printed at the prompt), #16547, #54500, #55641.

<details>
<summary>Minimal PTY reproduction script</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os, pty, select, signal, struct, time, fcntl, termios

pid, fd = pty.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.execvpe("opencode", ["opencode"], os.environ)

fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 40, 120, 0, 0))
os.set_blocking(fd, False)

out = bytearray()
sent_prefix = False
sent_tail = False
start = time.time()

while time.time() < start + 6:
    r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.05)
    if r:
        try:
            out += os.read(fd, 65536)
        except OSError:
            break

    if not sent_prefix and b"]11;?" in out:
        sent_prefix = True
        # First fragment: complete OSC 10 reply, then only the prefix of OSC 11
        os.write(fd, b"\x1b]10;rgb:2e2e/3434/3434\x07\x1b]11;rgb")
        deadline = time.time() + 2.0

    if sent_prefix and not sent_tail and time.time() >= deadline:
        sent_tail = True
        # Late tail of the OSC 11 reply; this is what leaks into the prompt
        os.write(fd, b":ffff/ffff/ffff\x07")

time.sleep(1)
os.kill(pid, signal.SIGTERM)
```

The rendered output then contains the literal string `:ffff/ffff/ffff`.

</details>

issues.title: desktop: plugin-provided server stuck loading after restart (event stream retries http://127.0.0.1:0)
issues.body:
### Description


A GUI plugin contributes servers with `ctx.add(Server, …)`. The first time, they work. After restarting Desktop (or opening a new window), selecting one of them shows the session list loading forever.

The renderer log repeats `[global-sdk] event stream disconnected` every second with `error: "Transport: Failed to fetch"`. In devtools the request is `GET http://127.0.0.1:0/api/event` → `net::ERR_UNSAFE_PORT`, while the logged transport URL is the real one.

Cause, as far as I can tell: `runtime/plugin/servers.tsx` restores the plugin's last inventory with the `offline` endpoint (`http://127.0.0.1:0`), and a server SDK context is created for it before the plugin reports. `client.tsx` then moves the transport to the real endpoint (the `transport.update` effect for plugin servers), but `createClientConnection` keeps the API it was created with and only replaces it through `reconnect`, which is read once at creation (`server.reconnect` is undefined for the restored placeholder). So the stream never leaves port 0.

### OpenCode version

 2.2.0 (Desktop, macOS); the code is unchanged on `dev`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. A GUI plugin whose `Server` source reports an entry with `http: { url, password }` and no `reconnect` (loaded from the server, so it arrives after the window's first render).
2. Open Desktop, pick that server: sessions load.
3. Quit and reopen Desktop (or Cmd+R), pick it again: the list never loads; the event stream hits `127.0.0.1:0`.

Server-side requests (`/api/session`) answer fine throughout.

### Operating System

 macOS 27 (arm64)

issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

## The idea

First of all... this feature is completely optional.

Some people love desktop companions.
Some people will disable it in 2 seconds.

Both are happy. 😄

I'd love to have a desktop pet that reacts to what OpenCode is doing, similar to an AI companion, but fully customizable and built for OpenCode.

---

# Settings

A new section:

Settings
→ Pets

Options:

- Enable Pets
- Active Pet
- Create Pet
- Import Pet
- Manage Pets

---

# Built-in Pets

Ship OpenCode with a few pets.

Example:

- Fox
- Cat
- Robot
- Ghost
- Bird

Users can switch between them anytime.

---

# Create Pet (AI)

For users who already have an image generation model configured.

Flow:

1. Enter pet name.
2. Upload 2–5 reference images.
3. (Optional) Describe personality/style.
4. Click Generate.
5. Preview.
6. Save.

Example:

Name:
CyberFox

Reference Images:
📷 📷 📷

Prompt:
Cute cyber fox wearing an orange hoodie.
Pixel-art style.

The generator creates a complete sprite pack automatically.

---

# Import Pet

Not everyone has image generation.

Some people use OpenCode Zen or other free text-only models.

For those users:

Click "Import Pet"

Import:

CyberFox.zip

Inside:

manifest.json

idle.png
thinking.png
coding.png
searching.png
terminal.png
testing.png
success.png
failure.png
sleeping.png
celebrating.png

OpenCode validates everything before importing.

---

# Generate Externally

This is probably my favorite part.

If the user doesn't have an image model...

OpenCode can export:

- pet_prompt.md
- manifest.json
- README.md

The prompt is the exact optimized prompt used internally.

The user can take it to:

- ChatGPT
- Gemini
- Claude
- Flux
- ComfyUI
- Midjourney
- or any favorite image model

Generate the sprites.

Zip them.

Import.

Done.

This means nobody is forced to pay for image generation.

---

# Reference Images

Reference images should always be the primary source.

The AI should preserve:

- face
- body
- colors
- outfit
- accessories
- proportions

Only expressions and poses should change.

Every sprite should clearly be the same character.

---

# Pet Reactions

The pet reacts to OpenCode events.

Examples:

😴 Idle

🤔 Thinking

⌨️ Coding

🔍 Searching

🧪 Testing

🎉 Success

😖 Error

💤 Sleeping

No AI logic.

Just event-driven animations.

---

# Interaction

Hover

Shows:

- current model
- current task
- current tool
- elapsed time
- tokens used

Single click

Shows current task.

Double click

Opens the exact session this pet belongs to.

Right click

- Open Session
- Change Pet
- Pause Animation
- Hide
- Close Pet

Closing OpenCode also closes the pet.

---

# Slash Command

/pet fox

/pet cyberfox

/pet robot

Instantly switches the active pet.

---

# Why I think this would be cool

- Completely optional.
- Doesn't affect CLI users.
- Doesn't affect users who don't like desktop pets.
- Highly customizable.
- Community can share pet packs.
- Works with any image model.
- Works without image models.
- Gives OpenCode a bit more personality while still being useful.

---

Not gonna lie...

Watching a tiny fox panic while my agent is debugging my terrible code would make waiting for builds a lot more entertaining. 😄

issues.title: providers: env-authenticated google/groq/openrouter models never resolve — "Model unavailable"
issues.body:
## Summary

On v2.0.18 every non-Zen provider (`google`, `groq`, `openrouter`) is absent from `opencode models` and from `GET /api/model`, and requesting one fails with `Model unavailable: <provider>/<model>` even though the API key is present in the environment, `opencode auth list` reports the provider as connected, and the cached models.dev catalog contains the model with full metadata. Only `opencode/*` models resolve.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.18 (npm `@opencode/cli@2.0.18`, running as the managed background service)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro, build 26200 (10.0.26200), x64
- Terminal: Git Bash on Windows (`TERM=xterm-256color`; no `TERM_PROGRAM` or `COLORTERM`)
- Shell: `cmd.exe` (`%COMSPEC%`); config sets `"shell": "bash"`
- Install/channel: `latest` (npm global at `D:\opencode\npm-global`), running as the managed background service
- Active plugins: `opencode-openai-codex-auth`, configured in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (registry latest 4.4.0). It fails to load on every attempt with `PluginModule.LoadError: Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function. (cause: SchemaError(Expected object at ["default"]))` — 98 occurrences in the log. No local `.opencode/plugin/` or `.opencode/plugins/` files are involved in the failures below.

## Reproduction

1. Set `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `GROQ_API_KEY` in the environment and sign in to OpenCode.
2. Confirm both providers are considered connected:
   ```
   opencode auth list
   # Google             Google                      stored
   # Google             GEMINI_API_KEY              environment
   # Groq               GROQ_API_KEY                environment
   ```
3. List models and observe that only `opencode/*` appears — 49 models, zero from any other provider:
   ```
   opencode models | sed 's|/.*||' | sort | uniq -c
   #     49 opencode
   ```
4. The same 49-only result comes from the running service's own catalog endpoint (`GET /api/model`, HTTP 200): every entry is an `opencode/*` id such as `big-pickle`, `space-bunny-free`, `nemotron-3-ultra-free`. No `google/*`, `groq/*`, or `openrouter/*` entry exists in the response.
5. Request a non-Zen model explicitly — it fails before any network call:
   ```
   opencode run -m google/gemini-3-flash "Reply with exactly: OK"
   # Error: Model unavailable: google/gemini-3-flash
   opencode run -m groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b "Reply with exactly: OK"
   # Error: Model unavailable: groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b
   ```
6. Control case in the same shell, same invocation — a Zen model succeeds:
   ```
   opencode run -m opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free "Reply with exactly: OK"
   # > build · nemotron-3-ultra-free
   # OK
   ```
7. It is not the user config. Reproduce with a minimal config and a private server:
   ```
   echo '{ "model": "opencode/space-bunny-free" }' > repro.jsonc
   OPENCODE_CONFIG=./repro.jsonc opencode run --standalone -m google/gemini-2.5-flash "..."
   # Error: Model unavailable: google/gemini-2.5-flash
   OPENCODE_CONFIG=./repro.jsonc opencode run --standalone -m opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free "..."
   # OK
   ```

## Expected Behavior

`opencode models` and `GET /api/model` should list the `google`, `groq`, and `openrouter` models that the catalog already knows about and for which a key is available, and `opencode run -m google/gemini-3-flash` should reach the provider instead of failing at model resolution.

## Actual Behavior

Non-Zen providers never enter the resolved model set. `opencode models` and `GET /api/model` return `opencode/*` only. Any non-Zen model fails with `ModelUnavailableError: Model unavailable: <provider>/<model>`, and the log shows the same for models that are demonstrably present in the cached catalog.

The catalog is not the problem. The cached `models-dev:catalog` row in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` is current and complete:

```
updatedAt : 2026-09-27T23:28:39.506Z
digest    : 64c46645616953a380a1b26671dc82bbfced17d696438f9922de5ba982398359
providers : 223
google       -> models:  39 | env: GOOGLE_API_KEY,GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY,GEMINI_API_KEY
groq         -> models:  16 | env: GROQ_API_KEY
openrouter   -> models: 384 | env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
opencode     -> models: 112 | env: OPENCODE_API_KEY
```

`google/gemini-2.5-flash` and `groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b` both resolve to populated entries, and the env var each provider declares is set. So resolution drops a provider that is catalogued and authenticated, while `opencode` — the one provider with a stored credential rather than an env var — survives.

The failure is consistent and silent: nothing warns that a connected provider was skipped. It surfaced only because the configured default model was `google/gemini-3.5-flash`, so every session died at the title step.

## Additional Context

Log evidence (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`), 36 `ModelUnavailableError` entries across several service runs (`run=f4dc6fd9`, `6a89fef3`, `44d28f78`, `115a2717`, `0395dce0`), so it is not a single unlucky start:

```
17  Model unavailable: google/gemini-3.5-flash
 9  Model unavailable: groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b
 2  Model unavailable: openrouter/google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp
 2  Model unavailable: google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite
 2  Model unavailable: google/gemini-3-flash
 1  Model unavailable: google/gemini-flash-latest
 1  Model unavailable: vercel/meta/llama-3.3-70b
```

- Affected providers are exactly those authenticated from the environment; the `opencode` provider, authenticated from a stored credential, works. Worth checking whether env-sourced credentials are wired into catalog resolution differently from stored ones.
- Timing does not match the known partial-catalog window in #36117 / #51703: the catalog here is fully populated on disk and the failure persists across many service runs and restarts over hours, rather than clearing after warm-up.
- The two symptoms may share one cause, which is why the plugin error is included here instead of being split into a separate report. `opencode-openai-codex-auth` never loads (`PluginModule.LoadError`, 98 log occurrences). If a plugin that fails to load aborts the remaining catalog/provider registration, that would explain both at once.
- Workaround in place: default and title models are now `opencode/space-bunny-free` and `opencode/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free`, so the session is usable. Non-Zen providers remain unusable.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: honor an existing ~/Projects folder (or a configured path) instead of ~/Documents/Default Project
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

The desktop app creates its managed "Default Project" at `~/Documents/Default Project` during first-launch onboarding, with the path hardcoded as `join(app.getPath("documents"), "Default Project")`. There is no config field, CLI flag, or env var to change it.

Why this is a problem:
- `~/Documents` is the user's space; apps shouldn't scaffold into it without asking.
- macOS TCC protects Documents/Desktop/Downloads. The app bundle declares no `NSDocumentsFolderUsageDescription`, so access can be silently denied with EPERM and no prompt (see #56479).
- Most developers already keep code in a dedicated folder (`~/Projects`, `~/Code`, `~/Developer`, `~/src`) and get a duplicate, empty "Default Project" in Documents they never asked for.

Proposal (any of these, in order of preference):
1. If unset, detect an existing `~/Projects` (or `~/Code` / `~/Developer` / `~/src`) and use it — or offer it — as the default project, instead of creating `~/Documents/Default Project`.
2. Add a configurable directory for the managed default project (e.g. `project.directory` in `opencode.json`, or let `session.new_location` accept an absolute path as proposed in #56932) so the desktop app reads it.
3. Don't create anything under `~/Documents` by default; fall back to the app data dir and let the user pick once during onboarding.

Benefits: no surprise folders in Documents, no macOS TCC failures, and new users land where their code already is.

Related: #46152 (different: proposes moving under Documents/OpenCode), #56932 (configurable default dir for new sessions), #56479 (macOS Documents access denial), #57777 (managed default project not restored).

prs.title: fix(core): keep permission reasons and feedback in MCP tool failures
prs.body:
### Problem

When a permission rule denies an MCP tool call, or the user rejects the call and leaves feedback, the model only gets `Unable to execute <server>_<tool>`. The MCP tool wrapper turned every non-`ToolFailure` error into that generic message and dropped the original error, so the deny reason and the user's feedback never reached the model. This happened for direct MCP calls and for MCP calls made from Code Mode.

### Change

The wrapper now turns `Permission.BlockedError` into a failure with the rule's message and `Permission.CorrectedError` into a failure with the user's feedback, keeping the original as `error`. Any other error keeps the generic message but now carries the original too, like the other leaves do. Plain declines are untouched and still end the step.

Failure text, from the tests in `packages/core/test/mcp.test.ts`:

```diff
 deny rule with reason "Search is disabled in this workspace"
-  Code Mode: Unable to execute demo_search
+  Code Mode: Search is disabled in this workspace
-  direct:    { type: "tool.execution", message: "Unable to execute direct_lookup" }
+  direct:    { type: "permission.rejected", message: "Search is disabled in this workspace" }

 rejected with feedback "Search the docs folder instead"
-  Code Mode: Unable to execute demo_search
+  Code Mode: Search the docs folder instead
-  direct:    { type: "tool.execution", message: "Unable to execute direct_lookup" }
+  direct:    { type: "permission.rejected", message: "Search the docs folder instead" }
```

I skipped the Visual section since this only changes the text the model reads in a tool result.

### Verification

- `bun run script/test.ts test/mcp.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 75 pass, 0 fail. With the source change reverted, both permission tests fail.
- `bun run script/test.ts test/mcp-attach.test.ts test/mcp-instructions.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 18 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/core`: no errors.
- `bun run check` from the repo root: 35 of 35 tasks pass.

prs.title: fix(tui): default animations off inside herdr panes
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related to #57462 (animated tabs cause high CPU/GPU use) and #57676 (lag with the session sidebar visible). Not claiming to close either — this is the multiplexer-specific slice of that work.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

prs.title: fix(core): name image jobs in their notices and warn about overlapping writes
prs.body:
When an agent sent a second image request before the first finished, it couldn't tell the results apart. Every notice for the same file read the same, and two jobs writing the same path raced. I saw this in a live test across xAI, Google and Zen: agents got three identical "Image request finished. Saved image: …/cap.jpg" notices and guessed which edit they were looking at.

Shell and subagent notices already carry an ID (`<shell id=…>`, `<subagent sessionID=…>`). Image notices now do too:

```diff
-Image request finished. Saved image: /proj/cap.jpg (xai/grok-imagine-image-2.0).
+<image id="image_01k…" state="completed" prompt="make the cap blue">
+Image request finished. Saved image: /proj/cap.jpg (xai/grok-imagine-image-2.0).
+Use the read tool on this path to view the image.
+</image>
```

- **Job ID:** the start result says `Image job <id> started…` and the output has `id`, so the agent can match the notice to the call. Restart recovery notices use the same wrapper.
- **Overlap warning:** when another image job is still writing the same file, the start result says `Image job <id> is still writing <path>; whichever finishes last overwrites the file.` That also tells the agent the previous edit isn't ready yet.

prs.title: fix(codemode): fail a program that stalls instead of holding the turn
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54340

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Code Mode has no timers, so a promise settles only through a tool or extension call, or through the program's own code. A program like `await new Promise(r => r)` therefore waits forever, and because `execute` has no time limit, the session holds its turn until inactivity eviction interrupts it an hour later.

The interpreter now counts its own steps and the host calls in flight, including their hooks. A new optional `stallMs` limit fails the program with a `Stalled` diagnostic once a whole window passes with no step taken and no call running. In that state nothing can ever settle the promise, so failing is always right. Slow tool calls and busy loops never trip it. Without `stallMs`, behavior is unchanged.

The `execute` tool sets `stallMs` to 30 s and tells the model not to use `execute` to wait or poll. I chose this over a wall-clock timeout because a timeout would also cut off legitimate long tool calls.

The hot-path cost is one integer increment per statement or expression. I measured no difference on a 400k-iteration loop.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests in `packages/codemode/test/codemode.test.ts` cover the never-settling forms, logs and calls kept before the stall, slow calls and hooks, busy loops, un-awaited promises at return, and how the stall interacts with `timeoutMs`. A new `TestClock` test in `packages/core/test/tool-execute.test.ts` fails without the fix.
- Ran the exact hanging program through a dev server: it returned `Execution stalled…` after 30 s.
- `bun run lint` passes, typecheck passes for 36/36 packages on `dev`, and codemode tests are 1408 pass.

prs.title: fix(codemode): visit inherited enumerable keys in for...in
prs.body:
### Problem

`for...in` in Code Mode only visited an object's own enumerable keys. JavaScript also visits enumerable keys inherited through the prototype chain.

```js
const p = { inh: 1 }; const o = Object.create(p); o.own = 2
const out = []; for (const k in o) out.push(k); return out
```

JavaScript returns `["own","inh"]`. Code Mode returned `["own"]`.

### Change

`for...in` now walks the chain in JavaScript's order:

```
chain = [source, ...prototypes]   // a string's prototype is String.prototype, not Array.prototype
for each level in chain:
  visit level's own enumerable string keys (existing own-key order)
  unless a nearer level has that key at all, enumerable or not
```

Null/undefined, tool references, and whatever `enumerableSource` already rejects behave as before. Built-in methods are non-enumerable, so arrays and strings still only visit their indexes, but a program-added enumerable property such as `Array.prototype.extra = 1` now shows up, like in JavaScript. Skipping keys deleted during the loop is still not done; I left that as an unchecked item in `interpreter-support.md`.

### Verification

From `packages/codemode`:

- `bun test`: 14798 pass, 1678 skip, 0 fail. New cases in `test/enumeration.test.ts` cover inherited keys after own keys, a multi-level chain, integer-like key order per level, shadowing by a non-enumerable nearer property, `Object.create(null)`, arrays and strings unchanged, and program-added enumerable keys on `Array.prototype`, `String.prototype` and `Number.prototype`. I checked each expected output against Node. One existing parity test asserted the old own-only behavior; I updated it to the JavaScript result.
- `bun test test/enumeration.test.ts test/parity.test.ts --rerun-each 10`: all pass.
- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc`: clean.
- test262 (`bun run script/sync-test262.ts ~/development/test262`, then a full run before and after, compared per file): 13330 pass of 15008 both before and after, with no file changing outcome. The remaining skipped `for-in` files fail on property descriptors, user-defined constructors, or deleted keys, so `skipped.txt` is unchanged.

From the repo root: `bun run check` passes.

prs.title: perf(core): write each assistant part as its own row instead of rewriting the message
prs.body:
**Stops rewriting a whole assistant message for every streamed part: each part becomes its own `session_part` row.**
On a 10-step tool-heavy session with screenshots, SQLite WAL writes drop by 84.4% (`47.89 MB -> 7.46 MB`, or 87.8% `47.89 MB -> 5.83 MB` with `experimental.media_blob`) and `fsync`s drop from 22 to 2. This is stacked on [#58915](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58915) and should land one release after it, so a one-release rollback still reads these rows.

❌ **Before**
1. Every durable text, reasoning or tool event re-encodes the assistant message and rewrites its full `session_message` JSON, including every earlier part and tool output.
2. Updating `session_message` also sets `time_created` on every write, dirtying both `time_created` secondary indexes 21 times per step. ❌

✅ **After**
1. The message row keeps an envelope with `content: []`, updated only on step start/end, retry, or failure (without re-setting `time_created` on updates).
2. Each part is a `session_part` row: a new part is one insert, and an update rewrites only that part row.
3. Tool media still moves to blob storage per part (`externalizePart` and offline `SessionBlob.split`), and rewriting content releases media the new parts no longer use.
4. Older messages with inline content are split into part rows only right before one of their parts is written. Envelope updates and reads (like starting a new step after a settled message) leave them as they are, and unchanged history is never migrated.
5. Forks copy a split parent's part rows and record blob refs for each forked message. An unsplit parent is copied inline as is, so old rows are never decoded during a fork. Imports split parts into rows.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Event["Durable step event"] --> Projector
  Projector -->|step start / end| Envelope["session_message (envelope, content: [])"]
  Projector -->|text / reasoning / tool| Part["session_part (message_id, ordinal)"]
  Legacy["Inline data.content"] -->|first part write| Split["delete + insert part rows, clear inline content"]
  style Part fill:#dcf5dc,stroke:#2f855a
  style Split fill:#dcf5dc,stroke:#2f855a
```

```diff
  on a part event:
-   message = decode(row);  edit message.content;  write the whole row (and re-index time_created)
+   split the message first if it still has inline content   (prepareAssistantParts, the only split path)
+   append:  insert one part row at the next ordinal
+   update:  find the latest matching part (type, call ID), apply the change, write that row only
+   replace: delete the message's parts, insert the new ones, release media they no longer name
```

📊 **Numbers**: scripted 10-step, 2-turn session (40 tool calls, 5 PNG screenshots at 380 KB each, 6 spilled 81 KB outputs) and 1-step 20-tool text session (`8 KB` output/tool)

| Measure | Before (`dev`) | After ([#58916](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58916)) | After + `media_blob` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10-step SQLite WAL written | 47.89 MB (11,623 pages) | 7.46 MB (1,811 pages, −84.4%) | 5.83 MB (1,415 pages, −87.8%) |
| Per-step SQLite WAL written | 4,788.7 KB / step | 746.1 KB / step | 583.0 KB / step |
| 10-step `session_message` (+ idx) WAL | 45.67 MB | 832.2 KB (−98.2%) | 309.0 KB (−99.3%) |
| 10-step `session_part` WAL | 0 B | 4.41 MB | 2.27 MB |
| 10-step WAL checkpoints / `fsync`s | 11 ckpt / 22 `fsync`s | 1 ckpt / 2 `fsync`s (−90.9%) | 1 ckpt / 2 `fsync`s (−90.9%) |
| 10-step final `.db` size | 4.25 MB | 3.89 MB | 2.72 MB (−36.1%) |
| 1-step 20-tool text WAL / JSON | 8.82 MB / 9.20 MB | 2.47 MB (−72.0%) / 208 KB (−97.7%) | — |

The new projector, fork blob-ref, conflict-split, and offline `SessionBlob.split` part tests fail without the change (31 pass across `session-projector.test.ts` and `session-stats.test.ts`; 2 pass in `packages/server/test/media.test.ts`).

↩️ **Undo:** revert this PR and keep [#58915](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58915). Writes go back to inline content, and the read side keeps showing parts already written to `session_part`. Rolling back past [#58915](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58915) as well would hide the assistant content of any message written while this was live. That's why the two land a release apart.

👀 **Read:** `projector.ts`. Check `prepareAssistantParts`, the one place a legacy row is split, which deletes stale part rows before inserting so a message never gets duplicate ordinals. Then check that `updateMessage` keeps the row's existing `content` through `json_set`, so envelope updates never move or drop it. Then check the blob ref handling in the three part methods, in `SessionBlob.split` (`blob.ts`), and in fork: forked messages copy empty envelopes, so their refs come from the parts. `message-updater.ts` now talks to the projector through the part methods instead of editing the whole message. The rest is test updates.

<sub>🔍 Found while profiling database writes during long tool-heavy turns · no user reports · measured with a scripted 10-step file-DB harness against SQLite WAL + `dbstat` · depends on [#58915](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58915)</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun run --cwd packages/core typecheck` and `bun run --cwd packages/server typecheck`: clean
- `bun run --cwd packages/core test test/session-projector.test.ts test/session-stats.test.ts`: 31 pass
- `bun test test/media.test.ts` (packages/server): 2 pass
- `bun run script/migration.ts --check` (packages/core): pass

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): normalize wildcard bind address in service registration URL
prs.body:
When hostname is set to 0.0.0.0 (listen on all interfaces), the service registration file recorded http://0.0.0.0:port as the client connection URL. Since 0.0.0.0 is a bind wildcard rather than a routable address, client auto-discovery could fail to connect to the background service.

Normalize 0.0.0.0 to 127.0.0.1 and :: to ::1 in both the registration URL and the incumbent check probe URL, matching the existing behavior in the remote tunnel target construction.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #49796

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When `hostname` is set to `0.0.0.0` in `~/.config/opencode/service.json` (listen on all interfaces), the service registration file at `~/.local/state/opencode/service.json` recorded `http://0.0.0.0:port` as the client connection URL. Since `0.0.0.0` is a bind wildcard, not a routable destination address, the second `opencode` client's auto-discovery fails to connect to the running background service.

`service-registration.ts` used `HttpServer.formatAddress(address)` which passes the bind hostname directly into the URL. The remote tunnel target construction already normalizes `0.0.0.0` → `127.0.0.1`, but the registration path missed this step.

Added `formatClientAddress()` to normalize `0.0.0.0` → `127.0.0.1` and `::` → `::1` for the registration URL, and applied the same normalization in `serviceURL()` used by the `findIncumbent` startup probe.

### How did you verify your code works?

Tested locally: with `hostname: "0.0.0.0"` and `port: 14096` in `~/.config/opencode/service.json`, the registration file now contains `http://127.0.0.1:14096` instead of `http://0.0.0.0:14096`, and a second `opencode` terminal connects to the running service without issues.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #58406

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Adds `searxng` as a built-in web search provider, next to exa/tavily/firecrawl/parallel/tinyfish, so search can run against a self-hosted SearXNG instance with no third-party API key.

The problem: every current provider calls a hosted service. There is no self-hosted option, so a user who wants search to stay on their own network cannot have it.

The one place this differs from the existing providers is the account. SearXNG's account is a server address, not a key, so `{ type: "key" }` cannot express it. It registers an `external` method whose form takes the URL, plus the usual `env` method for `SEARXNG_URL`:

```ts
editor.method.update({
  integrationID: "searxng",
  method: {
    id: "server",
    type: "external",
    label: "Your SearXNG server",
    form: [{ key: "url", type: "string", format: "uri", title: "Server URL", placeholder: "http://localhost:8080", required: true }],
  },
})
```

`execute` reads that URL back from the resolved credential's `metadata.url`, falling back to `SEARXNG_URL`. A bare host like `localhost:8088` gets `http://` prepended so it searches instead of throwing, and results without a `url` are dropped like the other providers do. Everything else follows `tavily.ts`: `Schema` for the response, `HttpClientRequest.get` + `filterStatusOk`, a 25s timeout, `{ url, title, content, time }`, first 8 results.

The instance must publish the JSON format (`search.formats` including `json` in `settings.yml`); otherwise SearXNG answers 403 and the request fails rather than silently returning nothing.

prs.title: feat(core): add the session_part table and read history from it
prs.body:
**Adds the `session_part` table and teaches every history read, and the projector after a rollback, to use it. Messages without part rows are written exactly as before.**
This is the first half of moving assistant message parts out of the `session_message` JSON. It ships one release before the write side ([#58916](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58916)), so rolling back that release still lands on a build that can read the new rows and keep streaming into them.

❌ **Before**
1. An assistant message's text, reasoning and tool parts live inside one `session_message.data.content` JSON array.
2. No build knows about a `session_part` table, so a release that writes parts there can't be rolled back without losing history. ❌
3. Even a read-only build would break a rollback mid-turn: its projector would read an empty inline `content`, append to it inline, and those parts would be hidden because reads prefer `session_part`. ❌

✅ **After**
1. A new `session_part` table holds one row per part, keyed by `(message_id, ordinal)`. Its rows cascade-delete with their message and session.
2. History reads (store, history, compaction text, stats) take a message's parts from `session_part` when it has any. If it has none, they use its inline content as before.
3. When a message already has `session_part` rows (written by [#58916](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58916) before a rollback), the projector loads them, writes changed parts back to their rows, adds new parts at the next ordinal, and keeps the envelope's `content: []`.
4. A fork copies a parent message's `session_part` content inline, so the forked message isn't empty.
5. Messages without part rows are never written to `session_part`, so behaviour is unchanged until the write side lands.

```diff
  read assistant rows:
+   load session_part rows for those messages, 500 IDs per query, in ordinal order
+   message has part rows?  content = those parts
    otherwise:              content = inline data.content (unchanged)
    then restore blob media, then decode
  projector update of an assistant message:
+   message has part rows?  envelope content = [];  update changed rows by position, insert new at max(ordinal)+1, delete extras
    otherwise:              write content inline (unchanged)
  fork:
+   parent rows go through withParts first, so split parts are copied inline
  tool stats:
+   count tool parts from session_part
+   count inline tool parts only for messages with no part rows   (never both)
```

📊 **Numbers**: 10-step tool-heavy session (40 tool calls, 5 PNG screenshots at 380 KB each)

| Measure | Before (`dev`) | After [#58915](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58915) (read only) | After [#58916](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58916) (writes enabled) |
|---|---|---|---|
| New table | 0 | 1 (`session_part`) + 1 index on `(session_id, message_id, ordinal)` | same |
| Extra queries per history read | 0 | 1 per 500 assistant messages (0 when page has none) | 1 per 500 assistant messages |
| SQLite WAL written (10 steps) | 47.89 MB (4.79 MB/step) | 47.89 MB (writes unchanged) | 7.46 MB (5.83 MB with `media_blob`) |
| WAL checkpoints / `fsync`s (10 steps) | 11 / 22 | 11 / 22 | 1 / 2 |

The new dual-read and stats tests fail without `withParts` and the `session_part` union in `stats.ts`. The rollback test (seed part rows for an in-progress message, apply tool and text events, read history) and the split-fork test both fail without the projector change. 304 pass across session-projector, session-store, session-revert, session-runner, session-runner-tool-events and session-step.

↩️ **Undo:** revert this PR. The migration only creates a table, and nothing writes to it until [#58916](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58916). After a revert, the empty table stays in existing databases and older builds ignore it. Don't revert this while [#58916](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58916) is live: the parts it wrote would stop showing up.

👀 **Read:** `updateMessage` and `writeParts` in `projector.ts`: they only touch `session_part` when the message already has rows there, and they match rows by position. Then `withParts` in `history.ts`, which runs before blob hydration so media inside parts still restores. In `stats.ts`, the `NOT EXISTS` guards keep a message from being counted twice. The migration was generated, not written by hand.

### Visual

  <text x="98" y="24" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.65" font-family="monospace" font-size="7">2. plugin</text>

  <text x="202" y="43" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-family="monospace" font-size="8">C1</text>

  <line class="flow" x1="66" y1="36" x2="87" y2="36" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity="0.9" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <polygon points="91,36 86,33 86,39" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9"/>
  <line class="flow" x1="148" y1="36" x2="169" y2="36" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity="0.9" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <polygon points="173,36 168,33 168,39" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9"/>
</svg>
```

### Problem

In `packages/merman`, flowchart subgraph IDs were only resolved as subgraph endpoints on invisible `~~~` links. Visible edges targeting a subgraph (`S1 --> S2 --> S3`, `Start --> S1`, `S1 --> Done`) created standalone phantom box nodes (`[S1]`, `[S2]`, `[S3]`) outside the subgraphs instead. That dropped inter-subgraph rank ordering, collapsed unrelated subgraph roots into rank 0 together, and scrambled internal branch routing inside downstream subgraphs.

```text
Before:                         After:
┌─ 1. seed ──┐  ╭────╮          ┌─ 1. seed ──┐
│ A1   A2    │  │ S1 │          │ A1   A2    │
└────────────┘  ╰─┬──╯          └─────┬──────┘
┌─ 2. plugin ┐    ▼                   ▼
│ B          │  ╭────╮          ┌─ 2. plugin ┐
└────────────┘  │ S2 │          │ B          │
┌─ 3. post ──┐  ╰─┬──╯          └─────┬──────┘
│ crossed    │    ▼                   ▼
└────────────┘  ╭────╮          ┌─ 3. post ──┐
                │ S3 │          │ C1 -> ...  │
                ╰────╯          └────────────┘
```

### Change

I extended flowchart parsing, ranking, frame separation, and routing so visible arrows can start or end on subgraph frames while keeping member node obstacle checks separate from frame endpoints:

```diff
 parseMermaidFlowchartDiagram
   parse nodes, edges, subgraphs
+  resolveSubgraphEndpoints (bare IDs -> subgraph endpoints, forward & backward refs;
+                            keep explicit shapes like API[Gateway] as nodes)

 layoutFlowchartWithDirection
-  expand only orderOnly (~~~) subgraph links in rankNodes
+  expand exit -> entry rank constraints and frame clearance for subgraph edges
   route member node edges and size subgraphBounds
   separateTopLevelItems (enforce connector + label gap on frame-linked items)
+  route subgraph-endpoint edges against settled subgraphBounds (with member routes locked)
+  re-evaluate subgraph labelSide / title clearance so ports and titles do not overwrite
```

### Out of scope

- Nested sibling subgraph overlap when sibling frames inside a parent wrap
- Deduplicating node membership when a bare node is referenced across two subgraphs
- Additional flowchart shapes (`((circle))`, `{{hexagon}}`) and general Mermaid preprocessor gaps

### Verification

- `bun test src/flowchart/flowchart.test.ts --rerun-each 10 --randomize` in `packages/merman` (1,840 pass, 0 fail)
- `bun run --cwd packages/merman test` (508 pass across 23 files, including `layout-audit.test.ts` at 60/80/120 viewports with 0 violations)
- `bun run --cwd packages/merman typecheck` and `bun run --cwd packages/merman typecheck:tsc` (0 errors)
- `bun run check` from repo root (35/35 tasks passed, 0 errors)

prs.title: fix(server): resolve requests without a location to a global scope
prs.body:
Closes #60004. On the shared background service, a request that names no location now goes to a small **global scope** instead of building a full location for `$HOME`. Opening Desktop with only repos open no longer sets up every global plugin over the home folder.

## Cause

The service runs from `$HOME`. A request with no `location[directory]` (or an empty one) fell back to `process.cwd()`, so it built a `$HOME` location: project discovery, a project row, and every global plugin's setup. Desktop main's `plugin.list()`, the app's "available to all projects" reads and its connect-time `location.get` all send such requests, on every reconnect. A global plugin that indexes at setup then indexed the whole home folder.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  req["request with no location"] --> before["before: process.cwd() = $HOME, full project location"]
  req --> after["now: server directory option, else the global scope"]
  after --> serve["opencode serve / stdio: the folder it started in"]
  after --> service["service: global config folder, project 'global'"]
```

## Change

- **Server:** `ServerOptions.directory` is the default location. Without it, requests that name none use the global config folder (`Global.config`, which respects `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`). Server code no longer reads `process.cwd()`. That covers the middleware, form, debug, MCP and PTY lookups, and the `session.create` and `session.import` fallbacks.
- **CLI:** `opencode serve` and `stdio` pass their working folder, so they behave as before. Service mode passes nothing.
- **Core:** a location in the global config folder resolves to project `global`. It writes no project row, runs no VCS discovery and reads no parent-folder `AGENTS.md`. It doesn't mark a project active, and `vcs.initialize` answers `unsupported`.
- **Protocol:** `ServerInfo.paths` gains optional `home` and `config`. The app's home detection and the TUI's fallback folder use `paths.home`, and older servers keep the old behaviour. The client is regenerated.
- **App:** `global` is also the ID of a repo with no commits and no remote. A global-scope session therefore only matches a `global` project that contains its folder.
- **Docs:** the plugin server guide explains the global scope. A plugin that indexes or watches should skip `ctx.location.project.id === "global"`.

## Compatibility

- **Older clients with a newer service:** their requests with no location land in the global scope instead of `$HOME`. The "available to all projects" lists now show only global config, without `$HOME/opencode.json` mixed in.
- **Embedded SDK hosts:** with no `directory` set, they now use the global scope instead of the host process's working folder. Set `directory` to keep the old behaviour.
- **`opencode run --attach` without `--dir`** against a service now runs in the global scope.

## Tests

Each test below fails when its fix is reverted.

- `server/test/fetch.test.ts`: a request with no or an empty location goes to the global config folder with project `global`, `session.create` lands there, `/api/info` reports `paths`, and `directory` overrides the default.
- `core/test/location-layer.test.ts`: the global scope has no VCS, writes no project row, and `vcs.initialize` answers `unsupported`.
- `core/test/instruction-discovery.test.ts`: the global scope reads no parent-folder instructions.
- `app` (`bootstrap`, `helpers`, `records`) and `tui/test/app-lifecycle.test.tsx`: home detection uses `paths.home`, and sessions are matched to project `global` by folder.

Follow-up: a plugin inventory that needs no location, so Desktop main never needs one.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round">
  <rect x="8.5" y="26.5" width="44" height="20" rx="3" opacity=".6"/>
  <line x1="16" y1="36.5" x2="44" y2="36.5" opacity=".6"/>

    <rect x="150.5" y="6.5" width="82" height="30" rx="3" opacity=".5"/>
    <g opacity=".35"><line x1="158" y1="15" x2="224" y2="15"/><line x1="158" y1="21" x2="210" y2="21"/><line x1="158" y1="27" x2="218" y2="27"/></g>
    <path d="M54 36 C100 36 110 21 148 21" stroke-dasharray="4 4" opacity=".5"/>
    <animate attributeName="opacity" values="1;1;.15;.15;1" keyTimes="0;.35;.45;.95;1" dur="4s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
  </g>
  <g opacity="0">
    <rect x="186.5" y="44.5" width="36" height="20" rx="3" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".12"/>
    <line x1="194" y1="54.5" x2="214" y2="54.5" opacity=".7"/>
    <path d="M54 36 C110 36 130 54 184 54" stroke-dasharray="4 4" opacity=".8">

### Issue for this PR

Closes #57738

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds a pin to Home sessions. The session row menu gets Pin / Unpin; pinned sessions move into a **Pinned** group above Today, in the order they were pinned, and are excluded from the dated groups. `session.pin` in the command palette toggles the same state for the open session, so it can also be bound in Settings → Shortcuts.

- `packages/app/src/home/sessions/pins.tsx` owns the store: `Persist.global("home.sessions.pinned")`, a `Record<serverKey, sessionID[]>`, so pins survive restarts and are per server.
- `createHomeSessionsController` merges pinned sessions into the record list before the `HOME_SESSION_LIMIT` slice and sorts them first by pin order, so a pin cannot be pushed out of the 64-row window. A pinned session outside the fetched index is loaded with `session.get`.
- `groupSessions` takes the pinned ID set and emits the Pinned group first.
- Deleting a session drops its pins, including child sessions removed with it. Pinning a subagent session is disabled because Home does not list those.
- `home/sessions/view.tsx` replaces `typeof navigator === "object"` with `"navigator" in globalThis`; `bun run lint:changed` flags the older form once the file is touched.

Limits: pins are local to the app and do not follow the user to another machine. There is no server field for them.

This was opened before design review of #57738 has happened. Happy to hold it, or change the interaction (pin from the tab menu, a server-side `pinned` flag) if that is what you prefer.

prs.title: perf(app): keep each tab's timeline when switching directories
prs.body:
**Switching back to a tab in another folder no longer rebuilds its whole conversation view.**
Each tab's timeline was thrown away whenever the selected folder (a "Location") changed, so returning to a long conversation re-rendered every loaded message. Nothing else on screen changes.

❌ **Before**
1. Open a tab in folder A, then a tab in folder B.
2. ❌ The app clears every kept timeline because the selected folder changed.
3. Going back to the tab in A rebuilds its view from every loaded message.

✅ **After**
1. Each tab's timeline keeps its own copy of the folder, data and Markdown settings it was built with.
2. Selected: the copy follows the live values. Hidden: it keeps its last values and never reads the selected folder's.
3. Going back to a tab shows the kept view as it was.

```diff
  createTimelineCache(session, render)
-   on Location change: clear every cached view
+   per view: own Location, Data and Markdown contexts
+     selected: follow the live providers
+     hidden:   keep the last values, never read the selected Location's
+   per view: own link checks and turn diffs for its own session
```

📊 **Numbers**: warm switch back to a tab with about 3k loaded messages, keydown to first paint, median of warm cycles 2–7, two runs per build (measured on an earlier revision, before the rebase)

| Switch back to a long tab | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Median, paint = idle | 134 ms | 86 ms |

17 browser tests pass; each of the 8 new cases (for example "a detached view's readers stay still when another Location is selected") fails without its fix.

👀 **Read:** `session/timeline/cache.ts` and `shell/routes/session-ui-provider.tsx`, where a hidden view freezes its values. Trade-offs while a tab is hidden: a file path in a message that finishes then isn't styled as a link until the tab is selected, a compaction row first drawn then uses the default style until selected, and a running shell stops updating its output until selected. Up to 16 views can now stay alive across folders; memory with the final code wasn't measured. The rest is routine.

<sub>🔍 Found while profiling tab switching · no user reports · the last commit and the rebase weren't re-measured</sub>

prs.title: fix(core): preserve plugin-supplied model variants
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/59836

### Problem

When a custom model is configured in `opencode.json` without `variants` or `capabilities.reasoning` and a plugin supplies its reasoning tiers in `model.transform` (for example `none`, `low`, `medium`, `xhigh`), `opencode.config.provider`'s late `model.transform` overwrites those variants with the default `["low", "medium", "high"]` list.

### Change

Skip default variant generation on custom models when an earlier `model.transform` already populated `model.variants`, unless `opencode.json` changes the model's effective SDK package.

```diff
 late config model.transform
   overlay explicit opencode.json fields
   if config omits variants and capabilities.reasoning:
-    if custom model or catalog model repackaged:
+    if (custom model with empty variants) or effective package changed:
       model.variants = Variant.resolve(model)
```

| `opencode.json` | Plugin `model.transform` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| omits `variants` | sets `[none, low, medium, xhigh]` | `[low, medium, high]` | `[none, low, medium, xhigh]` |
| sets same effective `package`, omits `variants` | sets `[none, low, medium, xhigh]` | `[low, medium, high]` | `[none, low, medium, xhigh]` |
| moves model to another `package`, omits `variants` | sets variants for old package | respelled for new package | respelled for new package |
| omits `variants` | none | `[low, medium, high]` | `[low, medium, high]` |

### Out of scope

- A plugin that sets `variants = []` on a custom model still receives default variants when `opencode.json` omits `capabilities.reasoning`.
- Aliases of catalog models (`inherit` with a catalog `base`) still reset from `source.base` in the late pass.

### Verification

- `bun run script/test.ts test/config/provider.test.ts --rerun-each 10 --randomize` in `packages/core`: 400 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run script/test.ts test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts test/plugin/models-dev.test.ts test/variant.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 78 pass, 0 fail

prs.title: fix(app): let a plugin server's event stream follow its endpoint
prs.body:
Closes #60005. A plugin's server now loads after a Desktop restart: its event stream follows the endpoint the plugin reports instead of retrying `127.0.0.1:0`.

## Cause

`runtime/plugin/servers.tsx` restores a plugin's last inventory on the placeholder endpoint `http://127.0.0.1:0`, and the app creates the server's SDK before the plugin reports. The transport moved to the real endpoint, but the event stream kept the API it was created with. Its only way out, `reconnect`, was read once at creation and was `undefined` for the placeholder.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  restore["restored server: 127.0.0.1:0"] --> report["plugin reports its endpoint"]
  report --> http["requests: new endpoint"]
  report --> before["stream before: retries port 0 forever"]
  report --> after["stream now: next reconnect resolves the endpoint; a connected stream moves at once"]
```

## Change

- **Every reconnect resolves the endpoint again.** For a plugin's server, the stream asks the plugin's `reconnect` if it has one at that moment, otherwise it takes the plugin's current endpoint.
- **A connected stream moves at once** when the plugin reports a different endpoint, instead of staying on the old one until it drops.
- **No double work.** The transport keeps its clients when the endpoint is unchanged, so a managed plugin whose own `reconnect` already moved the stream is not asked again.
- **The transport keeps its endpoint as plain values.** A plugin's endpoint can be a store proxy that changes in place, such as an SSH sign-in that issues a new password. Holding the proxy made the new endpoint look unchanged, so the clients kept the old password. The app's controller already copies credentials for the same reason (`runtime.tsx`).
- Sidecar and HTTP servers behave as before.

## Tests

- `test-browser/plugin-server-stream.test.ts` drives the real `createServerSdkContext`: the server starts on the placeholder, the plugin reports an endpoint, then another.
  - Without the reconnect change, the first step times out on port 0.
  - Without the move-at-once change, the second step times out.

This replaces #60006 by @Belkata, which found the cause. This PR also moves a connected stream when the endpoint changes and keeps the change inside the SDK context.

prs.title: fix(core): rewrite the image_generate description
prs.body:
The `image_generate` description read like a wall of rules: a cost warning, "omit model to use the default", and instructions for after the notice. It never clearly said to only use the tool when the user asks for an image. I rewrote it with one point per line, like the subagent tool:

```diff
-Generate or edit an image. Pass images to edit them or to guide style and subject. To make several images, call the tool once per image with distinct prompts. Omit model to use the default. Runs in the background: the call returns right away and you are notified automatically when the image is saved or fails. DO NOT sleep, poll, or check whether the file exists while it runs; continue with other work or end your response. After the notice, use the read tool on the path to view the image and mention the path to the user. Each call costs money, so don't regenerate unless asked or the result is clearly wrong.
+Generates a new image, or edits existing ones.
+Only call this when the user asks you to create or edit an image.
+Images you pass are used as the source to edit, or as references for style and subject.
+Each call makes one image. For several images, call it once per image.
+It runs in the background: the call starts a job and returns right away, and you are notified automatically when the image is saved, with its path. Never poll, sleep, or check for the file while you wait.
+Don't repeat a request unless the user asks.
```

What I dropped:
- **The cost line.** No other image tool I looked at mentions cost (Codex, Grok Build, Hermes), and it isn't true on a Codex login. "Only when the user asks" and "don't repeat" do the same job, and they're rules the model can follow.
- **"Omit model to use the default".** The `model` parameter already says not to set it unless the user asks, like the subagent tool.
- **"After the notice, use the read tool".** The notice itself already says "Use the read tool on this path to view the image."

I also fixed the `images` parameter. It ended with "Omit to create a new image", which reads as if passing images always means an edit, but references guide new images too:

```diff
-Images to edit or use as references, in order. Local file paths (relative to the session directory or absolute) or http(s) URLs. Omit to create a new image.
+Images to edit, or to use as references for style and subject when creating a new image, in order. Local file paths (relative to the session directory or absolute) or http(s) URLs.
```

"Don't repeat a request" stays because our benchmarks had agents regenerate unasked, up to 6–11 calls in a single run on MiniMax.

### Verification

- `packages/core`: `test/tool-image-generate.test.ts` passes (14), and `bun run typecheck:tsc` is clean.
- `bun run check` passes.

prs.title: fix(opencode): end an ACP prompt when its session goes idle
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60065

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

When a durable write fails during an ACP turn (for example `SQLITE_FULL`), the `session.execution.*` outcome can be lost. The adapter only ended a prompt on that event, so `session/prompt` stayed pending and every later prompt was refused with `Session already has an active ACP prompt`.

- `packages/cli/src/acp/turn.ts`: once the prompt is delivered, the turn also waits on `POST /api/experimental/session/:id/wait`. If the session goes idle before an outcome event arrives, the turn ends through the normal `settle` path, which still reports a step or execution error that was recorded.
- `packages/cli/src/acp/translate.ts`: a `session.execution.failed` that arrives before `session.inbox.delivered` now ends the turn instead of being ignored. That turn can never deliver its prompt, so there was nothing left to wait for.

Normal turns are unaffected: the terminal event is published before `awaitIdle` resolves, so an event still ends the turn first.

Only the ACP side is in scope here. Core storage retries stay in `fix/disk-full-session-recovery` / #53704.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test test/acp` from `packages/cli`: 102 pass.

prs.title: fix(core): do not run on another provider when the configured one is missing
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #58909

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When `model` names a provider whose config entry the schema rejected, the provider is dropped from the catalog. `Model.default` then returned the first available model, so the configured default silently resolved to a different provider — in practice the built-in free one — and the prompt and its tool calls ran there.

The default now resolves to nothing when its provider was never registered, and `ModelResolver` no longer picks an arbitrary model as a second fallback. A configured model on a provider that still exists keeps the existing fallback, including a disabled provider or a model that later left the catalog.

The run now stops with `No model is available for session …` instead of using another provider. It does not yet name the dropped provider; making the rejected config entry itself fail would be a larger change.

### How did you verify your code works?

With the config from the issue (invalid `capabilities.reasoning`, `model: probe/probe-1`) on an isolated `XDG_*` setup:

- Before: `> build · big-pickle`, then the free-usage error — the prompt went to the built-in provider.
- After: `Error: No model is available for session …`, and no request leaves for another provider.

prs.title: feat(tui): add screen reader mode
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Relates to #39368

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in screen reader mode. The full-screen interface redraws in place, which screen readers can't follow, so in this mode OpenCode uses the minimal interface (`opencode mini`), which appends to scrollback.

Turn it on with `--screen-reader` (`--no-screen-reader` forces it off), `OPENCODE_SCREEN_READER`, or `screen_reader` in `cli.json`. Plain `opencode` hands off to mini. It is never auto-detected.

In this mode:

- No splash, footer details, animation or color. `NO_COLOR` is also honored.
- Lines are labeled `you:`, `assistant:`, `tool:`, `tool error:`, `error:`, and `Working...` prints after your `you:` line when a turn starts.
- The input line starts with `$ ` (no left rail), so it is clear where to type.
- Menus, question lists and the permission prompt move the terminal cursor to the selected row, since screen readers read the line under the cursor. Digit keys in question lists select and Enter confirms.
- The terminal bell rings when a turn ends, when input is needed, and when a tool runs over 5 seconds.

To enhance the screen reader mode, mini also gets `/sessions`, `/rename`, `/fork`, `/undo`, `/redo` and `/mcp` (also in the command menu), and `--auto` is now accepted by mini. Auto-approve there only follows the flag, not the `autoaccept` config.

Docs are added to the live docs page, `services/www/src/docs/content/cli/tui.mdx`. I did not port the integration connect flow, tabs, themes or the sidebar to mini.

### How did you verify your code works?

Tested by hand with NVDA in Windows Terminal: prompts, streaming, labels, bell, menus, question lists, permission prompts and each new command. Added tests for the flag/env/config precedence, `NO_COLOR`, the handoff, labels, bell, cursor placement, the `$` prompt marker, `Working...` ordering, digit keys, `--auto`, and the session commands. `bun run check` passes. tui mini tests: 446 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed. cli tests: 340 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed (run with `--timeout 60000`, since the command tests spawn processes that take over 5 s on Windows).

I have not tested other screen readers, terminals or platforms.

prs.title: fix(core): drop a well-known source when its last credential is removed
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #59320

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

`opencode auth logout` deletes the credential but leaves the `.well-known/opencode` source registered. Without a credential, `Config.loadWellknownEntry` cannot resolve the manifest, so it falls back to `WellKnown.cached(origin)` and keeps applying the last remote config (models, policies). That is why logout looked incomplete.

`Credential.remove` in core now drops a well-known source when the removed credential was the integration's last one, so every core caller gets the same invariant instead of only the `server.credential` HTTP handler doing it. `WellKnown.remove` already existed and publishes `WellKnown.Event.Updated`, which the existing subscribers use to reload config and integrations. Other integrations, and well-known integrations that still have a credential, keep the previous path. No protocol or config schema changes.

Sources that were already orphaned before this fix are intentionally not pruned: a registered source without a credential is also the normal state between `integration.wellknown.add` and the first login, so earlier orphans are indistinguishable from a source the user just added and has not logged into yet. Cleaning those needs a one-time migration keyed on state we do not record today.

### How did you verify your code works?

New HTTP-level regression test in `packages/server/test/credential.test.ts`:

1. Register a well-known manifest with `config.model = embedded/model`.
2. Create two credentials for it; `/api/config` exposes that model.
3. Remove one credential: the integration and the model stay.
4. Remove the last credential: the integration disappears and `/api/config` no longer contains the model.

New core-level test in `packages/core/test/credential.test.ts` mocks `WellKnown` and asserts that `Credential.remove`, called directly without the HTTP layer, removes the source only when the last credential goes. With the rule implemented in the handler only, that core test fails.

Also ran `bun run check` at the repository root plus the core `credential` / `wellknown` / `integration` / `config` suites and the server `credential` suite, and `prettier --check` on the changed files.

### Visual

No visual change; this only affects CLI auth and config behavior.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(core): let agents ask another session a question
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60072

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Multi-session work is normal today: subagents, forks, background jobs, and the desktop voice delegator all run beside the session that started them. But the only sanctioned cross-session path is parent to child, so an agent that needs an answer from a sibling session improvises through a shared file or asks a human to relay it.

This adds two native tools over the existing session inbox. `ask({session, question})` resolves an existing top-level session by exact id or exact title, lists metadata only, and queues one bounded question into that session's inbox. `answer({replyTo, answer})` lets the target reply once back to the asker as a message. Texts are capped at 4000 characters, three questions per pair, and no message text or system prompt is read; the duplicate-answer guard compares stored metadata only. Zero schema, protocol, table, or client changes.

Core is the right home because the voice delegator already messages sessions by reading their transcripts. An agent tool should read no message text and be cooperative: the target decides whether to answer, and answers with a tool call.

### How did you verify your code works?

`bun test test/tool-ask.test.ts` — 7 tests covering admission (queued synthetic, envelope, metadata), every refusal class (self, child caller/target, archived, cross-project, unknown, ambiguous with ≤10 candidates), single-answer enforcement (forged `replyTo` and non-ask synthetics refused, second answer refused), the 3-per-pair and duplicate-pending caps, inbox promotion making the question model-visible, and permission denial through an agent ruleset. The exhaustive built-in-tool catalog test is updated for the two new names. `bun run typecheck:tsc`, oxlint, prettier, and ast-grep are clean. The remaining full-suite failures on this machine reproduce on the unmodified tree (filesystem watchers on system paths, MCP/SSE timeouts) and are unrelated.

Not a UI change.

prs.title: feat(core): offer gpt-image-2 on the Codex login
prs.body:
If you logged in with Codex ("Codex browser" or "Codex device code", which go to `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`), `image_generate` had no OpenAI image models. The Codex login's model filter only kept `gpt-N.M` chat models, so `openai/gpt-image-2` came back as "Model not found". The Codex backend does serve images, though. The Codex client generates them on a subscription with `gpt-image-2`, as JSON to `/images/generations` and `/images/edits`.

I probed the backend with a real Codex login:

| Call | Result |
| --- | --- |
| generate `gpt-image-2` | 200, image |
| edit, JSON with a data URL | 200, a true edit |
| edit, multipart upload (what we send) | 400 `Unsupported content type` |
| edit, 9.4 MB PNG as 11.9 MiB of uncompressed JSON | 200 (the ~1 MiB limit is only on `/responses`) |

So this PR makes two changes:

```diff
 core  plugin/provider/openai.ts (Codex login model filter)
+  allowlist: gpt-image-2 stays enabled, cost zeroed like the chat models
+  other image models stay hidden
 ai    providers/openai.ts
+  on a chatgpt.com baseURL, image edits use "json-edits"
 ai    protocols/openai-images.ts
+  "json-edits": always the JSON body on /images/edits,
+  never multipart
```

The allowlist has only the model the Codex client uses. The backend also returned images for `gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5`, `chatgpt-image-latest` and the `gpt-image-2.5` models, but I didn't check whether it quietly swaps them for another model, so they stay hidden.

Everything else keeps multipart edits. I checked that OpenAI's own API accepts the JSON form too, but OpenCode Console's edit endpoint takes only multipart, and Zen models use this same package.

### Out of scope

- "Sign in with ChatGPT" (token sharing, `chatgpt-token-sharing`, through `api.openai.com`) rejects image calls with 401 `hardened_oauth_rule_missing` ("This ChatPass credential is not authorized for the requested operation"). Chat still works with that credential. Its model allowlist already has no image models, so nothing changes there.

### Visual

### Verification

- End to end with my Codex login: I started a standalone server from this branch on a copy of the dev database, then called `POST /api/experimental/generate/image` with `openai/gpt-image-2`. A generation returned a PNG, and an edit of a photo added the requested red cap and kept the rest. On `origin/dev`, the same request returns `ModelNotFoundError`.
