prs.title: feat(core): make image generation a Code Mode tool
prs.body:
`image_generate` was a direct tool, offered next to `execute` on every request where an image model exists. I moved it into Code Mode, unpinned, so it sits in the catalog until an agent needs it, and the prompt stays smaller on every turn that doesn't generate images.

It gets its own `image` namespace rather than `opencode`, since `opencode` is about managing OpenCode itself (sessions, worktrees, models). That also keeps it clear of the internal plugin's `opencode_image_generate`.

```diff
 tools offered to the model
   execute
-  image_generate            (direct, every request)
 code mode catalog
+  image (Generate and edit images with the image models of your connected providers.)
+    generate                (tools.image.generate, not pinned)
```

The tool's effective name stays `image_generate`, so permission rules (`"image_generate": "deny"`), background jobs and restart recovery are unchanged. It's still registered only while some connected provider has an image model, and it re-checks when the catalog changes. With Code Mode denied it falls back to a direct `image_generate` tool like the other Code Mode tools.

### Verification

- `packages/core` `test/tool-image-generate.test.ts` (15 pass, twice): the tool shows up in the Code Mode catalog as `image.generate`, isn't pinned and isn't a direct tool; it appears and disappears with image models; a new test calls `tools.image.generate` through `execute`. The other tests run it with Code Mode denied, where it's direct. `test/lib/tool.ts`'s `executeTool` takes optional permissions for that.
- `session-execution`, `codemode` and `tool-schedule` tests pass (45).
- `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/core` and `bun run check` pass.

prs.title: perf(core): share credential-scoped provider discovery across locations
prs.body:
Provider, model and integration state is per Location, so built-in provider plugins that fetch credential-scoped data redid the same fetch in every Location. With 30 Locations open, GitHub Copilot hit `/models` 30 times at boot and 30 more times per account switch, and DigitalOcean, Azure and Modal did the same.

I added a small internal global service, `SharedRefresh`. A plugin gets a subscriber, points it at a key it builds itself (integration + credential connection ID + anything that changes the answer, like base URL), and gets back the shared value. It is not part of the plugin API.

```ts
const models = yield* shared.subscriber<CopilotModels.Snapshot>()
const remote = yield* models.use({
  key: `github-copilot:${IntegrationConnection.key(connection)}:${url}:${headersHash}`,
  load: fetchModels,
  // interval?: defaults to 10 minutes, equals?: defaults to deep equality
})
yield* models.changes.pipe(Stream.runForEach(refresh), Effect.forkScoped)
```

How it behaves:

- Callers with the same key join one in-flight load. A Location on a different credential gets its own entry.
- Each key refreshes in the background only while some Location uses it. When the last subscriber releases it or closes, the timer stops.
- A failed refresh keeps the last good value. If a key has no value yet, the next `use` starts a new load instead of waiting for the timer.
- `changes` only fires when the refreshed value differs, so an unchanged refresh doesn't trigger any provider or model reloads.
- Keys use the connection ID, not the token, so a token refresh doesn't create a new entry.

```diff
 Location N boot / credential switch
   plugin.load()
-    fetch upstream                      # once per Location
+    subscriber.use({ key, load })       # joins the shared entry, fetches once per key
   ctx.provider.reload()
```

I moved GitHub Copilot, DigitalOcean, Azure and Modal onto it. Requests per host with the fake upstream from the location-duplication harness (100 ms latency):

| Locations | Boot: Copilot / DO / Azure | Copilot switch: Copilot `/models` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 -> 1 / 1 / 1 | 1 -> 1 |
| 10 | 10 / 10 / 10 -> 1 / 1 / 1 | 10 -> 1 |
| 30 | 30 / 30 / 30 -> 1 / 1 / 1 | 30 -> 1 |

Every Location still ends up with the same model list (216 models in the run). Modal works the same way but the harness doesn't cover it because it needs a configured base URL.

One behavior change for Azure: switching to the account that is already active no longer refetches deployments, because the shared entry is reused. New deployments now show up with the 10-minute background refresh, which didn't exist before. I removed the Azure test that relied on that refetch (keeping the last good list on failure is now covered by the helper test), and changed the stuck-discovery test to block on the first account's initial load.

Out of scope: Console (it will move onto this helper with a 1-minute interval in a follow-up), wellknown remote config, and local discovery, which already shares its fetch through a module cache.

### What does this PR do?

Desktop and TUI explain that adopting V2 applies to every project sharing the data/configuration, requires stopping V1, and does not support later V1 imports or V2-to-V1 synchronization. Previously migrated profiles see the notice once too. Headless clients accept explicitly with `acknowledged: true`; clients and OpenAPI are regenerated.

Why consolidate: #50130 reports late V1 sessions missing from V2; #54272 adds recurring watermark imports. Both concern continued V1 use after cutover. This proposes an explicit one-way contract instead, since history synchronization alone does not cover shared configuration and plugins. Initial-import crash recovery stays; recurring compatibility watermarks are not added.

Existing omissions still need separate recovery. This does not overwrite V2 history, terminate V1, or claim to stop an old binary. Reinstalling V2 is not rollback: restoring V1 needs a pre-upgrade backup and separately preserving V2-only work. The original issue/PR remain for maintainer review.

### How did you verify your code works?

- 38 real SQLite migration tests + HTTP acceptance test pass. Removing the startup gate makes the new regression fail.
- Root `bun run check` passes (local Windows Node TS-stripping and Git-symlink checkout accommodations).
- Desktop/TUI and docs typechecks pass; generated OpenAPI verified.

### Screenshots / recordings

Interactive Desktop/TUI verification is pending; opening as a draft.

prs.title: fix(core): price Copilot long-context tiers and cache writes
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52089
Closes #59671 

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

GitHub Copilot costs were undercounted badly on long sessions. In my case (#59671): a 3h session on Copilot / Claude Haiku 5.5, 348 requests, ~344K average context, OpenCode showed $1.56 when the real bill is roughly $9.34 (between $2.03 and $10.15, since Copilot picks the price tier per request by prompt size).

Two causes, both in the Copilot provider code:

1. Copilot's `/models` payload ships two price tiers (`default` and `long_context`, the latter starting above `default.max_prompt_tokens`). The builder only read the default tier.
2. The builder hardcoded cache writes to $0 (`cache_write_price` is in the payload, unread), and both usage adapters dropped `cache_write_tokens`, so cache writes weren't counted at all.

Pricing that session's totals at the ≤100K rates with free writes gives $1.5557 — cent-exact with the displayed $1.56, which is how I know exactly which rates the old code applied.

The builder now emits the write price and a context-tier cost entry, which `SessionUsage.calculateCost` already applies per request, so no calculator change was needed. The adapters map `cache_write_tokens` into `cacheWrite`. While there I replaced their hand-rolled `noCache` arithmetic with `ProviderShared.subtractTokens`/`sumTokens` like the shared protocols use: three of the four paths left `noCache` undefined on responses without cache details, which downstream prices the entire prompt at $0, and none of them clamped against broken breakdowns.

Deliberately not addressed: Copilot's own reported billed amount (#35765) and the richer `pricing` shape from #59460.

### How did you verify your code works?

New unit tests against the Copilot rate card for Claude Haiku 5.5: long-context tier applies above 100K prompt tokens, default tier at exactly 100K, cache writes priced, reasoning billed as output, a malformed `long_context` object no longer drops the model from the catalog, cache-write mapping in all four adapter paths, plus regressions for the $0-prompt and negative-`noCache` cases. The adapter regressions fail on the parent commit and pass with this change. `bun run check` passes, and the `packages/core` suite has the same 4 failures as a clean `dev` checkout (all environment-related).

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" role="img" aria-label="Copilot session cost: displayed $1.56, actual about $9.34">
```

prs.title: feat(core): schedule prompts from agents, /schedule and the experimental API
prs.body:
**Agents, people and apps can now schedule a prompt for later: ask "check CI every hour for the next 8 hours" and the session wakes itself.**
Builds on #59401 (merged), which added the storage and timer. Everything here stays off unless `experimental.schedules` is on where the session lives.

💡 **Why**
#59401 fires schedules, but nothing could create one yet. This PR gives the agent, the user and apps a way in.

🆕 **Now you can**
- Let the agent schedule work itself. It gets `schedule_create`, `schedule_list`, `schedule_pause`, `schedule_resume` and `schedule_delete` in the `opencode` tool namespace. It can only see and change its own session's schedules.
- Type `/schedule every morning at 9 check CI` (or just `/schedule` to list them). The agent turns that into a schedule.
- Manage schedules from apps through `client.experimental.schedule.{create,list,get,pause,resume,delete}` (`/api/experimental/schedule`).
- Write `when` the short way: `{ in: "20 minutes" }`, `{ at: "2026-10-27T09:00" }`, `{ every: "1 hour" }` or `{ cron: "0 9 * * 1-5" }`, with an optional `tz`, plus `ends` and `prompt`.

🚦 **How it ships**
Off by default. With `experimental.schedules` off, the tools and `/schedule` aren't registered, and the API returns 403. They appear or disappear when config changes, without a restart. Conditional checks (`if` / `until` shell commands that need approval) come in the next PR.

```diff
+ agent / /schedule / app -> schedule({ when, ends?, prompt })
+   -> flag off where the session lives? -> 403, or the tools are hidden
+   -> another session's schedule?       -> not found
+   -> the timer from #59401 fires it later as a prompt
```

### Visual

prs.title: fix(ai): send OpenRouter image edits as input references
prs.body:
### Problem

Image edits through OpenRouter never worked. OpenRouter image models use the OpenAI images protocol, and when a request has input `images` that protocol posts multipart to `/images/edits`. OpenRouter has no such endpoint, so every edit came back as HTTP 404 for every model.

Just changing the path isn't enough either. OpenRouter's image API (`POST /api/v1/images`, alias `/images/generations`) is JSON only and reads input images from `input_references: [{ type: "image_url", image_url: { url } }]`. If you send OpenAI's `images` field instead, it silently ignores it and you get an unrelated text-to-image redraw.

### Change

I added an `imageInput` option to `OpenAIImages.model`, next to the `sizing` hook from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59927. It defaults to `"edits"`, so OpenAI, Azure, Vercel and the other hosts behave exactly as before. OpenRouter passes `"references"`:

```diff
 OpenRouter image request
-  images? -> multipart POST /images/edits        (404)
+  always  -> JSON POST /images/generations
+  images  -> input_references: [{ type: "image_url", image_url: { url } }]
+             bytes as data URLs, http(s) URLs as is
+  mask    -> UnsupportedOperation (OpenRouter has no mask parameter)
```

A request without images sends the same body as before. Response parsing didn't need changes, since OpenRouter returns OpenAI-style `data[].b64_json`.

This is stacked on https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59927 (`image-sizing-fixes`) because both touch the same lines in `openai-images.ts` and `openrouter.ts`. Once that merges this retargets to `dev` with only its own commit.

### Out of scope

- `Image.stream` through OpenRouter. Its stream events carry `media_type` but no `output_format`, and the protocol currently requires `output_format` on partial and completed events, so streaming there fails to decode. That's a separate fix.
- Per-model reference limits. `GET /api/v1/images/models` lists `input_references` `{min, max}` per model (some take 0). I'm leaving the count check to OpenRouter.
- Vercel AI Gateway edits already work through `/v1/images/edits`, so I left them alone.

### Verification

- Live: `POST /api/v1/images/edits` returns 404. `/api/v1/images/models` lists `input_references` for nearly every model and no `mask` parameter anywhere.
- Recorded `openrouter-images/edits-an-image-through-input-references` with `openai/gpt-image-1-mini` (about $0.002). The black circle fixture came back as the same circle in green, so it's a real edit.
- New unit tests in `test/image.test.ts`: no images keeps the plain body, bytes and URLs become `input_references` on `/images/generations` as JSON, and a mask fails with `UnsupportedOperation` before any request. These and the recorded test fail without the fix.
- `packages/ai`: `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`, `bun test` (1979 pass). Root: `bun run check`.

### Visual

prs.title: fix(tui): show execution failures that happen before any step
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/34839

### Problem

When a run fails before any step starts (an unavailable model, a variant that doesn't exist, instructions that can't load), the TUI shows a "Session failed" toast and then nothing. Once the toast fades, the transcript ends at the user's prompt.

The server already stores the error on the idle marker that ends the run. https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/53826 rendered it on desktop and in the TUI, but the TUI row change was reverted in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/54061. That version moved the error below a prompt the run never sent, and the reordering broke after `/model`, after a resync, and for live rows. Without it, the TUI's `ExecutionError` view never gets a row.

### Change

`reduceSessionRows` now emits a row for a failed idle marker, in its stored position. Nothing is reordered, so a prompt the failed run left unsent still shows below it in its usual pending style.

```diff
 second message, are you there?
+Error: Model unavailable: opencode/gpt-5.5
```

The error is skipped only when the turn's last step or compaction already shows the same error (same type and message), so a step failure isn't shown twice:

```text
on idle marker
  if it has an error and it differs from the last step/compaction error
    add a row for it
  forget the last error
```

A different error still shows. For example, a manual `/compact` that failed, followed by a run that failed for another reason, shows both.

### Out of scope

Three image routes sent sizes their provider ignores, rejects or bills at the wrong tier. I checked each one with live calls.

```diff
+  sizing,   # OpenRouter and Vercel pass their own body fields; OpenAI keeps `size`
```

No new failure paths.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep cursor style valid when config reload removes it
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #58992

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When `cli.json` is hot-reloaded and the `cursor` block goes from set to unset, `resolve()` returns `cursor: undefined`. Inputs that bind `cursorStyle={config.cursor}` (command palette, `DialogPrompt`, permission and form inputs) then pass `undefined` to OpenTUI's `cursorStyle` setter, which reads `style.color` and crashes.

`resolve()` now always returns a cursor, using OpenTUI's own default (`block`, blinking) when the setting is unset. That is the same cursor a fresh start without the setting gets, so all inputs get a valid value and the `if (config.cursor)` guards in the prompt are no longer needed.

There was a second problem behind the same reload path: `reconcile` keeps the store's cursor object, so Solid never re-applied `cursorStyle` to inputs that were already mounted. Without that, removing or changing `cursor` would stop crashing but would still not reach those inputs. `ConfigProvider` now replaces the cursor object after reconciling. OpenTUI ignores a style that has not changed, so this does nothing when the cursor setting is the same.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New `test/config-cursor.test.tsx` mounts a real `DialogPrompt` under `ConfigProvider` with `cursor: { style: "underline", blinking: false }`, removes `cursor` through the provider's update path and checks that the input switches to `block`/blinking. On `dev` it fails with the stack from the issue (`TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'style.color')` in `cursorStyle` → `setProp`); with this change it passes.
- New `resolve` cases in `test/config-v2.test.tsx` cover an unset cursor, an empty cursor and partial cursor settings.
- `bun run test` in `packages/tui`: 1557 pass, 3 fail, 2 skip. Before the change it was 1551 pass, 3 fail, 2 skip. The same 3 tests fail on `dev` without this change (`plugin-source.test.ts`, "Node reloads the local ESM graph…"). They run under Node, and the environment used here has Node 20.
- `tsc -b --force` in `packages/tui` passes, and the repo-wide `bun run check` (lint and typecheck) passes.
- `oxlint` on `packages/tui` reports 0 warnings and 0 errors, and `prettier --check` passes on the changed files.
- The `opencode-drive` script from the issue and a manual TUI hot reload were not run.

### Screenshots / recordings

There is no visual change beyond the cursor going back to the default after a reload, instead of the TUI crashing.

prs.title: chore(console): move console and stats to released solid-start
prs.body:
The console and stats apps were built on a pkg.pr.new preview of SolidStart from the devinxi work (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/4635). SolidStart 2 is now released, so I moved both apps to it and to a matching Nitro release.

### Versions

| Package | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@solidjs/start` (catalog) | `pkg.pr.new/@solidjs/start@dfb2020` | `2.1.0` |
| `nitro` (console, stats) | `3.0.1-alpha.1` | `3.0.260903-beta` |
| `vite` (console, stats) | catalog (`7.3.7`) | `8.2.4` |
| `engines.node` (console, stats) | `>=22` | `>=24` |

SolidStart 2 needs Vite 8 and Node 24. I pinned Vite `8.2.4` in the two apps, the version `packages/app` and `packages/desktop` already use, so the lockfile reuses that copy and the catalog stays on 7 for everything else. The deploy workflow already runs Node 24. Wrangler stays at 4.50.0.

### Code and config changes

```diff
 packages/console/app/
   src/global.d.ts                         # drop the APIEvent stub, @solidjs/start/server exports the real type now
   src/routes/download/[channel]/[platform].ts
-    import type { APIEvent } from "@solidjs/start"
+    import type { APIEvent } from "@solidjs/start/server"
   vite.config.ts
+    environments.client.build.copyPublicDir = true
 packages/stats/app/
   src/entry-server.tsx
-    import type { Asset, PageEvent } from "@solidjs/start"
+    import { ..., type Asset, type PageEvent } from "@solidjs/start/server"
```

- The request and page event types are now only exported from `@solidjs/start/server`.
- New Nitro turns off Vite's public dir copy and copies `public/` itself with `fs.cp`. That keeps the console's symlinks into `packages/ui` (favicons, manifest, social images) as absolute symlinks in `.output/public`. Turning Vite's copy back on for the client build gives real files again, same as before.

### Deploy

`sst.cloudflare.x.SolidStart` still finds what it expects: `.output/nitro.json` with preset `cloudflare-module`, `.output/server/index.mjs` and `.output/public`. The generated `wrangler.json` (compat date, `nodejs_compat`, `ASSETS` binding) is unchanged. Server chunks moved from `server/chunks/` to `server/_ssr/` and `server/_libs/`, and `.output/server/` no longer carries a copy of `public/`.

A few responses change, all in line with what the handlers already return:

- A `404` `Response` returned from an API route or middleware is now sent as is. The preview build swapped it for h3's generic JSON 404. This affects `/download/<channel>/<unknown>` (empty 404), proxied stats 404 pages, and `/data/compare/*.json` (now the JSON error the middleware builds).
- Stats now matches its API routes under `/data/`, so the newsletter form's `POST /data/api/newsletter` reaches its handler instead of the 404 page.
- Stats asset URLs and server function calls now carry the `/data/` base (`/data/_build/...`, `/data/_server`). The console proxy already serves `/data/_build/` and leaves prefixed URLs alone, so pages served through it are unchanged.
- Locale redirects from the console middleware (`/fr/black`, `/fr/auth`) now also set `oc_locale`, and `/fr/docs` sends that cookie once instead of twice.

### Verification

Compared against `origin/dev` in a second worktree, both built and served with `wrangler dev` on `.output` (compat date `2025-05-05`, `nodejs_compat`) with dummy SST resources and a local stub for the PlanetScale HTTP API.

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun run check` at the root, and `bun run typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc` and `bun run test` in both apps: pass.
- `bun run build` in both apps: pass. `wrangler deploy --dry-run` total upload: console 1291 → 1360 KiB (301 → 324 KiB gzip), stats 1654 → 1756 KiB (355 → 386 KiB gzip). Client CSS is the same size. Client JS is about 4% larger because Rolldown splits chunks differently.
- Route comparison (status, redirects, key headers, visible text, head tags, markup): 72 of 81 console routes identical (pages, locale and legacy redirects, docs proxy, `/data` proxy, sitemap, `config.json`, apple-app-site-association, 404s). For stats behind a local copy of the console proxy, 95 of 102 identical, including sampled lab, model and compare pages, `.md`/`.json`/`llms.txt` formats and canonical redirects. Every difference is one of the response changes listed above, plus `cache-control: immutable` on a 404 for a missing `/_build/assets/` file.
- Full-page Playwright screenshots of 16 console and 11 stats pages at 1440 and 390 px, pixel-diffed against the old build: no layout or style differences. The only changed pixels were the animated home hero and GitHub star counts that changed between runs because of GitHub API rate limits.
- Hydration and interaction checks on both builds, with matching results and no new console errors or hydration warnings: install tabs, FAQ toggle, client-side navigation, stats period toggle, theme switch, and the newsletter request path.
- `vite dev` for both apps serves the same pages without errors once Vite has finished its first dependency optimization.

prs.title: fix(core): keep running terminals out of eviction
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #48691

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Supersedes #48730, which was closed by the automated PR cleanup while waiting for review. Complements #59399: that PR keeps a location alive while a terminal socket is attached; this one keeps it alive while a terminal is still running after its client detached (panel closed, tab switched away, app restarted, connection dropped), which is the case in #48691. The two checks compose, and I will rebase onto #59399 once it lands.

Since #57416 the inactivity sweep keeps a location alive while a running session or a background job owns it. A running terminal counts as neither: terminals produce no session events, so a location whose only activity is an open terminal is still evicted on schedule and the Pty finalizer kills every terminal in it. That is the blank pane and "PTY session not found" in #48691, which the triage bot reproduced on v2.2.0 and current `dev`.

Before evicting an expired location, the sweep now also asks that location's Pty service for running terminals and refreshes the timer while any exist, the same way it already treats active sessions and background jobs. The probe uses `contextEffectOption`, so it only reads the cached graph and never boots a location; a graph that failed to build counts as having no terminals, so failed locations are cleaned up as before.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New case in `packages/core/test/location-activity.test.ts`: a location whose graph is the real `Pty` node, with a running `cat` terminal, stays cached when its deadline passes, and is evicted by the next sweep after the terminal is removed. The case fails without the fix.
- The existing eviction tests (waiting questions, background jobs, `experimental.location_idle_timeout`, non-canonical refs) pass unchanged. `packages/core` typecheck, the pty, location-activity, location-filesystem and browser-idle suites, oxlint and prettier are clean.
- The repro script from the bot's comment on #48691 exercises exactly this path: `POST /api/pty` with `sleep 4000`, no session activity, 1 minute idle timeout.

issues.title: Image resize returns a PNG ~10x larger than the JPEG candidates

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

When an image has to be resized, `resizeImageInProcess` in `src/utils/image-resize-core.ts` returns the first candidate under `maxBytes`. The candidate list always starts with PNG, so a photo-like JPEG gets sent as a PNG whenever the PNG is under 4.5 MB, even when the JPEG candidates are much smaller. The code comment says "Try both PNG and JPEG formats, pick the smaller one", but the code doesn't do that.

Real case: a 2400×1620 JPEG (285 KB base64) resized to 2000×1350:

| candidate | base64 size |
|---|---|
| PNG (returned) | 3,316,760 |
| JPEG q80 | 548,576 |
| JPEG q40 | 308,688 |

Reading three of these in one turn put about 10 MB of images into the request. My provider then kept timing out waiting for response headers.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Take any photo JPEG wider than 2000 px.
2. `read` it, or call `resizeImageInProcess(bytes, "image/jpeg")`.
3. The result is `image/png` and several times larger than the original file.

### Expected behavior

Return the smallest candidate under `maxBytes`, as the comment says. Alternatively, skip PNG when the input is JPEG.

### Version

1.4.0 (current `main` has the same logic)

issues.title: Set a startup-time budget targeting jcode-comparable latency and memory
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Set a startup-time budget for pi that targets jcode-comparable latency and memory, and close the gap measured by jcode's README benchmark against pi 0.62.0:

| Metric (median; 10 interactive PTY launches, Linux) | jcode v0.9.1888-dev | pi (same table) | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time to first frame | 14.0 ms (10.1–19.3) | 590.7 ms (369.6–934.8) | 42.2× |
| Time to first input | 48.7 ms (30.3–62.7) | 596.4 ms (373.9–955.2) | 12.2× |
| Idle RAM, 1 session (PSS) | 27.8 MB | 144.4 MB | 5.2× |
| Idle RAM, 10 sessions (PSS) | 117.0 MB | 833.0 MB | 7.1× |
| Extra RAM per added session | ~9.9 MB | ~76.5 MB | 7.7× |

Notes: jcode numbers come from jcode's own README ("Performance & Resource Efficiency"; RAM rows are with local embeddings off). pi 0.62.0 is the version listed in the README's version list for the RAM tables; the timing rows carry no stated version there. Pi's own best measured cold start is 2.55 s (`--no-extensions`, pi 0.78.0, #5402); ~2.7 s was reported in #7639.

### Why?

Startup latency is paid on every spawn, and current pi workflows spawn it constantly:

- Multiplexer setups (tmux/zellij; pi-mux, dmux) run one pane per session; each switch back pays the first frame plus a ~2.5–2.7 s cold start and multi-second extension reloads (#5905).
- `pi -c` one-shots and subagent fan-out multiply the cost: 16 concurrent spawns × 0.59 s ≈ 9.4 s before agents render, and 1000 one-shots at ~2.7 s each total ~45 min. Running many sessions at once also costs ~76.5 MB PSS per session vs ~9.9 MB for jcode.
- Session resume and switch sit on the same path: listing and parsing session files adds to per-switch latency (#5804, #6594).

Nielsen Norman Group response-time limits put 0.1 s at "instant" and 1.0 s as the limit for uninterrupted flow. jcode's 14 ms first frame sits far below the instant threshold; pi's 590.7 ms and 2.5 s cold start break flow on every spawn. For pane-per-session workflows, spawn speed decides whether multiplexers feel like background processes or warm tabs.

This builds on prior work rather than duplicating it: #7639 (startup benchmark, closed no-action), #6530 (Node CLI startup cost, unmerged), #5402/#5405 (138 MB eager provider SDK loads), #5380/#6892 (extension transpile cost), #2522 (bundled entrypoint), #5804/#6594 (fast session load). The ask is a jcode-parity budget on top of those.

### How? (optional)

- Add the CI startup gate #7639 proposed: benchmark cold start and TUI first frame with a hard budget — e.g. first frame < 150 ms, or a 4× improvement over the current baseline — measured like jcode's README (10 interactive launches).
- Lazy-load the remaining eager work: provider SDKs at top level (#5402/#5405), jiti extension transpilation with a persistent disk cache (#5380/#6892), sequential package resolution.
- Investigate an entrypoint that skips the Node bootstrap path where possible: bundled single-file CLI (#2522) and fast paths for version/RPC (#6530), working toward a compiled artifact like jcode's Rust binary.

### What happened?

in bytes. Because mcp.json sets server and global defaults rather than per-tool limits, the most
specific value set wins:
1. _meta["pi/maxOutputBytes"] on the tool in tools/list (set by the server)
2. maxOutputBytes on the server entry in mcp.json (also pi.registerMcpServer)
3. top-level maxOutputBytes in mcp.json (project overrides global)
4. 20 KB default
read_mcp_resource and resource listings for one server use 2-4; across all servers they use 3-4.

### Why?

Some tools return schemas, file trees, or search results over 20 KB. pi keeps the start and end,
saves the full text to a temp file, and the model spends extra reads to get the middle back.
There is no way to raise or lower the limit. Codex sets it per tool in config
(output_token_limit) and Claude Code lets servers declare it per tool
(_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]).

An extension's tool_result hook is a poor fit: ToolInfo does not expose a tool's tools/list
_meta, and rebuilding the text from structuredContent means duplicating pi's unexported MCP
content conversion (resource links, embedded resources, binary temp files) after pi has already
cut the text and written a temp file. Per-tool values in _meta and per-server values in mcp.json
(next to timeout) also avoid relying on one global limit.

### How? (optional)

Everything stays in extensions/mcp/ except adding maxOutputBytes to the shared server config
type and validator in core/mcp-servers.ts. The MCP extension resolves the limit and passes it to
limitMcpContent. Values must be positive integers: invalid mcp.json values are reported as
config errors, invalid _meta values are ignored. Codemode scripts still get the full result.

I'd like to implement this. Branch with docs and tests:
https://github.com/buYoung/pi/tree/feat/mcp-max-output-bytes

issues.title: google-vertex: provider reports "No API key found" on Google Compute Engine, where credentials come from the metadata server

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**Environment**
- Pi 1.4.0 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`), Node 24.22.1, Ubuntu 24.04 on a Google Compute Engine VM
- No `gcloud` installed or logged in; no key file. The VM runs as a service account with `roles/aiplatform.user`, so Application Default Credentials come from the metadata server.
- `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global` set

**What happens**
`pi --provider google-vertex --model gemini-3.5-flash -p "say OK"` stops with `No API key found for google-vertex.` before any request is made. `pi --list-models` lists no `google-vertex` models.

**Why (from reading the code)**
The provider's readiness check (`providers/google-vertex.js`, `resolve`) only accepts: a stored credential, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY`, or the existence of a file (`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, or `~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json`). On GCE none of these exists, although the request itself would work: the underlying `@google/genai` client with `vertexai: true` uses Google's auth library, which falls back to the metadata server. We checked that directly: a small script calling `GoogleGenAI({ vertexai: true, project, location: "global" })` answered on the same VM.

**Workaround we use**
Putting Pi's documented placeholder as the provider's key in `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (`"google-vertex": { "apiKey": "gcp-vertex-credentials" }`) makes Pi skip the file check and use the auth library. With that, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.5 Flash and 3.8 Flash worked, including tool calls.

**Suggestion**
Treat ambient credentials as ready when the project and location are set and the metadata server is reachable (or when running on GCE/Cloud Run/GKE), or let the check pass when `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and location are set and report a real auth error at request time instead of "No API key found".

**Related note (not a bug report)**
Through an OpenAI-compatible Vertex endpoint, Gemini 3 tool calls fail with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` because the thought signature is not returned with the tool call. The native `google-vertex` provider handles it; a short note in the Vertex section of the providers documentation would save time.

issues.title: Configured default model is sometimes replaced by a fallback at startup

labels.name: last-read
labels.description: A marker label for triaging

issues.body:
### What happens

`defaultProvider`/`defaultModel` points at a model from a provider registered by an extension (its catalog is discovered from a gateway at runtime). In 4 of 20 startups the session began with `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` instead. That model is not the configured default; it is the built-in fallback described below.

### Why

`findInitialModel()` uses the configured default only when `hasConfiguredAuth(provider)` is true, and `ModelRuntime` can still report a freshly registered provider as unconfigured because concurrent availability passes cancel each other:

```ts
// packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts
if (seq !== this.availabilityRefreshSeq) return;   // superseded pass returns without publishing
```

Extension providers register immediately before the awaited availability pass, and every registration also starts an unawaited `refresh()`. When the awaited pass loses that race it resolves with a snapshot that predates its own request, so the configured default is skipped and `findInitialModel()` falls back to the first `defaultModelPerProvider` entry whose provider has configured auth (in my case `deepseek` → `deepseek-v4-pro`).

### Minimal reproduction

`packages/coding-agent/test/model-runtime-availability-refresh.test.ts` — two concurrent availability passes plus a gate on the credential listing, no extension involved. It fails on current main and passes with the fix.

### Fix

Publish by publication order instead of start order: a pass publishes when it is newer than the last published pass and did not start before the last state change. Concurrent passes stop cancelling each other, and a stale pass still cannot overwrite a newer snapshot.

Branch ready in my fork: `meetchen:fix/availability-refresh-publication-order`.

I would like to implement and submit this fix myself.

issues.title: pi.exec() crashes the whole process with RangeError: Invalid string length when a child's output exceeds the V8 string limit
issues.body:
### Summary

`pi.exec()` (the execution helper behind extension `pi.exec`) accumulates a child's stdout/stderr into unbounded strings. A subprocess that emits more output than V8's maximum string length (~536M chars) makes the string concatenation throw `RangeError: Invalid string length` **inside the `Socket` `data` callback**, which escapes as `uncaughtException` and kills the whole Pi process — every session in it, not just the tool call.

We hit this in real usage on Pi 1.4.0 (the process exited with):

```
pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
RangeError: Invalid string length
    at Socket.<anonymous> (.../dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-KHTE6L5W.js:706:2453)
    at Socket.emit (node:events:531:35)
    at addChunk (node:internal/streams/readable:561:12)
    at readableAddChunkPushByteMode (node:internal/streams/readable:512:3)
    at Readable.push (node:internal/streams/readable:392:5)
    at Pipe.onStreamRead (node:internal/stream_base_commons:189:23)
```

`chunk-KHTE6L5W.js:706:2453` maps to the stdout data handler in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/exec.ts`.

### Root cause

`execCommand()` has no output bound; it keeps concatenating whatever the child emits:

https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/1e42501bb8043cd0dd533f57af0d1ec4e05ba2ac/packages/coding-agent/src/core/exec.ts

```ts
stdout += stdoutDecoder.write(data);   // no cap on the accumulated string
...
stderr += stderrDecoder.write(data);
```

Present since the unified-extensions exec helper was introduced; identical in v1.3.0 and v1.4.0. #11326 fixed the *decoding* of each chunk (multi-byte characters split across pipe chunks) but not the *accumulation* — the decoded string still grows without bound, so the crash above is still reachable on current `main` (`1e42501bb`).

### Repro

Any extension calling:

```ts
await pi.exec(process.execPath, ["-e", 'process.stdout.write("a".repeat(600 * 1024 * 1024))'], cwd);
```

The child only wrote ~600 MB — well within any reasonable tool-run — but the host process dies with `RangeError: Invalid string length` instead of the tool call failing. Because the throw happens inside a stream callback, it is not catchable by the caller; the extension cannot handle it, and anything else running in the same process goes down with it. The offending child is left running.

### Suggested semantics

A tool execution helper should fail like a tool call, not take the host down:

- bound the **combined** stdout+stderr bytes (we use 16 MiB downstream);
- once the cap is hit: stop draining the streams, terminate the child (SIGTERM, then escalate based on actual child exit), and return a normal result — nonzero exit with an explicit `output exceeded ... bytes; output is incomplete` indication — never a silent truncation that reads as success;
- (optionally, opt-in) record metadata-only diagnostics — counts and termination state, never output or arguments — so the original producer of oversized output can be identified after the fact.

This is the same crash class as #8028 (TUI `fullRender` clamped for the same reason), just on the exec path. We have been running the bound described above downstream since 2026-10-24 (with regression tests for: 17 MiB producer → capped 16 MiB + nonzero + explicit marker + following command still works; normal-sized output unaffected). Happy to send a PR if the approach sounds right.

issues.title: Durable: host coding-agent extensions (AgentSession-backed runtime or hook parity)
issues.body:
> AI-written: an AI agent drafted this issue on behalf of @SiebertLanhove from our integration notes.

### What do you want to change?

Let pi-durable host coding-agent extensions: either an AgentSession-backed Durable runtime, or Durable hooks with parity for the `ExtensionAPI` events extensions rely on.

Today (pi-durable 1.0.0, pi-coding-agent 0.99.1 and 1.0.0) an extension cannot run under `Harness`:
- `beforeCompact` returns only `{ decline }` or `{ summary }`. `session_before_compact` handlers mutate `customInstructions` or return a `CompactionResult` with `details`.
- `afterResponse` and `afterTools` are void, so `message_end` replacement and `turn_end` continuations have no counterpart.
- Tool registrations have no exposure tiers or `prepareLoadout`, which `setActiveTools` loaders and codemode use.
- `AgentSession` builds requests from `SessionManager`, whose synchronous `appendEntry`/`getBranch` ids extensions keep as state. Durable's transcript is separate and its commits are asynchronous.

The experimental durable agent lists "extensions" under "Not here".

### Why?

We run headless sub-agents through the SDK. Our extension-free roles moved to pi-durable 1.0.0: 45 forced SIGKILL recoveries (15 each for 3 roles), 0 duplicate completed tool steps, 1.8 to 2.9 ms/step SQLite cost. Agents whose profile uses compaction, session/context, dynamic-loadout or provider hooks must stay on `AgentSession` without step recovery. A local port of `AgentSession` onto Durable would be a second runtime to maintain against both packages.

### How? (optional)

A durable-backed `SessionManager` projection plus a replacing `afterResponse` and a richer `beforeCompact` would cover most of our cases. Is this planned?

issues.title: pi-env: exec hangs when a pipe-reader or waiter thread fails to start

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

﻿When the daemon cannot start one of an exec's pipe-reader or waiter threads, it panics instead of returning an error. This can happen when a job reaches its cgroup task limit.

Only the request's thread unwinds. The exec never gets a reply, cancellation no longer works, and the child keeps running. The daemon continues answering other requests, so the client waits indefinitely.

```text
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at .../std/src/thread/functions.rs:131:29:
failed to spawn thread: Os { code: 11, kind: WouldBlock, message: "Resource temporarily unavailable" }
```

The pipe readers and waiter use `std::thread::spawn` in `exec.rs` (lines 221 and 318). A job reaching its task limit therefore hangs instead of returning an error the caller can handle.

### Steps to reproduce

﻿1. Start the pi-env daemon through `new Connection({ command: [...] })`, wrapping its command with `systemd-run --user --scope -p TasksMax=28 -- <daemon>`.
2. Start an exec running `sleep 30` every 500 ms, without waiting for earlier execs to finish.
3. Once thread creation fails, cancel all the execs.

The last exec admitted before the failure never replies, even after cancellation. Later execs receive `spawn_error`. I reproduced the same behavior with `TasksMax=32` and `TasksMax=36`.

### Expected behavior

﻿The exec should return `spawn_error` when a required thread cannot be started. Any child already spawned should be killed and reaped, so the failed exec neither hangs the caller nor leaves a command running.

`main.rs` already uses `thread::Builder::spawn` and returns an error when the request's own thread cannot start. The pipe readers and waiter should use the same fallible API, with cleanup if any of those threads fail to start.

### Version

pi-env 1.3.0; affected code also present in 1.4.0.

issues.title: stripAnsi leaves private-parameter CSI payloads in tool output (ESC[<...M mouse reports, ESC[>...c replies)
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

`stripAnsi` in `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/ansi.ts` treats `<`, `=` and `>` as a valid CSI final byte, so for these sequences it strips only the first three bytes and leaves the parameters as text:

| input | returns |
| --- | --- |
| `ESC [ < 35 ; 59 ; 1 M` (SGR mouse report) | `35;59;1M` |
| `ESC [ > 0 ; 276 ; 0 c` (device attributes reply) | `0;276;0c` |
| `ESC [ 3 8 ; 5 ; 1 9 6 m` (control) | `` |

A private parameter byte should only belong to the sequence when digits or `;`/`:` follow it.

### Why?

The transcript renders tool output through `getTextOutput()`, which is `sanitizeBinaryOutput(stripAnsi(text))` (`src/core/tools/render-utils.ts:67`). `sanitizeBinaryOutput` then drops the leftover ESC, because `0x1B` is inside `[\x0E-\x1F]`, so the parameters get drawn as ordinary characters. On 1.4.0, `node -e "process.stdout.write('\u001b[<35;59;1Mstep 1\n')"` through the bash tool shows `35;59;1Mstep 1`.

The sanitizer also contradicts the input side of this repo: `packages/tui/src/stdin-buffer.ts:113` already parses this shape as one sequence (`/^<\d+;\d+;\d+[Mm]$/`). 8bf2bfab aligned `stripAnsi` with chalk `strip-ansi`, so the current behavior is deliberate. I think correctness wins for this one shape, since the two halves of pi disagree about it.

### How?

Insert `"[<=>]?(?:\\d{1,4}(?:[;:]\\d{0,4})*)?"` before the final byte, leave `CSI_FINAL` alone. Patch and two regression tests are ready: 0 of 237 existing cases change, and in a 720-case sweep only the 432 private-parameter shapes change. I can send a PR after `lgtm`.

issues.title: TUI freezes after entering an API key in /login when the pi.dev model catalog is unreachable
issues.body:
# TUI freezes after entering an API key in `/login` when the pi.dev model catalog is unreachable

## Summary

`ModelRuntime.login()` awaits a post-login model refresh with **no `AbortSignal` and no timeout**.
That refresh makes every credentialed built-in provider fetch its remote model catalog from
`https://pi.dev/api/models/providers/<id>` via a bare `fetch()`. If the connection to `pi.dev`
blackholes (firewall / GFW / corporate proxy silently dropping packets — i.e. no RST, no response),
the fetch promise never settles, `login()` never returns, and the entire TUI freezes right after the
user submits an API key. Pressing Esc does not help, because the login dialog's abort signal is never
wired into the refresh.

The startup path already guards the identical refresh with a 15s `AbortController`; the login path
simply lacks the same protection.

## Environment

- pi-coding-agent 0.82.0 (npm global install), Node v24.13.1, macOS
- Network behind a firewall that drops (not rejects) outbound connections to `pi.dev`

## Reproduction

1. Have a stored credential for any built-in provider (e.g. `openrouter` API key or `openai-codex`
   OAuth in `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`), so its catalog qualifies for refresh.
2. Make `https://pi.dev` blackhole (e.g. firewall rule that DROPs packets, or a network where it is
   unreachable without proxy).
3. `/login` any provider and enter an API key (or re-login when `models-store.json`'s `checkedAt`
   is older than 4h).
4. The credential is saved, then the UI freezes forever.

## Root cause

`packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts` (dist: `core/model-runtime.js`):

```js
async login(providerId, type, interaction) {
    const credential = await this.models.login(providerId, type, interaction);
    await this.refresh({ allowNetwork: this.modelNetworkEnabled }); // no signal, no timeout
    return credential;
}
```

Contrast with `ModelRuntime.create()` a few lines above, which wraps the same refresh in a 15s
`AbortController` (`options.modelRefreshTimeoutMs ?? 15_000`).

The refresh reaches `withRemoteCatalog()` (`core/remote-catalog-provider.js`), whose
`refreshModels()` does:

```js
const response = await fetch(url, { headers: {...}, signal: context.signal });
```

On the login path `context.signal` is `undefined`, so this `fetch` has no timeout at all.
`logout()` and `removeRuntimeApiKey()` call the same unprotected refresh.

Note the freeze is **not** caused by the provider the user is logging into — the catalog fetch goes
to `pi.dev` for *other* credentialed built-in providers.

## Expected behavior

`login()` should complete (or fail gracefully) within a bounded time regardless of catalog
reachability, and the login dialog's cancel (Esc) should abort the wait.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the startup path: pass an `AbortSignal` to the post-login/logout refresh, combining a
timeout with the dialog's signal. This is the local patch I am running (works, verified):

```js
async login(providerId, type, interaction) {
    const credential = await this.models.login(providerId, type, interaction);
    await this.refreshWithTimeout(interaction?.signal);
    return credential;
}

async refreshWithTimeout(parentSignal) {
    const timeoutMs = Number.parseInt(process.env.PI_MODEL_REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS ?? "", 10) || 15000;
    const signals = [AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)];
    if (parentSignal) signals.push(parentSignal);
    await this.refresh({ allowNetwork: this.modelNetworkEnabled, signal: AbortSignal.any(signals) });
}
```

(`logout()` and `removeRuntimeApiKey()` get the same treatment.)

The downstream code already handles aborts gracefully: `ModelsImpl.refresh()` swallows per-provider
abort errors and falls back to the cached catalog.

## Verification of the patch

With `fetch` to `pi.dev` monkeypatched to hang forever (honoring abort):

- before: `login()` never resolves (this is the reported freeze);
- after: `login()` resolves in ~timeout ms; with `interaction.signal` aborted it resolves
  immediately even with a 10-minute timeout configured.

## Workaround for affected users

Start pi with `PI_OFFLINE=1` (or `--offline`), which makes the post-login refresh run with
`allowNetwork: false` and skip the catalog fetch entirely.

stack trace is printed.

2. Press `Ctrl+G`.

The configured external editor opens, and pi resumes when the editor exits.

issues.title: [bug] GLM (Zhipu) HTTP 429 code 1308 (5-hour usage cap) is retried instead of failing fast

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

GLM (Zhipu / BigModel, `open.bigmodel.cn`) answers a request with HTTP 429 and a **hard 5-hour usage cap**:

```json
{"code":"1308","message":"已达到 5 小时的使用上限。您的限额将在 2026-10-29 02:54:39 重置。"}
```

`1308` is Zhipu's "5-hour usage limit reached" code. It is not a transient throttle — the limit resets in hours, so every retry is guaranteed to fail with the same answer.

pi retries it anyway, because both retry layers classify 429 as retryable without looking at the response body:

1. `packages/ai/src/utils/provider-retry.ts` — `isRetryableProviderError()` retries every `status === 429`. With `retry.provider.maxRetries: 12` the same request is re-sent 12 times before the call gives up.
2. `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts` — `isRetryableAssistantError()` matches the `"429"` entry of `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN` and none of `NON_RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_LIMIT_ERROR_PATTERN`, so the agent-level retry (`settings.retry.maxRetries`) fires on top of that.

The run therefore spends minutes on pointless requests and only then ends with:

```
Error: 429: {"code":"1308","message":"已达到 5 小时的使用上限。您的限额将在 2026-10-29 02:54:39 重置。"}
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Zhipu/GLM key against `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4` (or the Anthropic-compatible `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/anthropic`).
2. Use the account until the 5-hour cap is reached, then send any prompt.
3. Observe: repeated provider requests/retries for the same prompt, followed by the final `Error: 429: {...}` message above.

### Expected behavior

A 429 carrying Zhipu error code `1308` should be classified as a terminal quota/limit error:

- no provider-level and no agent-level retries (the body is already in `errorMessage`, so the existing text-pattern classifier in `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts` is enough for the agent-level loop),
- the error is surfaced immediately, ideally including the reset timestamp Zhipu reports in the message, so the user knows when to come back.

The same body is returned by both the OpenAI-compatible and the Anthropic-compatible Zhipu endpoints, so one classification covers both.

### Version

pi 1.4.0 (upstream `main` at the time of reporting).

issues.title: pi-durable: let durable tasks keep the conversation busy
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Kinda related to my previous #11141. I'd like a way for a task to keep the conversation busy (no new input while it runs).

My use case: at the end of a turn, I want to create a task that captures a git checkpoint snapshot of the whole repo. This task has two requirements:

1. It can't be cancelled by `Conversation.abort()`, otherwise it could produce corrupted snapshots
2. It has to keep the conversation busy: users shouldn't be able to prompt while it runs, because a new turn could write files mid-snapshot.

I can't find a way to do this in the current durable. The naive way to check whether a session is busy is to look at `live.run`: if it's defined, the session is busy (no more messages allowed); if it's undefined, it's idle.

This works fine, but tasks don't change `live.run`; only generation tasks do. So one could think: "I'll make my host's busy check look at both `live.run` and foreground (`background: false`) tasks". Only foreground, because background tasks should in fact stay in the background and not block. Then I'll create my checkpoint task as foreground.

This could work, but it raises two issues:

1. Foreground tasks are always cancelled by `Conversation.abort()`, with no way to opt out. I could live with that and make the checkpoint task handle its own abort.
2. It breaks manual compaction. Manual compaction should run in the background, yet it should be cancellable. How should it be classified? If it's `background: false`, then to keep conversing while it compacts, the busy check must NOT look at foreground tasks, otherwise the session is marked busy and you can't continue. If it's `background: true`, it's no longer cancelled by `abort()`, and idle waits stop including it.


### Why?

Without this, a host has to enforce busy itself while such a task runs, and other clients or extensions on the same session don't see it.

### How? (optional)

_No response_

issues.title: pi-durable: make extension start a task on each turn without a tool call
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

I'm not sure if I'm missing an existing pattern, so this is partly a question.

I'd like an extension to start its own task on every turn, with the same lifecycle as manual compaction: conversation-owned, cancelled by `abort()`, included in idle waits. As far as I can tell, extension code can only create tasks from a tool's `execute` or from another task. Hooks can't commit, and `conversationCreated` is host-only.

### Why?

Example: run the project's tests after each turn that edited files. The conversation should stay busy until they finish, Stop should cancel them, a restart mid-run should resume, and the result should be saved for the UI and the next turn. A task fits all of that, but:

- A tool only runs if the model calls it.
- `onYield` runs before the answer is committed, so a long test run delays it, and a hook can't save the result.

Today the host has to create the task itself, but this does not give the users of such hosts the power to create similar extensions themselves.

issues.title: `pi update --extensions` reports success without upgrading (check uses `npm view`, install uses `@latest`): update banner loops after every restart

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## What happens

1. pi starts and shows the banner: `Package Updates Available … Run pi update --extensions … Packages: - billion-context`.
2. I run `pi update --extensions`. It shows progress and finishes without an error.
3. I restart pi. The same banner lists the same package again. Identical on every attempt. It only stopped when I ran the command again ~10 minutes later.

pi 1.4.0 (managed npm install), Linux. Package: `billion-context`, configured in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` as `npm:billion-context`, installed into the pi-managed root `~/.pi/agent/npm/`.

## Timeline (measured from file mtimes + registry publish time, CET)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 16:24:32 | `billion-context` 0.1.209 published, `latest` dist-tag moves (registry `time`: `2026-10-28T15:24:32.406Z`) |
| 16:24:38 | `pi update --extensions` runs → `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/billion-context` is **still 0.1.208**; `~/.pi/agent/npm/package.json` spec rewritten as `"^0.1.208"` (mtime `2026-10-28 16:24:38 +0100`) — npm resolved pre-publish metadata |
| 16:25:36 | pi starts, banner appears (check sees 0.1.209, installed is 0.1.208) |
| 16:25 → 16:33 | several more `pi update --extensions` runs, all effectively no-ops; installed stays 0.1.208; banner keeps coming back after each restart |
| 16:33:55 | a run finally lands 0.1.209 (spec `"^0.1.209"`), banner gone |

## Why: the banner and the updater read different sources of truth

Line numbers below are for the shipped 1.4.0 build `dist/core/package-manager.js`, mapped through its source map to `packages/coding-agent/src/core/package-manager.ts`.

- **Banner:** `checkForPackageUpdates` (`interactive-mode.js`) → `package-manager.js:944` / `ts:1222` `checkForAvailableUpdates` → `js:1204` / `ts:1525` `npmHasAvailableUpdate` → `js:1229` / `ts:1550` `getLatestNpmVersion`, which shells out to `npm view <name> version --json` (full packument, `Accept: application/json`).
- **Update:** `update()` → `updateConfiguredSources` → `js:914` / `ts:1187` `shouldUpdateNpmSource` → `js:926` / `ts:1199` `updateNpmBatch` (specs `<name>@latest`) → `js:940` / `ts:1217` `installNpmBatch` → `js:1505` / `ts:1850` `getNpmInstallArgs` → `npm install <name>@latest --prefix <installRoot> --legacy-peer-deps` — npm resolves the **abbreviated** install metadata (`Accept: application/vnd.npm.install-v1+json`).

Those two registry documents are cached independently: registry.npmjs.org answers `cache-control: public, max-age=300` with an `age:` header, and npm reuses its own `~/.npm/_cacache` entries by etag. Measured on this package, they are different documents with different etags:

```
Accept: application/json                    27,467,984 bytes  etag "5d47b2ddd7a7da34…"
Accept: application/vnd.npm.install-v1+json  9,199,638 bytes  etag "86809dac608ed5b7…"
```

`billion-context` is an extreme case for this: 6877 versions and 685 dist-tags (CI publishes per-PR builds), so both documents are multi-megabyte and can lag several minutes after a publish. Net effect: `npm view` already reports 0.1.209 while `npm install pkg@latest` still resolves 0.1.208.

## The pi-side problem

This is not only npm behaviour:

1. `updateNpmBatch` / `installNpmBatch` (`ts:1199-1219`) never re-read the installed version after npm returns. pi reports success for an update that did not happen, and the user cannot tell "nothing to do" apart from "npm served stale metadata".
2. The startup banner re-flags the same package indefinitely, so the user loops `pi update --extensions` with no signal that they are actually waiting for registry/CDN metadata freshness — it looks like a broken updater.
3. The check decides what `latest` is, then the install asks npm to resolve `latest` a second time: the version pi announced is never the version pi requests.

Related but distinct reports: #10132 (reports "Updated packages" while pinned specs are skipped), #10055 and #8207 (installs the old version under pnpm), #10983 (asked for old → new version output, closed as no-action — that output alone would have made this visible).

## Expected behaviour

- After an update, compare the installed version against the version that was flagged; if it did not advance, say so, e.g. `billion-context still 0.1.208 — registry metadata may be stale, try again in a few minutes`, instead of a silent success.
- Resolve once and pin it: take the version from `getLatestNpmVersion` and install `<name>@<thatVersion>` so check and install cannot disagree.
- Do not re-banner a package whose update was just attempted in the same run with no version change (or show it as a distinct "attempted, version unchanged" state).

## Repro

Not deterministic, but reproducible whenever registry metadata for a package is stale — typically within ~10 minutes after that package publishes, worst for packages with very large packuments (thousands of versions / many dist-tags).

Run `pi update --extensions` within a minute or two of a new publish of a package you use. It finishes without error while `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/<pkg>/package.json` and the `^` spec in `~/.pi/agent/npm/package.json` still show the old version, and the banner returns at next start. The mismatch is visible with:

```bash
jq -r .version ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/<pkg>/package.json   # installed
npm view <pkg> version                                           # what the banner used
```

## Workaround

Run `pi update --extensions` again after ~5–10 minutes (registry `max-age=300` + npm cache), or `npm cache clean --force` right before it. `pi --offline` / `PI_OFFLINE=1` silences the banner (`npmHasAvailableUpdate` returns false early when `isOfflineModeEnabled()`, `ts:1525`) but also disables model catalog refresh, the pi self-version check and managed tool downloads, so it is not a clean mute button.

Side note (possibly a separate issue): `bili plugin list` reported the stale version for a pi-managed npm extension — `Installed version: 0.1.208` while `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/billion-context/package.json` already read `0.1.209` — i.e. it read a global npm copy instead of the copy its own text says is pi-managed.

I also submitted this through `/bug` (anonymous upload) on 2026-10-28; filing here for discoverability.

issues.body:
### What happened?

Recovery `context_edit` entries that omit a failed/aborted response newer than the last successful usage report invalidate that report, although its covered prefix is unchanged. The counter falls back to estimating all history, which can inflate context usage and trigger unnecessary compaction.

Reproduced offline using only `SessionManager.inMemory()` and the core counter, without loading extensions or making provider calls.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Append a user message containing `"x".repeat(40000)`, then a successful assistant message with text `"answer"` and usage `{ input: 4000, output: 100, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, totalTokens: 4100 }`.
2. Append user text `"next"`, followed by an assistant message with `stopReason: "error"`, empty content, and zero usage. `estimateProjectedContextTokens(session.buildSessionProjection(), session.getBranch())` returns **4,101**, including 4,100 usage tokens.
3. Call `session.appendContextEdit(failedId, null)` and estimate again: **10,003**, with `usageTokens: 0`. Only the failed suffix was removed.

### Expected behavior

Keep the valid 4,100-token usage and estimate the remaining suffix: **4,101**. Edits targeting the usage entry or its preceding history, and later compaction, should still invalidate it.

A small local fix checks the edit target position and preserves the expected result. I have a fix and regression cases prepared and would like to submit a PR after maintainer approval. Repository-wide checks are pending checkout dependencies.

### Version

Pi 1.4.0; the same condition remains on main at `a2c5657c86d38e5b330e72f27b2f0134c1e0b322`. Node 26.12.1, Arch Linux x86_64.

issues.title: Git package ports collide: install B keeps A, remove B deletes A

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Git remotes differing only by port share one package identity and checkout. `pi install B` reports success but keeps A's repository and replaces A's settings entry with B. Removing either URL can then remove the other's state.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Serve two different Git repositories at `http://127.0.0.1:18080/team/pi-tools.git` (marker A) and port `18081` (marker B). Direct `git clone` returns the correct contents from each.
2. In an empty directory, use a fresh profile with no extensions:
   ```sh
   export PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
   pi install http://127.0.0.1:18080/team/pi-tools.git --no-approve
   pi install http://127.0.0.1:18081/team/pi-tools.git --no-approve
   ```
3. After the second install, settings contain only B, but the checkout's origin and marker are still A. B receives zero requests during that install.
4. Separately, with a fresh profile containing only A, `pi remove http://127.0.0.1:18081/team/pi-tools.git --no-approve` exits 0 and deletes A's settings entry and checkout.

Reproduced twice with the released CLI and real repositories on loopback HTTP servers. Package subcommands reject `-ne`; these runs used empty profiles/projects and `--no-approve`.

### Expected behavior

Different ports must keep independent package state. Git parsing drops the port from `host`; package matching and cache paths use `host/path`.

I'd like to implement the fix and regression tests. Could a maintainer grant `lgtm` for a PR?

### Version

1.4.0 official npm release, Node 26.0.0, macOS arm64. Affected logic is unchanged on main `b2fcfee0835b7b09a2d34611442608b3925ac279`.

prs.title: Anthropic message threads
prs.body:
Anthropic can keep a conversation on the server (message threads beta).
A request can then continue from the previous reply and send only the
new messages, instead of the whole history every turn.

pi uses this when a session id is set and caching is on. It still builds
the full request, compares it with the previous one, and only sends the
new part if nothing earlier changed.

- Default: on only for the anthropic provider on api.anthropic.com.
  Gateways that drop unknown fields would lose the conversation.
  Override with compat.supportsMessageThreads.
- If the server rejects a continuation, pi resends the full request
  as a new thread. Other errors turn threads off for the session.
- New option StreamOptions.disableContinuation. The cache warmer sets
  it so warm requests don't replace the session's thread.
- cleanupSessionResources(sessionId) frees a session's thread state.

prs.title: fix(env): kill the daemon's commands when it is terminated
prs.body:
`Connection.close()` left running commands behind on a local Unix daemon.

`close()` ends the daemon's stdin and immediately sends `SIGTERM` (`connection.ts` `#teardown`). The daemon did not handle `SIGTERM`, so it died before reaching the `kill_all` it runs when stdin ends. A running command was reparented to init and kept going:

1. `env.exec(["sh", "-c", "exec sleep 30"])` on a local daemon.
2. `connection.close()`.
3. `sleep 30` keeps running with ppid 1.

This contradicts `docs/protocol.md` ("kills every process group it started ... when stdin ends") and `close()`'s doc ("it kills everything it started"). SSH connections were not affected: `SIGTERM` reaches the `ssh` client, and the remote daemon then sees stdin end.

## Changes
- `sys::on_exit_signal` (Unix): blocks `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT` and `SIGHUP` before any other thread starts, so every thread inherits the blocked mask, and waits for them with `sigwait` on its own thread. `serve()` uses it to kill every process group and exit with 128 + the signal. Commands are unaffected: `exec` and `pty` reset the signal mask in `pre_exec`, and std resets it for other children.
- Windows: no-op, and the problem remains there. Node's `child.kill()` on Windows is `TerminateProcess`, which, like `SIGKILL`, cannot be caught, so the daemon never runs `kill_all`. Its job object (`JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`) still kills each command's own process, but processes that one started leave the job (`JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK`, as in libuv) and keep running. The code comment and `docs/protocol.md` now say so. Fixing it needs the client to let the daemon act on the end of stdin before killing it (a grace period in `#teardown`); that is left for a follow-up.
- `docs/protocol.md` lists the signals and the Windows limit under Liveness.

## Testing
- New regression test in `test/remote.test.ts`: starts a command, closes the connection, and checks the command's process is gone. It fails against the previous daemon and passes with this change. Skipped on Windows, where the behavior is unchanged.
- `packages/env` vitest suite on Linux: 93 passed (SSH suites skipped, no SSH target). `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` for Linux, macOS, Android and Windows targets. `npm run check` passes.
- Not run on Windows or macOS; the Windows change is a no-op.

prs.title: fix(env): fail exec and pty with spawn_error when a helper thread cannot start
prs.body:
The pi-env daemon started an `exec`'s stdout and stderr readers and its waiter with `thread::spawn`. `thread::spawn` panics when no thread can be created, for example when a cgroup `TasksMax` or `RLIMIT_NPROC` limit is reached. When that happened after the child was already running:
- only the request thread unwound, so the exec never got a reply;
- its control channel was dropped, so `cancel` and `kill` reached nobody;
- the child kept running, even after the daemon exited.

`pty` started its reader, input writer and waiter threads the same way.

## Changes
- `exec.rs`: `spawn_reader` now uses `thread::Builder::spawn` and returns an `io::Result`. If a reader or the waiter cannot start, `run` sets `stop`, interrupts any readers already started, kills the process group, reaps the child, removes it from `groups`, and returns `spawn_error`.
- The waiter thread now gets the `Child` through a channel once it is running. If the waiter cannot start, the child stays with the caller, which can still reap it. Before, the failed thread's closure dropped the child without waiting for it.
- `pty.rs`: the same handling for the reader, writer and waiter threads. On failure the terminal is also removed from `terminals`.

## Testing
- Manual reproduction with a script that runs the daemon as `prlimit --nproc=N -- pi-env`. It starts 30 `sleep 30` execs 200 ms apart, aborts them all, then closes the connection. N ran from 37 to 70.
  - Before: for most N, one or two execs stayed pending forever after abort, and a `sleep 30` kept running after the daemon was closed.
  - After: every exec settles, either `aborted` or `spawn_error`, and no `sleep` is left running.
- `cargo build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test` all pass. The `packages/env` vitest suite passes (78 passed), and `npm run check` passes.
- There is no automated regression test. A thread-creation failure cannot be triggered reliably in a test: `RLIMIT_NPROC` counts all of the user's tasks and does not apply to root, and the daemon has no fault-injection hook.
- The Windows build was not compiled. The `exec.rs` change uses only existing cross-platform calls, and the `pty.rs` change is Unix-only.

Fixes #11433

Requested by @petrroll

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): strip private-parameter CSI sequences in stripAnsi
prs.body:
`stripAnsi` treated `<`, `=` and `>` after `ESC [` as final bytes. For control sequences with a private prefix it removed only `ESC[<` and left the parameters as text:

```
ESC[<35;59;1Mstep 1   ->  35;59;1Mstep 1   (SGR mouse report)
ESC[>0;276;0c         ->  0;276;0c         (secondary device attributes reply)
```

The fix accepts one private prefix byte only directly after a CSI introducer (`ESC [` or `0x9B`):

```
(?:(?:\u001B\[|\u009B)[<=>]|[\u001B\u009B][[\]()#;?]*)(params)?FINAL
```

Adding `[<=>]?` to the shared start of the pattern, as #11541 does, also treats `=`, `>` and `<` after a bare ESC as a prefix. `ESC =` / `ESC >` are complete keypad-mode sequences (terminfo `smkx=\E[?1h\E=`, `rmkx=\E[?1l\E>`, printed by readline, less and man). With the shared prefix, they take the digits of the text that follows:

```
ESC[?1l ESC>42 files   ->  " files"   (expected "42 files")
```

This change keeps that case as before. A chunk that ends in a bare `ESC=` is also no longer held back while streaming.

Tests:
- private-prefix sequences are stripped whole, including the 8-bit `0x9B` form
- digits after `ESC=`, `ESC>` and `ESC<` are kept
- `splitIncompleteAnsiSuffix` holds back an unfinished `ESC[<…`, but not a bare `ESC=`
- the chalk `strip-ansi` compatibility test still passes

closes #11377

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): strip private-parameter CSI sequences in stripAnsi
prs.body:
`stripAnsi` did not allow a private prefix byte (`<`, `=`, `>`) before the parameters of a CSI sequence (the `ESC [` family of terminal control codes). `CSI_FINAL` accepts those bytes as the closing byte, so for `ESC[<35;59;1M` (an SGR mouse report) the regex treated `ESC[<` as the whole sequence and left `35;59;1M` in the text. The same happened with `ESC[>0;276;0c` (a device-attributes reply). `sanitizeBinaryOutput` then removed the leftover ESC, so the parameters appeared as plain text in tool output and `!` command output.

This change adds an optional `[<=>]?` after the intermediate characters in `CSI_START`, so the prefix and its parameters are stripped as part of the sequence. `unfinishedAnsiAtEndRegex` reuses `CSI_START`, so a private sequence split at the end of a streamed chunk is now held back as well. Sequences without a private prefix behave as before. The generated compatibility cases that compare against chalk `strip-ansi` still pass.

**Testing**
- Added a case to `test/ansi-utils.test.ts` covering `ESC[<…M`, `ESC[<…m`, `ESC[>…c`, `ESC[=…h` and the 8-bit `\x9b<…M` form. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- Ran `test/ansi-utils.test.ts`, `test/tools.test.ts` and the bash executor/execution tests, and `npm run check`.
- Before: `stripAnsi("\x1b[<35;59;1Mstep 1")` returned `"35;59;1Mstep 1"` and `stripAnsi("\x1b[>0;276;0c")` returned `"0;276;0c"`. After: they return `"step 1"` and `""`.

Fixes #11377

Requested by @petrroll

prs.title: fix(tui,coding-agent): handle selection page keys in all scrolling lists
prs.body:
Fixes #7629. Supersedes #7680 by @muyiyr (co-author): same approach, rebased on current `main`, narrowed in scope, with a generic fullscreen capture flag instead of a page-key-specific one.

## Problem

`tui.select.pageUp` / `tui.select.pageDown` are configurable, but most lists ignore them:

- `SelectList` (slash commands, file autocomplete, theme/thinking pickers) and `SettingsList` (`/settings`) do not handle them.
- Editor autocomplete forwards only up/down to its list.
- Model, scoped models, auth, user message, llama search, and `/mcp` selectors have their own navigation without page keys.

In fullscreen mode there is a second problem: `tui.altScreen.pageUp/pageDown` default to the same keys and always scroll the transcript, so even a list that handles the keys never receives them.

With the remapping from the issue (`"tui.select.pageDown": "ctrl+v"`), Ctrl+V in an open autocomplete menu also pastes an image, because `app.clipboard.pasteImage` runs first.

## Changes

- `getSelectPageIndex()` (pi-tui): returns the index one page up/down, clamped to the list bounds. Used by `SelectList`, `SettingsList`, and the coding-agent selectors. Page keys clamp at the ends; up/down keep their existing wrap behavior.
- `Component.capturesViewportInput?: boolean`: while a component that sets it has focus, fullscreen viewport keys go to it instead of the transcript, the same rule focused overlays already follow on `main`. Transcript search and mouse wheel are unchanged. Set by `SelectList`, `SettingsList`, `Editor` (only while autocomplete is open), and the scrolling coding-agent selectors (session/tree selectors not while renaming or editing a label).
- `CustomEditor`: while autocomplete is open, page keys reach the menu before app actions, following the existing precedence exception for history keys.

Not set on `ctx.ui.select`, trust, first-time setup, and thinking selectors: they show every option, so there is nothing to page, and the transcript stays scrollable while answering an extension prompt (see #10769).

## Behavior change

In fullscreen mode, PageUp/PageDown move an open list or autocomplete menu instead of scrolling the transcript. Like with focused overlays, the other viewport keys (Ctrl+Home/End, prompt jumps) also go to the list, where they do nothing; mouse wheel and transcript search still work. Outside fullscreen mode, default bindings behave as before.

Extension UIs that wrap a list in their own component must expose `capturesViewportInput` (see the `preset.ts` and `tools.ts` examples); otherwise they keep the old behavior.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- Other selection keys vs app actions while autocomplete is open, e.g. `tui.select.up` remapped to Ctrl+P still cycles the model (#2133, #10408).
- `/resume` checks `app.session.*` before selection keys.
- Remaining hardcoded keys and key hints (scoped models Escape/Ctrl+C, `pi config` Ctrl+C, synthetic Enter in searchable submenus).
- #4748: extensions using their own pi-tui copy see default keybindings.

## Testing

- `npm run check`
- pi-tui: `SelectList`, `SettingsList`, editor autocomplete, and `TuiAltScreen` capture tests (all `node --test` pi-tui tests pass)
- coding-agent: model selector with remapped Ctrl+V/Alt+V, `CustomEditor` Ctrl+V paging vs image paste, searchable settings submenu, `/mcp` menu capture
- fullscreen: a focused `SelectList` keeps PageDown and Ctrl+Home away from the transcript; closing editor autocomplete gives PageUp back to the transcript

Stacked on #11371. Addresses #5363 for Bedrock API keys.

pi lists 16 Bedrock models that Bedrock only serves on Mantle, its OpenAI-compatible endpoint: OpenAI GPT-5.4 through GPT-6.1, gpt-oss, Grok 4.3/4.6, and Gemma 4. pi sends them to Converse, which rejects them as invalid model identifiers. models.dev v2 lists each model's APIs, so the catalog now maps models without a Converse API to the Responses API at the Mantle URL models.dev gives, with `{region}` filled in per request.
