prs.title: feat(ai): SigV4/IAM auth for Bedrock Mantle, plus strict mode, Daybreak models, and overflow detection
prs.body:
Stacked on #11372, which routes Mantle-only Bedrock models through the OpenAI Responses API with Bedrock API keys. This PR adds the IAM/profile auth that #11372 leaves for later, plus a few catalog gaps.

## SigV4 auth for Mantle

With #11372, AWS profile and IAM users get an error on Mantle models. Mantle accepts SigV4-signed HTTP requests ([docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/bedrock-mantle.html): "AWS credentials (supported for HTTP requests)"), so when no Bedrock API key is set, pi now signs each request instead:

- **Credentials** resolve like Converse: a profile from `/login amazon-bedrock` wins over ambient access keys, which win over the AWS default chain (profiles, SSO, ECS task roles, web identity).
- **Signing service** is `bedrock-mantle`. Mantle rejects any other scope ("Credential should be scoped to correct service: 'bedrock-mantle'").
- **Bedrock API keys** still win when set, so #11372's behavior is unchanged for them.
- **IAM permission:** the principal needs `bedrock-mantle:CreateInference`.

**No new packages.** `@smithy/signature-v4` and `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node` are already installed through `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime`. They're now declared at the versions it already resolves, so the lockfile changes by two lines. Hashing uses `node:crypto`, not `@aws-crypto`. This replaces the earlier version of this PR, which used `@aws/bedrock-token-generator`.

**Bundling** follows the Converse pattern: the signer lives in a Node-only `bedrock-mantle-sigv4.ts`, loaded through a variable-specifier import so browser bundles skip it. The Bun binary registers it with `setBedrockMantleSigV4Module`, like `setBedrockProviderModule`.

## Catalog and errors

- **Strict tool schemas:** #11372's Mantle compat drops `supportsStrictMode`, which the Converse branch sets from models.dev `structured_output`. This PR keeps it for Mantle models that report structured output.
- **Daybreak models:** `openai.gpt-5.6-cyber` (Daybreak Red) and `openai.gpt-daybreak-blue-5.6-sol` (Daybreak Blue) are on AWS's [model cards](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-cards.html) but not in models.dev. They're added through `addMissing`, so the models.dev entries take over once upstream lists them.
- **Context overflow:** Mantle's `invalid_prompt: prompt tokens (N) exceed model maximum (M)` errors are now detected as overflow.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** a SigV4 request carries an `AWS4-HMAC-SHA256` credential scoped to `<region>/bedrock-mantle`, plus the session token header. A Bedrock API key wins over AWS credentials. Catalog tests cover strict mode and the Daybreak models, and the overflow pattern has a test.
- **Against live AWS (us-east-1):**
  - A correctly signed request passes signature checks and reaches IAM authorization: 403 "not authorized to perform: bedrock-mantle:CreateInference".
  - A tampered signature gets 401 "The request signature we calculated does not match".
  - Invalid access keys get 401 "The security token included in the request is invalid".
- **Not verified:** a successful completion. Our IAM user is explicitly denied `bedrock-mantle:CreateInference`.

prs.title: fix: preserve legacy model catalog route on publish
prs.body:
Fixes #9099

## Problem

Pi `0.80.8`–`0.84.4` fetch the OpenRouter catalog from pi.dev but send every OpenRouter request through `openai-completions`. Per-model OpenRouter APIs start in `0.85.0`.

The publisher labelled every catalog `minimumPiVersion: "0.80.7"` and replaced that index entry on each run. Once the generator emitted OpenRouter `anthropic-messages` entries, pi.dev served them to older clients:

```text
Pi 0.82.1 gets: api anthropic-messages, baseUrl https://openrouter.ai/api
uses openai-completions anyway -> POST https://openrouter.ai/api/chat/completions -> HTML 404
```

The `baseUrl` is correct for `anthropic-messages`, which appends `/v1/messages`. The bug is serving that entry to clients that ignore `api`.

## Change

The publisher records generated catalogs under `minimumPiVersion: "0.85.0"`, so each run updates only the `0.85.0` entry and `defaultRevision`. The existing `0.80.7` entry is left alone. The regression test runs the real publish path against a local R2 stand-in and fails on the old publisher.

pi.dev already selects catalogs by the User-Agent's Pi version and needs no change. Its released-client tests (`0.80.8`, `0.82.1`, `0.84.4`, `0.85.0`, `0.99.0`) are on pi.dev `main`.

## Production repair

Merging stops future runs from breaking older clients. The live `0.80.7` entry still points to a mixed-API catalog and must be repointed to a legacy snapshot generated by the `v0.84.4` generator. This needs write access to the `pi-artifacts` R2 bucket; the endpoint is `R2_ENDPOINT` in `.github/workflows/publish-model-catalog.yml`.

### 1. Generate the legacy snapshot

```sh
git worktree add --detach /tmp/pi-legacy v0.84.4
cd /tmp/pi-legacy
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run generate:model-catalog
npm run check:model-catalog   # prints "revision": "sha256-..."
```

Check that every OpenRouter model uses the legacy API:

```sh
node -e 'const m=require("./.artifacts/model-catalog/models.json").openrouter; const bad=Object.values(m).filter(x=>x.api!=="openai-completions"||x.baseUrl!=="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"); console.log(Object.keys(m).length+" OpenRouter models, "+bad.length+" incompatible"); process.exit(bad.length?1:0)'
```

The snapshot has no typed `.all.json` files. Affected clients don't request them.

### 2. Rollout

1. Upload the snapshot. Nothing references it yet, so this is safe at any time:

   ```sh
   REV=<revision printed by check:model-catalog>
   aws s3 cp .artifacts/model-catalog/ "s3://pi-artifacts/models/v1/revisions/$REV/" \
     --recursive --exclude publication.json --endpoint-url "$R2_ENDPOINT" \
     --content-type "application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     --cache-control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
   ```

2. Merge this PR.
3. Make sure no publish run is queued or running (`gh run list --workflow publish-model-catalog.yml`). A run for a pre-merge commit uses the old publisher, and any run that read the index before the repair writes back its stale copy.
4. Download `models/v1/index.json`, edit it keeping existing entry metadata, and upload it with `--content-type "application/json; charset=utf-8" --cache-control no-store`:
   - `0.80.7` → `$REV`
   - `0.85.0` → the current `defaultRevision` (add the entry if missing)
   - `defaultRevision` unchanged
5. After about a minute, check that `curl -sL -A pi/0.84.4 -D - -o /dev/null https://pi.dev/api/models/providers/openrouter` reports `x-pi-model-catalog-revision: $REV`, and `pi/0.85.0` the current revision.

Clients pick up the change on their next refresh: immediately for fresh CI runs, within four hours for local installs, or right away with `pi update --models`.

### Reference validation

A snapshot generated this way on 2026-10-10 (`sha256-90b251b8df293406ca205db60a5f8b1285fef2d72e476cdd47a78c8f734effd6`, 38 providers, 1518 chat models) was loaded by released clients through their normal catalog refresh, with one intercepted request per model. Your revision will differ because upstream data changes.

| Client | OpenRouter | OpenCode, OpenCode Go, Fireworks |
|---|---|---|
| `0.80.8` | 392 → `/api/v1/chat/completions` | 130 of 136 |
| `0.82.1` | 392 → `/api/v1/chat/completions` | 136 of 136 |
| `0.84.4` | 392 → `/api/v1/chat/completions` | 136 of 136 |

The six `0.80.8` failures are OpenCode Go `openai-responses` models, supported from `0.81.0`. They fail with an explicit "no API implementation" error on `0.80.8`–`0.80.10`. This predates #9099; removing them would hide working models from `0.81.0`–`0.84.4`.

## Out of scope

The second comment on #9099 reports a separate client-side bug. Custom models in `models.json`, or registered by extensions, that omit `baseUrl` can inherit a URL meant for a different API. `0.85.0` fixed the common case. Pi can fix the remaining edge cases itself in a follow-up: inherit `baseUrl` only from a built-in model with the same `api`, otherwise fail with an error asking for it. Setting `baseUrl` explicitly avoids it on released versions.

## Validation

- `node --test scripts/publish-model-catalog.test.mjs`
- `npm run check`

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): make HTTP connect timeout configurable
prs.body:
## Summary

```diff
 configureHttpDispatcher(idleTimeout)
-  connect: { autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout: 2000 }
+  connectTimeout: httpConnectTimeoutMs ?? 10000
+  connect: { autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout: 2000 }
```

`httpConnectTimeoutMs` controls TCP and TLS connection time for direct requests and proxy CONNECT tunnels. The default remains 10 seconds; `0` or `"disabled"` removes the limit.

## Evidence

- **Before:** a local proxy returns CONNECT 200 and delays TLS for 12 seconds; installed Pi fails after 10516 ms with `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`.
  **After:** the same proxy returns HTTP 200 after 12020 ms when the connection timeout is 30 seconds. The new direct and proxy regression tests also fail on the old code and pass on this change.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The default preserves current behavior, and the setting can be removed without migration.

**Blast Radius:** HTTP transport

The setting changes only the connection budget. Header, body, provider-request, and WebSocket open timeouts remain independent.

Fixes #11115.

prs.title: docs: move documentation to the repository root
prs.body:
The docs now cover more than the coding agent (pi-ai, pi-durable, ...), so they move from `packages/coding-agent/docs` to `docs/` at the repository root.

## Bundling

npm can only pack files inside a package, so the coding-agent build copies `docs/` into `packages/coding-agent/docs/` (generated, gitignored) via `scripts/copy-docs.mjs`. Every release path packs after the build (npm tarballs, release binaries via `build-binaries.sh`, Nix, the evals image), so releases keep shipping `<package>/docs` with no changes to `files`, `build-binaries.sh` or the Dockerfile. The generated copy is byte-identical to the docs the package shipped before this change.

`copy-docs.mjs` is the place to filter what gets bundled later, since `docs/` will include pages unrelated to the coding agent.

## Links

Docs link to coding-agent files through the repository layout, e.g. `../packages/coding-agent/examples/sdk/`, so links work in the repository and on GitHub. `copy-docs.mjs` rewrites links that point into the package back to package-relative paths (`../examples/sdk/`) in the bundled copy. Links to other repository files are left unchanged.

## Runtime

- `getDocsPath()` returns the repository `docs/` in source checkouts and `<package>/docs` in npm installs and the binary.
- Compact rendering of `read` calls recognizes pages under `getDocsPath()`, which is outside the package root in source checkouts.

## Other references

Root README, coding-agent README (`../../docs/...`), the extensions URL in `migrations.ts`, the documentation test, the documentation audit eval, `.pi/prompts/pr.md`, `.pi/skills/add-llm-provider.md`.

## Before merging

pi.dev fetches docs from `packages/coding-agent/docs` on `main` and resolves `../` links against the package path. It needs to read `docs/` (with a fallback to the old path for older refs) and resolve `../` links against the repository root before this lands.

## Verification

- `npm run check`
- `test/documentation.test.ts`, `test/tool-execution-component.test.ts`, `test/config.test.ts`, `test/system-prompt.test.ts`, `test/changelog.test.ts`
- `npm pack --dry-run` includes all 46 docs files

prs.title: feat(ai): serve Claude models on Google Vertex AI
prs.body:
Stacked on #11370. `google-vertex` now lists the 13 non-deprecated Claude models that models.dev catalogs on Vertex's Anthropic Messages API (for example `claude-opus-4-8@default`).

## How it works

`src/api/google-vertex-anthropic.ts` reuses the Anthropic Messages implementation with a `fetch` wrapper:
- `/v1/messages` becomes `…/publishers/anthropic/models/{model}:streamRawPredict` (or `rawPredict`); token counting becomes `count-tokens:rawPredict`.
- The model moves from the body into the URL, and the body gets `anthropic_version: "vertex-2023-10-16"`.
- Authentication uses an Application Default Credentials or service-account access token instead of an Anthropic key.

The provider dispatches `anthropic-messages` models to this wrapper and Gemini to the existing Vertex API. Claude family rules (adaptive thinking, effort levels, temperature) apply as on other hosts.

## Dependencies

`google-auth-library@10.6.2` becomes a direct dependency. It is already in the tree through `@google/genai`, so the lockfile and install lock each gain one line. A `browser` field maps it to an empty module so browser bundles still build. Claude on Vertex needs ADC, which a browser can't provide anyway.

## Catalog compatibility

Released 1.4.0 clients only implement Google's Vertex API for `google-vertex`. This PR bumps `MINIMUM_PI_VERSION` to 1.4.1, so they keep the last compatible catalog.

## Testing

- **Unit tests**: cover the URL, body and header rewrite. One test drives the real Anthropic SDK through the wrapper and asserts the request it sends.
- **E2E**: a block gated on `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`.

Not verified against a live Vertex project. The `@default` model ids are models.dev's; opencode uses the same ids through the AI SDK.

No changelog entry because this PR targets a branch other than `main`.

prs.title: DRAFT: fix(coding-agent): run availability passes one at a time with a timeout
prs.body:
Parking this here for now.
I want to see whether it makes sense to go back to the one-at-a-time refresh we had before #7301 but with a timeout.

----
An awaited refresh could resolve before its availability pass saved. Passes ran concurrently, and only the most recently started pass could save its result; a superseded pass returned without saving and refresh() still resolved. At startup, the awaited refresh could lose to a fire-and-forget refresh started by an extension provider registration, so initial model selection read a snapshot without that provider and fell back to another provider's default. A login also cancelled any full pass that was running.

Availability passes now run one at a time. A request made while a pass is waiting to start joins it, so a caller always gets a pass that saw its changes. Each pass has a 10 s timeout, so a hung auth check or credential store no longer blocks the caller forever (#7301). A failed or timed-out provider check keeps that provider's previous state and is reported in getError().

The snapshot drops configuredProviders and all; hasConfiguredAuth reads the auth map.

Refs #8810, #9884

prs.title: fix(ai): honor Retry-After delays in agent-level retry
prs.body:
Fixes #10601. (Same gap as #9595, which was bot-closed before review.)

Problem: agent-level auto-retry ignores the server's `Retry-After` / `retry-after-ms`. A 429 with `Retry-After: 30` is retried after 2s and then on `2^(n-1)` backoff — earlier than the server asked — hammering a rate-limited or overloaded backend.

Trace: each API catch block flattens the provider error to a display string (`formatProviderError(normalizeProviderError(error))`), `normalizeProviderError` never reads response headers, and `AssistantMessage` has no field to carry them, so `retryDelayMs()` can only use the exponential formula. Provider-level `retryProviderRequest` parses the headers but is off by default (`settings.retry.provider.maxRetries = 0`) because it delays pi's own quota/usage-limit handling.

Solution:

- `parseRetryAfterMs(headers)`: extracted from `getRetryDelayMs` and shared. Provider-path behavior unchanged, including the malformed-date fallback (#9571).
- `extractRetryAfterMs(error)`: reads the hint from SDK errors carrying response `Headers`; every chat API error path now sets `AssistantMessage.retryAfterMs`.
- `retryDelayMs(policy, attempt, serverDelayMs)`: raises the per-attempt delay to the hint. `maxAgentDelayMs` stays authoritative: the hint is clamped to the cap and never lowers the exponential delay.
- Consumers: `retryAssistantCall`, `AgentSession._prepareRetry`, and the durable harness generation/compaction schedulers.

Tests: regression tests beside the retry suites (commented `#9595`) plus unit tests for `parseRetryAfterMs` and `extractRetryAfterMs`. `npm run check` is clean. `./test.sh` passes except two Windows-shell tests (`resolve-config-value` "uses stdin when the configured Windows shell requires it", `env-node` "uses stdin command transport for legacy WSL bash paths") that fail identically on unmodified main in my Linux environment.

prs.title: feat(durable): let extensions annotate aborted tool results
prs.body:
## Problem

An aborted tool gets a durable error result, but an extension cannot annotate it. `afterTool` runs only after execution; the abort handler builds its own result from committed progress. Returning a different result from `execute()` after cancellation does not help, and a call aborted before execution never reaches that code.

For example: a user cancels one search with “use a narrower query.” The search stops and its siblings continue, but the model receives only the generic aborted result, not the reason. Policy-driven cancellation has the same limitation.

## Proposal

Add `onAbort(call, result, api, context)` to `ToolHooks`. It uses the existing replacement-chain mechanism:

```text
abort mark → drain execution and owned work
           → durable progress → onAbort → one result entry + aborted outcome
```

Extensions keep cancellation metadata in their own documents, keyed by `api.taskId`, and read it through `HookApi.snapshot`. The README includes a small example; the specification describes the lifecycle.

This keeps cancellation mechanics in the Harness and application policy in extensions:

- No new `abortTask()` options, settings, persisted fields, document versions, or migrations.
- Returning `undefined` preserves the existing result. Retained output is not re-truncated after a tool reload; replacement content uses the normal content bounds.
- The task still ends `aborted`; returned controls cannot terminate or hand off the parent run.
- The hook has a fresh abort-invocation context, follows extension selection/order and ordinary error reporting, and may replay before settlement after restart.
- Successful execution and unsafe recovery do not call it. `afterTool` retains its execution-only contract.

A tool wrapper cannot cover pre-execution aborts or restart settlement. A `beforeRequest` transform could change a later model request, but would leave the persisted tool result different from what the model sees. This hook runs where the canonical result is decided.

## Verification

- `npm run check` passes.
- `./test.sh` passes in its isolated, credential-free environment; Durable: **985 passed, 4 skipped**.
- Eight new tests cover model/transcript agreement, sibling isolation, hook chaining/errors, pre-execution abort, content bounds, tool reload/removal, and replay across SQLite reopen without duplicate results or tool execution.

Draft for feedback on the hook's name and placement before committing to the interface. This is AI-assisted work prepared for review; it does not add application-specific cancellation state to Pi.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep active tool order when the same tools are set again
prs.body:
The system prompt lists tool snippets and per-tool guidelines in the order of the active tools. When an extension called `pi.setActiveTools()` with the same tools in a different order (for example `[...pi.getActiveTools()].reverse()`), the "tools" and "rules" sections came out different. pi then recorded a "System Prompt Update: tools, rules" message even though the active tools had not changed. On providers without mid-conversation system messages, this also rewrites the prompt head and loses the cache.

`_applyToolLoadout` in `agent-session.ts` now treats the requested names as a set:
- tools that stay active keep their current order;
- newly activated tools are appended at the end.

Reordering the same set therefore leaves the prompt unchanged. Adding a tool only appends its bullet. The same rule covers tool lists changed by `before_agent_start` handlers, since they go through the same function.

Testing:
- Added a test in `test/system-prompt-updates.test.ts`: it reverses the active tools between two prompts and expects a single system message. It fails without the change (a second message patches `tools` and `rules`) and passes with it.
- `npm run check` passes.
- `./test.sh`: all coding-agent suites pass. The only failure is an unrelated Anthropic model metadata test in `packages/ai`.

Fixes #11495

Requested by @badlogic

With `codemode.mode: "on"`, each declared tool gets a description suffix that says what a script call resolves to. For an object output schema, `describeOutput` shortens this to field names. Any other schema fell back to the whole rendered TypeScript type, collapsed onto one line. A tool with a union output schema therefore put its full output type, nested fields and comments included, into every request. The reporter's `process` tool, a union of 7 variants, added about 8,000 characters. Collapsing the type onto one line also left `//` comments in the middle of the text.

This change:
- **Unions:** for `anyOf`/`oneOf` schemas where every variant is an object, the suffix lists each variant's field names, joined by ` | `.
- **`const` fields:** `describeFields` now shows the value of `const` fields, so a discriminator like `action` stays visible. For example: `` `{ action: "start", process } | { action: "list", processes, truncated? }` ``.
- **Other multi-line types**, such as an array of objects: instead of the inlined type, the suffix says `` a value; `await describeTool("name")` shows its type ``. `describeTool()` already returns the full declaration.
- **Single-line types** such as `number` are unchanged.

Testing:
- I added a test in `test/suite/agent-session-codemode.test.ts` that checks the suffix for three tools: one with a union output, one with an array-of-objects output, and one with a `number` output. It fails without the change and passes with it.
- `node ../../node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/suite/agent-session-codemode.test.ts test/suite/agent-session-mcp.test.ts` passes, including the existing MCP description assertions.
- `npm run check` is clean.

Fixes #11501

Requested by @badlogic

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): show model scope in the fullscreen header instead of the shell
prs.body:
In fullscreen mode, the startup `Model scope: …` notice was still in the shell after pi exited. With `fullscreenExitOutput: "resume-hint"`, the shell showed it above the resume command.

Cause: `InteractiveMode.init()` printed the notice with `console.log` before the renderer started. In fullscreen mode that output goes to the terminal's normal screen. Pi then draws on the alternate screen, and when it exits the terminal switches back to the normal screen, where the notice is still visible.

The change:
- Building the notice text moves into `getModelScopeNotice()`.
- Regular mode prints it with `console.log` before the TUI starts, as before.
- Fullscreen mode adds it to the header container below the built-in header. It uses a `ThemedText`, so the text is built after the terminal reports its colors and follows theme changes.

Since fullscreen is the default `tuiMode`, this applies to every user who has `enabledModels` set and quiet startup off.

Testing:
- Added `packages/coding-agent/test/interactive-mode-model-scope.test.ts`. It checks two things for fullscreen: the notice renders in the header and `console.log` is not called, and nothing is added when startup details are hidden.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Manual check in tmux with `enabledModels` set:
  - fullscreen + `resume-hint`: before the change, `Model scope: claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-opus-4-5 (Ctrl+P to cycle)` was left in the shell after `/quit`. Now the line shows inside pi's header and the shell is clean after exit.
  - `tuiMode: "regular"`: unchanged, the line is still printed above the header.

Fixes #11508

Requested by @badlogic

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): report a deleted working directory instead of crashing on startup
prs.body:
Starting `pi` from a directory that has been deleted crashed with an uncaught Node `ENOENT ... uv_cwd` stack trace. This also happened for `--version` and `--help`. The cause is the unguarded `process.cwd()` call in `main()` (`packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts`).

`main()` now catches `ENOENT` from that call, prints one line telling the user to change to an existing directory, and exits with code 1. Other errors are rethrown unchanged. Argument handling is otherwise unchanged: `--version` still needs a valid cwd, but it now gets the readable error instead of a crash.

**Testing**
- Added `test/deleted-cwd.test.ts`. It stubs `process.cwd()` to throw ENOENT and checks that `main()` prints the message and exits with code 1. It also checks that a non-ENOENT error is rethrown. The first test fails without the change and passes with it.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Manual check with the built CLI. Before, all three commands below printed the `uv_cwd` stack trace. After, each prints `Error: The current working directory no longer exists. Change to an existing directory and try again.` and exits 1:
  ```sh
  d=$(mktemp -d); cd "$d"; rmdir "$d"
  pi -ne --version; pi -ne --help; pi -ne
  ```

Fixes #11509

Requested by @badlogic

issues.body:
`publish` is the last release job still competing for GitHub-hosted capacity. #14336 added the opt-in route for it (`publish` + `audio-capture-prebuilds` `collect` → `ecs-qwen-release-host`, gated by `ECS_RELEASE_HOST_RUNNER_ENABLED`), but the release-only machine was never provisioned, so the switch has never been on.

Today's release shows the cost. Run [40100919416](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40100919416): every job before `publish` landed on ECS runners and finished on time, then `Publish Release` waited **22.5 minutes** for a hosted runner (queued 15:09:58Z, started 15:32:30Z) behind 139 queued hosted jobs, and took 15.5 minutes once it started.

## Proposal

Put `publish` and `collect` on two runners of the **idle Hangzhou ARM64 pool**, and drop the architecture pin from the release-only label.

- **Label two runners**, one on `hz1` and one on `hz2`: `ecs-qwen-release-host`. One unblocks the lane; the second only matters when two manual releases overlap (`collect` ≈ 6 s and `publish` ≈ 16 min share the label; nightly is serialized by its concurrency group, manual dispatches are not). Nothing else needs to move: the seven-way validation wave stays on `ecs-qwen-hk4-host`.
- **Make the label arch-agnostic** in `release.yml` (`publish`) and `audio-capture-prebuilds.yml` (`collect`):

  ```yaml
  fromJSON('["self-hosted", "linux", "ecs-qwen-release-host"]')
  ```

  instead of the current `["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "ecs-qwen-release-host"]`. The label, not the CPU architecture, is what expresses "release-only"; keeping `x64` makes the hz pool unroutable and would pin the lane to one architecture forever, including after #10879 frees an x64 host.

## Why the hz ARM64 pool

- `ecs-qwen-hz1-*` (32) and `ecs-qwen-hz2-*` (32) are all online, carry only `self-hosted, Linux, ARM64`, and **no workflow in this repository references that label** (the `arm64` strings elsewhere are hosted `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, docker build platforms, and the cua driver release). They have never executed PR code, which is the credential-isolation property #14336 spent effort preserving.
- The x64 alternatives are not available: `hk1`/`hk2` carry `ecs-autofix`/`ecs-review` (PR bot lanes) and `hk1`'s runners are currently offline; `hk4` is the host #10879 is trying to drain.

## Why ARM64 is safe for `publish`

`scripts/build-standalone-release.js` builds all five targets from a single host by design ("release packaging cross-builds all targets from a single host"): it downloads the per-target Node/bun archives and stages native packages from `pnpm-lock.yaml` with `npm install --ignore-scripts`, so the host's own `node_modules` never defines the artifacts. `verify-installation-release` only checks archive presence and SHA256 and never executes target binaries, so no qemu is involved. `postinstall` is `patch-package`; nothing compiles for the host.

## Variables and kill switches

The existing `ECS_RELEASE_HOST_RUNNER_ENABLED` stays the **only** switch, and unset is exactly today's behaviour:

- unset → `publish`/`collect` on `ubuntu-latest` (current state);
- `true` → release-only label.

No second variable is proposed. An additional arch knob (`ECS_RELEASE_HOST_ARCH`) would only pay for itself if the lane ever had to pin a mixed fleet, and a free-form labels variable is worse: invalid JSON in a `fromJSON` expression fails the workflow before a job starts. If mixed x64/ARM64 release hosts ever exist, arch-agnostic routing already handles it with no variable at all.

## Activation order (so the release chain never breaks)

1. Label one runner on each hz host; confirm both are online and pick up the label.
2. Verify prerequisites on the machines: Node 22 on `PATH` (`self-hosted-node` hard-fails otherwise), corepack/pnpm, git, GNU `realpath`, egress to `github.com`, `registry.npmjs.org`, and the bun/Node distribution hosts, and **20–30 GB free** — `check-disk-floor.sh` only rejects below 2 GiB, but `publish` downloads five runtime archives and builds five standalone archives.
3. Land the two-line routing change (with the mirror test and both design-doc languages updated).
4. Set `ECS_RELEASE_HOST_RUNNER_ENABLED=true`.
5. Dispatch a **dry run** and confirm the routing: `publish` + `collect` on hz, `quality` on hk4, `notify_failure` still hosted. A dry run exercises the whole machine-dependent path and publishes nothing, so a broken ARM setup costs one dry run, not a release.
6. Watch the next real release end to end.

## Isolation invariant

While a runner carries `ecs-qwen-release-host`, its host must never take PR work — the boundary is the machine, not the runner process, because a PR job on the same host shares the filesystem and global tooling with a later `publish`. Today the hz hosts are unused, so the invariant holds trivially; if that pool is ever wired to CI, the release label has to move to a host that never runs PR code.

## Validation

- `npx vitest run scripts/tests/release-workflow.test.js` — the credential-isolation test already forbids the PR-shared `ecs-qwen-hk4-host` label on `publish`; extend it to also forbid `x64`/`ARM64` in the release-only label so the architecture decision cannot regress silently.
- The dry run from step 5 above, plus one real release.

## Rollback

- `gh variable delete ECS_RELEASE_HOST_RUNNER_ENABLED` → back to hosted in one step.
- Remove or keep the labels; routing already reverts with the variable.
- A misconfiguration fails visibly (90-minute `timeout-minutes` on `publish`) instead of hanging forever.

## Out of scope

- `audio-capture-prebuilds`' `ubuntu-latest` x64 lane still gates `publish` and can queue on hosted; it needs its own change (matrix `runner` values are literals).
- #10879 (draining `hk4`) stays independent; if it lands, an x64 release host can join the same label with no workflow change.
- `notify_failure` stays hosted on purpose.

## References

- Parent tracking: #10038 (move release workflows off hosted)
- Related: #10879 (hk4 still carries the PR-shared label)
- Implemented the opt-in: #14336, design in `docs/design/2026-10-16-release-jobs-off-hosted-pool.md`

issues.body:
## Problem

v0.26.1 itself shipped fine — `Release` run [40100919416](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40100919416) succeeded at 15:48:05Z, and both npm and the GitHub release are live. What never ran on time is everything the `release: published` event fans out to. Fifty minutes after the event (16:38Z), the lane looked like this:

| workflow | first job | hosted-queue wait |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Finalize Stable Release (opens the bump-version PR) | `finalize` | **50 min**, then started |
| Desktop release v0.26.1 | `Prepare release metadata` | **37 min** |
| Release VSCode IDE Companion | `prepare` | **40 min** |
| Release Managed server runtime | `prepare` | **42 min** |
| Release SDK | `release-sdk` | never started in 50 min |
| Sync Release to Aliyun OSS | `sync` | never started in 50 min |
| DSW Harbor Benchmark Release | `release_gate` | never started in 50 min |

Every one of those jobs needs a GitHub-hosted runner and none of them is doing hosted-only work. Three of them (`prepare` × 3) are 2–6 minute metadata jobs that spend ten times longer waiting than running.

This is the steady state, not an incident. Same lane, earlier releases: v0.26.0's `finalize` waited 10 min and then ran 39 min; `release-sdk` waited 16 min then ran 47 min; `Publish web-shell visuals` today waited **62 min for a job that ran 0 min**.

The queue it waits in, sampled at the same moment: 49 of 50 queued runs were on GitHub-hosted labels — 13 `Main CI Failure Issue`, 10 `tui-parity`, 4 `Managed Agent gate`, 4 `Qwen Triage`, 2 `Qwen Code CI`, and our 4 release jobs — against roughly 20 concurrent hosted slots. GitHub dispatches hosted runners FIFO with no per-workflow priority, so a release that finishes publishing at 15:48 simply joins the back of that line.

## Scope

#15461 covers `publish` — the last job that runs *before* the release exists. This issue is the other half: the seven workflows that start from scratch when `release: published` fires, each of which re-pays the hosted queue, and each of which is upstream or downstream of nothing that requires a hosted machine.

## Inventory

### Lane 1 — shared `ecs-qwen` pool, no new hardware

Light and secret-free: they carry `GITHUB_TOKEN` only, and they recompute release metadata that the queue delays by tens of minutes.

| workflow | job | last observed runtime |
|---|---|---|
| `desktop-release.yml` | `prepare` | 2 min |
| `release-vscode-companion.yml` | `prepare` | 6 min |
| `release-managed-runtime.yml` | `prepare` | — |
| `live-host-release.yml` | `prepare` | — |
| `dsw-swe-verified-release.yml` | `release_gate` | seconds |

`release-managed-runtime.yml`'s second job (`release`) needs a look: it is short but may carry publish credentials, in which case it belongs in lane 2.

### Lane 2 — `ecs-qwen-release-host`, behind `ECS_RELEASE_HOST_RUNNER_ENABLED`

Credential-bearing, so it cannot sit on the pool that also runs PR code (#10879: the `ecs-qwen-hk4-*` instances are dual-labelled and already serve PR CI).

| workflow | job | credential | last observed runtime |
|---|---|---|---|
| `finalize-release.yml` | `finalize` | `CI_BOT_PAT` — pushes the release branch, opens/approves the bump PR, enables auto-merge | 39 min |
| `release-sdk.yml` | `release-sdk` | npm trusted publishing | 47 min |
| `sync-release-to-oss.yml` | `sync` | Aliyun OSS AccessKeys | 7 min |
| `desktop-release.yml` | `publish` | release credentials | 1 min |
| `desktop-release.yml` → `sync-desktop-to-oss.yml` | `sync` | OSS AccessKeys | 2 min |
| `release-vscode-companion.yml` | `publish` | release credentials | 2 min |
| `live-host-release.yml` | `publish` | release credentials | — |
| `live-host-release.yml` → `sync-live-host-to-oss.yml` | `sync` | OSS AccessKeys | — |

Adjacent, same tax, probably worth riding along: `build-and-publish-image.yml`'s `build-and-push-to-ghcr` holds a hosted slot for **100 minutes** per release (GHCR credentials), and `web-shell-visuals-publish.yml`'s publisher waited 62 min for a 0-minute job today.

### Stays hosted

- Every `macos-*` and `windows-*` leg — no self-hosted platform for them.
- `report-failure` / `notify_failure` / `file-failure-issue` — they have to survive whatever broke the pool they report on.

## Constraints

- **Credential isolation decides the lane, not convenience.** A job holding a release secret never lands on `ecs-qwen`. The boundary is the machine: a PR job on the same host shares the filesystem and global tooling with a later release job.
- **Pool hygiene is not optional.** Every pool-routed job needs the `&restore_release_workspace` wipe anchor from `release.yml`, plus the disk-floor gate when it checks out or installs. Lane-2 jobs additionally need the `rm -rf` hygiene step that persistent workspaces require before artifact merges (same reasoning as `collect` in `audio-capture-prebuilds.yml`).
- **No new switch.** Lane 1 uses the existing `MAINTAINER_ECS_RUNNER_DISABLED` condition; lane 2 uses `ECS_RELEASE_HOST_RUNNER_ENABLED`, which is already the pattern in `release.yml` and `audio-capture-prebuilds.yml`. `ecs-qwen-release-host` is already registered in `.github/actionlint.yaml`.
- **Lane 2 lands behind #15461.** Without a machine carrying the label, flipping the switch queues lane-2 jobs forever. Unset stays exactly today's dispatch, so merging early is safe.
- **Order within lane 2 matters less than order of activation.** `finalize` is the one users notice (no bump PR → no `release/*` branch merge → the release never lands on `main`), so it is the first candidate once a release host exists.

## Tests

Routing and pool-hygiene contracts are pinned in:

- `scripts/tests/release-workflow.test.js` — already asserts the `ECS_RELEASE_HOST_RUNNER_ENABLED` expression and the wipe/disk-floor invariants; extend it to the newly routed jobs.
- `scripts/tests/desktop-oss-workflow.test.js`, `scripts/tests/desktop-isolation.test.js`, `scripts/tests/live-host-oss-workflow.test.js`, `scripts/tests/release-sdk-workflow.test.js`, `scripts/tests/build-and-publish-image-workflow.test.js`, `scripts/tests/install-script.test.js` — each parses one of the touched files.
- `web-shell-visuals-publish.yml` has no test; if it moves, it needs one.

## Acceptance

- With both switches unset, every listed job dispatches exactly as it does today.
- With lane 1 enabled, `release: published` starts its `prepare` jobs on `ecs-qwen` within seconds instead of 37–42 minutes, and the macOS/Windows build legs are the only hosted jobs in the lane.
- With lane 2 enabled, `finalize`, `release-sdk`, the OSS syncs and the publish jobs run on `ecs-qwen-release-host`, and the bump PR opens without waiting on hosted capacity.
- A dry-run release plus one real release shows no release job waiting on a hosted runner except the macOS/Windows legs and the failure reporters.

## Out of scope

The automation flood that fills the hosted pool. Moving the release lane protects releases; it does not give the pool back to the macOS/Windows legs or to PR CI. #10038 tracks the broader migration; the pool-contention side belongs with the runner-capacity work.

## References

- Parent: #10038 (move all release workflows off GitHub-hosted runners)
- Sibling: #15461 (`publish` + `collect` onto the idle hz ARM64 pool)
- Related: #10879 (hk4 still carries the PR-shared label), #14336 (the opt-in route this reuses)
- Design: `docs/design/2026-10-16-release-jobs-off-hosted-pool.md`

issues.body:
Track the non-blocking Suggestions from PR #15466 independently so its user-scope Skill activation delivery does not keep accumulating review-driven coverage, contract changes, and lifecycle changes. These items were explicitly classified as Suggestions by the reviewer. They are not being described as fixed, and this issue does not waive any Critical finding.

Assessment below is against exact PR head `f6dc34685623781653eb97bc4ca987088adf8e6b`.

- [ ] **R1-26** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593306)): The validator still accepts user-only/empty scope arrays, while the implementation always reloads workspace and optionally user. The only production sender sends ['workspace','user']; narrowing or defining the unused shapes remains follow-up contract hardening.

- [ ] **R1-11** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593319)): Session.reloadSkillSettings forwards includeUser into the atomic Workspace+User reload, and ACP forwards the option to each session. Direct Session-branch and session-carrying ACP regression assertions remain missing; this is additional coverage, rather than an observed incorrect path at this head.

- [ ] **R1-20** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593322)): Both user handlers omit the workspace trust gate as documented, and the new untrusted-secondary test checks user reconciliation. A dedicated untrusted-primary HTTP regression remains useful follow-up coverage.

- [ ] **R1-14** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593329)): The nested per-runtime/per-settingsChanges publish loop is present. Multi-key persistence is covered on the writer side; a multi-key route fan-out regression remains follow-up coverage.

- [ ] **R1-27** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593333)): The route filters outcomes by changed before constructing the mutation, preserving refused names only in results. A mixed changed/refused event regression remains follow-up coverage.

- [ ] **R1-12** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593336)): The route passes {userSettings:true}, reconcileSkills forwards its options, and the newly added untrusted-runtime test explicitly asserts that option at both coordinators. This closes the originally unobserved forwarding seam. A live route-to-child payload/activation regression remains optional follow-up coverage.

- [ ] **R1-9** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593342)): User activation emits the mutation before asynchronous reconciliation completes, with both session counts set to zero. The current protocol does not explain that timing distinction; document it in follow-up without changing the event schema or making these writes synchronous.

- [ ] **R1-19** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593346)): The accumulated-batch recheck still clears only User entries removed from next[block.list]; it does not clear a defaultDisabled block cancelled by an identical grant added earlier in the batch. Retain this mixed-spelling response edge case and both-order acceptance test as the reviewer's explicitly non-blocking follow-up. Hard disables must remain uncancellable by grants.

- [ ] **R1-13** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593351)): The generic next[block.list] removal recheck remains present. Add an enable-side defaultDisabled removal witness together with the batch cancellation follow-up; no claim that this coverage is already present.

- [ ] **R1-29** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593357)): The server still supplies capturePrimaryGenerationAssertion to the user writer; it may reject a user write while the primary generation is transitioning. Keep the ownership/failure-semantics choice and its HTTP regression as the reviewer's explicitly non-blocking follow-up, preserving commit-time settings safety.

- [ ] **R1-8** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593358)): The coordinator retains user-reload debt for a cold/idle child; the next successful refresh retires it. A later workspace refresh may therefore reread the user file once after a fresh child start. Keep this bounded extra-reload behavior and the cold/idle-versus-admissionPaused tests as the reviewer's explicitly non-blocking follow-up.

- [ ] **R1-21** ([original discussion](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#discussion_r4368593361)): All six new types are currently exported from both barrels and both client methods exist. Extend the public-surface regression fence in follow-up to prevent future export/method drift.

The formal review bodies also explicitly deferred additional non-blocking items. Preserve those records when planning this follow-up: eager route import cleanup; commit-time assertion coverage; app-level dependency injection coverage; case-variant no-op reporting; ACP workspace-only atomic-spy count; environment reapplication after settings reload; trusted-scope wording; SDK mode/state coupling; single-route name-limit coverage; null mode validation; and duplicate bare/registry batch result reporting. See [round 2](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#pullrequestreview-5644114261) and [round 3](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15466#pullrequestreview-5645731655) for the existing dispositions and exact witnesses.

Acceptance: retain the stated scope and test each selected item at its then-current head, including failure controls where relevant. In particular, preserve hard-disable precedence, workspace trust boundaries, atomic settings writes, the existing workspace-only default refresh, and the asynchronous activation contract. Any material policy change should be designed separately rather than folded back into #15466.

issues.body:
### What happened?

In the Web Shell, the **Branch** action disappears from every completed answer once a session is restored from disk, for example after `qwen serve` restarts. The transcript still holds valid `branch_checkpoint` records, and the daemon still accepts a branch at them.

I measured this on one session and one build: main `e6e2c9ef`; the files involved are unchanged up to `34843cb9`. The setup was a real `qwen serve` with the built Web Shell in headless Chromium, a scripted OpenAI-compatible provider, and `tools.codeModeOnly: true`. The session had a text turn and a Code Mode turn.

| State of the same session | Branch on text answer | Branch on Code Mode answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live turn | shown | shown |
| Page reload, same daemon | shown | shown |
| Fresh tab, same daemon | shown | shown |
| `qwen serve` restarted, session reopened | **missing** | **missing** |

![Branch lost after restart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/727413a2c5f3a873e4013d75eb16f7af0d939d96/pr13574/03-branch-lost-after-restart.png)

After the restart, with the same session:

- `POST /session/:id/load` returns 200. `POST /session/:id/branch {"atRecordId":"<persisted checkpoint uuid>"}` then returns 201 and creates the fork; the source JSONL's SHA-256 is unchanged.
- `GET /session/:id/transcript` returns 200 and includes both `branchRecordId`s.
- Over native ACP (`node dist/cli.js --acp`, stdio), the `session/load` replay updates carry no `_meta.qwenTranscript.branchRecordId` for any turn. The same holds on `9a02f405` and `d7b97654`.

The checkpoints and the branch RPC work. Only the restored replay window lacks the branch metadata, and Web Shell shows Branch only when `branchRecordId` is present (`packages/web-shell/client/components/MessageList.tsx:5980`).

Steps to reproduce:

1. Run `qwen serve`, open the Web Shell, send a prompt and wait for the answer. Hovering the answer shows Branch.
2. Stop and restart `qwen serve`, then open the same session from the sidebar.
3. Hover the same answer: only Copy is shown, and no answer in the session offers Branch.

### What did you expect to happen?

A restored session should offer Branch on every answer that has a persisted checkpoint, the same as during the live turn. The Web Shell smoke test `branches from an earlier completed Assistant response and resumes the fork` (`packages/web-shell/client/e2e/web-shell.smoke.spec.ts:130`) already assumes this: its mock daemon replays `agent_message_chunk` events carrying `_meta.qwenTranscript.branchRecordId` (`packages/web-shell/client/e2e/utils/mockDaemon.ts:626-630`) and expects Branch after `page.reload()`. The real daemon's paged transcript path produces exactly that shape; the load replay does not.

### Client information

```
Qwen Code v0.25.0
Model: fake-model
Fast Model: not set
Auth: openai
Platform: darwin arm64 (25.6.0)
Node.js: v24.18.1
Git commit: e6e2c9efd1
LSP: disabled
```

Platform: macOS (arm64).

### Login information

OpenAI-compatible API config pointing at a local scripted provider; no real-provider traffic.

### Anything else we need to know?

Code pointers at `34843cb9`:

- The `branchRecordId` decoration exists only in `replayTranscriptRecordPage` (`packages/cli/src/acp-integration/session/history-replay-page.ts:456`, block `:503-545`). `GET /session/:id/transcript` uses it (`packages/cli/src/serve/routes/session.ts:6492`). From reading `DaemonSessionProvider`, Web Shell uses that path only to fetch older pages.
- `collectHistoryReplayUpdates` (`history-replay-page.ts:339`) never adds `branchRecordId`. ACP `session/load` uses it (`packages/cli/src/acp-integration/acpAgent.ts:6038` and `:6282`, in `loadSessionWithProfiler`). The rewind replay uses the same helper (`acpAgent.ts:14224`, `sessionRewind`); I did not measure the rewind case.
- Live turns get the id from the prompt result's `qwen.branchPoint` (`packages/web-shell/client/daemon/session/DaemonSessionProvider.tsx:289`). Same-daemon reloads keep Branch, as measured above; I did not trace which path serves them.

A possible direction: apply the same `branchPointsByAssistantUuid` decoration to the load replay. The transcript reader already indexes branch points, so the restored window and the paged window would agree.

Found while verifying #13574 ([report](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13574#issuecomment-6081435732)). It is independent of that PR: text turns are affected the same way, on builds from before and after it.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

**问题：** 在 Web Shell 中，会话从磁盘恢复后（例如 `qwen serve` 重启后重新打开），所有已完成回答上的「分叉」按钮都会消失。但 transcript 里的 `branch_checkpoint` 记录仍然有效，daemon 也仍然接受在这些检查点上分叉。

**实测**（同一会话、同一构建 main `e6e2c9ef`；涉及的文件到 `34843cb9` 都没有改动）：

- 实时回合、同一 daemon 下刷新页面、同一 daemon 下打开新标签页：文本回答和 Code Mode 回答都有分叉按钮。
- 重启 `qwen serve` 后重新打开会话：两个回答都没有分叉按钮。
- 重启后，`POST /session/:id/branch`（参数为已持久化的检查点）返回 201，源 JSONL 不变；`GET /session/:id/transcript` 返回的结果里两个 `branchRecordId` 都在。
- 原生 ACP 的 `session/load` 回放事件不带 `_meta.qwenTranscript.branchRecordId`，`9a02f405` 和 `d7b97654` 上同样如此。

**期望：** 恢复的会话应该在有持久化检查点的回答上显示分叉按钮。Web Shell 冒烟测试的 mock daemon 已经按这个约定在回放事件里携带 `branchRecordId`，并期望刷新后仍能看到分叉按钮。

**原因定位：** `branchRecordId` 只在 `replayTranscriptRecordPage` 中添加，而这个路径只用于分页加载更早的历史；`session/load` 走的 `collectHistoryReplayUpdates` 不添加它。rewind 回放也用同一个函数，这个场景未实测。

这个问题是验证 #13574 时发现的，与该 PR 无关：文本回合同样受影响，PR 合入前后的构建表现一致。

</details>

issues.title: bug(core): Responses cleanup can break reasoning/tool-call adjacency

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/core
labels.description: Core engine and logic

labels.name: scope/content-generation
labels.description: AI content generation

labels.name: status/ready-for-human
labels.description: Specified but requires human judgment to implement; not suitable for an autonomous agent

issues.body:
# What happened?

The OpenAI Responses request pipeline can break the API's reasoning-item adjacency invariant in two transformations. A replayed `reasoning` item and the `function_call` it belongs to must be treated as one unit, but current cleanup handles them independently.

On current `main` (`4a029e64e6f025a9b58f2cddef0ff652eb9325a9`):

1. [`cleanOrphanedFunctionCalls`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/4a029e64e6f025a9b58f2cddef0ff652eb9325a9/packages/core/src/core/openaiResponsesContentGenerator/responses-converter.ts#L800-L827) removes a `function_call` whose output is missing but leaves the immediately preceding `reasoning` item.
2. [`downgradeRejectedReasoningItems`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/4a029e64e6f025a9b58f2cddef0ff652eb9325a9/packages/core/src/core/openaiResponsesContentGenerator/responses-reasoning-rejection.ts#L176-L209) removes signature-only reasoning or replaces reasoning with an assistant message, but leaves the following `function_call`. [`downgradeEncryptedReasoningItems`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/4a029e64e6f025a9b58f2cddef0ff652eb9325a9/packages/core/src/core/openaiResponsesContentGenerator/responses-reasoning-rejection.ts#L505-L512) delegates to the same transformation.

Both shapes are rejected with HTTP 400 by Responses endpoints:

```text
reasoning without its required following item
function_call without its required reasoning item
```

The build-path failure is not retried because ordinary 400 responses are non-retryable. The recovery-path failure occurs on the one permitted recovery retry and propagates unchanged. Since requests are rebuilt from persisted history and recovery does not rewrite that history, later sends repeat the failure.

This was first reported after PR #8169 merged in [discussion_r3974917500](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/8169#discussion_r3974917500) and [discussion_r3974917503](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/8169#discussion_r3974917503). The behavior remains unchanged after #11596 and #11652.

## Reproduction

A deterministic loopback HTTP/SSE probe exercised the public `ResponsesPipeline.executeStream()` path with synthetic identifiers and no credentials.

Normal request cleanup:

```text
converted input: [reasoning, function_call]
wire input:      [reasoning]
```

Reasoning-ID rejection recovery:

```text
first request: [message, reasoning, function_call, function_call_output]
retry:         [message, function_call, function_call_output]
```

Encrypted-reasoning rejection recovery with a visible summary:

```text
first request: [message, reasoning, function_call, function_call_output]
retry:         [message, assistant_message, function_call, function_call_output]
```

The signature-only recovery case produces the same retry without the assistant message.

Existing tests do not cover this invariant. The cleaner tests assert only call/output pairing and intentionally keep all other item types. The recovery test named `preserves tool call/result pairs when recovering encrypted replay` places its tool pair after all reasoning items, so it never exercises `[reasoning, function_call, function_call_output]`.

This is not the legacy missing-ID row in #11494: valid IDs reproduce the defect whenever an orphaned call is removed, and the recovery path does not depend on missing IDs. #8533 is the broader provenance design, not this wire-validity bug.

# What did you expect to happen?

Every request transformation should preserve or remove a replayed reasoning item and its following item atomically. Normal cleanup and both recovery classes should never emit a dangling `reasoning` or `function_call` item.

Regression coverage should include:

- orphan cleanup of `[reasoning, function_call]` when the call output is missing;
- ID-rejection recovery for reasoning with a visible summary and signature-only reasoning;
- encrypted-content rejection recovery for the same two shapes; and
- unaffected reasoning/message and complete reasoning/call/output controls.

# Client information

Source-level and loopback verification on macOS with Node.js 22.15.0, Qwen Code `main` at `4a029e64e6f025a9b58f2cddef0ff652eb9325a9`. No provider credentials or private endpoint were used.

# Login information

Synthetic local Responses-compatible endpoint; no login required.

# Anything else we need to know?

One issue is intentional: both failures have the same root cause—request rewrites do not model the reasoning/following-item pair as an atomic unit. No dedicated open issue was found by title, body, or comment search.

prs.title: fix(web-shell): reset follow pause when the session changes (#15038)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A reading pause now ends when the displayed session changes. The reconnect-completion effect added for #15009 keeps the pause across a replay in the same session; this change makes sure the pause does not follow the reader into a different session, where the new transcript would otherwise stay above the latest content.

## Why it's needed

The pause is stored in a ref that outlives the transcript. Before this change, switching sessions while scrolled up left the new session stranded mid-history: nothing had paused its follow behavior, but the old session's flag was still set. Resetting the flag in the existing session-scoped reset keeps the intended reconnect behavior and restores follow for the new session.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open a web-shell session long enough to scroll.
2. Scroll up to pause following.
3. Switch to another session and let its transcript replay.
4. Confirm the new session lands at the bottom and keeps following new messages.
5. Reconnect the same session (for example, reload while streaming) and confirm the reading pause is still preserved, matching #15009.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: switching sessions while paused left the new transcript at the old scroll position (`expected 600 to be 300` in the new DOM test). After: the new transcript lands at the bottom, and the same-session reconnect pause test still passes.

### Tested on

|     OS     |    Status     |
| :--------: | :-----------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  |     ✅        |

### Environment (optional)

Local unit/DOM tests and the full web-shell Vitest suite; no browser E2E run (Playwright browsers are not installed in this environment).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the pause is dropped on any session-key change, which is the desired boundary; same-session reconnects are unchanged.
- Not validated / out of scope: the exact failed CI job's log was unavailable; the local equivalent suite is green, and the new test covers the regression found in the changed code.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15038

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

当显示会话发生变化时，阅读暂停现在会结束。#15009 新增的“追赶完成”效果会在同一会话的回放期间保留暂停；本次修改确保暂停不会跟随读者进入另一个会话，否则新会话的记录会停留在最新内容上方。

## 为什么需要

暂停状态保存在一个比记录本身存活更久的 ref 中。修改前，在向上滚动时切换会话会让新会话停留在历史中间：并没有任何操作暂停了新会话的跟随行为，但旧会话的标志仍然存在。在现有的会话级重置中清除该标志，可以保留预期的重连行为，并恢复新会话的跟随。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 打开一个足够长、可以滚动的 web-shell 会话。
2. 向上滚动以暂停跟随。
3. 切换到另一个会话，并让其记录回放。
4. 确认新会话落到底部，并在新消息到来时继续跟随。
5. 重连同一会话（例如在流式输出期间刷新），确认阅读暂停仍然保留，与 #15009 一致。

### 证据（修改前与修改后）

修改前：在暂停状态下切换会话，新记录会停留在旧的滚动位置（新 DOM 测试中表现为 `expected 600 to be 300`）。修改后：新记录落到底部，同一会话重连的暂停测试仍然通过。

### 测试环境

|    操作系统    |    状态     |
| :------------: | :---------: |
|  🍏 macOS      | ⚠️ 未测试   |
| 🪟 Windows     | ⚠️ 未测试   |
|  🐧 Linux      |     ✅      |

### 环境（可选）

本地单元/DOM 测试和完整 web-shell Vitest 套件；未运行浏览器 E2E（当前环境未安装 Playwright 浏览器）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：任何会话键变化都会清除暂停，这正是期望的边界；同一会话内的重连行为不变。
- 未验证 / 范围外：无法获取失败 CI 作业的具体日志；本地等价套件全绿，新测试覆盖了在修改代码中发现的回归。

prs.title: fix(ci): preserve Maven suite results across cache write-back failures
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR hardens the SDK Java Maven cache path after the suite/write-back lock split. Failed MariaDB suites can still publish downloaded artifacts while preserving the original suite status, cache setup failures preserve the already-known suite result, and the final error annotation identifies the failed Maven stage. Cache seeds report copy failures, tolerate an unavailable cache or failed best-effort prune, and detach mutable resolver metadata before Maven runs. Write-back excludes the same metadata and partial-download files.

## Why it's needed

The lock relocation associated with #15262 already landed on main through #15128 and #15254. This branch is the remaining hardening delta: a failed suite should not throw away reusable downloads, a best-effort cache operation should not replace the suite result, and mutable resolver state should not be published as an immutable shared artifact. The test repair in 11c0f4b2fb12c also includes the deferred-status reporter in extracted shell snippets so those tests can exercise their intended paths.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Fail either Maven stage in the self-hosted MariaDB lane. Reusable downloaded artifacts should reach write-back, later suites should not run, and the step should retain the failed stage's status and annotation.
- Run a green and a failed suite with an unusable cache or missing job-local repository. The cache fault should produce a warning and preserve the suite result.
- Seed a warm cache containing resolver markers and version metadata. Mutable hardlinks should be detached before Maven runs; write-back should publish artifacts while excluding resolver markers, metadata and partial-download files.
- Exercise a cold cache and a seed prune failure. Both should still reach Maven; an actual copy failure should remain visible in the log.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The current base already runs Maven before acquiring the cache lock. On the remaining delta, the prior Linux A/B report found that failed MariaDB runs publish their download delta and retain failure, and that write-back excludes resolver markers. Its seed-prune regression was repaired by restoring best-effort pruning. The latest closeout comment records verification against the exact current head and distinguishes macOS tests from Linux shell witnesses and CI.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | Focused workflow guard tests; Linux-only cases skip |
| Linux | See the exact-head closeout evidence and CI links; macOS results are not Linux verification |
| Windows | Not run locally |

## Risk & Scope

The host cache remains best-effort. Failure to seed can increase network resolution. An unexpected bare-flock failure remains fatal. Real Maven resolver behavior and contention on the self-hosted pool require CI evidence beyond shell fixtures.

#15286 contains distinct follow-up work: existing-destination seed nesting, removal of old in-house artifacts from the host cache, self-hosted Checkstyle repository selection, and reference-release cache isolation. Those changes remain separately owned. Shared-helper and test-fixture extraction are deferred rather than widening this repair.

Related to #15262; the original lock relocation is already on main.

prs.title: fix(ci): keep sdk-java resolver bookkeeping and in-house jars out of the host cache (#15281)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The job-local Maven repository that the sdk-java suites resolve from no longer shares mutable inodes with the host cache:

- Every seed site drops `maven-metadata-local.xml` together with the other resolver bookkeeping names (`_remote.repositories`, `resolver-status.properties`, `*.lastUpdated`, `*.tmp`), so the unlocked Maven runs cannot rewrite a host-cache file through a seeded hardlink.
- The locked write-back removes the two in-house fixed-release coordinates from the host cache, prunes them at any depth rather than only at the repository root, publishes only job-produced files (the same five names stay job-local), and downgrades a failed cache-directory creation to a warning instead of reddening a green suite.
- The self-hosted Managed Agent Checkstyle leg resolves the SDK from the job-local repository the suite installed it into.
- The release builder's seed copies into the job-local repository instead of nesting a second `repository/` inside it, and drops the same bookkeeping names.
- The workflow meta-tests pin the five exclusions at every seed and both prunes, the write-back's children and their fd 9 closure, the host-side removal, the warning path, and the Checkstyle repository.

## Why it's needed

Moving Maven above the per-host lock is only safe while the job-local repository has no inode in common with the host cache. Maven's resolver rewrites its bookkeeping files in place, and the suites `install` two fixed-release in-house artifacts: seeded as hardlinks, both let an unlocked run mutate state that every sibling job on the host reads.

Correction to the earlier description: the lock-scope change itself ("only the write-back takes the lock") landed through #15128 and #15254 and is already on main. #15274 remains open with overlapping cache and deferred-status changes. This PR is the cache-isolation half that makes that scope safe, and it is judged on that, not on the lock wait from #15281.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open the `SDK Java (fast) / ubuntu-latest / Java 21` job of a PR that touches a managed-agent path. The self-hosted step should show the `cp -aln` seed and all three Maven invocations before any `Waiting for the sdk-java host lock` line; the lock wait should appear only at the cache write-back, and the write-back should remove the in-house coordinates before copying. Grep the job-local repository for `maven-metadata-local.xml` after the suite: it should hold only job-produced files.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: a seeded `maven-metadata-local.xml` and a seeded `qwencode-sdk` jar were the same inode as the host cache, so the unlocked `mvn install` changed the host file (same inode, SHA and mtime both moved). After: the host file is byte- and mtime-identical while the job-local copy is still written, the write-back publishes zero bookkeeping files and never the in-house coordinates, and the host cache loses the pre-PR in-house trees. N/A for UI.

### Tested on

|     OS     |                       Status                        |
| :--------: | :-------------------------------------------------: |
|  🍏 macOS  |                   ⚠️ not tested                    |
| 🪟 Windows |                   ⚠️ not tested                    |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ meta-tests, size baseline, lint, Prettier        |

### Environment (optional)

Meta-tests only: `scripts/tests/sdk-java-workflow.test.js` (129 passed), `scripts/tests/workflow-size.test.js` (239 passed, 1 skipped), `scripts/tests/sdk-java-lock.test.js` (14 passed). No JDK 21 / Maven in this container, so the real Java suite is left to CI.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a cold host pays the seed cost once, and the write-back is best-effort and capped at 300 seconds, matching the MariaDB lane. The write-back also deletes pre-existing in-house copies from the host cache — intended, because they are the stale fixed-release jars the in-house prune exists to stop publishing.
- Not validated / out of scope: the real ECS pool and its ticketed lock queue; the full JDK 21 Maven suite; the MySQL / MariaDB integration lanes; the hosted legs.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

Design documents: [English](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Related to #15281 (the lock-scope change landed through #15128 and #15254; this PR closes the cache-isolation gap that the smaller lock scope depends on).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

sdk-java 套件解析所使用的 job 本地 Maven 仓库，不再与宿主缓存共享可写 inode：

- 每个播种站点在删除其他解析器记账文件（`_remote.repositories`、`resolver-status.properties`、`*.lastUpdated`、`*.tmp`）的同时也删除 `maven-metadata-local.xml`，因此不持锁的 Maven 运行无法穿透播种的硬链接改写宿主缓存。
- 持锁的写回会在宿主缓存中删除两个内部固定发布坐标，按任意深度 prune 而不只匹配仓库根，只发布本 job 产生的文件（同样五个名字留在 job 本地），并把缓存目录创建失败降级为警告，而不是让绿色套件变红。
- self-hosted 的 Managed Agent Checkstyle leg 从套件安装到的 job 本地仓库解析 SDK。
- 发布构建的播种改为向 job 本地仓库内复制，而不是在其中再嵌套一个 `repository/`，并删除同样的记账文件。
- 工作流元测试钉住每个播种点与两处 prune 的五个排除名、写回子进程及其 fd 9 关闭、宿主侧删除、警告路径，以及 Checkstyle 的仓库。

## 为什么需要

把 Maven 移到池级锁之外，只有在 job 本地仓库与宿主缓存没有共同 inode 时才是安全的。Maven 解析器会原地重写记账文件，而套件会 `install` 两个固定发布坐标的内部构件：一旦以硬链接播种，二者都会让不持锁的运行改写同宿主上所有兄弟 job 都读取的状态。

对早先描述的更正：持锁范围的改动本身（“只有写回取锁”）已通过 #15128 和 #15254 落地并在 main 上。#15274 仍然开放，其中缓存和延后状态处理的改动与本 PR 有重叠。本 PR 是让该范围安全成立的缓存隔离部分，评审应以这一点为准，而不是 #15281 的锁等待。

## Reviewer 测试计划

### 如何验证

打开一个触及 managed-agent 路径的 PR 的 `SDK Java (fast) / ubuntu-latest / Java 21` job。self-hosted step 应先出现 `cp -aln` 播种和三次 Maven 调用，之后才可能出现 `Waiting for the sdk-java host lock`；锁等待只应出现在缓存写回处，且写回会先删除内部坐标再复制。套件结束后在 job 本地仓库里 grep `maven-metadata-local.xml`，应当只剩本 job 产生的文件。

### 证据（Before & After）

Before：播种出的 `maven-metadata-local.xml` 与 `qwencode-sdk` jar 与宿主缓存是同一 inode，不持锁的 `mvn install` 会改写宿主文件（inode 相同，SHA 与 mtime 都变化）。After：宿主文件字节与 mtime 完全不变，同时 job 本地副本仍被写入；写回不发布任何记账文件、也从不发布内部坐标；宿主缓存中遗留的内部目录被删除。UI 不适用。

### 测试环境

仅元测试：`scripts/tests/sdk-java-workflow.test.js`（129 通过）、`scripts/tests/workflow-size.test.js`（239 通过、1 跳过）、`scripts/tests/sdk-java-lock.test.js`（14 通过）。容器内没有 JDK 21 / Maven，真实 Java 套件交给 CI。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险与取舍：冷宿主要付一次播种成本；写回是尽力而为且上限 300 秒，与 MariaDB 通道一致。写回还会删除宿主缓存中遗留的内部坐标副本——这是有意为之，因为它们正是内部坐标 prune 要阻止继续发布的过期固定发布 jar。
- 未验证 / 范围外：真实 ECS 池及其票据化锁队列；完整 JDK 21 Maven 套件；MySQL / MariaDB 集成通道；hosted leg。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 issue

与 #15281 相关（持锁范围的改动已通过 #15128 和 #15254 落地；本 PR 补上更小持锁范围所依赖的缓存隔离缺口）。

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): exempt surefire-bound IT classes from the failsafe roster
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The `non-hosted` roster in `scripts/check-failsafe-reports.js` requires every `*IT` class of the job's family to appear in `target/failsafe-reports`. `packages/managed-agent-server` binds `ManagedAgentPackagingIT` to the `artifact-packaging` **surefire** execution (`pom.xml:347-351`) and excludes it from the mysql-integration **failsafe** (`pom.xml:510`). A class that is forbidden to run under failsafe can therefore never satisfy the roster, so the step fails after Maven has already reported success.

This names the surefire-bound classes per module, skips them in the roster with a line saying why, and fails the check if the module's pom stops binding such a name to **both** a surefire `<include>` and a failsafe `<exclude>` — so the exemption cannot drift away from the pom it describes.

The fast CI also exposed a pre-existing H2 error in the message-store fixture. This change binds that fixture to the managed JDBC template, matching the fix in #15802, so its binary-key query uses the correct parameter conversion.

## Why it's needed

This is #15820 item 1. It is not caused by any PR: it reproduces on a scheduled run of `main` itself with no PR code present, and it turns the full tier red for every managed-agent PR, which hides genuine regressions and makes each one pay for the same re-attribution.

The failure text points at the wrong thing, which is why it survived review. The job shows:

```
[INFO] --- surefire:3.5.6:test (artifact-packaging) @ qwen-managed-agent-server ---
[INFO] Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
[INFO] BUILD SUCCESS
##[error]packages/managed-agent-server: ...ManagedAgentPackagingIT ran no test in this job
```

The tests ran and passed. Only the roster disagrees, because it reads a report directory that this class is configured never to write to.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Read the two edits against the pom: the exemption list names `ManagedAgentPackagingIT` for `packages/managed-agent-server`, and that name really is bound to a surefire include and a failsafe exclude there. Then check the drift guard: if either pom binding disappears, the check fails rather than silently exempting a class that no longer needs it.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, on a PR carrying no managed-agent changes: `##[error]packages/managed-agent-server: com.alibaba.qwen.code.managedagent.ManagedAgentPackagingIT ran no test in this job`, with every other `*IT` in the leg reporting its counts.

After, with the exemption: the roster skips the class and prints `ManagedAgentPackagingIT runs under surefire, not failsafe`; a pom that drops either binding fails with `is listed as surefire-bound but its pom no longer binds it to a surefire include and a failsafe exclude`.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :--: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ `check-failsafe-reports` 22/22, prettier clean, eslint clean |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ CI |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ CI |

The follow-up fixture change is awaiting CI validation; the local results above apply to the roster change.

## Risk & Scope

- **Main risk or tradeoff**: the exemption is an explicit list rather than something derived from the pom, so a new surefire-bound IT class needs one line here. The drift guard makes the reverse mistake — a stale entry — fail loudly, and the alternative (parsing Maven's plugin configuration) is more machinery than this problem justifies.
- **Not validated / out of scope**: #15820 item 2 (the plain-`JdbcTemplate` VARBINARY reads in the `Hosted*IT` fixtures) is untouched here; that one changes how the ITs resolve the template and belongs with its own evidence.
- **Breaking changes / migration**: none — the roster is stricter than before in one direction only (a stale exemption is now an error).

## Linked Issues

Relates to #15820 (item 1). Does not close it — item 2 is still open.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

`scripts/check-failsafe-reports.js` 的 `non-hosted` 花名册要求该家族的每个 `*IT` 类都出现在 `target/failsafe-reports` 里。但 `packages/managed-agent-server` 把 `ManagedAgentPackagingIT` 绑到了 `artifact-packaging` 的 **surefire** 执行（`pom.xml:347-351`），同时又从 mysql-integration 的 **failsafe** 里排除（`pom.xml:510`）。一个被禁止在 failsafe 下运行的类永远无法满足花名册，于是 Maven 已经 `BUILD SUCCESS` 之后这一步才失败。

本 PR 按模块显式列出这类 surefire 绑定的类，在花名册中跳过并打印原因；同时若模块 pom 不再同时保留该名字的 surefire `<include>` 与 failsafe `<exclude>`，检查会失败——避免豁免清单与它描述的 pom 脱节。

fast CI 还暴露了消息存储测试夹具已有的 H2 错误。本 PR 同步 #15802 的修复，将该夹具绑定到 managed JDBC 模板，使二进制键查询使用正确的参数转换。该后续改动等待 CI 验证；上述本地结果仅对应花名册改动。

**为什么需要**：这是 #15820 的第 1 项。它不是任何 PR 引入的：main 自身的定时 run 在不含任何 PR 代码时就复现，并且让每个 managed-agent PR 的 full tier 全红，真实回归被淹没，每张 PR 都要重复归因。

**验证方式**：对照 pom 阅读两处改动；豁免清单里的名字确实同时具备 surefire include 与 failsafe exclude。再验证漂移守卫：任一绑定消失时检查失败，而不是悄悄继续豁免。

**实测**：`check-failsafe-reports` 22/22、prettier 与 eslint 均干净；CI 覆盖 Windows/Linux。

**风险**：豁免是显式清单而非从 pom 推导，新增 surefire 绑定的 IT 类需要加一行；反向错误（清单过期）会被漂移守卫报错。不解析 Maven 插件配置，是因为那套机具远超此问题所需。

**未覆盖**：#15820 第 2 项（`Hosted*IT` 里用普通 `JdbcTemplate` 读 VARBINARY）不在本 PR 范围。

</details>

prs.title: test(managed-agent): bind the full-application suites to the managed beans
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Every full-application test suite that still autowired the JDBC template and the transaction manager **by type** now pins them by name, to `managedJdbcTemplate` and `managedAgentTransactionManager`. That covers the acceptance fixture for the internal publication surface, the server integration suite, the extension-record fixture, and the remaining suites that were left on the default candidate after #15718.

## Why it's needed

The control plane publishes its own template and transaction manager as non-default candidates. A field or bean parameter that names only the type therefore resolves to Spring Boot's plain auto-configured beans, which do not convert `String` arguments for the `VARBINARY` identity columns. On H2 — the database every one of these suites runs against — the statement is refused outright:

```
Values of types "BINARY VARYING(144)" and "CHARACTER VARYING(36)" are not comparable
Values of types "BINARY VARYING(2048)" and "CHARACTER VARYING(8)" are not comparable
Values of types "BINARY VARYING(512)" and "CHARACTER VARYING(57)" are not comparable
```

Each of those showed up as a different flaking test on the managed-agent fast tier: the credential-enforcement acceptance test returning `500` instead of `403`, the server integration suite failing its turn-retry cleanup, and the extension-record fixture failing `listRecords`. They are one defect: the by-name migration in #15718 qualified the injection points that were red at the time and left the rest silently bound to the wrong bean.

Two sibling fixtures keep the unqualified form deliberately and are not touched: the same-context embedding suite asserts a plain host template next to the managed one, and the publication probe wiring only ever runs against MySQL, where the coercion exists.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The failures are data- and timing-dependent, so a reviewer should confirm the wiring and run the affected suites rather than look for a red-to-green transition.

1. Check that each suite's injection point now names the managed bean, and that no suite autowires either type without a qualifier under `@SpringBootTest`.
2. Run the suites: `cd packages/managed-agent-server && mvn -Dtest='ManagedAgentServerIntegrationTest,SurfaceAdmissionAcceptanceTest,ManagedExtensionRecordStoreTest,ManagedAgentDefinitionTest,ManagedTeamStoreTest' test`.
3. `mvn checkstyle:check`.

Expected: all green, 0 violations.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for UI. Locally, on this branch: the twenty-eight touched suites run `Tests run: 411, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` apart from the broker-gated `EventTransportBrokerGate`, which requires `qwen.gate.rocketmq.endpoints` and is not runnable outside that profile. `ManagedAgentServerIntegrationTest` alone: 57/57. `SurfaceAdmissionAcceptanceTest`: 328/328. `checkstyle:check` clean.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

JDK 21, `managed-agent-server` module tests on H2.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: these suites now share the production template and transaction manager, which is what the suites qualified in #15718 already do. No production code changes, no schema or endpoint changes.
- Not validated / out of scope: MySQL-only gates (`Hosted*IT`, `*MySqlIT`) still autowire by type in places; they run where the coercion exists, and are left for a follow-up that also excludes the plain autoconfiguration from the application so an unqualified injection fails at startup instead of binding silently.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none, test-only.

## Linked Issues

No issue: this is the residual of the by-name bean migration in #15718.

Publishes `available_commands_update` from each ACP session when its SkillManager cache changes, and unregisters that listener when the session is disposed. This replaces the earlier `Cache-Control: no-store` approach, which did not refresh server-side metadata.

Start a daemon session with a project Skill, edit its description and argument hint, and confirm the client receives an updated command snapshot after the SkillManager refresh. Closing the session must remove the listener.

The regression creates a real temporary `SKILL.md`, loads it through the real SkillManager cache and SkillCommandLoader, changes its metadata, refreshes the cache, and verifies the ACP update contains the new description and hint. It also verifies that a disposed session receives no later update.

Local validation: all 921 Session tests passed, the focused regression passed independently, and ESLint plus the pre-commit formatting/lint gate passed. Full CI on the updated head is pending.

macOS with Node.js 24.19.0.

## Risk & Scope

The net diff is limited to ACP session listener lifecycle and one regression test. It does not force per-request Skill scans or change route caching, trust boundaries, or command payload shape.

## Linked Issues

Closes #10918
