prs.title: feat(web-shell): allow embedding hosts to pick workspace directories
prs.body:
## What this PR does

An application embedding Web Shell can supply its own directory picker for the connected daemon through an optional callback. It takes precedence over native selection, receives an abort signal, and only fills the existing Add Workspace dialog. Registration, refresh, selection, persistence and trust continue through the explicit Add action. The Git URL source uses the same guarded picker for its existing parent-directory Browse action; the selected parent fills the clone target without starting a clone. Omitting the callback preserves the existing native capability and origin checks.

While a picker is pending, directory navigation is locked as well as input and submission: Parent is disabled and the folder list is hidden. A same-path selection therefore cannot be silently replaced by a mid-pick navigation. The hidden folder list keeps its layout space while picking; cancellation, errors and same-path selection restore its scroll position, while new directory results start at the top.

Pending selections are cancelled on close, unmount, connection/target changes, picker-source changes or replacement. Late results and errors are ignored even when the host ignores abort. The dialog releases its modal restrictions while a host picker is active so a host-owned interface outside the Web Shell portal can receive clicks and focus. Unclaimed focus parks on the busy Add panel, and returning from the host picker restores focus to Browse and preserves the dialog body scroll position.

## Why it's needed

An embedding application may already have a directory browser for a headless daemon and want to reuse it inside Web Shell's add-workspace flow. The existing public API requires a separate host-managed registration flow. The standalone directory browser remains separate from this integration use case.

The top-level optional callback, options-object signature and host-first behavior are implementation choices for review, not an approved public design. The [English design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/1d17fc1f8aca5a8c518af50567b7461e2e9bdf27/docs/design/web-shell-host-directory-picker.md) and [Chinese design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/1d17fc1f8aca5a8c518af50567b7461e2e9bdf27/docs/design/web-shell-host-directory-picker.zh-CN.md) describe the same decisions and limits.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Embed either public component with a host picker against a connected headless or cross-origin daemon. Browse should open that picker. Its returned daemon directory should fill the dialog without registering or granting trust. Explicit Add should retain normal registration, persistence, refresh and selection behavior.
2. Provide both a host callback and native capability. The host should win; cancellation and failures must not invoke native selection. Remove the callback and verify the original native capability/origin restrictions.
3. Leave a selection pending, then close, change the connected target/client or remove the host callback. The old signal should abort. Resolve or reject the old promise after a new selection starts; the current path, error and busy state must remain unchanged. Ordinary inline-callback rerenders should keep the selection alive.
4. With an existing path, open Browse and attempt Add, including a same-frame form submission: no registration should occur. In directory-browsing mode, Parent must be disabled and the folder list hidden without a false empty-folder message. Scroll the folder list and dialog body before Browse, then cancel: both positions should remain. Return the original path; focus should return to Browse and a subsequent explicit Add should register that path. Selecting a different directory should show its results from the top.
5. Select the Git repository source and Browse its parent directory. The chosen existing parent and repository name should fill the target; Clone and add must remain disabled while picking and require an explicit later action.
6. Render the host picker outside Web Shell. Verify real clicking, typing and Select/Cancel. After host cancellation, the Add dialog should remain editable and trap keyboard focus again.

### Evidence (Before & After)

New tests were run before implementation: public-entry cases failed because Browse was absent, lifecycle tests failed without signal/invalidation, and later regressions exposed submission of an old path, uncancelled host removal and a host interface blocked by the modal dialog. The final affected tests and browser checks pass without weakening those assertions or adding retries.

The [browser regression spec](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/1d17fc1f8aca5a8c518af50567b7461e2e9bdf27/packages/web-shell/client/e2e/web-shell.host-directory-picker.spec.ts) exercises the public embedded component and produces screenshots of the host interface, restored Add dialog, and selected path. The results below distinguish browser/component checks from full-repository validation.

- Current follow-up: **130 focused tests passed** (99 dialog, 9 shared dialog shell, 22 public entry). Eight new cases cover native/host cancellation, same-path selection, errors and new directory results. Before the fix, six scroll-restoration cases failed; the two new-directory controls passed. The full Web Shell and Hosted suites below remain earlier runs.
- Current browser checks: **4 targeted real-component cases and all 8 existing public-harness cases passed**, with zero retries. Before the fix, both picker modes lost list scroll (`180 → 0`); at the taller viewport, both also lost body scroll (`40 → 0`). The fix preserves both, including the collapsed combobox and locked navigation. The targeted fixture uses production styles and deferred data, not a live daemon. Removing list restoration or the height placeholder independently reproduces the corresponding failure.
- Current build, bundle, repository lint, typecheck and formatting passed. Upstream main was integrated, resolving the adjacent protocol-table conflict while retaining both entries. The reviewed head's [CI run](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40209738060) and its other three workflows completed successfully; new-head checks are reported separately.
- Previous round at `c34858f2c`: **496 Web Shell files / 13,323 tests passed**, including all 89 dialog, 9 shared dialog shell and 22 public-entry cases. The complete Hosted Harness session file also passed **677 tests**. Build, bundle, repository lint, type checking and formatting passed.
- The previous Linux CI run failed exactly seven Hosted Harness tests. Those same seven failed locally before integration and passed after taking the existing upstream fix `2a9fb6db523588768b7f32f4957dd9ea6394bcc6`. This PR adds no separate CLI/core fix. Main also supplied current lint gate definitions.
- The merged Git-parent picker initially failed five new component cases and a real browser focus assertion. Those unchanged assertions now pass. A forced host-mode mutation also made the new public native-modality test fail, confirming it protects the App wiring.
- Previous-round browser validation (2026-10-25): **all 8 distinct cases verified** with real Chromium and mock daemon HTTP/SSE. Seven passed on the initial run; the first case exceeded the old temporary configuration's 8-second cold-start wait before reaching interaction. Its preserved trace had no application/HTTP error. Rerunning only that case with the repository's existing 20-second assertion/60-second test budgets passed (21.7s). No behavior assertion was weakened and automatic retries remained zero. Only the original host-interaction case is tagged `@smoke`.
- Separate browser observation confirms a 100ms fade/zoom entrance-animation replay during modality remounts. The imported style alias matches Radix's state attributes. This corrects the earlier source-only rejection; visual blink severity was not measured and animation suppression remains deferred.
- Historical full preflight at `d9adb4b843992b2e12275582ffd1842aa9516a42` exited 1 with 36 failures outside Web Shell; their individual baseline causes were not established. **Full preflight was not rerun for this follow-up.** The recorded results distinguish prior full-suite runs from the current focused verification; no full-repository preflight or pending remote check is represented as passing.

<details>
<summary>Functional demo: host selection → filled path → explicit registration</summary>

Captured on 2026-10-23 with the committed public-component harness and mock daemon. The custom directory browser is host-owned fixture UI, not a new built-in browser. These are demonstrations of the implementation, not upstream baseline screenshots.

1. The host interface accepts ordinary clicks and input.

![Host directory picker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/3342f25bc9f1e900be61ba1b6a79b072d3019b60/docs/design/assets/web-shell-host-directory-picker-host.png)

2. Select fills the path; no registration has occurred yet.

![Selected path awaiting explicit registration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/3342f25bc9f1e900be61ba1b6a79b072d3019b60/docs/design/assets/web-shell-host-directory-picker-selected.png)

3. Explicit Register creates and selects the workspace. The capture observed one workspace POST, no native-picker requests, and no browser console/page errors.

![Registered workspace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/3342f25bc9f1e900be61ba1b6a79b072d3019b60/docs/design/assets/web-shell-host-directory-picker-registered.png)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Portable browser reproduction</summary>

After installing the pinned repository dependencies and building, run from `packages/web-shell`:

```sh
npx --no-install playwright install chromium
npx --no-install playwright test client/e2e/web-shell.host-directory-picker.spec.ts --config playwright.config.ts --project=chromium --workers=1 --retries=0
```

This is the portable recipe for the committed tests. The current eight-case run used a temporary configuration selecting system Chromium, one worker, zero retries and a 1280×900 default viewport, with the repository's 20-second assertion / 60-second test budgets: **8 passed (37.2s)**.

</details>

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :--: |
| macOS | Not tested |
| Windows | Not tested |
| Linux | Tested |

### Environment (optional)

Latest follow-up commit `1d17fc1f8aca5a8c518af50567b7461e2e9bdf27`, incorporating upstream `338f13366c1d86e586f7e0785942740da3503887`; original full-suite/preflight snapshot `d9adb4b843992b2e12275582ffd1842aa9516a42`. Upstream base `51f1d2c8bbf187c035e90d17b81332a2aadc358f`, source package 0.26.1, Node 24.19.0, Chromium 154.0.8037.57, Playwright 1.61.1. The browser test uses the public embedded component with mock daemon responses. The global `qwen` CLI was unavailable; the optional embedded callback is not configurable through that standalone entry.

## Risk & Scope

- R1-1 is partially addressed: focus and scroll restoration are fixed. Radix still remounts content when modality changes, so stable DOM identity is not promised. Concurrently opening another `DialogShell` can still lead to incorrect layer/`aria-hidden` ordering when Add becomes modal again; resolving shared layer coordination is deferred. Entrance animations also replay on remount; handoff-specific animation suppression is deferred. Classic-scrollbar horizontal movement and screen-reader announcements were not tested. R1-2 through R1-4 are addressed by focus/busy handling, regression/mutation coverage, and smoke selection.
- The round-4 scroll regression is addressed with a picker-scoped list snapshot and an inert height placeholder; no shared-dialog redesign is included. The six expressly deferred round-4 notes remain follow-ups: shared-shell invariant tests, Git suggestion bookkeeping witnesses, late-rejection assertions, target baseUrl/status dependency witnesses, native Git picker keyboard-focus restoration, and native-picker mock isolation. The native Git focus case has source support but was not independently reproduced in this follow-up and is not claimed fixed.
- R3-1 locks the two remaining directory navigation controls and avoids a false empty-list message while picking. It preserves the existing same-value suggestion invalidation and return focus; no additional path-state ref is needed. The five items explicitly deferred in the round-3 review body remain follow-ups.
- Round 2 deferred notes: adopted the target-token documentation, public native-modality test, neutral picker error text, connected-state documentation, registration mock reset and native capability wording. Dedicated availability/suggestion-reset mutation witnesses, a same-instance browser stale-result scenario and animation suppression remain non-blocking follow-ups.
- The host must return an existing absolute path on the same connected daemon and own its picker's accessibility, focus and stacking. Escape retains the Add dialog's close behavior and aborts the request before an ordinary host bubbling handler runs; an explicit host Cancel returning `undefined` leaves Add open. Independent host Escape ownership remains a review decision.
- Not validated: live daemon authentication/authorization and trust persistence, actual OS dialogs, React 18 runtime, other operating systems/browser engines or mobile layouts. Client abort does not guarantee that a server-side OS picker closes. No SDK/backend cancellation contract is changed.
- No required migration: the callback is optional. No standalone-browser exposure, directory-creation API or whole-dialog replacement API is included. Existing Git clone execution is unchanged.
- Most changed lines are tests and bilingual documentation. The public callback, lifecycle ownership and modal handoff are one integration flow and are kept together so the new API ships with observable regression coverage.

## Linked Issues

Closes #15186.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

嵌入 Web Shell 的应用可以通过可选回调，为当前连接的 daemon 提供自己的目录选择器。宿主选择器优先于原生选择器，接收 abort signal，返回值只回填现有 Add Workspace 对话框。注册、刷新、选中、持久化和 trust 仍通过显式 Add 完成。Git URL 来源已有的父目录 Browse 操作复用同一受保护的选择器；所选父目录仅回填克隆目标，不会启动克隆。未配置回调时，保留现有原生能力与同源检查。

选择进行中时，除输入和提交外，目录导航也被锁定：上级目录按钮禁用，文件夹列表隐藏。因此，选择过程中导航不会悄悄覆盖选择器返回的同值路径。选择期间保留隐藏列表的布局空间；取消、错误及同值选择恢复其滚动位置，新目录结果仍从顶部开始。

关闭、卸载、连接/目标变化、选择器来源切换或后续选择替换时，取消正在进行的选择。即使宿主忽略 abort，也丢弃迟到的结果和错误。宿主选择器进行中时，对话框临时解除模态限制，使 Web Shell portal 外的宿主界面可以接收点击和焦点。无人接管的焦点停放在带忙碌状态的 Add 面板；从宿主选择器返回时，焦点回到 Browse，并保留正文滚动位置。

## 为什么需要

嵌入应用可能已有面向 headless daemon 的目录浏览器，希望在 Web Shell 的添加工作区流程中复用它。现有公开 API 要求宿主另行管理注册流程。独立应用的目录浏览器与本集成场景保持分离。

顶层可选回调、选项对象签名和宿主优先行为是待评审的实现选择，不代表公开设计已获批准。[英文设计](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/1d17fc1f8aca5a8c518af50567b7461e2e9bdf27/docs/design/web-shell-host-directory-picker.md)与[中文设计](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/1d17fc1f8aca5a8c518af50567b7461e2e9bdf27/docs/design/web-shell-host-directory-picker.zh-CN.md)说明了对应的决策和限制。

## 评审者测试计划

### 验证方法

1. 为任一公开组件配置宿主选择器，连接 headless 或跨源 daemon。Browse 应打开宿主选择器；返回的 daemon 目录只回填对话框，不注册或授予 trust。显式 Add 应保持正常注册、持久化、刷新和选中行为。
2. 同时提供宿主回调与原生能力。应优先使用宿主；取消或失败不得调用原生选择器。移除回调后验证原有能力/同源限制。
3. 让选择保持 pending，再关闭、切换连接目标/client 或移除宿主回调。旧 signal 应 abort。在新选择开始后 resolve/reject 旧 Promise，当前路径、错误和忙碌状态不得改变。普通内联回调重渲染应保持当前选择。
4. 已有路径时启动 Browse 并尝试 Add，包括同帧表单提交：不应发生注册。在目录浏览模式中，上级目录按钮应禁用，文件夹列表应隐藏，且不能误报目录为空。在 Browse 前滚动文件夹列表和正文，再取消选择：两处位置应保持。选择器返回原路径后，焦点应回到 Browse；后续显式 Add 应注册该路径。选择不同目录后，其结果应从顶部显示。
5. 选择 Git repository 来源并 Browse 父目录。所选已存在目录与仓库名应组合回填目标；选择期间 Clone and add 不可用，后续仍需显式操作。
6. 在 Web Shell 外渲染宿主选择器，实际点击、输入、选择和取消。宿主取消后，Add 对话框应仍可编辑并重新约束键盘焦点。

### 前后对照证据

新增测试先于实现运行：公开入口用例因缺少 Browse 失败，生命周期测试因缺少 signal/失效保护失败；后续回归还暴露了提交旧路径、移除宿主未取消以及模态对话框阻挡宿主界面的问题。最终相关测试和浏览器检查已通过，未弱化这些断言或添加重试。

[浏览器回归测试](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/1d17fc1f8aca5a8c518af50567b7461e2e9bdf27/packages/web-shell/client/e2e/web-shell.host-directory-picker.spec.ts)通过公开嵌入组件交互，并生成宿主界面、恢复后的 Add 对话框和选中路径的截图。下列结果分别说明浏览器/组件检查与全仓验证。

- 当前跟进：**130 项聚焦测试通过**（99 项对话框、9 项共享对话框壳、22 项公开入口）。新增 8 项覆盖原生/宿主取消、同值选择、错误和新目录结果。修复前，6 项滚动恢复用例失败，2 项新目录对照用例通过。下列完整 Web Shell 与 Hosted 套件仍是更早轮次的运行。
- 当前浏览器检查：**4 项真实组件定向用例和全部 8 项既有公开 harness 用例通过**，零重试。修复前两种选择模式均丢失列表滚动（`180 → 0`）；较高窗口下还都丢失正文滚动（`40 → 0`）。修复后两者均保持，且组合框折叠与导航锁定不变。定向 fixture 使用生产样式及延迟数据，并非真实 daemon。分别移除列表恢复或等高占位，会再次触发对应失败。
- 当前构建、bundle、全仓 lint、类型检查及格式检查通过。已合入 main，解决协议表相邻行冲突并保留两项内容。被评审提交的 [CI 运行](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40209738060)及其余三项 workflow 已成功完成；新提交的检查另行报告。
- 上一轮 `c34858f2c` 快照：**Web Shell 的 496 个文件 / 13,323 项测试全部通过**，包括 89 项对话框、9 项共享对话框壳、22 项公开入口测试。完整 Hosted Harness session 文件的 **677 项测试也全部通过**。构建、bundle、全仓 lint、类型检查和格式检查通过。

### 环境

## 风险与范围

- R1-1 部分采纳：已修复焦点与滚动恢复。Radix 切换模态仍会重挂内容，因此不保证 DOM 节点身份。并发打开另一个 `DialogShell` 时，Add 恢复模态仍可能导致层级/`aria-hidden` 排序错误；共享层级协调暂缓处理。重挂也会重播入场动画，交接专用的动画抑制暂缓。尚未验证传统滚动条横向偏移及屏幕阅读器播报。R1-2 至 R1-4 已通过焦点/忙碌处理、回归与变异测试、smoke 筛选处理。

- 宿主必须返回同一已连接 daemon 上已存在目录的绝对路径，并负责自身选择器的可访问性、焦点和层叠。Escape 保留 Add 对话框的关闭行为，会早于宿主普通冒泡处理器取消请求；宿主显式 Cancel 返回 `undefined` 则保留 Add。独立的宿主 Escape 归属仍待评审。
- 未验证：真实 daemon 的认证/授权与 trust 持久化、实际 OS 对话框、React 18 运行时、其他操作系统/浏览器引擎或移动布局。客户端 abort 不保证关闭服务端 OS 选择器。本次不修改 SDK/后端取消契约。
- 无强制迁移：回调可选。不包含开放独立应用浏览器、创建目录或替换整个对话框的 API。现有 Git 克隆执行流程保持不变。

prs.title: feat(acp): display teammate activity without affecting leader output [13902 C/3]
prs.body:
Stack: **[#15657](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15657) → [#15658](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15658) → [#15659](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15659)**. This is **C**, based on B (`split/13902-team-coordination`, `435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a`), which depends on A (`3294001f39040a668fcbad20045b64e03dc1b6e6`). Base branch: `split/13902-team-coordination`. Split from #13902 at source commit `6ed7884c381dfe1c59bd975d6cf61dbb41ef441c`; candidate C: `1d6bc91dd3cf29e2010043e397ea8c429b72cf03`. Review C against B.

## What this PR does

Shows teammate tool progress and inter-agent messages as attributed activity notices. Tool activity names the acting teammate. An inter-agent message carries the recipient in `agent` and the sender in structured `author`, with direction shown in the message text. Failed tool results retain their failure status and description.

These frames are observational: they bypass the durable peer notification queue, do not wake the leader and are not persisted. The SDK classifies them as status notices, coalesces bounded tool progress while retaining discrete message/failure rows, and keeps the active leader text and usage stream intact. Web Shell renders the notices; child-session result collection and qwen-live filter this display source while retaining valid background responses. C reuses A's identity contract and B's sink/session lifecycle, and includes the activity and downstream-filter tests.

## Why it's needed

Durable reports tell the leader what a teammate concluded, but give the client little visibility while work is in progress. Display-only activity provides that visibility without scheduling a model turn for every tool call or mixing teammate traffic into the leader's answer and usage.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Verify candidate C and its B parent, build the candidate, then run C's focused CLI, SDK, Web Shell and qwen-live tests serially. Re-run the core coordination harness as a regression check for the changed producer. Run each `../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run <package-relative paths>` command from its package directory. The build exited 0; all 9 focused/regression test files passed, as detailed below.
2. Stream leader text and usage while a teammate emits tool calls/results and an inter-agent message. Confirm that activity appears as notices, leaves leader text continuous, keeps usage attached to the leader, and never queues an automatic turn or a persisted notification.
3. Check failed-tool display and message direction. Exercise repeated activity, user/branch boundaries and discrete message/failure rows; confirm bounded coalescing and stable origin event IDs.
4. Confirm that child-session result collection and qwen-live exclude `teammate_activity`, while the positive `background_notification_response` control remains visible.

### Evidence (Before & After)

On candidate `1d6bc91dd3cf29e2010043e397ea8c429b72cf03`, `npm run build` exited 0. The 8 directly changed test files passed **1772 tests**: CLI 1404, SDK 46, Web Shell 315 and qwen-live 7. The additional core coordination-harness regression file passed **99 tests**. Combined result: **9 test files, 1871 passed, no failures**. Runtime, UI E2E and standalone typecheck have not been run; matched before/after protocol and UI evidence is not available. This PR remains a draft. C's complete tree equals the fixed source tree, but tree equality does not establish runtime correctness or resolve inherited feedback. Historical passing counts from #13902 are not acceptance evidence for C.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Build and 9 focused/regression test files passed; runtime/UI E2E and standalone typecheck not run |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local isolated worktree; repository-root build followed by serial package-local Vitest runs completed.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: activity is ephemeral and disappears on reload; durable reports and roster notices remain B's responsibility. Attribution direction, coalescing boundaries and downstream source filtering require separate verification.
- Not validated / out of scope: exact-SHA runtime/UI and cross-platform validation are pending. This split preserves source behavior and does not repair its unresolved feedback.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: adds a teammate activity event/source and optional direction/tool metadata. No transcript migration is introduced because observational activity is not recorded.

Inherited unresolved feedback owned by C is not fixed by splitting:

- [R9-1: the recipient identity of an inter-agent message is interpreted as its author by the UI teammate prop/documentation](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372663).
- [R9-6: activity-specific structured fields are not reflected in the persistence schema declarations](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372680).

A's two replay findings and B's six coordination/test findings are also inherited through the stack; ownership remains with those layers.

Design: [English](docs/design/2026-10-11-agent-team-identity-projection.md) · [中文](docs/design/2026-10-11-agent-team-identity-projection.zh-CN.md). C restores the fixed source's paired documents, including the activity decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria and known gaps. The cumulative tree, including these documents, equals source commit `6ed7884c381dfe1c59bd975d6cf61dbb41ef441c`.

## Linked Issues

Related: #13785. Split source: #13902. This PR remains a draft. No automatic issue or PR closure is requested.

prs.title: fix(cli): align the Skills config catalog with runtime automatic discovery
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`GET /workspace/config/skills` and its workspace-qualified route keep one Skill inventory per workspace, and that inventory was only rebuilt when a configuration mutation or a workspace removal invalidated it. A Skill created directly on disk — including by the agent's own file-writing tools — therefore stayed invisible on the config endpoints for the daemon's lifetime, while the runtime Skills endpoints picked it up.

This PR aligns the catalog with the runtime's discovery model instead of adding a second, request-driven refresh policy. The retained `SkillManager` per workspace now watches the project and user Skill directories (`SkillManager.startWatching()` — the same chokidar setup, ignored-file filter, depth, and 150 ms debounce the runtime uses), so a Skill created, edited, or removed on disk lands in its cache as the change happens. Reads stay cache-backed: no request scans the filesystem, and the first read still enumerates fully. A background revalidation runs at most once per second — the runtime snapshot's revalidation interval — and covers what the watchers cannot observe, such as a Skills directory created after they started or a dropped event. It never blocks a read and keeps the last good catalog when it fails, retrying on a later read. Settings-derived state is untouched: it is still re-read on every request, and explicit invalidation still rebuilds the catalog immediately.

## Why it's needed

A management client consuming the configuration endpoint never shows a project Skill written outside the config APIs until the daemon restarts. Writing `SKILL.md` directly is a supported path — the agent does it with its own tools — and the file was already listed by runtime discovery, so the two endpoints disagreed about the same workspace. Reusing the runtime's discovery and revalidation semantics makes both views converge on the same mechanism, with the same bounded staleness, instead of the catalog following a separate policy.

## Mechanism reuse

- **Discovery**: `SkillManager.startWatching()` on the retained per-workspace manager. Project and user levels only; bundled Skills are immutable and extension Skills stay on the existing invalidation path.
- **Reads**: `listSkills()` from the manager's cache, exactly as the runtime endpoint answers from its snapshot.
- **Revalidation**: at most one background forced scan per workspace per second, shared by concurrent readers, with the last good catalog retained if it fails.
- **Invalidation**: unchanged — an explicit invalidation bumps the workspace epoch, drops the manager, and the next read rebuilds it from current settings.
- **Lifecycle**: every subscription is tracked per workspace and stopped when the manager is invalidated, when a workspace is removed, and at daemon shutdown; the next read after a removal re-subscribes. The throwaway `snapshot()` enumeration never starts a watcher.
- **Sharing and trust**: the native watcher is one per directory, shared by every `SkillManager` that watches it, so the trusted catalog and the workspace-service fallback serving the same workspace subscribe to a single chokidar set and it closes when the last subscriber stops. Only a trusted, non-safe-mode catalog watches at all; an untrusted or safe-mode read lists bundled Skills only, so it starts no watcher and does not create the user Skills directory.

## Freshness policy

- A change visible to the watcher is reflected by the next read (~150 ms debounce).
- A change no watcher could observe surfaces on the first read after the next one-second revalidation window; at most one read can be stale. The revalidation rescans only the two watched levels, so immutable bundled Skills are not re-read.
- A failed revalidation is logged, the previous catalog keeps answering, and the next read after the window retries.
- No read waits for a scan, so there is no read timeout to configure; unlike the runtime snapshot, the catalog never serves an empty placeholder in place of a good enumeration.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start `qwen serve` against a trusted workspace and read `GET /workspace/config/skills` once so the catalog is warm.
2. Create `.qwen/skills/download-verify-demo/SKILL.md` directly on disk (valid frontmatter), rather than through the install API.
3. Re-read the config endpoint: the entry appears on the next read after the watcher debounce, and at the latest on the first read after the one-second revalidation window. `GET /workspace/runtime/skills` lists it too.
4. Edit the description, then delete the directory, and re-read: the catalog follows both without a config mutation or daemon restart.

Expected: both endpoints list the same Skills within the same bounded window, with no request blocking on a full scan. Observed before this change: the config endpoint never listed it.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — this is a daemon-local read path with no user-visible/TUI change.

### Tests

`packages/cli`: `workspace-skills-status.test.ts` 57 passed, plus `workspace-service/__tests__/facade.test.ts` and `routes/workspace-skills.test.ts` 213 passed. `packages/core`: `skill-manager.test.ts` and the new `skill-manager.watcher-sharing.test.ts` 111 passed.

The cases cover external creation, edit, and removal through the real config provider without a child — applied by the watcher, asserting zero forced scans; watcher start/stop on invalidation and disposal; one native watcher per directory shared by two managers and by two providers on the same workspace; no watcher and no user Skills directory for an untrusted catalog; re-subscribing after a workspace removal; no watchers on the throwaway snapshot path; the pinned one-second revalidation boundary; one shared background scan for concurrent readers; and failure retention read after the rejection handler, followed by a successful retry.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   —    |
|  🐧 Linux  |   —    |

Linux and Windows are covered by CI; no platform-specific code is involved beyond the Skills watchers the runtime already uses.

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests from a source checkout (`npx vitest run` in `packages/cli`); no sandbox or runtime build involved.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the catalog now subscribes to the runtime's file watchers, with one native watcher per directory shared by every manager watching it. Subscriptions are tracked per workspace and released on invalidation, workspace removal, and shutdown; a watcher that cannot start is reported and leaves the one-second revalidation as the refresh path.
- Not validated / out of scope: extension Skill changes still rely on the existing invalidation path; the revalidation interval intentionally mirrors the runtime rather than becoming configurable.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Closes #15645

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

`GET /workspace/config/skills` 及其 workspace 限定路由会按 workspace 保留一份 Skill 清单，而这份清单只在配置变更或 workspace 移除触发失效时才重建。因此，直接写到磁盘上的 Skill —— 包括 agent 用自己的文件工具写出的 `SKILL.md` —— 在整个 daemon 生命周期内都不会出现在配置端点，而 runtime 的 Skills 端点却能立刻看到。

本 PR 不再新增一套按请求驱动的刷新策略，而是让配置清单与 runtime 的发现模型对齐：按 workspace 保留的 `SkillManager` 现在会监听 project 与 user 两个 Skill 目录（复用 `SkillManager.startWatching()`，与 runtime 相同的 chokidar 参数、忽略规则、监听深度和 150ms 去抖），磁盘上新建、修改或删除 Skill 会直接进入它的缓存。读取始终走缓存：没有任何请求需要扫描文件系统，首次读取仍会完整枚举。后台重验证最多每秒执行一次（与 runtime 快照的重验证间隔一致），覆盖监听器无法观察到的情况，例如监听启动后才出现的 Skills 目录、或丢失的事件；它不会阻塞读取，失败时保留上一份可用清单并在后续读取时重试。与设置相关的状态完全未变：仍然每次请求重读，显式失效仍然立即重建清单。

## 为什么需要

使用配置端点的管理客户端在 daemon 重启前永远看不到通过配置 API 之外写入的 project Skill。直接写 `SKILL.md` 是受支持的路径（agent 自己就会这么做），而且该文件早已被 runtime 发现列出，所以两个端点对同一个 workspace 给出了不一致的答案。复用 runtime 的发现与重验证语义，可以让两个视图基于同一套机制、同一有界陈旧度收敛，而不是让配置清单走另一套策略。

## 复用的机制

- **发现**：复用保留的按 workspace `SkillManager` 上的 `SkillManager.startWatching()`，只监听 project 与 user 级别；bundled 不可变，extension Skill 仍走既有的失效路径。
- **读取**：`listSkills()` 直接读 manager 缓存，与 runtime 端点用快照作答的方式一致。
- **重验证**：每个 workspace 最多每秒一次后台强制扫描，并发读者共享同一次；失败时保留上一份可用清单。重扫只覆盖被监听的 project 与 user 两级，不会重复读取不可变的 bundled Skills。
- **失效**：保持不变 —— 显式失效会提升 workspace 的 epoch、丢弃 manager，下一次读取按当前设置重建。
- **生命周期**：所有订阅按 workspace 记录，在 manager 失效、workspace 移除和 daemon 关闭时停止；workspace 移除后的下一次读取会重新订阅。一次性 `snapshot()` 枚举不会启动任何监听器。
- **共享与信任**：每个目录只有一个原生监听器，所有监听该目录的 `SkillManager` 共享它 —— 服务同一 workspace 的受信任清单与 workspace-service 兜底共享同一套 chokidar 订阅，最后一个订阅者停止时才关闭。只有受信任且非 safe mode 的清单才会监听；untrusted 或 safe mode 的读取只列 bundled Skills，因此不启动监听器，也不会创建用户 Skills 目录。

## 新鲜度策略

- 监听器能看到的变更，在下一次读取时生效（约 150ms 去抖）。
- 监听器看不到的变更，会在下一个一秒重验证窗口后的首次读取中体现；最多只有一次读取是陈旧的。
- 重验证失败会记录日志，继续用上一份清单作答，并在窗口后的下一次读取重试。
- 任何读取都不等待扫描，因此没有需要配置的读取超时；与 runtime 快照不同，配置清单不会用空占位替换一份好的枚举结果。

## 评审者验证计划

### 如何验证

1. 对受信任的 workspace 启动 `qwen serve`，先读一次 `GET /workspace/config/skills` 预热清单。
2. 直接在磁盘上创建 `.qwen/skills/download-verify-demo/SKILL.md`（frontmatter 合法），而不是通过安装 API。
3. 再次读取配置端点：监听器去抖后的下一次读取即可看到该条目，最迟在一秒重验证窗口后的首次读取中可见。`GET /workspace/runtime/skills` 同样能列出它。
4. 修改描述、再删除该目录并重新读取：清单都会跟随变化，无需任何配置变更或重启 daemon。

预期：两个端点在同一有界窗口内列出相同的 Skills，且没有任何请求阻塞在全量扫描上。改动前的实际行为：配置端点永远不列出。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 这是 daemon 本地的读路径，没有用户可见 / TUI 变化。

### 测试

`packages/cli`：`workspace-skills-status.test.ts` 57 通过；`workspace-service/__tests__/facade.test.ts` 与 `routes/workspace-skills.test.ts` 213 通过。`packages/core`：`skill-manager.test.ts` 与新增的 `skill-manager.watcher-sharing.test.ts` 共 111 通过。

新增用例覆盖：无 child 时通过真实配置 provider 的外部创建、编辑、删除，且确认由监听器生效（0 次强制扫描）；失效与 dispose 时启动/停止监听；同一目录两个 manager、以及同一 workspace 两个 provider 共享一个原生监听器；untrusted 清单不启动监听也不创建用户 Skills 目录；workspace 移除后重新订阅；一次性 snapshot 不启动监听；固定的 1 秒重验证边界；并发读者共享一次后台扫描；以及失败后在 rejection handler 之后读取仍保留清单，并在后续读取重试成功。

### 测试平台

macOS ✅；Linux 与 Windows 由 CI 覆盖（除 runtime 已在使用的 Skills 监听外没有平台相关代码）。

### 环境（可选）

从源码检出运行单元测试（在 `packages/cli` 下 `npx vitest run`），不涉及 sandbox 或运行时构建。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：配置清单现在会订阅 runtime 的文件监听器，每个目录只有一个原生监听器、由所有监听该目录的 manager 共享。订阅按 workspace 记录，并在失效、workspace 移除和关闭时释放；无法启动的监听器会被记录，此时以一秒重验证作为刷新路径。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：扩展 Skill 的变化仍依赖既有的失效路径；重验证间隔刻意与 runtime 保持一致，而不做成可配置项。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 Issue

Closes #15645

</details>

prs.title: fix(permissions): report malformed rules instead of dropping them silently
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A permission rule whose parentheses do not balance is parsed as inert: it matches nothing. Until now the only trace was a debug log line, which is off in default runs, so a `permissions.deny` / `permissions.ask` entry was accepted, validated, and then quietly protected nothing. This PR makes the drop visible: the permission manager warns on the console, naming the list, the raw rule and the consequence, using the same operator-facing breadcrumb `tools.eager` already prints from the same initializer; and `/permissions` keeps the unparsable rule in the listing, marked `(unparsable)`, so it can be seen and deleted instead of being filtered out. Matching semantics are unchanged — a malformed rule still matches nothing, so no allow/deny decision moves.

## Why it's needed

The asymmetry is what makes this a security problem rather than a logging nit: a malformed allow rule fails closed (nothing gets auto-approved), but a malformed deny/ask rule fails open — the restriction the operator wrote does not exist, and neither startup output nor `/permissions` mentioned it. The operator's mental model is "docker is blocked"; the runtime's behaviour is "no such rule". Turning silent fail-open into visible fail-open is the minimal, semantics-preserving step the issue asks for first: the operator still has to fix the configuration, but now they know there is something to fix.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Write a malformed deny rule into a settings file:

```json
{ "permissions": { "deny": ["Bash(docker *"] } }
```

Start the CLI. Before any prompt, stderr shows:

```
permissions.deny: ignoring malformed deny rule (unbalanced parentheses): "Bash(docker *". The rule has no effect; fix the parentheses to apply it.
```

Open `/permissions`, switch to the Deny tab: the rule is listed as `Bash(docker * (unparsable)`. Select it and delete it — the row disappears and stays gone on the next open. Then fix the rule to `Bash(docker *)` and restart: no warning, no marker, and a denied command prompts as before.

Focused suites:

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/permissions
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/opentui/dialog-data.test.ts src/ui/opentui/dialogs-permissions.test.tsx src/i18n
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: starting with `deny: ["Bash(docker *"]` printed nothing (the debug log file is off in default runs), and `/permissions` simply did not list the rule.

After, from the built CLI with that settings file:

```
permissions.deny: ignoring malformed deny rule (unbalanced parentheses): "Bash(docker *". The rule has no effect; fix the parentheses to apply it.
```

With the corrected rule `Bash(docker *)` the same run prints no warning — the negative control.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

macOS: Node 22.23.4, `npm run build`, all focused suites green, plus the headless run quoted above. Linux: Docker `node:22-bookworm`, same suites green, and `tsc --noEmit` clean for both packages. Windows was not run.

### Environment (optional)

Focused unit suites and a headless `dist/index.js` run with a temporary `HOME`; the Linux pass used a Docker volume workspace because a bind-mounted tree trips `rimraf` with `ENOTEMPTY`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a configuration that keeps a malformed rule now prints one line per bad rule at startup, and `/permissions` shows an extra row. No permission decision changes.
- Not validated / out of scope: the issue's other two asks — failing closed (rejecting a malformed deny/ask at load, or denying the tool it names) and the analogous `tools.disabled` typo check — are deliberately left out. The first changes runtime matching semantics, the second is a separate registry check; both fit a follow-up.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `parseRules` no longer writes to the debug log; reporting moved into the permission manager, its only caller.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15752

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

括号不配对的权限规则会被解析成惰性规则：它不匹配任何调用。此前唯一的痕迹是一行 debug 日志，而 debug 日志文件在默认运行下是关闭的，于是 `permissions.deny` / `permissions.ask` 里的条目会被接受、被校验，然后悄无声息地什么也不保护。这个 PR 把"被丢弃"变成可见：权限管理器在控制台告警，点明所在的列表、原始规则和后果，写法沿用同一个初始化流程里 `tools.eager` 已经在用的"面向操作者"面包屑；同时 `/permissions` 不再过滤掉无法解析的规则，而是把它列出来并标注 `(unparsable)`，让操作者能看到并删除。匹配语义完全没有变——畸形规则依旧不匹配任何东西，所以没有任何 allow/deny 判定会因此改变。

## 为什么需要它

这种不对称正是它属于安全问题而不只是日志问题的原因：畸形 allow 规则是 fail-closed（不会自动放行任何东西），但畸形 deny/ask 规则是 fail-open——操作者写下的限制并不存在，而且启动输出和 `/permissions` 都不会提到它。操作者的心智模型是"docker 被拦住了"，运行时的事实是"根本没有这条规则"。把静默的 fail-open 变成可见的 fail-open，是这个 issue 要求的第一步，也是改动最小、不触碰语义的一步：配置仍然要由操作者自己修，但现在他知道有东西要修。

## Reviewer Test Plan（评审验证计划）

### 如何验证

把一条畸形 deny 规则写进配置文件：

```json
{ "permissions": { "deny": ["Bash(docker *"] } }
```

启动 CLI。在任何提示词之前，stderr 会打印：

```
permissions.deny: ignoring malformed deny rule (unbalanced parentheses): "Bash(docker *". The rule has no effect; fix the parentheses to apply it.
```

打开 `/permissions`，切到 Deny 标签页：该规则显示为 `Bash(docker * (unparsable)`。选中它并删除，这一行会消失，下次打开也不再出现。再把规则改成 `Bash(docker *)` 重启：没有告警、没有标记，被拒绝的命令照旧弹确认。

定向测试：

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/permissions
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/opentui/dialog-data.test.ts src/ui/opentui/dialogs-permissions.test.tsx src/i18n
```

### 证据（改动前后）

改动前：用 `deny: ["Bash(docker *"]` 启动不打印任何内容（debug 日志文件在默认运行下关闭），`/permissions` 也完全不列出这条规则。

改动后，用该配置文件运行构建产物：

```
permissions.deny: ignoring malformed deny rule (unbalanced parentheses): "Bash(docker *". The rule has no effect; fix the parentheses to apply it.
```

把规则改成 `Bash(docker *)` 后同样运行不再打印任何告警——反向对照。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

macOS：Node 22.23.4，`npm run build`，上述定向测试全部通过，并做了上文引用的 headless 运行。Linux：Docker `node:22-bookworm`，同样的测试全部通过，两个包的 `tsc --noEmit` 也干净。Windows 未运行。

### 运行环境（可选）

定向单元测试，加上用临时 `HOME` 跑的 `dist/index.js` headless 运行；Linux 那轮用 Docker volume 作工作区，因为 bind mount 的目录会让 `rimraf` 报 `ENOTEMPTY`。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：如果配置里保留了畸形规则，启动时会按每条坏规则打印一行，`/permissions` 也会多出一行。没有任何权限判定发生变化。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：issue 提出的另外两项——fail-closed（加载时拒绝畸形 deny/ask，或直接拒绝它点名的工具）以及 `tools.disabled` 拼写错误的同类校验——有意未包含。前者会改变运行时匹配语义，后者是另一条注册表校验路径，都更适合作为后续 PR。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。`parseRules` 不再写 debug 日志，告警移到了权限管理器里，而它是唯一的调用方。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #15752

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): keep uniquely named MCP tools when names collide
prs.body:
## What this PR does

MCP tool discovery no longer lets one duplicated tool name collapse the whole server's tool list. Declarations are counted over the complete paginated `tools/list`, every declaration of a name that occurs more than once is skipped, and all uniquely named tools are kept. The debug log names each colliding group with its size (for example `'create' (7 conflicting declarations)`).

## Why it's needed

A server that lists two tools with the same name (the reporter's Unity MCP server emits several different `create` commands because it drops the command group from the tool name) made discovery fail entirely: `@google/genai` throws `Duplicate function name ... found in MCP tools` while converting the whole `tools/list` result, the error is folded into an empty tool list, and the caller then reports the misleading `No prompts, tools, or resources found on the server.` Every other tool of that server became unusable, and the health-check reconnect repeated the same failure on every attempt.

Advertise no declaration from a colliding group rather than picking one. Two tools can share a name and still be unrelated commands: execution sends only the name, and the server decides which command runs, so showing the model one declaration's schema can trigger a different command than the one described. That is the acceptance boundary recorded on #15741. Keeping the uniquely named tools is the part the client can do on its own; the server is the one violating the spec by reusing names.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Point Qwen Code at an MCP server that lists two tools with the same name plus at least one other tool. Before: the server contributes no tools and the log shows the duplicate error followed by `No prompts, tools, or resources found on the server.` After: the uniquely named tool is registered, both colliding declarations are absent, and the debug log (`--debug`) reports the group size.
2. Run `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/tools/mcp-client.test.ts`. Four cases cover this change: the colliding group plus a unique tool, a duplicate split across pages, a retry after a transient failure on page two, and a server that repeats a cursor. Each fails on the previous head and passes here; the file is 170/170 green afterwards.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no UI change. Test output:

```
# before (previous head)
AssertionError: expected [ 'create', 'other' ] to deeply equal [ 'other' ]
# after
src/tools/mcp-client.test.ts (170 tests) 2133ms
Tests  170 passed (170)
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only, macOS with Node 22. Linux was verified in a `node:22-bookworm` container with a fresh `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and a core package build.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a server whose tools all collide now contributes none of them, where the previous head kept one arbitrary declaration per name. Advertising a declaration whose schema need not be the command that runs is worse than leaving the group out, and the skip is reported with the group size.
- The adapter now follows the cursor chain itself and answers with a single terminal page. That is what makes cross-page counting possible, resets the bookkeeping on a retry, and keeps the SDK pager from spinning on a page filtered down to nothing.
- Not validated / out of scope: surfacing the skip notice outside `--debug` would need a new user-facing warning channel across packages; other conversion failures still collapse into the generic "no tools" message.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Closes #15741

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

MCP 工具发现不再因为一个重名工具就让整个 server 的工具列表失效。现在会在完整的分页 `tools/list` 上统计每个名字的声明次数，凡是出现多于一次的声明全部跳过，同时保留所有不重名的工具。debug 日志会按冲突组列出名字与组内数量（例如 `'create' (7 conflicting declarations)`）。

## 为什么需要

如果某个 server 列出两个同名工具（报告者的 Unity MCP server 因为丢掉命令分组，会产出多个不同的 `create`），发现流程就会整体失败：`@google/genai` 在转换整份 `tools/list` 结果时抛出 `Duplicate function name ... found in MCP tools`，这个错误被吞成空工具列表，调用方随后报出误导性的 `No prompts, tools, or resources found on the server.`。该 server 的其余工具全部不可用，健康检查重连时还会重复同样的失败。

对冲突组应当一个声明都不暴露，而不是随意挑一个。两个同名工具仍可能是完全不同的命令：执行时只发送名字，由 server 决定跑哪个，所以把某一份声明的参数 schema 展示给模型，可能触发与描述不符的另一条命令。这也是 #15741 中记录的验收边界。保留不重名的工具是客户端能独立完成的部分；违反规范复用名字的是 server。

## 评审验证步骤

1. 让 Qwen Code 连接一个列出两个同名工具、同时还有至少一个其他工具的 MCP server。修复前：该 server 不贡献任何工具，日志先出现重复名错误，再出现 `No prompts, tools, or resources found on the server.`。修复后：不重名的工具正常注册，两个冲突声明都不出现，`--debug` 日志给出组内数量。
2. 运行 `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/tools/mcp-client.test.ts`。新增四个用例分别覆盖：冲突组 + 唯一工具、跨页同名、第二页瞬时失败后的重试、server 重复返回同一 cursor。它们在上一版 head 上全部失败，在本改动后通过，整个文件 170/170 通过。

## 证据

N/A —— 无 UI 变化，测试输出见上方英文部分。

## 测试平台

macOS ✅、Windows ⚠️ 未测试、Linux ✅（`node:22-bookworm` 容器，全新 `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` 并构建 core 包后运行单测）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：如果某个 server 的所有工具都重名，现在将不贡献任何工具，而上一版 head 会每个名字保留一个任意声明。展示一份不一定会被执行的 schema，比整组不暴露更糟，而且跳过会带上组内数量写入日志。
- 适配器现在自己遍历 cursor 链并只返回一个终止页。这是跨页统计的前提，也让重试从空状态开始，并避免 SDK 的分页器在被过滤成空的页上打转。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：在 `--debug` 之外向用户提示被跳过的工具，需要新增跨包的用户可见警告通道；其他转换失败仍会退化成统一的 "no tools" 报错。
- 破坏性变更：无。

## 关联 Issue

Closes #15741

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): skip memory imports of files already loaded as context files
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a context file imports another file that is itself loaded as a top-level context file (for example `CLAUDE.md` containing `@AGENTS.md` while both are configured context filenames), the import is now skipped instead of expanding the same content a second time. The set of top-level files is computed once, after canonical de-duplication and before the parallel reads, so the result does not depend on batch order: the top-level copy always wins. Imports that reach a top-level file through a different path (for example a symlink) are matched by real path. In tree mode the skipped import is replaced by the existing "File already processed" marker; in flat mode it is omitted. No `include` instruction-loaded notification is emitted for the skipped import.

## Why it's needed

The duplicated content wastes context tokens and repeats instructions to the model, as described in #15679. The existing per-file `processedFiles` guard only covers imports within one file's tree, so sibling top-level files were not protected.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run `npx vitest run src/memory/memoryDiscovery.test.ts -t "#15679"` in `packages/core`. The new tests cover tree and flat import modes for a direct `@AGENTS.md` import, a symlinked import of a top-level file, the default context filenames, and the absence of an `include` notification for the skipped import. With the production changes reverted, the 5 new tests fail (content appears twice); with the change applied, all 5 pass.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (non-UI change). Test results on Linux, Node 24:

- New tests, before fix: 5 failed. After fix: 5 passed.
- `packages/core` memory suites (`src/memory`, `memoryImportProcessor.test.ts`): before 1161 passed / 2 failed / 1 skipped; after 1167 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped. The remaining failure (`formatContextFileDisplayPath` ANSI stripping) fails identically on `main` in this environment; the second baseline failure was a timing-sensitive latency test.
- Full `packages/core` vitest run: before 39389 passed / 15 failed / 18 skipped; after 39395 passed / 14 failed / 18 skipped. All remaining failures also fail on `main` in the same environment (extensionManager, hook-command-cgroup, LspConfigLoader, git-branches, git-worktrees, runtime-boundary bun, formatContextFileDisplayPath) and are unrelated to this change.
- `npm run typecheck`: passes.
- `eslint --max-warnings 0` on `packages/core` and `prettier --check` on the changed files: pass.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only (vitest, Node 24, Linux).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: this picks "the top-level copy wins" when a file is both a top-level context file and an import target; if maintainers prefer the import to win instead, the skip set would need to be applied the other way. This PR touches `memoryImportProcessor.ts`, which is also modified by #15430 (`validateImportPath`); the changes are in different functions but may need a rebase depending on merge order.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Windows runs (including case-insensitive path matching on Windows), a scenario with more than 20 context files spanning multiple read batches, and the full `npm run preflight`.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `readMemoryFiles` is internal and gains a parameter.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15679

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 做了什么

当某个上下文文件导入了另一个本身已作为顶层上下文文件加载的文件时（例如 `CLAUDE.md` 中包含 `@AGENTS.md`，且两者都是已配置的上下文文件名），该导入现在会被跳过，而不再第二次展开相同内容。顶层文件集合在规范化去重之后、并行读取之前只计算一次，因此结果不依赖于批次顺序：始终以顶层副本为准。通过不同路径（例如符号链接）指向顶层文件的导入会按真实路径进行匹配。在 tree 模式下，被跳过的导入会替换为已有的 "File already processed" 标记；在 flat 模式下则直接省略。被跳过的导入不会触发 `include` 类型的指令加载通知。

## 为什么需要

如 #15679 所述，重复的内容会浪费上下文 token，并向模型重复相同的指令。现有的按文件 `processedFiles` 保护只覆盖单个文件导入树内部的导入，无法保护同级的顶层文件。

## 审查者测试计划

### 如何验证

在 `packages/core` 中运行 `npx vitest run src/memory/memoryDiscovery.test.ts -t "#15679"`。新增测试覆盖：tree 和 flat 两种导入模式下直接导入 `@AGENTS.md`、通过符号链接导入顶层文件、默认上下文文件名，以及被跳过的导入不产生 `include` 通知。回退生产代码改动后，5 个新测试全部失败（内容出现两次）；应用改动后，5 个测试全部通过。

### 证据（修改前后）

N/A（非 UI 改动）。Linux、Node 24 下的测试结果：

- 新测试：修复前 5 个失败，修复后 5 个通过。
- `packages/core` 记忆相关测试（`src/memory`、`memoryImportProcessor.test.ts`）：修复前 1161 通过 / 2 失败 / 1 跳过；修复后 1167 通过 / 1 失败 / 1 跳过。剩余失败（`formatContextFileDisplayPath` ANSI 清理）在本环境的 `main` 上同样失败；基线中的第二个失败是对时间敏感的延迟测试。
- 完整 `packages/core` vitest 运行：修复前 39389 通过 / 15 失败 / 18 跳过；修复后 39395 通过 / 14 失败 / 18 跳过。所有剩余失败在相同环境的 `main` 上同样失败（extensionManager、hook-command-cgroup、LspConfigLoader、git-branches、git-worktrees、runtime-boundary bun、formatContextFileDisplayPath），与本改动无关。
- `npm run typecheck`：通过。
- 对 `packages/core` 运行 `eslint --max-warnings 0`，对改动文件运行 `prettier --check`：通过。

### 测试平台

macOS ⚠️ 未测试；Windows ⚠️ 未测试；Linux ✅ 已测试。

### 环境（可选）

仅单元测试（vitest、Node 24、Linux）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：当一个文件既是顶层上下文文件又是导入目标时，本 PR 选择"以顶层副本为准"；如果维护者希望以导入为准，则需要反向应用跳过集合。本 PR 修改了 `memoryImportProcessor.ts`，该文件也被 #15430（`validateImportPath`）修改；两者改动位于不同函数，但根据合并顺序可能需要 rebase。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：macOS 和 Windows 运行（包括 Windows 上不区分大小写的路径匹配）、超过 20 个上下文文件跨多个读取批次的场景，以及完整的 `npm run preflight`。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。`readMemoryFiles` 为内部函数，新增了一个参数。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #15679

</details>

releases.name: Release v0.26.3
releases.body:
<!-- qwen-release-notes:v1 -->

## Highlights

- Generated UI cards keep inputs and state across navigation and split views, show live views after initial calculation, and appear only for clients that can render MCP Apps. ([#15611](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15611), [#15787](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15787), [#15720](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15720), [#15790](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15790))
- Persistent session Workflow mode can be enabled with --workflow-mode on, /workflows mode on, SDK, or ACP, and workflow switches now reach the CLI sandbox. ([#15422](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15422), [#15743](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15743))
- Tool results shrink to remaining headroom before auto-compaction, and qwen-latest-series- or qwen4 aliases are detected with 1M-token context windows. ([#13599](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13599), [#15758](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15758), [#15762](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15762))
- Valid XML tool calls are recovered when parameters quote other call markup, malformed blocks are isolated, and quoted examples are not dispatched. ([#13579](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13579))
- ACP and daemon clients keep rewind identity consistent across retries, cancellations, checkpoints, recordings, and notifications, while SDK frames preserve subagent identity. ([#15441](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15441), [#15657](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15657))
- /autofix-pr start stops when the PR head branch has unpushed commits or uncommitted changes, preventing the watch from overwriting unseen work. ([#15736](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15736))

## Breaking Changes

No known breaking changes.

## Complete Change List

### Features

- feat(memory): opt-in extraction cadence after a no-op run ([#13571](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13571)) by @yiliang114
- Shrinks tool results to remaining headroom before auto-compaction, respecting explicit truncation settings and protected content to reduce unnecessary compaction. ([#13599](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13599)) by @yiliang114
- Keeps eligible Generated UI cards alive across history navigation, session switching, and split-view changes in the same page, preserving inputs, controls, and runtime state. ([#15611](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15611)) by @qqqys
- Adds persistent session Workflow mode through --workflow-mode on, /workflows mode on, SDK, and ACP controls, with saved mode shown in Ink and OpenTUI. ([#15422](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15422)) by @qqqys
- Adds opt-in composerVariant simple to Web Shell, providing a compact input with a limited add menu and shared editor, attachments, and session actions. ([#15663](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15663)) by @samuelhsin
- /autofix-pr start now stops if the PR head branch has unpushed commits or uncommitted changes, preventing the watch from overwriting unseen work. ([#15736](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15736)) by @wenshao
- Adds administrator-driven reclamation and reuse of idle resident CSI Workspaces with cleanup verification and atomic release. ([#15729](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15729)) by @doudouOUC
- OpenTUI terminals now draw the Mods band above the prompt and run Mod ui.render hooks there, matching the Ink terminal experience. ([#15699](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15699)) by @qqqys
- ACP live frames, persisted replays, SDK normalization, and transcript reduction now preserve subagent identity for thoughts, messages, and tool frames. ([#15657](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15657)) by @yiliang114
- Archived conversations are now managed in Settings → Archived conversations in Web Shell, keeping archive groups, filters, and lifecycle actions. ([#15557](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15557)) by @deggs7
- Managed Agent can now be embedded opt-in in a Java host's JVM and Spring context, with dedicated connection pooling or a supplied DataSource. ([#15718](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15718)) by @yiliang114
- /verify-pr now supports a failures ledger and rejects findings or blocked verdicts unless failures are attributed to the PR. ([#15764](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15764)) by @wenshao
- Adds the qwen-managed-agent-admin launcher for running managed-agent offline maintenance commands by name, with help and unknown-command handling. ([#15772](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15772)) by @wenshao
- feat(generated-ui): check a view's initial calculation before display ([#15790](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15790)) by @qqqys

### Bug Fixes

- Recovers valid XML tool calls when parameters quote other call markup, isolates malformed blocks, and prevents quoted examples from being dispatched. ([#13579](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13579)) by @yiliang114
- Carries rewind identity through ACP/daemon clients so retries, cancellations, checkpoint resolution, recording, and notifications stay consistent. ([#15441](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15441)) by @yiliang114
- Fixes release publishing checkout failures by using the run-scoped GitHub token for read-only checkout while keeping the bot PAT for write steps. ([#15728](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15728)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Pins pull request CI retries to the head SHA from the triggering event so reruns test the intended commit. ([#15734](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15734)) by @yiliang114
- fix(cli): forward workflow switches into the CLI sandbox (#15740) ([#15743](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15743)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Recognizes invite-only qwen-latest-series- model aliases as 1M-context models in the context-window detector. ([#15758](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15758)) by @wenshao
- Makes daemon-managed channels honor approvalMode even when no webhooks are configured, matching standalone startup. ([#15754](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15754)) by @qqqys
- Shows the exception class in managed-agent scan summaries for non-first row failures that have no message. ([#15725](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15725)) by @yiliang114
- Workspace Skill inventory queries now return a retained snapshot immediately and refresh in the background, while cold reads, deletion, and enablement wait for fresh data. ([#14890](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14890)) by @callmeYe
- qwen4 model identifiers are now sized with a 1,000,000-token context window by default when no upstream catalog entry defines them. ([#15762](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15762)) by @wenshao
- Acceptance tests now wait for the focused shell Tab byte to reach the child process before asserting exact input bytes, preventing flaky failures. ([#15763](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15763)) by @yiliang114
- Managed runtime distribution now publishes verified server artifacts to GitHub Releases and OSS without requiring Maven Central, keeping CLI downloads unchanged. ([#15782](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15782)) by @doudouOUC
- Generated UI is now offered only to sessions whose client can render MCP Apps, while unsupported clients receive a clear unsupported-client reason. ([#15720](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15720)) by @qqqys
- In Web Shell, live Generated UI cards now attach and show their interactive view immediately when tool results arrive instead of requiring reopen. ([#15787](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15787)) by @qqqys
- Desktop release preparation now resets Git metadata on self-hosted runners before checkout to avoid stale-workspace failures. ([#15761](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15761)) by @yiliang114

### Documentation

- Documents managed-agent shared-Session queue behavior and advises giving slow-probed gated definitions their own Session. ([#15724](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15724)) by @yiliang114

### Internal Changes

- Internal tests now compare git worktree prune dry-run results as an unordered set, making them insensitive to git output order. ([#15767](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15767)) by @yiliang114
- Managed snapshot pool test setup now allows a three-second database connection lease so schema creation on busy CI runners is less likely to fail. ([#15749](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15749)) by @yiliang114
- Installed npm and private Bun acceptance tests now run nightly and by manual dispatch instead of on every PR update, while source TUI PR behavior stays unchanged. ([#15719](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15719)) by @yiliang114
- Improved Managed Agent reliability testing by adding terminal recovery fault gates for failover scenarios. ([#15756](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15756)) by @wenshao
- Improved CLI test stability for review cleanup orphan-process handling by making process liveness deterministic. ([#15751](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15751)) by @yiliang114
- Hosted gates now use a shared zombie-aware liveness check, improving consistency when waiting for processes to stop. ([#15777](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15777)) by @wenshao

## Highlights

The bundled CLI 0.23.0 includes two fixes requested in #11022:

- Managed memory availability now respects the `memory.enableManagedAutoMemory` setting (#6941). Hosts that disable managed auto memory no longer see remember/dream requests admitted or managed-memory instructions in the system prompt; local patches can be removed.

milestone.title: v0.10.3
milestone.description:
Engine 0.10.3 implementation and release qualification. Includes the planned runtime, context, review, localization, terminal and installation/uninstall work, plus the full crate decomposition: no crate above 50,000 production lines, aiming for about 10,000.

Track concrete remaining acceptance on each issue; a landed slice or local check does not mean the complete issue or release has shipped. Contributor PRs retain their authorship. Complete planned implementation and product review before freezing one candidate for final local and hosted validation. Publication is a separate authorized release step. No calendar due date is promised.

With no cloud key and Ollama running, the TUI adopts Ollama on first launch (`Provider switched: deepseek → ollama`), but the headless and diagnostic paths still insist on DeepSeek:

```
$ codewhale exec "Reply with exactly: QA-OK"
error: DeepSeek API key not found.
...
zsh: ~/.zshrc is interactive only; use ~/.zshenv.
...
Failed to configure provider route deepseek / deepseek-flash.

$ codewhale doctor
Not ready: the deepseek route has no verified key → save one with /provider ...
```

`config.toml` written on first launch keeps `default_text_model = "deepseek-flash"`, so the adoption is re-done (and re-announced) on every TUI launch and never reaches `exec`/`doctor`.

Also: the bare line `zsh: ~/.zshrc is interactive only; use ~/.zshenv.` in the key-missing error reads like a shell error.

## Repro

Fresh `HOME`/`CODEWHALE_HOME`, Ollama with one chat model, main `715bb2ed02` release build: run `codewhale` (TUI adopts Ollama), quit, then `codewhale exec "hi"` and `codewhale doctor`.

Expected: one answer to "which model am I using" across TUI, exec and doctor — either persist the adoption, or have exec/doctor apply the same keyless-local rule and say so.

Evidence: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/j-cli-1.txt`, `j-cli-2.txt`.

2026-10-28: Engine `8c4b29c2b9` changes the zsh startup hint into Codewhale prose so it is not mistaken for a shell-generated error. A source-extracted diagnostic compiled and rendered; rustfmt and diff checks passed. The existing F3 Auto-default draft in the same file was not staged. This is a wording fix only; the TUI versus exec/doctor Ollama route mismatch remains open and is under source review.

### Engine local-catalog slice landed — 2026-10-28

Engine main `7c49574a6b` probes unknown Ollama tag capabilities with bounded concurrency, publishes an authoritative catalog only when the probe is complete, and fences automatic adoption against superseded discovery and changed endpoints. Four focused existing checks passed on the shared frozen Engine source; the local discovery checks used synthetic loopback fixtures. Receipt: `CW/artifacts/engine-shared-check-20261028/focused-checks.log`.

Desktop installed-model discovery and a real Ollama interaction have not been requalified with the current app and Engine. The issue remains open; no live-model or release proof is claimed.

## What a new user hits

Fresh desktop app (QA bundle codewhale-app `40766826`, bundled Engine 0.10.2, isolated `HOME`/`CODEWHALE_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), with Ollama running two tags: `qwen3:4b` (chat) and `nomic-embed-text:latest` (embedding).

1. Composer → **Choose a model** → the **Ollama** chip shows *Ready*; the Model list offers only **Default**.
2. Send "Reply with exactly: DESKTOP-QA-OK" → `Invalid request (400): "nomic-embed-text:latest" does not support chat`, card "Couldn't finish: this model can't chat. Pick another model."
3. **Choose model** again: the list still shows only `nomic-embed-text:latest`; `qwen3:4b` is not offered. The user has to know to expand **More** and type `qwen3:4b` into *Model ID* → **Use** (Return in that field does nothing).

So on the desktop, "Default" for Ollama resolves to an embedding model, and installed chat models are not listed. The TUI on main picks `qwen3:4b` from the same Ollama, using `choose_chat_tag` (`crates/tui/src/client/ollama_catalog.rs`, capability `completion`), so the desktop/app-server default path appears to bypass that rule.

Expected: the Ollama default is a chat-capable tag, and the model list shows the installed chat tags from `/api/tags`.

Not yet rechecked against current codewhale-app main + main Engine (build slots were busy); the 0.10.3 desktop bundles a newer Engine.

Evidence: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/jD1-desktop-default-embed-model.jpg`.

## 2026-10-28 current Engine + real local Ollama

A clean-source Engine build matching `bd9d4422ed` was made on macOS (all 4,160 source inputs rehashed unchanged; binary codewhale-hq/codewhale-app#334 `3eb1b93a0614f519c18e0f88811d805f4a0e035f8f2f874ed668b47ba6eebe7f`). In an isolated product home and workspace, with outbound network sandboxed to localhost, the actual local Ollama daemon exposed `qwen3:4b` for completion and `nomic-embed-text:latest` for embedding. Runtime API refresh returned only `qwen3:4b`; switching with no model selected it and persisted it, a new thread used it, and a tiny local turn completed successfully. Receipt: `CW/artifacts/7116-local-ollama-2/receipt.json`. The first harness start failed because its Unix socket path exceeded macOS limits; the shorter retry passed. This is Engine/runtime proof, not current desktop picker or installed-app proof, and the original cause remains unconfirmed. Source review also found that incomplete `/api/show` capability probes fail the authoritative roster refresh and can leave an older roster in place. Keep the issue open.

issues.title: Fleet workers spawn `codewhale` from PATH, not the running binary: all fail from the desktop Engine or a full-path install
issues.body:
## What happens

Every Fleet worker fails to start when `codewhale` isn't on `PATH`, even though a Codewhale binary is running the fleet:

```
$ codewhale fleet run tasks.json --max-workers 2      # run by full path, PATH=/usr/bin:/bin
Fleet run: fleet-b2dab371 tasks=2 leased=2 queued=0
$ codewhale fleet status
fleet: runs=1 ... completed=0 partial=2 failed=2 ...
$ codewhale fleet inspect fleet-b2dab371-local-1
latest_event: seq=6 failed recoverable=false reason=starting worker fleet-b2dab371-local-1: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

The local mock model received zero requests.

## Cause (source)

`configured_codewhale_binary()` (`crates/tui/src/fleet/executor.rs:57`) returns `$CODEWHALE_FLEET_CODEWHALE_BINARY` or the bare name `"codewhale"`, which is resolved on `PATH`. The CLI (`lib.rs:3894`, `:3956`) and the Runtime API (`runtime_api.rs:2065`) both use it.

## Why it matters for launch

- **Desktop:** the app starts its bundled Engine (`Codewhale.app/Contents/MacOS/codewhale app-server`) with the app's environment. Launched from Finder, `PATH` is `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, and codewhale-app never sets `CODEWHALE_FLEET_CODEWHALE_BINARY`. So `/v1/fleet/runs` workers either fail like this, or run whatever older `codewhale` happens to be on `PATH`, giving silent version skew against the Engine that owns the run.
- **CLI:** a full-path install not on `PATH` fails the same way. A machine with several installs (`~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, Homebrew) runs workers with a different version from the one the user started.

## Suggested fix

Fall back to `std::env::current_exe()` before the bare name. The Runtime API test harness passes its own `fleet_codewhale_binary` override, but `tests.rs:1410` defaults to `configured_codewhale_binary`, so check that tests relying on the old default still pass.

Repro: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/fleet/` (tasks.json, old-run.txt; mock model on 127.0.0.1:18930). Binary: main release build from 2026-10-27 13:54. The resolver is unchanged on origin/main (`478b29eae5`).

issues.body:

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

### Operating system 操作系统

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

Official script ([codewhale.net/install.sh](<http://codewhale.net/install.sh>))

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

### Terminal and shell 终端

*No response*

### codewhale doctor (optional)

```text
```

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

# The persistent "update available" header chip is never rendered — `app.update_available` is written and never read

**Labels:** `bug`

**Surface:** TUI (terminal interface)

**Version:** `codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f)`

**OS:** Linux (Linux Mint 22.2, x86-64)

**Confirmed present in:** `v0.10.1` tag and `HEAD` (`687a38c6e`, 2026-10-28) — 281 commits after the tag, still unreproduced.

---

## What happened

A newer release was available and Codewhale never told me — or told me only for twelve seconds, at startup, four days before I noticed.

Running `0.10.1` with `0.10.2` published:

| Fact | Value |
| -- | -- |
| Installed | `codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f)`, `/usr/local/bin/codewhale`, 8 Oct |
| `v0.10.2` published | 2026-10-24T17:31:14Z |
| Session started | 2026-10-25T04:27:16Z |
| Update-check cache written | 2026-10-25T04:27:11Z — **5 seconds before the session row** |
| Cache contents | `{"checked_at_unix": 1792902431, "latest_tag": "v0.10.2"}` |

So the startup check ran, reached GitHub about ten hours after the release, and correctly found `v0.10.2`. **The session that was told is the session I was using** — and I saw nothing across four days of continuous use.

Nothing suppressed it: no `CODEWHALE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK`, no `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`, no CI variables set, no `[update]` section in `config.toml`. The default check interval is one hour, so a fresh launch re-checks.

## The defect

`app.update_available` is assigned when the startup check completes, and **nothing in the tree ever reads it**. A repo-wide grep returns exactly three hits — the field declaration, its initialisation to `None`, and the assignment:

```
crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs:1676:        pub update_available: Option<String>,
crates/tui/src/tui/app/init.rs:850:            update_available: None,
crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:2247:            app.update_available = Some(notice.chip_label());
```

There is no render site, no serialisation, no non-Rust consumer. The write is dead.

**The field's own doc comment describes the feature that is missing** (`app.rs:1672–1675`):

```rust
/// Header chip label (e.g. `↑ v0.9.5`) set once by the fire-and-forget
/// startup version check when a newer stable release exists. Drives the
/// small persistent update chip in the header so the affordance survives
/// the transient toast without nagging (FINISH-0.9.4 #14).
pub update_available: Option<String>,
```

And the assignment site repeats the claim (`event_loop.rs:2240–2242`):

```rust
// Transient toast for immediate visibility, plus a durable
// in-transcript notice so the prompt survives the toast TTL and
// stays actionable during a busy session (#3961). The persistent
// header chip keeps a quiet affordance after both (#14).
```

`#14` — the persistent chip — was implemented as a field, a label generator and a doc comment, but never wired to the header.

## Why the test suite did not catch it

There is a test for the chip, and it passes:

```rust
// crates/tui/src/tui/ui/tests.rs:18665-18667
// The persistent header chip is quiet: version only, no action verb —
// the toast and this block carry the instructions (#14).
assert_eq!(notice.chip_label(), "↑ v0.8.47");
```

It asserts the **label generator** returns the right string. It never asserts that any render path consumes it — so a fully working `chip_label()` with no consumer passes cleanly. That is the shape of the defect: the unit under test is correct, and the integration is absent.

## What this costs a user

The three intended surfaces degrade to two, and the surviving durable one is weak:

| Surface | State | Reality |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Toast | works | **12 seconds** (`VERSION_HINT_TOAST_TTL_MS = 12_000`) |
| Transcript system message | works | scrolls away during a working session |
| Persistent header chip | **absent** | written and never read |

The failure mode is worst for the exact user the feature exists for: someone in a long session. The check runs once per process at startup; a session lasting days — mine is four days old — sees the toast once, at the moment of launch, when the terminal is still drawing. After that there is no indication at all, and the version drift is silent.

## What I expected

A quiet, persistent affordance in the header reading `↑ v0.10.2` for as long as a newer release is known — as the doc comment and the `#14` reference both describe. Clicking or a keystroke would show the update command.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install any release older than the latest, e.g. `0.10.1`, with `0.10.2` available.
2. Ensure no `[update]` config and no suppression env vars.
3. Delete `~/.codewhale/update-check.json` if present, then start a new session.
4. A toast appears for 12 seconds and one transcript line is written.
5. **Look at the header.** There is no chip. It never appears, in this session or any later one, even though `app.update_available` is `Some("↑ v0.10.2")`.

## Suggested fix

Two lines and a render, in rough order:

1. **Render it.** Emit the chip wherever the header's status chips are composed, gated on `app.update_available.is_some()`. The label is already correct and quiet (version only), so no wording decision is needed.
2. **Add an integration test that fails today.** Assert that after the version check resolves with a newer tag, the composed header contains the chip text — not that `chip_label()` returns a string. A test at the render boundary is what was missing.
3. Optionally, consider whether the 12-second toast alone is adequate for sessions that outlive the check interval; the chip was the answer to that question, which is why its absence matters.

## Notes

* The install resolved to `InstallMethod::Binary` (path has no `cellar`, `node_modules` or `.cargo/bin`), so the notice would advertise `codewhale update`. On this machine the binary is `root:root` in `/usr/local/bin`, so a self-update run as a normal user cannot replace it — a separate observation, not part of this defect, but it makes the advertised command fail with a permissions error rather than prompting for elevation.
* `app.update_available` is `None` initialised and never cleared. If a future render is added, check whether it should also be cleared when a check returns "no newer release" after previously finding one — the cache stores the latest tag, so a downgrade in `latest_tag` is possible in principle.
* `chip_label()` already distinguishes a staged release (`↑ v{latest} ready`) from an unstaged one (`↑ v{latest}`), which suggests a download-and-stage flow was intended alongside the chip. Worth confirming whether that path exists before wiring the chip.
* Reported from a read-only inspection of the source at `687a38c6e` plus the on-disk state of a `0.10.1` install; no code was modified and no issue was filed.

### Investigation claim — 2026-10-28

Coordinator verified on current Engine source that the update label is assigned but no rendering path reads it. Initial read-only scope is the TUI's existing footer and pet presentation (`crates/tui/src/tui/phase_strip.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/pet_watch/full.rs`) and their existing rendering fixtures. A safe persistent affordance must preserve higher-priority status and remote-control signals and handle narrow/ASCII layouts. Source is frozen for a contributor build; no fix or verification is claimed yet.

### Line-ending controls landed — 2026-10-28

Engine main `19d3178ee7` adds a validated preserve/LF/CRLF choice to the file-writing routes, preserving existing line endings by default and reporting actual written bytes. On the frozen combined Engine source, six focused existing test filters passed (seven cases total) for CRLF preservation, schema, byte receipt and queued-write cancellation. Receipt: `CW/artifacts/engine-shared-check-20261028/focused-checks.log`.

A model-driven reproduction of the reporter's natural-language request has not been exercised, so the issue remains In Progress rather than being closed based on the local tool checks alone.

2026-10-28 path claim addition: `crates/tui/src/tools/file_tool/tests.rs` (existing exact primitive-schema assertion). Engine worker released its checkpoint freeze after `fed2140d8b`; no build slot reserved yet.

No build until a frozen batch and shared build slot are agreed.

Plan: add a validated optional preserve/LF/CRLF choice across model-facing `write`, hidden `write_file`, and the `File` action schema/dispatch. Omitted choice keeps current semantics; explicit selection applies to new and overwritten files, with size checks on final bytes and truthful receipts. Preserve fresh-read/hash guards, path/approval/cancellation and atomic writes. Confirm Rust formatting does not override the chosen ending.

Existing checks to adapt: `write_file_over_crlf_file_preserves_crlf_line_endings`, `contract_write_over_crlf_file_preserves_crlf_line_endings`, `preserve_prior_line_endings_keeps_the_prior_style`, `test_input_schemas`, `contract_write_receipt_carries_written_size_and_sha256`, and queued cancellation. Review source `3690f9c4abe62d40601c91b8d3e37ce880b6ea64`; no implementation or verification claimed yet.

## 0.10.3 status — 2026-10-25

The current source receipt fix is [2c4f090a9f](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/2c4f090a9f>): when preserving an existing CRLF file, the write result says so. This does not add explicit LF/CRLF selection. That requested behavior remains an enhancement; this issue is not being represented as fully fixed.

### Before you start

### What happened? 发生了什么？

Leave these confirmations unchecked until you have personally verified them before submission. This draft does not claim a fresh duplicate search or reproduction on the latest release.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Codewhale's write tool converts CR-free content to CRLF when the overwritten file used CRLF (first newline decides) and reports plain success, so a user's explicit request to save with LF endings is silently not honored and the agent tells the user the file is LF.

Observed behavior:
write with LF-only content -> 'Successfully wrote 215 bytes'; the file on disk keeps CRLF on every line (next read and final workspace file); the agent claimed LF endings in 9/10 runs (grep_files for \\r returned 0 matches).

write 'Creates the file if it does not exist, overwrites it if it does' with the given content; the user explicitly required LF line endings only. Rewrite the whole file with your file write tool rather than with shell commands. Then tell me what the file now looks like.
