## 0.10.3 status — 2026-10-25

The first localization slice landed on main in [a129eb544a](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/a129eb544aa2c11f534971b92c619ea390f122d0>): question/approval/handoff/waiting chrome and the portable /color feedback use the locale catalog across all 15 packs. The combined UI batch passed 479 existing local tests. Actual 80×40 terminal checks covered single/multi question footers with more than nine options in French, Latin American Spanish, Ukrainian, Brazilian Portuguese and Russian (10 cases), plus Russian /color feedback through the portable-command bridge. Those observations used a synthetic loopback fixture, not a real provider. Remaining surfaces, including /undo and /diff prose, keep this issue open. This is unreleased candidate source.

---

**Version:** 0.10.2 (`ff466b2ed0bf`, npm build), Linux, `locale = "zh-Hans"` in `settings.toml`.
**Target:** 0.10.3

With the UI in Simplified Chinese, the main flow is translated: the composer placeholder 输入消息…, approval options 仅允许本次 / 不允许, the pet status 思考 / 回复 / 完成, the plan-handoff question 你想如何继续？, and the footer. But several messages you see in an ordinary session stay in English. None of these strings are in `crates/localization/locales/*.json`; they're hardcoded at the call site:

| What you see | Source |
| -- | -- |
| `/undo` note: `Undid your request "…". 1 file is back as it was before it: … The request and its reply were removed from the conversation.` | `crates/commands/src/debug/undo.rs:323` (`format!("Undid {request}. {count} before it:…")`) |
| `/diff` pager title `Changes since session start` | `crates/commands/src/debug/undo.rs:174` |
| `/color` note `Composer color for this chat: red` / `…reset to the theme default` | `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/session/color.rs:73-74` |
| Tool card status `… · waiting for approval` | `crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1411` |
| Plan handoff / question chrome: `Action required`, `Question 1 of 1`, `Other`, `Type a custom response`, `1-4 quick pick ↑/↓ move Enter confirm ←/h back Esc cancel` | `crates/tui/src/tui/user_input.rs` (e.g. `:459`) |
| Approval card `Save:   always ask first` | `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/mod.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/approval/ask_rules.rs` |
| Grouped activity `Explored 3 files: explore +3 ›`, `patch done · Updated tides.py · +1 -1` | `crates/tui/src/tui/history/tool_run.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/mod.rs` |

## Repro

1. Put `locale = "zh-Hans"` in `$CODEWHALE_HOME/settings.toml`, or choose 简体中文 in `/settings`.
2. In a Git repo, ask for a fix that runs a shell command and edits a file, approve the card, then run `/diff`, `/undo` and `/color`.

## Expected

These go through `tr(locale, MessageId::…)` like their neighbours, and appear in `en.json` and every locale pack. `scripts/check-tui-locale-parity.py` only checks keys that exist, so it can't catch strings that never became keys.

## Notes

* The CHANGELOG for 0.10.2 also says the pet's activity words and the update note follow the UI language, and both do. These strings are the visible gap next to them.
* Fix direction: move each string to a `MessageId`, add the en/zh-Hans/zh-Hant/ja values (the other locales can fall back), and consider a small lint that flags new user-facing `format!`/string literals in `crates/tui/src/tui/` and `crates/commands/src/` outside the localization crate.

Found while recording a Chinese-language 0.10.2 demo.

## PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7121 read-only review, 2026-10-28

Contributor head `3b71d2f99e7615a1c71eb7869dd713a7c847eaa5` by Boyce [aboyskyi@gmail.com](<mailto:aboyskyi@gmail.com>); main `fed2140d8b0058ffe62f276d2d605307d4e9458d`; their clean merge tree is `fdff7e4a50b4c9c8542c174f088cd07e564052e5`. All 29 added undo keys are present in all 15 locale packs and the placeholder names match the actual host replacement contract; this was a static structural check, not native-speaker review or a test run. The inherited dirty locale edits concern a separate OrcaRouter copy change; `git apply --check` on the PR patch succeeds against the current tree, but their owner’s work remains uncommitted and must be preserved.

Blocking review finding: a fallible presentation translation in the `Restored` outcome can return a plain error after files and App history have already changed, dropping the `SyncSession` action that would reconcile Engine state. A narrow repair should keep the typed successful restore and `SyncSession` action even if summary localization fails, formatting an honest English fallback from the restored outcome. Never turn a `RestoreFailed`/blocked outcome into success. The conversation-only undo path only prepares a payload before dispatch and does not have the same prior-mutation risk. Extend an existing undo check with translation failure; no new test files. Fork-level API reports `push=false` despite maintainer edits being enabled, so contributor-branch write permission remains unproved. No branch changes, hosted CI, or merges were made.

issues.body:
<!-- cw-0103-status-20261025 -->
## 0.10.3 status — 2026-10-25

Part 1 is on main in [10ce9cde28](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/10ce9cde28f7c19365a54e06398a11bb6f087304): oversized standing instruction files are bounded and head-truncated with a sized marker rather than silently dropped. [PR #7086](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7086) is now being prepared for 0.10.3 with its per-scope budgets and visible loss notices. Its content-policy reconciliation, guard/lifecycle behavior and reporting findings still need verification before merge. The PR is not yet landed.

<!-- /cw-0103-status-20261025 -->

---

## Problem

Standing instruction authority has two fixed ceilings, neither steerable by an operator, and both failure modes are invisible from the user's side.

**The ceilings (hard-coded, no config key).**

- `MAX_PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_BYTES = 48 * 1024` — `crates/tui/src/project_context.rs:384`. Everything that reaches the model as standing instruction authority — the repository-root → workspace `AGENTS.md` chain, the global fallback layer, `.codewhale/rules/*.md`, and any imported foreign files — shares this one budget. Documented as fixed at `config.example.toml:360`.
- `MAX_CONTEXT_SIZE = 100 * 1024` — `crates/tui/src/project_context.rs:366`. A context file over this is not trimmed: `load_context_file_with_symlink_policy` returns `Err(ProjectContextError::TooLarge)` (`:1083`; error text `crates/tui/src/project_context/types.rs:22`), the caller collects it as a warning and moves to the next candidate filename (`:565`), so that file's contribution is missing — while the chain still assembles ancestor files (`:620-665`) and merges the global fallback layer (`:684`, `merge_global_and_project_instructions` at `:946`). The agent then runs on a *broader* instruction set than the operator wrote, with nothing saying so.

`Config::instructions_paths()` selects *which* extra files load; their only ceiling is the fixed per-file truncation above, and no key controls either ceiling.

**Observed on a real workspace.** Global `~/AGENTS.md` = 54 KB, project `AGENTS.md` = 88,918 → 94,224 → 118,673 bytes over three days. The session log carries, once per launch:

```
WARN project_context: Dropping broadest-scope project instructions at the aggregate budget was=102031 now=49152 cap=49152
```

i.e. the broadest scope is dropped first, every session, and the project file has just crossed the 100 KiB line that turns it into a `TooLarge` skip.

**The notice gap — this is the part that hurts.** Nothing at session start says any of this happened:

- `as_system_block` (`types.rs:88`) emits instructions + rules + constitution; `ProjectContext.warnings` is **not** part of the prompt, so the model is not told either;
- the warnings surface only in `/context report` (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:500-508`) and `GET /v1/workspace/instructions` (the source map added in #6168);
- the trim itself is a `tracing::warn` (`project_context.rs:448`) plus a marker line inside the content (`:391`).

So an operator with a mature global + project instruction pair cannot tell that half their standing law was cut, or which file lost.

**The two ceilings behave differently for the same nominal 100 KiB, and the docs name a marker the code never emits — happy to split the marker-name fix into its own issue if you prefer.** `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:1261-1262` and `docs/zh_hans/CONFIGURATION.md:680` say of `instructions = [...]`: "Each file is capped at 100 KiB; oversized files are truncated with a `[…elided]` marker rather than skipped." The behaviour is real: `render_instructions_block` caps each source at `INSTRUCTIONS_FILE_MAX_BYTES = 100 * 1024` (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:98`) and truncates it (`:277-289`). What it emits is `[…truncated: N of M bytes omitted — consider splitting this instructions file]` (`:283`); the name `[…elided]` appears only in the rustdoc for `InstructionSource::File` (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:229`) and in those two docs. So the defect is the marker name, not the ceiling.

The asymmetry is the real problem: **the `instructions = [...]` array trims an oversized file and says so in-context; the `AGENTS.md` chain drops the file entirely.** One path is told to split its file; the other loses a layer and is told nothing.

## Proposed solution

Optional knobs, with today's behaviour as the default:

1. `[context] instruction_budget_bytes` (default 49152, with an absolute ceiling) — the shared aggregate budget. The `[context]` table already exists (`ContextConfig`, `crates/tui/src/config.rs:2332`; live key today: `project_pack`), so this is a new key, not a new table.
2. `[context] instruction_file_max_bytes` (default 102400) — per-file ceiling for the `AGENTS.md` chain, and for the `instructions = [...]` path, which carries the same 100 KiB cap hard-coded today.
3. **Skip vs trim stated explicitly, and the chain gets what the array already does.** For a file over the per-file ceiling, either trim with the marker the `instructions = [...]` path already uses (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:283`, including its "consider splitting" hint) or refuse with a message naming the file, the size, and the limit. Silently dropping a whole instruction layer should not be one of the options.
4. **A first-turn notice.** When content is trimmed or a candidate file is dropped, put one bounded line into the run's first turn — e.g. `project instructions: dropped <path> (118673 bytes > 102400); global layer trimmed to budget` — on the same disclosure channel as the sub-agent budget block, so the model can tell the operator and the operator sees it without running a report command.

## Use case

- A user whose global preferences and project `AGENTS.md` together exceed 48 KiB currently cannot tell which half the agent actually read. They discover it by noticing the agent breaking a rule that is written in the file.
- A project whose `AGENTS.md` legitimately needs >100 KiB (an architecture + invariants + workflow document) has no way to load it at all — the layer is dropped, and the failing file is named only in a warning that no default surface shows.
- Tuning: raising the budget for a documentation-heavy repo is a per-user decision, exactly what a config key is for.

## Alternatives considered

- **Split the files** (the workaround): the right first move for the reporter and it needs no code, but it does not solve the visibility half, and it does not help a project that needs >100 KiB.
- **Raise both constants, change nothing else**: makes the budget a moving target with no surface to see it, and a project file over the per-file ceiling would still disappear silently.
- **Keep the skip, fix only the docs**: the docs already claim truncation; making them match a silent skip keeps the operator blind.
- **Put every warning into the system prompt verbatim**: unbounded and re-sent every turn; a single first-turn notice costs one line.

## Impact

Standing instructions shape every turn, so a silent trim silently changes behaviour — and it is invisible in `/cost`, `/tokens`, and the context meter because those measure tokens, not sources. Affected: anyone with a mature global + project instruction pair over 48 KiB, and anyone whose project file crosses 100 KiB.

## Additional context

- Both ceilings and their failure messages verified against `upstream/main` `a2216fc0c`; behaviour reproduced with `codewhale 0.10.0 (dev)`.
- Existing markers: `project_context.rs:391` (broader-scope drop) and `:392` (rules block); `fragments.rs:309` (foreign rule trim).
- `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md` agent-ready standard: the reproduction above is exact and code-referenced.

### What problem does this solve? 要解决什么问题？

Currently I have to go into agents that had assigned work for hours and say continue to them if coordinator agents don't spot they are idle. When doing math verification by coding lean or math in general sometimes reasoning beyond the max limit 65k of deepseek is needed, sometimes even several-fold. Which is why I'm fine with reasoning only or thinking only unlimited continuation. In fact today on ver 0.10.1 the issue appeared multiple times when I assigned work to massive fleet of codewhales. Therefore an option in config would be appreciated.

Currently, it stops and the message i receive is: Warn Model reached the response output limit with no answer or tool call (requested allowance: 65536 tokens, including ││❯ reasoning)  

### What should Codewhale do? 希望 Codewhale 怎么做？

Add an option in codewhale to continue sending continuation for reasoning and thinking only outputs the same as with normal tool or answer outputs.

### Where? 在哪里？

_No response_

### Workarounds or other tools (optional)

I manually write continue, or have my automatic coordinators spot places where it happens. With herdr fork it is easy to spot idle agents, but it adds needless work.

### Contributing

- [ ] I would like to open a pull request for this. 我愿意提交 PR。

---

## 0.10.3 implementation status — source candidate

Implemented on `main` in [fb10884b4f](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/fb10884b4fb7749f4329725857c943eae6eb3642). This is unreleased 0.10.3 work.

```toml
[reasoning_only]
on_output_limit = true
max_reprompts = 2
```

The option is off by default. It retries an output-limit stop with no answer or tool call, including unstreamed reasoning, using the existing shared reasoning-only retry allowance. `max_reprompts = 0` disables this recovery. Ordinary TUI, exec, Runtime API and Fleet workers receive the setting; RLM retains its separate protocol. Request-scoped nudges have durable receipts without entering resumed conversation context.

This does not raise output limits or carry hidden reasoning forward. A fresh request may restart reasoning and incur provider cost; completion of a long proof is not guaranteed. Restart existing engines after changing the configuration. [Configuration details](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/docs/CONFIGURATION.md#reasoning-only-recovery-reasoning_only).

Local evidence: CLI builds passed; 124 focused existing tests passed (70 Engine/TUI, 54 localization). Twenty-three passing local synthetic scenarios cover bounds, shared exhaustion, empty/custom nudges, partial-response guards, v1/v2 worker resume, receipt durability and an actual TUI transcript view. Passing coverage for unchanged paths was reused; the terminal-stop/body-error Fleet case was rerun after correcting its existing transport replay path. All inference used loopback fixtures. No hosted CI, real DeepSeek/provider workload, release or deployment is claimed.

issues.body:
## What a new user hits

Main now adopts a running local Ollama on first launch when no cloud key exists (good). On that route the **second turn fails**:

```
Note Context recovery failed: The summary for making room was incomplete: provider stop reason length; the partial summary was not accepted. Original conversation was preserved.
Error The request still exceeds this model's context budget and automatic recovery did not complete. The conversation is saved; retry or choose a larger context route.
```

while the footer reads `context 33%` and `/context report` says `Window: 32768 tokens (16.2% used)`, `Overflow guard: 5468 tokens`.

## Repro (isolated, no keys)

1. Ollama running with `qwen3:4b` (reports `context_length: 32768` in `/api/ps`, 262144 in `/api/show`).
2. `HOME=$(mktemp -d) CODEWHALE_HOME=$(mktemp -d) codewhale` (release build of main `715bb2ed02` + working tree, `codewhale 0.10.2 (dev)`), in a tiny git repo.
3. TUI shows `Provider switched: deepseek → ollama`, footer `Ollama · qwen3:4b · thinking: max`.
4. Turn 1: "Read calc.py and add a subtract function" → completes (+2 −2 patch).
5. Turn 2: "Write a file notes.md with a 10-item list of python tips." → "Making room in the conversation… 55s", then the error above. No file written.

Log (`$CODEWHALE_HOME/logs/tui-*.log`):

```
WARN compaction: auto-compaction refused under pressure reason=RetainedFloor { floor: 8082, threshold: 5120 } billed=Some(6319)
INFO engine.turn: engine turn completion settled status=Failed
```

## Likely cause

Same shape as #5820 (closed 2026-09-05): `automatic_max_output_tokens` (`crates/tui/src/route_budget.rs`) reserves `API_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 65_536` for every non-DeepSeek route; clamped into a 32K window it leaves an input budget of ~5K, smaller than Codewhale's own static prefix (~4.8K by `/context report`: constitution 1803 + skills 2153 + policy). So any local 32K model fails as soon as history passes ~5K tokens, i.e. on turn 2. Not verified at source level beyond the threshold numbers above.

## Why it blocks 0.10.3

"No key → local model just works" is now the default first-run path, and it breaks on the second message.

Evidence: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/j05-steer-*.txt`, `j05-context-report.txt`, `homes/fresh-main/cw/logs/` (local QA artifacts).

prs.body:
## What and why

Closing a terminal can deliver SIGHUP while session persistence still has queued work. The signal handler previously exited after draining the Runtime API without asking the persistence actor to flush.

Flush the existing actor before signal exit, with one two-second timeout covering both command admission and acknowledgement. Run this alongside Runtime API draining; a second terminating signal still skips both waits. Report write failures or missing acknowledgement without changing the exit status.

This covers already queued work only. It does not capture TUI state that has not been queued or make checkpoint-only sessions appear in the resume picker. The timeout bounds the asynchronous wait, not synchronous filesystem operations already executing inside the actor.

## Issue

Refs #7095

This runs the real actor and SessionManager, including queued snapshot/checkpoint writes before shutdown, checkpoint retention, full-channel and acknowledgement timeouts, disconnected actors, and write-failure reporting. prs.title: fix(tui): route a streamed reasoning delta to the reasoning cell
prs.body:
Refs #7123

Fixes #7123

## What the user saw

Collapsed, one line of reasoning text showed outside the thinking card. Expanded, a single sentence was split: the first half inside the card, the second half below it as ordinary assistant prose.

## Root cause

`commit_streaming_display_tick` chose its destination cell by whichever cell happened to be live last (`app.streaming_message_index`), not by the kind of the block the delta belonged to. The engine keeps an assistant cell live after a text block ends — `ContentBlockStop(Text)` only sets `pending_message_complete`, and `MessageComplete` is emitted once per response — so when a response streams prose and then opens a reasoning block, the reasoning text was appended to the prose body. That is the split sentence.

Two more losses sat on the same boundary, both found in review:

- `streaming_thinking::start_block` resets `StreamingState` when a reasoning block opens. The display beat commits at most once per interval, so a boundary between beats left the last slice of prose in the buffer and the reset discarded it.
- `ThinkingComplete`'s translation branch drained block 0 by index, ignoring kind, so a text block that lost its boundary event was consumed and dropped.

## The fix

- `StreamingState::block_is_thinking` reports a block's own kind; the display beat routes by it. Reasoning always lands in the thinking cell, and a text delta still gets an assistant cell when its own was already closed.
- `start_block` delivers a pending prose tail before resetting.
- Every finalize path drains block 0 only when a block of its own kind owns it, including the translation branch.
- `MessageStarted` finalizes a live reasoning entry **before** `flush_active_cell` — that flush clears `streaming_thinking_active_entry` on every path and only marks the cell finished, so draining after it was dead code.
- `finalize_current` leaves the buffer alone when there is no live entry to deliver into, and `flush_pending_text_tail` resolves its destination before taking the buffer.

## This branch also repairs `main`

`main` does not build or lint on the current stable toolchain. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` only triggers on `pull_request`, so the direct pushes that introduced these were never compiled by CI. This PR is the run that finds them, so the fixes travel with it:

- `fetch_tag_profiles` (`crates/tui/src/client/ollama_catalog.rs`) became a `buffer_unordered` stream whose items borrow the tag from the caller's slice, so the closure inferred one lifetime per element and rustc refused three spawn sites with `implementation of FnOnce is not general enough`. The stream now owns its tags.
- `SessionManager::save_checkpoint` lost its last non-test caller when the terminal moved to `save_checkpoint_owned`, leaving `-D dead-code` to fail outside `cfg(test)`.
- Two clippy findings that `main` never had linted: `needless_return` in `session_manager.rs` and `unit_arg` in `provider_routes.rs`.
- Two `cfg` corrections in `crates/app-server` where an import was gated `cfg(test)` but its only user is `cfg(all(test, unix))`, breaking a Windows `-D warnings` build.

Each import is now gated exactly like the code that uses it, and both clippy findings are fixed rather than allowed.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-app-server --lib` with `-D warnings` — clean. This is the first time this tree compiles on current `main` in this environment.
- CI on `7e94f8c20`: `Lint`, `Test (windows-latest)`, `Version drift`, `MSRV check (1.89)`, `Safety gate`, `Mobile runtime smoke`, `Integrations`, `Plugin conversion`, `VS Code extension`, `npm wrapper smoke`, the workflow lints and `Extension host runtimes` on all three platforms pass.
- `Test (ubuntu-latest)` fails with 9 tests. None is on a path this PR touches — the diff is 10 files and contains no fixture, golden, schema or command catalog:

  *Fixture drift on `main`, the same class as the build breakage above:*
  - `tools::file_tool::tests::schema_stays_within_its_catalog_byte_budget` — the `File` schema is 3394 bytes against a 3200 budget; the largest property is `replace` at 326.

prs.title: fix(tui): route a streamed reasoning delta to the reasoning cell
prs.body:
Fixes #7123

## What the user saw

Collapsed, one line of reasoning text showed outside the thinking card. Expanded, a single sentence was split: the first half inside the card, the second half below it as ordinary assistant prose.

## Root cause

`commit_streaming_display_tick` chose its destination cell by whichever cell happened to be live last (`app.streaming_message_index`), not by the kind of the block the delta belonged to. The engine keeps an assistant cell live after a text block ends — `ContentBlockStop(Text)` only sets `pending_message_complete`, and `MessageComplete` is emitted once per response — so when a response streams prose and then opens a reasoning block, the reasoning text was appended to the prose body. That is the split sentence.

Two more losses sat on the same boundary, both found in review:

- `streaming_thinking::start_block` resets `StreamingState` when a reasoning block opens. The display beat commits at most once per interval, so a boundary that lands between beats left the last slice of prose in the buffer and the reset discarded it — the tail before a reasoning card never reached the transcript.
- `ThinkingComplete`'s translation branch drained block 0 by index, ignoring kind, so a text block that lost its boundary event was consumed and dropped.

A third, found on the third review round: the first attempt at the `MessageStarted` fix was dead code. `App::flush_active_cell` clears `streaming_thinking_active_entry` on every path and only marks the thinking cell finished; it does not deliver a delta that never reached it. Draining after that flush can never run.

## The fix

- `StreamingState::block_is_thinking` reports a block's own kind; the display beat routes by it. Reasoning always lands in the thinking cell, and a text delta still gets an assistant cell when its own was already closed.
- `start_block` delivers a pending prose tail before resetting.
- Every finalize path drains block 0 only when a block of its own kind owns it, including the translation branch.
- `MessageStarted` finalizes a live reasoning entry **before** `flush_active_cell`, which is the only point where the entry is still live.
- `finalize_current` leaves the buffer alone when there is no live entry to deliver into, and `flush_pending_text_tail` resolves its destination before taking the buffer.

## Scope

Five files, six commits, all in `crates/tui`:

```
crates/tui/src/tui/streaming/mod.rs        |  10 ++
crates/tui/src/tui/streaming_thinking.rs   | 163 +++++++++++++++++++-
crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs        |  25 ++++
crates/tui/src/tui/ui/frame.rs             |  83 +++++++++---
crates/tui/src/tui/ui/tests.rs             |  57 +++++++++
```

This replaces #7134, which also carried fixes for breakage on `main` that this PR does not need to own. #7129 has since merged those, so the diff here is the reasoning-cell fix alone.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --lib` with `-D warnings` — clean.
- CI on this branch is running; see the checks below.
- I could not run the test suite locally: linking the lib test target exhausts memory on this machine (rustc reaches ~8.5 GB RSS and LLVM aborts). CI runs it.

New tests, each asserting the cell that must *not* receive the text:

- `issue_7123_reasoning_after_prose_stays_in_the_thinking_cell`
- `issue_7123_drain_text_block_leaves_a_reasoning_block_alone`
- `issue_7123_reasoning_block_keeps_the_prose_tail_it_interrupts`
- `issue_7123_finalize_current_leaves_a_text_block_alone`
- `issue_7123_message_started_order_keeps_the_reasoning_tail`

`Test (ubuntu-latest)` may be red. Its 9 failures are pre-existing on `main`: the same 9 tests fail identically on #7129 and #7125. That is pre-existing breakage from direct pushes to `main`, not from this diff; per `CONTRIBUTING.md` a red check that is clearly explained is acceptable, so I left it out of scope rather than widening the diff.

prs.title: fix(tui): put vim `$` on the line's last character
prs.body:
## What and why

In vim composer mode (`composer_vim_mode = "vim"`), `$` leaves the cursor after the line's last character: on the newline, or past the end of the draft on the last line. `vim_enter_normal` already steps back off the end of the draft so the cursor sits on a character, and `x` deletes what is under the cursor, so `$x` did nothing on the last line and deleted the newline on any other line, joining it to the next.

Launch composer, `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app`, one key at a time. A one-line draft `hello`, then `$`, `x`, and `x` again, before:

```
$, x  ❯ hello
x     ❯ hello
```

After:

```
$, x  ❯ hell
x     ❯ hel
```

Three lines `hello`, `mid`, `world` with the cursor on the first, then `$`, `x`, and `x` again, before:

```
$, x  ❯ hellomid
        world
x     ❯ helloid
        world
```

After:

```
$, x  ❯ hell
        mid
        world
x     ❯ hel
        mid
        world
```

`$` now moves with `move_cursor_line_end` and then steps back one grapheme cluster when that lands on a newline or the end of the draft after a non-empty line. `x` takes the same step after it deletes, so `$xx` keeps taking characters off the end instead of reaching the newline; that replaces its old check, which only stepped back at the end of the draft. `o` relied on `$` landing after the last character, so it now calls `move_cursor_line_end` itself.

One edge moves with it: when `x` deletes the only character on the last line, the cursor now stays on that empty line instead of stepping onto the newline above, so with `a`, `o`, `b`, Esc, `x`, `i`, `c` the draft reads `a` / `c` where it read `ac`.

On a terminal that `paste.rs` doesn't trust to deliver bracketed paste, Normal-mode keys don't reach these handlers yet; #7126 fixes that.

## Issue

No-Issue: vim `$x` deletes nothing or joins lines instead of deleting the last character; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 3690f9c4a in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME, `composer_vim_mode = "vim"` in `settings.toml` and `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app`, sending one key at a time on the launch composer. Besides the rows above: `o` on the first of two lines opens a line between them in both builds (`hello` / `mid` / `world`), and `k`, `$`, `a`, `Z` on `a` / `c` appends to the first line (`aZ`) with this change.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 13908 of 13912 passed, with the 175 `vim` and `composer` tests among them. The 4 failures are plugin import tests (three in `plugins_dsh_tests`, plus `plugins_skill_tests::dsh_packages_import_through_the_reviewed_install_and_update_flow`, all "composition reviewer is unavailable"); the same 4 fail on `main` at 3690f9c4a without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`: clean.

- [x] One focused change, on 3690f9c4a; it merges cleanly into current `main`

- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: Note the VS Code extension's dependency on the Runtime API
prs.body:
## What and why

`crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs` reads as private to this repository, but it is the only API the community VS Code extension (`HengQuWorld/CodeWhale-VSCode`) talks to: it spawns `codewhale serve --http` and drives every feature through `/v1/*`. Nothing here or in the test suite would notice a route whose shape changed, so the breakage would first appear in that project's release.

This adds one short section to `crates/tui/AGENTS.md` recording the dependency, and the three wire details that have no fallback on the client side:

- the wrong-method feature detection — anything other than `404` means the route exists, so a fallback that answers `404` for an unrouted method silently disables features instead of failing;
- the `RUNTIME_LISTENING_PREFIX` line, whose port must be the requested one, followed by `401` anonymously and `200` with the bearer token;
- the `/v1/runtime/info` capability flags, which may only claim routes that all exist.

It closes with the rule an editor actually needs: additive routes and optional fields are safe; changing a shipped route's shape needs the extension's client updated in the same change, or both shapes kept.

No code, no behavior change.

## Issue

No-Issue: agent-facing documentation only; no code or behavior change.

## How I tested it

Docs-only, so no build or test run applies. Every claim was checked against source in both repositories:

- `serve --http` launch, listener-line and token handshake: `src/api/engine.ts` (`launch`, `probe`).
- Wrong-method probing: `src/api/api-client.ts` `probePath()` returns `statusCode !== 404`.
- Capability flags: `probeRuntimeInfoFlags()` client-side; advertised at `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:1345`.
- The extension uses no `app-server`, `--stdio` or `--socket` path, so the HTTP Runtime API is its whole engine surface.

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` — no Rust changed; there is nothing to format or test
- [x] Not a user-facing feature, so no `docs/features.toml` row

## What and why

`main` does not compile right now, so every PR built on it is red before review. This fixes the three errors that block it.

**The compile error.** `fetch_tag_profiles` hit ``error: implementation of `FnOnce` is not general enough`` through three call sites (`client.rs::fetch_catalog_delta`, `client.rs` route sweep, `local_ollama.rs::spawn_local_ollama_adoption_probe`). Since 7c49574a6 the per-tag async block borrows `&String` out of the caller's `tags` slice, so the stream's item type carries a caller lifetime and `tokio::spawn` cannot accept it. The function now owns an `String` per candidate; bounded concurrency (`SHOW_PROBE_LIMIT`) and result ordering are unchanged.

Worth knowing for anyone who hits this: the compiler's `help: consider adding an explicit type annotation to the closure's argument` (`|tag: &String|`) **does not fix it** — I checked that suggestion in isolation and it still fails.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep the turn metadata block out of /tree and /export
prs.body:
## What and why

The engine appends a `<turn_meta>` block to each user message it saves. The transcript leaves it out (`is_turn_metadata_block`, from #4681), and so do the resume picker, session titles and the ACP replay, but `/tree` and `/export` still read it as text.

`/tree` labels a user entry with its text blocks joined, so after one turn, before:

```
● 5fae47c9 [5fae47c9-…] user: say flat things <turn_meta> Current local date: 2026-10-29 C
```

After:

```
● f05aed51 [f05aed51-…] user: say flat things
```

`/export`, and the copy it puts on the clipboard, writes the block as a second content block of every user message. The export's header says hidden instructions are omitted and gives the workspace by folder name only, but the block carries its absolute path (shortened here). Before:

```
## 1. user

### Content 1: Text

say flat things

### Content 2: Text

<turn_meta>
Current local date: 2026-10-29
Current workspace: /…/ws
Current permission posture: Ask
Current sandbox posture: workspace-write (writes inside the workspace; network blocked) (local OS sandbox applied)
## Repo Working Set
Key files: README.md
When in doubt, use tools to verify and keep changes focused on the working set.
Git workspace: main | clean
</turn_meta>
```

After:

```
## 1. user

### Content 1: Text

say flat things
```

Three places now skip the block at the index `turn_metadata_text` returns, as `prompt_text` in `receipts.rs` already does: the journal label in `session_tree::tree_label`, the linear fallback in `tree_body` (used while a session has no journal yet; I didn't reach it in these runs), and `project_message` for the export. Only user messages are filtered, like `is_turn_metadata_block`. The saved session is unchanged.

prs.body:
## Summary

`/config pet_mode --save` answered "宠物模式未能保存：无法删除要被替换的文件。(os error 1175)", and
the same refusal hit every other settings toggle — "无法保存确认。脱敏仍然开启。". A separate
report showed a setup checkpoint failing to persist to a path printed with a
backslash missing, and `doctor` reporting a half-applied setup that did not
exist.

The settings half is not transient contention, so the first attempt at it
(retrying the code) did not fix it. Measured on the affected machine, same file
and same ACLs, only the parent directory varies:

```
D:\CodeWhaleData            ReplaceFileW 1175, MoveFileExW 32, rename fails
D:\                         same
D:\CodeWhaleData\<any sub>  OK
C:\Users\asus\Documents     OK
```

`DeleteFileW` succeeds in the refused directories and rewriting the file in
place succeeds, so the bytes can be delivered without a rename. That is what
this branch now does as a last resort.

## Changes

- **A settings write lands even where renames are refused.**
  `atomically_replace_settings_file` keeps the `ReplaceFileW` retry, then calls
  `rewrite_settings_in_place`. `atomic_write` does the same for
  `setup_state.json` via `rewrite_in_place`. The in-place write truncates and
  rewrites, so it is not atomic — an interruption can leave a partial file.
  `Settings::load_persisted` already tolerates a corrupt document by falling
  back to defaults with `load_error` set, which bounds the damage.

- **The fallback is narrow on purpose.** Only the contention codes fall back —
  5 `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`, 32 `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION`, 33
  `ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION`, 1175 `ERROR_UNABLE_TO_REMOVE_REPLACED` — so a full
  disk or a real permission bit still reports its own error rather than being
  retried into an in-place attempt that would fail the same way.
  `ReplaceFileW`'s 1176 and 1177 stay out of the list: they can leave the
  replacement consumed or altered, which a retry cannot undo.

- **Both writers retry briefly first** — six attempts, `n * 50ms`, 750ms in
  total — because ordinary contention (another instance reading the file, a
  scanner) does clear.

- **The message stops eating its own cause.** It used `{err}`, which prints only
  the outermost `context` and drops the source chain, so the path was the only
  thing left to look at. It now uses `{err:#}`.

- **`doctor` stops flagging a user's own temp-named logs.** The
  `stale_setup_temp_files` check matched any file whose name starts with
  `.tmp`, so scratch files such as `.tmp-build-release.log` made a clean home
  report as half-applied. It now matches what a staged write leaves behind when
  it never lands: `.tmpXXXXXX` with no extension.

- **A note keeps the backslashes in a path.** The wrong path in the first report
  came from here: the note is correct, the renderer is correct, and the note was
  the one that did not escape. A transcript note is machine-generated and names
  paths, but it goes through the markdown renderer, which honours CommonMark
  §2.4 — a backslash before ASCII punctuation is an escape, so `\.` yields `.`.
  `escape_note_backslashes` now doubles a bare backslash in note prose, at the
  one place every note passes through.

  Three regions are passed through exactly as written, because the renderer
  already copies them verbatim and doubling a backslash inside one would
  *print* the extra backslash: a fenced block (closed only by a run at least as
  long as its opener), a line carrying a delimiter the renderer treats as a
  passthrough (backtick, `*`, `~~`), and a table row.

  `_`-delimited emphasis is deliberately not a passthrough trigger: `_` is
  everywhere in identifiers (`setup_state.json`), and a false positive would
  leave the paths this pass exists to protect untouched.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing

Run locally on Windows:

- **The reported failure, before and after**, against the affected directory:
  - before: `config set pet_mode false` → exit 1, `settings.toml` mtime
    unchanged, value still `true`.
  - after: `config set pet_mode false` → `set pet_mode in
    C:\Users\asus\.codewhale\settings.toml`, mtime advanced, `pet_mode = false`
    written. Repeated with another key and the value restored each time.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-config --lib -- persistence` → **30 passed; 0
  failed**, including the new `an_in_place_rewrite_replaces_a_longer_document`,
  which rewrites a longer document with a shorter one and asserts the old tail is
  gone.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-runtime --lib -- only_a_held_destination` → **1
  passed**: the allow-list retries 5/32/33/1175 and refuses 2/3/112/87.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-config --lib -- only_a_contended` → **1 passed**.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- a_system_note` → **3 passed**;
  `a_fence_of_four_backticks_is_not_closed_by_three` → **1 passed**.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- doctor_setup_consistency` → **4 passed**,
  the two existing cases included, so the narrower match did not stop the check
  from firing on a real orphan.
- `codewhale doctor` on the authoring machine no longer prints the
  `half-applied setup detected (stale_setup_temp_files_in_codewhale_home)` line
  it printed before this change.

**What I could not determine:** *why* those directories refuse renames. Restart
Manager reports no holder; no process has them as its CWD (checked with junction
resolution); a handle opened with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` plus a mapped view does not
reproduce it; the ACL merge flags do not change the result. The fix therefore
targets the observable behaviour (delete works, rename does not) rather than the
cause. If a maintainer can name the mechanism, a narrower fix may be possible.

Not run locally: `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` and
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked`. CI is the
first full run; treat this section as what was actually observed, not a claim
about the whole gate.

## Checklist

- [x] Updated docs or comments as needed (root CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`, packed
      slice regenerated with `scripts/sync-changelog.sh`)
- [x] Added or updated tests where relevant
- [ ] Verified TUI behavior manually if UI changes (the note path is covered by
      unit tests on the rendered spans; the settings path was verified through
      the CLI against the real failing directory)
- [x] Harvested/co-authored credit uses a GitHub numeric noreply address (no
  external contribution in this change)

## Related Issues

No-Issue: two user-visible failures of the same class — a write refused because
a directory would not let go of the destination — whose parts turned out to be
independent defects.

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

prs.body:
## What and why

The vLLM Chat adapter sends low/medium/high uniformly, but reviewed Qwen3.8 templates accept low/medium/xhigh and reject high. Other reviewed templates expose only a thinking switch or low/high/max.

Add revision-sourced local template facts and apply them after generic vLLM shaping. Qwen3.8 legacy High/Max reaches xhigh; boolean templates omit fictitious effort; GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Vision receive their actual levels. Model effort uses chat_template_kwargs, omitting the top-level enum so older OpenAI schemas cannot reject xhigh/max before rendering. Preserve legacy aliases, separately named Thinking variants, unknown IDs and non-vLLM routes. Credentials, routing, messages/tools, sampling, token budgets, streaming and retries are unchanged.

## Issue

Closes #7124

## Validation

- Final upstream e8490b81b87d9411eb7f15b7bce7df7d038f7b1c: Linux config regressions report test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed. Exact checkout SHA is logged at https://github.com/gannp/codewhale/actions/runs/40651512918 (attempt 6).
- 36 offline registry-to-pinned-template checks pass; raw Qwen high rejection was reproduced before adaptation. No live inference or runtime changes.
- Formatting checked; a regression through the production Chat route added. Full repository CI remains separate and is still running.
- Local Windows cargo test could not link because MSVC link.exe is absent; this is recorded as unavailable, not a pass.

AI-assisted draft contribution. Canonical served-name facts are narrow and source-revision linked; arbitrary custom aliases/templates are not inferred.


DeepSeek-V4-Vision retains its pre-existing Off request spelling; only its enabled effort ladder is normalized.

prs.title: fix(tui): send a held key to vim Normal mode instead of typing it
prs.body:
## What and why

With `composer_vim_mode = "vim"`, Normal-mode keys type into the draft on any terminal that `paste.rs` doesn't trust to deliver bracketed paste: every Windows terminal, and anything whose `TERM_PROGRAM` is unset or isn't ghostty, iTerm.app, WezTerm or Apple_Terminal (tmux and VS Code's terminal set their own). There, the raw-paste guard holds each plain ASCII character for 8 ms to see whether a paste follows, and when nothing does, `flush_paste_burst_before_composer` inserts it. That happens before the event loop's Normal-mode arm sees the key, so `i`, `x`, `dd` and the motions all go into the draft as text, and Esc then clears the composer. The keys only start working after the session's first bracketed paste.

Launch composer, `TERM_PROGRAM` unset, one key at a time, before:

```
i            ❯ i
hello world  ❯ ihello world
Esc          ❯ Type a message…
0, x, w      ❯ 0xw
```

After:

```
i            ❯ Type a message…
hello world  ❯ hello world
Esc          ❯ hello world
0, x         ❯ ello world
w, x         ❯ ello orld
dd           ❯ Type a message…
```

A held character now goes to `vim_mode::handle_vim_normal_key` when no slash or mention menu is open, the condition that arm checks; it is absorbed in Visual mode, as the arm after it does; and it is typed into the composer otherwise. The function already does this for a held Space, which goes to the transcript when the composer is empty. A burst is still a paste: `abc` sent in one write lands in the draft as text in Normal mode, before and after.

## Issue

No-Issue: vim Normal-mode keys are typed as text on a terminal without trusted bracketed paste; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at b8afed5f2 in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and `composer_vim_mode = "vim"` in `settings.toml`, sending one key at a time on the launch composer. With `TERM_PROGRAM` unset, the results are above; `v` then `q` typed `vq` before and does nothing now. With `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app` the two builds give the same results, and the steps before the `abc` burst match what this change now gives with it unset; the burst itself differs, since a trusted terminal reads it as typed keys rather than a paste. `/he`, Esc, `x` reads `/hxe` with this change, as it does with iTerm.app, because the slash menu is open.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 13908 of 13912 passed, with the 260 `paste`, `vim`, `composer` and `event_loop` tests among them. The 4 failures are plugin import tests (three in `plugins_dsh_tests`, plus `plugins_skill_tests::dsh_packages_import_through_the_reviewed_install_and_update_flow`, all "composition reviewer is unavailable"); the same 4 fail on `main` at b8afed5f2 without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on b8afed5f2; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.body:
## What and why

`/undo` outcome messages were still hardcoded English — the remaining surface #7071 names after the `/diff` slice landed in 887a3c669 (#7101). This routes them through the presentation facet with translations in all 15 complete locale packs, following the exact `/diff` shape:

- `UndoCmd` registration gains `Caps::PRESENTATION`
- `patch_result` / `conversation_result` take a `&dyn CommandPresentationContext`; the internal reports return `Result` like `diff_report`
- 29 `CmdUndo*` keys: catalog enum + `ALL_MESSAGE_IDS` in `codewhale-localization`, resolve arms in tui `diagnostics_messages`, values in en + 14 packs
- the shared `FILES_NOT_REVERTED_NOTE` / `NO_FILE_CHANGES_NOTE` / `SNAPSHOT_REPO_UNAVAILABLE_PREFIX` consts became catalog keys (they had no other consumers)

English output is byte-identical to before: the exact-string assertions in `operations_tests.rs` and `debug_mutation_host_tests.rs` pass unchanged.

Not in this slice: `/edit` and `/retry` messages, the "Command capability unavailable" wiring errors, and host-provided `RestoreBlocked` text — the same surfaces `/diff` left unlocalized.

## Issue

Refs #7071 (undo portion) — I claimed this slice in [the issue](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/issues/7071#issuecomment-6444994400). With this and #7101, both surfaces the issue names as remaining are covered; leaving the close call to you in case more surfaces belong to it.

## How I tested it

```
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/commands undo     → test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/commands          → test result: ok. 28 passed; 0 failed
scripts/dev-test.sh tui debug_mutation_host  → test result: ok. 38 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p codewhale-localization --locked → test result: ok. 54 passed; 0 failed
python3 scripts/check-tui-locale-parity.py   → PASS (15 packs, 2673/2673 keys each)
```

Two red checks, both from `main` moving 28 commits past this branch's base (4b3053d16) — the PR merge ref carries them, and neither file is touched here:

- **Lint** — `cargo fmt` drift in `crates/release/src/install.rs` (from the install/uninstall work that landed on `main` after this branch was cut).
- **Test (ubuntu-latest)** — `exec_stream_drop_acceptance` and two `lifecycle_outbox_exec` integration tests in `crates/tui/tests/integration/`; this PR touches none of those paths (commands-crate messages, locale catalogs, and the two test files listed above).

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` on the branch itself is clean apart from that main drift.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] Behavior-preserving localization; existing tests cover it and pass unchanged
- [x] No new user-facing feature, so no `docs/features.toml` row needed

issues.body:
## Summary

Coordinate the remaining work needed for Skill Workshop to capture useful procedural discoveries during ordinary work and demonstrate that an authorized skill revision improves a later task. Build on existing learning, proposal, evaluation and publication contracts; measure gaps before adding mechanisms.

This is a contributor proposal for discussion, not an accepted roadmap or a claim that OpenClaw lacks self-learning.

## Problem to solve

After an agent discovers a reliable procedure or receives a useful procedural correction, the operator needs to know whether that lesson was captured in the right skill, whether it was applied, and whether it works beyond the original example.

Those are separate outcomes. A pending proposal is not an active skill; a valid file is not behavioral proof; completion of maintenance does not necessarily mean a file changed. The proposed outcome is reliable, inspectable reuse—not more generated skill files.

The supplied static review identified possible coverage gaps between foreground authoring, immediate repair and delayed experience review. It did not measure their frequency or run behavioral trials. In particular, short-turn admission is a hypothesis to investigate, not sufficient evidence for lowering a scheduler threshold.

## Existing behavior and related ownership

OpenClaw already documents immediate repair and experience review. Workshop owns proposal application, while automatic background maintenance can edit its directory directly. These paths must not be given identical validation or publication guarantees by implication. See [self-learning](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/self-learning.md) and [Workshop ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/skill-workshop.md).

| Existing work | Relationship to this proposal |
|---|---|
| steipete’s merged [#100692](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100692), closing [#95477](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95477) | Existing reusable-workflow suggestion work. Reconcile its current behavior and subsequent changes before proposing additional recognition guidance. This umbrella does not reopen the old “missing self-learning” premise. |
| [#123992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123992), closed with linked fix #123994 | Existing evaluator-result visibility work. Reuse or verify its projection rather than proposing outcome visibility as entirely new. |
| Zeus-Deus’s [#111943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/111943) | Adjacent model/reasoning policy proposal. No routing or model-policy change is included here. |
| anyech’s [#141102](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141102) | Existing collection-review eligibility/diagnostics discussion. Keep that decision on its owning issue; reuse its eventual contract. |

This is a coordination proposal, not a takeover of those items. If an existing umbrella already owns the remaining scope, attach the work there instead of opening a competing tracker.

## Proposed solution

Keep proposals and publication in Workshop, loading and refresh in the skills runtime, and permissions and execution capacity with their existing owners. Prefer an optional evaluator plugin over a new core controller. A quality result never grants authority to publish.

### Dependency-ordered workstreams

These are candidate PR units, not existing PRs or assignments. A workstream proceeds only after its gap and owner boundary are established.

| Unit | Change and independent value | Dependency / acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Characterize learning coverage** | Establish a synthetic behavior matrix for manual, foreground and experience-review paths, including current modes and runtime eligibility. Reconcile #100692 and later changes. | First evidence milestone. Separate contract tests from live-model trials. A prompt-text assertion does not prove recognition. Submit a standalone characterization PR only if maintainers want that artifact; otherwise carry its useful fixtures with the first demonstrated fix. |
| **B. Close demonstrated foreground capture gaps** | Improve existing guidance or authoring behavior only where A demonstrates a missing case. Prefer the owning skill or pending proposal; create a distinct skill only for a distinct procedure. | Depends on A. Show correct capture without an explicit learning request, no duplicate for covered work, and no failed attempt stored as a working solution. Preserve publication semantics and mode/permission boundaries. |
| **C. Demonstrate reuse and explain outcomes** | Use existing status, usage and evaluation projections to connect a proposal, its applied revision and a later task. Add only missing information. | Baseline fixtures from A; integrate B if needed. A fresh session must discover and use the authorized revision on changed input. Distinguish pending, applied, evaluated, failed, unavailable and abstained states. Do not silently reload the current session. Coordinate collection diagnostics with #141102. |
| **D. Reference behavioral evaluator** | Exercise exact candidate and baseline revisions through the existing evaluation extension contract; produce interpretable task outcomes. Prefer an optional plugin. | Requires agreement on placement and supported API. Use isolated synthetic tasks, baseline/candidate comparison or a no-skill control where meaningful. An incorrect skill must fail; evaluator absence must not be reported as a pass. Storage and publication remain Workshop-owned. |
| **E. Bounded evaluation and revision** | Optionally coordinate evaluate → revise → re-evaluate → stop through existing owners, without another persistent scheduler or proposal store. | Depends on D and explicit policy agreement. Bound attempts, elapsed time and resource use; honor cancellation; invalidate stale results. Any required-evaluation policy must define missing/error/timeout/skipped outcomes without changing advisory behavior silently. |
| **F. Short-turn review admission, only if justified** | Admit a demonstrated high-value short-turn case through the existing reviewer when foreground capture remains insufficient. | Depends on A/B evidence and a maintainer admission-policy decision. Preserve quiet-time, capacity, identity and authority controls; avoid duplicate or recursive review. No blanket threshold reduction or model call after every message. Omit this unit if the earlier work solves the gap. |

**First milestone:** A, the justified portion of B, and C. Reliable capture and reuse must not depend on building an optimizer.

**Second milestone:** D, then E if accepted. F is an evidence-triggered branch, not a mandatory feature.

### Proof required

Use scenarios covering a useful new procedure, a correction to a used skill, an already-covered lesson, routine work, a successful recovery, an unresolved attempt, denied authority and unavailable runtime capability.

For reuse, withhold the original solved answer and change the input. For optimization, reserve validation cases not used to select edits. Correctness and critical regressions take precedence over token or tool-call savings. Human review or inconclusive results are legitimate outcomes.

Fixtures, skill text and transcripts are evidence, not permission. Tests must not act on real external accounts or collect private conversations, credentials or personal facts.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use existing guidance unchanged:** preferred if characterization demonstrates sufficient coverage; retain useful regression proof rather than adding a feature.
- **Rely on explicit learning requests:** remains valid, but does not establish whether useful discoveries are consistently captured during ordinary work.
- **Lower review thresholds globally:** adds work without establishing that the lost cases contain reusable lessons.
- **Build a new learning service:** duplicates existing owners and is unnecessary unless a specific missing contract is demonstrated.
- **Apply an evaluation gate only to proposals:** cannot support a universal validation promise while direct maintenance remains outside that path. Either state the narrower guarantee or obtain agreement on a coherent change to the owner contract.

## Impact

Affected users are operators relying on learned skills across sessions. The intended benefit is fewer repeated procedural corrections and clearer evidence about what was learned. Frequency and magnitude have not been measured; no reliability percentage, runtime regression or release blocker is asserted.

## Evidence/examples

The input research was a static review pinned to OpenClaw `ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d`; it reported no executed tests or agent trials. Its relevant source pointers are [foreground guidance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts), [review admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/experience-review-scheduler.ts), and [proposal evaluation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/service-evaluation.ts). These are research provenance, not freshly reproduced current-main defects.

The related tracker items and current documentation above were inspected while revising this proposal. Current-source history and behavioral reproduction remain the first implementation step. Hermes supplied UX inspiration in the original research; neither Hermes parity nor a claim of mandatory automatic benchmarking is an acceptance criterion.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself, after agreement on scope and ownership. I would start with the coverage evidence and the smallest demonstrated foreground gap.

## Additional information

**Maintainer decision requested:** does the first milestone belong on a new coordination issue or an existing owner surface? Separately, should a reference behavioral evaluator start as an external plugin, and is an optional required-evaluation/revision policy wanted at all? Neither question assumes approval for a new core contract.

Initial scope excludes a new memory backend, model training, registry, persistent controller, external skill installation, automatic sharing, protected third-party skill edits, model-routing changes, mandatory auto-publication, age-only retirement and same-session context replacement.

### Closure criteria

- [ ] Each workstream is completed with evidence, shown unnecessary, or explicitly deferred with maintainer agreement and a linked owner where appropriate.
- [ ] Accepted learning cases demonstrate correct capture and later reuse; negative controls show meaningful abstention and preserved authority.
- [ ] Evaluation claims identify the tested revision, environment and limits; untested direct maintenance receives no implicit validation badge.
- [ ] No duplicate proposal store, scheduler, publication authority or ownership takeover was introduced.
- [ ] Accepted changes include relevant regression tests, documentation and actual runtime evidence where required.

Intermediate PRs should use `Related: #<umbrella>` and explain which workstream they advance. Only the change satisfying all remaining closure criteria should close the umbrella. Preserve the original contributors’ authorship when extending or reusing their work.

issues.title: [Bug]: one-shot session-target automations fail with "PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker" on PostgreSQL state
issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a Gateway whose `state`, `agent` and `workboard` families are on PostgreSQL, one-shot `agentTurn` automations that target an existing session (`sessionTarget: "session:<key>"`) finish with `Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker; only synchronous admission, migrations, and CLI one-shots may run on the main thread; verify database.postgres.connection and server availability.`, so the turn never runs.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Gateway with `database.families.state|agent|workboard.engine: "postgres"` (PostgreSQL 17.11, connection from a `pgdsn` file SecretRef).
2. From a Control UI (dashboard) session, add a one-shot automation:
   ```json
   {"name":"check","schedule":{"kind":"at","at":"<a few minutes ahead>"},
    "sessionTarget":"session:agent:main:dashboard:<id>","deleteAfterRun":true,
    "payload":{"kind":"agentTurn","message":"<instructions>"}}
   ```
3. Wait for it to fire, then read `automations runs <jobId>`.

Observed twice on 2026-10-28 with two separate jobs of this shape. Both failed, and I did not see a success.

### Expected behavior

The job runs an agent turn inside the target session and delivers its result there. That is the documented contract of the automations tool: "`session:<key>` + agentTurn runs a turn inside that existing conversation."

### Actual behavior

The run finishes with `status: "error"`, `completionStatus: "failed"`, and the PostgreSQL main-thread error as both `error` and `deliveryError`. No agent turn appears in the target session.

- Job `4f4f93cf-…` (fired 2026-10-29T02:24:00Z) failed in **61 ms**.
- Job `78a678cb-…` (fired 2026-10-29T04:35:00Z):

issues.body:
## Environment

OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (gateway + agent automations tool), long-lived single-user install. Also verified unchanged against current `main` source on 2026-10-29.

## Observed

The automations tool job schema (`createCronToolSchema` in `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts`) declares `owner` (`agentId`/`sessionKey`) as a job field usable for both `add` and `update` - it is omitted only in the management-only variant (`Type.Omit(job, ["declarationKey", "owner"])`). Passing `job.owner` on `update` reaches the Gateway and is rejected:

```
invalid cron.update params: at /patch: unexpected property 'owner'; must have required property 'jobId'; at root: unexpected property 'id'; must match a schema in anyOf
```

Root cause is the wire schema: `CronJobPatchSchema` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` is a closed object that intentionally excludes `owner` (and `scheduledToolPolicy`), while `CronAddParamsSchema` includes both. Ownership is therefore create-only - plausibly deliberate, since a neighboring field states the rationale "intentionally absent from the writable patch schema so external callers cannot spoof source ownership". The problem is the mismatch: the tool schema advertises the fields as patchable, and the rejection error is a confusing anyOf dump rather than a clear "create-only" signal.

## Isolation / Steps to reproduce

1. Create an automation while steering from a direct-message session; the stored job records that session key in `owner.sessionKey` and `scheduledToolPolicy.ownerSessionKey`.
2. End/delete that session (restart recovery or session cleanup).
3. Attempt to repoint the automation's owner via the automations tool `update` with `job.owner = { ... }` -> rejected with the error above. The CLI is no better: `cron edit` has no owner flag (`--session-key` only rewrites the top-level routing key).
4. Result: the two owner identity fields keep pointing at a deleted session forever. The only remedy is delete + re-create, which loses the run history and the job id.

## Expected

One of:

- (a) `owner` (and the derived `scheduledToolPolicy`) accepted in `cron.update` for the same authorized caller scope that may set them at create; or
- (b) the tool schema drops them from the update surface (mirroring the management-only variant) so callers learn they are create-only, with the docs saying so; plus
- ideally a repair affordance (`cron edit --owner-session-key`, or a doctor repair case) for owner identity invalidated by session deletion.

## Suggested fix

1. Admit `owner` into `CronJobPatchSchema` behind the same caller-scope check `cron.add` already applies - create-time provenance is caller-verified there, so update-time reassignment can reuse the identical trust model.
2. If create-only is intentional instead: remove the fields from the tool's update surface and document the limitation.
3. Either way, an explicit repair path for owner identity invalidated by session deletion would avoid delete+re-create surgery. We currently have one automation carrying a dead owner session key and had to weigh losing its run history just to purge a bookkeeping string.

## Related

No prior issue or merged PR found (searched: "automation owner sessionKey patch", "cron update owner unexpected property", "owner sessionKey automation", "automation owner patch"). On current main, `normalizeCronJobInput` normalizes owner for create and `CronJobPatchSchema` remains unchanged.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`openclaw update --dry-run --json` exits with an invalid-config refusal when authored configuration cannot be parsed, instead of returning the best-effort preview.

### Steps to reproduce

The existing `src/cli/update-dry-run-state.process.test.ts` case `keeps malformed config and state immutable during preview` creates an isolated profile with the config bytes `{ definitely-not-json\n`, then runs the real `openclaw.mjs update --dry-run --no-restart --timeout 1 --json` entry point.

This failed on commit `07bd3eff3be9bf5a25e0615456ecfa6b38b8e45a` in [scheduled CI job 123263988570](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40818038863/job/123263988570). The job uses Node 24.22.1 to launch the test runner and the pinned Bun 1.4.4 canary to execute this process-test group and its CLI child.

### Expected behavior

Return structured planned actions with `Would refuse update` notes and exit successfully, preserving authored configuration and state and recording no update run. This follows the existing immutable-preview regression and the best-effort handling in `preflightUpdateCommandSchemas`. A preview must not infer a database backend from an unparseable config. Actual updates must continue to refuse unsafe admission.

### Actual behavior

The child exits 1. The error is `Update refused: configuration is invalid`, followed by Doctor guidance. The assertion at line 254 expects exit 0; JSON-preview and byte-immutability assertions are never reached. The migration-pending preview case passes in the same run.

### Environment

Linux CI, source commit `07bd3eff3be9bf5a25e0615456ecfa6b38b8e45a`; isolated synthetic HOME, config and state directories. No live Gateway or user installation is involved.

### Additional context

The early database-engine wrapper now rejects `CONFIG_SOURCE_INVALID` before reaching preview handling. That refusal is needed for actual admission and PostgreSQL recovery status, so simply removing it or assuming SQLite would not restore the preview safely. This report does not claim that the failed case proved immutability: its final checks did not execute.

issues.body:
## Problem
`logging.audit` records live in `state/openclaw.sqlite` (docs gateway/audit.md "Storage, retention, and migration"), owned and writable by the same uid the agents run as. An agent (or a compromised process under that uid) can truncate/rewrite the DB, session transcripts and run logs, and nothing outside that uid notices. The audit ledger is immutable by API, but not tamper-evident against the host uid.

## Current workaround (custom)
A scheduled job hashes trace files (session JSONL, run history) and appends `seal path= size= sha256=` lines to the system log (journald / macOS unified log), which that uid can append to but not rewrite; shrinkage, rewritten prefixes and vanished files raise incidents.

## Request
A native tamper-evidence option, e.g. `logging.audit.seal: { sink: "journald"|"oslog"|"syslog"|"remote", intervalSeconds }` that periodically emits a hash-chain head (and per-file seals for configured trace roots) to an append-only sink outside the Gateway uid's write authority, plus `openclaw audit verify` to check the local ledger/traces against the sealed heads. Linux and macOS.

## Version
2026.10.3

issues.body:
Drop MESSAGE_CREATE event when receiving-bot-account has isDefault=true AND a more-specific-scoped binding matches for the target channel

## Summary
Currently, an openclaw gateway configured with multi-agent bindings + isDefault fallback causes multi-agent fanout on human messages: a single human message on a channel bound to specific agent B causes BOTH bot account A (isDefault=true) AND bot account B (bindings[peer:channel:cid]) to independently generate replies. Result: user observes duplicate/cascaded bot responses to single message. Config knob `channels.discord.allowBots=false` empirically closes cross-bot echo (bot X reading bot Y's output as input) but does NOT close human-triggered multi-agent fanout because human messages bypass allowBots gate entirely.

## Steps to reproduce

1. openclaw config with:
   - `agents.list[0] = {id: "hedwig", isDefault: true, ...}` (guild-scoped catch-all)
   - `agents.list[1] = {id: "nanami", bindings: [{peer: {kind: "channel", id: "CHANNEL_X"}, ...}]}`
   - Discord guild with both Hedwig APP and OpenClaw Nanami APP as members with View Channel permission on CHANNEL_X
   - `channels.discord.allowBots: false` (to rule out cross-bot echo)
2. Human user posts message in CHANNEL_X
3. Both bot APPs generate independent replies within seconds of each other

## Empirical evidence

- `cowork-session/state/a692-post-restart-check-20260820T0315Z.log` — 7 bot messages POST-baseline (post-restart with allowBots=false LIVE) including two 03:04Z→03:05Z fanout instances
- Human ghostclaw asked "How is everything" at 03:04:49Z; Hedwig APP replied 03:05:06Z; Nanami APP replied 03:05:58Z (both bot=true; distinct account IDs)
- Config state at incident: allowBots=false, gateway pid 92348 stable, hedwig.isDefault=true, nanami.bindings=[peer:channel:1534983396340793405]

## Expected behavior

When bot account A receives a MESSAGE_CREATE event on channel Y where:
- A has `isDefault: true` at scope broader than Y
- Some other agent B has a binding whose peer matches Y

Then A's gateway SHOULD drop the event before processing (delegate to B's more-specific binding). Alternatively, A's isDefault should be interpreted as "catches unhandled channels" — where "unhandled" means "no other binding matches at more-specific scope."

## Actual behavior

A processes the event independently, producing a Hedwig-voice reply that posts via A's account. B ALSO processes the event via its binding. User sees two replies.

## Proposed fix (server-side)

In gateway routing:
```
def route_message_create(event, agent):
    if agent.is_default:
        # Check if any other agent has a more-specific binding matching event.channel_id
        more_specific = [
            a for a in all_agents
            if a.id != agent.id
            and any(
                b.matches_channel(event.channel_id)
                and b.scope_depth() > agent.default_scope_depth()
                for b in a.bindings
            )
        ]
        if more_specific:
            return drop_event(event, reason="delegated_to_more_specific_binding")
    return process_event(event, agent)
```

Where `scope_depth()` returns integer (guild=1, channel=2, thread=3, etc.).

## Alternative: config-only workaround

Users could work around this by:
- Removing isDefault from agent A (loses catch-all behavior for untargeted channels)
- Adding per-channel exclusion bindings to A (requires schema support for exclusion bindings, currently unclear)
- Moving each specific-binding agent to a channel-scoped isDefault (requires schema support for channel-scoped isDefault)

Please confirm which config workaround is currently supported. Empirical schema audit `state/a692-schema-audit-20260820T0335Z.log` in-flight to determine feasibility.

## Impact

- Every openclaw deployment with a catch-all agent + per-channel bindings is affected
- User-observable duplicate replies degrade UX
- No config workaround currently identified without functionality loss

## Backward compatibility

Proposed fix is opt-in via new config knob `agents.default_delegation_mode` with values:
- `"catch_all"` (current behavior, default for backward compat)
- `"defer_to_specific"` (new behavior — drop when more-specific binding matches)

Users can migrate on their own schedule.

---

Robert to file at github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/new (or wherever upstream lives) using this body verbatim. ### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

### Summary

The release-tag resume test selects the fixture's default release branch instead of its table-selected tag, causing both test type checking and the runtime case to fail in CI.

### Steps to reproduce

At 07bd3eff3be9bf5a25e0615456ecfa6b38b8e45a, the existing candidate dispatch suite pauses after admission, reassigns the tag, and resumes the retained request. The original [tooling job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40818038863/job/123263984698) executes this complete test file. The original [test-types job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40818038863/job/123263983946) checks the root scripts graph.

### Expected behavior

The existing cases should exercise their selected release branch or tag. After that ref no longer contains or identifies the candidate, resume should reject with the corresponding context error before qualification dispatch or temporary-ref creation. The existing remote-only branch-descendant control should remain accepted.

### Actual behavior

Type checking reports TS2353 because `releaseRef` is not a supported `createDispatchFixture` option. At runtime, the tag case expects exit status `1` and receives `0` at `full-release-validation-at-sha.candidate.test.ts:345`. The branch-negative and remote-descendant cases pass in that same execution.

The table selects `v2026.8.1`, but its callbacks use the fixture's returned `releaseRef`, which is always `release/2026.8.1`. It therefore changes `refs/tags/release/2026.8.1` while the CLI retains the unchanged branch. The fixture already supports `includeTargetRef: false` and an explicit `--target-ref` argument.

07bd3eff3be9bf5a25e0615456ecfa6b38b8e45a; the affected table was introduced by #180230.

### Operating system

Linux CI, Node 24.22.1; runtime tests use Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1 and Vitest 5.0.5.

### Install method

Repository CI checkout with locked dependencies.

### Model

Not applicable; fixture-isolated script tests.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable; GitHub calls use the test fixture's executable and temporary Git repository.

### Impact and severity

The root scripts type check and release tooling test lane fail. The tag case does not exercise its intended retained-context rejection. This report concerns the test setup; these results do not establish a production release-policy failure.
