issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The canonical SQLite transcript recovery test advances `Date.now()`, although Memory Core's failed-rebuild cooldown now uses `performance.now()`, leaving its automatic retry inside the cooldown.

### Steps to reproduce

The observed execution is [scheduled CI job 123263984905](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40818038863/job/123263984905) at 07bd3eff3be9bf5a25e0615456ecfa6b38b8e45a. It runs `scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` with the pinned Bun runtime and selects `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-memory-sync.test.ts` through the infra project.

The existing case indexes a synthetic canonical transcript, archives it, damages the archive and confirms that a failed rebuild preserves published recall. It restores the archive bytes, advances the fixture clock by 30 seconds and calls automatic `sync()` without force before checking canonical restoration and clean status.

### Expected behavior

The fixture should advance the actual [documented 30-second retry cooldown](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/07bd3eff3be9bf5a25e0615456ecfa6b38b8e45a/docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md#L225-L229), then verify exact restored transcript contents, removal of the cold marker and cleared dirty/error state. Published source, chunk and FTS rows must remain unchanged during the failed rebuild.

### Actual behavior

Both equal-size rewrite controls pass. The damaged-cold rebuild/recovery case fails with `SessionTranscriptColdError` / `TRANSCRIPT_COLD`, from the hot-transcript guard through `loadTranscriptEventsSync`. The saved stack redacts the fixture caller's line and column; attribution to the final canonical read is inferred from the source, not printed by the runtime.

#186829 moved both retry-deadline creation and comparison to `performance.now()`. The [fixture's scoped spy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/07bd3eff3be9bf5a25e0615456ecfa6b38b8e45a/packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-memory-sync.test.ts#L199-L207) still advances only `Date.now()`. An automatic deferred sync intentionally retains the previous error, and old recall alone cannot demonstrate recovery. The clock mismatch is confirmed in source; a candidate correction has not yet been executed.

### OpenClaw version

Source 07bd3eff3be9bf5a25e0615456ecfa6b38b8e45a.

### Operating system

Linux x64, hosted CI.

### Install method

Repository CI, Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1, Vitest 5.0.5; Node 24.22.1 launcher.

### Model

None.

### Provider / routing chain

Memory search provider `none`, vectors disabled, isolated synthetic SQLite/archive state.

### Impact and severity

The existing recovery test fails in the scheduled infra invocation: this owner executes three cases, with two passing and one failing. That invocation reports 960 passed, 1 failed and 10 skipped; these are not whole-job unique totals. This establishes a CI fixture defect and missing recovery proof, not an observed live-user data-loss incident.

### Summary

The full-tree dead-code check reports the documented history-model projection measurement as an unused file. The script introduced in #187191 has a standalone Node command in its source header, but its executable root is missing from the canonical Knip configuration.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use source revision `82acfabb374991cdb9abeb8bb89984f0cb667733` with its declared frozen dependencies, Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0.
2. Run `pnpm deadcode:unused-files`.
3. Inspect the full-tree unused-file findings for `scripts/perf/history-model-projection-measure.ts`.

### Expected behavior

The measurement should be recognized as an executable root under the repository's [standalone-command convention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82acfabb374991cdb9abeb8bb89984f0cb667733/CONTRIBUTING.md#before-you-pr). Private child modules and unused exports should remain audited.

### Actual behavior

The [completed dependency-check job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40812528521/job/123246099340) reports zero production unused files and three full-tree unused files, including this measurement. Dependency installation completed successfully before the scan. The command exits with status 1.

### OpenClaw version

Source commit `82acfabb374991cdb9abeb8bb89984f0cb667733`.

### Operating system

Linux; the recorded CI runner is the Ubuntu 24.04 runner profile.

### Install method

Source checkout with frozen pnpm dependencies.

### Model

Not applicable; this is a repository static-analysis check.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable; no model request is involved.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The [script's documented launcher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/82acfabb374991cdb9abeb8bb89984f0cb667733/scripts/perf/history-model-projection-measure.ts#L1-L11) and the completed job above establish the mismatch. The introduction in #187191 adds the driver without adding a Knip root.

### Impact and severity

This contributes an incorrect unused-file finding to the repository's dependency check. The cited run also has other findings; correcting this registration alone does not make its aggregate check pass. No benchmark was executed for this report, and it makes no performance or runtime-correctness claim.

issues.body:
## Problem

Interrupting `openclaw dashboard --no-open` while the selected Gateway is still preparing Control UI assets prints the normal interruption notice, but the command keeps waiting and probing the HTTP document. A pending request, retry delay, or diagnostic response body can outlive the accepted interruption.

## Reproduction

Source: current main `e25c026eb75d34ecdeed1d64d68454fb919f3c19` (reports OpenClaw 2026.10.8), Linux, Node 26.12.1. No model or channel is involved.

1. Build the normal CLI with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`.
2. Use an isolated HOME/config/state and a loopback Gateway protocol peer that answers the ordinary readiness read. Its native HTTP document endpoint returns `503` with `Retry-After: 1`.
3. Run `node openclaw.mjs dashboard --no-open` against that selected local target.
4. After recording the first actual HTTP HEAD, send SIGINT or SIGTERM to the CLI process.

Actual: the CLI prints `Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.` (or SIGTERM), remains alive after 2.5 seconds, and the independent HTTP recorder observes HEAD count grow from 1 to 3 after interruption. Holding HEAD response headers reproduces the outstanding-request case. Interrupting during a terminal HTTP503 diagnostic body can also print a late failure and follow-up guidance after the accepted interruption.

Controls: a completed HTTP200 document produces ordinary dashboard output and exit0; a terminal HTTP503 without Retry-After still records HEAD plus diagnostic GET and exits1 with its diagnostic. The recorder uses native HTTP/WebSocket traffic and the normal executable; it does not replace the readiness function. This establishes local CLI cancellation, not a hosted deployment or browser-layout result.

## Expected behavior and scope

The shared document-readiness owner should observe the invoking command lifetime, cancel native transport and retry sleep, and allow the root CLI to finish with130/143. Its dashboard, guided browser-handoff, and setup-finalization callers should preserve cancellation and avoid subsequent handoff/delivery. Preserve completed success, non-cancellation failures, the existing preparation deadline, and Gateway-side asset-build behavior.

I plan to implement and test this bounded owner-level correction. Related accepted readiness behavior: #183713; Gateway asset-build cancellation in #145118 is a different owner.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Doctor logs `StateDatabaseMaintenanceScopeError` when a maintenance-owned agent database reaches its idle eviction timer while Doctor still holds maintenance custody.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Start Doctor maintenance with a disposable OpenClaw state containing an agent database.
2. Open the agent database in the Doctor maintenance scope.
3. Let its detached idle timer expire while Doctor still holds maintenance ownership.
4. Observe the agent database resource close warning.

An isolated regression test reproduces this with fake timers at the Doctor maintenance boundary on source commit `ff7c37bed6496a5559c9fb20974541f807680ef4`.

### Expected behavior
The maintenance-owned handle remains under Doctor's scoped cleanup and is closed with its lease released without a custody warning.

### Actual behavior
The detached timer attempts lease release without a maintenance scope and logs `Agent database resource close failed` with `StateDatabaseMaintenanceScopeError`. The same warning was observed during an actual 2026.10.6 Doctor run; normal Gateway startup succeeded afterward.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.6 custom source build; reproduced on upstream 2026.10.8 at `ff7c37bed6496a5559c9fb20974541f807680ef4`.

### Operating system
macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon.

### Install method
Source build; isolated pnpm/Vitest regression.

### Model
Not applicable; database maintenance path.

### Provider / routing chain
Not applicable.

### Logs
```text
[state/agent-db] Agent database resource close failed
StateDatabaseMaintenanceScopeError: this process holds maintenance ownership without an active schema lease or maintenance scope.
```

### Impact and severity
Doctor emits misleading resource-close warnings during maintenance. Observed during one multi-agent Doctor run and reproduced deterministically in an isolated test. Gateway serving was not observed to fail. Broader frequency and data impact are not established.

### Additional information
The idle timer runs detached, so it cannot borrow Doctor's maintenance scope. A companion change defers eviction while the handle is scope-owned; Doctor's scoped drain then releases the lease.

issues.body:
## Problem

`openclaw config patch --stdin --dry-run --json` waits for EOF after the CLI has accepted Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. An unfinished piped JSON5 input keeps preparation pending, so the ordinary startup wrapper eventually escalates to SIGKILL instead of exiting with130/143.

The normally built executable on main `e25c026eb75d34ecdeed1d64d68454fb919f3c19` reproduces both signals. The ordinary wrapper prints the accepted cleanup notice then naturally ends with SIGKILL. A causal control using the supported `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1` remains pending after that notice; sending the remaining valid input and EOF later causes `ok:true` dry-run output and only then the signal exit. Completed valid and malformed inputs preserve their normal0/1 outcomes, and independent config-byte readback is unchanged throughout. The relevant input and CLI owners remain byte-identical on current main `b2fec86802546120cf18c8f9e336ee3385f348fa`.

## Expected behavior and bounded scope

The existing invocation cancellation should stop the private native stdin reader and prevent canceled preparation from entering config-operation or mutation admission. The root signal owner should retain130/143 without late success JSON or misleading ordinary errors. Preserve TTY rejection, UTF-8/JSON5 validation, the byte cap, file input and non-canceled errors. Already admitted config writes retain their current settlement contract.

Canonical owners are `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts` for the private stdin reader and `src/cli/config-cli.ts` for prepare-before-admission. This changes no patch syntax, configuration, schema, permission, persistence format, shared byte-reader contract or startup-wrapper grace period.

## Implementation and acceptance

I plan to implement this bounded repair as Alix-007. The frozen external collector exercises the actual built command, native stdin pipe and OS signals on base and committed head, with ordinary/default and supported no-respawn controls. Tests will protect cancellation/late EOF at the owning preparation boundary and retain valid/invalid/file input behavior. Config-file readback must remain unchanged for these dry-run scenarios. No production Gateway, user data, real account or provider is used.

issues.title: [Feature]: Create single-use Discord channel invites with the message tool

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let the existing Discord message tool issue a single-use, expiring invite for an explicitly selected guild text channel using the configured Discord account.

### Problem to solve

A community organizer may ask their assistant for a fresh invitation to share with a new member. Discord supports creating this object, but OpenClaw's native Discord actions currently cannot issue it. Posting an existing URL does not create a fresh, limited-use invitation.

There is concrete demand for the underlying task: a [bot developer asks how to generate an invite in a guild their bot has joined](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/57677178/how-to-make-a-discord-bot-to-create-a-invite-in-other-guild), and the [fo40-bridge author describes a community join flow using one-use invites](https://developers.reddit.com/apps/fo40-bridge). These are external Discord workflows. Applying the task to OpenClaw's native message tool is an inference, not a claim that those authors use OpenClaw.

The proposed benefit is access through the existing selected-account, message-action, and requester-permission boundary. Users can already perform the task through Discord's UI or another integration.

### Proposed solution

Add one Discord-owned creation action, with `invite-create` as a suggested name. The first scope is an ordinary guild text channel, one use, a positive lifetime up to Discord's seven-day limit, and unique issuance. For example: “Create a single-use invite to this channel that expires in one hour.” A 24-hour default lifetime would match Discord's ordinary expiry default; the lifetime field name is a maintainer choice.

Use the existing Discord `channels` action gate and configured account. Fetch the target's actual channel type and guild from Discord and verify the eligible target and any supplied guild; do not trust model-provided guild metadata. Carry the host's trusted requester identity into the existing guild-action permission path and check `CREATE_INSTANT_INVITE` for that target channel. Let Discord enforce the bot's own permission independently. A bot's credentials or membership must not substitute for requester authority. Preserve the existing direct-owner origin rules and message action/target policies.

Issue `POST /channels/{channel.id}/invites` with a JSON body requesting the chosen `max_age`, `max_uses: 1`, `unique: true`, and ordinary membership (`temporary: false`). Return the created code/link and channel/guild identity, distinguishing provider-returned metadata from requested values. This action returns a tool result; it does not independently post the link elsewhere.

This requires the smallest addition to the shared closed action vocabulary and targeted-mutation facts, plus the Discord adapter, schema, guild-action dispatch, and existing REST owner. It does not require a new core tool or generic SDK.

### Alternatives considered

- Create the invite in Discord's UI. This works and is the simplest option for manual use.
- Use an existing Discord MCP server. [This implementation](https://github.com/ExilProductions/discord-mcp/blob/337d5c8dbb3ff208fc613f5797ef7e9de427b763/src/discord_mcp/tools/invites.py) already supports invite creation; a separately configured integration is a valid solution. A native action would keep the operation in the existing Discord account and message-tool policy surface.
- Use a script, skill, or custom plugin calling Discord's official API. This is feasible with current extension contracts. It requires maintaining that separate integration; a missing generic extension contract is not the justification here.
- Post a previously created invite. Useful when that link's lifetime and usage policy are appropriate, but it does not issue a new single-use object.

### Impact

- Affected: operators who manage Discord communities through the native message tool and want to issue fresh joining links.
- Severity/urgency: a native capability gap with working alternatives; no measured urgency has been established.
- Frequency: unknown. Public sources establish the task, not an OpenClaw usage rate.
- Consequence: the invitation step requires Discord's UI or another integration even when the assistant can already manage the target channel. No user counts or time savings have been measured.

### Evidence/examples

At OpenClaw main `341b0e5973b473b11c43940986d27b3126026efa`, [the shared action vocabulary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/341b0e5973b473b11c43940986d27b3126026efa/src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts) and [Discord's action discovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/341b0e5973b473b11c43940986d27b3126026efa/extensions/discord/src/channel-actions.ts) expose no invite creation action. Existing [guild-action permission handling](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/341b0e5973b473b11c43940986d27b3126026efa/extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.guild.ts) and [REST operations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/341b0e5973b473b11c43940986d27b3126026efa/extensions/discord/src/send.guild.ts) provide an implementation home. The same relevant action gap was checked separately in latest stable v2026.10.7 (`157d8c2bc3ea2fa183afdc11088e69690bf8e64e`).

[Discord's official contract](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/channel#create-channel-invite) defines the creation operation, lifetime, usage limit, and uniqueness. The demand links above establish external tasks; source inspection establishes the native entry-point gap. No live Discord or installed-plugin experiment was performed for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The first scope excludes invite listing/revocation, permanent or unlimited-use links, guest/stream/application invites, recipient binding, role assignment, member auto-add, Reddit integration, and a persistent invite manager. An invite allows guild entry subject to Discord's ordinary rules; it does not grant otherwise denied channel access. A one-use link remains shareable and is not restricted to a named person.

Suggested implementation: extend the existing Discord channel actions and guild-admin dispatcher, add a channel-scoped `CREATE_INSTANT_INVITE` guard using existing permission helpers, and call the existing account-bound REST client. Classify creation as a targeted mutation, without conversation-read/read-only or message-delivery semantics. Keep current host request assertions and account ownership checks through awaited permission work, gateway handoff, queueing, rate-limit handling, and result consumption. Reuse the Discord request owner's live assertion at dispatch and retries; the current effect-authority compatibility helper alone is not an authorization check. Do not mark the source conversation delivered merely because an invite was issued.

Use the current rate-limit machinery for a rejected 429. A timeout or lost response after dispatch can leave issuance unknown: do not automatically replay a unique create. Cancellation cannot revoke a link already accepted by Discord. No new credential store, config mechanism, dependency, or durable job is needed. The exact action/lifetime-field names and whether the existing `channels` gate is the preferred product grouping remain maintainer decisions; no implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- Through a real installed official Discord plugin and its native message tool, a permitted requester selects an eligible text channel and requests a one-hour invite. The result identifies that channel/guild and a real issued code; wire inspection shows one use, a 3600-second lifetime, and unique issuance. A consenting test account can join with it, and another attempted use fails under Discord's policy. Separately verify expiry of an unused short-lived invite.
- A requester with the necessary channel permission can create an invite without `MANAGE_CHANNELS`; lack of requester permission or bot permission fails without silently changing the target or privileges. Do not add invite listing as a prerequisite.
- Disabled account/gate, disallowed action/target, mismatched account or guild, and forged requester fields cannot issue an invite. Reject DMs, categories, and thread targets for this first scope. Existing caller/registration/account closure while queued prevents a new effect or unauthorized result exposure.
- Normal chat actions remain usable, two explicit create requests ask for distinct unique invitations, and a lost create acknowledgment produces an honest unknown outcome without a second automatic create or a fabricated chat receipt.

issues.title: [Feature]: Support keyterm prompting in ElevenLabs batch transcription

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low-priority cleanup, docs, polish, ergonomics, or speculative work.

labels.name: clawsweeper:bulk-filed
labels.description: ClawSweeper detected a high recent issue-filing volume from this author.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators pass an explicit vocabulary to Scribe v2 through the bundled ElevenLabs batch transcription provider using the existing `providerOptions.elevenlabs` configuration.

### Problem to solve

When transcribing recordings containing product names or specialized terms, an operator may want to supply a specific list of recognition hints. A [LiveKit developer requested this integration control](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408) on February 27, 2026, and supplied an implementation for that product. This is an external demand signal; applying the task to OpenClaw's recorded-audio workflow is an inference, not a report that this person uses OpenClaw.

OpenClaw already transcribes audio through Scribe v2. Its [current ElevenLabs implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts) reads only `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from provider options. A configured `keyterms` array reaches the provider request context but never enters the multipart request. The [provider documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/docs/providers/elevenlabs.md#provider-options) explicitly limits support to those three fields.

The missing capability is selecting the terms used by Scribe's recognition-bias mechanism within this native transcription path. This does not promise correct spelling for every recording or a general improvement in accuracy.

### Proposed solution

Support one additional, opt-in provider option, `keyterms: string[]`, for `scribe_v2` batch transcription. Reuse current provider-scoped configuration and merge precedence; no new top-level configuration or tool is needed. For example:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "media": {
      "models": [{
        "provider": "elevenlabs",
        "model": "scribe_v2",
        "capabilities": ["audio"]
      }],
      "audio": {
        "enabled": true,
        "providerOptions": {
          "elevenlabs": {
            "keyterms": ["OpenClaw", "Acme Research", "PostgreSQL"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Serialize the list as repeated multipart `keyterms` fields, following the provider's array contract and [official SDK request construction](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/f5d53e09e35717523435cee238ac5cc7f51966fb/src/elevenlabs/speech_to_text/raw_client.py#L177). Preserve each term's spelling and Unicode content; do not comma-join the list or encode it as one JSON string. Keep all option fields before the original file, preserving its filename, MIME type, and bytes; the shared multipart builder documents this ordering for streaming parsers. Keep array assembly provider-local rather than widening the shared scalar helper. A model-entry list replaces the audio-default list, as existing options already do. An empty list clears inherited terms; an absent or empty effective list sends no keyterms.

Keep this an explicit allowlisted addition. Preserve dedicated fields, existing scalar options, authentication, guarded HTTP transport, cancellation, and the synchronous transcript-text result. Reject an incompatible option shape or unsupported model rather than silently applying a different control. Surface provider validation errors through the existing error/fallback handling without truncating terms silently.

Document the option and its extra provider charge before users choose it. The [current API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert) currently permits up to 1,000 terms, requires each term to have fewer than 50 characters and at most five normalized words, and specifies disallowed characters. It adds a 20% surcharge; more than 100 terms also impose a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds per request. The provider remains authoritative for validation and future billing changes. No vocabulary is inferred from conversation history or sent by default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Explicit transcription prompt:** OpenClaw already forwards a configured prompt as context. It may help some tasks, but the current ElevenLabs API reference does not specify it as equivalent to structured `keyterms`. Preserve existing prompt behavior; this proposal does not claim it is useless.
- **Deepgram:** OpenClaw supports repeatable Deepgram keyterms after [#176781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176781). Switching providers is valid. This proposal retains the selected ElevenLabs account and model.
- **Official ElevenLabs skill or SDK, a CLI transcription model, or a custom provider plugin:** These can perform vocabulary-guided transcription outside the bundled adapter. The [official skill reference](https://github.com/elevenlabs/skills/blob/9a1a4b7fbb6ca02fbdc7f44f2271e6c829d0f421/speech-to-text/references/transcription-options.md) includes keyterms. These are real alternatives; native support avoids maintaining a separate transcription script or provider registration for one additional input.
- **Correct text afterward:** This can repair known spelling errors but does not give the recognizer a selected term list. An uncertain correction can also change meaning.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Operators using bundled ElevenLabs transcription for recorded audio with specialized vocabulary. The affected OpenClaw population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: The requested recognition control is unavailable in that adapter; ordinary transcription remains usable. No production outage or measured urgency is established.
- Frequency: A configured list would apply to matching transcription requests. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: Operators must accept transcription without that control, correct text, switch providers, or maintain another integration. Time savings and accuracy gains have not been measured. Enabling keyterms can increase provider charges.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original integration request and follow-up](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408); [LiveKit implementation #4967](https://github.com/livekit/agents/pull/4967). These concern the same author and task, not two independent users.
- [Official keyterm guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/speech-to-text/batch/keyterm-prompting) describes vocabulary biasing and distinguishes batch and realtime inputs.
- [Current options schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/config/zod-schema.core.ts#L627), [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts#L86), and [registered provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts#L22) establish the input path and missing mapping.
- [#177975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177975) already implemented three scalar options. This request adds a vocabulary input; it does not reopen that repaired bug or propose unrestricted forwarding.

Verification was static against the pinned main revision. No installed Gateway, live ElevenLabs transcription, or recognition-quality comparison was run for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The implementation owner is `extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts`; its former standalone media-understanding module was consolidated into registration. Suggested work is provider-local array serialization and validation, focused registered-provider coverage, and documentation. Public `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` already accepts string arrays. A new SDK contract, provider manager, dictionary store, or model-facing tool is unnecessary.

Preserve the existing media authorization, HTTP guards, and cancellation behavior applicable to the caller at dispatch; this option does not introduce a new universal execution context. A vocabulary does not authorize a transcription request. Keep terms out of diagnostic logs; they may contain names absent from the audio. No retention or permission change is requested.

Non-goals: Realtime/Voice Call/Google Meet transcription, TTS pronunciation dictionaries, vocabulary management, speaker-label output, asynchronous webhooks, redaction, multichannel results, unrestricted form overrides, or guaranteed accuracy. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- With an isolated configuration selecting `elevenlabs/scribe_v2`, native recorded-audio transcription sends two configured terms as separate multipart fields alongside one unchanged audio file, and returns the transcript through the existing path.
- Capture the actual HTTP body from the shipped transcription entry point, not only a helper call. Verify model-entry replacement of defaults, an empty list clearing defaults, and unchanged requests without a list.
- Existing scalar `false` values and dedicated model/language/prompt fields retain their behavior. Other providers do not receive the ElevenLabs vocabulary; unsupported response-changing keys remain excluded.
- An incompatible scalar value or unsupported model does not silently send an unconditioned Scribe request. Provider-side term rejection surfaces without truncation. With an actual cancellation-capable execution context, cancellation before dispatch prevents a request.
- In an authorized live check, submit a synthetic name-bearing recording with a valid small vocabulary and confirm provider acceptance and native transcript return. Recognition output is observational evidence, not a promise that every supplied term appears.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.10.8, repeated active-leases receipts and agent disk I/O errors were followed by evidence of deleted WAL/SHM descriptors, a different zero-byte directory-visible WAL, absent SHM, and fatal sqlite_wal_sidecar_identity_mismatch containment.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The installed sqlite-wal-DX5E3T-8.mjs module explicitly validates WAL/SHM descriptor/path identity. During Gateway operation, the directory-visible sidecars should remain the same files referenced by the Gateway's open descriptors and POSIX lock.

### Actual behavior

Repeated agent database clean-close receipt: active-leases events preceded email and heartbeat failures reporting disk I/O error | ERR_SQLITE_ERROR.

Before fatal containment, the directory-visible WAL was zero bytes and SHM was absent. Multiple Gateway descriptors referenced deleted WAL generations; another referenced openclaw-agent.sqlite-shm (deleted), and the Gateway retained a POSIX read lock on the deleted SHM inode. The descriptor and directory-visible WAL had the same device but different inode identities.

At 2026-10-29 03:09:44 UTC, OpenClaw emitted sqlite_wal_sidecar_identity_mismatch and terminated the Gateway without SQLite cleanup. systemd started a new Gateway process, after which active-leases receipts and disk I/O errors recurred.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.8 (dc2523e)

### Operating system

Linux; exact distribution/version NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. Database filesystem: local ext4 on /dev/sda1.

### Install method

npm-managed installation

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
agent database clean-close receipt: active-leases
disk I/O error | ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
2026-10-29 03:09:44 UTC level=fatal subsystem=infra/sqlite-wal event=sqlite_wal_sidecar_identity_mismatch message="SQLite WAL sidecar identity mismatch; terminating without SQLite cleanup" databasePath=<agent-db>/openclaw-agent.sqlite sidecarPath=<agent-db>/openclaw-agent.sqlite-wal pid=1045319
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

At approximately 2026-10-29 02:52 UTC:

- Directory-visible WAL: zero bytes.
- Directory-visible SHM: absent.
- Multiple Gateway descriptors referenced deleted WAL generations.
- A Gateway descriptor referenced openclaw-agent.sqlite-shm (deleted).
- The Gateway retained a POSIX read lock on the deleted SHM inode.
- The descriptor and directory-visible WAL device matched, but their inode identities differed.

Sanitised journal excerpts, descriptor/lock captures, source excerpts and hashes, and stopped-state integrity/hash manifests are preserved and available on request.

### Impact and severity

Affected: One per-agent database and its email/heartbeat workloads on a single managed Gateway.
Severity: High; normal database writes failed and the Gateway self-terminated through its WAL containment mechanism.
Frequency: Recurred repeatedly during the incident on both 2026.10.7 and 2026.10.8.
Consequence: Agent email and heartbeat operations failed. systemd restarted the Gateway after self-termination, but the failure recurred. The Gateway is now deliberately stopped for containment.

### Additional information

Last known good version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

The broad failure sequence was observed on 2026.10.7 and 2026.10.8 (dc2523e), including after a clean stopped-state database reset. The database is on local ext4, not a network filesystem.

Review of the installed 2026.10.8 code found that closeCachedOpenClawAgentDatabase() calls database.db.close() before releaseOpenClawAgentDatabaseLease(). The lease-release path emits active-leases after removing its own lease when another lease remains; it is a post-close receipt, not a demonstrated cross-owner close guard.

No explicit unlink was found in the reviewed agent lifecycle or WAL modules. The exact producer remains unattributed. The WAL identity check is the containment mechanism, not the demonstrated producer.

After the final containment stop, private working-copy checks returned integrity_check: ok and foreign_key_violations: 0. Live hashes were unchanged by those checks. This establishes stopped-state integrity only, not runtime readiness.

OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.4 was reviewed offline but not installed. The reviewed release notes did not identify a matching SQLite close, WAL/SHM, or lease correction.

Related reports: #125744, #132363, #163453, and #164294.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect state without a crash). Beta release blocker: No.

## Summary

Reloading a browser tab silently discards unsaved edits made in a chat file preview. The editor retains these edits across file-tab navigation and blocks in-app update reloads, but an ordinary browser reload does not ask for confirmation.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an existing editable text file from a chat filename link or Files panel.
2. Choose **Edit file**, click in the editor, and type additional text. Confirm that **Save** is enabled.
3. Reload the browser tab without saving.
4. Reopen the file. The unsaved text is gone and the original saved contents are shown.

Switching to another file tab and returning before step 3 retains the pending text, providing a control for ordinary in-page navigation.

## Expected behavior

An ordinary browser reload or tab close should offer the platform's unsaved-work confirmation while file drafts exist, including drafts whose previews were closed. Canceling should leave the exact draft usable; Save or explicit Discard should remove protection once no draft remains. This preserves the existing memory-only draft contract and does not require automatic file writes or durable autosave.

## Actual behavior and evidence

A Chromium reproduction at a83fd5dcf456df68e0889a1e40bc10d3a1359b70 used the existing bundled Control UI E2E harness, the real editor and keyboard input, and `page.reload()`. Both focused cases observed no browser dialog after enabling Save; the four existing editor recovery cases passed. The new assertion failed with `expected undefined to be 'beforeunload'` at the reload boundary, rather than during editor setup.

A separate live browser observation at 71ae98c377fb9e4ab8e9d73eeb733af0ad4cda65 reproduced the same result: 978 bytes of pending text reverted to the saved 745-byte file after reload, with zero dialogs. The saved file remained unchanged. This is loss of unsaved input, not saved-file corruption.

The file-draft owner registers `registerControlUiReloadGuard`, which protects application-triggered reloads. It does not register a browser `beforeunload` listener. The queued session-change owner already uses both guards. Existing file-draft reload tests substitute a reload callback and therefore do not exercise browser unload.

## Environment

- OpenClaw source: a83fd5dcf456df68e0889a1e40bc10d3a1359b70.
- Browser: Chromium on Linux for the current-source reproduction; Chromium on macOS for the live observation.
- Launch: repository bundled Control UI E2E fixture with synthetic Gateway responses for the current-source reproduction.
- Model/provider: not involved in the browser-unload reproduction.

## Impact and limits

Users can lose a file-editing session through an ordinary browser reload without an opportunity to cancel. The current-source reproduction failed in both attempts. File contents already saved on disk were preserved. Closing a tab uses the same unguarded document lifetime, but the observed pre-fix loss described here was reproduced through reload. Forced browser termination and persistent draft recovery are outside this report.

### Bug type

Behavior bug in test coverage.

### Summary

The Node Gateway session-deletion suite fails in `sessions.delete returns unavailable when active run does not stop` before checking the timeout response and preserved storage.

### Steps to reproduce

Use source commit `34625635a1c04944ca68d2897f68fb24866e5552` with its frozen dependencies, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, and Vitest 5.0.5. Run the complete `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` file through the Node test-projects runner and its `test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts` owner. The observed Linux run used the existing eight-worker budget and no test-name filter.

The existing scenario creates a real captured controller operation whose cancellation returns false, starts deletion, and waits for the cancellation attempt before checking admission.

### Expected behavior

The test should observe that admission remains closed while deletion drains the captured operation, then reach its existing 15-second fake deadline, retryable `UNAVAILABLE` response, and storage-preservation checks. The [drain owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/34625635a1c04944ca68d2897f68fb24866e5552/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-lifecycle-drain.ts#L96) explicitly releases the short mutation before waiting and retains a separate admission closure.

### Actual behavior

The complete unchanged Node file reports **20 passed, one failed**. At line 709, `isSessionMutationActive(storePath, target.aliases)` returns false where the test expects true. The later response and storage assertions are not reached.

```text
sessions.delete returns unavailable when active run does not stop
AssertionError: expected false to be true
Tests: 1 failed | 20 passed (21)
```

### OpenClaw version

Source commit `34625635a1c04944ca68d2897f68fb24866e5552`.

### Operating system

Linux x64.

### Install method

Source checkout with frozen pnpm dependencies.

### Model and provider / routing chain

No model call. The fixture invokes the real Gateway deletion handler and session controller with synthetic session data.

### Impact and evidence limits

This failure blocks Node validation and prevents the scenario from checking its intended timeout and storage result. It establishes a test-observation defect; it does not establish data loss or a production drain defect. The same full file passed all 21 cases under pinned Bun in [the baseline hosted job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40800487319/job/123207281926), so that runtime remains a separate control.

issues.body:
## Summary

Code Mode drops actionable warnings from a running `exec` result even though the native tool result contains them. This was reproduced on `a83fd5dcf456df68e0889a1e40bc10d3a1359b70` with an ordinary guest running a bounded Python terminal countdown in the Docker sandbox.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the OpenClaw harness with Code Mode and an ordinary guest sandbox, with the existing `exec` and `process` tools available.
2. Ask the agent to build and run a 15-second Python terminal countdown with optional keyboard control, inspect progress while it runs, and collect its final summary. The observed call was `python3 -B countdown.py`, with `workdir: "/workspace"`, `pty: true`, `yieldMs: 1000`, and `timeoutSeconds: 25`.
3. Compare the native exec result with the value returned to the Code Mode program while the command is running.

## Expected behavior

The structured running value should retain the execution warning already supplied by the native tool, so the agent can use that guidance when choosing a supported continuation. The running status and process session identity should remain usable.

## Actual behavior

The native result says:

> Warning: PTY is unavailable in sandbox mode; running without a PTY. Use a noninteractive command.

It then reports the running command and process follow-up guidance. The actual Code Mode value contains `status: "running"`, `sessionId`, `pid`, timestamps, `cwd`, `tail`, and `followUp`, but no PTY warning. The command is not classified as an error.

The same process was subsequently collected through `process poll` and exited successfully after about 15 seconds. This report concerns missing guidance; it does not request sandbox PTY or writable-stdin support, or claim the omission was the sole cause of an agent decision.

## Version and environment

- OpenClaw source revision: `a83fd5dcf456df68e0889a1e40bc10d3a1359b70` (2026.10.8).
- macOS host, native Docker sandbox, OpenClaw harness and Code Mode.
- No new configuration option or permission is required to reproduce the projection difference.

## Evidence and cause

`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-run.ts` includes the collected warnings in the running result's text but omits them from `details`. `ToolSearchRuntime.callValue` and `callExactValue` project non-error results to those details, so the warning is lost at that boundary.

A focused native process/Code Mode regression also reproduces the omission on unchanged production code using an existing rejected-store-environment warning. It confirms the warning in the native result before checking the structured value: the warning case fails because the field is absent, while the warning-free continuation control and 15 existing error, refusal, and budget cases pass.

## Impact

Agents using Code Mode receive less execution guidance than direct callers for the same running operation. The omission can hide an explanation of why an interactive continuation is unavailable, while leaving the command and generic continuation options visible.

issues.body:
## What happens

An SVG attachment can render successfully in the conversation and its zoomable image viewer, but **Download image** fails with “Could not download this image. Try again.” No file is saved, and retrying the same attachment does not help.

This affects saving the original generated diagram. The bytes remain available: the generic attachment card can offer a working file download when the SVG preview falls back to that card.

## Reproduction

Reproduced through the current Control UI at `a83fd5dcf456df68e0889a1e40bc10d3a1359b70` in Chromium:

1. Receive a conversation attachment with a valid SVG file, its original filename, and `image/svg+xml` MIME type.
2. Wait for its inline image preview to load.
3. Open the image viewer and select **Download image**.

The SVG is visible in the viewer, but the download action produces the retry error and no browser download. A focused browser scenario exercises the actual conversation event, attachment renderer, image viewer, and download action with fixed external media responses; it fails at the missing-download assertion, after the image has loaded.

## Expected result and cause

An authorized attachment should have a supported action that saves its original bytes and filename. SVG downloads should remain file downloads without opening an active SVG document or changing the raster-image and top-level blob restrictions.

The successful SVG preview hands its retained SVG blob to the lightbox. `downloadLightboxImage` then rejects that blob because `image/svg+xml` is outside the shared raster MIME vocabulary. The fallback file card uses a different download path. This explains the permanent failure; it does not establish why a particular restored history item falls back to a card.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On PostgreSQL families a successful `openclaw update --channel dev` with no Gateway running warns that the original-state capture is unavailable, refuses automatic restoration because "databases changed after snapshot capture; the writer is unknown", and leaves a capture with no sealed manifest, while the identical update on SQLite (same build, same steps, same machine) seals its manifest and reports the recovery set as stale because the update succeeded.

### Steps to reproduce

Same-build A/B, both runs 2026-10-28 on one machine, no Gateway, isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, fresh install each time:

1. Git `dev` checkout of `main` at `71d954df1533`, built; `origin` points at a local bare mirror whose `main` is `71d954df1533` + one commit (`58d2d164606c`, the #187113 patch) so the updater has a candidate.
2. **PostgreSQL run:** config `database.families.{state,agent,workboard}.engine = "postgres"`, `database.postgres.connection` env SecretRef to a disposable PostgreSQL 17.11 on 127.0.0.1 (`unaccent` installed). `onboard --non-interactive …`, `agents add probe`, `config set gateway.port 18996`, `doctor --fix`.
3. **SQLite run:** identical, with no `database` section.
4. In each: `openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev`, then `openclaw update status`.

### Expected behavior

Both runs behave like the SQLite run: no "Original state capture is unavailable" warning when nothing else is writing, the capture ends with a sealed manifest, `update status` reports `Update recovery set …: stale: its update already succeeded`, and automatic restoration stays available (or the refusal names a real writer).

### Actual behavior

| | SQLite (`71d954df` → `58d2d164`) | PostgreSQL (`71d954df` → `58d2d164`) |
|---|---|---|
| start of `validating` | — | `Warning: Original state capture is unavailable; the update continues without it. A running Gateway or another active writer changing state during capture is expected to cause this. …` (no Gateway or other writer existed) |
| result | `✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.8 (58d2d164) … 2 warnings` | `✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.8 (58d2d164) … 7 warnings` |
| restoration | `Warning: Automatic database restoration unavailable: update ledger database generation could not be observed. Snapshots retained …` | `Warning: Automatic database restoration unavailable: databases changed after snapshot capture; the writer is unknown. Snapshots retained …` |
| Doctor interval | `Doctor interval openclaw doctor; backup …; from SHA-256 1a6091ce… to …` | `Doctor interval post-plugin doctor; backup …; from SHA-256 a5cde27e… to SHA-256 c0d8a4eb…` (from ≠ to) |
| `update status` | `Update recovery set <capture>/manifest.json: stale: its update already succeeded.` | `previous Gateway shutdown unavailable: no such table: gateway_boot_lifecycle` then `Update capture: incomplete` / `Update capture at <capture> is incomplete: no sealed manifest is available. Retained files are unverified evidence for manual inspection.` |

Both updates activated correctly (checkout and `dist/build-info.json` at `58d2d164606c`, agents `main`/`probe` and `gateway.port` preserved, read-only `doctor` runs). The SQLite run's "update ledger database generation could not be observed" is itself a restoration refusal and may deserve its own look, but the PostgreSQL run is strictly worse: no sealed manifest and a "writer is unknown" verdict with nothing else running.

Code pointers on `bd10ba29d338` (untested hypotheses, from reading only): the "writer is unknown" refusal comes from `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-database-receipts.ts:118` when the Doctor receipt's `from` generations differ from the capture's; the capture-unavailable warning is the generic catch in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-initialization-run.ts:251`, which drops the nested cause; the incomplete-capture message is `src/infra/update-recovery-backup-status.ts:135`; `gateway_boot_lifecycle` is only queried through SQLite in `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-webhook-pins.ts:145`, so the PostgreSQL state family's SQLite anchor is probably being read as if it were the state database.

### OpenClaw version

main `71d954df1533` → `58d2d164606c` (2026.10.8), both runs on the same build

### Operating system

macOS (Darwin 27.2.0), Apple silicon Mac mini

### Install method

Git checkout of `main` (`dev` channel), Node 24 from Homebrew, isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1 OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external CI=1`

### Model

N/A (not model related)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

Synthetic Anthropic API key from `onboard --non-interactive`; plugins allowlist `["anthropic"]`; no channels.

### Logs

PostgreSQL run (redacted):

```text
17:57:56 openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev
Warning: Original state capture is unavailable; the update continues without it. A running Gateway or another active writer changing state during capture is expected to cause this. Database rollback uses the pre-migration snapshots taken after the Gateway stops. …
Phase: requested / staging / validating … Phase: activating … Doctor: maintenance begin … Doctor: maintenance release … Phase: finished
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.8 (58d2d164) (from 2026.10.8 (71d954df)); 7 warnings need attention.
Warning: Automatic database restoration unavailable: databases changed after snapshot capture; the writer is unknown. Snapshots retained at [path]/.artifacts/dist-runtime.openclaw-update-….tmp.databases.
Doctor interval post-plugin doctor; backup [path]/…tmp.databases; from SHA-256 a5cde27eb67ac03cc1e12029099b28804e7598dd15a1fe90b2a3231545a82b33 to SHA-256 c0d8a4ebf41c8abc5e499ab02770795d2e56a8549b0d870906aa4610de3a438e.
Post-migration write inventory: 5 databases; SHA-256 c0d8a4eb…
18:05:47 openclaw update status
previous Gateway shutdown unavailable: no such table: gateway_boot_lifecycle
Update capture: incomplete
Update capture at [home]/.openclaw.update-captures/f7dda8b4-… is incomplete: no sealed manifest is available. Retained files are unverified evidence for manual inspection.
```

SQLite run (redacted):

```text
18:25:47 openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev
Phase: requested / staging / validating … Phase: activating … Doctor: maintenance finish / release … Phase: finished
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.8 (58d2d164) (from 2026.10.8 (71d954df)); 2 warnings need attention.
Warning: Automatic database restoration unavailable: update ledger database generation could not be observed. Snapshots retained at [path]/.artifacts/dist-runtime.openclaw-update-….tmp.databases.
Doctor interval openclaw doctor; backup [path]/…tmp.databases; from SHA-256 1a6091ce7cb109031ff9c8a298a89b03f39e721ebab0a10f64e1b0f6f65095aa to …
18:32:58 openclaw update status
Update recovery set [home]/.openclaw.update-captures/271f4c7f-…/manifest.json: stale: its update already succeeded. …
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Full redacted logs and both update reports are available on request.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: installations with PostgreSQL families (state/agent/workboard) updating through `openclaw update`.
- Severity: annoying to data-risk-adjacent — the update succeeds, but rollback is declared unavailable for a reason that is false (no other writer), and every PostgreSQL update leaves an "incomplete" capture that `update status` flags for manual inspection.
- Frequency: both PostgreSQL updates observed today (this isolated run and the production 13-store installation's earlier runs) showed the capture-unavailable warning; the SQLite run did not.
- Consequence: operators cannot trust the updater's rollback story on PostgreSQL and accumulate captures that never seal.

### Additional information

Found while producing the proof for #187113; unrelated to that patch (the same warnings appear with and without it). Related: #186961 / #187006 (`database-engine-preflight` on PostgreSQL anchors), #187151 (preflight refusal hides its cause).

## Use case

A shared Slack builder can start an authorized coding task and receive private child completion, but cannot persist a later CI/review checkpoint for the same conversation. The requester is an admitted Slack user, not a Gateway owner. We need this to survive Gateway restarts without granting workspace users control-plane administration.

## Observed on 2026.10.8

- Native Slack request; configured agent permits `automations` (`cron` alias).
- Requester is not a configured Gateway owner.
- Native tool discovery omits `automations`; a real Slack probe could not create a one-minute same-thread reminder.
- `src/security/dangerous-tools.ts` includes `automations` in `GATEWAY_CONTROL_PLANE_TOOLS`, then `GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS`.
- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` applies that owner-only deny to the admitted non-owner turn. An ordinary allowlist does not override it.
- The automation tool and creator-authority code otherwise describe requester-scoped new-job creation. It is unclear which non-owner channel surface can reach that functionality.

Reproduction: admit a non-owner human to a Slack channel and an agent whose tool policy allows `automations`; ask it to schedule one reply in that thread after one minute. Inspect the actual tool catalog and accepted job, rather than accepting the model's promise. In our test, no automation tool or job was available.

The same ingress restriction remains in upstream `main` at `a8fe857038f62b209d7ef0b81e62b4a49fdfdbee`: `resolveGatewayScheduledToolAccess` exempts a verified scheduled occurrence's self-job tool, while ingress turns retain the owner-only rule. The newer `tools.gatewayPolicy.automations.scope: "caller"` restricts administrative grants; it does not itself expose this tool to non-owner ingress.

## Requested native capability

An explicitly enabled, caller-scoped schedule/checkpoint for an admitted conversation, with the runtime binding the creator, agent, account and original session. It should retain the caller's effective tool restrictions, permit cancellation/inspection only within that scope, and resume the original conversation for reconciliation and delivery.

This does not require command jobs, arbitrary destinations, cross-session wakes, global job administration, or making ordinary Slack users Gateway owners. Those can retain their existing restrictions.

## Acceptance cases

1. An admitted non-owner creates one bounded same-thread checkpoint and receives an accepted job ID.
2. Another requester/session cannot inspect, change, cancel or redirect it.
3. Restart preserves the accepted checkpoint and its caller restrictions.
4. On execution the original conversation reconciles current state and replies once; intermediate/raw child output is not announced independently.
5. Expiry, cancellation and completion stop the obligation without duplicate effects.
6. Command payloads, broader tool grants and foreign delivery targets remain unavailable.

## Related work

[Issue #41586](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41586) was resolved by native child-completion delivery. That path works for us. This request concerns a later external-work checkpoint after the child is idle, rather than child completion.

We verified an operator-installed one-shot command calling native `wake` with delivery disabled as an operator maintenance procedure. It survives restart and returns to the parent conversation, but does not solve requester scheduling. We have not patched core, added a privileged CLI wrapper, or broadened channel users into owners.

Is a supported requester-scoped ingress path intended already, or should this be tracked as a separate native capability?

issues.body:
## Summary

Signal normal reply turns wire only the shared typing `start` callback even though the Signal provider API and heartbeat sibling support an explicit terminal stop. Every completed, cancelled, failed, silent, or shutdown-cleaned reply therefore leaves provider typing active until Signal's own expiry.

Verified on current `main` at `5b67b61964b91357e981aa56e4848a037c451929`.

## Deterministic proof

Using the exact start-only callback shape wired by Signal:

```json
{
  "providerCalls": [{ "operation": "sendTyping", "stop": false }],
  "terminalStopCount": 0
}
```

After a successful start and terminal `onCleanup`, no stop call exists because the adapter supplied no `stop` closure.

## Root cause

- `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts` creates the shared reply pipeline with `typing.start`, calling `sendTypingSignal` for the inbound target/account, but omits `typing.stop`.
- `src/channels/typing.ts` correctly cannot perform provider cleanup when no stop callback exists.
- `extensions/signal/src/send.ts` already supports `{ stop: true }` and maps it to provider stop semantics.
- `extensions/signal/src/channel.ts` heartbeat wiring correctly provides both `sendTyping` and `clearTyping` with the same target/account and `stop: true`.

Existing turn coverage asserts only the start call and misses terminal cleanup.

## Impact

Signal users continue seeing OpenClaw typing after the turn has terminated, including NO_REPLY, cancellation, delivery failure, and shutdown cleanup paths. Target/account isolation is preserved.

## Repair direction

Add `stop` beside `start` in the Signal turn config, calling `sendTypingSignal` with the same target, config, base URL, account, and account ID plus `stop: true`. Preserve no-op behavior when the target is absent and add stop-error logging.

This adapter repair should compose with the shared late-start ordering fix in #127564; adding stop alone must not create a stale late start after terminal stop.

## Regression coverage

Cover success, cancellation, delivery failure, NO_REPLY/cleanup, identical account/target on start and stop, absent target, stop-error reporting, and dedupe across idle plus cleanup.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let `openclaw skills install` install a skill that lives in a **subdirectory** of a `git:` source — today the clone root is installed wholesale and `SKILL.md` must sit at the repo root.

### Problem to solve

- `git:<url>[@ref]` clones the repo and installs the **clone root** as the skill: the `#`/`@` fragment is parsed as a git ref only (`splitGitSpecRef` in `src/plugins/git-install.ts`, shared with plugin installs), the whole repo minus `.git` is copied, and the install fails unless `SKILL.md` is at the root (`hasSkillArchiveRoot` is a root-only check).
- Docs pin the behavior: "Git and local directory installs expect `SKILL.md` at the source root" (`docs/cli/skills.md`).
- This rules out the monorepo layout where a skill lives **next to the code it operates on**:

```
acme/toolkit/
├── cli/            # the commands the skill drives
├── evaluation/
└── skill/
    └── SKILL.md
```

- Colocation is the point: one PR changes command and skill together, so they can't drift between merges. Today the only options are moving `SKILL.md` to the repo root (one skill per repo, root pollution) or hand-cloning and installing from a local path (drops the git ref/provenance trail). Symlink workarounds like #49408 suggest real demand.
- Runtime skill loading already accepts grouping subfolders under a skills root (`skill-root-discovery.ts`), and archive installs relocate to a packed root — the gap is install-time only.

### Proposed solution

A documented way to point `skills install` at a subdirectory of a git source — any spelling that fits the spec grammar, e.g. `git:<url>#<ref>:<path>`, `git:<url>@<ref>#<path>`, or a `--subdir <path>` flag. Post-clone, relocate to the subdirectory before the root check (the primitive archive installs already use). Keep recording the resolved commit in `.openclaw/source-origin.json` — that's what makes installed content version-observable.

### Alternatives considered

- Hand-clone + `install <local-path>`: works today but loses ref/provenance and isn't declarable where a git source is expected.
- Moving `SKILL.md` to the repo root: one skill per repo, pollutes tool-repo roots.
- A plugin: install-source parsing is shared core surface (`parseGitPluginSpec`) with no hook a plugin could extend — this can only be core.

### Impact

- Affected: users installing skills from monorepos where the skill documents the repo's own commands (self-hosted tooling, eval harnesses, internal CLIs).
- Severity: blocks that layout entirely for git installs.
- Frequency: every install/refresh of such a skill.
- Consequence: permanent hand-clone/local-path detours with no version trail.

### Evidence/examples

Verified on current `main` (bec7b26) and tag v2026.9.2: `src/plugins/git-install.ts` `splitGitSpecRef` (`#`/`@` = ref separators only); `src/skills/lifecycle/source-install.ts` `installGitSkill` hands the whole export dir to `installLocalSkillDir`; `src/skills/lifecycle/archive-install.ts` `hasSkillArchiveRoot` checks the root only. Related: #49408 (symlink workaround), `docs/tools/creating-skills.md` (runtime subfolder grouping).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

None.

issues.body:
### Summary
An ACP-targeted message can be executed again by the ordinary agent runtime after its `reply_dispatch` hook times out or throws. The hook may already have performed work before it loses the claim, so the fallback can duplicate side effects and unexpectedly change runtimes.

### Reproduction
Reproduced at main commit `59773963d18023b26b6a66225f84a7d12fb2d57a` using Node 24.18.0 on macOS.

1. Dispatch a message to an ACP session through `dispatchReplyFromConfig`.
2. Register an ACP-eligible `reply_dispatch` hook with the real plugin hook runner. Have it perform an observable side effect, then either wait past its hook timeout or throw.
3. Provide an ordinary `replyResolver` spy.

Both cases call the side effect once, then unexpectedly call the ordinary resolver once. A regression assertion that the ordinary resolver is never called fails in both cases on that commit. This reproduction uses isolated test fixtures; it makes no model or channel requests.

### Expected behavior
Keep ownership with the selected ACP runtime. Report that the turn did not complete without automatically replaying the prompt through another runtime. Ordinary control commands should continue to work.

### Actual behavior
The claiming hook runner logs the timeout/error and returns an unhandled result. Dispatch then continues into the ordinary reply resolver as though no runtime had started the turn.

### Impact
A slow or failing ACP hook can cause duplicate execution and an unexpected runtime switch. The fallback does not establish whether the original work already completed or caused side effects.

### Proposed scope
A focused dispatcher guard using existing routing, delivery, cancellation and lifecycle paths, with public-dispatcher regression tests. No timeout increase, provider-specific retry logic or configuration migration.

issues.body:
## Problem

`openclaw connect <join-url>` keeps its join HTTP request alive after the CLI accepts Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. The private join-payload preflight does not observe the existing invocation signal; it continues until an unrelated request deadline and can later produce an ordinary error or proceed with a late result.

On main `e25c026eb75d34ecdeed1d64d68454fb919f3c19`, the real normally built CLI reaches a documented loopback `/j/<shortcode>` endpoint. With withheld headers, both signals produce the root cleanup notice but the child remains alive at2.5seconds, with one GET and zero natural closes. An incomplete200JSON body reproduces the same SIGINT result. A completed404 response is the legal control: natural exit1, one finished response close and the existing expired-join diagnostic. Independent on-disk HTTP recorder readback matches the captured observations.

## Expected behavior and scope

The existing invocation signal should cancel the private guarded join fetch and bounded body read. Accepted cancellation must retain root signal exit130/143, with no late join-result handoff or ordinary error output. Non-canceled HTTP errors, validation, redirect/TLS/hostname rules, headers, payload/byte limits, finally-release and normal join handling retain their existing behavior.

This is one bounded repair in `src/cli/connect-cli.ts` shared by all join-URL forms. It changes no option, configuration, protocol, permission, one-time redemption policy, target-file behavior, node runtime or service implementation. Cancellation after downstream node/service work has already begun is outside this HTTP-preflight fix.

## Implementation and acceptance

I plan to implement this repair as Alix-007. The same external loopback recorder and real executable will establish base RED and committed-head GREEN for SIGINT, SIGTERM, a partial body, and the completed404 control. Focused owner tests will retain normal valid-payload/direct-code/service expectations and cover cancellation and late preflight results. No real Gateway, pairing token, user channel or service installation is used in the public proof.

issues.body:
## Environment

OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (npm global install), Control UI webchat, multi-session install.

## Observed

When a turn fails to finish, the chat shows an error banner: "Couldn't finish this reply. Check the conversation before trying again.", with a Details disclosure, a copy icon, and a **Refresh** button. Per the reporter, the Refresh button does nothing: clicking it produces no visible action, no state change, and no recovery of the failed turn. It is the only recovery affordance on the banner, so a dead button leaves manual recovery only (reload the page, retry by hand). Screenshot available on request. Observed 2026-10-29, and the same dead button was observed on the previous version (2026.10.7) as well, so this is not a 2026.10.8 regression.

## Isolation

- The generic failure copy is a shared surface: #157939 documents one cause (a `database is locked` error on the reply path) dropping whole turns behind this same copy with no retry, and #182297 documents a false variant of the notice. None of those reports covers the banner's own controls.
- Control UI refresh affordances have their own UX threads (#150885 focus loss on refresh, #150266, #152091, #150351, #186758), but none concerns the reply-failure banner's Refresh button.
- Duplicate sweep 2026-10-29 (four phrasings) found no report of a dead Refresh button on this banner.

## Expected

The Refresh button does what it says: re-checks the conversation state and either completes or refreshes the failed reply presentation, or reports why it cannot. If a failure class is unrecoverable, the banner should show the correct affordance for that class (or a retry), not an inert button.

## Suggested fix

Wire the banner's Refresh to the conversation re-check it implies (or a retry of the failed turn), and render per-class affordances where recovery is impossible, instead of a control that silently does nothing.

## Related

#157939 (generic failure copy family, one documented cause), #182297 (false variant of the notice), #150885 (refresh focus behavior in Control UI), #163042 (the adjacent reply-visibility family).

issues.body:
### Summary

Add an option to deliver the audio transcript echo (`tools.media.audio.echoTranscript`) silently, without a push notification.

### Problem to solve

With `echoTranscript: true`, every voice note triggers two notifications on Telegram: one for the `📝 "…"` transcript echo and one for the agent's real reply a few seconds later. The echo is only a confirmation of what was heard, so the extra ping is noise, especially for people who send many voice notes. Today the only way to avoid it is to turn the echo off entirely.

### Proposed solution

New boolean `tools.media.audio.echoSilent` (default `false`). When enabled, `sendTranscriptEcho` (`src/media-understanding/echo-transcript.ts`) passes `silent: true` to the durable outbound send. The plumbing already exists end to end: `silent` is part of the outbound delivery params, is persisted by the delivery queue, and the Telegram adapter maps it to `disable_notification` (the same path `channels.telegram.silentErrorReplies` uses). Channels without silent delivery keep sending the echo as before.

### Alternatives considered

- A per-channel option such as `channels.telegram.silentTranscriptEcho`: the echo is owned by media understanding and goes through the generic `silent` delivery flag, so one setting next to `echoTranscript`/`echoFormat` is simpler and works for every channel that supports silent sends.
- Disabling the echo: loses the "what was heard" confirmation.

### Impact

Affected: users with `echoTranscript` enabled on Telegram (and other channels supporting silent sends).
Severity: annoying.
Frequency: every voice note.
Consequence: double notifications per voice message.

### Evidence/examples

Telegram Bot API `sendMessage` supports `disable_notification` ("Sends the message silently. Users will receive a notification with no sound."). OpenClaw already uses it for `silentErrorReplies` and the message tool's `silent` parameter.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

issues.body:
### What happened

During a genuine upstream provider outage (primary model accepting requests then stalling), the model fallback chain walked through **every** configured candidate and marked each one failed, even though the failure was a session/run-state error rather than a provider error. The turn died, and the operator-facing error copy named the **last fallback model tried** as the failing model — so an outage plus a run-displacement bug was surfaced as "model X is broken".

The chain never self-healed. It only recovered after the operator manually switched the primary model and restarted the Gateway.

This is a different angle from #148707 (reply loss itself): here the concern is the **behaviour and diagnosis of the fallback chain** under that condition. Full log evidence for the displacement itself was posted there: #148707 (comment).

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), npm global install, Node v24.20.0, Debian 13 x64
- Channel: Telegram, session `agent:main:main`
- Heartbeat every 45m (`isolatedSession: true`), plus inbound `sessions_send` from subagent workers and interactive operator turns
- Primary `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, 6 configured fallbacks

### Evidence

Provider timeout on the first candidate, then every subsequent candidate failing within ~30-50 ms with a harness error:

```
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed requested=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash candidate=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash reason=timeout next=google/gemini-3.8-flash detail=LLM request timed out.
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=google/gemini-3.8-flash reason=unknown next=openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free reason=unknown next=openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash reason=unknown next=openrouter/tencent/hy4-preview detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=openrouter/tencent/hy4-preview reason=unknown next=deepinfra/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=deepinfra/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct reason=unknown next=deepinfra/Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
21:01:34 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed candidate=deepinfra/Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct reason=unknown next=openai/gpt-5.6-terra detail=Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
```

Embedded-run durations for those candidates were 44ms, 34ms, 39ms, 35ms, 31ms, 33ms — no model was actually consulted for any of them.

The operator-visible error, emitted while a fallback was on screen:

```
21:13:16 [telegram] embedded run agent end: runId=... isError=true model=gemini-3.8-flash provider=google error=Agent run failed (model: google/gemini-3.8-flash). rawError=Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn: 6f65b538-...
21:13:16 [model-fallback/decision] candidate_succeeded candidate=google/gemini-3.8-flash next=openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free
```

Note the `candidate_succeeded` marker recorded immediately after an `isError=true` run end.

A `config.patch` hot reload landed mid-incident; the next failure carried a different detail (flagged as a possible additional trigger, not a claim of causation):

```
21:46:35 [gateway] config.patch write actor=openclaw-control-ui ... changedPaths=models.providers.deepseek.models,models.providers.google.models,agents.defaults.model.primary,agents.defaults.model.fallbacks
21:46:36 [reload] config hot reload applied (agents.defaults.model.primary, agents.defaults.model.fallbacks)
21:50:20 candidate_failed candidate=google/gemini-3.8-flash reason=unknown detail=prepared model catalog owner config was replaced during the read (/home/radek/.openclaw/agents/main/agent)
```

### Expected

- A harness/run-state failure should be classified as such, and should not be reported as a per-candidate provider failure.
- The chain should not walk every remaining candidate when the failure is demonstrably not model-specific.
- Operator-facing failure copy should name the underlying condition, not the last fallback model that happened to be current (cf. #134103).
- Ideally: either queue/serialize concurrent turn sources on one session key, or re-admit the displaced turn once, rather than dropping it and giving up.

### Impact

Total loss of availability for ~50 minutes despite seven healthy, separately verified models. The misleading error copy ("Agent run failed (model: google/gemini-3.8-flash)") sent the operator down the wrong diagnostic path — the operator reasonably concluded the first fallback was broken and hand-switched models, which is what actually masked the real cause.

### Related

- #148707 — reply lost when a second run displaces an in-flight turn (same incident; full trace posted there)
- #144908 — "no active tool authority snapshot" recurs repeatedly
- #148053 — model fallback chain never consulted (reason=none); this report is the inverse failure mode
