issues.body:
# Summary
Allow an optional provider/model override specifically for Skill Workshop background experience reviews, preserving foreground-model inheritance by default and failing closed when an explicit target is unavailable.

## Problem to solve
I want to use cloud models for interactive conversations but run background procedure/skill learning on a self-hosted local model (currently DeepSeek). Workshop inherits the foreground provider/model/auth profile, so enabling background learning cannot currently guarantee that these additional review calls remain local. I have left autonomous learning off rather than change every conversation model. This is a privacy/data-processing and cost-control feature request, not a claim of a security bypass or model-training feature. It does not make an already-cloud foreground conversation local.

## Proposed solution
- Add an optional owner-configured background review provider/model selection under the Workshop configuration. Exact key/schema should follow maintainer guidance.
- Unset: preserve existing foreground selection and behavior.
- Explicit target: resolve that provider’s own configured credentials; never pass a foreground provider’s auth profile/credentials to a different provider.
- If the target is invalid, unavailable, unauthorized, or lacks required tool support, skip/fail the review with an actionable diagnostic. Never silently fall back to the foreground/cloud model. Preserve the existing disabled-fallback policy.
- Preserve review eligibility, bounded context/output/time, cancellation, tool restrictions, provenance validation, and auto/propose publication rules. No changes to foreground chat, Dreaming, memory extraction, or RAG.
- Document the privacy boundary and any prompt-cache/cost trade-offs of choosing a different model.

Suggested acceptance tests: unset inheritance; explicit local provider routing from a cloud foreground turn; cross-provider credential isolation; unavailable target yields no foreground/cloud request; cancellation and tool restrictions remain intact; behavior works with both auto and propose where supported.

## Alternatives considered
- Switch all foreground chats to the local model: changes unrelated interactive behavior and does not fit mixed-model use.
- Disable autonomous learning: safe but prevents using the feature.
- Manual local learning sessions: useful workaround, not automatic background review.
- A broad cross-subsystem model convention: intentionally out of scope here.

## Impact
Affected: operators using mixed cloud/local providers who want local-only background learning.
Severity: blocks enabling this optional feature under that constraint, not an urgent runtime regression.
Frequency: whenever an eligible foreground conversation uses a different provider/model.
Consequence: leave learning disabled or accept an unwanted background processing destination. No measured cost/latency improvement is claimed.

## Evidence/examples
Installed version: OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (2f991cb), locally customized deployment. Also checked upstream main at 4843f39db21ba87dd10c69f9382c33e04118a233, so this request is not based solely on the local build.

- [Current self-learning contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4843f39db21ba87dd10c69f9382c33e04118a233/docs/tools/self-learning.md) explicitly inherits foreground provider/model/auth profile and disables model fallbacks.
- [Current strict configuration schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4843f39db21ba87dd10c69f9382c33e04118a233/src/config/zod-schema.root-shape.ts) exposes Workshop autonomous mode/channelNotices and maxSkillBytes, but no review-model override.
- Focused follow-up to #111943: the closing comment specifically asks for a request scoped to the subsystem still missing an override. This request excludes the earlier broad reasoning-effort/cross-subsystem proposal.
- Related draft #152243 routes semantic judgments through a selected provider, but describes fallback to the existing generative reviewer and focused authorship. It does not establish this local-only end-to-end review-model contract; please redirect here if that stack is the intended owner.

Reproduction/inspection: use a cloud foreground model, configure a separate local provider, and inspect supported Workshop configuration and review selection. There is no supported way to select the local model only for background reviews. This is source/config inspection; I did not enable reviews or generate cloud traffic to demonstrate the limitation.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?
Maybe, with maintainer guidance. Willing to follow with a focused implementation once the configuration and credential-selection contract is agreed.

issues.body:
### Summary

`openclaw doctor` reports `show_widget` as an unavailable allowlist entry on any install/surface that does not advertise the `inline-widgets` client capability, and because `show_widget` is a member of `group:openclaw`, the warning cannot be silenced by config without dropping that entire group. Request: a supported way to resolve this — either exclude capability-gated-only core tools from `group:openclaw`, or classify/suppress the warning the way gated core tools in built-in profiles already are (see #53702).

### Problem to solve

`show_widget` is a shipped core tool that is **conditionally available**: it declares `requiredClientCaps: ["inline-widgets"]` (`src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts`), so it is only registered/usable on surfaces whose client advertises that capability (Control UI, iOS, Android, macOS, Discord Activities, Linux Quick Chat). On a plain messaging surface such as Telegram it is unavailable.

It is nevertheless a static member of `group:openclaw`, because its catalog entry sets `includeInOpenClawGroup: true`:

```ts
// src/agents/tool-catalog.ts:344
{
  id: "show_widget",
  description: "Show an interactive widget on chat or an auto-fitting dashboard",
  sectionId: "ui",
  profiles: [],
  includeInOpenClawGroup: true,
},
```

Any operator whose allowlist references `group:openclaw` therefore gets, on every `doctor` run and gateway start, a warning that is structural and unavoidable on that surface:

```
[tools] tools.profile (messaging) allowlist contains unknown entries (show_widget). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.
[tools] agents.main.tools.allow allowlist contains unknown entries (show_widget). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.
```

This is unlike #146392 (where the message named a plugin that did not exist and was simply wrong): here the wording is *accurate* — the tool really is unavailable on this surface. The problem is that it is **noise with no resolution path**, and it is triggered by a group grant rather than by an explicit operator mistake:

- Removing `group:openclaw` silences it but drops ~51 unrelated core tools.
- Adding `show_widget` to `tools.deny` does not help (the warning is derived from allowlist analysis, not the deny list).
- `doctor --skip` / `--severity-min` do not help (`doctor --lint --all --json` returns `findings: []`; this line is advisory text, not a lint finding).
- No config key exists to alter group membership.

Note that `show_widget` is reachable via `group:openclaw`, `group:ui`, and the shipped `canvas` alias expansion (`SHIPPED_PLUGIN_POLICY_FAMILY_CORE_TOOLS = Map([["canvas", ["show_widget"]]])`), and `profiles: []` means no built-in profile grants it. So `group:openclaw` is the common path that drags it into an allowlist where it can never match on a messaging surface.

### Proposed solution

Two acceptable outcomes; maintainers should pick, since they have opposite tradeoffs:

1. **Exclude capability-gated-only tools from `group:openclaw`** (i.e. drop `includeInOpenClawGroup` from the `show_widget` catalog entry). This removes the warning at the source. Downside: operators who intentionally rely on `group:openclaw` and use a widget-capable surface (Control UI, Discord, iOS, Android, macOS) silently lose widget access, and must re-add `show_widget` literally (which then re-triggers the same warning on messaging-only surfaces). This is why we did **not** open a PR for the one-line change: it is a product decision, not a bug fix.

2. **Treat group-derived, capability-gated core tools as non-warnable** — extend the gating-aware suppression from #53702 so that an entry contributed by a shipped group, and unavailable solely because of a client-capability gate, is not reported as an operator misconfiguration in the doctor/CLI path. The runtime already suppresses this class of warning on the conversation path (`suppressUnavailableCoreToolWarning: true`); only the doctor/CLI path is affected.

We would prefer (2): it preserves the tool for capable surfaces while removing the unavoidable noise for messaging-only installs.

### Alternatives considered

- **`tools.deny: ["show_widget"]`** — does not silence it; the allowlist analysis that emits the warning ignores deny entries.
- **`doctor --skip <id>` / `--severity-min`** — no check id exists for this line (`findings: []`), so severity/skip filters do not apply.
- **Drop `group:openclaw` and re-state its members explicitly, minus `show_widget`** — works today, but it is a large manual rewrite of the allowlist purely to avoid a diagnostic, and it silently freezes the group membership (future additions to `group:openclaw` are lost).
- **Local patch of the `dist` bundle** — overwritten by the next update; not a real fix.

### Impact

- **Affected:** any operator with `group:openclaw` (or `canvas`) in an allowlist on a surface without `inline-widgets` — i.e. plain messaging channels (Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, ...) and CLI runs.
- **Severity:** low/cosmetic — nothing is broken; the tool simply does not exist on that surface.
- **Frequency:** always — every `doctor` run and gateway start, for as long as the group grant is present.
- **Consequence:** sustained warning noise in the same list that carries genuine plugin/config warnings, which trains operators to ignore the list. It also invites a harmful "fix": deleting a working group grant (or the widget tool) to make the message go away, silently losing widget access on surfaces where it works.

### Evidence/examples

Environment: OpenClaw `2026.9.6` (build `eb377ac`), npm global install, Ubuntu 24.04 / Linux 6.8, `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, Telegram direct channel.

Config shape (redacted): `agents.entries.main.tools.alsoAllow` includes `group:openclaw` and `canvas`; `tools.profile: messaging`.

Relevant source on `origin/main`:

- `src/agents/tool-catalog.ts:344` — `show_widget` catalog entry with `includeInOpenClawGroup: true`; `group:openclaw` is built by filtering `CORE_TOOL_DEFINITIONS` on that flag (`buildCoreToolGroupMap`).
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` — `SHOW_WIDGET_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPS = ["inline-widgets"]`, applied as `requiredClientCaps` unless a current-channel presenter or pinned-only surface is present.

`doctor --lint --all --json` on the same host: `{"ok":true,"checksRun":133,"checksSkipped":0,"findings":[]}` — confirming this line is not a lint finding and cannot be filtered via `--skip`/`--severity-min`.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance — we can open the one-line `includeInOpenClawGroup` change if option (1) is preferred, or a suppression patch if option (2) is preferred.

### Additional information

Related prior work on this same warning surface, different root causes: #146392 (closed; `pdf` absent from the catalog), #53702 (merged; suppressed gated core tool warnings for built-in profiles), #46071 / #45269 / #42726 (closed; the `apply_patch` / `memory_*` instances). This case is distinct: the tool is in the catalog and correctly classified as unavailable, but it is gated by a *client capability* (per-surface), which the doctor/CLI path cannot satisfy, so the warning is permanently present for messaging-only installs.

issues.body:
### Summary

`memory-lancedb` should register a memory search `runtime`, so the Control UI Memory page works when it owns `plugins.slots.memory`.

### Problem to solve

With the official `@openclaw/memory-lancedb` as the memory slot owner, the Control UI Memory page can't show or search anything. The plugin only registers `publicArtifacts`:

```js
// extensions/memory-lancedb/dist/index.js (2026.9.4 installed; 2026.9.6 from npm is identical)
api.registerMemoryCapability?.({ publicArtifacts: { async listArtifacts(params) { /* … */ } } });
```

Without a `runtime`, `ensureMemoryRuntime` returns `{ searchRuntimeRegistered: false }` and every host-side memory search call fails:

```
$ openclaw gateway call doctor.memory.status --params '{"agentId":"main"}'
{ "agentId": "main", "searchRuntimeRegistered": false,
  "embedding": { "ok": false, "error": "memory plugin unavailable" } }

$ openclaw gateway call memory.search --params '{"query":"test","agentId":"main"}'
Gateway call failed: memory plugin unavailable
```

Since #155117 the Overview shows a neutral "Host memory search is unavailable — memory-lancedb does not provide a host memory search runtime" hero instead of a failure. That is accurate, but the page is still empty and the Memories tab search still fails.

Meanwhile the memory system itself is healthy, so this is purely an operator-visibility gap:

- `openclaw ltm stats` / `ltm search`: LanceDB store OK, vector recall OK.
- `openclaw memory search "…" --agent main` and the agent's `memory_search` / `memory_get` return hits from the memory-core file index. memory-core's tool opens its manager through `getBuiltinMemorySearchManager` directly, not through the slot owner.
- `memory_recall` / `memory_store` / `memory_forget` and auto-recall work.

The agent can search its memory, but the operator can't see it from the UI. The only config-level "fix" is setting the slot back to `memory-core`, which drops the LanceDB tools and auto-recall and cuts off the stored memories. So users of the featured first-party memory plugin are left with a Memory page that never works.

### Proposed solution

Have `memory-lancedb` pass a `runtime` in `registerMemoryCapability`, like memory-core does (`createLazyMemoryRuntime`):

- `getMemorySearchManager(params)` returns a manager backed by the plugin's LanceDB store. It embeds the query with the configured embedding provider, runs the agent-scoped vector search it already uses for `memory_recall`, and maps rows to the result shape the Memories tab renders (text, score, source, id).
- `closeMemorySearchManager` / `closeAllMemorySearchManagers` release the table handles.
- Optional hooks (`authorizeSearchHits`, `classifyWorkspaceMemoryPaths`, `supportsWorkspaceMemoryReadSources`) can stay unset at first.

Plugin authors have already pointed out that a third-party slot owner which registers a `runtime` gets a working Overview and search (see #138366). The first-party plugin would then be the reference implementation of that seam.

### Alternatives considered

- **Fallback in core**: when the slot owner registers no runtime, `memory.search` and the Memories tab fall back to the builtin file-index manager, labelled as such. That mirrors what the agent's `memory_search` tool already does, and it would also help third-party slot owners without a runtime. But it would still show nothing of the LanceDB store itself, which is where `memory-lancedb` keeps its memories. It works as a complement, not a replacement.
- **Slot back to `memory-core`**: the UI works (file index only), but the LanceDB tools and auto-recall are lost. Not viable.

### Impact

- Affected: every install using `memory-lancedb` (featured in the plugin catalog) as the memory slot owner.
- Severity: annoying to workflow-blocking for operators. Nothing in the Memory page can be inspected, and the only way to audit memories is the CLI (`ltm list` / `ltm search`) or asking the agent.
- Frequency: always, by design of the current registration.
- Consequence: memories can't be reviewed from the UI, which makes it hard to spot bad or stale auto-captured entries.

### Evidence/examples

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Docker on Linux, `plugins.slots.memory = "memory-lancedb"`, Ollama embeddings; memory-core loaded as the dreaming sidecar. Startup log: `memory plugin not selected for the memory slot; skipping its indexing runtime and recall registration (consolidation lifecycle preserved) (plugin=memory-core)`.
- Discussed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/138366#issuecomment-5844801270. The issue author agreed it is a separate gap from the Dreams provider and preferred a `runtime` in `memory-lancedb` over a core fallback.
- Related: #153016 (same symptom with a third-party slot owner, closed by the neutral hero in #155117).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Should stay backward-compatible: `memory-core` as slot owner is unchanged, and the runtime only exists when `memory-lancedb` holds the slot.

issues.body:
Environment: OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac) shim as generated by the npm global install on Windows 11 x64; end-to-end failure originally observed 2026-09-08 on a 2026.8.x build; shim mechanism re-verified against the current install today.

Observed: multiline string arguments passed through the generated openclaw.cmd shim lose everything after the first line. The shim ends by re-invoking node with `%*` behind an `endLocal & goto #_undefined_# 2>NUL || ...` construction; the cmd batch parser cannot carry embedded newlines through that re-expansion, so a call like `openclaw.cmd ... --message "line1<newline>line2"` reaches openclaw.mjs as `--message "line1`. Demonstrated today with a batch file of identical construction: the child received only `ARGS=[--message "first line]`.

Consequence: any CLI flow that passes a multiline payload (for example --message into send/agent commands) silently truncates on Windows when invoked through the shim. The same call via `node openclaw.mjs` or the PowerShell shim carries the full text; that is our workaround. Secondary observation from the original incident: the shim surface also emitted CLIXML/XML-parse noise on the error stream under some invocation contexts (not re-chased).

Suggested fix: generate the Windows shim to route through PowerShell, or otherwise avoid cmd `%*` re-expansion for multiline arguments; alternatively document that multiline CLI payloads must go via node/openclaw.ps1 on Windows.

Related: #150974 (same generated shim, different failure: UTF-8 non-ASCII path on GBK consoles), #140631 (CLIXML noise in the PowerShell exec host).

issues.body:
Environment: OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Windows 11 x64, Node v26.8.2. Observed 2026-09-26; reproduced live the same day.

Observed: a workshop SKILL.md whose description frontmatter was a multi-line plain scalar (continuation lines starting at column 0) caused the skill to be skipped entirely: `openclaw skills info <name>` reported "not found", the curator inventory undercounted (67 loaded vs 68 SKILL.md files on disk), and no warning appeared on any user-facing surface we checked (skills list, skills info, skills check, curator status). Rewriting the description to a single line, same text, made the skill load immediately with no other change.

Steps to reproduce (verified on 2026.9.6):
1. Create a throwaway skill directory in a per-agent workshop skills directory containing a SKILL.md whose frontmatter is:

   ---
   name: repro-skip-test
   description: First line of a plain scalar description
   continued at column zero which breaks strict YAML parsing
   ---

2. Wait for the skill watcher to register the change.
3. `openclaw skills info repro-skip-test --agent <agentId>` returns "not found". No warning is printed anywhere.
4. A known-good control skill in the same directory loads fine, so discovery itself works; the failure is specific to the frontmatter shape.

Context: #108432 (fixed by #108926, landed 2026-07-16) established that genuinely malformed frontmatter should warn with the file path and parse error instead of silently hiding the skill. On 2026.9.6 this shape produced a fully silent skip on every surface available to a user, so either the fix does not cover this frontmatter shape/loading path, or the warning exists internally but is not surfaced.

Suggested fix: cover multi-line plain scalars (and any YAML syntax error) on all loading paths, and surface the promised file-path + parse-error warning on every surface that reports skill inventory, including skills info/check and the curator inventory count (which currently undercounts silently).

issues.body:
## Summary

Sixteen production call sites across eleven files throw or return the **byte-identical** string
`Session "<key>" changed while starting work. Retry.` No discriminator — no reason code, no call-site
tag, no cause field — reaches the log or the thrown error. When this fires in production, **which of
the sixteen branches ran is not knowable from the output.**

This is the diagnosability half of the family that #118873 / #117096 / #116694 / #121269 covered
behaviourally. Those are all closed and the stuck-session behaviour is fixed. The string is not.

## Verified against `main`

`587c7524e58`. `rg 'changed while starting work' src --type ts`, excluding tests and comments:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ts` | 573 |
| `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts` | 333 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-admission.ts` | 259 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` | 166 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-prepare.ts` | 185 |
| `src/sessions/session-diff-baseline.ts` | 41 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-entry-persistence.ts` | 98 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.ts` | 241, 284, 292 |
| `src/agents/agent-command-recovery-owner.ts` | 110, 132 |
| `src/agents/agent-command.ts` | 213, 220 |
| `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.ts` | 73 |
| `src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` | 57 (the shared helper) |

Three of these are in one function's three branches (`reply-turn-admission.ts:241/284/292`), so even
narrowing to a single file does not narrow to a single cause.

## Why it costs an operator a diagnosis

Production, `2026.8.1-beta.2`, one Discord channel session: **27 rejected runs across 4 inbound user
messages** between `09:58:05` and `10:24:09` (-03:00), each aborting in 4–8 ms with exactly this
string. Worst case, 9 attempts over 6 min 11 s before one user message ran. Every cluster started
within ~90 s of a gateway restart.

```text
[diagnostic] message processed: channel=discord outcome=error duration=4ms
  error="Error: Session \"agent:<redacted>\" changed while starting work. Retry."
```

The three plausible causes on that path — an `expectedSessionId` mismatch, a recovery-owner claim
returning `invalidated`, and the abort check — call for three different operator responses. The log
distinguishes none of them, so triage is guesswork or a source read per occurrence. Filing this
separately because a fix here is useful whether or not any specific admission bug is open: the next
one in this family will produce the same undiagnosable line.

## The seam already exists

`src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` already owns the discriminating helper:

- `resolveSessionWorkStartError()` already distinguishes *deleted* / *changed* / *still initializing*
  / *archived*, and
- `SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED_ERROR_CODE = "SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED"` (line 24) is already
  the shared code.

Roughly fourteen sites route through that helper. The sixteen above bypass it with a hardcoded
template literal, which is what makes them indistinguishable.

## Suggested shape

Not a behaviour change and not a message rewording — the retryable contract and the operator-facing
sentence can stay exactly as they are.

1. Give the helper a `reason` discriminator alongside the message (e.g.
   `session-id-mismatch` | `recovery-owner-invalidated` | `aborted` | `entry-deleted` |
   `initializing` | `archived`).
2. Route the sixteen hardcoded literals through the helper so the reason travels with the error.
3. Log the reason on the rejection path.

Happy to send the PR if the shape is agreeable — I would rather have the reason names settled by a
maintainer first than guess at the taxonomy.

## Version

`2026.8.1-beta.2` for the production data; source claims verified against `main` at `587c7524e58`.

> **Form note (edited 2026-10-08):** this is a feature request that was filed in bug shape. The sections below add what `feature_request.yml` asks for (alternatives, implementation intent) without changing the evidence above.

## Environment (form fields)

- Production data: `2026.8.1-beta.2`, npm global install, Linux (Debian in a Proxmox LXC).
- Model / provider routing chain of the 27 rejected runs: **unknown** — not recorded with the 2026-08 occurrences. The string is emitted before any model call, so the defect is model-independent.
- Steps to reproduce / actual: this is a diagnosability gap, verified by source inspection (table above) and confirmed by ClawSweeper on current `main`; no runtime repro on current `main` was run.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Status quo — read the source per occurrence.** What we do today; it costs a source read per incident and still cannot separate the three branches inside `reply-turn-admission.ts`.
2. **Reword the sixteen messages.** Rejected: it changes an operator-facing sentence and the retryable contract, and the next caller that copies the template literal is undiagnosable again.
3. **A stable public `reason` field on the shared error.** Possible, but it creates a compatibility obligation. ClawSweeper's recommendation — bounded **diagnostic-only** labels in operational logs, retry codes and public messages unchanged — is the shape we prefer.

## Implementation intent

We will open the PR once a maintainer settles the open question (diagnostic-only labels vs public field, and the label names). Not before: we would rather not pick the taxonomy unilaterally.

issues.body:
**Version:** 2026.9.6

**What happens.** When an isolated cron `agentTurn` job announces its reply, the `message_sending` hook runs from `deliver-prepare` (`runMessageSending(..., { channelId, accountId, conversationId, sessionKey? })`). The `sessionKey` it passes is `resolveCronDeliverySessionKey(job)` (`dist/session-target-*.mjs`): the job's `sessionTarget`/`sessionKey`, meaning the owner's human-facing session such as `agent:<id>:telegram:group:<chatId>:topic:<n>`, or nothing at all. It is never the cron run's own session (`agent:<id>:cron:<jobId>…`), and there is no `jobId` or `runId`.

**Why it matters.** A plugin can't tell a cron announce from a human-facing reply in the same topic. Our outbound "nothing new" gate is scoped to heartbeat and cron sessions by session key. Since 2026-09-14 it has judged 33 messages, all heartbeats and none from cron, although about 80 cron jobs announce into the same topics.

**Ask.** Add the cron identity to the `message_sending` (and `reply_payload_sending`) context for cron deliveries, e.g. `ctx.trigger = "cron"`, `ctx.jobId`, `ctx.runId`, and/or the run session key, while keeping `sessionKey` as the delivery session for compatibility.

**Repro.** Register a `message_sending` hook that logs `ctx`. Run `openclaw cron run <id>` for an isolated announce job whose reply isn't NO_REPLY. The logged `ctx.sessionKey` is the owner session or absent, and there is no job or run id.

**Related.** #90527 (closed, unmerged) tagged `ReplyPayload.origin = { kind: "cron", jobId }` but explicitly left the `message_sending` hook path out of scope. #107069 is the same provenance gap on the input side (`before_agent_run`).

issues.body:
### Summary

On a claude-cli (`liveSession: claude-stdio`) session, Claude Code auto-compacts the context on its own, but the session's `compactionCount` never advances. As a result `/status` shows a frozen, misleading `🧹 Compactions: N`.

### Evidence (OpenClaw 2026.9.6, Claude Code 2.1.282)

Session `agent:main:telegram:direct:<id>`, runtime Claude CLI, model `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`.

- `/status` → `🧹 Compactions: 51`. That value was accumulated earlier, while the session ran on embedded runtimes; it has not changed since the session moved to claude-cli.
- The Claude Code transcript of the same session (`~/.claude/projects/.../<id>.jsonl`) contains **17** genuine `{"type":"system","subtype":"compact_boundary"}` records in ~38h (counted by parsing records, not substring matches). All carry `compactMetadata.trigger: "auto"` (preTokens ~167–172k → postTokens ~3.5–11k); the last one is at `2026-09-25T21:13:39Z`.
- None of them are reflected in `compactionCount`.

### Root cause

- `extensions/anthropic/cli-backend.ts` declares `ownsNativeCompaction: true`. `compact_boundary` is only checked in `manualCompaction.validateOutput` (operator `/compact`) and in the cli-session-history import.
- `compactionCount` only advances via `incrementCompactionCount` from embedded compaction runs, manual `/compact`, and preflight compaction. The live claude-stdio runner has no path that turns an automatic boundary into a durable accounting fact.
- The status renderer reads `entry.compactionCount` directly.

### Related

- #138010 (open) restores *observation* of auto `compact_boundary` as a lifecycle event, but explicitly does not update session accounting.
- #137613 (open) notes the same frozen counter as a trap for re-arming CLI memory flush; the accounting decision is pending there.

### Expected

Either:

1. An auto `compact_boundary` (`trigger: "auto"`) on CLI-owned sessions increments `compactionCount` (building on #138010), or
2. `/status` labels the counter as OpenClaw-driven compactions only, or hides it / shows `n/a (managed by Claude CLI)` when the runtime owns native compaction.

Option 1 also unblocks the watermark problem described in #137613.

issues.body:
## Summary

Isolated automation (cron) runs are capped at a fixed **8 concurrent runs per gateway** (`DEFAULT_CRON_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS = 8`, `src/cron/service/run-admission-capacity.ts` `resolveRunConcurrency()` returns the constant), and the former knob `cron.maxConcurrentRuns` is now dead config (`src/config/dead-config-keys.test.ts`). #87174 was closed in May as "default 8 + documented supported knob"; the knob no longer exists.

## Version

OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (upstream main `359a8a35`), Linux x64, Node v24.21.0, 5 gateways on one host.

## Why 8 fixed does not fit a business workload

One gateway serves a whole company: ~20 recurring jobs (triage, hygiene, watchers, support checks) plus **work-loop jobs whose agent turn legitimately runs 1–2 h** (implementer + reviewer subagents, tests, deploy verification). We run 15 such queues (instance × kind of work).

- Every long work-loop run holds one of the 8 slots for its full duration. With 6 running, the remaining automations of *all* agents on the gateway compete for 2 slots; hourly jobs queue behind them.
- A trigger (`trigger.script`) evaluation also occupies a slot while it runs (measured: `runningAtMs` is set for the evaluation, ~2–3 s), so a 60 s gate on 16 jobs adds steady slot pressure.
- There is no per-agent or per-job concurrency class, so there is no way to say "work loops: at most N, never starve the watchers".

## Workaround we use (works, but it is orchestration we had to invent)

The trigger does not fire the cron run. It admits under a host lock and dispatches the work into an ordinary named session with its own code-mode tools: `sessions` patch (creates `agent:executor:lane:<queue>:<card>`, thinking) + `sessions_send` `mode: "followup"`, `timeoutSeconds: 0`. The turn runs in lane `nested:<key>`, outside the cron pool, and our gate enforces its own cap (8 work turns + 3 urgent). Side benefits: per-card persistent session (continuable later), subagent completions delivered reliably (vs. #44925). Costs: no per-run timeout on this route, a non-`NO_REPLY` final wakes a delivery turn in the trigger session, and admission/counting logic lives in our trigger script.

## Ask

1. Make run concurrency configurable again (global and ideally per agent/job class), or
2. document that long agent work should not run as cron runs and provide a first-class "dispatch a turn into a named session" action for triggers (with timeout and concurrency class), so this does not need custom admission code.

issues.body:
## Bug

`recoverStaleClaims` / `releaseClaimIfStillStale` in the durable channel ingress queue treat owner-loss recovery as a handler failure: every time a claim whose owner is gone (lease expired or process died) is released back to `pending`, the row's `attempts` is incremented and `last_attempt_at` overwritten, while `last_error` is never written.

The release contract explicitly says owner-loss must **not** consume retry budget (`release(..., { recordAttempt: false })` is used for all owner-lost paths in the drain: GatewayDrainingError, unadopted, superseded). `releaseClaimIfStillStale` is the only owner-lost path that violates this.

## Impact

- An event whose handler crashes or whose lease expires is re-dispatched each drain tick with `attempts` climbing toward the dead-letter limit (default 8), so a healthy event can be dead-lettered prematurely with no real handler failure behind it.
- The backoff computed from `attempts` is skewed, so the event may be retried far more aggressively (or far later) than the retry policy intends.
- The previous **real** handler failure (`last_error` / `last_attempt_at`) is erased by recovery, so the dead-letter diagnostic shows a misleading `lastError`.
- The row can churn: `claimed -> pending -> claimed` every recovery pass while the actual worker is still alive but its claim lease momentarily read as stale.

## Repro

Unit-level repro in `src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts` (included in the fix PR): enqueue an event, fail it once via `release({ lastError: "real failure", releasedAt: 20 })`, re-claim with a replacement worker, then `recoverStaleClaims({ staleMs: 5, now: 30 })`. Before the fix the row comes back with `attempts: 2` and `lastAttemptAt: 30` (budget consumed, real failure erased); after the fix it stays `attempts: 1` / `lastAttemptAt: 20` / `lastError: "real failure"`.

## Suggested fix

In `releaseClaimIfStillStale` stop incrementing `attempts` and stop writing `last_attempt_at` when returning an owner-lost claim to `pending`; keep the previous failure fields intact (same semantics as `release` with `recordAttempt: false`). Fix + regression test are in the PR that closes this issue.

issues.body:
## Summary

When grounded REM evidence is staged into the short-term store (`openclaw memory rem-backfill --path <path> --stage-short-term`), a single seed can carry text drawn from several source lines while its `path:startLine-endLine` citation names only the first of them. The resulting candidate, and anything promoted from it, points at a line that doesn't contain most of its text.

Two steps combine to cause it:

1. `coalesceGroundedRemItems` (dist `rem-evidence-*.mjs`, around line 347 in 2026.9.5; source `extensions/memory-core/src/rem-evidence.ts`) merges separately matched items under one key and unions their refs: `refs: uniqueStrings([...existing.refs, ...item.refs])`. The merged item's text covers every ref.
2. `collectGroundedShortTermSeedItems` (dist `cli.runtime-*.mjs` in 2026.9.5) derives the location from the first non-empty ref only (`signal.refs.find((ref) => ref.trim().length > 0)`), but sets `snippet: signal.text`, the full merged text.

So one ref is chosen by array order, and the others are dropped from the citation while their text is kept.

## Version

- Observed on `2026.9.5` (npm, macOS arm64, Node 24.18.0), and earlier on 2026.9.2.
- The ref-union merge is still on `main` as of 2026-09-24. I have not confirmed the seed-side first-ref selection on `main`, since the file layout changed. Please check whether it still takes only the first ref.

## Reproduction

1. In a workspace with dreaming enabled, create a daily note where the same idea appears on non-adjacent lines. For example, line 37 and line 89 both describe the same decision in different words.
2. Preview grounded evidence: `openclaw memory rem-harness --path memory --grounded --json`. In the grounded output (and in `DREAMS.md` after a real backfill), the merged item shows a bracketed ref list such as `[memory/2026-01-15.md:37, memory/2026-01-15.md:49, memory/2026-01-15.md:89]`.
3. Stage it: `openclaw memory rem-backfill --path memory --stage-short-term`.
4. Inspect the staged entry: `openclaw memory promote-explain <fragment-from-line-89> --json`.
5. Observed: `path` is `memory/2026-01-15.md`, `startLine`/`endLine` = `37`/`37`, but `snippet` contains text that only exists on line 89.

## Why it matters

Promotion writes the citation into `MEMORY.md` (`source=path:start-end`). A long-term memory whose citation points at a line that doesn't contain it can't be verified or corrected with a single lookup, which defeats the provenance guarantee. Merged items are also the highest-signal ones, since they merge because several sources agree, so they're the first to reach promotion.

## Suggested fix

Either:

- Emit one seed per ref, each with that ref's own text slice. Or,
- Keep the merge, but store all refs on the entry (for example `evidenceRefs: string[]`), set the range to the union only when the refs are contiguous, and have promotion render every ref.

At minimum, refuse to stage merged items whose refs span non-contiguous ranges until they can be cited correctly.

## Workaround

Single-ref grounded candidates only.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect Windows subprocess output decoding)

### Summary

On Windows hosts where `chcp` reports code page **866** (Russian OEM), OpenClaw 2026.9.5 still decodes `cmd.exe` output incorrectly despite the Windows console-codepage work merged in #72393.

The root cause is narrow: `resolveWindowsConsoleEncoding()` reads the active console code page correctly, but looks it up in `WINDOWS_CODEPAGE_ENCODING_MAP`, which does **not** contain 866. The adjacent `WINDOWS_OEM_CODEPAGE_ENCODING_MAP` already contains:

```ts
866: "cp866"
```

So on a CP866 console, `resolveWindowsConsoleEncoding()` returns `null`, and legacy bytes fall through to UTF-8 decoding.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: **2026.9.5** (`ec9c1a1`)
- OS: Windows 11 x64
- Node: **24.20.0**
- `chcp`: **866**
- Registry `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Nls\CodePage\OEMCP`: **866**

### Reproduction

A minimal decoder repro using CP866 bytes for the Russian word `Вход`:

- correct CP866 decode: `Вход`
- current fallback UTF-8 decode: `�室`

The same class of corruption appears in real `cmd.exe` directory output.

Before the local one-line patch, a regression harness against the shipped `resolveWindowsConsoleEncoding()` returned:

```text
RED expected cp866, got null
```

### Real behavior proof

Using the actual shipped `runCommandWithTimeout` export (the same subprocess/decoder seam used by `system.run`) to execute:

```text
cmd.exe /d /c "dir /b"
```

with a working directory containing Cyrillic filenames such as:

```text
1 Вход.png
2 О нас.png
4 Услуги - эксперсс-дизайн.png.png
6 Автор контент.png.png
8 Контакты контент.png.png
Услуги - сервисный уход-1.png.png
```

After adding only:

```ts
866: "cp866"
```

to `WINDOWS_CODEPAGE_ENCODING_MAP`, the live integration result is:

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "termination": "exit",
  "exactExpected": true,
  "replacementChar": false,
  "mojibakeSignal": false
}
```

and the exact Cyrillic filenames are preserved.

### Root cause

Current source in `src/infra/windows-encoding.ts`:

```ts
cachedWindowsConsoleEncoding =
  codePage !== null ? WINDOWS_CODEPAGE_ENCODING_MAP[codePage] ?? null : null;
```

`WINDOWS_CODEPAGE_ENCODING_MAP` includes UTF-8, GBK, Big5, Shift-JIS, EUC-KR and Windows-125x mappings, but not OEM 866.

The separate OEM map already knows `866 -> cp866`, so this is a lookup-table coverage gap rather than a missing decoder implementation.

### Suggested minimal fix

1. Add `866: "cp866"` to `WINDOWS_CODEPAGE_ENCODING_MAP`.
2. Add regression coverage proving a mocked/localized `chcp 866` resolves to `cp866`.
3. Keep an integration-style test proving CP866 `cmd.exe` output containing Cyrillic survives through the command-output decoder.

### Related

- #113219 — Windows exec/read mojibake on non-UTF-8 code pages
- #72393 — merged Windows console-codepage-aware command output decoder

The existing fix direction is correct; CP866 is simply not covered by the console lookup table.

issues.body:
## Problem

When users send messages, there is currently no way to automatically send a brief text acknowledgment (e.g., "On it, looking into this...") before the agent starts processing. This leaves users uncertain about whether their message was received and is being worked on.

## What we tried

We attempted multiple approaches to solve this:

1. **Documentation-based**: Added responsiveness instructions to `SOUL.md` - agent did not consistently follow them
2. **Moved to `AGENTS.md`**: Placed instructions at the very top of `AGENTS.md` (loaded every session) - still failed on the next message
3. **Auto emoji reaction**: Enabled `messages.ackReaction` with 👀 and `ackReactionScope: "all"` - this works great for visual acknowledgment
4. **Behavioral commitment**: Agent committed to "always send intent message first" - unreliable since it depends on agent discipline

The agent itself was unable to create a reliable solution because there is no hook or configuration option to inject a text message before processing begins.

## Proposed solution

Add configuration options similar to `ackReaction` but for text messages:

```json
{
  "messages": {
    "ackReaction": "👀",
    "ackReactionScope": "all",
    "ackText": "Looking into this...",
    "ackTextScope": "all"
  }
}
```

Or with more customization:

```json
{
  "messages": {
    "ackText": {
      "enabled": true,
      "text": "On it, processing your request...",
      "scope": "all",
      "delay": false
    }
  }
}
```

### Scope options (matching ackReactionScope)
- `group-mentions` - only in groups when mentioned
- `group-all` - all group messages
- `direct` - only DMs
- `all` - everywhere

## Why this matters

For users interacting with agents via messaging (WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram, etc.), there is often a delay while the agent:
- Reads context files
- Makes tool calls (web search, file reads, etc.)
- Processes complex requests

During this time (sometimes 20-60+ seconds), the user has no indication that work is happening. The emoji reaction helps, but a brief text message provides better UX:
- Confirms the message was understood
- Sets expectations that work is in progress
- Reduces "did it get my message?" anxiety

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.2.1
- Channels: Slack, WhatsApp, webchat

Thank you for considering this feature!

### Bug type
Behavior bug

### Summary
When OpenClaw attaches Playwright to an attach-only CDP browser, later native Chrome downloads can be redirected to Playwright's temporary artifact directory instead of Chrome's configured download directory.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Start Chromium with a configured default download directory and a CDP endpoint.
2. Use an OpenClaw browser profile that attaches to that existing browser through the Playwright CDP transport.
3. After the OpenClaw browser interaction, trigger a normal download from the browser's own UI.
4. Observe that the file is not saved to the browser's configured download directory.

### Expected behavior
Downloads initiated by the attached browser itself continue to use the browser's configured download directory.

### Actual behavior
After Playwright attaches to the existing default browser context, downloads can instead be sent to Playwright's temporary artifacts directory. The affected profile is attach-only, so OpenClaw should not change the browser owner's download preference.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.5 (production runtime; source-level behavior verified against current main)

### Operating system
Linux (Kali Linux workstation)

### Install method
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Model
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not relevant to browser download routing)

### Provider / routing chain
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not relevant to browser download routing)

### Logs
No additional logs attached. Source path: `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-cdp-transport.ts` calls Playwright `connectOverCDP` without `noDefaults`. Playwright documents that `noDefaults: true` leaves the existing default context's `acceptDownloads` setting at the browser's own setting: https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-connect-over-cdp-option-no-defaults

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Not attached. Source-level evidence and controlled real-browser reproduction will be added to the linked fix PR.

Affected: users attaching OpenClaw to an existing Chromium browser through the Playwright CDP transport.

### Additional information
A narrowly scoped fix should preserve the existing default-context behavior for externally owned/attach-only profiles while leaving OpenClaw-managed browser profiles' download interception unchanged. Playwright added `noDefaults` for daily-driver browsers in v1.60; the installed runtime is Playwright 1.63.0.

issues.body:
## Summary

When the LINE channel sends a pairing challenge or a question-answer notice through `sendLineHandlerText`, it first tries to reply using the webhook's single-use reply token and falls back to a push (`pushMessageLine`) if the reply throws.

The fallback triggers on **any** reply error that is not a `CHANNEL_PARTIAL_DELIVERY` error — including ambiguous network failures such as an `AbortError` or undici's `TypeError: fetch failed`, where LINE may already have accepted the reply before the connection dropped.

A push cannot deduplicate a reply that was possibly accepted, so the user can receive the exact same text **twice** (once as the reply, once as the push). The main auto-reply path (`auto-reply-delivery.ts`) already refuses this: `canFallbackAfterLineReplyFailure` only allows the push fallback when LINE definitively rejected the request (4xx other than 408) or the request never reached LINE.

## Impact

Users of the LINE channel can see duplicate messages for:

- Pairing challenges (first contact / access pairing)
- Question-answer notices ("That question is no longer waiting for an answer", "Could not record that answer", etc.)

This happens specifically under ambiguous network conditions (timeout, connection reset after dispatch, abort), which are exactly the cases where the reply may have been delivered.

## Reproduction

Trigger a `sendLineHandlerText` path (e.g. a pairing request with a valid reply token) while making `replyMessageLine` throw an ambiguous network error:

- `new TypeError("fetch failed")`
- `Error` with `name: "AbortError"`

Observe that `pushMessageLine` is called with the same text, sending a duplicate.

## Suggested fix

Reuse `canFallbackAfterLineReplyFailure` (shared with `auto-reply-delivery.ts`) in `sendLineHandlerText` so the push fallback only runs on a definitive rejection, not on ambiguous outcomes.

issues.body:
## Summary

Per the docs (`automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md`):

> "Agent-turn jobs default to the creating conversation when the create request carries session context. Callers without a session key, including CLI and API callers that do not supply one, fall back to `isolated`."

In practice, when a user asks the agent in a chat to create a recurring job, the outcome depends on which internal path the agent happens to use:

- via the `automations` tool from the channel turn → the request carries session context → defaults to `current` (bound to the creating conversation)
- via shell `openclaw cron add` (a common fallback when the tool is restricted in channel turns) → no session context → defaults to `isolated`

From the user's perspective both are identical ("create this cron from our chat"), yet the session target differs. Neither the user nor the agent notices the choice at creation time.

## Impact

`current`-bound jobs are a time bomb on long-lived chat sessions:

- The bound session's transcript grows over time; heavy jobs slow down and eventually hit run disposal (observed: `attempt disposed before transcript write`, twice).
- Concurrent activity on the same session (heartbeats every 30 min, user messages, interactive turns) rebounds the session mid-run (observed: `session rebound for sessionKey ...`, third consecutive failure — execution completed but delivery died).
- Real-world case: a 9-minute daily log-analysis job (`agentTurn`, self-contained payload: SLS queries + Excel export) bound to a Telegram direct session failed 3 workdays in a row. Three sibling jobs created from the same chat but via the CLI path (therefore `isolated`) never failed.

The failure mode is invisible at creation time: everything works while the session is young, then degrades progressively as the transcript grows.

## Proposal

- Default chat-created `agentTurn` jobs to `isolated` + `announce` delivery back to the creating conversation (keeps the UX: results still appear where the user asked).
- Treat `current`/custom session binding as an explicit opt-in for jobs that genuinely need conversation context (the docs' own table already reserves `current` for "context-aware recurring work" and `isolated` for "reports, background chores").
- Alternatively/additionally, a global `cron.defaults.sessionTarget` (cf. #57638) so operators can set the policy explicitly.

## Related

- #12301 — same domain (cron.add session-target default misrouting), closed stale; the underlying "which session should a created job target" question is still unresolved.
- #57638 — `cron.defaults` feature request (closed stale, unimplemented as of 2026.9.x).
- #97317 — isolated jobs inheriting full toolbox/context (the opposite direction of the same axis).

## Environment

Gateway 2026.9.5, single agent + Telegram channel, 6 cron jobs (5 isolated, 1 heartbeat on main).

issues.body:
### Summary

The `gateway.roles.definitions.*.sessions.others` help text states that explicit session membership can grant additional access. That is not true when the cap is `"none"` — membership is rejected before it is ever consulted. `"none"` is the value shipped in the documented example, so the sentence is misleading in exactly the configuration most operators start from.

### Affected docs path(s) or URL(s)

- `src/config/schema.help.core.ts:156` (surfaced by `openclaw config schema`)
- Also reachable in docs as the `sessions.others` description under `gateway.roles`

### Steps to reproduce / verify

1. Configure a role with `sessions: { others: "none" }` and make it `gateway.roles.default`.
2. As a user in that role, open a session that user did not create.
3. Observe `sessions.describe` returns `INVALID_REQUEST` / `Session "<key>" was not found.`
4. Add an explicit membership row for that user on that session.
5. Repeat step 2. The result is unchanged.

Source confirms it without needing the runtime:

`src/gateway/session-sharing-policy.ts:453`
```ts
if (sessionCap === "none" && role !== "owner" && role !== "admin") {
  return hiddenSessionNotFound(params.target.canonicalKey);
}
```
A member resolves to role `"member"`, which is neither `owner` nor `admin`, so the request is rejected before membership can matter.

`src/gateway/session-sharing.ts:186-194`
```ts
isMember: (_target, identityId) => row?.membership.has(identityId) ?? false,
});
if (
  row &&
  gatewayClientSessionCreator(params.client) &&
  sharing.sessionCap === "none" &&
  !sharing.isCreator(row.entry.createdActor)
) {
  return { error: hiddenSessionNotFound(target.sessionKey) };
}
```
`isMember` is supplied to the policy, but this gate consults only `isCreator`.

### Expected docs behavior/content

The description should scope the membership claim to the caps where it holds, e.g. note that membership grants additional access at `"view"` and above, and that `"none"` hides sessions from non-owners regardless of membership.

### Actual docs behavior/content

> Access to other people's sessions: "none" hides them, "view" allows reading, "suggest" permits the suggestion flow, and "write" permits participation. Explicit session membership can grant additional access.

Read plainly, this says membership is a way to grant access under any cap.

### Impact

On a multi-user gateway the practical choice is between `"none"` (private) and `"view"`/`"write"` (everyone sees everything). This sentence suggests a third option — keep `"none"` and grant membership per session — that does not exist.

Acting on it costs real time: I added membership rows for 20 profiles, observed no change, and only found the cause by reading the shipped bundle. Because the denial is reported as `hiddenSessionNotFound` rather than a permission error, nothing in the logs points back at the cap, so the docs are the main signal available and they point the wrong way.

### Evidence

Verified on `2026.9.5` (`ec9c1a1`) and against `main` at time of filing.

Before/after on a live gateway, same users and connections:

| `sessions.others` | `sessions.describe` | `board.get` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` + membership rows | 0 ok / 93 failed | failed |
| `write` | ok | ok |

`session_members` rows were present for those profiles throughout.

### Additional information

Happy to open a PR narrowing the sentence — I have one ready.

## Problem

OpenClaw 2026.9.4 rejects native image attachments above 25,000,000 pixels before the agent receives them. A 5658x5655 screenshot (about 32 MP) is rejected with `Image dimensions exceed the 25,000,000 pixel input limit`, even when its encoded byte size is within the media byte limit.

## Proposal

Add an owner-configurable inbound image decode limit under `agents.defaults`, for example `imageMaxInputPixels`, defaulting to the current 25,000,000 and capped at 50,000,000. Thread it only through the inbound image hydration/optimization path. Keep output pixel limits, media byte caps, timeout, and serialized image processing bounded.

The larger source should be downscaled during the existing sanitization/optimization path before it reaches the model. Do not raise global Rastermill limits, output limits, image-generation limits, or unrelated channel/media paths.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Omitted setting preserves the 25,000,000-pixel behavior.
2. A valid setting up to 50,000,000 is accepted; values above the cap and invalid values fail config validation.
3. A source image between 25 MP and configured max is admitted and resized/output-capped before prompt construction.
4. An image above the configured max is rejected before full decode, with a clear bounded error.
5. Output pixels/bytes, file limits, and worker concurrency remain unchanged.
6. Regression test covers the actual native attachment hydration path, not just the Rastermill helper.

Use case: bounded support for modern screenshots/phone captures such as ~32 MP without making the limit unbounded.

## Summary

Thinking/reasoning content from MiMo V2.6-Pro is rendered as visible content in the Control UI despite `reasoningDefault: "off"` in config and toggling `/reasoning` off per-session. The thinking blocks appear to be misclassified as `commentary` rather than `reasoning`, so visibility toggles have no effect.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23)
- Model: `xiaomi-coding/mimo-v2.6-pro` via `openai-completions` API protocol
- Provider: manually-defined `xiaomi-coding` provider (baseUrl: `https://token-plan-sgp.xiaomimimo.com/v1`, OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- Surface: Control UI webchat
- OS: macOS 15.7.9

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a manually-defined provider in `models.providers` with `api: "openai-completions"` and a baseUrl pointing to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving `mimo-v2.6-pro`
2. Set `agents.defaults.reasoningDefault: "off"` and `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault: "high"`
3. Start a conversation and use tools (exec, read, etc.)
4. Observe thinking/reasoning content visible in the chat output

## Expected Behavior

Thinking blocks should be hidden from the user when `reasoningDefault` is `off` and `/reasoning` is toggled off.

## Actual Behavior

Thinking content is rendered as visible `commentary` in the Control UI. Neither `reasoningDefault: "off"` in config nor the per-session `/reasoning` toggle suppresses it. Toggling `chatPersistCommentary` to `false` also had no effect.

## Suspected Root Cause

MiMo V2.6 changed its thinking output format compared to V2.5. The `openai-completions` parser likely does not recognize V2.6's thinking blocks as `reasoning` content and instead classifies them as `commentary` or regular content, bypassing reasoning visibility controls.

This is corroborated by a V2.6-specific report in the community: [tonyd2wild/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-DGX-Spark-Recipe#1](https://github.com/tonyd2wild/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-DGX-Spark-Recipe/issues/1) — *"Thinking leaks into `content` on turns after a tool result (vLLM `mimo` parser)"*

## Related Issues

- #40736 — Thinking content leaks to channel even when thinking is disabled (older, different cause)
- #153605 — reasoningDefault not respected in new sessions
- #24195 — Reasoning blocks appearing despite Think: off

## Additional Context

- This did **not** occur with `mimo-v2.5-pro` on the same provider and same config — only after upgrading to V2.6
- Thinking depth (`thinkingDefault: "high"`) works correctly — the model does think, it just leaks the thinking output visibly
- The model API call method and model name are unchanged per Xiaomi's release notes, so the output format change appears to be the differentiator


A proven terminal completion should remain `completed` when a later soft queue timeout observation is merged for the same run. The merge should preserve stronger terminal evidence instead of letting a later soft timeout reclassify the run.

### Actual behavior

The focused regression test failed: the existing completed outcome at `endedAt: 200` was replaced by a later `timed_out` outcome at `endedAt: 300`.

This makes the final run classification depend on whether the completed observation or the queue-timeout observation is processed last.

OpenClaw 2026.7.2 local source tree

### Operating system

WSL Ubuntu 22.04 on Windows 11

Local source checkout; tests run with node scripts/test-projects.mjs

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

Agent run terminal-outcome merge path; no external provider routing was required for the local reproduction.

```shell
Focused test failure summary:


node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/agent-run-terminal-outcome.test.ts -- -t "keeps a proven completion when a later soft queue timeout observation merges"

Observed: completed@200 became timed_out@300 after merging the later soft queue timeout observation.
Expected: status remained completed.
```

Relevant source observed locally:

- `src/agents/agent-run-terminal-outcome.ts`

issues.body:
### Summary

When another plugin owns the memory slot, memory-core runs only as the "dreaming sidecar". The loader activates it while the slot owner's `dreaming.enabled` is true. Turning that flag off unloads memory-core, and its disable path only clears timers. The `Memory Dreaming Promotion` job it created is therefore never removed: it keeps running beside the slot owner's own dreaming, across hot reloads and gateway restarts.

### Cause

- `src/plugins/config-activation-shared.ts:271`: a memory plugin that does not own the slot is disabled ("memory slot set to …").
- `src/plugins/loader-shared.ts:73-89` (`resolveDreamingSidecarEngineId`): the only exception, which returns `memory-core` iff `resolveMemoryDreamingConfig(<slot owner config>).enabled` is true. `loader-runtime-candidate.ts:310` then bypasses the slot decision for it.
- `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-cron.ts` `reconcileShortTermDreamingCronJob` removes the job when dreaming is disabled, but that code only runs while memory-core is loaded, and memory-core is loaded only while dreaming is enabled.
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` `stop()` → `disposeDreaming()` clears the reconcile timer and cleanup timeouts. It never removes jobs.

So the flag that should trigger the cleanup also prevents it from running.

### Reproduction

Tested on 2026.9.5 plus #155860, with `plugins.slots.memory` set to a third-party memory plugin, on 2026-09-23 (UTC):

1. 14:23:45Z: set the slot owner's `dreaming.enabled` to `true`. At 14:24:42Z the log shows `memory-core: created managed dreaming cron job.` The job is `declarationKey: memory-core:memory-dreaming-promotion`, scheduled at the owner's `frequency` (`15 1 * * *`).
2. 14:29:17Z: turn dreaming off (Memory page toggle → `config.patch`, hot reload applied). `openclaw.json` now has `enabled: false`.
3. The job is still listed and enabled. No `memory-core: removed … managed dreaming cron job(s)` line appears.
4. 15:31:47Z: gateway restart. memory-core is not loaded at all (no memory-core log line), and the job is still there.
5. 15:42Z: `openclaw cron rm <id>` removes it. Nothing re-creates it afterwards, which confirms the config itself is read correctly.

`removeStaleJobFamily` does not help here: it only prunes obsolete store partitions, and the job lives in the active store.

### Impact

With dreaming off on the slot owner, memory-core's promotion sweep still runs every night. It dreams twice, writes promotions into `MEMORY.md` beside the owner's own consolidation, and does so after the operator explicitly turned it off.

The same symptom was noted on 2026.9.1 (2026-09-04).

### Proposed fix

The gateway converges this job family itself. A system-job reconciler (next to heartbeat monitors and skill-collection reviews in `reconcileSystemJobs`) removes memory-core's managed and legacy dreaming jobs while slot ≠ memory-core and the sidecar is not due. A reload rule for `plugins.slots.memory` and `plugins.entries.*.config.dreaming` requests that pass on the same hot reload. PR: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156667

issues.body:
## Summary

After GitHub Copilot account discovery publishes a larger prompt limit for a model that is missing from the curated list, status and preflight context budgeting can stay at the provider's synthetic unknown-model fallback of 128,000 tokens.

## Environment

- Observed on OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (Linux arm64, Node 26), GitHub Copilot provider, default merge mode, normal saved Copilot auth, no authored model metadata or agent context cap.
- Source mechanism reproduced on `main` at `b28166ffb99c25b22f5d085400354d2f6a88a9c1`.

## Observed

- Native `/status` shows a 128k denominator for the selected model.
- `sessions.describe` on the same Gateway reports `contextTokens=128000`, while `models.list` reports `contextWindow=1000000` / `contextTokens=872000` for the same model.
- 128k is the Copilot unknown-model estimate, not the output cap being read as input.

`sessions.describe` is a projection. I have not proven that a 128k inference budget was persisted, or that compaction actually ran early in the affected session.

## Expected

When discovery is accepted for the same provider, exact model ID and API, with a compatible endpoint, it should replace the provider's unknown-model synthetic estimate. Authored caps, curated static limits, different routes, native rows, and failed or empty discovery should keep their current authority.

## Mechanism

1. The unknown-model branch of the Copilot plugin resolves a 128,000-token estimate. That row is not marked as synthetic.
2. Accepted discovery publishes an 872,000-token prompt budget for the same model.
3. The configured catalog keeps the synthetic static row next to the discovered row, and the cache takes the smaller value. Post-ready context warmup also reads only configured facts.

Status and preflight compaction/memory-flush planning both read this cache, so the risk is premature maintenance as well as a misleading display.

## Prior work

- #106930 proposed a broad discovered-over-static policy. Its author closed it unmerged and suggested a narrower, route/provenance-aware follow-up. This issue is about that narrower case.
- #153864 is adjacent (persisted session / patch-RPC budgets) but is a different path. This issue does not claim to cover it.

A draft PR with focused regression tests will follow.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (internal error text leaks to the user channel)

### Version
OpenClaw 2026.9.2 (3928bad), macOS 15.6 arm64, node 22.23.1. Telegram channel, forum-group topic session.

### Summary
When a requester session spawns a subagent and finishes its own turn with a normal visible reply **without** calling `sessions_yield` (child still running), the requester-settle wake (`dist/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake-*.js`, `MAX_ATTEMPTS=3`, delays `[30s, 120s]`) retries to wake the requester. If the **third** attempt's run fails, the default error text `⚠️ Agent run failed (model: …)` is **delivered to the user channel as a normal assistant message** (Telegram topic in our case). End users who never asked for anything see an internal English error in their working chat.

### Observed sequence (single incident, sanitized log)
```
2026-09-23T17:38:48.163+03:00 requester settle wake attempt 1 failed; retrying in 30s: Session "<requester-session>" changed while starting work. Retry. | SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED
2026-09-23T17:39:06.018+03:00 [main-session-restart-recovery] main-session restart recovery terminal: session=<requester-session> run=<uuid> status=ok reason=completed
2026-09-23T17:39:18.583+03:00 [agent/embedded] [tool-result-truncation] Truncated 0 tool result(s) for prompt history (maxChars=64000 aggregateBudgetChars=540000 aggregate=0) sessionKey=<requester-session>
2026-09-23T17:39:30.371+03:00 [agents/agent-command] [agent] run announce:requester-settle:main:<requester-session>:<uuid>:yield-1:retry-1 ended with stopReason=stop
2026-09-23T17:39:30.390+03:00 requester settle wake attempt 2 failed; retrying in 120s: completion agent did not produce a visible reply
2026-09-23T17:41:30.704+03:00 [agent/embedded] [tool-result-truncation] Truncated 0 tool result(s) for prompt history (maxChars=64000 aggregateBudgetChars=540000 aggregate=0) sessionKey=<requester-session>
2026-09-23T17:41:40.154+03:00 [agents/agent-command] [agent] run announce:requester-settle:main:<requester-session>:<uuid>:yield-1:retry-2 ended with stopReason=stop
2026-09-23T17:46:48.604+03:00 [agent/embedded] [tool-result-truncation] Truncated 0 tool result(s) for prompt history (maxChars=64000 aggregateBudgetChars=540000 aggregate=0) sessionKey=<requester-session>
2026-09-23T17:46:48.698+03:00 ⚠️ Agent run failed (model: openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5).
```
The transcript for the failed run records `"The agent run failed before producing a reply."`, runId `announce:requester-settle:main:<requester-session>:<uuid>:yield-1:retry-2`, and immediately after it an `outbound send ok … messageId=<id>` to the topic. Cause of the underlying run failure is not visible in the log (fails ~2s after model-fetch start, no error line).

### Frequency
`grep "requester settle wake attempt .* failed\|settle wake attempts exhausted" gateway.log` → 34 occurrences on 2026-09-22, 4 on 2026-09-23, rising since 2026-09-21 as topic sessions started using `sessions_spawn` more often.

### Expected
1. Runs started by internal wakes (requester-settle, heartbeat, compaction) should **never** emit default error text (`lifecycle.emitBasicError("Agent run failed")` in `dist/agent-command-*.js`) to the user channel — log only, same as the intentional-silence path.
2. Ideally: skip the requester-settle wake entirely (or settle quietly) when the requester has already produced a visible reply after the child was spawned.

### Related (not duplicates)
- #153417 — announce retries loop when requester yields no visible reply (retry policy); this issue is about the *failure text* of such a retry reaching users.
- #121187 — intentional `NO_REPLY` from a yielded requester retried as missing output.
- #138632 — settle wake deferred too many times drops result.

### Workaround on our side
Operational rule for agents: after `sessions_spawn` either `sessions_yield` in the same turn, cancel the child before ending the turn, or spawn with `expectsCompletionMessage: false` for fire-and-forget tasks. Plus a text patch of `"Agent run failed"` → silent token in dist as a temporary measure.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a declared `openclaw.build.staticAssets` source cannot be resolved, `runtime-postbuild` logs a warning, skips the file, and exits `0`. `build-stamp` and `runtime-postbuild-stamp` then run successfully and record the exact HEAD commit.

The result is a `dist/` that is missing declared, required extension assets while carrying full exact-SHA provenance. Nothing in the build path signals the omission. `scripts/check-openclaw-package-tarball.mts --require-bundled-workspace-deps` does catch it, but only during packaging — a source deployment that builds `dist/` and runs it directly never packs, so the incomplete build is never detected.

Warn-and-skip happens at `scripts/lib/static-extension-assets.mts:330` (`copyStaticExtensionAssets`) and `:369` (`copyStaticExtensionAssetsToRuntimeOverlay`).

### Steps to reproduce

On a clean checkout of `main` at `08f5fb80f301d8236cadb8acc853d95566fd7f10` with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and a completed `pnpm build`:

```bash
A=dist/extensions/code-mode-quickjs/assets
D=extensions/code-mode-quickjs/node_modules/quickjs-wasi

# make the declared staticAssets source unresolvable
mv "$D" "${D}.hidden"
rm -f "$A/quickjs.wasm" "$A/encoding.so"

node scripts/runtime-postbuild.mjs                                  # exits 0
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-stamp.mts             # exits 0
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/runtime-postbuild-stamp.mts # exits 0

cat dist/.buildstamp dist/.runtime-postbuildstamp
ls "$A"
```

Hiding the dependency is only a deterministic way to make the source unresolvable; any incomplete or inconsistent `node_modules` state produces the same result.

### Expected behavior

A declared static asset that cannot be resolved should fail the build, or at minimum prevent `dist/.buildstamp` and `dist/.runtime-postbuildstamp` from certifying that commit. Provenance stamps should not attest to a `dist/` that is missing declared required assets.

### Actual behavior

All three steps exit `0`. Both stamps record the exact HEAD commit while the two declared assets are absent from `dist/`:

```
HEAD                           08f5fb80f301d8236cadb8acc853d95566fd7f10
dist/.buildstamp               08f5fb80f301d8236cadb8acc853d95566fd7f10
dist/.runtime-postbuildstamp   08f5fb80f301d8236cadb8acc853d95566fd7f10
assets present                 activity.svg icon.png
quickjs.wasm                   MISSING despite valid stamps
```

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (repro at 08f5fb80f301d8236cadb8acc853d95566fd7f10)

### Operating system

macOS 27.0 (arm64), Node v24.21.0, pnpm 12.4.0

### Install method

Source checkout of `main` (pnpm)

### Model

N/A — build/packaging defect, independent of model

### Provider / routing chain

N/A — build/packaging defect, independent of provider

### Logs

```
[runtime-postbuild] static asset not found, skipping: extensions/code-mode-quickjs/node_modules/quickjs-wasi/extensions/encoding/encoding.so
[runtime-postbuild] static asset not found, skipping: extensions/code-mode-quickjs/node_modules/quickjs-wasi/quickjs.wasm
[runtime-postbuild] static asset not found, skipping: extensions/code-mode-quickjs/node_modules/quickjs-wasi/extensions/encoding/encoding.so
[runtime-postbuild] static asset not found, skipping: extensions/code-mode-quickjs/node_modules/quickjs-wasi/quickjs.wasm
runtime-postbuild: 13 phases completed in 5730ms (slowest: built plugin control-plane loads 1960ms)
```

### Impact and severity

Encountered on a live source deployment, not only in the synthetic repro. A managed Gateway was rebuilt from `main` and ran for roughly two hours without `dist/extensions/code-mode-quickjs/assets/{quickjs.wasm,encoding.so}`. All three provenance markers — `.buildstamp`, `.runtime-postbuildstamp` and `build-info.json` — agreed on the exact commit, so every stamp-based verification reported a correct, current build.

This matters because deployment tooling gates on exactly those stamps. `.agents/skills/openclaw-live-updater/scripts/update-main.mjs` requires both stamp heads plus `build-info.json` to equal the post-update SHA before it will restart the managed Gateway; an incomplete `dist` satisfies that check. The omission only surfaced later, and indirectly, when a macOS packaging run failed its tarball integrity check with `declared static extension asset is missing`.

Severity is moderate: no crash, and packaged artifacts are protected by the tarball check, but source deployments can silently serve an incomplete runtime that all provenance checks certify as good.

### Additional information

`scripts/check-openclaw-package-tarball.mts` already treats a missing declared static asset as fatal for a packed tarball. The gap is that the build and stamp steps that produce `dist/` do not apply the same rule, so the two paths disagree about whether the same `dist/` is valid.

Image is delivered to the chat channel. The Control UI shows only the text portion of the assistant reply for that turn; no image, no attachment entry.

Code trace on `main` @ `c1ead4b71e0`:

- `src/agents/openclaw-plugin-tools.ts:161-207` — `delivery.send` calls `runMessageAction` with `forceCoreDelivery: true, skipQueue: true, dryRun: false`. This is a live, ephemeral push through the core outbound owner and never populates the tool-result media queue.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-tool-media.ts:102` — `TRUSTED_TOOL_RESULT_MEDIA` is a hardcoded set. Plugin tool names are not members, so `details.media.mediaUrls` returned from a plugin tool is stripped by `filterToolResultMediaUrls()`.
- Result: both established Control UI ingest routes (trusted tool-result media, or assistant `ReplyPayload.mediaUrls`) are closed to plugin `delivery.send`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (main @ `c1ead4b71e0`)

### Operating system

macOS 12.7.6

### Install method

pnpm dev (source checkout of main)

### Model

Not model-dependent (defect is in the tool-result → transcript pipeline, before the model round-trip)

### Provider / routing chain

Not routing-dependent

### Additional provider/model setup details

N/A — the defect is in the tool-result → transcript pipeline, not in inference routing.

### Logs

N/A — no error is emitted; the media silently does not appear in the Control UI.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Code references above are sufficient for grounded verification against `main` @ `c1ead4b71e0`:

- `src/agents/openclaw-plugin-tools.ts:161-207`
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-tool-media.ts:102`
- `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.execution.ts` (baseline: native tool whose media does appear in Control UI)

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any plugin tool that returns media via the sanctioned `toolContext.delivery.send` capability from #127098.
- Severity: Behavior bug. Chat channel delivery works; Control UI users lose visibility of media the same turn produced.
- Frequency: Every invocation.
- Consequence: Control UI reviewers cannot see plugin-generated media without switching to the chat channel; degrades review, debugging, and audit workflows.

### Additional information

Follow-up to #120718. Of the three solutions proposed there, #127098 implemented Option C (a sanctioned `delivery.send` abstraction). Option A (extending `TRUSTED_TOOL_RESULT_MEDIA` for plugins) was not implemented, and the Control UI path continues to depend on it.

Two directions that would close the gap:

1. Mirror `delivery.send`-sent media into the assistant `ReplyPayload.mediaUrls` for the current turn so the Control UI renders what the chat channel received.
2. Ship Option A from #120718 — allow plugins to declare a tool as trusted local-media producer so returning `details.media.mediaUrls` from the tool result also survives `filterToolResultMediaUrls()`.

Either would restore parity with the native `image_generate` tool's Control UI behavior.



---

**Update 2026-10-08 — still reproducible on `main`** (v2026.10.1-beta.2 @ `e73b64b7f62`):

- `src/agents/openclaw-plugin-tools.ts` still calls `runMessageAction` for `delivery.send` with `forceCoreDelivery: true, skipQueue: true, dryRun: false` — media never enters the tool-result media queue.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-tool-media.ts` still exposes `TRUSTED_TOOL_RESULT_MEDIA` as a hardcoded set; plugin tools are not members, so `filterToolResultMediaUrls()` continues to strip plugin-tool `details.media.mediaUrls`.
- No mirror from `delivery.send` into assistant `ReplyPayload.mediaUrls` has landed on `main`. (See clawsweeper's 2026-10-08 review of this issue: `deliver-transcript.ts:45` passes `text` only, with mediaUrls flattened to filename text — confirming the mirror boundary is still the loss site.)
- Linked fix PR #156613 remains **open and unmerged**, blocked on merge conflicts (`mergeable_state=dirty`).
