issues.body:
### Bug type

Build failure (deterministic on Windows under real-time antivirus/file-watcher handle contention)

### Summary

On Windows, `pnpm build` (and `openclaw plugins build` for any plugin that ships a Control UI) can fail intermittently during the immutable generation publish step with the misleading error:

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '...\extensions\workboard\dist\control-ui\<hash>\index.css'
  at buildPluginControlUi (src/cli/plugins-control-ui-build.ts)
```

The publish step writes the bundle into a fresh `.build-*` staging directory and immediately `fs.rename`s it to the content-hashed generation directory. On Windows, a freshly-written directory can be transiently locked while antivirus or an indexer still scans it, so the first rename is denied with `EPERM` **even though the destination does not exist**. The code infers "the destination already exists" from the `EPERM` code, then reads the destination files to validate them, and crashes with `ENOENT` — and the surfaced message ("An immutable Control UI build was modified. Remove that build and rebuild.") points at the wrong cause.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows host (Node 24.x).
2. Run `pnpm build` (or build any bundled plugin with a Control UI, e.g. `extensions/workboard`). With real-time scanning enabled, this fails on the first attempt most of the time; repeated builds fail intermittently.
3. Observe the ENOENT crash and the misleading "immutable Control UI build was modified" guidance even though no build was modified.

A tight loop that writes two files into a fresh dir and immediately renames it reproduces the transient denial (~17% failure rate over 60 iterations on a Windows 11 host), and the real `workboard` build failed on 4/4 consecutive attempts before the fix.

### Expected behavior

The atomic publish should retry the rename a bounded number of times (the denial is transient), succeed, and only report a real "modified build" when the destination generation actually exists with mismatched bytes. If the denial never clears, it should fail with a clear, actionable error.

### Actual behavior

The build crashes with an ENOENT and a misleading "immutable build was modified" message, blocking `pnpm build` and plugin Control UI publication on Windows.

### Root cause

`src/cli/plugins-control-ui-build.ts` `publishImmutableGeneration`: the catch block treats any `EPERM` as "destination already exists" and unconditionally reads the destination to validate reuse, without first checking whether the destination exists. On Windows, `fs.rename` of a freshly-written directory can be denied with `EPERM` while the destination is still absent (transient handle), producing `ENOENT`.

### Evidence

- Before fix: `pnpm build` fails on the workboard Control UI step (terminal capture; exact EPERM -> ENOENT stack).
- After fix: the same `pnpm build` succeeds; the `extensions/workboard` generation `dist/control-ui/<hash>/index.css` is published and the manifest updated.
- Focused regression tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/plugins-control-ui-build.test.ts` — 21 passed, including new tests for transient-denial retry and clean failure.

### Impact and severity

Windows developers, Windows CI lanes, and anyone publishing third-party Control UI plugins on Windows are intermittently blocked by a confusing build error. The affected platform is a supported, first-class platform (dedicated Windows CI matrix).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Claude Code serializes its OAuth access-token refresh across processes with `~/.claude/.oauth_refresh.lock`. When the gateway's `claude-cli` backend spawns a short-lived `claude -p` for a turn at the moment another Claude Code process on the same host (an interactive session under the same login) is refreshing the about-to-expire token, the spawned process exits in ~9 s with Claude Code's own transient error:

```
Failed to refresh OAuth token: another Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh. This is usually transient; retry in a minute, and if it persists close other Claude Code processes or sign in again
```

`agent/cli-backend` treats this as a terminal `cli terminal failure`, the run raises `FailoverError`, and the model-fallback chain advances immediately (`candidate_failed reason=unknown`). The next candidate was also a `claude-cli` model, so it hit the same lock 9 seconds later, and the turn ended up on a third-party provider (OpenRouter) even though the Claude login was healthy the whole time: `~/.claude/.credentials.json` was rewritten by the lock holder 3 minutes later, `claude auth status --json` reported `loggedIn: true`, and a manual `claude -p` succeeded in 7 s.

Claude Code itself labels the condition "usually transient; retry in a minute". The backend should treat it as retryable rather than as a candidate failure.

### Steps to reproduce

Timing-dependent; observed once so far (2026-09-23 08:20 UTC) and not yet reproduced on demand.

1. OpenClaw 2026.9.5 on Linux, Anthropic via the Claude CLI route (`openclaw models auth login --provider anthropic --method cli`), Claude Code 2.1.280 logged in with a Claude subscription.
2. Agent model: primary `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8`, fallbacks `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`, `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`, `openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`.
3. Keep other long-lived Claude Code processes running on the host under the same login (interactive `claude` sessions / `claude remote-control`), so one of them performs the periodic access-token refresh.
4. Have a gateway cron job (here: an `openclaw cron` job on the agent) start a turn within the seconds the other process holds `~/.claude/.oauth_refresh.lock`.

### Expected behavior

The `claude-cli` backend recognizes this specific Claude Code error as transient and retries the same candidate once after a short wait (for example ~30–60 s, or as soon as the mtime of `~/.claude/.credentials.json` moves) before consulting the fallback chain. At minimum, two `claude-cli` candidates should not both be burned within 9 seconds by the same host-level lock. A config knob would also work (for example `agents.entries.<id>.claudeCli.retryOnRefreshLock`).

### Actual behavior

```
08:20:10Z WARN  agent/cli-backend        cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-4-8 durationMs=9380 runId=e94ccce8-… error=Failed to refresh OAuth token: *** Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh. This is usually transient; retry in a minute, and if it persists close other Claude Code processes or sign in again
08:20:10Z ERROR diagnostic               lane task error: lane=session:agent:leonard:cron:…:run:e94ccce8-… durationMs=10041 error="Failed to refresh OAuth token: *** Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh. …"   (FailoverError)
08:20:10Z WARN  model-fallback/decision  candidate_failed requestedModel=claude-opus-4-8 candidateModel=claude-opus-4-8 candidateRouteOrigin=requested attempt=1 total=4 reason=unknown
08:20:11Z INFO  agent/cli-backend        cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-4-6 trigger=cron useResume=false
08:20:19Z WARN  agent/cli-backend        cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-4-6 durationMs=8828 runId=e94ccce8-… error=Failed to refresh OAuth token: *** Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh. …
08:20:20Z WARN  model-fallback/decision  candidate_failed candidateModel=claude-opus-4-6 candidateRouteOrigin=configured-fallback attempt=2 total=4 reason=unknown
08:20:55Z WARN  model-fallback/decision  candidate_failed candidateProvider=openai candidateModel=gpt-5.6-sol attempt=3 total=4   (401, unrelated: no openai profile on this agent)
08:21:54Z WARN  model-fallback/decision  candidate_succeeded candidateProvider=openrouter candidateModel=anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6 attempt=4 total=4
```

(`***` is the gateway log's redaction of the word "another" — the literal CLI message is quoted in the summary.) Three minutes later `~/.claude/.credentials.json` was rewritten with a fresh access token; every subsequent `claude-cli` turn worked.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic, Node 24.19.0 (gateway runtime)

### Install method

npm package install; gateway run as a systemd service

### Model

anthropic/claude-opus-4-8 (Claude CLI route)

### Provider / routing chain

anthropic/claude-opus-4-8 → anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 → openai/gpt-5.6-sol → openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Anthropic via the Claude CLI route only (no Anthropic API key on the agent); Claude Code 2.1.280 with a Claude subscription login. The lock file name and this exact message are present in every Claude Code build on the host from 2.1.273 to 2.1.280.
- Four other long-lived Claude Code processes share that login on the host (interactive sessions and `claude remote-control`), so the periodic token refresh is usually performed by one of them, not by the gateway-spawned process.
- `openrouter` is an API-key profile on the agent (the only profile in its auth store, as expected under the CLI route).

### Logs

See "Actual behavior" above; runId `e94ccce8-dadf-4899-ad53-4ed52da8406e`, session `agent:leonard:cron:2f2b6648-…`, lane `cron-nested`. Happy to attach the full JSON lines on request.

### Impact and severity

Low-frequency but silent: a cron/heartbeat turn degrades onto a paid third-party provider while the Claude login is perfectly healthy. Before an OpenRouter fallback was configured on this agent, the same event would have been a hard turn failure. Because both `claude-cli` candidates fail for the same host-level reason within seconds, `anthropic/*` fallbacks give no protection against it. It also fires operator auth-alerting for what is not an auth problem.

### Additional information

Related but distinct:
- #8673 asks for retry around the gateway's own OAuth refresh call. Under the Claude CLI route the gateway performs no refresh at all (per the Anthropic provider docs it "never reads, persists, refreshes … the native login tokens"); the error here is produced by the Claude Code process and merely relayed, so the fix belongs in `agent/cli-backend`'s handling of the spawned process result.
- #89278 is the Codex-side analogue (a valid session failing a hard timeout in cron/heartbeat lanes).

issues.body:
## Summary

`openclaw wiki okf import` does not preserve the OKF-required top-level `type` field on imported concept pages. It writes `pageType` (plugin convention) and `okfType` (renamed) instead, and nests the original under `okf.frontmatter.type`. As a result, imported pages no longer satisfy **OKF conformance rule §11.2** ("Every frontmatter block contains a non-empty `type` field"), and a re-import of the resulting vault skips them with `missing-type`.

The docs state the opposite:

> Each page keeps the original OKF concept ID, source path, `type`, `resource`, `tags`, timestamp, and full producer frontmatter.
> — `docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md`

## Version

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), Linux x64
- Plugin: bundled `memory-wiki`

## Steps to reproduce

Create a two-concept bundle. One has a proper top-level `type`, the other only carries the plugin-style keys:

```
okf-repro/
  concepts/has-type.md
  concepts/pageType-only.md
```

`concepts/has-type.md`:
```yaml
---
type: documentation
title: With type
---
Body.
```

`concepts/pageType-only.md`:
```yaml
---
pageType: concept
okfType: documentation
title: Without top-level type
---
Body.
```

Import it:
```bash
openclaw wiki okf import ./okf-repro --json
```

## Actual result

```json
{
  "importedCount": 1,
  "skippedCount": 1,
  "warnings": [
    {
      "code": "missing-type",
      "path": "concepts/pageType-only.md",
      "message": "OKF concept is missing required non-empty type frontmatter."
    }
  ]
}
```

That part is correct — an input without `type` *should* be rejected.

The defect is in the **output**. The page that *did* import (from `has-type.md`) is written as:

```yaml
---
pageType: concept
id: concept.okf-okf-repro-...-has-type-11180591
title: With type
sourceType: okf
provenanceMode: okf-import
sourcePath: <bundle>/concepts/has-type.md
okfConceptId: has-type
okfType: documentation        # <- the OKF type, renamed
sourceIds:
  - source.okf.okf-repro
importedAt: ...
updatedAt: ...
status: active
...
okf:
  bundleName: okf-repro
  bundleKey: okf-repro
  conceptId: has-type
  sourceRelativePath: concepts/has-type.md
  frontmatter:
    type: documentation       # <- preserved only as nested metadata
    title: With type
    ...
---
```

There is **no top-level `type`**. The original value survives only as `okfType` and as nested `okf.frontmatter.type`.

## Expected result

The imported concept page keeps a top-level `type` with the original OKF value, e.g.

```yaml
type: documentation
pageType: concept
okfType: documentation
```

or the page id / `pageType` is derived without consuming the OKF `type` key.

## Why this matters

The import is **lossy in the round-trip direction**, which contradicts the documented "keeps the original … `type`" behaviour:

1. **Re-import skips the pages.** Feeding the resulting `concepts/` directory back through `wiki okf import` fails §11.2 on every imported page — the same rule the importer enforces on input. Verified with the repro above.
2. **External OKF consumers see a non-conformant bundle.** OKF v0.2 requires `type` on every non-reserved `.md`; consumers are told to tolerate unknown values but the field itself is mandatory (§11.2, §4.1: "`type` is the only always-required key").
3. **It is self-inconsistent.** These pages are addressed as first-class concepts (`id: concept.*`, counted under `Concepts:` in `wiki status`), yet they alone would fail the conformance check that the importer itself applies.

Consumers MUST NOT reject a bundle for unknown `type` values or unknown extra keys (§11), so adding `type` back is safe and non-breaking.

## Related observation (same subsystem)

The importer also writes `status: active`, while OKF §5.4 defines the lifecycle vocabulary as `draft | stable | deprecated`. `active` is accepted as an unknown value, but it does not map to a trust/lifecycle state (absent `status` means `stable` per §5.4). Worth aligning while this area is being touched.

## Environment

- Bundle built by hand to OKF v0.2 (https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/open-knowledge-format/blob/main/SPEC.md)
- Reproduced on a vault with `renderMode: obsidian`, `vaultMode: bridge`

Happy to test a patch.

issues.body:
On OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (`ec9c1a1`), is there a supported way to run ordinary `openclaw agent --local --session-key <non-main-key>` with the bundled `claude-cli` backend, retaining native session continuation but preventing bundled MCP listener startup?

The task-local configuration denies all tools (`tools.deny: ["*"]`), disables elevated access and agent-to-agent activity, and has no model fallbacks. A non-generative capture launcher replaces Claude, so the diagnostic cannot start a model. With network access denied, an ordinary local agent invocation stops before reaching that launcher with:

```text
Bundled MCP is enabled, but the OpenClaw MCP loopback server failed to start:
Error: listen EPERM: operation not permitted 127.0.0.1
```

In the installed build, `prepare.runtime-DMyLMH4U.mjs` enables the bridge when the registered backend has `bundleMcp` and `params.disableTools !== true`. `cli-backends-EpvEevsy.mjs` takes `bundleMcp` from the registered backend. The ordinary agent CLI registration exposes no disableTools flag. Deny-all tool policy does not appear to suppress startup on this path.

The required test is two separate local processes selecting the same persisted non-main session, with no tools. The documented stateless `infer model run` route and repeated fresh-session `agent exec` calls would not test that behavior. We are seeking a supported flag/configuration or supported entry point, without patching vendor code, enabling a plugin, or starting a Gateway.

Is a supported no-listener route available in this revision? If not, would exposing an ordinary-agent no-tools mode that reaches the existing disableTools path be the intended fix? No model/session-recovery failure is claimed here: execution stopped during preparation.

issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary After a Codex-native parent has already received successful child results via wait_agent and produced its final response, OpenClaw can still create a second synthetic announce:codex-native Main that repeats the final answer; the same failure chain was independently observed through both Telegram and WebChat. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use an existing OpenClaw conversation/session backed by Codex. 2. Restart the OpenClaw Gateway / Codex app-server lifecycle. 3. Continue using the same conversation after the restart. 4. Send a request that first produces a normal user-visible progress message, then spawns one or more Codex-native children, waits for their terminal results with wait_agent, and produces a final answer after receiving all child results. 5. In the failing observations, the native child or children complete successfully and the original Main receives their results and produces the correct final answer. 6. Immediately afterward, inspect the gateway log. 7. In the failing runs, OpenClaw logs: Active requester session could not be woken for subagent completion; falling back to requester-agent handoff: active requester session could not be woken: queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming 8. A separate announce:codex-native:::succeeded Main run is then created and produces the same final answer again. This sequence was independently observed once through Telegram and once through WebChat / Control UI. In the current WebChat case, immediately repeating an equivalent orchestration request in the same session did not reproduce the duplicate. The exact reproduction rate has not been established. ### Expected behavior When the active parent has already received the successful terminal child result through wait_agent and incorporated that result into its final response, the same child completion should not create another requester-visible Main execution. As a known-good comparison, an immediately repeated equivalent WebChat orchestration in the same session produced only one final response. ### Actual behavior The native child or children complete successfully, the original Main receives their results, and the original Main produces the correct final response. After that response is already complete, OpenClaw attempts to wake the requester for subagent completion. The wake fails with: queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming OpenClaw then falls back to a requester-agent handoff and creates a separate: announce:codex-native:...:succeeded Main run. That second Main produces the same final answer again. This is not one assistant message being rendered twice. The two visible responses correspond to two distinct Main executions. ### OpenClaw version 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1) ### Operating system Windows 11 host / Linux WSL (OpenClawGateway) ### Install method npm global installation using the OpenClaw-managed Node.js runtime inside WSL ### Model codex/gpt-5.6-sol (parent); openai/gpt-5.6-luna (native children) ### Provider / routing chain OpenClaw -> Codex app-server parent -> OpenClaw native Codex subagents -> OpenAI child models ### Additional provider/model setup details Current WebChat reproduction: Parent: codex/gpt-5.6-sol Native children: openai/gpt-5.6-luna Two independent native children were used. Child 1 calculated: 17 x 23 = 391 Child 2 calculated: 19 x 29 = 551 Both children completed successfully. The original parent received both results and produced: FINALITY_MULTI_OK 391 551 before the later synthetic announce:codex-native Main produced the same final result again. The earlier independent reproduction occurred through Telegram using the same Codex-native child / wait_agent execution path. issues.body:
[Bug]: Control UI chat — own sent message bubble disappears before reading (optimistic bubble retired without canonical row attached)

## Summary

In the Control UI chat tab, a message I just sent sometimes vanishes from the view while I am still reading it — the bubble is removed and no persisted row takes its place. The message text is NOT lost: it is safely committed in the SQLite transcript. What disappears is only the rendered bubble.

Root cause (from reading the bundled Control UI source): the optimistic local bubble is retired even when neither identity match (`id` nor `sendRunId`) finds the canonical persisted row, leaving a projection gap. Once a local source is retired it cannot be brought back by replayed events, so the gap stays visible.

Version: OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), Control UI web (Linux host).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Control UI chat tab (web).
2. Send a message.
3. Keep reading the just-sent bubble.
4. Observed intermittently: the bubble disappears before I finish reading, and nothing renders at that position.
5. Reload / re-open history: the message is present in history (it was persisted).

(The exact runtime trigger that desynchronizes the identities — workspace-prep custody, reconnect, or scope change — is not yet pinned, but the defect is independent of the trigger: the UI retires the local source without first confirming a canonical row is attached.)

## Expected behavior

The optimistic bubble must remain visible until a canonical persisted row is positively matched and replaces it. If no canonical row is matched at the retirement point, the local bubble should stay (fail-sticky), not be removed.

## Actual behavior

When both identity matches fail, the optimistic bubble is retired and not replaced; because retired local sources cannot be restored by replay, the message appears to vanish even though it is durably stored.

## Evidence (from bundled Control UI assets)

Bundled file: `dist/control-ui/assets/control-ui-boot-shared-jc3M3nDf.js`

The merge in `snapshot(...)` reconciles persisted rows against the local queue:

```js
snapshot(e, t, n = this.outbox(e,t)?.queue ?? []) {
  ...
  let o = new Map(a.map(e => [e.id, e]));
  s = n.map(e => {
    i.durableSeen.add(e.id);
    let t = o.get(e.id),                              // 1) match by id
        n = this.live.get(r)?.get(e.id)?.item;
    return t?.pendingRunId || t?.sendState === `waiting-model` ? t
         : n && n.sendRunId === e.sendRunId ? n       // 2) live, match by sendRunId
         : t && t.sendRunId === e.sendRunId ? this.project(e, t)  // 3) project by sendRunId
         : e;                                        // 4) no match -> treated as a new item
  });
  ...
}
```

The map is keyed by `id` (`new Map([...n, ...t].map(e => [e.id, e]))` in `allItems`). When neither the `id` nor the `sendRunId` matches, there is no branch that keeps the optimistic bubble attached to the canonical position; the local source is retired and the provisional UI state is dropped.

This matches the documented delivery/transcript model (https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/webchat):

> The Control UI replaces its provisional source with accepted custody, then with the canonical row. … Once custody, a consumption record, or a committed user-message receipt retires a local source, replayed terminal events cannot bring it back, even when its row is absent from a later history page.

and the documented triage order:

> If live assistant text appears during a run but disappears after history reload, check three things in order. First, whether the SQLite transcript contains the text. Second, whether the `chat.history` display projection stripped it. Third, whether the Control UI optimistic-tail merge replaced local delivery state with the persisted snapshot.

For this report: (1) the SQLite transcript contains the text — verified; (2) the row is visible after a history reload; therefore the disappearance happens at (3), the optimistic-tail merge replacing/dropping local state without a canonical row rendered at that position.

## Related

Same display-normalization / optimistic-projection area as #54255 (Control UI partially strips a token instead of handling the whole message), suggesting the identity/boundary handling in this projection path is incomplete.

## Suggested fix direction

Before retiring an optimistic source, require a positive canonical match (by `id` or `sendRunId`) and confirm the canonical row is attached at the same position. If no match exists, keep the local bubble (fail-sticky) rather than removing it.

## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect UI state without crash); no data loss.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

The documented `before_model_resolve` plugin hook is never invoked for models configured with a CLI `agentRuntime` such as `claude-cli`, so a plugin cannot make a pre-turn model override on that execution path.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure two Anthropic models to use the same CLI backend:

   ```json
   {
     "agents": {
       "defaults": {
         "model": { "primary": "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5" },
         "models": {
           "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5": {
             "agentRuntime": { "id": "claude-cli" }
           },
           "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5": {
             "agentRuntime": { "id": "claude-cli" }
           }
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```

2. Enable a plugin that logs every invocation and returns a same-backend model override:

   ```js
   api.on("before_model_resolve", (_event, _ctx) => {
     api.logger.info("before_model_resolve invoked");
     return {
       providerOverride: "anthropic",
       modelOverride: "claude-sonnet-5",
     };
   });
   ```

3. Start the gateway and confirm the plugin is listed among the loaded plugins.
4. Run a fresh CLI-backed agent turn.
5. Inspect the effective model and gateway logs.

Observed on the tested system: the turn runs as `claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5`, and the hook's log line is absent.

## Expected behavior

`before_model_resolve` should run once before the CLI model is normalized and the child process is prepared. A returned override that resolves to the already selected CLI backend should change the model passed to that backend for the turn.

This expectation is based on the hook documentation and the maintainer rationale when closing #62153: current `main` was said to supersede that PR with the supported `before_model_resolve` pre-turn override path.

## Actual behavior

For a CLI execution provider, `runAgentAttempt(...)` dispatches to `runCliAgent(...)` and returns before `runEmbeddedAgent(...)`. `resolveHookModelSelection(...)` is called from embedded-runner setup, and there is no corresponding call on the CLI runner path. The plugin loads without an error or warning, but the hook is never invoked and the primary model remains selected.

## OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)

## Operating system

Windows 11 host; WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 gateway environment

## Install method

npm global; gateway runs as a systemd user service in WSL2

## Model

`anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` with `agentRuntime.id = "claude-cli"`; attempted override to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` on the same backend

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> `claude-cli` agent runtime -> Anthropic subscription

## Additional provider/model setup details

Claude Code CLI 2.1.280 is authenticated through a Claude subscription; no Anthropic API key is used. Both the primary and requested override models resolve to `claude-cli`. Moving these models to the embedded provider is not equivalent because it changes the authentication and billing path.

The hook context should use the logical provider (`anthropic`) rather than the execution backend (`claude-cli`). A router comparing the current logical selection against `anthropic/<model>` will otherwise treat `claude-cli/<model>` as an existing manual override and preserve it.

## Logs

```shell
# Gateway startup confirms the plugin is loaded:
http server listening (..., prompt-model-router, ...)

# No invocation line appears for the test turn. The plugin emits this on every call:
prompt-model-router: agent=<agent> action=<route-or-preserve> model=<model> reason=<reason>

# Effective model returned by the test turn:
claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Hook documentation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/plugins/hooks.md
- CLI backend documentation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/cli-backends.md
- CLI/embedded dispatch: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/command/attempt-execution.ts
- Related routing request and implementation attempt: #62152 and #62153
- Related persistent-session model-switching request: #57941

The tested 2026.9.5 distribution and current upstream `main` have the same relevant branch structure: the CLI path returns before embedded setup invokes `resolveHookModelSelection(...)`.

## Impact and severity

- Affected: plugin authors and operators using CLI-backed models, including subscription-authenticated Claude CLI setups.
- Severity: blocks the documented hook-based per-turn routing workflow on the CLI runtime; no crash or data loss.
- Frequency: every observed CLI-backed turn in this setup.
- Consequence: all turns remain on the configured primary model unless the model is pinned manually at another boundary.

## Additional information

This is narrower than #62152/#62153: it does not request built-in keyword routing. The plugin hook already exists and is the supported extension surface; the bug is that the CLI execution path does not emit it. It also differs from #57941, where the hook fired but a model change in a persistent session was rejected.

A bounded implementation would invoke `before_model_resolve` during CLI preparation and initially accept only overrides that resolve to the already selected CLI backend. Cross-runtime overrides should fail explicitly or preserve the original selection with a warning. Relevant regression coverage should verify:

1. the hook fires once for a fresh CLI-backed turn;
2. a same-backend override changes the CLI model;
3. hook context reports the canonical logical provider;
4. a changed model replaces an incompatible warm child while retaining the native session binding; and
5. cross-runtime overrides are handled explicitly before a child process starts.

Current workaround: use explicit per-session, per-agent, or per-job model pins.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The built-in Anthropic shorthand table in `packages/model-catalog-core/src/provider-model-id-normalization.ts` (`normalizeBuiltInProviderModelId`) has two remaining problems on `main` (checked at `9e998a3a3`, after #155966):

1. **Bug: `sonnet` resolves to different models depending on the provider branch.** The `anthropic` branch maps `sonnet` → `claude-sonnet-5`. The `vercel-ai-gateway` branch of the same function maps `sonnet` → `claude-sonnet-4-6`:

   ```ts
   // anthropic branch
   "sonnet-5": "claude-sonnet-5",
   sonnet: "claude-sonnet-5",
   // vercel-ai-gateway branch
   "sonnet-5": "claude-sonnet-5",
   sonnet: "claude-sonnet-4-6",
   ```

   A user who writes the same shorthand gets the previous-generation model on one route and the current one on the other, with no warning.

2. **Request: move bare `opus` to `claude-opus-5-5`.** #155966 added Opus 5.5 (thanks!) and intentionally left the bare `opus` default on `claude-opus-5` ("Existing pinned models and the bare `opus` default remain unchanged"). Opus 5.5 is the successor in the Opus line, with the same 1M context / 128K output, and it is **cheaper** ($4/$20 vs $5/$25 per MTok). The unversioned shorthand therefore now picks the older, more expensive model. Could the maintainers either move `opus` → `claude-opus-5-5`, or state the criteria/timeline for doing so (e.g. once 5.5 leaves launch status)? If the current mapping is meant to stay, a note in `docs/providers/anthropic.md` saying that `opus` means Opus 5 would stop users from assuming it tracks the latest Opus.

Longer term, it may be worth deriving the unversioned shorthands (`opus`, `sonnet`, `fable`, `haiku`) from the newest non-deprecated catalogue row per family instead of a hand-maintained literal table. A unit test asserting "each unversioned shorthand resolves to the newest catalogue row in its family" would have caught the `sonnet` mismatch.

### Steps to reproduce

Against the released bundle (2026.9.1-beta.1; the `sonnet` mapping and bare `opus` behaviour are unchanged on `main`):

```js
const m = await import("<openclaw>/dist/provider-model-id-normalization-<hash>.js");
const norm = m.n; // normalizeBuiltInProviderModelId
console.log(norm("anthropic", "sonnet"));          // claude-sonnet-5
console.log(norm("vercel-ai-gateway", "sonnet"));  // anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
console.log(norm("anthropic", "opus"));            // claude-opus-5
```

Or read the two alias literals in `provider-model-id-normalization.ts` on `main`.

### Expected behavior

- `sonnet` resolves to the same model (`claude-sonnet-5`) through both the `anthropic` and `vercel-ai-gateway` branches.
- Bare `opus` resolves to the current Opus (`claude-opus-5-5`), or its pinning to Opus 5 is documented.

### Actual behavior

- `vercel-ai-gateway` + `sonnet` → `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`; `anthropic` + `sonnet` → `claude-sonnet-5`.
- `anthropic` + `opus` → `claude-opus-5`, although `claude-opus-5-5` is available, cheaper and supported (#155966).

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.1-beta.1 (1d96e5a); source behaviour re-checked on `main` @ `9e998a3a3`

### Operating system

Linux (WSL2), Node 24.15.0

### Install method

npm global

### Model

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 (shorthands `opus`, `sonnet`)

### Provider / routing chain

anthropic (api: anthropic-messages, agentRuntime: claude-cli); the `sonnet` mismatch is in the vercel-ai-gateway normalisation branch

### Additional provider/model setup details

The issue only shows up when no user alias catches the reference first. With an explicit alias map in `agents.defaults.models` (e.g. `"anthropic/claude-opus-5-5": { "alias": "opus" }`), the config-aware resolver honours the user alias even for `anthropic/opus`, so that is the current workaround. The built-in table still applies to users without alias maps and to call sites that use `normalizeBuiltInProviderModelId` / `normalizeStaticProviderModelIdWithPolicies` / `normalizeConfiguredProviderCatalogModelId` directly.

Related: #155966 (Opus 5.5 support), #137376 (static Anthropic aliases aligned with manifest).

### Impact and severity

Low–medium. Nothing errors, because both older models are still served. Users relying on the built-in shorthands quietly get a previous-generation model (`sonnet` via vercel-ai-gateway) or a more expensive one (`opus`).

issues.body:
**Summary.** Runs triggered by an inter-agent message (`sessions_send`) or by an async completion event are constructed with a **different tool roster** than runs triggered by a human message in the *same session*, with no tool-policy change in between. Because the tool list sits in the cached prefix, the first agent-sourced message arriving into a long-warm session costs a **full prompt-cache re-creation**.

Measured here at **159,387 cache-write tokens for a 4-character message payload**.

Environment: first observed on OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (`ec9c1a1`) and reproduced on `main` at `71cf3a4a16b` (see Steps to reproduce), Linux, `anthropic/claude-opus-5`, `agents.defaults.params.cacheRetention: "long"`.

---

## Steps to reproduce

**Reproduced on `main`** at `71cf3a4a16b` (2026-09-23 11:49 UTC), running from a source checkout, Linux, `anthropic/claude-opus-5`, `cacheRetention: "long"`, code mode enabled. The 2026.9.5 evidence further down still applies. On `main` the tools involved are different, but the mechanism and the cost are the same.

**Prerequisites**

- Two agents configured on one gateway: agent **A** (the observed session) and agent **B** (any second agent).
- **Neither side may be a subagent.** The relevant path is skipped when `requesterIsSubagent || targetIsSubagent`, so messaging a spawned subagent will *not* reproduce this.
- `diagnostics.cacheTrace.enabled: true`.

**Procedure**

1. In agent A's session, take a few ordinary human turns until the cache is warm.
2. Note the baseline from the latest `cache:state` snapshot: `toolCount`, `toolNames`, `toolDigest`, `systemPromptDigest`.
3. From agent A's session, call `sessions_send` to agent B's main session with a trivial payload.
4. B's reply is announced back into A's session as an inter-session message (`prompt:before` starts with `[Inter-session message] … isUser=false`), which starts a new run in A.
5. Compare that run's `cache:state` snapshot with the baseline, and read its first `cache:result`.

**Expected:** roster, `toolDigest` and `systemPromptDigest` unchanged; `cacheRead` keeps growing.

**Actual on `main`:**

```
run       origin               tools                                                toolDigest  stablePrefix  cacheRead  cacheWrite  broke
fc7078ad  human                exec, openclaw, sessions_yield, view_image, wait           e4d5ef002b  3edbb035      17168      158538      false
11f9534a  inter-session PONG   exec, message, openclaw, sessions_yield, view_image, wait  3d1fdd7894  0c4ee3ab      0          186580      false
```

The agent-sourced run **gained** `message`. On 2026.9.5 the change went the other way: five tools were *dropped*. So the direction differs between versions, but in both cases the roster depends on where the triggering message came from. The stable system-prompt digest changes as well, most likely because the `## Tooling` section follows the roster. A four-character payload cost **186,580 cache-write tokens**, and `broke` was reported `false` on a `cacheRead = 0` request.

**Variant needing only one agent.** A run triggered by an async completion event shows the same effect. Observed on `main` in an unrelated dashboard session, no deliberate probe:

```
time      origin            tools  toolDigest  stablePrefix  cacheRead  cacheWrite
13:05:47  human             5      e4d5ef002b  3edbb035      17168      29551
13:11:31  completion event  4      7a6cac860d  fcac6654      0          122458
13:13:03  human             5      e4d5ef002b  3edbb035      122874     4400
```

Here `openclaw` was dropped. The return to the human roster hit the older, still-live cache entry, so each non-human run costs one full re-cache, not two.

**Effect of code mode.** With code mode on, the provider-visible roster shrinks from about 50 tool schemas to 5–6. That makes the tool block smaller, but it does not stop the miss, because the roster still changes with origin and the system prompt follows it.

**Classifying runs by origin.** Join on `runId` across three trace stages: `prompt:before` gives the triggering text (agent-sourced runs carry the `[Inter-session message]` prefix), `cache:state` gives the roster, and `cache:result` gives the cost.

```python
import json
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open("cache-trace.jsonl") if l.strip()]
pb = {r["runId"]: (r.get("prompt") or "")[:40] for r in rows if r.get("stage") == "prompt:before"}
first = {}
for r in rows:
    if r.get("stage") == "cache:result":
        first.setdefault(r["runId"], r)
seen = set()
for r in sorted((r for r in rows if r.get("stage") == "cache:state"), key=lambda r: r["ts"]):
    if r["runId"] in seen:
        continue
    seen.add(r["runId"])
    s = r["options"]["snapshot"]
    o = first.get(r["runId"], {}).get("options", {})
    print(r["ts"][11:19], s["toolCount"], s["toolDigest"][:10], s.get("systemPromptDigest", "")[:8],
          "read=%s write=%s" % (o.get("cacheRead"), o.get("cacheWrite")),
          "|", pb.get(r["runId"], ""))
```

**What is and is not being reported.** Adjusting capabilities on a non-human-facing run may well be deliberate, and this report does not ask for authorization or client restrictions to be relaxed. The problem is that the adjusted roster sits **inside the cached prefix**, so a deliberate authority decision gets paid for as a full re-cache. One fix is to keep descriptors stable when the effective capabilities haven't changed. Another is to place the origin-dependent part after the cache breakpoint.

---

## Evidence 1 — same session, same minute, no tool policy at all

Session `agent:quip:main`, 2026-09-21. Crucially, `agents.entries.quip.tools` was **`null`** at this time — no profile, no allow, no deny. Verified from the config backup `openclaw.json.last-good`, timestamped 18:14 that same day. Configuration therefore cannot explain any of this.

```
18:13:21  human "ping"                    6 tools  [exec, gateway, secrets, session_status, web_fetch, web_search]
18:13:56  human                           6 tools  gateway present
18:13:59  "Agent-to-agent announce step"  5 tools  [exec,          secrets, session_status, web_fetch, web_search]
18:14:03  human                           6 tools  gateway present
18:14:05  "Agent-to-agent announce step"  5 tools  gateway absent
```

The roster alternates 6/6/5/6/5 within 44 seconds. The 5-tool runs are exactly the two agent-to-agent runs, and the tool they drop is `gateway`.

## Evidence 2 — measured cache cost in a warm session

Session `agent:main:dashboard:*`, 2026-09-22. Tool policy constant throughout (`tools.deny: ["automations","skill_workshop"]`, set before the window and unchanged). Origin classified from the `prompt:before` trace stage.

```
ts     origin  tools  toolDigest   suffixDigest   cacheRead  cacheWrite  broke
16:28  human   49     490545d7fa   b5d0aae45b94   107112     1268        false
16:38  agent   44     6d570bbb13   f31819f11efc   0          159387      false   <-- full miss
16:39  agent   44     6d570bbb13   f31819f11efc   38215      129032      true
17:18  human   49     490545d7fa   b5d0aae45b94   160749     14109       false
```

The message that caused the 16:38 miss was the 4-character string `PONG`, delivered via `sessions_send`.

Tools present on human-origin runs and **absent** on agent-origin runs:

```
dismiss_task, github_identity_status, screen, show_widget, suggest_task
```

No tools are added in the other direction. All five are human-surface/Control-UI tools, so omitting them from a non-human-facing run looks deliberate; the cache consequence appears not to have been costed.

Both the `toolDigest` **and** the `systemPromptSuffixDigest` change together on the origin switch.

## Evidence 3 — a third roster variant from a different non-human origin

Same session, 2026-09-21 19:05. A run triggered by an async completion event (not an inter-agent message) was built with **36** tools rather than 51, and also fully missed:

```
19:00:30  human             51 tools   read=163850  write=4136
19:05:13  completion event  36 tools   read=0       write=163798
19:07:43  human             51 tools   read=167986  write=7844
```

So at least three distinct rosters exist for one session depending only on what triggered the run.

## What does *not* happen (a prediction I got wrong)

Returning to human origin is **free**, provided it happens within the cache TTL. At 17:18 the roster reverted 44 → 49 and both digests came back byte-identical to their 16:28 values, re-hitting the older still-live cache entry (`read=160749`).

So the cost is **one** re-cache per inbound agent message, not two. Frequent alternation is cheap because both prefix variants stay warm; a single agent message into a long-warm session is the expensive case. Worth stating explicitly so the fix isn't mis-scoped.

## Diagnostic issues noticed along the way

1. **`broke` is unreliable for this class.** The `read=0` total miss at 16:38 reported `broke=false`, while the *partial* at 16:39 reported `broke=true`.
2. **Unexplained partial.** The 16:39 run had `toolDigest` *and* `systemPromptSuffixDigest` identical to the 16:38 run, yet read only 38,215 of the 159,387 tokens just written. Identical prefix, partial reuse. This may be independent of the roster bug.
3. **`systemPromptDigest` covers only the stable prefix.** The dynamic suffix is tracked separately as `systemPromptSuffixDigest`:
   ```js
   systemPromptDigest: digestText(splitSystemPrompt?.stablePrefix ?? params.systemPrompt),
   ...splitSystemPrompt ? { systemPromptSuffixDigest: digestText(splitSystemPrompt.dynamicSuffix) } : {},
   ```
   This is easy to misread as covering the whole system prompt — I spent a day measuring the wrong field and drew a false negative from it. Worth documenting, or naming the field `systemPromptStablePrefixDigest`.

## Requests

1. **Make tool construction depend on `(agent, session)` and not on what triggered the run** — or, if origin-varying tools are intentional, place them after the cache breakpoint so they don't invalidate the prefix.
2. **Record origin and tool-policy provenance in the `cache:state` snapshot.** It currently carries `toolDigest`/`toolCount`/`toolNames` but nothing saying *why* that roster was chosen. Classifying origin required joining against the `prompt:before` stage.
3. **Fix `broke` detection** so `cacheRead == 0` on a non-initial request is always reported.

## Possibly related: #146902

[#146902](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/146902) reports same-session tool-set churn where variants share a tool *count* but differ in *membership*, and asks maintainers to trace the source of the per-attempt allowlist on non-cron sessions, noting that only cron jobs could be accounted for.

Origin-dependent tool construction may be that answer. **I cannot confirm they are the same bug:** the tools involved differ from the ones here, that host is Windows on a different model and profile, and I have not reproduced their 43A/43B split. Filing separately rather than as a duplicate; closing one into the other is a maintainer call.

Their request 4 (the cache-trace redaction gate blocking prompt capture) is independently reproducible on this host.

Separate cache issues from this host, distinct causes: #155685 (rewind mints a new `sessionId` inside the cached suffix) and #155742 (two tool *schemas* alternating at identical roster and ordering).

*(Filed from local read-only diagnostics plus one deliberate `sessions_send` probe. Happy to share the analysis scripts or run an instrumented build.)*

issues.body:
## Summary

`openclaw dashboard` reports **"Gateway is not running."** on a host configured with `gateway.mode: "remote"`, even when the remote Gateway is healthy and reachable. The readiness check decides liveness purely from **local** signals (local port probe + local systemd unit) and never consults `gateway.mode`.

`openclaw tui` on the same host, with the same config, connects fine — so this is specifically a readiness-path gap, not a connectivity or auth problem.

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.9.5` (`ec9c1a1`), installed via mise (Node 26.8.2)
- Client host: Arch Linux (Omarchy 4.0.4)
- Gateway host: separate machine, reached over Tailscale at `wss://<host>.ts.net/`
- Client config:
  ```json
  { "gateway": { "mode": "remote",
                 "remote": { "transport": "direct", "url": "wss://<host>.ts.net/", "token": "..." } } }
  ```
- The same client host also runs `openclaw-node.service` (see second defect below)

## Reproduce

1. On host A, run a Gateway (loopback + Tailscale Serve).
2. On host B, configure the CLI with `gateway.mode: "remote"` pointing at A. Do **not** install a local gateway.
3. On host B:

```console
$ openclaw tui
# connects fine: "openclaw tui - wss://<host>.ts.net/ - agent main - session main"

$ openclaw dashboard --json
{"ok":false,"reason":"Gateway is not running."}
$ echo $?
0
```

Expected: `dashboard` resolves the remote Gateway's Control UI URL, consistent with `tui`.
Actual: reports the Gateway stopped. Note `--json` also exits **0** on failure, so callers must parse the body.

## Cause

`src/commands/gateway-readiness.ts:93`:

```ts
function gatewayLooksStopped(status: DaemonStatus): boolean {
  if (status.rpc && gatewayProbeResultSawGateway(status.rpc)) return false;
  const port = activeProbePortStatus(status);
  if (port?.status === "busy") return false;
  if (port?.status === "free") return true;          // <-- remote mode always lands here
  const runtimeStatus = status.service.runtime?.status;
  if (runtimeStatus === "stopped") return true;
  ...
}
```

In remote mode the local port is legitimately free (nothing local should be listening), so this returns `true` unconditionally.

`grep -n "mode" src/commands/gateway-readiness.ts` returns **nothing** — `gateway.mode` is never consulted in this file.

`src/commands/dashboard.ts` does import `isRemoteEnvironment` (line 4), but only uses it at line **203**, for a clipboard/browser fallback — long after `ensureGatewayReadyForOperation` at line **48** has already failed.

The codebase already has a consistent idiom for this, used in 8+ non-test sites:

- `src/tui/gateway-chat.ts:657` — `const isRemoteMode = config.gateway?.mode === "remote";` (this is why `tui` works)
- `src/gateway/probe-target.ts:17`, `src/gateway/tls-fingerprint.ts:23`, `src/node-host/runner.ts:155`, `src/gateway/auth-token-source-conflict.ts:37`

## Suggested fix

Short-circuit the readiness path in remote mode — a remote Gateway's liveness is a question about the remote RPC, not about a local port or unit. Roughly:

```ts
if (cfg.gateway?.mode === "remote") {
  // Liveness is whatever the remote RPC says; local port/unit signals are meaningless here.
  return status.rpc ? !gatewayProbeResultSawGateway(status.rpc) : false;
}
```

Happy to open a PR if the shape looks right.

## Downstream impact (why this bites harder than it looks)

Omarchy ships an OpenClaw launcher that gates on this call (`/usr/bin/omarchy-launch-openclaw`, pkg `omarchy 4.0.4-1`):

```bash
if ! url=$(dashboard_url); then
  if systemctl --user is-enabled --quiet openclaw-gateway.service 2>/dev/null; then
    timeout 60 openclaw gateway start >&2 || true
  else
    timeout 120 openclaw gateway install --force >&2 || true   # <-- installs a SECOND gateway
  fi
```

On a correctly-configured remote-mode host, the false "not running" sends this straight to `openclaw gateway install --force`, which installs a **second local Gateway** — with its own state dir, agents, workboard and scheduler — on a machine intended to be a pure client. That is a materially worse outcome than the launcher failing.

This also breaks Omarchy's Agent keybinding (`SUPER+SHIFT+CTRL+A` → `omarchy-agent --pick`) and `omarchy-agent-prompt`, which route through the same launcher: the terminal opens and exits immediately with no agent.

## Second, related defect: `gateway status` misreads `openclaw-node.service` as a Gateway unit

On a host running the **node** service with no local gateway:

```console
$ openclaw gateway status
Command: ... node run --host <gateway-host> --port 443 --tls
Service file: ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-node.service
Service config issue: Service command does not include the gateway subcommand
Gateway: bind=loopback (127.0.0.1), port=443 (service args)
Probe target: ws://127.0.0.1:443
Recommendation: ... reinstall with "openclaw gateway install --force"
```

It adopts `openclaw-node.service` as the gateway unit and reparses the node's `--host`/`--port` **client connection** args as gateway **bind** settings, synthesising a phantom loopback gateway on port 443 and then recommending `gateway install --force`. The node unit should be excluded from gateway unit discovery (it is detected as non-gateway — "does not include the gateway subcommand" — yet still used).

I suspect both defects go unnoticed because node-service + remote-CLI on one host is an uncommon combination; each is individually harmless in the usual local-gateway setup.

issues.body:
### Summary

The bundled `session-memory` hook names its snapshot artifacts (`memory/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md`) and stamps the `# Session:` header using `event.timestamp` — the moment the reset was **triggered** — rather than the time of the captured conversation **content**. For sessions that span midnight (or long-idle sessions, e.g. `session.reset.idleMinutes = 2880`), the artifact date and the content date disagree by up to days.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1), macOS 27.2 arm64, node v26.5.0
- `session.reset.idleMinutes = 2880` (48h); Telegram channel sessions that commonly span multiple days
- `hooks.internal.entries.session-memory = { enabled: true }` (default messages/llmSlug/model)

### Observed behavior

A Telegram session that ran Sep 21 14:59–15:38 was archived when the next inbound message arrived on Sep 22 08:56. Since auto-reset expiry is checked "when a subsequent turn is admitted" (per bundled-hooks docs), archiving always lands on the **next activity moment** — typically the following morning. The hook wrote `memory/2026-09-22-0856.md`: the filename date says today, but all captured content is from yesterday.

Reproducible on any cross-day session: the filename date is always the reset-trigger date, never the content date.

### Root cause

`dist/bundled/session-memory/handler.js`:

```js
const now = new Date(event.timestamp);
const localTimestamp = formatLocalSessionTimestamp(now, userTimezone);
const dateStr = localTimestamp.date; // filename prefix + "# Session:" header
```

The artifact date comes exclusively from the reset event time. None of the three hook options (`messages`, `llmSlug`, `model`) affect the date source — and `llmSlug: true` only replaces the `HHMM` suffix with a semantic slug; the date prefix still reflects the reset moment.

### Suggestion

The captured transcript already carries per-message timestamps, so deriving the artifact date from the last captured message is essentially free. Options:

1. Default `dateStr` to the timestamp of the last captured message instead of `event.timestamp`; or
2. Add a config option, e.g. `dateFrom: "reset" | "content"`, keeping current behavior as default if preferred.

Either fixes the misdating for long-lived/cross-day sessions without changing behavior for same-day sessions.

### Workaround

We disabled the hook (`openclaw hooks disable session-memory`) and archive memories via a scheduled job that reads the sqlite transcript store and buckets messages by their own timestamps. The built-in hook is otherwise great for continuity snapshots, so a fix would let us re-enable it.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Control UI Side chat is explicitly instructed to answer in American English, preventing normal language matching for non-English users, including Chinese-speaking users.

### Steps to reproduce

The reporter observes English-only replies in Control UI Side chat on OpenClaw 2026.9.5. A new browser/model reproduction was not performed while preparing this report.

The underlying restriction can be reproduced deterministically by inspecting the implementation:

1. Open `src/gateway/session-companion-ask.ts` at commit `aeff5c8d7438e32644d4617068918b8da936d625`.
2. Inspect `buildSystemPrompt(sessionKey)` at lines 106–119: the returned system prompt explicitly requires American English.
3. Inspect the call at line 596: the prompt builder receives only the session key, with no locale or response-language preference.

Suggested UI verification: open Side chat for a Chinese-language session and ask `这个会话目前在做什么？请用中文回答。` (What is this session doing? Please answer in Chinese.) Check whether the reply follows that request despite the conflicting system instruction.

### Expected behavior

Side chat should answer in the language of the operator's question and honor an explicit request for a response language. The UI locale could serve as a fallback when the question's language is ambiguous.

The Control UI documents Chinese and other supported UI locales, but its Side chat documentation does not describe an English-only response restriction. This is the requested behavior; no previously working release has been established.

- [Control UI language support](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui/settings#language-support)
- [Side chat documentation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui/chat#session-rail-and-side-chat)

### Actual behavior

The reporter experiences English-only Side chat replies. Both the installed 2026.9.5 bundle and upstream source contain this unconditional system instruction:

```text
Return a concise plain-text answer in American English with no markdown or JSON wrapper.
```

The prompt builder does not read a language/locale setting. Changing the Control UI display language therefore does not alter this instruction.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (installed package). The same instruction is present on upstream `main` at commit `aeff5c8d7438e32644d4617068918b8da936d625`.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0 (arm64)

### Install method

Global Node.js package installation.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

The effective Side chat utility model was not captured. This report establishes the language restriction in the shared prompt builder, not a model-specific failure.

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- [Hardcoded system prompt, lines 106–119](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/aeff5c8d7438e32644d4617068918b8da936d625/src/gateway/session-companion-ask.ts#L106-L119)
- [Prompt construction at the call site, line 596](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/aeff5c8d7438e32644d4617068918b8da936d625/src/gateway/session-companion-ask.ts#L596)
- Installed bundle: `dist/session-companion-ask-D7NFxIk3.mjs`, line 66, contains the identical English-only instruction.

### Impact and severity

Affected workflow: a Chinese-speaking user asking about a session through Control UI Side chat.

Severity: usability issue; replies are forced toward English even when the user needs Chinese. No crash or data loss is reported. The prompt restriction is unconditional; the number of observed UI attempts was not recorded.

### Additional information

Suggested fix: replace the fixed American-English instruction with a rule to follow the operator's requested language or the language of the current question, retaining the existing concise/plain-text constraints. Add coverage for a Chinese question, an explicit language override, and the normal English case.

Searched open and closed issues and PRs using Side chat/side-chat, language, English, Chinese, session-companion, and the exact phrase "American English"; no matching report or language fix was found.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (npm installation, Linux gateway)
- Control UI installed on an iPhone Home Screen
- Scheduled automation with Telegram delivery and web push notifications enabled

## Description

After a scheduled automation finishes, its conversation remains accessible through the stable automation session key, but links referring to the individual run no longer resolve.

This affects two navigation paths:

1. **Automations → Run history → Open run chat** displays “Session not found.”
2. Tapping the original **“OpenClaw agent finished”** web push notification opened the default/home view instead of the completed run’s conversation.

The automation itself succeeds, its summary appears in run history, and Telegram delivery succeeds.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a recurring automation that runs in an isolated session.
2. Let it complete successfully.
3. Open its run history and click **Open run chat**.
4. Separately, with web push enabled, tap its completion notification after the run finishes.

Use a retained/recurring job, not a self-deleting one-shot job: the observed failure does not require deletion of the job or its saved conversation.

## Expected behavior

Both links open the conversation associated with that specific completed run, including when newer runs exist.

## Actual behavior

The run-history button displays “Session not found.” Notification navigation was also observed opening the default view.

## Investigation

On the affected installation, after completion:

```text
agent:main:cron:<job-id>:run:<session-id>
```

No longer resolves, and `chat.history` returns no messages.

However:

```text
agent:main:cron:<job-id>
```

Resolves successfully and returns the completed conversation. The stable session entry's session ID matches the completed run. The short session ID used by the run's chat route also fails to resolve.

Relevant code paths in v2026.9.4:

- `src/tasks/cron-run-continuation-cleanup.ts` removes the idle run alias after the base session is persisted, without archiving the transcript.
- `ui/src/pages/cron/view-runs.ts` builds “Open run chat” from the run entry’s `sessionKey` (both the link destination and the navigation callback use that reference).
- `src/gateway/event-web-push.ts` builds the notification destination from the event’s session key.

This appears to be a mismatch between the lifetime of run aliases and the links generated for completed runs.

## Local workaround and limitations

We applied a local patch that directs automation-completion notifications to the stable automation session. This does not fix the run-history button and can open a newer conversation when tapping an older notification. End-to-end iPhone navigation after that patch is not yet confirmed.

The run-history failure and failed run-reference lookups were reproduced after applying that narrowly scoped notification patch. The notification landing on the default view was observed before the patch.

A durable fix should preserve navigation to the specific historical run rather than silently substituting the latest run.

## Related reports

- #131816 covers the behavior of the UI when an explicit session link does not resolve. This report concerns completed automations generating references that cleanup subsequently removes.
- #134373 covers a listed but undeletable cron session and a cleanup race. Here the run alias is absent, while the stable session still exposes the saved conversation.

All identifiers above are placeholders. No private transcript content or credentials are included.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Anthropic's fast/incremental tool-argument streaming skips Anthropic's own server-side JSON validation, and when a streamed argument value comes back malformed in a way that isn't just escape-sequence damage, the tool call fails with a generic, undiagnosable error. The process doesn't crash or hang: prompting the agent to continue sometimes lets it proceed, but that's inconsistent, not a reliable recovery path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Prompt your OpenClaw agent (2026.9.4, embedded runtime, Anthropic transport, `claude-sonnet-5` or `claude-opus-5`) to make a large or complex file edit, for example rewriting a large section of a file or writing out a multi-KB file.
2. The agent issues an `edit` or `write` tool call with a multi-KB argument payload to carry out the request.
3. The tool call intermittently fails with `Provider completed tool call with malformed JSON arguments`.
4. If you prompt the agent to retry the identical edit, it fails again, at the same byte position in the argument stream.

No deterministic minimal reproduction found; this only reproduces intermittently on large or complex payloads, not on every call. Prompting the agent to continue, rather than asking it to retry the identical edit, sometimes lets it proceed instead, though not reliably.

### Expected behavior

When I ask my agent to make a large or complex edit, it should complete the edit normally, not intermittently fail with a generic, undiagnosable error that only sometimes clears itself when I prompt it to continue.

With eager/fine-grained tool-argument streaming disabled (our local patch, described below), the exact same tool calls that had been failing succeed every time with valid JSON. That confirms normal buffered validation produces well-formed arguments, and the failure only appears once the fast-path streaming is enabled.

### Actual behavior

My agent's tool call fails with `Provider completed tool call with malformed JSON arguments`. It doesn't crash or hang the session; prompting it to continue sometimes lets it proceed, inconsistently. Either way, the error I see reads like a generic transport failure, with nothing diagnosable in the session's own output.

Code-level cause: OpenClaw's Anthropic transport streams tool-call arguments via `eager_input_streaming` (on by default for any non-Fireworks provider) or its fallback, the `fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14` beta header, both of which skip server-side validation to cut streaming latency. The client-side `repairJson` pass (`repairStringLiterals: true`) only fixes a narrow class of damage (bad escapes, stray control characters, unsafe integer literals), not a value that was never JSON-string-encoded at all. We captured one such payload: an `edit` tool call's `oldText` field broke immediately after the key. Valid JSON needs `: "` to open the string; instead the stream had a bare `>`, then fell straight into raw, unescaped file content for the rest of that field. The sibling `newText` field, later in the same object, was fully valid escaped JSON, so the corruption was localized to that one byte position, not a general encoding failure for the whole call.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4, embedded runtime

### Operating system

openclaw -> anthropic (direct, `anthropic-messages` provider), no proxy or router in between

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

Not pasting the raw captured payload here since it was a snippet of a private file being edited at the time; happy to share privately if useful. The error visible outside `journalctl` is generic (`Provider completed tool call with malformed JSON arguments`, no further detail); the real `rawError`, including the raw payload, only shows up in `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway`, not in default session output or default `logging.level`.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Impact and severity

Affected: anyone relying on Anthropic tool calls with large or complex arguments via OpenClaw's embedded runtime.
Severity: mid-task tool-call failures with a generic, undiagnosable error; not a crash or hang, but reprompting to recover is inconsistent, not reliable.
Frequency: intermittent, correlated with payload size and complexity, not proven deterministic; reproduced across four independent real sessions over about two weeks.
Consequence: work stalls on an unclear error until the operator reprompts (which doesn't reliably help) or already has `logging.level` raised or a diagnostic patch in place to see what actually happened.

### Additional information

What we did locally, since this reads as a real trade-off rather than a repair-heuristic bug, and our own UI never renders tool arguments incrementally anyway: patched the Anthropic transport to disable both streaming-without-validation mechanisms (`convertAnthropicTools`'s `compat.supportsEagerToolInputStreaming` forced `false`, `shouldUseFineGrainedToolStreamingBeta()` forced to always return `false`). A few options that might be worth considering upstream: a config knob to disable eager/fine-grained tool-argument streaming for the Anthropic transport, for anyone who'd rather trade latency for reliability; preferring a validated streaming mode by default if Anthropic offers one; or at minimum, surfacing the real underlying error to the session instead of the generic terminal message, so this is diagnosable without raising `logging.level` or patching in custom diagnostics.

### Summary

`workboard_release` correctly clears the claim (token/ownerId/heartbeat metadata removed from `metadata.claim`), but does not change the card's `status` field when no explicit `status` argument is passed — the card is left at `status: "running"` with no active claim, an inconsistent state (looks actively worked-on but isn't claimed by anyone).

Related to, but distinct from, #127785 (`workboard_move` leaves a *stale claim* after a status change). This is close to the inverse: `workboard_release` correctly clears the claim but leaves a *stale status*.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.5, gateway-native workboard plugin

### Repro (step by step)

1. `workboard_create` a scratch card (status `todo`).
2. `workboard_claim <id>` → card moves to `running`, `metadata.claim` set.
3. `workboard_release(id, token)` — no `status` argument passed.
4. `workboard_read <id>`:

**Actual:** `status: "running"`, `metadata.claim` absent (correctly cleared) — but an events entry of kind `"claimed"` is appended rather than a `"released"`-style event, and the card visibly still reads as actively running to anything inspecting `status` alone.

**Expected:** either `workboard_release` without an explicit `status` defaults to a sensible released state (e.g. `todo` or `ready`), or the docs/tool description make explicit that callers must always pass `status` on release, since the current default (leave status untouched) produces a card that looks claimed-and-running to any consumer that only checks `status`, not `metadata.claim`.

### Why this matters

Found while building a Workboard-based concurrency/reap layer on top of `workboard_claim`/`workboard_reclaim`/`workboard_dispatch` — any caller relying on `status` alone (rather than also checking `metadata.claim` presence) to decide whether a card is actively being worked will treat a released card as still running, and may skip re-dispatching it.

### Suggested fix

Either default `workboard_release` (no explicit `status`) to a defined released status, or make the current explicit-status-required behavior clearly documented in the tool description, since it's easy to assume release implies un-running.

## Summary
Two OpenClaw defects affect a native approval-gated CLI turn. The first loses the history admission needed to complete an approved command. The second sends a synthetic native-auth marker through the HTTP Anthropic transport.

## Defect 1: approved exec returns `auth-unknown`

Environment: OpenClaw `2026.10.10-beta.1`, Claude CLI, native approval in a direct message.

Reproduction: issue one harmless command requiring native approval, choose Allow Once, and observe `approval-request-failed`; the command does not execute.

Observed evidence: `auth-unknown` at `14:09:16.471 PDT`, followed by a normal resumed CLI turn (`trigger=user useResume=true session=present reuse=reusable`). In `src/agents/cli-runner/history-boundary.ts:134-146`, `prepareCliHistoryBoundaryOnce` returns no writer when the session target, session id/key, or admitted-run assertion does not match. `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts:1463-1473` maps the missing writer to `auth-unknown`.

Expected: the approved continuation preserves the admitted session target and history boundary and executes exactly once.

## Defect 2: synthetic native auth is sent as `x-api-key`

After the healthy native CLI auth check, `extensions/anthropic/provider-discovery.js:177-203` returns `CLAUDE_CLI_NATIVE_AUTH_MARKER`; its catalog path at `:205-257` publishes the `claude-cli` backend with `api=anthropic-messages`. `provider-request-config-DSpBEbyp.mjs:255-262` applies the marker as the configured auth header, and `ai-transport-host-CcZkAnMD.mjs:393-447` sends the request. The service returns `401 invalid x-api-key` at `13:39:36.143 PDT`, `13:42:04.406 PDT`, and `14:09:29.421 PDT`.

These defects share runtime context but have different causes. The first is a history-boundary admission failure. The second misroutes native authentication into an HTTP API-key header. No supported configuration-only fix is known, and disabling the Anthropic plugin removes the Claude CLI provider.

## Requested fix

1. Preserve the matching session target, session id/key, and admitted-run assertion across an approved continuation. Add a regression test for a normal resumed approval.
2. Keep native CLI authentication on the CLI backend. Do not pass the synthetic native-auth marker to an HTTP provider as `x-api-key`. Add a regression test for model discovery and transport selection.
3. Document the supported behavior and failure diagnostics.

No credentials, customer data, user identifiers, Slack IDs, local paths, or host-specific details are included.

issues.body:
# Bug: Slack plugin rejects JSON-escaped string params (`after`/`before`) — double-encoded tool args throw instead of being unescaped

## Environment

- OpenClaw CLI/Gateway: `2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)`
- Plugin: `@openclaw/slack` `2026.9.4` (installed via plugin npm project dir)
- Runtime: Node 26.8.2, macOS (LaunchAgent gateway)
- Channel config: 7 Slack bot accounts (socket mode), multi-agent setup

## Symptom

Gateway log fills with repeating CLI-command failures (observed every ~5-10s across all accounts, 878 occurrences in one day):

```
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: Invalid Slack read after timestamp ""1789746438.595899"": expected a Slack timestamp or ISO-8601 date string
```

Note the doubled quotes in the message: `""1789746438.595899""` — the incoming string value literally contains surrounding `"` characters.

## Root cause

In `@openclaw/slack/dist/actions-*.js`:

```js
const SLACK_TIMESTAMP_RE = /^\d+(?:\.\d+)?$/;
function normalizeSlackReadTimestamp(raw, field) {
  const trimmed = raw?.trim();
  if (!trimmed) return;
  if (SLACK_TIMESTAMP_RE.test(trimmed)) return trimmed;
  if (!ISO_8601_TIMESTAMP_SCHEMA.safeParse(trimmed).success)
    throw new Error(`Invalid Slack read ${field} timestamp "${trimmed}": ...`);
  ...
}
```

`readSlackMessages()` passes tool-call params straight through:

```js
after: readStringParam$1(actionParams, "after"),
```

When an LLM agent invokes the `slack read` tool with the timestamp **JSON-encoded twice** (i.e. the string argument value is itself `"1789746438.595899"` including quote characters), the regex fails and the plugin throws. This is a common LLM tool-arg encoding mistake — we saw it produced by 7 different agent accounts, so it's a behavioral pattern, not one bad agent.

Expected behavior: a JSON-escaped string param should be unescaped once before validation (or the validator should tolerate/trim surrounding quotes), instead of a hard error that surfaces as a CLI failure in the gateway log with no actionable feedback to the calling agent.

## Reproduction

Call the Slack `read` action with:

```json
{ "channelId": "C0123ABC", "after": "\"1789746438.595899\"" }
```

→ throws `Invalid Slack read after timestamp ...` (value is a valid Slack ts once unescaped).

## Suggested fix (either)

1. In `normalizeSlackReadTimestamp`, strip surrounding quotes before validation:
   ```js
   const trimmed = raw?.trim().replace(/^["']+|["']+$/g, "");
   ```
2. Better: fix at the SDK layer — `openclaw/plugin-sdk/param-readers` `readStringParam` should unescape a double-JSON-encoded string value (i.e. if the string parses as JSON and yields a string, return the inner value). This fixes the whole class of bugs for all plugins, not just Slack timestamps.

## Workaround applied locally

Patched `normalizeSlackReadTimestamp` in the installed plugin dist to strip surrounding quotes; verified errors stopped immediately after gateway restart (0 recurrences vs 878/day prior). Note this is overwritten on plugin update.

### Summary

An ordinary native Codex parent can lose access to its existing children when a forced-message initial turn is followed by an automatic completion turn: the delivery-mode change alters the registered tool catalog and rotates the parent thread.

### Steps to reproduce

The deterministic reproduction is `extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-child-continuity.test.ts` in PR #155353. It uses the real tool builder, bridge, binding store, and thread lifecycle with a protocol-fake native app-server/task tree; it is not a live Codex end-to-end reproduction.

1. Build the ordinary parent catalog for an initial turn with forced message delivery, which registers `message`.
2. Start the native parent thread and create a child in that task tree.
3. Build the same parent catalog for an automatic completion turn where message execution is not enabled.
4. Resume the parent and attempt to interact with the existing child.
5. With the pre-fix tool builder, observe that the catalog change causes a different parent thread and breaks child access. The proposed fix preserves continuity in both regression cases.

### Expected behavior

The regression asserts that a delivery-mode-only transition preserves the parent thread and existing child access. Message execution must remain denied on turns where it is not authorized; stable schema registration must not widen executable tool permissions.

### Actual behavior

The initial catalog includes `message`, while the automatic completion catalog omits it. That catalog difference rotates the native parent thread, leaving the existing child outside the new parent task tree. PR #155353 records two failing regression cases before the fix and two passing afterward, covering both advertised native-child capability shapes.

### OpenClaw version

Source-level reproduction accompanying PR #155353 (proposed fix commit: 8d3955f3de684c334c638ae0b39c0be4890c410d). Exact affected released version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

Source-level regression test; no deployment verification is claimed.

OpenClaw native Codex app-server integration; protocol-fake app-server in the regression test.

- Proposed fix and recorded verification: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155353
- Regression test: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8d3955f3de684c334c638ae0b39c0be4890c410d/extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-child-continuity.test.ts

- No live native-child end-to-end run, deployment, or recovery of already-separated task trees is claimed.

### Impact and severity

Affected workflow: an ordinary native Codex parent with existing children across this delivery-mode transition. The regression demonstrates loss of parent/child continuity, blocking further interaction with the existing child from the replacement parent thread. Production frequency and affected release range: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

Proposed fix: #155353. It stabilizes registration of the ordinary-turn message schema while retaining current-turn execution authorization and leaving restricted/subagent catalogs unchanged.
