issues.body:
### Summary

In team mode (Show all agents), keep each agent's non-empty named session groups visible under that agent instead of flattening every conversation into pinned/recent.

### Problem to solve

Named session groups are how operators actually run a busy Gateway: planning vs implementation, one product vs another, life-admin vs engineering. In a single-agent sidebar those groups are first-class. Switching to team mode throws that structure away.

Team mode is the right place to scan the whole roster — every agent, one list — but the current flatten makes that scan worse, not better. Sessions that were already sorted into “Project — Development” or “Ops” become an undifferentiated pile under the agent header. The operator has to either:

- stay in a single-agent sidebar and lose the fleet view, or
- use team mode and re-find work by title, recency, or memory.

The grouping did not become less valuable because more agents are on screen. It became more valuable: team mode is where you are trying to answer “where is this work, across the roster?” without clicking into each agent.

This is not a missing power-user flourish. Groups are already the Control UI's organization model. Team mode is the only primary session list that refuses to use them.

### Proposed solution

When **Show all agents / team mode** is on:

- Keep the agent header as the top-level scan unit (name/avatar still opens Home).
- Under each **expanded** agent, render that agent's **non-empty named session groups**, with the same membership as the single-agent sidebar for that agent.
- Preserve pinned sessions in their current team-mode place (agent-level pinned), then grouped conversations, then ungrouped/recent.
- Hide empty groups. A long catalog of empty headings under every agent would be worse than today's flatten.
- Do not add group create/rename/delete or nested groups in this request. Do not invent a cross-agent super-group. Membership stays whatever the session already has.

**Hierarchy decision:** Team mode remains agent-first: agent → named group → that agent's sessions. If two agents have sessions labeled `Planning`, render a `Planning` heading beneath each agent, not one cross-agent `Planning` bucket. Each session appears once under its own agent. This is a view of existing session categories, not a new relationship between agents and groups or a claim that multiple agents own one session.

Expected shape:

```text
main
  Project — Development
    Issue #120 / PR #…
  Ops
    weekly planning
  Other
    ungrouped chats
research
  Project — Planning
    …
```

Out of scope:

- Nested groups ([#137107](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/137107))
- Unpinning Home into a group ([#148573](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/148573))
- Per-agent group catalog ownership ([#142226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/142226)) — if that lands, team mode should still show each agent's own non-empty groups
- Completeness of members beyond the team-mode roster window ([#126701](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/126701)) — do not promise a group is complete if the roster page did not load those rows

### Alternatives considered

- **Keep the flatten.** Weak: team mode then cannot answer the question it exists for. Recency is a poor substitute for workstream identity once an agent has more than a handful of live conversations.
- **A global group list that spans agents.** Weak: group identity is still entangled with agent scope ([#142226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/142226), [#115348](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/115348)). Mixing every agent's “Planning” into one bucket would hide ownership.
- **Only use the Sessions page / filters.** Weak: that is a second surface. The daily path is the sidebar. Groups already work there for one agent.
- **Show every catalog group, including empty ones.** Weak: empty cross-agent headings already confused operators in the single-agent sidebar. Repeating that under every agent would make team mode unreadable.

### Impact

- **Affected:** Operators who use named session groups and also use Show all agents / team mode. This is the normal multi-agent Control UI path, not an edge case.
- **Severity:** Workflow friction. Nothing crashes, but the organization you already maintain becomes invisible in the view meant for supervising the whole team.
- **Frequency:** Every time team mode is used on a Gateway with grouped sessions.
- **Consequence:** Extra hunting, more agent-switching, and a strong incentive to stop using team mode (or to stop grouping) even though both features exist specifically to reduce that load.

The value is recovered attention: groups already encode “what this conversation is for.” Team mode should reuse that signal so you can scan the fleet by workstream, not by whichever session happened to move last.

### Evidence/examples

Current team-mode projection does not call the category grouping path. It rebuilds each agent as pinned + recent only:

```ts
// ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-navigation.ts
const sections = roster?.agentIds.flatMap((agentId) => {
  const agentRows = rows.filter((row) => this.sessionNavigationAgentId(row) === agentId);
  return [true, false].map((pinned) => ({
    id: `agent:${agentId}:${pinned ? "pinned" : "recent"}` as const,
    rows: agentRows.filter((row) => row.pinned === pinned),
  }));
});
```

The roster renderer then only accepts those agent-prefixed sections, so `category:…` groups never appear:

```ts
// ui/src/components/sidebar-agent-roster.ts
const sections = this.sections.filter((section) =>
  section.id.startsWith(`agent:${card.id}:`),
);
```

The session-list toolbar that exposes grouping is also omitted in roster/team mode (`app-sidebar-session-list-render.ts`). Docs describe team mode as sessions under collapsible agent headers, with no group preservation: https://docs.openclaw.ai/web/control-ui

Related, not duplicates:

- [#150466](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150466) — team-mode row/chevron polish; mentions groups only as a reason an agent might expand
- [#142226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/142226) — other agents' groups leaking into a single-agent sidebar (opposite direction)
- [#126701](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/126701) — named groups truncated by the global roster page
- [#103431](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/103431) — original grouped sidebar, closed; team mode landed later without carrying groups through

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Team mode and multi-user boundary

Team mode is a multi-**agent** view, not a multi-user permission model. Render group headings only from sessions already loaded **and visible to the current viewer**. This change adds no group create, rename, delete, or membership controls and grants no new access. The current group catalog is Gateway-wide; showing the same name under two agents does not create independently owned groups. Agent-scoped catalog ownership remains #142226.

### Additional information

We will implement this as a presentation-only slice:

- Reuse the existing category partition on each agent's already-loaded team-mode rows.
- Keep agent-level pins and Home-on-header navigation.
- Omit empty groups and omit group management / grouping-toolbar controls in team mode.
- Group headings must not imply complete membership; team mode still uses the bounded shared roster.

If completeness, empty-group policy, or per-agent catalog ownership need product decisions, they stay on the issues above rather than blocking this visibility gap.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (also verified 2026.9.4 and 2026.8.2 type definitions), macOS 14.8
- Affected plugin: `@wecom/wecom-openclaw-plugin` 2026.9.15 (latest npm release at time of writing)

## What happens
The plugin's `wecom-cli` tool calls `getWeComRuntime().config.loadConfig()` (`dist/src/cli/tool.js`, `resolveBot()` and `resolveBinPath()`). `loadConfig` was removed from `PluginRuntimeCore.config` (see the SDK migration guide, `docs/plugins/sdk-migration/how-to-migrate.md`: "`loadConfig` and `writeConfigFile` have been removed from the plugin runtime"), so the call throws a TypeError at runtime.

The plugin catches the error and rewrites it as "插件运行时未初始化，无法读取 openclaw 配置" ("plugin runtime not initialized"). The runtime is actually initialized — the API no longer exists. This made diagnosis significantly harder; it required source-level tracing to find the real cause.

## Impact
- `wecom-cli` tool is completely broken on OpenClaw 2026.9.x with the latest wecom plugin.
- The wecom channel messaging path is unaffected (different code path), so the failure is isolated to plugin tools that read config via the runtime.

## Local workaround (verified)
Patching both call sites to the documented replacement `config.current()` restores full functionality against 2026.9.5.

## Requests
1. Consider a short-lived compatibility shim (alias `loadConfig` → `current()`, or throw a descriptive "removed API — see migration guide" error) to soften the transition for third-party plugins.
2. Consider detecting references to removed SDK APIs at plugin load time and surfacing an explicit "plugin X uses removed API Y and needs an upgrade" warning, instead of letting plugins fail later with generic/misleading runtime errors.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Assistant-emitted **tool-call markup** is delivered verbatim to the channel. When a CLI-backed agent writes its tool calls as *text* instead of invoking them, the raw markup (`<invoke name="Bash">`, `<parameter name="command">…</parameter>`) is normalized as ordinary assistant text and sent to Telegram as a user-visible message.

In our case this produced a single ~40 KB Telegram message consisting of several hundred literal `<invoke name="Bash">` blocks, mostly `echo end1` … `echo end826`, in a shared group topic.

This is the same class as #88128 / #89151 (Codex/Harmony protocol fragments reaching channels), but a different markup family. The guard added by #89151 does not cover it.

**Where the gap is** — `src/auto-reply/tokens.ts` on current `main`:

```ts
const HARMONY_CHANNEL_MARKER_RE = /^\s*(?:set-thought\s+)?<[\w]*\|[^>]*>\s*$/;
const BOX_DRAWING_HR_ONLY_RE = /^\s*─{3,}\s*$/;

export function isInternalFormattingArtifact(text: string | undefined): boolean {
  if (!text) {
    return false;
  }
  return HARMONY_CHANNEL_MARKER_RE.test(text) || BOX_DRAWING_HR_ONLY_RE.test(text);
}
```

Anthropic-style tool markup (`<invoke name=…>`, `<parameter name=…>`, `<function_calls>`, `<invoke …>`) matches neither regex, so it passes straight through `normalizeReplyPayload` to every messaging channel.

Note on prior art: #132863 was closed as already implemented, pointing at requiring source-chat replies to go through the explicit message tool (`messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`). That is a *global* posture change — every turn without an explicit send becomes silent — so it is not a usable mitigation for setups that rely on normal assistant replies. It also does not address the artifact class itself, which is what #89151 established as in-scope for the shared normalizer.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an agent on the `claude-cli` backend bound to a Telegram group topic.
2. Drive a long multi-tool turn until the model degrades into emitting tool calls as literal text rather than as tool-use blocks (in our run this followed a series of tool calls that returned empty output; the model shrank its probes to `echo ping`, `echo x`, then `echo end1` … `echo end826`).
3. The assistant text block containing the literal `<invoke …>` markup is normalized as a regular reply and delivered to the topic.

We do not have a deterministic minimal repro — the trigger is model-side degradation. The delivery-side defect is deterministic and reviewable from the source above: no guard exists for this markup family.

### Expected behavior

A standalone assistant text block that consists only of tool-call markup is treated like other internal formatting artifacts: dropped in the shared reply normalizer via the existing silent-skip path, before channel delivery, with no empty-response fallback message.

### Actual behavior

The markup is delivered verbatim as a user-visible chat message. There is no supported way to prevent it short of the global `visibleReplies: "message_tool"` posture change:

- `message.*` / hook interception is documented as observational (`do not block, cancel, or rewrite`).
- Telegram transport only chunks oversized text; it cannot reject it.
- `isInternalFormattingArtifact` is the one content-level gate in the path and does not cover this family.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.2 (gap verified unchanged on current `main`, and in v2026.9.5)

### Operating system

Linux 7.0.0-29-generic (x64)

### Install method

npm global (`/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw`)

### Model

claude-opus-5

### Provider / routing chain

claude-cli → anthropic/claude-opus-5

### Additional provider/model setup details

Agent bound to a Telegram forum topic; normal (non-`message_tool`) reply delivery.

### Logs

Gateway logs for the affected day were already rotated out, so no runtime log is attached. The delivered message is the artifact; a sanitized excerpt:

```
echo end584
echo end585
…
echo end826
<invo
```

(The trailing `<invo` is the message truncated mid-markup by the channel size limit.)

### Suggested fix

Extend `isInternalFormattingArtifact` with a narrow, anchored matcher in the same shape as #89151 — matching only blocks whose entire content is tool-invocation markup, e.g. text that consists solely of `<(antml:)?invoke …>` / `<(antml:)?parameter …>` / `<function_calls>` elements and whitespace. Anchored and whole-block only, so prose that merely quotes such a tag (documentation, this issue) is unaffected.

Happy to open a PR if the approach is acceptable.

issues.body:
## Summary

Three related problems in memory indexing made a straightforward provider-side bug take hours to diagnose. All three are in the embeddings path; none require the provider bug to be interesting.

Version: **2026.9.4**. Provider: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible endpoint), model `text-embedding-3-small`.

## 1. One error message for six distinct conditions

`readEmbeddingVectors` throws `"<provider> embeddings failed: malformed JSON response"` from six different checks:

| condition | what actually happened |
|---|---|
| `!Array.isArray(data)` | response has no `data` array — the only genuine "malformed JSON" |
| `data.length !== expectedCount` | valid JSON, wrong number of vectors returned |
| `!Array.isArray(embedding) \|\| embedding.length === 0` | vector missing or empty |
| `indexed !== usesIndex` | some entries carry `index`, others don't |
| coordinate not finite | `NaN` / `Infinity` inside a vector |
| `index` out of range or duplicated | index collision |

The message names only the first. In our case the actual condition was the last one — the provider returned duplicate `index` values — and the wording sent everyone looking for corrupt UTF-8 in the source files instead.

It also names neither the file nor the chunk, so there is nothing to narrow down from.

**Suggestion:** distinguish the conditions in the message, and include what was observed (`expected N vectors, got M`, `duplicate index 1 at position 2`). A caller can act on that; `malformed JSON response` is unactionable.

## 2. One bad batch aborts the whole run and pauses search

A single failing batch ends the entire indexing run. Everything embedded successfully in that run is discarded — we observed `Indexed: 0/65 files · 0 chunks` after 15 successful embedding requests — and the agent is left at:

```
Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt
```

Semantic search then silently returns nothing until a human notices. For an assistant that relies on memory recall, the failure mode is invisible: it simply stops remembering.

**Suggestion:** skip the batch that failed validation, keep the rest, finish the run, and report the skipped units. A partially built index that says so beats no index at all.

There is a related trap: repeated runs appear to "fix" the problem, because the embedding cache shrinks the remaining work until a batch happens to succeed. That masks the real state — `openclaw memory reset` is the only way to see it.

## 3. `OPENCLAW_DEBUG_MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS` produces no output for remote providers

The flag exists (`embeddings-debug.ts`) but every `debugEmbeddingsLog` call site is on the **Gemini** batch path — upload, create, status, download, plus the Gemini client. There is not a single call on the `openai` path, so enabling the documented debug switch prints nothing at all when an OpenAI-compatible endpoint misbehaves.

Related: patching `globalThis.fetch` does not intercept these requests either — the embeddings client uses its own transport with an SSRF policy (`fetchImpl`). Verified positively: an `--import` loader loads in every process, including the sqlite workers, and observes zero requests. Diagnosing this class of problem currently requires putting a proxy in front of the endpoint.

**Suggestion:** log request/response shape (input count, returned count, status, first entry shape) for remote providers behind the existing flag.

## Reproducing the trigger

Not required to act on any of the above, but for completeness: the upstream returned `data[*].index` values with duplicates (e.g. `[0,1,0]` for three inputs) while status was 200, the JSON was valid and the count matched. `readEmbeddingVectors` rejected it correctly — the problem is purely in how that rejection is reported and handled.

issues.body:
### Summary

In the memory-wiki Related auto-blocks, when a page's backlink count exceeds `MAX_SHARED_SOURCE_FANOUT` (24), the entire "Referenced By" section is silently cleared and rendered as "No related pages yet." — instead of truncating to the first `MAX_RELATED_PAGES_PER_SECTION` (12) entries. The same constant also causes "Related Pages" to drop *all* candidates that share a source page with fanout > 24, rather than excluding only that shared source or truncating.

Highly connected hub pages (entities/concepts referenced by many notes) — precisely the pages where backlinks are most useful — lose their backlinks section completely.

### Affected version

- OpenClaw v2026.9.5
- Location: `dist/presentation-Dno2xLFC.mjs` (bundled), around line 2332

### Code

```js
const MAX_RELATED_PAGES_PER_SECTION = 12;   // line 1944
const MAX_SHARED_SOURCE_FANOUT = 24;        // line 1945

// line 2332 — the bug:
const backlinkPages = backlinks.length <= MAX_SHARED_SOURCE_FANOUT
  ? backlinks.slice(0, MAX_RELATED_PAGES_PER_SECTION)
  : [];                                     // ← whole block emptied above 24
```

The "Related Pages" filter (line ~2338) has the same shape: candidates are included only if `(sourceFanout.get(sourceId) ?? 0) <= MAX_SHARED_SOURCE_FANOUT`, so a shared source with >24 fanout excludes the candidate entirely rather than just skipping that source.

### Current behavior

- Page with ≤24 backlinks → "Referenced By" shows up to 12 entries. ✅
- Page with >24 backlinks → "Referenced By" shows "No related pages yet." ❌ (data exists, block wiped)
- Related Pages: candidates sharing a >24-fanout source are excluded wholesale. ❌

### Expected behavior

Truncate instead of clearing:

- Show the first 12 backlinks (respecting `MAX_RELATED_PAGES_PER_SECTION`), optionally with a footer like `…and N more`.
- For Related Pages, skip only the over-fanout *source id* when matching, not the whole candidate.
- Alternatively, make the fanout cap configurable so large vaults can raise it.

### Reproduction

1. Build a vault where one wiki page accumulates more than 24 backlinks (e.g. an entity page referenced across dozens of daily notes).
2. Run `openclaw wiki compile` and open the page's Related auto-blocks.
3. Observe "Referenced By" renders "No related pages yet." even though 25+ backlinks exist.

Confirmed on a production vault with:

- `entity.eric-kii` — 52 backlinks → block emptied
- `concept.book-library-system` — 42 backlinks → block emptied

### Workaround

Local patch replacing line 2332 with an unconditional truncation, then re-running `openclaw wiki compile --agent main`:

```diff
-const backlinkPages = backlinks.length <= MAX_SHARED_SOURCE_FANOUT ? backlinks.slice(0, MAX_RELATED_PAGES_PER_SECTION) : [];
+const backlinkPages = backlinks.slice(0, MAX_RELATED_PAGES_PER_SECTION);
```

Note this needs re-applying after every upgrade since the dist file name is hashed (we keep a re-patch script). A fix upstream (or a config knob) would remove the need for that.

Happy to provide additional details from the affected vault if useful.

issues.body:
## Problem

`workboard.cards.archive` accepts cards in every lifecycle status. Archiving a `ready`, `running`, or other non-terminal card sets `metadata.archivedAt` without changing its status, creating an `archived_but_active` row.

This is reachable during ordinary duplicate cleanup. Archived cards are excluded from dispatch and other active-card paths, so the operation can silently strand unfinished work.

## Reproduction

On OpenClaw 2026.9.3:

1. Create a Workboard card with `status: "ready"`.
2. Call `workboard.cards.archive` for that card.
3. Read it back: `status` remains `ready` and `metadata.archivedAt` is set.

## Expected

Archiving should reject non-terminal cards. Operators can move a card to `done` first and then archive it. Unarchive must remain available for legacy rows.

## Impact

Routine housekeeping can create hidden active work that neither dispatches nor appears in normal live-card views.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After a graceful Gateway replacement interrupts an ordinary Control UI request, recovery can finish the requested work in the same session while the original human prompt disappears from active chat history.

### Steps to reproduce

At commit `0b538f7d5a4d9e3328f572cc07fe23402f733f36`, run the existing real-Gateway case:

```sh
pnpm test extensions/qa-lab/src/control-ui-automation-management.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts --testNamePattern "an ordinary Control UI turn creates a disabled automation after its Gateway is replaced"
```

The case submits a request through the Control UI composer, waits until the user message is recorded and the controlled provider receives the request, replaces the owned Gateway, and waits for the same session to complete its disabled automation. The provider intentionally holds the first request without producing a tool effect; the prompt includes a fixture routing marker.

### Expected behavior

The original accepted prompt remains available once in the same conversation, separately from the new restart instruction. The [restart contract at the tested revision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0b538f7d5a4d9e3328f572cc07fe23402f733f36/docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md#automatic-resume) describes the same transcript and a new system input rather than replaying the original prompt.

### Actual behavior

The test fails on the exact original-prompt assertion: expected one match, received zero. Metadata-only observations through the same case establish:

- Before restart, the original message is present once in raw storage, projected history, and the rendered page.
- After restart, its original event ID, content length, and content hash are unchanged in raw storage. A new leaf-control record selects a null parent, leaving that event outside the active branch.
- The new restart message contains the resume instruction. Its private model prompt projection also contains the original request, explaining why the requested task can still complete.
- `chat.history(limit: 30)` returns four messages and no original prompt. The rendered page also has zero exact matches.
- The same session identity, completed status, and disabled-automation assertions pass before the failing history assertion.

The original stored bytes are retained; this report concerns active-history visibility, not demonstrated data deletion. The affected branch selection is in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-prepare.ts`: fresh restart provenance does not take the unanswered-user preservation path before orphan repair resets the active leaf.

### OpenClaw version

Source commit `0b538f7d5a4d9e3328f572cc07fe23402f733f36`.

### Operating system

Linux on the native Blacksmith Testbox runner; distribution version was not captured.

### Install method

Repository-native test preparation and real Gateway child through the maintained test command.

### Model

Deterministic test provider; no live model was used.

### Provider / routing chain

Control UI → real Gateway → controlled OpenAI Responses fixture.

### Impact and severity

The affected interruption leaves a completed conversation without its original visible request, even though the request remains stored and the agent can finish its work. This is reproduced in the named controlled scenario; general production frequency and other interruption timings were not measured. No fix or broader recovery guarantee is claimed by this report.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After the iOS app is relaunched, it opens the main chat instead of the chat that was open, so switching apps a lot keeps dropping you out of your conversation. Reproduced 2/2 in the Simulator on `v2026.9.2` and `v2026.9.3`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pair the iOS app with a gateway and open the main chat.
2. Tap New Chat and send a message. Wait for the reply.
3. Terminate the app (`xcrun simctl terminate <device> ai.openclawfoundation.app.debug`), then launch it again.
4. The app opens the main chat. The new chat is still listed under Sessions, with its reply.

### Expected behavior

The app comes back to the chat that was open. `#108233` / PR `#108241` ("preserve active chat across foreground reconnects") set that expectation for reconnects while the app is alive, and it holds: on both versions, switching to another app and back, or restarting the gateway while the app is away, kept the new chat open.

### Actual behavior

A relaunched process opens the main chat. In the source, `chatSessionKey` in `NodeAppModel` resolves to `focusedChatSessionKey` if set, otherwise the gateway's main session. `focusedChatSessionKey` is a plain in-memory `private var` and is never persisted, so a new process always starts with it empty.

`prepareForGatewayConnect` documents this as intended ("initial connects and target changes must not inherit another route"). The result for a user is still that the chat they were in is gone from view each time iOS relaunches the app instead of resuming it.

### OpenClaw version

iOS app built from tags `v2026.9.2` (`3928bad9`) and `v2026.9.3` (`1391f7cd`). The original reports are from the App Store build `2026.9.20` on an iPhone.

### Operating system

iOS 26.5 Simulator (iPhone 17) on macOS, Xcode 27.

### Install method

Built from source with Xcode (Debug, Simulator). The original reports are from the App Store build.

### Model

`ollama-cloud/glm-5.2` on the test gateway. Not relevant to this issue, which is client side.

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> ollama-cloud. Not relevant to this issue.

### Logs

Gateway log for the `v2026.9.3` run, redacted. The new chat existed and replied before the relaunch:

```
20:30:30 [ws] res ok sessions.create 210ms
20:31:31 [ws] res ok chat.send 67ms
20:31:35 [ws] res ok agent.wait 3560ms
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

After the relaunch the sidebar's Sessions list shows the new chat at the top ("just now"/"1 min. ago") while the main chat's transcript is on screen. Happy to attach screenshots if useful.

Source, `apps/ios/Sources/Model/NodeAppModel.swift`: `focusedChatSessionKey`, `chatSessionKey`, `focusChatSession`, `prepareForGatewayConnect` (`preservingFocusedChatSession`). The selected agent is persisted per gateway (`GatewaySettingsStore`); the focused chat is not.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: iOS users with more than one chat.
- Severity: annoying, you lose your place.
- Frequency: 2/2 on a forced relaunch in the Simulator. On a real phone it happens whenever iOS relaunches the app instead of resuming it. I have no measured rate for that.
- Consequence: extra taps to find the chat again.

### Additional information

Not a regression as far as I can tell: `v2026.9.2` and `v2026.9.3` behave the same.

I'd like to work on the fix if you agree with the direction: persist the last focused session key per gateway and agent (next to the selected agent id), reopen it after connect if it is still in the session list, and fall back to the main chat otherwise. Everything that clears the focused chat today (gateway target change, agent switch) would keep doing so.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect persisted state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

When an agent already has a pending Skill Workshop update proposal for a skill, another `skill_workshop` call with `action: "update"` for the same agent and skill creates a second pending proposal ID at `v1`.

The agent-facing update path does not enforce the intended workflow of inspecting and revising the existing pending proposal.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Call `skill_workshop` with `action: "update"` for a Workshop-managed skill and leave the resulting proposal pending.
2. Call `action: "update"` again for the same agent and target skill.
3. List pending proposals for the agent.

## Expected behavior

The second update should not silently create another review stream for the same agent and target skill. Core should return a structured result identifying the existing pending proposal and its current revision hash so the caller can inspect and revise it explicitly.

## Actual behavior

Two different pending proposal IDs exist for the same agent and target skill, both initialized at `v1`.

`proposeUpdateSkill()` delegates directly to `createPendingSkillProposal()`, which always allocates a new proposal ID. Only the separate `reviseSkillProposal()` path continues an existing proposal.

## OpenClaw version

Observed on `2026.9.4` (`3a9d69d`). The same implementation is present in stable `v2026.9.5` and current `main` as checked on 2026-09-19.

## Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04, Linux x86_64

## Install method

npm global

## Model

Not model-specific

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw core Skill Workshop agent tool

## Additional provider/model setup details

Not applicable

## Logs

```text
proposal A: created, v1
proposal B: created, v1
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- In `v2026.9.5`, `proposeUpdateSkill()` delegates to `createPendingSkillProposal()`, which allocates a new ID with `proposedVersion: "v1"`:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.5/src/skills/workshop/service-propose.ts#L152-L275
- `reviseSkillProposal()` is the separate path for continuing an existing proposal:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5e825a7bb8482e8278c3e83d5f96ce31ba0317d4/src/skills/workshop/service.ts#L93-L106
- The documented learning flow says a matching pending proposal is revised first:
  https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/self-learning#review-and-revert-learning

## Impact and severity

Moderate workflow and review-integrity risk. Repeated agent-driven learning can create competing pending drafts for one skill, fragment review history, and consume pending-proposal capacity. The live skill is not changed until a proposal is applied.

## Additional information

Related but not duplicate:

- #89544 concerns semantically duplicate drafts with different identities: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89544
- #125632 was a UI projection bug; this report concerns genuinely distinct persisted proposal IDs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/125632

Possible direction:

1. Before creating an agent-driven update proposal, check under the target-scoped lock for an existing pending update proposal with the same authorized agent and canonical target skill.
2. If one exists, return its proposal ID and revision hash without creating a new ID or consuming the autonomous mutation budget.
3. Keep `revise` explicit, hash-bound, and atomic so unapproved changes in the existing proposal are not silently overwritten.
4. Enforce the same invariant for concurrent update requests.

Acceptance criteria:

- A second agent-tool update for the same agent and target skill does not create another pending proposal ID.
- The response identifies the existing proposal and revision needed for an explicit `inspect` and `revise` flow.
- Concurrent updates cannot create duplicate pending streams for the same agent and target skill.
- Pending proposals for different target skills remain independent.

issues.body:
### Summary

The gateway's own WAL auto-checkpoint on `state/openclaw.sqlite` is reported as blocked on every attempt since boot, and has **never completed**:

```
openclaw-state WAL checkpoint PASSIVE blocked by a reader
  state=blocked  checkpointedFrames=866  logFrames=17091
  consecutiveBlocked=14  lastCompletedAtMs=null  never_completed=true
```

The WAL therefore keeps growing (unbackfilled 41.5 MB at 15:33 → 65.7 MB at 19:09) instead of being checkpointed.

### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.7 (c074824)**
- Windows 10.0.26200 (x64), Node v24.18.0
- State DB `state/openclaw.sqlite` ≈ 405 MB, `-wal` 47–73 MB

### What was ruled out

A Sysinternals **handle.exe** scan of all processes for `openclaw.sqlite`:

```
node.exe  pid: 33900  .sqlite  x7
node.exe  pid: 33900  -wal     x7
node.exe  pid: 33900  -shm     x1
```

**No other process holds any handle on the DB** — every handle belongs to the gateway process itself. This is not an external contender; the pin is **in-process**.

The gateway's own telemetry cannot name the holder either:

```json
"candidate_connection": {
  "connectionId": 2, "operation": "sqlite connection", "ownerKind": "worker",
  "threadId": 2, "ageMs": ~25200000, "transactionOpen": false,
  "trackedReaders": 0, "blockingOwner": "unknown",
  "readerCount": 0, "scope": "current-thread", "nativeStatements": "unobserved"
}
```

Note the internal inconsistency: it reports "blocked by a reader" while also reporting `readerCount: 0` and `blockingOwner: unknown`.

### Reproduction pattern

1. Maintenance stops the gateway, checkpoints cleanly, restarts:
   `[checkpoint] PASS | [('openclaw-agent.sqlite',(0,0,0)), ('openclaw.sqlite',(0,0,0))]` (12:00:01)
2. After restart (~12:03) the block immediately re-forms and **never** clears for the rest of the uptime (observed 12:03 → 19:05, 71 blocked records, `never_completed=true`).
3. Only another full gateway restart clears it.

### Correlated (NOT proven) impact

- `Agent run failed: the Gateway state database was busy (SQLite: database is locked)`
- repeated `cron: isolated agent setup timed out before runner start`

Same DB, same subsystem. Timing supports a link; no controlled reproduction was done, so causation is **unproven**.

### Suggested directions (guesses)

- Likely a long-lived connection or unclosed read snapshot inside the worker pool (threadId=2, `ownerKind=worker`) — a single un-reset statement pins the WAL.
- `blockingOwner=unknown` + `readerCount=0` + "blocked by a reader" suggests the reader-tracking path does not cover all connection kinds.

---
*Reported from a self-hosted single-user deployment. Paths sanitized.*

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`inheritSessionThread` is honoured by `resolveCronAnnounceDelivery`, but the
only code path that ever sets it is the **failure-alert** path.
`finalizeCronCompletionAnnouncement` never sets it, and no job config key or CLI
flag exposes it. The result on Slack Agent View is that every isolated cron job
announcing to the owner's DM stops posting at the top level and instead posts as
a reply inside whatever thread the owner most recently replied under, changing
as the owner moves between threads.

Nine scheduled jobs on this install were affected: an hourly news update, four
morning briefs, two weekly reports and a security summary. Failure alerts for
the same jobs post top level, which is the tell.

The thread-carry block is byte-identical in 2026.9.3 and 2026.9.4.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Slack app using `features.agent_view`, default `session.dmScope: "main"`.
2. Create an isolated cron job with an explicit DM target:
   `openclaw cron add --every 2h --message "..." --announce --channel slack --to "user:<ownerId>"`
3. Let it deliver once. It posts at the DM top level, correctly.
4. In Slack, reply to any message the bot posted in that DM (Agent View makes
   each of the bot's own posts a thread root).
5. Wait for the next run.

The announcement now posts inside that thread, and so does every later run of
every job with the same target.

### Expected behavior

A job that names `to: user:<ownerId>` delivers to that DM at the top level.
Conversation state from an unrelated thread should not redirect scheduled
output, or there should be a supported way to opt out.

### Actual behavior

The thread is adopted from the main session's stored route. Mechanism, from the
2026.9.4 bundle:

1. Agent View gives every DM a `thread_ts`, including the bot's own posts; the
   plugin computes `agentViewThreadTs = message.thread_ts ?? message.ts`.
2. With `dmScope: "main"`, `deriveLastRoutePolicy` returns `main` and
   `resolveInboundLastRouteSessionKey` targets `route.mainSessionKey`, so
   `updateSessionLastRoute` writes that `threadId` onto the **base** main
   session. Confirmed on this install: `agent:main:main`'s `delivery.context`
   held `{channel: slack, to: user:<ownerId>, threadId: <rootTs>}`.
3. An isolated job with no `sessionKey` resolves its delivery context from that
   entry (`main = storedDeliveryEntry ?? threadEntry ?? mainEntry`), and
   `resolveSessionDeliveryTarget` returns `threadId = lastThreadId` because the
   requested channel equals the last channel and the mode is `explicit`, not
   `heartbeat`.
4. Then, in `resolveDeliveryTarget`:

```js
const canUseSessionThread = options?.inheritSessionThread !== false
  && shouldCarrySessionThread({ resolved, explicitTo, route, lastRoute });
const threadId = explicitThreadId ?? route?.threadId ?? (canUseSessionThread ? resolved.threadId : void 0);
```

With an explicit `to`, `shouldCarrySessionThread` returns
`routesSharePeer(route, lastRoute)`, and both sides resolve to the same peer on
the same base session key, so it is `true`.

Because the bot's own cron post is itself a thread root, one owner reply under
any brief captures all subsequent briefs. It is self-sustaining.

Heartbeat delivery escapes only because `resolveSessionDeliveryTarget` is called
with `mode: "heartbeat"`, which discards `lastThreadId`.

**The flag exists but is unreachable from the completion path.** Its only
producer is the failure-alert path:

```js
...params.route.alternateRoute ? { inheritSessionThread: false } : {}
```

so a job's failure alerts post top level while its successful daily brief
threads. `inheritSessionThread` appears in no config schema;
`cron add|edit --help` exposes only `--thread-id`, documented as a Telegram
forum topic id; and the docs describe `topLevel: true` only for the `message`
tool's send/upload actions, not for cron delivery. It looks like the flag was
introduced for the failure-alert work (#128610, #102445, #126483) and never
wired to completions.

**Workaround, for anyone hitting this:** set the job's `sessionKey` to its own
isolated run session (`agent:<id>:cron:<jobId>`). That diverts the
delivery-context lookup to an entry whose `delivery` is `{kind: "none"}`, so no
thread is carried, and execution is unchanged because the scheduler passes
`cron:<jobId>` to the runner regardless of `job.sessionKey`. It does **not**
work for command-payload jobs, which never open a run session, so the bound key
does not exist and the lookup falls back to the main session. Nothing validates
that the key names an existing session, so a typo silently restores the bug.

### Suggested fixes

1. Expose the flag, e.g. `delivery.inheritThread: false` plus
   `--no-inherit-thread` on `cron add|edit`. The plumbing exists; only a
   producer on the completion path is missing.
2. Or stop carrying a session thread onto an explicitly targeted announce at
   all, treating it the way `mode: "heartbeat"` already is. A job that names its
   destination has stated its intent.
3. Consider whether an assistant's own Agent View post should become a
   route-defining thread root, since that is what makes this compound.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (also reproduced on 2026.9.3; the relevant block is byte-identical)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-1063-aws, Node v26.8.1, npm global install under nvm

issues.body:
### Summary

Let a configured `agents.*.sandbox.backend` activate its provider plugin at Gateway startup, the way configured harness runtimes and providers already do.

### Problem to solve

Enabling a plugin-provided sandbox backend takes configuration in two places, and only one of them is the thing the user is thinking about. Setting `agents.defaults.sandbox.backend: "openshell"` does not by itself activate the plugin on the Gateway side; the separate `plugins.entries.openshell.enabled: true` is what does that. The OpenShell quick start in `docs/gateway/openshell.md` includes both, so the documented path works exactly as written.

A user who sets only the backend gets this on their first tool call:

```
Sandbox backend "openshell" is not registered.
Load the plugin that provides it, or set agents.defaults.sandbox.backend=docker.
```

Failing closed here is right. What makes it awkward is that the message names neither the plugin nor the `plugins.entries` entry that is missing, and its actionable half suggests reverting to `docker`, which is the opposite of what the user was trying to do.

The asymmetry reads as unintended rather than deliberate, which is why this seemed worth reporting. The CLI already has a sandbox-backend activation scope: `resolveSandboxBackendPluginIds` collects `agents.defaults.sandbox.backend`, the per-agent `sandbox.backend` values and any persisted backend ids, skips the core ids, and resolves the rest through the installed-plugin index. The Gateway's startup plugin plan has no equivalent: it collects channels, agent harness runtimes, worker, speech, web search, model, generation, voice and memory-embedding providers, the memory and context-engine slots, and dreaming, and a search of that module for the string `sandbox` returns zero hits.

So every other kind of configured capability activates its plugin from the configuration that names it, and sandbox backends alone need a second entry.

### Proposed solution

Add a sandbox-backend collector to the Gateway startup plugin plan, mirroring the CLI scope that already exists: collect `agents.defaults.sandbox.backend` plus the per-agent `sandbox.backend` values, skip `docker`, `podman` and `ssh`, and resolve the remainder through the installed-plugin index the same way `resolveSandboxBackendPluginIds` does.

Fail-closed behaviour would not change. A configured backend whose plugin is genuinely absent still raises the same error; the difference is only that an installed, indexed plugin whose id the configuration already names gets loaded.

If a collector is not wanted, a smaller version of the same fix would help nearly as much: have config validation, or the error itself, name the `plugins.entries.<id>.enabled` entry that would resolve the backend, rather than pointing at `backend=docker`.

### Alternatives considered

- **Leave it and rely on the docs.** It works today, and the OpenShell page is accurate. It keeps a two-place configuration whose second place is only discoverable from a quick start.
- **Error-message change only.** Much smaller, no activation semantics touched, and it would have saved us the detour. It leaves the two-place configuration in place.

### Impact

- **Affected:** anyone configuring a plugin-provided sandbox backend, including `@openclaw/openshell-sandbox`, `@openclaw/mxc-sandbox`, and third-party backends.
- **Severity:** low. It fails closed, and the documented path is correct.
- **Frequency:** once per install, at the moment someone first turns sandboxing on, which is also the moment they are least sure whether they have configured it correctly.
- **Consequence:** the first tool call fails rather than the sandbox working, and the remedy is not derivable from the message, whose suggestion is to revert to `docker`.

### Evidence/examples

Read against `openclaw@2026.9.2`, in the published package:

- The Gateway startup plan (`dist/gateway-startup-plugin-ids-*.js`) contains the string `sandbox` zero times, while collecting harness runtimes and the provider families listed above.
- The CLI scope exists: `resolveSandboxBackendPluginIds` in `dist/plugin-registry-*.js`, reached from the `sandbox` command-path policy entry (`pluginRegistry: { scope: "sandbox-backends" }`) through `src/cli/plugin-registry-loader.ts`.
- The registry itself is process-wide and consulted before the built-in table, so an activated plugin's registration is visible to the agent path; the gap is purely about whether the plugin is loaded.
- The error text and the quick start are quoted above from `docs/gateway/openshell.md` and the runtime's own message.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

### Additional information

Found while building a macOS sandbox backend for [Maxiful](https://maxiful.ai), a commercial desktop product that runs an OpenClaw Gateway on the user's own machine. We are not blocked by this and are not asking anyone to prioritise it: we hit it, the cause took a while to find, and it looked like the kind of small inconsistency you would rather know about than not.

Thank you for the plugin SDK generally. The sandbox backend contract is a good shape to build against.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw version: `2026.9.4` (stock release, no local patches)
- Channel: Telegram (group chat with multiple bot accounts bound to different OpenClaw agents)
- Feature: `tools.media.audio.echoTranscript: true` (default `echoFormat`)

## Scenario

A Telegram group contains **multiple bot accounts**, each bound to its own OpenClaw agent (in our case 6 agents share one group). `requireMention: true` is configured for the group, so agents only react to messages that mention them.

1. User sends a voice note to the group addressed to **one** specific agent.
2. Telegram delivers the message to every bot account in the group.
3. Each bot's OpenClaw instance runs the media pipeline on its own inbound copy.
4. Every agent echoes the transcript.

## Actual result

The user receives **N identical transcript echoes** (one per agent/bot present in the group) instead of exactly one echo from the agent they addressed. In our group with 6 agents, a single voice note produces 6 identical `📝 "..."` messages.

## Expected result

Exactly one echo — from the agent the message was addressed to (or some single-winner strategy), not one per account.

## Root cause (from reading the shipped dist code)

`audio-preflight.ts` transcribes the first audio attachment **before mention checking** (by design, so voice notes work in `requireMention` groups). With `echoTranscript` enabled, `sendTranscriptEcho()` (in `echo-transcript.ts`) fires unconditionally right after transcription, before the mention gate decides whether the message is even routed to the agent's session.

Two independent dimensions multiply the effect:

1. **Per-account duplication:** every bot account in the group runs its own preflight → own echo. The mention gate would have suppressed 5 of the 6 agents from *processing*, but the echo already happened.
2. **No de-duplication/coordination** between agents sharing the same chat: each echo is "best-effort send to originating chat" with no awareness that other agents just sent the same text.

There is a partial workaround — `tools.media.audio.scope` (rules on `channel`/`chatType`/session `keyPrefix`) can deny audio understanding for non-primary agents in groups — but that's a blunt instrument: it disables the whole transcription capability for those agents in groups, so an *explicitly mentioned* secondary agent can no longer hear voice notes at all. That trades spam for lost functionality, which is worse for multi-agent setups where any agent may be addressed.

## Suggested directions for a future fix

- Echo only when the message actually passes the mention gate (or defer echo until routing decides this message is for this agent), while keeping pre-transcription for mention checking.
- Or: single-winner echo deduplication per (chat, attachment id) across agents — e.g. only the agent whose session will actually receive the message echoes.
- Or at minimum: make echo respect `requireMention` per group, so unaddressed agents stay silent.

## Why it matters

Any multi-agent Telegram deployment (multiple bot personas sharing one group) gets transcript spam on every voice note with `echoTranscript` on. The feature description ("Echo the audio transcript to the originating chat... Enable this when users need to verify what the system heard") implies a single user-facing confirmation, not one per co-located agent.

Happy to provide verbose logs or test on demand.

issues.body:
## Summary

`openclaw doctor --fix` exits **rc=0 while performing zero migrations** in two common situations:

1. **Non-interactive invocation** — `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, or plain `doctor --fix` with stdin closed/piped (`</dev/null`). It prints "awaits its database schema repair", does nothing, and exits success. Real migrations (workspace attestation import, `sessions.json` → sqlite) only run when a PTY is attached (e.g. `script -qec 'openclaw ... doctor --fix'`).
2. **Invalid config** — when `openclaw.json` contains keys the current version rejects, doctor prints a vague "Config unavailable" and **skips all migrations**, still exiting rc=0. The actual invalid-key list is only visible via a separate subcommand (`doctor --session-sqlite inspect` → "Invalid config: ..."), not from the run that skipped the work.

Automation cannot distinguish "migrated successfully" from "did nothing" — both return 0.

## Evidence

Hit while migrating an 18-agent fleet to 2026.10.8 (2026-10-28). Both facets cost real recovery time:

- Facet 1: a scripted sweep invoked `doctor --fix` per agent, trusted rc=0, and restarted gateways onto unmigrated state. ~25 min/agent of migration work silently skipped across 6 agents until re-run under a PTY.
- Facet 2: 6 of 18 agents had config keys rejected by 2026.10.8 (`meta.lastTouchedAt`, `agents.defaults.memorySearch`, `gateway.channelStaleEventThresholdMinutes`, `env.TAILSCALE_API_KEY`). Doctor reported "Config unavailable", skipped migrations, exited 0. We only discovered the cause by running `doctor --session-sqlite inspect`, which does surface the rejected-key list.

Note this is the exit-code/reporting layer, distinct from #134331/#137866/#142585 (which cover the legacy-workspace/attestation migration behavior itself).

## Expected behavior

- A doctor run that performs no migrations exits non-zero (or with an explicit machine-readable "deferred/needs-tty" status), never 0.
- A doctor run that skips work due to invalid config prints the rejected-key list in the same run, and exits non-zero.
- (Nice-to-have) A documented flag to force migrations fully headless, so automation doesn't need a PTY shim.

## Environment

- openclaw 2026.10.8, Linux (Ubuntu 24.04), systemd fleet of 18 agents
- Reproduced repeatedly on 2026-10-28; journals and per-agent recovery sequence available if useful

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The native Codex parent-local inference relay rejects an image-heavy request above its 32 MiB decoded-body limit, but converts the deterministic size error into a generic HTTP 502; Codex and OpenClaw repeatedly retry the oversized conversation before the agent fails without a model reply.

### Steps to reproduce

Two evidence levels are available: an observed real-provider conversation failure and an executed, isolated reproduction of the installed decoder boundary. No private conversation payload is attached.

**Observed conversation path:**

1. Use OpenClaw 2026.9.9 with `@openclaw/codex` 2026.9.9, managed Codex 0.160.0, ChatGPT OAuth, and `openai/gpt-6-astra` through the native Codex app-server.
2. The affected native conversation accumulated eight inline PNG data URLs in four `exec` tool-result records.
3. Continue that conversation. Codex logs a request of **33,599,844 uncompressed bytes** and approximately **20,639,399 compressed bytes**, then receives the local relay's generic 502. Further attempts keep replaying oversized requests.
4. OpenClaw logs three same-model retries, exhausts its transient retry window, and surfaces the final transport error. This agent has no configured model fallbacks.

The image-producing workflow itself is not included as a portable reproduction. The following boundary reproduction is deterministic and was executed against the installed dispatch implementation:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e '
import { readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { zstdCompressSync } from "node:zlib";
const dir = process.env.HOME + "/.openclaw/extensions/codex/dist/.setup/";
const file = readdirSync(dir).find(name => /^inference-dispatch-.*\.mjs$/.test(name));
if (!file) throw new Error("Installed Codex inference-dispatch module not found");
const { createCodexInferenceDispatch } = await import(pathToFileURL(dir + file).href);
const dispatch = createCodexInferenceDispatch({ context: {}, assertCurrent() {} });
for (const size of [33554432, 33599844]) {
  const wire = zstdCompressSync(Buffer.alloc(size, 32));
  const req = {
    headers: { "content-encoding": "zstd" },
    async *[Symbol.asyncIterator]() { yield wire; }
  };
  try {
    const upload = await dispatch.prepareHttp(
      req, false, "/responses", new AbortController().signal, () => {}
    );
    upload.settle();
    upload.releaseModelExecution();
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ decodedBytes: size, compressedBytes: wire.length, result: "accepted" }));
  } catch (error) {
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ decodedBytes: size, compressedBytes: wire.length, result: "rejected", code: error.code, message: error.message }));
  }
}'
```

This intentionally bypasses sampling/authorization preparation to isolate the actual decoder. It uses synthetic bytes, sends nothing upstream, and does **not** claim to reproduce a full provider turn. The `prepareHttp` signature above is for the installed 2026.9.9 build; current main has a different signature.

Observed output:

```json
{"decodedBytes":33554432,"compressedBytes":1043,"result":"accepted"}
{"decodedBytes":33599844,"compressedBytes":1047,"result":"rejected","code":"ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE","message":"Cannot create a Buffer larger than 33554432 bytes"}
```

### Expected behavior

Keep bounded request admission, but identify an oversized decoded request as a deterministic size failure rather than a transient connection failure. Surface an actionable size-specific error without repeatedly resending the same oversized history. Do not silently discard conversation content or unconditionally remove the memory bound.

Known-good controls: the installed decoder accepts exactly 33,554,432 bytes; a fresh one-shot Gateway request with the same agent credentials and `openai/gpt-6-astra` returns the requested `OPENCLAW_TRANSPORT_OK` marker successfully.

### Actual behavior

The compressed request is below 32 MiB, but its decoded body is **45,412 bytes over** the limit. zstd decompression throws `ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE` before forwarding. The HTTP proxy catches the local exception and returns the same sanitized 502 used for transient transport failures. Native Codex retries internally; OpenClaw subsequently retries the model turn as `server_error`.

The affected run terminates after about **147 seconds**, with three outer retries and no model reply. A fresh connection cannot make this unchanged oversized body fit.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.9 (bcfc888); `@openclaw/codex` 2026.9.9; managed `@openai/codex` 0.160.0.

### Operating system

Linux 7.2.9-1-cachyos, x64; Node v26.8.2.

### Install method

npm global OpenClaw, installed Codex plugin.

### Model

openai/gpt-6-astra

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Gateway -> native Codex app-server (stdio) -> private loopback parent-local inference relay -> ChatGPT/Codex backend.

### Additional provider/model setup details

ChatGPT OAuth. Agent primary explicitly selects `openai/gpt-6-astra` with no agent-specific fallbacks. Credentials are usable, and a fresh same-model request succeeds.

The last successful inference reported 85,638 input tokens; the native effective context window at failure was 258,400 tokens. Rejected requests have no provider-reported token count because they fail locally. The measured violation is the relay's **byte** limit, not a demonstrated token-context overflow. No compaction records were found in the affected native conversation.

### Logs

Sanitized Gateway excerpts, October 11, 2026, UTC:

```text
01:09:10 [agent/embedded] transient same-model retry 1/8 for openai/gpt-6-astra reason=server_error: delayMs=599
01:09:42 [agent/embedded] transient same-model retry 2/8 for openai/gpt-6-astra reason=server_error: delayMs=1239
01:10:16 [agent/embedded] transient same-model retry 3/8 for openai/gpt-6-astra reason=server_error: delayMs=4447
01:10:52 [agent/embedded] transient retry window elapsed for openai/gpt-6-astra after 3/8 retries; stopping same-model retries
01:10:52 Embedded agent failed before reply: unexpected status 502 Bad Gateway: Codex parent-local inference transport failed; retry on a fresh connection., url: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<redacted>/backend-api/codex/responses
```

Native Codex request log fields:

```text
Compressed request body with zstd pre_compression_bytes=33599844 post_compression_bytes=20639399
Request completed method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<redacted>/backend-api/codex/responses status=502 Bad Gateway
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Only sizes/types were inspected for the large tool results; no image or transcript content is included:

| Measurement | Bytes |
| --- | ---: |
| Relay decoded-body limit | 33,554,432 |
| Initial failed request before compression | 33,599,844 |
| Amount over the limit | 45,412 |
| Eight inline PNG data URLs in native history | 33,247,720 |

Inline image data is 98.95% of the initial failed request size.

**Latest-release and current-main source inspection:**

The latest GitHub release checked was [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1), published October 10. This is a source comparison, **not** a claim that the newer release was installed or the full conversation reproduced on it.

- [v2026.10.1 inference-upload.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.1/extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-upload.ts#L4): `MAX_BODY_BYTES = 32 * 1024 * 1024`.
- [v2026.10.1 inference-dispatch.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.1/extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-dispatch.ts): zstd decoding uses `maxOutputLength: MAX_BODY_BYTES`; rewritten payloads are bounded too.
- [v2026.10.1 inference-proxy.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.1/extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-proxy.ts): non-authorization local exceptions before response headers become a generic 502.
- Current main was also inspected and retains these bounds and error mapping. The checked main revision was [6b13e9e4142d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6b13e9e4142d02427949b5ffbb10db574997686e).

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed native Codex-backed Telegram conversation with large inline tool images.

Severity: blocks model replies in that conversation. The Gateway remains running and fresh same-model requests succeed.

Frequency: four failed runs across October 10-11 have the same terminal relay error; retained request-size logs confirm oversized bodies for the latest two. The decoder rejects the measured above-limit body deterministically.

Consequence: futile native and outer retries, about 147 seconds of delay on the quoted run, and terminal failure without a model reply. No data loss or additional billing impact is established.

### Additional information

This is distinct from these related items:

- [#150940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150940): image-heavy native history and storage-retention gap; related, but not this decoded relay limit and retry classification.
- [#125308](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/125308): long-session byte-budget and compaction recovery problems; related, but not this exact decoder boundary.
- [#142823](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142823): merged omitted-`instructions` fix for Responses Lite requests. The same public 502 string can represent different causes; the installed build already accepts omitted instructions.
- [#155987](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155987): merged request-byte reuse optimization explicitly preserves the 32 MiB body limit.

Last known good/first known bad release: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. This report does not establish a regression.

Temporary operational workaround: start a fresh conversation and carry forward text rather than the old inline images. Only the fresh same-model inference control was exercised; resetting the affected production conversation was not performed.

A useful repair would preserve memory/admission bounds while distinguishing decoded-size failures from transient transport failures, and define a supported path for oversized image-bearing replay context. No production code was patched during this investigation.

issues.body:
### Summary

A `nodes.invoke` targeting an iOS node that iOS has evicted from memory is dropped instead of being queued, even though the gateway already has a pending-action queue and already knows the node is coming back. Background-capable commands like `calendar.add` are exactly the ones that fall through.

### What happens today (2026.9.4)

1. `nodes.invoke` for a disconnected iOS node triggers a silent background wake (`sendApnsBackgroundWake`, `content-available`, `apns-priority: 5`, `wakeReason: "node.invoke"`).
2. The gateway waits `NODE_WAKE_RECONNECT_WAIT_MS` (3000) plus `NODE_WAKE_RECONNECT_RETRY_WAIT_MS` (12000).
3. If the node has not reconnected within those ~15 s, the invoke fails with `node not connected` and a visible nudge is sent: "OpenClaw needs a quick reopen — Tap to reopen OpenClaw and restore the node connection."
4. The command itself is gone. When the node reconnects seconds later, nothing is retried.

A queue for this already exists — `enqueuePendingNodeAction` with `pendingActionTtlMs: 600000` and `pendingActionMaxPerNode: 64` — but `shouldQueueAsPendingForegroundAction()` only admits an action when **all** of these hold:

- platform starts with `ios`/`ipados`
- the command is a foreground-restricted plugin command, or starts with `camera.`, `screen.`, `talk.`
- the error is `NODE_BACKGROUND_UNAVAILABLE`

So the queue covers commands that *require* the foreground, and skips the commands the app can actually execute in the background (`calendar.add`, `reminders.add`, `contacts.add`).

### Reproduction

1. Pair an official iOS build, approve `calendar.add` via `gateway.nodes.commands.allow`.
2. Background the OpenClaw app, then use several memory-heavy apps so iOS evicts it. Do not force-quit it.
3. `openclaw nodes invoke --node <id> --command calendar.add --params '{...}'`.
4. Observed: ~15 s later `TIMEOUT: node invoke timed out`, then `node not connected` on the next attempt, plus the "quick reopen" notification. Opening the app restores the connection; the calendar entry was never created.

Silent pushes at priority 5 are throttled by iOS and can be delayed well beyond 15 s after heavy memory pressure, so the wake itself is not at fault — the give-up window is simply shorter than the platform's relaunch latency.

### Suggested fix

- Queue the invoke as a pending node action when the wake times out or the node is not connected, not only on `NODE_BACKGROUND_UNAVAILABLE`, for commands the node declares and that do not require the foreground.
- Flush the queue on reconnect within the existing TTL, honouring `idempotencyKey`.
- Return something the caller can act on, e.g. `queued: true` with the action id, instead of a bare timeout.
- Optional: make `NODE_WAKE_RECONNECT_WAIT_MS`, `NODE_WAKE_RECONNECT_RETRY_WAIT_MS` and `pendingActionTtlMs` configurable. They are constants in `nodes-policy` and `node-wake-state` today.

### Why it matters

Assistants that write a calendar entry or a reminder for a user are the normal case for a phone node. Right now that only works while the app happens to still be resident, which from the outside looks random: the same command succeeds at 17:36 and fails at 17:38.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), Linux gateway, iOS node (iPhone17,3, ui v2026.9.20), relay-backed APNs registration, push delivery verified with `openclaw nodes push` (status 200, env production).

# Heartbeat Disabled State Not Persisting

## Summary
The heartbeat disabled state does not persist. After running `openclaw system heartbeat disable`, the heartbeat re-enables itself automatically after a variable period (1–10 days). This has happened 13+ times in 50 days, causing unwanted polling cycles and token waste.

1. Run `openclaw system heartbeat disable`
2. Verify with `openclaw system heartbeat status` or `openclaw system heartbeat status --json` (shows disabled)
3. Wait 1–10 days
4. Heartbeat re-enables automatically without user action

- Aug 3: Re-enabled (1 day)

## Diagnosis
The `disable` command succeeds (confirmed by `--json` output), but the disabled state is not persisted to the config system. On subsequent gateway restarts or state reloads, the heartbeat automatically re-enables.

## Expected Behavior
Running `openclaw system heartbeat disable` should:
1. Disable the heartbeat immediately
2. Persist the disabled state to the config system
3. Keep it disabled until explicitly re-enabled with `openclaw system heartbeat enable`

- OpenClaw version: (not specified in original report)
- OS: macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)
- Node: v25.9.0

They should participate in the graph without adding an ignore or weakening unused-file detection.

Both original scan scopes complete and the command exits 1. Production reports 3 files; full-tree reports 8, including all three commands above. The three paths are absent from `repositoryScriptEntries` in `config/knip.config.ts`.

Source commit acf995b629063dd5ac1db2737fd561b491566d6b.

Linux x64; Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Knip 6.40.0. Distribution version was not captured.

## Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ## Summary In a Teams **group chat**, a plain-text message with two @mentions and one emoji, and no files or pasted images, reaches the agent with `[msteams 2 attachments unavailable]` appended and two `image` media facts that have no path. The agent then tells the sender their "two attachments didn't come through" and asks them to resend files that never existed. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Set `channels.msteams.graphMediaFallback: true` and install the bot in a group chat. 2. In the group chat, send a message that @mentions the bot and one other user and ends with an emoji, with no attachment. Example: `@Bot can you tell @Other User what works now 🙂` 3. Inspect the user message the agent receives. ## Expected behavior No media facts and no "attachments unavailable" notice, because the message has no attachments. ## Actual behavior Agent-facing user message (names anonymized): ``` can you tell what works now? [msteams 2 attachments unavailable] ``` Media facts recorded in the transcript for that message: ```json "media": [{"contentType":"image","kind":"image"},{"contentType":"image","kind":"image"}] ``` The same message fetched with Graph (`GET /chats/{chat-id}/messages/{message-id}`) has `attachments: []`, `mentions: ["Bot", "Other User"]`, and this body: ```html
Bot can you tell Other User what works now?
``` The only non-text elements are two mentions and one emoji. The agent nevertheless sees two unavailable image attachments. ## Where it seems to come from (not yet confirmed) I could not capture the raw Bot Framework activity (nothing is logged at info level), so the exact trigger is unverified. Candidates: - `extractInlineImageReferences()` (`extensions/msteams/src/attachments/shared.ts`) turns every `` in the activity's `text/html` attachment into advertised inline media. If Teams renders the emoji (or mention) markup as `` in the bot activity's HTML attachment, those become image media facts. - `resolveMSTeamsInboundMediaBody()` (`monitor-handler/inbound-content.ts`) then counts each advertised fact without a materialized path as an unavailable attachment. Our deployment had a custom `mediaAllowHosts` that did not include `statics.teams.cdn.office.net`. That may be why the fetch failed instead of resolving, but even a successful download would hand the agent an emoji image as a user "attachment". Suggested direction: exclude emoji/emoticon inline elements (and anything that isn't user content) from advertised media, or render them as their `alt` text. The same message also lost the second @mention ("Other User" was removed from the text). That part is #102376; its fix PR #102379 was closed unmerged on 2026-10-17. ## OpenClaw version 2026.10.4 (`@openclaw/msteams` 2026.10.4). The relevant code paths are unchanged on `main` at 49c8d04. ## Operating system Linux container (`ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.10.4`) ## Install method Docker image on Kubernetes ## Model Not model-related: the notice is added before the model call. ## Provider / routing chain OpenAI-compatible gateway → Anthropic ## Logs Nothing is logged at info level; the unavailable notice is added silently.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a PostgreSQL installation whose database lacks the `unaccent` extension, `openclaw update --channel dev` is refused with "PostgreSQL family at … cannot be captured by this updater; use a version with a port and backup provider for that family", while the real cause (the family lookup failed because `unaccent` is unavailable) is swallowed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. PostgreSQL 17 database without `unaccent` (fresh `initdb`, `createdb`, no extensions beyond `plpgsql`).
2. Fresh Git `dev` checkout of `main` (`71d954df1533`), config with `database.families.{state,agent,workboard}.engine = "postgres"` and `database.postgres.connection` as an env SecretRef; `openclaw onboard --non-interactive …` (fails with the message in "Actual behavior", but writes the agent anchor), `openclaw doctor --fix`.
3. Run `openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev` with no Gateway running.
4. Run `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "unaccent" WITH SCHEMA "public";` on the database, repeat steps 2–3 in a fresh state dir: the update is admitted and completes.

### Expected behavior

The refusal names the actual failure, the same way `onboard` and `agents add` do on the same installation:

```text
PostgreSQL unaccent capability unavailable. Have a database administrator run: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "unaccent" WITH SCHEMA "public";
```

`readPostgresBackupFamily()` is resolved through the backup worker and can fail for connection, capability or schema reasons; the admission check should include that error's message (or at least its class) in the `database-engine-preflight` refusal instead of asserting a missing port/backup provider.

### Actual behavior

```text
validating — snapshot-space-preflight...
  ✓ snapshot-space-preflight (1ms)
Update refused: PostgreSQL family at [state]/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite cannot be captured by this updater; use a version with a port and backup provider for that family. Reverse-port to SQLite with the current binary before updating, or stay on the current version. See https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-engines.
Phase: finished

⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: database-engine-preflight.
Failed: database-engine-preflight — Exit code: 1; Update refused: PostgreSQL family at [redacted-path]; update-failed
```

The updater's own Doctor warnings box in the same run already says `PostgreSQL unaccent capability unavailable …` for both agent databases, but the refusal does not. Source: `src/infra/update-database-engine-admission.ts` lines 94–101 on `bd10ba29d338` — `try { family = await readPostgresBackupFamily(pathname, context.config); } catch { refuse("PostgreSQL family at … cannot be captured by this updater; use a version with a port and backup provider for that family"); }` discards the caught error.

### OpenClaw version

main `71d954df1533` (2026.10.8); code identical on current main `bd10ba29d338`

### Operating system

macOS (Darwin 27.2.0), Apple silicon Mac mini

### Install method

Git checkout of `main` (`dev` channel) in an isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, Node 24 from Homebrew; disposable PostgreSQL 17.11 (Homebrew) on 127.0.0.1

### Model

N/A (not model related)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

Synthetic Anthropic API key from `onboard --non-interactive`; no channels, no Gateway running during the update.

### Logs

```text
2026-10-28 17:54:00  onboard --non-interactive … (same database, before CREATE EXTENSION)
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "PostgreSQL unaccent capability unavailable. Have a database administrator run: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS \"unaccent\" WITH SCHEMA \"public\";" } }

2026-10-28 17:54:05  openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev
Update refused: PostgreSQL family at [state]/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite cannot be captured by this updater; use a version with a port and backup provider for that family. …
⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: database-engine-preflight.

2026-10-28 17:57:56  same steps after CREATE EXTENSION unaccent, fresh state dir
Phase: validating … Phase: activating … Doctor: maintenance release … Phase: finished
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.8 (58d2d164) (from 2026.10.8 (71d954df)); 7 warnings need attention.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Full redacted update output and the generated update report are available on request.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: PostgreSQL installations whose database was provisioned without `unaccent` (or with any other condition that makes the family lookup fail).
- Severity: annoying, with a wrong hint — the message tells the operator to reverse-port to SQLite or wait for a version with a port/backup provider, when a one-line `CREATE EXTENSION` is the fix.
- Frequency: always under that condition.
- Consequence: time lost chasing a provider/version problem that does not exist.

### Additional information

Observed while producing the real-behavior proof for #187113 (the fix itself is unrelated to this message). Related: #186961 / #187006 (earlier `database-engine-preflight` refusals on PostgreSQL families).
