issues.body:
## Current scope — 2026-10-21

The original report below is historical; the later [author correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/120385#issuecomment-5223526688) supersedes its claim that the cron allowlist was ruled out. The original scheduled-job failure was caused by finite core-only `toolsAllow` data suppressing bundle MCP. The suspected identity-binding commit was exonerated for that case.

The separate generated-media continuation mechanism identified in the [October19 follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/120385#issuecomment-6267849914) is addressed upstream by merged [#174696](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174696), commit [749464ce0a56](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/749464ce0a56c75d8b2ef9b4fa2caf745a8bc549). The completion now uses ordinary requester tools instead of forcing restart-safe tools. This does not explain the distinct 65-tool capture or prove all catalog reductions fixed.

Remaining scope: unexplained reductions need paired activation/final-catalog diagnostics on an updated build; cron outcome classification and configuration-warning requests remain distinct. #121796 added catalog-miss diagnostics, not universal failure classification; warning work is tracked by #130073. The merged media PR also explicitly records remaining first-completion prompt-cache misses, so normal tools do not imply full cache equivalence.

Our currently running Gateway is older than this merge; this update is based on current source and the upstream author's published proof, not a new live reproduction here. Keeping this broader issue open.

<!-- grynn-author-scope:120385:2026-10-21 -->

## Historical report (retained verbatim)

### What happened

Code Mode (`exec` bridge) builds an **incomplete tool catalog** for some execution contexts. Observed on one gateway over ~36h:

| Execution context | Catalog size | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| Interactive turn (main agent session) | 86 | openclaw 48 + mcp 38 |
| Scheduled cron/automation run | **47** | openclaw only, **0 MCP** |
| Internal pre-compaction memory-flush turn | **~40** | partial openclaw only — `openclaw:core:exec` itself missing |
| Some interactive turns, same session minutes apart | 75 | openclaw **37** + mcp 38 |

Guest code then fails mid-run:

- Scheduled run (cron session `295bed73`, 2026-08-07): `Unknown tool id: MCP.ibkr.get_account_positions. Did you mean: automations, browser, get_goal?`
- Memory-flush turns (repeatedly): `Error: Unknown tool id: openclaw:core:exec. Did you mean: read, write? at settle (openclaw-code-mode:controller.js:125:49)`
- New variant on a reduced-catalog turn: `Tool "openclaw:core:write" returned details that do not match its declared outputSchema` — the bridge rejected a core tool's own successful return (the file write did land on disk); `failurePhase:"bridge"`, repair disallowed.

Cron surfaces all of this only as **`⚠️ 🛠️ Exec failed`** — run history/diagnostics contain no guest error, so for two days this looked like model/prompt flakiness instead of a tool-surface regression.

### Impact

- On this gateway 3 of 28 automation jobs call MCP tools from Code Mode; **exactly those 3 fail on consecutive days** while the 25 non-MCP jobs keep passing. The same job bodies succeed when run interactively.
- Internal flush turns intermittently drop to a read/write-only surface and error out.
- 8 bridge failures logged in ~36h across the two failure modes.

### Timeline / suspect commit

- Last clean scheduled run of the canary job: `2026-08-05T22:19Z`. First failure: `2026-08-06T22:06Z`. Still failing after updating to `c25671cf275`.
- `d863dd5f5ec` ("refactor(agents): bind tool policy to exact execution identity", present in the running build) matches the observed mechanism — catalog contents vary by execution identity (interactive vs scheduled vs flush vs subagent) — **but** the first failure predates that commit's author date, so either an earlier commit opened the regression window (`2026-08-05T22:19Z → 2026-08-06T22:06Z`) or there are two contributors. Needs a bisect by someone who knows the intended identity-binding semantics.

### Ruled out

- **Job `toolsAllow`:** backed up and cleared the failing job's allowlist (normalizes to `["*"]` per `src/cron/tools-allow.ts`) → identical failure. An allowlist can only narrow a catalog that was already built; the MCP side is never registered for the scheduled identity in the first place.
- **Model/provider:** reproduces via `openclaw cron run <id>` independent of model.
- **MCP server health:** the same streamable-HTTP MCP server answers normally on interactive turns seconds later.

### Repro sketch

1. Configure any MCP server plus an automation whose prompt calls one of its tools via Code Mode.
2. Run the body interactively: journal logs `code-mode: cataloged 86 tools`, call succeeds.
3. Trigger via scheduler or `openclaw cron run <id>`: journal logs `code-mode: cataloged 47 tools`, guest gets `Unknown tool id: MCP.<server>.<tool>`, run ends `error: ⚠️ 🛠️ Exec failed` with no underlying error in diagnostics.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.6 @ `c25671cf275` · Linux x64 (PVE host) · node v22.23.1 · gateway under systemd user unit · one MCP server (official IBKR hosted MCP via local streamable-HTTP proxy)

### Possibly related

#85030 (MCP tools not injected into `sessions_spawn` subagent sessions) looks like the same family — execution-identity-scoped tool surface dropping MCP registration — but this report covers **cron/scheduled runs and internal memory-flush turns of the main agent**, plus the `outputSchema`-rejection variant hitting a core tool.

### Asks

1. Scheduled/flush (and subagent) execution identities should build the same Code Mode catalog as interactive turns — or the reduction should be explicit, documented, and reflected in the quick index the guest is shown.
2. Cron run diagnostics should surface the real guest error (`Unknown tool id: …`) instead of a bare `⚠️ 🛠️ Exec failed`.
3. Explain/fix the `outputSchema` rejection of `openclaw:core:write`'s legitimate return on reduced-catalog turns.

### Bug type
Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
With #187064 merged, the updater's delegated Doctor on a PostgreSQL installation gets through its anchor handling but fails at the end of maintenance with:

```
Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker; only synchronous admission, migrations, and CLI one-shots may run on the main thread; verify database.postgres.connection and server availability.
```

so `openclaw update --channel dev` still ends with `doctor-failed` and the update does not activate cleanly.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Git install on main, `state`/`agent`/`workboard` families on PostgreSQL 17 (13 stores, 11 agents with anchors), serving main `1b356b487d8e`.
2. Stop the Gateway; `openclaw backup create --verify` (ok); `openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev` to main `700930378c79` (contains #187064 / `537c3f3e0a85`).

### Expected behavior
The delegated Doctor completes maintenance and the update activates (as #187064's own PostgreSQL 17 proof did).

### Actual behavior
`Phase: activating` → `✓ database snapshot (344.84s)` → `openclaw doctor` runs its phases through `Doctor: maintenance finish` … `Doctor could not complete maintenance.` → `Doctor: maintenance release` → the error above → `✗ openclaw doctor (226.91s)`, `Failing check doctor (doctor-failed): Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: …`, `doctor process settlement: Doctor did not finish normally, but every tracked process group stopped. Preserving migrated state`. The run ended `FAILURE (cold-update)`; the updater restored the checkout to `1b356b487d8e` and the Gateway restarted healthy there (models identical to the pre-update snapshot). A fresh matched archive had been taken before the attempt. Standalone `openclaw doctor --fix` from the CLI entry (process role `cli-oneshot`) does not hit this guard on the same installation.

The guard is `assertEngineStoreExecutionAllowed()` (src/infra/database-engine/admission-scope.ts): main thread, `admissionDepth === 0`, role not `cli-oneshot`. Earlier the same step did not reach PostgreSQL at all; #187064 makes the delegated Doctor read the engine selection (`doctor-database-preflight.ts` → `readConfigSnapshotForEngineSelection()`), after which a store operation at maintenance release opens a PostgreSQL connection on the main thread outside an admission scope. In this configuration the Doctor is delegated through `update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts --doctor` (config-write authority with an executor fence), and that worker never installs a database process role, so `processRole.role` is undefined rather than `cli-oneshot` and the guard fires; the CLI entry (`src/entry.ts`) installs the role, which is why the standalone Doctor works.

### OpenClaw version
installed main `1b356b487d8e` (2026.10.8) → candidate main `700930378c79` (2026.10.8)

### Operating system
macOS 15 (Apple silicon Mac mini), Node 24 (Homebrew), PostgreSQL 17 (local socket)

Git checkout (`~/openclaw`, channel dev), gateway as a system LaunchDaemon run by a dedicated user

### Model
n/a

issues.body:
## Summary

Allow independent, reviewed test-line budget allocations to merge without repeatedly editing one shared scalar.

## Problem to solve

Concurrent PRs with justified regression coverage contend on `config/test-lines-baseline.txt`. A precisely measured ceiling can conflict again while exact-head CI is still running. This repeatedly blocked https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186977 even after its behavior, review, and test evidence passed.

The existing total counts literal LF bytes, while its comparison delta uses Git numstat. Changing `x` to `x\n` adds one counted newline but reports numstat 1/1 (net zero), allowing real growth through the inherited non-growing exception.

## Proposed solution

Keep the fixed scalar and add tracked per-change integer allocation records. The effective ceiling remains their sum. When allocation keys or values change, positive effective-ceiling growth must not exceed positive actual LF growth against the same selected base, including any simultaneous scalar movement.

Preserve the absolute ceiling and inherited non-growing behavior. Do not forgive existing debt. Pruning folds the measured total into the scalar and removes tracked records, including at zero slack; untracked files remain untouched. Review still owns necessity and any separate scalar-only reconciliation.

## Alternatives considered

A coordinated landing window would require pausing both shared ceiling edits and positive test growth until one head finishes validation. Ordinary auto-merge does not reserve that window. Repeated scalar refreshes have already failed to converge. Increasing a reserve or weakening validation would hide future growth.

## Impact

Maintainers can land independently reviewed regression budgets without shared-file conflicts while preserving the aggregate cap and rejecting overlap or double credit. This affects source CI policy only, not the installed runtime.

## Evidence/examples

Real Git fixtures reproduce both the independent-branch conflict and the numstat/LF mismatch. The proposed checker has passed dependency-free fixtures for both merge orders, overlap rejection, exact index/worktree handling, pruning with old branches, inherited debt, malformed input, and overflow. Registered tests and hosted checks remain required before landing.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug — Control UI WebChat live delivery (native/builtin agent runtime, non-ACP)

### Summary

In the Control UI WebChat, the **assistant body text is never streamed**. It appears as a single paint at the end of the turn, while the page timer shows a long elapsed time (e.g. "38s / 6.1k output tokens").

Frame-level capture on the live Gateway WebSocket shows the asymmetry clearly: within the same turn, `agent/thinking` delivered **346 incremental frames** (each carrying a `delta`), while `agent/assistant` delivered **only 2 frames**. The body actually arrived as whole `session.message` payloads (5.5–13.6 KB each).

Expected: body text streams incrementally like reasoning does.
Actual: body lands in one blob at the end.

### Environment

- openclaw **2026.9.3** (1391f7c), Windows 10 (10.0.19045), Node 26.8.2
- Gateway local on `ws://127.0.0.1:18789`, Control UI WebChat
- Providers observed: `deepseek/deepseek-flash` and `xiaomi-token-plan/mimo-v2.5-pro` (both reproduce)
- Runtime: OpenClaw Default (builtin harness, not a CLI/ACP backend)
- Reported as a regression vs 2026.7.x (aligned with #136260's "regression vs 2026.7.1-2")

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a gateway on 2026.9.3 and open the Control UI WebChat.
2. Ask for a long body-only reply (we used a ~1000-character classical Chinese text, and a ~5000-character one).
3. Observe: the reply appears in a single paint; the working timer keeps counting meanwhile.

### Evidence 1 — DOM mutation timeline (client side)

Injected into the Control UI page: a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` plus a 100 ms poll, recording `(t, assistantMessageInnerTextLength)`.

A single turn produced (ms since injection → assistant message length):

```
   40 -> 469        (baseline)
 5015 -> 1006
28283 -> 0          (new message group)
28570 -> 8
29589 -> 11
29665 -> 12
29931 -> 8
38224 -> 9
72693 -> 22
73189 -> 8384       <-- one sample: +8362 chars
73274 -> 8387
73459 -> 8412
```

The body jumped from **22 to 8384 characters inside a single <100 ms sample**, with no intermediate growth. The MutationObserver fires synchronously per DOM mutation, so partial states would have been recorded.

**Control observation in the same window:** the turn status line *did* grow incrementally (`8 -> 11 -> 12 -> 8 -> 9 -> 22`). So the renderer updates fine — only the body coalesces.

### Evidence 2 — Gateway WebSocket frame classification (decisive)

Installed a WebSocket recorder via `page.addInitScript` **before** connection setup (so it wraps `WebSocket` ahead of app code), then reloaded the UI. Frame classes for one long turn:

| stream          | frames | notes                                                      |
| --------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `agent/thinking`| **346**| every frame carries `"delta"`; spans ~100 s                |
| `agent/assistant`| **2** | sizes 1061 B and 2810 B                                    |
| `agent/item`    | 25     | `kind:"preamble"`                                          |
| `session.message`| 12    | **5.5 KB – 13.6 KB each** — this is where the body arrives |

Example thinking frame (incremental):

```json
{"type":"event","event":"agent","payload":{"runId":"...","stream":"thinking","data":{"text":"The","delta":"The"}}}
```

So the delta channel exists and is actively used for reasoning; the body simply does not use it.

Re-measured after setting `agents.defaults.blockStreamingDefault: "on"`: `agent/assistant` still = 2 frames. No change.

### Analysis / pointers (may be useful)

In `dist/builtin-openclaw-*.mjs`, assistant stream data is emitted by `emitAssistantStreamDataSafely`, which has a once-per-scope guard:

```js
const emitAssistantStreamDataSafely = (scope) => {
  if (!scope.delivery || scope.emitted || state.unsubscribed) return;
  ...
  scope.emitted = true;
```

and the delivery path coalesces appends into one scope:

```js
const coalesce = previous && isStreamAppend(previous) && isStreamAppend(delivery) && ...;
const scope = coalesce ? streamScope : flushAssistantStream(delivery);
```

Also note `shouldEmitPartialReplies: !(reasoningMode === "on" && !params.onBlockReply)` in the state init. With Control UI there is no `onBlockReply`, so when reasoning visibility is `on` partial replies are disabled. Toggling `blockStreamingDefault` did not change `params.onBlockReply` on this path, so it did not help. Turning reasoning visibility off was not separately retested.

Net effect observed: inter-token appends are merged into one scope and that scope emits once — reasoning (`stream:"thinking"`) is not subject to the same path and streams per-delta.

I could be wrong about the exact mechanism; the frame/DOM measurements above are the firm part.

### Related

- #136260 — "inter-tool assistant text no longer streamed … full text dumped at end" (P1; regression vs 2026.7.1-2). That report is about channels and states the dashboard/control-ui path was fine there, so it may not cover this.
- #138735 — canonical cluster for WebChat segmented-commentary duplication / dropped live text
- #140723 — WebChat duplication from reasoning-only retries re-streaming already-emitted text
- #144471 — closed (commentary duplication) — related fix landed on main

### Reproduction scripts

Both probes are small standalone Node/Python snippets (Playwright `page.evaluate` for the DOM observer; `page.addInitScript` + `WebSocket` wrapper for frame capture). Happy to paste them here or open a gist if useful.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (agents unavailable without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
After an unclean shutdown (SIGKILL-path reboot), every agent DB open triggers a `stale-lease` integrity gate that reports `healthy`, so DBs are not corrupt; but integrity gates serialize per agent (6–14s each), so N agents × serial gate = minutes of guaranteed agent unavailability after each unclean shutdown.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run a gateway with several agents on an Ubuntu VM. Version 2026.10.2 (b895d24-era binary); agent DBs under the `state/agent-db` machinery.
2. Reboot the VM via an unclean/shutdown-kill path (processes interrupted without a drain).
3. Restart the gateway. Observe each agent DB open go through a `stale-lease` integrity gate that eventually reports `healthy`.
4. Let Discord-facing traffic arrive during that window: gateway logs `chat metadata refresh failed: prepared chat metadata owner is unavailable for agent <anonymized>` and `Agent database preparation has ended: <anonymized>` repeatedly (34 error-class lines in ~90s observed), and Discord-facing agents do not respond.

Example anonymized gate lines from the journal:
`agentId=<anonymized> open elapsedMs=5809 (validation 5740, integrityGate 5711, integrity_check 75 tables 7184ms total)` → `integrityGateMode=tables, integrityGateOutcome=healthy`
`agentId=<anonymized> open elapsedMs=14108 (integrityGate 13963, integrity_check 10536ms)` → `integrityGateOutcome=healthy`

Observed twice in one evening (18:31 boot and 18:59 restart both grounded through the window).

### Expected behavior
DBs are verifiably healthy (every gate ends `healthy`), so the gate should not create a minutes-long global availability cliff after an unclean shutdown. Startup should recover promptly — e.g. parallel gates across agents, persisted healthy-quick_check results, or read-only availability while gates run.

### Actual behavior
Stale-lease integrity gating has no concurrency/parallelism or budget policy, so N agents × 6–14s serial gates = minutes of guaranteed unavailability after unclean shutdown. During the window Discord-facing agents do not respond and the journal fills with the `chat metadata refresh failed: prepared chat metadata owner is unavailable` / `Agent database preparation has ended` error lines.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.2 (b895d24-era binary)

### Operating system
Ubuntu VM (Linux)

### Install method
Gateway binary, single-VM deployment

### Model
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (defect reproduces in the state/agent-db startup path before any model routing; model not material to reproduction)

### Provider / routing chain
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not material to the state/agent-db open path)

### Additional provider/model setup details
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs
```text
agentId=<anonymized> open elapsedMs=5809 ... validation 5740, integrityGate 5711, integrity_check 75 tables 7184ms total ... integrityGateMode=tables integrityGateOutcome=healthy
agentId=<anonymized> open elapsedMs=14108 ... integrityGate 13963, integrity_check 10536ms ... integrityGateOutcome=healthy
chat metadata refresh failed: prepared chat metadata owner is unavailable for agent <anonymized>
Agent database preparation has ended: <anonymized>
```
(agentId values elided/anonymized.)

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Observed on live production 2026-10-18 after a hard reboot: every agent DB open triggers a `stale-lease` gate that passes `healthy`; 34 error-class lines in 90s during the window; second occurrence in one evening at 18:31 and 18:59.

### Impact and severity
- Affected: any gateway with multiple agents after an unclean shutdown.
- Severity: high for availability (agents unreachable for minutes; Discord-facing agents silent).
- Frequency: always/guaranteed after every unclean shutdown (not an edge case).
- Consequence: missed messages, no agent responses, and repeated `chat metadata refresh failed ... owner is unavailable` errors during the window. DBs are NOT corrupt; the protection mechanism's cost creates the outage.

### Additional information
Framed as an availability defect, not a corruption report (DBs healthy on every gate; `integrityGateOutcome=healthy` throughout). Suggested directions for consideration (question, not a requirement): parallelize integrity gates across agents; persist lease-gate results for healthy quick_check cases; or admit read-only access while gates run. Related upstream work: #168468 (startup SQLite integrity_check grind), #156917 (state-lifecycle lease takeover), #164941 (agent DB maintenance lease loss blocks doctor). Note per CONTRIBUTING: product behavior defect → bug report; version/OS/expected-vs-actual included.

issues.body:
# [Bug]: Control UI memory search uses legacy RPC for provider-runtime engines

## Summary

The Control UI memory page reports Hindsight as awake, but searching fails:

```text
Memory search failed: memory plugin "hindsight-openclaw" uses the provider runtime; retry memory.search with version: 2
```

The bundled UI calls `memory.search` without `version: 2`. The Gateway rejects
that legacy request for a provider-runtime memory engine. An authenticated native
version-2 search succeeds against the same configured provider.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: **2026.10.8 (dc2523e)**
- Memory plugin: **@vectorize-io/hindsight-openclaw 1.0.0**
- Platform: Linux, native per-user Gateway
- Selected memory slot: `hindsight-openclaw`
- Hindsight automatic recall and retention enabled
- Verified: 2026-10-28

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Hindsight as the memory slot and connect it to a reachable Hindsight instance.
2. Open the Control UI memory page. The engine shows as awake.
3. Enter a search query.
4. Observe the provider-runtime/version-2 error above.

## Expected behavior

The memory page searches the selected provider through its supported interface,
displays provider-based results, and can open a result without assuming it is a
workspace file.

## Actual behavior and source findings

In the installed package, `dist/control-ui/assets/config-page-DYr_CitY.js`
sends the equivalent of:

```js
client.request("memory.search", { query, agentId });
```

It also loads result detail through `agents.workspace.get` using a file path.

The Gateway's `dist/memory-search-WSMU9icp.mjs`
(`src/gateway/server-methods/memory-search.ts`) dispatches explicit
`version: 2` requests to the provider handler. The legacy path returns the
reported error when the selected backend is `provider-runtime`.

The version-2 response uses `hits` with provider-scoped references. Updating the
request alone would leave the UI's result rendering/detail path incompatible;
provider result details should use `memory.get` with the returned reference.

## Read-only verification

Using the existing authenticated CLI connection:

```sh
openclaw gateway call memory.status \
  --params '{"version":2,"agentId":"main"}' --json

openclaw gateway call memory.search \
  --params '{"version":2,"agentId":"main","query":"synthetic-memory-protocol-check-20261028-7f91","maxResults":1}' \
  --json --timeout 20000
```

Results, with memory contents omitted:

- `memory.status`: version `2`, provider `hindsight-openclaw`, status `ready`.
- `memory.search`: exit code `0`; response fields `version`, `agentId`,
  `providerId`, `hits`; version `2`, one hit.

The search was read-only; it did not create a test memory. A returned hit confirms
the request succeeds, not that the synthetic query should match a particular fact.
No runtime patch, engine change, restart or setting change was used.

## Suggested fix and regression coverage

- Make the Control UI memory page support the provider-runtime search protocol,
  including version-2 request/response handling and provider-reference detail reads.
- Preserve supported built-in memory behavior and existing authorization checks.
- Cover provider health ready, populated/empty search results, detail reads and
  provider errors without falling back to workspace paths for provider references.

This report is limited to the memory-page integration. It does not establish a
failure in Hindsight's automatic recall or retention hooks.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Reliability/observability gap (documented contract unreachable when it matters)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
The docs reserve `/health`, `/healthz`, `/ready`, `/readyz`, `/startup`, `/startupz` as Gateway check endpoints, and `/ready` correctly answers `503` once the listener is bound. But the listener binds only *after* the full startup phase chain (plugins.post-bind, ~9.6s on a trivial empty instance; ~60s on a real instance where `sidecars.main-session-recovery` alone took 34s). During that entire window every reserved check endpoint refuses connections — so the readiness contract exists precisely when it cannot be used. An external supervisor cannot distinguish "starting" from "dead or wedged": the only observable facts are (a) process exists, (b) nothing is listening. Config-reload drains are worse: the listener *closes* while `systemctl` keeps reporting `active/running`.

### Steps to reproduce (clean environment, no fleet state)
```bash
docker run -d --name ocl-ready node:24-bookworm sleep infinity
docker exec ocl-ready bash -c 'npm i -g openclaw@2026.10.5 --no-audit --no-fund'
docker exec ocl-ready bash -c 'export HOME=/tmp/fresh-home OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=*** && mkdir -p $HOME && openclaw gateway --port 18791 --allow-unconfigured > /tmp/gw-boot.log 2>&1 & GPID=$!; START=$(date +%s); for i in $(seq 1 90); do T=$(( $(date +%s) - START )); ALIVE=$(kill -0 $GPID 2>/dev/null && echo yes || echo no); HZ=$(curl -sS -m 2 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:18791/healthz 2>/dev/null || echo REFUSED); RDY=$(curl -sS -m 2 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:18791/ready 2>/dev/null || echo REFUSED); echo "t=${T}s alive=$ALIVE healthz=$HZ ready=$RDY"; [ "$HZ" = "200" ] && break; sleep 1; done'
```

Captured output (full log attached below):
```
t=0s alive=yes healthz=REFUSED ready=REFUSED
...
t=8s alive=yes healthz=REFUSED ready=REFUSED
t=9s alive=yes healthz=200 ready=503
```

### Expected behavior
A reserved check endpoint should answer as early as possible with meaningful semantics — e.g. bind the check listener (or a separate lightweight one) right after config admission, serving `/startup` `200` + `/ready` `503` while the phase chain runs, flipping `/ready` to `200` at `http server listening`. Then an external watcher can distinguish starting/dead/wedged. Alternatively, the docs should state explicitly that no readiness signal exists before first bind, so implementers know connection-refused during boot is *expected* and must not be treated as a wedge.

### Actual behavior
All reserved endpoints return connection-refused for the whole startup window (t=0–8s clean, up to ~60s with session state); at first contact `/healthz` is already `200` while `/ready` is still `503` — the readiness signal exists but only becomes queryable after the decisive phase (`plugins.runtime-post-bind`, total=9575.8ms in the captured log; 117 startup phases logged). On production VMs this window is where restart loops happen: watchers seeing process-alive + nothing-listening infer wedge and restart healthy-booting gateways.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.5 (1b58cb9) — clean `npm i -g` in `node:24-bookworm`, no fleet state

### OS
Debian bookworm container (docker), host Ubuntu 24.04; Node 24 (per engine range)

### Environment notes
Observed magnitudes on real instances: listener bind at ~58–70s with existing session state (`[gateway] http server listening (6 plugins ...; 58.1s)`), `main-session-recovery` phase 33.9s. During config-reload drain the listener closes while the process stays alive and `systemctl is-active` remains true — same unqueryability, opposite direction. Our operator-side workaround (bounded readiness wait before any restart decision) is deployed, but the fix belongs in the runtime: the check endpoints should be queryable throughout the lifecycle, or the docs must define refusal-during-boot as canonical so watchers can rely on it.

### Startup phase log (first bind at 9.6s)
<details><summary>117 phases — first and last shown</summary>

```
    [gateway] startup phase: entry.run-main-import starting total=125.4ms
    [gateway] startup phase: cli.main.gateway-run-select-environment starting total=477.5ms
    [gateway] startup phase: cli.command.config-ready starting total=1009.6ms
    ...
    [gateway] startup phase: plugins.runtime-post-bind 686.5ms total=9575.8ms
    [gateway] startup phase: plugins.runtime-attach starting total=9576.7ms
    [gateway] startup phase: plugins.runtime-attach 7.5ms total=9584.1ms
```
</details>

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After opening a workspace file and switching to another conversation and back, the selected Files panel can remain blank. The preview has been retired, but the loaded file catalog is still hidden.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a conversation with a saved workspace file in the Control UI.
2. Open Files and select the file in the project browser. The file reader opens and the catalog collapses.
3. Use the normal left sidebar to open a different conversation.
4. Select the original conversation again.

The observed case used a guest with access to both conversations, a saved Markdown file, and the desktop Files panel. The same transition also fails through the existing retained-panel test on the current UI source.

### Expected behavior

When task navigation retires the file reader, returning to Files should show the usable catalog, or its loading/error state. Saved files, current access checks and deliberate disposal of hidden readers should remain intact.

### Actual behavior

Files is selected and the correct conversation is presented, but its content is blank. The Files host has positive dimensions while its catalog has `hidden=true`, computed `display:none`, and zero dimensions. The catalog still contains loaded rows. No reader or iframe remains.

The current owner captures catalog navigation and hides the tree when the first preview opens. The retained-pane lifecycle subsequently calls `clearSessionWorkspacePreviews`, which removes the previews without restoring catalog navigation. `DesktopWorkspaceContents` continues hiding the catalog because `treeVisible` remains false. Ordinary catalog selection already restores that navigation through a separate path.

### OpenClaw version

Control UI source bf6bdd6c5fedb5e23f7bc206d26c625adbdec1ab, served through the development UI against an isolated Gateway at 09a58215b66ca511ae398ddf9e00e9c7b4eef9f6. The changed UI owner is current; this is not a claim that the entire Gateway was rebuilt at the UI revision.

### Operating system

macOS, Chromium desktop browser.

### Impact and evidence

The user cannot browse or reopen saved files from the returned Files view without a workaround. This reproduction establishes a presentation-state failure, not missing files or changed permissions.

The existing `chat-pane-embedded-panels.test.ts` retention scenario passes its reader-removal and catalog-node-retention checks but fails an added desktop catalog-visibility assertion: expected `hidden=false`, received `true`. The other ten tests in that file pass. The live guest journey independently reaches the same state through ordinary sidebar navigation.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

System-owned Skill Workshop collection-review cron turns inherit normal workspace bootstrap instructions despite executing inside the restricted Workshop root. In two observed runs, this led to out-of-root read attempts and failed review jobs. Setting `payload.lightContext: true` in the monitor generator removed the conflicting bootstrap context and both jobs subsequently completed.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed trigger/configuration:

1. Use OpenClaw 2026.9.4 with automatic Skill Workshop collection reviews and an embedded OpenClaw agent.
2. The agent's normal workspace bootstrap instructions direct it to read supporting files outside its Workshop directory.
3. Run the generated `skill-collection-review-<agent>` cron job without overriding its generated payload.
4. Inspect the injected workspace context and tool results: normal bootstrap instructions are present, and following their external read instructions conflicts with the Workshop execution root.

Two affected jobs were observed in this installation. The particular read attempts depend on the agent's bootstrap instructions and model behavior; this is not claimed to fail for every agent or every run.

### Expected behavior

The self-contained Workshop maintenance turn should receive context compatible with its restricted execution root. It should not be instructed by unrelated normal-workspace bootstrap files to perform reads that its tool policy rejects. Keep the root restriction and maintenance tool allowlist intact.

### Actual behavior

Two weekly collection-review jobs failed after attempting reads outside the allowed root. Their Workshop directories were empty; there is no demonstrated loss of review coverage for existing Workshop content in this incident.

The monitor payload includes the maintenance prompt and tools allowlist but omits `lightContext`. Inspection of the installed runtime showed normal bootstrap workspace selection on this rooted path. The existing lightweight context path filters out the normal workspace bootstrap files.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS under WSL; user systemd Gateway service.

### Install method

Global npm installation.

### Model

The successful post-patch runs recorded `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, using the embedded `openclaw` harness. The exact model metadata for the original failed runs is not included in this report.

### Provider / routing chain

Post-patch execution metadata: embedded OpenClaw harness -> OpenAI. No provider or routing change was part of the patch.

### Logs

Sanitized post-patch measurements from the two actual cron runs:

| Check | Agent A | Agent B |
|---|---:|---:|
| Completion status | ok | ok |
| Duration | 13.393 s | 16.376 s |
| Injected workspace files | 0 | 0 |
| Tool failures | 0 | 0 |
| Consecutive cron errors after run | 0 | 0 |

Tool activity stayed within each agent's Workshop root. No private bootstrap contents, account identifiers, or full session transcripts are attached.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Current upstream generator, inspected while preparing this report:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/84c154f37c94d1b3435a2533c30f679e92d647d3/src/cron/skill-collection-review-monitor.ts

The payload in `resolveSkillCollectionReviewMonitorSpecs` still lacks `lightContext`.

Minimal locally tested change:

```diff
 payload: {
   kind: "agentTurn",
   message: SKILL_WORKSHOP_MAINTENANCE_PROMPT,
+  lightContext: true,
   toolsAllow: [...SKILL_WORKSHOP_MAINTENANCE_TOOLS],
 },
```

Local validation:

- Compared original vs patched generator output for 23 configured agents. Removing only the added `lightContext` property made the generated specs deep-equal.
- Applied the equivalent change to both generated copies in the installed distribution (the monitor module and worker bundle); both passed `node --check`.
- After restarting the Gateway, reconciliation projected `lightContext: true` onto all 23 system-owned review jobs.
- Ran the two previously affected cron jobs; both completed with the measurements above.

### Impact and severity

Observed impact: two failed system-owned weekly maintenance jobs and repeated operational alerts. The filesystem boundary rejected the reads; this report does not claim an isolation bypass. Broader failure frequency is not measured.

### Additional information

Please consider generating these maintenance jobs with lightweight context, using the existing context-mode mechanism, and adding a regression test for the generated payload/root-compatible bootstrap behavior.

The local patch leaves the maintenance prompt, tools allowlist, execution root, schedule, and delivery mode unchanged. It is a distribution-local workaround and can be overwritten by an upgrade.

Validation limitation: the live Workshops were empty. Successful review/reconciliation of a populated Workshop was not tested in this incident and should be covered before treating this as a complete upstream fix.

Related but distinct: #141102 concerns runtime eligibility being rejected before launch; this issue concerns bootstrap context on an admitted embedded runtime. #97317 discusses full context inheritance for isolated crons more generally.

### Template fields (bug_report.yml conformance)
- **Bug type:** reliability/behavior defect (worker lifecycle)
- **Beta release blocker:** No
- **Steps to reproduce:** 1. Run an agent fleet with session archival + reconcile enabled. 2. Force a worker into a long native SQLite/fsync operation (large transcript, slow disk). 3. Observe: the single-keyed `lifecycle-archive` queue never admits later plans, each retaining its full transcript buffer; the scheduled-reconcile owner is never released, and gateway startup awaits it.
- **Expected behavior:** A wedged worker is terminated after a bounded settlement window, its queue slot freed deterministically, and later archive/reconcile work proceeds; queue admission is bounded so overload fails fast instead of buffering unboundedly.
- **Actual behavior:** `session-accessor.sqlite-archive.ts` — the one-shot archive path uses the same single-keyed `lifecycle-archive` KeyedAsyncQueue with no cap and no settlement timeout (message/error/exit handlers only; the AbortSignal cancels only a *pending* FIFO slot, not a wedged running worker). `session-transcript-reconcile.ts` — task-pool execution has messageerror/abort handling but no wall-clock timeout, so a native-stuck worker holds the scheduled-reconcile owner forever.
- **OpenClaw version:** main (2026-10-17/18 tree); incident signatures observed on 2026.10.4
- **OS:** Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, fleet VMs)

## Impact evidence (production incident)
RSS climbed 1.2→2.9 GiB while the JS heap stayed flat (~1.45 GiB), with `workerMemoryMissing` repeatedly listing `sqlite-store.worker.js` as `pending` — a live but unresponsive worker stuck in native SQLite. Every subsequent transcript buffer queued behind the wedged worker accumulates as external (non-heap) memory; lifecycle deletion/eviction/maintenance hang → stall → ownership wedge → silent channel outage while /healthz stays 200.

## Notes
Upstream's post-9.8 worker hardening (idle heap collection #154408, wait-for-admission/release-caller-memory/handle-capacity) is related but does not close this gap. A downstream reference implementation exists (bounded queue admission `SQLITE_ARCHIVE_QUEUE_MAX_PLANS` + unref'd settlement timeout with terminate-and-free-slot; reconcile timeout with owner relinquish; 34 tests passing) — a PR adapted to current main will follow. Reference branch: DarojaAI/openclaw `fix/issue-138`.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add a dispatch-only / handoff mode for agent-to-agent message delivery that drops a task into the target session without reply-back ping-pong or announce back to the requester.

## Problem to solve

Current `sessions_send` semantics are great for agent-to-agent conversation, but they are a poor fit for a very common controller/worker workflow:

1. Agent A chooses the next task and the responsible department/worker
2. Agent A sends a fully-formed task order to Agent B
3. The human then switches to Agent B's main session and continues there

In that workflow, Agent A's job should end after dispatch.

Today, `sessions_send` always carries the reply-back ping-pong + announce lifecycle. That creates several problems for pure handoff scenarios:

- the target agent's first reply is re-injected into the requester session as an `inter_session` message
- the requester agent may then respond to that injected message, creating an unnecessary extra loop
- the final announce step still runs even though the use case was dispatch, not conversation
- requester transcripts get polluted with worker-side acceptance / planning chatter
- in some UIs, the injected `inter_session` message can be visually confused with a user-authored message

This is not just cosmetic. It changes the workflow semantics. A one-way handoff ends up behaving like an internal conversation, which adds token cost, transcript noise, and routing confusion.

## Proposed solution

Add an explicit dispatch-only mode for A2A delivery.

Any of the following shapes would solve the problem:

1. Extend `sessions_send` with an explicit mode or flags, for example:
   - `mode: "dispatch"`
   - or `replyBack: false`
   - or `announce: false`
2. Or add a separate primitive such as `sessions_deliver` / `sessions_enqueue` with one-way semantics

Requested behavior for dispatch mode:

- persist the message into the target session
- let the target session continue normally from there
- do not run reply-back ping-pong
- do not re-inject the target's first reply into the requester session
- do not run announce back to the requester unless explicitly requested
- optionally allow a minimal structured ack if the caller wants delivery confirmation

This would cleanly separate two valid A2A patterns:

- conversation / coordination
- one-way dispatch / handoff

## Alternatives considered

- Using `sessions_send` as-is and relying on prompting to suppress reply/announce behavior is brittle because the current lifecycle is framework-driven, not just model-driven.
- Setting `timeoutSeconds: 0` is not enough because it changes waiting behavior, not the underlying reply-back / announce semantics.
- Hard-banning A2A for dispatch workflows is too restrictive because A2A conversation is still useful in other cases.
- Existing announce suppression requests help with one part of the problem, but they do not address the earlier reply-back reinjection into the requester session.

## Impact

Affected: multi-agent controller/worker setups, especially when one agent routes work to another agent's main session
Severity: Medium to High for orchestrated workflows
Frequency: Common whenever `sessions_send` is used for handoff instead of negotiation
Consequence: extra token usage, polluted requester transcripts, confusing turn ownership, and workflow drift from "dispatch" into "conversation"

## Evidence/examples

Observed behavior in the current flow:

1. Agent A calls `sessions_send` to Agent B with a fully-formed task order
2. Agent B replies normally
3. That reply is re-injected into Agent A's session as an `inter_session` user message
4. Agent A may respond to that injected message even though the handoff was already complete
5. The announce step then runs on top of that

Related issues that touch adjacent parts of the same lifecycle:

- #8299 `Feature request: config option to suppress sub-agent announce`
- #33478 `[Feature]: Structured Callback Actions and Thread Context Inheritance for Agent Handoffs`
- #39476 `A2A sessions_send: target agent can call sessions_send back, causing duplicate messages`

## Additional information

The current `sessions_send` behavior makes sense for agent-to-agent coordination. The missing piece is a first-class dispatch semantic for cases where the caller wants a clean handoff and does not want the requester session pulled back into the loop.

This should ideally be an explicit framework-level mode rather than something enforced through prompt conventions or magic strings.

issues.body:
## Summary
A required subagent completion can successfully send the final answer to a Slack DM thread through the message tool, return `NO_REPLY`, and still fail requester settlement with `visible_reply_missing`. The expected destination is `user:U000000001`, while the settled receipt identifies its actual DM conversation as `D000000001` (also observed in normalized `channel:d000000001` form).

These identifiers are synthetic. The defect is destination equivalence in delivery bookkeeping, not a failed Slack send or a request to accept unverified silence.

## Version and evidence scope
Reproduced against the unmodified 2026.9.2 delivery function and native delivery-evidence helpers with a controlled Gateway response. The relevant direct-delivery path was also inspected in published 2026.9.4 and current main at the pinned source below. This is not a claim of a live end-to-end run on main.

## Reproduction
1. Set up a required child completion with a user-facing requester, `requireVisibleReply: true`, Slack destination `user:U000000001`, account `default`, thread `1700000000.000001`.
2. Let the requester send its complete answer through the message tool to that user's verified DM conversation `D000000001`, in the same thread and account.
3. Return this synthetic successful requester result to `sendSubagentAnnounceDirectly`:
```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "result": {
    "payloads": [{"text": "NO_REPLY"}],
    "meta": {"stopReason": "end_turn"},
    "didSendViaMessagingTool": true,
    "messagingToolSentTargets": [{
      "provider": "slack", "to": "D000000001", "accountId": "default",
      "threadId": "1700000000.000001", "text": "Complete report delivered",
      "sourceReplyFinal": true
    }]
  }
}
```
4. Observe `{delivered:false, reason:"visible_reply_missing", error:"completion agent did not produce a visible reply"}` despite the completed send.

Expected: credit the committed final receipt only after verifying that the DM conversation belongs to the expected user, with identical account and thread. Do not resend the answer.

## Mechanism and fix direction
`hasMessagingToolDeliveryToSource` relies on `sourceDeliveryTargetsMatch`; normalization alone cannot establish the relationship between a user ID and a DM conversation ID. [Current direct-delivery source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/520bf609efacf80918d84c9a196288b646076574/src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-direct-delivery.ts).

An isolated candidate fix that resolves the receipt's conversation to the exact recipient and adds an equivalent destination to this attempt's delivery evidence changes the result to `{delivered:true, requesterVisibleFinalDelivered:true}`. It does not rewrite the outbound destination or bypass account/thread checks.

Regression coverage should include wrong recipient, different account, omitted account under a non-default account, wrong thread/provider, `final:false`, absent receipt, failed recipient lookup, abort, and requester ownership change during lookup. A focused native-function suite with those boundaries passes 24 cases against the candidate. Default-account omission must not become a wildcard for arbitrary accounts.

Related: #121187 (silent completion settlement), #142037 (different explicit-route bookkeeping defect involving top-level thread placement). Here the thread is identical; the mismatch is specifically user destination versus verified DM conversation.

issues.body:
## Summary

`memory-core` keys each workspace's recall/dreaming state by the **workspace path string** (`sha256(path.resolve(workspaceDir))`), not by a stable filesystem identity. When the same physical workspace directory is reachable via two different paths — the usual Docker case of a bind mount visible at a host path and a container path — the two paths hash to two different `workspaceKey`s, each backed by its own capped recall store. If the path the runtime passes to memory-core changes from one form to the other (e.g. an `agents.defaults.workspace` config change from container-form to host-form), the accumulated recall signal is orphaned under the old key and deep-dreaming reports `candidates=0` even though fresh material is being collected.

Confirmed on `2026.9.2`, and the keying logic is unchanged on the current default branch (through `2026.9.4`), so upgrading does not resolve it.

## Where

`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-state.ts`:

```
normalizeMemoryCoreWorkspaceKey(dir) => path.resolve(dir)   // lowercased on win32
memoryCoreWorkspaceStateKey(dir)     => sha256(normalize(dir))
```

`path.resolve` normalizes `.`/`..` and relative segments but does **not** resolve bind mounts — a bind mount is not a symlink; both paths are real paths to the same inode. So `/opt/app/workspace` and `/home/node/.openclaw/workspace` (same `dev`+`ino`) produce two distinct keys and two distinct `plugin_state_entries` namespaces (each capped, e.g. 512 entries).

## Impact

Deep-dreaming promotion (`rankShortTermPromotionCandidates`) reads the recall store for the *currently-resolved* key. When the resolved path flips:

- The old key still holds the accumulated recall signal (recallCount, uniqueQueries, score) but is no longer read.
- The new key starts empty and re-accumulates from scratch.
- Until the new key re-accumulates enough concentrated signal, **no entry crosses the promotion score threshold** (`DEFAULT_MEMORY_DEEP_DREAMING_MIN_SCORE`, 0.75) → `dreaming promotion complete (candidates=0)`.

This is silent (the run completes "ok") and disproportionately hits **mature, high-traffic workspaces**: they spread recall attention across many daily notes, so the fresh post-flip key can't concentrate enough signal on any single memory to cross 0.75. Low-traffic workspaces concentrate signal on few memories and keep promoting, which masks the defect.

## Reproduction (mechanism)

1. Run a workspace whose recall store has accumulated signal (memories recalled repeatedly over time), so deep-dreaming promotes normally.
2. Bind-mount that workspace at two paths (host + container view — standard Docker).
3. Change the workspace path the runtime hands to memory-core from one form to the other (e.g. `agents.defaults.workspace` container-form → host-form).
4. Observe: subsequent deep-dreaming runs report `candidates=0` despite ongoing recall collection; the pre-flip signal is intact but under the old key's namespace.

## Evidence it's the keying (not thresholds/dedup)

- The ranker never reads `MEMORY.md`; the only "already known" exclusion is the per-entry `promotedAt` flag — so it is not a wiki-dedup effect.
- Counterfactual on real data: under the split, the best available entry scored 0.7413 (< 0.75) → 0 candidates. Merging the two keys' signal for the same physical workspace yields **8 entries ≥ 0.75**. It is a 0-vs-8 difference, i.e. dispositive rather than marginal.

## Proposed fix

Key the workspace by a **stable filesystem identity (`dev`+`ino`)** or by an explicit stable `workspaceId` injected by the runtime, instead of `sha256(path.resolve(...))`, in `normalizeMemoryCoreWorkspaceKey` / `memoryCoreWorkspaceStateKey`.

Note: `realpath` is **not** sufficient — bind mounts are not symlinks. Only `dev`+`ino` (or an injected id) unifies the two path forms.

Back-compat caveat: changing the key derivation invalidates existing keyed state (would need a migration/rekey step), similar to the June state migration referenced in #123361 — worth planning so it doesn't strand the existing accumulated signal.

## Related (not duplicates)

- #97455 / #97458 (closed, not-planned) — same path-based keying primitive, but the opposite symptom (cross-workspace leakage in multi-user deployments) rather than a single workspace split across two orphaned keys by path aliasing.
- #123361 (open) — same symptom family (short-term recall working set frozen after a state migration), but attributed to the JSON→`plugin_state_entries` migration, not to path/bind-mount aliasing.
- #96118 (closed, not-planned) — same surface symptom ("dreaming runs but promotes 0"), different cause (candidates stuck at low confidence / memory search unavailable).

issues.body:
## Summary
Workboard dispatch launches every card as a subagent (`runtime.subagent.run`, session key `subagent:workboard-<board>-<card>`). Subagent sessions are intentionally view-only in control-ui, and the only offered action is "open parent session". When the dispatcher is a background/automation/heartbeat session, the worker's parent is ephemeral/unrelated, so an unfinished card cannot be continued anywhere.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create a card on the workboard and let automation/heartbeat dispatch it.
2. Open the worker session (e.g. `/chat/<agent>/...`).
3. UI shows: "View-only subagent" / "This is a subagent of {parent}. Continue the conversation in its parent session."
4. If the worker did not finish, there is no way to continue it; the parent is a background heartbeat session unrelated to the task.

## Expected
A Workboard card should be runnable as a **top-level, resumable session**:
- normal session key (no `subagent:` prefix), no parent lineage,
- visible in the session list, interactive, with Resume/Continue,

or, at minimum, an explicit **"Continue in new session" / "Promote to session"** action that copies the worker transcript into a normal session.

## Proposed change (staged)
1. **Core:** expose a plugin runtime API to spawn a top-level session, e.g. `runtime.sessions.spawn(...)`, or add an option to the existing spawn path (`backend: "session"` / `topLevel: true`) that creates a session without a parent.
2. **Workboard:** use that API in `dispatchAndStartWorkboardCards`; make `workboardSessionKeyForCard` return a normal key (`workboard:<board>:<card>`); replace the `subagent_ended`-based completion tracking (`syncWorkboardSubagentEnded`) with lifecycle derived from session events/status.
3. **control-ui:** enable composer + Resume/Continue for card sessions (currently disabled by `subagentSessionDisabled` based on parent lineage).
4. **Migration/doctor:** convert existing `subagent:workboard-*` session keys, or mark old cards as legacy.

## Code references (dist, v2026.9.4)
- `extensions/workboard/index.js` — dispatch passes `subagent: api.runtime.subagent`.
- `runtime-api-*.mjs` — `dispatchAndStartWorkboardCards` → `params.subagent.run({ sessionKey, ... })`.
- `runtime-api-*.mjs` — `workboardSessionKeyForCard` builds `subagent:workboard-<board>-<card>`.
- `control-ui-core-*.js` — `subagentViewOnly`, `subagentSessionDisabled`, `openParentSession`.
- `loader-runtime-load-*.mjs` / `runtime-*.mjs` — plugin runtime exposes `agent`/`subagent` only; there is no `sessions` runtime.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A card can be dispatched as a normal (non-subagent) session and is resumable from the UI.
- [ ] Existing cards keep working; a migration path is provided.
- [ ] Automation/heartbeat dispatch does not create uncontinuable orphans.
- [ ] (Fallback) "Continue in new session" available for legacy subagent workers.

## Priority
High for automation / managed deployments — tasks routinely get orphaned when dispatched from scheduled runs.

## Workaround today
Dispatch from a persistent foreground session instead of heartbeat, or copy the worker transcript and continue in a new session.

## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

Control UI changes the order of `show_widget` cards relative to surrounding progress text when projecting a multi-widget assistant turn, including live display and canonical history.

## Steps to reproduce

The deterministic repro uses synthetic messages only; no plugin or model credentials are required.

1. Start from upstream main `68b7893b3ca977a238af165717f7bc2a40e1a8f0`.
2. Construct one user turn with this recorded sequence:
   - assistant commentary `Step one`, timestamp 1000;
   - `show_widget` ToolResult for `Widget one`, timestamp 2000;
   - assistant commentary `Step two`, timestamp 3000;
   - `show_widget` ToolResult for `Widget two`, timestamp 4000.
3. Build the Control UI transcript with tool details hidden, first from live stream segments plus tool results, then from persisted history passed through `augmentChatHistoryWithCanvasBlocks`.
4. Compare the visible text/widget sequence. The proposed regression also covers `materializeVisibleStreamState` and the terminal assistant carrying the run's aggregated Canvas blocks.

## Expected behavior

The visible transcript preserves the recorded order in each representation:

`Step one → Widget one → Step two → Widget two`

Each widget appears once. This does **not** require a separate chat bubble for every widget; the concern is its position relative to the text.

## Actual behavior

On the unpatched source, the focused projection repro observes:
- Live stream: `Step one → Widget one → Widget two → Step two`.
- Canonical history projection: `Step one → Step two → Widget one → Widget two`.

Thus the chart/report may appear next to the wrong explanation, and live, final, and refreshed views can disagree about placement.

## OpenClaw version

Upstream main `68b7893b3ca977a238af165717f7bc2a40e1a8f0` (checked 2026-09-11).

## Operating system

macOS 26.4.

## Install method

Isolated source worktree, repository test and built Control UI harnesses.

## Model

None for the deterministic repro; synthetic commentary and tool results.

## Provider / routing chain

Synthetic Gateway messages → Control UI projection. No provider/API request.

## Logs and evidence

The regression compares the normalized visible sequence produced by `buildCachedChatItems`; it uses the actual Gateway Canvas-history projector rather than inventing a separate post-refresh message shape.

The relevant paths are `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread-build.ts` and `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread-items.ts`. Live previews can be attached to a nearby assistant before transient commentary is inserted, while historical Canvas projection can put tool-owned previews in later assistant content. That loses the interleaving already present in the tool transcript.

A focused UI-only patch and browser before/after evidence will follow in the linked PR. No change to Gateway protocol, storage, model APIs, plugin IDs, or global bubble-grouping policy is proposed.

## Impact and severity

Affected surface: Control UI turns that interleave commentary and multiple widgets.

Severity: visual/context mismatch; the report may no longer sit beside the explanation that introduced it. No data loss or authorization bypass was observed.

Frequency: reproducible with the synthetic sequence above; frequency across other providers and production installations has not been measured.

## Additional information

This is distinct from whitespace being collapsed inside commentary (#141932), and from duplicate Canvas refresh ownership addressed in #138155/#138593. Keeping one copy of a widget does not by itself preserve where that copy belongs.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw self-hosted gateway, systemd user service, Node.js v24 (24.19.0 on 2026.9.8, 24.22.1 on 2026.10.6), Linux x64
- Single-user deployment, active Discord channels, ~50 cron jobs (many spawning isolated agent sessions), browser automation in regular use
- ExecStart carries --max-old-space-size=4972 (host has ~10 GiB RAM + 4 GiB swap)

## Symptom
Gateway process RSS grows continuously from a ~2.1-2.5 GiB post-restart baseline until a restart is required. On repeated controlled restarts:

- 2026.9.8: RSS re-crossed 2.7 GiB within ~8h of restart; reached ~3.2 GiB within ~24h. Same shape on the prior install.
- 2026.10.6 (after full reinstall + upgrade): RSS ~2.1 GiB at restart → ~3.0 GiB at +12h → ~3.23-3.40 GiB at +17h. Sawtooth pattern: oscillates a few hundred MB, but the ceiling rises steadily.

The growth is NOT in the JS heap. Verified via the gateway's own diagnostics and /proc during live peaks: main heap stays ~1.4 GiB (well under the 4972 MiB cap), worker heaps total ~1.0-1.3 GiB, heap is stable across the growth period. The delta is off-heap: external/ArrayBuffers, which per the gateway's own memory-pressure log message are "not capped."

## Impact
The RSS growth ratchets the host swap band upward (swap never returns to baseline without a restart), and over ~3 days of uptime drives the box toward swap exhaustion. We experienced one hard wedge at ~4 days uptime (gateway unresponsive, in-flight replies lost, ~7.5h before manual recovery). Recovery is a gateway restart; recurrence is within hours.

## The monitoring blind spot (secondary bug)
The gateway's own "memory pressure: level=warning reason=rss_threshold" log fires reliably on the 2.52 GiB threshold in the heap-visible component on some builds — but on 2026.10.6 it produced ZERO rss_threshold lines across an entire day in which raw process RSS exceeded that threshold by ~0.7-0.9 GiB continuously (verified: journal grep count 0, /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS 3.2-3.4 GiB at the same timestamps). The internal monitor appears to measure a subset (heap + known structures) rather than process RSS, so it reports "no pressure" while the OS-level footprint is 30%+ past its own alarm line. Anyone relying on the gateway's self-reported memory health will miss this leak class entirely.

## Repro
We have not found a minimal repro. The deployment is long-lived (multi-week continuous uptime except for maintenance), high-turnover (isolated agent sessions created and destroyed by cron every hour), and uses browser automation. Recurrence is deterministic across restarts and survives a full reinstall (2026.9.8 → 2026.10.6) and a Node minor bump (24.19.0 → 24.22.1), which suggests it is not a one-batch leak but a steady-state accumulation — candidates: session-transcript worker lifecycle, archive/cache buffers in external memory, or per-turn allocations that never GC because nothing references them from the JS heap.

## Evidence available
- Redacted excerpts from the gateway's diagnostics export (heap ~1.4 GiB vs process RSS ~3.2 GiB at peak, worker/heap breakdown) — the full bundle contains deployment-identifying details so we will share sanitized sections on request, or run any instrumentation you specify on a live instance
- Hourly RSS/swap sample log across the growth curves (2.1 → 3.4 GiB over multiple restart cycles)
- Gateway journal excerpts (memory-pressure lines, worker startup states)
- Timeline documentation across three restart cycles

Happy to run any additional instrumentation on a live instance.

## Ask
1. Is off-heap/external memory growth a known issue on this usage profile? Any flags/mitigations to cap or force reclamation (e.g. periodic worker recycling, an external-buffer pressure trigger)?
2. Should the internal rss_threshold check measure process RSS (VmRSS) rather than the current subset? As-is it gives false "healthy" during a leak that consumes the host.

issues.body:
# Upstream report 2 — version migration can leave the running gateway older than the CLI

**Prepared 2026-10-28. NOT POSTED.**

---

## Summary

`npm install -g openclaw@X` installs into the **global prefix of whichever Node binary is first on
`PATH`**. If the gateway service (systemd, launchd, or a managed install) points at a **different**
prefix, the package is upgraded, `openclaw --version` reports the new version, and the running
gateway continues on the old code.

If the new binary has already been run (which `openclaw --version` does not, but any new CLI
invocation does), it migrates agent databases to a newer schema. The old gateway then refuses to
boot against a schema it does not know.

## Observed sequence (2026-10-28, this host)

1. Gateway service `ExecStart` used `/home/<user>/.hermes/node/bin/node ... /home/<user>/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`
   (OpenClaw 2026.10.3).
2. A supported Node was installed at `~/tools/node-26.12.1` (required by the 2026.10.6 eMudhra
   remediation: Node `>=24.22.1 <25 || >=26.12.1`).
3. `PATH=~/tools/node-26.12.1/bin:$PATH npm install -g openclaw@2026.10.8` installed into
   `~/tools/node-26.12.1/lib/node_modules/openclaw`.
4. The unit was repointed to the new **Node**, but still loaded
   `~/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js` — the **old** install, still 2026.10.3.
5. The gateway ran fine and reported **10.3**. `openclaw --version` reported **10.8**.
6. The 10.8 binary was invoked, migrated all five agent databases to the newer schema, and the
   gateway then failed to boot: `status=78/CONFIG`, sessions unavailable.

**Recovery required** using the same binary the unit runs: stop the gateway, run
`doctor --fix` with the matching binary, restart. Rolling back the package would not have worked —
the databases were already migrated forward.

## Why this is worth a fix, not just documentation

- The CLI and the service can silently diverge, and **the only reliable check is comparing the
  `dist/index.js` path in the running process with the version on disk at that path**. Neither
  `openclaw --version` nor `npm ls -g` reveals the mismatch.
- The failure appears as a **config error** (`Unrecognized key` / schema mismatch), which points the
  operator at their configuration rather than at a version split.
- Migrations are one-way, so the discovery happens after the point of easy return.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Warn on version skew at startup.** If the loaded `dist` version differs from the
   globally-installed version on `PATH`, log it prominently.
2. **Have `openclaw update`/`npm` guidance pin the install prefix** to the one the service uses, or
   report which prefix was targeted and whether a service is pointed elsewhere.
3. **Report the running build in the health endpoint** so a mismatch is visible without shell access.
4. **Refuse a forward schema migration** when the binary performing it is not the binary the service
   is configured to run — or at least say so before writing.

## Environment

- Before: OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (59cb447), Node 26.7.0
- After: OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (dc2523e), Node 26.12.1
- Install layout: systemd user unit; two `node_modules` prefixes present simultaneously
- Time to diagnose without the log: not established; the actual fix was found by reading the unit
  `ExecStart` against `ps -o cmd= -p <MainPID>`

## Mitigation now in place here

Service and CLI both pinned to `~/tools/node-26.12.1/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`, so the
two cannot drift again. This is a local workaround, not a product fix.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On macOS arm64, a standalone `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` on 2026.10.8 stopped a working managed Gateway after successful `update repair`, then spent over 53 minutes in offline maintenance with only two lines of output, while file captures and repeated read-only SQLite revision workers continued.

This report focuses on **prolonged, nearly silent offline Doctor maintenance**. The preceding update's package-retention failure is context, not an established cause of the slow Doctor.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed once on this affected installation; not a minimal or independently repeatable reproduction:

1. Start with npm-installed OpenClaw 2026.10.6, managed by a macOS LaunchAgent. Verify CLI/Gateway both report 2026.10.6 and connectivity is OK.
2. Preserve configuration/service files and take a consistent SQLite backup (backup `quick_check`: `ok`).
3. Run `openclaw update --tag 2026.10.8 --yes --timeout 1200`, with `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX` set to the existing runtime prefix. The updater installs and activates 2026.10.8, verifies the Gateway, but exits 1 during package-backup retention (see context below).
4. Verify CLI/Gateway both report 2026.10.8, runtime running, connectivity OK.
5. Run `openclaw update repair`. This returns exit 0, including `Gateway restarted and verified after Doctor repair.`
6. As an additional operator-selected maintenance pass, run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`.
7. Observe the Gateway stop and remain unavailable for over 53 minutes; Doctor output remains only the two lines below. OS-level inspection shows ongoing capture writes and read-only SQLite worker subprocesses.

**Important attribution:** step 6 was explicitly launched by our automation, not automatically appended by the core updater. We should not have treated a further offline Doctor as an unconditional requirement after successful repair. The report does not attribute the entire elapsed upgrade session or this additional outage to `openclaw update` alone.

### Expected behavior

Doctor's own `Gateway health will be checked after Doctor repair` message and the preceding repair's verified restart establish that the managed service should be restored after maintenance. We are not claiming an official maximum runtime or a known-good timing baseline.

For maintenance that must keep a messaging Gateway offline, please expose the active phase, elapsed time, capture counters/progress, and documented safe cancellation/recovery behavior. Consider preparing immutable package captures before the offline lock where safe, and clearly indicating whether an additional Doctor pass is necessary after successful update repair. These are requested improvements, not claims about an existing guarantee.

### Actual behavior

At 09:08:49 UTC+08:00 on 2026-10-29, Doctor had been running for **3,235 seconds (over 53 minutes)** without finishing. The managed bot was unavailable. `gateway status --deep` refused access because the state database was undergoing offline maintenance by the Doctor process. No force-kill, lock deletion, competing repair, or forced Gateway start was attempted.

Doctor stdout/stderr, redirected to a regular local file, remained:

```text
┌  OpenClaw doctor
Stopped the managed Gateway for Doctor repair.
```

Activity was visible only through external process/filesystem inspection. This is **not proof of a deadlock**; fresh writes demonstrate activity, but not bounded completion or useful user-visible progress.

### OpenClaw version

Before: `OpenClaw 2026.10.6 (fe06181)`.
During affected standalone Doctor: `OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (dc2523e)`.
After initial activation, CLI and running Gateway both reported 2026.10.8.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1 (build 26A434), arm64; Node v26.12.1; 24 GiB physical RAM.

### Install method

npm global in an existing per-version runtime prefix; standard managed LaunchAgent, loopback Gateway. The historical prefix directory was reused by the in-place upgrade, so its directory name does not represent the installed version. Update commands used explicit local HTTP(S) proxy environment variables. No inference request is needed to observe the maintenance issue.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

Sanitized observed timeline. All times are **2026-10-29, UTC+08:00**; process launch/check timestamps are from the local orchestration log, not estimates of exact internal lock acquisition.

| Time | Observation |
|---|---|
| 07:52:27 | Operator backup created; SQLite backup quick_check = ok |
| 07:52:44.427 | Update process launched |
| 08:10:41.546 | Update returned exit 1; CLI version check reports 2026.10.8 |
| 08:10:41.657 | Gateway check reports 2026.10.8, running, connectivity OK |
| 08:11:03.147 | `update repair` launched |
| 08:14:54.403 | Repair returned exit 0; standalone Doctor launched |
| 08:34:41 | Doctor still active; state DB explicitly under offline maintenance |
| 08:49:21 | Doctor still active; a fresh `sqlite-source-revision.worker.js ... content-version` child observed |
| 09:05:42.944 | Doctor payload capture's latest file write; 3,244 files / 359,424,575 bytes counted |
| 09:08:49.654 | Still incomplete; 3,614 files / 362,129,856 bytes; newest write at 09:08:49.332 |

At inspection, Doctor held the Gateway/state locks and an open capture directory under `<capture-root>/doctor-<id>/`. It also had an open plugin-capture `owner.sqlite`. OS process sampling showed main-thread stacks including `node::SyncProcessRunner::Spawn` -> `kevent` and SQLite `Database::Open`/filesystem-stat operations. Repeated short-lived children had this command shape:

```text
node <install-root>/dist/infra/sqlite-source-revision.worker.js \
  --openclaw-sqlite-readonly-child content-version <state-dir>/state/openclaw.sqlite
```

Status error (paths/PID sanitized):

```text
Gateway status failed: OpenClaw state at <state-dir>/state/openclaw.sqlite
is undergoing offline maintenance by sqlite-maintenance process <doctor-pid>;
retry when it finishes. For update progress, run openclaw update status --json.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Measured update phase durations from the updater's terminal result:

```text
requested (75.94s) -> staging (80ms) -> validating (250.99s)
-> activating (532.7s) -> restarting (4.22s) -> verifying (74.92s)
Gateway downtime: 592.4s.
Recorded recovery: verified serving 2026.10.8.
Recorded verification: service running (2026.10.8); version verified;
channels ready; HTTP ready.
```

Preceding update failure context:

```text
OpenClaw update failed: state-migrated-no-rollback.
Failed: verifying
Failed: package-backup-retention — Exit code: 1;
Package publication object changed: <redacted-install-root>
Automatic database restoration unavailable: databases changed after snapshot
capture; the writer is unknown. Snapshots retained.
Your Gateway is still serving 2026.10.8; nothing to restore.
Run openclaw update repair from the installed version to finish config and plugin maintenance.
```

Snapshot scale from the initial update log: shared DB 34,033,664 bytes; main-agent DB 265,056,256 bytes; two additional agent DB snapshots 692,224 bytes each. The shared DB is recorded twice in snapshot output; do not count that as two distinct stores. These are snapshot sizes, not a current total state-directory size.

Repair completed in approximately 231 seconds and logged:

```text
Restarted LaunchAgent: <gui-domain>/<gateway-label>
Gateway restarted and verified after Doctor repair.
Update finalization completed with warnings.
```

### Impact and severity

Affected: one local managed messaging Gateway, used via Feishu. High user impact: the standalone Doctor kept the bot offline for over 53 minutes at the last checkpoint, with no phase/counter progress in its output. The user repeatedly had to request status; only OS-level investigation could distinguish active capture work from a hang. Frequency: one instrumented attempt; no broad incidence claim. No data loss established, and no database contents or private chat records are attached.

### Additional information

- This is a live affected-host observation, not a proven root-cause diagnosis. Repeated revision checks may be relevant but have not been established as the bottleneck.
- The initial update's recorded 592.4-second outage and the later standalone Doctor outage are separate intervals; the intervening Gateway was verified running. Do not interpret the whole wall-clock session as one continuous core-update outage.
- Existing missing canonical transcript archive-copy warnings and acpx/codex migration-confirmation warnings were already present before this upgrade. They are not established regressions or proven causes.
- The updater also preserved local package overrides without reapplying them; this is not a pristine fresh-install reproduction. No contents from those overrides are included in this report.
- Related symptoms: #139485 (prolonged offline finalization; not claiming same root cause) and #157603 (historical snapshot/update delays; different version/path).
- Original logs and recovery snapshots are retained locally. This report includes only manually selected sanitized technical evidence; no config, credentials, absolute personal paths, database files, chat contents, or diagnostic ZIP is being published.
- Status is an as-of checkpoint, not a claim that the process can never complete. A final outcome can be added when available.

issues.body:
## Problem

`openclaw resume` does not cancel its private pre-TUI Gateway client when the CLI has accepted Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. This affects the initial connection, the recent-session lookup, and opaque handoff resolution. The normal TUI cancellation owner has not started yet.

## Reproduction

Source: current main `e25c026eb75d34ecdeed1d64d68454fb919f3c19` (reports OpenClaw2026.10.8), Linux, Node26.12.1. No provider/model or real channel is used.

1. Build the normal CLI with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`.
2. In a real PTY and isolated HOME/config/state, run `node openclaw.mjs resume agent:main:proof --url ws://127.0.0.1:PORT --token <synthetic-fixture-token>` against a loopback protocol peer.
3. Let the peer record but withhold either the ordinary connect acknowledgement or the subsequent `sessions.list` response. For the handoff sibling, use a valid locally encoded handoff and hold `sessions.resolve`.
4. Deliver SIGINT or SIGTERM only after the relevant actual request has been recorded.

Actual in all three stages: the real CLI prints its accepted-interruption cleanup notice, remains alive after 2.5seconds, and the independent native WebSocket recorder sees zero transport closes. The peer uses the real GatewayChatClient protocol, not a replacement for the resume command or TUI.

Controls: an ordinary no-match lookup closes its connection and exits1 with the existing message. A completed valid selection reaches the actual connected/idle TUI, records its normal read requests, then Ctrl-D closes both preflight/TUI connections and naturally exits0. These are local CLI and native-transport observations, not a real Gateway database, model, or remote-service acceptance claim.

## Expected behavior and scope

The resume preflight owner should observe the invocation lifetime, stop and join its private client, and leave130/143 to the root CLI. Cover connect, session listing, and opaque handoff together. Release this local cancellation ownership before ordinary `runTui` takes over; preserve real connection/read errors, cleanup failures, and normal no-match/attachment behavior. No Gateway authorization, session selection policy, protocol, config schema, or TUI behavior change is intended.

I plan to implement and test this bounded lifecycle correction. Existing resolution/handoff ownership was established by #140056 and #120664.
