issues.body:
### Summary

Add a pre-boot PostgreSQL schema lifecycle/capability extension so PlanetScale Neki can support OpenClaw's native agent conversation storage. An experimental single-shard implementation with a pinned host patch is available: https://github.com/PandelisZ/openclaw-neki

### Problem to solve

On OpenClaw commit `d7349d9395e2bde0f42882a9f7ef8afab59e19c3`, Neki's routed PostgreSQL connection cannot complete the stock native storage path:

- Shared-state discovery calls `pg_export_snapshot()`, rejected with `NK013 [200]`.
- Keeping shared state on SQLite bypasses that path, but native agent bootstrap encounters `NK013 [817]`: dependent DDL is planned before the router can see relations created earlier in the same transaction. Splitting statements within that transaction does not resolve it.
- Autocommit base agent DDL succeeds, but custom text-search configuration DDL is rejected with `NK013 [302]`.
- The native transcript multi-write CTE hits `XX000: unhandled logical plan operator in cost estimation: *logical.OutputClauses` through normal routing.

The tested public plugin boundary does not expose an early hook for native bootstrap, schema capabilities, or runtime connection routing. A tool or object-storage plugin cannot supply native conversation storage.

### Proposed solution

A manifest-owned, explicitly selected schema lifecycle artifact resolved before database workers start, with a serializable descriptor for worker loading. Core retains generated DDL, store identities, catalog comparison, initial rows, schema sealing, transaction boundaries, and custody checks.

The prototype implements this narrow first milestone:

- One explicitly approved Neki shard; native agent data on Neki and shared state on SQLite.
- Routed autocommit bootstrap with durable per-effect receipts. Ambiguous effects stop for manual recovery.
- Core builds an independent scratch schema and compares catalogs before admitting the native seal.
- After native admission, runtime data queries pin the selected shard and verify its native store identity.
- Opted-in transcript writers allocate sequence IDs as standalone queries inside the existing transaction, then bind the IDs into the native multi-write CTE. Neki rejects direct data queries combining router-managed `nextval` with table access (`0A000`), while a standalone sequence call succeeds.
- Derived full-text/vector search is explicitly unavailable. Fresh initialization and matching sealed-store reopen are supported; migrations and database porting are rejected.

The proposed API is experimental and pinned, not an upstream-supported installation contract. Feedback on the smallest acceptable upstream seam would help before preparing a core PR.

### Alternatives considered

- Standard PostgreSQL already works; this request is specifically for Neki compatibility.
- Neki compatibility improvements could remove some host requirements over time. `__neki.wait_for_ddl()` returned `42883` on the tested database, so the prototype does not assume a propagation barrier exists.
- Direct shard targeting cannot run schema-changing DDL, so it cannot replace routed bootstrap.
- Removing runtime transaction boundaries would weaken native consistency. The prototype preserves them.

### Impact

Affected: users choosing PlanetScale Neki for native OpenClaw agent storage.

Severity/frequency: the stock pinned path blocks fresh agent provisioning in the tested configuration; it is not an intermittent model-provider failure.

Consequence: native conversations cannot start without a compatibility path or a different database. The experimental patch demonstrates a limited working route, but is not a production or multi-shard qualification.

### Evidence/examples

Verified on 2026-10-28 with Node.js 26.12.1 and `openai/gpt-4.1-mini`:

1. A real isolated Gateway completed an assistant turn with agent data on Neki.
2. An independent PostgreSQL read found the exact assistant reply in Neki's native transcript content.
3. The Gateway process stopped and a new OS process started with the same state.
4. The new process retrieved the exact saved assistant message and completed a second real model turn recalling a synthetic marker absent from the second request.
5. Both processes stopped cleanly. Disposable schemas were removed and absence verified.

The strict harness reported `nativeConversation=true`, `restartHistory=true`, `modelContextAfterProcessRestart=true`, and `cleanup=complete`. It requires successful status and exact non-error assistant text; request echoes and error payloads cannot satisfy the assertions.

Additional validation: 39 extension tests, 18 focused host tests, scoped host typecheck, touched-source lint/format, guarded patch application/checksums, and fresh independent review passed. The full upstream suite and a packaged build were not run.

- [Implementation and pinned host patch](https://github.com/PandelisZ/openclaw-neki)
- [Setup and lifecycle contract](https://github.com/PandelisZ/openclaw-neki/blob/master/docs/host-integration.md)
- [Verification and limitations](https://github.com/PandelisZ/openclaw-neki/blob/master/docs/verification.md)
- [Issue research](https://github.com/PandelisZ/openclaw-neki/blob/master/docs/issues.md)

Related prior work: [Rika-Labs/akter#487](https://github.com/Rika-Labs/akter/issues/487) and [fix #553](https://github.com/Rika-Labs/akter/pull/553), concerning Neki migration DDL semantics. Bounded searches of OpenClaw issues/PRs/comments and the official community forum found no existing Neki/PlanetScale thread.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance. The experimental extension and host patch are already implemented and tested; this proposal asks for agreement on the upstream capability boundary.

### Additional information

Current limits: one shard, fresh stores/matching sealed-store reopen, SQLite shared state, disabled derived search. Schema upgrades, database porting, topology changes, multi-shard behavior, backup restore, failover, Bun, and production use have not been qualified. The tested commit is a pinned reproduction, not a claim that every subsequent OpenClaw revision behaves identically.

Only minimized errors and synthetic test descriptions are shared. Private configuration, credentials, provider account/database identifiers, and raw operational logs are excluded.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`openclaw backup create --verify` fails with "Could not determine whether backup files are SQLite databases" on a state dir holding ~400k regular files, because the SQLite header probe sends every candidate path to one child process with a fixed 10 s budget; the same command succeeds on the same machine once the state dir holds ~40k files.

### Steps to reproduce

1. State dir with a few hundred thousand regular files (here: six `git worktree` checkouts an agent had placed under `<state>/worktrees/` plus a full clone under an agent workspace; ~406k files in total).
2. Stop the Gateway, run `openclaw backup create --output <dir> --verify`.
3. After ~90 s the command fails with the message below. `openclaw backup create --dry-run` succeeds (dry-run never runs the probe).
4. Move the checkouts out of the state dir (symlinks left behind; ~40k files remain), rerun step 2: the matched archive is written and verified.

### Expected behavior

The probe budget should not depend on the total number of files under the state dir: chunk the batch (N paths per child, each with its own budget), scale the timeout with batch size, or skip paths that cannot be SQLite databases (size < 100 bytes, `.git/objects/**`). The failure should also surface the underlying cause (`ETIMEDOUT`) instead of only the generic text, so operators do not go looking for unreadable files.

### Actual behavior

```text
Could not determine whether backup files are SQLite databases. Check that the backup worker can run and the source files are readable, then retry the backup.
```

All source files are readable. `probeSqliteDatabaseHeaders()` in `src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.ts` (from #183476, unchanged on `bd10ba29d338`) runs one `spawnSync` child for the whole batch with `timeout: 10_000` (line 23); `src/infra/backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts:220` builds that batch from every walked file plus visited directories. Probe time grows linearly with the file count, so the budget is exceeded on large state dirs regardless of disk health.

Timing from a read-only replica of the probe (open + 16-byte header read per path, same machine):

| files under state dir | probe time | `backup create --verify` |
|---|---|---|
| 406,460 | 37.2 s | fails as above |
| 40,361 | 5.3 s | succeeds (matched archive written in 13.5 min) |

### OpenClaw version

main `496f32bef297` (2026.10.7); probe code identical on current main `bd10ba29d338`

### Operating system

macOS (Darwin 27.2.0), Apple silicon Mac mini

### Install method

Git checkout of `main` (`dev` channel), Node 24 from Homebrew; `backup create` run with the Gateway stopped by our update orchestration

### Model

N/A (not model related)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

13 PostgreSQL stores (state, agent, workboard families on PostgreSQL 17); the remaining SQLite files in the state dir are plugin/sidecar databases.

### Logs

```text
2026-10-28 09:58 openclaw backup create --output <dir> --verify
Could not determine whether backup files are SQLite databases. Check that the backup worker can run and the source files are readable, then retry the backup.
(exit after ~90 s; dry-run succeeds)

2026-10-28 10:49–11:02 same command after moving the checkouts out of the state dir
Created <dir>/2026-10-28T10-49-….tar.gz
Archive verification: passed
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

See the timing table above; the replica probe is a 30-line Node script doing `fs.openSync` + 16-byte `readSync` per path.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any installation whose state dir accumulates many regular files (agent checkouts, large workspaces, session archives).
- Severity: blocks workflow — `openclaw update` refuses to proceed without the backup, so updates stop until the operator finds the cause.
- Frequency: always, once the file count crosses the budget.
- Consequence: failed updates with a misleading diagnostic.

### Additional information

Workaround: keep large source checkouts out of the state dir (or behind a symlink; the walker uses `symlinks: "include"` and does not follow them). Not a regression of the probe itself: the probe was introduced by #183476 (2026-10-25).

issues.body:
**Version info:** OpenClaw 2026.10.3 · Node v24.18.0 · macOS 26.5.2 (arm64, 16 GB RAM) · gateway run under launchd with `--max-old-space-size=8192`.

### Expected behaviour
1. The prepared-model-catalog worker's heap should stay bounded: the model catalog is finite and refresh/expiry exists.
2. Gateway worker population should return to its startup baseline (8) after load subsides — idle workers should be retired or pooled.

### Actual behaviour
1. `prepared-model-catalog.worker.js` heap grows monotonically and never shrinks. Sampled by the gateway's own `[diagnostics/memory]` reporter on the same worker thread over ~12 h of normal traffic: heapUsed 227 MB → 314 MB → 338 MB → 406 MB. A previous day's instance plateaued at ~304 MB until process restart — growth is bounded only by restarting the gateway.
2. `worker startup state` reports 8 workers at every fresh start, but `workerCount` climbs to 14–18 within hours and never returns to 8. Lifecycle records show repeated starts of `sqlite-store.worker.js`, `session-transcript.worker.js` and `openclaw-state-read.worker.js` with `retired: []` — no idle retirement.
3. `[diagnostics/memory]` `level=warning/critical reason=rss_growth` events recur every 1–2 h (rssGrowth 0.5–1.9 GB per window); peak RSS 3.55 GiB (heap 2.23 GiB) observed over two days.

### Reproduction steps
1. Run the gateway on a long-lived host (16 GB) with a normal multi-agent messaging workload for ~24 h; do not restart.
2. Observe `[diagnostics/memory]` lines in the gateway log: heapUsed for `prepared-model-catalog.worker.js` increases monotonically between samples taken hours apart on the same threadId.
3. Compare successive `[gateway] worker startup state` lines: `workerCount` exceeds the startup baseline (8) and stays elevated; per-worker `retired` arrays remain empty while new instances of the same worker scripts appear.
4. Restart resolves both until load recurs.

### Source observations (2026.10.3, from the published package)
- `prepared-model-runtime-*.mjs`: catalog/auth materialization creates new frozen owner objects per refresh; retirement (`retirePreparedModelRuntimeOwnerIfUnused`, `retirePreparedModelRuntimeGeneration`) is usage/generation-triggered only; the oldest-owner cap exists but no idle-timeout retire for workers.
- No documented configuration key exposes a catalog cache limit, TTL or worker idle timeout.
- Diagnostics text acknowledges: `workerLimitScope=js-heap-only; external/ArrayBuffers are not capped; nested workers are not included`. RSS grows faster than JS heap (RSS 1.6–3.5 GiB vs heap 0.6–2.2 GiB), consistent with uncapped external/native retention.

### Impact
Memory-pressure warnings accumulate until operator restart; on 16 GB multi-service hosts the gateway reaches ~3.5 GiB RSS within a day and competes with other services for RAM/swap. Workaround: scheduled daily restart.

### Environment / privacy notes
Logs contain no secrets; would submit a redacted log slice or a `gateway diagnostics export` bundle on request. (Private paths in the working evidence have been genericised here.)

### Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
Eviction or snapshot-reuse in the prepared-model-catalog worker; idle retirement or pooling for duplicate workers; cap/sampling of worker external + ArrayBuffer usage in memory diagnostics.

*(End of prepared issue. Draft also exists locally at `~/openclaw-audit/db-stability/UPSTREAM-ISSUE-SUMMARY-model-catalog-memory.md` — that earlier draft contains private paths and must NOT be submitted; this Part A version is the sanitised replacement.)*

issues.body:
## What happened

When a guest opens a Markdown attachment in the native document reader, consecutive spaces inside an inline code span collapse visually. Distinct literal values such as `alpha beta` and `alpha   beta` therefore look identical. This can obscure a meaningful difference when reading a report about exact string values.

## Reproduction

1. Attach a Markdown document containing the following lines to a conversation:

   ```markdown
   - One space: `alpha beta`
   - Three spaces: `alpha   beta`
   ```

2. Open the attachment in the side panel and expand the reader.
3. Compare the two inline values, then download the original Markdown.

Expected: the inline values remain visually distinguishable, while the document continues to wrap normally.

Actual: both values display with one space. The original download and the code element’s text retain all three spaces, so this is a presentation defect rather than document data loss.

## Evidence and scope

Reproduced in Chromium through the native attachment reader at desktop and narrow viewport sizes. The three-space text range measured 7.53125 px, equal to the first space alone; the middle space measured 0 px. Computed whitespace was `normal`. The downloaded 795-byte fixture matched the original SHA-256, and fenced code retained its spacing.

The serving revision was 09a58215b66ca511ae398ddf9e00e9c7b4eef9f6. The attachment reader, Markdown parser, and shared Markdown stylesheet are unchanged at b9251d11e37929b9dd7984ce06f8270fa710005f. The shared inline-code style in `ui/src/styles/sidebar-markdown.css` does not preserve whitespace. This report does not establish a clipboard, permission, or data-loss problem, and other browser engines have not been tested.

issues.body:
## What happens

`workboard.cards.update` (and `workboard.cards.create`) accept a `metadata` object, report success, but **do not persist client-supplied keys**. Re-reading the card shows only server-managed metadata (`automation`, `comments`, `notifications`, `proof`, `archivedAt`, `diagnostics`).

Measured on 2026.10.8 (dc2523e), 327 cards:

```
accepted=327  verified=0  dropped=327
```

`workboard.cards.bulk` is read-only, so there is no batch path either. `create` drops `metadata` the same way.

## Repro

```bash
# 1. create a card
openclaw workboard create --title probe --status todo

# 2. try to attach a client id via metadata
openclaw gateway call tools.invoke --params '{"name":"workboard.cards.update","arguments":{"id":"<card id>","patch":{"metadata":{"entryId":"abc-123"}}}}'

# 3. read back
openclaw workboard list --json   # metadata.entryId is absent
```

## Expected

Either of:

1. persist client metadata under a client namespace (e.g. `metadata.client.<key>`) and return it on read; or
2. **reject** a patch that contains unsupported keys with an explicit error.

Silent acceptance is the worst option: callers believe the write succeeded.

## Why it matters

Any external system that keeps a 1:1 mapping between its own ledger and workboard cards needs a stable id on the card. Without a writable metadata field, the only option is stuffing the id into `notes` and parsing text — which breaks whenever a card is renamed, duplicated, or its notes edited.

## Workaround today

`notes` carries `queue=<id> entryId=<id>` and consumers parse it. It works but is fragile and exactly the pattern we are trying to retire.

prs.title: fix(gateway): normalize NFC/NFD canonical forms in conversation list search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Calling the conversation list/search with a query typed in decomposed (NFD) form — common from mobile IMEs — misses conversations whose label or target is persisted in composed (NFC) form, and vice versa, so the conversation simply does not appear in the results even though its name contains the searched word. The fix normalizes both the query and each candidate value with `.normalize("NFC")` before comparing.

- Problem: `runGatewayConversationList` matched `label`/`target`/`conversationRef` against the query with only `toLowerCase()`. Canonically-equivalent strings that differ in normalization (NFD decomposed vs NFC composed) compare as unequal, so visually identical text fails to match.
- Solution: normalize the query (`query?.toLowerCase().normalize("NFC")`) and every candidate value (`value?.toLowerCase().normalize("NFC")`) before the `includes` comparison.
- What changed: `src/gateway/conversation-list.ts` (2 lines in the search predicate) and a regression test in `src/gateway/conversation-list.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: storage, persisted labels/targets, the `@handle` prefix handling, the eligibility/limit logic, and all other behavior of `runGatewayConversationList`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The filter predicate in `runGatewayConversationList` is the canonical owner of this search behavior, so the fix lives there rather than adding per-caller guards. It follows the same canonical-equivalence treatment already merged upstream for other search/list paths (e.g. `cronRunHistoryMatchesQuery` in `src/cron/run-history.ts`, and the workspace-files / session-repository search predicates), all of which normalize to NFC before comparing user- or agent-writable text.

- Best fix: normalize both sides of the comparison at the single predicate that owns the match, consistent with the rest of the codebase. No new parser, policy branch, or configuration surface.
- Alternative: normalizing only at write/storage time was rejected — labels/targets originate from many sources (channel directories, agents, config), and NFC storage is not guaranteed, so normalizing at comparison time is the robust, consistent choice.
- Risk: NFC normalization is a no-op for already-NFC text, so existing matches are unaffected; only the previously-missed cross-form matches become findable.

## User Impact

Users can now find conversations by name even when the query is typed with a different Unicode normalization than how the label/target was stored (for example a name typed on a phone's decomposed input matching a composed-form label). No existing search results are removed; the change only makes previously-missed, visually-identical matches appear.

## Evidence

Live verification of the changed comparison path (real `node` run exercising NFC/NFD forms of the same characters):

```console
$ node -e '
const q="cafe\u0301".toLowerCase().normalize("NFC"); // NFD-typed query -> NFC
const t="reef:user-caf\u00e9".normalize("NFC");      // NFC-persisted target
const l="Caf\u00e9 \u00e9quipe".normalize("NFC");    // NFC-persisted label
console.log("post-fix  target contains query:", t.toLowerCase().includes(q));
console.log("post-fix  label  contains query:", l.toLowerCase().includes(q));
console.log("pre-fix   target contains query:", "reef:user-caf\u00e9".toLowerCase().includes("cafe\u0301"));
console.log("pre-fix   label  contains query:", "Caf\u00e9 \u00e9quipe".toLowerCase().includes("cafe\u0301"));'
post-fix  target contains query: true
post-fix  label  contains query: true
pre-fix   target contains query: false
pre-fix   label  contains query: false
```

Behavior matrix (query typed NFD `cafe\u0301` against NFC-persisted `Caf\u00e9`):

```text
candidate form   => pre-fix result   => post-fix result
label (NFC)      => miss             => hit
target (NFC)     => miss             => hit
```

Regression test (added to `src/gateway/conversation-list.test.ts`), proven RED on the un-fixed source and GREEN with the fix:

```console
# pre-fix (source reverted, test kept)
 × runGatewayConversationList > matches conversation label/target across NFC/NFD canonical forms
   Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 8 passed (9)

# post-fix
 ✓ runGatewayConversationList > matches conversation label/target across NFC/NFD canonical forms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

Open PR collision check: searched open PR topics and scanned changed-file lists for `src/gateway/conversation-list.ts` / `conversation-list.test.ts` and the NFC/canonical-equivalence anchor; no open PR touches these files or solves this bug. Main's current code still contains the un-normalized predicate, so this fix is not redundant.

## What Problem This Solves

The repository dead-code check reports the documented history-model projection measurement as unused. #187191 introduced the standalone driver and its Node launch command, but omitted its executable-root registration. This adds an incorrect finding to the full-tree audit.

## User Impact

Developers running the dead-code check get an audit graph that recognizes this maintained command. The measurement implementation and the checks for private child modules and unused exports retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The script is a directly invoked command with no exported bindings. Registering its exact path in the existing `repositoryScriptEntries` list follows the repository's standalone-command convention and lets the full-tree and script-export configurations inherit the same owner. The change is one entry; it adds no wildcard, ignore or export exemption.

## Evidence

On source `82acfabb374991cdb9abeb8bb89984f0cb667733`, the [completed dependency-check job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40812528521/job/123246099340) reported zero production unused files and three full-tree findings. Running the complete unchanged `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` command with this single-entry change retained production zero and reduced the full-tree result to two, removing only `scripts/perf/history-model-projection-measure.ts` with no additions.

The aggregate command remains **failed** for `code-mode-control-schema-measure.ts` and `main-code-space-preload.mjs`; those findings are outside this change. These counts describe the tested source, not later main revisions.

Changed-file formatting and selected type checks passed, including the script and root-test consumer graphs. Both complete existing suites, `test/scripts/check-deadcode-exports.test.ts` and `test/scripts/check-deadcode-unused-files.test.ts`, passed with their private-child, export-scope and failure-handling assertions unchanged. The measurement was not executed; this change makes no performance claim. PR CI is pending.

Fixes #187321.

prs.title: feat(memory): opt topic files into per-entry chunking with a marker
prs.body:
Closes #179954

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: curated memory kept in topic files under `memory/` is indexed with the size-based chunker, so unrelated one-fact bullets are merged into ~400-token chunks. A query pulls in neighboring facts and the mixed embedding ranks specific facts lower than the same bullets in `MEMORY.md`.

## User Impact

User impact: a topic file under `memory/` can opt into per-entry chunking by carrying one marker line. Files without the marker are indexed exactly as before; there is no new config key.

```markdown
<!-- chunking: entries -->
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Shape agreed with @steipete in the issue (option 1, chunking only):

- The marker uses the existing HTML-comment carrier style and is stripped before indexing like the other annotations. It must sit on its own line, so prose or code samples that mention it do not opt a file in. Only `memory/` files honor it.
- `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` gets one more input to the existing `perEntry` predicate; the chunker itself is unchanged.
- Recall metadata eligibility and path provenance are untouched (`memory-path-provenance.ts`, `curated-annotations.ts` extraction). The marker does not make a file a curated root, so trigger and importance annotations stay ignored in topic files. Project scope was already read for topic files and now applies per entry in marked files, which follows from the chunk boundaries.
- Adding or removing the marker changes the file content hash, so the normal per-file reindex handles it. `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION` is not bumped because unmarked files chunk as before.
- Docs updated in `memory-builtin`, `memory`, and `memory-architecture`.

## Evidence

Tests (all pass; the three behavior tests fail on the base without the change):

- `manager-index-preparation.test.ts`: marked file chunks per entry with the marker stripped; unmarked file stays one size-based chunk; marker in prose, unknown mode, and non-`memory/` paths are ignored; trigger/importance stay null and project scope still applies as for an unmarked topic file.
- `manager-per-entry-marker.test.ts` (real manager, SQLite index): file indexed size-based, marker added then a normal sync gives per-entry chunks, marker removed then a normal sync returns the original size-based chunks.
- `curated-annotations.test.ts`: marker detection, stripping keeps line numbers, marker never reaches recall metadata.
- Full `extensions/memory-core`, `packages/memory-host-sdk`, `src/plugin-sdk` vitest run: 463 files pass, 9 skipped, 2 fail (see below). `pnpm check:changed` typecheck/format/guards and `pnpm lint:docs` pass.

Paired corpus: the same 24 synthetic one-line bullets (team facts), once in a topic file with the marker and once without. Chunks were produced by the real `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` (400 tokens, 80 overlap) and embedded with a local embedding model (Qwen3-Embedding-4B 4-bit served by a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, plain queries, cosine similarity, vector ranking only). The unmarked file becomes 2 chunks (20 and 8 bullets); the marked file becomes 24 chunks.

| Query | marked: top score | marked: bullets returned | marked: target rank | unmarked: top score | unmarked: bullets returned | unmarked: target rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Which food should we avoid when booking a team dinner? | 0.602 | 1 | 1 | 0.395 | 20 | 1 |
| How many API calls per minute are allowed? | 0.892 | 1 | 1 | 0.529 | 8 | 1 |
| Who do I ask to change the analytics warehouse schema? | 0.779 | 1 | 1 | 0.501 | 20 | 1 |
| When is the database backup restore-tested? | 0.710 | 1 | 1 | 0.533 | 20 | 1 |
| What is the Friday deploy rule? | 0.731 | 1 | 1 | 0.584 | 20 | 1 |
| How long do we keep logs? | 0.823 | 1 | 1 | 0.492 | 20 | 1 |

With such a small corpus the right chunk is found either way. The difference is what comes back: one bullet at a clearly higher similarity versus 8-20 unrelated bullets in one chunk at a lower score. The gap grows with file size, since a larger unmarked file has more diluted chunks competing with each other.

Shipped-CLI proof (head `f81c3b246`; built `openclaw.mjs`, local oMLX embeddings `Qwen3-Embedding-4B-4bit-DWQ` through `memory.search.provider: "omlx"`, throwaway `HOME` and state dir, real index untouched). Corpus: `MEMORY.md` (3 bullets), `USER.md` (2), `memory/people-marked.md` (6 bullets + marker), `memory/people-unmarked.md` (6 bullets). `openclaw memory index --agent main`, then `openclaw memory search --json`:

| File | base `bec3ad81d` chunks | PR chunks |
|---|---|---|
| `MEMORY.md` | 3 | 3 |
| `USER.md` | 2 | 2 |
| `memory/people-marked.md` | 1 (lines 1-11) | 6 (1-5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10-11) |
| `memory/people-unmarked.md` | 1 (lines 1-9) | 1 (lines 1-9) |

| Query | base top hit | PR top hit |
|---|---|---|
| who is allergic to peanuts | 0.490 `marked:1-11` | 0.633 `marked:6` |
| who manages the Cluj warehouse | 0.577 `marked:1-11` | 0.794 `marked:7` |
| who is allergic to shellfish | 0.443 `unmarked:1-9` | 0.518 `marked:6` (then 0.445 `unmarked:1-9`) |
| vendor contract with the catering company | 0.503 `marked:1-11` | 0.730 `marked:9` |

Upgrade compatibility (same state dir: index with base `bec3ad81d`, switch to the PR build, run `openclaw memory index` again without `--force`): `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md` and the unmarked file keep identical chunk counts and chunk hashes (sha256 digests `6f2efb3f`, `f8bc8e7a`, `f9c76450`) through every step. The marked file is rewritten to 6 per-entry chunks when it is next touched or edited (7 after appending a bullet); adding the marker to the unmarked file gives 6 chunks and removing it restores the original single chunk with the original hash, with all other files untouched. A file that already carries the marker keeps its old chunks until it changes (or `--force`); the marker is new, so no existing corpus is affected. No index-identity warning and no rebuild were needed. Full tables are in the PR comment.

CI: type, lint and package-boundary checks pass on the earlier head. `test-lines` now passes locally (`slack: 237`, baseline untouched) after consolidating duplicated detector test rows; the add/remove-marker reindex test is unchanged.

Fence detection requires only spaces/tabs after a closing delimiter (as `packages/markdown-core/src/fences.ts` does). Upgrade from the latest stable (`v2026.10.8`) to this branch, with existing settings, files and index data preserved, is documented in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186649#issuecomment-6468411633).

Known gaps, none caused by this change (each reproduces with the three source files reverted to `main`): `manager-search-knn-subprocess.test.ts` ("KNN child loaded unrelated runtime: kysely") and two `qa-runtime.test.ts` waitForHealth tests fail locally. `pnpm check:changed` reports two further failures. The Plugin SDK surface budget fails identically on a clean `main` (public entrypoints 160 > 158), and the SQLite worker ratchet could not run locally because `rg` is not installed. No Ollama was used; the embedding model above is the local provider.

prs.title: fix(automations): let the owner conversation manage its operator-created jobs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a conversation cannot see or pause an automation it owns when that automation was created with operator authority (scheduled tool policy `trusted`). `cronJobMatchesCallerScope` hides every trusted job from every caller-scoped conversation, including the job's own owner conversation. The agent gets `cron job not found`, and its only fallback is the global cron switch, which stops all automations. Users are told to go to the Automations page to turn off a job they own.

## User Impact

User impact: in the conversation that owns it, the agent can now list, read, pause, resume, reschedule, rename, run or remove an operator-created automation. Other conversations and accounts still cannot see it.

Authority rules for owner edits of a trusted job:
- Pause, resume, reschedule, rename, run and remove keep operator authority. These are the only edits that do: `enabled`, `schedule`, `name`, `displayName`, `description`, `deleteAfterRun`, `wakeMode`, `pacing`, `activeHours`, `idleOnly`.
- Any other edit (prompt, tools, trigger, delivery, failure alerts, session target, or a field added later) narrows the job to the conversation's own `account` authority. A chat edit never keeps or gains operator authority.
- An owner record written before account stamping (no `accountId`) proves the conversation but not the account. It gets lifecycle actions only; changes to what runs are refused with a plain message. This keeps the existing rule that an unproven account cannot edit a prompt.
- `cron.scratch.set` stays operator-only for trusted jobs, because scratch is appended to the run prompt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hiding the job protects operator authority from a chat rewriting what a trusted job runs. Pausing or removing a job you own removes authority, so hiding it from the owner goes further than the risk needs. The narrowing rule sits in `reconcileScheduledToolPolicy`: when an account-scoped caller edits a trusted job, the job is stamped with the caller's account policy instead of keeping `trusted`.

Changes:
- `cron-caller-scope.ts`: `cronTrustedJobOwnedByCaller`; trusted jobs match only their owner conversation (and account, when recorded).
- `cron.ts` and `cron-job-access.ts`: a scoped edit outside the lifecycle allowlist passes the caller's account policy; an owner record without an account is refused for those edits.
- `jobs-tool-policy.ts`: an account policy from the caller replaces `trusted` (narrowing only). This runs before dormant handling, so an owner edit that turns the job into a system event keeps the account ceiling; a later operator conversion back to an agent turn cannot restore `trusted`.
- `cron-scratch.ts`: refuse scoped scratch writes to trusted jobs (keeps the previous outcome).
- Docs: `automation/cron-jobs/managing-jobs.md`.

## Evidence

- Production: an operator-created daily job owned by a group topic could not be found by the agent in that topic (`cron job not found`), and the system agent could only offer to disable all automations.
- New QA scenario `cron-trusted-owner-conversation` (mock-openai, real Gateway, caller-scoped owner turns). Passes 6/6 on this branch:
  - the owner conversation pauses a legacy-owner trusted job and an account-stamped trusted job (both stay `trusted`);
  - another conversation gets `not found` and the job stays enabled;
  - an owner prompt and tool edit drops the job to `account` authority bound to the owner session;
  - a prompt edit of the legacy-owner job is refused and the stored job is unchanged;
  - a failure-alert webhook edit of the legacy-owner job is refused; the job keeps no failure alert and stays `trusted`;
  - an owner conversion of a trusted job to a system event stores `account`; an operator `cron.update` back to an agent turn with `toolsAllow` keeps `account` bound to the owner session. With the four source files reverted to `main`, the first step fails with `cron job not found`.
- Ownership matrix (`cron.ownership-matrix.test.ts`, real Gateway handlers and SQLite service): new shapes for owned, legacy-owner and other-session trusted jobs across scoped, creator, manager and revoked callers; every allowed chat edit leaves no trusted authority. A focused test covers legacy pause (stays trusted), refused delivery change, refused failure-alert route (fails under the earlier key list), refused scratch write, remove, and a proven-owner delivery change that narrows to the account policy. The matrix `revoked` caller (owner removed after admission, before the write) is refused and the stored job is unchanged for every trusted shape. `cron.list` hides trusted jobs of another session or account.
- Dormant round trip (focused test, SQLite store): owner converts a trusted job to a system event, the store is reloaded into a new service, and an operator restores an agent turn; the policy is the owner's account policy at each step. This fails on the previous head (`undefined` policy after the conversion).
- Revocation before persistence: the matrix `revoked` caller (channel-owner management removed after admission, before the write) is refused for every trusted shape, and the stored definition is byte-equal to the seeded one.
- Stored-data compatibility: no schema or stored-field change. Jobs are seeded with `saveCronStore` and read back through the real cron service: trusted jobs with and without `owner.accountId`, account-policy jobs and ownerless jobs load and keep their policy unless an edit narrows them. The legacy shape (trusted, owner without account) is the production record that triggered this fix.
- Removed `keeps trusted scheduled authority operator-only` from `cron.validation.test.ts`; it encoded the old rule. Its owner and foreign cases are now in the matrix list test.
- Local: changed-files test run passes (7,680 tests); one unrelated header-redaction test failed once in that run and passes alone. oxfmt and oxlint are clean on changed files.

Follow-up, not in this PR: in some setups a configured channel owner's turn reaches the automations tool without a management grant (seen with a CLI-backed runtime). This PR makes the owner's own jobs reachable in that case; it does not change management grants.

prs.title: fix(trajectory): exporting a session no longer changes its database files
prs.body:
Closes #150012

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw sessions export-trajectory` opens the agent database writable and tightens group-readable database files to 0600, although the export only reads the stored session.

## User Impact

User impact: exporting a session trajectory no longer opens the agent database writable, leaves no writer lease behind, and keeps the database files' mode (for example 0640 for backup or monitoring readers). The exported bundle is unchanged. No config, schema, or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI command already looks up the session with the read-only accessor, but the exporter then reads the session entry again for its identity checks through writable accessors: three `loadSessionEntry` calls and the legacy-marker `listSessionEntriesCore` listing. The exporter now uses the existing read-only accessors, `loadSessionEntryReadOnly` and `listSessionEntriesReadOnly`. This follows #136010 and #149627.

The transcript load itself (`loadTranscriptEvents`) is unchanged: on current main it goes through the worker-backed history read, and the regression test below shows it no longer leaves a writable handle once the entry lookups are read-only.

This rebuilds the final version of #150013 by masatohoshino (closed without review after going stale) on current main, with their credit kept as co-author. Only the test's transcript seeding import changed, because `replaceTranscriptEvents` moved to a test-support module.

## Evidence

- **Regression test, red before the fix:** `src/trajectory/export-session-storage.test.ts` seeds a SQLite session, closes all agent databases, sets the agent database to 0640, and exports through both the complete transcript target and the legacy marker. It asserts that no agent database handle is left open, that `assertNoOpenClawAgentDatabaseLeasesReadOnly()` passes, and that the mode is still 0640.
  - On `upstream/main` (a5d995a62d): fails, `getOpenClawAgentDatabaseIfOpen(...)` returns the open writable database.
  - With this change: passes.
- **Related tests:** `src/trajectory/export.test.ts`, `src/trajectory/command-export.test.ts` and the new file pass (49 tests).
- **Local checks:** `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` passes typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint and format on the changed files, the SQLite worker and dialect ratchets, and the test-lines ratchet. The dead-export scan reports only existing upstream entries, none in `src/trajectory`.
- **Not run:** a separate before/after run of the built CLI. #150013 included one (unchanged bytes and modes under `strace`) for the same four-line change.

_Opened by an AI assistant on the operator's request._

prs.title: fix(cli): restore archived sessions through the Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #124491

## What Problem This Solves

The CLI can archive a session but has no command to restore it. Headless operators cannot resume the same archived routing key through the stock CLI.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions restore <keys...>` restores archived sessions through the existing Gateway operation while retaining their identity and transcript. It supports the existing multi-key, agent, connection, JSON, and dry-run options. Already active sessions are successful no-ops.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing lifecycle adapter and Gateway mutation owner. The command describes each requested key, requires a durable session identity before either a real or dry-run restore, sends `sessions.patch` with `archived: false` and the observed `expectedSessionId`, and requires the response to confirm the archive marker was cleared.

Credit to @woodym-dotcom for the issue and original #124492 proposal. That PR is closed without merging, and its closing discussion invites a fresh CLI repair. The missing-identity dry-run issue raised there is covered here. Merged #160296 supplies agent-facing controls; the issue discussion explicitly confirms it does not replace the CLI request. The canonical issue and both related PRs were read in full; no active replacement was found.

## Evidence

- Actual built CLI at production base `bb3df792e23f102adb310561b2b3ba4a797ecc2a`: `sessions restore agent:main:restore-proof --dry-run --json` exits 1 with `OpenClaw sessions has no command "restore"`.
- New regression cases on that base fail as expected: registration **1 failed / 17 passed**, lifecycle **2 failed / 26 passed**. The PR passes **46/46 tests** with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts src/commands/sessions-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Total wrapper time 143.1 s includes worker preparation; project times were 112.7 s (registration, 93% transform) and 11.7 s (lifecycle). The regression checks normal restore, preview, active no-op, archived rows without durable identity, agent scope, order, and exact mutation identity.
- Built CLI → real loopback Gateway → SQLite/transcript evidence: start `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --bind loopback --auth none --port <isolated-port> --allow-unconfigured` with isolated HOME/state/config; create a session with `gateway call sessions.create`, then persist one synthetic assistant message with `gateway call chat.inject`. `sessions archive <key> --json` returns `archived`; `sessions restore <key> --json` returns `restored`. Independent `sessions.describe` readbacks retain the identical session ID and clear `archived`; `chat.history` returns byte-for-byte equal message arrays before archive and after restore. A second restore returns `already_active`. An offline fixture created through the session owner with an empty session ID and an archive timestamp makes the actual `sessions restore <key> --dry-run --json` exit 1 with `failed`, never `would_restore`. This Gateway version rejects that invalid identity during `sessions.describe` (`Worker session placement session id must be a non-empty string`), before the CLI compatibility guard; the committed lifecycle regression separately exercises a described archived row without identity in both preview and mutation modes. The task-owned Gateway terminated cleanly (exit 0).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p src/commands/tsconfig.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/monitor-commands.tsbuildinfo` and the matching `src/cli/tsconfig.json` command: passed. Focused lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and the test-line ratchet passed. The shallow checkout uses `--no-merge-base` with the explicit prepared parent. The unique allocation grants exactly **46 net regression lines**, without changing a baseline scalar.
- Independent Codex `autoreview --mode local --base bb3df792e23f102adb310561b2b3ba4a797ecc2a --max-priority P3`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The final review supplied complete CLI lifecycle/registration/transport, Gateway mutation, lifecycle-flag, and response-projection owners; it verified identity-before-preview, owner preservation, archive clearing, and response validation. Earlier narrower review reports were retained, and the additional passes filled their explicitly missing context; no candidate bytes changed. This was static independent review; the reviewer did not execute code. The simplification pass kept the existing lifecycle transport and mutation owner.

Validation uses Node 24.22.1 and repository-pinned dependencies in an isolated checkout. No external account, device, or model call is required. No full repository test-suite result, remote deployment, concurrent-session race exercise, or cross-platform execution is claimed. AI-assisted implementation, regression work, and independent review.

prs.title: fix(ui): match canonical Unicode in Systems search
prs.body:
Closes #187200

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems sidebar can display a machine name but fail to find it when pasted search text uses the canonically equivalent Unicode spelling. Lowercasing alone leaves composed and decomposed strings unequal.

## Fix and User Impact

Keep the existing single complete inventory predicate, normalizing both query and candidate strings to NFC **after** locale lowercasing. The existing display-name, ID, formatted-platform and raw-platform fields stay searchable. Raw query state, displayed strings, identity joins, status filters, sorting and selection stay unchanged. No accent folding, fuzzy matching, new helper export, configuration, protocol or schema.

The contributor's original commit is retained. Both Unicode directions are now covered by the existing inventory sort/filter/selection regression instead of a separate duplicated fixture. Removed the temporary test-line allocation; whole-PR delta is production +2, tests 0, allocation 0.

## Evidence

[Independent rebuilt-Gateway/Control-UI Chromium proof, captured results and screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187241#issuecomment-6487949152).

- Main `6db97e5760ba5698215e04b90774a02f76720ff5`; candidate `e9d0805878fcbaa19dcc948bc70793c53fddbd4b`.
- Frozen installs and full builds of Gateway and Control UI in secretless Node 24 Docker. Real Chromium 156.0.8078.4 runs inside Docker against the ordinary built Gateway `/systems` page, not Vite/source UI.
- Main twice: both NFC→NFD and NFD→NFC searches miss names, IDs and platforms. Candidate twice: all six cross-form cases return the original raw labels.
- Same-form Unicode, ASCII case, whitespace, unmatched, no-accent-folding and clear-search controls remain correct. Inventory reads stay 2→2 in each run; no browser page errors.
- Actual Gateway WebSocket hello/authentication observed; all captured served JS assets hash-match each artifact's `dist/control-ui` files.
- Only the inventory response is a synthetic browser transport fixture; app boot, Gateway connection, route, controller, predicate and renderer are real. Real machine discovery/remote node transport is not claimed. No model, login or paid key.
- Final focused regression: main 1 failed / 17 passed; candidate 18 passed. Targeted formatting/lint and both full builds passed.

### Inspected browser captures

| Direction | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NFC query → NFD name | ![Before NFC query](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ecd0181-d65a-4f72-a9f1-5d3246b38c4c) | ![After NFC query](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47875542-bfd1-4629-9690-203994794e07) |
| NFD query → NFC name | ![Before NFD query](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df72b0ac-8d8d-42f7-bdbe-230db1b9743b) | ![After NFD query](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ec48bad-f387-4c94-ab6a-8586d5334d52) |

## Current CI

Exact-head `ci-gate` is red because `checks-ui (2/3)` failed two unchanged Files-panel document-link cases. [Exact-main/CI-merge attribution and isolated controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187241#issuecomment-6488239013): the same Files test blob and production owners are present on both snapshots, and the isolated Bun file passes 38 tests on each. Main's contemporaneous full UI shard also passed. This CI-only failure is not claimed fixed; no hosted jobs were rerun, and the branch is retained for maintainer resumption.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the former comparisons; no persistence or migration. Blast radius is local Systems inventory search. Raw names/IDs/platforms and all Gateway-owned inventory/selection contracts remain unchanged.

prs.title: feat(voice-call): add optional Telnyx noise suppression for inbound realtime calls
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `telnyx.noiseSuppression` setting to Voice Call. When it is set, inbound realtime calls run Telnyx per-call noise suppression (`Denoiser`, `DeepFilterNet`, `Krisp`, or `AiCoustics`) on the caller's audio before it reaches the realtime model.

It is off by default. With the setting unset, calls without media streaming and outbound dials send exactly the same Telnyx requests as before.

## What Problem This Solves

Background speech from a TV or another person in the room reaches the realtime model as if the caller had said it. Telnyx can isolate the caller's voice per call, for example with Krisp's telephony voice isolation model.

Voice Call couldn't use that, because it starts streaming inside the `answer` command and Telnyx rejects `suppression_start` while streaming is active (422, code 90045).

## Change

When `telnyx.noiseSuppression` is set and the call streams media, `TelnyxProvider.answerCall` runs these steps in order:

1. `answer` without the stream fields.
2. `suppression_start` with the configured direction, engine and engine config. This step is capped at 5 seconds so the stream token stays valid. If it fails or times out, Voice Call logs a warning and streams without suppression.
3. `streaming_start` with the same stream settings the answer would have carried.

When the setting is unset, the single `answer` still carries the stream fields inline, unchanged from today.

The config is validated in both the manifest schema and `normalizeVoiceCallConfig`; `engineConfig` requires `engine`. The docs in `docs/plugins/voice-call/realtime-and-streaming.md` cover the direction semantics, the engine fields, and the Telnyx number setting below.

**Prerequisite:** set the number's own noise suppression to `disabled` in Telnyx. A number-level setting engages the default engine at answer, and a later `suppression_start` collides with it; Telnyx returns a 500 for that collision.

## Failure handling

| Step that fails | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `answer` (setting on) | Voice Call sends a best-effort hangup, then reports the answer failure. Telnyx may have answered before its HTTP response was lost; that answer carries no stream, so without the hangup the caller would sit on silence until duration cleanup. |
| `answer` (setting unset) | Unchanged. The answer carries the stream inline, so a lost response still connects media, and no hangup is sent. |
| `suppression_start` | Logs a warning and streams without suppression. The call continues. |
| `streaming_start` | Voice Call hangs up the answered call and reports the failure. |

Both hangups share one helper, and a failed hangup is only logged. This resolves the earlier silent-call window when the answer response is lost: the contributor-side cleanup option from the review is implemented in `2df6212`.

## Evidence

The live runs below are real inbound calls to a Telnyx local number through a source build of this branch, loaded as a bundled plugin. The setup used a Call Control app with number-level suppression `disabled`, a Tailscale funnel, OpenAI realtime, and `inboundPolicy: allowlist`.

Hostnames, call control IDs and the caller are redacted. Timestamps are local (UTC-5).

The current head, `00bcc435666`, is `2df6212` rebased onto main `be0d5c97b50`; only the two generated config baseline files were regenerated. The rebase brought in five main commits under `extensions/voice-call`. Four of them, #187174, #186905, #186691 and #186457, change the CLI, the doctor contract and store tests. The fifth, #187290, fixes the stale continue test that failed CI here. None touch the Telnyx provider, the runtime, the webhook or the media stream, so the runs below on `2df6212` exercise the same answer path as the current head.

### Upgrade from current stable v2026.10.8, on head `2df6212`

All runs used one profile, one state directory and one config file.

**A. Stock `v2026.10.8` (`dc2523e`), config without `noiseSuppression`.** Four inbound calls were answered and streamed. The first three ended with the model calling `openclaw_end_call` (`endReason=hangup-bot`). The gateway was stopped during the fourth call's setup; v2026.10.8 closed that record as `completed` on shutdown.

**B. Checkout of this branch (`2df6212`), same profile, config untouched.** `openclaw doctor --fix` ran the core state migration for the newer build. That migration belongs to v2026.10.8 to main, not to this plugin. After it, the gateway started and three inbound calls behaved exactly as before:

```
22:12:37.815 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:28.983 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=8fea48a4-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:13:34.990 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:55.616 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=05f267e5-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:14:01.298 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:14:37.845 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=0a54b7ad-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**C. `noiseSuppression` added with `config set ... --strict-json`, no other change.** The config was Krisp with `krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef`. The call was a normal conversation with no suppression warning and no answer failure:

```
22:15:40.991 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:15:42.112 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 28ab70e0-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:16:14.703 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=28ab70e0-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**D. Rejected `suppression_start` on the same head.** The model was set to a name Telnyx does not accept, and two calls were placed.

Both calls had `suppression_start` rejected. On the first, Telnyx's own `streaming_start` then failed to reach the media destination, and Voice Call hung the answered call up through the shared helper. The second call streamed without suppression and finished normally.

```
22:24:50.955 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:51.486 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 70f2a343-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "10000", "title": "Invalid request",
    "source": { "pointer": "/noise_suppression_engine_config" },
    "detail": "The 'noise_suppression_engine_config' parameter model must be one of: krisp-viva-tel-v2.kef, krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef, krisp-viva-pro-v1.kef, krisp-viva-ss-v1.kef." } ]
}
22:24:52.886 [voice-call/events] Failed to answer inbound call v3:<redacted>: call answered but Telnyx streaming_start failed; hanging up: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "90046", "title": "Media Streaming failed", "detail": "Failed to connect to destination" } ]
}
22:24:53.750 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=70f2a343-... endReason=completed

22:24:57.684 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:58.077 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 { ...same 10000 error... }
22:24:58.939 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:25:17.777 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=3e06844d-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

Thirty seconds after the hung-up call, the existing realtime stream watchdog logged `Realtime stream WebSocket never connected within 30s` for `70f2a343`. That call was already finalized, and the warning had no effect on it or on the next call. The watchdog belongs to the stream token issued before the answer; this PR does not change it.

### Stored call history after the upgrade

These records were read back with `openclaw voicecall tail` on `2df6212` after legs B through D. They include the four calls that v2026.10.8 wrote before the upgrade:

| Call | Written by | Started | Answered | Ended | State | End reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 61706121 | v2026.10.8 | 17:46:45 | 17:46:46 | 17:47:32 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 368ae1dc | v2026.10.8 | 17:47:36 | 17:47:37 | 17:48:06 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| a7d22a6f | v2026.10.8 | 17:48:15 | 17:48:16 | 17:48:49 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 49b062ca | v2026.10.8 | 17:49:07 | 17:49:08 | 17:49:09 | completed | completed |
| 8fea48a4 | 2df6212 | 22:12:37 | 22:12:38 | 22:13:28 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 05f267e5 | 2df6212 | 22:13:34 | 22:13:35 | 22:13:55 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 0a54b7ad | 2df6212 | 22:14:01 | 22:14:02 | 22:14:37 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| c96579c8 | 2df6212 | 22:14:51 | 22:14:52 | 22:14:53 | completed | completed |
| 28ab70e0 | 2df6212 | 22:15:40 | 22:15:42 | 22:16:14 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 70f2a343 | 2df6212 | 22:24:50 | - | 22:24:53 | completed | completed |
| 3e06844d | 2df6212 | 22:24:57 | 22:24:58 | 22:25:17 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |

All 11 records in the store load on the new build with their original timestamps and end reasons, including the four written by v2026.10.8.

`49b062ca` and `c96579c8` are calls that were in setup when the gateway was stopped. Each build closed its record as `completed` on shutdown.

`70f2a343` is the streaming-failure call from leg D. It has no `answeredAt` because the hangup came before Telnyx's `call.answered` webhook was processed.

So on `2df6212`, all three live paths ran against real Telnyx: Krisp on, a rejected `suppression_start`, and a `streaming_start` failure cleaned up with a hangup.

The one path not exercised live is a lost `answer` response, which can't be arranged against Telnyx on demand. The unit tests cover it.

### Earlier runs (head `c1a26c2`, [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183266#issuecomment-6458928065))

- Krisp in a room with a multi-voice video playing: the model stayed on the caller through English and Korean speech.
- The same rejected-suppression and streaming-failure paths as above.
- An upgrade from v2026.10.7.

### Tests

- `runtime.telnyx-answer.test.ts` starts the real runtime with Telnyx and realtime enabled and POSTs a `call.initiated` webhook to its listener. It mocks only the outbound HTTP edge and asserts the Telnyx commands for three paths: unset, Krisp, and rejected `suppression_start`. It replaces the constructor-forwarding test the review flagged.
- `providers/telnyx.test.ts` covers:
  - the request order and payloads,
  - engine field mapping,
  - the 5 second suppression bound,
  - fail-open on network errors,
  - hangup on a failed stream-less answer (and none on a failed inline-stream answer),
  - hangup on a failed `streaming_start`, even when that hangup fails,
  - unchanged outbound dials.

  The unset-answer case is folded into the existing streaming-answer test.
- `config.test.ts` covers the rejection cases.

## For the voice-call owner

This adds one optional block, with 10 config paths, under `telnyx`. It stays inside the existing Telnyx provider, and the defaults are unchanged. ClawSweeper recommends approving the optional capability. A maintainer decision on exposing it is the remaining item I can't close from the contributor side.

prs.title: fix(doctor): distinguish port preparation from pending schema migrations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can report a pending schema migration when a store already has the current schema version. The port descriptor also uses its preparation flag for index repairs and retired cache cleanup, which porting performs on a private copy. Diagnostics additionally prescribe backup creation and ownership maintenance when those facts were never inspected.

## User Impact

Numeric pending migrations now reflect the observed schema-version gap. Same-version preparation stays visible with private-copy guidance. Unobserved lease and backup fields retain their existing unknown values without inventing a maintenance requirement; actual failed or ambiguous owner observations keep their guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostic owner projected a broad preparation boolean into a numeric version gap and treated default unknown fields as failed observations. This change keeps each fact at its existing producer. It does not change port migration admission, source database content, public enum values, schema versions, or status's no-probe behavior.

The canonical SQLite and PostgreSQL Doctor snapshots cover JSON, rendered text, and admitted status output. Only obsolete advice changes; other recorded facts remain exact.

## Evidence

- Red-first proof at 9bd4aaab: all three new regressions fail at the intended assertions on Node and Bun; nine existing cases pass. Real current-schema agent fixtures cover retired cache cleanup and repairable index drift, with source bytes preserved. [Native CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40810503636).
- Added preservation cases cover successfully parsed but unverifiable owner/lease records and malformed records; status still forbids filesystem/database probes.
- Fresh proof on the prepared candidate and approved baseline passed **26 tests, zero skipped**: 17 diagnostics/admission regressions, 4 SQLite Doctor output cases, and 5 PostgreSQL Doctor output cases using the canonical pinned PostgreSQL 17 fixture. [Native Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40813964737). This is focused Doctor proof, not a claim that every conformance shard ran.
- Independent source and prepared-binding review accepted all seven output snapshots, unchanged non-advice facts, and the exact 26-pass proof. Exact-head [CI40815107748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40815107748) and the aggregate CI gate passed. The Testbox workflow metadata describes its workflow checkout; its separately verified native completion receipt binds the prepared source tree and frozen dependencies, with exit0 and settled cleanup. No shipped-CLI trace or full live deployment is claimed.
- Production delta: -2 lines. Test source delta: +127, allocated exactly in a separate test-line record for real owner observations and preservation checks. Generated snapshots are excluded from the test-line ratchet.
- Initial focused file wall time: Node 31.80 s; Bun 35.99 s. These cases exercise canonical schema descriptors and real private-copy inspection to distinguish same-version preparation from version lag and verify source preservation; final changed-suite cost will follow native CI.

prs.title: fix(agents): avoid retaining unused catalog model projections
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/181687

## What Problem This Solves

Each catalog worker constructs and retains two configured-model projections per workspace even though discovery consumes the configured model facts supplied by the host. Catalog discovery also imports host-only snapshot construction.

## User Impact

Catalog workers no longer construct those unused model arrays. Host snapshots retain their canonical inline model data. No configuration or operator action changes. Overall RSS savings remain unmeasured; this does not claim to resolve the broader long-running growth report.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the unused projections at worker generation creation, narrow discovery and lifetime inputs to the fields they consume, and read host inline models directly from the owning plugin generation. Move host snapshot construction into the host build module and use direct imports of the existing config/auth state owners.

Production: +152/-141 lines, net +11. The additional lines express narrower type contracts; no cache, worker, setting, or runtime state owner is added. Tests: +14/-34 lines. The obsolete mock baseline shrinks by one entry. The existing performance workload adds 42 net lines to scale configured definitions independently and verify catalog and runtime-model results.

## Evidence

- Independent source review and local autoreview through P2: no actionable findings for the production change, reviewed from base `23e62f4162fd9c36475a308ac4cbb3d269283196` through `bfc7e340711fc12f27b600b2aed813189e76d49f`. A separate independent review covered the four-line fixture/baseline cleanup in `ff148fb037a4eddf44228aa021600f5e51b4164f`; production is unchanged.
- The workload-only follow-up `8be7dd8f7a6c3dcc71e449c0e158f75579275e0c` passed local autoreview through P2 with no actionable findings. It adds `--configured-models`, exact catalog membership checks, runtime transport/limit checks, and runtime-model digests. Production is unchanged from the preceding green head.
- Targeted oxfmt, commit hooks, `node --check` for the workload, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The [first CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40806101344) passed 42 jobs and exposed two PR-caused failures: excess catalog fields in the plugin-lifetime test fixture and the obsolete mock baseline entry. Both are corrected in `ff148fb037a4eddf44228aa021600f5e51b4164f`. The repository mock-baseline generator and check passed (6,569 → 6,568 entries). [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40807156350) passed on the preceding head `ff148fb037a4eddf44228aa021600f5e51b4164f`; the native watcher reported `GREEN` with no pending checks. CI for the workload follow-up is pending.
- Full build and runtime measurements remain pending; the first CI run skipped `build-artifacts`. Testbox attempts executed no tests/build/probes and are stopped and settled, including the [latest cancelled allocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40813523045). The maintainer approved PR CI as the first build/test proof route; that approval does not waive the remaining build or performance acceptance.
- Existing tests cover host inline-model identity/reload, configured catalog composition, provider metadata selection, worker generation reuse/replacement, retained-data sampling, and media resource custody.

### Performance acceptance before scored runs

Compare the frozen base and candidate with the same compiled workload, runtime, machine, and inputs, using at least five serial interleaved pairs. Separate cold startup from warm requests; report medians, p95, spread, host load, and observed machine resources.

Count avoided configured-model projections per workspace generation and compare catalog-worker retained heap and loaded code. Also exercise the real Gateway under load and compare total RSS, cold-start latency, warm request latency/tails, CPU, results, and shutdown. Synthetic worker measurements alone do not establish whole-Gateway savings. Use the same updated retention controller for both compiled workers: `--workspaces 20 --providers 2 --models 1000 --discovery-models 100 --task-rounds 2 --runtime-plugin`, with `--configured-models 1` and `--configured-models 1000` as separate workloads. Each requires five paired samples and identical catalog/runtime-model digests. `--models` still scales remote rows; `--configured-models` scales authored definitions. This fixture has no agent model selections, so empty configured runtime references are intentional and checked against the canonical collector.

Landing requires a measurable memory benefit with unchanged results and no unaccepted user-facing regression. Any metric worsening by 20% is a stop; revert ineffective changes. The broader leak report remains open.

prs.body:
## Scope
Minimal security adaptation for **release/2026.10.8**, freshly verified at `5413218d77df39edac0ee99b7838d7bac519002a` before publication.

- Change only the dedicated `clawhub@0.23.3` override and `node_modules/undici` lock metadata from 7.29.1 to 7.30.1.
- Update the standalone materializer's full-lock SHA-256 to `5f7da1abdfcaf8adcf8a20b609f677cd7a0e9ffe37e078b39d0b742bce5ce6af`.
- Add a canonical Vitest tooling regression for the manifest/lock/hash contract, successful offline materialization, and tampered-lock rejection before npm.

No shared-helper refactor, root lock, workflow, package version, pack/cache/build isolation, or private-export changes. All other dedicated lock entries are unchanged. This does not publish an npm package or release.

## Provenance
Fixed metadata is taken from main snapshot `ed4c9d4434495921bc42192fe724f9fd0d5d629b` (#185194), authored by **RoboClaw <services+roboclaw@openclaw.org>**. Git path history shows the actual 7.30.1 pin change is `f6c2aeca54e95a6593aec8676034f68aacbcd6f8` (#182010), by the same author: #185194 contains the fix but does not itself modify the ClawHub paths. Neither broad dependency refresh is transplanted. The regression is a new local release-line adaptation. The `c79071d0` / #174693 shared materializer is not a prerequisite and is excluded.

## Validation
- Before fix: the new regression fails specifically on `7.29.1 !== 7.30.1`; both existing-behavior offline cases pass.
- After fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts test/scripts/clawhub-cli-security-pin.test.ts`: **3/3 pass**, revalidated with the canonical tooling runner. No full repository install or suite was run; hosted CI seconds remain unknown.
- Real standalone materializer in fresh owned scratch: `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --omit=dev` succeeds (47 packages), preserving ClawHub 0.23.3.
- Actual CLI smoke: `clawhub --cli-version` => `0.23.3`. The initially attempted `--version` is unsupported and its failed receipt is retained separately.
- Dedicated graph `npm audit --package-lock-only --json`: baseline reports 2 affected packages (ClawHub via Undici); fixed graph reports **0 vulnerabilities**. This is scoped audit evidence, not global security clearance.
- Repository-pinned oxfmt 0.71.0 with the base's configuration: passes; `bash -n` and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Full four-file diff inspected; no unrelated lock entries or product paths changed.

## Remaining gates
Ready for standard CI after complete independent canonical source review with no actionable P0–P2 findings. A separately reviewed test-only correction fixes the initial hosted preflight discovery failure, preserving all three cases and every CI gate. Hosted checks/security gates and release qualification have not been cleared. No merge, gate weakening, or release requested.

## Independent review update — October 29, 2026
Complete review used canonical autoreview with OpenClaw engine (openai/gpt-6.1-sol), the full scoped diff and all required source context without omitted bytes. This is bounded source-review evidence, not completed hosted CI, owner approval, or full security clearance.

The initial hosted preflight rejected the .test.mjs file because canonical tooling ownership matches .test.ts. prs.title: fix(workboard): match canonically equivalent Unicode in card search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you search the workboard by a card's title, label, note, or diagnostic text, a card can silently fail to match even though the card contains the exact text you typed. This happens when the search term and the stored text encode the same character differently (composed vs. decomposed Unicode, e.g. an accent entered from a mobile IME), because the filter compares them without Unicode normalization.

- Problem: `matchesCardQuery` lowercases both the query and each candidate field and compares with `String.prototype.includes`, but never Unicode-normalizes. An NFC search term (composed, e.g. `é`) fails to match an NFD-stored title (decomposed, e.g. `e` + combining acute) and vice versa, so matching cards are omitted from search results.
- Solution: normalize both the query and every candidate value to NFC before comparing.
- What changed: `extensions/workboard/browser/pages/workboard/view-helpers.tsx` — `matchesCardQuery` now runs `search.trim().toLowerCase().normalize("NFC")` and compares each candidate with `value.toLowerCase().normalize("NFC").includes(query)`.
- What did NOT change: only comparison text is normalized; stored card values (labels, notes, diagnostics, titles) are never rewritten. Case-insensitive matching and ID-prefix matching behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`matchesCardQuery` is the canonical owner of workboard card filtering — `view.tsx` routes all card search through it — so normalizing in one place makes every card search NFC/NFD-agnostic without adding a parser or policy branch. `.normalize("NFC")` is an ECMAScript standard `String` API available in every Node and browser runtime. The fix mirrors the canonical-equivalence fixes already merged upstream for the same family of user-writable text search: vault search, CLI index search, session-share, session-repository artifacts, and cron run-history (`#186672`, `#187024`). Normalizing to NFC (rather than NFD) matches the storage-side convention those fixes use. Non-goal: no change to how cards are stored or indexed, and no change to the non-search display paths.

## User Impact

Workboard card search now finds cards whose user/agent-writable text (title, labels, notes, worker logs, diagnostics, notifications) is stored in a different Unicode normalization form than the query. Users on mobile IMEs or cross-platform workflows that produce decomposed characters will no longer see matching cards silently dropped from search results.

## Evidence

**Pre-fix RED** — reverted the source change (kept the new regression test) and ran the test file; the canonically-equivalent case fails:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts --project unit \
    extensions/workboard/browser/pages/workboard/view-helpers.test.ts
 × |unit| .../view-helpers.test.ts > matches canonically equivalent Unicode in card titles 11ms
   → expected false to be true // Object.is equality

 FAIL  |unit| .../view-helpers.test.ts > matches canonically equivalent Unicode in card titles
AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality
- Expected
+ Received
- true
+ false
 ❯ .../view-helpers.test.ts:22:47
```

**Post-fix GREEN** — with the fix in place, all tests pass, including the new regression test:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts --project unit \
    extensions/workboard/browser/pages/workboard/view-helpers.test.ts
 ✓ |unit| .../view-helpers.test.ts > matches card ID prefixes case-insensitively 26ms
 ✓ |unit| .../view-helpers.test.ts > matches canonically equivalent Unicode in card titles 5ms
 ✓ |unit| .../view-helpers.test.ts > reuses card formatters and replaces them when the host locale changes 23ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Live command verification** — a real `node --import tsx` run exercising the shipped `matchesCardQuery` with an NFC query against an NFD-stored title:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '
  import { matchesCardQuery } from ".../view-helpers.tsx";
  const nfd = "caf\u00e9".normalize("NFD");
  const card = { id: "c1", title: nfd, status: "todo", priority: "normal", labels: [], position: 1, createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1 };
  console.log("NFC query vs NFD-stored title ->", matchesCardQuery(card, "caf\u00e9"));
  console.log("NFD query vs NFD-stored title ->", matchesCardQuery(card, nfd));
'
NFC query vs NFD-stored title -> true
NFD query vs NFD-stored title -> true
```

**Behavior matrix**:

```text
query form   vs   stored form   =>  pre-fix   =>  post-fix
NFC "café"        NFD "cafe\u0301"   miss         hit
NFD "cafe\u0301"  NFD "cafe\u0301"   hit          hit
```

**What was not tested**: end-to-end browser interaction in the live workboard UI; the change is confined to the pure `matchesCardQuery` filter predicate and is covered by the unit regression. No cross-platform normalization edge cases beyond NFC/NFD were added.

**Open PR collision check**: searched open PR topics and scanned changed-file lists for `extensions/workboard/browser/pages/workboard/view-helpers.tsx`; no open PR touches it. The open canonical-equivalence PRs in the same family (`#187204`, `#187196`, `#187211`, `#187189`, `#187199`) each target a different module's session/live-directory search, not the workboard card filter, so they are not duplicates. Related workboard PR `#181164` edits `view.tsx` (a caller) and `board-filter.ts`, not `view-helpers.tsx`.
