prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The production unused-export check still reports an exact-input transcript query whose recovery caller was removed by #185730. Its tests also cover useful reader and JSON behavior, so retiring the query requires keeping those controls at their live owners.

## User Impact

Current transcript reads retain admission fences, physical database identity, reset history, legacy-row navigation, and payload bounds. The change introduces no configuration or stored-data migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retired predicate has no production caller. Its existing cases now exercise the live readers and the SQL field-projection/codec boundary. The database-worker inventory removes the obsolete operation and explanation, and its complete canonical output refreshes existing source-derived rows without changing classification policy.

## Evidence

The reader and SQLite SQL/codec cases passed before the predicate was removed, including both earlier-fence variants, symlink aliases, later-input exclusion, typed nested provenance, duplicate-member first selection, and NUL-key handling. Existing affected reader and worker consumers also passed. These tests call the surviving owners, whose implementations are unchanged by the deletion.

All three complete dead-code commands still report unrelated existing findings. Exact-set comparison removes only this predicate from the production results; the other findings and the dependencies command's unrun conditional arm are preserved.

Generated inventory consistency, the worker ratchet, affected type checks, changed-file lint/format, and the generator-consumer test passed. The original scanner failure is recorded in [scheduled CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40800487319/job/123207281276).

The configured [PostgreSQL conformance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40818084275/job/123264324959) executed and passed every SQLite and PostgreSQL case in the owner file, including compact extraction and first-member selection.

CI currently has an inherited release-fixture type error: `releaseRef` is missing from the fixture options used by a release test. The same error reproduced on the tested merge parent. Remaining CI checks are still running.

prs.title: fix(ui): restore keyboard focus after copying
prs.body:
Closes #187201

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes keyboard focus dropping out of a shared Copy button when its clipboard write completes, so the next Enter cannot copy again.

## User Impact

Keyboard users can keep using the completed Copy control. A newer Copy action or deliberate move to another control keeps its focus.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared action records whether it owned focus before native disabling, then restores focus only for its current, latest attempt. Its deferred check lets the existing clipboard fallback restore newer focus first. Pending native-disabled behavior, copied text, announcements and feedback timing are preserved. Production grows by 17 lines in the canonical action; the exact 142 test-line increase has its own allocation record.

## Maintainer reproduction

prs.title: fix(secrets): avoid false plaintext findings for config-owned env markers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated `models.json` intentionally stores an env SecretRef variable name as its API-key marker. `openclaw secrets audit --check --json` incorrectly reports a custom marker such as `FACTCHAT_API_KEY` as plaintext even when the same configured provider owns that exact reference.

Fixes #121543. Related to #87723.

## User Impact

Source-owned custom env markers no longer produce misleading plaintext warnings. Other providers, sensitive headers, losing aliases, and literal credentials retain their findings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audit reuses the writer’s `normalizeSourceProviderLookup` and `resolveConfigSecretRef(..., includeResolved: true)`. It first selects the canonical source provider, then exempts only that provider’s API key when its exact value equals the owning env-reference ID. This preserves provenance through populated shorthand and `$include` resolution without adding another parser or changing serialization.

Credit to @cho2559 for the report, @SebTardif (#121578), @wangmiao0668000666 (#121594), @LiuwqGit (#121633), and @Alix-007 (#87873) for earlier work. All four earlier PRs are closed **without merging**; #121578’s closing discussion invites a fresh repair. This implementation addresses the populated-include, canonical-winner, and import-cycle concerns in those discussions. Merged #97622 covers known markers on the config audit surface and does not resolve this custom-provider case. The issue comments and related PR discussions were read in full; no active replacement was found.

## Evidence

- Regression before/after: applying the new tests to production base `b703c84a84c947e198b6a683408a3ddaba9179c4` gives **2 failed / 28 passed**. Only the owned populated-include marker and canonical winning env marker fail. The PR passes **30/30 audit tests**; cross-provider, header, losing-alias, and literal-winner controls remain covered.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/secrets/audit.test.ts src/agents/models-config.runtime-source-snapshot.test.ts src/agents/models-config.merge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **46 tests passed across 3 files**, 189.1 s total including isolated worker preparation. The infra project took 107.7 s and the writer merge project 16.7 s. The four new audit cases took 7.6 s; they use the existing real config/SQLite audit fixture rather than a second mocked loader.
- Built production CLI evidence: `pnpm --silent openclaw secrets audit --check --json` on an isolated populated `$include` fixture goes from base **exit 1 / plaintextCount 1** to PR **exit 0 / plaintextCount 0**. Running the built `node openclaw.mjs secrets audit --check --json` with a losing alias and an unrelated provider still exits 1 and reports exactly those two paths (`providers.openai.apiKey`, `providers.unrelated.apiKey`). Both runs use the real config loader and audit command; the on-disk generated catalog is a synthetic fixture. The repository runtime build completed successfully.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`: passed. The test shard `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-tools.json --incremental` also passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-import-cycles.ts`: passed. Format, focused lint, `git diff --check`, and the test-line ratchet passed. The prepared parent comparison uses `--no-merge-base` because this isolated checkout is shallow. The unique allocation grants exactly the **46 net new regression lines**, without changing a baseline scalar.
- Initial independent Codex `autoreview --mode local --base b703c84a84c947e198b6a683408a3ddaba9179c4 --max-priority P3`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings in the selected patch and supplied provenance/provider-owner context. Its report explicitly states that **unchanged audit and loader context was unavailable**; it did not execute tests. A supplemental run attempted to supply the complete audit and snapshot owners, but the helper refused `--dataset src/secrets/audit.ts` as a **sensitive path before starting a reviewer**. That guard was not bypassed. Therefore no complete-context local review is claimed, and this remains **Draft pending hosted review** of the implementation and the new evidence. The simplification pass retained the existing owners and the one-file **+18/-0** production change.

Validation uses Node 24.22.1, repository-pinned dependencies, isolated config/state, and synthetic values. No real provider request, external tenant, Windows-specific behavior, or full repository test-suite result is claimed. AI-assisted implementation, regression work, and independent review.

prs.title: fix(ci): bound artifact verification GitHub API requests
prs.body:
Closes #130570.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: release artifact verification can wait indefinitely when a `gh api` connection stalls before the existing retry loop can run.

## User Impact

Release operators get bounded request retries and a clear failure instead of losing the entire validation job to one stalled request. The verification callers run on Ubuntu and require GNU `timeout`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bound each GET in the shared verifier to 30 seconds, with 10 seconds of SIGKILL grace for a TERM-resistant process. Deadline exits 124/137 enter the existing three-attempt retry policy. Authentication rejection, fresh-artifact-only 404 retries, stdout isolation, and immutable artifact/producer checks retain their existing owner.

Credit to @wangmiao0668000666 for the withdrawn, unmerged #123037 and its [explicit continuation invitation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/123037#issuecomment-5817489484), and Vincent Koc for the existing GET-retry repair #120654. I read the complete issue and related PR discussions, including unmerged #108986. Current main still contains the unbounded call. This continuation avoids introducing timeout configuration or test-only production hooks.

## Evidence

Validated on Node 24.22.1 using the repository wrappers. Production script blob `926072ea84446b6c0486ceda78cdceab7d119e3a` is unchanged from the previously reviewed head; this follow-up adds four boundary regressions and the exact 29-line test allocation.

**Real transport, executed October 29:** official `gh 2.63.2` (release archive SHA-256 verified), real Bash, GNU timeout and jq, with HTTPS_PROXY pointing to an isolated loopback TCP blackhole. Only synthetic fixture authentication was supplied; no GitHub account or external request was used. The complete command was `bash <base-or-head-script> verify-upload "Loopback artifact" 789 docker-e2e-shared-images-release-aabbccddeeff-123456-2 <64-character-fixture-digest> 123456 2`, launched by the local Python transport probe.

```text
current-main owner (83cfa434563b): 42.02s, still stalled; externally stopped
  connections: [0.10s]; stdout/stderr empty
candidate owner: 96.08s, exit 1 naturally
  connections: [0.07s, 32.08s, 66.10s]
  retries: 2; deadline diagnostics: 3; stdout empty
  final: GitHub API GET failed after 3 attempt(s).
```

The existing unchanged-owner process probes additionally recorded first-stall recovery at 32.11s and a TERM-resistant child receiving TERM, then being killed and allowing recovery at 42.10s. Those two probes substitute the gh process and are separate from the new real-gh transport evidence.

**Committed regressions:** `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/shared-image-artifact.test.ts`:

- Candidate: **15 passes**, 17.59s Vitest duration.

They inject process exits and fake backoff; actual TERM/KILL timing is covered by the separate process/transport evidence above, not claimed as a committed wall-clock test.
- Existing auth, HTTP, tuple/digest, archive and provenance controls pass.

**Other checks:** `bash -n scripts/docker/shared-image-artifact.sh`; `node scripts/run-format.mts --check test/scripts/shared-image-artifact.test.ts` with oxfmt; `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json test/scripts/shared-image-artifact.test.ts`; repository tsgo wrapper using an external scoped config extending the standard root-test config; test-line ratchet; `git diff --check`: all pass. prs.title: fix(infra): keep managed-service handoff recovery deadlines on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a managed-service Gateway update can hang its activation, or refuse a healthy service stop, when the host clock is corrected while the detached handoff helper is parking or restoring the Gateway.

The sealed helper's command runner, `runServiceCommand`, turned its deadline into a subprocess budget with `deadline - Date.now()` and handed that value to `spawn({ timeout })`, which Node enforces on the monotonic clock. Any step between the deadline seed and the dispatch resizes the budget the helper believes it has:

- a **backward step** inflates it — a 5 s stop budget becomes ~95 s, so a stalled `systemctl stop` or the parent-exit wait keeps running past its allowance and activation hangs;
- a **forward step** collapses it — the command returns `{ code: 1 }` before dispatch and parking fails with `systemctl stop failed or exceeded the parent-exit deadline` or `managed update parent exit exceeded the activation deadline`.

Two more defects rode the same path:

- **Fractional and zero timeouts.** Node rejects a non-integer `timeout` with `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`, and reads `0` as "no timeout". Subtracting two `performance.now()` values yields a fraction, so moving to the monotonic clock alone was not enough.
- **Re-derived cross-process epoch.** `parentExitDeadlineAt` is a wall-clock epoch written by the updater and read by the helper. Re-converting it after every awaited command let parking, the parent-exit settle loop and the commit decision resolve one deadline to different instants mid-park.

## User Impact

User impact: a managed update keeps its intended elapsed-time allowances when the host clock is corrected mid-handoff — parking still stops the unit within the 330 s parent-exit budget and recovery keeps its 40 min budget — instead of hanging or aborting before the service is touched.

- No configuration, CLI flag, error string, wire format, or on-disk shape changes.
- With a stable clock the helper dispatches the same commands with the same budgets; the only difference is that `spawn` now receives an integer (e.g. `2500` ms for a `2500.5` ms budget) instead of a value Node would reject.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One deadline per clock domain.** Every process-local deadline now seeds and reads `performance.now()`. The only wall-clock value left is the cross-process `parentExitDeadlineAt` epoch: `monotonicDeadlineFromWallClock()` converts it once at the boundary into a single `activationDeadline()` that parking, the parent-exit settle loop, the sleeps, and the commit decision share. `armActivationDeadline()` starts the shutdown reserve on the monotonic clock at activation, so the reserve is no longer re-derived after each await.
- **Integer budget with a live floor.** `Math.max(1, Math.floor(Math.min(timeoutCap ?? remaining, remaining, …)))` satisfies `spawn`'s integer contract, and the lower clamp keeps a positive sub-millisecond budget at 1 ms instead of `0`, which would disable the timeout entirely.
- **Fixtures step both clocks.** The launchd and parent test-support preloads now move `Date.now` and `performance.now` together, so they model a real clock rather than a single-clock skew.
- **Alternatives rejected.** A tolerance window around the wall-clock deadline would keep both clocks in play; a second monotonic deadline beside the epoch would duplicate the owner. Converting once and measuring once removes the failure by construction.
- **What did NOT change:** the 330 s parent-exit and 40 min recovery allowances, `SCHTASKS_TIMEOUT_MS`, the lease and parent-identity guards, the command set and argument shapes, error strings, and the `parentExitDeadlineAt` wire format.

## Evidence

Each row pairs the same input on both revisions; the only difference is the deadline domain.

### Contract, before and after

| Surface | Before (wall clock) | After (monotonic) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Remaining budget for `spawn({ timeout })` | `deadline - Date.now()`; resized by every step between seed and dispatch | `deadline - performance.now()`; unchanged by a step |
| Timeout handed to Node | fractional (`1000.4`, `2500.5`) → `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`; `0` → timeout disabled | `Math.max(1, Math.floor(…))` → integer ≥ 1 ms |
| Activation deadline | `parentExitDeadlineAt = Date.now() + parentExitTimeoutMs`, re-converted after each await | `armActivationDeadline()` on `performance.now()`; converted once, shared by park / settle / commit |
| Recovery deadlines (launchd restore, foreground park, restart delay) | seeded and read on `Date.now()` | seeded and read on `performance.now()` |

Node's contract, checked directly rather than through this PR:

```text
$ node -e "require('node:child_process').spawn(process.execPath,['-e','0'],{timeout:1500.5})"
RangeError [ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE]: The value of "timeout" is out of range.
It must be an unsigned integer. Received 1500.5
    at validateTimeout (node:child_process:1039:11)
```

### Unit — red on the base revision, green on this head

`src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-command-source.test.ts`, production file reverted to `origin/main` while the new regressions stay in place, then this head:

```text
$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts \
    src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-command-source.test.ts

# base (origin/main production file)
 × keeps the spawn timeout on the monotonic clock across a wall-clock rewind (BUG-165)
   → the inflated 30 s timer never fires, so the command never settles
 × dispatches an integer spawn timeout for a 1000.4 ms monotonic deadline
   → expected 1000.4 to be 1
 × dispatches an integer spawn timeout for a 2500.5 ms monotonic deadline
   → expected 2500.5 to be 1500
 × starts a real subprocess from a fractional remaining budget
   → spawn rejects the timeout; the command resolves { code: 1 }
 Tests  4 failed | 8 passed (12)

# this head
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  12 passed (12)
```

### Complete sealed helper lifecycle under a stepped clock, against a real systemd unit

Each arm runs the sealed `handoff.cjs` the build itself writes — published `openclaw@2026.10.8` versus this head — and drives it through the real control protocol on stdin (`park`, then `commit`), so `activationDeadline`, `parkGatewayService`, `finishGatewayServicePark`, and `runOwnedUpdateCommand` all execute unmodified inside the shipped helper. The unit is a real `openclaw-gateway.service` under systemd; the clock step is applied inside the helper process only, by a `--require` hook that shifts `Date.now` after the deadline is seeded.

| Helper | Clock step | First `systemctl --user show` budget | Control replies | Unit after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| published `2026.10.8` | −90 s | 418621 ms (330 s + 90 s) | `parked`, `committed` | `inactive` |
| published `2026.10.8` | none | 328725 ms | `parked`, `committed` | `inactive` |
| published `2026.10.8` | +90 s | 238763 ms (330 s − 90 s) | `parked`, `committed` | `inactive` |
| this head | −90 s | 328683 ms | `parked`, `committed` | `inactive` |
| this head | none | 328741 ms | `parked`, `committed` | `inactive` |
| this head | +90 s | 328557 ms | `parked`, `committed` | `inactive` |

The published helper spends the parent-exit budget on the wall clock, so its remaining subprocess budget moves one-for-one with the step. This head converts the epoch once and then consumes a monotonic interval, so the budget stays at the configured 330 s in either direction.

A step larger than the budget stops the pre-fix helper from parking at all, while this head still completes the handoff:

| Helper | Clock step | `systemctl` calls | Control replies | Unit after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| published `2026.10.8` | +400 s | none — the inspect deadline is already past | `cancelled`; parking failed: "systemd service does not match the exact active gateway parent" | still `active` |
| this head | +400 s | 328736 ms | `parked`, `committed` | `inactive` |

Raw rows from the run (2026-10-29 03:47–04:08Z):


### Real managed-service upgrade, published driver → this head

The repo's published-driver cell (`canonical-upgrade.yml`, [run 40799038640](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-managed-upgrade-proof/actions/runs/40799038640), success) installs `2026.10.8` as a real npm global behind a systemd user unit, then updates it to this change (`402e33f67433`; the six changed files are byte-identical at the current head, whose extra commit only merges `main`):

### Not covered

- The harness drives the sealed helper through its own stdin control protocol instead of letting a Gateway spawn it, and the update child is a placeholder, so package installation itself is not part of the table above; the canonical cell above covers a completed upgrade with settings and session data intact.
- Native `launchd` and Windows Scheduled Task runs were not repeated for this revision; the command runner is shared and covered by the unit suite, but only the `systemd` surface was exercised end to end with a real service.

prs.title: fix(telegram): deleting an already-gone message is reported as a failure
prs.body:
Closes #127534

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: deleting a Telegram message is reported as failed (`ok: false, deleted: false`) even though the message is gone. This happens when the first delete succeeds but its response is lost and the retry gets "message to delete not found", and also when the message was already deleted.

## User Impact

User impact: agents and operators get `{ ok: true, deleted: true }` when Telegram confirms the message no longer exists, so automation stops repeating or escalating a delete that already worked. Refusals that leave the message visible (`message can't be deleted`, `MESSAGE_ID_INVALID`, `MESSAGE_DELETE_FORBIDDEN`) are still reported as `ok: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram's "message to delete not found" shared one no-op pattern with refusals in which the message stays visible, so every match was mapped to a failure. Only the absence response now counts as success. It still skips error logging as before, and retry policy is unchanged. The error taxonomy stays conservative, as the issue asks: the other three refusals keep their failure result.

This is the same direction as the earlier closed proposal #157370, written fresh on current `main`.

## Evidence

- Regression tests in `extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.test.ts` drive the registered `delete` action through the real HTTP fixture:
  - "reports a delete as done after a lost delete response": the first `deleteMessage` connection is reset, the retry gets `400: message to delete not found`, and the test expects `{ ok: true, deleted: true }` after exactly two `deleteMessage` calls.
  - "reports a delete as done when it is already gone": a single `deleteMessage` gets `not found`, and the test expects `{ ok: true, deleted: true }`.
  - On `main`, both fail with `expected { ok: false, deleted: false, …(1) } to deeply equal { ok: true, deleted: true }`. With the fix, both pass.
  - Negative controls already in the suite still pass: `message can't be deleted` (same file) and `MESSAGE_DELETE_FORBIDDEN` (`send.telegram-http.test.ts`) remain `ok: false` with one call.
- Focused files `action-runtime.test.ts`, `send.telegram-http.test.ts` and `send.transport-close-proof.test.ts` (the only tests that call `deleteMessageTelegram`): 3 files, 92 tests, all passing. I also started the full `pnpm test:extension telegram`; it hit my local 25-minute limit after 17 files (269 tests passed, 0 failed), so PR CI covers the rest.
- Local checks: `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test` and oxlint on the changed files are clean, and the line-cap, max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets pass. The full `pnpm check:changed` run was stopped by host memory pressure during the SQLite worker ratchet. This change does not touch database code.
- Gap: no Telegram Test Server run. The tests use a local Bot API HTTP fixture with Telegram's documented `400: Bad Request: message to delete not found` response. I don't have QA broker credentials for the `telegram-e2e-userbot` lane.

prs.title: fix(msteams): preserve non-bot mention names in inbound text
prs.body:
Related: #102376

## What Problem This Solves

Teams inbound preparation removes every `<at>...</at>` span, erasing non-bot display names before the agent sees the message. For example, `@Bot so @Other User and Third Person can use you; also ask @Unidentified User` loses both user names.

## What Changed

Normalize mentions at the existing inbound preparation owner, before debounce, for activity text and HTML attachment fallback. Remove a display span only when its matching mention entity unambiguously identifies `activity.recipient.id`. Preserve other, unidentified and conflicting names as readable `@Display Name` text. Decode HTML once and retain emoji sprite alt text.

This is content normalization only. `wasMSTeamsBotMentioned`, bot-mention admission, allowlists, permissions and routing are unchanged. Span matching controls which display text is removed, not whether the message is addressed to the bot.

Original fix/report credit: @wyf027; prior context: @galiniliev's closed, unmerged #102379. Contributor commits are preserved, including the latest bot-identity fixture correction.

## Evidence

[Clean exact-head built-Gateway proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184361#issuecomment-6488127578): real bundled Teams plugin over loopback BotFramework, persisted chat history, actual local provider HTTP requests and Connector reply markers. Main erases both user names twice; candidate preserves both twice while still stripping bot addressing. HTML, bot-only, ambiguous-span, mismatched-span, mention-required, unknown-recipient and denied-sender controls are recorded.

The earlier dirty-source capture is superseded. The clean transport run proves ordinary mixed-mention messages; it does **not** claim that two same-conversation HTTP activities formed a batch, because durable ingress serialized that lane. Actual SDK batched input and lifecycle ownership remain covered by the existing regression suite.

Focused owner and media-fixture tests: 23/23 passed. Net test-count growth is zero. Two added regression cases are consolidated into existing lifecycle cases with exact `BodyForAgent` equality; test allocation is tightened from the contributor's latest 62 to 20 lines. Production delta +41/-7; test delta net +20.

## What Remains Unfixed

This completely addresses non-bot mention-name loss only. #102376's entity-quote and forwarded-message rendering requests remain open; this PR does not close that issue or add those features. Loopback proof is not a live Teams tenant or Graph API claim.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores previous content normalization without a migration. No schema, persisted-state format, configuration or permission change. Blast radius is Teams activity text and HTML attachment fallback before agent dispatch; admission and routing remain untouched.

prs.title: fix(automations): CLI-runtime owners can't see or manage ownerless automations
prs.body:
Related: #147614, #157126, #157144

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: admitted owners using CLI-backed agents cannot see or manage existing ownerless automations because the later MCP request constructs the tool outside the owner's automation-management scope.

## User Impact

Authorized owners regain Gateway-wide list/get/update of existing automations through CLI MCP. Removing owner membership or revoking the grant still denies access, and later callers without management authority remain caller-scoped. Ownerless jobs remain ownerless. No configuration or stored-data migration is required.

This carries existing management authority across a host-owned boundary, so it needs the repository's exact-head security approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automation tools bind management authority when constructed, before their later execution. The host-only CLI grant now retains the exact live construction scope, and tool resolution enters it under the admitted caller identity and stored request scope. The construction identity deliberately omits execution's requester-grant issuer. Actual execution retains the existing one-use, method-bound grant and final-effect checks.

The retained callback rechecks the exact grant row, active run, abort/currentness and current channel-owner membership. Stale scope exits any ambient management scope rather than inheriting it. The implementation builds on current requester-origin and detached-listener ownership; it does not restore superseded listener or ambient-authority code.

This semantic repair is based on `f91bca9546f5`. Its seven changed files are byte-identical to reviewed source `683a0212960fb997b1758ceaa55bc248a84b2c79`; unrelated preceding model-locality changes are excluded from this PR. A local merge check against `1e48ec3a9e3` succeeds.

## Evidence

- **Live Claude CLI proof:** new QA scenario `cron-claude-cli-owner-management` (live-frontier, `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6`, subscription auth). A configured channel owner asks the Claude CLI agent to `get` and then disable an automation owned by another account. On this branch the agent replies with the success marker; the job is disabled and keeps its original owner. With the four source files reverted to `main`, the same live turn fails with `cron job not found: <id> ... For cross-session management, use a fresh authenticated configured channel owner ...`, which is the production report in #186696.
- **Production:** on 2026.10.8, a configured channel owner on a `claude-cli` agent got `cron job not found` for a job owned by the same conversation, with no `cron: admin management` log line; the same owner on the embedded runtime is granted management.
- **Real boundary regression:** `src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-cron-management.integration.test.ts` drives the actual detached loopback HTTP MCP listener, production tool resolution and isolated durable Cron persistence. On the unchanged owner it fails with `expected 'caller' to be 'gateway'`; with this repair it lists, reads and updates the ownerless job without assigning an owner.
- The same scenario then removes the configured owner and observes update refusal; revokes the grant and observes HTTP401; starts a later unentitled run on the same listener and observes caller scope with no access to the job. The only mocked boundary is unrelated attached-node inventory.
- **Construction/execution separation:** a real HTTP regression proves the admitted identity cannot mint a requester grant during construction, while execution can mint and redeem its one-use grant. It failed before the construction identity was narrowed and passes afterward.
- Final affected command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-http.async-scope.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-cron-management.integration.test.ts src/agents/tools/cron-tool.management.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **21/21 pass** (7 HTTP-scope, 1 durable Cron integration, 13 management controls). Wrapper wall **65.13s**, including compiler/bootstrap work; the integrated owner scenario took **6.772s**. These are test costs, not production-latency benchmarks.
- Earlier broader affected runs cover **85 distinct tests across the runs**, including grant-store, grant construction, authority and requester-continuation consumers. Core/gateway test types, touched type-aware lint, formatting, scoped line-cap and diff checks pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 review completed scoped-clean on the final seven-file patch.
- Simplification keeps the existing grant row and Cron authority owner; no second authority registry, wire credential, database schema or permission option is added. Construction and execution share one identity builder with an explicit phase. Necessary patch growth is the retained host callback and separate real authority/revocation regressions.

Current-head CI and independent maintainer security approval are still required; no approval or merge readiness is inferred from older-head checks.

prs.title: perf(state): reference submitted JSON in plugin-state receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin-state writes echo their complete JSON values in native commit receipts even though the host already holds the serialized input. This repeats large snapshots across the worker boundary. Related: #187193.

## User Impact

No SDK or storage behavior change. Large plugin-state writes transfer smaller authority receipts; committed values, expiry, eviction, ordering, and durable settlement retain their existing owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin-state publication owner substitutes an admission-local submitted-value reference only when the captured committed postimage exactly matches the input. The host reconstructs the complete row before the existing receipt validation and publication checks. Worker-generated values and compound operation receipts still carry full postimages. The reference is released after native finish has serviced settlement, including lost-reply recovery.

The additional encoding/decoding code preserves the existing full-row publication contract and worker-derived metadata without adding a cache, SDK surface, schema, write, or authority bypass.

## Evidence

The committed `scripts/perf/plugin-state-authority-receipts.ts` exercises real SQLite workers with 10,000 synthetic sessions, 44 synthetic plugin identities, eight warm actors, lifecycle phases, and entry patches. Its declared JSON body-size mix is 24 × 1 KiB, 12 × 4 KiB, 6 × 16 KiB, and 2 × 64 KiB. This is a sensitivity workload, not a measured production size/frequency distribution. Setup and readback are excluded. Fifty rounds contain 2,200 plugin writes and 400 each of actor adoption, completion, and entry patch. A synthetic minute means one round, independent of execution speed.

Baseline: `5492aee09fb9` (merged #187193), macOS / Node 26.12.1. Final candidate results:

| Authority class | Base bytes / 50 rounds | Candidate bytes / 50 rounds | Base → candidate synthetic MB/min |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `plugin_state` | 16,078,160 | 835,000 | 0.3215632 → 0.0167000 |
| `session.actor.adoptRun` | 2,090,015 | 2,115,215 | 0.0418003 → 0.0423043 |
| `session.actor.completeTurn` | 868,624 | 872,224 | 0.01737248 → 0.01744448 |
| `session.entry.patch.commit` | 22,400 | 22,400 | 0.000448 → 0.000448 |
| **Total** | **19,059,199** | **3,844,839** | **0.38118398 → 0.07689678** |

Plugin state contributes **84.36%** of baseline known authority bytes. Its receipt bytes fall **94.81%**, total bytes **79.83%**. Actor differences track temporary database-path lengths embedded in unchanged actor receipts. Both arms have 8,800 unmeasured admission messages; this table covers measured receipt payloads.

The isolated store-owner run uses the same 44 stores and 10,000 idle sessions, with **2,200 writes per arm**. CPU is untraced; allocation is a separate 4-KiB sampling pass including collected objects:

| Arm | Main CPU ms | Sampled allocation bytes | GC count / total ms / max ms | Host load before → after | RSS / main heap after (MiB) |

prs.title: test(skills): pin Skill Workshop behavior at real entry points before plugin extraction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill Workshop is moving from core into a bundled, enabled-by-default plugin (#173605). Its current tests mostly call Workshop internals directly, so they can't show that behavior stays the same after the code moves.

## User Impact

None. This PR adds tests only: no production changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

These are characterization tests: each one pins the behavior an operator sees today at the entry point they use. They import only modules that stay in core after the move (the agent tool set, the Gateway dispatcher, the CLI program, the command pipeline, the skills loader, Doctor, Gateway maintenance, the Gateway server, and the Control UI app), never Workshop modules. The same files are meant to pass unchanged before and after the cutover.

Refreshed on current `main`. Updated to intended changes since the first draft:

- The CLI archive hint now names `--agent`.
- The tool has `draft` and `discard`.
- Doctor exports retired proposals to `.drafts/`, and moves earlier `.archive/.retired-proposals/` exports there too.
- Background reviews call `skill_workshop` directly, without Tool Search (#173889).
- Channel notices carry the Learned marker (#182329).
- The `/learn` tests now pin how the request reaches the agent, not the full prompt wording, which Workshop owns.

New contracts:

- **Propose mode and drafts:** a review in `propose` mode can only save drafts and cannot discard them; the foreground lists, views and discards drafts (tool). `skills.workshop.list`/`read` return on-disk drafts for `operator.read`; `applyDraft` and `discardDraft` are `operator.admin` only, and apply refuses a mismatched skill name (RPC). A real-Gateway review in `propose` mode saves one draft, changes no skill and posts no notice (e2e). The Control UI shows drafts as a diff against the live skill and sends `applyDraft`/`discardDraft` (UI e2e).
- **`/learn drafts`:** with no drafts it answers without a model turn; otherwise it rewrites the turn over the selected drafts, narrowed by skill name, with the focus text.
- **`/learn` and memory plugins:** with a selected memory plugin's learning tools, one turn routes to both skills and memory; with `skill_workshop` denied it learns into memory alone; with both denied it replies with the combined refusal.
- **Daily maintenance:** an oversized, settled learned skill is dieted as one `curator` change that `restore` undoes. Unused-skill cleanup does not run in `propose` mode or when tool policy denies `skill_workshop`.

## Evidence

Local runs on `main` at `f03f131879683` (merged):

| Area | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Tool, RPC, CLI, `/learn`, config, Doctor, skill loading, maintenance (10 files) | 64 tests pass |
| Real-Gateway review and notice history (2 e2e files) | 11 pass, plus a targeted rerun of the channel-notice cases |
| Control UI (app e2e) | 5 pass |

`pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxfmt, type-aware oxlint and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files.

Merge danger: two-way door. Blast radius: tests only.

Tracking issue: #173605

## What Problem This Solves

With `tools.media.audio.echoTranscript` enabled, every voice note produces two notifications on Telegram: one for the transcript echo and one for the agent reply that follows, so the confirmation-only echo becomes notification noise.

User impact: operators can set `tools.media.audio.echoSilent: true` to deliver the transcript echo without a push notification (Telegram `disable_notification`) while the agent reply keeps notifying normally. Default is `false`, so existing behavior is unchanged; channels without silent delivery keep sending the echo as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sendTranscriptEcho` is the single owner of echo delivery for the media-understanding path, audio preflight, and the plugin-SDK preflight runtime, and it already receives the effective config. It now forwards `silent: true` to the durable outbound send when `echoSilent` is set. The outbound path already carries `silent` end to end (delivery params, durable queue persistence, Telegram adapter mapping to `disable_notification`, the same route `channels.telegram.silentErrorReplies` uses), so no channel code changes are needed. Config schema, field help/label, docs, the generated config-doc baseline hashes, and the common-tier snapshot are updated.

## Evidence

- New integration test in `src/media-understanding/echo-transcript.integration.test.ts` drives the real durable SQLite queue with a fake Telegram outbound adapter: the default echo reaches the adapter without `silent`, and with `echoSilent: true` the adapter receives `silent: true`. - `pnpm test src/media-understanding/echo-transcript.integration.test.ts src/media-understanding/echo-transcript.test.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts src/config/schema.tiers.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/media-understanding-runtime.test.ts src/media-understanding/audio-preflight.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all passed.

prs.title: fix(usage): count copied session history once
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Usage counts copied session history twice. Rewind, branch switch, fork at a message, the session manager's branched session and the subagent parent fork copy earlier transcript events, including their provider usage, into a new session window. The usage scanner counts each window, so every copied turn on the new window's visible path is counted again. On one large Gateway, 9,071 assistant turns (2.21B tokens, about 1.2% of all tokens in 30 days) were copies; 8,707 of them had timestamps earlier than the window that held them.

## User Impact

User impact: Usage tokens, cost and message counts count each turn once. A rewound or branched session, a fork and a subagent that starts from its parent's context count only the turns made after the copy; the source session keeps counting the copied turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

The writers that copy history now record where the copy ends, and the usage scanner skips everything up to that point:

- **Writers:** the new transcript header records `inheritedThrough`, the id of the last copied event (`createSessionTranscriptHeader`, `planSessionMessageCut` for rewind, switch and fork, `buildForkedChildTranscriptEvents` for the subagent parent fork, `createBranchedSession` in the session manager). The header already carries lineage (`parentSession`) for forks.
- **Reader:** `dropInheritedTranscriptEvents` (`session-cost-usage-rollup-scan.ts`) drops records up to the marker after the visible path is selected, so branch selection still sees the full tree. The SQLite scan now reads from before `seq 0`, where the session header is stored (empty transcripts keep the old start). The session usage time series skips the same events.
- `USAGE_COST_ROLLUP_VERSION` 10 → 11 rebuilds cached rollups from transcripts.

Accepted edge cases:
- Copies written before this change have no marker and keep their double count. A Doctor backfill could mark them; it is not part of this change.
- Session logs still list copied messages with their tokens; they are a message log, not a total.
- If the marker's event id is missing from a transcript, nothing is skipped (counts stay as before rather than dropping usage).
- Older builds ignore the extra header field (no reader validates the header as a closed object), so rollback keeps working.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway, synthetic state (40 sessions), 5 `sessions.rewind` and 5 `sessions.fork` calls through the Gateway, then the Usage overview request after the cache settled. Decoded rollups of the new windows:

  | Build | New rewind windows (5) | Fork windows (5) |
  |---|---|---|
  | `main` (`83cfa434563b`) | each counts 1 copied turn | each counts its copied prefix (for example 14,546, 28,074, 20,751, 59,704 tokens) |
  | this PR | each counts 0 | each counts 0 |

- Upgrade: the same state with copies made by `main`, then this PR's `doctor --fix` and Gateway. Rollups (v10) are rebuilt as v11; the totals equal `main`'s (those copies predate the marker); transcripts are identical (41,273 rows); `openclaw.json` keeps every existing key.
- `session-cost-usage-worker-refresh.test.ts` (new cases): a rewind, a fork and a subagent parent fork produced by the real writers, plus one new turn, scanned with the real SQLite scanner (header at `seq 0`), count only the new turn (5 tokens). With the reader change removed they count 15, 15 and 35; with the scan still starting after `seq 0` they also fail.
- `session-manager-branching.test.ts` asserts the branched session's header marker.
- Every test file that uses the changed writers, the usage infra suites and the Gateway usage suites pass. `tsgo` (core) and oxlint pass. `pnpm check:changed` passes except `lint core`, whose findings are all in files outside this diff (current `main`); the dead export scan was skipped (its entries are outside this diff).

Observed while testing, not changed here: on both `main` and this PR, the Usage total drops by about 0.85–1.0M tokens after the rewinds in the synthetic state, beyond the copy effect. It is identical with and without this change and needs its own investigation.

Merge risk: #167275 also bumps `USAGE_COST_ROLLUP_VERSION`; whichever lands second takes the next number.

## Draft scope and provenance

Base: release/2026.10.10 at b9917570de91184704c9c2b0d5c65aea06796f72. A2UI 0.12.0, retaining Zod 3.25.76 and all public declarations/exports. No broad Zod-4 migration, A2UI removal, or vendored-parser replacement.

This is a **local Zod-3 adaptation**, not a cherry-pick or upstream Zod-3 release. It implements early upper-bound rejection from Colin McDonnell's upstream Zod commit a0ebf970f2d752e5f58527cd2942ff48be4f46bd (colinhacks/zod#6652; GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5). Only three parser branches are changed in the TypeScript source and its ESM/CJS runtime outputs. Original copyright and licensing are unchanged. The existing Discord-focused local adaptation informed the approach, but this patch targets the separately installed Zod package, not Discord's embedded parser.

## Behavior and reachability

Oversized array max/exact-length and set max/exact-size abort before element or outer-refinement work. Valid transforms and preprocessors, lower-bound failures, wrong input types and successful union alternatives remain covered. Intentional compatibility delta: the rejected branch is aborted, so element issues disappear and a failing union may return invalid_union instead of a dirty branch's too_big.

A2UI 0.12 catalog loading turns JSON Schema maxItems into a real Zod array bound. A regression loads a function catalog through the public Catalog API, then proves the generated bounded schema rejects oversized arguments without visiting an element. Catalog schema generation and existing resolution/validation tests remain passing.

The exact-version pnpm patch also reaches other direct consumers of Zod 3.25.76 and zod-to-json-schema. It does not patch Zod-4 subpaths or the parser embedded in Discord's SDK. No advisory-wide clearance is claimed. No new protocol-wide resource bound is added.

## Actual validation

- New regression: unpatched checkout fails all 21 assertions/tests; patched checkout passes 21/21, across ESM/CJS, sync/async and the real A2UI Catalog integration.
- Native Vitest wrapper passes. Production Canvas bundles build without the undefined-ZodEffects warning caused by the rejected broad migration.
- Installed-package byte comparison: exactly src/v3/types.ts, v3/types.js and v3/types.cjs change. All declarations and other package files are identical. Patched TypeScript parser source compiles.
- Strict public declarations retain the same six pre-existing v0_8 declaration errors, byte-identical diagnostics before/after; no new public-type failure or migration.
- Existing self-contained upstream tests: 258/258 pass before and after.

## Remaining blockers — do not mark ready

**The package-patch guard is intentionally unchanged and rejects the new Zod patch.** Explicit authorization to register this exact patch in the existing allowlist is still needed. This draft does not disable, relax, reclassify or bypass that gate. The patch is not landable until that decision is resolved.

Independent canonical full-context security review and hosted checks are still required. Local validation is not independent review clearance. No ready-for-review request, force-push, merge or release is authorized by this draft. Existing aggregate source/proof and PR #186177 remain untouched.

prs.body:
Fixes #187153

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw dashboard` keeps probing a slow/preparing Control UI document and can print a dashboard handoff after the operator has already interrupted the command.

## User Impact

Accepted interruption cancels the in-flight readiness request and retry delay, then exits without issuing a late browser pairing handoff or dashboard diagnostic. Text and JSON modes use the existing command lifetime. Guided browser onboarding and setup finalization pass the same lifetime into their shared readiness calls.

## Why This Change Was Made

Thread the existing command-owned AbortSignal through the shared document readiness owner and its fetch/retry work. Stop downstream handoff/output after cancellation, while preserving unrelated request/sleep errors and cleanup. No additional signal-exit gate, permission rule or config option is added.

## Evidence

Fully built baseline and candidate in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker. Real isolated Gateway discovery/auth/RPC and actual dashboard CLI run normally; a process-local HTTP fixture delays only the document HEAD response to model a preparing document. Main repeats continue issuing HEADs after accepted SIGINT and later print the dashboard URL; candidate repeats stop after the initial HEAD and suppress late handoff. JSON and normal-completion controls are included in the evidence comment.

Focused owner/shared-caller suites: 102 tests passed before the guided repair; the repaired browser handoff suite passes 15 tests, including abort rejection with progress cleanup and no browser credentials, while ordinary document failures still return false for fallback. Baseline regressions fail for both continued probing and cancellation being returned as false. The guided helper now rethrows the command abort after its progress cleanup, so the guided caller never receives a recoverable browser-failure result. Test-line delta -1; production +37. Formatting/type-aware lint pass; independent timeout and diagnostic coverage remains.

Observed captures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187220#issuecomment-6487714271

Merge danger: two-way door; revert restores previous cancellation behavior without a state migration. Blast radius is CLI document readiness during dashboard or onboarding handoff, not Gateway startup or browser authentication policy.

## Scope

Draft targeting `release/2026.10.10` (observed base `b9917570de91184704c9c2b0d5c65aea06796f72`, train-local qualification). Focused mitigation for the Zod parser **embedded inside** Discord’s browser SDK, not a broad dependency refresh or a claim of clean dependency audits.

The published `@discord/embedded-app-sdk@2.5.0` bundles its own Zod 3 implementation. Updating the separately installed Zod package does not change those bytes. A baseline regression invokes element refinements on an oversized array; the patch rejects the collection before element or outer-refinement work.

## Implementation and provenance

- Adapt the early upper-size rejection behavior from Colin McDonnell’s upstream Zod commit `a0ebf970f2d752e5f58527cd2942ff48be4f46bd` ([colinhacks/zod#6652](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6652)), referenced by [GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5).
- This is a **local Zod-3 adaptation**, not a cherry-pick or Zod-4 migration. Six small branches across the ESM/CJS vendored parsers change: oversized array max/exact-length and set max/exact-size return the existing invalid result before traversal.
- Preserve valid parsing/transforms, lower-bound failures, SDK authentication/scope fallbacks, declarations and exports. Early abort intentionally omits element/refinement issues and may wrap a union branch in `invalid_union`; regression coverage and the patch documentation make that compatibility change explicit. The bundled Zod-3 map API has no upper-size constraint.
- Register one exact-version package patch and regenerate only its lockfile identity. No unrelated dependency versions, audit exceptions, or check behavior change.
- Authentication/browser-build test scaffolding is adapted from local aggregate commit `8e6f7bd28af9e7bebf03ff08bf0001e4fc7561be`, authored by `roboclaw-bot`, preserved in `f0a0c53aa23b80bd68267fc48cfdda020db77c26`; this is not an upstream OpenClaw fix being backported. New early-rejection and compatibility coverage belongs to this isolated local adaptation.
- Upstream alternative checked on 2026-10-29: SDK stable 2.5.0 and beta 3.0.0-beta.3 both fail the early-rejection regression. [discord/embedded-app-sdk#318](https://github.com/discord/embedded-app-sdk/pull/318), authored by renovate-bot (head `81e49dfa871e935641d9b9591ed789e837dc89e1`), remains open; it is not a published compatible fix. This small patch avoids the previous whole-parser replacement.

## Validation

- Unpatched published SDK: regression fails (oversized array executes 3 element refinements).
- Patched parser: 48 direct ESM/CJS, sync/async regression assertions pass, including arrays, exact lengths, sets, nested paths, valid transforms and wrong input types.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/discord-sdk-zod.test.ts`: 7 tests pass, including both SDK entrypoints and the actual production browser build.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --noEmit`: pass.

- Byte comparison of all 196 published SDK files: exactly the two vendored parser files differ. Published/installed hashes and the patch hash are documented in `patches/README.md`.

## Boundaries / remaining gates

This is the beta train-local backport of #187289 at exact source commit 0c38cbb44b5edc1597d7dec30feb615638ffa9ee (author: roboclaw-bot). The 58-line patch and 208-line test file are preserved exactly. Registration is adapted to this train and its lockfile is regenerated locally. Original source/proof and #186177 remain untouched; no extended-stable or A2UI work is included.

Both the Discord SDK regression file and owning package-patch guard tests pass: 15 tests total. The direct matrix passes 48 cases on this train's installed SDK. Regenerated patch matches after normalizing optional Git hunk function labels. All 196 published files were compared: only the two documented parser files differ. These are bounded checks, not a full repository build or native lifecycle/packaged-plugin qualification.

prs.title: fix(update): never lose a managed handoff silently
prs.body:
Refs #186813. Thanks @masterdevill for the detailed report and follow-up diagnostics.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes managed updates disappearing without a terminal outcome when started by an agent exec inside the Gateway service.

## User Impact

Linux handoffs run independently of the Gateway and its exec cleanup. If the helper and updater nevertheless die, the next update status or startup reconciliation records `handoff-terminated` with the last phase and safely disposes of an owned npm stage that never reached activation. Uncertain cleanup retains the stage and records a warning. The installed updater must contain this fix; downloading a newer candidate cannot repair the old launcher.

## Why This Change Was Made

A systemd scope changes cgroup placement but retains the exec's process ancestry and inherited OOM score. Exec finalization can therefore reap a supposedly detached handoff, and its inherited `oom_score_adj=1000` also makes it an attractive OOM victim. A manager-launched transient service escapes both inheritances, uses its own slice and `KillMode=control-group`/`OOMPolicy=stop`, and receives the prepared environment through a private environment file. Automatic triage keeps its existing scope lifetime.

The exact killer in the reported incident is not established. No post-transfer 60-second watchdog was found: validation runs without that admission deadline. Native proof reproduced the ancestry and OOM-score hazards; the observed field memory peak alone does not prove OOM.

The existing update ledger owns orphan detection. It now records the Gateway parent separately from the handoff/helper lifetime, so an alive serving Gateway cannot indefinitely keep a dead update marked running. Cleanup uses the existing package-stage lifecycle owner, verifies recorded directory identity and absence of surviving work, and never handles activated stages or backups. No SQLite schema, dependency, or user-facing option changes.

## Evidence

### Exact-head Linux/Bun CI repair

The failed `core-runtime-infra-storage-state-hosted-6` cases were reproduced with a real same-user `ssh-agent` in a private Docker fixture (Debian 12, overlayfs, Node 26.12.1, repository-pinned Bun). With no protected daemon the original tests passed; with `ssh-agent` hiding its cwd, both killed-handoff cases failed. Diagnostic census output identified that daemon as the unverified PID. Stage identity checks and awaited cleanup ordering were unchanged.

The Linux census now uses native process birth ticks to exclude opaque, unreferenced processes older than every recorded handoff driver. Equal/later/unknown births remain protected, and explicit stage/run references always retain custody. The separate helper receipt participates even after driver-history pruning. The pruned fixture now actually omits that helper from driver history rather than fabricating an impossible zero birth identity. A second defect discarded cleanup warnings after `handoff-terminated`; advisory cleanup steps may now append without changing the terminal outcome, and refusal diagnostics include the census reason/PID.

Linux commands, with isolated HOME/state and the pinned `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH`:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/restart-sentinel.update-result.test.ts src/infra/update-run-reconciliation.worker.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-maintenance-contention.test.ts src/infra/openclaw-process-census.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/openclaw-process-census.test.ts src/infra/update-run-reconciliation.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The four-file Linux replay passed 120 tests in 29.08s (59.99s with compiler preparation); after preserving all original Doctor assertions and consolidating env teardown, the final two-file Linux replay passed 68 tests in 16.71s (20.84s including preparation). The private container's sentinel was removed only to exercise host census inside its isolated PID namespace; a separate replay with the sentinel present passed all 9 reconciliation tests in 17.19s, proving conservative retention plus the recorded warning. The fixture and its ssh-agent were removed afterward. There are no platform skips, retries, timeout increases, relaxed filesystem identity checks, or schema changes.

The 30 directly importing consumer files were replayed through the repository wrapper with isolated HOME/state and the Node runtime: **27 files passed, 3 existing platform/opt-in files skipped; 522 tests passed, 20 skipped, no failures**, across six groups in 774.63s. Existing real integration test costs included Gateway cleanup authorization 60.039s and Doctor retirement 54.530s/42.003s; these tests were unchanged.

Core/infra-test/services-test typechecks, touched-file lint/format, the line-cap ratchet and import-cycle check pass. Fresh independent review of the final repair is clean (no actionable P0/P1 findings).

- Regression was red on the untouched base: after killing the validating helper, status stayed `running` instead of reporting `handoff-terminated`. The new production-boundary cases retain a live Gateway parent and cover both retained and pruned helper history, real child termination, stage preparation, SQLite worker settlement, last-phase recording, and stage removal. Container process-census uncertainty deliberately retains the stage with a warning.
- Native isolated systemd proof (Debian 12, systemd 252.39): a synthetic Gateway user unit had `MemoryMax=256M`. The old scope retained the exec anchor as ancestor and `oom_score_adj=1000`; it did not survive anchor cleanup/Gateway exit. Its properties were `Slice=app-openclaw-update.slice`, `KillMode=control-group`, `OOMPolicy=stop`, and `MemoryMax=infinity`. The throwaway container and units were removed. This proves native lifecycle mechanics, not a full Debian 13 npm update.

Empty, quoted, multiline, Unicode, dollar, backslash, tab, and CR values survived byte-for-byte; the helper could unlink the private file after startup. EnvironmentFile avoids the systemd >=250 restriction of bare `--setenv=NAME`.

Existing mutation admission and package disposal were extracted unchanged into leaf modules. Both installed-artifact tests pass (31.92s including preparation; about 3s of tests).


prs.title: fix(ci): batch generated publisher tree inspections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated-PR publication starts a separately supervised Git process for each path it inspects, repeating the same tree reads across a multi-file update.

## User Impact

No user-facing change. Generated publishers inspect trees in bounded batches while retaining their overlap, freshness, publication, and cleanup decisions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing publisher now owns one phase-local metadata map per inspected tree. It preserves exact modes, object types, object IDs, missing entries, and the byte-sorted first-overlap decision. Targeted NUL-delimited reads retain directory entries and split path arguments into 64 KiB batches. Every read still completes through the existing Git lifecycle owner before its output is used; no observation is cached across a base refresh.

Production: +25 lines for bounded inspection ownership. Tests: +58 lines, including a real four-file publication regression and ordinary-error, cancellation, and failed-cleanup controls.

## Evidence

- Complete baseline/candidate publisher runs through the pinned Git owner used local Git remotes and stub PR mutation functions. Both published the exact four requested blobs and matching HEAD, preserved unrelated content, pushed/mutated once, wrote the expected summary, and removed Git auth. The inspection budget failed on the original policy (16 reads) and passed on the candidate (4 reads).
- Dependency-free real Git proof used the action's pinned Git owner `88095dc00eef288c3829909d4dc64a9e249fa7ef`, Git 2.56.0, and Python 3.15.1. Eleven baseline/candidate cases agreed, covering first/last overlap, directory/file replacements, executable mode, symlinks, deletion/adoption, ignored gitlinks, and tab/LF/non-UTF-8 names beneath a generated root.
- A 12-path disjoint comparison used 36 tree inspections before and 3 after; matching the desired tree used 24 before and 2 after. A first-path conflict used 3 in both versions. These are process counts, not elapsed-time or billing measurements.
- Chunk-boundary, ancestor/child, empty-selection, missing-entry, and missing-object checks agreed. Literal/noglob/default pathspec modes agreed; glob/icase modes were rejected with exit 128 in both versions. An initial scratch harness incorrectly expected glob mode to succeed; its unfinished environment controls were corrected and completed without replaying the passed cases.
- Python compilation, targeted pinned oxfmt 0.74.0, and `git diff --check` passed. Two independent source reviews and autoreview are clean.
- Focused Vitest suites and ordinary exact-head CI are pending. This PR remains draft until the numbered native checkout completes its required proof.

Follow-ups: canonical promotion of the shared Git-owner action pin remains separate; this change does not claim the newer owner's wait-loop improvement for the pinned action. Root-level pathspec-magic filenames are a pre-existing discovery/read/mutation contract issue; this change preserves that behavior and does not claim arbitrary-path support.

prs.title: chore(config): keep the transcript iterator private
prs.body:
Fixes #187240

## What Problem This Solves

The scheduled dead-code checks report `readTranscriptEventsFromDatabase` in `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-read.ts` as an unused export, so CI dependency hygiene cannot pass. The iterator has no consumer outside its own module: its only caller, `loadTranscriptEventsFromDatabase`, lives in the same file.

## Why This Change Was Made

Drop the `export` keyword so the iterator stays private to its module. No query, read fence, byte budget, JSON decoding, iterator cleanup, or public API changes — `loadTranscriptEventsFromDatabase` remains the synchronous entry point and keeps its signature. Removing the keyword is the smallest cutover; adding a suppression or a knip allowlist would hide a real finding instead of fixing it.

## User Impact

No runtime or user-facing change. The scheduled `deadcode:exports` job stops reporting this symbol; the aggregate job still has other unrelated findings, which this fix intentionally does not touch.

## Evidence

Observed result first — the finding disappears from the same knip invocation the scheduled job uses:

```text
$ npx knip@6.40.0 --config config/knip.all-exports.config.ts --no-progress --reporter compact --no-config-hints --exports --exclude duplicates

# before (base)
src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-read.ts: readTranscriptEventsFromDatabase
34 lines of findings

# after (this branch)
(no match for readTranscriptEventsFromDatabase)
33 lines of findings
```

The aggregate check still exits non-zero because other findings remain in the job, exactly as the issue describes; the change removes only this one.

Covering tests, run on the branch (Node 24.22.1, the version the SQLite safety check requires):

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-transcript-authority.test.ts --run
      Tests  9 passed (9)
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-transcript-reconcile.readiness.test.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-accessor.reset-boundary-race.test.ts --run
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  13 passed (13)
```

`tsc -p tsconfig.core.json` reports only two pre-existing `@noble/hashes` resolution errors in `packages/gateway-client`, unchanged from the base checkout; no new errors.

What was not tested: the full scheduled CI workflow, and the other unrelated knip findings in the same job.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep, git diff, knip, vitest, and tsc to confirm the export had no importers, apply the removal, and verify the finding disappears. The implementer understands the code: the iterator is an internal implementation detail of the synchronous reader, and keeping it non-exported preserves every read-fence and cleanup invariant. All evidence above comes from real local runs.

prs.title: [2026.9] fix(discord): reject oversized vendored Zod collections early
prs.body:
## Scope

Draft targeting `extended-stable/2026.9.33` (observed base `e93b50ad2400871616c2e6588d57488dba94ecad`, package version 2026.9.35). Focused mitigation for the Zod parser **embedded inside** Discord’s browser SDK, not a broad dependency refresh or a claim of clean dependency audits.

The published `@discord/embedded-app-sdk@2.5.0` bundles its own Zod 3 implementation. Updating the separately installed Zod package does not change those bytes. A baseline regression invokes element refinements on an oversized array; the patch rejects the collection before element or outer-refinement work.

## Implementation and provenance

- Adapt the early upper-size rejection behavior from Colin McDonnell’s upstream Zod commit `a0ebf970f2d752e5f58527cd2942ff48be4f46bd` ([colinhacks/zod#6652](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6652)), referenced by [GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5).
- This is a **local Zod-3 adaptation**, not a cherry-pick or Zod-4 migration. Six small branches across the ESM/CJS vendored parsers change: oversized array max/exact-length and set max/exact-size return the existing invalid result before traversal.
- Preserve valid parsing/transforms, lower-bound failures, SDK authentication/scope fallbacks, declarations and exports. Early abort intentionally omits element/refinement issues and may wrap a union branch in `invalid_union`; regression coverage and the patch documentation make that compatibility change explicit. The bundled Zod-3 map API has no upper-size constraint.
- Register one exact-version package patch and regenerate only its lockfile identity. No unrelated dependency versions, audit exceptions, or check behavior change.
- Authentication/browser-build test scaffolding is adapted from local aggregate commit `8e6f7bd28af9e7bebf03ff08bf0001e4fc7561be`, authored by `roboclaw-bot`, preserved in `f0a0c53aa23b80bd68267fc48cfdda020db77c26`; this is not an upstream OpenClaw fix being backported. New early-rejection and compatibility coverage belongs to this isolated local adaptation.
- Upstream alternative checked on 2026-10-29: SDK stable 2.5.0 and beta 3.0.0-beta.3 both fail the early-rejection regression. [discord/embedded-app-sdk#318](https://github.com/discord/embedded-app-sdk/pull/318), authored by renovate-bot (head `81e49dfa871e935641d9b9591ed789e837dc89e1`), remains open; it is not a published compatible fix. This small patch avoids the previous whole-parser replacement.

## Validation

- Unpatched published SDK: regression fails (oversized array executes 3 element refinements).
- Patched parser: 48 direct ESM/CJS, sync/async regression assertions pass, including arrays, exact lengths, sets, nested paths, valid transforms and wrong input types.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/discord-sdk-zod.test.ts`: 7 tests pass, including both SDK entrypoints and the actual production browser build.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --noEmit`: pass.
- Focused repository oxlint and oxfmt checks: pass.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, package-patch guard and `git diff --check`: pass. Native lifecycle / packaged-plugin qualification is not claimed.
- Byte comparison of all 196 published SDK files: exactly the two vendored parser files differ. Published/installed hashes and the patch hash are documented in `patches/README.md`.

## Boundaries / remaining gates

This does **not** remove the separately installed Zod-3 dependency or claim that the advisory is globally cleared. Beta 2026.10.10-beta.5 and stable 2026.10.8 also use SDK 2.5.0 and need the embedded-parser repair; this PR includes no unqualified cross-train commits. Their direct Zod 4.6.5 pins are a separate dependency scope.

Keep draft pending full independent review, hosted checks and release/packaged-plugin qualification. No ready-for-review request, merge, tag, or release is authorized by these local checks.

prs.title: fix(security): bound custom A2UI schemas on extended-stable
prs.body:
## Draft scope and provenance

Base: extended-stable/2026.9.33 at e93b50ad2400871616c2e6588d57488dba94ecad. A2UI 0.11.0, retaining Zod 3.25.76 and all public declarations/exports. No broad Zod-4 migration, A2UI removal, or vendored-parser replacement.

This is a **local Zod-3 adaptation**, not a cherry-pick or upstream Zod-3 release. It implements early upper-bound rejection from Colin McDonnell's upstream Zod commit a0ebf970f2d752e5f58527cd2942ff48be4f46bd (colinhacks/zod#6652; GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5). Only three parser branches are changed in the TypeScript source and its ESM/CJS runtime outputs. Original copyright and licensing are unchanged. The existing Discord-focused local adaptation informed the approach, but this patch targets the separately installed Zod package, not Discord's embedded parser.

## Behavior and reachability

Oversized array max/exact-length and set max/exact-size abort before element or outer-refinement work. Valid transforms and preprocessors, lower-bound failures, wrong input types and successful union alternatives remain covered. Intentional compatibility delta: the rejected branch is aborted, so element issues disappear and a failing union may return invalid_union instead of a dirty branch's too_big.

A2UI 0.11 catalog loading does not translate maxItems, and its stock source declares no collection upper bounds. This is defense-in-depth for custom bounded schemas accepted by the public Catalog API, not a claim that unbounded stock protocol arrays are protected. The regression exercises that real Catalog invoker and proves oversized arguments do not visit elements or execute the function.

The exact-version pnpm patch also reaches other direct consumers of Zod 3.25.76 and zod-to-json-schema. It does not patch Zod-4 subpaths or the parser embedded in Discord's SDK. No advisory-wide clearance is claimed. No new protocol-wide resource bound is added.

## Actual validation

- New regression: unpatched checkout fails all 21 assertions/tests; patched checkout passes 21/21, across ESM/CJS, sync/async and the real A2UI Catalog integration.
- Native Vitest wrapper passes. Production Canvas bundles build without the undefined-ZodEffects warning caused by the rejected broad migration.
- Installed-package byte comparison: exactly src/v3/types.ts, v3/types.js and v3/types.cjs change. All declarations and other package files are identical. Patched TypeScript parser source compiles.
- Strict public declarations retain the same six pre-existing v0_8 declaration errors, byte-identical diagnostics before/after; no new public-type failure or migration.
- Existing upstream tests: 57 pass and one unchanged ENOENT failure before/after because the published package omits specification/v0_9/json/server_to_client.json. No test or product gate is skipped or weakened.

## Remaining blockers — do not mark ready

**The package-patch guard is intentionally unchanged and rejects the new Zod patch.** Explicit authorization to register this exact patch in the existing allowlist is still needed. This draft does not disable, relax, reclassify or bypass that gate. The patch is not landable until that decision is resolved.

Independent canonical full-context security review and hosted checks are still required. Local validation is not independent review clearance. No ready-for-review request, force-push, merge or release is authorized by this draft. Existing aggregate source/proof and PR #186177 remain untouched.

prs.title: fix(gateway): match canonical NFC/NFD conversation list labels
prs.body:
# fix(gateway): match canonical NFC/NFD conversation list labels

## What Problem This Solves

`conversations.list` filters candidates by comparing the lowercased query against
`[entry.conversationRef, entry.target, entry.label]` without Unicode canonical normalization
(`src/gateway/conversation-list.ts`, after the existing `@`-prefix strip). A composed (NFC) query
therefore never matches a decomposed (NFD) stored label or target, and an NFD query never matches
an NFC stored label, even though the two strings are canonically equivalent and render alike.
The Unicode-carrying fields are `label` (configured/implicit conversation names such as IRC group
names) and `target` (normalized transport addresses).

## User Impact

Querying conversations for `München` now finds a conversation whose stored label or target is the
decomposed `Mu\u0308nchen` form, and the reverse query works for composed labels such as `#Zürich`.
Case-insensitivity and literal ASCII comparison are unchanged (`munchen` still does not match
`München`; no diacritic folding). Matching is comparison-side only: the returned
`conversationRef`, `target` and `label` keep their stored bytes and nothing is normalized for
storage or display.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follow the accepted canonical-normalization shape of this family: normalize both comparison
operands at the comparison site with `value.toLowerCase().normalize("NFC")`, after the existing
`@`-prefix semantics rather than before them, with no stored/displayed value rewrite and no new
helper or configuration.

The filter keeps its exact membership semantics: the `discoveredConversationRefs` bypass for the
current request's channel discovery, the eligibility pass and the limit applied after filtering
are unchanged. Only the canonical form of the two comparison operands changed.

## Evidence

Base `f0401d55f` (real Gateway dist built from that commit), candidate `f496539c` (this branch,
real Gateway dist built from this worktree). Both runs use the same isolated Gateway state and
config; the base run writes the registry rows, the candidate run reads the same rows.

Credential-free seed (no third-party account or live transport): IRC is an in-repo channel whose
directory is config-only. Config `channels.irc.allowFrom: ["Mu\u0308nchen"]` and
`channels.irc.groups: {"#Mu\u0308nchen": {}, "#Zürich": {}}`; the real RPC
`conversations.list {agentId, channel: "irc"}` registers identities into the conversation registry
(`registerConversationAddresses` → `session-accessor.sqlite-conversation.ts` conversation write),
and the query calls then omit `channel`, so they read the registry through `listConversations`
and exercise the filter instead of the channel-discovery bypass.

Real `conversations.list {agentId: "main"}` registry read (base-written rows, bytes preserved):

```
direct  target "münchen"    label null
group   target "#München"  label "#Mu\u0308nchen"   (23 4d 75 308 6e 63 68 65 6e)
group   target "#Zürich"    label "#Zürich"          (23 5a fc 72 69 63 68)
```

BEFORE (base `f0401d55f`), real RPC `conversations.list {agentId, query}`:

```
query "München" (NFC)   -> {"conversations": []}          # defect: NFD label/target missed
query "Mu\u0308nchen"   -> 2 rows (direct + "#Mu\u0308nchen")   # same-form control still matches
query "munchen"         -> {"conversations": []}          # ASCII control
```

AFTER (candidate `f496539c`), same state and RPC shape:

```
query "München" (NFC)   -> 2 rows: target "münchen" (NFD) and label "#Mu\u0308nchen" (NFD),
                           returned label bytes unchanged: 23 4d 75 308 6e 63 68 65 6e
query "Mu\u0308nchen"   -> same 2 rows
query "Zürich" (NFC)    -> 1 row: label "#Zürich", bytes 23 5a fc 72 69 63 68
query "munchen"         -> {"conversations": []}          # ASCII control unchanged
```

Focused regression (folded into the existing `src/gateway/conversation-list.test.ts` filter case,
which already mocks persisted routes):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/conversation-list.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 \
  -t "filters persisted routes before applying the result limit"
# BASE (production reverted, tests kept): 1 failed | 7 skipped
#   AssertionError: expected [ undefined, undefined ] to deeply equal [ 'München personal', … ]
#   wall 4m23s
# CANDIDATE: 1 passed | 7 skipped, wall 3m27s
```

The base/candidate rows in that case pair a decomposed stored label `Mu\u0308nchen personal` with
an NFC query and a composed stored label `#Zürich finance` with an NFD query, assert the returned
labels keep their original bytes (the decomposed label contains U+0308, the composed label U+00FC),
and assert the ASCII query `munchen` returns no rows.

Test-line ratchet:

```
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts
Test lines OK: 6244018; ceiling: 6320000; slack: 75982.
```

Boundaries: the `@`-prefix strip still runs before normalization; query calls with `channel` keep
the `discoveredConversationRefs` bypass (unchanged, and the shipped proof therefore uses the
registry path); `conversationRef` is still compared as a raw canonical id; no storage, protocol,
or display value changes.

Cleanup: isolated Gateway state/config under a temporary directory were removed after the runs and
the Gateway port was released; no leftover Gateway or test processes remain.

Not tested: live third-party channel transports (not needed for this comparison-side fix); the
full `conversation-list.test.ts` worker-read case is blocked on this host by the Node 24.13.1
embedded SQLite 3.51.2 WAL-safety gate (`OpenClaw requires SQLite 3.51.3+ …`), which is
environmental and unrelated to this change; the folded filter case and the shipped runs are green.

Precedent: #184374 #187024

Remove the unused wrapper and type while leaving the shared reader, worker, kernel, and writer-ordered publication intact.
