prs.title: docs(plugins): require live model discovery for bundled providers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The provider docs let a bundled provider ship with only its static model rows and a hard-coded thinking ladder. So new vendor models need an OpenClaw release, and each provider can copy thinking levels that the catalog already declares.

## User Impact

There is no runtime change. Provider authors and agents now read three things in the docs:
- A bundled provider with an OpenAI-compatible `/models` API must opt into live discovery.
- `discoveryMode: "strict"` does not enable discovery by itself.
- A thinking ladder built from the catalog efforts uses `resolveEffortThinkingProfile`, not a hard-coded level list.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`model-catalogs.md`:**
  - Live discovery is now required for bundled providers that have a `/models` API.
  - The strict-mode paragraph now says it changes only how results are reported. With a static or manifest-backed `buildProvider` and no `liveModelDiscovery` or custom `run`, the provider serves its static rows. A `buildProvider` that discovers, as NVIDIA and KiloCode use, also counts as live listing. Before, the page stated `strict` as the bundled requirement and called live discovery optional ("If your provider exposes…"), so an author could set `strict` and get no listing.
- **`runtime-hooks.md` and `provider-hooks.md`:**
  - With no hook, the ladder is the base levels plus any `xhigh` or `max` in catalog `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` or `thinkingLevelMap`. `supportedReasoningEfforts` alone never removes base levels; a `null` `thinkingLevelMap` entry does.
  - To expose exactly the advertised efforts, return `resolveEffortThinkingProfile(ctx.compat?.supportedReasoningEfforts)`, as OpenRouter, OpenCode and vLLM do.

## Evidence

- `pnpm lint:docs` reports no errors in the changed files. The one error it reports is in an ignored local `docs/internal/` file.
- `pnpm docs:check-links` finds 0 broken links. `oxfmt --check` passes.
- I read the behavior in the code:
  - `src/plugin-sdk/provider-entry.ts`: `discoveryMode: "strict"` without `liveModelDiscovery` wraps the static `run`.
  - `src/auto-reply/thinking.ts`: `appendCatalogAdvancedThinkingLevels`.

prs.title: fix: warn before browser reload discards file edits
prs.body: Fixes #187221 ## What Problem This Solves Reloading a browser tab while editing a file silently discards its unsaved text. File drafts already survive file and conversation navigation and block application-triggered reloads, but the browser's own reload and close actions bypass that application guard. ## User Impact After editing a file, an ordinary browser reload or tab close offers the platform's unsaved-work confirmation. Cancel leaves the exact draft available for continued editing, including drafts retained after leaving their editor. Saving or explicitly discarding the final draft removes the warning. Drafts remain memory-only: choosing to leave still discards unsaved edits and never writes them to the file automatically. ## Why This Change Was Made The existing retained-draft owner now registers a browser unload listener alongside its application reload guard. Both follow the same draft-map lifetime, so closing a preview does not remove protection and resolving one of several drafts does not release the others. This uses the existing listener abstraction and the pattern already used by queued session changes; file-save authority, conflict detection and expected-hash handling are unchanged. The regression extends the existing full-browser editor recovery suite. It uses visible editor controls and keyboard input before a real reload, rather than replacing the reload callback. The dedicated test-line allocation covers its measured 79-line net growth; the shared ceiling is unchanged. ## Evidence The unchanged base a83fd5dcf456df68e0889a1e40bc10d3a1359b70 failed both new native-unload cases after reaching editing and enabling Save: no beforeunload dialog was emitted. All four existing recovery cases passed. This baseline used bundled Control UI code in Chromium with synthetic Gateway responses; it demonstrates the browser boundary without claiming durable file-write proof. Candidate 4bd63c436ddbabd47a8cde0452ea7731a4c9dcf4 passed changed-file formatting/lint/i18n, 38 compiler graphs with the final affected graph refreshed, and 156 unique related UI/unit/browser cases. The six-case bundled browser file passed in 24.95 seconds (including its existing recovery cases); its native test invocation took 26.55 seconds. The new cases prove actual unload confirmation and cancellation, continued exact editing, retained drafts after conversation navigation, expectedHash on Save, Discard without a write, and a clean reload once the draft settles. Canonical automated code review is clean. The inspected before/after captures and 7.48-second recording below use the same synthetic content and 1280×900 viewport. Native browser receipts record two canceled reloads and a canceled tab close on the fixed build, then a clean reload with zero dialogs after Save. Headless page captures exclude browser chrome; the clearly marked evidence cues describe those actual native events while the images and video show the surrounding editor state. These captures do not claim a real server write or coverage of other browser engines. Independent engineering review, including the visual evidence, is clean. The exact-head hosted CI gate passed. An additional live join used this exact candidate UI with an existing compatible Gateway and its unchanged administrator identity. A normal model request created a fresh note, then actual Files/Edit input triggered the native reload confirmation. Cancel preserved the exact draft; continued editing produced one successful compare-and-swap Save with the original file hash and workspace identity. A clean reload reread all 333 saved bytes, exactly matching both the submitted text and the Gateway’s returned hash. This live join used real Gateway/file I/O without restarting or reconfiguring that Gateway. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Baseline reload loses the typed paragraph with no dialog; saved text remains\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3a6fe78-9df4-43b2-bb91-281685a468b0) | ![After canceling the native reload confirmation, the exact unsaved paragraph remains editable\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a049aca2-a951-4a10-a073-3f8953dda188) | ### Actual editor interaction, native dialog cancellation and clean reload after Save https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ca2487c-8081-4a14-8072-4dad0420be8d ### Visual verification - Baseline: a83fd5dcf456df68e0889a1e40bc10d3a1359b70 - Exact head: `4bd63c436ddbabd47a8cde0452ea7731a4c9dcf4` - Scenario: Type into the real file editor, reload and cancel the native confirmation, continue editing, navigate away, cancel reload and tab close, then Save and reload cleanly\. - Runtime/build: Bundled Control UI in Chromium; exact candidate tree b458f9970dc9b66dd9a7e9a92110ce854aa36a0d\. Synthetic Gateway I/O; original baseline and candidate draft\-owner blobs recorded by native run\. - Baseline reload: 0 dialogs; unsaved paragraph lost - Fixed native confirmations: 2 reloads and 1 tab close prompted; all canceled - Final Save: Original expectedHash preserved; clean reload emitted 0 dialogs - Real keyboard activation and native Chromium Page\.reload; no mocked unload callback - Exact draft retained after cancellation and conversation navigation; Save and Discard covered in the six\-case browser file - Headless page captures cannot render browser chrome; evidence cues report separately recorded native beforeunload events and cancellation - Matched 1280×900 viewport, synthetic content, route, theme and framing; production owner pinned before and after

prs.title: fix(agents): Claude CLI session usage and cost count only the last model call
prs.body:
Related: #148603

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session token counters, reply usage, cron run records and OpenAI-compatible run usage undercount Claude CLI turns, because they report only the last model call (with Claude Code's stream-start output count) instead of the whole turn.

## User Impact

User impact: `sessions.list` / `/status` token counts and estimated cost, reply usage footers, cron run usage and `/v1/chat/completions` usage for `claude-cli` turns now match the turn total that Claude Code reports, the same way embedded runs already do. Context sizing is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#148682 fixed the transcript writers but left live `agentMeta.usage` on the last call (listed under "Not in scope"). The Claude stream parser already keeps the terminal turn total in `diagnosticUsage`. `buildCliRunResult` now uses it as the run's billing `usage`, marked `contextUsage: { state: "unavailable" }` like the embedded runner's aggregate (`buildCompletedAgentUsageMeta`), and keeps `lastCallUsage` as the latest call for context accounting. Only the Claude stream-json path sets `diagnosticUsage`, so other CLI backends are unchanged.

`docs/gateway/opentelemetry/model-calls-and-metrics.md` said reply accounting keeps the last assistant message; it now describes whole-turn billing usage and last-call context sizing separately.

Decision for maintainers: #120100 kept live `usage` on the last call when it added `diagnosticUsage`, as a scope choice ("Reply/session accounting and context-window behavior remain unchanged"), and #148682 deferred the switch. This PR proposes making Claude CLI live `usage` the whole-turn billing total, matching embedded runs and `docs/cli/infer.md` ("`usage` keeps the runtime's aggregate billing usage ... `lastCallUsage` describes only the last physical API call").

Not covered here, so this PR does not close #148603: the per-call output count from the final `message_delta` for each assistant message (the issue's stream-start output observation) still comes from the assistant snapshot.

Known limit, unchanged by this PR: a turn with several interim `result` records (background-task continuations or injected input on the warm transport) still reports only the last segment's total. It can undercount but never double-counts.

## Evidence

- Regression in `src/agents/cli-runner.turn-usage.test.ts` ("reports and persists the terminal Claude turn usage for a multi-call turn") runs `runPreparedCliAgent` and the real `updateSessionStoreAfterAgentRun` on a temporary store. On base 5ff57b8e742 it fails: `agentMeta.usage` is `{ input: 2, output: 1, cacheRead: 27376 }` instead of the turn total `{ input: 6, output: 77, cacheRead: 54631 }`, and the session row stores inputTokens 2 / outputTokens 1. With the fix it passes; the row stores 6 / 77 and `totalTokens` stays at the last call's prompt (27,378).
- `cli-runner.context-engine.test.ts` expectation updated from the last call to the turn total.
- Consumer suites: 12 files / 343 tests (cli-runner spawn, context-engine, reliability, turn-usage, trajectory, cli-run-settlement, command/attempt-execution.cli, command/session-store, isolated-completion(+usage), agent-command ingress diagnostics, auto-reply memory usage diagnostics). `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxfmt, oxlint, `git diff --check` pass.
- Local review: Codex autoreview (`--mode branch`, base 5ff57b8e742, P2): scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.85)". A separate full-repo read-only review found no blocking issues.
- Real Gateway proof (isolated state, loopback, Claude Code 2.1.310, `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` on the claude-cli runtime): one tool turn (ToolSearch, then read, then the answer) through `/v1/chat/completions`.
  - Before (5ff57b8e742), 4 model calls: Claude `result.usage` in 6 / out 418 / cacheRead 29,878, but the endpoint reported `completion_tokens: 6` and the session row `inputTokens: 2`, `outputTokens: 6`.
  - After (this branch), 3 model calls: Claude `result.usage` in 6 / out 233 / cacheRead 28,822; the endpoint reported `completion_tokens: 233`, `prompt_tokens: 28,828`, and the session row `inputTokens: 6`, `outputTokens: 233`.

- Rebased onto main 07bd3eff3be after #187120 and #187144 fixed repo-wide baseline-ratchet and lint failures; the patch is unchanged. Reran turn-usage, context-engine, attempt-execution.cli, session-store (113 tests) and tsgo:core on the rebased head: pass.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): one failed Claude CLI launch breaks every later turn in the conversation
prs.body:
Closes #187115

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after one failed Claude CLI launch (for example a missing binary during an auto-update or an aborted start), every later message in that conversation fails with the same stale error until the Gateway restarts or the user runs `/new`.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed launch only fails its own turn; the next message starts a fresh Claude process. When the launcher cannot confirm that a started child was cleaned up, replacement stays blocked exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The warm session handle is registered before the child exists. On launch failure, `waitForExit()` awaited the rejected startup and rethrew the launch error (since #171016), so the live-session registry kept a rejected cleanup join for the owner key and every later turn rethrew it. The turn already reports its own launch error. `waitForExit()` now resolves for a plain launch rejection, which by the owned stdio launcher's contract means no child remains, and still rejects with `OwnedStdioCleanupError` when startup cleanup could not be confirmed, keeping the #139657 rule that uncertain cleanup blocks replacement. As a side effect the failed session's `record.cleanup` now runs instead of leaking.

`OwnedStdioCleanupError` is now exported next to `createOwnedStdioProcess` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime`, so plugins can recognize the rejection the SDK docs already describe; docs updated in `sdk-overview/infrastructure.md` and `sdk-subpaths.md`.

## Evidence

- `extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime.test.ts`:
  - "replaces a session whose launch failed without a child": turn 1 launches a missing binary, turn 2 on the same live session runs the protocol fixture. Red on base 5ff57b8e742 (turn 2 fails with turn 1's `ENOENT ... posix_spawn '.../missing-claude'`), green with the fix; live-session cleanup runs once.
  - "keeps a launch with unconfirmed cleanup blocking replacement": a launch rejecting with `OwnedStdioCleanupError` still rejects the handle's `waitForExit()` (fails if the catch is simplified to always resolve). The registry half (rejected join retained, `record.cleanup` skipped) is covered by the existing "retains natural cleanup until replacement is safe" registry test.
- Suites: anthropic cli-runtime (66), yield, task-ownership, transport close, cli-process; `cli-live-session-registry.test.ts`; `src/process/owned-stdio.test.ts`. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxfmt, oxlint (max-lines), `git diff --check`, `check:test-mock-exports`, `sync-plugin-sdk-exports --check` pass.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff --base 5ff57b8e742 --head <first version of this commit>`: "No Plugin SDK API changes" (ack digest ff7b090f); the later amend touched only tests and docs.
- Local review: Codex autoreview (`--mode branch`, base 5ff57b8e742, P2) on the final commit: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.85)". A separate full-repo read-only review asked for the unconfirmed-cleanup test and the sdk-subpaths line, both added.
- Field report: #174204 (closed for its credential-transport cause) shows `cli live session cleanup failed: Error: secret delivery aborted` followed by repeated identical turn failures.
- Real Gateway proof (isolated state, loopback, default warm `claude-stdio` live session, Claude Code 2.1.310, `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`): turn 1 launches a `claude` on PATH whose interpreter is missing (spawn ENOENT); before turn 2 in the same session, `claude` becomes a symlink to the real binary, with no config change or restart.
  - Before (5ff57b8e742): `cli live session cleanup failed: Error: spawn …/bin/claude ENOENT`; turn 2 fails in 74 ms with the same `spawn …/bin/claude ENOENT` and starts no Claude process; shutdown reports `completed … with warnings: cli-live-sessions`.
  - After (this branch): turn 1 reports the same ENOENT; turn 2 logs `cli live session start`, `cli turn … durationMs=2411`, replies `pong`; shutdown completes cleanly.

- Rebased onto main 07bd3eff3be after #187120 and #187144 fixed repo-wide baseline-ratchet and lint failures; the patch is unchanged. Reran anthropic cli-runtime, transport close, cli-process, cli-live-session-registry, owned-stdio (90 tests) and tsgo:extensions on the rebased head: pass.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: existing claude-cli conversations lose their native Claude session (reset with `reason=mcp`) on the first turn after upgrading past #186776, and again whenever `tools.toolSearch` is toggled.

## User Impact

User impact: stored Claude conversations keep resuming after the upgrade and across tool-search toggles, keeping Claude's native tool history, compaction state and prompt cache. A toggle is handled as prompt drift, as #186776 intended. No config or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

#186776 sets `alwaysLoad: false` on the OpenClaw loopback MCP server when tools are deferred behind ToolSearch. The resume hash canonicalized only the loopback URL, so this upfront-loading hint changed `mcpResumeHash`, and `resolveCliSessionReuse` checks that hash before prompt/tool drift. The hint does not change which tools exist, and discovery is already part of the prompt hash (reuse-with-drift) and the warm-process fingerprint (so a warm child still restarts on a toggle). The resume canonicalization now pins the loopback server's `alwaysLoad` to `true`, which keeps the hash byte-identical to existing bindings; deleting the key instead would cause one more reset. The raw `mcpConfigHash` and the config sent to Claude still carry the real value.

The upgrade regression in `prepare.existing-session.test.ts` missed this because it injected a loopback-config helper that ignores `deferTools`; it now uses the real builder.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.existing-session.test.ts`, red on base 5ff57b8e742 and green with the fix:
  - default discovery upgrade case: `invalidatedReason: "mcp"` on base (expected the pre-existing `"prompt-tools"` path for the old-format binding).
  - new case: a binding written by an eager turn (matching `promptToolNamesHash`, `alwaysLoad: true` hash) then a turn with `tools.toolSearch: true` -> base `{ mode: "invalidate", invalidatedReason: "mcp" }`, fix `{ mode: "reuse-with-drift", drift: { reasons: ["system-prompt"] } }`. This goes through the real `withCliToolSearch` -> `createMcpLoopbackServerConfig` -> bundle hash -> `resolveCliSessionReuse` path.
- Related suites: prepare.existing-session, bundle-mcp (+codex, gemini, user-config, discovery-lifecycle), prepare, prepare.command-continuity, prepare.completion-tools, cli-session, command/attempt-execution.cli-mcp, cli-runner.reliability pass. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, oxfmt, oxlint, `git diff --check` pass.
- Local review: Codex autoreview (`--mode branch`, base 5ff57b8e742, P2) on the final commit: scoped-clean, "patch is correct (0.84)". A separate full-repo read-only review asked for the production-path resume case above, now added.
- Real Gateway proof (isolated state, loopback, Claude Code 2.1.310, `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` on the claude-cli runtime, native login): turn 1 in conversation X with `tools.toolSearch: false` ("Remember the word PELICAN"), then unset `tools.toolSearch` (default discovery on), restart the Gateway on the same state, turn 2 in X ("What word did I ask you to remember?"); turn 2 launched with `--tools ToolSearch` and Claude used ToolSearch, then `mcp__openclaw__read`.
  - Before (5ff57b8e742): `cli session reset: provider=claude-cli reason=mcp`; Claude started a new `--session-id` (24229e50… vs turn 1's 447700e3…) and recovered the word only through the `sessions_history` tool.
  - After (this branch): no reset; Claude ran with `--resume 299f5d68…` (turn 1's native session, matching `result.session_id`) and answered from native history.
- Follow-up candidate, not in this PR: `createTestMcpLoopbackServerConfig` is still used by prepare.test.ts / prepare.command-continuity.test.ts / prepare-mcp.test-support.ts and ignores `deferTools`.

- Rebased onto main 07bd3eff3be after #187120 and #187144 fixed repo-wide baseline-ratchet and lint failures; the patch is unchanged. Reran prepare.existing-session, bundle-mcp, cli-session, prepare.command-continuity (61 tests) and tsgo:core on the rebased head: pass.

prs.title: fix(cli): close the resume pre-TUI client on an accepted interrupt
prs.body:
Fixes #187154

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw resume` opens a private Gateway client before the TUI owns cancellation. When the CLI accepts SIGINT/SIGTERM during that pre-TUI phase — initial connect, recent-session lookup, or handoff resolution — the command prints its cleanup notice, the transport stays open, and the awaits keep pending, so the process outlives the accepted interruption.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resume-cli.runtime.ts` created and stopped its pre-TUI client without registering anything the CLI signal barrier could interrupt. Each pre-TUI client is now tracked by a `registerSignalExitGate(finished, interrupt)`:

- `interrupt` calls `client.stop()`, which closes the transport and rejects pending `listSessions` / `resolveSession` awaits.
- `finished` resolves when that branch's `finally` has stopped the client, so the barrier finishes its drain after the transport is closed.
- The gate is released in the same `finally`, so a normal resolution or a connection error does not leave a registered gate behind.

## User Impact

Ctrl-C during `openclaw resume` now closes the Gateway transport instead of leaving a connection open behind the signal barrier; the accepted interruption's cleanup completes and the command exits with the signal's code.

## Evidence

Head `3609ea629`, Node 26.12.1, the existing resume harness with the mocked `GatewayChatClient`.

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/cli/resume-cli.test.ts \
    -t "closes the pre-TUI client" --maxWorkers=1
# with the fix:
✓ closes the pre-TUI client when the command is interrupted
# reverting src/cli/resume-cli.runtime.ts to upstream/main:
× closes the pre-TUI client when the command is interrupted
  AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called at least once   # client.stop never called

$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/cli/resume-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Tests  14 passed | 3 skipped (17)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <2 touched files>     0 warnings, 0 errors
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <2 touched files>
All matched files use the correct format.
```

The regression holds `resolveSession` pending, drains the signal barrier with `waitForSignalExitBarriers("SIGINT")`, and asserts the interrupted command stopped the client and settled with an error. The three skipped cases are the file's existing real-Gateway boundary block, which needs a live Gateway.

Not covered here: the reporter's PTY run against a loopback protocol peer that withholds the connect acknowledgement or `sessions.list`. That scenario exercises the same gate, but a connect still in flight has no client handle yet, so its cancellation depends on `GatewayChatClient.connect` itself; this change starts once the client exists.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git grep` across `resume-cli.runtime.ts` and the CLI signal barrier to find the missing cancellation seam, then added the per-client signal gate and the regression. The implementer understands the code: the barrier interrupts registered gates, so each pre-TUI client registers one and releases it once stopped.

prs.title: fix: doctor memory merge can empty MEMORY.md when the merge write fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor`'s legacy root memory merge can leave `MEMORY.md` empty or torn when the merge write fails (crash, Ctrl-C, ENOSPC/EPERM mid-write), silently destroying the agent's durable memory.

The merge archived only the *legacy* `memory.md` before overwriting the canonical `MEMORY.md` with a truncate-in-place `writeFile` — the pre-merge canonical bytes existed nowhere else. The truncated file is also what the doctor note reports as a completed repair when the error is caught upstream, so the loss is silent.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed or interrupted doctor memory merge now leaves the live `MEMORY.md` byte-for-byte intact, and the pre-merge canonical content is preserved as `MEMORY.md.pre-merge` beside the existing legacy archive for recovery. The merge success note reports the new backup path.

The publication matches the existing memory writer (`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-markdown.ts`): `replaceFileAtomic` with `preserveExistingMode`, the workspace's actual directory mode passed back as `dirMode` (publication can no longer widen a private `0700` workspace to `0755`), the permission-error copy fallback left disabled (its unlink-then-recreate path would reintroduce the tear), durable temp+fsync+rename semantics, and the workspace directory resolved through `realpath` before publication so configured workspace aliases keep working (the atomic writer rejects symlinked parents by design; the alias is resolved for publication only, and the final-file symlink rejection is unaffected because earlier bounded reads already verified the canonical file as a regular file).

## Why This Change Was Made

The same function already treats atomicity as a requirement one step earlier (the legacy archive move is an atomic rename, and the archive is re-read "after the atomic move"), but the canonical overwrite — the one mutation with no recovery copy — bypassed that. The fix reuses the existing atomic-replace owner (`@openclaw/fs-safe/atomic`) and the existing timestamped repair archive directory, rather than adding new state or helpers.

## Evidence

**Shipped CLI, successful merge through a workspace directory alias** (`openclaw doctor --fix`, workspace configured as a junction alias to a case-sensitive directory):

```
│  Workspace memory root merged:
│  - current: ...\oc-proof2\ws-alias\MEMORY.md
│  - backup:  ...\ws-alias\.openclaw-repair\root-memory\2026-10-27T08-13-09-701Z\memory.md
│  - pre-merge backup: ...\ws-alias\.openclaw-repair\root-memory\2026-10-27T08-13-09-701Z\MEMORY.md.pre-merge
│  - merged legacy content from: ...\ws-alias\memory.md
│  - removed legacy file: ...\ws-alias\memory.md
```

Verified through the junction's real target afterwards: `MEMORY.md` holds the merged content in the exact byte format `main` produces, the repair directory holds both `memory.md` and `MEMORY.md.pre-merge`, and `memory.md` is gone from the live path.

**Shipped CLI, failed publication** (`MEMORY.md` marked read-only, so the publication rename fails with `EPERM`):

```
│  Workspace memory repair could not be completed: EPERM: operation not
│  permitted, rename '...\ws-ro\MEMORY.md.42020.c558acb6-....tmp' -> '...\ws-ro\MEMORY.md'
=== after the run ===
canonical bytes: "# Canonical\n"          (intact, still read-only)
backups: memory.md ("# Legacy\n"), MEMORY.md.pre-merge ("# Canonical\n")
workspace listing: no temp leftovers
```

**Completed upgrade from latest stable** (stable `2026.10.7` via `pnpm dlx`, then this build, both through the shipped Doctor CLI on the same isolated case-sensitive workspace + state dir):

1. `openclaw@2026.10.7 doctor --fix` on the split workspace: merges with its own note format and no canonical backup (exit 0).
2. This build's `openclaw doctor --fix` on the same state dir: completes the shared-state-DB migration custody and finishes with "Doctor complete" (exit 0, zero split/shadow findings).
3. Post-upgrade check: the stable-merged `MEMORY.md` is preserved byte-for-byte, no re-merge or rewrite occurred, and the workspace holds only the merged file.

Data-model compatibility: the merge output format is byte-identical across stable `2026.10.7`, `main`, and this head — existing data loads and works unchanged, and `openclaw memory status` on a merged workspace reports the memory file with normal dreaming path resolution.

**Regression tests** (`src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts`; red on `main`, green on this head; verified executing locally on a case-sensitive NTFS scratch dir since the canonical/legacy pair requires one):

- `preserves canonical memory when publication fails with ENOSPC` / `with EPERM`: a failed publication leaves the live file intact, no fallback recreates it, the pre-merge backup holds the original bytes. The fixture path is canonicalized (`realpath`) like the shared temp-dir helpers, so the rename interception matches the resolved publication destination on hosts whose tmpdir sits behind a symlink (macOS).
- `preserves the workspace mode across a successful merge`: a `0700` workspace stays `0700` (POSIX-checked in CI; Windows chmod is a no-op).
- `merges through a symlinked workspace directory alias`: a configured alias is followed for publication and the merged file lands in the same canonical file (POSIX red on head, green with the fix, via CI; on Windows the junction variant executes green — the fs-safe parent rejection it fixes is POSIX-only, so Windows cannot reproduce the red).

Checks per the review acceptance list: `pnpm vitest run src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts src/commands/doctor-memory-recall.test.ts` — 19/19 pass; oxlint clean on both touched files; `git diff --check` clean; `pnpm tsgo:prod` all lanes pass.

<details>
<summary>Test environment notes and gaps</summary>

The canonical/legacy pair (`MEMORY.md` + `memory.md`) can only coexist on a case-sensitive filesystem, so this repair suite no-ops on case-insensitive hosts (existing tests in this file already guard with `if (!(await seedMemory())) return;`). Local verification used a per-directory case-sensitive NTFS scratch dir (NTFS `setCaseSensitiveInfo`); CI runs the suite on Linux, where the alias test also reproduces the POSIX red/green for the parent-rejection fix.

Upgrade note: stable `2026.10.8` was published today and is correctly refused by this repo's pnpm `minimumReleaseAge` supply-chain policy, so the upgrade run uses `2026.10.7`, the newest installable stable.

Not covered: an injected publication failure during a full interactive `openclaw doctor` run (the CLI failure above uses a read-only canonical file, a real OS-level denial through the shipped CLI). The repository-wide lint shard crashes on this Windows box from memory pressure; the changed files are oxlint-clean directly and CI runs the full lint on the exact head.
</details>

---

**Note on this re-submission:** the previous PR (#184858) was closed automatically on 2026-10-28 when a fork of this repository on my account was deleted by an unrelated local cleanup. The commits and the diff are unchanged — the head commit is the exact same `4f35bf1` that addressed all three items from the review of `053e647` (fixture path canonicalization included). Please treat this as the continuation of #184858 rather than a new proposal; if you would prefer to keep the original thread, let me know and I will close this one instead.

Updates `github.com/openclaw/peekaboo` from 4.9.5 to 4.9.7
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/openclaw/peekaboo's releases.

v4.9.7

4.9.7 - 2026-10-23

Highlights: Report window close through the daemon as closed when an app keeps the closed window alive; let see observe Chrome windows whose titles carry the app name or are elided; close apps that re-exec themselves with --foreground; and keep the Mac chat, menu bar and Inspector accurate.

  • Report window close through the daemon or Bridge as closed when the app keeps the closed NSWindow alive, instead of exiting 1 with an indeterminate postcondition: the Bridge readback now applies the same exact-window Accessibility presence check as the in-process path. Thanks @​goutamadwant! #1131, fixes #1129.
  • Let peekaboo see observe Chrome and other apps whose Accessibility window title appends the application name or whose WindowServer title is middle-elided, instead of failing with "inconsistent response evidence: window-context window title". Thanks @​L1uYun! #1130.
  • Close windows of apps that re-exec themselves with window close --foreground, whose frontmost PID AppKit reports as -1. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1124.
  • Classify Dock separators and the Trash from their Accessibility subroles, so peekaboo dock list hides separators unless --include-all is passed, reports included separators as separator instead of blank unknown items, and identifies a localized Trash (such as "Papierkorb") as trash. #1120.
  • Use the Mac app's saved Vision model for image analysis even when its provider does not report vision support (OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible, LM Studio and many Ollama models), surfacing the provider's error instead of silently switching models. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1127.
  • Keep the Mac chat's streaming answer together when you queue a follow-up, and keep Retry on the prompt that failed. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1126.
  • Show a failed Mac agent tool as failed, not completed, in the menu bar, while cancelled tools stay cancelled. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1134.
  • Highlight the Inspector control in the front window under the pointer, including floating panels and popup items past their window, instead of the smallest control anywhere on screen; windows of untracked apps such as the Dock now stop the hover from reaching what they cover. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1133.
  • Place Inspector highlight boxes on the correct display when a display does not start at the primary display's origin. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1132.
  • Restore source builds after the pinned MCP Swift SDK commit became unreachable upstream when its pull request branch was rebased. #1135.
  • Remove the unused public DialogError.inputSuppressedUnderTests case from PeekabooAutomationKit along with the dead test-only dialog typing hook that threw it; release builds could never throw it, so only SwiftPM consumers that switch over every DialogError case need to drop that branch. #1123.

Local patch adaptation uses qualified stable source 48c0b99eeab904925c456b5e308407653cd36f76 (derived from preserved security aggregate f0a0c53aa23b80bd68267fc48cfdda020db77c26), not represented as an OpenClaw upstream backport.

The latter includes slash normalization and generated-code escaping despite its interceptor-warning title.

**Draft only — not ready for review.** Exact-head independent canonical review, hosted checks, native Windows/browser execution and wider train qualification remain required before any readiness decision. No ready-for-review, merge, tag or release is authorized.

prs.title: feat(codex): host cloud inference on enrolled workers
prs.body:
Related: #154388

## What Problem This Solves

Cloud placements need to run Codex inference with the worker’s authentication and workspace rather than launching the model process on the Gateway.

## User Impact

Opt-in **Full node placements** can run the exact enrolled app-server, execute native tools there, and continue conversations while the existing workspace remains available. Defaults are unchanged; unsupported carriers fail closed rather than falling back locally.

Operators provision **one private worker-only bundle** at the configured state directory’s `worker-provisioning/codex`: `config.toml` and its single Node `.mjs` auth helper. Configuration/helper bytes determine the command identity—no separate environment selectors or manually supplied versions. Use private permissions, allow the exact versioned command through the existing node policy, publish while stopped, then restart/reprovision workers after changes. This replaces the three inputs proposed earlier in this unshipped PR; it adds no configuration field or budget exception.

Gateway auth profiles and local GitHub credentials are not forwarded. Selected Platform/subscription account constraints remain enforced; competing profile or supervision ownership is rejected. Dedicated ephemeral non-container nodes retain their own managed-identity transport and platform trust. Shared/container workers do not inherit them. Hosted native GitHub handoff stays disabled; host-owned tools retain managed GitHub execution.

**Limits:** Linux/keyless validation uses the ordinary first-party model route with synthetic external responses—not commercial model reasoning, cloud bootstrap/platform-identity attestation, P5 custom-provider eligibility, or Windows/macOS private-config qualification. No retained-disk, worker-loss recovery, replacement-workspace guarantee or immediate pruning deadline is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Private enrollment, production client selection, duplex transport and cleanup use existing placement, invocation and workspace owners. Resource readiness gates effects, not initial tool declaration. The bounded byte framer has real native consumers; caller-owned cleanup distinguishes transport closure from observed native exit.

One Codex provisioning owner validates the private bundle, parses its helper and derives the same identity for enrollment and registration. Lease staging preserves byte-equality checks; runtime verifies both enrolled content and the **captured admitted command**, so replacing content and its version cannot reuse an old admission. No alternate environment-input path remains.

The existing retained HOME also owns native metadata under `.openclaw-worker`. Watchdog custody may outlive teardown; no competing retention owner is introduced. The intentional plugin configuration surface grows by one entry (4889 → 4890) for explicit inference locality.

## Evidence

**Current private-bundle candidate, reconciled with pinned main `26cc81a8`:** only the two generated configuration artifacts changed from accepted `e19a2c90`; all 80 non-generated authored blobs/modes are identical. Inherited role/profile dispatch, workspace manifest/recovery and shutdown ownership changes were inspected. Current-base Bun composition and types were renewed; Node and focused unit results below are explicitly reused prior-base evidence, not reruns.

| Proof | Result and boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Reused Node composition (`8889b596` base) | **54.022s**, Vitest 103.84s; real paired Full node, ordinary catalog/implicit Codex, authenticated catalog HTTP from `worker:16`, exact versioned app-server, native command/reconciliation, same-thread second turn, cancellation and joined cleanup. |
| Current-base pinned Bun composition | **32.964s**, Vitest 77.82s; actual Bun Vitest/Gateway/catalog HTTP `worker:15`, with the same native and authority assertions. Pinned bytes/revision verified before and inside isolation. |
| Reused bundle regressions and consumers | Eight enrollment regressions red before cutover; **99 focused cases** passed across seven files. The additional captured-command regression was separately red, then its native lifecycle case passed after repair. Counts overlap, not 100 distinct cases. |
| Current static/configuration checks | Production/test/E2E types, owner-generated config check and diff check passed. Current Bun proof rebuilt the runtime. Unchanged authored code reuses its lint/format proof. |

The current Bun run exited 0 and its container was independently confirmed absent; the reused Node run also exited 0 with confirmed cleanup. Inference accepts only the distinct worker synthetic credential, never the Gateway decoy. Forbidden and pending-revocation effects stayed zero. Helper/native extinction was **113/1164ms prior-base Node**, **89/1146ms current Bun**, before the unchanged five-second auth expiry and before node shutdown. Pending writable-result reassignment is **refused**, not claimed successful. Permission narrowing saves the mode, stops the captured carrier and reports its Full-only replacement cannot apply it.

**Both budgets now pass:** environment names **457/457** after complete input-owner cutover; test lines **6,306,309/6,310,000**, slack 3,691, using the exact ceiling already landed on main in #186785. No PR-authored ceiling, baseline exception, ignore, suppression or unrelated deletion was added.

**Review/CI:** fresh independent autoreview (P0–P2) of the complete bundle delta against `4a3935ef` returned scoped-clean; previous scoped implementation/repair reviews remain applicable. This generated-only reconciliation reuses those reviews for byte-identical authored code; it is not a new substantive repair. Review is static and did not execute project code. The [hosted needs-human/security hold](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186646#issuecomment-6465061095) is not cleared or overridden. Last fully inspected published-head CI ([40670818783](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40670818783), `5a3b87e1`) ended **87 passed / 5 failed / 24 skipped**. Published head `f75b79e81971c68c1217eff340cab8d898c24fc1` still needs new-head hosted CI and review disposition.

**Historical native compatibility is bounded evidence, not a blanket continuity claim.** Actual released 0.160.0 → candidate 0.164.0 proof passed in 126.132s on the earlier `b0966db1` composition, through genuine plugin-code transition and same-state Doctor. Stored fingerprints and the exact predecessor log identify existing `runtime identity changed` rotation; the same OpenClaw session/history continues, the original rollout/tool item remains byte-identical afterward, and the new rollout contains continued conversation. Same physical native UUID, every hidden native-state item, full updater/package installation and byte-identical config are not claimed. The public native catalog reader’s managed-predecessor refusal remains recorded.

A later unchanged one-off failed **before candidate consumption**: released-native execution and visible reply succeeded, but the post-shutdown binding namespace was empty. Bounded investigation of the exact released writer found an intentional successful-but-unbound path when capability support is unknown, with short-lived cleared-placeholder expiry, plus a separate coverage-error clear path. **Which branch occurred is unconfirmed** because the decision trace was not retained. No key/namespace mismatch or unconditional Gateway-stop clear was established. This is an investigated local failure, not a proven candidate migration regression or repaired flake. No retry-for-green, seed, extra delay, weaker oracle or retention change was used; the earlier pass stays prior-base evidence.

<details>
<summary>Source bindings, prerequisites and retained failure history</summary>

- **Scope:** 82 P8 files, +4799/-219 against `26cc81a8`. The accepted 16-file private-bundle repair is preserved intact. This history-preserving main merge changed only two owner-generated artifacts relative to `e19a2c90`; all 80 non-generated authored blobs/modes were preserved. No excluded stack or P5 feature commits were imported.
- **External verification prerequisites:** [P5 #186614](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186614), historical published head `f028a758` used to bind these proofs, owns archive fix `f6a08fc6` and pinned-Bun runner work `e49494a2`. Their exact overlays were used only for proof and restored. All nine runner paths and both budget files match pinned main. P5 is not a feature dependency for this first-party slice.
- **Runtime bindings:** Bun pin `openclaw-v1.4.4-20261026-191755ec11-webkit-b82bc917e9`, revision `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`. Reused Node snapshot `3d1919311913886e9eac1756c7054134ba6626417daca86de91d8adb6c9447fa`; current-base Bun snapshot `06656972383fe2e3427493fc70be01968fbc02e0380721a516c6d840d7d50110`. These are source-bound local proofs, not hosted CI.
- **Catalog boundary:** only two named official catalog GETs use authenticated loopback simulation through the real worker. Parsing/auth/implicit runtime selection remain real; no base-URL shortcut, availability injection, forced harness or POST inference override. Optional metadata/utility work is opted out; the exact optional plugin feed is deliberately unavailable, not fabricated as trusted. Other remote requests remain rejected. External DNS/TLS/dispatcher behavior and historical CI HTTP status remain unqualified. Bundle staging here is synthetic operator provisioning, not cloud bootstrap.
- **Reused proof:** 116 affected main-defaults/Doctor/apply-patch/database cases passed before bundle repair; earlier 53 catalog/startup/prefix/projection cases and 401/403/transport-failure controls remain scoped prior evidence. Other overlapping runs include 213 cases across 18 files, 108 enrollment/bootstrap, 47 custody, 32 repairs, 96 auth/cleanup consumers, 73 Codex and 17 native lifecycle. SDK comparison at `3e31de22` found 172 reachable-type changes, no entrypoint additions/removals, removed exports or direct-signature changes; this bundle repair adds no SDK subpath.
- **Actual repairs:** premature registration-time live config access, borrowed-probe ownership, async-input queue exhaustion, omitted HOME/native metadata placement, and stale-command content replacement were reproduced and repaired at their owners. No capacity/timeout/permission relaxation was used.
- **Retained failures/non-outcomes:** offline archive/HOME setup; source acknowledgment, origin/profile, alias/auth and transcript-page-limit errors; restart/container-inspection failures; unclassified pairing and released-baseline missing-binding failures. The original exact-native-UUID assertion was a corrected proof premise, not a production-policy fix. Deletion/aborted-manifest, CODEX_HOME, queued-result, pending-move and helper-only-exit assumptions were corrected against existing owners. A closed-port readiness probe received the host egress proxy’s 502 on Node/Bun; independent closed-listener proof matched, while the unchanged case passed network-none. No proxy/test workaround was added.
- **Older CI:** `8333de7a` ended 84 passed / 10 failed / 24 skipped. Registration/probe/input defects have local repairs; unchanged Node/Doctor expectations, reproduced unchanged Deepgram deadline, catalog-availability history and aggregate failures remain recorded. No CI rerun, duplicate hosted review or policy override was requested.

</details>

## Contributor credit

Adapted from the selected worker/native-runtime portions of Galin Iliev (@galiniliev)'s commits `fa6b7bc1fb5db71d8a1ef2e0883c01971608ee4e` and `d0cce88f317a4a29996a85686304246ea2701428`, at his request.

prs.title: fix(state): re-assert read admission before consuming a completed read
prs.body:
Closes #184738

## What Problem This Solves

A state read can hand its value back after the database admission that authorized it was revoked, so a caller acts on a reply from a scope that is no longer admitted.

- Problem: `consume()` re-checks only the caller signal once a read settles, so an admission revoked while the read is in flight still produces a successful reply.
- Solution: re-assert the operation authority in `consume()` (`authority.assertCurrent()`) whenever this operation is not draining, so revoked delivery authority surfaces as an error instead of a reply.
- What changed: one guard plus assertion in `src/state/openclaw-state-read-operation.ts`, and one regression test folded into the existing `src/state/openclaw-state-db-readonly.worker-lifecycle.test.ts` suite.
- What did NOT change: the read transport, snapshot and cleanup ownership, caller-signal handling, or the accepted-reader settlement contract from #175443.

## Why This Change Was Made

#175443 replaced `consumeReadOutcome`, which re-asserted admission, with a version that checks only the caller signal; it also added lifecycle coverage proving that an already-selected query still settles while a failed transport stop is retried. Those two facts constrain the repair: a blanket re-assert rejects supported drainage, because `resource.close()` aborts the internal controller before joining transport retirement.

`authority.assertCurrent()` is the canonical check (signal, maintenance scope admission, captured database admission, open-allowed), so no new mechanism is introduced. It now runs only while this operation still owns its scope; `close()` aborts the controller as its first statement, which makes "draining" exactly the condition that must stay exempt.

## User Impact

Ordinary reads are unchanged, including accepted reads that settle while the database closes or a failed transport stop is retried. When delivery authority is revoked while a read is in flight — for example Doctor clearing a terminal open failure and invalidating the recorded admission — the caller receives an error instead of a reply from a revoked scope.

## Evidence

Verified on `dafc0f8af54`, rebased onto current `main` so the branch carries main's test-line ceiling.

Folded regression `rejects a settled read whose database admission was cleared before delivery` is red on `main` and green with the fix, while the settlement-contract test `retries transport stop and settles the already-selected query` stays green:

```
$ npx vitest run --reporter=dot src/state/openclaw-state-db-readonly.worker-lifecycle.test.ts

main:   × rejects a settled read whose database admission was cleared before delivery
        Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11)
fix:    Tests  11 passed (11)
```

Related state read suites (worker lifecycle, snapshot admission, signal custody, retained, reader cleanup, error mapping, source identity, warm source, read worker): 52 passed.

Real path proof: real SQLite state database, real shared-state read pipeline, and a real admission mutation through `clearOpenClawStateDatabaseOpenFailure`. `config.health.read` runs through the asynchronous read-only SQLite operation, so the revocation lands while the read is in flight. No mocked transport and no fabricated admission context:

```
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/proof-final-gjhr node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs \
    read-admission-revocation.proof.mts read

control read (backup.runs, no revocation): delivered 1 run(s)
control read (config.health.read, no revocation): delivered ok=true
revocation: clearOpenClawStateDatabaseOpenFailure invalidates the admission
main: revoked read (config.health.read): DELIVERED ok=true from a revoked scope
fix:  revoked read (config.health.read): REJECTED with
      "OpenClaw state database read admission changed"
```

`check:test-lines-ratchet` passes on this head. The folded regression is a **+17** net delta (18 added, 1 removed); current `main` carries a raised ceiling, so the gate reports slack instead of an overage:

```
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base refs/remotes/origin/ci-ratchet-base --no-merge-base
Test lines OK: 6246621; ceiling: 6320357; slack: 73736.
```

Gates: exact-head CI green (71 checks pass, `openclaw/ci-gate` passed), `oxfmt --check` clean, `oxlint` clean, targeted `tsc` on the state test shard reports no diagnostics for the changed files, `check:test-mock-exports` clean.

Accepted edge case: settlement and consumption share one continuation, so the guard cannot separate a reply that settled microseconds before a revocation from one that settles during drainage. It covers authority revoked while the read is in flight, and drainage stays exempt on purpose.

prs.title: fix(node): profile node services share one macOS supervisor log
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on macOS, every named-profile node service writes its supervisor output to the same `~/Library/Logs/openclaw/node.log`, so their logs mix. Follow-up to #180288, raised by Codex review there (`src/daemon/constants.ts:165`).

This PR originally also kept `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` in node-host child commands; that half landed separately on `main` in #180951, so this branch now takes `main`'s `host-env-security.ts` and carries only the log prefix.

## User Impact

Profile node services on macOS write supervisor output to `node-<profile>.log` (launchd points stdout and stderr at that one file), matching the existing `gateway-<profile>` supervisor logs. The default node keeps `node.log`.

No new configuration, flags, or migration. Default-profile node services are unchanged. Named-profile node services only exist on `main` since #180288 (the latest stable v2026.10.6 refuses to install them, shown below); after updating, `node install --force` rewrites the prefix and keeps the unit, state, and pairing.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveNodeServiceIdentityEnvironment` now derives `OPENCLAW_LOG_PREFIX` from the profile, the same way the Gateway's supervisor log prefix is derived. The launchd writer already builds the log path from this prefix.

## Evidence

### Tests

Red on base `27a8456` and green with this change (real Linux, WSL2 Ubuntu, Node 26.12.1):

| Test | Base | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/daemon/constants.test.ts` (profile `work` log prefix) | 1 failed / 18 | 18 passed |
| `src/daemon/node-service.test.ts` (real launchd plist writer: log path is `node.log` for the default, `node-<profile>.log` for profiles) | 1 failed | passed |

**Merged `main` again (head `5acd6f0`, `main` at `39b3d94`)** to resolve a conflict in `node-service.test.ts`. `main`'s #182763 had moved this test onto a shared `withNodeHome` fixture. I kept `main`'s version and re-added the plist log-path assertion. The diff against `main` is still only `constants.ts` +2/-1, `constants.test.ts` and `node-service.test.ts`. Production code is unchanged since `9bc7ee2`, where the macOS proof below ran. On `5acd6f0`, `constants.test.ts` and `node-service.test.ts` pass (WSL2, Node 26.12.1), and oxfmt, oxlint and `git diff --check` are clean on the changed files.

On the earlier merged head `9bc7ee2` (with `main` at `c5d525b`), these plus `invoke-system-run.environment.test.ts`, `host-env-security.test.ts`, `service-env.test.ts`, `launchd.test.ts`, `runtime-hints.test.ts`, `daemon-cli/status.install-hints.test.ts` and `node-cli/daemon.test.ts` pass: 206 tests.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/daemon/constants.test.ts src/daemon/node-service.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

`pnpm tsgo:core`, the services test type graph, type-aware oxlint on the changed files, and `git diff --check` pass on the merged head.

### Live: real macOS install (launchd, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Node 26.12.1)

Run by @PollyBot13 on their Mac mini, thank you! Head `9bc7ee2` was built from source and installed as two throwaway named-profile node services through the real CLI (`openclaw --profile pr180503a|pr180503b node install --host 127.0.0.1 --port <unused> --no-tls`). Each service points at its own unused loopback port, so every supervisor-log line (`connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:<port>`) shows which service wrote it. The proof script was a reviewed local adaptation of mine (explicit result status, verified cleanup, and shared-log output limited to the test services' lines). The PR source was unchanged.

| | `pr180503a` (port 47811) | `pr180503b` (port 47812) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LaunchAgent | `ai.openclaw.node.pr180503a`, running | `ai.openclaw.node.pr180503b`, running |
| `StandardOutPath` and `StandardErrorPath` | `~/Library/Logs/openclaw/node-pr180503a.log` | `~/Library/Logs/openclaw/node-pr180503b.log` |
| Its lines in its own log / the other profile's log | 2 / 0 | 2 / 0 |
| Its lines in the shared `node.log` | 0 | 0 |

The machine's own Gateway PID and default node job did not change. The existing `node.log` kept its inode and original content. Both test services, their plists, state and logs were removed afterwards.

Reading the transcript:
- The `OpenClaw 2026.10.6` banner is this head's own version (`package.json` is still `2026.10.6` on `main`). The service command runs the source build (`<work>/source/openclaw.mjs`). The released v2026.10.6 refuses named-profile node installs (see below).
- `env OPENCLAW_PROFILE` and `env OPENCLAW_LOG_PREFIX` show `<unset>` only because the plist has no `EnvironmentVariables`. LaunchAgents keep the service environment in the 0600 `service-env/<label>.env` file that the generated wrapper loads (visible in `ProgramArguments`). The prefix shows up as the log paths above.

### Live: install and upgrade (real systemd, WSL2 Ubuntu, Node 26.12.1)

An isolated Gateway (profile `ocprgw`, loopback, token auth) and a profile node installed as a real user service (`openclaw --profile ocprnode node install …` → `openclaw-node-ocprnode.service`), paired over loopback.

- **Fresh install with this branch:** the persisted service environment has `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=ocprnode`, `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT=openclaw-node-ocprnode`, `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_KIND=node`, `OPENCLAW_LOG_PREFIX=node-ocprnode`. On base the same install persists `OPENCLAW_LOG_PREFIX=node`.
- **v2026.10.6 (latest stable, `fe06181dc5e`; v2026.10.5 behaves the same):** `openclaw --profile ocprupg node install …` is refused (`named profiles cannot override OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT for Linux service management`) and no unit is created, so stable has no named-profile node services to carry over.
- **Profile state written by v2026.10.6, then used by this branch:** v2026.10.6 wrote the `ocprupg` profile's config and exec approvals (`exec-policy preset yolo`). After the documented manual-upgrade step `openclaw --profile ocprupg doctor --fix` with this branch (before it, the first command on the old state reports `Client credentials require backed-up migration custody; … run openclaw doctor --fix` — `main` behavior, unrelated to this diff):

| | Written by v2026.10.6 | Read and used by this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exec approvals defaults / `tools.exec.mode` | `full`, `off`, `full` / `full` | unchanged |
| `node install` for the profile | refused, no unit | `openclaw-node-ocprupg.service`, enabled/active, `OPENCLAW_LOG_PREFIX=node-ocprupg` |
| Gateway → node → `system.run` (runs under the v2026.10.6 exec policy) | — | exit 0; child keeps `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=ocprupg` and finds its running unit |

- **In-place update of a named node installed by `main` `27a8456`** (which includes #180288), via the documented `node install --force` (run on head `4e2a731`, before `main` was merged in; the log-prefix change is identical on `9bc7ee2`):

| | Installed by `main` | After `node install --force` with this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit / state dir / profile / kind | `openclaw-node-ocprnode.service`, `~/.openclaw-ocprnode`, `ocprnode`, `node` | unchanged |
| `OPENCLAW_LOG_PREFIX` | `node` | `node-ocprnode` (intended) |
| `openclaw.json`, `config-journal-fingerprint.key`, `control/services.sqlite` (sha256) | `b7e89b236bb4`, `2b962b05b12c`, `6cca4ac60edf` | unchanged |
| Gateway pairing | 1 paired device, 0 pending | same device id, 0 pending (no re-pairing) |
| Service | enabled, active | enabled, active |

`client/credentials.sqlite` and `state/openclaw.sqlite` are rewritten by the running node on every start (a plain restart without an update changes them too), so their hashes are not compared. All test services, units, profiles, and the token were removed afterwards.

Default-profile nodes: the identity they persist is unchanged (`node` prefix; covered in `constants.test.ts` for unset and `default`). I did not run a live default-profile install: on this host it requires the account's real `~/.openclaw` state, which I left untouched.

Production: `constants.ts` +2/-1. Tests: `constants.test.ts` +5/-4, `node-service.test.ts` +5/-1.

Not run live on macOS: the `main` side, where both profile services write the shared `node.log`. That behavior follows from the source (`OPENCLAW_LOG_PREFIX: "node"` on `main`), and the red `node-service.test.ts` case above shows it through the real launchd plist writer.

prs.title: fix: resume goals in existing local Codex sessions
prs.body:
Related: #180208, #185273.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Goal Start and Resume reject existing local Codex sessions even though ordinary turns in those conversations work.

## User Impact

Operators can resume the same local Codex goal with its identity, objective, and history retained, using the existing budget-accounting rules. Resume asks the model to read the current saved goal before working, so an objective edited while paused takes effect.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing native input commit and acknowledgement path for both local and cloud-worker Codex sessions, while keeping worker transcript authority specific to workers. Select native admission before built-in admission so an existing session with no recorded harness cannot enter both paths. Existing session identity, operator authority, busy-work, placement, and native thread-ownership checks remain enforced.

**Difference from #180208:** that PR continues an active local Codex goal after a normal turn ends. This PR handles explicit Start/Resume admission in an existing conversation. It is independent of the continuation patch and adds no automatic pursuit or restart replay.

## Maintainer decision requested

This extends the intentional runtime support boundary. Please confirm that explicit Goal Start and Resume should support existing local Codex sessions through the shared native admission owner. ClawSweeper recommends approving this focused extension; #180208's automatic-continuation work remains separate. Maintainer approval is not yet recorded.

## Evidence

- **Conflict update (`c2c5269fbc3`):** merged upstream `main` at `acf995b629063dd5ac1db2737fd561b491566d6b` and resolved six conflicts after upstream retired restart-safe admission and moved the Goal commit guard. Local Codex selection still precedes built-in local input admission; worker transcript authority remains worker-only. The merged #185273 Resume-after-Stop fix and typed invalid-goal errors are retained.
- **Current-candidate validation:** 44/44 public Goal admission/continuation regressions passed, including built-in, recorded local Codex, unrecorded local Codex, worker setup/revocation controls, identity/history retention, and idempotent replay (152.83s including cold worker preparation). Core and Gateway-server test typechecks, targeted core/root-test lint, formatting of all nine PR files, Goal MDX validation, and whitespace checks passed. Lint used the repository's source-backed core/root-test configurations after a broader configuration encountered pre-existing borrowed dependency links; no dependency links or lint guards were changed.
- **Independent review:** a separate native read-only reviewer assessed the full nine-file candidate against `acf995b629063dd5ac1db2737fd561b491566d6b` at P0–P2 and found no actionable defects. Static review only; the shared autoreview helper could not launch because its `codex` executable was unavailable. This is not a helper-validated clean report. Current-head hosted CI is pending publication/completion; maintainer scope approval remains outstanding. No fresh hosted re-review has been requested. The prior real-model scenario below has not been rerun after this integration; previous-head proof is retained with that boundary.

- **Prior-head review follow-up (`0fdc43d4672`):** fixed ClawSweeper's documentation finding by aligning the Control UI eligibility paragraph with existing local Codex admission and keeping native admission separate from worker setup. Focused docs formatting, MDX validation, and whitespace checks pass. This is documentation only; runtime and real-model proof are unchanged. [ClawSweeper accepted the supplied live behavior proof and identified no runtime defect](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186524#issuecomment-6461116165). Hosted CI and the published `openclaw/ci-gate` passed on prior head `0fdc43d4672835a8d77271939ad62eb25b896c48` ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40636054606), [published gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40638377509)). That prior-head CI completed with no pending or failed checks; it is not current-head CI proof. ClawSweeper has not re-reviewed this documentation-only follow-up: its dispatch was deduplicated with `review_request_required`. The earlier hosted Codex review failed without publishing findings and is not claimed as passed. Maintainer scope approval and any requested fresh hosted review remain outstanding.

- **CI lint repair (`9f0f056c391`):** reproduced the `check-lint` failure from run `40632910651` using the same root-test lint wrapper. Changed only two accesses to the `__openclaw` wire field from dot to bracket notation; the wrapper now passes. Runtime code and proof assertions are unchanged, so the real-model evidence below remains applicable. The subsequent hosted `check-lint` job passed on `9f0f056c391`.

- **Base red:** the production Goal RPC regression rejected local Codex Resume with `requires an idle built-in local session with recoverable history`. The built-in variant passed.
- **Real behavior, passed:** a built production Gateway and real native Codex model, using disposable staged native auth and isolated Gateway state, started a synthetic goal; an operator paused and edited it; public Resume then caused real `get_goal` lookup and completion of that same goal. The new final marker existed only in the edited objective. Goal ID, creation time, session ID, objective, and prior stored history were retained. Replaying the same Resume operation returned its receipt with no new run or messages.
- The first live attempt exposed overlapping built-in/native admission for an unrecorded harness; that producer defect was repaired and added as a third regression variant. Authentication-only fixture failures were resolved by using the supported native home route with the live-test owner's staged HOME; credential portability policy was not relaxed.
- **44/44** Goal admission/queue/SQLite regressions passed (wall **123.90s**, Vitest **119.45s**); the final focused built-in/recorded-Codex/unrecorded-Codex variants also passed (**61.33s** wall). Hosted CI completed successfully; the linked run provides timing.
- The complete live scenario passed in **54.67s** (test **36.40s**), including model effects, visible reply, history, and replay checks.
- Production runtime build, core and Gateway-server test typechecks, focused lint/format, whitespace check, and fresh independent source review passed.

Sanitized live receipt (synthetic identifiers omitted):

```json
{"proof":"local-codex-same-goal-resume","followedEditedObjective":true,"preservedHistory":true,"completed":true,"replayedWithoutNewRun":true}
```

Reproduce with an available native Codex model and live-test auth:

```sh
OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_GOAL_RESUME=1 \
OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_HARNESS_MODEL='<configured-native-model>' \
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts \
```
