prs.title: fix(macos): Mac tab shows a blank or stale page when a load fails
prs.body:
Related: #183927

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Mac tab shows a blank white page (new tab) or silently keeps the previous page (loaded tab) when a page fails to load, and Reload does nothing for a failed first load.

## User Impact

User impact: when a link is broken or the Mac is offline, the tab now keeps the address that was tried, says why it could not be opened, and offers Reload, which retries that address. Stopping a load, navigating somewhere else, and download or default-browser handoffs still keep the current page without an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main-frame failures reached `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.navigationDidFail(for:)` without the error, so the tab only retired its link alias and published unchanged state (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardWindowController.swift:1467-1470`, `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardNativeBrowserHost.swift:269-272` on `70c70646d86`). Reload called `webView.reload()` (`DashboardNativeBrowserHost.swift:174`), which replays the last committed item; a failed first load never commits one, so nothing happens.

The tab owner now receives the error. Deliberate interruptions (`NSURLErrorCancelled`, and WebKit's policy interruption 102 used for response-policy cancels such as downloads and default-browser handoff) are ignored as before. Any other failure shows a native failure view over the tab's web view: a title, the system error description (no page content and no URL), and a Reload button. The tab keeps the failing URL; the published tab URL prefers it, and Reload (the button or the toolbar) loads it again. The next navigation that starts clears the failure.

The failure view is AppKit, added as a subview of the reading tab's `WKWebView`, so it follows the existing presentation frames and hiding and the untrusted page cannot script or restyle it. It is layer-backed and sets its background in `updateLayer()`: the first revision was a plain opaque view filled in `draw(_:)`, and in the running app it painted over the whole dashboard window (see the running-app proof below). No bridge, Control UI, or privileged dashboard failure-page code is involved. Favicon and alias handling from #184839 is unchanged: a failed navigation never commits, so the shown page keeps its icon.

## Evidence

### Running-app proof

The packaged app built from this branch (debug, ad hoc signed, `ai.openclaw.mac.debug` 2026.10.7) ran on macOS 27.2 arm64 with Xcode 27.1, launched with `--dashboard` against a task-owned loopback Gateway and HTTP fixture. Accessibility drove it by process id, and the native failure view, which WebKit keeps out of the accessibility tree, was read and clicked from the window via Vision text recognition. Window screenshots and a recording of only the app's windows.

1. A new tab opens an address nothing listens on. The failure view shows "This page couldn't be opened / Could not connect to the server.", the address bar keeps `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/first-load`, the fixture starts, and the failure view's Reload loads the page (fixture: one request for `/first-load`).
2. The loaded page follows a link to another unserved address. The failure view shows, the address bar keeps `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/broken`, the fixture starts, and the toolbar Reload loads it (one request for `/broken`). The failure view is gone after each recovery.

The first revision (`9ad45a61910`) passed the same flow, but while the failure view showed, its background covered the whole dashboard window: chat, tab strip, address bar and toolbar. `e164e6e589e` makes the view layer-backed, and it now stays inside the tab.

The Browser panel of `e164e6e589e` at full resolution, cropped from the window screenshots (the failure view's text is small grey on dark in the full-window shots below):

Failed first load, then after the failure view's Reload:

![panel-failed-first-load](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-10-new-tab-failed.png) ![panel-recovered-native-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-11-new-tab-recovered-native-reload.png)

Failed navigation from the loaded page, then after the toolbar Reload:

![panel-failed-navigation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-21-loaded-tab-failed.png) ![panel-recovered-toolbar-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-22-loaded-tab-recovered-toolbar-reload.png)

The same crop from frames of the `e164e6e589e` recording at 9 s (first load failed), 21 s (recovered), 25 s (navigation failed) and the last frame (recovered), so the sequence can be checked without playing the video:

![frame-09s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-t09s.png) ![frame-21s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-t21s.png) ![frame-25s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-t25s.png) ![frame-end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-end.png)

Text recognized in each crop and frame: [text.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/text.txt).

Failed navigation, `9ad45a61910` (whole window covered) and `e164e6e589e` (failure view inside the tab; the address bar shows the attempted URL):

![before-loaded-tab-failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/before-21-loaded-tab-failed.png)
![after-loaded-tab-failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-21-loaded-tab-failed.png)

Failed first load and recovery with `e164e6e589e`:

![after-new-tab-failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-10-new-tab-failed.png)
![after-native-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-11-new-tab-recovered-native-reload.png)
![after-toolbar-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-22-loaded-tab-recovered-toolbar-reload.png)

Recordings: [`9ad45a61910`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/before-recording.mp4), [`e164e6e589e`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-recording.mp4). Build identity, scenario logs and fixture request logs are next to them ([fixed identity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-identity.txt), [fixed scenario log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-scenario.log)). The bottom-left avatar is masked.

With `e164e6e589e`, on the same Mac: `swift test --filter DashboardNativeBrowserTests` (Xcode 27.1): 27 tests in 4 suites passed. SwiftFormat and SwiftLint `--strict` on the changed file: clean. `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: only the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation.

### Offscreen renders and regressions

Each image is an offscreen render of the reading tab's web view from the real `DashboardWindowController` in the regression harness. The grey band at the bottom is a test harness readout, not app UI: it prints the tab state `DashboardNativeBrowserHost` publishes to the dashboard (loopback port masked). The tab strip and address bar are Control UI web chrome and are not part of these renders.

New tab whose first load fails, before (blank white page) and after (native failure view with Reload; the tab state already reported the attempted URL on base):

![a-before-new-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-before-new-tab.png)
![a-after-new-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-after-new-tab.png)

Loaded tab whose navigation to `/next` fails, before (old page stays and tab state still reports `/article`) and after (failure view; tab state reports the attempted `/next`):

![a-before-loaded-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-before-loaded-tab.png)
![a-after-loaded-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-after-loaded-tab.png)

Focused real-WKWebView regressions in `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/DashboardNativeBrowserTests.swift` (`DashboardNativeBrowserFailureTests`), driving `DashboardWindowController` and its navigation delegate against task-owned loopback `DashboardHTTPFixture` endpoints:

- a new tab opened on a released loopback port shows the failure, keeps the attempted URL in tab state, and after the endpoint comes back the failure view's Reload button loads it;
- the same from an already loaded page: the page and its favicon stay, tab state shows the attempted URL, toolbar Reload loads it, and Back stays available after the retry;
- stop, replacement navigation, and a non-displayable response (download policy cancel) show no failure.

Results on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Swift 6.4 (Command Line Tools), base `70c70646d86`:

- `swift test --filter DashboardNativeBrowserFailureTests` on this branch: 3 tests (5 cases) passed.
- The same flows on base (tests rewritten to base APIs, failure-view assertions dropped): the failed first load never retries (`Time limit was exceeded`, still waiting for the retried load), and after a failed navigation from a loaded page the tab state still shows the old page's URL (`failed.url == attempted.absoluteString` is false).
- Siblings `DashboardNativeBrowser|DashboardHTTPFixtureTests|DashboardBrowserDownloadTests|DashboardBrowserCookieBoundaryTests`: 34 tests in 7 suites passed.
- `swift build --build-tests`, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` (0 files need formatting), `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` (only the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation, also on base), `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base <current main>` on the stacked follow-up for #183928, whose diff against main includes every file of this branch (not run separately on this branch): every guard passed except `lint apps` (the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation) and `macOS app CI tests` (1 failed, 607 passed), whose one failure is the tooling test `test/scripts/generate-gateway-protocol-plugin.test.ts`, which builds the Swift package itself and fails on this machine with the Command Line Tools manifest link error (`Package.__allocating_init` undefined); it does not touch the files in this change.

## Related work

- #152668 (open, prepare integrated tab logins before opening links) touches `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.swift`, `DashboardWindowController.swift` and `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`. No shared lines: its host change removes `self.onOpen?()` in `open` (line 160 on `70c70646d86`), a few lines above this stack's `navigate`/`perform` changes; its controller hunks are in lines 99-559, ours at 1331-1496. It already conflicts with current main on its own. Whichever lands second regenerates the i18n inventory with `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` (the inventory records source line sites).
- No open PR covers #183927 or #183928 (searched by symptom and by the owner file names).

## Gaps

- The offscreen renders under "Offscreen renders and regressions" come from the real `DashboardWindowController` on a host without a logged-in GUI session; the running-app proof above is the window evidence.
- The offscreen renders and the test results under them were built with the Command Line Tools (Swift 6.4) only, no Xcode; the running-app proof and its test run used Xcode 27.1. Xcode-only SwiftUI macro plugins (`@State`, `@Entry`, `#Preview`) were replaced locally by equivalent desugaring plugins, and two unrelated XCTest-based test files were left out locally because the CLT ships no XCTest. Nothing in this change uses SwiftUI. The `macos-swift` CI job is the authoritative native run.
- A failure after a document committed (`didFail` mid-load) takes the same path but has no dedicated test.
- Known edges, unchanged in scope: the failure view sits over the tab's web view, so a snapshot of a failed loaded tab (for example Annotate) still captures the previous page underneath; a same-document navigation by that previous page (`pushState`, hash change) does not start a provisional load and so leaves the failure shown; Reload retries a failed POST as a plain GET of the same URL.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix: preserve running exec warnings in Code Mode
prs.body:
Fixes #187224

## What Problem This Solves

When an exec command yields a running session with an execution warning, Code Mode currently receives the process identifiers and continuation guidance but loses the warning. A real Docker-sandbox countdown reproduced this: native exec explained that PTY was unavailable and recommended a noninteractive command, while the structured running value contained no such explanation.

## User Impact

Code Mode agents retain the existing execution warning in `warningText` and can use it when choosing how to continue the same process. Calls without warnings omit the field. The command remains a running success, and its session identity, deadline, output, and follow-up guidance remain available.

This change does not enable sandbox PTY or writable stdin, change approvals or execution routing, or alter terminal and failed result classification. There is no configuration or persistent-state migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exec producer already collects the warnings but includes them only in the running result's display text. Structured callers consume `details`. The fix places those same warnings in the existing running-result contract and documents that field; generic Code Mode projection remains unchanged.

The regression extends the existing real-process Code Mode recovery case with warned and warning-free variants. It checks that a warning generated by the native environment sanitizer exists before projection, is retained in the running value, and leaves the same-process recovery path usable. The separate test-line allocation covers the measured additional regression lines without changing the shared ceiling.

## Evidence

Before the fix, an ordinary guest on source `a83fd5dcf456df68e0889a1e40bc10d3a1359b70` launched a 15-second Python countdown with `pty: true`. The native Docker result emitted the PTY warning, while Code Mode returned `status: "running"` without it. The same process was polled to successful completion; the omission is not claimed to be the sole cause of an agent decision.

The native process/Code Mode regression fails on unchanged production at the missing-warning assertion, after confirming that the native result emitted it; the warning-free control and 15 existing cases pass. On commit `347a5ec70f3261833690b83e10f9d0c879714905`, changed-file formatting/lint, all seven selected type-check groups, and the related/protected native test batch pass: 58 files, 874 tests passed, four conditional skips. The separate live Anthropic reviewer suite was not run; approval and authorization integration tests passed. The native regression, failed/refused results, result-budget controls, and prompt-prefix stability are included. The measured test-line total is 6,246,528 against an effective ceiling of 6,320,203; this change's allocation is 33 lines.

The ordered remote command took 1,176.839 seconds including type checks, the required runtime preparation, and the test batch. The exact-head live Docker scenario now retains that same PTY warning in structured `warningText`. The actual command parameters matched the baseline (`pty: true`, 1,000 ms yield, 25-second timeout); the agent inspected progress and collected the same process at 15 seconds with exit code 0. The session finished without active work. Terminal input remained unavailable as intended.

Independent engineering review is clean, and canonical AutoReview reports `scoped-clean` at P0–P3 for the exact committed range. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40814509499) passed all 43 selected jobs; 27 unselected platform/release or empty-matrix placeholders remained skipped. The changed-file single-worker command, `pnpm test src/agents/code-mode.agent-loop.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, passed 17 cases in 11.61 seconds of Vitest wall time (40.37 seconds including native worker preparation). The two continuation cases took 952 ms and 962 ms. Per-file CI seconds are not separately reported here.

[ClawSweeper’s exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187244#issuecomment-6487779268) returned Platinum readiness/proof and Diamond patch quality with no findings. The final target check at `b919810d770ce7b85e21c3ab6f9428ba6d73f898` still fails only on the missing structured warning, with 16 controls passing; the target has not superseded this repair.

prs.title: fix(agents): agents fail to reach another agent by its display name
prs.body:
Related: #140203

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent cannot reach another agent when it uses that agent's display name instead of its agent id.

## User Impact

User impact: when an agent sends to or spawns a display name such as "Nova", the error now names the correct agent id. The agent retries with that id and the call succeeds.

`agents_list` now also shows `identity.name` when an agent has no `name`. With a spawn allowlist, agents see `main` as "Nova" and use `main` from the start.

Agent ids stay the only routing key. A display name never routes a call. No config or default changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Many setups keep the id `main` and give the agent a display name. Other agents know only the display name. They pass it as `agentId`, and the call fails with `Agent "Nova" not found`. Nothing in the error tells the agent the correct id.

The change adds one helper in `src/agents/identity.ts`. It finds the agent whose `name` or `identity.name` matches the unknown `agentId`. The match ignores case. The helper adds a hint only when exactly one reachable agent matches. Hidden or denied agents never appear in the hint.

- `sessions_send` adds the hint to both "not found" errors. The existing session access check decides which agents the requester can reach. That check reads `tools.agentToAgent`, the per-agent `tools.agentToAgent.send` list and `tools.sessions.visibility`.
- `sessions_spawn` adds the hint to the target policy error. The spawn allowlist decides which agents the requester can reach.
- `agents_list` and the Gateway agent list use one shared rule for the display name: `name`, then `identity.name`.

## Evidence

Live tests on a local Gateway with a real local model (Ollama `gemma4:12b`). Each setup uses an isolated home and two agents. `main` has `identity.name: "Nova"`. `mark` has no name. `tools.agentToAgent` allows `main` and `mark`. Each trial sends one message to `mark`.

### Round 1: no spawn allowlist

Message: "Ask Nova what 2+2 is. Use agents_list first, then sessions_send." `agents_list` lists only `mark` on both builds, because it lists spawn targets.

| Build | Trial | First `agentId` | Error text | Recovered |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main `b0966db` | 1 to 3 | `nova` or `Nova` | `Agent "Nova" not found. Run openclaw agents list to see configured agents.` | No, 0 of 3 |
| This branch | 1 to 3 | `nova` or `Nova` | `Agent "Nova" not found. Did you mean agent id "main" (Nova)? Run openclaw agents list ...` | Yes, 3 of 3. The retry with `main` returned "4". |

![Before: main sends to nova and gets a plain not-found error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/proof/agents-list-identity-name/proof/agent-name-hint/before-main.png)

![After: the error names main and the model retries with main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/proof/agents-list-identity-name/proof/agent-name-hint/after-branch.png)

### Round 2: `mark` has `subagents.allowAgents: ["*"]`

| Scenario | Build | `agents_list` shows | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| "Ask Nova ... use agents_list, then sessions_send" | main `b0966db` | `mark`, `main` | 0 of 3 recovered. Each send to `Nova` failed with the plain error. |
| same | This branch | `mark`, `main` named "Nova" | 3 of 3 sent to `main` on the first try and returned "4". No hint was needed. |
| "Start a sub-task on Nova using sessions_spawn" | main `b0966db` | `mark`, `main` | 0 of 2 reached `main`. One spawn to `Nova` failed. One model spawned a child of `mark` with no `agentId` and called that a success. |
| same | This branch | `mark`, `main` named "Nova" | 2 of 2 spawned on `main` on the first try. |
| "Use sessions_spawn with agentId Nova. Do not call agents_list." | main `b0966db` | not called | 0 of 3 recovered. Error: `agentId "nova" is not in the configured agent registry (allowed: main, mark)` |
| same | This branch | not called | 4 of 4 recovered. Error: `... (allowed: main, mark). Did you mean agent id "main" (Nova)?` The retry with `main` was accepted and returned "4". |
| "Use sessions_send with agentId Nova", with `mark.tools.agentToAgent.send: []` | This branch | not called | 3 of 3 got the plain error with no hint. `mark` cannot send to `main`, so the hint stays silent. |

In the send-denied trial that told the model to use `agents_list` first, the model never sent to "Nova". So it shows no hint result. The three direct send-denied trials above cover that case.

![Before: agents_list shows main without a name, and both sends fail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/proof/agents-list-identity-name/proof/agent-name-hint/base-agents-list-no-name.png)

![After: agents_list names main as Nova, and the model sends to main directly](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/proof/agents-list-identity-name/proof/agent-name-hint/head-send-direct-to-main.png)

![After: two spawns fail, the hint names main, and the spawn on main succeeds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/proof/agents-list-identity-name/proof/agent-name-hint/head-spawn-hint-recovery.png)

### Tests

Each new case fails without its fix and passes on this branch:

- `src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts` "suggests only a sendable agent id": unique name and non-Latin name get the hint. A shared name, agent-to-agent messaging off, an empty per-agent `send` list and `self` visibility get no hint. An explicit `send` grant under `agent` visibility gets the hint.
- `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-target-policy.test.ts`: a hint for an allowed agent. No hint for an agent outside the allowlist.
- `src/agents/tools/agents-list-tool.test.ts`: `name` first, then `identity.name`.

Consumer tests pass: `src/gateway/agent-list.test.ts`, `src/agents/identity.test.ts`, `src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.allowlist.test.ts`, `src/agents/subagents/spawn/acp-spawn.test.ts` and `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.test.ts`. `pnpm tsgo:core`, the `agents-tools` test typecheck lane, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` pass on the changed files.

Gap: the hint reads names from config only. An agent with a name only in its workspace `IDENTITY.md` gets no hint. The Gateway agent list has the same limit.

prs.title: fix: preserve original SVG image downloads
prs.body: Closes #187222 ## What Problem This Solves An SVG attachment can render correctly in the conversation's image viewer while **Download image** always fails with a retry error. The image-download path treats its original SVG payload as an unsupported raster format, so retrying cannot produce the file. ## User Impact The viewer now saves the original SVG with its existing filename and exact bytes. Raster downloads, zoom, attachment admission, and the existing generic file-card recovery remain unchanged. This does not add another supported upload format or allow opening active SVG documents. ## Why This Change Was Made The download owner sends SVG bytes through the existing file downloader with an inert `application/octet-stream` Blob. Wrapping the Blob changes its download MIME type without decoding, rasterizing, or rewriting the file. It also preserves the filename instead of deriving an incorrect `.svg+xml` extension through the raster filename helper. The shared raster MIME vocabulary and top-level blob guard are unchanged. The existing 30-second download URL lifetime is retained; the change adds no dependency, setting, protocol, or storage behavior. ## Evidence A current-source browser regression reproduced the original failure after an incoming conversation event, attachment rendering, and lightbox opening. It failed at the missing browser-download assertion after the SVG loaded successfully. The same scenario checks exact original bytes and filename both initially and after a history reload, plus absence of SVG script execution or a new page. A real guest created a packing guide and matching SVG/PNG files in an isolated workspace. Through the ordinary composer file picker, its unchanged SVG reached the real `image/svg+xml` lightbox: the baseline produced the error and no download, while this candidate saved `parcel-flow.svg` with all 5,155 bytes and the exact source SHA-256. PNG lightbox and original Files downloads also preserved their bytes. This live route and the incoming-message regression cover different entry points explicitly; the normal outgoing unsupported-format recovery card was preserved. Changed-file formatting/lint and applicable production/test type graphs passed. ## User Impact

The intended result is stable, provenance-marked model input while canonical visible transcript bytes remain unchanged. Actual vendor cache hits, token savings and billing have not been measured. Preserving prepared hook enrichment is still a specific maintainer product decision, described below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing model projection resolver and idempotent source-envelope annotator remain the only owners. Assembly, phase and submission carry typed provenance to that resolver. Frozen dispatched projections, current-message identity, source authority, ordinary/raw/internal/settled paths and hidden runtime carriers retain their existing owners. No schema, protocol, public SDK or dependency change.

## Evidence

Current author maintenance (2026-10-29), candidate **878becd404a6bc70bdf1eaab62822e92ad15bac2**, normally merges pinned official main `a4e20a8b24440efd9b8a1792ce400be85a697080` into the existing branch. The one adjacent declaration conflict retains both `modelPromptProvenance` and main's `normalizeToolCallIds`; normalization remains inside the existing provider transform before request measurement and output budgeting. Three fixture arguments/reads retired by #181482 were removed without restoring the old steering lease/ack mechanism. Assertions, timeouts, database admission, policies and baselines were not relaxed.

- **Current candidate:** nine complete files pass **118 distinct cases**. The eight affected caller/sibling files pass 116 cases in 1007.03 s of native-wrapper wall time across two supported configurations; the formal Anthropic replay file passes two cases in 356.51 s. Compilation, import and cleanup are included in these times. This covers all three context-engine provenance/preprocessing modes, unchanged direct-submit source-envelope controls, frozen projections, fallback and late media, hidden runtime retry/reopen, pasted-text retention, authority revocation, request-prefix measurement/cache ordering, foreground and attempt callers. The replay's stronger transport limits are stated below.

- Production closure types: PASS, 51.01 s. Current test-consumer types first detected three retired steering API errors, then PASS in 117.06 s after the fixture migration. Typed lint PASS in 68.12 s; format, eight-file line-cap, whitespace and native assertion-safety gates PASS. Test-lines ratchet: 6,246,449 / 6,320,000, leaving 73,551 lines; no authored ceiling change.

The first four-production-file canonical-main negative control exceeded the unchanged 180 s preload hook deadline: **zero tests executed, 26 skipped**. After the normal candidate context-engine file qualified the fixture, a supported filesystem-cache-disabled control with the same regression fixture and the four complete production modules from pinned main executed the target assertions: **two missing-source-warning failures, one already-canonical control passing, 23 unselected**, 436.94 s wrapper wall time. - `test/scripts/frv.test.ts`: 115 passed

## What Problem This Solves

Codex session catalog search silently omits sessions when the query and the stored session name use canonically equivalent but different Unicode forms. An NFC `Café` query misses an NFD `Cafe\u0301` title, and the reverse pairing fails too.

Precedent: #184847, #186672 (same comparison-only NFC pattern in the Beam and Session Share catalogs; this PR applies it to the Codex catalog owner).

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize only case-folded comparison text to NFC at both ends of the existing Codex catalog comparison: the query needle in `prepareCodexCatalogQuery` and the cached `searchText` built in the resident index row order. Both operands move together, so either canonical spelling matches regardless of the stored form. Stored and returned session names, thread IDs and page boundaries stay unchanged. No new helper, dependency, configuration or public API.

Production LOC: +3/-3. Classification: `behavior-completing`.

## User Impact

Operators find a Codex session by either canonical spelling of its title. ASCII case-insensitive search, cwd filtering and missing-query behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real catalog path in secretless Docker (Node 24.22.1): the Codex control fixture returns genuine thread rows; `control.listPage({ searchTerm })` runs the production index query and resident row order. Regression coverage exercises both canonical directions plus ASCII controls.

prs.title: fix(opencode): match canonically equivalent Unicode in session search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenCode catalog search misses an existing native session when its title or cwd uses decomposed Unicode and the search uses the composed equivalent, or vice versa. Lowercasing alone does not make those spellings compare equally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply NFC after the existing lowercase conversion to the query and searchable projections at the existing OpenCode catalog owner, following #187148. Keep the records themselves untouched. This is two line replacements, not a new helper or SDK export.

## User Impact

Canonically equivalent titles and cwd now match in catalog search. Raw titles, cwd and native IDs retain their spelling. Exact-ID equality, native ownership/continuation, discovery bounds and pagination policy are unchanged. No storage migration, auth change or new configuration.

## Evidence

[Real upstream OpenCode store and built Gateway comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187189#issuecomment-6486767640), head `a64ca866eb0bb607aea7c01feaa3df1a16029213` against main `8d46327b2656a3bb09889167570c4a35eb061e42`:

- Installed actual upstream OpenCode 1.19.5 in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker. Created real local sessions through its server API and verified them with its CLI; no login, fake executable or SQL seeding was needed.
- Two isolated built Gateway profiles per ref, authenticated `sessions.catalog.list` through the bundled plugin: main finds one same-form title; head finds both NFC/NFD titles for either query form.
- ASCII, exact native ID, absent/no-query, native row spelling and first/next-page controls pass. NFC cwd search also finds the existing NFD cwd only on head.
- 21 focused tests passed; final canonical boundary cases pass for the existing v1/v2 fixture branches. Scoped lint and repository formatter parity pass.

The unit fixture CLI is not the runtime acceptance proof. The real-store comparison qualifies local listing on OpenCode 1.19.5, not provider execution or login. Scan limits are unchanged; the runtime fixture contains three sessions, not a frontier stress workload.

## Simplification

Preserved the contributor's commit. Folded canonical search into the existing list/read boundary instead of retaining a duplicate standalone matrix. Whole-change production delta **0**, test delta **0**, two files; no baseline increases or SDK additions.

## AI Assistance

AI assisted source tracing, regression consolidation and the real upstream-store/Gateway proof. Contributor @wangmiao0668000666's implementation and commit are retained.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the old search behavior; this change does not write or migrate native sessions. Blast radius is OpenCode catalog text filtering. Wrong normalization could omit a result or add a textual match, while exact-ID validation and continuation ownership remain unchanged.

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

A final true conflict against official main `53fb615a` was limited to the generated configuration hash. This branch normally merges that fixed main and resolves the hash with the official generator. Independent blob review preserves the feature/authority/Gateway owners; the only tracked help-file change comes from official main. Current-head CI is reported above separately from preceding evidence.

The items in [the prior/current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127770#issuecomment-5377643651) are covered by explicit consent, bounded fallback, actual conflict repair, a concrete opt-in proposal, published-stable compatibility, the final-effect authority fence and actual Gateway evidence. [The later evidence reminder](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127770#issuecomment-6051721637) is addressed by this refreshed evidence and description. prs.title: feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

prs.title: fix(update): capture and seal original state on PostgreSQL families
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #187155: PostgreSQL updates can report original-state capture unavailable, classify their own database writes as an unknown writer, and leave recovery status unable to recognize a successful update.

## User Impact

PostgreSQL originals are captured and sealed through the existing exact backup provider, updater writes are attributed, and status reads the configured engine to recognize successful captures as stale. The installed updater must contain this repair. No schema, configuration option, CLI option, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Original capture supplied no maintenance custody; parent generation observation skipped PostgreSQL; status read its SQLite anchor instead of the PostgreSQL ledger. This reuses the existing custody and engine-selection owners. Unparseable configuration keeps recovery files visible with unreadable outcomes, and all status inspection remains bounded by its existing deadline. Foreign-write refusal and uncertain-child custody remain intact.

Thanks @etzelm for the same-build SQLite/PostgreSQL comparison.

## Evidence

- Capture and attribution regressions fail on pinned base `44ffd0a845b32480ffaf46ff6cfbcaa2267491c1`. Public stale-success status fails with the pre-fix status reader after the capture repair. The final five-family PostgreSQL conformance cases pass, including public status with valid and malformed configuration.
- All 24 affected/proof files were exercised: 292 cases pass; two SQLite WAL-reader cases fail identically on base and patch. A read-only SQLite 3.54.0 open changes WAL ctime while its bytes and mtime stay unchanged, triggering the existing stopped-capture fingerprint. PostgreSQL conformance qualification uses vector and the documented 512-lock budget. Doctor's rename proof passes on tmpfs (overlayfs is explicitly unsupported).
- Fixed the deadline unit fixture's fake-clock hang: engine initialization now stays outside that timer-only fixture, preserving real exports, all assertions and all three cases. Before: pending beyond 120 s; after: 3/3 pass, 1.56 s test time (23.12 s wrapper). No timeout/retry/assertion weakening.
- Core, infra-test and CLI-update typechecks; touched-file oxlint/oxfmt; Madge (zero cycles); diff and max-lines/test-lines/mock-export ratchets pass. Final Codex review is clean through P2. Production +113/-28 lines (net +85); tests +116/-116 (net zero); docs +6.
- **Live same-build A/B passes:** task-owned PostgreSQL 17.11 state/agent/workboard stores versus SQLite, isolated HOME/state, no Gateway or other writer. Native generated metadata was untouched; all five production files match the reviewed source byte-for-byte. New PostgreSQL run/capture `7f3f4f2b-af1f-49c5-9e1b-758d34d9da9e` succeeds (20.735 s), seals four exact capsules, and public status reports `stale: its update already succeeded` (2.170 s). SQLite run/capture `5fc7c4e6-67fc-4f04-a686-fdad23604d31` does the same (11.764 s / 3.649 s). Captured and live Workboard sentinels, both agents, and configured ports are retained. No capture-unavailable or unknown-writer warning.
- **Proof limits:** these are fresh same-build/channel-convergence updates. Separate next-commit activation attempts fail identically on both engines at the existing native guard: `Cannot bridge inspect-Duxclsbo.js export findSystemGatewayServices` (PG 272.070 s; SQLite 282.390 s). A supported clean package rebuild does not remove that failure. Candidate output contains the export but lacks source-origin region comments required by `scripts/lib/update-compat-chunks.mts`; CI environment causation is unproven. No compatibility guard/generated metadata was changed, and candidate activation is not claimed. Repeated already-current runs retain existing skipped/ambiguous semantics.
- Existing slow boundary cases remain: final capture/status 39.978 s, exact rollback 41.327 s, parent-bookkeeping cases 41–53 s, rollback consumer file 184 s test time. Full `check:changed` / SQLite inventory was skipped under the campaign's local gate budget. PR CI supplies broad proof.

<details>
<summary>Live commands and local regression commands</summary>

Inside the task-owned container, separately for `ENGINE=postgres` and `ENGINE=sqlite`:

```sh
export HOME="/work/.artifacts/l1956/live-reviewed-$ENGINE/home"
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="/work/.artifacts/l1956/live-reviewed-$ENGINE/state"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json"
openclaw workboard create 'Update recovery sentinel' --notes 'Synthetic update reliability proof' --json
openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev
openclaw update status
openclaw workboard list --json
openclaw agents list --json
openclaw config get gateway.port
```

PostgreSQL exact capsules retain 97 state tables, 39 tables for each agent, and 18 Workboard tables. Both captures retain six SQLite image/anchor entries.

Focused proof used repository wrappers with isolated HOME/state and distinct compiler caches:

```sh
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TASK_PG_DSN" -- src/infra/database-engine/update-preflight.conformance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/status.deadline.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/flows/doctor-health.fleet-preflight.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(sessions): find native sessions with equivalent Unicode titles
prs.body:
Related: #187189, #187196, #187204, #187211. Follows #187148.

## What Problem This Solves

Native OpenCode, Claude, Pi and Codex session searches omit existing sessions when a title and query use canonically equivalent composed/decomposed Unicode spellings.

## User Impact

Equivalent spellings now find the same native sessions. Raw titles, cwd and IDs keep their original spelling. Exact-ID reads, continuation ownership, existing provider-specific search fields, discovery limits and pagination behavior remain unchanged. No migration or new configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply NFC after the existing lowercase conversion at each provider's existing comparison owner. Codex's cached title projection, resident query, and shared paired-node/native-overflow post-filter now agree. Claude's exact-ID lookup retains its original input and equality; only the later textual filter is canonicalized. No SDK exports or new normalization abstraction.

This incorporates all four original commits from @wangmiao0668000666, with author metadata preserved:

- OpenCode: `a9e5c236ca085223477e19680af5889054e7ee1b` (#187189)
- Claude: `89752284e77552985dcc91530f33bf81b415a398` (#187196)
- Pi: `cc1b90af213d07679fc9f92e0eb8eabdef9c43de` (#187204)
- Codex: `f830a4387052971a0e86f3311d1ff0fa933bf198` (#187211)

## Evidence
Detailed native-store setup, before/after output, controls and upstream source citations: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187238#issuecomment-6487341156.

Head `55981f15bff0225b30a16beff523f6ecd45b8cdb`, main `61e0cf581df7cea360bb7670b136e59b8d8105aa`, secretless Node 24.22.1 Linux Docker:

- Real OpenCode 1.19.5 SQLite store created by its CLI server API; real Pi 1.4.0 sessions created by its installed SessionManager; actual Claude CLI-format local project files; real Codex 0.165.0 app-server-created/named sessions with persisted genuine user inputs. No login or credentials were supplied; no successful model reply is claimed or needed for catalog listing.
- Built Gateway catalog dispatch, main twice and candidate twice for every provider: either NFC/NFD query finds one same-form title on main and both titles on head. All providers included; none dropped.
- ASCII, absent/no-query, raw-value preservation, exact-ID reads and first/next-page controls pass. Existing Codex title-only text search remains title-only; its direct ID reads still succeed.
- 176 successful Gateway RPC calls, zero CLI failures; both candidate repetitions were repeated after the Codex post-filter repair. Initial owner checks: 105 tests across seven files. After that repair: 46 affected Codex tests across five files pass, including paired-node and >20,000-row overflow callers; those two cases fail on the preceding head. The original five consolidated regression cases fail on main. Scoped lint and repository formatter parity pass.

Codex sibling source was inspected and pinned before relying on the native format, including its [session-name index](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ce0323f2f2d3b25e82806cd555237da3db4e1897/codex-rs/rollout/src/session_index.rs#L20-L68). Claude files are authored native-format fixtures, not a Claude login/turn claim. Runtime stores contain three sessions each; existing frontier tests and unchanged source protect bounds, rather than a new stress campaign.

## Simplification

Folded duplicate standalone matrices into existing list/read, title-precedence, beyond-batch, cached-title, federated-host and overflow boundaries. Existing assertions remain meaningful. Whole-change production **+2**, tests **0**, twelve files; no baseline increase. The remaining growth is the comparison-only NFC projection and separation from Claude identity lookup; the shared Codex filter now folds its query once rather than once per row.

## AI Assistance

AI assisted tracing, consolidation and isolated native-store/Gateway proof. The four contributor commits and credit are retained.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous text matching; no native store is rewritten or migrated. Blast radius is native session catalog text filtering for these four providers. An incorrect projection could hide or add a textual match; exact addresses, continuation grants and discovery frontiers remain owned by their existing paths.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): New Session project list stays blank when loading fails
prs.body:
Related: #186844

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the New Session project picker looks empty, with no explanation, when `projects.list` fails.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed project list shows the error and a Retry button. A saved project stays selected until discovery succeeds or the user chooses a folder. Start does not fall through to the current folder on a failed first read.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog swallowed a rejected `projects.list` and left the picker with nothing to show. Recording the error as a successful empty catalog would also clear a saved project, which is the protection from #155619. The failure is stored separately, and `ready` still means a successful list. The session-projection identity check that can reject the list is unchanged.

## Evidence

Failed discovery, with the draft still in the composer:

![Failed project discovery](https://github.com/DonnieFi/openclaw/raw/fix/186844-projects-list-error/proof/pr-187062/failed.png)

After Retry, Registered Project is listed and the draft is still there:

![Recovered project list](https://github.com/DonnieFi/openclaw/raw/fix/186844-projects-list-error/proof/pr-187062/recovered.png)

- `vitest run --config ui/vitest.config.ts src/lib/projects.test.ts src/pages/new-session/project-chip.catalog.test.tsx src/pages/new-session/submit-gates.test.ts` — 3 files, 40 passed. The picker test rejects a refresh, keeps the visible rows, shows the error and Retry, then recovers.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.places.e2e.test.ts -t "shows a retry when project discovery fails"` — 1 passed. The mocked Gateway returns `Session projection changed while preparing the listing. Retry the request.`, Retry restores Registered Project, and the typed draft stays.

Closes #127565

## What Problem This Solves

Signal's inbound reply adapter supplies typing start but no terminal stop. Completed turns leave the indicator to expire on the client's timeout, particularly when a `NO_REPLY` turn sends no message that could otherwise clear it.

## User Impact

Signal reply turns now send the existing terminal typing-stop operation for the same target and account. No configuration or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The adapter now binds `sendTypingSignal(..., { stop: true })` to the existing shared reply lifecycle. That lifecycle remains the sole owner of ordering a pending start before terminal cleanup, deduplication, and error reporting. A failed stop uses the existing typing-error callback. The local helper removes duplicated account/target bindings and reduces production code by two lines.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway before/after transport capture and controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187232#issuecomment-6487649056).

- Built main `7f843716fbcba38114489df88eccde60fdd88ef0`: two inbound `NO_REPLY` turns sent typing start without stop.
- Built candidate `c659e5e72b53a7b12013324b58603c456d28713d`: both sent start then terminal stop, with no later keepalive in the 14-second observation windows.
- Normal reply and provider-rejection controls delivered their reply text; candidate also sent terminal stop. A deliberately rejected stop did not block the ordinary reply.
- The normal Gateway CLI loaded the bundled Signal plugin using the existing external-native transport against a local signal-cli-compatible JSON-RPC/SSE fixture and a deterministic local model fixture. This proves emitted RPCs, not real Signal service/client UI behavior. No personal account or external provider credentials were used.
- Contributor's existing regression remains unchanged. No tests added or run in the repair pass (zero-test ceiling).
- Simplification pass retained the focused callback fix: production +9/-11 (net -2), tests +12/-13 (net -1), no new files.

Contributor: @yousan. Original report: #127565.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting fully restores the old callback wiring; no state migrations or persistent format changes. Blast radius is Signal typing cleanup only. A wrong callback could leave typing stale or log a transport error, while reply delivery remains independent.

prs.title: fix(release): surface hidden FRV blockers in status and watch
prs.body:
## Problem

The 2026.10.8 release retrospective (P1) found three blockers that `scripts/frv.mjs` hid:

1. FRV [40394524874](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40394524874): npm artifact producer run 40395590978 failed `Prepare npm artifacts / Check npm package contents` at about 20:36 UTC on 10-26, and the parent's `Qualify release npm artifacts` job failed seconds later. `frv status` only reported plan children, so the failure didn't show up for about 2.5h, until every child was green.
2. FRV [40418292207](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40418292207): GitHub returned HTTP 500 for four child dispatches (`Run normal full CI`, `Run plugin prerelease independent validation`, `Run release checks independent validation`, `Run product performance evidence`). `frv watch` printed one line per failed parent job and kept polling. Nobody noticed for about 1h40m. The failures also landed before the plan sealed, when `status` only printed plan availability.
3. A partial rerun carries unselected failed jobs into the new attempt. In releaseChecks run 40395616917, attempt 2 copied `Gateway E2E / Repo E2E (Gateway 3/4)` from attempt 1. `frv status` showed only `active` for that child and no job, so the carried failure wasn't visible.

The real GitHub job shape also differs from what the watcher assumed. In a rerun attempt's listing, a carried job gets a new id and the **new** `run_attempt`, but keeps its original `started_at`/`completed_at`. For the run above that was `completed_at` 20:56:45Z against an attempt-2 `run_started_at` of 22:01:42Z. The existing "carried forward" label keyed on `run_attempt < attempt`, so it never fired on real data. The watcher also labeled every earlier-attempt listing as carried, because it passed the current attempt.

## Solution

All changes are in the existing owners in `scripts/frv.mjs`. There's no parallel classifier:

- `failedJobEvent` (the watcher's job-failure classifier) now takes the attempt whose listing holds the job. It detects carried-forward jobs from either the legacy `run_attempt` shape or the real timestamp shape (`completed_at` < the attempt's `run_started_at`). It returns a `carried` flag.
- `pollRelease` flags these as blockers when they're newly reported:
  - any failed **current-attempt** parent job, which covers dispatchers, artifact gates and verdict jobs
  - a policy-blocking job in an `artifact:*` producer's **current** attempt
  - a policy-blocking failure carried into a child's current attempt

  Blocking jobs come from the existing `evaluateReleaseChildPolicy`, with the plan's `targetVersion`, so advisory and waived jobs never stop the watcher. These don't stop it either:
  - superseded attempts, which are reported as history only
  - producers dispatched by a superseded parent attempt. The watcher now records the dispatching parent attempt for each child.
  - job names that are still materializing, such as a duplicate row or an unfinished row during a rerun
- `watchRelease` returns `blockers` as soon as a poll reports one. The CLI then prints the blocker and the next step (`frv status`, then `frv continue --failed --dry-run`; an undispatched child needs a fresh all-group FRV) and exits 1. Reported-event state keeps a restarted watcher from stopping again on the same blocker.
- `frv status` adds `blockers`, shown as `blocker:` lines in text output:
  - Sealed plan: failed current-attempt parent jobs, plus policy-blocking jobs from each child's composite attempt evidence. That includes carried failures while the child is still active. Blockers also move qualification to `blocked`.
  - Unsealed plan: failed current-attempt parent jobs. This shows dispatch failures before the seal. If the parent ends without a plan, the existing error now names these blockers.
- Docs: `docs/reference/full-release-validation/continuation.md` and the `release-openclaw-ci` skill describe the new status blockers and watch exit behavior.

Not included, follow-up: retrying an idempotent child dispatch after checking for an existing run. The dispatch and its "not retried to avoid creating a duplicate child" refusal live in the workflow shell (`.github/workflows/full-release-validation.yml`), not in `frv.mjs`. Changing it would grow this PR into workflow dispatch semantics.

## Impact

- `frv watch` also exits 1 at the end of a failing tree, because a failed `Release Decision` or `Verify full validation` job is a current-attempt parent failure. First-attempt child job failures are still reported without stopping the watcher. `status` lists them as blockers.
- `frv watch` now exits non-zero early on these blockers instead of running until the tree is terminal. Operators rerun the same command to keep following; it doesn't stop again on blockers it already reported.
- `frv status` and `frv status --json` gain a `blockers` field. Existing fields are unchanged.
- The watch-state dedupe key for child job failures now uses the listing attempt. With the real GitHub shape this key is unchanged. Watch state written by an older watcher that used the synthetic legacy shape may report one extra line.

## Evidence

- New regression tests use job shapes taken from the runs above. All 6 fail on `origin/main`'s `scripts/frv.mjs` and pass with this change:
  - `frv.test.ts`: "lists failed child dispatches as blockers before the plan seals" (40418292207)
  - `frv.test.ts`: "stops on failed child dispatches without waiting for the parent" (40418292207)
  - `frv.test.ts`: "stops on a current artifact producer failure but not on a recovered or superseded one" (40394524874 / 40395590978). It also covers rerun rows that are still materializing and a producer from a superseded parent attempt. Both of those steps were mutation-checked: they fail when their guard is removed.
  - `frv.test.ts`: "stops once on a failure carried into a partial rerun" (40395616917 shape). It replaces the old carried-label test, which used a synthetic `run_attempt` shape that GitHub doesn't produce.
  - `frv.release.test.ts` real CLI: "lists producer and carried-forward failures as blockers while the tree is active (json=true/false)"
- An independent review found five issues and all five are fixed: superseded producers, rerun rows still materializing, waiver `targetVersion`, blockers in the terminal-unsealed error, and `blockers` in status JSON when GitHub observation is unavailable. Status still learns of an artifact producer failure only through its parent waiter job, such as "Qualify release npm artifacts"; it doesn't read `artifact:*` producer runs directly. The watcher does read them.
- `timeout 900 pnpm test test/scripts/frv.test.ts test/scripts/frv.release.test.ts test/scripts/frv-cli.test.ts test/scripts/frv-cancellation.test.ts test/scripts/frv-proof-broker.test.ts test/scripts/frv-test-exclusions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 319 passed. Wall time is about 61–67s, mostly the existing `frv.release.test.ts` CLI suite. The new tests add about 1s: two CLI spawns at about 0.4–0.6s each, and unit cases in milliseconds. No real timers, sleeps or polling.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/frv.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 123 passed, about 1.4s wall.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed files and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --incremental` are clean. oxfmt check is clean and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Live read-only `node scripts/frv.mjs status` on the real runs:
  - Before the change: neither run showed the producer failure or the dispatch failures. 40418292207 reported only `4 missing`, and 40394524874 listed only stale Release Decision blockers.
  - After the change, 40394524874 prints `blocker: parent job "Qualify release npm artifacts" failure (attempt 1) …/job/121831522997`.
  - After the change, 40418292207 prints a `blocker:` line for each of the four failed dispatchers (`Run normal full CI` …/job/121908927410 and the others).
  - Both runs also list the downstream `Release Decision` and `Verify full validation` failures.
- Not run: full local gates, Testbox, live `frv watch` against an active FRV.

## What Problem This Solves

`policy compare --policy 'candidate.jsonc '` trims an explicit filename before reading it. When both literal and trimmed filenames exist, it compares the wrong file. A missing literal path can also incorrectly report a clean comparison when its trimmed spelling exists.

## What Changed

Return the original nonblank explicit `--policy` argument, matching existing `--baseline` behavior. Operators compare the file they selected, including quoted leading/trailing filename spaces. Missing literal files produce the existing invalid-file finding.

Blank-option fallback, configured-path trimming, comparison rules, permissions, live Gateway enforcement and configuration semantics remain unchanged. No public contract or SDK export is added.

Thanks to @Alix-007 for the report and original fix; their commits are preserved.

## Evidence

[Built Linux CLI before/after evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187218#issuecomment-6487517292): main twice and candidate twice with trailing-space absolute paths, leading-space relative paths, and missing literal paths with existing decoys. Ordinary filenames, explicit decoys, literal baseline paths and blank-option configured fallback are controls. All fixture hashes are unchanged after comparisons.

Focused policy CLI suite: 38/38 passed inside the isolated container. Formatting passed for both changed TypeScript files.

Regression cases are consolidated into existing conformance and missing-file tests: net test-count growth is zero. Whole-PR production delta +1/-1; test lines +35/-12. The contributor's bounded allocation is tightened from 33 to 23 lines.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting fully restores previous filename selection. No persisted state, migration, schema or permission changes. Blast radius is explicit nonblank filename selection by `policy compare`; policy rules and live enforcement are untouched.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep CLI settlement from resurrecting retired native sessions
prs.body:
Closes #186613

## What Problem This Solves

A CLI turn can hand back a native session binding that another writer already cleared or replaced, so settlement restores the retired CLI session and the next turn resumes it.
- Problem: `persistCliSessionBindingResult` re-applied the result binding through the `!preserveBinding` branch unconditionally; the store guard compares session identity, lifecycle revision, and writer run id, but never the binding itself. A binding-only clear or replace during the turn was invisible at settlement.
- Solution: settlement now refuses that write when the result names either the native session this turn admitted or a fork successor it published mid-turn, and another writer cleared or replaced it. Explicit clears, genuinely new recovery ids, and intact bindings still settle.
- What changed: `src/agents/cli-session-store.ts` checks the protected session ids before `applyCliSessionBindingResult`; `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-entry-cli.ts` forwards the admitted binding; the session-store regression covers clear/replace for both the admitted and the published-successor case.
- What did NOT change: `preserveBinding`, stopped-first-turn publication, the existing lifecycle/writer guards, and callers that pass no admitted binding.

## Why This Change Was Made

The writer that clears a binding owns the outcome; settlement must not race it back in, and the fork path publishes a successor that this turn also owns until settlement.
- Best fix: extend the existing settlement guard at the point of effect instead of adding another continuity owner.
- Alternative: compare whole binding objects including `authEpoch` and cursor — rejected because the native session identity decides whether this turn still owns continuity.
- Risk / non-goals: a result naming an id that is neither the admitted nor the expected binding keeps today's write path, so new recovery ids still publish. Recovering a binding that was already lost is out of scope.

## User Impact

Clearing or replacing a CLI session binding stays in effect after settlement, including a fork successor the turn published, so the next turn starts a new native session instead of resuming the process that was retired.

## Evidence

Red on the base implementation and green with the fix, driving the real session store and settlement entry point (SQLite, no mocks). Command: `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/cli-session-store.test.ts`

```text
base implementation + new regressions:  Tests  3 failed | 30 passed (33)
fixed implementation:                   Tests  33 passed (33)
consumer attempt-execution.cli.test.ts: Tests  87 passed (87)
```

Cases covered: the admitted binding cleared or replaced mid-turn, and a published fork successor cleared or replaced before settlement; each asserts the working and durable entries keep the other writer's outcome.

Static gates on the changed files: `tsgo` production core and the agents-root test shard exit 0; `oxlint` 0 warnings / 0 errors; `run-format --check` clean.

What was not tested: no live Gateway with a real CLI turn was executed in this environment. The installed Claude Code is authenticated against a non-Anthropic compatible endpoint, so OpenClaw refuses its native history across the auth boundary, and the turn fails at stdio startup cleanup; that is a host limit, not a claimed result. The regressions exercise the real store and settlement entry point, and the consumer command tests cover candidate admission to settlement.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep/git and the existing session-store harness to trace the settlement path, then extended the guard to published fork successors and added the red/green regressions. The implementer understands the code: settlement may only publish a native session this turn still owns, so an admitted or just-published successor that another writer cleared or replaced must not be written back. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `waitForSolid` for rendered recovery state instead of queued frames or synchronous notice reads. Query the status again while waiting rather than capturing a missing element. Actions remain outside polling. Remove the obsolete frame-wait import and a redundant Discard-presence assertion: the required Discard callback count still fails if the button is absent or broken. Net test-line change is zero; no timeout, retry, skip, baseline or dependency changes.

## Evidence

- **Before:** temporarily delaying the actual `chat-view-notices-content.tsx` module load by 400ms reproduces the hosted reconnect assertion and two synchronous sibling failures: **3 failed / 2 passed**. The temporary Vite load hook returns `null` to the normal loader; it does not mock notice code or values.
- **After:** the final patch passes all **5 tests in 5.49s** with the same real-module delay. The normal focused lane also passed 5 tests in 5.95s before the final redundant-lookup consolidation.
- Focused syntax lint, formatting, independent review and `git diff --check` passed. Native test-line ratchet on base `e1c5147e7cb1` passes with **net delta 0**; main itself is 788 lines above its ceiling, which this PR leaves unchanged.
- Focused execution used the already-qualified checkout at `79c379bebebe`. The startup test, lazy notice owner/content, Solid wait helper, render helper and chat view are byte-identical on the new main base `e1c5147e7cb1`; only this reviewed test patch was transferred. Reviewed-head GitHub CI now reports SUCCESS for checks-ui (1/3), (2/3), (3/3), and openclaw/ci-gate. Those checks were read back, not rerun for this evidence update.
- #182832 was merged while this repair was being prepared. This follow-up addresses the demonstrated synchronization defect; it does not attribute the historical off-roster-route failure to that PR.

Reversible test-only change; no runtime or installation action.

## Application runtime evidence

[Actual source-entry runtime trace and upload limitation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186623#issuecomment-6463895669): isolated Chromium entered through `ui/index.html → ui/src/main.ts`; the real lazy notice HTTP response was held unchanged for 1,418 ms, then Retry reached `chat.send` once and Discard removed recovery without another send. Runtime behavior is unchanged by this test-only PR. An inspected recording and four stills exist locally, but GitHub attachment upload was denied because this contributor lacks repository write access. No media was publicly attached; the comment publishes the actual trace.
