prs.title: fix: message sent mid-turn is lost and the reply fails when the model request is retried
prs.body:
Closes #184909

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a WebChat reply ends with "Unable to finish this reply" (`SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite`), and the second message disappears from history, when a message is sent while the first model request is still waiting and that request then fails with an overload or a dropped connection.

## User Impact

The first message is retried and answered, and the message sent mid-turn then runs as its own turn with its own answer, as [queue steering](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/queue-steering) documents ("each steered user input gets its own delivered answer in order"; after a failed request "the steered message runs as its own turn afterwards"). On current `main` neither happens: the reply fails and the second message is lost from history. No docs change is needed; behavior returns to what the page already says.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the failed attempt settles, the embedded runtime already withdraws the waiting steer from its queue before any model sees it (`MessageInjectionWithdrawnError`). But steer adoption keeps any input whose queue acceptance was recorded as consumed ("a negative final receipt cannot undo earlier native acceptance"), so it never falls back to a follow-up turn. It is written after the failed reply instead, the transient retry treats it as a stale trailing user message, and saving the retry's answer trips the newer-user-turn guard.

That rule exists because, after an acknowledgment, a failure alone cannot prove the input went unused, so replaying it could answer it twice. A withdrawal is different: the queue removal succeeded, which is positive proof. This change carries that proof as `withdrawn: true` on the rejected outcome, and the session controller's input receipt gets `withdraw()` to return the custody the acknowledgment claimed. Steer adoption (reply path) and the controller steer (Gateway path) use it and then fall back as for any rejected steer. Indeterminate outcomes and plain failures after an acknowledgment stay consumed, unchanged.

Accepted edge case: the order released at the acknowledgment is not re-held, so a steer admitted in the short window before the withdrawal can be answered before the withdrawn one.

<details>
<summary>Why the existing safeguards did not help</summary>

- The retry's foreign-pending-input check (`prepareForeignPendingUserTurns`) only covers input still held by a live sender. Here the steer had already been settled as consumed, so it was ordinary history by the time the retry ran.
- The #162439 regression test for this contract was removed in a test cleanup on 2026-10-15; the session-controller refactor (#175837) then added the acceptance rule. The new tests below cover the contract at the steer-adoption and controller boundaries.

</details>

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, before and after.** Isolated Gateway built from `main` and from `main` + this change, scripted OpenAI-compatible model, `chat.send` like the Control UI, no network. FIRST is sent; the model holds request 1 for 8 s; SECOND is sent 1.5 s later and steered into the run; request 1 then returns `503 server_is_overloaded` or the connection resets. Each run first checked the built output for the change (0 files on main, 1 on the PR build).

| Run | Transcript error | Model requests | Chat history afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, 503 (x2) | 2/2 | 2 | FIRST, "couldn't be completed" |
| main, connection reset | 1/1 | 2 | FIRST, "couldn't be completed" |
| this PR, 503 (x2) | 0/2 | 3 | FIRST, answer, SECOND, answer |
| this PR, connection reset | 0/1 | 3 | FIRST, answer, SECOND, answer |
| control: tool step before the failure, main and PR | 0/2 | 3 | FIRST, tool call, SECOND, answer |

With this change the retried request carries only FIRST (the exact request that failed) and the third request is SECOND's own turn. Main logs the issue's sequence each time:

```
[agent/embedded] transient same-model retry 1/8 for stub/stub-agent reason=overloaded
[agent/embedded] Merged and removed orphaned user message to prevent consecutive user turns. ... trigger=user
Embedded agent failed before reply: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <session>
```

A logged run on `main` with tracing in the steer wait showed `agent_settled` → queue removal succeeded → outcome accepted anyway, which is the decision this change corrects.

**Tests (red on `main`, green here).**
- `agent-runner-steer-adoption.question-recovery.test.ts`: new `withdrawn` row in the existing "early ACK ... through a %s outcome" table. On `main` the first input ends `consumed`; here it stays `waiting` for its own turn. The accepted, rejected and indeterminate rows are unchanged.
- `session-controller.steer.test.ts` "keeps custody of a %s steer until a withdrawal returns it to the queue": the existing unconfirmed case plus a plain failure and a withdrawal after an early ACK. Unconfirmed and failed stay indeterminate and consumed on both; a withdrawal returns the input to the queue only with this change.

Test lines are net −2 against `main`: the adoption suite shares its FIFO-followup and enqueue fixtures, and the controller cases fold into the existing indeterminate-custody test.

**Checks.** The 90 test files that import the changed modules pass (1,685 tests, including the steering, queue, abort and follow-up suites); `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass; oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files.

Not covered: a live provider (the scripted model returns the same 503 and connection reset the issue reports), and providers other than an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; this change does not touch request building or transcript order beyond restoring the separate turn. No config, schema or dependency change.

prs.title: fix(minimax): stop result downloads inheriting task private-network trust
prs.body:
Related: #182425 (its follow-up note: "Re-evaluating the existing private-network trust that MiniMax, xAI, and Vydra already apply to their guarded downloads is a separate follow-up")

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a MiniMax setup that trusts a private relay with `request.allowPrivateNetwork` also lets the URLs that relay *returns* reach private hosts.

- **Problem:** MiniMax video (`video_url`, and the `download_url` from `files/retrieve`) and music (`audio_url`) result downloads reuse the task's request policy. When `models.providers.minimax.request.allowPrivateNetwork` is set because the MiniMax endpoint is a LAN relay, any result URL in the provider response — and any redirect from a public result URL — is fetched from the Gateway host even when it points at a private or link-local address. #182425 closed this for BytePlus and Runway ("result downloads inherit neither task credentials nor task-specific private-network trust") and left MiniMax as a separate follow-up because it changes currently allowed behavior.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** the submit, status-poll and `files/retrieve` metadata requests still go to the configured endpoint with the configured policy, headers and proxy. MiniMax result downloads already sent no task headers. A private explicit proxy configured in `request.proxy` stays authorized for result downloads. xAI and Vydra are untouched. No config key, schema or shared downloader change; nothing is written to the user's config.
- Requested by a maintainer/owner? The follow-up is named in the #182425 PR body; no issue was filed.

## User Impact

User impact: with `request.allowPrivateNetwork` on MiniMax, generated videos and tracks still download from public result URLs, directly or through the configured proxy, but a result URL (or a redirect) that points at a private address now fails with `SsrFBlockedError` instead of being fetched.

**Contract change that needs a maintainer call:** a setup whose MiniMax relay hands back result URLs on a private host (including the relay's own host) stops downloading those results. #102072 deliberately applied the request policy to result downloads; #182425 then set the opposite rule for BytePlus and Runway and deferred MiniMax. This PR applies the #182425 rule to MiniMax; if MiniMax should keep same-origin private results, that is a narrower variant (admit only the configured endpoint's origin) that I can switch to.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **What changed:** `extensions/minimax/media-provider-runtime.ts` gains `fetchMinimaxResultDownload`, which fetches the result URL in strict guarded mode without `allowPrivateNetwork`, using the configured dispatcher or the environment proxy, the options BytePlus and Runway use. When the task opted into private networks and `request.proxy` is an explicit proxy, the dispatcher keeps `allowPrivateProxy: true`, so the operator's private proxy host stays authorized while result targets do not. The video (`video_url`, file `download_url`) and music (`audio_url`) download callbacks use it; `fetchMinimaxResponse` keeps serving the task API calls unchanged.
- **Root cause:** #102072 applied the MiniMax request policy to every fetch in the media providers, including downloads of URLs taken from provider responses, so endpoint trust became result-URL trust.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** the existing tests asserted that downloads carry `ssrfPolicy: { allowPrivateNetwork: true }`; they now assert the strict result-download options. `extensions/minimax/media-result-download-policy.test.ts` drives the real guarded fetch in table-driven cases: private video and music results and a public-to-private redirect are blocked, and a public HTTPS result downloads both directly and through a private explicit proxy. The four blocking cases fail on `upstream/main`; the private-proxy case failed on this PR's first revision (the review's P1) and passes now.
- **Review round:** fixes clawsweeper's P1 (private configured proxy) and P2 (test-line budget: the suite is consolidated from 122 to 81 lines; the PR no longer raises `config/test-lines-baseline.txt`: #186785 reserved 8,000 lines (ceiling 6,310,000), which covers this PR's 93 lines of coverage, so the branch takes `upstream/main`'s file).
- **Docs:** `docs/tools/video-generation.md` gains one sentence after the #182425 paragraph saying MiniMax video and music result downloads follow the same rule.
- **Checks run on the touched files:** oxfmt, oxlint, a scoped tsgo over `extensions/minimax/**` (tests included), the line-cap, assertion-safety, test-lines, max-lines and test-timeout-race ratchets, and the docs MDX check. `check-test-mock-exports.mts` was not run (it does not finish on this machine); the one new `vi.mock` spreads `importOriginal`. In `extensions/minimax/video-generation-provider.test.ts`, the timing assertions `Number.isInteger(timeoutMs)` and `toBe(300000)` also failed on unmodified `upstream/main`, under Node and the pinned Bun alike: #186484 moved `resolveProviderOperationTimeoutMs` onto `performance.now()`, so request timeouts became fractional (for example 299999.98 ms). `src/media-understanding/shared.ts` now rounds the remaining budget up to whole milliseconds, never above the operation budget, with a regression case in `src/media-understanding/shared.test.ts`; the whole file passes on this branch.

## Evidence

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** result-URL admission for MiniMax video and music downloads when the MiniMax endpoint is a private relay trusted with `request.allowPrivateNetwork` and traffic goes through a private explicit proxy.
- **Real environment tested:** Ubuntu 26.04 x64, Node 24.22.1, source checkout at `upstream/main` 8ea0a67f4c3, at this PR's first revision 949eb25f9a0 and at this branch. Real sockets only: a forward proxy on 127.0.0.1 that logs every `CONNECT`; an HTTPS MiniMax relay; an HTTPS internal-only service; an HTTPS server standing in for the public host 93.184.216.34 (the proxy routes that address to it, and `/redirect.mp4` there answers 302 to the internal service). TLS uses a throwaway CA passed via `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`; synthetic API key; scratch `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `MINIMAX_API_KEY=synthetic-key NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=ca.pem node --import "$REPO/scripts/tsx.mjs" run-minimax-result-download-proxy.mts "$REPO" tls/` — the script imports the real `buildMinimaxVideoGenerationProvider` and `buildMinimaxMusicGenerationProvider`, sets `models.providers.minimax` to the relay with `request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` and `request.proxy: { mode: "explicit-proxy", url: "http://127.0.0.1:<proxy>" }`, runs one generation per result URL, and prints the outcome, the proxy's `CONNECT` targets and the internal service's hit count.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
# upstream/main 8ea0a67f4c3
video https://93.184.216.34/video.mp4: downloaded "public-cdn-video-bytes"
  proxy CONNECTs: 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 93.184.216.34:443; internal service hits: 0
video https://93.184.216.34/redirect.mp4: downloaded "internal-only-bytes"
  proxy CONNECTs: 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 93.184.216.34:443, 127.0.0.1:<internal>; internal service hits: 1
video https://127.0.0.1:<internal>/secret.mp4: downloaded "internal-only-bytes"
  proxy CONNECTs: 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 127.0.0.1:<internal>; internal service hits: 1
music https://127.0.0.1:<internal>/secret.mp3: Error: MiniMax generated music download: malformed audio response
  proxy CONNECTs: 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 127.0.0.1:<internal>; internal service hits: 1

# first revision 949eb25f9a0 (review P1)
video https://93.184.216.34/video.mp4: SsrFBlockedError: Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
  proxy CONNECTs: 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 127.0.0.1:<relay>; internal service hits: 0
(redirect, private video and private music: SsrFBlockedError, internal service hits: 0)

# this branch
video https://93.184.216.34/video.mp4: downloaded "public-cdn-video-bytes"
  proxy CONNECTs: 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 93.184.216.34:443; internal service hits: 0
video https://93.184.216.34/redirect.mp4: SsrFBlockedError: Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
  proxy CONNECTs: 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 93.184.216.34:443; internal service hits: 0
video https://127.0.0.1:<internal>/secret.mp4: SsrFBlockedError: Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
  proxy CONNECTs: 127.0.0.1:<relay>, 127.0.0.1:<relay>; internal service hits: 0
music https://127.0.0.1:<internal>/secret.mp3: SsrFBlockedError: Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address
  proxy CONNECTs: 127.0.0.1:<relay>; internal service hits: 0
```

(On `main` the music case reached the internal service and then failed only because that service answers `video/mp4`.)

- **Observed result after fix:** running `node` against the real providers through the real proxy, `main` sends the redirect and both private result URLs to the internal service; the first revision blocked them but also refused the public download because it dropped the private proxy's authorization; this branch downloads the public result through the proxy and stops the redirect and the private targets before any `CONNECT` to the internal service.
- **What was not tested:** no paid MiniMax generation against `api.minimax.io`; no Gateway boot or agent tool call — the providers were driven directly. Direct (no proxy) mode was run for the private video and music URLs in the first revision (both blocked, zero internal hits); a direct public download cannot be shown without real internet access.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** the relay, proxy, internal service and the 93.184.216.34 stand-in are local synthetic servers, not MiniMax infrastructure; the MiniMax response shapes are the ones the providers parse today.

prs.title: fix(gateway): align session agent avatar URLs with the agent list
prs.body:
## Summary

- Session identity projection still emitted a bare `/avatar/<id>` for every `looksLikeAvatarPath` source after #182730 fixed only the HTTP handler for unversioned **data** URLs.
- **Narrowed residual:** Control UI intentionally rejects external HTTP avatar URLs (`isRenderableControlUiAvatarUrl` / `resolveTrustedAvatarUrl` only accept `data:` or same-origin `/...`). Projecting remote sources as absolute URLs therefore produced rows the UI can never render. Remote agent avatars stay on the bare Gateway route.
- Renderable **data** URLs now follow the agent-list contract: `/avatar/<id>?v=<revision>` via `gatewayAssistantAvatarUrl`.
- Local path sources keep the bare Gateway route (already served without `v`).

Fixes #182688

## What Problem This Solves

Session list owner/participant avatars did not share the agent-list URL contract for **data** avatars: they missed the `?v=` revision used for cache busting. Earlier drafts also tried to project remote HTTP sources as external URLs; that path is incomplete for Control UI and is dropped here.

## User Impact

Data-URL agent avatars on session owner/participant rows use the same revisioned URL shape as the agent list, so a changed data avatar refreshes consistently across surfaces. Remote configured sources remain on the Gateway-owned route the UI can request.

## Evidence

### Red on base (`upstream/main`)

Main's `projectSessionParticipant` only builds a bare Gateway path when `looksLikeAvatarPath(avatar)` is true. Data URLs match that path check (they contain `/`) and therefore land on `/control/avatar/main` **without** `?v=`:

```text
main projectSessionParticipant(dataUrl) => avatarUrl: /control/avatar/main   # missing ?v=
```

Focused projection + **sessions.list owner.actor** fixture on this branch:

```text
✓ versions data avatars and keeps remote sources on the Gateway route
✓ sessions.list owner actor carries the same revisioned agent avatar URL
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

`sessions.list` row used by Control UI (`owner.actor.avatarUrl`) now matches:

```text
/^\/(?:control\/)?avatar\/main\?v=[a-f0-9]+$/
```

### Real-Gateway UI e2e (registered for CI)

`ui/src/e2e/session-agent-avatar-revision.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` starts an isolated Gateway with a data-URL agent identity, asserts `sessions.list` owner avatarUrl is revisioned, then opens Control UI and requires `/avatar/main?v=...` network loads with 200/304 plus sanitized screenshot/network JSON under `.artifacts/control-ui-e2e/session-avatar-revision/`.

Registered in `test/vitest/vitest.ui-paths.mjs` (`uiE2eRealGatewayTestFiles`) and `test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts` private-server list (serial; owns its Gateway).

Local full private-qa rebuild was blocked on this host (live-Gateway dist fence under `requireVerified`, and tsdown heap/network limits). The `sessions.list` owner path is proven by the list fixture above; the browser e2e is the CI real-flow proof.

### Scope note (ClawSweeper head `be01eb04b0a`)

- Dropped remote-external projection branch after confirming Control UI never loads external avatar URLs.
- Only data-avatar `?v=` remains; remote stays bare Gateway route.
- Added `resolution: null` for `PreparedGatewayAssistantAvatarProjection` in `2fddb062a5c`.

## Test plan / ratchet notes

- [x] Red-on-base: data avatar missing `?v=` on main
- [x] Focused unit + `sessions.list` owner fixture: `src/gateway/session-identity-projection.avatar.test.ts` (2/2 green after rebase)
- [x] Real-Gateway UI e2e file registered for CI
- [x] Local ownership tooling suite after rebase: 14/14 passed
- [x] Local `check-test-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main`: 6246317 / ceiling 6320000 / slack 73683
- [x] CI gateway shard + UI e2e shards (all pass on `c840887d6e8`)

### Rebase onto current main

Head `c840887d6e8` is rebased onto `a4e20a8b244` and is **MERGEABLE**.

- Conflicts were **fixture-only** (`config/test-lines-baseline.txt`), not the production projection. Main still emits bare `/avatar/<id>` for data avatars.
- Dropped this PR’s ceiling bump again: main’s `#187162` restored measured headroom (`6320000`), which already covers this PR’s measured total. Local ratchet OK (slack 73683). No baseline change remains on the branch.
- Earlier `checks-ui-e2e (3/7)` failure was an unrelated flake in `chat-workspace-files.e2e.test.ts` (timeout waiting for Remove notes.md); not in this PR diff. Retriggered via empty commit after that shard could not be admin-rerun.
- Lint stripe `check-lint-core-2` and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` are green on this head.

Commits after rebase:
- `839c3afee3a` align session agent avatar URLs
- `8fd4047419d` `resolution: null` for PreparedGatewayAssistantAvatarProjection
- `70a9f23c2d9` keep remote session avatars on the Gateway route
- `d8ae1e30d18` admit session avatar e2e in ui-e2e ownership rosters
- `069c253f542` read session owner avatarUrl from actor only (typecheck + HTTP delivery proof + e2e repair)
- `d5a53b6806a` prove session owner avatar URL delivery and repair real-Gateway e2e
- `c840887d6e8` empty CI retrigger after unrelated ui-e2e flake

PR CI on `c840887d6e8`: **73 pass / 0 fail** (real-gateway shard intentionally SKIPPED on pull_request).

## Summary
- Target base: `extended-stable/2026.9.33` at `e93b50ad2400871616c2e6588d57488dba94ecad`.
- Backport only the ClawHub CLI security pin from #182010 (`f6c2aeca54e95a6593aec8676034f68aacbcd6f8`), preserving ClawHub `0.23.3` and every other locked dependency.
- Update the manifest override and single undici lock node from `7.29.1` to `7.30.1`, synchronize the standalone materializer checksum, and add a dependency-free regression script.
- Preserve original RoboClaw authorship and roboclaw-bot, steipete, and RomneyDa coauthor attribution.

## Scope
Four files, +31/-5. No shared materializer refactor, Vercel/workflow/cache changes, old-proof changes, root lock changes, package publication, or version bump. The source is #182010, not the later #185194 which already contains this pin.

## Validation
- Regression fails against the baseline (`7.29.1`) and passes on the fixed tree; independently rerun successfully before publication.
- Real standalone materialization succeeds: 47 packages, ClawHub `0.23.3`, expected lock checksum.
- Materialized CLI `--help` and `--cli-version` pass; version output is `0.23.3`.
- `npm audit --omit=dev --json` against the materialized graph reports zero vulnerabilities at all severities.
- JavaScript syntax, Bash syntax, and `git diff --check` pass; full narrow diff inspected.
- An initial smoke attempt used unsupported `--version` and failed; the failed receipt is retained separately from the corrected passing `--cli-version` receipt.

## Remaining gates
Draft only. Full independent canonical review capacity remains unresolved, and required hosted checks/review must still complete before readiness or landing. No review bypass or ready-for-review claim.

prs.body:
Related: #186967

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a claude-cli turn that outgrew the per-turn frame budget reported `CLI JSONL output exceeded 20000 lines; refusing to parse output.` — a message that reads like a **failed task** even when every tool side effect (writes, commits) had already landed and only the terminal `result` was dropped. The reporter's session had completed a 40-minute build-and-commit run; the requester saw an error for work that succeeded.

## User Impact

User impact: the three CLI JSONL flood-guard error messages now state what actually happened — the guard is per-line or per-turn, it does not roll back work already performed, a finished result may have been discarded even though the work completed, and the session remains usable. This is suggestion 2 of #186967; it is orthogonal to the budget-accounting changes in the open PRs #166127 and #160209 (retained-vs-charged semantics stay their scope).

## Why This Change Was Made

`streamJsonOutputLimitErrorText` produced the same terse "refusing to parse output." sentence for all three guard kinds, with no indication of the guard's scope or that completed work survives. The issue's suggested wording asks for exactly three facts: the limit is per turn/per line, work may have completed, and the session is still usable. The per-line variant stays scoped to its single line and does not claim a per-turn scope.

## Evidence

- `execute.output-limit.test.ts`: the two behavioral assertions updated to the new messages, plus a new `streamJsonOutputLimitErrorText wording` describe pinning the three variants' scope words (`per-turn` vs `per-line`), the kept-work sentence, and the session-usability sentence.
- `execute.output-limit.test.ts` and `cli-output-stream.test.ts`: 49 tests green on head `dc0442753d6`; `oxlint` on touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## Risk and Compatibility

- Error-string only; no budget, parsing, or control-flow change. Downstream consumers matching the exact old sentence (log filters, alert rules) would need to update their pattern — a repo-wide search shows no such matcher in this repository.

## LOC

production +12/−5 in 1 file; tests +30/−2 in 1 file. No docs or generated code.

## Not Tested

- No live claude-cli run; the wording is covered directly at the error-builder boundary with the exact limits from #186967 (20,000 lines / 8 MiB).

## Real behavior proof (shipped CLI entry, deterministic, redacted)

Reproduced end-to-end through the shipped CLI entry point (`openclaw agent exec`, which runs the built `openclaw.mjs` → `dist/` CLI) on macOS (darwin-arm64), Node v26.12.1, head `f07b987e4bc`. No network, no API keys, no loopback: a deterministic `claude` stand-in on `PATH` answers the claude-cli probes (`auth status --json`, `--version`) and, for real turns, emits claude stream-json records: turn 1 emits 20,001 ordinary JSONL records (one past the per-turn 20,000-line guard) followed by a completed `result` record that the guard then discards; turn 2 emits a normal short stream. Config was pinned with `agents.defaults.model: "claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5"`; all state lived in an ephemeral `--state-dir`.

**Turn 1 — overflow turn (new wording, exit 1):**

```
[agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 activeSessions=1
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:owner:74f369b551… durationMs=1201 error="CLI JSONL output exceeded 20000 lines for this turn; the turn stopped and a finished result may have been discarded even though the work completed. The flood guard does not roll back work already performed; check those effects (writes, commits) before continuing with a smaller request — the session remains usable." errorName=FailoverError
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 candidate=claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 reason=format next=none
CLI JSONL output exceeded 20000 lines for this turn; the turn stopped and a finished result may have been discarded even though the work completed. The flood guard does not roll back work already performed; check those effects (writes, commits) before continuing with a smaller request — the session remains usable.
[turn 1 exit code: 1]
```

**Turn 2 — subsequent turn on the same runner context (completes, exit 0):**

```
[agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 activeSessions=1
[agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=268 outBytes=63 outHash=2909566a9de1
Follow-up turn completed normally: the session remained usable.
[turn 2 exit code: 0]
```

**Base-red contrast (same harness, dist built without this PR):** the same 20,001-record turn produces the old terse message and no recovery guidance:

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:owner:1473c0fbcbe9… durationMs=1247 error="CLI JSONL output exceeded 20000 lines; refusing to parse output." errorName=FailoverError
CLI JSONL output exceeded 20000 lines; refusing to parse output.
[turn 1 exit code: 1]
```

**Base-red execution of the changed regression assertions:** with the PR test file copied onto base `a58b82fa970` (git worktree, no other changes), all 5 tests in `execute.output-limit.test.ts` fail against the old wording — e.g. `expected 'CLI JSONL output exceeded 20000 lines…' to contain 'exceeded 20000 lines for this turn'` / received `"CLI JSONL output exceeded 20000 lines; refusing to parse output."`, and the runner-level assertions fail with the old messages. On PR head `c6dda1f0c75` the same file plus `cli-output-stream.test.ts` is green: 48 passed (2 files).

Limits: the trace exercises the shipped CLI entry with a deterministic claude-cli stand-in rather than the live claude binary; the flooded variant is the per-turn line budget from #186967 (20,000 frames).

prs.title: feat(apps): show paused child sessions in native chat
prs.body:
Related: #186387

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS, macOS and Android chat show a subagent that paused on `sessions_yield` as **Done**, drop the parent's waiting line when only paused children remain, and hide a Swarm group once its only unfinished children are paused.

## User Impact

User impact: native chat now matches the web chat from #186387. A paused child reads **Paused** in the Swarm widget (outlined marker plus a "Paused" count in the group summary) and in the macOS session sidebar, its group stays listed, and on iOS/macOS the parent's "Waiting on subagents" line stays open for it — naming it with "· Paused", or counting "N paused" — without the parent looking like it's working. A paused child whose own children are running reads **Running**.

Design by josh (@jalehman).

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8cb34bf0-96df-41ab-aa9f-6c710ab3a5fd)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/63387546-d490-4309-8d75-beac336b016c)

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already sends `subagentRunState: "paused"` (#185918) and keeps `status: "done"`; the native projections checked `status` first. Each native owner now applies the web rule (`isPausedChild` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-subagent-wait.ts`) at the same point: the shared Swift Swarm projection and wait resolver (used by iOS and macOS), the macOS sidebar row facts, and the Android Swarm projection. No Gateway or protocol change.

What does not carry over, and why:

- **No elapsed timer:** the Apple wait line never had one, so a paused-only wait already shows no clock. Android has no "waiting on subagents" line at all; it only has the Swarm widget.
- **Post-resume note** ("{name} is paused"): no native surface tracks the `sessions_yield` handoff or resume, so there is nothing to swap. The Apple wait line keeps showing "Waiting on subagents · Paused" while a paused child remains.
- **Android Sessions screen:** it shows no per-child Done state, only Running/Unread/Failed/Attention signals, so a paused child was never misreported there; unchanged.
- **Wear OS Agent Pulse:** the watch payload has no paused state. The phone keeps sending exactly what it sent before (only groups with queued/running work; paused children counted as done). Adding a paused field to the watch is a separate protocol change.

## Evidence

### Android Swarm widget (debug build, emulator, existing `swarm` screenshot fixture plus two paused children)

The capture-only fixture adds one paused child to the research group and a second group whose only unfinished child is paused. That fixture change is not part of this PR.

**Before** (current main, `9a35a81`): the paused child counts as Done (green dot, "2 Done"), and the paused-only review group is missing.

![Android Swarm widget before: research shows 2 Running, 2 Done, 1 Failed; no review group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75fbe620-7320-4b39-91ed-ac172ddc43ae)

**After** (this branch): "1 Paused" with an outlined marker, and the review group stays listed.

![Android Swarm widget after: research shows 2 Running, 1 Paused, 1 Done, 1 Failed; review group shows 1 Paused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/480b2a47-977d-4f2e-ba19-6873f98b51f1)

Not captured: iOS/macOS (no macOS host available, see below) and the Apple wait line.

### Checks

- Android unit tests (`:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` for `ChatSwarmProgressTest`, `WearAgentPulseProjectionTest`, `ChatControllerSwarmProgressTest`, `SessionsScreenGroupingTest`): pass. The new `pausedChildrenReadPausedAndKeepTheirGroupListed` fails with the paused mapping removed (red check run locally).
- `:app:ktlintCheck`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (net delta 0), `git diff --check`: pass. SwiftFormat 0.63.1 (the pinned version) `--lint` on `OpenClawChatUI` and the touched tests: pass.
- **Swift:** new tests in `ChatSwarmProgressTests`, `ChatSubagentWaitTests` and `ChatSessionSidebarRowTests`. This Linux host has no Swift toolchain, so they were not run locally; macOS CI is their proof. I tried a Crabbox macOS lease for Apple proof and screenshots, but its desktop bootstrap stopped with "Sign in to the worker macOS account before dispatching a desktop session", so there are **no Apple screenshots** in this PR.
- Local autoreview (branch vs. `9a35a81`, P0–P2): no findings.

## Worked on by

- @jalehman

prs.title: fix(usage): count only measured turns in usage reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Usage page shows every total as a lower bound (`≥`) and blanks throughput, average tokens per message, average cost per message and cache hit rate whenever a single turn in the range has unknown provider usage. On one large Gateway, 311 of 843,337 assistant turns in 30 days (0.04%) still had unknown usage after #184845, so the cards stayed blank for the whole range.

## User Impact

User impact: Usage totals, charts, ratio cards and exports always show their values. A turn whose provider usage is unknown (a failed or interrupted request) adds no tokens or cost; it still counts as a message, and as an error when it failed. The `≥` marks, the "Lower bound" chip text, the blank ratio cards and the partial heatmap days are gone. The Gateway's separate "partial answer" notice is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tracking completeness through every aggregate cost more than it gave: one unknown turn hid every ratio, and #184845 needed transport- and API-specific rules to decide which unknown turns were "really" zero. Counting only measured turns is simpler and, at the observed rate, accurate to well under 0.1% of turns.

- **One decision point:** `parseUsageCostTranscriptRecord` treats usage marked `usageReport: unavailable` as no usage (no tokens, no cost, no missing-cost entry). The turn's role, error and tool counts still count.
- **Removed:** the completeness flag from usage totals, rollup buckets, quarter summaries, the packed overview rows, the session time series, the shared overview builder and aggregates, the Usage page, the `openclaw gateway usage-cost` output, `/status` and `/usage cost` text.
- **Reverted #184845:** its transport rule and stored-transcript rule are no longer needed. The transport keeps #120008's marker, which other consumers (live context and session status) still use.
- **Cache rebuild:** `USAGE_COST_ROLLUP_VERSION` 9 → 10 (old rollups counted unknown turns as missing-cost entries) and the quarter-summary format 1 → 2 (the totals vector drops its flag column). Old rows are rejected by version and format checks and rebuilt from transcripts; no schema or DDL change.

Accepted edge case: a turn whose usage is unknown but was billed is under-counted by its tokens and cost. That was already true for the totals (they were labelled `≥`); the label is what goes away.

## Evidence

- Independent check on one large Gateway (read-only, aggregates only; 30 days): totals recomputed from raw transcripts (live, cold-archived and deleted sessions) match the Usage page within 0.3% for tokens, cost and message counts. 23,898 turns had unknown usage; all but 311 were requests that failed before any output.
- Tests: all test files that mention `usageReport`, the usage infra/shared/gateway suites, `ui/src/pages/usage`, `gateway-cli.coverage.test.ts` and the affected transport suites pass. Rewritten cases: a session with a billed turn (10 tokens), a request that failed before output and an interrupted turn with partial counters and a recorded interim cost reports exactly 10 tokens, 0 missing-cost entries, 3 assistant messages and 2 errors, and no completeness field; incremental refreshes keep known billing and ignore unknown usage. Tests that only checked lower-bound behavior are removed.
- Upgrade through real Gateways (isolated state, 200 synthetic sessions over 30 days, 550 failed turns). Each source build seeded the state with its own code and its Gateway built the usage cache; then this PR's `doctor --fix` ran and this PR's Gateway answered the Usage page overview request (`sessions.usage`, `projection: "overview"`) and `usage.cost` for the last 30 days:

  | Source | Failed turns stored as | Source Gateway | This PR after upgrade | Transcripts |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `main` at the merge base (`34625635a1c0`; v9 rollups, format-1 quarter rows) | accepted, partial output and counters, `usageReport: unavailable` | lower bound, 535 missing-cost entries | exact, complete, 0 missing-cost entries | identical (34,544 rows) |
  | v2026.10.8 (latest stable) | empty, zero usage (predates #120008) | exact, complete | exact, complete | identical (34,544 rows) |

  "Exact" means tokens and cost equal the fixture truth. The v9 rollups and format-1 quarter rows the source wrote were rejected and rebuilt from the unchanged transcripts (decoding them with the new layout could not produce exact totals). `openclaw.json` keeps every existing key; `doctor --fix` adds only its defaults and migration markers.
- `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-usage-overview-quarters.e2e.test.ts` (real Gateway, exact overview totals through the packed rows) passes.
- `tsgo` (core, UI) and oxlint on the changed files pass. `pnpm check:changed` passes except `lint core`, whose findings are all in files outside this diff (current `main`), and the dead export scan, whose entries are also outside this diff.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` made no changes. Removed English keys: `usage.common.atLeast`, `usage.lowerBound`, `usage.lowerBoundShort`, `usage.unavailable`.

Merge risk: #167275 also bumps `USAGE_COST_ROLLUP_VERSION`; whichever lands second takes the next number.

prs.title: fix: relative time labels overstate ages at day boundaries
prs.body:
﻿Closes #186781

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: relative age labels in CLI/UI surfaces overstate ages at **day boundaries** — the same double-rounding defect class as #186744, one level up. `formatTimeAgo` and `bucketRelativeTimeMs` round minutes, then re-round the already-rounded value into hours and days:

```ts
const hours = Math.round(minutes / 60);            // minutes is already rounded
...
: `${Math.round(hours / 24)}d`;                     // and rounded again
```

So a 2.49-day-old session renders `3d ago` (and 3.49d renders `4d ago`). The chained rounding shifts every `Nd` boundary ~30 minutes early.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw status`, `openclaw sessions`, `openclaw skills list`, `openclaw nodes status`, `openclaw exec approvals`, devices inventory, channel status, the TUI, and Control UI session hovercards/timestamps now render multi-day ages at the correct day boundary, consistent with round-to-nearest (2.49d → "2d ago", 2.5d → "3d ago", 3.49d → "3d ago", 3.5d → "4d ago").

## Why This Change Was Made

Hours and days were computed by re-rounding the already-rounded minute count (`Math.round(minutes/60)`, then `Math.round(hours/24)`), which overstates every day boundary by ~30 minutes. The fix rounds once at the display unit boundary from the original duration, mirroring the #186744 approach: `Math.round(durationMs / 3_600_000)` and `Math.round(durationMs / 86_400_000)`. Behavior-compatible with all previously pinned outputs (47h→"47h ago", 48h→"2d ago", 60m→1h, 48h→day 2, 7d, 8d) and only changes the buggy half-hour windows at day boundaries.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof through the shipped consumers, executed on this branch (fix, `35823dd`) and on the PR base (`upstream/main` @ `e2184d8`) with the same tsx harness that imports the actual shipped modules (no mocks).

### Red on base (`e2184d8`) — actual terminal output

```
== CLI shipped consumer: formatSessionAgeCell(updatedAt) (src/commands/sessions-table.ts) ==
  2.49d (215136000ms) ago -> rich="3d ago" plain="3d ago"
  2.5d (216000000ms) ago -> rich="3d ago" plain="3d ago"
  3.49d (301536000ms) ago -> rich="4d ago" plain="4d ago"
  3.5d (302400000ms) ago -> rich="4d ago" plain="4d ago"
== CLI formatter: formatTimeAgo / formatRelativeTimestamp (format-relative.ts) ==
  2.49d -> formatTimeAgo=3d ago  formatRelativeTimestamp=3d ago
  2.5d -> formatTimeAgo=3d ago  formatRelativeTimestamp=3d ago
  3.49d -> formatTimeAgo=4d ago  formatRelativeTimestamp=4d ago
```

Production dead-code CI reports `isStaleUnendedSubagentRun` as an unused export. Run retention still needs the comparator internally, but its only external caller is a test that also checks the same cases through the retained-run API.

## User Impact

Subagent retention behavior is unchanged: current execution and queued owners, age and explicit-timeout handling, recent completion, and active-descendant child links retain their existing rules. This removes one unnecessary export without changing a public API or stored data.

Keep the comparator private to its existing owner and remove the direct test import/assertion. The existing ended, long-timeout, and unknown-timestamp cases continue through `isRetainedUnendedSubagentRun`, alongside every existing identity and child-link case. The [scheduled dependency job at the original source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40800487319/job/123207281276) reports this exact export. prs.body:
Closes #126227

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a structured failure with an own enumerable `__proto__` field can lose its native Error identity during normalization, causing Error-based retry policies to stop after the first attempt.

## User Impact

User impact: structured error codes and statuses remain available, and normalized failures continue to behave as Errors across retry and bounded-response paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep native assignment semantics while a temporary target Proxy ignores only the prototype-changing field. The original Error is returned; no Proxy escapes. Apply the repair to the canonical normalizer, dependency-free retry package, and two standalone script copies. Their separate dependency boundaries remain intact, and the stricter structured-error isolator is unchanged. Production delta: +32/-12 across four files.

This resumes closed, unmerged #126237 and #176212 after reading the issue's complete discussion and all comments/reviews on both PRs. #126237 closed for inactivity; #176212 was author-closed without an explanation or replacement reference in its public timeline. Credit to @RabbitDong-on for the report, @ruel225 for compatibility analysis, and @McgAtom for the compact native-assignment approach. prs.title: fix(memory): dreaming deep phase promotes nothing when the recall store overflows
prs.body:
Closes #150635

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Dreaming's deep phase never promotes anything once the short-term recall store reaches its 512-entry cap, because the nightly session-transcript ingestion evicts every entry that collected real recalls before the promotion ranker can use it.

## User Impact

User impact: durable memories that users actually recall can now accumulate the multi-day recall and query-diversity evidence the deep-phase gates require, so `memory promote` stops reporting `promotedCount: 0` on installs where a single day of session transcripts fills the store.

## Why This Change Was Made

The nightly ingestion stages hundreds of entries carrying only ingestion-derived signal (`dailyCount`), all stamped with the sweep time. Retention kept the 512 most recently stamped entries and compared signal counts only on a timestamp tie, so recall-bearing entries were evicted before they could be ranked. Those staged entries can never be promoted either: the ranker scores unique queries from `userQueryHashes`, which only an interactive recall writes, so `minUniqueQueries` can never be met by ingestion-only signal.

Retention now keeps entries that carry recall evidence ahead of staged entries. Ordering among equally-evidenced entries is unchanged, so entries still lose their slot by recency as before.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (replaces the synthetic-entry evidence)

The earlier revision proved the comparator with synthetic in-memory entries handed straight to the retention function. That is not the shipped path, so this revision proves the behavior through the real record -> store -> read -> rank -> promote chain. Redacted terminal output from `node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-utils.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` in the PR worktree:

```
[proof] store after nightly overflow: {
  totalEntries: 512,
  cap: 512,
  recallBearingEntries: 1,
  stagedEntries: 511,
  recalledRecallCount: 3,
  recalledUniqueQueries: 3
}
[proof] ranked promotion candidates: {
  thresholds: { minScore: 0, minRecallCount: 1, minUniqueQueries: 1 },
  candidateCount: 1,
  candidateRecallCount: 3,
  candidatePath: 'memory/2026-10-01.md'
}
[proof] promotion applied: { promoted: 1, memoryMentionsFact: true }
```

Read that as the flow a user actually gets: three interactive recalls on one memory, then a nightly staging pass that fills the store to its 512-entry cap with 511 ingestion-only rows. The recalled row survives retention, is the only row the ranker can promote, and the promoted fact reaches `MEMORY.md`.

The same real path is now the committed regression test in `extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-utils.test.ts` - it calls `recordShortTermRecalls` and then reads the persisted store with `readStore` instead of constructing store objects in memory.

### Bounded protection

Protection is now scoped to rows the promotion ranker can still act on. `isProtectionEligible()` in `short-term-promotion-utils.ts` excludes rows that are already promoted, whose origin is blocked, whose snippet is a contaminated dreaming snippet, or whose path is outside the short-term corpus. Rows that cannot be promoted no longer hold a slot, so fresh staging admission is not starved - the regression test `does not let ineligible recalled rows starve fresh staging` pins that.

Rows that are eligible keep their recall priority; ordering among equally protected rows is unchanged.

### Test and gate status

- `node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-utils.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` - **2/2 pass**
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the three touched files - clean
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the three touched files - `No problems in 3 files`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` - exit 0, re-verified cold on the exact tree that is now pushed (the incremental build cache at `.artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` was removed first)

### CI on the reviewed revision

The one job that failed on the previously reviewed head was `check-test-types`, and it **was** caused by this diff: the staged-entry fixture in the new test omitted `userQueryHashes`, which `ShortTermRecallEntry` requires, so the extension test type graph rejected it (`TS2741`). The defect was in the test fixture only, not in shipped code. Commit `3b8d48efee0` adds the missing field, and the job is green on that commit. `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` is green on the same head.

### Note for maintainers

The retention policy question raised on the issue thread is a product decision this PR does not settle on its own: it preserves recall evidence for rows that remain promotable, but how long that protection should last and how much capacity fresh staging is guaranteed remain maintainer decisions. This revision narrows the blast radius of the change (only promotable rows are protected) and leaves those two policy values explicit rather than inheriting them implicitly.

## Notes for maintainers

- The issue thread notes the bounded retention policy needs a maintainer decision. This PR deliberately keeps the existing policy (same 512-entry cap, same eviction count, same recency ordering within a tier) and changes only which entries the cap protects, so it does not need a new configuration surface.
- `userQueryHashes` is used as a second recall-evidence signal because `recallCount` can stay at 0 when a repeat signal is deduplicated while the query hash is still recorded. Both are only written by interactive recalls.

prs.title: feat(claws): add local packages through the gateway and preserve setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Integrations cannot add a converted local Claw package through a running gateway: the gateway Add API only accepts ClawHub coordinates, while an offline writer cannot mutate live gateway state.

## User Impact

An admin-authorized client can plan and add an absolute local package path on the gateway host. Installation uses the existing Claw checks, lifecycle, plugin consent, integrity validation, and rollback. Retrying an installation that rolled back before agent creation preserves its first-run instructions. Imported memory and skills no longer cause the first turn to discard custom setup instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source adapter feeds the existing Add owner:

```text
local package or ClawHub coordinate
  → resolve and inspect
  → plan + integrity check
  → native Add lifecycle
```

Local planning and application require `operator.admin`. Remote clients must transfer their package to the gateway host first. Rollback retires the existing workspace setup state along with a workspace it created and removed.

## Evidence

- Before: local source payload rejected by the gateway schema. After: an actual handler test installs instructions, the exact avatar bytes, and `BOOTSTRAP.md` as an ordinary agent.
- Before: failed Add → rollback → retry reports complete but omits `BOOTSTRAP.md`. After: the same actual-handler regression preserves the setup file.
- Regression coverage follows native Add through first-turn workspace preparation: imported memory and skills preserve a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md`; stock-template cleanup and explicit completion retain their existing behavior.
- Focused plan/apply, authorization, stale-source, schema, plugin handoff, and stateless rollback tests pass. Core type graphs, boundary checks, targeted lint and formatting pass.
- The full build passes, including CLI startup and plugin SDK export checks.
- Live isolated gateway proof at combined stack head `e33e4d5ca2b`: a fresh Stalk Bot installation completed a real agent turn with all 236 characters of custom setup instructions and 3,459 characters of memory injected without truncation. The setup file remains after the turn.
- Real WebSocket authorization regression passes for local packages: admin installation succeeds, nonadmin plan/apply is rejected, and real device-token revocation at the pre-effect gate prevents agent creation and plugin publication. The catalog positive control remains covered. No authority predicate is mocked; assertions cover agent configuration, installed-plugin records, and extension directories.
- Final setup regression and existing workspace sibling cases: 53 tests passed. Final runtime build passed; private workspace-logic changes do not alter the declaration/SDK export surface checked by the preceding full build.

**Merge risk:** reversible code change; affects the Claw Add source boundary and cleanup of newly created workspaces. Existing ClawHub behavior remains covered.

Prior-head CI blocker: the unchanged updater mock check also fails on [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38991549274/job/117275051710); the [native classifier](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38992603758/job/117280609263) marks it pre-existing. That aggregate remains red; no exception or unrelated fix is included. The conflict-only stack restack onto `acd27635` preserves all three core patches exactly; current-head CI must run separately.

Additional private-QA full-build check: SDK declarations exceed the private testing budget. An isolated captured-main build produces the same 456 public-reachable declaration files byte-for-byte (5,440,829 bytes versus the 5,340,536-byte cap). No budget change or unrelated repair is included. Runtime/UI artifacts were generated; the full command is recorded as failed.

Compatibility evidence is scoped to the existing state contract and production boundaries. Compared directly with `v2026.10.4`, setup state remains version 1, `WorkspaceSetupState` fields are identical, and the complete `workspace_setup_state` SQL definition is byte-identical. The PR changes no persisted schema or config format. Existing completed state skips reconciliation; rollback cleanup only retires a newly created, uncommitted workspace. The 48 passing workspace cases plus 5 native Add cases cover retained completed timestamps/content, stock cleanup, concurrent completion, custom pending setup, and explicit completion. This is not a claim that a full product upgrade was executed.

Paired saved runtime proof: before the setup fix (`5ffb1320fcc`), `bootstrapExists=false` and `bootstrapInjected=false`; after (`e33e4d5ca2b`), `BOOTSTRAP.md` injected 236/236 characters without truncation and remained present after the turn. The baseline predates the fix; it is not an exact current-merge-base replay.

## Main refresh (2026-10-27)

Merged current `main` (`cfccaef15a4`) into this branch instead of rebasing, so the stacked #174960 keeps its history. Conflicts were resolved against main's publisher package names, Claw drafts, workspace attestation hashes, and rollback effect leases; the gateway validators were regenerated.

Main's Gateway Add now holds plural state leases (#184784), but its bootstrap setup-state write still requested generic worker admission, so lease admission refused every Claw that ships `BOOTSTRAP.md` ("State lease worker ownership was refused"). `8d64690136b` passes the held lease identities to the worker and asserts them inside the transaction, as worktree capacity does. The existing local Add handler test fails on the unfixed code and passes with the fix; it now confirms the Gateway config-write application, which main's Add requires.

Local proof on `ed5ea8ff143`: 14 focused test files pass (Claw Add plan/apply/stateless/manifest, local handler, Gateway method scopes, workspace and bootstrap, agent creation, state-lease transactions; 2m17s wall with `--maxWorkers=1`); `tsgo:core`, core src test types, oxlint, oxfmt, `protocol:check`, and `gateway:validators:check` pass. The real-Gateway e2e was not rerun locally; PR CI covers it.

Upgrade compatibility after the refresh (ClawSweeper's data-model request): the PR's diff against `main` touches no persisted schema, migration, config, or Doctor file. Its only schema change is the Gateway wire protocol (Add request params and the plan-response manifest disclosure), which is not stored. Lease identities travel only in the in-process worker command. The `workspace_setup_state` table and `WorkspaceSetupState` shape belong to `main` and this PR leaves them unchanged. Existing completed setup still skips reconciliation; a never-completed workspace with a custom `BOOTSTRAP.md` now stays pending until setup completes, which is the intended fix.

prs.title: fix(codex): shed abandoned cleared bindings at namespace capacity
prs.body:
Fixes #125910.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server thread-binding namespace rejects new bindings after 50,000 rows accumulate, leaving later requests unavailable until the state database is cleaned manually.

## Why This Change Was Made

Earlier revisions of this PR moved the namespace to evict-oldest, which let the SQLite store delete binding rows it cannot read: retirement fences, legacy-clear provenance, live leases, and active sessions all ranked the same as garbage. This revision keeps reject-new everywhere and puts capacity recovery at the binding domain boundary.

`session-binding-overflow.ts` wraps the composed binding store's `mutate`, the only insert path. When an insert fails with a row-count limit error, the wrapper pages the worker-backed handle on the same namespace with `entriesInKeyRange` (512-row pages, storage-side ordering, decode in the storage worker) and sheds up to a few strictly validated disposable rows per failure through `observe` + `compareAndApply`, then retries. A lexical cursor persists across calls and wraps at the end of the namespace, so spaced failures keep advancing instead of re-reading the same protected prefix, and rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered. Destructive eligibility is decided on the raw record, not the tolerant codec: a lease in any malformed shape, a retirement marker in any shape at all, and any non-object row are preserved as ambiguous. Everything else (active bindings, retirement fences, live leases, `conversation:legacy-` provenance) fails closed with the original limit error, and hosts without ranged listing stand down the same way instead of scanning inline.

The sync store stays exactly where it was: hot reads. Listing and deletion during recovery run on the worker side of the store broker, so a full namespace never turns into a whole-table decode on the Gateway thread.

Sidecar migration keeps its main-branch reject-new store: at capacity the existing failure path retains the source, and no live row can be displaced by an import.

## User Impact

A namespace clogged with abandoned cleared rows recovers on its own instead of hard-failing every new session. Fences, leases, legacy-clear provenance, live bindings, and every ambiguous existing record are never shed; when nothing strictly disposable exists the limit error surfaces unchanged.

## Evidence

- `session-binding-overflow.test.ts` (17 tests; runs in the database-workers shard on the forks pool for the broker): recovery sheds an abandoned cleared row while an older live binding survives; fail-closed when the namespace holds only a retirement fence plus a live binding; a live lease is never shed; legacy-clear provenance survives recovery while an abandoned row next to it is shed; a cleared row with a non-object lease is preserved while a strictly valid abandoned row next to it is shed; a namespace of only ambiguous rows rejects with both rows intact; a host without ranged listing propagates the limit error with no inline scan; recovery through `createLazyCodexAppServerBindingStore(state, undefined, recoveryState)`, the exact production composition; a scan stalls mid-prefix under a one-page budget and the next insert resumes from the persisted cursor and succeeds (goes red when cursor persistence is broken); rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered.
- `session-binding-overflow.registered-path.test.ts` (new): the real extension entry boots and builds the binding store plus the lazy recovery adapter from `api.runtime.state` itself; the openers delegate to the plugin-state test factories (same worker-backed SQLite stores, fixture module resolution; production additionally needs the Gateway host broker no in-process test has), with the binding namespace cap clamped 50,000 -> 3 as the only knob. Through that registered assembly: a fresh session's lease admission overflows, recovers, starts exactly once, and sheds exactly the disposable cleared row while the live binding and a held row survive; and a caller whose authority is revoked at admission gets zero deletes with the disposable row intact.
- Real run, isolated state dir, production plugin-state store plus the production lazy composition over real SQLite at capacity (3/3: retired fence, live-leased cleared row, abandoned cleared row): the insert recovers, only the abandoned row is shed, both protected rows survive, and a fresh store handle on the same database still shows fence + lease + the new binding afterwards. Verbatim output is in the review reply below.
- `doctor-contract-api.overflow.test.ts`: at capacity the sidecar source is retained, nothing is imported, and the pre-existing row is intact (limit error injected through the production registration path); a revisited legacy sidecar cannot resurrect its cleared thread because the canonical cleared marker wins and the source archives without its row.
- Sibling Codex checkout inspection (`../codex`, origin/main 286d4ecf44): threads persist durably as rollout files plus the state db with paged listing and no retention eviction (`codex-rs/rollout/src/state_db.rs:352`, `codex-rs/rollout/src/maintenance.rs`), so shedding an abandoned OpenClaw binding row can never delete native Codex data.
- Before the final test-lint and format-only follow-ups, the full `extensions/codex` suite, `check-changed` lanes, and fresh `$autoreview` were clean with no actionable findings.
- At prior head `e721d349d2b6c9dca567e240c681829378c8fc45`, the registered-path test lint findings and the two overflow files' formatting were addressed without changing recovery behavior. PR CI at that head was green, including `check-test-types`. The xAI type failure seen at `f8d62fcb212d7adb73e5a51f89a3be618be7623f` was fixed upstream by #177830, and this PR does not change xAI.
- At current head `58efcd3c65f944499b2ff7454f05787e4ecadccc`, the final-delete negative control now starts revocation only after the unbound observation completes, limits rejection to caller-bound stores, and asserts exactly one `compareAndApply(delete)` attempt before rejection while preserving the disposable row. The strengthened assertion failed with zero attempts before the timing correction and passes with one after it. The low-value source-snippet inventory was removed; the registered production-path behavior test remains.
- Current validation: both overflow files passed 18/18 tests in 9.05s warm; the boundary suite passed 12/12 in 4.05s; oxlint, oxfmt, and production extension typecheck passed. Full extension-test typecheck passed with the already-landed #177830 xAI baseline fix temporarily overlaid and then restored. Without that overlay, the local branch reports only the known xAI baseline error, not an error in this PR's changed files.

Remaining evidence gaps: this head strengthens the final-delete negative control but does not supply a shipped Gateway fresh-session recovery trace with real session reset/reassignment lineage, a latest-stable upgrade run, or the maintainer's retention-policy decision. Those gates remain open and are not represented as complete here.

## What this PR is not

This is a partial fix with one open policy decision and no claim to close the underlying issue's storage architecture. Shedding strictly validated abandoned cleared rows is a durable-retention change, and it needs an explicit maintainer decision before merge; the review thread carries the full inventory. The store-level eviction primitive (storage-side disposal by policy rather than a domain-side sweep) remains the owner's call, as does any broader migration of the sync binding reads onto the async handle.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep MCP startup backoff and failure cooldowns on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MCP startup backoff, catalog retries and repeated tool-failure cooldowns currently depend on wall time. A clock correction can reconnect a failing server early or keep a recovered server unavailable long after its intended cooldown.

## User Impact

Configured MCP servers retain their existing elapsed retry windows across forward and backward wall-clock steps. Human-facing retry messages remain ISO timestamps. Display/bookkeeping timestamps remain on the wall clock.

## Fix

Use the existing `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts` owner for core deadline reads and writes, converting remaining time to wall time only when rendering retry messages. No local helper, new retry policy, configuration, SDK or state format. The contributor's original commit is retained.

Clock regressions reuse the existing startup/catalog recovery cases rather than adding duplicate fixture/test scaffolding. Existing Date/performance fake-clock coverage and the performance-based catalog-expiry spy remain coherent.

Related monotonic deadline precedents: #185704, #184711, #184056, #183356. This does not alter the request-lifecycle fix in #184056.

## Evidence

[Captured built-Gateway traces through a real local MCP transport](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187198#issuecomment-6487397647).

- Baseline main: `61e0cf581df7cea360bb7670b136e59b8d8105aa`.
- Candidate: `9d2648c7fd8a3aef2677027110a78ca30519bcac`.
- Ordinary agent turns use Tool Search, tool_describe and dispatch_action against a real Streamable HTTP MCP server, driven by a credential-free local model fixture.
- Tool cooldown, twice per direction: main admits a fourth request early after +10m and still blocks after 61 real seconds with -10m; candidate blocks the early request and recovers after the real cooldown. No-step controls pass twice on both builds.
- Separate startup/catalog transport failures reproduce early and late retries twice each on main. Candidate retains the five-second first-owner/catalog window, with no-step controls twice for each failure kind.
- Only Date.now is stepped inside task Gateway processes; performance/timers and the system clock are unchanged.
- Both frozen installs/full builds and targeted formatting/lint passed. All 62 focused tests pass in Docker, including real stdio cases. Final regression on main: 2 failed, 9 passed.
- Whole PR delta: production +6 net lines (shared-helper imports), tests 0.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the original in-process clock arithmetic; no persisted-state migration. Blast radius is recovery scheduling for failing configured MCP servers. Retry durations, authorization-denial suppression, first-owner early retry, connection recycling, tool policies and catalog publication boundaries stay unchanged.

prs.title: fix(discord): native slash commands fail in a plugin-bound thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native slash commands fail with `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` in a Discord thread that a plugin has bound with `/codex bind`. The Gateway logs `Session key does not contain an agent id; resolve it with the configured default agent.` I saw `/status` and `/codex binding` fail this way on main at da60d41, and `/codex detach` fail the same way on an earlier main commit, 572cb278b243. A plain message in the same thread works. Native commands in a DM or a top level guild channel do not hit this, and neither do threads bound to an ACP or subagent session.

## User Impact

Native slash commands in a plugin-bound thread now run against the same session as in an unbound thread, with the agent that thread's route selects. A plugin command such as `/codex binding` reaches its handler with the thread id and parent id it uses to find its binding. No configuration change is needed.

In an in-process run at an earlier head, 59a4746d, `/codex binding` in a plugin-bound thread failed with `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` and never reached the plugin, while `/status` worked, when the channel routed to a non-default agent and the binding record named a different agent.

One base refusal is not kept, on purpose. With a `match: { channel: "discord", accountId: "*" }` route binding and no narrower scope, `/new` and `/reset` in a plugin-bound thread under a disabled parent failed on main with the session key error. They now reach the existing `binding.channel` recovery exception, as in an unbound thread with that route binding. The failure was the crash and not a rule about disabled parents, so I did not add code to keep it. Without that route binding a disabled parent still blocks `/new`, as a test pins.

The source at v2026.8.1-beta.1, the stable tags I sampled through v2026.10.5 and main has this failure, and I did not run those releases. v2026.7.35 resolved the key to the default agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native route passes the thread binding record's session key to `resolveDiscordEffectiveRoute` as the bound session. That function calls `resolveAgentIdFromSessionKey`, which throws when a key has no agent id, and a plugin binding key such as `plugin-binding:codex:...` has none. The inbound message path has skipped plugin-owned records since #45318, at `message-handler.routing-preflight.ts:57-59`. It treats them as unbound, and the plugin command finds its own binding from the conversation. This change adds the same guard in `native-command-route.ts`.

The guard returns `undefined` where the message path returns an empty string, because the native dispatcher does not treat an empty string as unbound. `src/channels/native-command-session-targets.ts:13` would take it as the command's session key, and `native-command.ts:304` tests `boundSessionKey != null` to bypass the ACP guild guards for `/new` and `/reset`. An empty string would let those commands skip a disabled-parent denial.

An unbound thread takes its agent from the channel route, and plugin binding metadata has no agent id, so the record's agent can differ from the route's. For a plugin-owned record, `native-command.ts` now takes the agent for the session lookup, the plugin command call and the reply recording from `effectiveRoute.agentId`. Other thread records and configured bindings keep their previous agent. Before this, the shared plugin runtime at `src/plugins/plugin-command-execution.ts:58` rejected the mismatched agent and session pair before any handler ran.

Telegram and Slack thread commands use the core runtime binding route, which classifies plugin-owned records, so this change is Discord only. #146898 overlaps on the call chain only. It edits `route-resolution.ts` for free ACP keys, which this change does not touch.

## Evidence

Focused tests fail on main and pass with this change. A local Gateway run on da60d41 and 915f97d shows the session key failure and its fix end to end against a stand-in for Discord, but not the non-default-agent path, which only the focused tests cover. No real Discord client, server or model was used in either, and that is the live gap.

The tests are in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command.interaction-boundary.test.ts`, in a `plugin-bound thread` describe. The change adds five cases to the 16 on main at eb8fa7d, 21 in all. The cases drive the real internal Discord client. REST, session lookup, the status reply builder, the agent turn, the reply recorder and the `codex` handler are stubs. Parsing, access policy, route resolution and plugin command dispatch are real.

- Three cases use agent `main`. `/status` must run against `agent:main:discord:channel:<thread id>`. `/codex binding` must reach the handler with that session key, `args: "binding"` and the thread and parent ids. `/new` under a disabled parent must get `This channel is disabled.` with no context build and no agent turn.
- The work-route case routes the channel to `work` and gives the plugin-owned record `main`. `/status` must run against `agent:work:discord:channel:<thread id>`. The session lookup, the handler call and the recorded reply must all use agent `work` and that session.
- The refusal case has an agent-owned subagent record that names `main` with bound session `agent:work:subagent:bound`. The handler must not run, and the reply must be `⚠️ Command failed. Please try again later.` Before #180173 the shared plugin runtime threw on this mismatch. It now catches the error and drops its text.
- At 8ffec518 all 17 pass. With only `native-command-route.ts` reverted to da60d41, 13 pass and the work-route case and the three `main` cases fail with `Session key does not contain an agent id`. With only `native-command.ts` reverted to 59a4746d, 16 pass and the work-route case fails with `The agent-scoped session key belongs to "work", not "main".` With the agent always taken from `effectiveRoute.agentId`, 16 pass and the refusal case fails. With only the reply recording on the record agent, 16 pass and the work-route case fails. At 99f07dc0 all 21 pass. With both source files reverted to eb8fa7d, 17 pass and the work-route case and the three `main` cases fail with `Session key does not contain an agent id`. With the agent always taken from `effectiveRoute.agentId`, 20 pass and the refusal case fails. Each variant ran once.
- At 59a4746d, defaulting the agent id in `session-key.ts` failed the three `main` cases and returning an empty string from the guard failed two. Dropping every bound session key passed that file but failed `loads model picker data from the effective bound route`. Keeping the configured binding fallback for plugin-owned records passed all 15 and is equivalent, because `native-command-route.ts:53-65` skips the configured resolver whenever a thread record exists.
- At 2b6df40b, whose production code matches 8ffec518, the neighboring suites `native-command.status-direct`, `message-handler.preflight.acp-bindings`, `acp-bind-here.integration`, `native-command.model-picker` and `native-command.plugin-dispatch` pass 6, 2, 1, 31 and 25 tests. The whole Discord extension project, 266 files and 2604 tests, passed at 59a4746d. It passed again at 99f07dc0, 257 files and 2627 tests.
- Test cost, as `docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md:30-36` asks. At 2b6df40b the 17 case file took 16.28, 19.62 and 20.39 s in Vitest. At 59a4746d the 15 case file took 19.15, 26.91 and 27.86 s with tests at 9 to 16 percent, under the 5 s per-file target, and one back to back pair put the 12 case da60d41 file at 15.75 s against 17.48 s for the 15 case file. CI seconds will be added after CI runs.
- At 8ffec518 `tsgo:extensions:test` passes, and `oxfmt --check` and the type-aware extensions oxlint pass on the test file. At 2b6df40b, with `--base da60d41 --no-merge-base`, the line cap, assertion safety and mock export ratchets passed, and the database worker, database dialect and timeout race ratchets, `config:docs:check` and `plugins:inventory:check` passed on the same production code with an earlier test fixture. `check:max-lines-ratchet` failed with `New max-lines suppressions are forbidden` for three `ui/` files. Those files and the max-lines baseline are byte identical to da60d41, and the check printed the same output on a da60d41 tree.

I also ran a local Gateway on da60d41 and 915f97d, and `native-command-route.ts` at 8ffec518 is byte identical to 915f97d. It used the Crabline Discord stand-in, a loopback mock model, fake tokens, and isolated home and state directories. Crabline's Discord driver does not send interactions, so a small local shim injected the slash commands and the Allow once click as `INTERACTION_CREATE` events. Native `/codex bind` and Allow once stored one `plugin-binding:codex:` row with `pluginBindingOwner: plugin` on both builds. Native `/status` and `/codex binding` then ran in that thread. `/codex detach` and the other native commands share the route code and were not run on the fixed build.

| Native command | main da60d41 | fix 915f97d |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/status` | `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` | status card with `Session: agent:main:discord:channel:<thread id>` |
| `/codex binding` | `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` | `Codex conversation binding:` block naming the bound workspace |

The main log has two `Session key does not contain an agent id` lines, one per command. The fixed build logs none, and the binding row was unchanged on both builds.

`.agents/skills/openclaw-testing/SKILL.md:51` accepts an isolated mock-Gateway harness as boundary proof when the live gaps are stated, and `.agents/skills/discord-e2e/SKILL.md:29-31` says a human slash command needs a manual Discord client.


## Additional Evidence

Built Gateway through mocked Discord gateway/REST: main twice fails /status and plugin /proofprobe after plugin binding approval; candidate twice returns status and matching agent/session context. Default-route controls pass on both. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177850#issuecomment-6432527783

### Not fixed here

Unrelated slash-command failures are outside this fix. This additional transport proof covers the default-agent route, not non-default-agent or unauthorized-user behavior.
