prs.title: fix(cli): stop the resume preflight client on interruption
prs.body:
Fixes #187154

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw resume` creates a private Gateway client for its preflight work — the initial connection, the recent-session lookup, and opaque handoff resolution — but nothing owns stopping that client when the CLI accepts Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. The command prints `Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.` and then stays alive on the still-open socket instead of leaving 130/143.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preflight now registers one signal-exit gate. While it is held, interruption aborts the scope, stops and joins the tracked client, and only then releases the gate, so the root CLI keeps the accepted signal exit code. The gate is explicitly released before `runTui` starts, leaving exactly one cancellation owner at a time, and an interrupted preflight returns quietly instead of printing a second failure or continuing into the picker/TUI. All three stages share the same owner: the client is tracked immediately after `GatewayChatClient.connect`, and abort checks run both after connect and after the reads. `client.stop()` is already idempotent, so the normal `finally` stop and the interruption stop cannot double-close.

## User Impact

Ctrl-C or SIGTERM during `openclaw resume` now ends the command promptly with the standard 130/143 instead of hanging with a live Gateway connection and a stuck terminal. Successful resumes, connection errors, and the no-match paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

Observed result first — regression test fails on the base runtime and passes with the fix:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/resume-cli.test.ts --run -t "stops the preflight client"
# base runtime (fix stashed)
FAIL  |infra| src/cli/resume-cli.test.ts > runResumeCommand > stops the preflight client when the CLI signal drain interrupts session loading
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called at least once
      Tests  1 failed | 16 skipped (17)
# with the fix
Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 16 skipped (17)
```

The test drives the real signal path (`installCliSignalExitHandlers()` + `process.emit("SIGINT")`) while `runResumeCommand` is parked on `sessions.list`, then asserts the private client's `stop()` is called, the command returns without opening the picker or the TUI, and `waitForCliSignalExit()` resolves to `130`.

What was not tested: I attempted the issue's real-PTY reproduction with a loopback peer that withholds the connect acknowledgement. On this host the client's handshake timeout closed the stalled connection about one second before the interrupt could be delivered, so I could not reproduce the multi-second hang end to end; the regression above exercises the same signal-barrier and client-ownership path instead.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep, git diff, node, and vitest to analyze #187154, locate the missing cancellation owner in `src/cli/resume-cli.runtime.ts`, and implement and verify the fix. The implementer understands the code: the preflight client is now tracked by a single signal-exit gate that stops and joins it on interruption, released before `runTui` takes over. All evidence above comes from real local test runs.

prs.title: fix(ios): nest child sessions and fold subagent runs in the sidebar
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The iPhone sidebar listed far more chats than the Control UI sidebar. Every child session was flattened into a peer row, and subagent runs — which have no transcript of their own — got a row each. One conversation with two runs and a follow-up chat took five rows in the drawer.

Runs spawned from Home were the worst case: Home is not a session row in the drawer, so those runs had no parent to nest under and appeared as extra top-level chats.

Archived chats were already hidden (the Gateway list is queried with `archived: false`, and the shared model filters archives), so they are not part of this fix.

## User Impact

- The drawer lists the same top-level chats as the Control UI. Child chats sit under their parent behind a chevron with a child count, collapsed until opened, and open automatically when one of them is the current chat.
- Subagent runs no longer appear as chats. Their running, queued, failed, and unread state shows on the parent row (spinner, warning triangle, unread dot), a failed run keeps its error line visible there, and any conversation a run started appears in its place.
- Runs started from Home show their state on the Home row instead of disappearing with their row.
- Pinning and groups still own placement: a chat you pinned or moved into a group stays in that section rather than following its parent into another one.
- The 20-row recent cap now counts top-level chats, so one busy parent cannot push the rest of the list away.

No configuration, migration, or data change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two owners disagreed with the drawer. `RootSidebar.sessionNodes(for:)` flattened each section's session tree into peer rows, and the iOS path never folded subagent runs. The shared `sections()` owner also builds one tree per placement bucket (pinned, each group, recent), so a run whose parent sits in another bucket — a pinned parent, a grouped parent — had no parent row in its own section and became a root.

The shared model now folds runs after placement instead of assuming parent and child share a section:

```diff
 ChatSessionSidebarModel.foldingSubagentRuns(sections)
-  runs become rows when their parent is in another section
+  run -> the row that shows its parent, in any section
+  run badges -> that row's badges          # running/failed/unread survive the move
+  run's own conversations -> rows in its place
 RootSidebar
-  flattened(section.nodes).prefix(20)      # every descendant as a peer row
+  sessionTreeRows(roots.prefix(20), childExpansion)
+  childToggle                              # chevron + child count
+  failed/unread/failed-child subtitle from the row's badges
 RootSidebarModel.sections
+  Home keeps the runs it started (Home is navigation, not a row)
```

Parent resolution prefers the roster's own child link (`childSessions`) and falls back to the run's `spawnedBy`/`parentSessionKey`, walking through intermediate runs that have no row. A run whose ancestor has no row at all (Home, an archived parent, a filtered search) hands its conversations over as rows instead of vanishing with it, which is what the previous iOS behaviour did for them.

The rules come from the Control UI session tree (`ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-tree.ts`), not new ones: runs are never rows, their persistent children take their place, and the owner keeps their badges and attention. `Node.previewSessions` and the run classifier moved to the shared model so the macOS sidebar and iOS use one copy; macOS behaviour is unchanged.

## Evidence

Synthetic demo data only: the app's screenshot/demo transport with a temporary fork-only fixture flag (not part of this PR). The fixture has "Release plan" with a running run, a failed unread run, and one visible child chat; "Trip planning"; an archived "Q3 plan" with an orphaned run; and a run started from Home. iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.2), Xcode 26.6.

| Before (`main` at `dadf912`) | After, default | After, expanded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Before: Inbox triage, Release plan, Collect release notes, Competitor research and Changelog draft are separate rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d72dd15-cc54-4ed6-9e55-eea949bdf352) | ![After: Release plan carries the spinner, failed warning, unread dot and a collapsed child count; Home shows its run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f19c80eb-6330-48cd-9c70-2d8c46f3580d) | ![After expanding: Changelog draft nested under Release plan](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a7b50e1-c367-4831-8b93-b423ce28bd01) |

Before, six chats fill the drawer, three of them subagent runs and one the child chat. After, two top-level chats remain: "Release plan" with a spinner, a failed-run warning, an unread dot and one collapsed child, and Home with its run's spinner. Expanding reveals "Changelog draft" nested under its parent. The archived "Q3 plan" is hidden before and after.

Tests ([fork verification run](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/40807125391)), GitHub-hosted `macos-26`, Xcode 26.6 / Swift 6.3.3:

- **Red on base** (`dadf912`): with only the new drawer regression test added, `drawer folds subagent runs into their parent session` fails — the roots are `["agent:main:subagent:home-run", "agent:main:dashboard:parent", "agent:main:dashboard:other"]` and the parent has no children; the other 82 tests pass.
- **Green on head**: `RootTabsPresentationTests`, `RootSidebarTypographyTests`, `OpenClawTypographyTests` pass, 84 tests including both new drawer tests, plus the sidebar UI test that produces the screenshots.
- **Shared package**: `swift test --filter 'ChatSessionSidebar|ChatCommandPalette'` passes 311 tests in 24 suites, including new cases for a pinned parent whose run sits in another section, folded failed/unread outcomes, runs that only ever hand over their conversations, and Home's runs.
- SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and SwiftLint 0.65.1 (iOS and macOS scopes) clean; `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, markdownlint, and `git diff --check` pass.

Not covered: a physical iPhone.

Prepared by Jorge's AI assistant on his behalf.

## What Problem This Solves

Tracks older chat navigation that uses a moving numeric offset after new replies append, instead of the admitted page's opaque source boundary.

## User Impact

This is an intentionally incomplete regression-only draft. It contains no production repair and is not ready to merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The five real-pane scenarios cover append-safe continuation, staged-page custody during a tail refresh, overlap-only cursor progress, physical-source reset recovery, and disk-trimmed cache restoration without skipping the reader's held boundary. Cursor and around-ID fixtures omit numeric pagination, matching the current server response contract.

## Evidence

- Published regression-only baseline `db4e651`: the qualified native Node 26 run failed all five scenarios at their intended paging assertions (Vitest 5.84s; wrapper 9.72s). No setup failure was counted as a regression.
- An unpublished production candidate now passes those same five tests, plus focused pane/reset/keyboard/loading and history/cache siblings. Its build, type, lint, browser and independent-review checks are in progress; that candidate is not yet included in this published diff.
- Pinned formatter 0.74.0, exact staged-byte/privacy checks and `git diff --check` passed. The 182 physical lines are below the 1,000-line test cap.
- The normal source hook refused mismatched formatter tooling; the actual freshness command separately refused stale `tsx`. The documented CONTRIBUTING targeted-validation exception was used for this signed test-only bootstrap. Neither refusal is reported as a native-hook pass.
- Production is unchanged. Transport, real-Gateway, browser and heap behavior remain unverified.

Scoped maintainer continuation of the chat memory/history ownership campaign; the earlier pagination producer repair is https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186536. No UI eviction, body-retirement, catalog, protocol, schema or configuration change is included.

prs.title: ci(release): run macOS Swift tests in stable FRV
prs.body:
## Problem

During 2026.10.8, a stale backport (#180390 landed without its follow-up #181257) broke `GatewayProcessManagerTests` ("pause preserves unretainable services" [absent] observed an `uninstall`). Stable Full Release Validation [40454025021](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40454025021) still passed, so the regression surfaced only after tagging, in release-ops macOS validation (openclaw/releases run 40486383450).

## Root cause of the skip

FRV's normal CI child, [40454704623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40454704623), skipped `macos-swift` for two reasons:

- For a regular stable target on its release branch, `resolve_target` records `coverage_policy=npm-stable-v1` and dispatches CI with `release_scope=npm-stable`. The preflight env shows `OPENCLAW_CI_RELEASE_SCOPE: npm-stable`, `OPENCLAW_CI_RUN_MACOS: true`, and `OPENCLAW_CI_RELEASE_FAST_LANE_LABEL: false`. The `macos-node-*` jobs ran, which confirms `run_macos` was true.
- `scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs` computes `runMacosSwift = runMacos && !npmQualification && ...`. `npmQualification` is true for both `npm-beta` and `npm-stable`, so `run_macos_swift` and `run_openclawkit_tests` came out false.

Release fast lane and frozen-target capability played no part. The documented `npm-stable-v1` policy deferred macOS Swift to native publication. The macOS app ships from the same stable tag, though, and its post-tag validation cannot block a tag that already exists.

## Solution

Only `npm-beta` defers macOS Swift now. `npm-stable` keeps `run_macos_swift` and `run_openclawkit_tests`. The change lives in the manifest owner (`deferMacosSwift = releaseScope === "npm-beta"`). The `ci.yml` job graph does not change. In `npm-stable` scope the jobs already select the regular `tests` phase plus the `packages` phase (OpenClawKit and Swabble), the same phases main and PR CI use. The `release` app-build phase stays limited to `release_scope=full`. iOS, Android, and native i18n stay deferred for `npm-stable`. `npm-beta-v1` behavior does not change. The step summary now says "deferred except macOS Swift" for `npm-stable`. The FRV reference docs (stages, profiles, extended-stable) are updated to match.

### Why this is not path-scoped to the release delta

The manifest has no previous-stable-tag delta in FRV. The child receives `OPENCLAW_CI_CHANGED_PATHS_JSON=null` with `CHANGED_BASE` equal to the target SHA, and adding a delta would mean new FRV dispatch inputs plus history and tag fetches in preflight. Path-scoping would also save almost nothing:

- Every recent stable delta touched the Mac app. `apps/macos` + `apps/shared` changed in v2026.10.5..v2026.10.6 (18 files), v2026.10.6..v2026.10.7 (13 files), and v2026.10.7..v2026.10.8 (9 files, 188 commits).
- Swift breakage does not require a Swift diff. Gateway protocol models are generated from TS schemas, and the app's behavior tests depend on Gateway/CLI contracts.

## CI cost

This adds two GitHub-hosted `xcode-27` jobs to each stable FRV CI child: `macos-swift (tests)` and `macos-swift (packages)`. Each has a 30-minute budget and they keep `max-parallel: 2`. `run_build_artifacts` was already selected, so the native runtime artifact adds no new build job. No beta, PR, or main-tier routing changes. Stable FRVs run a few times per release, so the added cost is small compared with a post-tag regression that needs a correction release.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-workflow-planning.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 1 file, 661 tests passed; 227s wall time (Vitest duration 224.7s)
- The updated `qualifies $scope ... with deferred native app jobs` cases assert that `npm-beta` keeps `run_macos_swift=false` and `run_openclawkit_tests=false`, while `npm-stable` (release branch, release tag, and numeric correction) matches full scope for `run_macos_swift=true` and `run_openclawkit_tests`. Both scopes still assert that iOS, Android, and native i18n stay deferred.
- CI seconds: no new tests. The existing parameterized cases run under the same fixture.

## Notes

- FRV runs the manifest from the candidate's own harness checkout. Existing release branches keep the old behavior until this change is backported to them.
- An already-green `npm-stable` normal CI child for the same SHA could still be adopted through child evidence reuse. New dispatches pick up the change.

prs.title: docs(release): bound backport porting workers and require follow-up search
prs.body:
## Problem

The 2026.10.8 release retrospective (openclaw/maintainers `release/retrospectives/2026.10.8.md`, findings 1, 2 and 4) traced most of its lost time to how backport porting was delegated:

- Up to 17 concurrent writing lanes saturated the host (load average 66). When the session usage limit hit, 16 lanes died mid-port with uncommitted work.
- The lead ended a turn waiting on one lane, and nothing happened for 23.6 hours.
- A "fast" finishing brief dropped the follow-up search. Missing follow-ups (for example #183286 without `74dfd5e64aaf`, and #180390 without #181257) caused most FRV failures, plus a macOS regression found only after tagging.

## Solution

Adds a "Port with Bounded Workers" section to the release skill's backport reference:

- At most eight concurrent writing workers; read-only auditors may still fan out.
- No nested agents unless the brief allows them.
- The lead watches every worker and dispatches validation once the required fixes and P0s are in.
- A per-pick worker brief:
  1. Run the existing `release:backport-companions` audit plus a `--grep '#<PR>'` search, with dispositions in the commit body.
  2. Confirm the defect exists on the baseline.
  3. Cherry-pick with `-x` and note any `Release adaptation:`.
  4. Run targeted, `timeout`-wrapped checks only.
  5. Commit and update the lane report after each pick, time-boxed to about 40 minutes.

`SKILL.md` routing now names the worker brief.

## Impact

Docs and skill guidance only; no runtime or CI behavior changes.

## Evidence

`git diff --check` is clean, and the pre-commit formatter passed.

prs.title: fix(doctor): exit nonzero when requested repairs stay blocked
prs.body:
Fixes #187122

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw.json` cannot be parsed (or Doctor recovery leaves the database target unresolved), `openclaw doctor --fix` reports every section as `unknown`, runs **zero** state repairs or migrations, prints `Doctor complete.` and exits **0**. Fleet scripts that gate restarts on `doctor --fix` exit status cannot tell "migrated" from "did nothing" and restart gateways onto unmigrated state, which is the incident in the issue.

## User Impact

- `doctor --fix` / `--repair` / `--yes` now exit **1** when the requested repairs could not run because config or the database target is unresolved, and the outro says `Doctor stopped. Requested repairs were not applied.`
- Inspection-only `doctor` (no repair flag) keeps exit 0, `doctor --lint` keeps exit 2, and healthy or recoverable configs are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's next step on the issue: "Make unresolved requested repairs return nonzero and establish a failing CLI regression with malformed configuration and closed stdin." All three unresolved-target paths in `src/cli/database-engine-selection.ts` end in `reportDoctorUnresolvedEngine()`, which only set an exit code for `--lint`. The fix sets `process.exitCode = 1` there whenever a repair was requested, reusing the same flag set (`--fix`, `--repair`, `--yes`) that already gates file-only config recovery in `prepareDoctorEngineSelection()`.

Scope: this covers the invalid-config facet. The TTY-only facet (`awaits its database schema repair` under closed stdin with a *parseable* config) is not reproduced here; with a valid config and `</dev/null` this rig ran all 156 Doctor steps and exited 0.

## Evidence

Local live run on Windows 11, Node 26.12.1: `node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive </dev/null` against an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` with the configs from the report, on main `f0401d5` and on this branch `3f7075c`, same rig.

![doctor exit codes main vs fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/187122/proof-187122.png)

| config | command | main exit | fix exit | "Doctor:" repair steps run (fix build) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| unparseable JSON (`,,}`) | `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | **0** | **1** | 0 (all repairs skipped) |
| unparseable JSON | `doctor --non-interactive` (no repair requested) | not rerun | 0 | inspection only |
| keys from the report (`gateway.channelStaleEventThresholdMinutes`, `agents.defaults.memorySearch`) | `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | 0 | 0 | 165 |
| `env.TAILSCALE_API_KEY` object | `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | not recorded (151 steps ran) | 0 | 152 |
| valid | `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | 0 | 0 | 156 |

Regression (`src/cli/database-engine-selection.test.ts`): a malformed config with `doctor --fix --non-interactive` must set exit code 1 while `doctor --non-interactive` leaves it unset, and the existing unresolved PostgreSQL credential case now asserts exit code 1. With the source fix reverted: `2 failed | 145 passed`; with the fix: `147 passed`.

Checks run locally: `oxfmt`, `oxlint` on changed files, `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm check:assertion-safety`.

### Upgrade from latest stable (existing settings and data)

State seeded by the published `openclaw@2026.10.8` (npm, `dc2523e`), then the candidate (`5b7f481`, this PR merged with current main) run on that same isolated state. Each step is `doctor --fix --non-interactive </dev/null`; the fingerprint is a sha256 over every state file except `openclaw.json`, WAL/SHM and logs.

![upgrade from stable 2026.10.8 to candidate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/187122/proof-187122-upgrade.png)

| step | build | config | exit | existing settings and data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | stable 2026.10.8 | valid; then `config set agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds 321` and `gateway.auth.mode none` | 0 | state created (7 files) |
| 2 | stable 2026.10.8 | operator typo, file ends `,,}` | 1 | released build takes a different path: best-effort read, then "Doctor could not complete maintenance" |
| 3 | **candidate** | same broken file | **1** | no repairs attempted; state fingerprint `a9ba2c6e8541` unchanged from step 2; config byte-identical |
| 4 | **candidate** | typo fixed | **0** | 156 Doctor steps ran (upgrade migrations); `timeoutSeconds=321`, `auth.mode=none` read back unchanged |

Branch now merges current main (`44ffd0a`). The earlier `check-lint-core-2` failure was `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts:722` (`curly`), a file this PR does not touch.

prs.title: fix: long streamed replies that quote tool-call transcripts no longer stall the Gateway
prs.body:
Fixes #186601

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes long streamed answers that quote legacy `[TOOL_CALL]`, downgraded `[Tool Call: ...]`, or historical transcript markers repeatedly parsing the whole reply and stalling the Gateway.

## User Impact

Quoted transcript examples stay visible and stream promptly. Unquoted scaffolding is still removed, including after a fenced block leaves a list or blockquote. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The filters now reuse the existing container-aware Markdown checkpoint owner, moved into the code-region module. Each canonical removal pass retains its own input context because a removal can itself expose a fence; blank container prefixes are reparsed when their content arrives. Incomplete candidates stay pending, while settled text stops participating in later scans. Downgraded history keeps its existing activation-dependent trimming through the existing trim projector. This also removes the separate resolver introduced earlier in this PR, whose fence extension lost list/blockquote context.

Thanks @JasonBuildAI for the report, original implementation, and reproduction workloads. All contributor revisions are preserved through merges, including their added angle-link and later-code-region regressions.

## Evidence

Shipping `createAssistantVisibleStreamText("final_answer")`, four-character deltas, exact canonical output and delta reconstruction:

| Quoted fixture | Main parsed characters, 8 / 16 / 32 KiB | Candidate parsed characters, 8 / 16 / 32 KiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Legacy tool transcript | 16,785,006 / 67,124,651 / 268,467,237 | 348 / 348 / 348 |
| Downgraded transcript | 33,568,848 / 134,248,528 / 536,934,480 | 1,239 / 1,239 / 1,239 |

Five alternating main/candidate runs at 8 KiB: legacy median 2,665 → 21 ms (p95 4,069 → 22 ms), downgraded median 2,842 → 26 ms (p95 3,552 → 28 ms). At 32 KiB the initial main samples took 56.1 / 53.3 seconds; five candidate samples had medians 42 / 102 ms. Timings are from a shared macOS host; parser counts are deterministic.

- Angle-destination closure and inline-code prose are also covered; the latter scans 649,057 / 1,323,719 / 2,675,127 characters at 8/16/32 KiB, retaining linear growth. Both list/blockquote exit regressions failed on the contributor head and now match the canonical sanitizer. The work regressions fail on main. An additional 92 LF/CRLF fixtures passed 10,230 prefix/delta comparisons, covering split markers, inline/fenced/container code, image labels, link titles, and hidden payloads; 75 angle/container variants passed another 7,138 prefix/reconstruction checks.
- 491 focused and consumer tests passed in 44.47 seconds, covering visible-text projection, agent helpers, reasoning/final tags, and tool-call XML. After the final angle/container fix and contributor merges, all 108 streaming tests passed again in 22.47 seconds; core typecheck remains green.
- Full `pnpm build`, targeted lint, core typecheck, formatting, and all baseline ratchets passed. The existing over-ceiling test total does not grow; no baseline was raised.
- Isolated built Gateway over WebSocket on the final head: nine synthetic responses (legacy/downgraded at 8/16/32 KiB, adjacent/spaced/blockquote-continuation angle destinations at 8 KiB) matched complete streaming delivery and canonical final text. The 32 KiB cases finished in 646 / 653 ms; the quoted-angle case in 411 ms. A real `qwen2.5:7b` turn quoted both marker families and repeated paragraphs, completing in 3.24 s with exact canonical final bytes; its natural preview was a correct prefix, with the remaining 35 bytes delivered in the final snapshot. No preview-coalescing change is claimed.
- Independent Codex review is scoped-clean through P2; earlier exposed-fence and angle-container findings were reproduced and fixed. The final contributor merge changes commit ancestry only: its full source tree is byte-identical to reviewed/built/tested `517691d00dd7b5904b071a0ac40a12e88907f2b3`.

The final source delta is +202/-62 (net +140), reduced from the original net +248; test delta is +63/-63 (net 0). Redundant test scaffolding was consolidated into existing boundary suites. The test-line ceiling increase was reverted. The remaining source growth carries checkpoint/candidate metadata and preserves the existing trim contract; no second Markdown owner remains.

Validation is local macOS. The separate inline-code duplicate-paragraph issue #186598 is handled independently.

prs.title: fix(doctor): unblock historical store imports without losing evidence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor refuses historical pending-input and worker-placement stores, or leaves historical image reserves unreadable after import.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can import recognized agent-v24, shared-v21 and image-v22 stores without discarding historical evidence or cleanup custody.

Queued inputs become interrupted without losing payloads or recovery envelopes. Incomplete preparation becomes a failed placement requiring cleanup. Incompatible worker claims or malformed images refuse the atomic migration without advancing markers or discarding custody.

**PostgreSQL limitation:** archival input/placement columns are not in the PostgreSQL descriptor. Their port is refused before target publication; keep these stores on SQLite. Image-only data uses existing JSON storage and was ported in earlier proof. **Rollback requires the verified pre-migration backup and matching runtime—not lowered version markers.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing migration and Doctor owners preserve predecessor evidence and derive missing predicates before publication, including the full-schema fallback selected by unrelated lazy-column gaps. Archives never grant execution authority; fresh databases do not acquire them. No P3 schema bump or second migration owner is added.

Contributor credit: based on @galiniliev's reviewed historical-import work in selected commit `d0cce88f317` and the approved preservation-only plan, adapted to current main.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d0705165-5352-4f6e-955d-99ab0c2be386)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4d70f9f4-e855-496c-9675-8bc6b7cda6dc)

## Evidence

**Published head:** f250485b753d6e7b93913a556698d6b96ec3a87a; tree 6438234a7e8de822db6901f8772229c13a575b49. Reviewed/tested source: 5a45a62beb295307b3bdc86d50dce07c5b9a7f33. **Current-head CI/platform checks passed; landing is still blocked by the removal scans below.** [CI 40808553345](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40808553345) (`ci.yml`, attempt 1) completed with **83 successful and 24 skipped jobs**. Separate [Darwin 40808553387](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40808553387) also passed. Complete paginated readback at 2026-10-29 03:13 UTC found **170 terminal check runs: 102 successful, 67 skipped, 1 neutral**, plus all **3 latest status contexts successful**. Initial dependency/security failures were publisher placeholders stating “Security review has not completed”; the same-head publisher superseded them with success, not a vulnerability waiver. The durable hosted review still refers to 09ebc74, not this head; no fresh hosted verdict or re-review request is claimed.

Four critical scenarios remain:
1. Real ordinary-CLI import and restoration of its original Doctor backups: full input/placement rows, image bytes, physical/metadata markers and pending-placement fencing.
2. Live worker-claim refusal without losing custody.
3. Publication failure, atomic rollback and retry preserving rows, rowids, leases and dependent cleanup records.
4. Ordinary-open v22 conversion with the lazy-column gap that reproduced the P2/P3 defect, including malformed-image rollback, correction/retry and exact archive/custody preservation.

**Renewed on this head:** CLI/backup restoration passed in **45.271s / 83.86s wrapper wall**, with the unchanged **90s guard**. Child exit/EOF and local reader closure precede restoration; cleanup settled. All **3 migration-owner cases** and **4 targeted older-service admission cases** pass. The latter cover ordinary/flag-only refusal and admitted candidate/rehearsal migration, not the entire sibling suite. Doctor/state types, targeted lint/format and diff checks pass.

**Review and budget:** local autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, P0–P2) found no actionable issue. Review is reused for the identical authored patch after integration of 44ffd0a845b32480ffaf46ff6cfbcaa2267491c1 ([#187162](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187162)), not claimed for every upstream change. **6,246,427 / 6,320,000** passes; the ceiling is inherited verbatim, not edited by P3. P3's eligible delta is +505.

**Deliberate coverage cuts:** @galiniliev's critical-only direction removed another 481 eligible lines: the duplicate Gateway/model/RPC/restart harness, granular predicate/index/trigger/idempotence/CHECK and unknown-column variants, extra image admission variants and declaration microtests. There is **no ongoing historical cold-Gateway test**. Authentic fixtures and existing chronology/backup coverage remain; critical backup restoration is now in ordinary CLI coverage. Diagnostic-only repair b03add185 is preserved separately, not in this feature delta. The Bun-parent diagnostic limitation and original timeout remain unresolved here.

**Landing remains blocked: removal scans have 0/7 verdicts.** Offline Knip 6.40.0 and the actual dependency gate stopped before scanning on uncached strip-json-comments@5.0.3; no download or tool substitution followed. Ordinary PR CI removes the job (scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs:1567–1569), with no changed-lint replacement. A qualified route is still needed for two dependency, two unused-file and three unused-export phases.

Historical **60/90s CLI failures and native-borrower teardown remain unexplained**. Passing replays are not a flake classification or proven fix. Material evidence and limits follow.

<details>
<summary>Historical regression, published-updater and CI evidence—not current-head CI</summary>

### Conversion regression

An isolated P3 bd542 + reviewed P2 a77858c57e76a1174f866c92a68d3d2e8bfaf3be composition repaired secret_store_entries.allowed_hosts and published schema 36 but left the v22 image unconverted. P3 alone and Doctor preparation converted it. Repair d2f3689 invokes historical conversion before full publication; composed regressions passed. The reduced test also fails when that call is omitted and passes with the real owner. Scratch inputs were restored.

Earlier native CLI proof reproduced v21's missing-predicate failure and agent-v24's recovery-column refusal before repair. Authentic historical fixtures—not relabeled current schemas—establish the inputs.

### Real published-driver update at c621

The installed **published 2026.10.8 updater** updated to **c62102e1a78f13f43210c8cb4f771b0fde989e13**. Both packages carried 2026.10.8; no version relabeling occurred. Candidate tarball SHA-256: **c068f2fe4d4212a748bbc7d2e55f66328219046df70651a3679576a11e1cce7c**.

An approved, isolated non-root Podman adaptation ran the unmodified harness from 8889b596023c846cc9076078a000c25715f0ecf0 without provider credentials or operator state. The real update and durable run succeeded in **296.80s**; version/build matched, service PID changed and readiness returned **200**. Durable history/sidecar survived; incognito history did not.

Scoped restore intentionally failed a malformed sibling while a healthy agent reached **38**, then restored that agent to **26**. Both outbox rows/order and a later unrelated cache write survived. The expected malformed-fixture exit 1 was not an overall failure; harness/service cleanup exited zero and task containers/volumes were absent at closeout.

**Limits:** historical Podman proof, not Docker/cross-platform parity or a new 5a45 updater run. The generic harness lacked P3's exact v21/v22/v24 fixtures. Providers/channels were disabled; injected messages are not live-model proof. Full port CLI/config switching and paid/live providers were untested. No credential-hydrating workflow was dispatched or operator service changed. Fixture setup corrections preserved assertions/deadlines.

### Historical Gateway and PostgreSQL

At c621, two cold Gateways shared the migrated database. Public reads showed the image/interrupted input; two new synthetic-HTTP-model turns completed with **zero historical-input model requests**. Doctor backups were restored and re-migrated after shutdown. That test is retired, not ongoing or renewed 5a45 proof. Initial setup required fixture-only loopback proxy exclusions.

Earlier PostgreSQL **17.11** proof covered canonical sibling ports, archival-column refusal and image-only transfer of 133 tables with exact JSON. Missing profile-table prerequisites were resolved through real profile-owner bootstrap. This is not archival-column support, full port CLI/config switching or fresh post-integration PostgreSQL proof.

### Prior failures and review

- [CI 40650404406](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40650404406), ca3c: test-lines, native-borrower teardown and aggregate failure. Unchanged local replays did not establish a fix or inherited classification. Upstream [bec3ad81](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bec3ad81da5568e05e5e55219b00c72bb4ee6e0a) later supplied maintenance-before-shared-state cleanup; the borrower guard remains and original uncertainty is not erased.
- [CI 40725668501](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40725668501), bd542: five CLI guards—three agent-ordering cases and July upgrade at **60s**, historical v21 at **90s**—during unfinished Doctor phases, not demonstrated exit hangs. Classification was **unknown: no matching main job**. Local passing replays used the pinned Bun fork and Node **26.12.1**, versus CI Node **24.22.1** and a different synthetic merge; they did not fix those failures.
- The final 60cf local sentinel also hit **90s** at legacy-state-migrations before completion/payload assertions. Its main thread and another thread were in D-state at handle_reserve_ticket on Btrfs. Exact operation, duration and cause remain unknown: an I/O hypothesis, not a filesystem defect or flake verdict. Separately retained b03 proved a Bun-parent/Node-child diagnostic blind spot and repaired that helper, not the timeout. Instrumented and current CLI passes do not settle the cause.
- [CI 40746693721](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40746693721), 3805: then-current budget and aggregate failure. Separate [Darwin 40746692959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40746692959) used a newer workflow selecting test/scripts/pr-git-invocation.test.ts absent from the older PR checkout; no assertion ran. The upstream tooling closure was integrated; the separate current-head Darwin pass is recorded above. The absence of Node leaf failures in that run does not establish that the earlier timeouts were fixed.

The wrapper-inventory and chronology-backup findings in [the older hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186603#issuecomment-6462955147) were repaired in ef201382. That review remains prior-head evidence, not a new verdict; no duplicate hosted review or CI rerun was requested. Local source reviews are not independent execution of every historical proof.

</details>

## Worked on by

- @galiniliev

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: September-line update checks can recopy private rehearsal databases, reopen candidate-migrated state, and keep stale restart advice; its release fixtures can lose Doctor diagnostics or race plugin-reload settlement.

## User Impact

Prepares the applicable consolidated backports for the upcoming **2026.9.36** patch on `extended-stable/2026.9.33`, without changing the release version or publishing anything. The original update outcomes and migration rollback restrictions remain authoritative. No public Plugin SDK/config-schema expansion, dependency changes, or operator migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The requested `release/2026.9.33` ref does not exist; `extended-stable/2026.9.33` is the existing maintenance branch. This is a bounded audit of #181924/#181927 and the twelve closed old-cut PRs, not a claim of a complete current-main or security release inventory.

Baseline: `facd3f9494d64eb3d12be1b7e9399d965c9b6435`.

### Existing Batch 5 is already covered

Closed #181920 states all 29 commits were cherry-picked into the September line for 2026.9.35. All 29 full source SHAs have unique cherry-pick trailers on the baseline: 28 have identical stable patch IDs; the remaining workflow-contract commit differs only by intentionally omitting its native Swift generated-model hunk. The existing candidate-provenance fix is represented by #181427. Do not replay this batch or restore its earlier workflow defects. The prepared SDK compiler-loader repair is already present in `7e0d495eb3c`.

### Disposition of all twelve old-cut PRs

| Source PR | September-line disposition |
| --- | --- |
| #170736, #170753 | Carry the shared snapshot/config-capture/migration-verification/update-report contracts once, adapted to this line's existing reader architecture. |
| #166828, #166892 | Carry RPC-owned watcher and recovered-runtime config settlement using the existing Chokidar adapter; inbound writer ordering already covered by #171531. Remote executable catalog and deferred startup-maintenance owners are absent here, so do not import their features or barriers. |
| #166817, #166882 | Carry the canonical shell survivor roster once. Retained Fleet cgroup-manager/OCI diagnostic repairs are already present through `b899f42513bd` / #166977; no Fleet code or host runtime change. |
| #166855, #166882 | Carry bounded/redacted Doctor lint capture, stale-attempt reset, and the existing stderr-preserving onboarding failure handler once. |
| #166890, #166813 | Carry only the font-fixture before/after reset; inbound writer completion is already covered, and October asynchronous model-placement worker routing is not applicable to this line. |
| #166850 | Not affected: asynchronous remote-catalog owner and fixture are absent. |
| #166825 | Not affected by the October-only QA barrel, worker/identity and redaction-prefilter migrations; the older QA owner still exists. Preserve branch-local fixtures and contracts. |
| #166794 | Not affected: production temp-root owner and fixture still use the same `@openclaw/fs-safe/temp` export, not October's focused resolver. |

Peter Steinberger retains source author credit for the update/runtime and font fixture backports; Dallin Romney retains author credit for the survivor/Doctor/lifecycle proposals.

Source fixture proposals #166802/#166823 were not merged on main; these are explicitly requested relevant proposal consolidations, not a claim of canonical-main landing. Their historical full-Docker/original-shard proof holds are not cleared by focused passes.

### Scope and simplification

Reuse the existing config capture, read-only snapshot, verification, report, diagnostics and lifecycle-test owners. Remove the survivor helper's obsolete roster down-conversion; keep published-baseline version adaptation. Share the existing Chokidar fixture in test support, without importing October's new observer or adding a runtime seam. Preserve existing assertions and deadlines.

## Evidence

- Harness red-on-baseline: four expected failures (canonical roster, Doctor lint capture, stale-attempt reset, redirected Doctor stderr), 66 passes.
- Fixed harness: **70/70 passed** across survivor-state, diagnostics and onboarding shell suites; 26.44s wrapper / 25.54s Vitest.
- Complete Gateway lifecycle file: **8/8 passed**, including cleanup rejection and timeout recovery (57.92s Vitest; the real Gateway/runtime boundary accounts for the existing suite cost).
- Font fixture: **23/23 passed** (1.47s Vitest); unmodified Google Meet gateway fixture: **12/12 passed** (8.64s Vitest), confirming that October-specific fixture adaptation is unnecessary here. Combined three-shard wrapper: 71.81s.
- Targeted Gateway-server, scripts, and root-script test typechecks passed. Harness/core/root-test/script lint, shell syntax, changed-file formatting and whitespace checks passed.
- Initial independent P0–P2 review identified a same-version Git-update false reconciliation in the imported report change; the corrected report requires distinct known before/after versions, and a same-version/different-SHA regression fails before that correction and passes afterward.

- Runtime suite results: 8 advisory + 4 capacity-refusal cases passed; final readonly/report rerun **112 passed / 1 pre-existing skipped**, CLI Doctor **20 passed**; the shared-state rehearsal case also passed. Runtime owner proofs cover recorded migration handoff, file-only config capture, shared rehearsal snapshot reuse/write refusal, live-WAL snapshot capacity and cleanup, capacity-versus-corruption guidance, and recovery reporting. The initial live-WAL test exposed an October helper-signature mismatch; the September fixture now explicitly creates its `writes` table and the affected suites pass.
- QA packaged bootstrap/repair selection: **7 passed**, 70 unselected cases skipped (23.56s wrapper). The synthetic packaged CLI binds its configured port during both auth and update commands, proving the placeholder listener is released first.
- Core production, QA project, infra/state/CLI-update test graphs and targeted runtime/QA lint passed. Final independent P0–P2 review returned **scoped-clean** after the report correction.

Separate pre-existing Batch 5 concerns remain outside this delta: the artifact collector checks a retained preparation identity before its producer completes, and continuation requires a preparation log identity even when failed preparation produced no candidate. These already exist on the pinned September baseline; this PR neither introduces them nor claims to repair or qualify those recovery paths.

Full Docker survivor/upgrade qualification, Linux/Bun and hosted broad CI are not claimed. Nothing merged, no release tag/version changed, and no package, Docker, native, or ClawHub artifact published.

Final commits: `95e9050cc32e` (runtime/update), `0115c2875f5b` (survivor/Doctor/lifecycle), `32665a07ef80` (font fixture). Whole change: 30 files, +601/-166 lines.


## Narrowed scope and current qualification status — October 29, 2026

The pushed corrective head is `550e329d3a43ec62214da0a5b77a344df0d830b2`, based on current release tip `e93b50ad2400871616c2e6588d57488dba94ecad`. It restores only the original **30-file, +601/−166** change; its patch is byte-identical to the original three-commit submission. All original authorship/history and the superseded aggregate security history are retained; this is content reduction, not rewritten commits. The preceding sections are preserved original-submission context and historical scoped evidence, not a completed review of this head.

### Seven primary sources adapted into three original commits

- **Update/runtime — Peter Steinberger, `95e9050cc32e`:** `0ac773b4382d31ca13c6e15b5a85716d59309a01` and `d128f0d5b41f7a0b44bff57712ccc3486286f6b5`; `47538facd06171f0a12fadc9cc47e79a391058d3` is the older-line adapter, not an eighth independently counted primary source.
- **Survivor/Doctor/lifecycle — Dallin Romney, `0115c2875f5b`:** `f13af5968f4514a6e828b475dd66a14996574958`, `cd3346e5a90aec8f3ce72f391087e7c68585fd7b`, `6dd10c239edc6c97b50ab9077a4b96d32e69172f`, `5f40bd029f23878b17c4762a5553131b9ee4d8d4`. These include authored proposals; no unsupported main-landing claim.
- **Font fixture — Peter Steinberger, `32665a07ef80`:** only the reset from `9ef85029b0d270b57838c84c612ea4f70d145249`.

Unrelated A2UI/Discord Zod patches, dependency upgrades, ClawHub/Vercel toolchain work, release-validation plumbing, Mermaid/Vitest changes and other runtime backports are **deferred to separately scoped, source-attributed work**. None is included or qualified by this narrowed diff.

Local verification of the pushed head: **239 tests / 10 files passed**, exact tree/patch equality and signature verified, narrow diff and affected shell syntax checks passed. These are targeted local checks, not complete hosted CI/FRV or cross-platform/native acceptance.

**Full canonical review remains outstanding.** The aggregate review's capacity refusal is not cleared by this scope correction; historical scoped reviews are not approval of this whole head. No review, merge, FRV, release or publication approval is claimed. No version or dependency changes are introduced by the narrowed diff.


Ledger reconciliation completed October 29, 2026: all seven narrow source assessments remain needed/adaptation_required (not landed); eMudhra and Docker already-present portions are recorded separately, with unresolved qualification caveats preserved. Expanded work is deferred, not qualified by this PR.

prs.title: fix(ui): task progress card says no active work while a child session is paused
prs.body:
Related: #186387, #185918, #182832

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the task progress card ignores a child session that is paused on `sessions_yield`, so a card whose only remaining child is paused reads **No active work**, even though the transcript already says **{name} is paused**.

## User Impact

User impact: the progress card counts paused children next to the existing buckets, as in **Delegated work: 1 running · 1 paused** or **Delegated work: 1 paused**. A paused child is shown as unfinished but not as active work, so with only paused children left the card keeps its paused step marker and shows no spinner, consistent with the chat waiting line from #186387.

## Why This Change Was Made

`projectProgressCardRuntime` (from #182832) counted running, queued, waiting, failed and stopped children, but a paused child (`subagentRunState: "paused"`, `status: "done"`) matched none of them. The projection now reuses `isPausedChild` from the same module to count those children in a separate `paused` bucket. The bucket is deliberately left out of the `hasActiveSubagentRun` sum, so a paused child never makes the parent read as working; a paused child whose own descendants are running still counts as **waiting** through its `hasActiveSubagentRun`. The card's runtime line renders the new bucket with the existing `{count} …` wording and ` · ` separator. `docs/tools/progress-card.md` describes the new count.

No Gateway or protocol change.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI e2e (Details → Task progress), light theme, 1100×850, synthetic content. Before = current `main`, after = this PR.

**Only a paused child left** (parent resumed; the transcript already shows "Changelog audit is paused")

| Before | After |

| ![Before: progress card reads No active work while a child is paused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d5b640c-d448-42fa-b92f-b1b2ea50b4e0) | ![After: progress card reads Delegated work: 1 paused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec230634-3f53-4b6c-a097-4c2f0ec5897c) |

**One running child, one paused child** (card crop)

| ![Before: Delegated work: 1 running](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46d0f790-2f13-45df-aa69-a9536bbac5ae) | ![After: Delegated work: 1 running · 1 paused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd061e0e-b60a-4f68-9e14-4f9bd736065d) |

In both paused-only captures the current step keeps its paused marker and no spinner is shown. Not captured: dark theme, mobile, and the composer/board placements (covered by the unit test below).

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-subagent-wait.test.ts`: a paused child is counted as `paused` alongside every other bucket, and a paused child does not make `hasActiveSubagentRun` true.
- `ui/src/components/session-progress-card.test.ts`: the composer, details and board placements render `1 running · 1 queued · 1 paused · 1 failed`.

prs.title: fix(acp): bind delayed ACP spawn dispatch to its child incarnation
prs.body:
Closes #133612

## What Problem This Solves

An in-flight ACP spawn could admit its original task into a child session that an operator reset or deleted and recreated before the first Gateway dispatch reached the admission owner. The delayed `agent` dispatch carried only the logical session key, so once the successor incarnation occupied that key the old spawn's work was admitted into it instead of being rejected as stale.
- `launchAcpChildThroughGateway` sent `sessionKey` but no committed child-session identity, and `spawnAcpDirect` did not forward the initialized child's identity.
- The launch request now carries `expectedExistingSessionId` and `expectedExistingSessionLifecycleRevision` (or `null` when absent). Both flow through the existing Gateway `agent` expected-session path (`agent-request-preflight.ts` → admission controller → `assertExpectedExistingSession`), which rejects the dispatch once that incarnation is retired. Reset preserves the session ID but bumps `lifecycleRevision`; delete/recreate changes both.
- What did NOT change: public `agent` RPC logical-session-key semantics, the admission controller, session-work admission handoff, successor-safe spawn cleanup, and normal accepted-child behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ACP spawn owns the child incarnation it provisioned, not whichever session later occupies that key. The existing admission owner already understands exact-session constraints, so the narrowest fix is to forward the two parameters it already supports — no new protocol, config, schema, or dependency. A session-ID-only constraint would have missed the same-ID reset schedule.

Alternative: the process-local session-work admission handoff mentioned in the issue. The expected-session constraint is strictly smaller and reuses the landed admission path; the handoff would duplicate authority the admission owner already provides.

## User Impact

An operator reset or delete/recreate of a child session while its first ACP dispatch is in flight no longer admits the old spawn's work into the successor. The stale dispatch is rejected before the successor starts work, and failure cleanup leaves the successor session intact. Ordinary spawns behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Current head: `a7062b6e1bd` (rebased onto current main; mergeable/CLEAN with 60 checks passing). Command:

```text
pnpm test src/agents/subagents/spawn/acp-spawn.authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
...
✓ rejects a held ACP spawn dispatch after the child lifecycle owner applies reset 7823ms
✓ rejects a held ACP spawn dispatch after the child lifecycle owner applies delete and recreate 6779ms
✓ accepts the unchanged ACP child and executes its synthetic runtime turn 24366ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       13 passed (13)
```

The new cases drive the real `sessions_spawn` ACP tool through the real in-process façade/dispatch, with a synthetic ACP runtime backend and the real session lifecycle owner:
- **reset**: hold the first `agent` dispatch, apply `sessions.reset` to the child (same session ID, new `lifecycleRevision`), release. The dispatch rejects with "changed"; the synthetic runtime's `runTurn`, `ensureSession`, and `closeRuntime` are never called; the successor session entry and ACP runtime handle remain.
- **delete and recreate**: hold, delete the child row, reinitialize a successor ACP session, release. The stale dispatch rejects with "changed"; no successor backend execution; the successor entry and handle remain.
- **unchanged child**: no mutation; the spawn is accepted and the synthetic ACP `runTurn` actually executes for the provisioned child handle with the expected text.
- The gate also asserts the dispatched `expectedExistingSessionId`/`expectedExistingSessionLifecycleRevision` equal the committed child entry. With the production forwarding removed, those fields are absent and the cases fail — the regression is effective.

A synthetic ACP backend through the real spawn/Gateway/lifecycle owners is the confirmation path requested in the review; no dispatch or session-store mock is used for the final-effect cases.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. It traces the ACP spawn launch path (`acp-spawn.ts` → `acp-spawn-gateway.ts`) against the Gateway admission owner (`agent-request-preflight.ts`, admission controller, `assertExpectedExistingSession`) to find the delayed dispatch was unbound from the provisioned child incarnation. The fix forwards the initialized session ID and lifecycle revision through the existing constraint, covering both reset and recreate.

A wall-clock correction during browser action download collection can end its 250 ms quiet window early and omit sibling downloads from the action result.

## What Changed

- Use `performance.now()` directly for both the download event timestamp and elapsed-time calculation. No local clock helper or plugin SDK export.
- Consolidate clock-step coverage into the existing sibling/slow-save ownership test, retaining the assertion that unrelated later downloads do not join the action. Fake performance wherever the affected tests fake Date. Net test-count growth: zero.

Thanks to @SunnyShu0925 for the report and original fix; their commits are preserved.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway / real Chromium browser HTTP bridge evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186850#issuecomment-6486955204). The targeted process-local clock probe logs the timestamp write, a +10-second Date.now step, and the subsequent elapsed-time read. No system-clock changes.

Focused browser session suite: 27/27 passed in the isolated container. Formatting check passed for all four changed browser files. Production delta against merge base: +3/-2 including the timestamp comment; test lines +9/-6, test count +0.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting fully restores the previous timing behavior. No persisted state, configuration, schema, permissions, or public API changes. Blast radius is the quiet-window collection of sibling downloads started by browser actions.

prs.title: fix: relative time labels overstate ages at half-minute boundaries
prs.body:
﻿Closes #186744

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: relative age labels in CLI/UI surfaces overstate ages by up to 2x in a ~0.5s window at each half-minute boundary (e.g. 89.5s renders "2m ago", 29.5s renders "1m ago" instead of "just now"), because `formatTimeAgo` and `bucketRelativeTimeMs` round to whole seconds first and then round again to minutes.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw status`, `openclaw sessions`, `openclaw skills list`, `openclaw nodes status`, `openclaw exec approvals`, devices inventory, channel status, and the TUI now render ages at minute boundaries correctly and consistently with OpenClaw's other formatters (`formatDurationHuman(89_500)` → `1m`, `formatDurationCompact(89_500)` → `1m30s`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both functions computed `minutes = Math.round(Math.round(durationMs / 1000) / 60)`, so any duration whose seconds-rounding overshoots a minute boundary (e.g. 89.5s → 90s → "2m") overstated the age. The fix rounds once at the display unit boundary: `Math.round(durationMs / 60_000)`. This is behavior-compatible with all previously pinned outputs (0→"just now", 29s→"just now", 30s→"1m ago", 47h→"47h ago", 48h→"2d ago", 60s→1m, 1h, 2d) and only changes the buggy half-minute windows.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof through the shipped consumers, executed on this branch (fix, `31ed1b0`) and on the PR base (`upstream/main` @ `b0966db12046`) with the same tsx harness that imports the actual shipped modules (no mocks).

### Red on base (`b0966db12046`) — actual terminal output

```
== CLI shipped consumer: formatSessionAgeCell(updatedAt) (src/commands/sessions-table.ts) ==
  updatedAt 29500ms ago -> rich="1m ago" plain="1m ago"
  updatedAt 89500ms ago -> rich="2m ago" plain="2m ago"
  updatedAt 89750ms ago -> rich="2m ago" plain="2m ago"
== CLI formatter: formatTimeAgo / formatRelativeTimestamp (src/infra/format-time/format-relative.ts) ==
   29500ms -> formatTimeAgo=1m ago  formatRelativeTimestamp=just now
   89500ms -> formatTimeAgo=2m ago  formatRelativeTimestamp=2m ago
   89750ms -> formatTimeAgo=2m ago  formatRelativeTimestamp=2m ago
== Shared bucket: bucketRelativeTimeMs (packages/normalization-core/src/format.ts, consumed by Control UI) ==
   89500ms -> { value: 2, unit: "minute" }
== Control UI shipped consumer: ui formatTimeAgo / formatRelativeTimestamp (ui/src/lib/format.ts) ==
   89500ms -> formatTimeAgo="2m ago"  formatRelativeTimestamp="2m ago"
```

### Green on fix (`31ed1b0`) — actual terminal output

```
== CLI shipped consumer: formatSessionAgeCell(updatedAt) (src/commands/sessions-table.ts) ==
  updatedAt 29500ms ago -> rich="just now" plain="just now"
  updatedAt 89500ms ago -> rich="1m ago" plain="1m ago"
  updatedAt 89750ms ago -> rich="1m ago" plain="1m ago"
== CLI formatter: formatTimeAgo / formatRelativeTimestamp (src/infra/format-time/format-relative.ts) ==
   29500ms -> formatTimeAgo=just now  formatRelativeTimestamp=just now
   89500ms -> formatTimeAgo=1m ago  formatRelativeTimestamp=1m ago
   89750ms -> formatTimeAgo=1m ago  formatRelativeTimestamp=1m ago
== Shared bucket: bucketRelativeTimeMs (packages/normalization-core/src/format.ts, consumed by Control UI) ==
   89500ms -> { value: 1, unit: "minute" }
== Control UI shipped consumer: ui formatTimeAgo / formatRelativeTimestamp (ui/src/lib/format.ts) ==
   89500ms -> formatTimeAgo="1m ago"  formatRelativeTimestamp="1m ago"
```

What the harness exercises: `formatSessionAgeCell` from `src/commands/sessions-table.ts` is the exact function that renders the age column in `openclaw sessions` (and the shared age label used by `status`/`nodes status`); `ui/src/lib/format.ts` is the Control UI's own formatter used for session hovercards and timestamps. Both consume the two functions changed here, so the displayed age is corrected in every listed surface. The `just now`/`1m ago` values are locale-independent outputs of those modules.

Regression tests (committed with this PR):
- `src/infra/format-time/format-time.test.ts`: `formatTimeAgo(29_500)` → "just now", `formatTimeAgo(89_500)` → "1m ago".
- `packages/normalization-core/src/format.test.ts`: `bucketRelativeTimeMs(89_500)` → `{ value: 1, unit: "minute" }`.

Checks run locally: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/format-time/format-time.test.ts packages/normalization-core/src/format.test.ts` (pass); format and oxlint on the changed files (pass).

Environment note: a full openclaw binary boot (pnpm openclaw) is verified working on this machine from the PR head (reports OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (31ed1b0)). Rendering a live relative-age label at ~89,500ms still requires a running Gateway with a session updated ~89.5s ago, and a browser Control UI timestamp requires a running Control UI + browser, neither of which is available in this environment. The evidence above instead runs the real shipped modules and their real CLI/Control UI consumers end to end via tsx; no mocks or stubs are involved. The Control UI i18n loader logged a non-fatal zh-CN irtual: scheme warning and fell back to the default locale; the exercised values do not depend on locale.




### Shipped CLI sessions output (minute fix, `31ed1b0`) - actual terminal output

Real `openclaw sessions` against an isolated local Gateway profile with a seeded session store (`--profile occliteproof`, dev agent `openclaw-agent.sqlite`). The Age column is rendered by `formatSessionAgeCell` -> `formatTimeAgo` in the shipped binary:

```
$ openclaw --profile occliteproof sessions
| direct | agent:dev:s-25m   | 26m ago | ...   <- 25m elapsed (rounds up 26m)
| direct | agent:dev:s-3h    | 3h ago  | ...   <- 3h elapsed
| direct | agent:dev:s-47h   | 47h ago | ...   <- 47h elapsed
```

Note on the minute boundary: the double-rounding defect this PR fixes produces a wrong minute count only inside narrow 0.5-second windows at each half-minute (e.g. 89.5s..90.0s renders `2m ago` on base vs `1m ago` on the fix). A real CLI invocation has ~60-90s startup latency in this environment, so a live `sessions` run cannot land inside those 0.5s windows; the exact boundary behavior is therefore proven in-process against the shipped `formatSessionAgeCell`/`formatTimeAgo` (base red / fix green above) plus the committed regression tests. The shipped CLI output above demonstrates the real entry point renders the Age column through the fixed formatter.


### Why a live boundary capture is physically impossible (measured)

The exact minute boundary this fix changes is a 0.5s-wide window (89.5s..90s). Seeding a session at exactly 89.5s and running the shipped CLI shows the window is unreachable in a real run:

```
$ pnpm openclaw --profile occliteproof sessions        # gateway already running
# seeded agent:dev:s-89.5s at 20:31:40Z (updated_at = now - 89500)
# the CLI binary took 80.6s to boot and render, so the age column read 170s -> "3m ago"
| direct | agent:dev:s-89.5s  | 3m ago | ...   <- seeded at 89.5s, rendered at 170s
| direct | agent:dev:s-149.5s | 4m ago | ...
```

By the time the CLI renders, the seeded 89.5s age has drifted past the 90s boundary (80.6s startup vs a 0.5s window; second run measured 74.5s, so boot time varies by seconds), so the changed output cannot appear in a live run. The same holds for the Control UI (browser startup ~12s). The boundary behavior is therefore proven in-process against the real shipped consumers (base red: 89500ms -> "2m ago"; fix green: -> "1m ago") plus the committed regression tests - the strongest evidence physically available in this environment.


### Live boundary capture through the shipped CLI - green on `31ed1b0`

The 0.5s boundary window (89.5s..90s) is reachable in a real run by seeding a spread of `updated_at` offsets that brackets the CLI's boot latency, so whichever value the binary actually renders at falls inside the window. Seeded 100 sessions with offsets 14.0s..23.9s and ran the shipped `openclaw sessions` against the running Gateway:

```
$ pnpm openclaw --profile occliteproof sessions
| direct | agent:dev:b-19000 | 1m ago | ...   <- rendered age ~89.0s
| direct | agent:dev:b-19200 | 1m ago | ...   <- rendered age ~89.56s  (IN 89.5s..90s window)
| direct | agent:dev:b-19600 | 1m ago | ...   <- rendered age ~89.96s
| direct | agent:dev:b-19700 | 2m ago | ...   <- rendered age ~90.05s  (past the 90s boundary)
```

The boundary row `b-19200` renders `1m ago` in the shipped binary. On the base (`b0966db`) the same age renders `2m ago` (proven in-process above: 89500ms -> "2m ago"). This is the shipped CLI entry point producing the corrected boundary output, complementing the in-process red/green and regression tests.

prs.title: fix(pr): resume pre-push corrections after workflow repair
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A reviewed pre-push correction remains bound to earlier workflow code even after that code is repaired, leaving maintainers unable to resume through the native owner.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177381 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186821.

## User Impact

No product-runtime change. The explicit correction-only successor command preserves the reviewed source, hosted publication lease and review evidence after existing custody and lock requirements are satisfied. It requires fresh preparation gates; it does not recover uncertain processes or waive CI.

## Why This Change Was Made

The owner verifies the exact predecessor, official-main successor, source head/tree, review and hosted head. It archives and verifies preparation evidence, preserves `prep.env` byte-for-byte, invalidates only `gates.env`, and changes the binding through a transaction that also verifies the operation lock. The shared historical validator preserves existing merge admission and signature gates.

Hosted CI caught an ordering regression: an invalid first-admission binding reached `binding.json` before its tree was validated. The correction restores structural validation before the read, preserving the original regression assertion. Test-only braces and explicit string conversions resolve the lint failures.

Final scope: **7 files, 747 changed lines**. Production **+240/−39 (net +201)**; tests/support **+431/−1**; docs **+36**. Production growth implements the explicit safe continuation capability and shared history validation. PR 177381's retained lock, source and workflow binding remain untouched.

## Evidence

- Signed head: `909f86f735a9d9d62d14c2de258ebcfc2d0bf59f`; tree `d2ce6274efda7eb1d5bc57dc9b740910e85aa0f5`; frozen branch base `f996c1c487a0fcb456a73c9af49e360b99d14de5`.
- Linux CI/build actually checked merge `cb91a2725fca158d5b701d2c469b47bbcc929a84`, tree `d895c6a42efb4f794dd0235247c340b9aa0fb81a`, with ordered parents base `a83fd5dcf456df68e0889a1e40bc10d3a1359b70` and the head above.
- [Corrected CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40810774303) **passed**. All changed files executed completely: recovery **29/29**, binding **29/29**, successor **18/18**. The original first-admission binding-drift case passed. Actual runtime: **Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1 / Linux x64 / Vitest 5.0.5**. Changed lint, production types, test types and ratchets passed. Both required ci-gates and exact-head dependency/security-sensitive statuses passed, including [security reconciliation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40811658955).
- [Fresh build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40810774236) **passed after a cache miss**: actual SDK declarations **1m44.7s**, full build **4m44s**, artifact verification passed on that merge.
- [Fresh Darwin](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40810774253) **passed**, checking the exact source head/tree above with workflow `cb91a272`: Node **24.22.1**, darwin-arm64, Vitest **5.0.5**. Dependency-cache **43 passed**; wrappers **103 passed/6 skipped**; materialized anchors **5 passed**; operation locks **60 passed**; Git invocation **4 passed/12 Windows cases skipped**. The captured-revision/archive case passed. This does not establish successful recovery of PR 177381.
- Historical head `f1e57b81`: [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40809640463) failed the recovery regression and lint; binding **28/28** and successor **18/18** passed. Its [build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40809640408) and [Darwin](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40809640354) passed. These are old-source results; the corrected-head receipts resolve the two failures.
- Local proof is separately source-bound: the initial postimage passed **13 actual-owner/alias checks** using Node 24.22.1, Git 2.56.0 and signed disposable repositories; the correction passed **17 actual-owner controls** covering valid v1/v2 bindings, old/new source-commit refusal, preserved refs and malformed-layout refusals. Transaction exit-74 controls do not prove signal or detached-process custody. Live GitHub alias behavior and actual native use on PR 177381 remain unproved. A malformed v2 record missing its snapshot still fails closed with a generic Git-read diagnostic.
- Native oxfmt 0.74.0, syntax, whitespace and signed-commit hooks passed. Independent production/test and correction reviews found no actionable source issue. Autoreview identified an archive-selection test defect; the corrected test requires exactly one newly created archive and preserves prior archives and exact bytes.
- As of **2026-10-29 03:23:46 UTC**, [Claw review](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/40811737555) has **started on this exact head**, with [acknowledgement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187206#issuecomment-6486995658). No completed verdict or rank-up disposition exists yet; successful dispatch is not review approval.

**Final autoreview and native merge HOLD.** The original intact-context dry run refused before reviewer launch: **590,372 bytes** exceeded the installed helper's **512,000-byte hard cap**. The corrected head requires **591,025 bytes of complete source context, plus diff and guides**. A supported final review route capable of admitting that complete context is still required. Hosted review is additional evidence, not a substitute. This PR is not native READY or merge-qualified; GitHub ready-for-review admits ordinary CI only, auto-merge is disabled, and no inherited-failure exception is selected.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): refuse brief files that would corrupt call instructions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `voicecall call` and `voicecall start` accept malformed UTF-8 brief files after silently changing their instructions during decoding.

## User Impact

Both commands reject malformed file bytes before initiating a call, name the file, and tell the operator to re-save it as UTF-8. Valid Unicode, including a deliberate replacement character, remains supported. Input files are not modified.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a reusable plugin-local fatal TextDecoder at the existing shared brief-file reader, with no core import or additional validation pass. Preserve BOM bytes so JSON parsing retains its existing behavior. Regular-file/symlink safety, the 16,000-character limit, brief schema and call authorization remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Fully built main and candidate in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker. Run the actual built `voicecall call` and `voicecall start --brief-file` commands against the normal Gateway and shipped `mock` telephony provider: malformed files initiate mock calls on main, but candidate rejects them before call creation. Each command has two before/after runs plus valid UTF-8 and leading-BOM controls. Mock calls are explicitly ended; this is CLI admission proof, not a real telephony-delivery claim.

Focused CLI suite: candidate 29 pass; main 1 fail/28 pass. Formatting/type-aware lint pass. Test-line delta -1; production +11; docs +2 against baseline. Existing size-limit and Unicode/symlink coverage absorb the added regression rather than adding another fixture.

Observed captures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187174#issuecomment-6487089758

Merge danger: two-way door; revert restores prior decoding without a state migration. Blast radius is voice-call CLI file-brief admission only, not inline briefs, Gateway callers or provider delivery.
