prs.title: feat(stepfun): default to Step 5 Preview with USD usage pricing
prs.body:
Related: #153525 (overlapping Step 5 Preview proposal). This is an independent implementation with official USD pricing and newly captured OpenClaw Web proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Step 5 Preview needs a default catalog entry with USD usage pricing; China endpoints also lost catalog capabilities and prices because their native URLs were not declared by the provider.

## User Impact

New Standard and Step Plan setups select Step 5 Preview by default. Repeating onboarding preserves an existing primary model, fallbacks, and ownership of the `StepFun` / `StepFun Plan` aliases; existing installations can explicitly select `stepfun/step-5-preview` or `stepfun-plan/step-5-preview`.

Standard usage estimates use the official USD rates per million tokens: **$1.00 input, $0.05 cached input, $2.70 output**. Step Plan remains zero in the token-cost catalog because it uses subscription credits. China accounts still receive their separate CNY bill; OpenClaw displays the documented USD estimate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider-owned manifest is the canonical catalog and price source. Add Step 5 Preview to both provider surfaces with 1,048,576 context, 65,536 maximum output, text/image input, and low/medium/high reasoning. Switch the shared default model identifier; reuse existing request shaping and cached-token accounting. Live validation caught a second owning-boundary gap: the implicit-catalog endpoint gate rejected `.com` URLs, suppressing both discovery and pricing. Declare all four native Standard/Plan endpoints in the plugin and mirror that metadata in the external-provider catalog. Custom proxies remain excluded. No new configuration option, migration, or core transport path is introduced.

The docs use the plugin catalog in merge-mode examples, keeping model capabilities and prices in one place. Runtime TypeScript is +9/-2 (seven net lines protect existing normalized alias ownership); catalog metadata is +102/-0 for model rows and endpoint ownership; tests are +222/-108; docs are +46/-68.

Sources: [model guide](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/guides/models/step-5-preview), [official USD price table](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/guides/pricing/details), [Step Plan](https://platform.stepfun.ai/docs/en/step-plan/overview).

## Evidence

**Live OpenClaw Web validation — candidate `ee6842c1f8dae16a98391115f4adf1b7ba9e0dfc`, isolated local Gateway, real China Standard API, no mocked provider.**

Computer Use drove the real Control UI, submitted a file-reading task, and captured these unedited browser screenshots. The final candidate called `step-5-preview` successfully (HTTP 200 streaming), read the workspace file, and returned marker `STEP5-WEB-20260923` and `137 + 256 + 89 = 482`. The new turn made two file reads and completed with 333 output tokens. The configured primary model is `stepfun/step-5-preview`; no custom model/cost rows were supplied (`models: []`).

![Step 5 Preview real OpenClaw Web conversation and tool execution](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a798a4d5-e312-41ea-ac8a-d8506688cb33)

The Usage page now attributes 86,830 tokens and about **$0.04** to Step 5 Preview, with 50.7K cached tokens, three total tool calls, and zero errors across both turns. The Control UI JSON export reports 35,455 uncached input, 687 output, and 50,688 cache-read tokens: **$0.0398443**, verified against `(input × 1 + output × 2.7 + cacheRead × 0.05) / 1e6`, with zero missing-cost entries.

![Step 5 Preview USD usage after real calls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3ec796d-4c51-4a3b-8cf5-f81e9e78aaac)

![Step 5 Preview model costs and cache accounting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3147a6bf-0502-4239-8f87-5a88330449c3)

<details>
<summary>Controlled before/after: the same original real conversation</summary>

Before declaring native endpoint ownership, the first candidate produced a correct response but the Usage page showed $0.00 and two missing-cost entries. After the fix, without another model call, the same 32,929 tokens were repriced to **$0.0184524** and **zero missing-cost entries**. The `sessions.usage` Gateway receipt reports 16,703 uncached input, 354 output, and 15,872 cache-read tokens:

`(16703 × 1 + 354 × 2.7 + 15872 × 0.05) / 1e6 = $0.0184524`

Before:

![Before endpoint repair: real usage incorrectly unpriced](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d19c2686-eef0-4c20-bb42-8c8fba4819d1)

After (same original conversation):

![After endpoint repair: the same usage priced in USD](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fc4d92a-82b2-4b20-9b27-b233100062c0)

</details>

### Review follow-up

The default change is intentional and explicitly requested for this PR. Fresh Standard and Step Plan setups use Step 5 Preview; existing explicit selections and aliases must retain their previous meaning. The maintainer can still decide whether to accept that default policy before merging.

The P1 alias finding is addressed at the StepFun onboarding owner: add the default alias only when no existing entry owns its trimmed, case-insensitive name. Twelve region/surface/normalization cases failed before the repair by resolving the old alias to Step 5, then passed after the repair through the actual SDK alias resolver. The new-model default tests remain green. The requested after-repair Web/price evidence is now included above, and all five inline images were confirmed to load anonymously in a browser.

Real CLI validation on final head `eb8beb5bbae`: fresh China Standard onboarding saved primary `stepfun/step-5-preview` and alias `StepFun`. Re-running both China Standard and Step Plan onboarding against a previous-setup configuration retained primary `StepFun`, fallback `StepFun Plan`, and the old whitespace/case-varied Step 3.5 aliases. `openclaw models status --json` then reported `resolvedDefault: stepfun/step-3.5-flash`. These runs used isolated state/workspace directories and skipped service installation. The follow-up changes onboarding alias ownership only; model/request/price code is unchanged from the live Web proof commit above.

### Automated checks

- 54 focused tests passed across provider catalog/request shaping and four onboarding auth choices, including new default selection and preservation of existing primary/fallbacks. The manifest → endpoint owner gate → effective catalog regression failed for both CN endpoints before the fix and passes for all four native URLs, while custom proxies remain excluded. Before implementation, the new-model expectations failed; before changing the default, 18 of 23 default-selection checks failed.
- The live-proof commit runtime, all external plugins, SDK declarations and Control UI build: `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed. The final follow-up head `eb8beb5bbae91ea95fe5719da8ef15d359458264` passed the same build again. A full `pnpm build` also passed before the endpoint-metadata follow-up.
- Changed-scope checks: formatting, guards, all 25 core/UI typecheck shards, plugin production/test typechecks and the dead-export scans passed before the alias follow-up. The broad run was stopped during full-core lint after a separate plugin-boundary declaration preparation timed out at 300 seconds; it is **not** reported as a full gate pass. Final alias-focused syntax lint passed; the final alias-follow-up plugin production typecheck (`tsconfig.extensions.json`) also passed. Hosted CI is separate.
- Independent Claude diff-scope review through the repository autoreview helper: no accepted P0–P2 findings; live validation is reported separately above. A fresh alias-follow-up review was also scoped-clean. Codex reviewer exited before producing a report; its result is not counted as approval.

### Hosted CI follow-up

The ready-for-review run on head `eb8beb5` is still running. [`check-dependencies`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35849554342/job/107144324148) failed in Knip with `scripts/run-swiftlint.mts: swiftlint` (unlisted binary). That script and `config/knip.config.ts` have identical blob SHAs in the tested main parent `760dc1498db8` and CI merge `5510839fe613`; neither file is changed by this PR. This is recorded as a main-side tooling follow-up, not a green CI claim.

### Direct API contract checks

- Real `step-5-preview` streaming requests succeeded both with and without `stream_options`. The default stream delivered final usage.
- A repeated prompt reported 2,843 prompt tokens, 86 output tokens, and 2,560 cached prompt tokens in `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. At the published USD prices, the expected cost is `(283 × 1 + 86 × 2.7 + 2560 × 0.05) / 1e6 = $0.0006432`.
- The provided credential is China-region: China Standard inference was tested; the international endpoint rejected it with 401. Authenticated international and Step Plan inference are **not** claimed as live-tested; their catalog/default behavior is covered by the four-region/plan setup matrix. The maximum context/output limits and image capability follow official documentation, not a maximum-size live stress test.

Keys and browser authentication material are excluded from this PR and all captures.

prs.title: feat(skills): diet oversized learned skills in daily Workshop maintenance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Learned skills only grow: each lesson patches more text into `SKILL.md`, which every run that uses the skill reads in full, and nothing in Skill Workshop ever shrinks them. On one production agent, 46 of the 48 learned skills with saved versions grew and none shrank; one doubled to 20 KB over 10 patches.

## User Impact

User impact: in `auto` learning mode, the daily Workshop maintenance pass now shrinks one oversized learned skill per agent per day, with no user action and without changing the skill's rules. Each diet is one versioned change in the skill's history; `openclaw skills workshop restore <name>` undoes it, including the reference files it added. `propose` and `off` modes are unchanged, and there are no config, schema, or SDK changes. An agent whose tool policy denies `skill_workshop` (its documented Workshop opt-out) gets no daily maintenance: no diet, and also no unused-skill archive, which until now ran for such agents.

A diet makes two to four tool-free calls on the agent's primary model and sends the skill's text to that provider (documented).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Pick:** `SKILL.md` body over 12 KB (the existing sprawl threshold), unchanged for a day, taken in name order, rotated by calendar day (day N takes entry N mod count). No new state; a skill that cannot be dieted cannot block the others.
- **Rewrite:** the model names whole `##` sections that only some runs need; OpenClaw copies them verbatim into new `references/` files (re-pointing relative links) and the model tightens the rest, ending with a lookup index.
- **Mechanical checks:** every link and heading anchor resolves, including anchors into existing reference files, every new reference is linked, `SKILL.md` shrinks by at least 20%, every file passes normal Workshop validation. Sections with in-page links, and skills with titled or reference-style links, are not moved.
- **Independent review:** a separate model call compares the original and the rewrite rule by rule and reports rules that are missing, weakened, moved out of reach of the runs they apply to, or added. One repair pass; otherwise nothing is written.
- **Authority:** the daily gate skips agents whose tool policy denies `skill_workshop`. Auto mode is read from the live config before every diet model call, again by the completion owner right before dispatch (`assertCurrent`), and again at publish, so turning learning off mid-diet stops further provider calls and writes.
- **Publish:** one versioned `curator` change. Under the skill lock, the file list, `SKILL.md` and every Markdown support file must match what the candidate was validated against; any concurrent edit refuses the diet. A new shared `publishSkillOverlay` helper now also backs draft apply.

The approach adapts [skill-diet](https://github.com/nicobailon/skill-diet) (ideas, no code). An earlier manual pilot found that before/after behavioral tests saturated (both versions passed every task) while a rule-by-rule audit caught real losses, so the audit is the gate.

Accepted edges: the rotation is per day, so a Gateway restart re-attempts that day's skill; a skill that is one long procedure section, or already has broken anchors, is skipped, costing one model call per turn.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway (fresh `--profile`, state inside the worktree, real `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`), seeded with a copy of 85 learned skills from a production agent; live state was never written. Real agent turns triggered the daily pass end to end. OpenAI's implicit runtime selection put these turns on the **Codex harness** (recorded `agent_harness_id = codex`):

| Skill | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `crabbox-provider-preflight` | 20.1 → 7.8–8.0 KB, all 8 branch sections moved to 4 references; reproduced on 4 builds, including the final one |
| `serialized-heavy-check-orchestration` | 12.3 → 7.5 KB, 3 sections moved |
| `github-issue-root-cause-investigation` | Rejected (a single 11 KB procedure; cut only 5%); nothing written |

- **Rule audits** of published outputs by a fresh model: 0 missing, 0 weakened (3 audits).
- **Behavioral eval** (12 scenarios, blind-graded together): original 32/36 vs dieted 33/36 on `gpt-6.1-sol`, 0 forbidden actions; `gpt-6-luna` 8/12 vs 7/12, where 2 of the dieted runs failed on eval-harness tool discovery.
- **OpenClaw harness:** with the model pinned to `agentRuntime.id: "openclaw"`, a fresh session (recorded `agent_harness_id = openclaw`) triggered the same pass: `crabbox-provider-preflight` 20.1 → 8.2 KB, 8 sections moved. The diet runs on both runtimes.
- **Undo:** `openclaw skills workshop restore` returned the skill byte-identical to the original.
- The first iteration exposed a prompt flaw (moved rules were summarized back into `SKILL.md`, only −22%); fixed before the runs above.
- **Tests:** `pnpm test src/skills/workshop/skill-diet.test.ts src/skills/workshop/drafts.test.ts src/skills/workshop/library.test.ts src/agents/harness/agent-end-side-effects.test.ts src/skills/workshop/skill-lint.test.ts`: 53 passed. The new file has 16 tests at about 5.5 s with `--maxWorkers=1`. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, oxlint, and oxfmt are clean.
- **Local review:** autoreview (Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, up to P2) over the full candidate diff against `8889b596`. Nine passes raised 12 P2 findings, all fixed: reviewer ignoring additions and lost reach, several link/anchor integrity cases, and a reference-creation race. prs.title: fix(litellm): image edits fail for Gemini models because n is always sent
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #169120

## What Problem This Solves

Single-image edits through the bundled LiteLLM provider always send multipart `n=1`. LiteLLM's Gemini edit backend rejects that explicit unsupported parameter with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError`, even though omitting `n` already means one output image.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the LiteLLM **edit** request builder changes: include `n` when `count > 1`, otherwise use the endpoint's existing single-image default. Multi-image edits retain their requested count and normal error handling. No global `drop_params`, new retry, model-name special case, or transport change.

The contributor's commit is preserved. A follow-up narrowing commit restores the original generation builder and its default-count assertion. **Image generation is unchanged**, including JSON `n: 1` for a single generated image. The issue reports that generation already works; changing that behavior is unnecessary.

## User Impact

Single-image Gemini edits no longer fail solely because OpenClaw supplies redundant `n=1`. Explicit multi-image requests still send their count rather than silently dropping an unsupported parameter. Other providers and generation requests retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Current integrated head `401c2aad24c67e9c53aa098d47821341dadba1b2` merges current main `a7fe06b17a966`. The reported conflict was only in the provider test file: upstream’s consolidated layout is retained, with default-edit omission, explicit multi-image count, and generation count=1/count=2 assertions preserved. The production provider is byte-identical to proven `d91502a7840fb0c8a3767a281de3af3ffc74bae0`, so the linked Gateway A/B evidence carries; this integration does not add a real-provider claim. Fresh isolated frozen install, changed-file format check, and provider suite pass **20/20**. Current delta: production **+5/-1**, tests **+13/-5**.

[Built-Gateway A/B multipart captures and output receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169129#issuecomment-6432278843), comparing pinned main `ce503a58dad3b06cfba1cc357bab3e5a0435f024` with narrowed candidate `d91502a7840fb0c8a3767a281de3af3ffc74bae0`:

- Fresh isolated Linux `node:24.22.1` containers installed frozen dependencies and passed supported `pnpm build:runtime`. The runtime artifact contains the final production change; the final amendment only consolidated tests.
- The shipped agent command dispatches to the built Gateway, whose real `image_generate` tool runs the LiteLLM provider against a local LiteLLM-compatible HTTP fixture. It receives a real PNG file part. The fixture models the reported Gemini contract: reject explicit edit `n` with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError`; accept omission and return a known valid PNG.
- **Main twice:** default count and explicit count=1 each send multipart `n=1`, receive HTTP 400, and persist no output PNG.
- **Candidate twice:** the same default/explicit-one operations omit `n`, receive HTTP 200, and persist one PNG each. Shipped image metadata decoding reads both as 1×1 PNGs, 68 bytes each.
- **Controls on both refs:** shipped `infer image edit` with non-Gemini `gpt-image-2`, count=2 sends `n=2` and writes two PNGs. `infer image generate` with the Gemini route, count=1 still sends JSON `n: 1` and writes one PNG. Generation behavior is unchanged.
- Gateway image work is asynchronous: the first agent turn acknowledges task admission. The recorded failure/success is the actual provider operation and persisted artifact, not a claim that this initial acknowledgement failed.
- Before integration, candidate provider tests passed **10/10** and changed-file format checks pass. The strengthened existing default-edit multipart regression fails on main exactly at `form.has("n")` (true versus expected false) and passes with the fix. Default omission is consolidated into the existing multipart test; explicit multi-image count remains a distinct regression.
- Simplification retains one request builder and adds no helper/state owner. That pre-integration delta was production **+5/-1**, tests **+20/-0**; current integrated totals are listed above.

Earlier contributor evidence exercised the public CLI and a real LiteLLM 1.105.0 proxy with stubbed Vertex AI. That remains earlier-head evidence, not a real Gemini API run. This new run proves the narrowed production path through a built Gateway but also uses local model/provider fixtures.

**Outstanding proof prerequisite:** the [previous review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169129#issuecomment-6109716373) explicitly requests an actual Gemini image returned through LiteLLM because the dependency's AGENTS.md requires real provider APIs. No Gemini credentials are available to this proof lane. The known PNG above is fixture output, not real Gemini output, and does not satisfy that requirement if it remains applicable.

## Not fixed here

Generation is intentionally unchanged. This does not enable Gemini multi-image counts, globally discard unsupported parameters, prove semantic image-edit quality, or establish real Gemini deployment behavior. Unsupported explicit multi-image parameters still surface their normal errors.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores explicit `n=1` on single-image LiteLLM edits; no schema/config migration or durable-state change. Blast radius is LiteLLM multipart image edits. Generation and other providers are untouched.

prs.title: feat(codex): support command-auth custom Responses providers
prs.body:
Related: #131261 (custom Codex providers and platform credential proxies; this does not implement the historical provider-ID proposal).

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot use a custom Responses provider's Codex-owned token command without OpenClaw looking for host credentials.

## User Impact

Custom providers can opt into `auth: "native-command"`. Codex owns token-command execution and refresh; OpenClaw does not borrow stored profiles or ambient OpenAI credentials.

Operators must use an **unowned custom provider ID**, explicitly configure Codex at the model/provider level, and configure a matching native `model_providers` command-auth entry. The configured model and effective native route must use the same HTTPS Responses endpoint, without URL credentials/fragments, competing API keys/profile bindings, headers or authored request/transport overrides. A forced environment runtime alone is insufficient. Explicit profile pins are rejected as mixed credential ownership, not silently ignored. Direct host credential APIs reject this mode; first-party and main-session explicit-profile validation, operator-model policy and approval-review boundaries remain intact.

**Ordinary sessions only:** isolated completions, supervised native sessions, manual compaction and remote-exec cloud placement remain unsupported. Native automatic compaction remains available; separate final-answer recovery uses the settled-tool fallback rather than another credential. Worker-hosted transport is outside this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared eligibility serves availability, harness support and preparation. Dispatch skips unrelated automatic OpenAI accounts and stale automatic pins; native configuration is validated before thread creation. No separate token store or command executor is added.

Includes reviewed fixes for exact offline archives and fixed Node/Bun testing in the existing runner; neither broadens auth nor relaxes isolation.

## Evidence

**Published head:** `67207ccfd5fed07f83a24acfb71745e8d4fefaa9`; tree `ba93c4b00e75b5aef9c414d5aea43713ecaa1185`. The managed publisher added only an empty marker commit atop verified implementation head `7e9a3164c94e4ccde2ae89fda89933204cb3826a`; source is unchanged. Exact canonical `44ffd0a8` integration preserved all 56 authored blobs/modes and the complete net PR patch. Whole PR: **56 files, +1,587/−353**.

### Current-head proof

Both flows were bound to the verified implementation head and this same published tree and ran sequentially through the existing immutable network-none runner with Node 26.12.1 and native pnpm 12.15.0.

| Proof | Result | Test / full invocation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native effective-endpoint refusal | Real config/read; mismatch rejected before thread/start, resume or turn/start; native close confirmed | **Pass: 2.330s / 61.437s** |
| Real Gateway ordinary session with credential decoys | Actual token command and exact bearer/provider/model; no host credential source; `agent.wait` publishes the visible answer; no native auth file; client/Gateway/provider cleanup | **Pass: 9.871s / 250.571s**, including prerequisites |

Both exited 0; container absence was independently confirmed. Four auth guards and four catalog idle-custody cases passed (43.22s and 53.62s; 21 custody cases deliberately unselected), along with merged-source imported-contract types and diff/tree/blob/patch checks. Lint, format and independent review are reused from unchanged authored bytes. Review's missing visible-terminal assertion was restored instead of duplicating the payload check; the current Gateway run verifies it.

These are real Gateway/native-client executions against a **synthetic HTTPS provider and token command**, not commercial-provider entitlement, health, live-model reasoning/tool selection or P8 worker acceptance. No live provider credential was used.

### Terminal current-head CI

On exact published head `67207ccfd5fed07f83a24acfb71745e8d4fefaa9`, [CI 40809689209](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40809689209), attempt 1, completed successfully: **91 jobs — 65 passed, 26 skipped, none failed or pending**. [PR tooling Darwin 40809688885](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40809688885/job/123236803467) also completed successfully; the previously missing selected-Git suite actually executed, with 4 passed and 12 platform-skipped cases.

The complete two-page inventory contains **153 check runs: 91 passed, 61 skipped, 1 neutral**, with none failed or pending. All three current commit-status contexts pass. Four provisional “review has not completed” failures and five pending status records are superseded, not current test failures. Native CI classification returns no failing leaf and no rerun command. No formal GitHub reviews or durable current-head ClawSweeper verdict were returned: maintainer-authority/dependency policy statuses are **not** scanner qualification. The unchanged **NO VERDICT** hold and **0/7 removal phases** below remain independent landing blockers despite green CI. Observation: 2026-10-29, approximately 03:20 UTC.

### Retained critical coverage and deliberate reductions

The authorized P0 reduction removes **540 eligible test/support lines**, including helpers; net PR eligible growth is **+633**. Retained: real command-auth execution with hostile credentials; endpoint refusal before native effects; mixed-profile/plaintext/header and direct/auxiliary credential-egress guards; archive integrity, trusted binary execution, independent isolation and cleanup. The native check stays in its automatic database-worker lane.

Deliberately dropped: accountless/restart/catalog/history checks, planner/harness shapes, config permutations, selector source/default/store-call microtests, unsupported-compaction feedback, archive diagnostics and parser variants. This is **not equivalent coverage**. No unrelated main tests, production guard, routing, timeout, ignore or suffix changed.

**Budget passes: 6,246,555 / 6,320,000; 73,445 lines of headroom.** The ceiling is inherited exactly from canonical `44ffd` / #187162, alongside the full base. P5 did not raise it or take a waiver.

### Before landing — unresolved blockers

- **Removal verdicts: 0/7.** Dependency/full (2), unused-file (2) and export (3) phases are unrun. Own offline Knip 6.40.0 qualification lacks `walk-up-path@4.0.0` (`ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_TARBALL`; downloaded 0/added 0). Task-cache dependency-fetch approval is pending; no installation, alternate tool/cache or retry. **Ordinary `pull_request` CI selects 0/7**, so green CI cannot replace these gates.
- **Hosted input safety: NO VERDICT.** The [hold](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186614#issuecomment-6463002323) remains unresolved. Trusted diagnostics report `agent_input_scan` / `findings`, `retryable=false`, `unclassified_finding` / `material_not_reviewed`, with **2 findings**. Available metadata for finding 0: detector 17, decoder HTML, `verified=false`, scanner material line 1733, patch ID 1 from `62177f294dc0a120ccec25330c3ae6f4a591c090` to `59617f8728c0dc38b06731c97ac31257f4b0d953`. This is **not a qualified repository filename/line**; unverified does not mean benign. No detected values are reproduced. A ClawSweeper maintainer must qualify both findings against that exact submitted material, or remove/rotate a genuine credential through the security owner. Test deletion and passing execution do not release this hold; no policy override or duplicate review was requested.


<details>
<summary>Historical failures, owning repairs and prerequisite provenance</summary>

**Auth repairs.** Availability/preparation regressions were red on `86d4d441` before `1ec35fba` added shared native eligibility. Competing-header controls were red before repair and green afterward. Real Gateway proof then found automatic OpenAI profile selection missed by native-attempt proof; `f53f8440` fixed the producer with red/green coverage. Earlier two-phase Gateway passes are historical; current acceptance is one decoy phase.

**Runner prerequisites.** Four-file `f6a08fc6a7885cc75518848502e2eaf7eaa74b20` repaired the actual offline setup failure: only existing public archives selected by the installed fs-safe manifest and lockfile, SRI-verified with recorded hashes, enter the snapshot—not the surrounding cache. `e49494a26bfb6bd2026824e9186ac2db3c5720d3` adds fixed `--isolated-runtime=node|bun` to that runner. Node stays default/orchestrator/build/entry; Bun is one read-only pinned executable, SHA-256/revision-verified at admission and entry. No arbitrary path/command/env passthrough, broad mounts, network or isolation relaxation. Focused/static and independent review plus contained Node/Bun child/loopback/absence proof passed. An initial sysfs-counting smoke failure was corrected without weakening isolation. The original P8 verification patch remains byte-identical: SHA256 `fe004d65b4aa3ccffa44c495ea897938bff59390f9423527374ce1f7550deaca`. Both prerequisites are included in this PR.

**CI repairs.** `af9c3893` moved prepared contracts to their leaf owner, fixing the PR-caused Madge cycle (1→0); `5dc349b0` separated concrete inputs after the resulting leaf-boundary failure, with red/green proof. `ddc4541b` fixed Bun's reversed directory enumeration by sorting both arrays before exact equality; extra/missing files still fail. Red/green oracle proof and Bun/Node checks passed. Earlier `45fc7534` CI was red in that archive shard and aggregate gate. Prior budget failures were not waived; the current inherited budget passes.

**Prior published CI remains historical.** [Main CI 40728964753](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40728964753) on `b560714fe18f7a59084876aa9402cb167499da83` settled **89 jobs: 63 passed, 26 skipped**. Its separate [Darwin job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40728964595/job/122959761289) was red: the newer workflow/synthetic-merge source selected `test/scripts/pr-git-invocation.test.ts` while checking out an older PR head lacking it. Canonical #185964's complete owner/test/workflow closure is now integrated. The current-head Darwin run above supplies the new passing platform verdict; the old failed receipt remains historical.

**Cleanup uncertainty remains.** A wrong-config build attempt was canceled before tests; its stopped container was removed with ownership verified. Actual **3-second outer Gateway cleanup recurred** after successful native work, including an accountless pass with decoys unreached. `af9c3893` joins client/Gateway cleanup with errors retained; diagnostics placed the deadline at the outer Gateway after client/native closure. The helper suite was **11 passed / 1 failed**: an unchanged post-shutdown host-loopback compaction request returned a Response instead of rejecting. Neither uncertainty is fixed by current passes or #187090's source change. No timeout increase, suppressed failure or retry-for-green.

</details>

prs.title: fix(memory): use monotonic clock for session index pass deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session-memory index scheduler stores pending, last-activity, and retry deadlines using wall-clock timestamps. If the clock steps forward while transcripts keep changing, a later notification recomputes the original five-minute deadline as already expired and publishes the index early. Clock rollback can instead stretch the delay. The full-reindex retry cooldown shares the same clock domain with the session retry owner.

Use `performance.now()` consistently for these process-local deadline seeds and comparisons at the three existing memory-core owners. No local clock helper, SDK expansion, persisted timestamp rewrite, new option, or dependency. The original commit by SunnyShu0925 is preserved.

## User Impact

Background session indexing still waits for the quiet period or original five-minute cap, regardless of wall-clock correction. Retry cooldowns measure elapsed time rather than clock adjustments. FTS publication, stored transcript timestamps, search results and normal no-step scheduling retain their contracts.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway six-run before/after FTS proof and focused regression results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186829#issuecomment-6486739129).

- Main `f996c1c487a0fcb456a73c9af49e360b99d14de5`, twice; candidate `58271c77ac0cfde109175caf9c7311ea189a91cc`, twice; one no-step control per revision.
- Real authenticated Gateway `/tools/invoke` starts the shipped `memory_search` tool's retained manager. Actual session creation and transcript injection trigger the normal notification/indexing path. The probe does not call scheduler methods or substitute a memory manager.
- Repeated activity leaves the original work pending until monotonic 280 s. A process-local +120 s Date step is followed by another real transcript append, forcing recomputation of the original pending deadline—not merely observing an already-armed timer.
- Main recomputes a **0 ms** delay and publishes real `memory_index_chunks_fts MATCH` rows at 280 s. Candidate recomputes **20,000 ms**, remains unpublished at 299,999 ms, and publishes at the original 300 s deadline. Both repetitions agree. Both no-step controls publish at 300 s. Final Gateway search retrieves the indexed marker in every run.
- Secretless Docker, Node 24.22.1, built Gateway/plugin artifacts, explicit task profiles/state/config paths, supported keyword-only memory. No real provider keys and no system-clock changes.
- Consolidated behavioral regression fails on main: quiet case passes, wall-step maximum-deferral case observes an unexpected early `session-delta`. Candidate: **90 passed across six touched suites**. Targeted formatting/lint: clean, zero warnings/errors.

## Simplification

Merged duplicate quiet/coalescing and maximum-deferral setup into one parameterized regression, and wired the existing FTS fixture's Date/performance clock pair once in `beforeEach`. Other Date-controlled fixtures now also control performance. Merge-base delta: **production +10/−10 (20 changed lines); tests +34/−34 (net zero)**.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the prior deadline arithmetic without a migration. All monotonic readings remain process-local; no persisted epoch changes. Blast radius is memory-core background session scheduling and its coordinated full-reindex retry cooldown.

## What Problem This Solves

The ChatGPT importer rejects valid export directories named with a `.json` suffix and valid JSON export files named `BACKUP.JSON` or without an extension.

## User Impact

Operators can supply an extracted JSON export file regardless of its filename, or a directory containing `conversations.json`. Conventional paths and repeated-import skipping continue to work.

## Fix

Select the export file using actual directory status at the existing loader instead of inferring filesystem kind from the filename suffix. The existing realpath, regular-file admission, UTF-8 validation, parser and vault writer remain authoritative. No configuration or storage-format change. The CLI documentation describes accepted paths.

The contributor's original commit is retained. Regression coverage reuses the existing serialized-text/image test across four layouts rather than duplicating import setup.

## Evidence

[Captured public built-CLI output, independent generated-file readback and transcript bytes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187175#issuecomment-6486662863).

- Main `f996c1c487a0fcb456a73c9af49e360b99d14de5`: `.json` directory, uppercase file and extensionless file each fail twice.
- Candidate `3dd48a1deac2a34542d86ef6363f977c3c71a38f`: all three layouts import twice, with exact transcript readback from generated Markdown.
- Ordinary `conversations.json` file and ordinary directory controls pass twice on both builds.
- Every successful import is repeated: skipped=1, created/updated=0, generated page bytes unchanged. All source/config bytes remain unchanged.
- Secretless Node 24 Docker; frozen installs and full builds passed. No account, model or paid key.
- Focused regression: main 3 failed / 3 passed; candidate 6 passed. Targeted formatting and lint passed.
- Whole PR delta: production 0, tests 0, docs +4.

Not tested: ZIP extraction, remote ChatGPT services or large-export performance; this correction only selects a supplied directory or extracted JSON file.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores suffix-based path selection without changing persisted formats. Blast radius is local ChatGPT export-path admission for the Memory Wiki importer; regular-file and UTF-8 safety checks remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix: record delivered messages in destination conversations
prs.body:
> **Current head: `f6a9db4cd26a81090685d6dc9fb09dba90a67ee1` — HOLD.** [Delivered-PDF fix, WebChat capture, Discord and Anthropic live proof, bounded anomaly attribution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169438#issuecomment-6130521749). The older `de583` evidence below remains historical. Before landing, rebase onto then-current main, resolve conflicts, then run hosted CI and ClawSweeper on that resulting head.

## What Problem This Solves

A message could be visible in a chat but absent from that chat's model history. Cross-chat message-tool sends used transcript-only mirrors, failure alerts had no destination row, and cron and heartbeat deliveries used separate writers or awareness notes. A follow-up such as “what did you just send here?” therefore lacked the message it referred to.

Closes #168683
Closes #168684

## Why This Change Was Made

Route confirmed core sends and settled native-plugin sends through one destination-transcript owner, reusing the serialized background-result writer. Preserve active-turn ordering, generation fencing, canonical replay identity and managed-media settlement. A producer already writing that conversation is skipped; producerless alerts are not. Cross-agent, ambiguous and unrepresentable destinations produce diagnostics rather than invented history.

Migrate cron, cross-chat message-tool sends, routed replies, failure alerts, subagent completions, external heartbeats, Workshop notices and the shared exec-approval fallback. Remove superseded destination mirrors and heartbeat awareness notes, while retaining source-reply/dispatch UI bookkeeping and Slack's existing suppression policy. Confirmed delivery marks the receiving chat active. Post-send recording failure does not resend an accepted message.

The released Plugin SDK `mirror` input remains accepted through the current SDK major with a bounded deprecation warning; it cannot redirect history or restore a second writer. Bundled callers use automatic destination recording.

[Conversation transcript ownership ADR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/de583443efa045e47275d67645042306584d0941/docs/refactor/conversation-transcript-ownership.md#status-and-order).

## User Impact

Cross-chat sends, alerts, subagent completions and heartbeat deliveries now enter the destination's model history once. Normal replies and same-chat message-tool sends do not gain a second model-visible row. No configuration migration, database schema or stored queue shape changes.

Google Chat first contact can make one metadata GET to classify a previously unseen space. Concurrent lookups share it. Inbound events, existing lookups and send responses seed a bounded account/credential-scoped cache. Known classifications and permanent 403/404 failures remain cached for the lifecycle; transient failures and incomplete responses retry only on a later send after **15 minutes**. Revocation before lookup prevents token acquisition and HTTP; accepted sends still settle. Slack's existing cache and Matrix's local-only lookup are unchanged.

## Evidence

Frozen candidate: **`de583443efa045e47275d67645042306584d0941`**, including main `31a46b00588` for the required Slack CI repair. The following are observed results, not inferred from source:

- **4374:** 1,433 tests passed, **74 expected files = 74 executed**, no missing/extra files, 11 canonical-entrypoint shards, 497.65 seconds. Includes affected owner suites and the integrated cron failure/timeout paths.
- **4377:** full `check-changed` passed against that main base, without skip flags. Core/extension/script/test types, formatting, lint and ownership guards passed. Script, production and full-tree Knip scans each reported **zero** findings. Existing nonfatal lint/SDK-inventory warnings remain.
- **4365 on parent `bf4209718cf`:** 159 tests, **8 expected = 8 executed**, including initial-revoked zero-token/zero-HTTP authority, pending revocation, accepted-send settlement, location-only payloads and cache policy. [Executed guarded-HTTP evidence and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169438#issuecomment-6119785850). This is isolated HTTP-fixture execution, not live Google credentials or servers.
- **4371:** all seven required new mutation controls failed at their intended assertions: zero backoff, disabled retry, permanent-error retry, single-flight removal, wrong status classification, direct SQLite canonical replay identity and memory canonical replay identity. All source hashes restored. **4373:** restored replay positives passed, **2 expected = 2 executed**, 3 tests. These owners are unchanged by the final main integration. An additional exploratory background-wrapper timestamp-copy mutation survived its text-only test; it is not counted as proof.
- Retained unchanged-input mutation receipts cover destination/creatorless/cron/routeReply/subagent/SDK (**4327**), alert (**4314**), producer/current-chat skips (**4348**), thread/cross-agent/retry/local routes (**4350**), heartbeat (**4338**), exec fallback (**4315**), rejected/uncertain/post-send failure (**4352**), recovery text (**4316**), recovery media/native/normalization (**4351**), receipt threads/media (**4353**), guarded Google transport (**4359**) and location-only output (**4362**). Earlier managed-media/recovery-generation controls **4210/4212** remain unchanged-input evidence.
- **Upgrade 4310/4313:** 46 and 58 tests passed using source-derived v2026.10.1-compatible row JSON, real SQLite sessions/transcripts/cron/recovery and retained legacy mirror metadata. This was **not** a binary-authored or physical old-schema upgrade. The Docker survivor was waived because this PR changes no stored shape, update, Doctor or plugin-loading path.
- Runtime **4375** passed. A subsequent E2E preparation failed asset copy before running tests (**4376**); **4385** completed canonical remaining asset/postbuild/stamp phases without recompiling TypeScript.

### Fresh real-model Telegram rounds

[Redacted per-case timelines, row counts and actual answers](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169438#issuecomment-6119790067).

**4378 and 4444:** two independent complete fresh Test Server rounds on the frozen candidate, each doctor-first with its own forum and ports, real `openai/gpt-4.1-mini`, **14/14 expected case records per round**, 14 and 13 provider requests. Both passed:

- Tool A → B: exact sent payload recalled in B, one destination row, zero duplicate rows in A.
- Normal reply and follow-up: one stored answer and one occurrence in follow-up provider history.
- Same-topic tool: real-model recall from existing producer-owned history, no additional canonical row.
- Unowned job failed twice: one alert; both real-model answers named the job, two failures and command exit 23.
- Cron A → B: exact “7 pear crates and 3 apple crates” payload/reference recalled; one destination row.
- Cron `session:B` → B: exact “4 ready pallets and 2 pending pallets” payload/reference recalled; one model-owned row, no added canonical row.

Both forums and all six jobs were removed; credential/runtime scratch and guarded key files were removed and ports were free. Round 2 request 10 recorded HTTP 200 then a transport failure, but its cron succeeded/delivered and the single visible payload, stored row and subsequent real-model recall were observed. Historical main controls **4339/4363** belong to `b569c88b927`, not the newly integrated main.

### Slack and native status

- **4367 vs 4368:** the original Slack suppression failure reproduced identically on `bf420` and clean main `1ea4da07a22` (15 passed/1 failed, 1 expected = 1 executed on each). The main repair `91231e054e7` is integrated, and that exact suppression case now **passes**.
- **4425:** the final Slack file executed exactly once, 15 passed/1 failed. A different native-root/stop-rejection case failed Slack HTTP ingress at line 1747. Logs show restart-signal fence at 11:56:08, SIGTERM at 11:56:10, then the event processed at 11:56:12 and rejected with “Gateway is shutting down” / `GatewayDrainingError`, before transcript-owner recording. **Not attributed.** A separate baseline/runtime and further rerun were explicitly waived for this hold; the assertion was not weakened.
- Historical native summary-profile failures matched **4068 vs clean-main 4096**. The final integrated native suite **4424 now passes all 9 tests**, 1 expected = 1 executed, including those four cases. Historical failures are not presented as current-head failures.

### Hosted CI and attribution

[CI run 38218249000](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38218249000), exact frozen head, completed with 81 successful jobs, 21 selector-skipped jobs and three failures in its initial attempt. The one authorized failed-job retry also failed the same two substantive jobs plus the aggregate gate. No further rerun or main integration is planned.

- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-19`: `sessions-rewind.test.ts` expects one `session_upstream_links` SELECT during fork and observes two on hosted Linux. **Reproducible on hosted Linux; not reproduced locally; not attributed.** Canonical Bun 1.4.2 proofs on clean base `31a46b00588` passed both the isolated file (**4454**, 25 tests, 1 expected = 1 executed) and exact hosted four-file set/order (**4455**, 122 tests, 4 = 4). The candidate passed the same isolated file (**4456**, 25 tests, 1 = 1) and exact four-file set/order (**4457**, 120 tests, 4 = 4). Direct fork, SQL-observer and mutation/cache files are unchanged; no causal link to destination recording was established. The count assertion remains unchanged.
- `build-artifacts`: the built SQLite lifecycle proof reports terminal `agent.wait` **`AbortError: agent run aborted` without a qualifying stopReason** while the fixture intentionally races session deletion. **Reproducible on hosted Linux; not attributed.** A prior hosted-only occurrence on #168996 failed [38123493810](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38123493810/job/114423118706); its [38124577177 attempt 2 build-artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38124577177/job/114429812565) passed. That is prior-occurrence evidence, **not proof this failure is inherited**. Exact-base CI skipped this built proof, so its green status does not supply a baseline.
- `openclaw/ci-gate`: aggregate failure from those two jobs. Hosted native and Slack-containing test lanes otherwise passed; the separate local Slack failure above is still disclosed.

Code and assertions were left unchanged after the bounded attribution checks and one retry. No green CI claim or inherited-failure override is made.

Hosted ClawSweeper is **`ready` on the exact head**, reviewed October 12 at 08:19 UTC: [final review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169438#issuecomment-6115155290). It reports no findings or remaining contributor steps and accepts the bounded attribution as complete. Its verdict is ready for **maintainer review**, with the explicit landing hold retained; this does not make the red CI green.

## Known limits

Internal transcript-only publications remain outside this change. X session-key parity remains #168686; creator-reset behavior remains #169258; native-only projection, including polls, remains #169297. Recovery adds history only when one accepted normalized-text payload proves the delivered content; ambiguous multi-payload/media/presentation/native recovery warns instead of guessing or resending.

Reverting changes future recording behavior; already-appended ordinary history rows remain. The blast radius is destination model history, not provider wire conversion or channel send semantics.

**HOLD — no merge, landing, override or auto-merge authorized.** The unattributed Slack failure remains disclosed for the eventual landing decision.

prs.title: fix: preserve original prompts after Gateway restarts
prs.body: Fixes #187143 ## What Problem This Solves An ordinary Control UI request can disappear from chat history when a graceful Gateway restart interrupts it before the first response. The resumed task can finish successfully while the conversation shows only the restart instruction and the resulting work. The original bytes remain stored, but orphan recovery has moved the original message off the active history branch. ## User Impact The accepted human prompt remains visible as its original message, separately from the new system resume instruction. Recovery keeps the same session and creator, and continues to use current authority. This requires no configuration change or migration and does not replay the original execution or promise exactly-once behavior for arbitrary interrupted external actions. ## Why This Change Was Made Fresh restart inputs carry `internal_system` provenance with source `restart`. The session-boundary orphan repair did not recognize that continuation when deciding whether to preserve an unanswered human message. It reset the active branch and folded the old text into the new input's private model projection instead. This change handles that existing restart input in the existing preservation guard. It leaves shared provenance policies used by fallback, accounting, and other runtimes unchanged. The regression reopens persisted history and checks that the original row and a distinct resume row remain. The real-Gateway case also checks original message identity and provenance, creator identity, one disabled automation, and visibility after reloading the page. ## Evidence - On base `0b538f7d5a4d9e3328f572cc07fe23402f733f36`, the real Control UI/native Gateway replacement case reproduced original history and rendered-message counts changing from one to zero. Selected identity/hash observations showed the stored original was unchanged while a new leaf-control record detached it; the returned page contained only four messages, so the history limit was not responsible. - The focused persisted-boundary regression failed on the unfixed owner and passed with the correction. All 11 selected owner/caller/control files passed, totaling 148 tests, including prompt-prefix stability and restart authority controls. - Changed-file formatting/lint and the selected compiler checks passed. The existing real-Gateway restart case passed on the committed tree: original message once with the same ID, separate resume instruction once, unchanged session/creator, one disabled job, and original text visible after reload. The scenario took 25.1 seconds of test time (84.3 seconds including Vitest setup/transform). The deterministic case uses a controlled Responses provider and its existing routing marker. A separate normal guest request for an onboarding plan was exercised on the production-identical `74cebbb` runtime. Native OCM stop/start replaced the Gateway after admission, with `hasActiveRun: true` and before the first assistant reply. Recovery kept the original message ID/hash, session, creator, owner, visibility, guest scopes, and model selection; one resume input led to a useful completed plan. The pre-stop projected status was `queued`, so this observation does not claim the original live provider request had already started. The live command's final exact-text DOM lookup timed out because the long answer left the original outside the rendered window. A read-only scroll of the same recovered conversation revealed it once, without another user prompt or restart. The original failed observer record is retained alongside that completed readback. Independent engineering review and the canonical automated review are clean on `60a33153dd9b76b179bce216a19ef8c376daf58b`. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40806384923) passed on that head, including lint, compiler, and test-size checks. The dedicated real-Gateway CI family was scope-skipped on this head; the named restart case was executed through the separate native proof above. The unrelated channel-management case was not rerun in that focused invocation. [ClawSweeper’s exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187157#issuecomment-6485749858) reports Diamond with no findings. The final target was also reproduced as broken at `8d46327b2656a3bb09889167570c4a35eb061e42`; the same scenario passed with this patch combined with that target (21.7 seconds of test time). ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Before the fix: only the restart instruction and completed response remain in active history\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3bc42b8-054e-48c0-bfd8-162c8795f4b6) | ![After the fix: the original user prompt remains above the separate restart instruction and completed disabled automation\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fff63701-baca-4f3d-8e08-548e90f13913) | ### Exact\-head controlled\-provider restart and recovery https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b90485a-93ca-4234-9e15-33c0b6f71d39 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 0b538f7d5a4d9e3328f572cc07fe23402f733f36 - Exact head: `60a33153dd9b76b179bce216a19ef8c376daf58b` - Scenario: Submit a disabled\-reminder request through Control UI, replace the Gateway at the controlled provider checkpoint, and inspect the completed conversation\. - Runtime/build: Real Gateway and Chromium with a controlled Responses provider\. Tested tree a7805569223c1e766e55f709b24652e4b732a914, committed unchanged as 60a33153dd9b76b179bce216a19ef8c376daf58b\. Browser viewport 1280×900; matched main\-conversation crops 970×780\. - Original prompt in active history: before: 0; after: 1, same message identity - Restart input: 1 separate system resume instruction - Requested automation: 1 job, still disabled - Same synthetic request, viewport, light theme, and identical crop\. Native generated job IDs/timestamps differ between independent fixtures\. - The candidate also reloads and scrolls to the original\. Baseline server history contains no original row, so the viewport cannot explain the before/after difference\. - Before observation\-only overlay changes only diagnostics in the test; production source matches the baseline commit\. - Final browser assertions passed on the exact committed tree\. - Captioned video preserves the full recorded interaction; its last frame is held for readability\. - Original screenshots and source recording retained during review\.

prs.title: fix(gateway-client): bound terminal content identities
prs.body:
## Problem and fix

Accepted terminal receipt lists kept full serialized reply content after visible history changed. The 32-receipt count limit could retain several large copies of a reply.

Hash the existing canonical content tuple with full SHA-256 through the existing streaming serializer. Content fallback keys are now 79 ASCII bytes. Persisted ID, import identity, sequence and key precedence remain unchanged; full text, rich content, media and import metadata still affect equality, including suffix differences.

The public helper returns an opaque, ephemeral correlation key. This changes its content fallback representation without changing persisted IDs or requiring a storage migration. Run bodies, inferred terminals and receipt-less finishing ownership are preserved.

## Validation

- Original reducer regression on published baseline `85090c9`: one intended failure (`108041 > 80`), 56 sibling cases passed.
- Production candidate `2bec93859dd1109aa01b1b7b8e06f917f5ce143b`: 205 tests passed across reducer, fingerprint, run-event, PR-refresh and TUI owners.
- A subsequent test-only fixture correction names its attachment before constructing the array. All 12 fingerprint cases, the package test-type graph and scoped type-aware lint pass; assertion values and production source are unchanged.
- Independent full-source review, fresh full review and the fixture-only delta review found no actionable issue. Normal configured content, format and freshness commit hooks passed.
- The first CI attempt failed package test types on the corrected unchecked array access; it also reported a braces lint failure in `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts`, the test-line budget guard, and a bundled root-help timeout during runtime build. The timeout cause remains unclassified. These failures are retained as failed evidence.
- Canonical standalone protocol and gateway-client builds, including declarations, pass on the integrated source. Plain Node loads of both emitted public entries and a browser-target bundle assert 79-byte keys, large-clone equality and suffix distinction; the bundle has zero external imports. Bundle execution used Node, not a real browser.
- Default full application build passes in the existing exact-source manual run, including declarations. Its normal application artifact passes the same plain Node public-entry and browser-target bundle assertions after native commit verification. This reuses unchanged build inputs across the final test-budget-only commit; browser execution remains Node-only. The selected remote allocation queued and was stopped before payload execution. The maintainer explicitly approved CI-first publication for this PR. `ci:full` was applied before the first production push. The named default full-build job passes; the complete manual run is not claimed green. 

- The normal application artifact also passes the original-order public reducer replay in plain Node through both emitted entries: 40 distinct large late finals, visible-history removal, 32 retained 79-byte content receipts, identical-final replay deduplication and suffix-distinct acceptance. The original run body remains intact. Together with the full application build, this completes the latest ClawSweeper proof suggestion; real-browser whole-app heap/navigation measurement is deferred to the resident-window work.
- Final-head [CI run 40805037082](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40805037082), attempt 1 at `702f8e5`, completed with failure. Two substantive E2E failures were independently attributed outside this change: session-diff token styling evaluates a detached token in an empty-history fixture that supplies no final-content digest input; the automation restart case does not find the original prompt in a direct backend history response after successfully creating its disabled automation, and that persistence/filter path does not call client final-content identity. Their underlying causes remain unknown. No matching failed-baseline reproduction, CI rerun or aggregate green result is claimed. Follow-ups retain the retry-safe attached-token styling oracle and the restart history omission investigation. Landing uses the documented attributed-failure route with the failed result preserved.

The fingerprint tests use an independent Node crypto oracle and cover Unicode, lone surrogates, stable key order, rich content, media, import identities, status notices and persisted precedence. PR-refresh deduplicates repeated identical large content finals while still refreshing suffix-distinct finals; the oversized arbitrary persisted-key guard remains covered.

## Scope

Production: +29/-16 (net +13), for bounded canonical receipt ownership and its sibling comment. Dependency metadata: +4/-0, declaring the runtime-owned hash dependency and lock importer. Tests: +162/-1.

This bounds content fallback keys, not arbitrary persisted identity strings or all session memory. No measured Firefox heap, latency, whole-app retention or deployment claim.

prs.title: fix(ci): give unfitted agents-support release shard 90-minute headroom
prs.body:
## Problem

The full-release `checks-node-agentic-agents-support` job runs the agents-support suite under Node and then Bun inside one hosted job capped at 60 minutes. On slow hosted runners it no longer fits: during 2026.10.8 release validation it took 38m29s, then 59m40s, then was cancelled at the 60-minute cap twice. On job 122066874734 both runtimes passed completely (402 files / 5,335 tests; Node 2032.8s, Bun 1466.2s) and the job was cancelled 9 seconds later in post-steps.

## Solution

Add `agentic-agents-support` to `LONG_UNFITTED_RELEASE_SHARDS`, so the unfitted release row keeps 90-minute whole-job headroom like the other long owners until it has complete timings and is split.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-release-node-test-plan.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 5 passed, about 8s wall time, CI cost negligible. The new `agentic-agents-support` case fails without the code change.
- Release run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40454704623 (attempt 3, job 122066874734).

prs.title: fix(setup): emit structured JSON errors for one-shot failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes setup automation receiving a string `error` instead of the [documented CLI JSON failure envelope](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli#json-failures) when a one-shot request fails.

## User Impact

Scripts can read `ok`, `error.type`, and `error.message` consistently for setup preconditions, thrown execution failures, and unavailable inference. Existing inference `status` and recovery `guidance` remain beside the envelope. Consumers of the former string error should use `error.message`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing core failure formatter at the shared conversational setup gate, covering setup and its onboarding callers without another renderer. Human output, inference admission, and output-draining exit behavior stay intact. No config, provider request, protocol, or stored-data change.

## Evidence

- Scenario: One-shot setup errors use the documented CLI failure envelope; Human diagnostics and inference recovery metadata retain their behavior
- Entry: Built OpenClaw CLI, node dist/entry.js setup --yes --json, isolated home/state/config, Linux Node24.22.1; disputed owner ran unmocked: src/commands/system-agent-with-inference.ts, shared setup/onboarding gate
- Same command on base `1e93aee` and head `1aa6c8e`: `node dist/entry.js setup --yes --json`
  - Before (base): RED exit1 with error as a string, incompatible with the published common JSON contract
  - After (head): GREEN reused f3a68b0 build capture: exit1 with error.type=cli_error and error.message containing the original --yes/--message recovery text; one JSON stdout document. Final head only repairs the existing test mock and has identical production inputs
- Readback (subprocess,config-file): Actual child exits1; parsed stdout contains ok:false and error.type/message; human stderr matches baseline; config bytes unchanged
- Proof harness: Frozen native driver SHA256 76d629b3a48bf92373bc59c8a6726c0e25b4ab5734040787788b9e26901771e7; build f3a68b0 verified 2026-10-29 02:49 UTC, explicitly reused after a test-only follow-up. git diff f3a68b0..1aa6c8e names only src/commands/system-agent-with-inference.test.ts; production code, dependencies and build inputs are identical
- Control: Human-mode refusal keeps its message and empty stdout; help exits0; inference status/guidance and secret redaction covered by existing consumers
- Other callers checked: rg runSystemAgentWithInference src finds setup, onboard, hidden alias and two existing suites; rg error/status/guidance in both suites identified the direct JSON consumer; both suites updated together
- Tests: OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/system-agent-with-inference.test.ts --maxWorkers=1; 9 pass after the final test-only follow-up, exit0. The unchanged security-redaction consumer retains its 6 passing cases from the f3a68b0 candidate run; 15 distinct cases covered (measured cost: Final changed command file single-file/single-worker 204.95s (87% cold transforms); unchanged security consumer 150.85s from the f3a68b0 candidate (91% transforms). All 15 cases retained, no new fixtures or timers)
- Not tested: No live model/provider turn; broad suites run through PR CI

Scoped tsgo and sourcePerformance build passed on the equivalent f3a68b0 production snapshot; final changed-file type-aware lint, oxfmt, diff, mock-export and test-line ratchets pass. prs.title: perf(state): attribute authority payload bytes by request class
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Authority payload bytes are aggregated without a request class, so operators cannot identify which SQLite command families produce large commit and settlement receipts.

Related: #186348, #186234.

## User Impact

Prometheus now exposes the existing bounded `request_class` label on `kind="authority"` payload-byte series. Unknown or unattributed classes use `other`. Aggregate byte totals and message/unmeasured counters retain their meaning. Documentation includes a bytes-per-minute query.

## Why This Change Was Made

The broker already knows each job's class. It now binds that telemetry fact to the job's private admission port before dispatch; ordinary commit delivery and settlement recovery use the same class. The metrics owner and exporter reuse their existing bounded-class path. There is no extra serialization, payload decoding, schema change, or change to authority checks, FIFO ordering, durability, or receipts.

This is the observability-only first step. It does not claim reduced allocation or CPU. Production code grows by 3 lines to carry and export the requested attribution; no cache or second receipt protocol is introduced.

## Evidence

- Final head `89bd720ba360fe0a5683c924d52a009ed8a81b45`: [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40809092057) and `openclaw/ci-gate` are green. PR checks: 76 passed, 58 skipped, no failures or pending checks. Left unmerged for maintainer handoff.

- Regression on the pre-fix source: five failures covering bounded authority classes and native commit/failed-delivery settlement accounting. The same focused tests pass with the fix.
- Collector, admission/settlement, broker reply/cleanup, and Prometheus exporter: 74 tests pass across five files (58.01 s total runner time; individual test execution remains small).
- Real plugin-state publication tests: 17 pass; a real write exercises the broker-to-private-port class binding while preserving resident namespace reads.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped clean through P2 on the final local diff against `496263aa5cc6d8a1200c72b4ef3511888253358c`. The Codex helper refused startup because its requested provider route did not match operator config; configuration was not changed. Rebase to `89bd720ba360fe0a5683c924d52a009ed8a81b45` is patch-identical (`git range-diff`); incoming main changes do not touch the implementation or tests here.
- Final telemetry adjustment rerun: 67 tests pass across collector, admission, and plugin-state publication (15.23 s Vitest duration); the previously passing 24 reply/cleanup/exporter tests are unchanged.
- Targeted infrastructure test typecheck, `pnpm tsgo:test:root` (all four shards), changed-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass.
- First-head CI exposed the profiler’s exact-source instrumentation anchor: [failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40807968821/job/123231833047). Reproduced locally (1 failed / 14 passed); updated the anchor to preserve the new class argument. The same profile test file now passes all 15 tests (8.29 s runner time). Independent review of the two-line repair is clean through P2. No CI rerun was requested; the repair is included in the new head.
- Test-line ratchet: 6,246,290 lines, effective ceiling 6,320,170; 73,880 lines of headroom after rebasing. This PR changes neither the scalar nor allocation records.

Synthetic owner measurements confirm payload conservation; these are ten real plugin-state register writes per shape, not a whole-Gateway stress comparison:

| Value size | Authority bytes before | Authority bytes after | New class |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 KiB | 14,370 | 14,370 | `plugin_state` |
| 32 KiB | 331,840 | 331,840 | `plugin_state` |
| 64 KiB | 659,520 | 659,520 | `plugin_state` |

The 64 KiB fixture's committed value JSON accounts for 99.4% of authority bytes. That postimage is needed by the canonical namespace owner; a follow-up may reconstruct caller-known JSON from a request-local reference, but this PR makes no producer change or production-largest-class claim. No production Gateway was accessed. A Team-shaped Gateway census, allocation/CPU A/B, and whole-Gateway stress measurements remain follow-up work, not evidence for this observability-only PR.

prs.title: fix(gateway): children spawned by a cron run die when the parent run ends
prs.body:
Closes #185961

## Decision for maintainers: cron reassignment

**Behavior change:** with this PR, children spawned by a cron-root run keep running after the parent run returns, **including when that cron job is later reassigned or deleted**. Today they die when the parent returns, whether or not anything was reassigned. That is the reported bug, and the reason the issue asks where the child's lifetime should start.

- Children still stop on `/stop`, on aborting the parent with its descendants, and on a reset of the requesting session (the existing requester-wide subagent cleanup), the same as children of a main session.
- The cron root's own session stays fenced, which is what #161085 protects: a child writes only to its own session, and its completion report runs as a new run in the cron key with its own fresh fence.
- If children should also stop when the cron job is reassigned, each child would need to hold a cron-root lease for its whole life. This PR does not add that; I'm happy to follow up if you prefer that design.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sub-agents spawned by a run in a cron job's base session (`agent:<id>:cron:<job>`) fail with "Guarded request authority is no longer active" once that run ends, and their completion reports never reach the cron session.

## User Impact

User impact: children spawned from a cron-root run keep working after the parent run returns, and their results are delivered back to the cron session, the same as children of a main-session run.

## Why This Change Was Made

A stable cron root fences its own provider requests for the life of its run (#161085): the run's prompt executes inside `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority`, which marks the fence inactive when the run returns. `sessions_spawn` runs inside that prompt and launches the child through the in-process `agent` dispatch. The child's queued work captures the async context, so the child, and later its completion-report turn, inherit the parent's fence and fail on their first provider request after the parent returns.

The in-process `agent` handoff (`withInProcessGatewayDispatch`) already starts accepted autonomous runs outside two caller-owned scopes, the caller's transcript writer and its operator tool authority, because they "must not retain the caller's … authority after that invocation closes". This change adds the caller's request fence to that list, through `runOutsideGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` in `fetch-request-authority.ts`. The child then establishes its own fences when it runs, like any other run.

The request store can also carry a per-request egress check (`beforeRequest`). A run installs it only around its own provider stream call (`attempt-stream-settle.ts`), not while tools execute, so none is active when `sessions_spawn` hands off and none is dropped.

## Evidence

On unchanged `main`, both the mock-model Gateway runs and the live runs with a real Anthropic model show the reporter's exact error chain: the child's next provider request fails with "Guarded request authority is no longer active", the completion-report turn into the cron session fails with the same error, and the Gateway logs `Subagent announce give up (permanent_failure)`. With this change, the child finishes and its report reaches the cron session in both.

### Gateway regression (built Gateway process, local mock model)

`test/gateway-cron-root-subagent-spawn.e2e.test.ts` (new, one case) starts the built Gateway with a local OpenAI Responses mock. An `agent` request on `agent:main:cron:child-lifetime` spawns one child with `sessions_spawn`; the child's provider replies are held until the parent's `agent` request has returned. The case requires the child's second provider request and the report turn into the cron session to both arrive. Tool search is off so `sessions_spawn` is a direct tool, as in the existing `cron-isolated-spawn-only-child-delivery` QA scenario. Unchanged `main`, Gateway log (ids shortened):

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=subagent:agent:main:cron:proof-job error="Guarded request authority is no longer active." taskKind=spawn sessionKey=agent:main:subagent:3966…
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="Guarded request authority is no longer active." taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:main:cron:proof-job runId=announce:v1:…
[agents/subagent-announce] Subagent completion direct announce failed for run e0da64e0… err={"name":"GatewayClientRequestError","message":"Guarded request authority is no longer active.",…}
[warn] Subagent announce give up (permanent_failure) run=e0da64e0… requester=agent:main:cron:proof-job
```

Mock-model Gateway runs of this scenario: unchanged `main` failed 4 of 4 with the chain above (the child never reaches the model); with this change 9 of 9 passed. Those counts come from a longer local version of the test; the committed case is that scenario trimmed to its core assertions (the committed case waits on the child's own run with `agent.wait`: on unchanged `main` it fails as soon as that run ends with `status: "error"`, 1 of 1; with this change it passes 2 of 2 in about 20 s).

### Live run (real Anthropic model)

Same built Gateway with `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, reached through a local recording proxy that holds the child's first reply until the parent's `agent` request has returned. The parent was asked to spawn one child and reply `SPAWNED`. The child was asked to read a file and reply `LIVE-CHILD-OK`. Three runs on each side, cron key `agent:main:cron:live-child-lifetime`: `main` failed 3 of 3 as below; with this change 3 of 3 completed and delivered the report (in two of them the child answered with a sentence instead of the exact marker word, but its run finished and the report arrived). Excerpts from the first pair:

Unchanged `main`: the model's reply to the child's first request (a `read` call) arrives, then the child's second request fails inside the Gateway before it leaves, and the report turn fails on the fence:

```
response role=parent tools=[sessions_spawn] … response role=parent text="SPAWNED"
parent run returned status=ok
response role=child status=200 tools=[read]
[model-fetch] error provider=liveproxy api=anthropic-messages model=claude-sonnet-5-5 elapsedMs=0 sessionKey="agent:main:subagent:4f9c…" requestNumber=2
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="Guarded request authority is no longer active." taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:main:cron:live-child-lifetime runId=announce:v1:…
[warn] Subagent announce give up (permanent_failure) … requester=agent:main:cron:live-child-lifetime
```

With this change:

```
parent run returned status=ok
response role=child status=200 tools=[read]
response role=child status=200 text="LIVE-CHILD-OK"
response role=report status=200 text="The live-child task finished successfully and returned exactly LIVE-CHILD-OK. …"
[agent] run announce:v1:agent:main:subagent:1978…:b355… ended with stopReason=stop
```

No "Guarded request authority" line in that Gateway log.

**Unit:** the existing launch case in `server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.authorization.test.ts` now also runs the launch inside a request fence and requires the launched run to see none (both tool-authority variants). It fails on `main` (the launched run inherits the fence) and passes here.

**Consumers:** 17 related test files (every `server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.*` suite, `server-plugin-subagent-runtime*`, `subagent-spawn.in-process-gateway`, `subagent-announce-completion-delivery`, `fetch-guard.authority`, `attempt-execution-phase`): 164 of 164 pass. One fork-transport timeout under a loaded host passed 3 of 3 on rerun; that test reads through `sessions.get`, not the changed `agent` path.

**Test lines:** net +108 against `main`: one root-cause unit test (+10, fails on `main`) plus one Gateway case (98 lines) for the report turn into the cron session, which no unit layer reaches; ClawSweeper's review of the issue asked for exactly this regression. The Gateway case takes about 22 s, mostly Gateway startup; it waits on the child's run and then on the report, so a regression fails as soon as the child's run ends.

**Stopping a detached child** (existing coverage, rerun on this change): `subagent-control.accepted-stop.test.ts`, `subagent-control.commands.test.ts` and `subagent-announce.requester-settle-cancel.test.ts` pass (92 tests with the launch test). Locally, aborting the child (`sessions.abort`) or resetting the cron root (`sessions.reset`) after the parent returns stopped the child before its next provider request (2 of 2 each; the child sent no further request).

**Operator revocation** (one-off proof run, not committed): the cron-root parent was started by an operator connected with its own device. After the parent returned, an admin revoked that device's operator token (`device.token.revoke`), then the held child was released. 2 of 2 runs on this change; the child never reached the provider:

```
02:42:55.560 [gateway] device token revoked device=8483… role=operator
02:42:55.582 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=subagent:agent:main:cron:child-lifetime error="Session turn no longer owns controller admission" taskKind=spawn runId=100e39c3…
agent.wait → {"status":"error","stopReason":"rpc","providerStarted":false}; provider requests from the child: 0
```

**Checks:** `pnpm check:changed` on the change: typecheck, format, lint, line-cap, test-line, assertion and mock ratchets pass. Its remaining failures do not involve this change: Knip reports unused exports in untouched files (`extensions/knowledge/src/conversation-access-view.ts`, `src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-manifest-comparison.ts`, `src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-cleanup.ts`), and the SQLite worker ratchet could not run on the test host (`rg` missing).

Not tested: a cron job woken by `sessions_send`, and the CLI-runtime (`claude-cli`) parent path. Both reach the child through the same `agent` handoff.
