prs.title: fix(plugins): continue self-held session sends after reload
prs.body:
## Why

A root session's original `sessions_send` can be lost when the admission guard refuses to wait while that turn holds a reloading plugin. The target has not accepted the send; re-running the model is not a safe substitute for retaining that exact send.

## Changes

- Retain the original send only after a private `NoAccept` refusal proves that admission did not occur. Join the obsolete owner before using the replacement outcome to continue.
- Replay the original send once only when the exact replacement operation has a healthy outcome. Settle the retained operation with one completion wake, including on failure. Failed or unknown outcomes do not replay.
- Keep the original conversation-policy identity and selected participant/source authority pinned. Re-evaluate current authorization and sandbox policy before replay without weakening a restriction captured earlier.
- Keep classification and policy preparation separate from the executor. Retain the classification entry’s sandbox predicates through final admission using the existing source-authority owner; the classification helper no longer performs a post-effect recheck that replaces a known accepted result with an uncertain result.
- Normalize retained resume arguments to admission-only execution. Keep explicit invalid resume timeout/watch requests rejected.
- Include late channel-recovery failures in private replacement health without changing the public restored projection. Forward product-test cancellation to the existing managed child owner.

## Impact

This is root-originating continuation only. A root send to a native child is supported; a native-originating send is still denied. Collector, cron, worker and remote-originating contexts remain unsupported and reject early.

Retention is process-local, not a durable restart queue. Stop does not claim to retract an already accepted send, and restart does not recover retained sends. There is no new configuration or public reload-status change.

## Base integration

`main` was merged at `a919e5ecc4f6c579e16ab21499ccda3acaa1fb07` in merge commit `c8ab8cd64ff98cb17e65461b42bc2f6b64634d36` (tree `aeec667762151057b95750de4f9f9f59e96d7dc4`), joining the earlier PR head `5aff0439b5c2d0d5426d7ee1dfcbbce9b8ca97e7` (feature commit `f239726aa340123954d1450d0873739776c29008`, tree `b59ba20c230b8fc111d55066e9c4fe75e69ca4da`).

- `main` was merged because the PR conflicted with it. Three paths conflicted: `config/test-lines-baseline.txt`, `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-communication.ts` and `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.ts`. Both source conflicts come from #185730, which removed the subagent `terminalOwner` field and restart-recovery admission. The resolution keeps those removals and every line this PR adds; it introduces no new behavior.
- For 36 of the 37 PR paths, the lines added and removed relative to the new base match those relative to the old base. Seven of those files also changed on `main`, in separate hunks: `attempt.ts`, `session-tool-handoff.ts`, `sessions-send-communication.ts`, `agent-run-admission-phase.ts`, `agent-run-admission-types.ts`, `agent-turn-service.ts` and `server-plugin-in-process-authority.ts`. `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` now equals `main`'s, so this PR no longer changes it.
- Two independent reviews and a lead review accepted the resolution and found no conflict-resolution defect. One reviewer read the seven overlapping modules and the product test files whole; the other checked those modules only at the hunk level.

## Static repair after merge CI

Source commit `979c83811135cd8c95d740a5cd93a6c6db5cfb6c` (tree `5413b1353c838a274febc9dfc990a7caa8531970`) was published as head `83c2faf2f75d372f31c396a5a1cee49b492d581c`.

CI run [40795074130](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40795074130) tested the previous head `7595b27` merged into `main` at `71d954df153317e7ce83fbc0509be20405299258`. It found these PR-caused failures, which `979c838` addresses without behavior changes:

- **12 TypeScript errors in this PR's files** (`check-prod-types`, `check-test-types*`, declaration build, SDK boundary): a follow-up failure result without `selfHeld`, a replay-port result type, an untyped mutable refusal `stage`, a closure over a possibly undefined `child`, and test-only typing in `attempt.sessions-yield.test.ts`, `sessions-send-self-hold.test.ts` and `server-plugin-reload-lifecycle.test.ts`. The fixes are type-only, except that the follow-up failure now carries an explicit `selfHeld: undefined`. That path runs only after an accepted start, so it is never retained.
- **One import cycle** (`madge-import-cycles`, 84 modules): `agent-admission-refusal.ts` imported `agent-run-admission-types.ts` for a type, closing a cycle through the agent tools. It now declares the two dispatch ports it uses locally. The runtime import-cycle check was already clean.
- **The assertion-safety ratchet** flagged a new type assertion in `agent-admission-refusal.ts`; the typed refusal removes it.
- **The PR wrapper inventory** omitted the new `src/plugins/plugin-replacement-operation.ts`, which failed `eager-import-closure` (2 tests) and `pr-worktree-provision` (3 tests). The file is now listed in `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`.

Local evidence for the repair:

- Of the 12 type errors, only the 5 production sites were reproduced locally first, with the experimental `oxlint --type-check` diagnostic; the 7 test-type errors were seen only in CI. After the repair, that diagnostic reports no problems in all 36 changed TypeScript files. It is not the canonical type check: local `pnpm tsgo:core` still refuses its input before analysis ("Declaration input escapes checkout"), so canonical type and declaration analysis did not run locally.
- `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` reproduced the same 84-module cycle, then reports 0 cycles after the repair.
- `eager-import-closure` passes 35/35. Of the three failing `pr-worktree-provision` cases, two pass locally and the third is skipped on macOS.
- On the exact repaired tree, the self-hold suite passes 25/25. A supporting run with the same TypeScript source, before the inventory line was added, passed communication (47), requester continuation (11), reload lifecycle (14), `attempt.sessions-yield` (12), `server.agent-late-admission` (1) and `sessions-send-reply-flow.requester` (4). Formatting, diff, test-line (6,245,435 against 6,320,000) and assertion-safety checks pass.

Remaining CI failures on run 40795074130 that this PR does not cause, as far as the evidence shows:

- **Inherited from `main`:** the `mock-exports` ratchet (its inputs are byte-identical to `main`), and `server.channels-start-outcomes`, `server.approval-forwarding` and `server-startup-secret-owner-isolation`, which fail with the same titles in scheduled `main` CI.
- **Probably inherited:** `subagent-registry` "does not restore a superseded lifecycle after a successor is released" asserts gateway root work that #187090 removed on `main`. This PR touches neither file. Inferred, not reproduced on `main`.
- **Unclassified:** `server.context-prewarm.remote-proof` measured 1,340 ms against a 500 ms budget.

CI run [40802305283](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40802305283) tested `83c2faf` merged into `main` at `7074b619ff3087cb61d0825e3ff3457300ccb9ad`. The canonical production and test type checks, declaration build, SDK boundary and import-cycle check passed there. Its remaining failures:

- **Test-line ratchet:** 6,247,272 lines against a ceiling of 6,243,924; this PR adds 2,417. `main` had lowered the ceiling after this PR's base and has since restored it to 6,320,000 (#187162). This PR does not change the ceiling; the next run passed against the restored ceiling.
- **Lint:** a missing-braces error in `sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts`, a file this PR does not change. It came from `main` (#187065), also failed scheduled `main` CI, and is fixed on `main` (#187144).
- **Unclassified:** `server.context-prewarm.remote-proof` failed again (844 ms; 1,340 ms on the previous head). Its 500 ms budget is the largest gap between 20 ms heartbeat callbacks during the post-ready warmup window, not warmup or request latency. The test and the four core modules it exercises are identical on this PR, its CI base and the CI merge, and no causal path from this PR is established; it is also not shown to be inherited.

## Revocation proof

Current head: `b31e43ac536d40585d28e19bc6c9a29131ca87ce`, an empty publication bookkeeping commit on test commit `20068cd16f0fba183851189a7782e60f1b1029eb`. Tree: `20b00d8a25926d85ae091dadec0b210d38ec62d4`. CI run [40808307564](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40808307564) passed on this head, merged into `main` at `960debc51780c899df913ea2ddf3cf971a80ea02`.

The new product test `server.plugin-reload-send-revocation.product.test.ts` answers the earlier review's request for end-to-end proof that revoking the selected participant during a retained replay prevents the target effect. It runs a real Gateway with trusted-proxy TLS and two paired operator devices, Alice and Bob, in a shared session; Bob joins through the real `session.members.add` RPC. No authority, participant or executor is mocked.

1. Alice's turn holds the reloading plugin. Bob's steer joins her running turn, and the model selects Bob as the `sessions_send` user only after it has seen that steer.
2. Admission refuses the send because the turn holds the reloading plugin, so it is retained with `not_accepted` / `plugin_reload_self_hold`. The healthy replacement then replays it once with the same idempotency key.
3. A pass-through spy on the Gateway transport arms only on that retained receipt and fires exactly once, after the root turn has ended and the replacement has settled. It records state only and does not decide the outcome.

Results:

- **Bob allowed (control):** one target effect, one target transcript receipt and one settlement wake in Alice's conversation; no undelivered notice.
- **Bob revoked:** in the barrier, a real `device.token.revoke` revokes Bob's device and his own next request is refused. The replay is then refused by the retained Gateway continuation, whose captured authority is Bob's: the outcome is `error` with "Gateway continuation authority is no longer active". That check fires earlier than agent admission. The target receives no model request, provider effect or transcript receipt for the message. Because the settlement wake runs under the same revoked source, Alice gets no model wake; the host writes exactly one durable "could not continue this conversation automatically" notice to her conversation instead. Alice's own authority still works.
- In both cases there is one original send and no accepted retry, plugin retention returns to 0, target pending inputs are empty, and the managed child process tree is joined.

Each case needs a real Gateway, model fixture, plugin reload, two TLS operator clients and a real revocation, which is why the cases take tens of seconds rather than using callback ports. The test keeps the default 120,000 ms budget, binds private handoff stores before imports, and reuses a small plugin fixture helper extracted from the existing product test without changing its behavior. Two independent reviews and a lead review accepted the proof tree.

## Evidence

- **Exact-head CI passed.** Run 40808307564 on `b31e43a` completed successfully and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed, including canonical production and test type checks, the declaration build, SDK boundary, import-cycle checks, duplicates (no test clones), lint and ratchets (6,249,477 test lines against a ceiling of 6,320,170). Under Bun, the new revocation test passed in 64 s with the same oracles as locally (allowed: one effect, one wake, outcome `accepted`; revoked through `device.token.revoke`: no effects, no target model requests, no wakes, one notice, outcome `error`). The existing three-case test passed in 74 s (effects 1, 1 and 0; one wake each), and `server.context-prewarm.remote-proof` passed in 12 s. CI did not run these product tests under Node.
- On the proof tree, normal wrapper runs pass locally: the existing three-case test in 89.6 s (Node) and 104.4 s (Bun), and the new two-case revocation test in 90.3 s (Node) and 81.9 s (Bun). Earlier, on a heavily loaded host, the existing test had timed out at 120,000 ms on the merged tree under both runtimes; no timeout was changed.

Historical evidence for the reviewed feature tree `b59ba20`, before the merge. Reviewed change snapshot: `062aafd6dbe1d6c25f4696b7e84b609e499ae3c2d53ada981b4c59f2a5005281` (binary diff SHA-256 from base `228596060e33dfcddbb6740416f381daac6f84fe`).

- The 97 focused tests passed. Late channel failure and newly enabled sandbox denial have failing-before/passing-after evidence. Removing only retained-resume normalization reproduces the real admission-only rejection; restoring it passes the real-factory default-resume case. Explicit invalid resume controls remain rejected.
- Same-config regression barriers remove a per-session sandbox opt-out through the real durable or memory storage owner. Preparation and pre-executor changes refuse with zero executor calls; a change at the executor’s final source check has zero effects and retains the conservative uncertain status. Five original causal failures pass, including preservation of a known result after an accepted effect. A no-change positive and a newly sandboxed-but-allowed row verify one replay and the executor sandbox flag. Handoff and executor are explicit unit-test ports; these are not sessions.patch RPC tests.
- Local ClawSweeper was unavailable in this environment. The selected maintainer fallback is local AutoReview plus one hosted ClawSweeper review.
- **Local AutoReview: one actual run, P0–P3, INCOMPLETE (exit 2), not a clean review.** It reviewed the old base against prior local snapshot `660111f3b78ffa52dc495d82c7854912436af127dfd74e2dcba80bc1b9d7cfab`, with 37 changed full-file bodies and 62 unchanged contracts. All 24 partition reports returned, but that is not 24 complete assessments: required caller/full-body context was not guaranteed to accompany each assigned change.
- All six review findings are accounted for. Four (API1, API3, API5 and API6) are implemented: late recovery health, current sandbox classification, retained resume normalization and product-child cancellation. Two (API2 and API4) concerned historical index-only variants at `381e0ec3d153c5f02063ea21622b753de8c60fda` and were replaced in the committed candidate. They were valid findings, not false positives.
- Independent A/B affected verification of snapshot `062aafd6` passed with no findings, and lead review accepted tree `b59ba20`. Independent and lead reviews of the static repair tree `5413b13` found no code defects; a reviewer's correction to the evidence wording is reflected here.

## Gaps

- ClawSweeper re-reviewed head `b31e43a`: ready for maintainer review, with no findings. Its remaining test note is that a complete Gateway scenario failing on the merge base is not shown; the failing-before evidence above comes from focused tests, not that scenario.
- `server.context-prewarm.remote-proof` passed on this head, and passed in isolated runs at both the earlier CI merge and its base. The heartbeat gaps it measured in the two earlier CI runs (1,340 ms and 844 ms) remain unexplained.
- CI ran the normal product tests only under Bun; the Node runs above are local.
- Historical, not current evidence: local `pnpm tsgo:core` refused its input before analysis, and the one local AutoReview is INCOMPLETE and covers neither the merge nor the later commits.
- The late channel-recovery producer alias is statically reviewed and lifecycle health is unit-tested. The real channel-recovery producer wiring is not exercised by a failing-channel fixture.
- Native Windows runtime proof is unrun. Existing Windows ownership/prequalification coverage is not a native Windows product run.
- Combined Gateway plus attempt/CodeMode completion-cohort behavior is not proved by the separate boundary tests. These gaps are disclosed, not waived.

prs.title: fix(mattermost): match canonically equivalent names in live directory lookup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost directory lookups miss entries when the stored name and the typed query use different Unicode composition forms. A channel display name stored decomposed (`Mu\u00fcnchen`) is not matched by a user typing the composed `München` in the channel/group search, and a peer search typed as `Mu\u0308ller` is forwarded to the server as decomposed bytes, so the server-side match on stored user names misses too.

`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/directory.ts` owns both lookups: `listMattermostDirectoryGroups` filters `ch.name` and `ch.display_name` against the query, and `listMattermostDirectoryPeers` forwards the query as the `/users/search` term.

Precedent: #187024 (same shape: compare canonical forms after the existing lowercase conversion, stored text untouched) and #187148, today's combined sweep that landed the Slack, Feishu and Telegram siblings of this exact fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both call sites lowercased with `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` but never applied a canonical form, so byte-wise `includes` split visually identical channel names, and the peer search term reached the server in the composition form the user happened to type. This change appends `.normalize("NFC")` to the query, to the `name`/`display` projections in the group filter, and to the peer search term. Stored channel names, display names and user records keep their original spelling; group/peer ordering, limits and returned entries are unchanged. No new helper, index, storage migration, option or configuration key.

Production LOC: +6/−4.

Classification: `behavior-preserving` (comparison-only normalization; peer term is forwarded canonical so the server compares like with like)

## User Impact

Searching the Mattermost directory now returns the same channel or peer when the two sides use different Unicode composition forms, which users experience as "I typed the right name but the picker shows nothing". Unrelated names still do not match, and case and whitespace behavior are unchanged. Server-side peer matching receives the canonical term, so results depend on the name the server stored, not on how the client typed it.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `cda3b745995ddf12b5ffa2dc885368618e7e2291`
- Current-main RED baseline (source): `5228f2425599f174d2bc84a5d1ff750de3b7ea83`
- Production entry: `listMattermostDirectoryGroups` and `listMattermostDirectoryPeers`, the read path behind Mattermost channel-group and peer directory lookups.
- Canonical owner exercised: `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/directory.ts`
- Decision surface: the typed `query` string against stored `name`/`display_name` (groups) and the `/users/search` term (peers).
- Recorder/readback boundary: returned `ChannelDirectoryEntry[]` values and the recorded `/users/search` request body from the mocked Mattermost client, with no live Mattermost server or model calls.
- Acceptance RED: on current main, query `München` against a channel whose `display_name` is `Mu\u00fcnchen` returns no matching entry, and query `Mu\u0308ller` is forwarded to `/users/search` as decomposed bytes.
- Acceptance GREEN: exact head returns `{ kind: "channel", id: "channel:chan-nfd", name: "general", handle: <original display name> }` and forwards `term: "müller"` in canonical form, while the pre-existing cases (public/private channel labels, batched peer pagination, search limits) keep their exact results.
- Legal controls: the two pre-existing sibling regressions in this file pass identically on both refs; no fixture text was rewritten.
- Cleanup: isolated remote tree `/data/openclaw-test/a1028/mm1`; no production server, Gateway session or configuration was touched.

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace

Node 24.22.1, secretless, Vitest single file. `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/directory.test.ts`.

```text
# RED — current main source 5228f242559 + new regressions
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 6 passed (8)
   Duration  135.46s (cold transform cache)
```

```text
# GREEN — exact head cda3b745995 + same tests
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
   Duration  26.96s
```

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/directory.test.ts` — 8/8 pass on exact head; the two new regressions fail on current main source.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — clean.
- Not tested: a live Mattermost server's own Unicode handling of `/users/search`. The client forwards a string; the group filter is a pure in-process comparison over returned channel records, and the existing suite already drives both call shapes through the mocked client boundary.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: +6/−4; Test LOC: +41/−0 (two new regression cases appended to the existing directory suite).
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the file's existing `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` helper and the existing filter/search path; no new search path, index, or config surface.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. Stored names are unchanged; only match selection for composition-variant queries and the forwarded term's form change.

## Merge risk

Two-way door: comparison-only change inside one directory module, fully reversible. The blast radius is which channels and peers match a directory query; an incorrect normalization could change match selection, but cannot rewrite stored channel names, display names or user records.

The Gateway suite stopped exercising two later-parent prompt scenarios when #185730 removed the restart test that imported them. prs.title: fix(ci): avoid fixed delays after fast Git commands
prs.body:
Related: #187165

## What Problem This Solves

CI checkout and generated-publication policies add a fixed 50 ms wait to fast Git commands, accumulating avoidable delay across repeated repository reads.

## User Impact

Internal CI and publication work can observe completed Git commands sooner. No product configuration, permissions, retries, or required operator actions change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Git owner now uses Python's bounded process wait instead of an unconditional sleep. It wakes on direct-child exit while retaining the existing 50 ms cancellation/deadline checkpoints. Descendant draining, failed-cleanup fencing, lock reclamation, Windows Job settlement, and exit-code precedence remain authoritative and unchanged. The inline workflow owner was regenerated through its existing generator.

Source delta: +4 lines in the shared owner and +4 in its generated projection; tests unchanged. These lines express the bounded wake-on-exit operation without adding a second lifecycle path.

## Evidence

- Five interleaved baseline/candidate samples per interpreter, each executing 25 real Git HEAD reads through the actual policy owner on macOS. All outputs had the same SHA256; owner fixed-sleep calls fell from 25–26 per sample to zero.
  - Apple Python 3.9.6: median 1.423 s → 0.543 s.
  - Python 3.15.1: median 1.384 s → 0.378 s.
- 16 focused existing cases passed: generated-owner identity and supplemental-fetch lock recovery (2), plus checkout lifecycle/fixture isolation, early leader exit, deadlines, SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP, failed drain, POSIX group extinction and failure diagnostics (14). Linux-policy and platform-policy cases executed locally on macOS; this is not native Linux or Windows proof.
- Proof used a qualified existing physical dependency install with the candidate owner/workflow and current helper overlaid, identical focused-test/caller inputs, and exact source restoration afterward. [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40809364612) passed: 52 successful jobs, 22 skipped, zero failures or pending jobs.
- Generator `--check`, Python syntax compilation, targeted oxfmt check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent lifecycle/history reviews found no actionable issues. Local autoreview through P3 was scoped-clean on the complete staged candidate against `960debc51780c899df913ea2ddf3cf971a80ea02`; no findings.

- [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187203#issuecomment-6486761985) reviewed `8b96140f6a60a2d75e2d162065ee1a1ba0e55c76`: zero findings and no before-merge actions.

Limits: this is scoped command-latency evidence, not measured GitHub-billed minutes, CPU/RSS savings, or native Windows settlement proof. The previously observed macOS locale-publication timeout is a separate unresolved attribution; this PR does not claim to fix it. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable because its checkout is dirty, so the maintainer fallback is local autoreview and one completed hosted ClawSweeper review.

prs.title: fix(agents): narrow union-parameter tools under Gateway tool policy
prs.body:
fix(agents): narrow union-parameter tools under Gateway tool policy

**Problem.** The Gateway tool policy narrowed actions only when a tool declared `action` as a top-level string field. If a tool used `Type.Union([…])` where each variant declared its own literal `action`, `narrowActions` hit the same "top-level string action field" refusal on every turn. This left `codex_threads` and the four Feishu tools (`feishu_perm`, `feishu_wiki`, `feishu_drive`, `feishu_docx`) unusable whenever a policy restricted their actions.

**Precedent.** #186395 fixed the same failure mode for `personal_instructions` by narrowing on the top-level `action` field; this change extends the same contract to union-parameter variants.

**Fix.** In `src/agents/gateway-tool-policy.ts`, when `schema.anyOf` is present, `narrowActions` now:
1. Iterates each union variant.
2. Reads `action.const` or `action.enum` from the variant's properties.
3. Keeps only variants whose action is listed in `tools.gatewayPolicy.actions.<tool>`.
4. Returns `undefined` (withholds the tool) if no variant is allowed.
5. Preserves the original refusal when a variant has no `properties`, no `action`, or neither `const`/`enum`.

No field-level path or execution-side assertion was changed, so existing string/action narrowing remains untouched.

**Affected tools.** All five tools below declare union-parameter schemas and are currently blocked by this refusal when an action policy is configured:
- `extensions/codex/src/native-thread-tool.ts` (`codex_threads`)
- `extensions/feishu/src/perm.ts` (`feishu_perm`)
- `extensions/feishu/src/wiki.ts` (`feishu_wiki`)
- `extensions/feishu/src/drive.ts` / `doc-schema.ts` (`feishu_drive`, `feishu_docx`)

**Evidence.**

- Unit red/green on server (docker, Node v24.22.1, `--maxWorkers=1`):
  - Base (`e00a185728d`): `Tests 2 failed | 11 passed (13)`, failures at `narrowActions` "top-level string action field".
  - Candidate (`1201c5d905b`): `Tests 13 passed (13)`.
- Shipped-run on an isolated live Gateway (`gateway.mode: local`, `tools.gatewayPolicy.allow: ["codex_threads"]`, `actions.codex_threads: ["list"]`):
  - Base: `tools.invoke {name:"codex_threads", args:{action:"list"}}` → `Gateway tool policy requires codex_threads to declare a top-level string action field.`
  - Candidate `action=list` → policy allows, tool proceeds to execution.
  - Candidate `action=read` → `Gateway tool policy denies codex_threads action "read".`
- Static gates:
  - `tsgo:core` EXIT 0.
  - `oxlint` 0 warnings / 0 errors.
  - `oxfmt --check` PASS.
  - `test-lines` ratchet PASS (6302559 vs ceiling 6310000, slack 7441; baseline untouched).

**Not tested / honest gaps.**
- The five Feishu tools were not each booted in an isolated live Gateway; the same `narrowActions` code path is covered by the unit suite and the `codex_threads` shipped-run.
- Codex tool execution fails inside the container because the Codex home/threads environment is unavailable; the policy-layer pass/fail behavior is what is being proven.
- The shipped-run used the source CLI entry point (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts`) rather than a dist bundle; its argv/config/state path is identical to the packaged CLI.

**Cleanup.** Isolated proof state/config lives only in the temporary container tree and was not merged into any production Gateway, token, or config.

## What Problem This Solves

Three operator-facing gaps in the Docker/Compose docs, all reported with production evidence on 2026.10.7:

1. Nothing warns that `docker compose exec openclaw-gateway openclaw <command>` boots a full CLI runtime inside the Gateway container. Scheduled host jobs polling `channel status` / `cron list` / `agent list` overlap, and the Gateway stalls (the reporter measured ~160 s per invocation and Discord 1006 disconnects).
2. `openclaw config validate` only checks plugin-owned schema where the plugin is available, so validating a config copy in a plugin-less container can report `valid: true` for keys the live Gateway then rejects on hot reload.
3. Compose stop grace periods (Docker's 10 s default, 90 s in many files) are far shorter than the Gateway's shutdown budget, so the container is killed mid-drain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Documentation only; no runtime behavior changes.

- `docs/install/docker/compose-operations.md` gains "CLI invocations against the Gateway" (cost depends on the command; overlapping jobs cost the same host/state whether they run via `exec` or the one-shot `openclaw-cli` service; use the HTTP probes for routine health polling) and "Stop grace period".
- The grace-period section separates the 325 s overall allowance (315 s drain + 10 s reserve, 330 s managed service stop timeout) from what an ordinary Compose stop actually drains: `STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000` caps admitted-work drain, and the rest is kept for cancellation and durable cleanup. `stop_grace_period: 340s` stays as the covering example.
- `docs/cli/config.md` (`config validate`) now says generated bundled channel schemas are normally checked without loading the runtime (`ensureChannelSchemas` seeds `GENERATED_BUNDLED_CHANNEL_CONFIG_METADATA`), that incomplete discovery can defer even those (`preserveUnavailableConfig` continues before `ensureChannelSchemas`), and that unavailable plugin schema yields `valid: true` with warnings while the Gateway can still reject the keys on hot reload.

## User Impact

Operators stop discovering these three the hard way — unresponsive Gateways from status polling, a "valid" config rejected on reload, and unclean stops that force a full session revalidation on the next start.

## Evidence

Docs-only change, so the proof is the documentation checks plus the source of the numbers:

```text
$ git diff --check
(no output)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check docs/install/docker/compose-operations.md docs/cli/config.md
All matched files use the correct format.

$ grep -n "STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS" src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop-shutdown-budget.ts | head -2
14:const STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000;
146:      : Math.min(STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS, Math.max(0, budget.timeoutMs - budget.reserveMs)),

$ node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs
checked_internal_links=16116
broken_links=0
```

Changed files: `docs/install/docker/compose-operations.md` (+31), `docs/cli/config.md` (+1). No links added, so no new routes; headings added are anchor-safe.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git grep`/`git show` to confirm the shutdown budget constants and the current wording of both pages, then wrote the two sections and the caveat. The implementer understands the content: the grace period must cover the 315 s drain plus the 10 s reserve, and plugin-owned schema can only be validated where that plugin is loaded.

prs.title: fix(doctor): run --fix migrations headless and never exit 0 when work was skipped
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor could report success when malformed config prevented database selection, or when final validation only printed invalid-config errors without recording a failed repair.

Fixes #187122. Thanks @JordanNewell for the fleet reproduction.

## User Impact

Automation now receives exit 2 when config parsing or database selection prevents inspection, and exit 1 when final validation leaves invalid config or a required migration deferred. Blockers include their paths and next steps; JSON preflight failures include `status: "blocked"` and retain the existing findings/error envelope. A healthy no-op can still succeed, and optional diagnostics remain advisory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pre-bootstrap engine reporter and final validation owner both lost failure status. Final validation now records its findings and uses the existing repair-refusal/cleanup path; its implementation lives with the existing validation-finding conversion instead of growing the already-full config-write runner.

Current main already honors headless `--fix` consent. Isolated CLI fixtures verified schema repair without `--yes` or a PTY, and verified that all four reported keys already migrate: `memorySearch` to `memory.search`, the environment value to `env.vars`, and retirement of the metadata/Gateway tuning keys. This change preserves those migration and backup owners. No schema, dependency, or option changes.

## Evidence

Real CLI fixtures use isolated HOME/state, separate free ports, and piped stdin (Node 26.12.1). Each invokes the built package entry through `node <isolated-runtime>/dist/entry.js doctor <args>`, with `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` pointing at its synthetic fixture. No operator state or running Gateway is used:

```text
--fix                         exit=0  schema=38  backups=1
--fix --non-interactive       exit=0  schema=38  backups=1
four reported legacy keys     exit=0  migrations verified
malformed config + --fix      exit=2
malformed config + --json     exit=2  status=blocked  ok=false  reason=unparseable-config
invalid gateway.port          exit=1  path and remediation present
```

- Baseline malformed-config CLI: exit 0 and “Doctor complete. Database checks remain unknown.” Fixed CLI: exit 2 and an explicit blocked/no-migrations message. `doctor --json` returns exit 2, `status: "blocked"`, `ok: false`, and the parse reason in findings.
- Real isolated CLI, piped stdin: `doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` upgraded the synthetic v17 agent database to schema 38 without `--yes`; plain `doctor --fix` with piped stdin also exited 0, with schema 38 and one backup verified independently. The reported four-key fixture migrated successfully.
- Real isolated CLI: `doctor --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` with invalid `gateway.port` exits 1, lists `gateway.port`, and prints `doctor --fix` / `config unset` guidance. A separate invalid-value `--fix` run encountered this host mount's pre-repair staging warning, so it is not counted as migration proof.
- The process regression rejects the baseline exit-0/“Doctor complete” result. The final regression executed in 323 ms in the consumer run; its earlier focused run took 99.3 s wall time, dominated by shared source/runtime preparation (97% transform).
- Commands: `pnpm tsgo:core`; `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json <three-touched-test-paths>`; `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig <core-or-test-tsconfig> <touched-files>`; `oxfmt --check <touched-files>`; `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <touched-and-importing-files> --maxWorkers=1` (native macOS private `TMPDIR`).

- Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its runner checkout contains unrelated edits; it was left untouched. The permitted autoreview fallback was used.

prs.title: fix(backup): give each SQLite header probe batch its own deadline
prs.body:
Fixes #187150

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw backup create` sends every walked state-dir path to one SQLite header-probe child with a fixed 10 s `spawnSync` timeout. Probe time grows linearly with file count, so once a state dir holds a few hundred thousand regular files (e.g. git worktrees an agent checked out under `<state>/worktrees/`), the single child times out and the backup aborts with a generic "Could not determine whether backup files are SQLite databases" error, even though every file is readable.

## User Impact

- Large state dirs back up again: the probe deadline no longer depends on how many files the state dir holds.
- When a probe child does fail, the error now ends with the underlying cause (for example `Cause: spawnSync node ETIMEDOUT`) instead of only the generic text, so operators do not go looking for unreadable files.
- Classification is unchanged: every path is still probed in an isolated child (no live SQLite descriptors are opened in-process, no path-pattern skips), and any failed batch still aborts before an archive is published.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's next step on the issue: "Fix the probe's fixed total deadline and establish a failing regression showing that a large readable discovery workload aborts before archive publication." `probeSqliteDatabaseHeaders()` now splits the deduplicated paths into batches of `SQLITE_HEADER_PROBE_BATCH_SIZE` (4096) and runs one child per batch, each with its own 10 s budget. On this machine a 4096-path batch takes at most 263 ms, so the per-child budget keeps a ~38x margin, and total time even dropped (11.8 s vs 16.0 s) because smaller JSON payloads are cheaper to parse.

## Evidence

Local live run on Windows 11, Node 26.12.1: isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` with 200,000 small regular files under `<state>/worktrees/` plus `openclaw.json`; `node openclaw.mjs backup create --output <dir> --verify` on main `44ffd0a` and on this branch, same state dir.

![backup create on 200k-file state dir, main vs fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/187150/proof-187150.png)

| build | exit | elapsed | archives written | output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | **1** | 41 s | **0** | `Could not determine whether backup files are SQLite databases. ...` |
| fix | **0** | 371 s | **1** (5,510,356 bytes) | `Archive verification: passed` |

The shipped probe worker timed directly on the same 200,001 paths:

| mode | children | slowest child | total | vs 10 s per-child budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main: one child for everything | 1 | 16,049 ms | 16,049 ms | exceeds, backup aborts |
| fix: 4096 paths per child | 49 | 263 ms | 11,823 ms | each child far under budget |

Regression in `src/infra/backup-create.sqlite-header-probe.test.ts`: 8,193 paths (two full batches plus one real SQLite header) must be classified completely across 3 children, and a timed-out child must surface `Cause: spawnSync node ETIMEDOUT`. Against main's probe: `expected [ 8193, true, 1 ] to deeply equal [ 8193, true, 3 ]`; with the fix: passes.

Checks run locally: `oxfmt`, `oxlint` on changed files, `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm check:assertion-safety`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/backup-create.sqlite-header-probe.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): paired-node Claude continuations retain Gateway context
prs.body:
Closes #145636

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI continuation on a healthy paired node can fail with a Gateway-runtime or capability error after its originating request ends. Detached work retains a live Gateway resolver but deliberately does not retain the direct request context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two paired-node readers now use the existing resolver-first `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext` in the current request-scope owner. This integrates with main's `PluginRuntimeExecutionFrame` storage instead of reintroducing the former AsyncLocalStorage owner or a second accessor. A resolver returning `undefined` remains authoritative: stale direct context cannot revive a retired owner.

The command policy, expected connection and pairing generation, dispatch-time authority, and skill/run/placement lifecycle checks remain intact. There are no configuration, protocol, database-schema, or public SDK changes.

## User Impact

A detached Claude continuation can use its still-live Gateway and connected paired node. A retired owner fails before any node lookup, policy check, or dispatch.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh onto main `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`; current head `eb7a861ea7c06c277806dd2c6d0dba6b0f9c0443` also checks the captured Gateway remains current at dispatch and skill authority use. [Remote focused tests](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40626335729) passed 18 tests across both affected Gateway suites on a temporary child of this head. Full CI and refreshed real-node proof remain pending; earlier evidence below refers to the revisions identified there.

Reconciled against main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d`. The production diff is two reader substitutions, plus focused regression coverage.

### Actual Gateway and signed-node boundary

The same temporary source-runtime fixture starts the actual Gateway with an isolated home, config and state, loads a startup plugin through the normal loader, and captures its real context in an authenticated RPC. A separately signed WebSocket node completes normal local device pairing and command approval, verified in the persisted pairing records. After the capture RPC finishes, the fixture invokes the production `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun` in a resolver-only scope and repeats with a retired resolver plus deliberately stale direct context.

Main before the fix, observed with clean shutdown:

```json
{"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":0,"ok":false,"error":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":1,"ok":true}}
```

Exact candidate after the fix:

```json
{"head":"2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d","expectedFixed":true,"actualGateway":true,"signedNode":true,"devicePaired":true,"commandApproved":true,"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":1,"result":{"ok":true,"payload":{"exitCode":0,"stderrTail":"","truncated":false},"payloadJSON":null,"error":null}},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":0,"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"}}}}
```

The fixture exited 0, and the Gateway reported a clean shutdown.

This exercises real Gateway startup, plugin loading, authenticated RPC, signed WebSocket transport, persisted device/command pairing, NodeRegistry and the changed production invocation owner. The node returns a synthetic successful Claude-command payload. It does not establish live Claude model inference or a full terminal-close/Web-composer UI walkthrough.

The fixture uses synthetic data only. Update checks, telemetry and hosted catalog refresh are disabled with the documented config/environment opt-outs. Proof code and generated logs are temporary and are not committed.

### Regression coverage and checks

- Before the two reader substitutions: 13 failures / 3 passes across the invocation and paired-node skill suites. Detached dispatch failed unavailable; stale-context retirement incorrectly dispatched; skill preparation failed its Gateway/capability boundary.
- After, on the identical candidate tree: 27/27 tests across node invocation (5), paired-node skills (11), request-scope owner (7), and native Bash execution policy (4). Existing coverage for command denial, pairing-await authority retirement, capability requirements, skill delivery/authoring and publication retirement remains active under the resolver-only scope.
- Combined focused command: `pnpm test src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 85.02s wall time including the first compiled-subprocess generation.
- Per-file exact-head cost using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts` 5/5, 34.08s wall (21ms test bodies); `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts` 11/11, 65.68s wall (23901ms test bodies). The existing skill suite exercises real node-command subprocess/SQLite lifecycle boundaries; no new per-test Gateway boots, timers, or serial configuration were added. Hosted [changed-node CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276/job/111133298553) passed both files separately: invocation 5/5 in 22.88s (15ms test bodies), skills 11/11 in 19.83s (9.768s test bodies).
- Independent `autoreview --engine codex --mode local --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --max-priority P2`: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Four-file type-aware lint (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed files>`) passed in 22.70s. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The aggregate check passed conflict, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, database-worker, timeout-race, dependency, config, plugin-boundary and other prerequisite guards, plus the core graph boundary and full production-core typecheck.
- Hosted [CI run 37098465276](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276) passed on this exact head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, production types, all selected test-type stripes, lint, selected tests and guards. The [fresh review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145741#issuecomment-5644398815) resolves the previous integration concern and finds no actionable introduced issues: overall Platinum, proof Diamond.
- Full repository build/check/test is not claimed as locally passed. The bounded `check:changed --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --head HEAD` attempt ran 605.19s and stopped at its 600s budget during the broad 27-graph test-typecheck lane: `agents-root` passed, `agents-other` was interrupted (143). Remaining test graphs and later aggregate checks were not completed locally. The separate changed-file type-aware lint passed; the subsequent hosted CI run completed successfully and covers the selected global verification gates.

### Historical CI failure

[The old head's native-Bash policy job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34680714684/job/103518938237) reported `allowlist/on-miss`: expected `allow`, received `deny`, after 7.764s with a 5s fixture run budget. That is consistent with timeout-sensitive authority rejection, but the historical assertion omitted the denial message and run outcome, so the exact denial reason cannot be established from that log.

The integrated main already contains [the Date-based watchdog change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/62a8182e40d955ddcd509ba977badb37ea691d2a) and the independent [native-Bash fixture stabilization in #115184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ce11e2e25c3b0ad6360b8c4e5bd7f17357f81c42), which freezes the policy matrix's Date clock and asserts a non-timeout exit. The local native-Bash matrix passes 4/4 on this candidate. No native-Bash production policy, test fixture, or CI configuration is changed by this PR; a passing replay is not being presented as proof of the old run's exact cause.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Usage, cron, transcript archives and approval lookups can disclose session-derived information outside the session list.

## User Impact

Session-specific aggregates and lookups respect membership; global cost and meeting archives remain unavailable to invitation-only roles.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the canonical visibility predicate at aggregate selection and preserve the existing restricted-role denial for unscopable archives.

Stack step **10/17**, based on [fix/guest-access-07-projects-20261026](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/tree/fix%2Fguest-access-07-projects-20261026). Review and merge in order; each upper PR contains only its own slice against its predecessor.

Previous: [filter project and task summaries](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184508).

Next: [retire coordination fixtures through canonical cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185982).

Stack order: [complete stack](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184515#stack-order).

## Evidence

### Current-head qualification — 2026-10-29

Head: `d152c631039f5e433a312a0c187f3868bac188f4`, rebased onto pinned main `a4e20a8b24440efd9b8a1792ce400be85a697080`.

- The sole merge conflict was `config/test-lines-baseline.txt`. Main restored its approved **6,320,000** ceiling in #187162; that file now matches main and is absent from this PR’s diff. Clean main measures **6,246,028**; this PR adds **+140** guest-access regression lines, for **6,246,168**. No tests were deleted and main’s deliberate headroom was not reduced.
- **28 scoped suites / 389 tests passed**; core typecheck, eight-file typed lint, formatting and diff checks pass. The eight authored code/test blobs remain identical to the independently reviewed prior head.
- The inherited curly-lint failure was fixed on main by #187144. The [exact-head CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40806469156/job/123229797081) now **passes**. The previous hosted review’s sole before-merge item—retain main’s approved ceiling while resolving conflicts—is addressed. The [exact-head hosted re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184509#issuecomment-6414268765) completed with **no findings and no before-merge items** (readiness, proof and quality 5/6).

### Fresh AWS integration plan and expected versus actual

Crabbox doctor passed before fresh AWS `openclaw-check` lease `cbx_065d51a3a570`. Observed hardware: **c7a.2xlarge, 8 CPUs / 15.2 GiB RAM**, public networking, no Tailscale and no IAM role. Hardware/no-role admission preceded installation. [The current-head run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5713c9ac571b87b36daf2cd8eec3084e) separately built pinned main `a4e20a8b` and head `d152c631`, then booted real isolated TLS/WebSocket Gateways through the normal `pnpm openclaw` CLI.

This is **fresh execution, not carry-over** from `10779dda`: incorporated main range `48f40fb0a2f328a4f364767a232786411ad82997..a4e20a8b24440efd9b8a1792ce400be85a697080` changes execution-approval store admission identity (`src/infra/exec-approvals-store.ts`). The 153-case paired AWS plan was therefore rerun on this exact head.

Plan: A owns shared/uninvited/draft sessions with canonical recorded usage (11/23/37 tokens). B receives shared and draft membership during each observed member stage, while draft visibility remains denied. C is a non-member throughout all observed summary rows. Read usage detail/overview, compact cron list, cron run summaries, pending exec approvals and global cost/archive guards under view/none/invited. Each primary surface has its own add/remove cycle: B's **first request after the remove ACK** reads that surface on its retained socket, with no sleep, reconnect, cache helper or intervening evidence read.

For invited pending approvals, A grants B/C genuine preparatory membership while they register their own requests, then removes it before observed policy rows. Only A registers draft requests under restricted modes. None controls use A's requests and do not synthesize foreign-source B/C requests. No internal approval-runtime flag, forged reviewer, administrator scope, approval decision or command execution is used.

| Surface and case | Expected | Pinned main actual | Head actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| All surfaces, view/none | Existing results unchanged | baseline results | identical in all 102 paired rows |
| Usage, B invited member | shared only, 11 tokens | empty — omission reproduced | shared only, 11 tokens |
| Usage, C non-member | empty | empty | empty |
| Cron list/runs, invited B/C | B member: shared only; C always empty | all three sources disclosed | expected filtering |
| Approvals, invited B/C with legitimately retained requests | B member: shared only; before/removal and C: empty | shared + uninvited disclosed | expected filtering |
| B's first reads after removal | shared absent | usage absent; cron/approvals still disclose | shared absent on every surface |
| Global usage cost and transcript status, invited A/B/C | FORBIDDEN | allowed | FORBIDDEN |

**153 paired cases completed (153 rows per revision): all head policy assertions pass, all 102 view/none pairs are unchanged, and exactly 26 main-red/head-green rows were reproduced**—2 usage omissions, 18 cron/approval disclosures, 6 global guards. Public response identities, filtered counts and exact usage totals/costs were checked. Both variants reported zero unexpected failures, settled process groups, restored source and removed isolated state.

Evidence was collected and hashed before release; hashes matched afterward. Lease cleanup was independently verified at **2026-10-29T02:53:20.521Z**: released, no host, not ready, cleanup complete and no provisioning resource remaining. No real user data or model credentials were put in the Gateways, and no model inference was invoked.

Both revisions used the same diff (SHA-256 `dbbf9c2b14e5697057acd18f3b9a6524aab832d6505a370ddf1309706767c4b4`). Documentation counts/hashes also reflect disabled bundled plugins in the fixture. These test-only edits were restored and never committed or pushed.

### Historical original-stack evidence

Slice head: `d20d5eadb0b42d7dbe5b1475c1e92a7390db05ae`, on fixed main `5bf0c41a03f1dba03d625460607ed5b959710458`. The complete 13-file integration matrix passed 46/46 on pinned Bun at `ddc49fd63d3b82e41eb6c74af4ad935a56aebc8f` before this main rebase. Main's canonical fixture repairs are preserved and duplicate prerequisite changes removed. Prefixes are not separately built locally; each requires its own current-head hosted CI and review.

The final authenticated integration covers persisted usage rows and totals, a real disabled cron job, and real execution-approval get/list/wait/events. Removing membership after preparation removes usage/counts and rejects cron publication; removal also revokes pending approval visibility. Global cost and transcript archives deny invited guests while administrators retain access.

At prior prefix `fee6104096f6b3518e6e16709a6aae9e86a935d1`, the complete usage-cache file passed 10/10 under pinned Bun plus the core and Gateway-method-test type graphs. The aggregate code is unchanged by this restack. Its deliberate pre-activation fixture annotation is removed by final config activation.

The [stack evidence ledger](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184515#evidence) records runtime results, prior build/upgrade proof and limits. Integration tests are owned by the final activation PR. Current-head hosted CI and review remain required before landing.
