prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled dependency analysis still reports an unused database recovery module after #185730 retired its callbacks and progress consumers. The module is unreachable in both the production and test-aware graphs, leaving an unused-file finding in CI.

## User Impact

This completes removal of that internal recovery orchestration. Active database admission, deferred-agent readiness, shutdown joining, and stored data keep their existing owners and behavior. There is no configuration or migration action for users.

## Why This Change Was Made

The former helper coordinated an initial recovery pass with per-agent retries after database preparation. All consumers disappeared in the restart-resume cutover. Removing the orphan file closes that exact residue without changing its live admission and preparation dependencies or weakening the scanner.

## Evidence

The [original scheduled dependency job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40800487319/job/123207281276) at `34625635a1c04944ca68d2897f68fb24866e5552` reported this path in both unused-file graphs. On the exact candidate, the complete `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` result changes from 3 to 2 production findings and 7 to 6 full-tree findings. The only removed path is this module; no new finding appears. The aggregate remains failed for the unrelated existing findings.

Selected formatting parity and type checks passed. The complete `src/gateway/server-agent-database-startup.preparation.test.ts` suite passed all 24 cases, including independent small-agent admission, shutdown joining, and stale removal/move/deletion protections. Its controlled migration/model dependencies do not establish live Gateway or upgrade behavior.

The other maintained surfaces also ran. `pnpm deadcode:dependencies` reports the same 32 value and 8 type symbols, with unused files reduced from 3 to 2; it remains failed, so its internal second `&&` arm is unrun. prs.title: fix(codex): saved user turn is reported as a failed write when prompt annotation is refused
prs.body:
Closes #179892

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a saved user turn is reported as a failed write, and its persisted-message notification is skipped, when Codex native prompt annotation is refused.

## User Impact

User impact: a refused prompt annotation no longer raises a false persistence error for a turn that was saved, and persistence listeners are still told the admitted turn was persisted. A refused annotation with no host admission still writes nothing, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Annotation only adds provenance to an admission that is already durable. The fix catches and logs annotation failures inside the mirror promise instead of letting them reject the promise registered with `markRuntimePersistencePending`. Keeping the catch inside that promise preserves the existing ordering: persistence waiters still wait for annotation to settle. When annotation fails and there is no host admission, the function returns as it did before rather than falling back to the generic mirror writer.

## Evidence

- New admission test where `annotateCurrentUserTurn` rejects: no `onPersistenceError`, exactly one persisted-message notification, the admitted message unchanged, and no extra transcript writes. It fails on `main` without this change (`onPersistenceError` is called).
- The existing `transcript-mirror*.test.ts` suites pass (44 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.



## Real behavior proof (production Gateway, before and after)

These are redacted logs from a production Gateway running 2026.10.5 (source build). This change was deployed there on 2026-10-21. Run and session IDs are replaced with labels; timestamps are UTC.

**Before the fix (2026-10-20).** Annotation was refused at turn start. When the run settled, the Gateway reported a failed user-turn write:

```
18:00:08.001 [agent/embedded] failed to mirror codex app-server prompt at turn start error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-A> sessionId=<session-A>
18:03:46.522 [gateway] agent user transcript persistence failed: Error: native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence
```

The user turn had been saved anyway. In the agent's session database, `<session-A>` holds the admitted user message at seq 1 (created 18:00:05). The session's last event is at 18:03:46, the same moment the false error was logged.

**After the fix (2026-10-21 to 2026-10-22).** The same refusal happened on five Codex turns. Each one logged only the new warning, with no persistence error:

```
2026-10-21 19:51:25.581 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-B> sessionId=<session-B>
2026-10-22 02:35:56.558 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-C> sessionId=<session-C>
2026-10-22 13:25:39.513 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-D> sessionId=<session-D>
2026-10-22 13:27:28.648 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-E> sessionId=<session-E>
2026-10-22 13:30:47.032 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-F> sessionId=<session-F>
```

From 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-27, the Gateway journal has 1 `agent user transcript persistence failed` line. It is the pre-fix one above. In each of the five post-fix sessions, seq 1 is the saved `role: "user"` message, with no provenance annotation written.

**A caveat about current `main`.** The refusal seen in production, "would restore redacted evidence", was removed from `main` in #169063. The bug itself is still there. In `extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.ts` (`main` at 1b1c96578f6), `annotateCurrentUserTurn` is still awaited without a catch inside the promise registered with `markRuntimePersistencePending`. The annotation binder still throws on its remaining guards: "cannot replace an edited admission", "conflicts with recorded provenance", "does not match admitted content" and "no longer available for native annotation". Any of these produces the same false persistence error and skipped notification. I haven't observed those remaining refusals in production.

I re-ran the added admission test against `main` at 2868c5448f7 today. Without this change, it fails at `expect(onPersistenceError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. With this change applied, the file passes (5/5).

`pnpm deadcode:unused-files` reports three maintained measurement commands as unused even though their source headers document direct execution: workspace request bytes, session file/title preparation, and session maintenance scheduling. prs.title: perf(gateway): preserve encoded history for unrestricted viewers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening or reconnecting a conversation with initial history needlessly decodes and re-encodes the transcript for named viewer roles that have no model restrictions, when startup metadata is present.

## User Impact

The initial conversation snapshot sends the same bytes with less main-thread work and allocation. Restricted viewers still receive the current model redaction, and metadata still filters Access grants. There are no configuration, protocol, storage, or authorization changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history worker already prepares immutable JSON segments. `projectOperatorModelRead` needs to filter metadata for named roles, but previously also materialized and mapped all messages even when its model projection was an identity operation. Gate that message projection on the owner's existing `restrictsModels` fact. No new snapshot cache or lifetime is introduced; subscription admission, retained disclosure checks, ordering, worker reads, and rollback stay in their existing owners.

Runtime production delta: **+1 net line** (the explanatory comment); one condition replaces the old condition. The removed work is the transcript parse, no-op traversal, and subsequent serialization. The restricted path remains necessary for the public per-viewer model-disclosure contract. The reproducible benchmark adds 206 tooling lines; including that script, the non-test/non-doc delta is +207.

## Evidence

Acceptance declared before measurement: identical authorized wire bytes, no unrestricted materialization, less CPU/allocation, and unchanged restricted-viewer redaction. The committed workload is `scripts/perf/history-model-projection-measure.ts` (usage in its header).

Owner microbenchmark on macOS, Node 26.12.1: 65 prepared viewers interleaved across two named roles, 80 messages including tool calls/results, a 266,945-byte history window, startup metadata present. Five passes of 650 responses per revision (**3,250 operations per side per mode**), after 130 warmup operations. CPU is measured with `threadCpuUsage` in the untraced pass; allocation is a separate 4 KiB sampling pass including collected objects. Figures below are the median pass, per response.

| Model projection + nested response serialization | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU | 0.22874 ms | 0.00648 ms | −97.2% |
| Sampled allocation | 816,507 B | 11,568 B | −98.6% |
| Transcript materializations | 1 | 0 | removed |
| Initial response bytes | 267,339 B | 267,339 B | identical |

The script verifies exact wire equality for every viewer before measurement and leaves encoded segments unflattened while timing, as the segmented transport does. Baseline CPU pass range was 0.221–0.234 ms; candidate 0.0063–0.0080 ms. Host load averages (1/5/15 minutes) were 32.40/34.92/30.78 on base and 33.94/35.07/31.03 on candidate. These are owner-phase results, not a whole-Gateway percentage or total subscribe latency. Authorization and transcript-window worker round trips are untouched. The deletion fast path applies: no ten-minute whole-Gateway stress campaign or production load was run. Full RPC phase attribution, sessions.list/loop p99, and whole-Gateway GC/RSS remain unmeasured here.

Regression proof on base `496263aa5cc6d8a1200c72b4ef3511888253358c`:

- The interleaved unrestricted/restricted viewer regression fails because unrestricted startup history becomes parsed objects. It also verifies restricted redaction, unchanged input bytes, and metadata Access-grant filtering.
- The existing subscribe-handler test, extended to request encoded initial history with approval replay and startup metadata, fails on the same unwanted materialization. Its sharing/replay revocation cases retain rollback coverage.

Focused validation: 23/23 tests passed across `chat-history-model-policy.test.ts`, `sessions.messages-subscribe-history.test.ts`, `operator-model-presentation.test.ts`, and `session-fast-mode-presentation.test.ts` (143.05 s Vitest duration, 173.15 s wrapper wall time, including cold compilation). These existing integration files exercise real transcript storage and retained authorization; the new interleaving regression took under one second. Scoped lint, oxfmt, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, the gateway-methods test typecheck, and `git diff --check` passed. Test-lines ratchet: 6,246,116 against 6,320,000 (73,884 slack); no ceiling change. No Testbox lease was used under the focused-checks/PR-CI policy.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): fresh reviewer, P0–P2 scope, complete local diff plus relevant owner source/contracts, no actionable findings. Autoreview refused before inference because its requested provider route did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed. Reviewer confirmed the measurement scope excludes transcript reads, actual socket transport/compression, and whole-Gateway latency. Exact-head CI is green at `e6ba6c951f975bb341db6f9f46b9505631aa3766`: 60 passing checks, 54 intentional skips, no failing or pending checks. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40807608064) and the aggregate CI gate passed without retries. The pre-push rebase was patch-identical to the reviewed change (`git range-diff`); PR remains ready and open for maintainer landing.

## What Problem This Solves

Selecting a model result in the command palette opens the general Models page, leaving users to locate that model's provider in the provider list.

Fixes #186447

## Why This Change Was Made

The command palette now passes the model's URL-encoded provider through the existing `?provider=` route contract, following the linked issue's acceptance criteria. Generic Models navigation stays unfiltered. This is navigation only; it does not change the selected model, credentials, or configuration.

## User Impact

Selecting a model result opens Models with its provider filter filled in. The generic Models command still opens the unfiltered page.

## Evidence

- Pinned base: `8cebac4847362f4d5b9f94656551789e9f3756c7`. With the production change absent, the focused regression assertion fails because navigation receives only `model-providers`; it does not receive `?provider=fixture`.
- Tested head SHA: `222af4fba6f00dbfcdc8299e117cba7f4a8865e3`. The focused assertion passes and navigation receives `?provider=fixture`.
- The real production call chain runs the built Control UI command palette through a real local Gateway using synthetic catalog data; it makes no external model-provider calls.

- Negative control: the generic `Models` command opens `/settings/model-providers` with an empty filter; the browser flow observed `0` `config.patch` requests.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode's lifecycle, parity and failure-origin contracts ran under Bun in CI without also exercising a Node test host.

## User Impact

Adds Node-host coverage while retaining Bun coverage and the existing Node-only contracts. No executor default, runtime timeout, sandbox boundary or user configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the three Code Mode contracts in a distinct both-host cohort at the shared CI planner. Exact targets, broad project plans and database-worker ownership retain their existing routing. Consolidated planner tests cover normalized paths, both host invocations, failure retention and sibling exclusions.

The real shard runner exposed an ordinary lifecycle fixture's implicit 1,500 ms budget: the first QuickJS invocation on Node timed out before bridge dispatch. The fixture now inherits the canonical 10,000 ms product default; deadline-specific tests retain explicit budgets. The host-denial late-settlement scenario explicitly keeps 1,500 ms because its deadline forces parking before releasing its held sibling. The original cold invocation and production timeout accounting remain intact.

The earlier exact ceiling amendment became obsolete when main independently raised its ceiling to 6,320,000. This PR removes its own ceiling edit; the natural merge keeps main's value. The five source/test files retain the reviewed +50 net test lines, with no added budget or configuration surface.

## Evidence

Prepared candidate: `5a022cae0a8328ed7566d1ca7d201096533c60ff`, based on frozen main `71ae98c377fb9e4ab8e9d73eeb733af0ad4cda65`. CI must test its merge with current main.

- Independent review of the five source/test files: two passes, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The subsequent ceiling-only conflict repair was independently checked; all five source/test blobs remain unchanged. These are source reviews, not runtime execution.
- Before baseline refresh, the consolidated tooling candidate passed 79 tests. The real six-invocation runner retained one failure and completed all sibling invocations: Node lifecycle 21/22, Bun lifecycle 22/22, parity 16/16 per host, failure-origin 60/60 per host.
- Original-order diagnostics showed `timeout`, host failure phase, no bridge dispatch and zero bridge calls. After the fixture correction, lifecycle passed 22/22 on both hosts. All seven other fixture-caller files passed 98 cases per host (196 overlapping executions), including the explicit late-settlement deadline.
- Those earlier runtime results belong to their recorded pre-refresh trees. Focused Testbox attempts for the refreshed candidate were stopped while queued and executed no tests; existing local installs did not match the frozen inputs.
- Fresh [CI run 40807505089, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40807505089) passed on this published head. Its actual checkout was merge `5ce6a28a2d92f26c3afc414b316dc8ae8f7fd9e9`, tree `93ab079bd3a429aa3ff94d6a086d7062d99869d8`, with ordered parents `7e75d4900ebea39e593b12680875b38fdc6e84de` and `5a022cae0a8328ed7566d1ca7d201096533c60ff`.
- The [real lifecycle shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40807505089/job/123230380823) completed 22/22 cases on Node, then 22/22 on Bun, preserving both guest executors and original cold order. The same job passed TTS-delivery 4/4 and source-reply-loop 8/8 on Bun. The [host-denial shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40807505089/job/123230380752) passed 21/21 on Bun, including the explicit late-settlement deadline.
- Fresh [runtime-planner tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40807505089/job/123230380798), [57 shard-runner cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40807505089/job/123230380757), and the [tooling-test typecheck](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40807505089/job/123230807039) passed. This applies the unchanged-head ClawSweeper rank-up move; no additional review request is needed.

Candidate commit hooks, targeted formatting, `git diff --check`, and the CI types/lint/ratchet lanes passed. The separate macOS tooling job remains in progress; native auto-merge must wait for required gates.

prs.title: fix(update): avoid recopying admitted rollback images
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native update rollback capture prepares a private SQLite image to establish the source generation, disposes it, then prepares the same database again for the recovery snapshot. Large database families pay for the extra acquisition and byte comparison while activation is stopped.

## User Impact

This change carries that exact admitted image into the recovery snapshot within the same capture operation. No schema, configuration, persistent cache, or operator action changes.

**Measured d70 bounded qualification FAILED; merge remains blocked.** The maintainer accepted the precisely disclosed historical CPU/RSS tradeoff, and those original FAILED results remain below. The single d70 matrix completed successfully but exceeded the explicitly bounded first-capture RSS median. No new or worse regression is accepted, no threshold was changed, and no performance rerun follows this result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generation owner retains one cleanup-owned image per admitted SQLite family. The snapshot owner consumes it after checking its exact identity. The existing inventory/engine admission, final integrity and foreign-key checks, normalized/publication hashes, post-capture generation, and later rollback refusal remain in place.

Retention covers the whole inventory admission interval. Rejected images, failed transfers, and cancellation join cleanup; a failed transfer does not reacquire another image. Ordinary generation readers still dispose their private image.

Production change: +410/-244 (net +166), justified by the explicit image ownership and cleanup transfer. Tests: +746/-96 (net +650). Measurement harness: +195/-1 (net +194). Release-note context: avoid repeated large-database acquisition during native update rollback capture; the measured candidate remains unqualified for promotion.

## Evidence

Base: `d3184ac52b6a2df26a5dc6e856581f42178f3978`. Current publication head: `9811d1256f98c22731a1cfffc1a41de58c238b9e` (metadata correction only). Runtime/harness/dependency proof head: `d70aa2322071058e3a2ca4f2878fba3a12fdc7a3`. The original production and 77-case proof head is `fdfbe06dfcdf73fc6163373be7edbee23397e2ee`; corrected performance evidence remains bound to `38171331c9cb4250b86e8b68e46523f62b4ce39d`. Later changes repair static issues and the correctness fixture; old receipts are not rebound to new bytes.


The signed metadata fixup imports the exact test-budget policy already landed in [#186785](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186785), commit `1e13102e40a53392b4dfa2d2dedafe31061139f0`, blob `3e3b728b60e3266fefe87966538fe39755879589`. Only `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` changes (+6/-1); every other tracked entry is identical to d70. No new ceiling was selected, no tests were deleted, and no main/runtime/schema changes were imported. The +650 test-line failure remains recorded below; fresh exact-head CI now passes with the existing upstream policy. Native READY means preparation/publication only: the failed RSS bound remains the merge hold. Package count failures retain the scoped attribution below. Retained execution receipts are not relabeled as 9811 executions.

- Original regression fails on Node 24.22.1 and the repository-pinned Bun fork with native copying both auto/off: 6,316,032 observed private-image JavaScript read bytes exceed the 4,211,200 bound for the 2,105,344-byte fixture.
- First candidate passes that unchanged bound and all 18 fresh/retained integrity cases on both engines. Two newly added fixture assertions failed and were corrected. A separate independent source review identified a cleanup-classification gap, corrected with pre-classification and PostgreSQL cleanup-refusal cases. The production commit `fdfbe06dfcdf73fc6163373be7edbee23397e2ee` passes all 77 tests in the three changed test files on both Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun (154 passing cases); the native command joined with exit 0 and settled cleanup.
- The counter observes JavaScript comparison/hash reads. It does not measure every native SQLite/copy read or physical device I/O. Auto mode is not evidence that reflink succeeded.
- Independent source review identified and verified the cleanup ownership and measured-checkout binding corrections. Fresh review of the final head found no P0–P3 defects; its source-correctness verdict does not override the failed performance gate.
- The original three-file run covers committed WAL, original/stopped/maintenance capture siblings, integrity/foreign-key/catalog corruption, FULL-auto-vacuum normalization, later-write rollback refusal, and cleanup failure. Additional restore/cancellation/staging and final static evidence are described below. The published-driver compatibility lanes and current-head hosted CI pass. Package npm12/aggregate failures remain explicitly attributed below; the bounded performance rule remains FAILED.
- No live database was copied or changed for this proof, and no service restart or deployment is part of this PR.

### Maintainer acceptance of the disclosed historical tradeoff

On 2026-10-28, the maintainer explicitly accepted the corrected-harness matrix's measured tradeoff for the 23.698–24.990% reduction in 16 MiB logical reads. This accepts these disclosed outcomes, not unspecified new or worse regressions:

- Node, auto, 2 MiB, repeated CPU p95: 80.641 → 92.498 ms (+11.857 ms; 1.147034×).
- Node, auto, 16 MiB, repeated CPU p95: 163.448 → 181.199 ms (+17.751 ms; 1.108603×).
- Node, off, 2 MiB, repeated CPU p95: 83.058 → 103.650 ms (+20.592 ms; 1.247923×).
- Bun, auto, 2 MiB, repeated CPU p95: 91.861 → 122.120 ms (+30.259 ms; 1.329400×).
- Bun, off, 2 MiB, repeated CPU p95: 88.653 → 97.868 ms (+9.215 ms; 1.103945×).
- Node, off, 2 MiB, first-capture lifetime-RSS median: 686,160 → 722,384 KiB (+36,224 KiB; 1.052792×). This median was disclosed but was not the gated maximum-across-samples RSS statistic.

The five CPU p95 misses, both ≥20% stops, and the original matrix remain FAILED under the original numerical rule. Acceptance is an explicit owner tradeoff decision, not a rewritten measurement or a generic waiver. The original thresholds and all samples remain below. Final performance qualification below remains FAILED. Hosted CI and the published-driver compatibility lanes now pass, with the separate package-count failures attributed below. No merge, deployment, Gateway restart, new/worse regression acceptance or additional source change follows merely from this historical decision.

### Final-head qualification rule, declared before measurement

The single final matrix compares frozen base `d3184ac52b6a2df26a5dc6e856581f42178f3978` with current head `d70aa2322071058e3a2ca4f2878fba3a12fdc7a3`, using committed workload SHA-256 `9b4b39452c72ca46598c71b4f560c094c63cbc0682c468fac45d2d1800aaf2eb` for both variants. The eight cells retain five serial baseline/candidate timing pairs and one separate count pair each: 96 children and 192 first/repeated-capture rows. Node 24.22.1, pinned Bun `191755ec1`, independent frozen dependencies, disk-backed ext4 fixtures, cold lazy-import timing, full-byte integrity oracles and all samples remain required. No prewarming, forced GC, profiling or repeat-for-green is allowed.

The original numerical gates remain reported unchanged. An original-rule CPU-p95 failure is accepted only in one of the five named repeated-capture cells above, and only if **both** its ratio and positive absolute increase are no worse than that cell's historical raw values; the displayed rounded values are not extra tolerance. The disclosed Node/off/2 MiB first-capture RSS median is likewise bounded by its historical ratio and +36,224 KiB increase, separately from the unchanged maximum-across-samples RSS gate. All other original gated metrics must remain within 5%; a new or worse failure, including a new/worse 20% stop, blocks qualification. Each 16 MiB runtime/mode cell must retain at least a 10% median logical-read reduction. This is a bounded owner-accepted tradeoff, not a change to the historical FAILED verdicts.

The isolated run requires at least 16 minutes remaining after preparation. Its whole-work deadline is the earlier of start + 30 minutes and the native returned expiry minus four minutes; each 120-second child shares that deadline. Incomplete work does not qualify. Controller and fixture temporary roots are separate; artifact capture and native release must settle. This plan permitted required CI and one exact-head ClawSweeper re-review, with auto-merge off. Package Acceptance run [40707223528](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40707223528) separately checked the exact candidate through the published driver; terminal results and the remaining RSS hold are recorded below.

### Final-head matrix result — bounded qualification FAILED

The rule above was published and read back byte-for-byte at 2026-10-28 14:36:16 UTC (body SHA-256 `3b8330db9713a75d0ca2f23342cf4a3290761512ed08635c737900faae1cd6b7`). First measured child started at 14:55:52.213 UTC. All 80 timing and 16 count children joined in the declared serial order, producing all 192 first/repeated-capture rows. - **Bounded owner-accepted rule: FAILED** on the explicitly bounded Node/off/2 MiB first-capture lifetime-RSS median: 685,648 → 739,840 KiB, +54,192 KiB (52.921875 MiB), 1.079037640×. Accepted bounds were 1.052792352× and +36,224 KiB (35.375 MiB). The new increase exceeds the accepted absolute allowance by 17,968 KiB (17.546875 MiB).

The earlier filtered-regression versus full-file durations used different selections and are not a paired comparison. This result uses identical isolated-process capture workloads. It demonstrates a read reduction and fails the published overall acceptance rule; readiness stays blocked.

### Predeclared performance acceptance

Workload: the committed `backup-capture` mode in `scripts/perf/update-doctor-generation-measure.ts`, invoking the real in-process rollback-capture owner on freshly created SQLite fixtures. Compare the frozen base and candidate in separate remote worktrees on one lease, with the same frozen dependencies, Node 24.22.1 and repository-pinned Bun, and native auto/off modes. Use allocated 2 MiB and 16 MiB payloads. Fixture setup, entry-module imports, copy-control probe, and a real clock-age wait stay outside capture timing; first-capture timing includes lazy owner imports and source-loader compilation.

For every runtime × mode × size cell, run five serial ABAB process pairs. Each process reports its first capture and one repeated capture separately; these are process/owner temperatures, not a claim that OS caches are cold. Report all samples, median, empirical five-sample p95, min/max, host load, CPU, RSS, filesystem, and the separate control-copy method. Keep count-instrumented samples separate from timing samples.

Acceptance:
1. Exact snapshot contents, generation authority, and cleanup/integrity assertions pass. The scoped read bound remains two required private generation observations plus the named header allowance; the redundant acquisition is absent.
2. At 16 MiB, the median Linux logical read volume (`/proc/self/io` rchar delta) falls by at least 10% in every runtime/mode cell.
3. For every first/repeated-capture cell, candidate median and p95 wall time and combined user/system CPU must be no more than 1.05× baseline. Process-lifetime maxRSS must be no more than 1.05× baseline (the same existing RSS field and threshold). Any 20% regression is an immediate stop, not dismissed as noise.
4. Retained staging must stay within the existing space admission on a non-CoW fallback, with successful or refused cleanup accounted for. A separate copy-control result is reported only as that probe's result, not as proof of every capture transfer.

A failed rule blocks readiness. Repeated timing does not erase a failed sample, and no timeout increase or integrity bypass qualifies a result.

Reproduction shape (run once for each source root, engine, mode, size, and pair):
```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/update-doctor-generation-measure.ts baseline backup-capture 1 "$BASE_ROOT" auto 16 timing
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/update-doctor-generation-measure.ts candidate backup-capture 1 "$CANDIDATE_ROOT" auto 16 timing
```

prs.title: fix(msteams): Teams messages with an emoji report phantom unavailable attachments
prs.body:
Closes #177341

## What Problem This Solves

Teams renders emoji as HTML sprite images. Ordinary text with mentions and emoji can therefore reach the agent with pathless image facts and a misleading attachments-unavailable notice, causing requests to resend files that never existed. HTML-only emoji can also lose its entire body when the sprite is excluded from media without preserving its text.

Related: #57366 was an earlier repair closed unmerged. Mention-name preservation (#102376) and Gateway admission (#178554) are separate and not fixed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify verified Teams emoji sprites at the shared HTML extraction owner. Require the Teams CDN hostname plus an emoji asset path or pictographic alt marker; a genuine image on the same host remains media. Preserve a recognized sprite's alt text before HTML-to-text conversion, including when the message has no activity.text.

Reuse current main's linear HTML scanner and its tag ranges rather than restoring the old backtracking img regex or adding a second parser. Media extraction and body extraction share sprite replacement. URL classification parses once. No download permissions, authentication, Graph policy, mention normalization, storage or admission behavior changes.

## User Impact

Emoji stays text instead of becoming a phantom unavailable attachment. Mixed messages retain their real images. Actual unavailable attachments still produce the existing warning. The contributor's commit is preserved.

## Evidence

[Worker-owned built Gateway before/after proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177373#issuecomment-6486171903), head `db7716c5516b70aaeb4c70abb689ce7ca4b1855d`, Node 24.22.1:

- Pinned main twice and candidate twice through real Teams BotFramework `/api/messages` ingress in isolated Docker Gateways, with the existing private-QA loopback transport and synthetic local Connector/model fixtures.
- Persisted agent input via `chat.history`: main advertises phantom images; candidate has no sprite media, keeps HTML-only 🙂, and retains exactly one stored PNG in mixed messages.
- Real-image, same-CDN nonemoji and genuine-unavailable controls preserve their behavior.
- Final repetitions: 24 accepted activities, 24 agent inputs, 24 local model requests and 24 delivered Connector replies across both refs.
- Five focused files: 90 tests pass; final compact advertisement matrix: 21 pass. Integrated regressions on main: three intended failures, 30 passes. Scoped lint and repository formatter parity pass.
- Repaired our CI test-type errors by preserving literal media kinds and contextually typing the expected-media table; scoped owner test types and the 21-case matrix pass. This follow-up changes test typing only; production bytes and the runtime proof are unchanged.

This uses representative documented sprite markup, not a captured reporter payload or a real Microsoft tenant. The earlier contributor-based runtime reproduced #178554 after classification, including plain-image controls. No admission repair was added; after integrating current upstream changes to the touched owners, both final candidate repetitions delivered all replies. This does not claim to fix that separate race.

## Simplification

Consolidated duplicate advertised/download/content/facts regressions into existing owner matrices. Retained sprite-without-alt, genuine CDN image, mixed image, reference de-duplication and text precedence coverage. Final production delta **+48**, tests **−3**, four files; no baseline increase or new test file. Remaining growth implements sprite recognition and text preservation while retaining the current linear parser.

## AI Assistance

AI assisted source tracing, test consolidation and the isolated Gateway proof. @LiuwqGit's implementation and commit are retained; thanks to the reporter of #177341.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous classification; no persisted format or migration changes. Blast radius is Teams inbound HTML sprite/media classification. An incorrect classifier could suppress a genuine inline image or lose an HTML-only message, covered by the real-image/CDN and emoji-only controls above.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

## Verification

<!-- forone-current-submission:start -->
### Current submission status — 2026-10-29

The earlier shared curly failure is confirmed on official-main CI [40800487319](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40800487319/job/123207281187); the upstream owner already supplied #187167 / #187144. ## Real behavior proof

The prior reviewed head has successful hosted CI; current-head CI is tracked below. Current 47-file canonical autoreview and focused integration checks are complete. ### Adopted official cached-title repair and current integration

The remaining [UI 2/8 failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39469559363/job/118790829856) is `chat-widget-scroll.e2e.test.ts`, “keeps touch flings continuous through widgets and preserves the reader during streaming”: 257 px total travel did not exceed the existing 260 px assertion. The complete UI, test, scripts, shared/canvas source trees, widget HTML SDK owner, dependency lock/manifests, and CI/runtime setup owners are identical to official main `79262d0571694dbf083b7d1bf5a206cc8fb93936`. Two bounded, unchanged official-base replays used the canonical UI E2E wrapper, Node 24.19.0, and normal Chromium mobile touch emulation, without CPU throttling. These are failing whole-case controls on macOS, not passing controls or reproductions of the Linux CI assertion. The earlier official 0 > 120 touch assertion is also different. ### Native touch-fling CI diagnosis

prs.title: fix(cli): load Unicode PowerShell completion files on Windows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PowerShell completion installation failing to load when the Windows state directory contains non-ASCII characters, and cached completion corrupting Unicode command choices in Windows PowerShell.

## User Impact

Windows PowerShell users can reload installed completion from Unicode paths and receive the original Unicode choices. Re-run the existing completion installation command to repair a previous profile. No configuration or migration is required. Existing UTF-16 profiles keep their encoding; ASCII and non-Windows output remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows PowerShell reads BOM-less script files as ANSI. Declare UTF-8 only when the existing profile/cache writer emits non-ASCII text. Keep profile preservation, atomic publication, and stdout generation with their existing owners.

## Evidence

Native Windows, Node 24.22.1, actual `powershell.exe` 5. The command-entry reproduction used `registerCompletionCli` with `completion --shell powershell --install --yes`, a real cache under a task-only `state ü 空` directory, and then dot-sourced the resulting profile. Paths below are redacted; no platform or filesystem mocks.

```text
BEFORE
profilePrefix: 23204f (no BOM)
powershell.exe: exit 1
CommandNotFoundException: the cache path is decoded incorrectly

AFTER
profilePrefix: efbbbf
powershell.exe: exit 0
{"major":5,"loaded":true}
stderr: ""
```

The committed regressions exercise actual PS5 file decoding for new/existing profiles and the real CLI cache writer with a bounded fixture command registry, then request completion through `CommandCompletion.CompleteInput`. Existing tests evaluated script strings directly and therefore missed file decoding.

- Unmodified owner: **3 failed, 16 passed, 3 existing POSIX-only skips**; the two Unicode-path cases fail on profile reload, and the cached choice is decoded incorrectly.
- Repaired owner: **19 passed, 3 unchanged skips** across both files; 12.10 s wall time, about 7.6 s native profile test time. Native PS5 processes are necessary to test its file decoder. GitHub’s incremental CI matrix skipped the Windows job; the native Windows/PowerShell results above are local.
- Targeted maintained production/test types, typed lint (four files), formatting and whitespace checks passed. Independent manual review and canonical complete five-file P0–P3 review: scoped-clean, zero findings; all six file/context hashes unchanged. The compatibility consumer suite had 19 passed, 1 failed, 10 skipped: its untouched Windows Bash/MSYS fixture fails identically on the clean base, with no added skip or weakened assertion. Full exact-head CI passed on `4088c2c3d5cc8c2ee08cf025999f14811cf30181` (run 40628894530). Native Windows timings above are local; GitHub CI timing is not presented as a measured before/after test-cost comparison.

<details>
<summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

The two existing file producers remain the owners. No new API, setting, dependency, shell invocation in production, or wrapper is introduced. One existing profile table gains two concrete filesystem-decoding cases; one CLI-writer regression protects Unicode cache contents. Distinct open completion PRs #173223 (quote escaping) and #162918 (option terminators) were inspected and do not repair file encoding.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

On a fresh profile, looking up a client identity could fail with "run openclaw doctor --fix" instead of reporting that no identity exists yet. The credential owner now reports absence for an empty bootstrap store, and the next write initializes it as before.

- Problem: `openClientCredentialCustody` threw for a store file whose schema transaction had not committed (schema version 0, empty catalog) whenever the caller was read-only, so `loadDeviceIdentityIfPresent`/`loadDeviceIdentityIfPresentAsync` surfaced an internal error instead of an absent identity.
- Solution: treat that verified empty-bootstrap state as absence: skip schema creation, release custody, and let the existing missing-store result path answer the read.
- What changed: `src/infra/client-credential-store.ts` (owner decision) plus regression coverage in `src/infra/client-credential-store.test.ts` and `src/infra/device-identity-worker.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: migration callers still fail closed on an empty store; partial schemas, unsupported versions, integrity checks, admission receipts and legacy-readiness gates are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The store file is published before its schema transaction commits, so a reader can legitimately observe a version-0 file with no tables; that is a bootstrap state, not corruption. Reporting absence restores the read contract that existed before the credential cutover (#124745) while keeping every invalid-schema guard fail-closed.

- Best fix: yes — the owner decides absence once, so every caller (device identity, chat request key, tokens) inherits it without local special cases.
- Alternative: catching the error in each caller — rejected: duplicate policy at projection layers and it hides genuinely unsupported schemas.
- Risk / non-goals: an existing but truncated store is now reported as absent rather than "run doctor"; the next writer re-initializes the schema in the same file.

## User Impact

Fresh or half-initialized profiles no longer surface an internal "client credential store is empty" error during identity lookup; the identity is created on the next write as before. Operators no longer need to run `openclaw doctor --fix` for this benign race.

## Evidence

Runtime proof through the shipped caller `loadDeviceIdentityIfPresentAsync` with a real empty credential store file (Node v24.22.1 / SQLite 3.53.4), on the PR head:

```console
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof-empty-bootstrap.ts
fixture: existing empty credential store /tmp/proof-185297-EjnOsP/client/credentials.sqlite bytes= 0
read #1 (loadDeviceIdentityIfPresentAsync) => null
read #2 => null
create after absence => deviceId: 072278f5c44d88c1b4455a994be76ac80729be147fd7203f491d5ab9dab7bb7a
read #3 => deviceId: 072278f5c44d88c1b4455a994be76ac80729be147fd7203f491d5ab9dab7bb7a
```

The same script on the pre-fix head aborts before it can report absence:

```console
$ git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/infra/client-credential-store.ts && node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof-empty-bootstrap.ts
fixture: existing empty credential store /tmp/proof-185297-RnCAYU/client/credentials.sqlite bytes= 0
Error: Client credential store is empty; run openclaw doctor --fix.
```

Regression coverage: the new store-level test is red on the base commit and green with the fix; the device-identity worker test now asserts absence plus an uninitialized schema.

```console
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/infra/client-credential-store.test.ts src/infra/device-identity-worker.test.ts src/infra/device-identity.test.ts src/infra/device-identity-async.test.ts src/infra/device-identity.state-dir.test.ts
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/client-credential-store.test.ts > reports absence for an existing empty bootstrap store and creates on the next write
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/device-identity-worker.test.ts > device identity local worker > returns absence for an existing empty credential store without initializing it
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  45 passed | 1 skipped (46)
```

What was not tested: concurrent bootstrap from two runtime processes and Windows runtime behavior; both are recorded as residual risk above.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used git history (`git log -S`), source tracing across the credential store and its callers, and `node --import tsx` runtime scripts to verify before/after behavior. The implementer understands the code: the owner decides "empty bootstrap means absence" once, releases SQLite custody, and the next write creates the schema, while migration and invalid-schema paths stay fail-closed. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

The alternative review was explicitly approved for this PR and is not a CLI pass; the subsequent brace-only delta also received mechanical review.

These Gateway tests use a scripted loopback Responses provider. They are not hosted-model, real-channel, restart, local Codex, or production-scale proof. Hosted CI for the repaired candidate and its CI duration are not established by these local runs.

Native preparation reported `build:false` and `runtime:false`, and the effective build/runtime input fingerprints matched that source. The unchanged producer stamps still record precommit producer HEAD `70159c5dc95809b55cb60713a558d871ef08ecad` with `inputsClean:false`. This is supported source-equivalent artifact reuse for that source, not a claim that the artifacts were freshly built at either repaired commit. No new model call accompanied the CI follow-up.
