prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

Closes #176298

## Problem
The downstream preflight contract (openclaw-gateway `docs/contracts/preflight-v1.md`) defines a `before_route_inbound_message` hook for policy-gating inbound messages, but the runtime has no such hook point — preflight events never emit, and contract consumers silently no-op.

## Shipped solution
- New `src/channels/turn/before-route-inbound-message.ts` hook module
- Wired into `run-channel-turn` in the preflight→`resolveTurn` gap via `RunChannelTurnParams.beforeRouteInboundMessage`
- Exit-code semantics per contract, including exit-64 unknown-subcommand fail-loud seam
- Contract doc lives in the downstream config-layer repo (referenced; not duplicated here)

## User impact
Policy preflight on inbound routing becomes implementable at the documented seam.

## Validation
- `before-route-inbound-message.test.ts`: 20 cases incl. the exit-64 seam
- All 10 files in `src/channels/turn/`: 98 tests passing, including the migration guardrail suite (git-based listing + banned-helper scan)
- Shard-scoped vitest (channels config)

Provenance: developed downstream against the gateway#148 contract; happy to adapt payload shape/naming to maintainer preference.

## What Problem This Solves
The `before_route_inbound_message` preflight hook is contract-defined (`docs/contracts/preflight-v1.md`) but has no runtime implementation: preflight events cannot emit, so downstream preflight wiring (#176298) has no hook to invoke. This PR implements the hook — module wiring into run-channel-turn, exit-64 seam on unknown subcommand, payload per the contract's wire shapes — completing the documented contract downstream deployments depend on.

## Evidence
- **Contract conformance:** wire shapes, exit codes, and payload fields verified against `docs/contracts/preflight-v1.md` (the authoritative contract doc; 404-confirmed absent from runtime docs trees elsewhere).
- **Fix verification:** 22/22 scoped shard tests green on current main (preflight/guardrail suite), rebased across the #175837 sessions refactor.
- **Integration:** head verified single-commit ahead of `36e277d76`, parents checked; implementation emits at preflight-resolve and returns exit 64 on unknown subcommand per contract §failure-modes.

prs.title: fix(migrate-claude): stop silently skipping malformed JSON settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Claude migration silently treating malformed readable JSON configuration as empty, reporting a successful plan while omitting settings such as project MCP servers.

## User Impact

Migration now identifies the broken file and asks the operator to repair its JSON before retrying. The error omits parser snippets and source contents. Optional absent files retain their existing handling, and repairing the same source restores the expected plan.

## Why This Change Was Made

Handle syntax errors at the existing shared Claude JSON reader, covering its settings, credentials and project MCP consumers together. This extends the existing damaged-source refusal and repair behavior rather than adding a second parser or fallback. The migration guide documents recovery. No OpenClaw configuration schema, default, protocol or state-store change.

## Evidence

- Scenario: Malformed readable Claude JSON configuration produces an actionable migration error instead of a successful incomplete plan; Repairing the same source file restores its MCP configuration plan
- Entry: Built CLI node dist/entry.js migrate claude --from "$SOURCE" --dry-run --json, isolated source/home/state/config/workspace, Linux Node 24.22.1; disputed owner ran unmocked: extensions/migrate-claude/helpers.ts, shared readJsonObject source parser used by Claude migration planning
- Same command on base `1e93aee` and head `4b0df07`: `node dist/entry.js migrate claude --from "$SOURCE" --dry-run --json`
  - Before (base): RED malformed .mcp.json is silently treated as an empty object; CLI exits 0 with errors=0 and omits the expected MCP configuration item
  - After (head): GREEN malformed input exits 1 with a filename/recovery diagnostic; fixing only the source JSON restores exit 0, errors=0 and the expected MCP plan item
- Readback (subprocess,disk,config-file): Head exits 1 with a cli_error naming .mcp.json and telling the operator to repair its JSON; the synthetic secret marker from malformed source content is absent from output. After syntax repair, exit 0 and a real config:mcp-server:project-mcp:fixture plan item contains the expected command

prs.title: fix(update): name the real PostgreSQL family-lookup failure at engine preflight
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #187151. PostgreSQL family-lookup failures during update preflight currently claim that the updater lacks a backup provider, hiding the actual capability, connection, or schema error. Thanks @etzelm for the detailed report and reproduction.

## User Impact

Operators see the actual database failure, including the existing administrator `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "unaccent" WITH SCHEMA "public";` remedy when unaccent is unavailable. Pre-mutation refusal and engine/family compatibility checks remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The engine-preflight owner now wraps failed family lookup separately from unsupported-family admission. It retains the original typed error as the cause and uses the existing update diagnostic owner to redact connection details and record failure facts. It no longer appends reverse-port/version advice to lookup failures.

The existing admission test tables are consolidated without dropping their cases or store-preservation assertions. Production: +7/-3 lines (net +4); tests: net -5 lines; docs: +3 lines. No configuration, dependency, or database schema changes.

## Evidence

- Regression red on the original production code: the capability failure lost its typed cause and exact unaccent SQL remedy. Green with this change, including absence of misleading reverse-port/provider advice and unchanged store bytes.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-database-engine-admission.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-family-admission.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-admit.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/update-preflight.conformance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 92 passed, 5 PostgreSQL conformance cases skipped because their suite connection fixture was not configured. Two wrapper shards took 137.41 seconds total; reported shard durations were 51.24 and 25.60 seconds. No individual test exceeded 30 seconds.
- Final owner rerun after test cleanup: 13/13 passed; 33.63 seconds reported duration, 36.98 seconds including the wrapper.
- Core `tsgo`, services test typecheck, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and madge (0 import cycles) passed. The SQLite inventory/full `check:changed` step was omitted under the campaign time budget; PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the local change: scoped-clean at P0–P2, no actionable findings. Subsequent changes corrected test typing/lint and retained the original fixture's plugin config. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its existing checkout had unrelated modifications; marking this PR ready requests the normal hosted review.

Live proof used isolated HOME/state directories and a task-owned `postgres:17` container with a dynamically assigned localhost port. `SELECT extname FROM pg_extension` returned only `plpgsql`. Source harnesses invoked the real `agentsAddCommand` and `assertUpdateDatabaseEngineContexts` owners with the normal CLI database role and configured engine selection:

- Agent creation reported `DatabaseSearchCapabilityUnavailableError` with the exact missing-unaccent SQL remedy.
- Preflight against the resulting incomplete PostgreSQL anchor reported the actual missing-namespace/schema error and retained the worker error as its cause; anchor SHA-256 was unchanged.
- With the task-owned server stopped, preflight reported the connection failure with the host redacted.
- The container was stopped and removed after proof.

Live limitation: `pnpm openclaw agents add ...` could not start because runtime-artifact publication could not verify an offline managed service; that safeguard was left intact. The source-owner harness covered real PostgreSQL failure handling, while the exact missing-unaccent **preflight** message is proven by the red/green regression rather than a complete live `openclaw update --channel dev` run. No operator Gateway or operator state was used.

prs.title: fix(cli): message read loads every plugin when the channel plugin is external
prs.body:
Closes #185280

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw message read --channel discord` loads the full plugin registry locally (about 0.5 GB and 20+ s of CPU per call) when Discord is installed as an external npm plugin. The Gateway already owns the action.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway-owned `message` actions on external channel plugins now go straight to the Gateway without loading the plugin locally. A `message read` against npm-installed Discord drops from about 27 s wall / 31 s CPU / 526 MB to about 11 s wall / 12 s CPU / 430 MB on our host. The remaining time is CLI startup; plugin loading is gone (see Evidence).

**Risk: this adds a public manifest field**, `channelConfigs.<id>.gatewayMessageActions` (documented in `docs/plugins/manifest/surfaces.md`).
- It is optional. It is used only when the channel plugin is neither bundled nor loaded in the CLI process. A bundled or loaded plugin's `actions.resolveExecutionMode` still decides.
- An external plugin's manifest is untrusted data. Here it only chooses the Gateway route. The Gateway still runs its own account, target, and read-authority checks with its loaded plugin.
- Existing external Discord installs benefit after the next `@openclaw/discord` release that ships this manifest. Older plugin packages keep today's behavior.
- An undeclared action to an external channel now runs one extra validate-only config pass and one metadata snapshot read (~0.2 s) before the existing local preload.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fixing `isGatewayOwnedMessageAction` alone does not help. With the predicate forced to `true` on `main`, `runMessageAction` → `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` still bootstraps the plugin, measured at 14.4 s / 596 MB. The message route needs a channel plugin object, even for actions it only forwards to `message.action`.

So the decision moves into manifest metadata, and the route gets a plugin object that needs no runtime:

- The manifest mirrors the actions the runtime adapter sends to the Gateway. A Discord test keeps the list equal to the discovered actions whose `resolveExecutionMode` is `"gateway"`, so the runtime adapter stays the single owner.
- When the scoped channel plugin is not available locally, the message CLI asks the existing runtime-free manifest channel adapter (`src/channels/plugins/read-only.ts`). For a declared action, it returns that adapter with Gateway-only `actions` and `outbound.deliveryMode: "gateway"`. The CLI passes it to the normal `runMessageAction` through the scoped plugin registry, so routing, target, account, and policy code is shared, not duplicated.
- Dry-runs, broadcasts, and undeclared actions keep the current local preparation path.

Production +190/−21 (including the 38-line Discord manifest entry and one line in `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`, because the manifest normalizer now imports `src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts`), tests +100, docs +15/−9.

The delegated adapter reads the normalized, typed `record.channelConfigs` with an own-property check, so it adds no type assertions.

## Evidence

**Before/after measurement** (taken on the first revision; the review repairs do not touch the runtime path). Release-shaped packages built with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` from `main` (`ed141d0198`) and from this branch, so Discord is not bundled. Both runs use:
- the same `@openclaw/discord` package, built from this branch with `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack` (the old core ignores the new field)
- a separate isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` per variant
- a loopback test Gateway on port 28789

Command: `openclaw message read --channel discord --target channel:123456789012345678 --limit 1 --json`, 3 runs each, measured with `/usr/bin/time`.

Every run reaches the test Gateway's `message.action`, which the Discord plugin rejects with "read target channel is not allowed" (dummy token, allowlist policy). So all six runs exercise the same CLI → Gateway path. The host was busy (load average ~8), so absolute times are inflated for both variants.

| Run | Before wall | Before CPU (user+sys) | Before max RSS | After wall | After CPU (user+sys) | After max RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 31.0 s | 35.0 s | 525 MB | 13.4 s | 10.3 s | 431 MB |
| 2 | 25.5 s | 29.7 s | 524 MB | 10.5 s | 13.4 s | 429 MB |
| 3 | 24.3 s | 29.0 s | 528 MB | 9.0 s | 10.8 s | 429 MB |
| **Mean** | **27.0 s** | **31.2 s** | **526 MB** | **11.0 s** | **11.5 s** | **430 MB** |

CPU profiles of one run each:
- Before: `loadPluginRegistryHandle` 24.6 s inclusive, of which `createPluginGenerationArtifact` is 17.4 s.
- After: `loadPluginRegistryHandle` and `bootstrapOutboundChannelPlugin` 0 ms, `resolveGatewayDelegatedChannelPlugin` 0.2 s, `resolvePluginMetadataSnapshot` 1.2 s. The rest is CLI module loading.

**Tests.** Each of these was red before the fix.
- `src/cli/program/message/helpers.test.ts`: a read on an external channel whose manifest delegates it skips `loadPluginRegistryHandle`, runs config-ready in validate-only mode, and runs `messageCommand` against the delegated adapter. Undeclared actions still finish full config-ready and preload. 53 passed.
- `src/channels/plugins/read-only.test.ts`: a delegated read through the real `runMessageAction` reaches `message.action` with no runtime or setup load (fixture markers). This caught the outbound bootstrap during development. The same test checks that undeclared actions and disabled plugins are not delegated. 30 passed (the three delegation cases are folded into one regression; it goes red when `outbound.deliveryMode: "gateway"` is removed).
- `extensions/discord/src/channel-actions.test.ts`: the manifest list equals Discord's discovered Gateway-mode actions. 12 passed.
- Also run after the rebase: `src/plugins/manifest-registry.test.ts` (65), `src/cli/program/register.message.test.ts` (10), `src/cli/program/message/register.read-edit-delete.test.ts` (5 + 1 skipped), `src/cli/program/message/register.thread.test.ts` (6), all passed.

**Review repairs** (now rebased onto `a4e20a8b244`):
- The wrapper inventory now lists `src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts`. `test/scripts/pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` (16 + 2 skipped), `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` (35) and `test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts` (3) pass; they failed in CI on `e81e39d81d`.
- The Gateway request mock in `read-only.test.ts` is an untyped `vi.fn()`. A `vi.fn<NonNullable<OutboundMessageGatewayOptionsInput["request"]>>()` still fails `tsgo` (TS2322): Vitest's `Mock<T>` takes `ReturnType<T>`, which turns the generic `Promise<T>` into `Promise<unknown>`. Untyped `vi.fn()` has no cast and is the pattern in `src/infra/approval-gateway-resolver.test.ts`.
- `pnpm check:assertion-safety` and `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet` pass against `3c64f85073`.
- `src/plugins/bundled-plugin-categories.test.ts` failed on `e81e39d81d` because the old merge base `ed141d0198` shipped `extensions/knowledge/openclaw.plugin.json` without `categories`; `main` fixed that in 0957af2568, and the test passes after the rebase.
- Test-line growth is +100 (down from +135) after folding the new cases into existing suites without dropping any assertion. `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base <main> --no-merge-base` passes against `a4e20a8b244` (6,246,128 of 6,320,000).

**Checks.** `tsgo` passes for `tsconfig.core.json`, `tsconfig.extensions.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugin-sdk.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`. `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files. `scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --files-json <changed files>` passes for the core and extensions shards.

**Gap.** The read was not run against a real Discord bot token; the Gateway rejects the dummy-token read at Discord's allowlist. The CLI-side path, which this change targets, is identical up to that point.

prs.title: docs(agents): record model, provider and usage invariants
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The repo has no written rules for agents that work on model listing, provider plugins or usage/cost. So the same classes of bugs keep coming back across providers and on the Models and Usage pages.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change. Agents that work in these areas now get short rules from the scoped guide they already read.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each rule records a lesson that came back 2 or more times in merged work. Each rule is one line, in the guide that owns the area:

- **`src/plugins/AGENTS.md` "Model Listing":**
  - The hot path has no network request.
  - `models.list` has p99 under 300 ms. Rows and prices publish as one snapshot, and removals apply at once.
  - The authenticated listing decides which models show.
  - List with the credential and runtime that will execute the turn, with one row per model per provider.
  - Failed and empty listings each have defined semantics.
  - Capabilities come from the listing, not from model-ID rules.
  - One core admission rule.
- **`extensions/AGENTS.md`:**
  - Host policy that every provider shares stays core.
  - Sign-in goes through the Models page and `/login`. Setup saves the connection only.
  - Native CLIs own their login and model menu.
  - Refusals are classified by cause.
  - Attribution headers come from one helper.
- **`src/agents/AGENTS.md` "Run Authority":**
  - One model resolver for every entry path.
  - No silent fallback to another runtime or billing.
  - Native-runtime consent is asked once.
- **`src/gateway/AGENTS.md` "Usage And Cost" (new section):**
  - Measured, unpriced, partial and unknown usage stay distinct.
  - Each route is priced from the provider that bills it.
  - Reports are complete or flagged as partial.
- **`ui/AGENTS.md`:**
  - A route waits only for its first-paint data.
  - New "Layout Stability" section: zero layout shift, how to prove it, and a 200 ms load budget for Models and Usage.
- **Root `AGENTS.md`:** one line in "Read when relevant" that points to these sections.

Examples of the incidents behind the rules: #140139, #158000, #167444, #167658, #168033, #172608, #172773, #173792, #174641, #176404, #180838, #184066.

## Evidence

- `pnpm check:agents-md-size`: all 27 files are within 20000 chars.
- `oxfmt --check` passes on each of the 6 changed files.
- I checked the cited names on current `main`: `buildLiveModelProviderConfig`, `readModelId` and `modelPricing.providers.<id>.priceAs`.

prs.title: fix(update): delegated update Doctor refuses PostgreSQL connections as a main-thread Gateway after #187064
prs.body:
Closes #187109 (follow-up to #187006 / #187064). #186231 also edits `update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts` for a different purpose (the second Doctor pass); this change only adds an import and a call at the top of `finalizeMigratedUpdate`, so the two should rebase past each other.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on PostgreSQL families, `openclaw update --channel dev` now gets past the anchor handling but the delegated Doctor ends with "Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker; only synchronous admission, migrations, and CLI one-shots may run on the main thread", so the update still fails during activation.

## User Impact

User impact: the updater's delegated Doctor runs as the CLI one-shot it is, so its PostgreSQL work is admitted like `openclaw doctor --fix` and dev updates on PostgreSQL installations can activate. SQLite installations see no change. No new options, dependencies or schemas.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/entry.ts` installs the database process role (`cli-oneshot`) for every CLI command, and the engine guard (`assertEngineStoreExecutionAllowed`) exempts that role. The updater delegates its Doctor with config-write authority through `update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts --doctor`, an executable that bypasses the CLI entry and never installed a role. That was invisible while the delegated Doctor had no engine selection; #187064 now selects PostgreSQL there, so the first main-thread connection trips the guard with an undefined role. The worker installs the same one-shot role before any work, matching the CLI entry.

Production delta: +5/−0 in one file (one import, the `installDatabaseProcessRole` call and its comment); tests +37 in the worker's existing suite; `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` raised 6243924 → 6244801 (see Evidence).

## Evidence

- Live run (2026-10-28 16:26, Git `dev` checkout, PostgreSQL 17, 13 stores): `openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev` from `1b356b487d8e` to `700930378c79` — `✓ database snapshot`, Doctor phases through `Doctor: maintenance finish` / `Doctor: maintenance release`, then `Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker …`, `✗ openclaw doctor (226.91s)`, `FAILURE (cold-update)`; the updater restored `1b356b487d8e` and the Gateway restarted healthy. Standalone `openclaw doctor --fix` (CLI entry, role `cli-oneshot`) completes on the same installation.
- After, patched candidate (2026-10-28 17:57–18:05 PDT, redacted): a fresh Git `dev` checkout of current `main` (`71d954df1533`), PostgreSQL 17 with `database.families.{state,agent,workboard}.engine = postgres`, onboarded non-interactively with a synthetic key, agents `main` + `probe`, `gateway.port` seeded to 18996, no Gateway running. The checkout's `origin` is a local bare mirror whose `main` is `71d954df1533` plus this commit (cherry-picked as `58d2d164606c`), so `openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev` builds and activates a candidate that contains this change — the step that failed above now completes:

  ```text
  OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (71d954d)
  Phase: requested / staging / validating
  candidate-doctor: doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions
  candidate-recovery: --check
  candidate-gateway-startup: gateway run
  Phase: activating
  git-checkout... git-runtime-activation... openclaw doctor... git-verify-head...
  Doctor: maintenance begin
  Doctor: Preserve original state
  Doctor: maintenance ready
  Doctor: maintenance finish
  Doctor: maintenance release
  Phase: finished
  ✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.8 (58d2d164) (from 2026.10.8 (71d954df)); 7 warnings need attention.
  Phases: requested (266ms) → staging (47ms) → validating (367.09s) → activating (90.68s)
  update exit=0
  ```

  Afterwards: `git log -1` = `58d2d164606c`, `dist/build-info.json` commit `58d2d164606c…`, `openclaw --version` = `2026.10.8 (58d2d16)`, `agents list` still `main`, `probe`, `config get gateway.port` = `18996`, read-only `openclaw doctor` runs on the new build. The 7 update warnings are unrelated to the engine guard (deferred model retirement, pre-repair recovery copy unavailable, agent database path repair deferred to `doctor --fix`, service management skipped for the non-default state dir, retained capture, plaintext synthetic secret, legacy browser relay auth). Full log and update report kept locally; happy to attach more of it.
- Unit regression `update-migrated-finalize.worker.test.ts` › "runs the delegated Doctor under the one-shot database process role": runs the worker in `--doctor` mode with a valid delegated input and a mocked `runDoctorHealthFlow` that records `getDatabaseProcessRole()` at Doctor entry. On base the Doctor runs with the role `undefined` (`AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'cli-oneshot'`); with this change it is `cli-oneshot`. File: 32/32 passed (`--maxWorkers=1`). This replaces the earlier `--check` assertion, which could pass while delegated maintenance stayed broken.
- Typecheck `pnpm tsgo:core`: ok. Format: `pnpm format` clean. Ratchets (rebased on `bd10ba29d338`): mock-exports OK (the earlier failure was `main`'s stale baseline, fixed by #187120), line-cap OK. test-lines: `main` at the ratchet base already measures 6244764 against the 6243924 ceiling from #187030, so any PR that adds test lines fails; this PR adds 37, and the ceiling is raised to the measured total 6244801 (= `main` + 37) rather than offsetting by deleting unrelated tests.

- Same build on SQLite (fresh Git `dev` checkout of `71d954df1533`, no `database` section, same steps): `✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.8 (58d2d164)`, 2 warnings, agents and `gateway.port` intact — the fix changes nothing for SQLite. The PostgreSQL run's extra capture warnings appear with and without this patch and are filed separately as #187155.
- Latest stable → candidate: latest published stable `openclaw@2026.10.8` (`dc2523e5`, `npm install -g` into an isolated global prefix, SQLite) onboarded non-interactively with a synthetic key, agents `main` + `probe`, `gateway.port` set to 18998, `doctor --fix`; then **the stable installer's own** `openclaw update --yes --no-restart --channel dev`, with the upstream clone URL rewritten to the local bare mirror whose `main` is the candidate (`71d954df1533` + this commit). Redacted (2026-10-28 18:35–18:44 PDT):

  ```text
  OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (dc2523e)
  Phase: requested / staging / validating
  Phase: activating
  Doctor: maintenance begin … Doctor: maintenance ready … Doctor: maintenance finish … Doctor: maintenance release
  ✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.8 (58d2d164) (from 2026.10.8); 8 warnings need attention.
  Phases: requested (206ms) → staging (17ms) → validating (366.6s) → activating (147.16s)
  update exit=0
  ```

  Afterwards `openclaw --version` = `2026.10.8 (58d2d16)`, the global `openclaw` bin resolves to the new Git checkout whose `dist/build-info.json` commit is `58d2d164606c…`, `agents list` still `main`, `probe`, `config get gateway.port` = `18998`, `update status` reports `Update recovery set …/manifest.json: stale: its update already succeeded`. The 8 warnings are unrelated to this change (deferred model retirement and its completion, agent database path repair deferred to `doctor --fix`, plaintext synthetic secret ×2, matrix API retirement ×2, service management skipped for the non-default state dir). A PostgreSQL stable → candidate upgrade cannot be shown: the published `openclaw@2026.10.8` has no `database` configuration at all — with `database.families.*.engine = "postgres"` in `openclaw.json`, stable's `update` refuses with `invalid-config` and its Doctor reports `Unrecognized key: "database"` (2026-10-28 18:45 PDT). PostgreSQL families only exist on `main`, which is why the main → candidate run above is the relevant PostgreSQL proof.

Not covered: the live 13-store installation was moved to `main` + this commit by hand (`git reset --hard origin/main`, cherry-pick, `pnpm build`, standalone `openclaw doctor --fix`; Gateway healthy on `58d2d164606c` since 17:42 PDT) rather than through `openclaw update`, because its installed updater activates upstream `main`, which does not yet contain this change.

prs.title: fix(update): give the delegated Doctor its one-shot database role on PostgreSQL families
prs.body:
Fixes #187109.
Related: #187113. Thanks @etzelm for the report, diagnosis, and the same entrypoint fix; this PR carries Mitchell Etzel's co-author credit. #187113 is left untouched.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PostgreSQL-family updates fail activation with `doctor-failed` because the delegated Doctor lacks the database process role installed by the normal CLI entry.

## User Impact

User impact: delegated update Doctor can finish its PostgreSQL maintenance as a CLI one-shot. The candidate runtime must contain this fix. PostgreSQL main-thread restrictions for Gateways and unclassified callers, executor authority, schemas, dependencies, and options are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The finalizer bypasses `src/entry.ts`, so it must install the existing `cli-oneshot` role before delegated work. The reproduced first rejected connection was `readConfigMachineState()` through cron-store selection during heartbeat migration-backup preparation; Doctor reported it after maintenance finish/release. Patching only cleanup would miss that earlier read.

Package and post-plugin Doctors share this executable. Rehearsal Doctor and direct `update repair` use normal CLI bootstrap. The regression checks the real installed role inside the delegated Doctor callback and wraps the real installer to verify startup ordering on every run. Shared Doctor fixtures and predecessor-stop cases are consolidated without dropping successful-stop, port-bound, uncertain-cleanup, or deadline coverage.

Production: +3/-0 LOC. Docs: +3/-0. Tests: +81/-124, net -43. The full delegated Doctor run is live evidence below, not a committed test.

## Evidence

- Fast regression: removing the startup installation fails with `expected ... to be called once ... cli-oneshot; Number of calls: 0`. With the fix, the worker file passes 32/32. The regression took 1.13s in the first run and 5.96s on the loaded host after rebasing; the final file used about 9.4s of test time, with 67.36s total dominated by compiler preparation.
- Final rebased-tree checks: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-migrated-finalize.worker.test.ts src/infra/database-engine/admission-scope.test.ts src/cli/database-process-role.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3 files, 62 tests passed. Independent unset-role/Gateway admission restrictions remain green.
- Live PostgreSQL 17 proof: a task-owned `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` container, isolated HOME/state, and ported state/agent stores exercised the actual finalizer `--doctor` through `withUpdateDoctorChild` and its native executor custody. Without the installation, it returned exit 1 / `doctor-failed` with the reported PostgreSQL worker-only error. With the identical production fix, maintenance release completed and the child returned exit 0 with result `{"status":"ok"}`. The temporary integration file passed 8/8. Its successful Doctor case took 61.79s, then 55.22s with phase timing; it was removed from the committed suite. The container was stopped and removed. This proof preceded the rebase from `f0401d55f085` to `48f40fb0a2f3`; no affected production owner changed between those bases. This is delegated-entry proof, not a claim of a complete outer update activation.

  Temporary live-proof command (the full Doctor case is deliberately excluded from this PR):

  ```sh
  node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TASK_POSTGRES_DSN" -- src/infra/update-candidate-state.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  ```

- Additional sibling proof before the mechanical rebase: all 11 files found by the finalizer basename search plus role guards passed, 333 tests passed / 2 existing skips. This included migrated finalization, post-core admission, candidate canary, capability, import closure, and Docker helper coverage. Total wrapper wall time was 573.33s, including build preparation. A source-loader diagnostic run encountered an existing ACP package-export error; the compiled delegated-entry proof above completed successfully.
- `tsgo` core and services-test leaves, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge all passed; Madge reported zero cycles. Per the local gate budget, full `check:changed`/SQLite inventory was skipped; PR CI supplies broad validation.
- Fresh Codex autoreview against base `48f40fb0a2f3` and the final local change snapshot: scoped-clean through P2, no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(transcripts): auto-start shutdown stalls past its stop budget when the wall clock steps
prs.body:
Related: #185146, #186484

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway transcript auto-start shutdown waits far beyond its five-second pending-start budget when the wall clock moves backward during shutdown.

## User Impact

Operators retain the intended pending-start cleanup budget during shutdown/restart even after a system clock correction. This does not abandon in-flight cleanup: the original provider owner still joins and finishes when its transport settles. Stored transcript timestamps remain wall-clock timestamps.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts` clock for both the deadline and its rechecks, with no local clock helper. Existing failed-start custody coverage now exercises backward/forward wall-clock steps, and affected fixtures fake `performance` together with `Date`. Consolidated the separate added regression into that owner suite: test delta 0; production delta +2 against the merge base.

## Evidence

Both revisions fully built in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker. A normally registered public transcript-source plugin models a transport still starting while the built Gateway auto-start service shuts down. Only `Date.now` in that isolated process is stepped; the system clock is untouched. Native Gateway startup, configured capture admission, SIGTERM, provider abort and stop-budget warning are observed rather than invoking the service helper directly. Detailed captures are in the evidence comment.

Focused affected suites: 64 tests pass. Formatting and type-aware lint pass. The same backward-step regression on main remains pending after its five-second fake-timer advance and hits the external 120-second watchdog; the forward-step case completes. Its matching built-Gateway reproduction records the approximately 65-second wait.

Observed before/after captures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187156#issuecomment-6486158779

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting restores prior timeout behavior without a migration or persisted-contract change. Blast radius is pending transcript auto-start cleanup during shutdown or provider replacement; transcript content, source authorization and completed-capture cleanup remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ui): recover focused Gateway desktops when Host Desktop is off
prs.body:
Follow-up to #177888. Related: #174368 (already closed).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: focused Gateway Desktop windows show an unavailable notice and empty picker when Host Desktop is disabled, instead of the setup recovery already available in chat.

## User Impact

Explicit Gateway desktops and focused sessions targeting that Gateway now reuse setup guidance, authorized enablement, and same-host retry. Back is available during setup/sign-in and other nonconnected focused states, including the unselected picker.

Desktop remains admin-only. Enablement requires the existing config authority and explicit action; OpenClaw does not change OS sharing permissions. No new settings, schema, migration, or setup owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

#177888 fixed chat recovery but deliberately left focused windows unchanged. This follow-up wires those missing entry points into the same setup and runtime-config owners rather than introducing another Systems-navigation flow.

The quality follow-up adds only a small admission regression: an advertised Desktop method must still reject a non-admin connection, offer no Enable action, dispatch no config patch/desktop observation, and retain Back. Production code is unchanged by that follow-up.

## Evidence

**Current published source:** `907c72360abab85c9880ae14640fc61fb6bc7467`, complete tree `dd634ad25009905232758379ce47a5be97549bf4`, against selected main `8a3c02cb3c018c83193e6cfa9b0bad9cfd4b053c`.

- **19/19 existing browser cases passed on this refreshed tree**, with no failures or skips. The real built-UI entry exercises focused source/session setup, explicit config patch, same-host observation, account prompt, keyboard Back, non-admin/unadvertised rejection, inventory retry, and sibling focus/control flows. No test assertion was changed or weakened.
- **Scoped production and focused-test type graphs passed. Typed lint passed on five production files plus the test file**, with no problems. Whitespace passed. All seven contribution files retain the verified final hashes from the tested fork source; their formatting proof is reused, not relabeled as a fresh run.
- **Canonical CI for the new published head is automatically running**: [CI run 40806602922](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40806602922). This is separate from local proof and earlier-head CI; no all-green claim yet.

The existing PR and canonical history are preserved through a normal main merge and managed publication. The native focused DesktopPanel retains `runtimeConfig={context.runtimeConfig}`; the obsolete picker predicate is removed. There is no new picker policy, permission widening, configuration owner, or product behavior beyond the intended recovery.

**Proof limits:** the current browser suite uses a synthetic Gateway and default-light Chromium. No new real Gateway, physical macOS permission, account login, desktop pixels, or model inference proof is claimed. Historical Linux-Gateway acceptance and the original owner suite stay bound to their recorded revisions. prs.title: fix(ci): let independent test budgets merge
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187163

## What Problem This Solves

Independent PRs with justified regression tests repeatedly conflict while editing the same test-line ceiling, including https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186977.

## User Impact

Maintainers can review separate test-budget records that merge independently. The aggregate test-line limit, inherited-debt checks, and review requirement remain in force. This changes repository validation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the fixed scalar and add tracked integer records under `config/test-lines-allocations/`. When the parsed allocation map changes, positive effective-ceiling growth cannot exceed positive actual test-line growth against the same selected base. This includes scalar movement, so an older branch cannot reuse credit that pruning already folded into the scalar.

The checker now measures changed sources in the same literal-LF units as the total. Git numstat reports zero net lines for an unterminated line gaining its final newline; the previous check could therefore admit real growth through the inherited non-growing exception.

Pruning folds the measured total into the scalar and removes tracked allocation records, including at zero slack. Index/reference snapshots remain exact; untracked files are ignored and preserved. Scalar-only reconciliation remains separately review-owned.

The change reuses the existing scalar parser, Git snapshot loader, checker, and CI routing. It adds 94 tooling lines and 170 net test lines; its own allocation is exactly 170. The extra tooling owns record loading and exact changed-source LF accounting. No package/runtime surface or dependency changes.

## Evidence

- Original dependency-free checker: two real branches with independent grants failed after merging; a newline-only increase incorrectly passed with numstat delta zero.
- Patched native checker: eight real-Git fixture groups passed, covering both merge orders, overlap/double credit, unallocated growth, literal LF and inherited debt, staged/worktree snapshots, deleted/untracked records, prune plus old-branch grants against both bases, and malformed/overflow inputs. Disposable fixtures were removed.
- Exact source review at frozen base `64cb11485db8b0c30bab2e359124dcf99bd5fb0a`: independent reviewer found no actionable issue. Local autoreview completed one P0–P3 pass with scoped-clean status and no findings on staged snapshot `dfca9f91eaae88dce40513c781e2b56a7fed5ead7ef6029bfa9762ce9b2f63be`.
- Targeted native formatting, `git diff --check`, and docs inventory passed.
- Current-head [CI run 40804056614](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40804056614) tested `e4f13c0ea6f30915777ab206034c45db618284bd` through merge `de335931853c8dee7167da9d36ae4181b8d0dc09`, with ordered baseline `44ffd0a845b32480ffaf46ff6cfbcaa2267491c1` and PR-head parents. All **99 relevant cases passed**: [10 checker and 64 changed-scope cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40804056614/job/123219184869), plus [25 check-family cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40804056614/job/123219184805). Corrected [changed-file/script lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40804056614/job/123219675188), type, docs, format, guards and all remaining selected proof jobs passed. The seven brace corrections were independently reviewed as behavior-equivalent; their two added test lines are included in the 170-line grant.
- The current [ratchet job passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40804056614/job/123219184781): **6,246,092 total; 6,320,170 effective ceiling; 74,078 slack**. Upstream https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187162 reconciled the scalar before this tested merge. This PR leaves the scalar unchanged and adds only its measured 170-line allocation. The earlier debt failure is historical, not the current gate result; no additional scalar reconciliation is pending here.
- Overall CI remains **failed: 30 successful jobs, 28 skipped, one root failure and its aggregate**. The sole root is [core-lint job 123219675109](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40804056614/job/123219675109): existing `eslint(curly)` at `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts:722`, alongside existing session-manager max-lines warnings. The failing source, warning subjects, lint configuration, runner and dependency inputs have identical Git objects in the actual baseline and tested merge. The informational classifier labels it new because the scheduled main job passed without comparing selected scope; this attribution uses the inspected source objects instead. The native inherited-failure route retains the real red result and all review/security requirements.
- The native focused Testbox request queued and was stopped before tests. Its provider reports completed while native reconciliation retains custody because no Actions association is available. No Testbox test pass is claimed; hosted CI supplies registered proof.
- [Exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187164#issuecomment-6486165504) completed on e4f13c0e with zero findings, Before merge: None, and no Rank-up moves. Maintainer source review and independent inspection of the raw CI logs are complete.

Closes #158816

## What Problem This Solves

Malformed installed SKILL.md files disappear from inventories without explaining why. Operators need the rejected path and loading error, including when querying a running Gateway.

## User Impact

`skills list`, `info` and `check` report rejected files and discovery failures in text and JSON. Valid siblings remain available, rejected files do not inflate loaded counts, and warnings update or clear with the published inventory. Output is bounded to 64 diagnostics plus an omitted count, with bounded paths/messages and safe terminal rendering. No configuration, persisted-data migration, dependency or permission change is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rejection facts follow the canonical loader, shared per-pass root reads, source preparation, worker snapshots, skills.status and CLI formatters. Diagnostics participate in the existing fingerprint, so changing or removing an invalid file publishes a revision even if valid skills are unchanged. Main's native observations and safety reconciliation remain the refresh owner.

Current head `11073d11e15a0c264384ab85fa1d5b5a9464a36b` integrates official main `054c4ba7f663e78b95972d8e557fd1c102a5aa69` to repair a confirmed conflict in skills CLI output. Independent review also caught discovery-stage rejections bypassing the collector. The same bounded collector now retains those facts and forwards the existing owner callback, preserving logging, root precedence, link/hardlink admission, discovery limits and retired interfaces.

## Evidence

It requires exact rejection facts on synchronous and worker inventories, exposes both reasons on all three text/JSON CLI surfaces, keeps the outside skill unloaded and clears warnings after repair/removal. Existing worker cases retain native warning publication and generated-plugin child facts across cached reuse and passive refresh. No new sleeps, timeouts or production test seams are added.

prs.title: fix(doctor): preserve legacy upgrade state and diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177381

## What Problem This Solves

Published legacy upgrades can fail backup discovery before Doctor can retire valid heartbeat configuration, or retain legacy session stores after importing native assignments whose optional lifecycle revisions are absent. Doctor can also report pending state migrations when the current database contents are valid but the raw schema header is deliberately deferred for an unfenced older updater.

## User Impact

The existing upgrade flow can preserve original backup bytes, native assignment ownership, and accurate database health reporting. Malformed configuration, uncertain identity, stale assignments, and invalid database ownership or catalogs retain their refusal behavior.

Release-note context: repair legacy upgrade backup discovery, native assignment certification, and deferred-header database diagnostics. No configuration surface, schema version, execution permission, port admission, or publication fence changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Backup discovery uses the existing validated, read-only heartbeat projection after legacy normalization. Only the backup resolver selects it; writable automatic repair cannot retire heartbeat before durable migration. Original configuration bytes and environment-reference provenance remain intact.
- Native assignment repair accepts equal optional lifecycle revisions only after binding-key, physical-session, and connection-fingerprint checks. One-sided absence remains unknown; populated mismatches remain stale. Released 2026.9.4 emitted optional host lifecycle revisions.
- State diagnostics now read the canonical effective content version and perform full read-only maintenance admission on their existing private snapshot. The strict port descriptor remains unchanged. Decode failures retain the raw header; owner refusal after successful decoding retains the effective version. This follows the deferred-header contract introduced in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/141109.
- The original fixture changes request the operator's existing allowlist policy before baseline capture and the native-proof agent's existing full policy after creation. Host restrictions, approval equality, archive verification, and the strict Doctor oracle remain unchanged.
- The schema-guard fixture uses ordered full Buffer reads, an exact file-count check, and native byte equality. It retains the 8 MiB specimen and every lifecycle assertion while avoiding Vitest's allocation of entries for both large Buffers.

## Source Review

Candidate `55de928c20e021a97e98c00b2109f769de301ea6`, based on `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`: nine paths, net **+26 production lines**, **+169 test lines**, and **+7 fixture setup lines**. The production additions separate backup-only validation from writable migration, restore the shipped optional-revision identity contract, and use the canonical state-health owner.

Independent owner reviews passed for each correction. Formatting, diff checks, signed-commit hooks, and the fresh full-PR two-pass autoreview passed. Review is source evidence, not runtime proof. Any sandbox limitation inspecting the sibling Codex checkout remains separate from the direct inspections below.

The new real-SQLite diagnostics regression covers raw/header metadata 15 with current content 35, unchanged original bytes, continued strict-port refusal, current header without a redundant marker, and malformed/missing/newer marker plus metadata/owner/catalog refusals. Its complete **17-case file passed on the current PR merge**, including the deferred-header regression and refusal siblings. The new unit regression against old production remains **UNRUN**. Separately, the retained 6ba failure and corrected 55de package success now establish actual-CLI, same-fixture before/after coverage of the diagnostic boundary; the limits are recorded below.

## Observed Validation

prs.title: fix(gateway): mark failed restart-safe browser chats unread
prs.body:
Closes #160003

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes failed browser chat turns staying read when workspace preparation fails after restart-safe admission, before the agent takes over.

## User Impact

Users see unread activity for a browser turn that fails after they mark the admitted message as read. Internal CLI Goal work and progress refreshes stay quiet. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The restart-safe terminal writer omitted the visibility fact required to advance session activity. Carry that fact through the existing chat work admission to the terminal event. Keep the unread predicate and durable claim rules unchanged.

Retry preparation retains its original conditional await from #164682 (`00daeebaf390ac9144c567ca399dd8a3707dc1ee`). Fresh sends reserve synchronously when preparation needs no worker read. The correction removes the unrelated unconditional await introduced in the first revision.

Thanks @wangmiao0668000666 for the original investigation and withdrawn repair in #159285. This repair keeps visibility with the current terminal admission owner.

## Evidence

- Windows, Node 24.22.1, 2026-10-28. The SQLite regression fails on unchanged main `19327c5541386286543348cb27eab7a6cb2b9274`: visible settlement leaves `lastActivityAt` undefined. The hidden control passes.
- Separate running source Gateways accept real `chat.send` requests from signed browser and CLI clients. A task-local Git URL rewrite holds an actual clone request at a localhost HTTP endpoint. After acknowledgment, `sessions.patch {unread:false}` establishes the read baseline. Releasing HTTP 404 causes the real workspace preparation failure. Public `sessions.list` reports the outcomes below.

| Source | Browser terminal activity | Browser unread after failure | Hidden CLI Goal unread |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unchanged main | Not advanced | false | false |
| Fix | Advanced after the read baseline | true | false |

- The retained Gateway runs cover the initial conditional-await snapshot and commit `5b20a6a8daa0e5165cf698c7a102d358ca995541`. The correction reuses that proof: the visibility writer, work admission, lifecycle projector, and unread helper match the initial snapshot exactly. Final admission differs only by removing a local Goal alias. This is source-reconciled proof reuse, not a final-head Gateway rerun.
- The exact pending-Stop case failed on `5b20a6a8` in CI and local replay. With conditional awaiting restored, the same case passes locally: 1 passed, 34 filtered out; 68.57 s Vitest, 77.43 s wrapper.
- The corrected snapshot passes all **158 tests across 6 files**, including the full session mutation/Stop suite, worker settlement, admission, dispatch errors, and lifecycle projection. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods.session-narrow-mutations.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-restart-recovery.worker.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-work-admission.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-dispatch-errors.test.ts src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-pre-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Vitest duration: 217.18 s; wrapper wall time: 229.96 s. Targeted Gateway-method TypeScript compilation, type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and the test-line ratchet pass. New-head CI remains separate evidence.
- The final diff adds 8 and removes 3 production lines. Tests add 67 and remove 77 lines, a net reduction of 10. All 12 dispatch-error scenarios remain covered. No baseline was raised. Visibility stays with existing terminal custody; no new request type or state owner is introduced.
- Fresh independent Codex review covers the complete six-file corrected snapshot against `19327c5541386286543348cb27eab7a6cb2b9274`, through P2: no actionable findings. The initial review missed the scheduling regression; hosted ClawSweeper identified it. The correction also removes the mock forwarding assertion requested by that review. The separate local autoreview/ClawSweeper CLI was not run.

CI on the first revision ([run 40620822884](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40620822884)) passed types, lint, budgets, and most test jobs. The pending-Stop regression prompted the correction above. Two embedded-agent retry assertions also failed:

- The persistent Codex `server_error` assertion (expected 9 calls, received 5) also fails on scheduled main ([job 122575644875](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40615065526/job/122575644875)). A local replay reproduces it: 155 passed, 1 failed.
- The retry-budget assertion (progress false, budget 8; expected 2 calls, received 3) passes in that main job and in the local replay. The same assertion also fails on scheduled main `dafda2f722f19dfc1a56216e8be5af4ff9fe46a3` ([job 122596018302](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40621333872/job/122596018302), same test and support-file line 332), confirming it is pre-existing. A passing local replay alone was not used for that classification.

One earlier candidate run passed all 95 assertions but failed teardown in two files with Windows `EPERM` resolving `C:\$Extend\$Deleted`. The unchanged-base replay passed all 94 tests. This repair does not claim to fix that intermittent cleanup failure.

The Gateway proof uses isolated synthetic sessions, real device pairing, real Git, and the normal session projection. It does not claim browser rendering, successful provider inference, or graceful process shutdown. Task-owned Gateway trees were stopped and joined.

Current-head follow-up (2026-10-28): [CI run 40624240313](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40624240313) completed with only the two embedded-agent retry assertions above failing ([job 122605692136](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40624240313/job/122605692136)); both have matching main evidence. The pending-Stop failure is absent. Hosted ClawSweeper reviewed `f68aca61056b89318731e89d023896cf022798f7` with no actionable findings and marked it ready for maintainer review. This is not an all-green CI claim.

prs.body:
Related: #186338

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two scheduled CI assertions that fail when an automation resumes inside an existing conversation.

## User Impact

No production or permission behavior changes. This repairs the scheduled tool-policy checks without weakening call-time restrictions.

## Why This Change Was Made

#186338 intentionally retained the conversation's full automation catalog for stable continuation prompts, but this integration test still expected every placement to hide management actions. The existing four-placement/two-runtime table now checks visibility by placement and attempts each management action on the current job, requiring the scope-denial error before any Gateway dispatch. Child/detached catalog restrictions, sibling denial, self-filtered listing, tool caps, yield behavior, CLI self-removal, and run-retirement checks remain intact.

Requested by @vincentkoc; commit co-authored by Vincent Koc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/4c131d11-6724-4dd4-8e28-778fe151eff9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/3d36399a-f7d7-4549-89f3-090dfeb33283)

## Evidence

- Independently confirmed [scheduled CI run 40621333872, job 122596018095](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40621333872/job/122596018095), revision `dafda2f722f19dfc1a56216e8be5af4ff9fe46a3`: two `add`-catalog assertion failures at line 280. Failed/current test and factory sources were byte-identical.

- This is an explicitly requested known-red-main repair. Direct main push was attempted through the verified managed identity and rejected with **GH013: Changes must be made through a pull request**; this PR is the required fallback.

prs.title: fix(ci): avoid redundant Git probes in publisher fixtures
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/133228

## What Problem This Solves

Publisher test fixtures repeatedly spawn Git to read immutable seed data and to run an auth probe whose result the caller explicitly discards.

## User Impact

CI/test-only cost reduction. No shipped behavior, configuration, migrations, or operator action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the initial commit with the existing immutable template, then carry it into each independent copy. Honor the established `inspect(..., false)` opt-out before spawning Git: the Git-owner caller already records auth state separately. Default and explicit auth checks retain the same strict status/output check. No assertions or fault scenarios are removed. The standalone scenario now uses the canonical temp-directory tracker with immediate per-case cleanup. Production delta: 0; test-helper delta: +21/-21 (net 0).

## Evidence

- Same 21 publisher cases pass on Node 26 before and after. A transparent subprocess counter in the existing worker pool measures **41 fewer Git invocations**:

  | Probe | Base | Candidate |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | Discarded auth probe | 21 | 0 |
  | HEAD queries, including existing-PR heads | 27 | 7 |
  | Independent owner auth checks | 21 | 21 |
  | Fixture inspections | 21 | 21 |

- Actual pinned Bun: all 24 publisher/setup cases pass. Standalone publication scenarios and Node setup-failure rows pass. Temporary real-Git controls verify contaminated headers still fail default/explicit inspection and warm copies isolate refs, hooks, config, and initial HEAD, including a custom workspace.
- Qualified oxfmt, focused syntax/root-rule oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass. Exact-head PR CI is now successful: [run 40804952921](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40804952921). Linux CI passed all 108 Git-owner tests and all 178 workflow-guard tests.
- Refreshed local autoreview (Codex, P0–P3) covers base `c1101ee6e0c3f5896266b9fc25de2110edbfe402` and helper blob `d7b1cea1695d3accedd128a668cb290d1e410568`. Its index-only finding was that the old committed index lacked the working-copy cleanup; the final commit includes that reviewed cleanup. Independent source review found no actionable source issue.

**Local proof limitation:** locale-finalizer scenarios hit 30-second Bash 5.3.12 source-resolution timeouts before publication. The first failing case reproduces with the original helper; an isolated 32 KiB here-string probe also hangs under that shell. [GNU patch 16](https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/bash/bash-5.3-patches/bash53-016) addresses the Darwin pipe-sizing defect. An isolated GNU Bash 5.3.16 build clears that original source-resolution hang, but then the first locale scenario times out later during publication (`control-ui-locale-finalizer.test-support.ts:478`). That later 30-second timeout reproduces with both the final helper (exit 1, 77.465s) and original helper (exit 1, 69.863s). The full locale suite is intentionally excluded from PR CI by `scripts/lib/ci-proof-test-inventory.mts`, so it remains an explicit baseline proof gap and named follow-up: diagnose the macOS locale publication timeout. The installed shell was not changed. No timeout, assertion, or shell-contract workaround is included.

The baseline instrumented run was 73.405s; the initial candidate was 63.163s and the final revised candidate was 58.919s. These single noisy samples are diagnostic, not a CI-minute, CPU/RSS, or billing-savings claim.


CI first caught six added helper lines against the existing test-line ceiling. The final revision removes that growth through canonical cleanup and redundant-binding removal; no ceiling or assertion was weakened. The original CI run also reported an unrelated `eslint(curly)` error in `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts:722`, already present in the base; the revised exact-head CI run passes, including lint and test-line ratchets.

The [exact-head ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187165#issuecomment-6485884788) reports no findings and no before-merge work for `d78703c5fafdfea043ef532c0f15f59755d1cc7b`.

prs.title: fix(test): retain selected Bun through isolation
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A launcher selects the pinned absolute Bun executable before isolating test HOME/cache. `pinnedBunEnv` carries only PATH, so a nested formatter resolves a new empty cache and stages the same runtime again. This was observed while qualifying https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186469: its existing dirty-to-formatted fixture entered the Bun stager and downloaded a second executable archive.

## Canonical fix

Carry the already-selected absolute executable in the existing `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH` provision. Keep relative CI `bun` PATH-only. The resolver, checksum/revision admission, explicit-override behavior, isolated HOME/cache and formatter policy remain owned by their existing modules. `test-live` already binds the selected local executable before changing child CI defaults; this applies the same ownership invariant to all callers of the shared provision.

Production +11/-6 (net +5), justified by preserving runtime identity across the child-environment ownership boundary; tests +25/-1 (net +24). Reuse existing cache-resolution cases and the two-route launcher proof; no extra child or test matrix. The cache case resolves under a different HOME/cache with only the provision and requires the original executable, no second stage and no isolated cache creation. The launcher child also retains its cache/exit/argument assertions. It already inherits an explicit path, so it is supporting integration proof rather than the discriminating regression.

## Prospective qualification rule — recorded before benchmark execution

- Real flow: reuse the committed `changed-lanes.test.ts` dirty-file to formatted-file check and its actual changed-plan → package script → `run-format` → formatter chain. Two formatter invocations per body; identical diagnostics, file selection and source bytes; dirty exits 1, formatted exits 0.
- Counts first: after local selection of a verified absolute Bun and before HOME/cache isolation, carry only the shared provision. Candidate must use that selected executable and perform zero additional staging/downloads against an empty isolated Bun cache. The existing injectable resolver fixture establishes the baseline extra-stage red case without a network download. Mock staging counts are resolver evidence, not formatter timing.
- Comparable timing: preseed both isolated caches from identical already-verified Bun bytes/stamps outside measurement. Warmup separately; five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs on the same host. Cold empty-cache behavior is reported separately, not timed as a failed baseline versus successful candidate.
- Record host load, wall/user/system CPU/peak RSS, median/p95/spread and exact output parity. Every measured metric must hold or improve; a 20% adverse move is an immediate stop, and smaller regressions require explicit acceptance. Otherwise retain the draft.
- Use only committed workloads, existing focused runner and existing dependency ownership. No new cache, fixture framework, benchmark service or paid box allocation.

## Observed qualification

At exact head `a94d7d5b31adddda7f496a708cb82b636e58235a`, the native physical checkout passed the frozen install and 114 tests across pinned-Bun, launcher, and dev-tool suites. The tooling-test typecheck, production and changed-test lint, targeted formatting, and the committed real dirty-to-formatted case also passed. That last run executed one selected test; 67 other tests were intentionally skipped.

A separate before/after resolver probe used the complete production owner with the existing injectable synthetic stager. Baseline selected a different executable and staged again after HOME/cache isolation; candidate retained the selected executable, performed zero additional stages, created no isolated cache, and left the parent environment unchanged. These are resolver work-count results, not network-download or formatter timing measurements.

Independent review of all five callers and local autoreview found no actionable code issue. The latest exact-head ClawSweeper review requested the formal qualification above and real-flow/performance evidence; performance evidence remains open.

The draft is retained because the promised alternating A/B performance comparison has not run. The unchanged committed case creates an unpredictable worker HOME and resets XDG_CACHE_HOME inside test setup. There is no existing independent Bun-cache selector or preseed seam, so outer-cache preparation cannot satisfy the prospective requirement to preseed both actual isolated caches outside timing. An independently owned baseline checkout can solve dependency availability, but cannot solve that cache-preparation constraint. No setup hook, runtime override after isolation, or fixture change will be introduced to manufacture a passing comparison.

No benchmark has run for this candidate. No ordinary Actions billing reduction is claimed: the relative workflow-provisioned `bun` path stays unchanged. Release-owned changelog; this is development/test runtime ownership.

prs.title: fix(plugins): stop plugin updates from starving behind a renewing lifecycle lease
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin updates and forced installs losing admission repeatedly to shorter plugin lifecycle operations, with wait messages identifying only an opaque lease token.

Fixes #167050. Thanks @itanyplus for the incident timeline and follow-up.

## User Impact

An already waiting command gets admission before later acquisitions once the active operation releases or expires. Wait messages include the recorded purpose, PID, and host. Active installers retain exclusion through npm work and settlement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The state lease store now records expiring FIFO intents in the existing lease table. Admission and grant remain in the existing transaction; polling refreshes intent expiry without changing arrival order. Cancellation cleans up the exact owner's intent, and crashed or stalled waiters expire after 30 seconds. Diagnostic holder metadata is separate from process-bound reclaim authority, so recording an installer PID cannot permit takeover while its npm children survive.

There is no SQLite schema, dependency, CLI option, or config change. Current main's retained-artifact cleanup checks for candidates before acquiring and repeats hourly; its 30-second startup/retry delay is not an unconditional reacquisition loop. The 30-second heartbeat keeps its owner token. The reporter's actual rotating process remains unidentified. The npm install owner already repairs and verifies the `openclaw` peer link before and after npm, so that path is preserved and checked by the live fixture.

The consumer run also exposed a pre-existing worktree capacity race under a controlled schedule: completed checkouts retained old pending-byte debt when a postcheck refused, so concurrent creates could reject each other. The bounded owner correction settles only decreases of its own existing debt on refusal. Peer debt, safety reserves, refused increases, and live commit authority are preserved.

## Evidence

- Base CLI reproduction: isolated state, no Gateway running, periodic fixture acquisition every 50 ms. `pnpm dev plugins update --all` logged rotating holders/advancing expiry and finished only after competition stopped: 250 rotations, zero yields.
- Regression is red on the base: the waiting update exhausts its acquisition budget behind `periodic-5`; the recorded holder description is absent from warnings. Native and worker success/cancellation, FIFO ordering, abandoned-intent expiry, active renewal, and diagnostic/reclaim separation are covered.
- Focused owner suite: 25 passing tests, 21.06 s reported duration; the new contention cases take about 0.4 s each. Three consumer suites caught an owner-construction ordering assumption; the constructor was factored without changing their authority assertions, then all 27 tests passed.
- Live CLI/npm proof: a loopback registry served a synthetic plugin at 1.0.0 and 1.0.1. `pnpm dev plugins install npm:openclaw-lease-fixture@1.0.0 --force --accept-capabilities --acknowledge-install-policy-warning`, then `pnpm dev plugins update openclaw-lease-fixture@latest --accept-capabilities --acknowledge-install-policy-warning` while a separate process repeatedly acquired the lifecycle lease. Isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and profile were used. Result: `{"code":0,"observedWait":true,"completedWhileCompeting":true,"rotations":294,"yielded":134,"elapsedMs":15193}`. The selected install record points to version 1.0.1, and its `node_modules/openclaw` is a symlink. The warning names the fixture purpose/PID/host.
- Selected all 86 consumer test files found through the changed lease owner. Across completed groups and focused repairs, 1,086 tests passed, six cases were skipped in PostgreSQL-tagged suites, and three destination-authority E2E cases were blocked during setup by the host volume's existing group-writable ancestor. No permissions were changed and no guard was bypassed. The two product failures found by the broad run (heartbeat retention and capacity debt settlement) were repaired; final affected replay: six files, 81 passing tests.
- Capacity proof: controlled concurrent hydration reproduces both disk-space refusals on the unchanged base. The new owner regression is red on the original capacity worker and green with the fix, including refusal of a debt increase; the same controlled service case now passes in 1.319 s. Completed-worker retention is green in 1.186 s. No timeout, retry, assertion, or baseline was weakened.
- Final checks: core typecheck, state-test typecheck, focused capacity-test typecheck, lint on touched source/tests, oxfmt, madge (zero cycles), and `git diff --check` pass.
- Slow-suite observation: the unchanged archive/worktree lifecycle file spent about 200.2 s across 20 cases. Its fixture constructs isolated Git/SQLite state and performs real archive/restore work; no base performance comparison is claimed. E2E build preparation took 3m27.8s, including 2m45.9s compilation. PR CI remains broad proof.
- Isolated Codex autoreview at P0/P1 against `dafda2f722f19dfc1a56216e8be5af4ff9fe46a3`, including unchanged cleanup/storage/worker-owner context: no actionable findings. The final complete diff, including retention and capacity repairs, passed the same isolated review with no actionable P0/P1 findings.

Production delta: +156 lines (+228/-72); tests: +177 lines (+178/-1); docs: +7 lines. Existing tests were preserved; the added cases cover distinct admission, cancellation, expiry, and diagnostic safety contracts. The full SQLite inventory check is omitted under the local gate budget; PR CI supplies broad checks.

prs.title: fix(browser): omit unparsable gateway hint from extension pairing
prs.body:
Closes #186454

## What Problem This Solves

A browser node whose relay is local but whose Gateway is remote receives a pairing string the shipped Chrome extension always rejects, so setup ends at "Manual setup required (malformed_response)".
- Problem: for `gateway.mode: "remote"` over plaintext `ws://`, the pairing builder copied the remote Gateway URL into the optional `gateway` hint even though the extension accepts only `wss://` or loopback `ws://` hints. `parseGatewayHint` returned null, so `validatePairingFields` rejected a pairing whose relay URL and token were valid.
- Solution: publish the optional hint only when the extension can parse it. The relay URL, token, and relay validation are unchanged.
- What changed: one shared URL predicate in `extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-pairing.ts` now drives both relay-URL validation and hint emission; a regression test covers the plaintext remote case in `extension-pairing.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: the extension's URL policy, relay transport validation, `wss://` hint behavior, and `--gateway-url` validation errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The producer emitted optional metadata its only consumer is guaranteed to reject; fixing the producer keeps the plaintext-connection restriction intact.
- Best fix: omit unusable optional hints at the producer instead of relaxing the extension's URL policy (a plaintext non-loopback Gateway is still refused).
- Alternative: make the extension tolerate the hint — rejected because the hint carries no authority and widening that check increases risk for every pairing.
- Risk / non-goals: only the unusable-hint case changes; local loopback hints and `wss://` remote hints keep their current bytes.

## User Impact

`openclaw browser extension pair` and the native macOS bootstrap now hand the installed extension a pairing it accepts when the browser node uses a local relay in front of a plaintext remote Gateway, instead of requiring manual setup.

## Evidence

End-to-end on this branch: the shipped CLI produced the pairing string, the installed unpacked extension (Google Chrome 138, MV3 service worker) accepted it, and the extension authenticated to the real loopback relay daemon.

```text
$ openclaw browser extension pair --json          # this branch
{"pairingString":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension#<token>","relayPort":19199,"remote":false}

Chrome 138 + unpacked extension, relay daemon on 127.0.0.1:19199:
[1] pre-fix CLI pairing (…?gateway=ws%3A%2F%2F192.168.1.20%3A8080…)
    extension parse : null
    pair message    : {"ok":false,"error":"Invalid pairing string."}
[2] fixed CLI pairing (…/extension#<token>)
    extension parse : {"relayUrl":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension","token":"<token>"}
    pair message    : {"ok":true}
    relay daemon    : [browser/extension-relay] extension authenticated and connected to relay
    status          : {"paired":true,"state":"on","relayUrl":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension"}
```

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| browser-node + plaintext `ws://192.168.1.20:8080` | hint emitted, parser returns null, extension rejects | hint omitted, extension pairs and connects |
| browser-node + `wss://gateway.example.com:9444` | parser accepts | parser accepts (unchanged) |
| direct-remote `wss://…:9443` | parser accepts | parser accepts (unchanged) |

The new regression test is red on `origin/main` and green with the fix; the relay integration test still passes:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-pairing.test.ts --run
 ✓ omits a plaintext non-loopback gateway hint that the extension cannot parse
 Test Files  1 passed (1) · Tests  5 passed (5)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay/gateway-relay-route.integration.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1) · Tests  9 passed (9)
```

What was not tested: native-host registration and the macOS app bootstrap were not exercised (no macOS host); the CLI entry point, the installed extension, and the standalone relay daemon covered that path instead.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source reading plus `node --import tsx` and a headless Google Chrome run to trace the pairing builder into the shipped extension and the live relay. The implementer understands the code: the extension rejects any pairing whose `gateway` hint fails its own `isAllowedWebSocketUrl` check, so the producer must not emit a hint that check rejects. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.
