prs.title: improve(ios): skip unused qualification compilation work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The iOS qualification Debug build uses a generic simulator destination. Limit it to the admitted Apple Silicon host architecture and disable compiler index-store generation, which qualification does not consume. Keep the existing native build receipt identity, stock simulator, live pairing/chat/relaunch, independent transcript reader, resource readiness gate, and deadlines.

## User Impact

This changes qualification compilation only. The declared hosted improvement and final-head functional qualification both passed. The prior stacked CI had one inherited mock-exports failure, detailed below. After the fixture prerequisite landed, main-targeted CI exposed a test-line budget interaction. That main-owned ceiling repair is now incorporated; the patch-identical rebased head `02d2d0eb6417c5acad2d30d59dc5e4babd2a9269` is awaiting fresh CI, as detailed below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Qualification runs on an admitted Apple Silicon host and does not consume compiler indexing. The two settings remove that unused work without changing runtime assertions.

## Acceptance rule (before hosted measurements)

Use the canonical `scripts/ios-release-e2e.ts --mode stock --build-only` entry point on `xcode-27-xlarge`. Compare five baseline and five candidate builds serially in baseline/candidate order, each with a new product/build directory, separate pinned baseline/candidate source checkouts, and the same toolchain. Shared OS/package/compiler inputs remain warm and are explicitly reported; these are cold-product builds rather than fresh-VM cold builds. Report native build wall-clock median, p95, range, compiler work counts when present, and host load/resource observations. Do not sum overlapping compiler task durations into wall-clock savings.

Accept at least 5% lower median native build time with no 20% or greater p95 regression. Preserve exact-source admission and native build receipts. Then require one fresh full stock qualification of the candidate, including actual pairing/chat/relaunch and independent transcript-reader UI proof. Revert the settings if no measurable gain is established. No store or TestFlight upload occurs.

## Evidence

- Existing qualification/native-build tests: 115 passed.
- Negative control fails the existing real command boundary for the two missing build settings.
- Both affected test typecheck leaves passed.
- Source/test type-aware lint, formatting, docs MDX, and diff checks passed.
- AutoReview (Codex, P0/P1), local change snapshot against `0b538f7d5a4d9e3328f572cc07fe23402f733f36`: scoped-clean, no findings.
- The paired native build measurements and fresh qualification of the final stacked head passed (results below).

Committed non-publishing [native comparison workload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/02ba247211a34f9f930b5eb3c61cd2988f9720c4/.github/workflows/ios-release-e2e.yml). An initial fixture run hit Node’s default Git tree output buffer before measuring any build; the bounded full-tree reader was reproduced and repaired before starting the ten build samples.

The first full stock qualification ([40797073813](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40797073813), exact candidate head) built successfully and passed live pairing/chat/relaunch, including all three provider request stages. The independent reader then failed at `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.swift:990` waiting for the `Worked` disclosure. Its unchanged long-chat fixture contains only text messages; the completed-work presentation change in #181339 intentionally stopped folding narration into work. This was an inherited fixture mismatch, repaired separately in #187147. The run is failed and does not satisfy the complete-qualification acceptance requirement.

## Fixture prerequisite and final functional proof

Fixture prerequisite #187147 is squash-merged into main at `5af53307f8faec719626d689974db38d7f48cb71`. This PR now targets main. Full stock qualification was performed at head `315cd51921ac709e8451c75f5a22f9ba010457f6`; the current patch-identical rebased head is `02d2d0eb6417c5acad2d30d59dc5e4babd2a9269`. The compiler diff remains byte-identical to the original measured diff. The current diff contains only the compiler settings, existing test expectations, and documentation; the prerequisite fixture files are already on main. The prerequisite passed full stock qualification 40799101203 with the existing compiler profile.

The original benchmark remains pinned to baseline `0b538f7d5a4d9e3328f572cc07fe23402f733f36` and candidate `74b38ca11b3d44281fde99b782d880edc557af07`, retained at `test/ios-build-profile-measured-74b38ca`. Those measurements isolate the compiler change before the fixture repair; they are not exact-head timings for the new combined source. Fresh [stock qualification 40801319752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40801319752) passed on final head `315cd51921ac709e8451c75f5a22f9ba010457f6`. Its proof records matching target/harness/workflow SHAs, `complete=true`, both UI tests passed, all three provider stages received, and cleanup confirmed. The fresh native build took 217.310s with no receipt reuse; the job completed in 12m5s. Simulator readiness still waited 137.164s for idle headroom, so the compiler improvement does not claim to eliminate startup pressure. Fresh AutoReview (Codex, P0/P1), with the native/receipt/CLI and fixture source supplied, is scoped-clean on this stacked head.

## Hosted native build measurements

[Comparison 40797065770](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40797065770) passed all ten native-build samples and the predeclared timing rule. Each sample used a new product directory with receipt reuse disabled, on one five-CPU/14-GiB Apple Silicon xlarge host, Node 24.22.1, Xcode 27.1 (27A9275), and the iOS 27.0 runtime. The workload uses the canonical `scripts/ios-release-e2e.ts --mode stock --build-only --build-dir ...` entry point.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Native build median | 289.398s | 156.839s |
| Native build p95 | 486.488s | 232.723s |
| Native build range | 278.416–486.488s | 153.541–232.723s |
| Harness median | 296.061s | 162.659s |
| Harness p95 | 499.621s | 242.323s |
| SwiftCompile tasks per sample | 186 | 93 |
| SwiftEmitModule / C compile / linker tasks | 38 / 70 / 60 | 19 / 35 / 30 |
| Compiler index files per sample | 8,018–8,031 | 0 |
| Compiler index bytes per sample | 94,298,408–96,560,352 | 0 |

Native build median improved 45.8%; p95 improved 52.2%. With five samples per arm, nearest-rank p95 is the observed maximum. No overlapping task durations are added together.

| Serial pair | Baseline native build | Candidate native build |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 486.488s | 232.723s |
| 2 | 289.398s | 156.839s |
| 3 | 284.869s | 156.535s |
| 4 | 278.416s | 153.541s |
| 5 | 296.470s | 180.163s |

These are cold-product builds, with shared download/toolchain/OS caches and checkout-local generated inputs warming across pairs. Pair one is slower for both arms and remains included; these measurements do not establish fresh-VM savings or attribute the whole improvement to either individual setting. The host-only build halves compiler and linker task counts, and compiler index generation also disappears. Original exact source SHAs and the fixture-only final-head delta are recorded above.

Resource observations: pressure flags stayed at 1 and no swap deltas were observed. Peak sampled compressed resident memory was approximately 1,328 MiB baseline / 909 MiB candidate. The first baseline's peak load was 48.61 versus 7.40–9.50 for later baselines and 7.58–8.65 for candidates, so first-pair/max comparisons carry that caveat. The 15-second host/60-second process samples can miss short peaks. Diagnostics had no unavailable probes or output truncation; maximum collection duration was 166 ms, probe command wall time about 0.23% of harness time in either arm, and collector Node CPU about 0.04–0.05% (excluding observation subprocess CPU). This does not establish that release-lane resource starvation is eliminated.

## Prior stacked PR CI

[CI 40801418521](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40801418521), exact head `315cd51921ac709e8451c75f5a22f9ba010457f6`, completed with only `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and its aggregate gate failing. Every other selected job passed. The failed subcheck reports 14 closed mock factories in `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts`.

This is inherited: tested merge `94d65522d86c521a943d4ab7fcdf7f388f27f093` has fixture base `f669d6ed3812e04da7b1ab8c2039fda45c4566a0` and this PR head as parents; its only changes from that base are this PR's three files. The failing test sources, mock guard/scanner/parser/resolver, baseline ledger, package/lock, tsconfig and CI owner match the later main input `cb5a4388f310d8b7c5d461e4f875561215260c1d`. Main commit `a968dc19900d` (#187090) changed these factories without changing their exact-fingerprint baseline. The guard compares the current factory inventory to that ledger, so an unchanged file against the prepared base still fails. No branch-related CI failures remain; the inherited failure is recorded, not retried or reported green.

## Main-targeted CI and headroom repair

[CI 40804022730](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40804022730) tested merge `42211d905c63ecdd030e3bfe0f42a56420a5ccd4` (main `5af53307f8faec719626d689974db38d7f48cb71`, PR head `315cd51921ac709e8451c75f5a22f9ba010457f6`). It had two failed root jobs: the unchanged inherited `sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts:722` curly-brace lint error, and test-lines. The latter reported 6,245,924 lines against a 6,243,924 ceiling, with this PR adding two expectation lines. This interaction is branch-related and was not admitted as an inherited-only exception.

Main #187162 (`44ffd0a845b32480ffaf46ff6cfbcaa2267491c1`) already repaired the finite ceiling. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Matrix CLI action errors bypassing the [documented JSON failure envelope](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli#json-failures), making ordinary configuration and safety refusals difficult to handle with a shared CLI parser.

## User Impact

`matrix ... --json` action exceptions now exit nonzero with `ok:false`, `error.type`, and `error.message`. Scripts reading the old string `error` or private `success:false` exception payload should use the standard envelope. Successful domain results, including their domain-specific status fields, retain their existing shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

Let the existing host plugin-action wrapper and root renderer handle JSON exceptions. Remove the private exception-rendering callback and all five callers rather than adding a Matrix-specific formatter or SDK export. Human diagnostics, crypto/state ownership, account admission, and returned domain results keep their current handling. No configuration, Matrix request, protocol, or storage change.

## Evidence

- Scenario: Matrix CLI action exceptions use the common JSON error envelope; Human diagnostics and returned domain results retain their existing handling

- Same command on base `1e93aee` and head `460512c`: `node dist/entry.js matrix devices list --json`
  - Before (base): RED devices list emits string error; matrix verify backup reset --json emits private success:false and string error

- Readback (subprocess,config-file): Parsed child stdout has exactly one ok:false/error.type/error.message document and exit 1 for missing homeserver and backup-reset confirmation refusal; human stderr retains its prefix; configuration bytes unchanged

- Other callers checked: rg runMatrixCliCommand/onJsonError extensions/matrix/src identified the shared owner and all five private exception callbacks; callback host, root JSON renderer, direct commands, and local-state-owner finally/cleanup paths read
- Tests: OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/cli.local-state-owner.test.ts extensions/matrix/src/cli.test.ts extensions/matrix/src/cli-direct.test.ts --maxWorkers=1; 47 focused tests pass, exit 0; 17 intended RED assertions before the production change (measured cost: Single-file/single-worker lanes: cli.local-state-owner.test.ts 191.92s (runner total 202.77s), cli.test.ts 31.26s (runner total 41.70s). Existing cold transforms dominate 95%/77%; changed assertions add no new fixtures or waits)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an explicit top-level Slack send can be treated as a different conversation when the inbound context also carries a synthesized reply anchor.

## User Impact

User impact: `message_tool_only` replies sent explicitly to the current Slack channel are recorded as delivered instead of being left as a mute terminal turn, while real thread-root sessions remain isolated.

## Why This Change Was Made

For `topLevel: true`, delivery placement now compares the receipt with the thread identity parsed from the admitted session key. This avoids treating `currentThreadTs`, which may be an auto-reply anchor, as proof that the admitted conversation itself is threaded. Bound Slack thread sessions can intentionally use an unsuffixed session key, so the classifier also preserves `sameChannelThreadRequired` as the authoritative fallback. Session preparation resolves that fact once from the admitted message-action capability (or host recovery context); both the installed terminal hook and subscription completion consume it. Callers without an admitted fact remain conservative: only an explicit `false` allows clearing a transport reply anchor, so older CLI callers cannot acquire new false source-completion evidence.

## Evidence

The original reviewed PR head fails the new unsuffixed bound-thread classifier regression (`expected false`, `received true`; 1 failed and 14 passed). A classifier-only correction also fails the bound-thread installed-hook regression (1 failed and 27 passed). The final installed-hook behavior proof checks that a standalone channel final send records delivery exactly once and returns `terminate: true`, while suffixed and unsuffixed bound thread sessions record no source delivery and do not terminate.

Session, execution-phase, and stream tests cover the admitted-fact propagation seams, including distinct policy/transcript session keys and admitted `false` overriding a recovery `true`.

The corrected candidate passes:

428 passed across 13 files

oxfmt --check: passed

The full 428-test replay, changed-file formatting/lint and all 19 core-test graphs pass on this candidate. Production and root-test typechecks passed on the preceding `a6b73145fa1b03f7fdbe1a43c506b25f12eafc20`; this follow-up changes only three test fixtures, with no production changes.

The two hosted core-test stripes exposed obsolete `sandboxSessionKey` arguments in the billing and cron lifecycle fixtures. Revision 6 reviewed this exact candidate with no actionable code findings, while retaining the unexplained recursive-spawn CI failure and live Slack proof as merge risks.

Hosted CI is not green: the latest observed checks include 174 successes and two failures, consisting of [one recursive-spawn boundary test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34929273844/job/104254086366?pr=148721) and the aggregate gate. The repository CI wrapper replayed the complete 10-case production-boundary file in original file order on those frozen merge/main inputs. As root, merge passed 10/10 and main failed the original line-449 assertion (1 failed, 9 passed). In a separate task-owned copy as existing nonroot uid/gid 65534, merge failed that same assertion (1 failed, 9 passed) and main passed 10/10. Node 24.20, max workers 3 and an 8192 MiB heap budget were pinned; nonroot runs set both CI/GHA flags. Even after task-local Git/rsync extraction, both attempts reported 7 failed / 217 passed / 1 skipped files and 18 failed / 3559 passed / 2 skipped cases; this is matching aggregate statistics, not proof that every failure has the same cause. Remaining local issues include native-tool compatibility/library resolution and root-owned worker rejection. The replay host differs from GitHub's runner. No timeout, retry policy, assertion, runtime guard or unrelated source was changed; no successful complete-prefix replay or hosted CI rerun is claimed.

The earlier frozen-lockfile dependency install encountered a Matrix native-library download reset; linking was completed with lifecycle scripts disabled for those pure-logic tests. This installation limitation is separate from the hosted spawn failure.

### Real Slack transport validation — September 15

The exact candidate `7ac1347296fd5699a9bc9e227e512577ee26057a` was subsequently started through the supported CLI in task-owned Linux state, with a dedicated, explicitly authorized Slack app and test channel. A deterministic loopback Responses provider selected normal advertised tool calls; the unmodified embedded runtime and Slack transport executed them. This uses real Slack receipts, not fabricated transport results or paid inference, and is transport/lifecycle proof rather than model-quality proof.

- **Ordinary channel positive control:** a real standalone ingress with `requireMention:false` and `replyToMode:off` entered an unsuffixed channel session. A `message` send with `topLevel:true`, `final:true` visibly reached the parent channel; its real receipt matched the UI platform identity and reported `sourceReplyRoute:current-source`. Supported history and a bounded read-only query of the existing native run-outcome table paired that exact run/session/model with `tool_delivered/completed`, no active run and no pending input.
- **Genuine-thread paired control:** a real Slack thread reply entered the actual suffixed source session under per-channel `replyToMode:all`. Its first `topLevel:true`, `final:true` send visibly reached the parent channel with a receipt containing no thread identity and no current-source route marker. That successful result did **not** end the run: the same source run issued a second tool call, omitting `topLevel` and `threadId`. Normal routing inherited the original Slack thread; its real receipt and thread UI identity matched and the result reported `sourceReplyRoute:current-source`. The first ordinary-input attempt uncovered only a fixture bug: the Responses adapter appends a protected internal-context user carrier after the actual user. It produced probe text without a tool send and is not counted as a pass. The live fixture now skips only that complete carrier envelope on verified version-4 sessions; its 14 secretless protocol regressions pass. The successful ordinary case and the single genuine-thread case were independently reviewed. No production source, tool schema, admission check, timeout or assertion was changed to produce the live results. Credential values, private Slack identifiers and raw platform timestamps are intentionally omitted.

**Remaining limits:** the unsuffixed runtime-bound-thread case still has deterministic classifier, installed-hook and subscription regressions, but no live transport proof. Missing current-source route markers are observed result markers, not direct captures of subscription booleans or hook exactly-once internals. Ordinary message-tool display mirrors are not asserted to be durable final delivery mirrors. The unexplained hosted spawn failure remains unresolved; these live Slack controls do not make CI green or establish an unrelated-failure diagnosis.

The preceding CI and live-transport notes are historical evidence for head `7ac1347`. This branch now merges current `main` at `6c513528` in non-force commit `0b405858`. The nine merge conflicts were resolved against the refactored `agentSession` flow while preserving propagation of `sameChannelThreadRequired`. GitHub reports the current head as mergeable.

These failures are outside this PR's changed paths, but without a same-main control run I am not attributing them to infrastructure or to this PR. No unrelated assertions or production code were changed to mask them.

### Current-main maintenance — October 1

Merged current main (00f3a206302), preserving the recipient/account/physical-part checks and the extracted test fixtures. prs.title: perf(gateway): reuse Code Mode control schemas across turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Code Mode rebuilds its invariant `exec` and `wait` schemas for every turn, so real argument validation repeatedly generates and compiles the same validator functions.

## User Impact

Reduces main-thread allocation and CPU when assembling and validating Code Mode controls. Tool schemas, descriptions, cancellation, and execution authority keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The validation owner already caches by schema identity. Publish the two fixed schemas once from the Code Mode owner so that cache can work across turns; keep descriptions, runtime limits, and execute closures bound to each turn. No new cache, invalidation policy, runtime option, or compatibility path.

The production change moves the same schema definitions to module scope. The small line increase is two named constants and their references, replacing repeated construction without changing their contents.

## Evidence

Acceptance declared before measurement: remove redundant compiler work with unchanged validation and turn-specific execution; measure CPU and allocation in five interleaved owner pairs, plus code-space growth in an isolated synthetic Gateway. Small verified wins count; compiler-call reduction alone does not establish retained-code savings.

Owner probe: five fresh processes per arm in alternating AB/BA order, 5,000 assemblies per process over 170 rotating synthetic sessions, two real validations per assembly. Imports, 200 warmup assemblies, and explicit GC are outside measurement; allocation uses V8's native cumulative allocation counter.

| Owner metric (median) | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| CPU / 5,000 assemblies | 265.476 ms | 34.032 ms |
| Allocation / 5,000 assemblies | 224.804 MiB | 58.131 MiB |
| Recompiles / 2,000 warmed assemblies (separate count pass) | 4,000 | 0 |

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/code-mode-control-schema-measure.ts --source <frozen-owner.ts> --iterations 5000`; the script header explains the separate count pass and source substitution.

Regression: real exec/wait validation over three fresh turns makes six extra TypeBox `Compile` calls on main, versus zero expected after warming. The same test verifies each turn's displayed timeout and its own AbortSignal, so schema reuse cannot reuse an earlier turn's execution closure.

Validation: 65 focused Code Mode/agent-loop/prompt-prefix tests and 38 import-closure tests passed. Changed-file formatting/lint, strict root-script typechecks, the agents-tools test typecheck, and export-name collision checks passed. Test-line ratchet: 6,245,959 against the 6,320,000 ceiling (this PR does not edit the ceiling).

Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), P0–P2, no actionable findings. The final diff was checked after mechanical lint cleanup.

Runtime LOC: **+4** in the production owner (25 added / 21 removed). The extra lines name the two shared schemas; no additional branch or runtime state owner. Separate additions are 37 regression-test lines and 191 diagnostic/benchmark lines. The requested non-test diff is +195 lines overall (216 added / 21 removed), including those 191 tooling lines.

<!-- Gateway evidence -->
<details>
<summary>Synthetic Gateway measurements and attribution limits</summary>

Built baseline `4e84ee84b27ee69bcb146c472df3a1bae1ccb252` and candidate `9543383f4c0d046e4eee7e2aca29e1d461b6f68f`. Clean rebases produced the current head `ca89e6546dea22f8dc61c5e4313a13bb063c977c`; range-diff confirms the patch is identical, with no intervening changes to the owner, regression, validator, tool bridge, or lockfile. Each ran the canonical harness for 30 minutes after warmup: 10,800 sessions, 40 plugins, 65 WebSocket clients, Code Mode/native subagents, cron, sidebar/list/search/history churn, 120 foreground turns and 120 tool calls. Minute V8 samples and compiler-caller counts were recorded with `main-code-space-preload.mjs`. Allocation used separate ten-minute passes without that compiler preload, with the same fixture timestamp per comparison. Allocation-pass host load mean/max was 22.03/39.94 on base and 30.23/41.81 on candidate.

These are diagnostic arms, not a controlled whole-Gateway timing verdict: compiler wrappers add overhead and host contention was materially different. No intervals or pauses were excluded. No A/A controls were run, no observed increase is attributed to the change, and no whole-Gateway speedup is claimed. The invariant-schema change uses the authorized focused owner/work-count acceptance path.

| Gateway metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU (%) | 6.340 | 7.048 |
| Allocation (MiB/s, separate pass) | 17.689 | 17.622 |
| GC (s/min) | 0.140 | 0.197 |
| Event-loop p99 (ms) | 28.819 | 41.583 |
| Event-loop samples | 83766.000 | 81191.000 |
| Client sessions.list p99 (ms) | 34.810 | 124.376 |
| Client list samples | 3624.000 | 3622.000 |
| Server list handler p99 (ms, histogram estimate) | 28.880 | 63.267 |
| Server list handler mean (ms) | 6.534 | 8.265 |
| Server handler samples | 3605.000 | 3604.000 |
| RSS (MiB) | 2519.885 | 2641.100 |
| Heap used (MiB) | 548.841 | 538.937 |
| Post-GC old generation (MiB) | 396.528 | 412.573 |
| Host load mean | 18.549 | 30.240 |
| Host load maximum | 41.343 | 68.073 |

The repeated validator producer is removed: **150 compilations during the baseline workload versus zero during the candidate workload** (the two candidate controls compile at startup). This **does not explain or fix the larger long-running code-space retention symptom**: code+metadata curves remain similar, and bytecode/source sizes stay stable. Continued native optimization or inline-cache warmup is a hypothesis, not a diagnosed defect.

| Minute from process start | Base code+metadata MiB | Candidate code+metadata MiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 5 | 50.820 | 50.223 |
| 10 | 56.869 | 57.034 |
| 15 | 59.474 | 59.700 |
| 20 | 61.513 | 61.688 |
| 25 | 63.533 | 63.945 |
| 30 | 64.995 | 65.146 |

At minute 30, used code_space is 56.492 → 56.613 MiB and code_large_object_space is 0.342 → 0.342 MiB. Samples are unforced; shutdown samples are not mixed into this table.

| Arm | GC kind | Count | Total ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | Maximum ms |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Base | minor | 1286 | 2291.427 | 2.925 | 5.591 | 12.143 |
| Base | incremental | 85 | 64.816 | 1.134 | 1.299 | 1.669 |
| Base | major | 85 | 1849.023 | 33.567 | 39.455 | 128.001 |
| Candidate | minor | 1322 | 3235.418 | 5.003 | 19.167 | 67.775 |
| Candidate | incremental | 84 | 63.496 | 1.013 | 1.078 | 1.101 |
| Candidate | major | 84 | 2618.023 | 67.967 | 149.375 | 323.458 |

Major/incremental GC percentiles have fewer than the required 200/1,000 samples and are context only. Absolute total-GC difference is +57.1 ms/min; its attribution is inconclusive under the differing host load and diagnostic instrumentation.

</details>

CI: the [initial run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40802148127) completed with 40 successful jobs. Its test-line guard used a ceiling lowered during the measurement campaign; rebased over [#187162](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187162), which restored headroom. The current local ratchet passes with 74,041 lines of slack, preserving the full regression.

The initial run also encountered an inherited lint error: `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts:722` lacks braces (`eslint(curly)`). The file is byte-identical on the initial PR head and its main parent `48f40fb0a2f328a4f364767a232786411ad82997` (blob `f151db5a0c4e7994f921b9a13fe6c365978a8b7a`), and `pnpm exec oxlint --threads=1 src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts` reproduces the same failure. The scheduled-main classifier called it new because an older main run passed; current-source comparison proves it is outside this diff. No CI rerun was requested.

Exact-head [CI run 40804335181](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40804335181) is **green** for `ca89e6546dea22f8dc61c5e4313a13bb063c977c`: 43 successful jobs, 28 skipped. Both core lint stripes, baseline ratchets, and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. PR remains ready and open for maintainer merge.

prs.title: feat(sessions): transcript archive retention config + post-archive vacuum pass
prs.body:
This is the content of [openclaw/openclaw#176078](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176078) (transcript-archive retention) rebuilt with upstream ancestry. The original PR was stuck closed-unmerged and could not be reopened because its head branch (`DarojaAI:fix/issue-137`) had orphan history with no merge-base against `openclaw/openclaw` main; GitHub refuses cross-repo PRs without common history. This branch is recreated from upstream main with a single squashed commit carrying the same change, pushed as `DarojaAI:retention-rebased`.

---

Closes #176077

## Problem
No retention control exists for transcript archives: archive accumulation is unbounded, and SQLite freelist pages are never reclaimed after archive passes — long-lived agents fill disk (fleet incident class, see issue repro).

## Shipped solution
- `session.maintenance.archiveAfter` config (`PositiveDurationSchema | false`), resolved to `archiveAfterMs` in `store-maintenance.ts`; malformed values disable archival rather than destroy history; help copy + labels + docs updated
- `reclaimSqliteFreePagesAfterArchivePass`: WAL checkpoint → freelist check → `incremental_vacuum(N)` on modern stores, full `VACUUM` retrofit on legacy ones — wired into `enforceSessionHistoryMaintenanceSerialized` post-pass, best-effort with next-pass retry
- Tests: 3 new eviction cases (age-driven archival without budget, inspect-as-mutation/warn-immutability, post-archive reclaim + retrofit); `session-history-eviction` 7/7, `store-maintenance` + zod extensions 28/28, `schema.help.quality` 24/24

## User impact
Operators gain a bounded archive footprint; maintenance passes shrink on-disk state instead of only moving it.

## Validation
Touched+adjacent src files typecheck clean (scoped tsgo); touched test files exit 0 individually. Known pre-existing `TS7016` in `src/media/qr-runtime.ts` (missing `@types/qrcode`) reproduces identically on pristine main — unrelated to this branch.

Provenance: fix developed downstream (DarojaAI/openclaw-gateway#137), reference-ported; happy to adapt to maintainer preferences on config naming/placement.

## What Problem This Solves
Operators running long-lived agents have no retention control on transcript archives: archive accumulation is unbounded and SQLite freelist pages are never reclaimed after archive passes, so disk fills on busy deployments (repro in #176077). This PR adds the bounded-retention config surface plus incremental vacuum so archive growth stays within operator-set bounds.

## Evidence
- **Behavioral repro:** with no `session.maintenance` config, transcript archives grow without bound and freelist pages are never reclaimed (#176077 repro; observed unbounded archive accumulation on a 5-minute journal cadence in production).
- **Fix verification:** 34/34 scoped shard tests green on current main (eviction, store-maintenance, schema help/quality suites), rebased across the #175837 sessions refactor.
- **Surface:** `session.maintenance.archiveAfter` (`PositiveDurationSchema | false`) resolved to `archiveAfterMs` in store maintenance; eviction tests cover the reclaim and legacy full-vacuum retrofit paths.

prs.title: perf(gateway): skip unused skill discovery for draft titles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Draft title preparation discovers workspace skill commands on every ordinary message, although the canonical title-source parser only consumes those commands for slash input. On skill-rich workspaces, this is unnecessary CPU and allocation before utility-model inference.

## User Impact

Ordinary draft titles prepare with less CPU and allocation. Skill slash commands, metadata stripping, utility-only inference, cancellation and current-authority checks retain their existing behavior. No configuration, schema, cache or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the source with the existing parser first. Only a null result takes the existing skill-discovery path and resolves again. This deletes unused discovery work without introducing a second parser or a persistent cache. The four-line production increase preserves the existing registered-slash-command contract; ordinary and slash inputs still share the same inference owner.

## Evidence

Five alternating base/candidate comparisons, 2,000 title calls per arm per comparison, separately for untraced timing and sampled allocation. Baseline: `700930378c7987f517323c72158dbde2e5120337`. The owner executes real model selection and skill discovery against 40 synthetic plugins and 40 workspace skills; only inference is replaced with a fixed response. All title result hashes match.

| Per title call | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean main-thread CPU | 1,548.80 µs | 25.37 µs | −98.36% |
| Median main-thread CPU | 1,472.12 µs | 25.14 µs | −98.29% |
| Mean sampled allocation | 542,264 B | 22,456 B | −95.86% |
| Skill preparations | 1 | 0 | removed |

All five comparisons improve. CPU sample ranges: base 1,198–1,977 µs, candidate 24–27 µs. Allocation ranges: base 541,375–543,322 B, candidate 22,090–22,917 B. Counts-only attribution finds 1,522 µs/call inside skill preparation, producing 40 command records; warm worker-message deltas are zero. CPU timing host load by arm: base `[18.45, 22.87, 25.31, 21.85, 21.78]`, candidate `[20.06, 18.92, 24.27, 22.97, 23.04]`. Allocation-pass load ranges: base 20.74–23.43, candidate 18.96–26.70.

Reproduce with the committed script, using distinct output directories and alternating revisions:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/sessions-files-title-measure.ts --mode title --instrument timing --requests 2000 --revision 700930378c7987f517323c72158dbde2e5120337 --output .local/title-base
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/sessions-files-title-measure.ts --mode title --instrument timing --requests 2000 --output .local/title-candidate
```

Repeat with `--instrument allocation` and new output directories. `--instrument counts --requests 100` isolates the phase census. Usage lives in the script header; the shared performance README is unchanged.

The same script also measures the unchanged file-list owner: 1,000 touched files, 20 calls per instrument, 48.84 ms main-thread CPU and 35.18 MB sampled allocation/call. Its separate census counts one root admission, 1,000 file stats, one directory listing and one Git discovery/call; no warm worker round trips. A subsequent write is reflected in the next result. Directory listing metadata and per-file stat have different alias/symlink admission contracts, so this PR preserves those reads rather than duplicating filesystem policy in an application fast path.

Validation:

- Regression on unchanged production: the two ordinary-text cases fail because skill preparation runs once instead of zero; registered slash cases pass. Candidate owner file: 36/36 pass (43.33 s total, approximately 3.4 s test execution).
- Existing `sessions-title.test.ts`, `dashboard-session-title.transport.test.ts`, and `dashboard-session-title.incognito.test.ts`: 52/52 pass, including revocation, cancellation, utility-only selection and real loopback mock-provider transport (133.10 s including compiler preparation).
- Export-name collision guard and both required import/source closure test files pass (38 tests).
- Focused oxfmt/oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, the Gateway root test typecheck, and `git diff --check` pass. Test-lines ratchet: 6,242,741 against 6,320,000; ceiling unchanged.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean at P0–P2. Autoreview preflight refused the requested provider because it did not match operator configuration; configuration was not changed. The reviewer inspected the complete three-file change and relevant owners. Subsequent rebase only incorporated unrelated UI/workspace-writer changes.

Production delta: **+4 lines** (10 added, 6 removed); regression: +21; measurement tooling: +307. The small production increase retains the existing slash-command path while removing ordinary-input discovery; no second parser, compatibility shim or persistent cache is added.

Scope: this follows the explicitly requested fast path for deletion of unused work. These are owner CPU/allocation measurements, not whole-Gateway latency claims. No ten-minute Gateway stress, 65-client workload, GC/event-loop/sessions.list tails, or live-service load test was run. PR CI supplies broad validation; exact-head results are tracked separately.

prs.title: fix(openrouter): keep prepared thinking efforts current after a catalog refresh
prs.body:
AI-assisted: yes

Fixes #160758

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where OpenRouter models kept offering and selecting a stale reasoning effort (for example `xhigh`) after OpenRouter dropped it, because the effort metadata was copied into the prepared catalog row at discovery time and the in-process capability cache refreshed later without updating that row.
- Users had to wait for the model catalog to be rebuilt past the discovery cache window before sessions showed the current effort choices.
- Follow-up (review finding): route projection copied the catalog provenance marker onto rows that then received an operator-authored `thinkingLevelMap` from logical overrides, so a warm capability cache could replace that authored map with cached catalog data. The marker is now cleared whenever logical overrides declare effort metadata.
- **Related:** #160651 (merged) brought configured catalog-route rows to parity with non-configured rows and explicitly left this catalog-refresh behavior as follow-up work; this PR completes that follow-up. The issue's review also names the missing distinction between declared and catalog-derived fields as the blocker for the fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** Prepared OpenRouter rows still carry the catalog's advertised efforts (existing contract), but rows built from the canonical OpenRouter route are now marked `catalogReasoningEfforts`, and the OpenRouter thinking hook replaces those catalog-derived effort fields with the currently loaded capabilities (the same catalog's current generation) while keeping operator-authored compat facts. Explicit configured declarations never carry the marker, so they keep winning. The run-side frozen thinking capability also prefers the runtime model's refreshed efforts for marked rows.
- **Authored-setting precedence:** `applyLogicalOverrides` now drops the marker when the override declares a `thinkingLevelMap`, so an operator-authored map stays authoritative across capability refreshes on every projection path (unmanaged, unresolved, and selected routes).
- **Out of scope:** No change to custom/proxy route discovery rows (they keep owning their discovered efforts), no change to the capability cache fetch/refresh behavior, and no new I/O on the synchronous session-read path: the hook still only reads capabilities already loaded in memory, exactly as in #160651.
- **Highest-risk area:** Provenance merge points for the new marker (`overlayCatalogMetadata`, route projection, model registry rows).
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The marker is cleared when a configured overlay declares effort metadata, when logical overrides author a thinking map, or when capabilities cannot cross a route change, all covered by dedicated tests; existing catalog carry/overlay/route-projection suites all pass unchanged.

## User Impact

- Sessions on canonical OpenRouter models now offer and select the reasoning effort levels OpenRouter currently advertises, following a capability refresh without a restart or catalog rebuild, matching the behavior #160651 already established for configured rows.
- Explicit operator declarations of `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` or `thinkingLevelMap` are unchanged and still take precedence; an operator-authored thinking map is no longer replaced by refreshed catalog data.
- **Success criteria:** After a missing-model load refreshes the capability cache to `["high","medium","low"]`, a prepared row that still carries `xhigh` resolves thinking levels without `xhigh`; with a cold capability cache the prepared row's own snapshot is kept; custom routes are unaffected; a row with an operator-authored `thinkingLevelMap` keeps that map and its own discovered efforts after the same refresh.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `extensions/openrouter/index.ts` (`withOpenRouterCatalogThinking`), `extensions/openrouter/provider-catalog.ts` (`buildOpenRouterLiveModel`), the marker plumbing in `src/agents/model-catalog-*.ts` and `src/auto-reply/thinking*.ts`, the marker-clearing in `src/agents/model-catalog-route.ts` (`applyLogicalOverrides`), and the regression fixtures `extensions/openrouter/catalog-reasoning-refresh.test.ts` and `src/agents/model-catalog-route.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Isolated worktree of this branch on Node v26.7.0. Two evidence layers: (1) the vitest regressions below, and (2) a real-path run (see `Real-path run` below) that drives the real discovery, the real capability-cache refresh, a real prepared session, and the real final provider request, with only the upstream OpenRouter endpoint impersonated by a local HTTPS endpoint (transport-level redirect; the request URL stays `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/openrouter/catalog-reasoning-refresh.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/model-catalog-entry.test.ts src/agents/model-catalog-metadata.test.ts src/agents/model-catalog-lookup.test.ts src/agents/model-catalog-route.test.ts src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts extensions/openrouter/provider-catalog.test.ts extensions/openrouter/prefer-runtime-model.test.ts extensions/openrouter/index.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.compat-route.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/openrouter-model-capabilities.test.ts
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <evidence>/real-path-proof.mts   # real-path proof, before & after the marker-clearing fix
  pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:extensions
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  extensions/openrouter/catalog-reasoning-refresh.test.ts
  - refresh follows: prepared row keeps xhigh while cold; after a real
    missing-model cache refresh the hook offers ["low","medium","high"]
  - authored map + warm cache: operator map {off:null, low:"low", high:"high"}
    keeps the row's own ["low","medium","high","xhigh"] efforts; the same row
    still carrying the marker would be clobbered to ["low","medium","high"]
  Tests 4 passed (4)
  src/agents/model-catalog-route.test.ts
  - selected-route projection with an authored thinkingLevelMap override:
    projected thinkingLevelMap == authored map, catalogReasoningEfforts == undefined
  - no effort override: marker survives projection
  Tests 25 passed (25); focused suites 163+ passed across 10 files
  tsgo:core PASS, tsgo:extensions PASS; validate.sh (oxfmt+oxlint+tests+tsgo) green

  real-path-proof.mts (real modules, real in-process capability cache, no stubs):
  [discovery] gen-1 row: efforts ["xhigh","high","medium","low"], catalogReasoningEfforts=true
  [session]  cold-cache levels = ["low","medium","high","xhigh","ultra"]
  [refresh]  real missing-model load -> real cache efforts ["high","medium","low"]
  [session]  warm-cache levels = ["low","medium","high","ultra"]   <- stale xhigh gone
  [run]      runtime model compat (resolveDynamicModel hook) = ["high","medium","low"]
  [request]  final provider request captured at the endpoint:
             model acme/effort-model, reasoning {"effort":"high"}
  [p1]       authored-map row projected without the marker; warm-cache levels keep
             ["low","medium","high","xhigh","ultra"]; marker-kept counterfactual
             drops to ["low","medium","high","ultra"]
  RESULT: ALL CHECKS PASS
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** A prepared session on a canonical OpenRouter row resolves current efforts after a real cache refresh and the final chat/completions request carries `reasoning: {"effort": "high"}` (no stale `xhigh`); a row with an operator-authored `thinkingLevelMap` keeps the authored map and the row's own efforts across the same refresh.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** Main symptom: reverting `extensions/openrouter/index.ts` to main made the refresh regression fail with an extra `"xhigh"` level. P1 follow-up: running the same real-path script with only the marker-clearing in `applyLogicalOverrides` reverted produced `RESULT: CHECKS FAILED` — the authored row was clobbered to `["low","medium","high","ultra"]` on the warm cache and the projected entry kept `catalogReasoningEfforts=true`.
- **What was not tested:** No live OpenRouter API call was made (no credentials); the upstream catalog/response endpoint is impersonated by a local HTTPS endpoint at the system boundary while discovery, refresh, prepared-session resolution, and the transport request all run through the real code paths. CI lanes (changed-project tests and full test-type check) are pending on GitHub Actions.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** The upstream OpenRouter service is simulated at the transport boundary; everything on the client side of that boundary (guarded discovery fetch, real capability-cache load/refresh, prepared-session thinking resolution, runtime model resolution, request build, and HTTP send) runs the real production code.
- **Review state:** Addressed the ClawSweeper P1 finding (clear catalog provenance after configured thinking-map overrides) and supplied the requested real-path prepared-session + final-request evidence. CI re-running on the new head.

prs.title: fix(google-meet): gateway restart drops active Meet captures and transcripts never finalize
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #150143

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users running a Google Meet capture (`--mode transcribe`) would lose the session entirely when the gateway restarted mid-meeting: `openclaw googlemeet status` reported no sessions, the durable transcript stayed unfinalized forever (`meeting_transcript_sessions.stopped_at` NULL, no row in `meeting_transcript_summaries`), and no summary was ever written.
- Also fixes the transport-admission defect ClawSweeper flagged on the first two revisions (P1): on SIGTERM/SIGUSR1 restarts the run loop closes root-work admission *and* the close prelude aborts the gateway request entry before plugin services stop, so the shutdown drain's gateway RPCs (`browser.request` for final captions/browser departure, `voicecall.end` for the phone transport) were rejected — first at the router with `unavailable during gateway restart`, then (revision 2) even earlier at `GatewayRequestEntryLifetime.enter()` with `Gateway request entry is closed`; the transcript bridge could then store a summary after a failed final capture while the browser stayed joined.
- **Related:** #150143 carries `clawsweeper:queueable-fix` / `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear` / `clawsweeper:source-repro`; the ClawSweeper Codex review confirmed the restart gap exists in current main and that no open transcript PR supplies Google Meet shutdown cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** On gateway shutdown, the Google Meet plugin now drains every active session through the exact same leave path as an explicit `googlemeet.leave` — durable transcripts finalize (`stoppedAt` + summary rows), transports are released, and per-session cleanup failures are logged without blocking the remaining sessions.
- The plugin already owns a complete leave/finalization flow (`MeetingSessionRuntime.leave` → durable transcript stop → transport cleanup); the only missing piece was the plugin-lifecycle connection. Gateway close already invokes registered plugin services (`pluginServices.stop`), so registering a `google-meet` service whose `stop` performs the drain is the narrowest repair. The shutdown hook only drains an already-initialized runtime; it never instantiates the runtime just to discover there is nothing to clean up.
- **Shutdown cleanup admission (core fix):** `completeGatewayClose` now wraps `pluginServices.stop()` in a shutdown-owned cleanup root (`runWithGatewayShutdownCleanupAdmission` in `src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts`). This is the owner-bound cleanup path the review asked for: the gateway router admits requests issued from the close sequence's own async chain (nested root via the existing `AsyncLocalStorage` admission path in `server-methods.ts`), while external/ordinary requests stay fenced for the whole drain — the fence is not reopened process-wide. The tracked root also joins the existing `waitForGatewayRestartFenceSettlement`/drain accounting, so a stalled cleanup still surfaces in shutdown diagnostics instead of outliving exit.
- **Request-entry cleanup admission (revision 3, P1 from the ClawSweeper review of `47b68c1`):** the real close prelude (`markClosePreludeStarted` in `server-lifecycle.ts`) aborts `requestEntryLifetime` *before* `completeGatewayClose` stops plugin services, so the drain's in-process RPCs were rejected in `dispatchGatewayRequestInProcessRaw` → `GatewayRequestEntryLifetime.enter()` before the router ever consulted the cleanup root. `enter()` now also admits chains that own the shutdown cleanup root (`isInsideGatewayShutdownCleanupChain()` reads the same `AsyncLocalStorage` admission context the close sequence runs `pluginServices.stop()` in). Cleanup entries stay tracked in the lifetime's active set, so `sealAndJoin()` still joins them before transports close; external callers never observe the cleanup context and stay fenced for the whole drain, and once entries seal the barrier is absolute again.
- **Connection-work tracking admission (revision 5, found by a real end-to-end restart run):** the close sequence drains *received connection work* (`shutdown step "received connection work"` → `connectionWork.drain()`) **before** the `gateway close` step runs `pluginServices.stop()`. The real gateway's canonical request context binds `trackExecution` to `connectionWork` (`server-request-context.ts`), so the drain's `browser.request` dispatches were rejected with `"Async work scope is closed"` — Chrome never clicked Leave call, and the failed leave path stalled the whole close (60s+, no exit). Unit tests missed it because their contexts used a caller-scope `trackExecution`. `trackExecution` now tracks shutdown-cleanup-chain executions into the calling chain's scope (the close's `cleanupWork`) instead of the drained connection scope; external requests keep the original binding and still reject after the drain. Regression: `server-request-context.test.ts` "tracks shutdown cleanup chain executions into the caller scope after connection work drains" (a drained real `AsyncWorkScope` rejects outside the chain, resolves inside it).
- The google-meet shutdown-service tests moved to `extensions/google-meet/service-shutdown.test.ts` because `extensions/google-meet/index.test.ts` is over the line cap and the baseline ratchet rejects any growth there (CI `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failure on the first revision); coverage is unchanged.
- **Out of scope:** startup reconciliation of historically orphaned `stopped_at IS NULL` rows and re-attaching to still-open Meet tabs (both larger alternatives per the issue); forced-kill scenarios cannot be covered by any in-process hook. No new configuration or storage semantics.
- **Highest-risk area:** gateway shutdown sequencing — a slow leave could delay shutdown.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Sessions drain sequentially through the existing per-meeting lock, and per-session errors are caught and logged so one failed leave cannot strand the others. The five-second plugin-service grace (`MCP_RUNTIME_CLOSE_GRACE_MS` via `disposeRuntimeWithShutdownGrace`) lets the remaining close steps (channels, harnesses, runtime disposal) advance while the drain is still running, and every cleanup RPC carries its own dispatch deadline, so a hung transport cannot extend the join indefinitely. Per the close sequence's pre-existing contract, retirement still joins plugin-service cleanup and its request entries before transports and the registry close (`await pluginServicesCleanup` + `finishRequestEntries` in the close finally phase) — so a slow Meet leave can extend shutdown **completion** up to its RPC deadlines, the same join-before-retirement behavior every plugin service already had, now visible because the drain actually executes. Finalization in the overrun case (a leave still running when its dispatch deadlines expire) is not guaranteed; observed live in the real restart e2e: a normal drain completes the whole close in 1.4–1.7s (exit code 0, stopped_at + summary + Leave click), and a deliberately slow leave (page only reaches post-call 8s after the click, past the 5s leave window) still finalizes the transcript (stopped_at + summary written ~400ms after SIGTERM) and exits cleanly in 5.1s with the browser tab released, matching the join-before-retirement contract above.

## User Impact

- After a gateway restart (graceful stop/drain), meeting transcripts captured before the restart are finalized: `stopped_at` is set from the live capture, the summary is written, and `openclaw transcripts` no longer shows a dangling session with `no summary.md`. Saved utterances remain readable either way.
- **Success criteria:** with an active Meet capture, stopping the gateway leaves the session through the normal leave path; the transcript session row gets `stopped_at` and a summary row, matching an explicit `googlemeet leave`.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/server-request-entry.ts` (cleanup-chain admission inside `enter()`, covered by `server-request-entry.test.ts` "admits shutdown-owned cleanup RPCs through request entry after the close prelude", which drives the real `kernel.beginClosePrelude()` + real `dispatchGatewayRequestInProcessRaw` + real method registry), `src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts` + `src/gateway/server-close.ts` (shutdown-owned cleanup root around `pluginServices.stop`, with `src/gateway/server-close.shutdown-admission.test.ts` now probing through a real aborted `GatewayRequestEntryLifetime` during the real draining close lifecycle), `src/gateway/server-request-context.ts` (shutdown-cleanup-chain executions track into the caller's scope once connection work has drained, covered by `server-request-context.test.ts`), `extensions/google-meet/index.ts` (new `api.registerService` shutdown drain + initialized-runtime peek), and the regression tests in `extensions/google-meet/service-shutdown.test.ts` ("registers a shutdown service that leaves active sessions through the leave path", "keeps draining remaining sessions when one leave fails during shutdown", "stops cleanly when the runtime was never initialized").

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** git worktree rebased onto origin/main `4bc73868a82`; real gateway kernel close prelude (`kernel.beginClosePrelude()`), real in-process RPC dispatch (`dispatchGatewayRequestInProcessRaw`) with a real method registry, real gateway close lifecycle (`prepareGatewayClose`/`completeGatewayClose`), real `startPluginServices` host, real `GatewayRequestEntryLifetime`, and the real process-wide admission module (`src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts`) exercised in `src/gateway/server-request-entry.test.ts` + `src/gateway/server-close.shutdown-admission.test.ts`; real `GoogleMeetRuntime`/`MeetingSessionRuntime` leave path exercised in-process (external voice-gateway RPC boundary mocked).
A full real-process end-to-end restart run (see the next two evidence items) additionally exercised the real gateway process, a real paired node host (`openclaw node run` with `browser.proxy` + `googlemeet.chrome`), a real headless Chrome 151 managed through CDP by the browser plugin, and the real transcript SQLite state database. The only external stand-in was the Google Meet origin itself: a local TLS server serving a stateful Meet-like page (pre-join → in-call with rolling caption rows → post-call) that satisfies the real `meetStatusScript`/`meetTranscriptScript`/`meetLeaveScript` DOM contracts, reached through Chrome's `--host-resolver-rules` mapping so the plugin still dispatches against `https://meet.google.com/...` URLs.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # RED/GREEN at the real request-entry boundary (same tests, with vs without
  # the enter() cleanup-chain admission in src/gateway/server-request-entry.ts):
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-request-entry.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-close.shutdown-admission.test.ts
  # Post-rebase affected suites + full google-meet extension suite:
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-close.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-close.shutdown-admission.test.ts src/gateway/server-request-entry.test.ts \
    src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts src/gateway/server-in-process-dispatch.abort.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-in-process-dispatch.error-cause.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-in-process-execution-lifetime.test.ts extensions/google-meet/
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental \
    --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json --builders 1
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mts --base origin/main
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-assertion-safety-ratchet.mts --base origin/main
  skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh src/gateway/server-request-entry.ts \
    src/gateway/server-request-entry.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.shutdown-admission.test.ts \
    src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts extensions/google-meet/service-shutdown.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  # RED — real close prelude (kernel.beginClosePrelude) + real in-process dispatch,
  # WITHOUT the enter() cleanup-chain admission:
  × server-request-entry.test.ts > admits shutdown-owned cleanup RPCs through
    request entry after the close prelude
    → Error: Gateway request entry is closed
  × server-close.shutdown-admission.test.ts > keeps plugin service cleanup admitted
    after restart draining fences ordinary requests
    → AssertionError: expected [ 'plugin-services' ] to strictly equal []
  Tests  2 failed | 13 passed (15)

  # GREEN — with isInsideGatewayShutdownCleanupChain() consulted in enter():
  ✓ admits shutdown-owned cleanup RPCs through request entry after the close prelude
    (cleanup-chain dispatch reaches the real handler: { ok: true, payload: { cleaned: true } })
  ✓ keeps plugin service cleanup admitted after restart draining fences ordinary requests
  Tests  15 passed (15)

  # Real-module probes (tsx against the real server-request-entry.ts + gateway-work-admission.ts,
  # real restart ordering: markGatewayRestartDraining → lifetime.beginClose → cleanup chain):
  # before fix — cleanup RPC rejected at the entry barrier the review pointed at:
  {"probe":"plugin-service-stop-rpc-during-drain","admitted":false,"error":"Gateway request entry is closed"}
  # after fix — cleanup chain admitted, external requests fenced before/during/after cleanup:
  {"probe":"external-ordinary-request-during-drain","admitted":false,"error":"Gateway request entry is closed"}
  {"probe":"plugin-service-stop-rpc-during-drain","admitted":true}
  {"probe":"router-root-admission-in-cleanup-chain","admitted":true}
  {"probe":"external-ordinary-request-after-cleanup","admitted":false,"error":"Gateway request entry is closed"}

  # Post-rebase affected suites (origin/main 4bc73868a82):
  gateway close/entry/dispatch suites:  Test Files  6 passed (6)   Tests  107 passed (107)
  src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts:  Tests  41 passed (41)
  extensions/google-meet/ (full):  Test Files  29 passed (29)   Tests  395 passed (395)
  tsgo test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json:  0 errors
  tsgo core.test.gateway-server shard:  exit 0
  check-line-cap-ratchet: Line-cap ratchet OK: 9 changed source files; no new violations.
  check-assertion-safety-ratchet: exit 0
  validate.sh (oxfmt + oxlint + related tests + tsgo:core):  [validate] 全部通过 ✅
  ```
- **Real-process end-to-end restart evidence (added for the revision-4 "needs proof" items; commit `761ace8b68f`):**
  ```bash
  # Topology: one host, all real processes; only the Meet origin is a local stand-in.
  #   fake-meet-server.mjs (TLS 127.0.0.1:8443)  <- Chrome --host-resolver-rules MAP meet.google.com 127.0.0.1:8443
  #   real gateway process (openclaw gateway run, transcripts enabled, google-meet + browser plugins)
  #   real node host process (openclaw node run --commands browser.proxy,googlemeet.chrome)
  #   real headless Chrome 151 (browser plugin managed CDP)
  #   real CLI: openclaw googlemeet join https://meet.google.com/red-shut-run --transport chrome --mode transcribe
  # Then: kill -TERM <gateway> and observe the page event log + the gateway's SQLite.
  ```
  ```text
  RED   (both fixes removed — reproduces main):  SIGTERM -> gateway exits 449ms (no drain)
        meeting_transcript_sessions: stopped_at = NULL, summaries = 0 rows, leave-clicked = 0
        (issue #150143 repro: orphaned capture, transcript never finalizes)

  GREEN (this PR, real leave through the real page):
        SIGTERM 08:02:24.612 -> gateway exit code=0 after 1734ms
        leave-clicked at 08:02:25.278, post-call-shown at 08:02:25.279   (real Chrome Leave-call click)
        stopped_at = 2026-09-18T08:02:25.175Z (SIGTERM+~400ms), summaries = 1 row,
        utterances = 21 rows captured live from the caption stream before the restart,
        summary participants = [Ada Lovelace, Grace Hopper], overview/decisions/actionItems
        generated from the real captured lines by the real heuristic summarizer.
        googlemeet transcript <id> before the restart already returned live caption lines.

  SLOW  (same run, page only reaches post-call 8s after the leave click):
        SIGTERM -> stopped_at + summary written SIGTERM+364ms, gateway exit code=0 after 5060ms
        leave-clicked = 13 (persistent clicks across the leave window); the post-call switch
        itself lands past the 5s leave deadline, so browser tab release is best-effort here —
        matching the overrun caveat above (transcript finalization still guaranteed by the
        final capture, which had already collected the caption buffer).

  # The GREEN/SLOW runs first failed before 761ace8b68f with exactly:
  #   "Browser control could not leave the Meet tab: Async work scope is closed"
  # and the gateway then never exited (>60s) — see the connection-work bullet above.

  # Post-fix unit/validate: server-request-context.test.ts + server-request-entry.test.ts +
  # server-close.shutdown-admission.test.ts + gateway-work-admission.test.ts: 79 passed;
  # validate.sh (oxfmt + oxlint + related tests + tsgo:core): all green.
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** during a real restart drain (`markGatewayRestartDraining` → real close prelude aborting `requestEntryLifetime` → real `completeGatewayClose`), a plugin service stop that issues gateway requests passes **both** shutdown barriers: `GatewayRequestEntryLifetime.enter()` admits the chain because it owns the shutdown cleanup root, and the router admits it through the same root — so the Google Meet drain's `browser.request` final capture/departure and `voicecall.end` RPCs reach their handlers instead of being rejected with `Gateway request entry is closed` / `unavailable during gateway restart`. Cleanup entries stay tracked in the lifetime's active set, so `sealAndJoin()` still joins them before transports close; ordinary external requests stay fenced before, during, and after cleanup (verified by real dispatches that keep rejecting with `Gateway request entry is closed`), and the cleanup root settles so drain accounting is unchanged. At the plugin level, invoking the registered service's `stop` with a joined session still ends the call via the real leave path (`endMeetVoiceCallGatewayCall` invoked, `googlemeet.status` reports `ended`); one failing leave does not strand the remaining sessions; `stop` without prior runtime use is a clean no-op. Transcript DB finalization on leave (`stoppedAt` + summary rows) is exercised by the existing durable-transcript coverage (`src/meeting-bot/session-runtime.test.ts`), which this shutdown path reuses verbatim.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** before the patch, nothing connected gateway shutdown to the Meet session runtime (no plugin service). Revision 1 registered the service but the drain's RPCs were rejected by router admission during restart draining; revision 2 added the cleanup root but the real close prelude's earlier `requestEntryLifetime` barrier still rejected them (`Gateway request entry is closed`) — both proven by the RED runs above — so final captions were lost, the browser could stay joined, and `stopped_at` stayed NULL (issue repro steps 2–4).
- **What was not tested:** a meeting on the real `meet.google.com` origin (the end-to-end run below substitutes the Meet origin with a local TLS stand-in page that satisfies the plugin's real page-script DOM contracts — every process boundary in between is real, including the gateway process, node host, Chrome 151, CDP, RPC routing, and the transcript SQLite database); forced SIGKILL termination (not coverable by any in-process shutdown hook); CI lanes pending on this PR.
- **Proof tier:** L3 (real-process end-to-end restart: signal → drain → Chrome departure → transcript finalization → clean exit)
- **Proof limitations:** the in-process suites mock the external voice-gateway RPC boundary and browser transport; the full signal-to-exit run loop is covered by the existing `server-close.plugin-failure.test.ts` restart-mode harness. The real-process e2e below closes the remaining gap end to end (real signal → real drain → real Chrome departure click in a real page → real transcript finalization in the gateway SQLite → real exit code 0), with the Meet origin itself replaced by the local stand-in page.

prs.title: fix(discord): match canonically equivalent autocomplete labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord slash-command autocomplete misses choices when the label and the typed fragment use different Unicode composition forms. Typing `München` in an autocompleting option returns an empty list when the resolved label is stored decomposed (`Mu\u0308nchen`), and the reverse fragment misses composed labels.

The autocomplete closure in `buildDiscordCommandOptions` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command.options.ts`) is the comparison owner between the fragment Discord sends (`interaction.options.getFocused().value`) and the labels resolved through `resolveCommandArgChoices`, which include user-authored agent names, model display names and skill names.

Precedent: #187024 (same shape: compare canonical forms after the existing lowercase conversion, stored text untouched). Siblings already landed: #186329 (workspace filenames), #186794 and #187024 (cron metadata and run history), #184374 (session titles), #186922 (TUI pickers).

## Why This Change Was Made

The closure lowercased the typed fragment and each label with `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` but never applied a canonical form, so the `includes` filter split visually identical text. This change appends `normalize("NFC")` to the fragment and to the compared label projection. Choice values, returned `{ name, value }` payloads and the 25-choice Discord cap keep the resolver's original spelling; authorization, deadline and caching behavior are unchanged. No new helper, option, configuration key or storage change.

Production LOC: +3/−2.

Classification: `behavior-preserving` (comparison-only normalization)

## User Impact

Autocomplete now offers the same choice when the user's fragment and the stored label use different Unicode composition forms, which users experience as "autocomplete does not know this name". Unrelated labels still do not match, and ASCII, case and empty-fragment behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `a48af7a4b7bd4c590ff2ff35549f289528fc564d`
- Current-main RED baseline: `e85b3c8ddf64f463bf12b5abed67e55253f6a739`
- Production entry: the option `autocomplete` handler produced by `buildDiscordCommandOptions`, i.e. the handler attached to the Discord application command that the gateway registers.
- Canonical owner exercised: the autocomplete closure in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command.options.ts`
- Decision surface: the focused option fragment (`interaction.options.getFocused()`) scored against resolved choice labels.
- Recorder/readback boundary: the `interaction.respond` payload (`{ name, value }[]`) captured from the real handler with a Discord-shaped interaction object; no Discord network, token or gateway socket.
- Acceptance RED: on frozen main, fragment `München` against the label `Mu\u0308nchen` responds with `[]`.
- Acceptance GREEN: exact head responds with the unchanged choice `{ name: "Mu\u0308nchen", value: "nfc" }`.
- Legal controls: the other 10 cases in the same file—option serialization, `/acp` autocomplete, `/think` dynamic choices, policy rejection deadlines, revoked access, plugin command dispatch ownership, dynamic refresh and group-DM restrictions—pass on both refs.
- Cleanup: isolated remote tree; no Discord application, token, guild or gateway state was touched.

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace

Node 24.22.1, secretless, Vitest single file. `extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command.options.test.ts`.

```text
# RED — frozen main e85b3c8ddf6 + new regression
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ [ { name: 'München', value: 'nfc' } ] ]
Received: [ [] ]
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 10 skipped (11)   # filtered with -t canonical
```

```text
# GREEN — exact head a48af7a4b7b + same regression, whole file
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
Duration  26.83s
```

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command.options.test.ts` — 11/11 pass on exact head; the new case fails on frozen main.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — clean.
- Not tested: a live Discord client interaction. The handler is exercised with a Discord-shaped interaction object through the real `buildDiscordCommandOptions` output, and the change only touches the comparison projection, so the payload shape Discord receives is unchanged.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: +3/−2; Test LOC: +22/−0 (one case appended to the existing options suite).
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the file's existing normalization helper and choice resolver; no new comparison path, resolver, or config surface.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. Responded choice names and values keep their original spelling.

## Merge risk

Two-way door: comparison-only change in one autocomplete closure, fully reversible. The blast radius is Discord autocomplete filtering; an incorrect normalization could change which choices appear for a fragment, but cannot change values, the 25-choice cap, authorization, or registered command payloads.

prs.title: fix: restore Files catalog after preview retirement
prs.body: Fixes #187107. ## What Problem This Solves Files can return as a blank panel after a user opens a workspace file, selects another conversation in the sidebar, and comes back. Opening the reader hides the catalog; task navigation deliberately retires that reader, but previously left the catalog hidden even though its rows were loaded. ## User Impact Returning to Files restores the catalog’s folder, search, filter and scroll position so the user can continue browsing saved work. Hidden readers and their pending transfers are still retired. Saved files, retained drafts, access checks and the layout of other panels keep their existing owners. No configuration or migration is required. Retirement updates navigation synchronously and defers catalog reads until Files is visible. An already-selected catalog keeps its newer navigation instead of replaying an older preview snapshot. ## Why This Change Was Made The workspace owner already records catalog navigation for ordinary reader selection. This change reuses its field-restoration logic when clearing previews, while separating that state update from the immediate reads used by an explicit tab selection. The existing presentation admission performs the deferred refresh. App tabs update an existing catalog return snapshot, preventing an older folder or filter from returning without introducing catalog reads for app-only navigation. Rendering and CSS continue consuming the owner’s state, and the final retirement notification continues canceling pending preview work. The regression extends the existing retained-panel scenario to select desktop presentation and assert catalog visibility, retaining its reader-disposal and DOM-identity assertions. A separate owner lifecycle case protects deferred reads and restoration of the correct catalog query. ## Evidence The failure was reproduced through a real guest UI connected to an isolated Gateway: open a saved Markdown file, use the sidebar to select another conversation, then return. The original preview was gone, but the catalog still had `hidden=true` and `display:none` inside a visible Files panel. The current UI’s served state module was matched byte-for-byte to the baseline source through its source map. The desktop regression fails on the baseline with expected `hidden=false`, received `true`. Formatting, changed-source lint, affected type checks and all 12 directly related test files (218 cases) pass, including deferred reads, app retirement, current authority, draft preservation and canceled transfers. The two changed test files completed together in 4.05 seconds of runner time. Independent review and canonical AutoReview are clean. The exact-head live journey returns to a visible catalog, preserves the unsent draft, retires all preview readers, and reopens the original saved file with identical bytes. The comparator file and both workspace identities are unchanged. Closing the last preview keeps the existing panel-close behavior; reopening Files is usable. Hosted CI completed with pre-existing mock-export ratchet and restart-history failures, independently reproduced on qualified baselines; the mock-export repair is already on main. The three initially failing UI jobs passed unchanged retries. Final composition checks passed both UI type graphs and 113 affected cases, and the test count fits the restored repository ceiling. The live baseline uses current UI source bf6bdd6c5fedb5e23f7bc206d26c625adbdec1ab against the existing isolated Gateway at 09a58215b66ca511ae398ddf9e00e9c7b4eef9f6; it is not a full Gateway rebuild at the UI revision. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Files is blank after the preview retires during task navigation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e2e9fe1-8f1f-4455-a796-2aa54cfcefec) | ![Files shows its saved file catalog after returning to the task](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/299dd006-a5ad-4b3c-9864-4333145ed9c1) | ### Before and exact\-head after: preview, task switch, return https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e2875a5-7332-47ac-8f3d-b29971b8d5a6 ### Visual verification - Baseline: bf6bdd6c5fedb5e23f7bc206d26c625adbdec1ab - Exact head: `5159447d4f5f4944a834006cb6ebb3630f926252` - Scenario: Open preview\.md, use the ordinary sidebar to select another task, then return to Files\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw Control UI 5159447d4f5; existing isolated Gateway 09a58215b66c\. Browser\-loaded state\-module source maps exactly match the baseline and reviewed Git revisions\. - Catalog after return: Before: hidden/display:none/0×0; after: visible/display:flex/1130×956 - Preview retirement: 0 preview tabs, readers and iframes after navigation, on both revisions - Correct attribution: preview\.md belongs to the original task; comparator\.md remains in the comparator - Saved work: Two real reopens returned the same 84\-byte file and workspace identity; original and comparator byte hashes are unchanged - Protected input: Unsent draft survived; no chat\.send calls - Last\-preview close: Existing panel closure preserved; ordinary reopening shows the usable catalog - Same 1440×1000 viewport, light theme, guest, fixtures, expanded Files layout and navigation sequence - Before/after exact source joins retained - Actual live scenario and preservation controls passed on 5159447d4f5 - Original recordings retained; published comparison removes startup and the unrelated post\-close conversation surface - Remote owner/consumer regressions and cancellation/current\-authority controls passed; the visual return is independently visible - The after run additionally preserves an unsent draft; its sidebar marker changes, while file data, layout and navigation are equivalent\.
