prs.title: fix: keep New Session tooltip from blocking sidebar controls
prs.body: Fixes #187088. ## What Problem This Solves Hovering the sidebar rail’s New Session button opens a shortcut hint to its right. When that hint overlaps a neighboring session-group header, its keycap text receives the pointer instead of the header. Moving directly from the plus button to the group can prevent the group’s normal controls from responding. ## User Impact The pointer can reach the adjacent group header and its actions while the informational hint is visible. The hint keeps its content, placement, and accessible description. New Session remains a native link: context menus, middle-click, and modified-click keep their normal behavior, and opening the form does not create a conversation or discard an unsent draft. ## Why This Change Was Made The New Session link owns a read-only tooltip containing a shortcut hint or disabled explanation. It now opts into the shared tooltip’s existing `pointerThrough` capability. The shared default remains unchanged, so rich tooltips containing links continue to accept pointer input. No permission checks, routing rules, styles, timers, or new interaction mechanism are introduced. The existing sidebar interaction scenario now waits for the rail tooltip to actually open and moves directly to the neighboring header. Removing the intermediate composer hover prevents the test from passing by dismissing the hint before it reaches the obstructed control. Group/catalog URLs, native-tab gestures, draft preservation, and no-session-creation assertions remain intact. The contribution adds one production line; the existing test changes by ten added and two removed lines. ## Evidence On base `700930378c7987f517323c72158dbde2e5120337`, the strengthened compiled Chromium scenario fails at the original header hover: the shortcut’s `span.kbd__text` intercepts pointer events for the 30-second action timeout. The other four sidebar cases pass. The current integrated tree passes changed-file formatting/lint, the selected UI and consumer type graphs, and all five sidebar interaction cases. That file took 31.72 seconds, including its UI build and native browser-tab journey. Existing resident-link/shell controls and all 29 tooltip cases in each of Chromium and WebKit also pass; those results were reused after verifying that their relevant sources and dependencies are unchanged. Independent source review and the separate structured review found no actionable defects. The matched live guest captures below use the same blank conversation, viewport, theme, route, tooltip geometry, and pointer coordinates. On the original base, the hint receives the click and the group stays expanded. On `20cf502d23566e71d6af1c71b9e692eac6ac3db0`, the header receives the click and collapses. Both runs preserve the unsent draft and produce zero session-creation requests. The existing Gateway’s relevant contracts are unchanged; this is local UI behavior proof rather than whole-Gateway qualification. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40795951875) passed all seven mocked UI shards and all three UI unit shards. Its three failing rows were traced to existing mock-export, sessions-send lint, and restart-history defects. The [main-branch run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40796541972) reproduces the same mock and restart failures; the lint error also reproduces on the exact CI parent. The mock correction has landed in #187120; the restart repair is tracked by #187143. These failed statuses remain explicit. On the current target, the direct pointer scenario still fails without this fix, while all five sidebar cases pass with it, including the agent-menu changes already on main. The contribution fits the measured test-code capacity restored by #187162. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Shortcut hint intercepts the header click and the group stays expanded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0257ba7f-f050-43c4-8fb6-41e6d20754f4) | ![Pointer reaches the group header and collapses it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/45eccda0-3cb9-4fed-8622-fc88464116dc) | ### Before and after: real pointer movement and one header click https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfc6fd48-6f68-4bb0-92e0-0970592c551e ### Visual verification - Baseline: 700930378c7987f517323c72158dbde2e5120337 - Exact head: `20cf502d23566e71d6af1c71b9e692eac6ac3db0` - Scenario: Hover the rail New Session button until its shortcut hint opens, move directly to the adjacent group header, and click once\. Desktop viewport1440×900; matched720×300 crops exclude unrelated content\. - Runtime/build: Current\-source Control UI on an existing isolated guest Gateway; matched viewport, route, fixture, theme and pointer coordinates\. Backend09a58215 unchanged\. - Header rectangle: x62,y48,width237,height24 on both revisions - Tooltip rectangle: x48\.5,y53\.125,width153\.015625,height25\.75 on both revisions - Header response: Before: stays expanded; after: collapses - Protected state: Unsent draft preserved;0session\-creation requests on both runs - Actual live guest connection; no model turn - Pointer movement and input cue shown - Native\-link regression: red before, green after; all original assertions retained - Shared interactive rich\-tooltip browser control passes - Matched crops omit unrelated UI without hiding the measured interaction

prs.title: improve(ui): open Files directly in supported browsers
prs.body:
Related: #180298.

## What Problem This Solves

Choosing File can reopen a media-source chooser when the user wants to browse files and document providers directly.

## User Impact

On browsers exposing direct file browsing, **Files** opens that route with unrestricted file types and multiple selection. Unknown extensions and `.stl` files use the normal attachment pipeline. Selection stages a draft; sending stays explicit.

**Scope:** this is the supported-browser Files contribution, not final cross-platform separation. Browsers without the direct API retain their existing File/Attach… route. The iPhone experience and final unsupported-browser UX remain reserved to #180298; no overlapping chooser is newly accepted as the desired fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mounted composer invokes `showOpenFilePicker()` from the user gesture, then uses the existing attachment admission, preparation, draft and send owners. Cancellation preserves the draft; failures report errors without silently opening a different chooser. Late results cannot populate a replacement draft or unmounted composer.

Image-only composers, arbitrary documents, file-provider access, upload policy, size checks, lazy camera registration and permission documentation remain intact. No file-type allowlist, custom filesystem browser, persistent handles, permission changes or deployment is introduced.

Proposed and directed by **Vitor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit)**.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @TheAngryPit](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dfd1f162-7d1d-4dc0-a7e0-0a65c7817bd8)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b60fbede-a126-4413-8cdc-4dc34b504a62)

prs.title: improve(ios): narrow release source checkout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Recent successful iOS release runs spent roughly 5–8 minutes checking out every branch and tag. Use the existing Android checkout policy for Store Release and daily TestFlight: check out the selected commit at depth one, fetch its complete ancestry with historical blobs omitted, and let release-note reads hydrate the files they need. Preserve exact source, main ancestry, recorded public baselines, signing, and upload behavior.

## User Impact

Release operators should spend less time acquiring source. Mobile build and publication behavior is unchanged. The hosted comparison passed the declared acceptance rule: median complete source acquisition fell from 535.546s to 124.654s (76.7% lower).

## Why This Change Was Made

Release notes need the selected source ancestry and public baselines; unrelated branches, tags, and historical blobs can be fetched only when needed.

## Acceptance rule (before hosted measurements)

Compare baseline and candidate checkout policies on the same pinned source `0b538f7d5a4d9e3328f572cc07fe23402f733f36`, using five fresh `xcode-27-xlarge` VMs per arm, serially interleaved baseline/candidate. Measure the complete checkout/history path through frozen dependency preparation, the release owner's later main fetch, source materialization, public baseline resolution, real release inventory, and selected historical evidence reads. Report component and complete-path median, p95, range, stored Git bytes, and host load/resources.

Accept at least 20% lower median complete-path time, no 20% or greater p95 regression, and identical selected source tree, complete ancestry, inventory, and evidence. Candidate must retain no unrelated branch/tag refs. Include lazy blob reads in measurements. The consumer step pins Git diff blob IDs to their full 40 characters so object-store size cannot change incidental index-header formatting; full evidence content still has one strict expected hash. The comparison never signs or uploads mobile builds.

## Evidence

- Focused mobile release CI/routing: 25 tests passed, including a real Git fixture for both platforms, a later main fetch, and ancestor/non-ancestor public baselines.
- Negative control: the old iOS workflow fails the new history fixture at the intended missing-history boundary.
- Workflow sanity/actionlint/zizmor and docs MDX checks passed.
- Targeted lint, tooling typecheck, formatting, and required macOS workflow guard suite passed (two repository-wrapper shards).
- AutoReview (Codex, P0/P1), local change snapshot against `0b538f7d5a4d9e3328f572cc07fe23402f733f36`: scoped-clean, no findings. Assessment covered supplied diff/test evidence; unchanged source was unavailable to that reviewer. The hosted comparison below supplies the required performance and real history-consumer proof.

The committed non-publishing [comparison workload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/tree/c984c78b8700/.github/workflows) lives only on the diagnostic branch. The initial baseline reached the real evidence owner but its fixture digest used a repository-dependent abbreviated blob-ID length. Exact local reproduction established that only nine index headers differed; the corrected fixture retains strict content checks and does not alter production code. That failed fixture run provides no accepted performance samples.

## CI attribution

Current [PR CI 40801427013](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40801427013) reports `check-lint-core-1` failing on `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts:722` (`eslint(curly)`: `if (slack) originalRoute.channel = "slack";`). Its tested merge is `0d1b394cd60b7559ed84c9a4112821a683b45947`, with main input `cb5a4388f310d8b7c5d461e4f875561215260c1d` ([#187065](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187065)). The failing file's blob is identical in that main input and the tested merge (`f151db5a0c4e7994f921b9a13fe6c365978a8b7a`); this PR changes neither it nor the core lint configuration. The automatic report calls it new relative to the last passing scheduled main job, but the exact merge inputs establish that it is inherited from this newer main commit. The failure is retained, not retried or relabeled green. All jobs have now settled. `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` also failed on 14 closed mock factories in `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts`. Main commit `a968dc19900d` (#187090) changed those factories without updating their exact-fingerprint baseline. The failing files, complete path inventory, guard/scanner/parser/resolver, baseline ledger, package/lock, tsconfig and CI owner are identical between tested main and merge; only this PR's three intended files differ. The guard compares the whole current inventory against the ledger, which explains why unchanged files fail. This second failure is also inherited. All other selected jobs passed; the aggregate gate reports those two failures. No branch-related CI failures remain.

## Hosted checkout measurements

[Comparison 40797835681](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40797835681) passed all five baseline and five candidate samples, serially interleaved on fresh `xcode-27-xlarge` VMs. Every sample verified the exact source tree, all 121,756 source ancestors, public release baseline, real release inventory, and selected historical evidence hashes. Every candidate retained only the intended main ref. Later main fetches and lazy blob reads are included in the complete boundary.

| Metric | Baseline median | Candidate median | Baseline p95 | Candidate p95 | Baseline range | Candidate range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Checkout (s) | 489.353 | 13.237 | 522.655 | 42.994 | 316.513–522.655 | 11.755–42.994 |
| Explicit history fetch (s) | 0.018 | 55.462 | 0.022 | 65.367 | 0.015–0.022 | 53.426–65.367 |

| Source materialization (s) | 8.591 | 7.284 | 9.485 | 10.804 | 7.679–9.485 | 6.237–10.804 |
| Public baseline resolution (s) | 1.864 | 1.555 | 2.001 | 1.880 | 1.445–2.001 | 1.199–1.880 |

Complete-boundary median improved 76.72%; p95 improved 72.31%. With five samples per arm, nearest-rank p95 is the observed maximum. Git object storage median fell 92.62%. Component medians are not summed to obtain complete-boundary time.

| Serial pair | Baseline complete boundary | Candidate complete boundary |

All hosts reported five CPUs, 14 GiB, arm64 macOS 27, Node 24.22.1, Git 2.56.0, and Xcode 27.1 (27A9275). Two hosted image revisions occurred: `20261026.0314.1` for baseline 1–4 and candidate 2–3; `20261023.0307.1` for baseline 5 and candidate 1/4/5. Their published macOS/kernel and relevant toolchain/SDK listings match, while unrelated package patch versions differ. Both images occur in both arms. Descriptive same-image ranges retain the improvement: old image 388.941s baseline versus 114.895–157.145s candidate; new image 363.304–567.534s baseline versus 113.938–124.654s candidate. prs.title: fix(update): stop Gateway respawn loops during Doctor maintenance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway respawn loops during update Doctor maintenance when the outgoing Gateway has already released its state lease but launchd still has its KeepAlive job loaded.

## User Impact

Candidate Doctor unloads the owned, enabled LaunchAgent before maintenance and retains the existing receipt so finalization can restore it, including with `--no-restart`. Unloaded or disabled services stay stopped; foreign installations and foreground-owner protections are unchanged. No schema, config, or CLI option changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

A process lease disappearing does not mean its supervisor is stopped. Remove the candidate's lease-liveness shortcut and let the existing native service owner decide whether a stop is needed. This is a candidate-side fix; it does not require changes in an already-installed updater.

Simplification: removes a duplicate ownership decision and obsolete lease mocks. Production −15 lines, tests +17 net, docs +6. The added regression covers the missing-lease respawn window and the unloaded/disabled controls.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced against base `d5d681f676344`: the respawning case returned without stopping; unloaded and disabled controls passed. All three pass with this fix, using the real update receipt writer.
- Focused service-maintenance, post-update/finalization, and CLI failure-output suites pass. The added three cases took 0.87 seconds combined; the native proof took 12.24 seconds. CI timings are not yet available.
- Native macOS proof with a disposable product-generated KeepAlive LaunchAgent: predecessor exited with no Gateway lease, candidate stopped/unloaded the job, one restoration receipt persisted, and no process respawned across the next 11 seconds. Test service and state removed.
- Targeted CLI-update TypeScript check, scoped oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Private runtime package build and tarball integrity checks pass.
- Independent review and local ClawSweeper committed-range review completed with no actionable correctness or security findings. ClawSweeper reviewed the complete four-file range `d5d681f676344..2a445f55db7ec` (high reasoning); runtime proof was performed separately, not by the reviewer.

- Published `2026.10.8` driver → patched candidate (same version, distinct build) with `--no-restart`: activation and service/version/channel/HTTP/core readiness verified; 61.11 seconds downtime, with the service unloaded during Doctor custody and restored afterward. Update and health commands exited 0; seeded session, disabled cron job, and config settings survived. Candidate tarball SHA-256: `c618aecb3c712567dbbc2621031cb232265624ddcb31b2d24f6765a84007b8a8` (built from base `d5d681f676344` plus this patch before the commit was made).
- Upgrade limitations: Doctor emitted advisory fixture/account, legacy configuration, and retained-runtime warnings; automatic snapshot rollback was unavailable because the original Gateway held ownership during capture. No rollback/fault injection, Windows/Linux native run, or exhaustive timing sweep is claimed. The deterministic regression and native unloaded-job proof exercise the specific missing-lease window.
- Teardown: offline copies of both databases passed `PRAGMA integrity_check`; disposable services/state and artifact server removed. Existing host LaunchAgent hashes and live Gateway PID were unchanged.

Declaration test fixtures start the same two Node parser processes again for every fixture, including suites explicitly selected by Windows CI.

## User Impact

The five-pair comparison fails the prospective all-metric rule. Windows execution remains unverified, and no billing saving is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare the two immutable normalization source strings and their stripped JavaScript once in the existing fixture-package owner. Keep the actual Node parser under both Node and Bun, then write fresh physical files and manifests into every fixture. Preparation failures propagate without publishing a partially prepared value.

Source inspection finds 35 constructions across the three Windows declaration suites (70 parser children before this change), with two preparations per helper module instance afterward. This is a source-derived opportunity, not an observed Windows count. Ordinary pull_request CI disables Windows before test selection. The helper dependency chain can select these suites in the ordinary runtime lane, but making this PR ready or applying ci:full cannot provide Windows proof. The sibling build-all fixture uses the same owner.

prs.title: fix(codex): stop background exec completions from replaying full history into a fresh thread
prs.body:
Related: #183286, #179363, #172026, #178982

## What Problem This Solves

When a background `exec` finishes in a Codex-backed WebChat session, the completion wake does not continue the session's bound native thread. It starts a fresh transient thread, replays the full session history into it uncached, and does it again for the follow-up turn. On a long session every completion wake costs a full uncached history read. In one observed session, four completion wakes each sent about 190k uncached input tokens.

This finishes, for event wakes, what #183286 started: tool declarations belong to the session, not to the turn. #183286 kept seven native Codex thread, plugin, and supervision declarations stable across owner and completion turns. A completion wake still differed from the user turn in three other ways, and each one alone forces a new thread:

1. **Tool-policy scope.** The default session-event source policy caps every follow-up at the producer's tool list. A wake with a cap runs as a turn-scoped restricted turn, which the Codex harness serves on a transient thread with native code mode off (48 eager dynamic tools instead of 10).
2. **`skill_workshop` schema.** The personal-library schema is published only on human turns that carry an authoring grant. A wake publishes a narrower schema, the dynamic tool catalog fingerprint changes, and the bound thread rotates. The Claude CLI runner already fixed this in #172026 (`resolveStableCliSkillAuthoring`); the embedded/harness path never used it.
3. **Conversation context.** An internal (WebChat) session stores no delivery route, so `buildSessionEventContext` never matched the wake's own WebChat route and dropped the session chat type. The wake's developer instructions then lacked the "You are in a WebChat direct conversation" line, the live thread config fingerprint changed, and Codex had to cold-resume the thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each layer is fixed where the difference starts, without widening authority:

- **Scope (A).** A cap from a conversation-scoped producer turn is the session's own policy, and the follow-up re-derives that policy itself. `createCodingToolsGatewayCaller` marks the caller identity session-scoped when the policy scope is `conversation` and no caller-supplied source policy exists, and `session-event-target` skips it only when the follow-up's destination is the same session. The mark is not set when group, per-DM, or sender policy narrowed the producer (`groupPolicy`/`senderPolicy`). Those come from the inbound request, the wake cannot rebuild them, and the cap keeps carrying them. The caller-inheritance merge keeps the mark only for an inherited owner of the same agent and session that has no narrower cap of its own. Cross-session follow-ups, sender-narrowed producers, and turn-scoped producers keep the cap exactly as before.
- **Policy lifetime stays host-owned.** No public SDK option is added. The host already computes the attempt's policy lifetime for Codex (`pluginHarnessToolPolicyScope`, `resolvePluginHarnessToolPolicies`). Host policy preparation now records that value in the attempt's host capability, and the host's tool construction (`createToolSurfaceAsync`, which is how Codex builds every dynamic tool) passes it to the internal tool options. A plugin cannot set it through tool options: a plugin-supplied `toolPolicyScope` is overwritten by the host value, and when the host has none the cap stays in place (fail-closed).
- **`skill_workshop` (B).** The #172026 helper moves from `cli-runner/` to `src/agents/stable-skill-authoring.ts` as a per-runtime factory and is also applied at the embedded attempt dispatch. Internal turns publish the session's last human shape with an expired grant: the declaration matches, personal-library calls fail with `AUTHORITY_EXPIRED`, and workspace calls keep the ordinary no-grant rule (unsandboxed runs only). Grants that are already expired (transcript follow-ups, stranded-reply recovery) now carry `expired: true` and no longer replace the remembered human shape.
- **Context (C).** For a session that stores no delivery route, an event on that session's own WebChat route (`channel: "webchat"`, `to: <sessionKey>`, the shape `chat.send` and subagent announce already use) keeps the session chat type. Events routed to any other session still get none.

Out of scope, noted for follow-up: when a thread's config does change (for example a model switch), Codex can take longer than OpenClaw's 2-second unload budget to close a code-mode thread after `thread/unsubscribe` (measured 0.7 s, 2.9 s, and 10.6 s in this harness). The cold resume then fails with "Codex did not confirm unloading its previous configuration". With this change, completion wakes no longer take that path.

AI-assisted: written with Claude Code. Every claim below was checked by running it.

## User Impact

- Background `exec` completion wakes in Codex-backed sessions continue the bound thread with native code mode on. The wake reads the session prefix from cache instead of replaying the full history uncached, and the next user turn stays on the same thread.
- No tool, personal-library, or workspace access is widened. Sessions narrowed by group, per-DM, or sender policy keep today's behavior, including the fresh-thread wake.
- On internal turns with a remembered personal default target, `skill_workshop` calls that rely on that default now return `AUTHORITY_EXPIRED` instead of running against the workspace. Explicit `target=workspace` calls keep the no-grant rule.

## Evidence

Regression tests, each shown failing without its fix and passing with it:

| Test | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| `host-capability.tool-policy-scope.test.ts` (new): host-prepared scope reaches tool construction; a plugin-supplied `toolPolicyScope: "conversation"` does not | 2 failed, 1 passed (host value not injected) | 3 passed |
| `session-event-permissions.test.ts` "bounds a same-session background completion's final effects: same-session" | fails: `writeOffered: false`, expected `true` (the producer cap is kept) | passes |
| `agent-tools.session-event-cap.test.ts` "a sender narrowed by toolsBySender" (real `createOpenClawCodingTools`, real caller identity, no mock) | fails: `expected true to be undefined` when the sender check is removed | 3 passed |
| `stable-skill-authoring.test.ts` "keeps the human shape when a follow-up passes an expired grant" | 1 failed, 3 passed | 4 passed |
| `session-event-context.test.ts` "keeps the session chat type only for $route" | 1 failed, 2 passed | 3 passed |
| `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` "offers the human turn's skill_workshop definition on an internal turn" | asserts the surfaces differ without the helper | equal with it |

### Authority controls around the same-session exemption

`session-event-permissions.test.ts` "bounds a same-session background completion's final effects" runs the production path: a real `captureSessionEventTargetForHost` under a caller identity, the real `enqueueSessionEventForHost` admission, the real harness host capabilities and managed tool surface, and a real file write. Each row captures a producer whose ceiling lists only `read`:

| Row | Producer identity | Follow-up tool surface | File after the follow-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| `same-session` | same session, marked session-scoped | `write` offered | written |
| `restricted-sender` | same session, not marked (the caller leaves the mark off when `senderPolicy` or `groupPolicy` narrowed the turn; see the caller test above) | no `write` | unchanged |
| `cross-session` | other session, marked | no `write` | unchanged |
| `revoked-before-write` | same session, marked; the session permission mode is set to `read-only` after the tool surface is built | `write` offered, call refused (authority/permission error) | unchanged |

Result: 4 passed. With `session-event-target.ts` restored to its base version, the `same-session` row fails (`writeOffered: false`).

Expired personal-library calls: `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` builds the real coding tools for an internal turn and shows `skill_workshop` with `target: "personal"` rejected with "fresh message" (`AUTHORITY_EXPIRED`). `stable-skill-authoring.test.ts` shows an expired grant refuses personal-library calls and never replaces the remembered human shape; the sandboxed-run refusal for workspace calls is unchanged code from #172026 and is not re-tested here.

What this does not show: the embedded dispatch wiring (`resolveStableEmbeddedSkillAuthoring` at `run-attempt-dispatch.ts`) is a single call covered by the two tests above through the same factory, not by a dispatch-level test.

Touched suites: the files above plus `gateway-caller-context.test.ts` and `agent-tools.delegated-authority.test.ts` pass. The new production-boundary rows pass 4 of 4. `tsgo` core and the `src` test shards: clean. `oxfmt` on the repository: clean. `check:test-mock-exports` and `check:max-lines-ratchet` against the base commit: OK (the PR adds no mock factory and no line to `agent-tools.ts` or `cli-runner/prepare.ts`).

### Required test lanes that fail on this PR's CI

Three required lanes failed on the earlier heads. Each was checked against `main`:

- `src/gateway/mcp-http.exec-completion.test.ts` "an empty CLI final": fails the same way with every file this PR touches restored to `origin/main` (`1e89f5b3fe8`), and fails in CI on unrelated PRs (for example https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40290743775 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40292785214). It is inherited.
- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts` "drains a restored interrupted predecessor before later cohorts": fails the same way with the PR's files restored to `origin/main`, and fails in CI on an unrelated PR (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40292474849). It is inherited.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.operator-continuation.test.ts`: all 20 tests pass locally on this branch merged with `origin/main`. I could not reproduce the CI failure. By construction this PR cannot reach that path: the new session-scoped marking requires `toolPolicyScope: "conversation"`, which that test never sets, so its follow-up ceiling is unchanged. I did not find this failure on another PR, so I cannot call it inherited.

Live run against a real Codex app-server (codex 0.162.1, the version pinned on `main`), an isolated gateway, and `chat.send`. Script: user turn, a turn that starts `exec` with `background=true`, the completion wake, then a user turn. Wire capture of the app-server JSON-RPC, base `4fa442e3327`:

```
# stock (4fa442e3327)
in thread/start None dynTools=10
-> thread thread-A
# user turn
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20064 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# user turn that starts the background exec
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20204 cached= 20061
usage thread-A in= 21343 cached= 20201
usage thread-A in= 21589 cached= 21340
out turn/completed thread-A completed
in thread/start None dynTools=48
-> thread thread-B
# completion wake (turn 1 of 2)
in turn/start thread-B
usage thread-B in= 29269 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-B completed
in thread/start None dynTools=48
-> thread thread-C
# completion wake (turn 2 of 2)
in turn/start thread-C
usage thread-C in= 29183 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-C completed
```

```
# this branch
in thread/start None dynTools=10
-> thread thread-A
# user turn
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20064 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# user turn that starts the background exec
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20204 cached= 20061
usage thread-A in= 21336 cached= 20201
usage thread-A in= 21632 cached= 21333
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# completion wake (turn 1 of 2)
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 21761 cached= 21629
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# completion wake (turn 2 of 2)
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 21830 cached= 21758

```

The live run used commit 591bd2b60aa on base `4fa442e3327`. The branch was then rebased onto `d4ae3a73118` without conflicts. Typecheck and the regression and affected suites were rerun after the rebase. Commit `80b8c1192d9` came later: it moves the marking decision into `createCodingToolsGatewayCaller` and adds the tests above, with no change to the runtime behavior traced here; the live trace was not repeated.

Stock: each wake turn starts a fresh thread with 48 dynamic tools and 0 cached tokens. Patched: one thread with 10 dynamic tools for the whole session. The wake turns are plain `turn/start` calls on the bound thread, reading 99% of their input from cache, with no `thread/resume` or `thread/unsubscribe` in the wire log. The next user turn stays on the same thread. (The stock run's next user turn did not reach the app-server before the harness stopped, so it is not shown.)

What this evidence does not show: the harness covers a WebChat direct session with no group, per-DM, or sender policy. Sessions with those policies are covered by the unit tests above, not by a live run.

prs.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): tool-returned images fail on GPT-6/6.1 Sol and Kimi K3
prs.body:
Closes #186753

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: image-reading tools fail with `Validation error: This model doesn't support the image field for user messages` on Amazon Bedrock GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol and Kimi K3 (and any other non-Nova/non-Claude route), because OpenClaw nests tool-returned images inside `toolResult.content`.

## User Impact

User impact: agents on any Bedrock route can read images returned by tools; Nova and Claude keep today's nested layout unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

AWS documents [`ToolResultContentBlock.image`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_ToolResultContentBlock.html) as supported only by Amazon Nova and Anthropic Claude. The previous fix (#149336) special-cased `openai.gpt-5.6-sol`, so every new route needed another name match (as #186834 / #186835 propose). This change inverts the selector: Nova and Claude keep nested images, and every other route, including unknown routes and opaque application-inference-profile ARNs, uses the existing labeled sibling-image relocation, which was accepted by every route tested, Nova and Claude included. Claude detection reuses the existing `isAnthropicClaudeModel`, so Claude behind an application profile with a Claude name/canonical id stays nested.

The relocation body moved unchanged into `tool-result-images.ts`. `stream.runtime.ts` was already over its line cap, and the line-cap ratchet rejects any growth there.

Accepted edge case: Nova behind an opaque application-profile ARN gets the sibling layout. Nova accepts user image blocks, so the request still succeeds.

## Evidence

**Regression test** (`stream.runtime.test.ts`, the existing relocation test extended to GPT-6.1 Sol, Kimi K3 and an opaque profile ARN; asserts Nova and Claude stay nested): red on `origin/main`, green with the fix.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock
 Test Files  13 passed (13)
      Tests  160 passed (160)
```

**Live Bedrock ConverseStream through `streamSimpleBedrock`** (us-east-1, synthetic 64×64 PNG with a red square and a blue circle; one assistant turn with two parallel tool calls, one returning the image and one returning `status: GREEN-42`):

| Route | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `global.openai.gpt-6-sol` | ❌ ValidationException (image field) | ✅ "a red square and a blue circle … GREEN-42" |
| `global.openai.gpt-6.1-sol` | ❌ ValidationException (image field) | ✅ |
| `global.moonshotai.kimi-k3` | ❌ ValidationException (image field) | ✅ |
| `global.openai.gpt-5.6-sol` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0` (nested) | ✅ | ✅ |
| `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` (nested) | ✅ | ✅ |
| `global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5` (nested) | — | ✅ |

The input context was byte-identical after every request, so stored history is not rewritten.

**Real agent turn** (`openclaw agent exec --config <pinned bedrock config> --cwd <dir with shapes.png + status.txt>`, prompt asks for both files to be read with the `read` tool in one step):

- `main`, GPT-6.1 Sol: `status: "error"`, `Validation error: This model doesn't support the image field for user messages. Remove image and try again.` after 5 retried model requests.
- This PR, GPT-6.1 Sol: `ok`, "The image shows a red square on the left and a blue circle on the right. “status: GREEN-42”"
- This PR, Kimi K3: `ok`, "…a red square on the left and a blue circle on the right. Status line: `status: GREEN-42`"
- This PR, Claude Sonnet 5.5: `ok`, "…a red square on the left and a blue circle on the right, on a white background. The status line reads: "status: GREEN-42""

**Gates:** `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes green (typecheck extensions/tests, lint, format, line-cap ratchet, plugin boundaries) except `dead export scan`. That lane reports 86 existing unused exports, all under `src/` (gateway, infra, agents, sessions), and none in `extensions/amazon-bedrock`. `git diff --check` clean.

Gap: the live agent proof used the embedded `agent exec` path rather than a separate Gateway process. The provider stream path exercised is the same.

The temporary tsrs release-age exceptions remained after their documented expiration.

## User Impact

## Evidence

Verified the root and all five platform packages passed the documented seven-day cutoff. A frozen install succeeded under the normal policy, and `git diff --check` passed. This is a seven-line metadata cleanup.

The workflow leaves `dependency-cache` disabled, so it does not compute or use the semantic dependency-cache fingerprint. Its pnpm store cache hit, while every dist-build restore key missed, including the broad prefix. The previous fingerprint hypothesis therefore does not explain this failure. Runtime sources, build commands, package versions and lockfile are unchanged.

The underlying cold-build timeout remains unexplained. A passing cached build is not a cold-build reproduction, and no matching baseline timeout or successful rerun is claimed.

## Landing Status

Required checks passed. The retained native maintainer workflow cannot admit this attributed optional secondary-workflow failure: its ordinary route rejects an unsuperseded failed check, while its failed-CI exception accepts only a failed `ci.yml` attempt. prs.title: fix(agents): don't stop CLI-backed replies as stalled while the model is still thinking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

CLI-backed replies could be stopped as stalled even though the model was still producing new thinking. That thinking did not count as semantic progress.

## User Impact

Long reasoning turns on CLI backends now keep running instead of being cut off by stall recovery. Fuller reasoning output still displays. Configured limits stay unchanged. No extra configuration or migration is required; nothing has been deployed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The parser marks fresh thinking text and positive per-message thinking-token deltas as progress. The handler credits the current attempt only after the output-suppression guard allows the output. Replays, prefixes, heartbeats, stale output, tool-owned output and yielded output never count. An optional SDK hook makes one private, read-only assessment before semantic stall recovery. It is limited to 10 seconds or the remaining hard budget, whichever is shorter. Unavailable, obsolete or failed captures resolve once as unknown, so capture cannot loop. Without a hook, the existing recovery path runs with no added delay. The stop, hard-deadline and attempt/backend registration fences are unchanged. The change does not swap models or threads or send a new Claude health ping. The adapter reports only current local facts or unknown. This change does not cover the separate CLI no-output timer or general node and supervisor health.

Test-size tradeoff: this PR no longer changes `config/test-lines-baseline.txt`. Main now carries a measured 6,320,000 ceiling (#187030); the merged tree contains 6,243,715 test lines (76,285 slack). This is a test-size ratchet, not a watchdog budget.

## Evidence

- Current head: `c8517dae82af70449183cac4e490cafe4932951f`, which merges main `d44b7df3` into `03d06ad4`. The only conflict was the test-line ceiling; it takes main's value, which drops this PR's earlier +649 raise. The repair commit `f633ba42` merged main `bf6a97a1` onto the previous head `7d376121` and fixed its three CI failures:
  - **Import cycles (madge):** `session-controller.watchdog.ts` imported the backend handle contracts, which pulled agents, auto-reply and config back into the infra diagnostics that import the watchdog. The turn-status contracts now live in two import-free leaves (`src/plugins/cli-backend-turn-status.types.ts`, `src/sessions/session-controller.turn-status.types.ts`). The assessment slot takes structural attempt/backend views. The Claude status adapter no longer imports `cli.runtime.ts`. The SDK exports the same names from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/cli-backend`.
  - **Test types:** the deliberately malformed assessment fixture now casts through `unknown`.
  - **Merge conflict:** `execute-plugin.policy.test.ts` keeps both the turn-assessment suite and main's new schema-discovery test.
- **Test-line ceiling:** `03d06ad4` raised the ceiling by this PR's 649 net test lines. That raise is gone on `c8517dae`: main's own headroom covers the PR, and the ratchet passes with the baseline file identical to main.
- Focused tests: 203 passed across the 6 changed test files (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on the watchdog, plugin policy, command-progress, output events, output reasoning and Anthropic runtime suites). On `c8517dae`, core, core-test, extension, extension-test and agents-other types, madge and runtime import cycles all pass. One Anthropic test outside this diff, `session-catalog.test.ts` › "reports the discovery frontier and finds and reads an exact ID beyond it", fails locally on unmodified main `d44b7df3` as well.
- `check:changed` against `bf6a97a1`: core, core-test, extension and extension-test types, changed-file lint, format, madge and runtime import cycles, plugin boundaries and deprecated-API guards pass. Two stages fail identically on unmodified main `bf6a97a1`: the plugin SDK surface budget (160/3841/2226 on both) and the dead-export scan (only files this PR does not touch).
- AutoReview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, branch `bf6a97a1..f633ba42`): **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Diff-only evidence; it did not execute code.
- **Inherited failure:** `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-session-steering.e2e.test.ts` › "cancels queued work visibly when Stop targets the whole session" fails with `pendingInputs.total` 1 instead of 0. It fails identically on unmodified main `bf6a97a1` (local run, same assertion). It runs in this PR's `checks-node-changed` shard. CI on `f633ba42` and `03d06ad4` confirmed it: `checks-node-changed-1` fails only on this test, and every other check passed on `03d06ad4`. The failure is not in this PR's watchdog or CLI paths.
- Still not proven: a real shipped CLI/Gateway turn past the semantic stall window. The long-duration proof is synthetic.

<details>
<summary>Previous head `7d376121` evidence (superseded)</summary>

- Head: `7d37612183c869206a4b5fcae673a7c99885ce6a`, a signed merge preserving the contributor's commits and integrating main `19f4a68b4aaf0e4b02422829fc49e86fb27e1802`. All three conflicts are resolved; private steering-context handling and native status invalidation remain covered.
- Focused validation: **204 tests passed across 7 files**, including every changed test file and the steering consumer. Core and extension TypeScript checks, targeted production/test lint, formatting, test-line ratchet, and diff checks pass.
- Full `pnpm build` passes on the corrected head. The previous declaration/build blocker is no longer present on this integrated tree.
- Fresh local AutoReview (Codex, P0–P2) of the complete staged candidate against main `19f4a68b` completed **scoped-clean** with no accepted findings; the signed commit preserves that reviewed tree. This was source-only and did not include unchanged context. A separate independent source review covered the determining modules on the incoming head with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- **Still pending:** required exact-head CI and a real shipped CLI/Gateway turn beyond the semantic stall window. The existing long-duration proof remains synthetic; it is not evidence of live vendor behavior. The PR is not yet merge-ready and has not been deployed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Original-head evidence (historical; superseded statuses retained for context)</summary>

- AutoReview (Codex through the configured ClawRouter, P0–P2), base c8b7c4c4 → head 9e7808f7: **incomplete, not clean**. It ran 7 passes with 0 accepted findings. 4 batches had gaps in determining context, and a full intact pass would not fit the fixed 512k prompt capacity. Published head 93178e78 has the same tree.
- [Hosted ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186446#issuecomment-6459136186) reviewed 93178e78 against main dafda2f7. It found no code issues but says the merge conflicts must be fixed before merge.
- Two independent local source reviews passed, and the code-comment contract audit reported no open questions. I deferred one non-blocking nit from an earlier review.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 81 passed. Across all 8 affected files, 225 passed with 1 existing Linux skip. That result comes from 9e7808f7 and is reused because the inputs did not change.
- Real parser/handler/watchdog tests failed 2 cases before the fix and pass after it. Obsolete-capture tests went from 3 failed and 24 passed on the old code to all 27 passing.
- Local core lint, format, diff check, SDK import/export and ratchets pass. The canonical store declaration guard blocks the core SDK compiler and extension typed lint, so I don't claim a static compiler pass. The full build is unproven, and CI is pending.
- No shipped CLI or Gateway turn has run past the semantic stall window. The proof comes from a harness with real modules and a synthetic native process, not live vendor behavior.
- Three merge conflicts with main remain. This PR is not merge-ready and has not been merged or deployed.

</details>

prs.title: fix: stop replaying completed turns with legacy saved replies
prs.body:
Related: #166300
Related: #166340

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes completed conversations restarting themselves when a legacy saved final has no durable delivery identity.

## User Impact

Routine restarts no longer run those old turns or send resumption notices. New authenticated input can continue in the same conversation. The saved reply, capture time, and route remain in one local transcript artifact explicitly marked delivery-unconfirmed; unrelated delivery notices remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing pending-final owner recognizes a completed run with a matching terminal marker and no unfinished execution, delivery, harness, or started-attempt owner. It reuses atomic local settlement instead of dispatching another model turn. There is no external replay, tombstone, synthesized notice debt, age cutoff, schema change, or new state owner. Identified pending finals and genuine interrupted work retain their normal recovery path.

This handles the pending-final variant adjacent to #166340, whose draft deliberately excludes pending finals. It does not close the full unmatched-fence report. Terminal execution cannot prove historical channel delivery: the original reply stays available locally rather than being blindly resent. Recovery-owner acceptance of this historical-state disposition is requested before merge.

## Evidence

- On pinned main, an isolated SQLite startup regression reaches the actual runtime boundary and fails its zero-call assertion. With the change, it settles without runtime, model/tool, notice, or final-send calls.
- The regression checks the completed run/end time, saved text and metadata, preservation of an acknowledged unrelated notice, same-session foreground admission, and stable repeated startup without duplicate artifacts.
- 17 focused tests passed: the 13-test terminal/startup suite plus four interrupted, identified pending-final, and notice controls. The terminal suite passed again with the exact terminal-writer residue fixture (13/13; 14.98s command wall).
- Production core types, the agent-session test type graph, targeted lint/format, line-cap and SQLite-worker ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed. No new main-thread SQLite calls (171→171).
- Proof uses synthetic state and a rejecting runtime boundary, not live provider/channel traffic or an installed-updater run. The full repository suite was not run.
- Focused validation passed: 17 selected tests; the final terminal-writer startup fixture suite passed 13/13. Core and affected test types, targeted lint/format, the SQLite worker ratchet, and diff checks passed.
- Independent `autoreview` reviewed all five changed files in full plus the startup, settlement, transcript transaction/CAS and foreground-admission owners; no actionable P0–P2 findings. Secret scanning of the complete candidate diff passed. This is an AI-assisted contribution.

Simplification kept classification and atomic settlement with their existing owners and cut over the sole classification caller. No competing recovery machinery was added. Production delta: +85/−20; tests: +94/−2; docs: +8.


### Shipped Gateway behavior proof (2026-10-21)

Exact-head isolated Gateway restart proof passed: no historical provider execution, saved reply retained locally as delivery-unconfirmed, and a fresh authenticated turn completed. Full sanitized evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178732#issuecomment-6306233298

Latest-stable upgrade/data compatibility proof also passed: released v2026.10.5 settings, transcript, and an identified pending-final obligation survived the documented Doctor migration and current-Gateway startup. Full sanitized evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178732#issuecomment-6306282928\n\nOnly the maintainer disposition decision remains open.

<!-- upstream-integration-2026-10-26:start -->
### Current main integration — 2026-10-26

Merged current main while preserving both completed legacy-final retirement and terminally failed legacy-continuation settlement. Current owner custody and failed/timeout/killed outcomes remain distinct. Focused completed/failure/delivery tests, targeted types/lint, formatting and independent P0-P2 review passed.

Reviewed integration base: `f84df5359d794f2d682769c6446cefabb99e9961`. Updated PR head: `afd39278718e173f3142335801da9d7b99fe4a54`.

Required hosted CI gates for this exact updated head succeeded (CI, dependency review and security-sensitive review): [exact-head checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/afd39278718e173f3142335801da9d7b99fe4a54/checks). No current check failure or pending check remained at readback. Fresh ClawSweeper review completed on this same head: the completed-child interruption finding is resolved, with no remaining code finding. The historical-delivery disposition remains a maintainer decision. Existing maintainer product/API decisions remain open. No downstream runtime or modified package was distributed.

The fresh upstream review identified a real integration defect from main's child-interruption notification owner: preserving an already completed legacy child also recorded a false interruption in its surviving parent's transcript. Completed-outcome settlement now skips only that interruption notice; genuine interrupted-child notices remain. A regression through startup marking, recoverStore and the real parent transcript failed before the guard and passed afterward, alongside the genuine-interruption control. Focused terminal/residue tests, targeted types/lint/format and independent P0-P2 review passed. This restores the intent of main's child-interruption notification change without changing the proposed historical-delivery disposition.

prs.title: fix: Gateway stops report cleanup failure after an exec is refused before launch
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after one exec call is refused before its command starts, every later Gateway shutdown reports an owned-process cleanup failure. A typical trigger is a tool call whose signal times out while the relay waits for launch permission.

## User Impact

User impact: a clean stop or restart no longer fails with "Plugin runtime still owns resources" or "service child cleanup identity lost" just because an exec was cancelled before launch earlier in the process. Real identity loss is still reported.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the relay anchor sends `prepared`, it has no command yet. It is waiting for the launch frame. If the launch-authority check threw before the host wrote that frame, the relay host treated the refusal as identity loss and rejected cleanup without a receipt. The process supervisor keeps that rejection for the life of the process, so every later `shutdown()` rethrew it.

Now the POSIX control sender returns a distinct `ServiceChildLaunchNotInitiatedError`, but only when `launch()` was never called. In that case the host fails startup with the original refusal, starts the normal cleanup deadline and sends `cancel`. The anchor already handles that message. It reports "command startup cancelled before spawn", and its closing receipt retires the relay through the usual extinction join.

Cleanup still fails closed when the frame may have been written, when the anchor never answers (the hard deadline fires), or when the relay has already left `starting`. That matches the rule from openclaw/openclaw#183247 that missing closing evidence rejects cleanup.

`bash-tools.exec-launch-policy.integration.test.ts` used to require shutdown to reject after a retained-child refusal before launch. That expectation pinned the bug. The test now checks that the refusal reached the relay's launch boundary and that shutdown is clean, and its unused `expectedCleanupFailure` plumbing is gone.

Start-frame construction moves into `service-child-relay-preparation.ts` without behavior changes, so `service-child-relay-host.ts` stays under its 700-line cap. The Windows `BrokerChild` launch path is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New real-relay test `supervisor.prelaunch-initiation.real.test.ts`. A refusal before the launch frame rejects with the original `TimeoutError`, the command never runs, a later spawn succeeds, and `shutdown()` resolves. The negative control refuses after calling `launch()`, and shutdown stays fenced.
- `service-child-relay-host.test.ts`. The revoked-at-`prepared` case now plays the anchor's `startup-error` and `closing` replies and gets the original refusal back. A new case checks that a silent anchor still hits the hard deadline.
- Red/green on `d44b7df3`. With the new tests on unmodified sources, 4 of 58 fail, and they are exactly the new and changed cases. With the fix, all 58 pass across the six affected relay, supervisor and exec launch-policy files.
- `pnpm test -- src/process/supervisor src/process/spawn-broker` passed 356 tests with 0 failures and 77 platform skips.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed typecheck for core and core tests, lint, format, and the line-cap and max-lines checks. Two checks failed on code outside this diff. The first-party mock export check flags `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts` and fails the same way on clean `origin/main`. The dead-export scan lists 41 exports, none in files this PR touches.
- Seen in production. A refusal at 19:58Z showed up at a 20:23Z Gateway stop as "Failed to reset global singleton lifecycle state", wrapping "service child cleanup identity lost: TimeoutError: request timed out".

prs.title: fix(pr): unblock attributed artifact-build failures after primary CI passes
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184660

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: maintainer merge admission rejects an attributed optional artifact-build failure despite successful primary CI, and a PR bound to older tooling cannot select current tooling before its first merge intent.

## User Impact

Maintainers gain an explicit admin admission route for the documented artifact-build workflow only. Primary CI, security, every required check, exact-head review and preparation, and confirmed operator authority remain mandatory. The new tooling must land through the existing trusted workflow before use.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the failed artifact run, failed review result, unchanged-input attribution and evidence intact while separately verifying the successful primary run. Bind failed jobs to current optional check identities; other failures and newer artifact runs still block admission.

Allow explicit `merge-run --current-workflow --admin-evidence <file> --confirmed-operator-admin` only when no outcome or unresolved capture exists. Native locks and official-main source verification preserve the original binding, with provenance retained through older bound tooling's reconciliation and completion.

## Evidence

- Prior proof at `2383aec34a06`: 329 focused cases passed across runs in the artifact, current-workflow, prior-CI, authority, cancellation, recovery, outcome and binding suites.
- Expected-red proof reproduced the frozen baseline's artifact-run refusal. A separate overlay of the bound `merge-outcome.sh` from `2f36ac26164d` passed lost-acknowledgment reconciliation, old-writer succession/completion and current-reader verification, with one merge and one comment.
- At that same head, canonical tooling test typecheck, changed script/test lint, formatting parity, docs lint, staged line-cap ratchet and private-content guard passed. Live GitHub API checks verified the new inventory fields and native optional-check markers.
- Two-pass autoreview of `77c9dc706b3e..2383aec34a06` returned `scoped-clean` at P0–P2 with zero findings; signed commit tree matches the final proven source capsule.
- At `7a81691754e5`, [artifact admission CI proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40633581283/job/122635871273) passed all 19 cases, including the three final-writer cases below. [Authority and REST-observation siblings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40633581283/job/122635871307) passed 22 and 59 cases respectively. These are fresh follow-up results; the earlier 329-case proof is separate.
- [Primary CI run `40633581283`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40633581283) completed successfully at exact head `7a81691754e5`, including the remaining compact suite and aggregate gate.
- One-pass autoreview of `2383aec34a06..7a81691754e5` returned `scoped-clean` at P0–P2 with zero findings; the new execution proof is linked above.
- Net LOC: +261 production for exact API qualification and locked admission provenance; +418 tests, including this +111-line test-only follow-up. Ordinary watcher and cancellation contracts remain unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Observed final-effect trace at 7a81691754e5</summary>

prs.title: fix(update): stop a newer CLI from migrating state the Gateway service still runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A bare global npm install under a different Node can leave a newer CLI beside an older managed Gateway. Even an ordinary CLI config-health write could then migrate shared state forward and prevent that Gateway from starting.

Fixes #186898. Thanks @tomdailey55 for the report and recovery details.

## User Impact

The CLI refuses a forward migration when the service definition proves an older installation will open the same state. The error names both versions, the service root, and the update command. Current-schema databases and unknown service installations keep their existing behavior.

Status, Doctor, and Gateway status explain installation skew; Gateway startup also warns about a different CLI on PATH. A newer-schema startup failure names the existing writer version and recovery action instead of presenting a config-key error. Only a strictly newer writer version is described as newer than the Gateway; same-version and unknown writers retain the original schema-support and backup guidance. Runtime readers retain their inspection advice; Doctor maintenance never recommends rerunning Doctor for a newer schema and omits an uninformative same-version writer sentence. The updating guide explains Node/global-prefix differences and the managed updater's installation ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

The schema runtime owns the decision immediately before migration effects. CLI inspection reads the package belonging to the service definition's entrypoint and carries those facts through SQLite worker admission and reuse keys. Doctor checks agent-only pending migrations too. The native updater retains its existing verified maintenance/rehearsal path.

Deferred publication of already-applied content stays with its existing owner; shipped older readers already reject the newer content version before publication.

No SQLite schema, persisted field, dependency, config option, or CLI option changed. Writer diagnostics reuse `schema_meta.app_version`.

## Evidence

### Main integration — `b978c049fedd6bcb015f2730f2a348b8e6626a02`

Merged `origin/main` at `e25c026eb75d34ecdeed1d64d68454fb919f3c19` (including #187120) with a two-parent merge; no rebase. Git applied the merge without textual conflicts. The three named tests (`status.gather`, `run.option-collisions`, and `server-startup-schema-refusal`) retain the existing L1939 expectations unchanged while main's cron receipt synchronization and mock-export cleanup are included. No additional production or test changes were needed. This integration supersedes the earlier cron race/main-baseline failure evidence below.

Proof on the merged source, with isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under this worktree's `.artifacts/l1939-main-merge/`:

- Full `pnpm build`: exit 0, 237.35 s wall; includes `check-cli-bootstrap-imports` (10.6 s), SDK exports/declarations and Control UI packaging.
- Same 11 focused files through `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node|bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <files> --maxWorkers=1`: Node 210 passed (235.16 s wall); pinned Bun 202 passed, 7 existing runtime-specific skips (250.50 s wall). All named merge-boundary tests and all four cron routes passed on both runtimes.
- Node/Bun cron file: 63.05/75.28 s wall, about 17/35 s summed test time; no individual case exceeded 30 s. Doctor finish/revalidation: 53.64/79.49 s wall. No flaky replay or timeout/assertion changes.
- Touched-file oxlint and oxfmt, targeted test types, and `git diff --check`: pass.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base origin/main`: pass, 6486 grandfathered factories.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main`: pass, 6,243,623 lines against 6,320,000 ceiling. The ceiling is inherited unchanged from merged main; this PR does not raise it. Relative to merged main, the mock baseline only removes the three entries already made obsolete by this PR's real-export-preserving mocks.
- Isolated Codex review of the complete merged candidate against pinned main: no actionable P0/P1 findings. The initial review setup rejected shared scratch; rerun used the macOS private temporary directory with isolation intact.

The 11 files were `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/run.option-collisions.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-schema-refusal.test.ts`, `src/infra/sqlite-worker-shared-state.test.ts`, `src/cron/service.failure-alert-notifications.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts`, `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.finish-revalidation.test.ts`, `src/state/openclaw-agent-db.checkonce.test.ts`, `src/state/openclaw-state-db-checkonce.test.ts`, and `src/infra/sqlite-user-version.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(pr): avoid piped-input stalls during baseline preparation
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177381

## What Problem This Solves

Baseline preparation can stop at write-mode blob hashing while Git waits for piped stdin. The observed interruption occurred during signed baseline reconstruction; its lower-level pipe failure remains unknown.

## User Impact

Maintainer preparation uses a completed input snapshot for both hashing and storing blobs. Existing object contents, executable modes, signatures, review requirements, and admission rules stay intact.

This change does not release the retained lock or replace the immutable workflow binding for #177381. That task still needs a supported lifecycle decision.

## Why This Change Was Made

Write-mode hashing now uses the existing private, read-only, unlinked snapshot path and retains Git's `-w --no-filters` semantics. Removing the separate pipe path keeps one input lifecycle and preserves cleanup and Git error diagnostics.

Production: −1 line; tests: +51; documentation: +1. The tests extend real signed replay and correction validation, retaining existing read-mode cases.

## Evidence

- Frozen base: `d5f7d57eff508f815ef03f6560ca12b2b3d4aa0a`; signed head: `b65d471a7a774644d14281d990c1babba297105e`; reviewed five-file diff SHA256 `0f2d933f42f2c713b30840c01ff2fac80ad3d93c5344f19f58f0e0811a0b0641`.
- Actual baseline/correction owner CLI proof on the identical source postimage, subsequently committed unchanged, using Node 24.22.1 and Git 2.56.0: all six expected outcomes passed. Old production rejects the regular-file input contract; the candidate passes an uninstrumented control, CRLF/Unicode executable content, empty content, and 1 MiB binary content. Independent object IDs, complete stored bytes, signed ancestry, correction approval/refusal, and failed-Git cleanup were checked.
- This is deterministic transport-contract red/green proof, not reproduction of the original hang or qualification of the top-level lock/publication wrapper.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stranded checkpoints and skipped cleanup when the standalone Code Mode engine probe fails during parallel execution, result validation, or resource disposal.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186487

## User Impact

Internal measurement-harness repair; executor selection, runtime behavior and defaults are unchanged. Failed measurements now retain checkpoint custody, attempt every cleanup stage and preserve the workload error alongside cleanup errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register continuations at their producer, join launched sibling executions before unwinding, then join all disposals and close the host and scheduler independently. Clear both timers after cleanup settles. The script grows by 43 lines to enforce this ownership boundary; three regression tests exercise late checkpoint returns, rejected disposals and host-close failure.

The investigation report also makes the explicit Node-host selector and remaining QuickJS pool-retirement and cumulative-budget proof gaps visible. This change supplies no new engine performance or ShellBench result.

## Evidence

- Frozen baseline: `a302dc559cf033cefe30d32fe47eefb2d5360b53`.
- Targeted formatting, Node 26 syntax checks for the probe and test, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Local autoreview found no actionable P0–P3 findings (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, medium, Ultrafast; complete local snapshot against the frozen baseline, committed as `19f25595b65f2322958c45494cd38dd8e45deb1c`). An independent read-only review also found no actionable issues and verified the subsequent mechanical fixture-lint corrections.
- [CI at `cef21ce68dc7`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40710375138/job/122895610544) passed all three regression tests under a Bun host; types and changed-file lint also passed. The only failure was the mock-export ratchet, which required isolation reasons for the fixture's four deliberately closed factories. Head `9a45577f275` adds those reasons. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40714243008/job/122908349618) also passed all three regressions under Bun; the full exact-head CI run completed successfully (31 jobs passed, 28 intentionally skipped). Initial fixture lint errors were corrected in `cef21ce68dc7`.
- This checkout has no dependency installation. A focused Blacksmith Testbox was queued, then stopped and reconciled before any test or measurement ran.
- The regression fixture runs the committed synthetic guest strings through a mocked executor boundary; it does not establish real VM behavior.
- Node-host lifecycle/parity validation, standalone success smoke, five alternating fresh-process engine pairs and a new matched ShellBench pilot remain separate qualification work. The pilot must bind a fresh adapter to its source revision and verify both effective `tools.codeMode.executor` and observed execution by that engine; enablement alone cannot establish an engine comparison.

- Exact-head ClawSweeper review found no actionable correctness or security issue. Its optional rank-up asks for a real-executor failure capture. That capture is deferred because this checkout has no qualified dependencies and both focused remote allocations were stopped while queued. The current fixtures prove the script's ownership and cleanup ordering with mocks; they do not establish native worker retirement. A qualified standalone failure capture remains named follow-up work.

- Durable CI follow-up: preserve Node-host execution of the existing lifecycle, engine-parity and failure-phase suites while retaining Bun coverage. The selector's `nodeRequiredFiles` set excludes its members from Bun, including under `dual-all`; simply adding these suites there would trade away coverage. Use the existing selector/runner to add a filtered Node pass for these three suites without duplicating whole infra/agents groups.

Merged as `0aab38aa8acf258fa4696663694cfcca7a08dd0d`. The host-coverage follow-up is tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186866.

prs.title: fix(agents): a quota-class failure should prefer the model chain over a same-profile auth rotation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a quota-class provider failure (HTTP 429 with a usage/plan-limit body), the embedded agent rotates the auth profile and re-runs the **same** model before the configured model-fallback chain is consulted. When the provider has exactly one usable profile - or when the rotation re-selects the profile that just failed - that rotation is a no-op: it spends a provider attempt against the same exhausted plan and delays the chain that could have recovered the run.

The `rate_limit` path already has a rotation cap that escalates to the model chain (`MAX_RATE_LIMIT_PROFILE_ROTATIONS`), and the `overloaded` path escalates through `overloadProfileRotationLimit`. What is missing is the rule that **a rotation which lands on the same profile is not a rotation at all**.

## User Impact

A quota-class failure now advances the model chain in the same failure instead of burning an attempt on the exhausted profile first. A run that has a working fallback chain configured recovers on the first quota error rather than the second.

## Why This Change Was Made

`advanceAuthProfileCandidate` advances by **index** over the prepared auth attempts. When two prepared attempts carry the same profile id (an OAuth attempt and an inline attempt for the same profile, or two routes for one profile), the "rotation" re-selects the profile that just failed and still reports success. The caller then retries the same model against the same exhausted plan.

The fix keeps profile rotation useful whenever it can actually change the credentials:

- The rotation is reported as a rotation only when the active profile changes.
- When the rotation re-selects the failed profile and a model chain is configured, the controller reports "no rotation", so the failover policy resolves to `fallback_model` and the chain advances immediately.
- Without a configured chain the existing same-profile retry is preserved, so a single-model deployment loses nothing.

Scope notes:

- The `overloaded` path is untouched.
- The session/request model-pin contract (#151980) is untouched; this change is about auth profiles, not model pins.
- The failed profile is still marked in cooldown exactly as before; only the decision to *retry* the same profile changes.

Related: #141115 (a 429 must consult the chain - this PR is the ordering half of that class), #151980 (session model pins stay strict; this change touches auth profiles, not model pins), #186418 (the request-level ladder half, carried by #186420).

## Evidence

Focused test run on this branch (rebased onto main at `fdeb8f7e`):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-embedded-agent-run.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts
    -> Test Files  1 passed (1), Tests  42 passed (42)

New coverage in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts`:

- a quota-class rotation that re-selects the failed profile reports no rotation, so the caller advances the model chain;
- a quota-class rotation that moves to a different profile still reports a rotation and still counts toward the rotation cap;
- without a configured model chain the same-profile rotation still retries, so single-model deployments keep their existing recovery.

One existing fixture was updated: "waits for the provider floor before exhausting recovery and rotating credentials" used an `advanceAttemptAuthProfile` stub that returned `true` without moving the active profile. A successful rotation moves the active profile, so the stub now does the same; the assertions are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): agent.run can carry a fallback ladder so a pinned model no longer dead-ends on a quota 429
prs.body:
Closes #186418
Related: #151980, #141115, #181981

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation caller that pins a model on the WebSocket agent.run request loses the agent's configured model-fallback ladder, so a quota-class 429 ends the run instead of advancing to the next candidate.

The request schema had no way to express a chain, so the only lever an automation caller had was to pin a model - which silently suppresses the configured ladder. Operators who configured a working fallback chain for the agent had no caller-side way to keep it alive.

## User Impact

User impact: automation callers can now send an explicit fallback ladder with their agent.run request, so a provider quota window on the pinned model no longer ends the run - the run advances to the next candidate the caller named.

This is opt-in and additive. A request that pins a model and sends no ladder behaves exactly as before: the pin stays strict and the configured chain stays suppressed, which is the contract #151980 asks to keep.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway already had the pieces to carry a run-scoped chain, but the wire protocol could not express one. Rather than relax the strict-pin contract, this change adds an explicit field so the caller states the chain it wants:

- agent.run accepts an optional fallbacks array of provider/model refs. Entries are trimmed, de-duplicated, and bounded to 16.
- The ladder is authorized exactly like a model override: a caller without the model-override scope is rejected with INVALID_REQUEST and a clear message.
- Every named model is checked against the agent's visible model set and the caller's operator authority before the run starts, so a caller cannot widen model access by naming extra chain entries.
- The chain travels with the run as a request-scoped override, so it is used for this run only and does not become session state.

The request-level pin remains the primary model; the ladder only adds candidates behind it.

## Evidence

Focused test runs, both green on this branch (rebased onto main at d2491817):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-request-preflight.test.ts
    -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 33 passed (33)

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts
    -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 44 passed (44)

Typecheck:

    pnpm tsgo:test:root -> exit 0 (all root shards)
    pnpm tsgo:test:packages -> exit 0

New coverage:

- src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-request-preflight.test.ts - a request that carries both a pinned model and a ladder keeps the ladder and reports it as request-scoped; a request with a ladder but no model-override scope is rejected; a request with no ladder leaves the override unset.
- src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts - a request-supplied ladder survives a pinned model during model selection, and a request-supplied chain that names a model the agent cannot use is rejected before the run starts.

Behavior with no fallbacks in the request is unchanged, so existing agent.run callers are unaffected.

Closes #113709.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes invalid trajectory JSON/JSONL exports when a tool argument contains quoted text such as `echo "=== deploy token ==="`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final support-file safety pass currently treats serialized JSON as raw text. A match can consume an escaped quote or delimiter and invalidate an otherwise valid export.
