prs.title: fix(models): a saved login stays invisible to the Gateway when its settings write is rejected
prs.body:
Closes #186949

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after `openclaw models auth login` saves credentials but the provider settings write is rejected (for example a read-only Nix-managed config), the running Gateway is never told about the new credentials. Turns keep failing with HTTP 401 until the Gateway is restarted.

## User Impact

User impact: credentials saved by a login reach the running Gateway even when the settings write fails. The settings failure is still reported exactly as before ("Credentials saved, but provider settings could not be applied: …"), and the Nix-managed config stays untouched. No config or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The login flow saves credentials, writes provider settings, then calls the existing `refreshProviderAuthAfterLogin`. A settings-write error left the `try` before the refresh. The fix runs a best-effort refresh for saved credentials before rethrowing the settings error. The recovery lives in `refreshSavedAuthAfterRejectedSettings` (`auth-refresh.ts`):

- It does nothing when the login was cancelled, and checks current login authority before it starts. A login that lost authority during the failed write reaches neither the `models.authRefresh` RPC nor the hosted `refreshAfterLogin` callback.
- It never throws. A recovery failure, including a hosted callback that aborts and rejects, cannot replace the original `ProviderAuthConfigApplyError` or its cause.
- It does not claim the rejected settings were applied. It only republishes the saved auth state.

Production: `auth.ts` +2/-2, `auth-refresh.ts` +16. Tests: +28/-19 in `auth.test.ts`, +5/-1 in `auth-authority.test-support.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests, red on the base or the previous head:**
  - `auth.test.ts` › "identifies a config failure after credentials are saved and preserves its cause (Gateway refresh)". Expects the `models.authRefresh` call after the rejected settings write. It fails on the base: there is no refresh call.
  - `auth.test.ts` › "… (hosted refresh)". A hosted `refreshAfterLogin` aborts the login and rejects, and the original `ProviderAuthConfigApplyError` and its cause must survive. It fails on the previous head (e742544): the error was replaced by `ProviderCredentialsSavedError`.
  - `auth-authority.test-support.ts` › "does not publish after authority ends at beforeCommit / writeAuthority". These now also assert that neither the hosted callback (beforeCommit) nor the Gateway RPC (writeAuthority) runs. Both fail on the previous head: the refresh ran.
  - All of these pass on this head, together with the other authority cases (8/8).
- **Checks:** type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check` and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass. `tsgo:core:test` passes for the changed graphs (29 shards, run one at a time; the first attempt was killed by host memory pressure).
- **Live run: does not separate base from fix.**
  - Setup: an isolated Gateway built from this checkout, `OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1`, a read-only config.
  - Steps: from a separate CLI process, run `openclaw models auth login --provider moonshot --method api-key`.
    - The CLI reports `Credentials saved, but provider settings could not be applied: Config is managed by Nix …`.
    - The config file's sha256 is unchanged.
    - Without a restart, passive `models.authStatus` (no `refresh`) already lists `moonshot:default`. A model turn through a local stub also uses the saved key.
  - Base and fix behave the same here.
  - The reason: while a Gateway owns the state root, the CLI does not persist locally. It routes the login to the owning Gateway (`models.authLogin`, `src/cli/local-state-owner.ts`), so the credential is written inside the Gateway process, and this path shows no difference. A separate-process write only happens when no Gateway owns the state.
- **Gap, the reported path:** I could not run the reported path (Codex device-code login, "no account" until restart). I have no ChatGPT account. The device-code and token endpoints are fixed to `https://auth.openai.com` in `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts` and cannot be pointed at a local stub through config or environment.
- **Ratchets:**
  - `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (test lines) is expected to fail: `main` is already over the test-line ceiling, and the three added cases are needed to cover the review findings (net +13 test lines). I did not delete unrelated tests to offset them.
  - `auth.ts` is already over the 700-line cap (929 counted lines). With this head it is 935.

prs.title: fix(telegram): match canonically equivalent sticker text in cached search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cached Telegram sticker search misses stickers when the stored description or set name and the typed query use different Unicode composition forms. A sticker cached from a vision description stored decomposed (`Mu\u0308ller` motif) is not found by a user typing the composed `Müller`, and the reverse query misses composed descriptions.

`searchStickers` in `extensions/telegram/src/sticker-cache-store.ts` is the only comparison owner for the cached sticker index: it lowercases the query, the description and the set name, then scores substring and per-word matches.

Precedent: #187024 (same shape: compare canonical forms after the existing lowercase conversion, stored text untouched). Siblings already landed: #186329 (workspace filenames), #186794 and #187024 (cron metadata and run history), #184374 (session titles), #186922 (TUI pickers).

## Why This Change Was Made

The scorer lowercased both operands with `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` but never applied a canonical form, so byte-wise `includes` split visually identical text in the full-description match, the per-word match and the set-name bonus. This change appends `normalize("NFC")` to the query, the description projection and the set-name projection. Cached records keep their original description, set name and emoji; scoring weights, ordering, limit and the returned records are unchanged. No new helper, index, storage migration, option or configuration key.

Production LOC: +6/−3.

Classification: `behavior-preserving` (comparison-only normalization)

## User Impact

Searching the cached sticker index now finds the same sticker when the two sides use different Unicode composition forms, which users experience as "the sticker I described is not found". Unrelated stickers still do not match, and emoji, case and whitespace scoring is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `5bbd7dad23ceffcbb0901e3b78201bb6a680152c`
- Current-main RED baseline: `e85b3c8ddf64f463bf12b5abed67e55253f6a739`
- Production entry: `searchStickers`, the read path behind the Telegram sticker search tool over the plugin-state sticker cache.
- Canonical owner exercised: `searchStickers` in `extensions/telegram/src/sticker-cache-store.ts`
- Decision surface: the typed `query` string scored against cached `description`, `setName` and `emoji`.
- Recorder/readback boundary: the returned `CachedSticker[]` (matched `fileUniqueId`s) from the real plugin-state store fixture, with no Telegram API or model provider calls.
- Acceptance RED: on frozen main, query `Müller` against a cached sticker whose description is `Mu\u0308ller sticker` returns no entries.
- Acceptance GREEN: exact head returns `mueller-unique`, while the existing emoji and `FOX` cases keep their exact result sets and ordering.
- Legal controls: the two pre-existing table cases (`🦊` returning both fox stickers, `FOX` with `limit: 1` returning the first) pass identically on both refs, and the cache-stats case is unaffected.
- Cleanup: isolated remote tree and a temporary plugin-state directory fixture; no production cache, Gateway session, bot token or configuration was touched.

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace

Node 24.22.1, secretless, Vitest single file. `extensions/telegram/src/sticker-cache.test.ts`.

```text

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)
Duration  121.08s (cold transform cache)
```

```text
# GREEN — exact head 5bbd7dad23c + same table case
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
Duration  28.97s
```

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/sticker-cache.test.ts` — 6/6 pass on exact head; the new `Müller` case fails on frozen main.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — clean.
- Not tested: live vision descriptions from a real provider. The scorer is a pure function over cached records and the existing suite already caches real record shapes through the plugin-state fixture; the change touches only the comparison projection.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: +6/−3; Test LOC: +2/−0 (one table row appended to the existing search case).
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the file's existing normalization helper and scoring path; no new search path, index, or config surface.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. Cached records and their stored text are unchanged; only match selection for composition-variant queries changes.

## Merge risk

Two-way door: comparison-only change inside one scorer, fully reversible. The blast radius is cached-sticker match selection and score-derived ordering ties; an incorrect normalization could change which stickers match, but cannot rewrite cached descriptions, set names, emoji, timestamps or index entries.

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu live directory lookups (`channels.directory` peers and groups) miss people and group chats whose stored name is canonically equivalent to the query but stored in the other Unicode composition form. A user whose Feishu `name` is stored decomposed (`Mu\u0308ller`) is not returned for a query typed as composed `Müller`, and the reverse query misses composed names.

Both live listers now share one lookup, `listFeishuDirectoryLive` in `extensions/feishu/src/directory.ts`, which compares the query against `entry.id` and `entry.name`. The same predicate therefore covers user names and group/chat names, on every page of the bounded pagination loop.

Precedent: #187024 (same shape: compare canonical forms after the existing lowercase conversion, stored text untouched). Siblings already landed: #186329 (workspace filenames), #186794 and #187024 (cron metadata and run history), #184374 (session titles), #186922 (TUI pickers).

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared lookup lowercased both operands with `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` but never applied a canonical form, so byte-wise `includes` split visually identical text. This change appends `normalize("NFC")` to `q` and to the two compared fields. Only the comparison projection changes: emitted `ChannelDirectoryEntry`/`FeishuDirectoryGroup` values keep the provider's original spelling, and the peer limit shortcut, group page-token validation, `filter` application, page bound and static fallback are unchanged. No new helper, option, configuration key or storage change.

Production LOC: +4/−3.

Classification: `behavior-preserving` (comparison-only normalization)

## User Impact

Directory search now finds the same user or group when the two sides use different Unicode composition forms, which users experience as "search ignores that name". Genuinely different names still do not match, and ASCII, case and whitespace behavior is unchanged. Returned entries keep their original ids and names, so routing keys are byte-identical for previously matching queries.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

prs.body:
Related: #146408.

## What Problem This Solves

Restores unknown-allowlist warnings when a silent availability probe runs before agent tools are assembled.

## User Impact

Operators receive the existing diagnostic once. Tool selection, deny filtering, filter callbacks and audit reporting keep their behavior. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only a reporting call consumes the existing warning key; silent callers omit the optional callback. MCP adapters preserve the supplied reporter. The existing policy pipeline and bounded cache remain the single owner.

This maintenance normally merges official main `f25b36e95b0161b324ad772127264fb0021c4d6c` to resolve the exact failed test-line ratchet. It adds no author logic, test or budget exception: 13 of the 14 PR files are byte-identical to the previous head; `attempt-tool-prepare.ts` only absorbs upstream removal of the retired restart-recovery path. Relative to current main, the complete proposal is production -9 lines and tests +48 lines. No configuration, dependency, protocol, schema, timeout or assertion changes are introduced.

prs.title: fix(codex): materialize native tool-output images from raw response items
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #153949.

Codex's native `ImageView` tool (and other native tools that hand back an
image) surfaces to OpenClaw as a raw `function_call_output` /
`custom_tool_call_output` response item whose `output` array contains a
nested `{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:image/png;base64,..."}`
entry. `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` (the Codex media owner)
only recognized raw `image_generation_call` items and returned immediately
for anything else, so this event shape was silently dropped.
`readCodexResponseOutput` deliberately omits non-text tool output from the
text transcript on the assumption that the media owner picks it up
(`extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-tool-output.ts:129`), so
the image bytes never reached the transcript or Control UI at all: the
assistant's reply referenced "the screenshot above" while no attachment
existed anywhere.

## What Changed

- `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` now also inspects
  `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output` raw items, scanning
  their `output` array for `input_image` entries.
- Each `image_url` is validated through the existing
  `sanitizeInlineImageDataUrl` guard (same validation already used for
  Codex history payload sanitization) and decoded via the existing
  `parseImageDataUrl` helper.
- Valid images are materialized through the exact same
  `recordImage`/`materializeImage` path already used for
  `image_generation_call` results, so they get the same size cap,
  concurrent-completion dedupe, and delivery/transcript wiring as
  generated images, and are marked as a side effect
  (`hadPotentialSideEffects`).
- Invalid or missing `image_url` values are skipped (fail closed): no
  placeholder, no partial write.

This is scoped to the raw-response-item media owner only; it does not
touch the `image_generation_call` path, billing/side-effect
classification for actual image generation, or the separate
dynamic-tool-image rendering path added in #120577 (which covers a
different event shape — dynamic tool results carried on typed thread
items, not this nested raw `input_image` payload).

## Evidence

New regression test, reverted against the pre-fix source
(`git checkout HEAD~1 -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts`)
to confirm it fails without the change:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
...
FAIL  |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media
AssertionError: Target cannot be null or undefined.
 ❯ extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts:394:34
    392|     const mediaUrl = result.toolMediaUrls?.[0];
    393|
    394|     expect(result.toolMediaUrls).toHaveLength(1);
```

Restored the fix and reran — passes:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media 51ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed | 29 skipped (30)
```

Full relevant suites, all passing (89 tests):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.replay-safety.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.final-media.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.test.ts
...
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # media.test.ts + replay-safety.test.ts: 50 passed
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # run-attempt.final-media.test.ts: 9 passed
Test Files  1 passed (1)   # tool-media-payloads.test.ts: 24 passed
```

Formatting/lint on the changed files:

```
$ npx oxlint extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts
(no issues)
$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
$ git diff --check
(clean)
```

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs`'s repo-wide "line-cap growth ratchet"
check fails in this checkout, but it fails identically (same file list,
same counts) on unmodified `upstream/main` with these two files stashed
out — it's flagging pre-existing large files unrelated to this change,
not anything this PR touches.

`tsgo --noEmit` on the `extensions/codex` project reports 1618 errors in
this checkout, all `TS2307: Cannot find module 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/*'`
(missing generated plugin-sdk type declarations from a partial/source-only
dependency setup) plus pre-existing `any`/`unknown` findings in unrelated
files (e.g. `src/supervision-tools.ts`, `src/session-cli.ts`). Confirmed
the exact same 1618-error count with this branch's two files stashed out
against unmodified `upstream/main` — the type-resolution gap is an
environment limitation of this sandbox, not something introduced here.

Was not able to run a live Codex app-server round-trip in this sandbox (no
Codex credentials/harness available here); the evidence above proves the
event-projection behavior through the same test harness and fixtures the
existing `image_generation_call` regression tests in this file use.

prs.title: fix(agents): subagent results never reach the parent while a sibling waits for its reply
prs.body:
Closes #164334
Related: #164241, #158603, #161114

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a finished subagent's result never reaches its parent when another child in the same yielded batch has paused with `sessions_yield` `waitFor: "message"` and its pause notice was already delivered.

## User Impact

A parent that receives a child's "paused awaiting continuation" notice now still gets its other children's results as they finish, whether or not it has sent that continuation yet. The paused child's own result arrives separately after it resumes. Previously the parent stayed idle with zero wake attempts, even though `sessions_yield` had just told it the sibling's completion "will arrive as a later turn". In the reported case, that lasted about six hours until a human sent a message.

Plain `sessions_yield` pauses without a notice keep their existing one-combined-delivery behavior. There is no config, schema or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A consumed pause notice hands the paused child's continuation to its requester. The child still sat in its frozen yield batch, and the batch waits for every member. The paused child was waiting for its requester, and the requester was waiting for the batch.

Consuming the notice now detaches that child into its own completion wave (`batchRunIds: [self]`), keeping its own completion custody. Frozen batch membership is mutual: wave selection, the wave's descendant scope and kernel outcome settlement skip a member whose own batch no longer lists the settling run.

Requester cron/operator authority follows the split. A yield authority still covers only its original cohort, requester session, operator and rearm generation, but each detached wave of that cohort can use it. It is narrowed as waves settle and released after the last one. Settled operator rows keep their binding, so a stray retry fails closed exactly as `discard()` already requires. The cohort rules and frozen-wave selection moved into small sibling modules to stay within the line caps.

Known limit, unchanged by this PR: the in-memory requester final attachment is keyed by the cohort's original run IDs and is never remapped. Resuming a paused child already created a new run ID, so a cohort containing a message-wait pause could not match it before this change either.

## Hardening and authority boundaries

- Each detached wave retains the original operator, requester incarnation and frozen cohort generation; no newer authority is borrowed.
- Admitted turns retain their own lifecycle while earlier waves settle. Custody releases only after both scoped work and admitted delivery acknowledgements finish; original-source revocation still cuts it off immediately.
- Exact admitted-wave retries may retrieve the Gateway's cached result, but cannot create new input/execution if the cached outcome is missing.
- Operators without Cron-management entitlement receive lifecycle-only acceptance tracking, never a Cron capability or new permission.
- No persisted schema, config option, orchestration registry or live Gateway change.

## Evidence

Raw red/green excerpts, reproducible commands, SHA-256 bindings, postcommit build metadata, and proof limitations: [proof behind the proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164366#issuecomment-5974580321).

Reviewable immutable source: [Gateway admission regressions](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts), [receipt/lifecycle tests](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/agents/subagents/requester-cron-authority-cohort.test.ts), and [actual acceptance boundary](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.ts).

Exact candidate: `a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8`.

- **Real Gateway admission + SQLite proof:** `server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts` runs the public `agent` method through the actual Gateway handler, admission/actor identity and runtime stores. Original operator revocation, expired authority, requester reset, late retirement, cached retry, cache eviction and a retired delivery claim are exercised. The agent-command/provider bridge is synthetic; this is not a live model or ordinary outside-harness UI demonstration.
- **Non-Cron negative control:** an `operator.write` client with no admin override and no Cron entitlement originally reached execution/input staging twice after cache eviction. The repaired code replays without changing transcript/admission count, rejects cache-missing retry, and still delivers the next detached completion. Cron authority stays undefined.
- **Original-source liveness:** cached retries and their captured dispatch assertion reject independently revoked channel-owner grants and registry lifecycle rotation while the operator profile and requester session remain unchanged. The after-await case is owner-level assertion proof on a genuinely admitted/cached wave, not a raced public transport request.
- **Timing reproductions:** late-wave retirement, ambiguous sibling/final acknowledgements, and zero-scoped-turn unsettled receipts failed before their repairs. Immediate revocation remains covered. Prior fixture-reference errors are not counted as bug reproductions.
- **Coverage retained:** 18 Gateway cases and 37 authority/cohort cases pass; retirement tests were moved intact into a coherent sibling module to meet the line-cap ratchet. Existing registry/lifecycle/completion/outbox/codec cases remain.
- **Validation:** full `pnpm check:changed` passed including production/test types, lint, dead exports, runtime cycles and line caps. `git diff --check` and six-file format validation passed.
- **Independent review:** final full-delta autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean for this exact head. Earlier actionable findings were reproduced and repaired, not waived. The reviewer assessed supplied source/test evidence; its isolated sandbox did not independently execute the repository.
- **Build:** postcommit `pnpm build` passed in 378.64s; `dist/build-info.json.commit` matches this exact head. An earlier build was invalidated by removal of temporary review inputs during compilation; it was not credited, and the stable-namespace rerun passed.
- **CI/security:** current-head CI/ClawSweeper reconciliation and authorized upstream security approval remain pending. No merge/deployment has been performed.


---

prs.title: feat: let sandboxed plugin tabs invoke declared session actions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tabs need narrowly authorized session actions without receiving Gateway credentials or a general-purpose parent HTTP proxy. This replaces #80388 and builds on #107323.

## User Impact

Plugins can expose declared actions for the parent-selected session. Revoking device authority or session access while an action waits now prevents the action from running. Failed action-enabled pages show a sanitized explanation and Retry, which obtains a fresh grant before reloading.

Existing canonical session navigation and the direct iframe flow for tabs without actions are preserved. The unused `allowChatNavigation` schema field is removed; no second public navigation API is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge keeps authorization in the existing Gateway dispatcher, registered action scopes, trusted session context, persisted access checks, and payload/result schemas. Sandboxed pages receive neither bearer tokens nor mutation cookies.

This refresh addresses the [latest review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102#issuecomment-5005741905): recheck both authorities synchronously immediately before invoking the plugin handler, provide recoverable page errors, remove the obsolete schema field, and repair the reported lint errors. Earlier navigation and causal MessagePort test fixes are retained; branch history is preserved.

## Evidence

Validated source: [`edbac97f93bc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102/commits/edbac97f93bc6fc633779cdee607b081abc0063c).

- **Gateway: 6 tests pass.** The real dispatcher, persisted session authority, and row-preparation boundary are exercised. Current authority permits one action effect; revoking the device or removing session membership while preparation is held returns `UNAVAILABLE` with **zero effects**.
- **Plugin UI: 51 tests pass** across document, page, and bridge suites. New cases cover an HTTP failure followed by Retry with a fresh grant, policy-error reporting, and redaction of a redirect error's private URL/token.
- **Regression sensitivity demonstrated:** keeping the new tests but restoring affected production files from `82f71f3` makes both authorization-revocation cases and all three new error/retry cases fail. The current-authority control still passes. Restoring the repaired files produces the passing results above.
- **Independent review:** no actionable high/medium-priority findings in the 11-file refresh.
- **Static checks pass:** changed-file formatting, type-aware oxlint, UI stylelint, UI i18n catalog validation, and `git diff --check`. The PR context/evidence policy also accepts this description locally.

**Remaining verification gaps (not waived):**

- **Browser/screenshots/end-to-end evidence is blocked.** Chromium crashes with `SIGTRAP` before loading the isolated fixture; a minimal launch without PR code reproduces the crash, including with `--no-sandbox`. The installed stock Firefox ESR also exits before Playwright can connect; no Playwright-patched Firefox is installed. No current-head browser assertions, network captures, or before/after screenshots were produced. Historical captures are not presented as current proof. Full Gateway startup, authenticated WebSocket flow, production cookies, plugin discovery, and deployment remain unverified. The retained navigation tests pass in the focused UI suite, but their separate base-fail replay has not been recorded.
- The broader changed-file check stops at the line-cap ratchet because this host's Git 2.34.1 does not support `git cat-file --batch -z`. Its preceding conflict-marker check passes; later gates and broader type checks are not claimed as passing.
- Replaying the two previously failing chat-test files yields 8 passing assertions but an unhandled Lit `ChildPart has no parentNode` exception in `chat-message.mcp-app.test.ts`. The run therefore fails. Those files are unchanged, but that alone does **not** establish that the failure is unrelated to this PR; causality remains unresolved.
- New-head hosted CI has not yet been validated. Maintainer review and the screenshot requirement remain outstanding.

prs.title: fix(acp): tolerate owner-repair verdicts on discarding close with clearMeta (#151859)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses openclaw/openclaw#151859 (task-maintenance discard teardown), resolving the P1 review blocker identified on openclaw/openclaw#152131 while complementing the task-maintenance cleanup deduplication in openclaw/openclaw#152613.

When an ACP session record has an unmigrated or unverifiable backend locator (raising `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired` with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`), automated task maintenance cleanup (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser` in `src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts`) fails closed every minute even though it explicitly requests to destroy both persistent state and stored metadata (`discardPersistentState: true`, `clearMeta: true`, and `allowBackendUnavailable: true`). Because teardown was blocked by the record's own provenance verdict, residue records survived and triggered repeated maintenance failures indefinitely.

*(Note: Gateway CLI deletion in `src/gateway/session-reset-acp.ts` returns earlier from cancellation and omits `clearMeta`; this PR focuses strictly on the maintenance closer path where `clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` are supplied together).*

In #152131, an attempt was made to permit discard-close past owner-repair verdicts, but it inadvertently suppressed owner-repair errors even when `clearMeta` was false or omitted. That introduced a P1 state lifecycle violation (`[P1] Preserve ownership failures when the session metadata is retained`), because an unmigrated session metadata entry would be retained on disk after a reset without notifying the operator or prompting for offline migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

To satisfy the product owner's state lifecycle decisions (*Preventative Preservation & Action Observability*):
1. **Strictly gate owner-repair bypass on `clearMeta: true`**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.close-session.ts`:
     - Recovery branch allows `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` with `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(acpError)` **only** when `Boolean(input.discardPersistentState) && Boolean(input.clearMeta)` and `input.allowBackendUnavailable`.
     - In both the fast-reset branch and recovery branch, fresh-session preparation catches `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(freshError)` **only** when `input.clearMeta` is `true`.
2. **Preserve fail-closed semantics for retained resets**:
   - When `clearMeta` is `false` or omitted (undefined), owner-repair errors are **always preserved and rethrown**, whether `discardPersistentState` is `false` or `true`. Stored metadata in the session store and SQLite database remains byte-for-byte intact.
3. **Comprehensive Regression Coverage**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`:
     - Fast-reset path (`identityHasStableSessionId` false): verifies retained resets (`clearMeta: false` and `undefined`) across both `discardPersistentState` variants reject with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` and leave metadata intact; verifies discarding reset with `clearMeta: true` deletes metadata and bypasses runtime close.
     - Recovery path (`identityHasStableSessionId` true): verifies retained resets reject and leave metadata intact; verifies non-discarding close rejects; verifies discarding close with `clearMeta: true` succeeds, records `runtimeNotice`, and deletes metadata without invoking `runtime.close`.

## User Impact

- Task registry maintenance cleanly purges residue ACP sessions whose backend locators are unverifiable or unmigrated, stopping perpetual maintenance log spam without manual intervention.
- Sessions undergoing non-destructive resets or retaining metadata are strictly protected from silent provenance mutation and continue to fail closed with directions to run Doctor repair.

## Evidence

### Real Runtime Verification: ACPX Backend Wiring & Production Task Closer

Executed against real SQLite session storage (`openclaw.sqlite`) wired to the actual ACPX locator check (`assertAcpxSessionOwnerLocator`) and production maintenance closer (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser`):

```text
=== ACPX & TASK REGISTRY MAINTENANCE CLEANUP VERIFICATION ===
[Setup] Unmigrated ACPX session initialized in SQLite:
  • sessionKey: legacy-session-1
  • backend: acpx | mode: persistent
  • state database: openclaw.sqlite

[Backend] Verified authentic ACPX locator check:
  • Exception: AcpRuntimeError [ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED]
  • Detail code: SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
  • Message excerpt: ACP session "legacy-session-1" has an unqualified or unverifiable backend locator. Stop the Gat...

[Test 1] Retained reset attempt (clearMeta: false)...
  -> Rejected as expected: fail-closed against unmigrated state
  -> Error detail: ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED [SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED]
  -> Stored metadata in SQLite preserved byte-for-byte: true

[Test 2] Invoking actual loadTaskAcpSessionCloser() from src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts...
  • Task closer loaded successfully from production task registry
  -> Production maintenance cleanup completed successfully!
  -> Metadata purged from openclaw.sqlite (readAcpSessionEntry?.acp): undefined (deleted)

=== ALL PRODUCTION & BACKEND VERIFICATION CHECKS PASSED ===
```

### Data-Model & Migration Compatibility Proof

- **SQLite Schema Version**: Unchanged (native state schema remains `v17`, verified by `pnpm check:native-state-schema-version`).
- **Data Migration / Backfill**: None required. No table schema, column, or type definitions are modified.
- **Backward & Forward Compatibility**:
  - Pre-existing session entries in `openclaw.sqlite` remain byte-for-byte intact and fully backward-compatible across upgrades.
  - Normal operations and retained resets (`clearMeta: false` or omitted) continue to fail closed and preserve stored metadata byte-for-byte in SQLite without modification.
  - Only explicit destructive cleanup (`clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` with `allowBackendUnavailable: true`) removes the session record from SQLite.

### Automated Suites & Ratchets

- **Unit & Control-Plane Test Suites**:
  - `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`: 10/10 tests pass across unit and acp projects.
  - Full `src/acp/control-plane/`: 42 files, 329/329 tests pass.
- **Ratchet & Quality Audits**:
  - `pnpm oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`: 2 changed files; no growth/violations.
  - `pnpm check:assertion-safety`: OK, 0 new unannotated assertions.
  - `pnpm check:changed`: All 21 checks passed (typecheck core, typecheck core tests, format, ratchets, Knip deadcode, import cycles).

prs.title: feat(ui): add saved gateway account switching
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This repair closes the remaining Gateway-profile correctness and proof gaps:

- Active profile removal uses the returned survivor projection directly, so the deleted URL cannot be reintroduced by fallback loading.
- Query-aware migrated credentials are sent only to their owning exact endpoint at the outgoing WebSocket client boundary.
- Successful token-mode migration retires the old origin-scoped token; clearing an owned migrated profile retires both exact and legacy slots.
- Query-distinct profiles cannot recover a neighboring profile's credential.

Profiles remain local browser metadata. Credentials remain session-scoped; no server-side account or shared credential store was added.

## Evidence

- Pushed head: `9b7ed952e4a4d0fd5367c96074b62b93496f38cb`.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec vitest run ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-registry.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.test.ts --reporter=dot` — **117/117 passed** across 4 suites.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec oxfmt --check ui/src/app/settings.ts ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/pages/connection/connection-page.ts` — passed.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 tsgo:ui` — passed from an independently owned checkout install.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 ui:build` — passed: **3,401 modules**, **840 finalized sidecars**, startup JS gzip **345,895 B** under the **352,235 B** limit; startup CSS **44,978 B** under the **51,200 B** ceiling.

## Fresh headed-browser proof

Run on 2026-09-11 against exact-head build `8023b23`/the pushed repair checkout, using disposable token Gateways and temporary state:

- `ws://127.0.0.1:19889` with a synthetic redacted token label `personal`.
- `ws://127.0.0.1:19890?account=team` with a synthetic redacted token label `team`.
- Real headed Chromium opened `http://127.0.0.1:19889/settings/connection`; the UI reached the actual WebSocket Gateway handshake and displayed token-authenticated connected state for both endpoints.
- Browser flow added and switched to the query-bearing Team profile, then confirmed removal of the active Team profile. The page reconnected to the surviving `19889` profile and the removed row stayed absent.
- The outgoing-boundary regression captured the actual client constructor options: migrated exact URL plus its owned token; after token-mode hello, the exact token key existed and the legacy origin key was gone.
- The clear regression seeded an owned origin-migrated token, cleared it, and verified both that profile and a query-distinct neighbor loaded with an empty token; the legacy key was absent.
- Browser storage and console diagnostics were redacted: no token values were retained. Browser console reported 2 development/runtime errors from the session; no zero-console-error claim is made.

## Limitation

After the browser's first successful token handshake, the Gateway issued a device grant. Clearing the visible Gateway secret and clicking Connect therefore remained connected through device authentication; this does not claim that clearing revokes an existing device grant. The no-token-reuse claim is proven at the outgoing client boundary and by the storage regression, while the live browser proof confirms the real handshake, profile switching, survivor removal, and endpoint identity.

The final post-push exact-head startup check launched runtime `9b7ed95` but detected that the runtime build stamp was still from `8023b23` while the rebuilt UI was `9b7ed952`, and correctly returned HTTP 503 rather than serving a mixed build. The interactive headed-browser receipt therefore comes from the immediately preceding compatible runtime; the final-head changes are covered by the 117-test suite, exact-head UI build, and the outgoing-boundary regression.

No new ClawSweeper review was requested.

prs.body: Fixes #186954 ## What Problem This Solves Markdown document previews display `alpha beta` and `alpha beta` identically even though the original document and the rendered text node retain the different values. This makes reports containing exact literal values harder to interpret. ## User Impact Inline code in the native Markdown reader preserves its interior spacing and continues to wrap in narrow readers. The change also applies to other previews using the shared Markdown style. Original Markdown and download bytes, parser normalization, ordinary prose, and fenced code keep their existing behavior. File-link chips retain their separate styling. ## Why This Change Was Made The native reader already receives the correct text; the shared inline-code rule lets the browser collapse its spaces. Setting `white-space: pre-wrap` at that rule fixes the presentation without adding a renderer, rewriting document content, or changing the read lifecycle. The existing selector excludes fenced code and file-link chips. ## Evidence The native guest reader reproduced the defect at desktop and narrow viewport sizes: three interior spaces occupied 7.53125 px, equal to one space, with a zero-width middle space. prs.title: fix: queued follow-ups drop the implicit reply target
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
-->

Closes #142268

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Queued follow-up answers on resolver-less channels (Telegram after restart, no live dispatcher) dropped the implicit reply target, so `reply_to_message_id` was missing.

This PR restores that injection for same-channel external/legacy turns. It does **not** claim ordinary overlapping-turn parity through a live Telegram Test Server run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued follow-up delivery already stores `messageId` / `originatingReplyToId` at admission. Payload resolution only applied reply tags and never ran the same implicit-injection helper the live path uses.

Queued payloads now go through `resolveReplyThreadingPayloads`. Implicit `currentMessageId` is injected only for resolver-less channels, with the same origin/provenance exclusions as `routeReply` (same-channel external or legacy user turns). Channels that own `resolveReplyTransport` keep correlation at `routeReply`, so empty/`replyToId` opt-outs survive. Restart-sentinel still keeps `originatingReplyToId`. Explicit `replyToId` still wins. `replyToMode` `off` / `first` / `all` stay authoritative.

## User Impact

On resolver-less transports, queued follow-up answers reply to the triggering same-channel message. Cross-channel and internal/inter-session IDs are not forwarded. Channels with a transport resolver still decide correlation at final routing.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit. Head SHA: `c6f38a93c8f7f9266efe7d3b39dbfd1aa799494b`. Marker: `PROOF_OK_c6f38a93`.

Focused Vitest after this revision (`test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts`): `followup-delivery.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.channel.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.implicit-reply.test.ts` + `followup-delivery-payloads.test.ts` + `followup-turn-admission.test.ts` — **137 passed**.

Coverage:

- same-channel queued `messageId` still injects `replyToId` on resolver-less channels
- Discord-origin / Slack-destination IDs are withheld at decision time
- inter-session child announcements stay unthreaded
- restart-sentinel keeps `originatingReplyToId`
- explicit `replyToId` survives excluded implicit IDs
- empty `replyToId` opt-out survives decision and delivery through the real channel resolver
- decision-to-delivery matrix matches those exclusions through the real channel resolver
- core tests use a fixture channel; they no longer import `extensions/qa-channel`

Sabotage: switching decision injection back to unguarded `resolveFollowupCurrentMessageId` turns the foreign-channel and inter-session tests red.

Runtime observation on `ba68eaeb` used the real Gateway + Telegram transport after restart and recorded the queued answer referencing message 11. That remains the dispatcher-less recovery proof. Telegram Test Server E2E for ordinary overlap was **not** rerun (no Convex QA broker credentials on this fork).

## Maintainer refresh — September 14, 2026

Refreshed onto `82a9bef596011a6145d7f639d9773ff5e7267f7d`, preserving the original patch and contributor authorship. Current candidate: `6d592e236f8d40d33c911391ad795ed59062b439`.

Fresh review exposed an empty-target regression on channels without a transport resolver. The shared threading owner now distinguishes an absent reply target from `replyToId: ""`; the latter remains an explicit opt-out. Inline explicit-reply directives still override that implicit-threading opt-out. This is an owner-level condition change, not a follow-up-specific workaround.

Verification:
- Added regressions failed on the pre-repair candidate: **3 failed, 46 passed**.
- Repaired candidate: **183 passed across 7 suites**, covering queued delivery, channel boundaries, admission/provenance, resolver delegation, shared threading, empty/false opt-outs, inline override, first-reply slot accounting, and deduplication.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.channel.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.implicit-reply.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery-payloads.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-admission.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-plumbing.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-threading.test.ts`
- `git diff --check` passed. The repair adds one net production line (an explanatory comment) and 61 test lines. Full changed-surface static checks and hosted CI are tracked separately; this section does not claim they have completed.
- This is deterministic owner/channel-boundary proof, not new authenticated live-channel proof.

Review adjudication: the fresh autoreview returned four reports, not a scoped-clean result. The index-only empty-target finding is resolved in the committed candidate. Two resolver-owned issues were verified as unchanged baseline behavior and recorded as follow-ups: **resolver-owned empty/false opt-out consistency** and **separating explicit inline current-message resolution from implicit correlation policy**. The reported QA dedupe mismatch was not established: that resolver returns a native message reference without `threadId: null`, while the dedupe owner treats `replyToId` as a conversation thread only for the explicit-null transport contract. No new unresolved P0–P2 regression was independently confirmed in this candidate.

prs.title: fix(macos): keep authored agent order when saving config
prs.body:
Closes #165055

## What Problem This Solves

An unrelated macOS config save alphabetizes the agent roster and can change which agent the Gateway treats as first.

The first PR revision also refused saves for valid configurations whose Gateway intentionally returns `raw: null` to protect secrets. The prior follow-up restored those saves through the existing `config.patch` contract. This follow-up fixes a separately reproduced Unicode scanner defect that rejected existing quoted keys beginning with a literal combining mark.

## User Impact

Existing configurations retain authored object-key order across local-file and Gateway saves. Valid redacted Gateway configurations remain editable, and quoted Unicode keys survive unrelated full-document saves. No config option, migration, or change to secret redaction is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removing `.sortedKeys` alone is insufficient because Swift dictionaries do not retain JSON source order. Both full-document save paths use one source-aware writer. Local saves read the existing file under their existing lock; Gateway saves retain the source with the loaded document's route lease and revision hash.

When the Gateway intentionally withholds source text, the app instead sends only the differences from the loaded structured baseline through `config.patch`. Unchanged agent entries and redacted credentials are omitted, so the Gateway-owned source retains their order and values. Explicit `replacePaths` preserves full-array edit intent for reorder, shrink, and subtree deletion instead of invoking ID-keyed upserts. Revision, route, fallback, and local credential-preservation guards remain in place.

The writer scans Unicode scalars so a literal combining mark cannot absorb an opening quote into a Swift grapheme cluster. Foundation still owns JSON5 validation and key decoding.

The full-document writer retains existing keys, omits deleted keys, appends new keys deterministically, and accepts JSON5 comments, quoted/unquoted keys, escapes, and trailing commas. Retained array values keep their object order when moved or when neighbors are inserted/deleted. Arbitrarily moved-and-modified array objects without stable identity receive deterministic order; comments and whitespace are normalized as before.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `ae4cd9bbcab468fbde71ef994386d2a1aa81e0b6`. Unicode follow-up parent: `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`. Base: `c3b2b7d3fc1a053d2f6907e55e1629c16fc53706`. macOS arm64, Swift 6.4.

### Unicode compatibility control and repaired behavior

At the published parent `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`, Foundation accepts a strict JSON document whose quoted key and string value begin with literal U+0301 scalars. An unrelated browser edit fails in both production save owners:

```text
BEFORE local save refused; original fixture unchanged
BEFORE raw-present Gateway save throws DecodingError; no config.set request
AFTER three local saves succeeded; combining-mark key/value and authored order retained
AFTER three raw-present config.set saves succeeded; key/value/order and baseHash retained
```

The exact production `OpenClawConfigFile.saveDict`, `ConfigStore.load/save`, and `ConfigJSONWriter` sources were compiled with synthetic transport/peripheral adapters and run using `sandbox-exec -f proof.sb unicode-before-proof before` and `unicode-after-proof after`. The sandbox denies operator files, network, preferences/Keychain services, and child processes. Only disposable fixtures were used; this is not installed-app/live-Gateway E2E.

The new parameterized Swift regression fails before for both double-quoted JSON and single-quoted JSON5, then passes with scalar scanning. It creates literal combining marks through Swift scalar escapes rather than JSON escape tokens and checks preservation across repeated unrelated edits, including strings containing delimiter/comment text.

### Valid raw-null compatibility control and repaired behavior

The exact published first revision `21fa0613ea2f389d6d1eeb998d85ccd3c1c03a12` refuses a valid raw-null save with ConfigStore error 4. At prior head `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`, the repaired production `ConfigStore.load/save` owner succeeds against the same boundary.

A synthetic configuration deliberately gives its token the same value as an unrelated configuration field. The exact production `redactConfigSnapshot` owner therefore returns `raw: null` while retaining structured configuration. The proof then exercises five edits through the compiled production Swift save owner and applies the captured requests using the exact production `applyMergePatch` owner:

```text
browser off, browser on, browser off, provider-model reorder, provider-model shrink
5/5 saves succeeded through config.patch
Every request retained baseHash=synthetic-revision
Unchanged gateway/auth and agents were absent from every patch
Auth credential retained; agent roster remained zmain,alpha
Model reorder and shrink retained exact replacePaths and final array intent
```

The Swift owner ran in an OS sandbox against disposable fixtures. Gateway transport and peripheral app adapters were synthetic. This is direct save-owner plus production redaction/merge-contract proof, not an installed-app/live-Gateway end-to-end run. No operator configuration, installed app, or live Gateway was changed.

### Original ordering control

At the earlier first PR revision, compiled exact baseline and repaired local/Gateway serialization owners showed:

```text
Baseline: three unrelated local saves and three config.set encodings -> alpha,zmain
First PR revision: all six retained authored zmain,alpha
All three config.set requests retained baseHash
```

The full-document writer was unchanged by the prior raw-null compatibility follow-up; the scalar scanner correction above is new on this candidate. The earlier raw-null refusal is superseded by the repaired behavior above.

### Tests and checks

- Current exact-source pure serializer and merge-patch tests: **10 tests / 13 cases passed in 0.002s** in a separately linked, audited OS-sandboxed Swift Testing executable. This includes the failing-before literal Unicode regression, existing JSON5 comments/escaped keys/trailing commas, array movement/insertion/deletion, minimal patches, and array replacement/subtree deletion.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw` passed in **20.72s**.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` passed in **21.36s**. This is test-bundle compilation, not native suite execution.
- Strict pinned SwiftLint on both follow-up files passed with zero violations. Full macOS SwiftFormat, native i18n verification, and `git diff --check` passed. Touched tests now use required failable UTF-8 conversions.
- Broad macOS lint / `check:changed` still report only the unchanged, previously documented `QuickChatFocusedTextCapture.swift:232` multiple-trailing-closure violation. All other changed-check lanes passed; no unrelated production fix is included.
- Current independent P2 AutoReview: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable P0-P2 findings. Reviewed source bytes match this candidate. Scope is this two-file Unicode follow-up versus the published parent. The inherited Codex auth attempt failed with HTTP401 and is not counted as a clean review.
- Earlier raw-null repair retains its five production-owner saves, nine pure tests/eleven cases, and clean compatibility review at `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`. Those are explicitly earlier-head measurements; the compatibility owner was not changed by this follow-up.

### Remaining checks and limits

Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper reassessment are pending. Previous-head green CI is not current-head validation. Full native test execution requires disposable macOS CI/VM and was not run on the operator desktop. The separate generic JavaScript full-suite attempt was interrupted without an aggregate result and is not claimed as passed or as native proof.

prs.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets
prs.body:
Related: #70903

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who resolve a provider billing or usage condition before its recorded reset time stay locked out of the saved auth profile until the stored window expires. There is no supported way to clear it, and the `models auth list` / doctor billing hint is a dead end.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New `openclaw models auth clear-cooldown <profileId>`: one owner-routed, locked write that resets the persisted cooldown, block, disable, and failure counters. It does not touch credentials or auth order. After the write it runs the same shared Gateway auth refresh (`models.authRefresh`) as the sibling `models auth` write commands, so no manual Gateway restart is needed.
- The `models auth list` / `models status` / doctor billing hint now names this command, including `--agent <id>` for the store it came from, because the mutation path rejects an ambiguous agent roster.
- Inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` failures have a health record (`inline-api-key:<provider>`) but no profile row. The command accepts that id when the record exists, so the hint shown for inline keys also works.
- The reset follows the health row that was displayed, not only the credential owner. A row in the agent's own database (a child's local override of an inherited credential, or an inline-key failure) wins over the owner's row after reload, so it is reset too; an agent without such a row gets no database created.
- `usage.ts` is a grandfathered oversized file, so the line-cap ratchet rejects any growth there. `updateOwnedAuthProfileUsage` moved unchanged into `usage-owner-write.ts`, next to the new reset. The dropped-bookkeeping log comes from `main`'s `state-observation.ts`. `usage.ts` shrinks by 29 lines (751 → 722). The move adds no test seam: the dropped-write test mocks the `store-runtime.js` module boundary, as `main` does since #164320.

It does not add polling, shorten provider backoffs, change fallback policy, or remove credentials.

## User Impact

Operators can re-evaluate a recovered provider with one command, without editing SQLite or repeating OAuth. If the failure still applies, the next request restores the cooldown normally.

## Evidence

Head `509ead90b58`, rebased onto `main` at `2f620b970a0`. The last commit addresses the two open P2 findings on `ba7b9103fb4`:

- **Local health row (P2):** the reset wrote only the credential owner's store, so a child's own usage row for an inherited credential stayed, won again after reload, and the command still reported success. It now also resets the agent's own row when one exists. A real-store test seeds that row, clears it, and rereads through a fresh runtime; it fails on the previous implementation. A second test shows an agent with no row keeps no database (it fails if the second write is not gated).
- **Shared state-db hint (P2):** with a roster such as `coder`/`reviewer` no agent owns the shared store, so doctor printed the command without `--agent`. The Shared target now falls back to a configured agent; owner routing reaches the shared profile from any of them. A doctor test covers it and fails without the fallback.

Results on this head:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` passed on `usage-owner-write`, `usage.inherited-owner`, `auth-profiles.markauthprofilefailure`, `usage`, `auth-clear-cooldown`, `auth-unavailability`, `doctor-auth.profile-health`, `doctor-auth.shared-health`, `models-cli`, and `root-command-descriptions`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and the `tsgo` test configs `core.test.agents-root`, `agents-other`, `agents-tools`, `commands`, and `commands-doctor` passed.
- `check:line-cap-ratchet --base upstream/main` and `check:test-mock-exports --base upstream/main` reported OK; `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` were clean.
- `check:max-lines-ratchet` currently fails on `main` itself (`ui/src/pages/agents/agents-page-state.ts` is listed as stale); this PR does not touch it.

## Remaining merge evidence

- No inspectable real-flow proof yet. A shipped-CLI run against an isolated state directory is refused by the CLI's state-store guard while an installed Gateway service uses another state directory, and the command would refresh that Gateway. Needs an environment without that service for: blocked profile -> `models auth clear-cooldown <profileId>` -> Gateway auth refresh -> recovered provider request.
- Maintainer approval of the user-facing CLI contract is still required before merge.

prs.title: fix(ui): session New window/New tab always fails with "Allow pop-ups" in the macOS app
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #144582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of the native macOS app choosing "New window" or "New tab" from the Control UI session tab menu would always see the toast "Allow pop-ups for this site, then try again." There is no way to allow pop-ups for the embedded WKWebView, so both actions were dead ends (the same actions work in a regular browser).

- **Related:** #144582 (labels: clawsweeper:queueable-fix, clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear, clawsweeper:source-repro).

## Why This Change Was Made

The web side reserves an inert `about:blank` popup via `window.open` and later redirects it to the session route. The macOS shell's `createWebViewWith` delegate classifies the `about:blank` request as ignorable and returns nil, so `window.open` returns null and the UI reports a blocked popup. The fix hands the final session URL to the existing native `openclawLink` bridge (already used by the Browser panel's external open) whenever that bridge is present, and keeps the previous `window.open` reservation as the browser fallback.

- **Intended outcome:** inside the macOS app, New window / New tab from the session menu hand the final session URL to the native link bridge instead of failing; no popup-blocked toast. The receiving default browser opens the Control UI session route; it needs its own gateway sign-in, so a previously paired browser renders the session directly while a never-paired browser lands on the Control UI login gate (an explicit sign-in surface) rather than the session.
- **Out of scope:** creating a native dashboard window/tab for the session (the shell has no such API today; whether to add one is flagged as a maintainer decision below); browser popup semantics are unchanged.
- **Highest-risk area:** routing the action through the native bridge hands a credential-free URL to the default browser, which does not inherit the app's WebKit credentials — a browser that never signed in to this gateway will not see the session.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The native receiver already validates main-frame + trusted same-origin source before opening; the posted URL intentionally carries no credentials (Gateway credentials must not be exposed in URLs), and an unauthenticated receiving browser is stopped at the login gate, which the E2E now asserts explicitly. Without the bridge (regular browsers), or if the post throws, the previous flow including the blocked-popup toast is preserved and covered by tests.

## User Impact

macOS app users can open a session from the session menu's New window / New tab items again: the session route now opens through the native link handoff in the default browser instead of failing with an impossible "Allow pop-ups" instruction. The receiving browser must be signed in to the gateway itself: an unpaired browser reaches the Control UI login gate (explicit sign-in) rather than the session; a browser that has already paired renders the session directly. Regular browser behavior is unchanged.

- **Success criteria:** with the native link bridge present, both menu actions post the final same-origin session URL and never call `window.open`; without the bridge, the previous reservation + toast flow is kept. The posted URL grants nothing on its own: a never-paired receiving browser stops at the login gate without rendering the session.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.ts` (bridge handoff placed before the popup reservation); regression fixtures in `session-menu-navigation.test.ts` ("hands … to the native shell link bridge instead of a blocked popup", "falls back to the browser popup when the native link bridge rejects the post"); the real-Gateway E2E in `ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (real Gateway + served Control UI + a page-level `openclawLink` bridge stand-in, covering both actions, the posted destination loaded verbatim in a paired isolated browser context, and the never-paired context stopping at the login gate).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 26, Playwright Chromium, a real Gateway child process built from this branch (`createOpenClawTestInstance`), and the Control UI served from this branch's source. The page-level `window.webkit.messageHandlers.openclawLink` bridge is installed through a browser init script before any page script runs — the same surface the macOS dashboard shell installs — and, like the native receiver, it does not open anything inside the source browser. The handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts that share no cookies, storage, or page state with the source page, modeling how an external default browser receives the `NSWorkspace.open` handoff: one context signs in to the gateway once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface (the analog of a previously paired default browser) and then navigates to the posted URL verbatim with no credential parameters appended; a second, never-paired context loads the same posted URL and must stop at the Control UI login gate. The macOS app itself is not runnable in this environment.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts ui/src/app/native-link-routing.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** real-Gateway E2E (`session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, head `d626215`) output:
  ```text
  ✓ hands session New window and New tab to the native link bridge instead of a popup 28328ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed (1)
  ```
  Both "New window" and "New tab" from the session menu post to the bridge:
  ```json
  [
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" },
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" }
  ]
  ```
  with zero `window.open` reservations from the menu code and no "Allow pop-ups" toast. The destination is then verified the way an external default browser receives it, in isolated contexts that share no state with the source page: the paired context first signs in once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface, then navigates to the exact posted URL verbatim — no `gatewayUrl` or token parameters appended — and renders the session's transcript, so the loaded session comes from the handed-off URL plus the receiving browser's own independent sign-in state. The never-paired context loads the same posted URL and stops at the `openclaw-login-gate` sign-in surface without ever rendering the session: the handoff grants nothing by itself, and an unauthenticated browser reaches an explicit sign-in flow instead of the session.
- **Observed result after fix:** with the `openclawLink` bridge present, `open-new-window`/`open-new-tab` hand the final same-origin session URL to the bridge and never touch `window.open`; the blocked-popup toast no longer fires. A receiving browser already signed in to the gateway renders the intended session from the posted URL; a never-paired receiving browser is stopped at the login gate. Without the bridge (regular browser), the previous reservation + fallback flow is preserved (covered by unit tests).
- **Before evidence:** with `session-menu-navigation.ts` restored to its pre-patch state (same worktree, patched E2E), the E2E fails — `AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { type: 'open-link', …(2) }`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)` — the bridge never receives anything because every attempt goes through the `about:blank` popup reservation, matching the report (so the destination steps are never reached on unpatched code). At unit level the regression tests fail on main with `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called … Number of calls: 0`.
- **What was not tested:** live macOS app / WKWebView runtime and the native Swift receiver (no macOS hardware in this environment); the native receiver path is unchanged and covered by existing native tests.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (real Gateway, real served Control UI, real browser; the WKWebView host bridge surface is installed at page level as the shell does, not mocked at module level; the handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts — one paired through the real sign-in surface, one never-paired — rather than a state-sharing same-browser tab).
- **Proof limitations:** no macOS environment available; the WKWebView message-handler transport and the Swift-side `NSWorkspace.open` handoff would need a reporter/maintainer repro on macOS. The bridge contract asserted in the E2E matches the existing native `DashboardWindowController.receiveLinkMessage` validation (main frame, trusted same-origin source, http(s) URL). The posted URL is credential-free by design: it grants session access only in a browser that already signed in to the gateway, and an unpaired browser lands on the login gate (now asserted explicitly). Whether the macOS session actions should instead open an app-owned authenticated destination (a new app window/tab that retains the app's WebKit credentials, as the ClawSweeper review recommends considering) is an open maintainer decision — this PR keeps the external-browser handoff and makes its sign-in requirement explicit and tested rather than building new native windowing unilaterally.
- **Review state:** Follow-up on the ClawSweeper review of `8d40173`: reworked the E2E destination step that previously appended `gatewayUrl` and token parameters before loading the posted URL (which overstated what an unpaired default browser receives) — the destination now signs in explicitly first and loads the posted URL verbatim, and a never-paired negative case asserts the login gate; the destination-access claim in this body is corrected accordingly. Rebased onto latest main (`d626215`). CI lanes pending on the updated head. Note: `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` previously failed on `quota-reset-status.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` ("expected 'Signed in' to be 'Ready'") — a main-level failure unrelated to this PR's files (the same test fails identically on other current PRs, e.g. #146400) and not chased here.

prs.title: fix(workboard): reject unsupported card metadata keys
prs.body:
Fixes #187079

## What Problem This Solves

`workboard.cards.create` and `workboard.cards.update` accept unsupported top-level metadata, report success, then silently discard it. The reporter measured 327 accepted writes and zero retained values on 2026.10.8. A caller cannot distinguish a durable write from lost data.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject unsupported metadata at the existing Gateway create/captureSession/update boundary, before mutation. The error identifies unknown keys and lists the supported fields. Persisted and server-owned normalization remains unchanged; this does not add arbitrary client metadata storage or a namespace. The finite supported-key record is checked against `WorkboardMetadata`.

The contributor's RPC-boundary repair and commits are preserved. A superseded normalizer refactor was removed; neither oversized store file nor its line-cap baseline grows. Regression cases are consolidated into the existing RPC matrix rather than a duplicate standalone fixture. Whole-change delta against the merge base: production +41, tests −3, documentation +3.

## User Impact

Unsupported writes now fail clearly rather than falsely succeeding. Rejected updates leave the card, timestamps, events and revision untouched; rejected creates do not create a card. Supported templateId writes and server-owned archivedAt semantics remain unchanged. First-party UI, CLI, agent-tool and internal producers were inspected before implementation; no incompatible automatic metadata producer was found and no caller changed.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway before/after results and compatibility controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187098#issuecomment-6484982337) on head `26f08fd2b2e20d1200b030bfb2cc82e855ff52b0` and main `acf995b629063dd5ac1db2737fd561b491566d6b`, Node 24.22.1.

- Two isolated real Gateway runs per ref: main accepts then drops entryId; head rejects create/update in every run with an actionable structured error.
- Supported metadata readback, rejection atomicity, archivedAt ownership, real CLI, actual UI draft payloads and registered agent-tool controls pass. Candidate also reads and updates a main-created card without losing supported metadata.
- 144 focused Gateway/store/tools/CLI tests pass. Final regression matrix fails in the two intended cases on main.
- Scoped lint, repository formatter parity, targeted docs MDX and official source line-cap comparator pass; no baseline increase.

No model/login was needed. UI controls exercise actual payload builders through the Gateway, not browser rendering. This is checkout-built proof, not release-package upgrade qualification.

## AI Assistance

AI assisted source tracing, regression consolidation and isolated built-Gateway proof. Contributor @yy19971996's implementation and commits are retained, with credit to the reporter of #187079.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores silent acceptance; this change writes no new state or migration. Blast radius is integrations sending unsupported top-level Workboard card metadata: they now receive an error instead of false success. Supported metadata and existing first-party producers retain their behavior.

prs.title: fix(bedrock): tool-returned images fail on GPT-6/6.1 Sol and Kimi K3
prs.body:
Closes #186753

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: image-reading tools fail on Amazon Bedrock with "This model doesn't support the image field for user messages" on GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol and Kimi K3, because OpenClaw nests the tool's image inside `toolResult.content`.

## User Impact

User impact: tool-returned images work on those three Bedrock routes, the same way they already work on GPT-5.6 Sol. Other Bedrock models (including Claude) keep the nested layout unchanged. No config or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

#149336 added a provider-local relocation for GPT-5.6 Sol: the image moves to a labeled sibling block in the same user message, and the tool result keeps a placeholder pointing at it. Tool results stay contiguous, tool-use IDs and status are kept, and stored history is not rewritten.

The selector only matched `openai.gpt-5.6-sol`. This PR turns it into a short list and adds the three routes the reporter confirmed with paired live Bedrock requests in #186753 (nested rejected, sibling accepted and described correctly). Routes the reporter found accepting the nested layout are left alone.

Production +10/-2, tests +7/-5.

## Evidence

- **Regression test, red before the fix:** `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` › "lifts %s tool images into user content, keeping result associations" now runs for `us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol`, `global.openai.gpt-6-sol`, `global.openai.gpt-6.1-sol` and `global.moonshotai.kimi-k3`. It drives the real `streamBedrock` request builder and checks the wire payload.
  - Base: the GPT-5.6 Sol case passes; the other three fail because their images stay inside `toolResult.content`.
  - Fix: all four pass, and the same context still serializes nested for an unaffected model.
- **Focused tests:** `pnpm vitest run extensions/amazon-bedrock/`: 13 files, 163 tests pass.
- **Checks:** oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files pass, `git diff --check` is clean.
- **Live proof, Kimi K3 over ConverseStream (this head, `119a3612fe`):** a throwaway Gateway built from this branch, with `amazon-bedrock` / `bedrock-converse-stream` / `auth: "aws-sdk"`, model `global.moonshotai.kimi-k3` in `ap-northeast-1`, and `tools.allow: ["read"]`. One `openclaw agent` turn through the Gateway asked the model to call `read` on a 64×64 solid-green PNG and name its color. Excerpt from the stored session transcript (image bytes and paths elided):
  ```text
  assistant  api=bedrock-converse-stream  stopReason=toolUse
             toolCall id=call_9d88…2112 name=read args={"path":"swatch.png"}
  toolResult toolCallId=call_9d88…2112 toolName=read isError=false
             content=[text "Read image file [image/png]", image image/png <bytes>]

I did not repeat the base run. GPT-6 / GPT-6.1 Sol were not exercised live.
