prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm reload paints cached transcript rows and then changes their inline link labels, images, archive notices, and avatars as unrelated live requests finish. The measured dashboard-deep-link evidence showed link restyling changing thread height by 58 px, a late archive notice adding 96 px, and image loading at roughly 1.3–1.6 seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep bounded last-known display facts with the existing scoped, disposable transcript snapshot. Restore titled links, intrinsic image dimensions and previously displayed thumbnail bytes, canonical notice facts, and avatar sources with each retained row. Live authority still gates reads/actions. Unchanged catch-up preserves the displayed row.

The snapshot is limited to 80 rows, eight links/images per row, bounded strings, and 32 thumbnails/8 MiB globally with the existing 256 KiB inline ceiling per image. Animated/full-size originals and credential-bearing URLs are excluded. Scope, window pruning, reset and sign-out share the existing snapshot lifecycle. Projection version 10 invalidates the older disposable projection and includes main’s terminal-widget reconciliation. No Gateway protocol, configuration or server storage changes.

## User Impact

Warm transcript rows show their last-known complete content while reconnecting. Missing or evicted bytes retain the existing loader. Main's header viewers/sharing and archived/read-only session hydration are retained in the same snapshot owner. Provider-policy notices also retain one DOM node as live facts update, including equal-valued snapshots and the blocked-state transition.

## Evidence

Current head **`b5763c39f49ae807f080adeda819d17debcdabf6`**, rebased cleanly onto **`cb5a4388f310d8b7c5d461e4f875561215260c1d`**. Ready PR; **stop before merge**. Exact-head CI is complete: the test-line gate passes with zero slack, all three UI unit shards and five of six UI browser shards pass, including the provider-notice regression. Remaining reds and matched controls are classified below. Fixed runtime retained exactly one provider-notice node in all ten loaded cases, with zero replacement/removal/missing/hidden counts. Subsequent counter-only rebases keep the implementation and regression files byte-identical. Earlier warm-reload timing/filmstrip results remain explicitly prior-head.

## Accepted tradeoff

The maintainer accepted the prior signed-in chat paint cost of +22.7 ms and LoAF blocking cost of +24.7 ms for complete cached rows. A matched CPU-profile pair found no cheap owner-level fix: object URL creation, title resolution and snapshot parsing were not the dominant cost. The earlier dashboard FCP increase of 184 → 192 ms (+8 ms) was also accepted with reversed-order controls (A/A 0 ms, B/A +8 ms, repeated A/B +4 ms). These are prior-head results, not a claim about this final confirmation.

### Prior-head five-pair confirmation

Inspected filmstrips show zero targeted visible late link/image changes in 5/5 warm reloads on each route; baseline has one or two change batches. Both arms already have zero thread-height change. All captured frames were inspected. The paired rig shows a managed image and a session-link label; it does not independently cover a seeded PR title, archive divider, or visible transcript avatars. The extended 80-row Team fixture separately qualifies two links, two images (ticketed no-store and cacheable no-cache), a canonical notice and avatars, with zero late fact/height changes in one warm smoke; it retains two thumbnails totaling 177,520 bytes. The combined native regression covers all four kinds. It now parameterizes chat and dashboard entry routes and accepts only the approved <=0.5 px geometry residual, retaining literal-zero fact changes.

Browser Element Timing and the first captured transcript frame are separate measurements. Screencast delivery is not display-vsync; capture timestamps can precede browser paint entries. Other page transitions remain (syntax coloring, sidebar/Details, reactions and widgets); this is not a whole-page stability claim. The captured-frame median moves +4.443 ms on chat and +95.704 ms on dashboard, with overlapping IQRs and mixed pair signs; the dashboard rise is reported as inconclusive timing, not hidden as a win. Chat LoAF marginal medians rise 14.9 ms; the paired median is +8.4 ms with mixed signs.

## Test-lines ceiling

Maintainer decision **2026-10-28**: PRs may raise `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` to the exact new total for justified tests, with justification in the PR; main is reset to its real total so the ratchet is green again.

This PR adds **+784 net test/support lines**, including **three lines** in the provider-notice follow-up. Existing owner tables and the combined native regression protect bounded link/image facts and retained thumbnail bytes; gateway/account/session isolation; scope/reset/sign-out, quota and window eviction; stale authority and media lifecycle; and complete warm reload of session/PR titles, ticketed/cacheable images, canonical archive notices and avatars. The follow-up extends the existing table to clone the provider notice and keeps a first-node handle through the native blocked-state update. It adds no test cases, fixture or timing wait. The table proves equal-valued publication identity; native proof covers the mounted pane lifecycle and live state transition.

`pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base cb5a4388f310d8b7c5d461e4f875561215260c1d --no-merge-base` reports **6,243,924 total / 6,243,924 ceiling / 0 slack**. Main's test audit reduced the total during this follow-up. The combined value is **6,243,140 main + 784 justified lines** and absorbs main's prior overage without carrying forward spare allowance. The base temporarily carried a 6,320,000 ceiling; this PR removes the remaining 76,076 lines of reserve after its own additions.

## Provider-notice catch-up investigation and repair

The original CI failure was `chat-provider-policy-notice.e2e.test.ts`: its visibility poll passed, then `notice.boundingBox()` returned null. This provider-policy card is transient composer run state; the cached canonical notices are archive/divider rows. A parent/live publication could still replace the composer card, so the mounted flow was instrumented.

On one AWS **c7a.4xlarge** lease, **`cbx_b861d553fbc5`**, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3d6416f99de8c4f55ee45339c6d77702), both arms used the **134 actual files from CI shard 2/7**, **four Vitest workers** and a **four-CPU affinity limit**, matching the failing CI worker/CPU envelope. The host has 32 GiB rather than CI's 16 GiB; these are reliability/DOM-count results, not latency measurements. Temporary identical ordering placed the ten notice repetitions first so they overlapped the other three workers; every remaining selected file ran once. Existing assertions stayed intact, with no extra await between the visibility poll and box measurement. A temporary MutationObserver/frame probe recorded node identity, removal and hidden ancestors; all instrumentation/ordering edits were restored and are absent from the PR.

| Instrumented arm | Notice assertions | All selected files/tests | Card replacements/removals | Same-state replacements | Runs with same-state replacement | Missing/hidden selected-node samples |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pre-fix head `9b82c52749f572f0ceda1504b6463055fd5ea67c` | 10/10 pass | 134/541 pass | 27 | 17 | 9/10 | 0 |
| Main `2742aa01664c441571418805545bc012b6294228` | 10/10 pass | 134/539 pass | 29 | 19 | 9/10 | 0 |
| Fixed runtime at `93f53c85b05f7dbc6a9eeee05399112f1a9edff7` | 10/10 pass | Remaining load workload canceled after measurements; final CI supplies broad proof | 0 | 0 | 0/10 | 0 |

The null-box assertion did **not** reproduce in these 20 instrumented cases. The probe confirms an inherited replacement defect in both arms, including same-state swaps and all buffering→blocked updates; it does not establish a painted empty-frame gap. Synchronous replacement can invalidate a node that Playwright has just resolved even when a replacement is already present.

The view called a JSX-producing helper on reactive updates. Its identity memo did not preserve the DOM when an equal-valued notice object or another tracked display dependency changed. The repair gives shared status markup one reactive component owner and keeps the provider card in a non-keyed `Show`: copy, role and tone update in place, and explicit clearing still removes it. The superseded renderer helpers and memo are deleted. No reveal gate, timer, cached transient authority or production probe is added.

A one-line extension to the existing provider-state table fails **all five identity cases before the repair**, then all **26 tests pass** with it. The native regression also retains its first element handle through the blocked update. `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view-notices.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`: **7.95 s wall**, 26 passed (latest invocation after the private prop rename; earlier repair invocation 6.52 s). Independent review of the follow-up and subsequent complete private-prop rename is **clean through P2**. Earlier full-source review remains resolved through P2: the avatar finding was declined because this task explicitly reuses the existing scoped same-origin avatar URL cache; imposing WebSocket authority on that cache would change its existing HTTP behavior. Credential-bearing and unknown/cross-origin sources remain excluded.

## Final-head validation

Current full follow-up: **+9 runtime lines / +3 test lines**. Whole PR UI runtime **+786** (**+771 handwritten, +15 generated validator**). The requested production-stat filter reports **2,785 additions / 1,285 deletions = +1,500**, across 65 files. Growth implements the approved bounded display contract and retained notice-node contract.

The repaired runtime at `93f53c85b05f7dbc6a9eeee05399112f1a9edff7` passed changed UI lint (0 errors/9 warnings), UI/native types, 513 focused tests/19 files, nine native tests/three files (both cached-row routes, reconnect and first-pane state), and the matched asset comparison. All ten policy repetitions passed under the same 134-file/four-worker/four-CPU workload, retaining exactly one node each and zero replacement/removal/missing/hidden counts. After immutable receipts were copied, the remaining duplicate load workload was deliberately canceled to perform the required counter refresh; no all-134-pass claim is made for that canceled fixed-runtime run. Lease `cbx_f762bd6b1f53` is released with no host. The completed exact-head CI is the broad final proof; its remaining failures are classified below. The notice implementation and regression files are byte-identical after rebase; updated main includes unrelated UI/test/translation changes.

Prior-head broad proof remains historical: the full UI e2e run completed with 859 files passed, 2 failed, 4 skipped; 3,222 tests passed, 2 failed, 4 skipped in 5,065.04 s. It exposed the known 1/64 px geometry residual (maintainer-approved <=0.5 px tolerance, literal-zero fact assertion retained) and a QA Lab permission error reproduced on pinned main. Lease `cbx_fb465dfb4d95`, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3607daf3a641d41baee15671d0c42dc0). Prior-head focused proof was 487 unit/18 files and 9 native/3 files; it is not substituted for exact-head CI.

## Asset budget

The complete-row feature's prior matched build measured **1,263,025 B main → 1,275,806 B candidate** chat boot gzip (+12,781 B). The chat ceiling is **1,276,669 B**, calibrated from a same-toolchain candidate measurement while preserving main's existing 811 B headroom. Measurement logic and all other budgets are intact. The repaired-runtime matched comparison passes: **1,261,685 B main → 1,273,889 B candidate** (+12,204 B), below the cap. This is a byte-size result, not a new latency claim. The dedicated budget regression suite previously passed 42 tests; this follow-up keeps its measurement logic unchanged.

prs.title: feat: add Cloudflare Clef CLI text and image decisions
prs.body:
Closes #175581

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who already have an authenticated Cloudflare `cf` CLI cannot select hosted Clef Decision models without writing their own adapter. This optional, private plugin registers Clef, Clef Flash, and Clef Omni for Boolean, Choice, and Score decisions, including one embedded PNG, JPEG, or WebP image with text, through the existing `api.runtime.decisions.evaluateV2` contract. It changes no chat model and adds no core tool. Audio, video, multiple images, lists, sort, and tags stay unsupported. Screenshot admission remains #166113 / #166114. Supplied evidence goes to Cloudflare and incurs normal Workers AI usage charges.

## Evidence

Head `1ecd065f9703ddcde1be5ab1a6519cf50fbcd631` rebases the reviewed plugin onto `15ae101a0d8` and corrects the guide. Runtime plugin sources are unchanged from `a4c924769e0`. The registered-host live run loaded the real plugin and a consumer, called the public SDK runtime, and used a real `cf` child with the existing CLI login. Inference and `context.isAdmissible` were not mocked.

Observed terminal output, with the random generation id omitted:

```jsonl
{"case":"allowed-sdk-dispatch","outcome":{"status":"ok","result":{"model":"clef-flash","answers":{"red":{"type":"boolean","probabilityTrue":0.9737}},"usage":{"inputTokens":213,"outputTokens":0}},"provenance":{"providerId":"cloudflare-clef","rubricVersion":"1"}},"cliDispatches":1}
{"case":"revoked-caller-source","rejected":true,"additionalCliDispatches":0}
{"case":"caller-cancellation","rejected":true,"activeRequests":0,"childProcessesAlive":0,"requestFilesRemaining":0}
{"case":"disposed-consumer","rejected":true,"additionalCliDispatches":0}
{"case":"revoked-provider","outcome":{"status":"unavailable","reason":"retiring"},"additionalCliDispatches":0}
```

That run passed 7/7 tests in 31.64 seconds. After this rebase, the focused adapter file passed 18/18 tests in 4.69 seconds. Reproduce the live suite with an existing CLI login:

```bash
OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_CF_CLEF=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_USE_REAL_HOME=1 \
  pnpm test:live -- src/decisions/cloudflare-clef.live.test.ts
```

Real-home mode is selected only for the CLI login. The test overrides OpenClaw state, config, and agent paths into its temporary workspace. This is in-process production-runtime proof, not a WebSocket handshake and not a real profile-store revocation.

## Problem and user impact

Operators with an authenticated Cloudflare `cf` CLI cannot select hosted Clef Decision models without writing their own adapter. This optional plugin adds Clef, Clef Flash, and Clef Omni for Boolean, Choice, and Score decisions using the Gateway user's existing CLI OAuth login. It changes no chat model and adds no core tool.

Supported evidence: text/JSON and **one embedded PNG/JPEG/WebP image with text**. `decision_evaluate` accepts that inline image with `contractVersion: 2` and tagged state `{type: "image", dataUri, text?}`, then dispatches it through the selected V2 provider. Plugin code can pass the same state to `api.runtime.decisions.evaluateV2`. Audio/video, multiple images, lists, sort, and tags stay unsupported. A local screenshot file path is separate admission work in #166113 / #166114. Supplied evidence goes to Cloudflare and incurs normal Workers AI usage charges.

## Repairs following review

- **Released-host compatibility:** npm `openclaw@2026.10.4` exports only the V1 Decision SDK. Removed the false `>=2026.10.4` install/compatibility claims. The package is now **private, source-checkout-only, with both npm and ClawHub publication disabled**. No future host release number is invented; a real released V2 host must be verified before enabling publication.
- Added the package-local README and replaced the repository-private test helper import with `openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-env`.
- **Production-path defect found by the new proof:** declared static plugin-owned auth scope and the synthetic/non-secret CLI marker in the manifest, matching the runtime provider. Before this correction, real prepared host dispatch returned `credentials-unavailable`; direct adapter tests missed it.
- Replaced raw temporary-directory creation with the public SDK private-workspace helper and cleanup. Fixed the abort-rejection lint defect and two test type errors.
- Regenerated plugin inventory and config baselines using their owners. Exactly 24 introduced plugin config paths are accounted for (three Clef settings plus the existing generic per-plugin envelope); core/channel config budgets and hashes are unchanged.

## Authority-chain and real CLI proof

The new `src/decisions/cloudflare-clef.live.test.ts` loads the actual plugin through the production loader plus a minimal consumer plugin. The consumer invokes **the public SDK runtime**, then the actual prepared model/catalog/auth owner, provider host, adapter, and CLI. Neither inference nor `context.isAdmissible` is mocked or replaced by an always-true predicate. A real `cf` child uses the existing CLI OAuth login.

OpenClaw state/config/agent paths and synthetic media are isolated from the running Gateway. The observation executable only records child startup and delegates to real `cf`. It does not forward termination: on POSIX the CLI inherits the observer's process group, deliberately testing the transport's negative-PID group kill. Both recorded PIDs must be dead, private files removed, and host active-request count zero before proof completes. This suite is POSIX-only, not a Windows cleanup claim.

The five cases establish: a permitted native image decision; host-issued operator-source revocation before another CLI starts; actual consumer-instance disposal; actual provider reload/retirement; and cancellation settlement of the observer and real CLI. The operator identity is synthetic and bound through the host's authority issuer/caller context. The installed Gateway was not restarted or migrated.

`OPENCLAW_LIVE_CF_BINARY` and `OPENCLAW_LIVE_CF_PROFILE` optionally select the CLI executable/profile.

## Validation

- 18 focused adapter tests passed on the rebased head, including typed wire translation, image limits, malformed results, credential-override rejection, environment isolation, cancellation/deadlines, cleanup, and authority refusal.
- 9 package publication/collection tests passed on the previous head, including the formerly failing plugin-release suite.
- The registered-host live test passed all five scenarios in **4.871 seconds test time**; both live files passed **7/7 tests in 31.64 seconds wall time** (CI seconds unavailable).
- All six live adapter-level cases were rerun successfully on the repair: text and image on each of Clef, Flash, and Omni, with Boolean/Choice/Score questions. They are transport/typed-answer proof, not general accuracy claims; the new host-path evidence closes the previous direct-context gap.
- Targeted core host-proof typecheck and type-aware lint passed on the previous head. The changed-graph preflight hits unrelated gateway/infra root-budget limits; the canonical `other` test graph was checked directly rather than running every core shard.
- Config baseline was regenerated on this rebase. Plugin config paths moved from 4711 to 4735. Core stayed 2565 and channel stayed 4043. Generated plugin inventory, public extension-test import boundary, temporary-directory lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed on the previous head.
- Fresh Codex repair review completed. Its one P2 suggestion to add observer signal forwarding is not applied: the unchanged production transport already kills the entire POSIX group, and a forwarder would conceal a group-termination regression. Actual observer/CLI liveness and cleanup are checked, and Windows is explicitly excluded.

Prior-head CI also reported failures in unrelated Discord/Signal/Telegram ingress, memory reindex, terminal delivery, and Android Wear suites. They were inspected but not reproduced on base, so this PR does **not** claim their inherited status is proven. Updated-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.

## Merge conflict

Resolved again onto `15ae101a0d854480cfb500a5e241055450da39da`. The only conflicts were the generated config baselines. Regenerating them left core 2565, channel 4043, and plugin 4737, which is 24 plugin paths over the new main count of 4713. Core and channel hashes are unchanged.

## Simplify

The optional plugin stays. It is the existing Decision provider owner: one codec, one CLI transport, and the prepared V2 contract. This pass did not add a second image API or cut production code. It removed the guide claim that `decision_evaluate` is text/JSON-only. The tool already accepts `contractVersion: 2` inline image state. A local screenshot path stays a separate admission feature.

Follow-up on head `a4c924769e0`: current main's package-boundary compile selects every extension whose tsconfig extends the packaged boundary base, then requires a bundled or published surface. This package is private, `bundledDist` is false, and both publication flags are false, so that opt-in failed with `No packaged surface for extension boundary: cloudflare-clef`. The opt-in tsconfig is removed. Adapter tests on this head: 18/18 passed.

## Repository adoption

**Answer: yes. Adopt this as a repository-owned optional plugin.**

Keep it in this repository. Leave the package private, source-checkout only, with `publishToClawHub: false` and `publishToNpm: false`, until a released host that exports the V2 Decision runtime is verified. Do not publish it, and do not add a core tool or a chat model. The public SDK contracts stay the implementation boundary, so a later independent package remains possible. This is the contributor's adoption request for the decision on this pull request. It is not a maintainer approval, and it does not approve the workspace lockfile change.

## Beta compatibility and native-tool follow-up

Commit `39e0e9ec65a195980d760c682165068894ee5f94` adds two additions on top of the previously reviewed head (no rebase and no production plugin changes):

- Document verified Decision V1-only exports in both published `2026.10.4` and `2026.10.10-beta.2`. Discovery/picker metadata does not prove provider registration. This V2 candidate remains private and source-checkout-only; publication stays disabled and no released compatibility floor is claimed.
- Extend the existing registered-host live suite to exercise the actual native `decision_evaluate` bridge (`createDecisionTool`) as well as the SDK, including native caller-source revocation with no additional CLI dispatch.

Updated live proof: **1 test passed, six logged scenarios, 50.77 seconds wall / 5.991 seconds test**. SDK and native dispatch each used real Clef Flash with a synthetic red image and returned Boolean `probabilityTrue: 0.9737`. Revoked callers did not dispatch; cancellation settled with zero active requests, live child processes, or remaining private request files. Consumer disposal and provider retirement checks also passed. This is POSIX in-process source-host proof, not a WebSocket handshake, profile-store revocation, whole-Gateway upgrade, or soak certification. The installed Gateway was not changed.

Reproduction on this host uses the existing live command above with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`. Scoped MDX validation (two docs), type-aware lint of the changed test, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. A prior full source build passed in 9m 1.7s before these docs/test-only additions; no fresh full build is claimed. CI time for this follow-up is not yet available.

The branch still requires separate base-conflict resolution and maintainer adoption/dependency approvals. Prior failing extension CI reported `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-index-recovery.test.ts:138`; its inherited status has not been established. Neither source inference nor this documentation update authorizes a live Gateway switch; isolated upgrade/recovery and soak validation remain pending.

The contributor explicitly requested commit/push and hosted ClawSweeper review after the local AutoReview attempt failed authentication without producing a report. That attempt is not counted as a completed review.


## PR simplify follow-up

Head `a75fb0624a33c7b04626951ad5f65c8e27ee361b` applies the repository's `pr-simplify` pass across the complete 20-file proposal. The smallest coherent stage remains a private, source-only optional Decision provider; publication and any shared media-contract expansion remain deferred.

- Removed the codec's redundant whole-batch validation. `evaluateVersion` owns input admission before prepared dispatch; the adapter retains Clef-specific model, input-shape, question-ID and rubric limits. Response decoding/validation and live authority checks remain intact.
- Consolidated identical codec checks across model names (four duplicate executions removed) and removed the fixture's self-check. Real subprocess dispatch still covers all three model routes; typed translation, image framing/full-size input, malformed responses, credential/routing refusal, failure categories, cancellation and private-file cleanup retain their assertions. The separate opt-in adapter/live-host suites remain unchanged.
- Kept the single provider/codec/transport and entrypoint: no new state, wrappers, core tools, SDK contracts or compatibility fallback. Retained manifest/package discovery, auth and release metadata, generated config/inventory artifacts, navigation and setup/compatibility docs because each serves installation or the provider contract. No unrelated hunks or new dependencies were added.

Delta against merge base `15ae101a0d854480cfb500a5e241055450da39da`: production TypeScript **+415/-0**, tests **+650/-0**, metadata/docs **+627/-5**. Relative to the preceding PR head only: production **-2 lines**, test LOC unchanged, four fewer duplicate test executions. No broader size reduction is claimed.

Fresh proof: **14/14 offline adapter tests passed** (4.24 seconds wall); scoped formatting, commit-hook formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The registered-host live rerun failed its first allowed SDK dispatch with `unavailable/credentials-unavailable` (54.39 seconds wall). The CLI login check succeeded, including with the adapter's filtered environment and isolated working directory; the host failure's cause is not established. Earlier successful live runs above remain prior-input evidence, not a passing result for this head.

The scoped type-aware lint wrapper expanded into SDK declaration preparation; that preparation was interrupted (exit 130), so no fresh lint/typecheck pass is claimed. Local AutoReview again failed authentication without producing a report. After being told the review was unavailable, the contributor explicitly directed commit, push and ClawSweeper review. Hosted review/CI remain outstanding. Nothing here certifies a whole-Gateway upgrade or soak; the installed beta is unchanged.


## Simplify (cf51c14fca6)

The plugin README no longer repeats host compatibility, publication rules, or live-test commands. That policy stays in the Clef setup guide, which the README links to. Codec, CLI transport, manifest, offline tests, and both live suites are unchanged: each still covers a distinct failure (wire translation, process settlement, catalog limits, direct CLI inference, and registered-host authority).

Against `origin/main` at this head: 20 files, +1650/−5. This revision is docs only, −42 README lines, and no production or test delta. The live `credentials-unavailable` discrepancy, maintainer dependency approval, and repository-adoption decision are unchanged.


## Live proof on cf51c14fca6

Registered-host suite rerun on 2026-10-29 against head `cf51c14fca6`. `cf` 1.0.0-beta.12 already had a valid OAuth login. The suite loaded the real plugin in-process, kept OpenClaw state, config, and agent paths in a temporary workspace, and delegated to the real `cf` binary. The running Gateway was not restarted. One test passed in 5.458s; wall time including worker startup was 65.53s.

```jsonl
{"case":"allowed-sdk-dispatch","outcome":{"status":"ok","result":{"model":"clef-flash","answers":{"red":{"type":"boolean","probabilityTrue":0.9737}},"usage":{"inputTokens":213,"outputTokens":0}},"provenance":{"providerId":"cloudflare-clef","rubricVersion":"1"}},"cliDispatches":1}
{"case":"allowed-native-dispatch","outcome":{"status":"ok","result":{"model":"clef-flash","answers":{"red":{"type":"boolean","probabilityTrue":0.9737}},"usage":{"inputTokens":213,"outputTokens":0}},"provenance":{"providerId":"cloudflare-clef","rubricVersion":"decision-v1-5c8ca25498a3175a5d021b3b"}},"cliDispatches":1}
{"case":"revoked-caller-source","rejected":true,"additionalCliDispatches":0}
{"case":"caller-cancellation","rejected":true,"activeRequests":0,"childProcessesAlive":0,"requestFilesRemaining":0}
{"case":"disposed-consumer","rejected":true,"additionalCliDispatches":0}
{"case":"revoked-provider","outcome":{"status":"unavailable","reason":"retiring"},"additionalCliDispatches":0}
```

Prepared SDK dispatch and native `decision_evaluate` both returned ok for the synthetic red square. The earlier `credentials-unavailable` result did not recur. Revoked callers, cancellation, consumer disposal, and provider retirement started no further CLI work.

prs.title: fix: exclude fenced dreaming ranges from memory indexing and recall signal
prs.body:
Closes #172547

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed dreaming output written into daily memory notes under `openclaw:dreaming` fences is embedded, returned by memory search, and staged into short-term recall, even though it is scratchwork that can never be promoted.

Scope confirmation: this branch implements the scope Peter Steinberger set on #172547 on 2026-10-27: "Managed inline dreaming fences should be excluded from default memory retrieval, before chunking." and "@CloudCorpRecords, please go ahead with your branch on that scope."

## User Impact

User impact: memory search and recall signals no longer surface fenced dreaming scratchwork, while ordinary note content keeps its exact citation line numbers and the note files themselves are never modified. Indexes built by earlier versions rebuild once through the existing chunking generation, so already-indexed fenced chunks are reconciled away, and already-staged fenced candidates stay unpromotable through the existing rehydration owner. No new config option.

## Why This Change Was Made

Index preparation now blanks managed fenced ranges (blank lines, never deletions, so line numbers stay exact) before chunking, for memory sources only. The fence policy lives in one new owner, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/dreaming-fences.ts`, exported through the host internals and the `memory-core-host-engine-indexing` plugin SDK surface. Promotion rehydration imports the same helpers and its private copy of the fence regexes and overlap logic is deleted, so indexing and promotion cannot drift on what a fence is. `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION` moves from 6 to 7 so the existing reindex owner rebuilds stored indexes instead of a parallel migration.

## Evidence

- New unit tests for the shared module: 12/12 pass (closed, unclosed, mixed, stray-marker, and CRLF cases).
- Index-preparation tests, including two new fence cases (mixed note excluded with original line numbers; fence-only note produces no chunks): 9/9 pass.
- Differential fuzz of the shared overlap helper against the pre-cutover rehydration implementation, transcribed verbatim: 72,871 cases, 0 mismatches (an earlier run of the same comparison covered 235,839 cases, also 0 mismatches).
- Acceptance scenario from the issue thread, exercised at the preparation and promotion-guard boundaries: a synthetic daily note with ordinary facts before and after a managed fence produces no chunk containing fenced text or markers, chunk texts and start/end lines are identical to a pre-blanked control (the after-fence fact still ends at its original line), the source string is unchanged, and the promotion guard refuses the fenced range and both marker lines while admitting the ordinary lines.
- Red/green check: the pre-change path (strip annotation carriers, then chunk) leaks the fenced text into chunks; the new path does not, and keeps the ordinary facts.
- `tsc --strict` on the new module: clean.

Honest limits: the local runs above used a vitest-shim harness because this sandbox cannot install the repo toolchain (pnpm self-install fails here), so the repo's own test suite, typecheck, and lint are CI's to confirm. The full end-to-end pass from the issue (real memory index, search, and promote paths with isolated state and a real local embedding model) was not run locally because no local embedding model is available in this environment; it is a reviewer or CI step, not something claimed here. The branch was brought current with main by a merge commit; conflicts were resolved by reapplying the branch changes at their current locations, and the resulting diff against main is exactly the 8 intended files.

prs.title: fix(ui): agent panels interrupt native mobile chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agent-driven panels interrupt chat inside the native iOS and Android apps when a tool presents a panel or a session gains an automatic resource.

## User Impact

User impact: native mobile chat stays visible until the user opens a panel. Manual panel controls and explicit dashboard navigation remain available; macOS and ordinary web browsers, including narrow/mobile browsers, keep their existing behavior. No settings or saved layouts are migrated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identify native mobile WebViews using their existing host/bootstrap provenance and platform, rather than viewport width. This also covers iOS shared-auth pages and Android message-port startup, which do not necessarily provide the embedded-chrome flag. Only host provenance is retained, not credentials.

Native mobile clients no longer advertise agent UI-command support, and discard incoming commands before they can navigate to another session. The existing presentation owners also suppress automatic desktop discovery/reveal, board presentation commands and first-board reveal, and restore chat-first layouts without rewriting saved preferences. Manual controls are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on base `50bb32ef09475b3f91e30ad0d9ec78a2c213a8e8`: an incoming agent browser-panel command visibly opened the panel, failing the native-mobile no-reveal assertion.
- The bundled Control UI regression now passes for both a native-mobile bootstrap fixture and an ordinary mobile browser: native no-reveal, web behavior preserved, capability advertisement checked, and manual Files opening works in both.
- Focused host/startup, shell-command, active-resource, board and sidebar tests pass (152 tests); existing session-panel toggle/intent tests also pass (20 tests).
- Production and test UI typechecks, touched-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent local review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Review was limited to the supplied diff/test evidence; it did not execute the tests or inspect unchanged repository context.

The images below show the actual bundled UI with synthetic content and a mocked Gateway at 390 × 844. Native bootstrap metadata is emulated; this is not an installed iOS/Android app or live-agent/model test. Physical-device/native-shell validation remains a follow-up.

prs.title: chore(agents): cover final system prompt hook context
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

**Problem:** The embedded runner has no regression test proving that `before_agent_run` sees system-context mutations made by `before_prompt_build`.

**Why now:** OpenClaw 2026.9.4 passed a stale pre-assembly system prompt to the gate; current `main` fixed the behavior incidentally, but the contract remains unprotected.

**Value:** Plugin policies can rely on the documented final-system-prompt contract without a repeat of the stale-snapshot regression.

**Fix:** Add one production-path embedded-runner test that injects a marker, captures `before_agent_run.event.systemPrompt`, and compares it with the model session prompt.

**Scope:** One test file, 26 added lines, no runtime or public API changes.

**Risk:** Test-only; the main risk is coupling to setup details, mitigated by asserting only the public hook contract and final session prompt.

**Proof:** Current-main source inspection, historical stale-path comparison, a shipped `openclaw agent --local` trace through an isolated synthetic plugin/provider, the test-line ratchet, `git diff --check`, and PR CI.

**Non-goals:** No runtime change, no second policy gate, and no worker-placement changes.

**Maintainer ask:** Confirm this is the right embedded-runner boundary for preserving the documented hook contract.

## What Problem This Solves

The embedded runner lacks regression coverage proving that `before_agent_run` receives the final system prompt after `before_prompt_build` system-context mutations.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. Plugin authors gain regression coverage for the documented final-system-prompt contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

In OpenClaw 2026.9.4, the runner captured `systemPromptText` before prompt assembly, so `before_prompt_build.prependSystemContext` reached model inference while `before_agent_run.event.systemPrompt` still contained the earlier snapshot. Current `main` [refreshes the prompt after assembly](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fdeb8f7efdd7c70e319c9e41db9cffc4577c348e/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-phase.ts#L213), behavior introduced incidentally by [729c6b1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/729c6b1cc3d0f4aecfceb9af36a815acbdc8f799).

The new test exercises the complete embedded-runner path rather than manually piping one hook result into another. It injects a synthetic marker from `before_prompt_build`, captures the next gate event, and verifies that both the gate and final model session receive the same prompt. This would fail against the [2026.9.4 stale snapshot](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3a9d69d/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-phase.ts#L101-L102) while preserving the current runtime unchanged.

This is separate from [#182142](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182142), which covers final prompt admission for worker-placed sessions.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Current `main` at `fdeb8f7efdd7c70e319c9e41db9cffc4577c348e` — verified that the post-assembly refresh remains in place and no runtime patch is needed.
- `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base fdeb8f7efdd7c70e319c9e41db9cffc4577c348e` — passed with 144 lines of slack after rebasing onto the current shrink-ratchet baseline.
- Shipped-entry-point trace on OpenClaw `2026.10.3` using isolated state, a synthetic local plugin, and a loopback mock OpenAI-compatible provider:
  - `before_prompt_build` prepended `WORKSHOP_GOVERNANCE_CONTEXT_V1`.
  - `before_agent_run.event.systemPrompt` contained the marker (`7735` bytes; SHA-256 `9a32eb7aa63841e038daa0a0a394d3c96233bd5cbda0209c8e7cf1eeb8fc1e04`).
  - The actual model-bound `/v1/chat/completions` system/developer payload also contained the marker (`7350` bytes; SHA-256 `8efd329a52925297f727b78c5bf8bd03391861d68453c5686738ffb7d1f8c928`). Transport serialization changes the byte shape; the exact internal gate/session equality is the assertion added by this PR.
  - The embedded runner returned `proof-ok`; no external provider, credential, private conversation, or production Gateway was used.
- Focused command attempted: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
  - Local result: blocked before test collection because the prepared dependency tree has TypeScript `7.1.0-dev.20260922.1`, while current `main` requires `7.1.0-dev.20261016.1`; the runner failed resolving `typescript/fs`.
  - No dependency install or lockfile mutation was performed. PR CI provides the exact-version test run.

prs.title: fix(ui): judge composer model availability by the session's selected runtime
prs.body:
Related: #186358. This PR fixes the composer's runtime-blind credential banner. The "selection does not take effect" part of the report is not changed here (see Not covered).

## What Problem This Solves

A model can have several runtime routes, for example the OpenClaw API route plus a native `claude-cli` route. When the session runs that model on its selected runtime (`claude-cli`, authenticated through `claude auth login`), the composer still decides availability from the base catalog route. If that base route has no OpenClaw-stored Anthropic credential (`unavailableReason: "missing-auth"`), the composer shows "No provider credential is configured for this model. Set it up in Model Setup." even though the selected native route is available and its turns succeed.

## User Impact

With a native Claude CLI login and no OpenClaw Anthropic profile, a session running a Claude model on the Claude CLI route no longer shows the false "No provider credential" banner. Sessions on the base route without a credential still show it, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveChatModelUnavailableReason` (in `ui/src/lib/chat/model-select-state.ts`) only read each catalog entry's top-level `available` / `unavailableReason`. It now takes the session's selected runtime and projects every matching entry through the existing `resolveModelRuntimeEntry`, which the model picker already uses. That gives the per-runtime availability, so the selected `runtimeChoices[]` entry decides. The composer (`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-model-setup.ts`) passes `activeSession.agentRuntime.id`. Without a selected runtime, or when the runtime is not one of the entry's choices, the previous base-route behaviour is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Tests

`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-model-setup.test.ts` has a new case, "uses the session's selected runtime for the credential banner". The catalog entry has a base route that is `missing-auth` and a `claude-cli` runtime choice that is available.

- Session runtime `claude-cli`: no banner. This fails on main, which shows "No provider credential…", and passes on this branch.
- Session runtime `openclaw`, or none: the banner is still shown. This control passes on both.

`chat-model-setup.test.ts` and `model-select-state.test.ts` pass 54/54.

Checks run locally: oxfmt, oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` and `git diff --check` are clean.

### Live run

### Live run (Windows 11, Chromium)

This is the real Control UI (`scripts/control-ui-mock-dev.ts`, Vite dev build) in Chromium. For this run only, the mock was patched locally, and that patch is not part of this PR:

- Catalog entry `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`: base route `available: false, unavailableReason: "missing-auth"`, and runtime choice `claude-cli` `available: true`.
- The main session runs that model with `agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" }`, and for the control with `openclaw`.

Only the session runtime and this PR's two UI files differ between panels.

![live run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/186358/proof-186358.png)

| | main, runtime `claude-cli` | this branch, runtime `claude-cli` | this branch, runtime `openclaw` (control) |
|---|---|---|---|
| "No provider credential is configured for this model…" banner | **shown** | **not shown** | shown (that route has no credential) |

### Not covered

- A real Claude CLI login. This machine has no Claude Code install, so the catalog shape is taken from the source-level analysis in the issue review.
- The reported picker selection that "does not take effect", which may involve the session patch path. That part is not changed here.

prs.title: fix(mcp): unreachable remote MCP server no longer blocks Doctor-gated Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #162228, #144911, #143070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: standalone Doctor lint rejects an otherwise usable installation when a configured remote HTTP/SSE MCP service is unavailable, including a server that initializes but never answers its tool-catalog request.

## User Impact

Recognized remote connection, authentication and deadline failures become actionable warnings tagged `mcp-service-unavailable`. An error-threshold Doctor gate can proceed while the affected remote tools remain unavailable.

**Scope narrowed in response to review:** local stdio startup failures remain errors, including ambiguous `mcp-remote` proxy failures. Numeric JSON-RPC errors, unknown failures, invalid catalogs, pagination-integrity failures and cleanup failures also remain errors. This is a partial fix, not a resolution of every case in #162228; it no longer asks maintainers to accept broken local children as warnings. No config or stored-data migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP owners now retain a typed availability classification through catalog collection and startup backoff. The pagination owner supplies a typed deadline error; classification uses transport provenance and structured error fields, never server-message text. Doctor preserves the strongest finding when different inspection contexts report the same server, so an earlier warning or deferred-auth notice cannot hide an error.

The repair is reconstructed on newer main at `f91bca9546f5`, reusing the existing catalog-projection owner rather than expanding the oversized runtime module. Current updater probe deferral, OAuth inspection ownership, last-good catalogs and retry behavior are preserved. A local merge check against `1e48ec3a9e3` succeeds; its newer enterprise-MCP capability preparation is not overwritten.

## Evidence

### Actual compiled CLI behavior — October 21

Ten independent ordinary standalone invocations used credential-free synthetic private config/state, real loopback MCP transports and the compiled CLI:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json \
  --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --severity-min warning
# Repeat each scenario with --severity-min error.
```

| Synthetic failure | Finding at warning threshold | Exit: warning threshold | Exit: error threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Refused remote Streamable HTTP connection | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Initialized remote server delays `tools/list` beyond the real 10-second deadline | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Remote catalog repeats its pagination cursor | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Missing local executable | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Local stdio child exits during initialization | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |

Every invocation reported `checksRun: 1`. At error threshold, remote-only warnings were filtered out (`findings: []`, exit0). Representative sanitized output projection:

```json
{"scenario":"refused-http","threshold":"warning","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"warning","errorCode":"mcp-service-unavailable"}
{"scenario":"catalog-deadline","threshold":"error","code":0,"checksRun":1,"severity":"below-threshold","errorCode":null}
{"scenario":"closed-stdio","threshold":"error","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"error","errorCode":null}
```

**Build provenance/limit:** this CLI proof ran on [assembled fork commit dda926bb935](https://github.com/Grynn/openclaw/commit/dda926bb93528517d02666179d4478579af6e4a9), which contains this exact repair plus separately reviewed immutable-launcher/runtime fixes and other local units. All 13 files in this PR are byte-identical there to `92b501e7e5af68ad01b829ff005739fe69ed45b1`. Its full `pnpm build` passed with the live-service safeguard enabled. This is real compiled CLI evidence, **not an exact standalone PR-head build, a production deployment or a full installed-release Doctor certification**. No serving credentials, user state or model calls were used. The older blocked CLI attempt remains historical evidence, not a success claim.

### Regression and cost evidence

- Production Doctor detector covers real refused HTTP, typed catalog deadline, remote auth and malformed/integrity controls. Same-server warning/error aggregation has genuine baseline failures and repaired passes. Stdio remains error without requesting a severity-policy exception.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **60/60 pass**, measured wall **51.65s**, peak RSS **5,591,232 KiB** (includes compiler/bootstrap work; not a steady-state latency benchmark).
- After final owner extraction: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-start-backoff.test.ts src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retirement-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **32/32 pass**, measured wall **57.73s**, peak RSS **5,532,380 KiB**.
- Focused types, type-aware lint, formatting, scoped line-cap and diff checks pass. Final independent P0–P2 review of the full 13-file repair completed scoped-clean; its former compiled-CLI evidence gap is now addressed with the explicitly scoped proof above. Current-head PR CI remains separate from these local checks.
- Simplification: failure/retirement projection uses the existing catalog owner; the old duplicate retired-catalog literal is removed. Necessary growth is typed failure provenance and strongest-severity aggregation, plus distinct real transport/ordering regressions; no new manager, database schema or runtime policy option.

prs.title: fix(ui): match canonical NFC/NFD names in chat workspace search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fix canonically equivalent Unicode searches in four reachable Control UI filters: desktop Files catalog, mobile session files, local skill discovery, and installed-skill library. Each owner lowercases then normalizes only its comparison copies to NFC, following #186672, #186794 and #187024. No global normalizer, storage/display rewrite, server-echo change, dependency, or new option.

Includes wangmiao0668000666's original #187036 commit and the cherry-picked #187050 commit, preserving authorship. #187050 is covered here.

## User impact

A composed query now finds decomposed filenames/descriptions and vice versa. Retained missing output files are a concrete Files reproduction: their names remain in session history after the files disappear, and the server's already-canonical filesystem search cannot mask the local mismatch. ASCII case-insensitive substring behavior remains unchanged, without diacritic folding.

The proposed fifth correction, the legacy embedded rail fallback, is intentionally excluded: current regular sessions always choose desktop/mobile; only native catalog keys select the fallback. The native catalog has no file-list operation, and the built baseline's file-list call for a catalog key returned `files: []`. No supported user path populating that fifth filter was established, so this PR retains only the four proven corrections.

## Evidence

[Real built-Gateway/Chromium results and inspected before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187036#issuecomment-6483903838).

- Main `f25b36e95b0161b324ad772127264fb0021c4d6c` and candidate `cb09af821b928a85aa88c2ad90f41577efc44daf`, both built inside secretless Docker using Node 24.22.1.
- Four real UI owners × NFC→NFD, NFD→NFC, ASCII × two repetitions per revision: **48 observations**. All 16 Unicode searches missed on main; all 24 candidate searches matched; all 16 ASCII controls matched.
- Workspace descriptions loaded from real `SKILL.md`; library fixture created and saved through each real UI into its personal SQLite library. No mocked Gateway transport or injected UI state.
- Consolidated library regression: both canonical directions fail on main; candidate skills suite **22 passed**. Workspace loading/rail suites **41 passed**.
- Targeted formatting passed; targeted lint: zero errors (four existing mobile memo warnings outside the diff).

## Simplification

Removed duplicated added regression setup and replaced a static toolbar-copy assertion with a compact two-direction behavioral regression. Against the merge base: **production +16/−5 (net +11), tests +12/−13 (net −1)**. The removed contributor-added regression scaffolding is covered by the stronger real Gateway/browser comparison; the unexercisable rail correction was also removed.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting fully restores the prior comparisons; no state migration or persisted bytes change. Blast radius is local filtering of Files and skills in the Control UI. Raw lowercased server-echo equality remains byte-exact, and remote discovery ranking is untouched.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): truncate memory index labels without splitting surrogate pairs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The standing Knowledge index clips long record labels with raw UTF-16 `String.prototype.slice` in `memory-index.ts`:

```ts
// base, memory-index.ts:49 (upstream/main 7c87e3a892d)
return flat.length > max ? `${flat.slice(0, max - 1).trimEnd()}…` : flat;
```

`promptLabel` owns prompt-facing Knowledge labels (`TITLE_MAX = 80`, `CLAIM_MAX = 110`, `HANDLE_MAX = 60`), all below the 200-unit record-title contract, so valid labels really are clipped; when the clip falls between an astral character's halves the label ends with a lone high surrogate.

`memory-index-hook.ts` (`readMemoryIndex` -> `pinIndex` -> `appendSystemContext: text`) pins this index and appends it to the system prompt every turn, so the lone surrogate enters the prompt bytes and becomes U+FFFD at serialization for the session.

## User Impact

A page or claim label whose 79/109/59-unit clip lands inside an emoji or other astral character is rendered to the model corrupted: its last visible character becomes U+FFFD while the trailing ellipsis still appears, so the model cannot match the label back to `knowledge_lookup` input. The pinned index repeats this every turn until compaction or a new session.

## Why This Change Was Made

```ts
// candidate
return flat.length > max ? `${truncateUtf16Safe(flat, max - 1).trimEnd()}…` : flat;
```

`truncateUtf16Safe` is already the truncation owner across this plugin and keeps the width contract: the clip may stop one UTF-16 unit before the cap and the ellipsis still fits inside `max`. ASCII and in-cap labels are byte-identical to before. Behavior-preserving for well-formed input, behavior-completing for split pairs (`Precedent: #186707`).

## Evidence

Pinned base: `7c87e3a892dffa9280b9618dc01792c955ad20d1`; candidate head: `f991ffeb00a342fc6082702fbbb6008c98cbed07`.

The regression folds into two existing cases, adding no test lines (delta 0, as the test-lines ratchet requires):
- `memory-index-hook.test.ts` (existing byte-stable index case) saves its second label as `${"p".repeat(78)}<U+1F3AF> review` (87 units, valid under the 200-unit contract) and asserts the serialized hook result carries the clipped label. Real path: `memoryFixture` store, real `node:sqlite`, real `before_prompt_build` hook -> `readMemoryIndex` -> `buildMemoryIndex`. No mocks.

BEFORE (base tree, de-hardlinked so link counts are 1; original `memory-index.ts` md5 `909910d99edef67babadf437d69909bf`):

```text
$ /data/openclaw-test/a1028/runr.sh /data/openclaw-test/a1028/trunc-base-1 \
    "node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge/src/memory-index.test.ts \
       extensions/knowledge/src/memory-index-hook.test.ts --maxWorkers=1"
FAIL memory-index-hook.test.ts > appends a byte-stable index for owner-private sessions until the cutoff moves
AssertionError: expected '{"appendSystemContext":"## Knowledge …' to contain
  '- note: <78 x p>…'
Received: … "- note: <78 x p>\ud83c…\n- note: Renamed playbook title\nAll pages are listed."}
FAIL memory-index.test.ts > renders instruction-like or markup labels as ID only
AssertionError: expected 'xxxxxxxx<U+FFFD>…' to be 'xxxxxxxx…'
Tests  2 failed | 10 passed (12)
```

The base JSON shows the split literally: the clipped label is 79 units ending in U+D83C, the high half of U+1F3AF, so the serialized result contains `\ud83c` before the ellipsis and is not well-formed.

AFTER (candidate tree, same command, same tree contents otherwise):

```text
$ /data/openclaw-test/a1028/runr.sh /data/openclaw-test/a1028/trunc-1 \
    "node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/knowledge/src/memory-index.test.ts \
       extensions/knowledge/src/memory-index-hook.test.ts --maxWorkers=1"
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  12 passed (12)
```

Candidate: the serialized hook result has `- note: ` + 78 x `p` + U+2026 (pair dropped, not half-kept) and no `\ud8` escape; `promptLabel` returns `xxxxxxxx` + ellipsis, not `xxxxxxxx` + U+D83C + ellipsis.

Controls still green in the same cases: the in-cap `Brightpath analysis playbook` and renamed labels are unchanged, and instruction-like or markup labels still return `null`.

## Merge Danger

- Three files, +5/-4: one production import and expression, three modified test lines, no added test lines (delta 0). No new files, exports, options, or helpers; only the truncation call changes, leaving the `max` contract, markup/instruction rejection, and empty-label `null` return untouched.
- A preview may shrink by one UTF-16 unit when the boundary falls inside a pair, matching the "may stop one unit before its cap" behavior used elsewhere in the plugin.
- No open PR in the 300-newest `openpr_files-1028.tsv` map touches `memory-index.ts`, `memory-index-hook.ts`, or `memory-index.test.ts`; #186366 only edits `docs/plugins/knowledge/*.md`.
- Not tested: no local full-suite, typecheck, or lint run (local test/build forbidden); only these two files ran, remotely.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): shorten claim titles without splitting surrogate pairs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Remembering a claim whose derived title's 199-unit shortening boundary splits an astral character persists a lone UTF-16 high surrogate. `knowledge_record` returns an ill-formed title, and ordinary UTF-8 encoding replaces that surrogate with U+FFFD.

## Fix

Thanks to @wangmiao0668000666 for the report and original repair; the contributor commit is preserved. The existing remember title producer uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper instead of raw slice. Word-boundary trimming, the <=200 title budget, original body/evidence, subject resolution and persistence contracts remain unchanged. No new helper, API, configuration or migration.

## Evidence

Built main `db6efe4ecc2b6075d2ffab1b8ed940cbd0ff69a0` and candidate in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker. Real enabled Knowledge plugin, actual Gateway agent turn and genuine `knowledge_remember` / `knowledge_record` tool dispatch through a local deterministic Responses model provider; fresh isolated profile/config/state/database paths confirmed before each run.

**Two runs on main and two on candidate**, each with four inputs and five genuine tool calls:

- Split boundary: `198 A + emoji + trailer`. Main returns a durable 200-unit title containing lone high surrogate **55357** before ellipsis—`isWellFormed=false`, UTF-8 replacement present. Candidate returns **198 A + ellipsis**, 199 units, well-formed with no replacement.

All existing assertions remain, while the duplicate standalone fixture/read is removed. Whole-PR delta against merge base: **production +1; tests 0**. Existing docs accurately describe the unchanged <=200 title contract; user-visible context is recorded here rather than editing the release-owned changelog.

## Merge Risk

One clipping call at the producer. No compatibility path or behavior change for ASCII, intact pairs or short titles. ## What Problem This Solves

Cron run-history search silently misses visibly identical job names, summaries and errors when stored text uses NFD and the query uses NFC, or vice versa.

Apply NFC after the existing lowercase conversion to both operands in `cronRunHistoryMatchesQuery`, consistent with the landed cron-job search repair in #186794. Reuse this same predicate for both in-memory selection and the database worker's bounded candidate scan. No storage rewrite, new normalizer, SDK/config change or alternate search path.

## Evidence

Inspectable [real run receipts, CLI/RPC query output, repeat matrix, paging and original-byte captures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187024#issuecomment-6481565524).

Built main `bf9709250b87bec4a26637046096092ee68d3366` and candidate `3a1643668a9bcf414b44ae468aa778d047d03deb` runtime artifacts in secretless Node 24.22.1. A real Gateway creates seven disabled command jobs through public `cron.add`; shipped `cron run --wait` executes each twice and creates 14 genuine run rows per ref. Successful commands produce summaries, and nonexistent Unicode command names produce ordinary persisted execution errors. No rows are seeded with SQL, and no model/provider key or channel delivery is needed.

- Both NFC/NFD directions are queried for job names, captured summaries and recorded errors, twice per ref, through both `cron runs` and public Gateway `cron.runs`, in per-job and all-history scope. Main returns zero for all opposite-form searches; the candidate returns the two real runs for each job.
- Both shipped query routes use the real database read worker: `cronRunsHandler` dispatches `readCronRunHistoryCandidates` to `cronReadOnly`, whose bounded scan calls the shared predicate. There is no separate SQL text prefilter or replacement worker fixture.
- ASCII/case/whitespace and absent-query controls, status and agent filters, ascending/descending order and five offset pages pass on both refs. Repeated public readback preserves original UTF-8 job-name, summary, error and diagnostic bytes.
- All 11 existing run-history tests pass. The existing bounded-worker search case now uses a decomposed diagnostic and a composed uppercase query; it fails on frozen main with zero matches instead of one. Formatting passes.

Simplification: production +3/-3 lines; test count unchanged and test lines -4. The added standalone predicate case is consolidated into the existing storage/paging regression without dropping its bounded-read, projection or ordering assertions. Contributor commits and documentation are preserved.

## Merge risk

Two-way door: comparison-only change, fully reversible, with no persisted state or schema migration. Blast radius is filtered cron run-history queries, including the Gateway worker path; incorrect normalization could change which runs match, but does not alter stored text, status, sort order or paging policy.

prs.title: fix(cron): normalize NFC in automation list search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automation list search misses visibly identical names and descriptions when the query and stored text use different canonical Unicode forms, such as composed `ü` versus `u` plus a combining diaeresis.

## User Impact

`cron list --query` and `cron.list` find canonically equivalent NFC/NFD metadata while preserving the original job names, descriptions and identities. ASCII matching, filters and pagination retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the same **lower-case-then-NFC comparison pattern** landed in [#186672](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186672) (`9a5581b4ce`). Normalize the query and the existing cached search haystack, not stored fields. The shared lowercase helper is deliberately unchanged, and no new normalizer is introduced.

The WeakMap remains owned by the existing read-snapshot generation. Haystacks are still prepared once per row generation, and caller visibility is still checked on every list request before sharing a sorted snapshot. No new schema, configuration, public API or permission changes.

## Evidence

Frozen main: `3eb6e8df529bfc83ec5e2c228a00ffc707426416`. Candidate: `16815546302bb1be69d32f55fbc69ec92e656af8`.

Built Node 24.22.1 CLI and a real built Gateway in secretless Docker. Five legitimate disabled jobs were created through ordinary `cron.add`; no raw SQL seeding, model call, job execution, paid key or personal state. The same queries ran **twice per ref through both shipped entry points**:

```text
node <built-root>/openclaw.mjs --profile <task-profile> cron list --all --agent main --query <text> --json
Gateway RPC: cron.list { includeDisabled: true, agentId: "main", query: <text> }
```

| Stored field / query form | Main, both runs and boundaries | Candidate, both runs and boundaries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NFD name `Mu\u0308nchen report nfd`; NFC query | 0 matches | correct job, 1 match |
| NFC name `München report nfc`; NFD query | 0 matches | correct job, 1 match |
| NFD description `Cafe\u0301 office nfd`; NFC query | 0 matches | correct job, 1 match |
| NFC description `Café office nfc`; NFD query | 0 matches | correct job, 1 match |
| ASCII name, padded uppercase query | correct job | same correct job |
| Absent phrase | 0 matches | 0 matches |

These are **48 primary query calls**, plus controls. Independent `cron.get` readback before and after searching compares UTF-8 name/description bytes with the creation inputs and job IDs with the creation responses: unchanged on both refs.

Enabled/disabled, schedule-kind, conditional-trigger and agent filters still apply. Equivalent NFC/NFD prefix queries page through both matching jobs on the candidate with a stable snapshot revision; main sees only the job matching each raw representation. A normal revision-guarded `cron.update` rename invalidates the cached row: the candidate finds the new decomposed name using a composed query through both CLI and RPC, the old query stops matching, and readback preserves the new original bytes.

Focused checks: **39 tests passed across two suites**, formatting and type-aware lint passed. The consolidated canonical cache/visibility regression fails on main at the missing match. It also retains the once-per-row-generation work guard, visibility rechecks, mutation invalidation and original-name snapshot assertion.

Simplification reuses that existing regression owner instead of adding standalone fixtures. Against frozen main: production **+3/-2 (5 gross lines)**, tests **+7/-7 (net 0)**, documentation +4/-3. No ceiling or baseline exception.

Not exercised: native macOS/Windows processes or scheduled job execution. The stored NFC/NFD input forms are explicit task-owned Unicode strings; no OS-input normalization is assumed.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: revert restores raw comparison behavior; no stored-data migration. Blast radius is automation metadata query matching through the existing cached list reader. Original metadata, identity, visibility and scheduling stay authoritative.
