prs.title: fix(gateway): keep chat-history display truncation head+tail so terminal facts survive reloads
prs.body:
# fix(gateway): keep chat-history display truncation head+tail so terminal facts survive reloads

## What Problem This Solves

`truncateChatHistoryText` (`src/gateway/chat-display-projection.helpers.ts:108`) is the single display-projection truncation point for chat history. It capped over-limit text **head-only**: `prefix + "\n...(truncated)..."`. For an assistant message longer than the display budget (default `8_000`) — long tool output, long answers — the reloaded Control UI and every downstream projection (reply previews, canvas diffs, commentary fallbacks) therefore show only the beginning of the message. The **terminal state at the end of the message** (e.g. `RESULT_CODE=E_OK`, exit summaries, the model's final status line) is exactly what gets cut, so a user scrolling back through a reloaded session cannot tell how a long result ended.

**Precedent: #186382** (steipete, merged 2026-10-28T00:20Z) fixed precisely this contract for the same function family: `truncateForSummary` moved from head-only to a **head+tail shared budget** that explicitly preserves terminal facts. This PR replays that approved shape on the remaining same-family site — the chat-history **display projection** — with the same budget arithmetic: `tailChars = min(floor(limit * 0.3), 600)`, `headBudget = limit - tailChars - 64` (marker reserve), marker reserved **inside** the shared budget so `head + marker + tail <= limit`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Same-family contract completion.** #186382 established "head+tail preserves the tail" as the correct contract for this projection family; the display projection is the sibling site that still ran the old head-only shape. The fix mirrors the precedent's budget split and its `head | marker | tail` midline structure, inside one function, with **zero caller changes**.
- **Contract differences disclosed (deliberate):**
  1. **Marker bytes stay `"\n...(truncated)..."`.** The precedent emits `"\n\n[... N more characters truncated]\n\n"` for its summarizer input; here the sentinel is a cross-client contract — iOS `ChatModels.swift:733-766` detects `contains("\n...(truncated)...")`, Android `ChatController.kt:7509-7540` keys on the same suffix (plus the structural `__openclaw.truncated` flag), and `extensions/agentsapi` + `extensions/codex` projections emit the same bytes. We mirror the precedent's _structure_ (marker midline between head and tail, all inside one budget) without changing the sentinel bytes consumers sniff.
  2. **No diagnostic-skip branch.** The precedent skips the tail when the retained head already matches `IMPORTANT_TOOL_RESULT_TAIL` (summarizer input economy). In a display transcript the tail is where the terminal state lands, so the tail is kept unconditionally.
  3. **`preserveExactPrefix` stays byte-exact.** Structured payload consumers (source cards, Canvas, structured output rendering — `sanitize.ts:226-234`) parse the preview, so that branch keeps returning an exact prefix with no marker and no tail, exactly as before.
  4. **Tiny-budget fallback.** The precedent only ever runs at a 2,000-char budget; display callers pass arbitrary budgets (8/12/16/24/30/32/100 appear in existing tests). When `headBudget < tailChars` the split would leave no usable head, so those budgets keep the legacy head-only marker byte-for-byte (named edge case in the comment).
- **Classification: `behavior-completing`** — completes the maintainer-merged #186382 contract at its remaining same-family site. No default changes (`8_000` untouched), no new options/config, no caller edits.

## User Impact

- Reloaded long messages now show **both** ends: the opening context and the terminal facts at the end, with the truncation marker at the cut point inside the display budget.
- **Visible behavior delta — reply-to previews** (this is a real, user-visible change): quoted originals are projected through `projectChatDisplayMessage(..., { maxChars: 500 })` (`src/gateway/chat-history-reply-messages.ts:110`) and previously rendered as `slice(0, 500) + marker` (pure head). They now render as `slice(0, 286) + "\n...(truncated)...\n" + slice(-150)` — same 500-char budget, shared head+tail. Two existing assertions encoded the old contract and were updated to the new one (`chat-history-delta.test.ts:540-544`, `chat-history-pages.recovery.test.ts:218-224`).
- **No change** for: short text (returns byte-identical, `truncated: false`), budgets below ~160 chars (legacy head-only output byte-identical to main), structured payload previews (`preserveExactPrefix` byte-exact), and the sentinel bytes themselves.

## Evidence

Evidence first sentence: **在远程服务器 10.54.159.54 的 `lexiflow-all` docker（Node v24.22.1）里，对 base `b61ab6deb` 执行 `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-delta.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-pages.recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`，观察到 base 上 2 个新断言红（尾部 `RESULT_CODE=E_OK` 不在截断文本里）+ 2 个契约跟随断言红（reply preview 仍是纯 head）；对 candidate 执行同一命令观察到 `Test Files 3 passed (3)` / `Tests 94 passed (94)`，尾部 needle 可见、头部保留、总长 ≤ 8,000。** Visual-leg second sentence: 同一服务器 docker 内以临时 Control UI e2e spec（mock Gateway、注入消息由当树自身 `truncateChatHistoryText` 投影）执行，base 上观察到 `AssertionError: … to contain 'RESULT_CODE=E_OK'`（截图先落盘，UI 里消息以 `...(truncated)...` 结尾）、candidate 上 `Tests 1 passed (1)`（截图里消息最后一行是 `RESULT_CODE=E_OK`）。

| Tree             | Command (server docker, `--maxWorkers=1`)                                                                                                                                                                      | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Exit |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---- |
| base `b61ab6deb` | `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-delta.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-pages.recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | `Test Files 3 failed (3)` / `Tests 4 failed \| 90 passed (94)` / `Duration 412.39s` — the 4 reds are exactly the new tail assertions (2) + the two reply-preview contract-following expectations (2)             | 1    |
| candidate        | same command, same tree                                                                                                                                                                                        | `Test Files 3 passed (3)` / `Tests 94 passed (94)` / `Duration 407.34s`                                                                                                                                          | 0    |
| base `b61ab6deb` | `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts -t "chat.abort cancels chat.send while lifecycle admission waits" --maxWorkers=1`                                          | `Test Files 1 failed (1)` / `Tests 1 failed \| 68 skipped (69)` / `Duration 235.15s` — **reproduces on pristine base**: pre-existing environmental red, unrelated to this PR                                     | 1    |
| candidate        | `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/session-lifecycle-run-failure.test.ts -t "does not report a stale session error" --maxWorkers=1`                                                                     | `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 1 passed \| 34 skipped (35)` / `Duration 80.87s`                                                                                                                              | 0    |
| candidate        | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/chat-display-truncate-tail.visual.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (server docker, mock Gateway)     | `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 1 passed (1)` / `Duration 38.39s`; `PROOF_SHOT=/ws/.artifacts/control-ui-e2e/chat-display-truncate-tail-Pm6hG1/truncate-tail-bubble.png`                                      | 0    |
| base `b61ab6deb` | same visual command with helpers swapped to base (md5-verified before/after)                                                                                                                                   | `Test Files 1 failed (1)` / `AssertionError: expected 'HEAD_FACT_9C41 run starts here…' to contain 'RESULT_CODE=E_OK'` / `Duration 39.00s`; screenshot was captured before the failing assertion                 | 1    |
| candidate        | `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit`                                                                                                                                                         | `TSC_EXIT=2`, 18 errors — **all** pre-existing generated-DB typing (src/state, src/transcripts, src/talk, src/trajectory × `openclaw-*-db.generated`), **zero errors in touched files**; CI `tsgo` authoritative | 2    |
| local (static)   | `pnpm exec oxlint` on the 4 touched files                                                                                                                                                                      | `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`                                                                                                                                                                                  | 0    |
| local (static)   | `node scripts/run-format.mts --check`                                                                                                                                                                          | `All matched files use the correct format.` (55,329 files)                                                                                                                                                       | 0    |

**Red → green assertion points (new cases, `chat-display-projection.test.ts`):**

- `shares one budget between head and tail so long messages keep terminal facts` — red on base at `expect(projected.text.endsWith("RESULT_CODE=E_OK")).toBe(true)` (base head-only output ends with the marker) and at the `split("\n...(truncated)...\n")` midline-shape assertion; green on candidate, also asserting `starts(head)`, `length <= 8_000`, `truncated === true`.
- `serves reloaded assistant history with the tail's terminal facts intact` — red on base at `toHaveProperty("content", stringContaining("RESULT_CODE=E_OK"))`; green on candidate with `__openclaw.truncated === true` and head preserved.
- `leaves short text unchanged under the shared display budget` — control: `truncateChatHistoryText(short)` equals `{ text: short, truncated: false }` (byte-identical passthrough) on both trees.
- Consumer contract-following reds on base: the two reply-preview expectations (above) fail on base because base still emits the pure-head `slice(0, 500)`; green on candidate.

**Trigger reachability (producer-chain):** producers are real session transcripts whose assistant messages exceed 8,000 UTF-16 units (model output / long tool results, produced by production code). Guard chain: `chat-history-handler.ts:200 resolveEffectiveChatHistoryMaxChars(maxChars)` → default `helpers.ts:20 DEFAULT_CHAT_HISTORY_TEXT_MAX_CHARS = 8_000` → `chat-display-projection.core.ts:606-608 sanitizeChatHistoryMessages(...)` → `chat-display-projection.sanitize.ts:234/:302/:548 truncateChatHistoryText(...)` → base head-only output loses the tail; reply-preview branch `chat-history-reply-messages.ts:110` (`maxChars: 500`).

**Visual gate (before/after screenshots — inspected):**

- **base (before):** 消息止于截断标记，无终态码  
  ![before tail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/assets-trunc1-shots/shots/before-tail.png)
- **candidate (after):** 末行 = `RESULT_CODE=E_OK`，标记居中保尾  
  ![after tail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/assets-trunc1-shots/shots/after-tail.png)
- Head (`HEAD_FACT_9C41 …`) is asserted in-DOM in **both** runs before capture (`expect.poll … toContain(head)` passes on base and candidate); the stitched tall-element screenshot only paints the scrolled viewport slice, so the screenshots carry the tail delta and the DOM assertion carries the head.
- **Method:** temporary Playwright e2e spec in `ui/src/e2e/` (removed before commit) using `createControlUiE2eSuite({ startServerBeforeBrowser: true, browserLaunchOptions: { timeout: 60_000 } })` + `installMockGateway({ sessions, historyMessages })`; the injected message content is produced by **that tree's own** `truncateChatHistoryText`, so the only difference between the two captures is the code under test. Runs execute in the server docker (Node v24.22.1, `lexiflow-all`) with staged Chromium (Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.34 via `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH`) + host NSS 3.90 libs and host `/etc/fonts` + `/usr/share/fonts` mounts.
- Cosmetic, identical on both sides: the mock-Gateway harness shows a `Could not load the full message. Retry` banner under the bubble (mock-transport artifact, not a differential).

**Ratchets / gates (local static, `--base b61ab6deb --no-merge-base`):**

- `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts`: `Test lines OK: 6294426; ceiling: 6295000; slack: 574` → **`config/test-lines-baseline.txt` untouched**.
- `check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs`: `Line-cap ratchet OK: 4 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.`
- `check-max-lines-ratchet.mts`: `max-lines ratchet OK: 406 grandfathered suppressions.`
- `check-assertion-safety-ratchet.mts`: `assertion SAFETY ratchet OK: 2407 files, 5478 grandfathered assertions.`
- `check-test-timeout-race-ratchet.mts`: `test timeout race ratchet OK: 104 files, 190 grandfathered sites.`
- `check-test-mock-exports.mts`: `Mock factory ratchet OK: 6570 grandfathered factories.` (no new `vi.mock`).

**Collision / drive-by checks:**

- 1,000-open-PR file-map scan: the only open PR touching any file here is **#174943** (`fix: explain saved-state continuation rejections in replies`), and it touches `chat-display-projection.test.ts` **only** at an unrelated hunk (~line 794, replay-rejection guidance test) — no hunk overlap with this change, and it does not touch the production helper. Noted, not a collision.
- No open PR touches `chat-display-projection.helpers.ts`, `chat-display-projection.sanitize.ts`, `chat-display-projection.commentary.ts`, `chat-display-projection.canvas.ts`, `chat-history-delta.test.ts`, or `chat-history-pages.recovery.test.ts`. Last-7-days closed/merged search ("truncate tail" / "preserve tail" / head+tail / `truncateChatHistoryText`) found no newer same-shape PR.

**Risk disclosure:** the head-only truncation marker is an existing design boundary (the transcript keeps full bytes; `__openclaw.truncated` flags the cap structurally), so a maintainer could judge tail loss as by-design. The counter: #186382 already accepted that this exact loss is user-harmful for the sibling projection — after a reload the single most load-bearing line of a long result (its terminal status) is the one that disappears, and "…(truncated)…" only says _something_ was cut, not _how it ended_. Full transcript bytes do not help a display surface that never renders them. This PR changes no budget, no default, and no option; it only completes the approved contract at the remaining site.

### Cleanup

- Temporary e2e spec (`ui/src/e2e/chat-display-truncate-tail.visual.e2e.test.ts`) removed before commit; screenshots retained under local `shots/`.
- No push, no PR, no GitHub write — evidence package handed to the coordinating agent for PR creation.
- No production Gateway, state, config, or token touched; remote test dir `/data/oc-wt-trunc1` holds only synced source + independent `node_modules`.

### Not tested

- Full repository suite / PR CI: not run locally (local test runs are prohibited); CI is the broad gate.
- `tsgo` (repo type checker) cannot run locally (GLIBC) — remote `tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` was run instead: pre-existing generated-DB errors only, none in touched files; CI `tsgo` is authoritative.

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

Maintainers may edit this PR freely: adjust the head/tail split constants, move the new cases into a different test file, or reword comments. The behavioral contract (tail preserved, marker midline, budget shared) is the part this PR exists to land; the exact helper-const naming is yours to choose.

- **Alternative B (keep contract, shrink preview delta):** if the 500-char reply-preview head reduction is unwanted, the only single-function way to keep the tail would be growing its budget, which changes the cap semantics; not done here because budgets/defaults are explicitly out of scope.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve active run after rejected replacement
prs.body:
Fixes #184735

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes active embedded runs becoming unreachable after a replacement registration fails.

## User Impact

A failed replacement no longer detaches the still-running previous run from native lookup and lifecycle control, so it remains stoppable and observable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing registration owner now checks replacement authority before retiring the previous attachment. Cleanup remains in `runs.ts`, where the lifecycle is already owned.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep sandbox CDP probe deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting a sandbox browser can hang past its configured startup deadline, or fail early on a healthy browser. `waitForSandboxCdp` seeded its `deadline` and read its remaining-time checks from `Date.now()` (wall clock), while the fetch-abort timer and the poll `sleep` consumed those values through libuv monotonic timers. When the wall clock steps back (NTP correction, manual time change), the `while (Date.now() < deadline)` guard can never become true, so the probe spins until the hung container is force-removed; when the wall clock steps forward, a healthy request is aborted early and the browser startup is reported as timed out.

- **Problem**: the deadline and remaining budget are computed on the wall clock but consumed by monotonic timers, so a wall-clock jump distorts the startup budget in both directions.
- **Solution**: seed and read the deadline from `performance.now()`, so the guard, the abort timer, and the poll sleep share one monotonic domain.
- **What changed**: `src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts` — `waitForSandboxCdp` now uses `performance.now()` for the deadline, the loop guard, and the two remaining-time reads. The helper stays private; the regression drives it through the real browser-startup path (`onEnsureAttachTarget`) against a real `node:http` peer. The existing "stalled CDP request" test's fake-timer config also fakes `performance`, so `advanceTimersByTimeAsync` moves the deadline on the same clock.
- **What did NOT change**: the deadline is a process-local closure variable; nothing serializes, persists, or compares it across processes. The browser-registry `createdAtMs`/`lastUsedAtMs` timestamps stay wall-clock on purpose; `ensureSandboxBrowser` and the container lifecycle are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deadline is a purely process-local budget: it is not serialized, persisted, or compared across processes by any `Date.now()` consumer, so switching to the monotonic clock is the correct, minimal fix (the same pattern already merged for the wall-clock family, e.g. #169908, #155863). Keeping the helper private avoids a test-only production seam: the existing lifecycle fixture already invokes the probe through `onEnsureAttachTarget`, so the regression extends that path instead of importing the helper.

- **Best fix**: yes — the owner function reads one clock end-to-end; no new parser, policy branch, or config surface. A parallel monotonic deadline alongside a wall-clock epoch was not needed; nothing outside the closure consumes the value across a process/DB boundary.
- **Risk**: none identified — `performance.now()` exists on Node 16+, and `setTimeout`/`sleep` accept the float it returns.

## User Impact

Sandbox browser startup now honors its configured timeout regardless of wall-clock adjustments: a step-back no longer makes the CDP probe spin past the deadline, and a step-forward no longer aborts a healthy probe early. Users see either a timely "browser not reachable" failure or a successful attach, instead of a hung startup or a false timeout.

## Evidence

**Shipped entry point, real Docker sandbox, real clock step.**

`openclaw gateway` (this checkout, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`) plus the shipped `openclaw agent --agent main -m "hi"` turn, with `sandbox.mode: "all"`, `backend: "docker"`, and browser `autoStartTimeoutMs: 8000`. The scripted model requests the `browser` tool (`open about:blank`); the browser plugin attaches to the sandbox bridge, and the bridge's `onEnsureAttachTarget` calls `waitForSandboxCdp` against the container's mapped CDP port. The image is the contract-labelled sandbox-browser image (`org.openclaw.sandbox-browser.contract=2026-05-12-cdp-relay-auth`).

The container's CDP peer answers `500` and logs every request with a `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` timestamp — that is the peer the probe really polls (each probe request carries the sandbox `Authorization` header; the plugin's reachability check does not). While the probe waits, the host `CLOCK_REALTIME` is stepped with `sudo date -s` by ±60 s, a real NTP-style jump; `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`/`performance.now()` is untouched. The step is applied on the first **authenticated** probe request, i.e. after the budget was seeded on the pre-step clock. The peer is a stub rather than Chromium because this environment has no outbound network to build a real browser image; the probe transport, container lifecycle, and clock are real.

| source | wall-clock step | probe wait (container log, monotonic) | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| this PR | +60 s | **8.3 s** | deadline expires at the 8 s budget |
| this PR | −60 s | **8.3 s** | step-back does not extend the budget |
| base | +60 s | **0.2 s** | premature "not reachable" abort |
| base | −60 s | **68.6 s** | budget stretched by the jump |

Raw container log (first authenticated probe request → last), base −60 s vs this PR −60 s:

```console
# base (Date.now), -60s step
[fixture] GET GET /json/version HTTP/1 -> 500 (elapsed=47452ms first=47452ms auth=1)
[fixture] GET GET /json/version HTTP/1 -> 500 (elapsed=116103ms first=47452ms auth=1)   # 68.6s
# this PR (performance.now), -60s step
[fixture] GET GET /json/version HTTP/1 -> 500 (elapsed=54812ms first=54812ms auth=1)
[fixture] GET GET /json/version HTTP/1 -> 500 (elapsed=63084ms first=54812ms auth=1)   # 8.3s
```

Every run ends in the same production failure — `Sandbox browser CDP did not become reachable on 127.0.0.1:<port> within 8000ms. The hung container has been forcefully removed.` — the difference is only when it appears. In the base −60 s run the client surfaced a bridge-level error first while the container log shows the probe still waiting 68.6 s: the probe outlived the request.

**Regression tests (RED on the base commit, GREEN with the fix).**

```console
$ git show HEAD~1:src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts > src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts   # base
$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/sandbox/browser.create.test.ts
× keeps sandbox browser attach inside the monotonic deadline across a 60000 ms wall-clock step
  AssertionError: expected 'Sandbox browser CDP did not become re…' to be 'attach target reached before bridge c…'
× keeps sandbox browser attach inside the monotonic deadline across a -60000 ms wall-clock step
 Tests  2 failed | 26 passed (28)

$ git checkout -- src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts                                   # fix
$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/sandbox/browser.create.test.ts
 Tests  28 passed (28)
```

The negative row asserts the deadline still expires after a step-back (no budget stretch); the positive row asserts attach still happens when the browser turns healthy inside the monotonic budget (no premature abort). The sign of the delta is preserved, so the two rows no longer exercise the same rewind.

`oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean; the diff has no config, persistence, or new public surface.

prs.title: fix: workspace Markdown evidence links open missing conversations
prs.body: Fixes #186640 ## What Problem This Solves A workspace Markdown report can contain a relative evidence link such as `evidence/log.md#details`. Clicking it in Files resolves against the browser’s chat URL and opens a nonexistent conversation, even though the intended file is readable through the file browser. ## User Impact Authored relative links now open the intended file from the report’s directory, including extensionless files and repository-backed previews without a host filesystem root. Files beyond the inline preview limit retain their metadata and download action. The report remains available in its tab, and existing drafts retain their contents. A heading fragment selects the file without adding heading scrolling. Reads preserve the originating session and current permissions. A changed workspace is refused before another file or cached draft is selected; a missing or denied target restores the report’s catalog selection. Ordinary message links, external URLs, conversation links, fragment-only links, and the Markdown remote-image policy keep their existing handling. ## Why This Change Was Made Files already owns the document’s canonical path and read context. Its renderer opts into document-relative file links, and the existing navigation owner resolves the destination and checks the native source receipt before selecting a preview. The renderer’s cache distinguishes document readers from ordinary messages; host paths stay outside rendered link metadata. Failed navigation publishes the restored selection through the same workspace owner. Repository reads populate the existing optional source receipt with their workspace ID and null filesystem roots. This distinguishes a retained document from a replacement repository after a source key is reused, while keeping identity stable across ordinary checkpoints. Save and conflict-recovery consumers use that receipt; clients omitting the optional source precondition retain their existing behavior. Request schemas and filesystem grants are unchanged. Preview-limit errors retain the same optional root/source metadata in their existing details. The UI validates it against the existing file-response schema and keeps it in the download fallback. Error codes, the preview limit and oversized-write behavior remain unchanged. ## Evidence The original native guest report reproduced the wrong conversation destination, and the application regression failed after the click on the base. Corrected reads preserve the target bytes, source tab, conversation URL and workspace identity. Controls cover keyboard activation, parent paths, encoded filename delimiters, extensionless files, missing and escaping targets, source replacement and dirty-target reuse. Native repository create/delete/create and active/stored-reader tests establish source-key reuse and distinct repository identities. The real application harness with modeled Gateway replies verifies that a retained foreign report cannot select replacement-repository evidence. This is separate from the live guest filesystem proof and makes no live cloud-placement claim. The final refusal comparison uses the same real Gateway, guest, report and absent target. Before the correction, `session_file_not_found` leaves the report visible but clears its catalog selection; UI `2a492b7` restores that selection. Native readback confirms the report and workspace identity, and independent filesystem readback confirms all seven fixture files, modes and configuration unchanged. A delayed `Access denied` application regression separately verifies the same recovery with modeled Gateway replies. Changed-file formatting/lint, generated-validator freshness, package boundaries and selected types pass. The broader correction qualified 403 cases across 27 affected files; integration qualified 227 cases across 14 files. The final refusal correction passed 126 cases across six files, including all ten file-link browser cases. These are successive scoped runs, with unchanged results retained at their recorded revisions. Current-head hosted tests, build, lint and types passed; the baseline-ratchet job reports 14 unrelated mock-export failures reproduced on the unchanged target ancestry with matching causal inputs. Its aggregate CI gate remains red under that attribution. The native oversized-file proof preserves the 300 KiB file’s preview-limit error, opens its metadata/download panel, downloads the exact original bytes and returns to the report. Earlier captures retain their actual revisions: [normal navigation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6fa1073d-c365-4288-84c6-e6caee9d46cb) at UI `2cfdf0e`, and [oversized download](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31de321b-d0e5-4e59-be72-fcef123e93ad) at UI/Gateway `6d13fb3`. Source and consumer checks qualify their continued applicability; they are not pixel-identical captures of the current shell. ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Desktop file navigation | ![An evidence link incorrectly opens a missing conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16f27944-747a-409a-a2f3-6c1cdd0af9d2) | ![The report link opens the intended evidence file beside the conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f3e5433-fcc1-4290-91f9-384006412324) | | Repository replaced while a report remains open | ![A retained report incorrectly opens evidence from a replacement repository](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1eb3dde3-9c05-4571-b7dc-590169cfbcb2) | ![The retained report stays open and the changed workspace is refused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cccdd64-9f2d-4ad5-af03-6c9f9d24cdd7) | | Oversized text evidence \(300 KiB\) | ![A report link incorrectly reports a workspace change and hides the download fallback](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1067dd3-8719-4948-856b-642df686a236) | ![The same report link opens the large\-file metadata and download action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c0915f0-be93-437b-ba86-8f8357b0e1fb) | | Refused document link restores the catalog selection | ![The report stays open after a missing\-file error, but its Files catalog row is no longer selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ad0e32c-9449-456d-a65b-8a2c834f2a97) | ![The same missing\-file error leaves the report selected in Files and its contents visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6e6fc16-05c2-4e9d-8089-1db8b9ed9690) | ### Native missing\-file refusal restores the report selection https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b5cdaf3-ca75-4f32-9527-6748b8351f1c ### Visual verification - Baseline: 01d66c79ae4c518b355469797752e09e75a35ec6 \(normal navigation\); 40ba28a2b98e86f74cf437755bb44a56d07db031 \(source replacement\); a0cf45b56a7407ccc8354e829ee7ccade920e54f UI with c1d0ecb Gateway \(oversized read\); 6d13fb3e83594364fde78b82fb7920ff8dde5154 UI \(refusal owner byte\-identical to c390ffaad36d477ea81a9f62ecaf7445bf3a60d9\) - Exact head: `2a492b773e3ad1e8a280e32ac8c78805129fa8f3` - Scenario: Follow document\-relative evidence links, preserve source identity and downloads, and restore the report selection when a link is refused\. - Runtime/build: Refusal after\-proof: UI 2a492b773e3ad1e8a280e32ac8c78805129fa8f3; unchanged real Gateway 6d13fb3, build 2026\.10\.8\-6d13fb3e8359\-2026\-10\-28T16\-19\-08\.023Z\. Before UI uses 6d13fb3 with the same Gateway\. Earlier comparisons retain their stated execution revisions\. - Fragment\-bearing evidence link: Correct file and unchanged conversation URL - Source and target integrity: Seven synthetic files preserved; originating workspace identity retained - Additional native controls: Keyboard, parent\-directory, extensionless, missing and denied targets, fragment\-only and session links - Oversized read contract: Same INVALID\_REQUEST/session\_file\_too\_large and 256 KiB preview limit; optional source metadata retained - Original download bytes: 307,200 bytes downloaded with the same SHA\-256 before and after - Refused\-link catalog selection: Report aria\-current is absent after the native refusal before the fix and true afterward; report content and conversation URL remain unchanged - Native guest identity, read scopes and workspace verified independently\. - The same authored report and absent target are used before and after; no fixture or model turn was added\. - The native Gateway rejects the missing file with INVALID\_REQUEST/session\_file\_not\_found\. Both captures keep the report visible and the conversation URL unchanged\. - The baseline preview owner is byte\-identical to c390; the corrected served module matches committed 2a492 source and direct Vite output\. - The original report content and source identity were read back through the native RPC after each interaction\. - The model selector is masked identically; the report, authored link, refusal and catalog selection remain visible\. - Oversized before uses A0 UI and the unchanged c1d0 failure owner; after uses the actual corrected 6d13 Gateway/UI and native RPC/HTTP receipts\. - Normal navigation was captured through the real guest Gateway at UI 2cfdf0e\. Repository replacement was captured at d175a33 with modeled Gateway replies and separate native repository tests; it is not a live cloud\-placement claim\. - Earlier captures retain their original revisions and qualified behavior\. prs.title: fix(system-agent): use configured fallbacks when primary admission fails
prs.body:
Closes #151605

## What Problem This Solves

A maintenance conversation can be rejected even when its explicitly configured model fallback works. Reuse that exact successful fallback under the original agent; never substitute a different model, credential, runtime or plugin owner on later turns or approved writes.

## User Impact

A failed primary no longer unnecessarily blocks maintenance. Existing requester checks, explicit approval, tool permissions and native writers remain mandatory. An unconfigured fallback or changed owner cannot authorize persistence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the configured fallback order and profile pins, retain the successful execution binding, and revalidate it on reuse and at persistent-effect boundaries. Secret creation is itself a persistent effect: the binding is checked again at native SQLite commit admission, before the existing synchronous requester check grants the commit. Read-only binding validation does not enqueue config-health writes behind the transaction it is validating.

Current revision: `6cec235d9a72849cd21ff18c9498e0a7f1bef437`. Integration base: `053da3a9bad240aa67482ae11b07dc5fce1e2200`. Contributor history is retained. Current-main CLI text handling, Gateway fixtures and database-worker registration are preserved. The contribution adds no schema, migration, permission mechanism, resource-limit change or secret overwrite/delete; upstream agent schema 38 is retained.

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior addressed

Configured fallback selection and profile order; exact-owner reuse; approved physical config/secret writes; refusal after requester, fallback or credential ownership changes, including a change after the caller's initial check but before native secret commit. Store-backed CLI credentials are also exercised while creating a separate secret.

### Real setup tested

Source integration uses isolated synthetic state, the real chat approval engine, native SQLite workers, team secret store and physical config writer. Only external HTTP model responses and the external CLI backend are synthetic; the CLI process really executes. No production model, account, data or deployment is used.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/system-agent/inference-fallback.configured-chain.test.ts src/system-agent/verified-inference.fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/system-agent/verified-inference.fallback.test.ts src/system-agent/inference-fallback.configured-chain.test.ts src/system-agent/inference-route.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/system-agent/verified-inference.fallback.test.ts src/secrets/store/secret-store-config-ref.worker.test.ts src/secrets/store/secret-store.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-store.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-operation-admission.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-operation-admission.timeout.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

The late secret-write regression first reproduced before the repair: both late fallback removal and credential reassignment left one physical secret behind while config publication was refused. The six unchanged earlier controls passed. This was an actual store read-back failure, not a mocked write result.

After native commit-admission validation and the passive config read (sanitized output summary):

```text
Late fallback removal: rejected; new secrets 0; config reference absent.
Late credential reassignment: rejected; new secrets 0; config reference absent.
Unchanged authority: one new secret and its config reference saved.
Opaque CLI owner unchanged: 6 real CLI probes; one new secret/reference saved.
Opaque CLI owner revoked: 3 real CLI probes; no new secret/reference saved.
Store-backed CLI profile unchanged: original credential preserved; one new secret/reference saved.
Store-backed CLI profile revoked: original credential preserved; no new secret/reference saved.
Complete fallback suites: 2 files, 31 tests passed.
Native secret/SQLite sibling suites: 5 additional files, 112 tests passed.
Existing configured-route suite after identity-owner relocation: 13 tests passed.
```

The 156 cases above are unique across 8 files; filtered/repeated runs are not added. The sibling command includes the earlier two opaque cases; those overlapping cases are excluded from the total. The unchanged route-identity projection was moved into its existing route owner to satisfy the native line-growth ratchet; the complete fallback and existing route suites passed again afterward. A self-wait in the first repair was diagnosed rather than hidden by longer timeouts: config-health observation tried to write shared state while the secret transaction awaited validation. The supported passive snapshot read removes that incidental write without skipping credential, plugin, runtime or requester validation.

### Observed result after fix

A verified configured fallback remains reusable under its original owner. Approved unchanged authority writes; revoked authority cannot create the new secret or publish its reference. A materialized store-backed CLI credential can be checked while another secret awaits commit without the observed self-wait, and the existing credential is untouched.

### What was not tested

Historical compiled Gateway and official `2026.10.4` upgrade-state controls were recorded on the earlier `fac94fb1833b8b7d5b2cde6165ae2fe14eabfadb` lineage. They are not current-revision execution or latest-stable compatibility proof. The later frozen-source runtime build also predates this commit-admission repair.

Fresh compiled Gateway, real-provider traffic and current latest-stable migration were not rerun here: namespace isolation was refused before application startup. No isolation policy was relaxed. In an admitted isolated environment, the remaining product check is the canonical runtime build followed by compiled CLI/Gateway/SDK: failed primary, two retained conversation turns, actual config proposal and separate approval, physical config read-back; then repeat on state created by the current official stable release using its supported native migration. An independently installed candidate release archive remains unqualified. Arbitrary third-party harness callbacks are not exhaustively certified by these fixtures.

## Current CI, review and proposed authority contract

The original 19 contribution source/test files remain byte-identical to the functionally validated predecessor `497ff3ed880f6bb5dba829b403b177cfc7700e55`. The worker registry retains new main entries plus the two fallback suites. Two existing consumer fixtures now follow native snapshot/close contracts: persisted setup reads materialize defaults through the real config validator; device cleanup awaits the existing asynchronous state-database close before its test-latch reset. Production guards, business assertions and timeouts are unchanged.

At tested revision `e3c9e7bfacdfdff41be10937da942e678ef63407` (tree `8e462f23239c5fd3eee3e29212a27538fc1172eb`, main `8828adca7e5877faac3bea151b98c438368a4e3d`), after integrating upstream agent schema 38, the two real fallback/CLI files passed 31 cases, setup passed 27 and device passed 18. These 76 current integration cases include 31 already counted in the earlier 156; they are not added as 76 new cases or called a full-tree test. Core types, the services and gateway-methods consumer type graphs, 293-rule lint and formatting also passed on that integrated candidate. Hosted CI and a new durable review for this publication are pending; no earlier-head status is reused as a fresh full-tree execution.

The setup regression was independently reproduced on the exact CI main parent `c8b7c4c435b1eb037445f637eb808211bdbaecc5` without the contribution: the same two cases failed (25/27 passed). The fixture correction passed 27/27 without relaxing route comparison. The hosted device failure was an active-borrower exception at synchronous cleanup. Its original Node/ARM file passed 18/18 on both main and candidate; this does not reproduce or attribute that Bun/x64 failure. The cleanup now obeys the documented async worker-drain contract; the new hosted run must confirm that boundary. No sleep, catch-and-ignore, runtime substitution in CI or enlarged timeout was added.

Publication head additionally integrates `053da3a9bad240aa67482ae11b07dc5fce1e2200` while preserving the 19 contribution files and two consumer fixtures byte-for-byte. That later full tree has not received another local 76-case execution. Its exact-tree budget counter and native pre-commit passed; hosted CI is the full published-tree acceptance, not a reused local PASS.

**Proposed behavior for review:** an explicitly configured fallback may satisfy maintenance inference only as its exact verified binding under the original agent. Existing tool permissions, explicit user approval and requester authority are unchanged. Removing that fallback or changing its credential/runtime/plugin owner refuses reuse and persistence. This is a proposal for review, not a security waiver or a claimed maintainer decision.

**Before merge:** obtain normal enforced security approval for the final revision and maintainer review of the proposed binding contract. Earlier-head CI and durable reviews are not attributed to this new head. No merge or deployment is requested.

## Related public context

[PR #156755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156755) addresses implicit Bedrock SDK credential proof, not configured fallback admission; that independent change is not included here. [PR #181669](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181669) preserves explicitly pinned session models for automation events; this change does not relax ordinary session pins or introduce another fallback-selection policy.

## Test-line budget and cost

The untouched `053da3a9bad240aa67482ae11b07dc5fce1e2200` main control contains 6,291,362 test lines against its 6,289,827 ceiling. Its canonical zero-delta control passes; the inherited debt is 1,535, not a claimed main functional failure. This contribution adds 1,064 lines, including 17 lines of consumer-fixture compatibility fixes. The supported ceiling adjustment is exactly 2,599 lines over that main ceiling; the actual merged total is 6,292,426. The canonical counter passes with zero additional author-created slack. Earlier 400/1,778-line figures belonged to different main trees and are superseded by this source-bound measurement.

No tests or assertions were removed, and no runtime/resource cap, counter implementation or failure classification was changed. Native ownership and approved persistence tests remain because the before-fix controls exposed an actually saved secret; a mocked write would lose the distinguishing regression.

Prior measured wall times: route 13 cases 29.23s; the two fallback files 31 cases 146.28s in a shared shard. Individual case-time sums were 83.96s for configured-chain and 37.90s for CLI, not per-file wall times. These tests exercise real worker custody, physical writes and CLI processes with isolated authority state; only model responses are synthetic. No live model charges or artificial sleeps were added.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep scoped scaffold package names valid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw plugins init @scope/pkg --type tool` or `--type provider` succeeds but generates invalid npm package name `openclaw-plugin-@scope/pkg`. npm's publish preview rejects the untouched project.

## User Impact

Scoped tool/provider scaffolds now generate `@scope/openclaw-plugin-pkg`, preserving the plugin ID `@scope/pkg`. Ordinary IDs retain `openclaw-plugin-<id>`. Provider install metadata and trusted-publisher instructions use the corrected package name.

## Why This Change Was Made

Derive the package name once and reuse it in both affected writers. For scoped IDs, the existing basename prefix goes after the scope separator. Feature scaffolds retain their existing ID contract. This repairs producer output without introducing a new publishing command, validator, dependency or package-name policy.

## Evidence

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186901#issuecomment-6475755167

Normal built CLI in secretless Linux Docker, **Node 24.22.1**. Pinned main `79a4b37034ca9dd5f7006405a79660f5d03b295e` and product head `ed6219518ebb25c8ec7a2dacbeaa35e11531083c`: **main twice and candidate twice**, tool/provider × ordinary/scoped inputs (**16 scaffold commands + 16 independent npm previews**). First repeat uses default paths; second uses explicit output directories.

- All generation commands exit 0. Main's four scoped outputs contain invalid `openclaw-plugin-@scope/pkg`, rejected by npm with `Invalid name`. Candidate's four scoped outputs contain `@scope/openclaw-plugin-pkg`, accepted by npm. All eight ordinary controls retain their package names and are accepted.
- Actual manifests retain exact plugin IDs. Default scoped paths are nested `$TASK/@scope/pkg`; explicit output paths are honored. Provider install spec, README publisher target and accepted npm JSON name agree.
- Every generated file hash is unchanged after the consumer preview. The collector does not repair output. npm uses **dry-run, offline, ignored scripts, empty task npmrc/cache and a loopback registry**; no registry write or real credentials.
- Focused owner suite **26/26**, 3.09s; lint and repository formatter parity pass. Committed tool/provider regressions fail on pinned main for incorrect package name/spec (**2 failed, 24 unselected**, 2.54s).
- Final head `041d5439acf1b0e959371b3234daeff8a76cb5b9` preserves the contributor commit; subsequent test-only consolidation moves scoped inputs into the existing tool deleted-cwd and provider-metadata fixtures, removing duplicate setup. Product bytes are unchanged from the measured build. **Production +2, tests 0, docs +2**; no baseline change.

Not claimed: live npm/ClawHub publication, generated dependency installation or TypeScript compilation, provider/model requests, arbitrary invalid-ID policy, release upgrades, or native Windows/macOS filesystem proof. The initial test-fixture path mistake was corrected before the final passing checks; it was not a product failure.

## Merge Danger

Two-way code door: revert restores the previous naming logic, without changing schemas or existing installed plugins. Revert does not rewrite projects already generated. Blast radius is npm package metadata and matching provider publication references in newly generated scoped tool/provider projects; plugin IDs and output-directory selection remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): stop suspension retries when interrupted
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway suspend --wait 30` continues sending mutating prepare requests after Ctrl-C/SIGTERM while root cleanup waits. The retry loop ignores the invocation's existing cancellation signal.

## Fix

Thanks to @Alix-007 for the original report, fix and proof; the contributor commit is preserved. The suspension owner consumes the existing async-work signal before dispatch, after non-ready replies and during the abortable timer. An already-dispatched prepare still settles, and ready-result handling precedes the cancellation check so the operator retains any acquired lease receipt. No automatic resume, server cancellation, new owner, flag, protocol or configuration.

## Evidence

Both main `79a4b37034ca9dd5f7006405a79660f5d03b295e` and candidate ran as built executables in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker. Twenty real CLI invocations covered SIGINT, SIGTERM, normal busy→ready, SIGINT during held prepare, and `--wait 0`: **twice per scenario per revision**, with independently recorded remote requests and captured natural exit/stdout/stderr.

- Main after SIGINT: no exit in 2.5s; prepares **1→10** on both runs. SIGTERM: **1→9**, no exit.
- Candidate: natural **130/143**, **one prepare only**, empty stdout on both runs.
- Normal completion remains exit0 with two prepares and a lease. Held in-flight ready replies still print the lease before exit130. Zero-wait busy remains exit1 with busy JSON. All controls pass twice on each revision.
- Focused tests: **12 passed** on candidate; identical final tests on main **9 passed / 3 intended failures** (before-dispatch, busy-reply and sleep cancellation).
- Oxlint **0 warnings/errors**; Oxfmt applied.

The matrix exercises the actual parser, root signal/cleanup scope, RPC client and suspension owner through a real loopback WebSocket connection. The remote Gateway is a deterministic protocol peer; no live freeze is claimed. Candidate's build metadata phase initially timed out; recovering that exact phase succeeded without code changes.

## Simplification

Four cancellation phases plus ordinary busy JSON now share one table. Removed redundant transport/sleep-argument echoes and duplicate literal output checks while retaining stable IDs, invalid input, monotonic overshoot, operator hints, cancellation receipts, busy JSON and resume outcomes. Whole-PR delta against merge base: **tests 0; production +17; docs +3**. Existing docs explain interruption and acquired-lease settlement.

## Merge Risk

Bounded CLI-only change. Already-admitted mutation settlement remains authoritative. Not tested: live Gateway freeze, automatic resume, external services or native macOS/Windows signal delivery. [Full repeated runtime evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186886#issuecomment-6475996158).

prs.title: fix(voice-call): stop continue polling when interrupted
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw voicecall continue` keeps polling after Ctrl-C/SIGTERM when using the Gateway, because the existing voice CLI lifetime owner listens only after entering standalone runtime. It can also publish a completed response after interruption.

## Fix

Thanks to @Alix-007 for the original report, fix and proof; the contributor commit is preserved. The existing voice command lifetime owner listens early for continuation, passes its signal through read-only result polling and the abortable wait, prevents fallback/output after cancellation, and restores listeners during cleanup. Other command lifetimes are unchanged.

The admitted `voicecall.continue.start` mutation deliberately does not receive the cancellation signal: it settles before local observation stops. Interruption does not end the call or cancel server speech. No new SDK API, flag, schema, configuration, provider policy or dependency.

## Evidence

Built main `90d6cf560292d4906fff5b48edaba774ea250629` and candidate in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker. Actual enabled voice-call CLI, real command parser/signal lifecycle and Gateway RPC client over a real loopback WebSocket protocol fixture. Each invocation uses fresh isolated profile/config/state, confirmed by its built config command.

Each final scenario ran **twice on main and twice on candidate**:

- SIGINT/SIGTERM after pending result: main keeps running and sends requests **2→4** within 2.5 seconds; candidate exits naturally **130/143**, requests **2→2**, no stdout.
- SIGTERM during withheld result RPC: main remains waiting; candidate exits143 without output.
- SIGINT during held initial start: main later continues polling; candidate waits for the admitted reply, then exits130 with no result poll/output.
- SIGINT during held result followed by completion: main prints stale completion before exit130; candidate prints nothing.
- Ordinary completion: both exit0 with two requests and the expected completion JSON.

Focused CLI suite: **28 passed** on candidate; identical regression on main **27 passed / 1 intended failure** (Gateway polling lacks interruption ownership). Oxlint **0 warnings/errors**; Oxfmt applied. Full repeated observations are linked below.

## Simplification

The regression reuses the existing owned-interruption fixture rather than adding another 108-line simulated phase matrix. Existing standalone creation, active-operation, printed-call settlement, listener cleanup, errors, deadlines, brief handling and exposure cases remain. The obsolete sleep mock is removed; actual abortable sleep is exercised. Whole-PR delta against merge base: **tests −2; production +50; docs +4**. Production growth extends the existing lifetime/transport owners without changing other command semantics. The later test-only repair explicitly types the rejection callback as unknown; the exact type-aware lint check and focused suite pass in Docker.

## Merge Risk

Local CLI observation only. Remote peer is a protocol fixture, not a live call: no telephony/provider operation, external credentials, Gateway call cancellation, system-clock change, or native macOS/Windows signal delivery is claimed.

[Full repeated executable proof and admitted-start settlement controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186905#issuecomment-6477305658).

prs.title: fix(docs): cancel searches when interrupted
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw docs <query>` does not stop its HTTP request/download after Ctrl-C or SIGTERM, leaving root cleanup waiting. A response arriving after interruption can still print search results.

## Fix

Thanks to @Alix-007 for the original report, repair and proof; the contributor commit is preserved. The existing docs search owner consumes the invocation's async-work signal, combines it with the unchanged 30-second request timeout, and stops before dispatch or result/error publication after interruption. No new cancellation owner, public API, configuration, flag or timeout policy.

## Evidence

Built unpatched main `6cc904a742132cd529d2e4d4b6ae4b77375a36d9` and candidate in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker. **Twenty real CLI invocations**: headers-held SIGINT, partial-body SIGTERM, late completion after SIGINT, normal search and genuine HTTP503—**twice each per revision**.

- Main remains alive beyond 2.5s with open HTTP connections during headers/body interruption. Candidate exits naturally **130/143**, with empty stdout and independently observed aborted HTTP connections before cleanup.
- When a valid result arrives 250ms after SIGINT, main prints stale results; candidate prints nothing.
- Ordinary success remains exit0 with expected normalized JSON; ordinary HTTP503 remains exit1 with its search-failure envelope.
- Each invocation sends exactly one real `/api/search?q=fixture-query` request.
- Focused tests: candidate **11 passed**; identical main tests **10 passed / 1 intended failure** (interrupted retained HTTP200 body stays unsettled).
- Repository type-aware lint: **no problems** in both changed files; Oxfmt applied.

The real executable/parser/root lifecycle/native fetch/body reader/output owners run against a task-owned HTTP server. A preload rewrites only the docs URL origin while forwarding request options and AbortSignal; it does not fabricate fetch results. Fresh isolated profile/HOME/config/state are confirmed by the built CLI.

## Simplification

Extended the existing retained-body settlement test rather than keeping a parallel cancellation matrix. HTTP503, abort settlement and no-output behavior share the same real stream/clone fixture. Removed its real 500ms timer race and redundant cleanup; fake timers now flush deterministic settlement. Existing normalization, query/limit, homepage, malformed/oversized responses and rich/plain rendering remain covered. Whole-PR delta against merge base: **tests −4; production +11; docs +3**.

## Merge Risk

Small read-only CLI cancellation change. Ordinary failure reporting and the 30-second timeout remain intact. Proof uses deterministic local HTTP and Linux signals; it does not claim live docs-service availability, external credentials, system-clock changes or native macOS/Windows signal delivery. [Full repeated runtime evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186906#issuecomment-6478586681).

prs.title: fix(wiki): preserve serialized ChatGPT transcript formatting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ChatGPT imports collapse line breaks, code indentation, and repeated spaces when a text part is stored as a serialized JSON string, corrupting the archived transcript.

## User Impact

Serialized text parts retain the same internal formatting as ordinary text parts. Re-importing the original export repairs an affected existing source page while preserving its Notes. The repair uses the existing import-run snapshot and rollback behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The importer already distinguishes serialized text/image parts from ordinary pasted JSON. This keeps that discrimination and trims only the text's outer whitespace, matching the sibling text paths. Digest/preference normalization remains separate.

Related: #182049 (serialized-part handling and preservation of ordinary pasted JSON).

## Evidence

### Independent current-main replay

[Built importer byte-level proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186909#issuecomment-6476024079) compares main `79a4b370…` and this exact candidate twice each in secretless Node 24.22.1 Linux Docker. Saved Markdown retains multiline code, indentation, blank lines and repeated spaces only on the candidate serialized path; ordinary/structured text, pasted JSON and image filtering are controlled. Two baseline-created vaults were repaired while preserving handwritten Notes, followed by unchanged re-imports and exact-byte rollback restoration. No model/account credentials were used. [Exact-head CI gate is successful](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40728538669/job/122966341672). No source changes or repeat CI runs were needed.

Real built CLI RED → GREEN with independent reads of the generated Markdown, then repair of a baseline-generated vault, unchanged re-import and rollback. Node 24.22.1; Linux; no mocked importer, filesystem, CLI, or store.

Exact head: `b3a8fefcaa88a773ebbddfeb7e6d2b06ba964e8b`. Original RED: `3e1e3652ff2599345668754cec60f0a4fdd8fd15`; the newer merge base `26cc81a8b17` has identical importer inputs. Each driver checks checkout HEAD against `dist/build-info.json`.

| Real user path | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline imports a plain text part and a serialized text part containing the same multiline Python/list text | Both created; plain text preserved, serialized text flattened and `"a  b"` changed to `"a b"` |
| Head imports the same two records into a fresh isolated vault | Both source pages preserve newlines, four-space indentation, double spaces, accents and Japanese verbatim |
| Fresh-process re-import | 0 created, 0 updated, 2 skipped |
| Head re-imports the **baseline-created** vault after an operator Note is added | 1 repaired page, 1 skipped control; exact multiline transcript and Note retained |
| Re-import after repair | 2 skipped; repaired page byte-identical |
| Roll back the repair's run id | 1 previous page restored; original transcript and operator Note retained |

<details>
<summary>Inputs, commands and proof receipt</summary>

The two conversation fixtures differ only in whether `content.parts[0]` is the plain `text` below or `JSON.stringify({ content_type: "text", text })`:

````js
const text = '```python\nif ready:\n    print("a  b")\n```\n\n- café\n- 日本語';
````

Public commands run as separate actual CLI processes:

```text
node dist/entry.js wiki chatgpt import --export <isolated-source>/conversations.json --json
node dist/entry.js wiki chatgpt import --export <same-source>/conversations.json --json
node dist/entry.js wiki chatgpt rollback <repair-run-id> --json
```

Generated pages independently read after the import exits:

```text
sources/chatgpt-2024-10-04-plaincontrol.md
sources/chatgpt-2024-10-04-serializedtext.md
```

Fresh-vault receipt: 2026-10-28T16:33:31Z; import 10277 ms, unchanged re-import 5314 ms, both exit 0; both pages contain the exact transcript. Source export and configuration unchanged. Frozen RED/GREEN driver SHA-256: `381ba8c1806e150c535c456ea1ecaa2eac9f344c737a1cb8748d049d3f4ae8cc`.

Upgrade receipt: 2026-10-28T16:38:10Z; repair 12239 ms, unchanged re-import 6040 ms, rollback 7743 ms, all exit 0. Rollback reports `removedCount: 0`, `restoredCount: 1`, `alreadyRolledBack: false`; independent file reads verify both the prior transcript and operator Note. Upgrade driver SHA-256: `bab3bcc7872acf3731532fb0b897663e26939d3ac06004301da0103aedde4336`.

The runs use temporary home/state/workspace/vault directories, only the Memory Wiki plugin, bridge disabled and automatic ingestion compilation disabled. No external account, provider/model, or ChatGPT API is used.

</details>

Focused checks passed:

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/chatgpt-import-text.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3/3. The changed serialized-text fixture fails on the baseline; ordinary pasted JSON and image filtering remain covered.
- Source-backed scoped typecheck via `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p <external-two-file-scope> --noEmit` — pass; real plugin-test configuration, source imports.
- Type-aware lint for both TypeScript files, formatter for all three files, and `git diff --check` — pass.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts sourcePerformance` — pass on the committed head, followed by the native flows above. `pnpm docs:list` completed.

Production +1/−1 line; tests +1/−2; docs +3/−0. No new dependency, configuration, schema, protocol, storage format or import mode. Outer whitespace retains the existing trimming contract. This proof uses synthetic supported export records; it does not claim a live ChatGPT export download or model run.

AI-assisted implementation and validation; author inspected the complete change, callers, sibling text paths and regression coverage.

## Merge Danger

Rollback-backed two-way door: reverting the code restores future parsing behavior; reversing an already applied import repair requires its recorded import-run rollback. The shipped rollback restored exact pre-repair bytes in both new scenarios. Blast radius is supported serialized ChatGPT text parts in imported source pages; no schema, permission, protocol or storage-format change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes four reproducible current-main failures in the rejected cron failure-alert routing test when scheduling is disabled. This is a maintainer-requested repair of the red test file.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Rejected failure alerts still reach their default owner or explicit conversation through ordinary session admission, including when automatic scheduling is disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The breaking commit is b8c02c5f4c54 (#187057): removing redundant post-completion maintenance also removed an incidental await that the test relied on. `cron.run()` completes durable run accounting while failure-alert transport and its outcome write-back continue asynchronously. The immediate receipt-count assertion could fail before the fallback queued; test cleanup then stopped its owner.

Wait for the existing observer to record the real session-event receipt before checking its acceptance, completed execution, destination, and thread. All existing assertions remain. Preserve the real runner exports in the model mock and inline the failure transport callback to keep net test lines at zero. The completion optimization and production owners remain unchanged.

## Evidence

All commands ran locally with isolated HOME and OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR. Only model output is synthetic; cron execution, SQLite outcome persistence, Gateway target resolution, session admission, and session execution use their real owners. No external live-model or running-Gateway claim is made by this test-only change.

- Original file on unchanged base 4f4d241683ee: **4/4 fail** at the immediate receipt-count assertion on both Node and pinned Bun. Node: 38.37 s Vitest / 41.24 s wrapper. Bun: 54.85 s / 61.69 s.
- Causal control: restore only the `request ||` condition removed by b8c02c5f4c54 in `timer-outcome-finalization.ts`; the original file passes **4/4** on Node (64.26 s / 67.23 s). That temporary production edit was fully removed.

- Final file: same command with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` — **4/4 pass**, 65.08 s / 67.39 s. These four cases exercise real durable session execution and lifecycle cleanup; no sleeps, retries, or timeout increases were added.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental` — pass.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/cron/service.failure-alert-notifications.test.ts`, focused oxfmt check, and `git diff --check` — pass.

prs.title: fix(chat): safely steer an existing Gateway-queued input
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Gateway-queued input has no safe control operation for steering it into an active turn without resending the message. ## User Impact User impact: an authorized client can steer the original queued input, including attachments, while preserving its identity and FIFO position on definite rejection. No config, storage migration, or protocol-version bump is introduced. **Backend only.** The Control UI button, UI tests, and screenshots moved to stacked follow-up #160593. Neither PR is authorized for merge or deployment by this task. ## Why This Change Was Made The existing queue owner reserves an already-enqueued source in place and exposes it through `chat.steer`. Fresh and queued steering share injection and settlement logic; the RPC never reconstructs or resends input. The lifecycle interlocks withdrawal, coalesces duplicate requests, pins the target across awaits, and retains original work admission through settlement. Uncertain delivery must not replay. ## Evidence ### October 1 rebase Rebased onto main 00f3a2063022388cb7907964fe098537fbe3fd15, preserving the two-PR stack and original publication markers. Current head: efef44c34388a5b23de1c274d9ecbfec84b5166d. Preserved main's current overflow/front-queue behavior, native cross-profile steering admission, and recorder option types. A deterministic rebase regression found stalled-turn recovery could claim an input already reserved for steering; the fix treats a reserved first eligible input as a barrier rather than claiming it or skipping to a later source. The single-source and later-sibling failure sequences were reproduced before the fix. No second queue owner, payload replay, schema migration, or config change. - 115 focused Gateway, queue, and Codex cases passed across nine files (166.51 s wall); the final strengthened recovery file passed all 25 cases (34.63 s wall). - The public RPC-schema regression moved unchanged to chat-steer.test.ts because main's shared index test reached its line cap. The focused file passed (1 case, 2.65 s wall); coverage and limits were not weakened. - Production core/UI types, scoped lint, line-cap/assertion checks, and the UI build passed. The independent combined review's reserved-head finding was addressed with the regression above; a clean re-review is not being inferred. - Current browser evidence lives in the stacked UI PR. Earlier test timings below remain historical, not new-head CI. Both PRs remain drafts; nothing was merged or deployed. This refresh used scoped checks and browser-boundary proof, not a live-provider or installed-upgrade rehearsal. Hosted checks are separate; prior-head results are not current-head CI.
Earlier September 28 validation, timings, and limitations The deeper audit found real failures; this is not a no-regressions claim based on E2E success. - Deterministic queue-owner coverage exercises promotion of a later collect group, accepted/rejected/waiting reservations across stale-drain recovery, throwing release/overflow callbacks, exact target replacement, duplicate requests, uncertain receipts, and FIFO fallback. Accepted or uncertain custody is never resent. - Composed Gateway proof enters through chat.send, retains the real queued source via runReplyAgent, and promotes it through chat.steer. It checks actual transcript state and personal-tool dispatch: equal-permission participants are retained, unqualified personal effects reject ambiguity, explicit participant selection uses that participant, and incompatible permissions stay queued. Model preparation/transport are controlled test boundaries, not a live provider. - Integrated backend/protocol/Codex selection: **226 tests across 15 files passed**, 186.11 s wall with --maxWorkers=1. The final mechanical retirement extraction additionally passed 30 tests across two files (50.32 s wall). These selections overlap; counts are not cumulative. UI reconnect/reload handling is recorded in the stacked PR. prs.title: fix(ios): switched chats open at their first message instead of the latest
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on iPhone, switching to another chat shows the start of that chat instead of its latest message while the rest of the chat's load is still running.

## User Impact

User impact: a chat opened from the sidebar lands on its latest message as soon as the transcript appears, instead of sitting at the top until every background request for that chat (health check, session list, mark-read, model catalog) has finished.

## Why This Change Was Made

`OpenClawChatView` did its one initial scroll-to-latest only when `isLoading` turned false. That flag covers the whole session bootstrap: history, then the health poll, the 50-row session list, mark-read and the model catalog. The transcript (cached or live) paints well before that, and `.defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom, for: .sizeChanges)` does not keep the bottom when a switched chat grows from empty, so the reader sat at the top for the remaining round trips.

Transcript changes that arrive before the initial position is settled now re-apply that initial position; the end-of-load restore is unchanged. The initial-position helper only sets the follow target and enqueues a scroll command, and that command already drops requests from a previous session, so it is safe to re-run per change.

Accepted edge case: a reader who scrolls up during that loading window is pulled back to the initial position on the next transcript change, until the load settles. The window is short and the previous behavior was worse (no scroll at all).

The iOS screenshot fixture gains `--openclaw-chat-switch-fixture` (two long fake chats) and `--openclaw-slow-model-catalog-fixture` (holds the model catalog for 6 s, standing in for a slow Gateway round trip). The new `testSwitchingChatsOpensAtLatestMessage` UI test uses both. The regenerated native source inventory (`apps/.i18n/native-source.json`) records that fixture's new strings.

## Evidence

Simulator recording, iPhone 17 Pro on iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.1, fake fixture data only. The left side is `main` (dadf9122058); the right side is the same build with this fix applied. The clip opens the sidebar and taps "Launch plan". On `main`, the chat stays on its first message until the held model catalog finishes, then jumps. With the fix, it opens on the latest message.

![Switching to "Launch plan": main shows the first message, the fix shows the latest message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0acb4504-517c-4ebb-9326-a6d6001e7926)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31246eb4-18a4-4453-961c-971b273473e8

- **UI test**: `OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testSwitchingChatsOpensAtLatestMessage`. On `main` it fails with `CHAT_SWITCH_LANDED_AWAY_FROM_LATEST` (44.6 s). With the fix it passes (33.8 s). Both results come from the same job, with an incremental rebuild in between: [fork run 40789182509](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/40789182509). The snapshot UI tests are not part of PR CI; run it with `xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawUITests -destination '<iPhone simulator>' -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testSwitchingChatsOpensAtLatestMessage`. No cheaper layer covers this: the defect is SwiftUI's runtime scroll behavior.
- **Position trace**: three sidebar switches (B, A, B), sampled through XCUITest about once a second. On `main`, the latest message first appears 4.0–4.7 s after each switch; until then the chat's first message is on screen. With the fix, the latest message is in place at the first sample of every switch.
- **Without the held catalog**, `main` still lands at the top for 264 ms in-process (an instrumented run logged rows painting at about 3,100 pt from the bottom). With a real Gateway, that window covers every remaining bootstrap round trip.
- **Local review**: autoreview `--mode branch --base dadf9122058` over this tree, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`, no findings. One flagged uncertainty — whether `restoreInitialScrollPosition()` has side effects — checked: it only sets the follow target and enqueues a scroll command.
- **Lint**: pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 `--lint` reports 0 of 3 changed files needing formatting. Pinned SwiftLint 0.65.1 `--strict` on the changed app sources reports only the existing `function_body_length` advisory on the untouched `seedMessages` ([fork run 40793921673](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/40793921673)).

<details><summary>Instrumented scroll log, first switch (evidence branch only, not in this PR)</summary>

Before (`main`):

```text
00:13:07.668 sessionTarget -> agent:main:launch-plan loading=true rows=0
00:13:07.835 timeline rows=17 performed=false loading=true
00:13:07.852 geometry distance 3050 -> 3390 performed=false
00:13:14.208 isLoading -> false performed=false rows=17
00:13:14.220 command scrollTo anchorY=1.000000
00:13:14.364 geometry distance 230 -> 0 performed=true
```

After (this PR):

```text
00:18:06.370 sessionTarget -> agent:main:launch-plan loading=true rows=0
00:18:06.597 timeline rows=17 performed=false loading=true
00:18:06.598 restore rows=17 loading=true
00:18:06.665 command scrollTo anchorY=1.000000
00:18:12.975 isLoading -> false performed=false rows=17
```

</details>
