prs.title: fix: keep agent settings focused during identity refresh
prs.body: Fixes #187103 ## What Problem This Solves While a user has keyboard focus on an agent's settings button in the sidebar menu, another agent's identity refresh can replace that focused button. Focus falls to the document body, and pressing Enter leaves the current chat open instead of reaching the selected agent's settings. This can happen when another authorized client saves an agent's `IDENTITY.md` through the Gateway. ## User Impact The agent menu keeps the focused settings control usable while it displays refreshed identities. Enter continues to open the intended agent's settings without switching the active chat agent or changing its unsent draft. An agent that actually disappears still loses its row, and pending creation still replaces that row's settings action with its existing disabled state. This restores the existing keyboard workflow. It adds no configuration, permission, protocol or storage change. ## Why This Change Was Made The shared menu already keys its rows, but the sidebar constructed each row's nested content inside a memo that was replaced on inventory publication. The parent row could survive while its focused child button was destroyed. The sidebar now creates its keyed menu-entry mapping once for the menu's lifetime, using the existing Solid `mapArray` pattern. Each entry reads the current agent and live parameters, so names, avatars, selection, pending status and ordering continue to update. Group-avatar content and the Show all entry remain reactive as the roster changes. The shared menu continues to own keyboard navigation and control registration; no focus-recovery mechanism is added. ## Evidence The original keyboard journey fails on the base when an accepted identity refresh is inserted after Tab focuses another agent's settings: the button disconnects, Enter targets `body`, and the existing route assertion times out. The regression retains that journey and also checks the unsent draft after returning from settings. Related roster coverage checks initially empty menus, replacement snapshots, pending creation and actual removal. Remote changed-file formatting, lint, i18n verification and the selected type graphs passed. The menu cases (11), existing agent-menu browser cases (6), pending-agent cases (2), and the focused keyboard E2E (1) passed. The latter retains the original settings navigation and subsequent agent-switch assertions while adding the identity refresh and draft check. A real Gateway baseline also reproduced the failure: an actual identity-file save emitted the event, the UI read and displayed the new identity, the focused settings button disconnected, and Enter left the chat and draft unchanged. The served UI module matched the recorded baseline and the page did not reload during the recording. The matching real-Gateway scenario passed on this head in Chromium and WebKit: the original settings control stayed connected and focused, Enter opened the intended agent’s settings, the active session stayed unchanged, and Back restored the unsent draft. Each capture verified the served source and build identity and had one document load. Independent engineering review found no unresolved defect. All selected UI, type, browser and performance CI lanes passed in [CI run 40791696243](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40791696243). The remaining failure is the inherited mock-export baseline: the same 14 factories fail on exact main revision a968dc19900d, and their complete source, target-export, scanner, baseline-ledger and dependency inputs are unchanged in this PR’s tested merge. The CI aggregate and its published status mirror that failure; those checks remain failed. This change does not modify those factories or their inputs. The evidence establishes this identity-refresh failure and its repair. It does not identify the trigger of an earlier intermittent keyboard CI failure or claim focus preservation when the roster physically reorders. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Before: the focused settings button disappears when another agent’s identity refreshes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/805f3200-30fa-473b-bfe0-36f8c6e3eb90) | ![After: the original settings button remains focused after the identity refresh](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8f85268-b2fb-4d56-8605-da2e85f3639f) | ### Before and after: keyboard focus, identity refresh, and Enter destination https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/119c7512-2108-4083-b867-6b84ab8266d8 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 2742aa01664c441571418805545bc012b6294228 - Exact head: `62347ba7f47b597a710c173efb8558bf13b906ed` - Scenario: Focus agent A settings with the keyboard while chatting with agent B, save B’s identity through the Gateway, then press Enter\. - Runtime/build: Exact source UI 62347ba; isolated Gateway build 2026\.10\.8\-6d13fb3e8359; Chromium and WebKit live interaction passes\. - Before: Original settings control disconnected; focus moved to body; Enter stayed in chat\. - After: Original control and focus retained; Enter opened agent A settings\. - Preserved state: Active chat remained B and the unsent draft survived return from settings; asserted outside the privacy crop\. - Real Gateway identity\-file save and accepted identity refresh observed in both runs\. - Served source and UI build matched the recorded baseline and fixed commits\. - Chromium and WebKit passed retained\-control, navigation, session and draft assertions on the fixed head\. - Cropped to exclude private data; video plays at 0\.1×\. Capture\-scale changes normalized to native pixels without interpolation or substituted product frames\.

prs.title: fix(ui): match canonical NFC/NFD forms in Control UI skills search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Case-insensitive search in the Control UI skills surfaces compared lowercased strings without Unicode canonical normalization. A composed (NFC) query did not match a canonically equivalent decomposed (NFD) stored value, and the reverse.

Two genuine user-facing surfaces are affected:

- `ui/src/pages/skills/discovery-view.tsx` — the local skill discovery filter (`entry.name`, `entry.description`, `entry.attribution`).
- `ui/src/pages/skills/library-view.tsx` — the installed-skill library filter (`entry.slug`, `entry.name`, `entry.description`, `entry.ownerLabel`).

Skill names and descriptions are user-authored and may be stored in either canonical form in practice: macOS filenames routinely decompose, while pasted or typed text is usually composed.

Concrete repro (real browser, production-built Control UI): skill A is stored as `München Skills` (NFC), skill B as `Mu\u0308nchen Notes` (NFD). Searching `München` (NFC) returned only A before; now it returns both. The symmetric case (NFD query against NFC copy) also matches now.

## User Impact

- A user searching for a skill by a visibly identical name gets "no skills" even though the skill exists, when the stored canonical form differs.
- Both directions are fixed: NFC query → NFD copy, and NFD query → NFC copy.
- Installed-skill library search behaves the same way for descriptions.
- Displayed and stored values are untouched: cards and rows still render the original bytes (regression asserts exact NFD code units).
- Remote ClawHub discovery results still bypass the local filter and retain registry ranking; `mine`/`team` scope filtering is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Comparison-side only: lowercase first, then normalize the transient comparison copy to NFC on both the query and each candidate text, then compare with the existing `includes` substring policy.

- No stored/displayed value rewriting, no migration.
- No new helper, config, validator, or dependency: `.normalize("NFC")` is a standard `String` method, identity on ASCII.
- The existing settings-navigation helper (`settingsSearchTextMatches`) was deliberately not reused: its short-query word-prefix semantics differ from the plain substring behavior these filters require.

Production diff: 2 files, 9 insertions / 3 deletions. Regression is folded into existing cases in `ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.test.tsx` (no new test blocks); test-file numstat is 94 added / 95 removed (net -1), so the repo test-line ratchet stays green.

Precedent: #184847

Related: #186672. Also in the same accepted family: #184374, #186329 (Gateway workspace file search), #186794 (cron list search).

## Evidence

Base: `4909daab9ea2436a71e5ae1fda00af7332ca5acb`. Head: `b61954f38e50922406ffe277d18c885af1d4ddbb`.

| Check | BEFORE — base `4909daab9` | AFTER — head `b61954f3` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Focused unit `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1` | **FAIL**: 2 failed / 18 passed — `expected null not to be null` (NFC query missed NFD name) and `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'existing-skill' ]` (composed query missed NFD description) | **PASS**: 20 passed (20), 17.00s |
| Test-line ratchet `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts` | — | **PASS**: exit 0, `net delta: -1` (tree over ceiling, change adds no test lines) |
| Browser, discovery search, composed `München` query | only the NFC-named skill; the NFD-named skill is absent | both canonical forms are listed |
| Browser, discovery search, decomposed `Mu\u0308nchen` query | only the NFD-named skill; the NFC-named skill is absent | both canonical forms are listed |
| Browser, library search, composed `Résumé` query | `My skills 0` — the NFD-stored description is missed | the NFD row is listed with its original description bytes |
| Browser, library search, decomposed `se\u0301ance` query | `My skills 0` — the NFC-stored description is missed | the NFC row is listed |
| Producer, shipped skills loader (`prepareWorkspaceSkillStatus`, the loader behind `skills.status`) against on-disk `SKILL.md` fixtures | NFD `Re\u0301sume\u0301 support` and NFC `Séance planning` reach the client byte-for-byte | identical bytes; the producer never rewrites stored text |

### Viewable before/after captures

All captures are from the production-built Control UI bundle in Chromium with the in-repo mock Gateway transport; the query code units are logged for every fill (`U+00FC` vs `U+0075 U+0308` for “München”; `U+00E9` vs `U+0065 U+0301` for “Résumé”/“séance”).

| Discovery, composed query | Discovery, decomposed query |

| Library, composed query | Library, decomposed query |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-assets/nfc-search-2026-10-29/skills/before-library-nfc-query.png) | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-assets/nfc-search-2026-10-29/skills/before-library-nfd-query.png) |
| ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-assets/nfc-search-2026-10-29/skills/after-library-nfc-query.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-assets/nfc-search-2026-10-29/skills/after-library-nfd-query.png) |

Exact typed code units: [query-code-units.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-assets/nfc-search-2026-10-29/skills/query-code-units.txt). The two discovery AFTER captures are byte-identical because the fixed page renders the same result for both canonical query forms; the logs above prove the typed queries differed.

Evidence tier (honest): unit RED/GREEN on the committed production files; a real-browser Control UI run on the harness-built production bundle with the in-repo mock Gateway transport; and a producer-chain proof calling the real shipped skills discovery loader against on-disk `SKILL.md` fixtures on base and candidate. No single browser-to-live-Gateway-process run exists for this renderer-only change; a live-Gateway variant was attempted and blocked because that worktree had no prebuilt `dist` while the runtime-artifact guard refused to rebuild on this host. The personal-library SQLite producer was not exercised outside the mock transport. Captures were taken at `a17cec50f`; `git diff a17cec50f b61954f3 -- ui/src/pages/skills/discovery-view.tsx ui/src/pages/skills/library-view.tsx` is empty, so the proof keys to the current head's production bytes. Screenshots show only Control UI chrome and synthetic fixture copy — no IPs, API keys, tokens, phone numbers, emails, or non-public endpoints.

## Classification

`behavior-completing`

## Merge danger

None beyond normal review. The change only normalizes transient lowercased comparison copies; `.normalize("NFC")` is idempotent on already-NFC text and identity on ASCII, so existing substring/case matching is unchanged. No schema, config, protocol, API, or stored-value change. Accepted edge (same as the precedent family): canonical normalization does not fold compatibility variants (ligatures, full-width forms); those remain distinct.

prs.title: fix(browser): keep the action navigation grace on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A browser interaction guarded by an SSRF navigation policy releases request interception too early when the host wall clock steps forward mid-action: the 250 ms action-navigation grace can collapse to zero, so a document request issued inside that grace no longer passes through the navigation policy.

- Problem: `runCancellablePageInteraction` keeps request interception installed for a 250 ms grace after the raw action settles (`BROWSER_ACTION_NAVIGATION_GRACE_MS`). The grace is computed from wall-clock reads (`Date.now()` seeds `actionSettledAtMs`, then `Date.now() - actionSettledAtMs` is read back) while the wait itself is a monotonic `setTimeout` (`sleepWithAbort`). When the wall clock jumps forward by 250 ms or more (NTP correction, VM snapshot restore, manual clock change), `elapsedMs` overstates the real elapsed time, `remainingMs` becomes zero, and the grace sleep is skipped.
- Solution: seed and read the elapsed grace on the monotonic clock (`performance.now()`), so the grace computation and the wait share one clock domain.
- What changed: `pw-tools-core.interactions.navigation.ts` stamps `actionSettledAtMs` and computes `elapsedMs` with `performance.now()`; the existing grace regression in `pw-tools-core.interactions.navigation-guard.test.ts` now freezes the monotonic clock, jumps the wall clock, and asserts the request guard stays installed for the full grace (suite change is net-negative in test lines).
- What did NOT change: the grace constant, the sleep behavior, the policy check order, or any public surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

The forward-step direction briefly disables a security boundary: a document request arriving inside the intended 250 ms grace escapes the SSRF policy check. A backward step only extends the window by the 250 ms cap, which is why the forward direction is the user-visible defect. Both readings are process-local elapsed time, never persisted, serialized, or exchanged, so a monotonic reading is the correct domain.

This is the same `wall-clock-remaining-budget` pattern already fixed for the sibling download-drain path in #186850 and the operation budgets in #186484; this file was not covered by those migrations.

## User Impact

Users whose host clock is corrected (NTP, VM restore, manual change) while a guarded browser interaction settles now keep the full 250 ms navigation grace, so document requests arriving right after the action stay protected by the SSRF policy. Previously the grace could collapse to zero and request routing was released early.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof through the shipped entry point**: isolated Gateway (`openclaw gateway`, loopback, token auth) + managed headless Chrome + shipped `openclaw browser` CLI (`navigate`/`snapshot`/`click`/`tabs`), no in-process calls. Fixture: `/start` links to `/first`; `/first` schedules a document navigation to a blocked host 120 ms after load, and that host is mapped back to the fixture server, so an escaped request is logged as real network I/O. Policy: `browser.ssrfPolicy = { allowedHostnames: ["127.0.0.1"], blockedHostnames: ["denied.test"] }`. Clock step: an `--import` preload shifts `Date.now()` by +60 000 ms at the first read on the grace seed line (`pw-tools-core.interactions.navigation.ts:506`) and for every later read. Three runs per variant, same script/config/fixture, only the production file differs.

```console
# pre-fix (production file at origin/main: Date.now seed/read)
RUN=1 VARIANT=pre-fix firstNav=1 click=ok deniedRequestHitNetwork=1 finalUrl=<empty>
  fixture: ... REQ host=127.0.0.1:18990 path=/first
  fixture: ... REQ host=denied.test:18990 path=/denied
  fixture: ... DENIED_REQUEST_REACHED_NETWORK
  clock: [CLOCK-PROOF] seed=Date.now line=...navigation.ts:506 step=60000ms ARMED
# RUN=2, RUN=3 identical: 3/3 denied requests reached the network

# fixed (current head: performance.now seed/read)
RUN=1 VARIANT=fixed firstNav=1 click=policy-blocked deniedRequestHitNetwork=0 finalUrl=http://127.0.0.1:18990/first
  fixture: ... REQ host=127.0.0.1:18990 path=/first
  clock: [CLOCK-PROOF] seed=performance.now line=...navigation.ts:506 step=60000ms ARMED
# RUN=2, RUN=3 identical: 3/3 intercepted, page stays on /first
```

`firstNav=1` is the allowed navigation completing in every run. In the fixed runs the intercepted request surfaces as the guard's existing `browser navigation blocked by policy` error on the click, and the page stays on `/first`.

**Behavior matrix**

```text
same Gateway + CLI + Chrome + fixture, wall clock +60 s after action settles
scenario                                        => pre-fix                          => fixed
denied document request 120 ms after /first load => reached the fixture server (escaped) => intercepted before network I/O, page stays /first
```

**Guard-lifetime regression (pre-fix red / post-fix green)** — fake timers advance past the delayed-navigation observation window plus the full grace; `performance.now()` is frozen and `Date.now()` jumps 100 s right after the action settles, while the guard's own lifetime is asserted.

```console
$ vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.navigation-guard.test.ts -t "blocks a private final URL after an earlier safe navigation"
# pre-fix (source reverted to origin/main): the guard is released before the grace
FAIL  AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
      Tests  1 failed | 23 skipped (24)
# post-fix: the guard is still installed at 249 ms and released at 250 ms
      Tests  1 passed | 23 skipped (24)
```

Full touched suite, post-fix: `Tests 24 passed (24)`.

**Targeted checks**

```console
$ oxfmt --check <touched test file>            # All matched files use the correct format.
$ oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <touched test file> # Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
$ node --import tsx scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts
Test lines OK: 6302528; ceiling: 6310000; slack: 7472.
```

**Collision check**: no open PR touches this file; #186850 / #186484 changed sibling files only.

prs.title: fix: keep spawned helpers in the Draft audience
prs.body: Fixes #186662 ## What Problem This Solves Delegating work from a Draft conversation can create a Shared helper without anyone choosing to share it. In a guest workflow, the parent remains Draft while another admitted guest can read the helper's result. The omission affects hidden native helpers, visible spawned sessions, and fresh ACP conversation wrappers. ## User Impact A new child spawned from a Draft source starts as Draft before receiving its task or inherited context. The creator and administrators retain their existing access, and the parent can still receive the helper's completion. Making a child visible continues to control navigation and persistence without selecting a wider audience. When Draft creation is disabled, a new child from a Draft is refused with guidance to continue in the existing Draft or ask an administrator to enable Draft creation. This applies even if the policy changes during preparation. Existing Draft conversations and children already created can continue their work; an internal transcript-identity change does not create a new conversation. Each child keeps its own sharing state. Publishing the parent later does not publish the child, explicit Shared choices through other creation paths remain valid, and existing children retain their stored audience. This preserves the documented same-Gateway visibility trust model and existing runtime admission restrictions. ## Why This Change Was Made The initial creation writers already resolve the authorized parent and stamp the child's creator and sandbox provenance. They now select the existing Draft field at that point instead of leaving it absent, which per-session readers interpret as Shared. The visible-session path uses the current creation-policy owner introduced by #186828; this PR adds spawn inheritance to that resolver. The prerequisite is merged. The native and ACP writers check the current Draft policy before creating resources and again through their existing initial-write guards. Once the child row exists, later initialization remains continuation of that same conversation. ACP creator and parent preparation is kept together while its existing writer retains the actual database mutation. A hidden helper using forked context replaces its provisional transcript identity. Generic replacement deliberately clears visibility, so this initial fork carries a private continuation flag through the existing writer transaction. The transaction preserves the child's current committed audience, including an explicit sharing choice made while preparation awaited. Generic resets, Talk forks, membership cleanup and public-share invalidation retain their existing behavior. No new storage representation, parent read or additional write is introduced. ## Evidence ### Failure and focused checks A real guest Draft conversation delegated a benign picnic-planning task before the fix. Another guest was denied the parent history but could read the Shared helper's matching result and list it under the known parent. The capture uses known session keys; it does not establish arbitrary session discovery or released-runtime behavior. Native regressions reproduced both the missing initial audience and visibility loss during initial fork installation. Strict-policy regressions also failed on the earlier enabled-only candidate: initially disabled creation and a policy replacement during preparation both admitted a child. The corrected native/ACP owner suites pass all 90 tests across six affected files. The integrated Gateway creation, fork, worktree rollback and existing-key controls pass all 58 tests across four files, with all 38 selected compiler graphs passing. Qualified unchanged consumer results are retained separately. The enforced per-file line cap passes. The accepted main prerequisite #187030 sets the total test-code ceiling to 6,320,000. Its native count covers this unchanged patch; source qualification of the accepted tail gives 6,312,053 lines for this PR composition, leaving 7,947 lines of headroom. This is reuse of the measured aggregate and unchanged counted inputs, not a second counter execution. [CI on the original published head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40715693361) passed all selected Node, UI, build, type, structural, documentation, security and PostgreSQL conformance lanes. Source-authority revocation, creator/sandbox lineage, native fork continuation, admitted ACP initialization, and ordinary reset/public-share behavior are covered at their existing owners. No extra ACP permissions or external-runtime access was granted for testing. ### Real Gateway and guest UI On source `eb6039c630f1c6159c5eef0db54e1b9f20599658`, an ordinary guest created a Draft and received a useful picnic plan. The native configuration owner then disabled Draft creation without restarting the Gateway. The same Draft completed a shopping checklist, retaining its session identity, audience and every earlier message. A subsequent natural request for a helper reached `sessions_spawn` and returned an error containing `session visibility is disabled: draft`, with guidance to continue in the existing Draft or ask an administrator to enable Draft creation. Both an administrator's session lookup and the independent native stored-entry accessor confirmed that the proposed child did not exist. The parent remained usable and retained its work; the screenshot shows the assistant's explanation, while the native tool receipt establishes the actual policy refusal. Under that same disabled setting, a fresh ordinary Shared conversation successfully delegated to a Shared helper and received its completion. Creator, administrator and foreign-reader result fingerprints matched. A foreign subscription established before the refused Draft attempt received **0 Draft/refused-child content events**, then **32 Shared-child events, including 6 message bodies**, on the same connection. The retained enabled-Draft run proves the complementary case: the helper was Draft while running, its creator/admin could read the result, its parent received completion, and the foreign guest was denied history/list/content-event access. Publishing the parent did not publish its child; explicit Shared choices and legacy Shared rows remained readable. The before/after audience screenshots come from that earlier candidate and are explicitly source-qualified. Readback on the captured eb6039c6 source independently confirmed those fixtures' identities, audiences, access and result fingerprints after the preview update. ### Existing state and restoration The change uses the existing optional visibility field. It adds no schema, migration, persisted row type, configuration option or installation/dependency change. The private fork-continuation boolean is an operation/write option, not stored session data; omitted options retain generic replacement behavior. Native before/after preservation matched all eight original session identities and their selected creator/audience/lineage/workspace/sandbox metadata, profile/project state, and 243 recorded filesystem entries across the source-preview update. After the scenario, an independent native join verified the three new rows, exact child lineage and creator attribution, refused-child absence, and the original dirty project's Git state and four authored files. The original configuration bytes and absent session setting were restored exactly. These source-preview checks are supplemented by the packaged stable-upgrade proof below. Sandbox provenance was verified, not an independent container-execution claim. The creation-policy prerequisite #186828 and test-budget prerequisite #187030 are merged. This PR targets `main`. The final prepared head is `0deae9202adb2738e01c5e2a70b10c62eaf740f4` on accepted main `0ded0ed7a8cae4867a3a201e32cccbfbfe9bde70`. Its three commits are content-equivalent to the reviewed patch, all 20 changed files are byte-identical to the captured source, and the relevant upstream contracts were inspected. Focused native proof and live media are reused with their original execution/capture identities. Exact-head review reports no findings. Final-head CI completed with inherited channel-startup failures, as described below. ### Fresh installation and stable upgrade The exact `0deae920` candidate was packaged and installed as runtime build `2026.10.8-0deae9202adb-2026-10-28T23-11-02.901Z` (package SHA-256 `fca855a910792b669426b4a64e69743e5dd74f7df84f110df7c7e0881b530b3e`). A fresh environment started with no sessions and served the matching bundled UI. Its first real guest Draft request spawned a Draft helper, received its completed result, and denied a second guest access. A separate default-Shared conversation remained readable by that guest. A second isolated environment began on official stable `v2026.10.8` (`dc2523e5`). Real guest turns created a Draft, an explicit Shared conversation and a legacy default-Shared row with no stored visibility field. After disabling Draft creation, native OCM upgrade switched that existing environment to the candidate. The Gateway was drained and stopped before the upgrade, then restarted with the candidate package. Session identities, lifecycle revisions, creator attribution, sandbox provenance, stored visibility presence, history fingerprints and reader access all matched across the upgrade. The disabled setting also survived. On the upgraded Gateway, the existing Draft continued successfully. Its fresh helper request returned the canonical disabled-Draft error, and both native lookup and the installed public session-store accessor confirmed the proposed child was absent. A Shared helper completed under that same disabled policy. Re-enabling Draft creation allowed a new Draft helper to complete while denying the foreign reader; the legacy default-Shared conversation also continued. The same foreign subscription saw zero private/refused-child events, 36 Shared-helper events including 6 message bodies, and 38 later Shared events after the private case. The original absent session configuration was restored. Final independent native metadata reads passed for all five upgraded and three fresh rows, including exact child lineage and refused-child absence. This proves completed-conversation upgrade and ordinary same-boot delegation. It does not claim active-run restart recovery, independent sandbox execution, or new captures of the retained media. ### Final-head CI attribution [Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40780518031) completed with 73 successful jobs, 24 skipped jobs and three failed jobs: two channel-startup shards and their aggregate gate. All four failing cases reproduced without this patch on the target baseline, and again on main `4a2a1962` after its startup refactor: 8 controls passed and the same 4 cases failed across `server.approval-forwarding.test.ts`, `server.channels-start-outcomes.test.ts` and `server-startup-secret-owner-isolation.test.ts`. Minimal Gateway startup leaves the account-start readiness gate unresolved; these cases do not exercise the changed spawn or fork branches. The failed Security Review commit status explicitly projects that CI failure and reports no independent security finding. The changed behavior lanes passed. These failures remain recorded as failures; this PR does not repair that separate startup defect. ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Foreign guest reading a Draft helper: retained, source\-qualified comparison | ![Before the fix, another guest can see the helper task and result\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a40f3fcd-fa93-4123-a741-d94553ec8021) | ![After the fix, the same foreign\-reader flow is denied\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52855116-16b9-4890-a34a-d986ad53e87d) | | Captured eb6039c6 with Draft creation disabled: continuation followed by helper refusal | ![The existing Draft finishes a useful shopping checklist after Draft creation is disabled\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bb1c584-ecdc-4709-a874-a43417d5c8d6) | ![The same Draft reports that the helper could not start and continues its work\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2eae796f-b904-4cbe-a3e1-e997139858d8) | ### Retained natural helper request and refusal, captured on eb6039c6 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0bf6381-374c-41e8-a1eb-3197fca2682f ### Visual verification - Baseline: 1d91d505af4a6f007be28cc52ab480c520d62d89 - Exact head: `0deae9202adb2738e01c5e2a70b10c62eaf740f4` - Scenario: Delegate work from a Draft without widening its audience\. With Draft creation disabled, continue an existing Draft, request a helper, and verify refusal while an ordinary Shared helper still works\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw source eb6039c630f1, real Gateway and guest UI, build 2026\-10\-28 16:19 UTC - Existing Draft: Same session identity and audience; earlier messages preserved; useful continuation completed\. - Fresh Draft helper: Native policy error; proposed child absent from the stored\-session accessor; zero children created\. - Shared helper control: Completed normally; creator, administrator and foreign\-reader result fingerprints match\. - Foreign event subscription: 0 Draft/refused\-child content events; 32 Shared\-child events, including 6 message bodies, on the same connection\. - Restoration: Original configuration bytes restored; original fixtures and dirty project preserved\. - The recording and second comparison were captured on eb6039c630f1c6159c5eef0db54e1b9f20599658\. The current head is a content\-equivalent rebase: all 20 changed files are byte\-identical, and relevant upstream behavior was source\-qualified\. - The first comparison was captured on baseline 1d91d505 and earlier candidate 2136dc50\. Source qualification and existing\-fixture API readback on eb6039c6 preserve that audience evidence; no new captures on the rebased head are claimed\. - The natural request reached sessions\_spawn and returned the disabled\-Draft policy guidance; assistant prose alone is not the refusal evidence\. - The native metadata join verified creator, sandbox stamp, lineage, session identity, audience and refused\-child absence\. A sandbox stamp is not an independent container\-execution claim\. - Native viewport 1440 by 1000; all published frames use the same 1130 by 1000 sidebar crop\. - Separate package compatibility proof ran on exact head 0deae920: a fresh installation and an actual v2026\.10\.8 upgrade preserved existing conversations and proved enabled Draft inheritance, disabled Draft refusal, and ordinary Shared behavior\. The retained media keeps its original capture identity\.

prs.title: fix: preserve cancellation and timeout causes in run diagnostics
prs.body:
Closes #186365

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes terminal diagnostics losing known cancellation and timeout causes, making interrupted runs difficult to explain.

## User Impact

Native embedded runs report the initiating user abort, restart, supersession, external signal, runtime abort, intentional yield or timeout when known. Timeouts retain their owner source and attempt phase. These are optional diagnostic fields; cancellation, retry and terminal-status behavior stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the first accepted interruption before callbacks can reenter, independently of later terminal-status refinement. Forward it through normal cleanup and early exit to `run.completed`, stability records and OpenTelemetry spans. Reuse existing run/session/trace correlation and typed owner facts rather than guessing from provider error messages.

Stability recording, saved-bundle readback, support ZIP export and OpenTelemetry use the same closed-enum normalizer, including for untyped JavaScript events. Unknown values are omitted, raw abort reasons are not copied, and duration metric dimensions are unchanged. Small type/projection extractions keep existing oversized files within the repository's growth limits.

## Evidence

- Eight owner/forwarding regressions failed before cause recording. The real automation-yield reproduction also showed the missing cause before the yield-owner repair. The regression injects a conflicting restart at the accepted session-abort handoff and confirms yield remains the initiating cause.
- The saved-bundle repair first reproduced 11 failures through the actual writer/reader and support ZIP export: known interruption fields were lost on readback. The repaired path preserves bounded values, omits unknown values and accepts legacy bundles without those fields.
- The final focused run passed 190 tests across 11 files and five shards in 273.53s: terminal outcomes, abort/deadline owners, cleanup, stream finalization, the real embedded attempt and full yield suite, stability recording/readback, support export, and real OTel span/metric export. Two existing Windows-only skips remain in support export. No skip or baseline exception was added.
- Fixture consolidation removes repeated setup and overlapping assertions while retaining distinct cancellation, reentry, cleanup, yield, sanitization and metric-label contracts. Against the original base, counted test lines decrease by three; the test-lines ratchet passes without raising the ceiling. This removes the previous revision's 327-line growth, including for merge candidates already above the ceiling.
- After the unchanged build-identity extraction, all 47 affected bundle/support-export tests passed again (two existing Windows skips; 134.52s), and targeted native TypeScript compilation passed including affected tests and SDK consumers.
- Line-cap and whitespace checks pass. The existing build-identity reader moved unchanged into a sibling module so the oversized bundle reader does not grow. Against the original base, production is +361/-136 (+225), tests/support +877/-880 (-3), and docs +8. Production growth is needed to record the first accepted interruption once and forward bounded facts to existing diagnostic consumers.
- Focused syntax lint and formatting pass; documentation lint and SDK export registration passed on unchanged inputs. Full build and ordinary type-aware lint remain blocked locally by a retained Windows artifact lock, which was left intact. Hosted CI must cover those gaps. No deployed or live-provider proof is claimed.
- CI run 40605542020 on head `93b65172aebbc2366897c16ce136da658404fc0b` exposed three PR-caused static failures: a build-identity type-import cycle, a new wall-clock test-timeout helper reference, and an obsolete max-lines suppression. The shared build-identity contract now lives in the leaf module; the settlement test waits under the Vitest cancellation signal with unchanged result/no-drain assertions; the obsolete suppression is removed. The exact Madge check reports zero cycles, the timeout-race ratchet passes without baseline changes, and focused root-config syntax lint and formatting pass. The same CI run already confirmed the test-line no-growth exemption.
- Fresh local Codex autoreview covered the complete local candidate against base `2937d6581241ca1854601c3ab7a8594838352a49` at P2. It reported one INDEX-only finding: the old index lacked the saved-bundle fix that was present and correct in the reviewed working tree. Staging the reviewed files resolved that finding; the index then matched the working tree exactly. No other P0-P2 findings were established. That review covered published head `93b65172aebbc2366897c16ce136da658404fc0b`. The following repair is covered by the fresh review below. Local ClawSweeper remains unavailable because its checkout lacks installed dependencies.

- After the final CI repairs, all nine stream-finalization tests passed with a clean exit in 258.77s, including 182.94s rebuilding the compiled worker cache. Targeted native TypeScript compilation passed, including the affected tests and SDK consumers. The prior bundle/support-export proof is reused because runtime statements and the three optional build-identity fields are unchanged.
- Fresh local Codex autoreview of the final staged four-file repair against `93b65172aebbc2366897c16ce136da658404fc0b`, including the existing promise helper as context, returned scoped-clean at P2 with no actionable findings. The reviewed snapshot is published as `f90ed91ea4fd8898e394818113f23b7f8f25a901`. A fresh hosted ClawSweeper review is requested for this repaired head.
- CI run 40608808267 on `f90ed91` found one remaining stale max-lines baseline entry after the suppression removal. Canonical `--prune` removed only `src/logging/diagnostic-stability.ts` (407 entries to 406), with no source/test changes. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-max-lines-ratchet.mts --base 2937d6581241ca1854601c3ab7a8594838352a49 --no-merge-base` now passes: 406 suppressions and environment budget 457/457. Whitespace validation passes. This exact shrink-only maintenance is committed as `83ce2bd`; existing code-review and behavioral proof remain applicable, and fresh CI will validate the new head.

prs.title: fix: start explicitly requested accounts in minimal test Gateways
prs.body:
Fixes #187073

## What Problem This Solves

Minimal test Gateways can finish startup and accept an explicit `channels.start` request without ever invoking the channel provider. The account remains behind a startup promise that minimal mode never releases, preventing the existing approval-forwarding, manual-recovery and credential-file-recovery fixtures from completing.

## User Impact

This restores explicitly requested account startup in the minimal Gateway test harness, including access to the owning Gateway approval runtime. It is a supporting validation correction; no production or guest-facing feature is introduced. Minimal mode continues to omit autonomous sidecars. Full Gateways retain their existing readiness release, and account ownership, cancellation, closing and crash-loop suppression remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel manager correctly waits for the Gateway generation's startup gate before handing an account to its provider. Full startup releases that gate through `onChannelsStarted` after startup observers complete their admission work. The minimal post-attach branch previously returned after logging without invoking the callback.

That branch now releases the same gate after logging succeeds, checking the tracked cancellation signal and live closing state immediately beforehand. The existing startup-readiness test helper covers successful logging, failed logging, cancellation and closing while preserving sidecar suppression. There is no new start policy, timer, configuration option or manual-start exemption.

## Evidence

On base 4a2a1962d9caaf965c0432c7c9a84e5a40290f7d, native remote execution reproduced four failures across these existing real Gateway files:

- `src/gateway/server.approval-forwarding.test.ts`: the account never received its Gateway approval runtime.
- `src/gateway/server.channels-start-outcomes.test.ts`: manual recovery observed zero provider starts and the in-flight recovery case timed out.
- `src/gateway/server-startup-secret-owner-isolation.test.ts`: repaired credential-file recovery timed out while waiting for provider startup.

The candidate passed all **208 cases in nine files**, including those regressions, every direct test consumer of the modified owner/helper, channel-manager gate and approval binding, full-mode startup readiness and cancellation, and current database-startup controls. Changed-file formatting/lint and selected production/test type checks also passed. The native test batch took 174.1 seconds; the complete ordered remote invocation, including preparation and type checks, took 738.3 seconds. Commit e91693622315a33579f03e04dbf5e357f22b4316 has the exact tested tree.

Committed-range AutoReview (Codex, P0–P3) completed cleanly for base 4a2a1962 through head e91693622315a33579f03e04dbf5e357f22b4316, with the full affected owner context supplied and no actionable findings. Independent engineering review also completed cleanly. ClawSweeper reviewed this same head with no findings. This change has no UI surface or new external-provider behavior requiring visual or model proof.


Additional integration proof on main revision d821a7fd1dc8ff8ab54d7518c02dba7f6553f932 reproduced the approval-runtime failure before applying this patch. The exact combined tree then passed **175 cases in three focused startup, channel-manager and approval-forwarding files**, including the preserved full-mode and cancellation controls.

[CI run 40790895061](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40790895061) completed with every selected test, type and other check row passing. The mock-export ratchet and its aggregate gate remain red: all 14 reported factories are in unchanged shutdown/spawn-broker fixtures. The same owner check reproduced those exact failures on a968dc19900db67a0b4230b68d9df5e2d52c13b3, and the scanner, ledger, dependency and affected-source inputs match the CI result. This patch adds no mock factory or baseline allowance.

prs.title: fix(cron): include untruncated agent output in webhook delivery
prs.body:
Related: #185873

> Deliberately **Related, not Closes**: this PR delivers the recommendation's
> detached/isolated half; the named-session half — the reporter's original repro lane —
> needs the cron-owner follow-up documented under **Fix scope**, so the issue must stay
> open until that lands (same Related-over-Closes call the review asked for on #185766).

## What Problem This Solves

Cron webhook deliveries truncate long agent output: the finished-event payload only
carries the bounded `summary` (2,000 characters + `…`), so a webhook receiver silently
loses the rest of an otherwise successful report. Issue #185873 reproduces this on a
2,718-character reply; this change adds an additive, webhook-only `outputText` field
that carries the run's full final agent text for isolated and current-session
agent-turn jobs, with the bounded `summary` left byte-for-byte unchanged.

ClawSweeper's recommendation on the issue:

> **Recommendation:** **Add separate full output:** Define an additive webhook-only
> final-text field for named-session and detached agent turns, with boundary coverage
> for long output, silent replies, and failed runs.
>
> Why: Source confirms the missing full-text payload, but historical implementation and
> current documentation define summary-bearing completion events, and a maintainer has
> explicitly preserved the summary cap.

This PR implements the recommendation's **detached/isolated half** with the three
required boundaries (long output, silent replies, failed runs). The named-session half
is disclosed below under **Fix scope** — it cannot be delivered without editing
`src/cron/service/state.ts` (occupied by #185848) and adding new capture through the
auto-reply owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The full text already exists in the cron owner lane: `runIsolatedAgentJob` returns
  `outputText` as "Last non-empty agent text output (not truncated)"
  (`src/cron/service/state.ts:245-246`), produced by
  `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-finalize.ts:390,407`. It was simply dropped by the
  explicit field enumeration in the detached branch of
  `src/cron/service/timer-execution.ts` before the webhook event was assembled in
  `src/cron/service/timer-job-runner.ts`.
- The maintainer-preserved summary cap stays exactly where it is:
  `pickSummaryFromOutput` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/helpers.ts:67-74`) is untouched, and
  persisted run history, `openclaw automations runs`, and chat announcements keep the
  bounded `summary`. The new field is projected only into the primary webhook payload
  (`delivery.mode: "webhook"`); the persistence codec enumerates fields
  (`src/cron/run-event-codec.ts`, `src/cron/store/run-result.ts`), so nothing new is
  stored or fanned out to Gateway clients.
- Fix classification: **behavior-completing** (additive field on an existing payload,
  no existing field or cap modified).

## User Impact

- Webhook receivers of isolated/current-session agent-turn automations get the complete
  final report in `outputText` whenever it is non-empty; the `summary` they already
  consume is unchanged.
- Silent/empty runs: the field is absent (no fabricated keys).
- Failed runs: the error webhook keeps its existing text-free payload (no `summary`,
  no diagnostics, and now explicitly no `outputText`).
- Operators see no change in run history, announcements, Control UI, or config: no new
  option, validator, or persisted state was added.
- Known boundary (documented in `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md`): main-session
  and named-session (`session:<key>`) agent turns do not carry `outputText` yet.

## Evidence

- proof base SHA: `364c0d4ebcd400ee4285eb989ed60d2a8b000b93` (the `main` this patch was
  proven against on 2026-10-27; every red/green leg below ran there)
- proof candidate SHA: `ccdf3ec35a9969c4b4bf2b5cb3baa99990312acf`
- current head SHA: `a6a54c9b7…` — the identical seven-file change rebuilt directly on
  `main` `2742aa016…` on 2026-10-29 (details under **Rebuild**). The 2026-10-28
  `main` merge that `3526945…` recorded is gone: that merge left GitHub computing this
  PR's diff against a stale merge base, which surfaced as 905 changed files,
  `CONFLICTING`, a false `security-sensitive-changed`, and an unreadable
  `This branch has conflicts` UI.
- Red = base without the patch; green = candidate. Both legs use the same commands and
  the same loopback harness (isolated Gateway state under `/tmp`, zero-credential
  OpenAI-compatible model stub returning a 3,939-character final answer, loopback
  webhook receiver recording raw bodies).

### Unit red/green (vitest, one file)

| Leg | Command | Exit | Wall time | Assertion point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Red (base) | `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/cron/service.persists-delivered-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 1 | 91.62s | `sends untruncated outputText while the summary keeps its bounded shape` fails: `expected undefined to be 'CRON_FULL_OUTPUT_PROOF_…'` (webhook body has no `outputText` on base) |
| Green (candidate) | same command | 0 | 159.41s | 16/16 pass, including all three boundary tests |

The two boundary tests (`omits outputText when the run produced no non-empty output
text`, `keeps failed-run webhooks free of both summary and outputText`) pass on both
legs: they lock the additive contract's absent-key behavior.

### Shipped-CLI × live Gateway proof (base red / candidate green)

Both legs: `node <dist>/index.js gateway run --port 18999` (real Gateway, isolated
`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), `automations add --webhook http://127.0.0.1:18991/hook --session
isolated --model stub/stub-long`, `automations run <job> --wait`, then
`automations runs <job> --limit 1 --sort desc --json` plus the receiver's raw body log.
Leg script: `bash /tmp/oc-cron1-proof/run-leg.sh <red|green> <dist>/index.js`.

| Leg | Command | Exit | Wall time | Webhook body observation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Red (base dist, `OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (364c0d4)`) | `bash /tmp/oc-cron1-proof/run-leg.sh red /media/vdc/oc-cron1/dist/index.js` | 0 | 226.80s | 1 POST; `status:"ok"`, `deliveryStatus:"delivered"`; **no `outputText` key**; `summary` length 2001, ends with `…`, `summaryEqualsFullText:false` (full text 3,939 chars) — issue reproduced |
| Green (candidate dist, build-info `commit: ccdf3ec35…`) | `bash /tmp/oc-cron1-proof/run-leg.sh green2 /media/vdc/oc-cron1/dist/index.js` (identical rerun of the first green leg; both exit 0) | 0 | 219.14s | 1 POST; `status:"ok"`, `deliveryStatus:"delivered"`; **`outputText` present with the complete final text** (3,938 chars, equals the stub's full answer trimmed of surrounding whitespace); `summary` still 2,001 chars ending `…`, byte-identical to the red leg (`md5` match) |

<details><summary>Green leg output (candidate dist, build-info commit ccdf3ec35)</summary>

```text
$ bash /tmp/oc-cron1-proof/run-leg.sh green2 /media/vdc/oc-cron1/dist/index.js
gateway healthy after 5 polls
job=a9fbf1d5-6095-421f-83a1-3b938ab6e4b6
run-exit=0
greenleg wall=219.14s exit=0

webhook body analysis (same script as the red leg):
{"deliveries":1,"status":"ok","deliveryStatus":"delivered","hasOutputTextKey":true,
 "outputTextEqualsTrimmedFullText":true,"summaryLen":2001,"summaryEllipsis":true,
 "summaryMd5MatchesRedLeg":true}
run history (automations runs --json): status ok, summaryLen 2001, hasOutputTextKey false
```

`outputTextEqualsTrimmedFullText: true` compares the delivered field against the
stub's complete 3,939-character answer trimmed of surrounding whitespace
(the value is 3,938 characters; the stub text ends in a space from its repeat
unit) — no internal truncation.

</details>

### Boundary coverage (Recommendation requirement)

1. **Long output** — 3,939-character final answer: `outputText` equals the full text
   with only surrounding whitespace trimmed (3,938 characters; no internal
   truncation), `summary` remains exactly 2,001 characters ending in `…`
   (byte-identical between red and green legs: `summary_md5_match: true`).
2. **Silent replies** (unit, loopback HTTP body) — `outputText: undefined` and
   whitespace-only `outputText` both omit the key from the JSON body; the existing
   success-with-empty-summary suppression (`deliverySuppressionReason: "empty"`, no
   POST) is unchanged.
3. **Failed runs** (unit, loopback HTTP body) — a run with `status:"error"`, a
   summary, and output text delivers the error webhook without `summary`,
   diagnostics, or `outputText`; `error` and `status` keep their existing shape.

### Summary cap untouched (control)

`pickSummaryFromOutput` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/helpers.ts:67-74`) and the
2,000-character diagnostics cap (`src/cron/run-diagnostics-normalize.ts:12`) are not
modified. In the shipped proof the `summary` string is byte-identical on the red and
green legs (`md5` match), and `openclaw automations runs --json` shows the same
2,001-character summary with no `outputText` on both legs — the new field is
webhook-only.

### Fix scope (disclosure)

- Covered: detached lanes — `sessionTarget: "isolated"` and `"current"` agent turns
  (the `runIsolatedAgentJob` path), which own the untruncated text end-to-end.
- Not covered: named-session (`main` / `session:<key>`) agent turns. The full text of
  those turns exists only inside the session-event handoff
  (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts:438`,
  `summary ??= truncateUtf16Safe(payload.text, 2000)`); the settled contract
  `SessionEventOutcome` (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-contract.ts:32-52`)
  exposes only the bounded `summary`, `runCronSessionTurn`
  (`src/cron/session-run.ts:295`) forwards only that summary, and the scheduler's
  `runSessionEvent` return type is declared in `src/cron/service/state.ts:267-271` —
  a file held by open PR #185848 and excluded from this change. Covering that half
  requires a `state.ts` contract change plus new capture through the auto-reply owner;
  it is intentionally left for a follow-up with the cron owner.

### Impact surface

| File:line | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/cron/types.ts:163-168` | `CronEvent` gains optional `outputText` with ownership comment | Type-only; optional field, never persisted or fanned out |
| `src/cron/types.ts:272-273` | `CronJobExecutionResult` gains optional `outputText` | Carries the value to the webhook literal; persistence codecs enumerate fields, so no storage growth |
| `src/cron/service/timer-execution.ts:437-442, 552-555` | Detached branch forwards `res.outputText` (was dropped by explicit enumeration) | Isolated lane only; main-session/script/command branches unchanged |
| `src/cron/service/timer-job-runner.ts:170-174` | Primary webhook event literal adds a conditional `outputText` spread | Webhook-only surface; empty/whitespace output omits the key |
| `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts:222-228` | Error-run webhook payload strips `outputText` alongside the existing summary/diagnostics strip | Failed-run payload shape identical to today |
| `src/cron/service.persists-delivered-status.test.ts:205-285` | Three boundary tests + loopback helper (real `sendGatewayCronWebhook`, real HTTP body) | Test-only |
| `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md:230-241`, `docs/cli/cron.md:208` | Document `outputText` and its boundaries | Docs-only |

Isolation from #185848 (occupies `src/cron/service/state.ts`, `src/cron/service/ops-stream.ts`,
`failure-alerts.ts`, `run-recovery.ts`, `src/cron/delivery-*.ts`,
`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-delivery-trace.ts`, `src/cron/store/*.ts`,
`src/gateway/server-cron-completion.ts(+test)`, `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-add.ts`,
`cron-input-validation.ts`, `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`,
`src/config/*cron*`, `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.*`): **zero files in common**.
`CronServiceDeps.sendCronWebhook` and `CronEventContext` signatures are unchanged;
the whole change routes through `types.ts` optional fields plus the webhook event
literal in `timer-job-runner.ts`. Collision check was run against the current open-PR
file map (`gh pr list --state open --limit 200 --json number,files`): none of the seven
touched files appear in any open PR.

### Test-lines justification

No ceiling bump is needed on the rebuilt head. `main` now carries measured headroom:
`config/test-lines-baseline.txt` reads a 6,320,000 ceiling documented as
"Measured bf6a97a1765 plus pending regression additions: 6,312,681 lines. Keep 7,319
lines of bounded headroom for remaining regression work". This PR's +82 test lines
(three behavioral tests plus the loopback helper that drives the real
`sendGatewayCronWebhook` path, nothing deleted) fit that reserved headroom, so the
branch does not touch the baseline file at all. Verified on the rebuilt head:

```text
$ pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet
Test lines OK: 6312490; ceiling: 6320000; slack: 7510.
```

The earlier 2026-10-27/28 discussion of raising the ceiling to 6,286,508 and then to
6,300,526 belonged to the pre-rebuild head, where `main`'s measured total sat above its
own ceiling and a bump was the only way through; dropping it removes line churn from
`config/test-lines-baseline.txt`, which several other open PRs also edit.

### Rebuild

The 2026-10-28 `Merge main into fix/cron-webhook-full-output` commit (`3526945…`) left
the PR in a state no maintainer can merge: GitHub reported 905 changed files and `+23708/−8739`
for a seven-file fix, `mergeable: CONFLICTING`, and `security-review-required` triggered
by auth/secrets paths that existed only in that phantom diff (`gh pr diff` refused with
`HTTP 406: the diff exceeded the maximum number of files (300)`).

The branch was rebuilt as one commit on `main` `2742aa016…` instead of carrying a merge
commit. The result:

| Signal | Before (`3526945…`) | Rebuilt (`a6a54c9b7…`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| changed files | 905 | **7** |
| additions/deletions | +23708/−8739 | **+120/−3** |
| `mergeable` | `CONFLICTING` | **`MERGEABLE`** |
| `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` | FAILURE (phantom auth paths) | **pass — "No sensitive product changes"** |
| labels | 42, incl. `channel: *`, `app: *`, `extensions: *`, `size: XL`, `security-review-required` | **7**: `docs`, `gateway`, `size: S`, `proof: sufficient`, `P2`, `rating: 🦐 gold shrimp`, `status: ⏳ waiting on maintainer` |
| `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` | touched (conflict) | untouched |

The rebuild applied the same patch to current `main`: all seven hunks applied cleanly
(the only conflict was the baseline line, resolved by keeping `main`'s headroom version)
and no source line changed. Local verification on the rebuilt tree: `pnpm test
src/cron/service.persists-delivered-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **16/16 pass**
(135.7s, Node 24.22.1), `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on the seven files,
`git diff --check` clean, and the five touched-file ratchets plus the test-lines ratchet
OK against `origin/main`.

### Gates

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| oxlint | `pnpm exec oxlint <5 touched src files>` | 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| format | `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <5 touched src files>` | clean |
| docs format | `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/format-docs.mts --check` | clean (1405 files) |
| whitespace | `git diff --check` | clean |
| adjacent tests | `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-primary-webhook.test.ts src/gateway/server.cron.test.ts src/cron/service.trigger-eval.test.ts src/cron/service.session-payload.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | the four non-`server.cron` files pass 65/65; all failures are in `server.cron.test.ts` (next row) |
| adjacent tests (environmental) | `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/server.cron.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 4 timeouts fail **identically on base and candidate** (45s test timeout on this loaded host; base-code comparison run produces the same 4 failures and same passing set — failure diff zero, not attributable to this change) |
| ratchets | `check-line-cap-ratchet`, `check-max-lines-ratchet`, `check-test-mock-exports`, `check-assertion-safety`, `check-test-timeout-race-ratchet` (each `--base origin/main --no-merge-base`, rerun on the rebuilt head) | all OK; no new violations/suppressions |
| test-lines ratchet | `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` on the rebuilt head | `Test lines OK: 6312490; ceiling: 6320000; slack: 7510` (no baseline change) |
| typecheck (core) | `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` | only pre-existing TS2883 vitest-type portability errors in files this PR does not touch (`src/tui/*-test-support.ts`, `test/helpers/*`); none in touched files |
| typecheck (cron test shard) | `pnpm exec tsc -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --noEmit` | same pre-existing TS2883/TS5088 class only, none in touched files |
| `pnpm tsgo` | unavailable on this host | the pinned `@tsrs/linux-x64-gnu` native binary requires GLIBC ≥ 2.34; host has older glibc (`GLIBC_2.34…2.32 not found`). Fallback: full `tsc` runs above + CI |

### Cleanup

- All proof state lives under `/tmp/oc-cron1-proof/` (`state-red/`, `state-green/`,
  JSONL webhook logs); Gateway, model stub, and webhook receiver are terminated by the
  leg script's `trap cleanup` (explicit `kill <pid>`, no `pkill` matching the agent's
  own command line). Loopback ports only (18991/18992/18999).
- No production Gateway, session, token, or user config was touched; the model stub is
  a loopback OpenAI-compatible server with a synthetic key; the webhook receiver is a
  loopback HTTP sink.

### Not tested

- Named-session (`main` / `session:<key>`) webhook output — intentionally out of scope
  (see Fix scope); the issue's original repro used `sessionTarget: "session:veille-ia"`,
  so that lane's webhook payload remains summary-only until the follow-up lands.
- Full CI suites (left to PR CI); only the touched test file was run locally
  (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` equivalents above).
- The `completionDestination` (announce-mode completion webhook) payload is unchanged:
  its event is built from the persisted run-result projection, which does not carry
  `outputText` by design.

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

- Production change is four small hunks: two optional type fields, one previously-dropped field forwarding in the detached branch, one conditional spread in the webhook event literal, and one extra strip in the existing error-payload destructure. The fence-like summary cap code (`pickSummaryFromOutput`, diagnostics cap) is untouched.
- The conditional spread is the entire silent-run contract: empty/whitespace output omits the key rather than sending `outputText: ""`; the boundary tests lock that absent-key behavior.
- Docs landed in `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md` + `docs/cli/cron.md` because `webhooks.md` is the inbound Gateway-hooks page (declares itself separate from outbound delivery) and the canonical outbound `delivery.md` is occupied by #185848 — move the doc line there once #185848 lands if preferred.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- **Land-ready as is:** implements the issue's ClawSweeper recommendation for the lane whose owner already produces the untruncated text, with two-head shipped-CLI × live-Gateway proof (summary md5-identical across legs) and all three required boundaries.
- **Wait for the named-session half (single combined PR):** blocked structurally — that half needs a `state.ts` contract change (file occupied by #185848) plus new capture through the auto-reply owner, which violates the additive/no-new-capture scope this PR is holding to. Recommended instead: land this half, follow up with the cron owner for `session:<key>`.
- **Alternative — replace `summary` with the full text:** rejected; the maintainer explicitly preserved the 2,000-character cap, and run history / announcements / `automations runs` depend on the bounded shape (proven unchanged).
- **Scope statement:** webhook-only additive key on the primary delivery payload; no config, persistence, RPC, or fan-out change; issue #185873 stays open for the remaining lane.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions: Keep Allow edits from maintainers enabled</summary>

Maintainers may push directly to this branch (Allow edits from maintainers stays
enabled), including scope reductions, follow-up split, or landing as-is.

</details>

prs.title: fix: goals fail to resume after stopping a run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Goal Resume fails with “requires an idle built-in local session with recoverable history” after an operator stops a run, even after that work has fully settled. Definitive admission refusals also appear as an unconfirmed update.

## User Impact

Operators can resume the same stopped Goal without resetting the conversation or losing its history. Unsupported admission is reported as a rejection instead of leaving an uncertain operation waiting for reconciliation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit Resume may follow a settled abort, not just the special running-Goal replacement flow. Apply that distinction to local and supported Codex cloud-worker admission, while retaining live-work exclusion, freshness, placement, session identity, and current-authority checks. Use the existing typed Goal rejection contract so the existing UI can retire the refused request. Ordinary chat and Goal Start eligibility are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Integrated main `5516b9086e6092af42dac1ac42e635267e70d3b5` into the contributor branch after the admission-owner refactor. The retired restart-recovery module stays deleted; both current local and worker Resume predicates receive the fix.
- Fresh shared AutoReview of `5516b9086e6092af42dac1ac42e635267e70d3b5..60ff8e09bbe2922b9da9459fd5ca86c5cfe0259b` completed with no actionable P0-P2 findings. A separate independent source review also found no blockers.
- Current candidate: all 42 Gateway Goal tests and all 33 UI Goal recovery tests passed. Restoring the three production files from the baseline, while retaining the regression tests, made both targeted regressions fail for the expected admission defects.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40793088673) completed with one attributed upstream failure: the full-tree mock-export ratchet reports 14 violations in `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts`. [Main independently reports the same 14 violations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792935936/job/123184172493). The two tests, baseline ledger, checker and inspected checker inputs are unchanged between the protected-main parent and the tested PR merge. `security-fast` passed; all other jobs passed or were skipped. CI remains failed and is recorded in native pre-existing-failure evidence for landing; no CI rerun or unrelated source repair is claimed.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Claim:** an operator can Resume the same Goal after Stop has settled, and a definitive unsupported-admission refusal retires the pending UI operation.
- **Exercised surface:** production Gateway Goal RPC admission, queue/lifecycle handling and SQLite state, plus the existing UI Goal recovery owner.
- **Scenario/fixture:** Stop, wait for settlement, Resume with a new operation, complete, and replay the receipt without duplicate execution; unsupported admission retains its typed `goal-invalid` rejection.
- **Command/environment:** Crabbox `provider=local-container`, lease `cbx_bff6cd3713ae`, run `run_76ce59bd0f38`; Linux, `node:24-bookworm`, Node 24.20.0, pnpm 12.15.0, one test worker and bounded compiler threads. Canonical baseline source plus the six-file reviewed patch reconstructed tree `116593a9972df7b5c36a050230d4f7bf14ed5d01`, checked before execution; source hashes were checked and restored after the baseline replay.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.chat-goal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/chat/chat-goals.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
# With the three production admission files restored from the baseline:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.chat-goal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose --testNamePattern='stops automatic pursuit and resumes|keeps an unscoped reply-dispatch hook'
```

- **Observed result:** candidate Gateway 42/42 and UI 33/33 passed; baseline replay failed exactly the two intended regressions. The candidate source hashes matched again after restoration.
- **Artifact/trace:** the executed run produced `green.log`, `ui-green.log`, `red.log`, and `receipt.json`. Summary of the captured output:

```json
{"proof":"goal-stop-settlement-resume","green":{"passed":42},"uiPassed":33,"baselineRegressionFailures":2,"canonicalTree":"116593a9972df7b5c36a050230d4f7bf14ed5d01"}
```

- **Limits:** model execution and worker transport are simulated. This proves the production admission/state boundary and UI rejection contract; no live-model, real cloud-worker transport, deployed Gateway, or production-session mutation is claimed. The initial Windows rsync trial ended before test execution and is excluded from these results.

The proof command exited 0 and its captured receipt was verified. Crabbox's controller subsequently exited 7 on a workspace-owner renewal after lease release; the owned container's removal was verified. This cleanup diagnostic is separate from the executed test results.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6a8980dd-79eb-483e-82d8-8acc149cefef)

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.title: fix: stop attributing historical assistant output to new attempts
prs.body:
Closes #186349

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes output observers attributing an earlier assistant's abort, error or usage to a new embedded attempt when the new attempt has no model response.

## User Impact

Plugins receive only the current attempt's assistant in `llm_output.lastAssistant`, or no assistant when this attempt produced none. This corrects diagnostic attribution; it does not retry runs or repair provider stalls.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing current-attempt selector, including its completed-event fallback, at the hook producer. Internal historical `result.lastAssistant` remains unchanged. The hook contract already permits an absent assistant and describes attempt-local output; no new field or migration is needed.

## Evidence

- All three added result-owner regression cases failed on the baseline by observing the historical aborted assistant; they pass with the fix. Covers precheck/no response, transcript response and completed-event fallback.
- 40 focused tests passed: result owner (35) and wired hook privacy/lifecycle (5). Wrapper wall time 103.40s; file durations 86.17s (mostly transform) and 5.92s. Hosted CI timing pending.
- Targeted pinned native TypeScript compiler, supported focused syntax lint, formatter, whitespace and line-cap checks passed. Normal type-aware lint was blocked by a retained build-artifact lock on Windows; the lock was left intact. Hosted CI must cover that gap. No live-provider proof claimed.
- Independent consumer/contract audit and local Codex autoreview at P2 against base `2937d6581241ca1854601c3ab7a8594838352a49`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its checkout has no installed dependencies; hosted review remains applicable.
- Simplification: reuse one existing selector, with no added production helper/state/API. Delta: one production-line replacement, 32 test lines and two documentation lines.

prs.title: fix(telegram): suppress duplicate DM transcript windows while preserving delivery-only context
prs.body:
Related: #89855, #112548, #130551, #172711, #179399

## What Problem This Solves

Existing plain Telegram DMs receive ordinary recent user/assistant turns twice: through canonical session replay and a supplemental transcript `chat_window`. Blanket suppression would also remove delivery-only context excluded from normal replay.

## Change

Keep the existing plain-DM suppression predicate and pass `deliveryOnly: true` through the shared transcript-context owner. Select the bounded recent window first, then restore only supported delivery mirrors. Fresh DMs, explicit replies, topics, and groups retain their existing context selection. No config, schema, or storage-format changes.

## Evidence

Current head: `df377682122984deb56e11e8d0e2ec4bdf929911`. Merged main `870c16e66d940d629f8676d3293fb87ab174b3ee` to incorporate the upstream test-line budget repair in [#186785](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186785). The failing CI snapshot had 6,294,266 test lines against a 6,294,048 ceiling. With upstream's reviewed budget, the refreshed tree has 6,302,332 lines against a 6,310,000 ceiling (7,668 lines of headroom). The standalone test-line ratchet passes. No PR-specific ceiling increase or test deletion was needed.

The six-file PR patch is byte-for-byte identical to the independently reviewed `9d5d58e2ed2` candidate. It preserves #186081's turn-identity/completed-answer reconciliation alongside bounded delivery-only filtering. Original commits, human credit, and both sets of SQLite regressions remain intact.

**Current-head focused validation:**
- All 41 tests pass: SQLite transcript (3), Telegram prompt context (15), shared transcript context (9), and tool-prefix stability (14), in 153.28 seconds across the four selected Vitest shards.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.sqlite.test.ts src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.prompt-context.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- `git diff --check` passes. Previous targeted lint and formatting results are reused for the unchanged six-file patch.
- Budget check: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 870c16e66d940d629f8676d3293fb87ab174b3ee --no-merge-base` passes.
- Local Codex autoreview covered the complete six-file candidate against base `b46d011db972a982bf8b8b94331505473dd07851`, at P0–P2 coverage, before committing that unchanged index as `9d5d58e2ed2`. Completed with no actionable findings; that result is reused for the byte-identical six-file patch after this mechanical merge. Source review is separate from runtime proof.

**Live Telegram Test Server proof passed on prior head `09618b32c5e141cd74e35b91d88b9388ac0727dc`.** Five actual Gateway processes shared isolated SQLite state across four orderly replacements. A Convex-leased, independently authorized TDLib user observed the dedicated Test Server bot's replies. All seven captured Google Gemini 3.8 Flash requests returned HTTP 200; the runner's mock server received zero conversational/generation requests and two ancillary embedding requests.

- Ordinary user and assistant history reaches the provider exactly once before and after restart.
- An announcement from a real Cron job remains in the next model context after restart, exactly once.
- A final `message.send` reply is observed by TDLib and remains in runtime context after restart. Its persisted mirror has `final: true` and tool-call/source-turn correlation; verification does not rely solely on the original function-call arguments.

[Live proof and reproduction source for `09618b32c5e1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183190#issuecomment-6430787664) contains redacted provider-request excerpts and counts, native message receipts, restart/cleanup evidence, exact setup and commands, and reproduction scripts. This refresh reuses that runtime evidence; the live scenario has not been rerun on `df377682122`. The personal Gateway was not modified or restarted.

[Historical fixture proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183190#issuecomment-6400568002) covers `57a4cb127d2a`, including the explicitly seeded legacy `cron-direct-delivery-context` compatibility check. The committed SQLite regression was also verified red on original parent `bfcaa1b2cd1cf2f0e7d617b773e4743218eb219c` and green with the fix.

## CI and review status

Fresh CI is pending for `df377682122`. [The previous run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40623379325) failed solely on the test-line budget inside `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`; the other two reported failures were its aggregate CI gates. All other checks within the baseline-ratchets job passed. The refresh incorporates the upstream budget fix and the exact failing check passes locally.

[Earlier CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40428812707) and its [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40430950078) passed for `09618b32c5e1`; those results are prior-head evidence. The existing ClawSweeper review accepted the live proof and found no actionable defects on that prior head. No merge into main has been performed.
