prs.title: fix(slack): hand transport authority to route-discovery lookups
prs.body:
Related: #185972

## What Problem This Solves

Slack outbound route discovery keeps issuing authenticated Slack API requests after the transport authority that authorized the send has been invalidated. The Slack `resolveOutboundSessionRoute` implementation (`extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`) drops the `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback that `src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts:235` forwards into it, so none of its three remote lookups revalidate current authority before touching the network:

- Enterprise owner-heartbeat DM workspace discovery — `users.info` + `auth.teams.list` (`extensions/slack/src/enterprise-user-route.ts`)
- D-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (`extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts`)
- G-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (same owner)

When a Gateway restart or delivery supersession invalidates the worker admission between message acceptance and route discovery, Slack still receives authenticated destination-metadata requests. Remote consequence: a workspace-controlled D/G conversation id or a revoked token keeps being probed after local authority expired; the request cost lands on the operator's credentials.

**Precedent: #185972** — `fix(googlechat): stop metadata lookups after sender authority expires` (merged 2026-10-27). Its body states verbatim:

> "Separate follow-up: audit Slack's analogous route-discovery callback handoff."

This PR is that follow-up. Same shape, same mechanism: forward the **existing** `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback into the route-discovery network owner; zero new validators/options/config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK contract already documents the parameter's purpose (`src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts:619-620`):

```ts
/** Revalidates transport authority before new route-discovery network requests. */
assertDirectAdapterHandoff?: () => void;
```

Slack already implements the guard everywhere except the route path:

| Path | State before this PR |
| --- | --- |
| Action path (`action-runtime.ts:276-282`, `312-319`, `actions.ts:229`) | already forwards the callback into `createSlackLookupClient` / write clients |
| Send path (`client-delivery.ts:390`) | already fences delivery via `beforeRequest` |
| Conversation metadata (`channel-type.ts:60-67` → `client-options.ts:176-190`) | `resolveSlackConversationInfo` already accepts the callback and `fenceSlackReadFetch` asserts it before every fetch |
| **Route path (`channel.ts` `resolveOutboundSessionRoute`)** | **dropped it — the only remaining gap** |

This change forwards the already-supplied callback at the three route call sites, widens `resolveSlackChannelType`'s parameter type to pass it through, and hands it to `createSlackLookupClient` in `resolveSlackEnterpriseUserTeamId` (that factory already accepts and fences it). The fence implementation itself is untouched; action and send paths are untouched; no other channel is touched.

Production LOC: +15/−13 (net +2 across three files: `channel.ts` +12/−12 — the two identical conversation-lookup argument objects consolidate into one shared lookup scope, which both forwards the callback and keeps this over-cap file from growing, as the line-cap ratchet requires; `channel-type.ts` +1; `enterprise-user-route.ts` +2/−1). Test LOC: +154/−5 (net +149).

Classification: `behavior-completing` — completes #185972's transport-authority handoff coverage for Slack's analogous route-discovery path.

## User Impact

An accepted message keeps its successful receipt and local history. With **current** authority, route discovery is byte-for-byte unchanged: the same requests go out and the same routes resolve (proven live below). With **invalid** authority, Slack no longer receives new route-discovery metadata requests; the route resolution fails with the authority error instead of silently completing a lookup the operator's admission no longer covers. Callers without handoff context (`src/gateway/conversation-list.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`, `src/infra/outbound/targets.ts`, cron delivery targets) pass no callback and behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Heads

- Base (RED): `d45ff6de6c486eb7d68931492e84af4842e02e44` (`docs: point logo work to the brand-kit README (#186198)`, current `main` at pickup)
- Candidate (GREEN): `c9dd1c0a42` (branch `fix/slack-route-discovery-handoff`, rebased onto main `dafda2f722`; production diff identical to the originally reviewed head. Red/green and dist proofs below were recorded at pre-rebase head `45b95e3f9650d22d847d1d81bcd74a1b8f31f35e`; the rebases left the production diff byte-identical. History: `45b95e3f` → rebased to `08e8c0e99c` (baseline bump dropped) → `fe08c2f4c3` (contributor-side rebase onto newer main) → `c9dd1c0a42` adds the `enterprise-user-route.test.ts` assertion alignment, see Maintainer edits.)

### Trigger reachability (producer-chain)

The stale-authority input is produced by production code, not by a test-only seam:

1. **Producer** — `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-transcript.ts:64`: `assertDirectAdapterHandoff: () => stateContext.workerContext.admission.assertCurrent()`. The worker admission assertion is the owner-held liveness check; it fails after Gateway restart or when the delivery is superseded by a newer admission.
2. **Forwarder** — `src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts:228-236`: the **only** caller that forwards the handoff into `resolveOutboundSessionRoute` (`:235`).
3. **Drop point (base)** — `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts` route implementation discards `params.assertDirectAdapterHandoff` for all three remote lookups.
4. **Fence (already shipped)** — `extensions/slack/src/client-options.ts:176-190` `fenceSlackReadFetch` asserts the callback before every fetch once it is attached.

### Red → Green assertions

- **RED (base)**: with a handoff callback that throws, route resolution still completes and the remote lookups still fire — `users.info`/`auth.teams.list` (Enterprise), `conversations.info` (D/G) — and the callback is never invoked. Exactly the 3 new stale tests fail at their `.rejects.toThrow("transport authority expired")` assertion; all other 53 tests pass.
- **GREEN (candidate)**: the same stale callback is invoked before any request and the route rejects with the authority error with **zero** network requests (stub request-log delta `[]`).
- **Legal control (no false positives)**: with a current callback, both base and candidate resolve the same routes (`to: team:T11111111:user:U12345678`, `to: user:U09G2DJ0275`) and the lookups run normally — the fence only rejects genuinely invalid authority.

### Commands × exit

```sh
node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/slack/src/channel.test.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

| Head | Exit | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base `d45ff6de6` | 1 | 3 failed / 53 passed (56) — fails exactly at the 3 stale-authority assertions | 1m19.6s |
| candidate (pre-rebase `45b95e3f`) | 0 | 56 passed (56) | 1m22.2s |
| candidate (rebased `08e8c0e99c`) | 0 | 55 passed (55) — one low-value passthrough test removed, see Maintainer edits | 3m16.4s |
| candidate (final `c9dd1c0a42`) | 0 | 66 passed (66) — adds `enterprise-user-route.test.ts` (11) to the run; its exact-args expectation was aligned with the forwarded callback | 3m50.2s |

```sh
pnpm exec oxlint extensions/slack/src/channel.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts extensions/slack/src/enterprise-user-route.ts extensions/slack/src/channel.test.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.test.ts
node scripts/run-format.mts --check <the same five files>
node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-max-lines-ratchet.mts --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-mock-exports.mts --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base d45ff6de6 --no-merge-base
```

| Check (candidate) | Exit | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| oxlint | 0 | 0 warnings / 0 errors (5 files, 259 rules) |
| format `--check` | 0 | all matched files use the correct format |
| line-cap ratchet | 0 | OK — no new violations or over-cap growth (`channel.ts` stays at/below its base counted lines) |
| max-lines ratchet | 0 | OK — 407 grandfathered suppressions unchanged |
| mock-export ratchet | 0 | OK — 6576 grandfathered factories unchanged |
| test-lines ratchet | 0 | OK with no ceiling change (`Test lines OK: 6293949; ceiling: 6294048; slack: 99` at final head vs pinned base `dafda2f722`) |
| `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit` | 2 | 17 errors, **all in untouched extensions** (codex/line/nostr/onepassword/policy/test-support/vault/visitor-access, TS2883/TS4023/TS4058 portability noise); zero errors in any slack file. The repo's tsgo gate cannot run on this host (tsrs binary needs glibc ≥2.34); classic tsc substituted. |
| `pnpm build` (dist) | 0 | dist built from candidate sources for the shipped-run proof |

### Shipped-run proof (dist artifacts + real HTTP, loopback Slack API stub)

Setup: `pnpm build` dist; loopback stub records every request (`users.info` / `auth.teams.list` / `conversations.info`) and answers Slack Web API shapes; driver invokes the **dist** plugin route contract (`dist/extensions/slack/api.js` → `slackPlugin.messaging.resolveOutboundSessionRoute`) with `SLACK_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/`, proxies unset, and a seeded installation-identity state (Enterprise for the heartbeat cases, workspace for the D-channel cases — mirroring what the monitor owner registers after `auth.test`).

In the dist build with `SLACK_API_URL` pointing at the loopback Slack stub, the candidate route-discovery path invokes the forwarded handoff before each request: with current authority the enterprise heartbeat route issues `users.info` + `auth.teams.list` against the stub and resolves `team:T11111111:user:U12345678` (handoff asserted 2×), the D-channel route issues `conversations.info` and resolves `user:U09G2DJ0275` (handoff asserted 1×); with stale authority the handoff throws first and the stub request-log delta is **empty** for both paths.

```text
candidate (dist) driver output, one line per case:
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"team:T11111111:user:U12345678","baseSessionKey":"agent:main:main:account:default:team:t11111111"},"handoffCalls":2,"stubRequests":["users.info","auth.teams.list"]}
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":false,"error":"A request error occurred: transport authority expired (proof fixture)"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":[]}
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"d-channel-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"user:U09G2DJ0275","baseSessionKey":"agent:main:main"},"handoffCalls":1,"stubRequests":["conversations.info"]}
{"label":"candidate-d45ff6de6+fix","case":"d-channel-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":false,"error":"transport authority expired (proof fixture)"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":[]}
```

Base dist comparison (same driver, same stub, same command): with stale authority the lookups still go out and the routes resolve — the shipped defect shape.

```text
base dist driver output (same command, same stub, stale-authority cases resolve and the stub receives the requests):
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"team:T11111111:user:U12345678"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["users.info","auth.teams.list"]}
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"enterprise-heartbeat-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"team:T11111111:user:U12345678"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["users.info","auth.teams.list"]}
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"d-channel-current-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"user:U09G2DJ0275"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["conversations.info"]}
{"label":"base-d45ff6de6","case":"d-channel-stale-authority","outcome":{"resolved":true,"to":"user:U09G2DJ0275"},"handoffCalls":0,"stubRequests":["conversations.info"]}
```

**Evidence grading (honest):**

- **shipped-run** — everything in this section: dist-built Slack plugin artifacts, real fence, real HTTP to the loopback stub, base-vs-candidate comparison at the dist route boundary.
- **producer-chain** — the *live-Gateway orchestration* of a naturally invalidated admission (Gateway restart / delivery supersession mid-flight) was **not** orchestrated on this host; the stale-authority input's production origin and invalidation owner are the file:line chain above, and its fence behavior is proven at the dist boundary. The dist driver seeds the installation-identity state directly (the monitor owner's `auth.test` registration path is not exercised).

### Test-lines ratchet

No ceiling change. The pre-rebase head bumped `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` 6286403 → 6286591, which conflicted with `main`. The first rebase dropped the bump, but CI pins an immutable comparison commit (`ci-ratchet-base`, here main `874dc86b` at push time) whose ceiling 6293290 sat 475 below its own test total, so this PR's net +149 failed the gate there (`over by: 624`). Re-rebasing onto current main `dafda2f722` — whose ceiling was since raised to 6294048 — absorbs the +149 cleanly. Measured at the final head with the ratchet's own working-tree method against the pinned base: `Test lines OK: 6293949; ceiling: 6294048; slack: 99`. If a future rebase re-trips this gate, the fix is to raise the ceiling by exactly the PR's net add with this note as justification.

### Scope and risk

| File:line (candidate) | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts:369-374` (Enterprise heartbeat lookup call) | forwards `params.assertDirectAdapterHandoff` into `resolveSlackEnterpriseUserTeamId` | With current authority, no behavior change (same requests, same routes). With invalid authority, route resolution now fails instead of issuing `users.info`/`auth.teams.list` discovery. |
| `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts:387-394` (shared conversation-lookup scope) → `:395` (D-branch) / `:407` (G-branch) | both classification call sites share one lookup scope carrying the callback | Same as above for `conversations.info`; consolidating the duplicated argument object is also what keeps this over-cap file at its base counted lines (line-cap ratchet). |
| `extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts:148-155` | `resolveSlackChannelType` parameter type widened to carry the optional callback (runtime passthrough already existed) | Additive optional parameter; every existing caller unaffected. |
| `extensions/slack/src/enterprise-user-route.ts:8-13,25` | accepts the optional callback and passes it to `createSlackLookupClient` (already-fenced factory) | Additive optional parameter; non-route callers of this function pass nothing and behave as before. |

- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: **none** — no new option, validator, or configuration surface.
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the shipped `fenceSlackReadFetch` / `createSlackLookupClient` handoff plumbing from #185972's era; nothing new invented.

### Cleanup

Proof scaffolding lives in `/tmp/oc-slack1-proof` (loopback stub, driver, request logs); the stub process is killed after capture. No production Gateway, session, token, or config was touched; no real Slack API was contacted.

### Not tested

- Live Gateway-process heartbeat delivery with a naturally invalidated admission (not orchestrated on this host; producer-chain + dist-boundary proof instead).
- Real Slack API (all HTTP targets are the loopback stub).
- Socket Mode / monitor / action / send paths (untouched by this change; their existing fence tests remain green).
- The repo's `tsgo` typecheck gate (host glibc too old for the tsrs binary); classic `tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit` substituted — zero slack-file errors.

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

- Production change is forwarding one existing optional callback at three route call sites plus one parameter-type widening; `fenceSlackReadFetch`, the action path, and the send path are untouched.
- `channel.ts` consolidates the two identical conversation-lookup argument objects into one shared scope; that consolidation is also what keeps this over-cap file (line-cap ratchet) at its base counted lines, and it carries no behavior change.
- The `channel-type.test.ts` passthrough case from the original head has been **removed**: it asserted mocked client arguments for a params object that flows through verbatim at runtime, so it passed on base by design and duplicated the G-route stale-authority regression. All red/green stale-authority coverage lives in `channel.test.ts`; `channel-type.test.ts` is now byte-identical to `main`.
- One existing `enterprise-user-route.test.ts` expectation updated: it pinned the lookup-client factory to exactly one argument (`"sending-fixture"`); the forwarded callback makes the real call `("sending-fixture", undefined, undefined)`. Expectation-only change — the test's workspace-selection behavior assertions are untouched, and the file passes 11/11.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- **Land-ready as is:** verbatim harvest of the follow-up named in #185972's body, reusing the shipped fence plumbing, with dist-boundary shipped-run proof plus unit red/green.
- **Alternative — revalidate in `confirmed-visible-message` or centrally at the fence factory:** rejected deliberately; the SDK contract (`src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts:619-620`) places revalidation at the route-discovery network owner, and centralizing would change callers that carry no handoff context (`conversation-list.ts`, `send.ts`, `targets.ts`, cron delivery targets).
- **Scope statement:** Slack route discovery only; no config, protocol, authorization, or storage surface; no other channel touched.

</details>

<details>Additional instructions: Keep Allow edits from maintainers enabled</details>

prs.title: fix(plugins): install from the literal local path when it ends in whitespace
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw plugins install "<dir> "` installs the trimmed sibling directory instead of the directory the user named. A trailing space in a directory name is legal on POSIX; `resolveUserPath` trims the spec before the local install path is resolved, so the install silently selects the neighbor.

Fixture with two siblings, `probe-dirs/plug` (plugin id `probe-beta`) and `probe-dirs/plug ` (plugin id `probe-alpha`): current main installs `probe-beta` when the user passes `probe-dirs/plug ` and reports `Installed plugin: probe-beta`.

## User Impact

- `openclaw plugins install "<path> "` installs exactly the named directory.
- Unchanged for ordinary paths: relative, absolute, and `~/` paths resolve as before; a whitespace-only spec still fails with `Plugin install source must not be empty.`
- Behavior change disclosed: a local plugin/hook install spec with leading or trailing whitespace is no longer trimmed. It either exists literally or fails with `path not found: <literal>`. Specs without boundary whitespace are byte-for-byte unaffected.
- `openclaw hooks install` local sources use the same resolver and get the same fix. No new option, validator, config key, or stored format.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveUserPath` trims by design (`src/infra/home-dir.ts` → `resolvePathWithHome`), which is right for user-typed config paths but wrong for a quoted local install locator: the shell already delimits the name. Blank admission stays intact; only boundary whitespace of a non-blank spec is preserved.

Two sites on the same install path are updated together so the result is consistent, not partial:

- `src/infra/install-flow.ts:resolveExistingInstallPath` — the deferred package-dir install resolves the spec here (`plugins/install-package.ts`, `hooks/install.ts`). This site actually selected the trimmed sibling.
- `src/plugins/install-source-plan.ts` — `resolvePluginInstallSourcePlan` and the managed `case "local"` resolve the same spec for source classification and managed install requests.

One owner: `resolveLiteralInstallPath` lives in `install-flow.ts` and `install-source-plan.ts` imports it. Non-blank values use `path.resolve(expandHomePrefix(value))`, the accepted shape from #186475/#186746; blank values keep `resolveUserPath`.

Classification: behavior-preserving for specs without boundary whitespace; behavior-correcting for explicitly quoted literal paths.

Not fixed here: the git-URL and `npm-pack` branches of `install-source-plan.ts` still call `resolveUserPath`; they are not filesystem path locators on this flow.

Collision disclosure: open PR #185654 also touches `src/plugins/install-source-plan.ts`, but only the git-URL `.replaceAll("@", "%40")` line (~140). prs.title: fix(agents): keep top-level Slack requests' sessions_send completions top-level
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With Slack `replyToMode: "off"`, a delayed `sessions_send` completion promotes the triggering top-level message timestamp into `thread_ts`, creating an unsolicited thread.

Keep `sessions_send`'s existing admitted-current destination and thread precedence. Do not adopt the spawn route resolver: its fallback-first pairing can choose stale `agentTo`/`agentThreadId` instead of the admitted current route. Remove only Slack's off-mode synthetic reply anchor when it equals the current inbound message ID. Genuine threads and non-Slack routing retain the existing path. No SDK/config fields or authority rules change.

## Evidence

Inspectable [signed ingress, delayed completion `chat.postMessage` requests, SDK versions and threaded/admission controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187065#issuecomment-6484331947).

Built main `bf6bdd6c5fedb5e23f7bc206d26c625adbdec1ab` and candidate `19a51e9d4de3d5b317edd67ca0b55d01c86481c2` runtime artifacts in secretless Node 24.22.1. The shipped Gateway loads its bundled Slack plugin and actual Slack Bolt 5.1.0 / Web API 8.2.0 SDKs against local Slack-compatible HTTP services. Signed Events API requests enter the real HTTP adapter. A deterministic local Chat Completions fixture exercises shipped Tool Search discovery/description and dispatches the real `sessions_send`; a real worker agent run is held until the requester acknowledges and another DM turn has replied on the same main session. The completion calls `message` without a destination or thread override.

- Main twice: the SDK posts the delayed completion with `thread_ts` equal to the original top-level message timestamp.
- Candidate twice: the SDK omits `thread_ts`; the result stays in the original conversation, not the later DM.
- Genuine threaded requests retain the actual thread root on both refs, including after the later inbound turn.
- All 23 conversation/admission tests pass. The existing current-source-over-stale-fallback regression remains passing: original-recipient/thread 42 wins over stale-recipient/thread 99 after inbound metadata changes. The top-level Slack case now exercises the actual reply flow, not factory-call spying, and fails on main. Numeric-thread coverage remains in the legacy-DM case. Test count delta: zero. Formatting passes.

This is native SDK API-placement proof against local services, not a real Slack workspace, UI screenshot or real-model claim. The captures distinguish the raw user-ID DM target from the API-resolved DM channel instead of treating those representations as different recipients.

Simplification: production +8/-1 lines (9 gross), no new helper or runtime import. The contributor's two factory-spy cases are removed in favor of the existing composed admission regression; the contributor commit is preserved. The Slack threading page documents the corrected completion placement.

## Merge risk

Two-way door: no migration or persisted-state change; reverting restores the prior route capture. Blast radius is delayed `sessions_send` requester completion placement for off-mode top-level Slack messages. The admitted destination and genuine-thread precedence remain protected by the existing regression and transport controls.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve native continuation and yield acknowledgements
prs.body:
Related: #167410 (not a claim to close all reported timeouts).

## What Problem This Solves

Preserve a managed native parent's saved tool declarations while its last terminal child's completion is still awaiting delivery. This fixes a distinct gap after execution protection correctly ends: rebuilding the catalog for the completion turn could rotate the parent thread and make a follow-up to its original child fail lineage validation.

The PR also retains the original delayed-completion authority regression. Current main already owns that async-lifetime behavior; no stable-only lifetime patch is added to main.

## Reproduction and scope

A packaged Gateway + packaged native Codex test on the prior PR head completed two ordinary turns on one child, then genuinely yielded while the third result was pending. Automatic delivery resumed with a changed tool catalog, started a second native parent, and the original-child follow-up failed lineage checks. The provider was deterministic local scripted Responses, not a real model or OAuth acceptance test.

The new regression exercises the real harness lifecycle with a nonempty native tool catalog, holds terminal-child delivery after the execution pin releases, and admits the completion with no current executors. With only the catalog owner restored to the prior implementation, it fails with two native thread starts instead of one. With the repair, it preserves the original parent and rejects execution of the old tool.

## Follow-up: preserve terminal yield acknowledgements

A fresh live run on the separate stable candidate completed five original-child turns and automatically resumed all three delayed results, but two yield acknowledgements became `aborted by user`. It was not counted as a full acceptance pass.

The native dynamic-tool `item/completed` event precedes the handler's return. Interrupting at that point can replace the model-visible result with cancellation, even after OpenClaw has recorded terminal release. Waiting a JavaScript event-loop tick does not establish native output commitment.

The lifecycle owner now waits for matching `rawResponseItem/completed` function/custom output receipts in its existing model-response inventory. These prove recording in native model history before interruption. Nested Code Mode waits for the outer output; web/image calls are not incorrectly required to emit function outputs. No new protocol, timer, persisted state, or authority relaxation is introduced.

## Ownership and safety

- Read pending-delivery custody from the existing completion owner; no new custody registry or persistent state.
- Require the same physical native client, current assignment/history ownership, and the existing claimed delivery owner.
- Recheck catalog eligibility after reading native metadata.
- Keep execution pins released at terminal completion; never restore old executors.
- Release declaration eligibility when delivery settles, is abandoned, or loses custody.
- Share the existing child-execution predicate between its two monitor consumers; the oversized monitor file shrinks.

## Evidence — current rebased upstream head

Source: `9c948da8a43477fb375ba8c7e5c08b14ef4b8ec2`, rebased onto pinned main `a919e5ecc4f6c579e16ab21499ccda3acaa1fb07` on 2026-10-28.

- At source-equivalent predecessor `d2b9766017ba75a56c419f8a316214201a145bdc`, 108 targeted cases across ten files passed in 215.03 seconds wrapper wall time, including delayed-completion authority, pending catalog custody, same-child follow-up, lifecycle/steering/output receipt tests and the real native-process yield test.
- Production plugin types, scoped extension-test types, targeted type-aware lint (including pinned Bun parity), formatting, pinned-base line-cap and test-line budget checks passed.
- Independent source review of this exact range found no actionable P0–P2. The original production/test patch is unchanged; the old test-budget-only increase was removed because upstream now owns a larger shared ceiling. Upstream shutdown, subagent cleanup, sidebar and annotated UI receipt fixes are preserved.
- The real native case uses pinned Codex 0.164.0 and synthetic inference. Historical controlled-failure evidence below still documents the patch mechanism; neither a new full packaged upstream acceptance nor hosted CI success is claimed for this rebased head.
- The initial lint attempt on the preceding base could not stage the pinned Bun parity runtime in an offline container. Canonical staging resolved the tooling prerequisite; no lint gate or parity check was bypassed.

### Full-suite registration correction and hosted CI

The current head adds only the missing `run-attempt-lifecycle-controller.output-receipt.test.ts` entry to the database-worker test plan. Hosted CI on the predecessor caught that direct test selection was insufficient to prove full-suite discovery. The exact final head passed 54 configuration cases on both test runtimes plus four receipt cases (112 executions, 215.31 seconds wrapper wall), and scoped lint/format. Production/test source is otherwise unchanged, so the preceding source checks remain applicable.

A separate hosted `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failure lists 14 mock-export sites in `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts`. Both files are byte-identical to pinned upstream main `a919e5e`; the same diagnostics reproduce locally. This inherited check is **not fixed or claimed green** by this PR. [Failing job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40791343185/job/123177622310). No gate or baseline was weakened.

## Historical source validation — pre-rebase head

Source: `7ac126cd15dc6f67d14944b4b4a97c1b8697313e`, based on pinned main `58bf6decb46a946365900bb6d2f93b96e9b52f69`.

- Controlled original-controller comparison: both new direct/nested receipt regressions fail on premature native interruption; candidate bytes restored afterward.
- 57 lifecycle/steering/receipt/native cases passed across four files (67.60 seconds total wrapper wall time). Existing fixtures now explicitly model recorded output; no assertions were weakened. Two native-sibling cases moved out of the oversized suite.
- 29 full-attempt dynamic-tool, parent-continuation and original-child follow-up cases passed across three files (59.52 seconds wrapper wall time).
- Real pinned native Codex process plus production run-attempt/bridge/lifecycle and a synthetic local Responses provider: recorded `yielded` output precedes `turn/interrupt`, no aborted acknowledgement, owned native process exits. The case took 6.464 seconds; it exercises an actual process/history boundary that the cheaper lifecycle tests cannot prove.
- The native test's host fixture supplies an eligible yield; it does not certify child-claim admission or automatic continuation. It uses isolated state and no operator credentials. The first setup attempts exposed test-lane/session-seeding omissions; those were corrected, not counted as product failures or successful proofs.
- Production plugin types, scoped test types, targeted lint/format, pinned-base line-cap ratchet and exact test-line budget passed. Fresh independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the production repair; native proof source was separately reviewed by the lead.
- Simplification: one receipt bit in the existing call inventory replaces the assumption that a flushed response is ready for interruption; no parallel lifecycle or registry. The production delta for this follow-up is 17 added / 3 removed lines.

## Historical packaged proof (prior head, not current-head certification)

`f8699fea349def102ef4377b5009a556819583ac` passed 52 targeted tests plus packaged continuation in a fresh isolated installation: one parent, one original child, five persisted child turns, three genuine yields and three once-only automatic consumptions (96.19 seconds). Archive SHA-256 `2bbc9dc04691464cd91545c296d64651bdced78f307751d3da1699262ad13839`; build ID `2026.10.7-pr184848-f8699fea349-20261027`; native Codex `0.164.0`.

That packaged proof used scripted local HTTPS Responses/WebSocket inference with no external network. It is historical after the acknowledgement repair, not a rebuilt-package or real-model/OAuth acceptance claim. The prior controlled catalog regression fails with two parent thread starts when only its owner repair is reverted.

## Evidence — live 2026.10.7 backport acceptance

On 2026-10-28, a fresh uninterrupted live native acceptance run passed against installed custom build `2026.10.7-custom-continuation-e7de3d6695e-20261028`, backport commit `e7de3d6695e0b4881b109291c666e60121989580`. The running Gateway reported `2026.10.7` and pointed to that installed package.

One native child completed two ordinary turns, then three delayed turns (25-second delay requested each). Each delayed completion automatically resumed the parent after an explicit `sessions_yield` acknowledgement of `status: yielded`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Turns completed with the same native child | 5/5 |
| Confirmed yields on turns 3–5 | 3/3 |
| Automatic parent resumptions | 3/3 |
| Results consumed once | 5/5 |

No polling during delayed checks, manual wakeups, child replacements, or user interruptions. No `nothing_pending` or interrupted acknowledgements were counted. Mirrored notifications were deduplicated: this proves once-only consumption, not transport-level exactly-once delivery. An earlier interrupted run was inconclusive and is excluded from this table.

These live results apply to the **stable custom backport**, not the upstream PR head. [Live acceptance report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184848#issuecomment-6480604481).

## Limits and operational impact

No live installation, restart, configuration change or merge is part of this PR-body update or the live acceptance run. The stable 2026.10.7 backport remains separate; its installed custom package passed the live acceptance above. That does not certify a rebuilt package of the upstream PR head. The observed duplicate native notifications and intermediate visible-reply warnings are not claimed fixed by this acknowledgement patch. No claim of production restart recovery, provider/OAuth recovery, or all-plugin test-type coverage.

## Test-line budget

The upstream ceiling is preserved unchanged at 6,320,000. The old PR-specific budget increase is no longer part of the diff. The repository's exact test-line and pinned-base line-cap checks passed on the rebased head. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available for this head.

prs.title: fix(ui): plugin install says outcome unknown during an OpenClaw upgrade
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Plugins page says "The Gateway did not confirm the installation outcome. Reconnect and check installed plugins before trying again." when you click Install while an OpenClaw upgrade is running.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who try to install a plugin during an upgrade now see "Installation blocked: an OpenClaw upgrade is in progress, try again when it finishes." Before this change, they were told the outcome was unknown and asked to reconnect, even though nothing was sent to the Gateway and nothing needs to be checked.

## Why This Change Was Made

While an update is running, the Control UI suspends config writes, and plugin installs go through that same write path. When the UI refused the write itself, the error reached the install handler as a plain `Error`. The handler could not tell that error apart from a lost transport, so it fell back to the "status unknown" recovery text. The shared config-mutation runner now throws a typed `ConfigMutationRefusedError` that includes the refusal reason. The install handler maps the `suspended` reason to the new message, which is the wording the maintainer chose. Other refusal reasons and Gateway failures are handled as before.

## Evidence

Mock-Gateway Control UI E2E: an update run is active (`update.status.activeRun.status = "running"`) and Install is clicked on a catalog card. In both runs, no `plugins.install` request is sent.

| Before (`origin/main`) | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: installation outcome unknown](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51d93dd3-359d-44ef-a434-f1e353733b18) | ![After: installation blocked by upgrade](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3de8b959-5892-4b77-8dd3-91d50c7e4e03) |

- New focused regression in `plugins-consent.test.ts`. It fails on `origin/main` (outcome-unknown text) and passes with this change.
- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run src/pages/plugins/plugins-consent.test.ts src/pages/plugins/plugins-page.persisted-install.test.ts`: 8 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files: clean. `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` produced no baseline changes.
- Local review gap: local Codex autoreview was unavailable because the configured API key was rejected (401). The Claude engine was unavailable because its weekly usage limit was reached. A hosted ClawSweeper review is requested instead.

prs.title: fix: allow session tools in system continuations
prs.body:
Related: #185730

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes person-scoped session tools refusing authorized system continuations after background command completion.

## User Impact

System-triggered turns can spawn and continue work using the session principal's current authority, without another user message. Revocation or ownership changes still prevent later effects. Scheduled jobs keep their existing authority model.

## Why This Change Was Made

The restart redesign resolved principal authority for restart input, but other system admissions still depended on the previous turn's caller or had no person authority. Trusted host inputs now share the existing principal resolver at admission, selecting the assigned human owner or verified human creator and checking current grants before effects. Public provenance alone cannot select this path. This removes the restart-specific resolver and inherited person grants from ordinary transcript continuations.

Sessions without a human principal gain no person authority; their refusal now explains that a person must resume the work. There are no configuration, dependency, schema, or persisted-shape changes.

## Evidence

The exec-completion regression fails on the base and passes with the fix through real event admission and the managed `sessions_spawn` tool, omitting `user`. Its second child launch is refused after the principal is demoted at the effect boundary. Only model decisions and the final child launch are synthetic; no live Gateway or real user state was used.

Local proof passed with `nice -n 5` and at most eight Vitest workers: 177 tests across nine focused files, followed by 29 passing tests in the two files with final fixture corrections. The existing operator-run cancellation suite also passed all 15 tests. Core typecheck, the three affected test type graphs, targeted lint, formatting of all 27 changed files, and `git diff --check` passed. Prompt-prefix stability is included in the 177-test run.

The final exec regression was replayed on the base with production changes temporarily reversed: event execution started but principal authority was absent, and the test failed. Production edits were restored and the final principal suite passed all seven tests.

The complete change is production +429/−220 (net +209), tests +161/−167 (net −6), and docs +7. Necessary growth covers shared admission, current-owner validation and release ownership; no limit or baseline was raised. Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the final snapshot. prs.title: fix(update): restore managed Gateway after updater process death
prs.body:
Refs #164800. Supersedes #186328; this draft combines the helper and repair lanes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a managed Gateway remaining stopped when its updater is killed before, during, or after package publication, including when the updater itself stopped the service.

## User Impact

The live helper settles the interrupted update and restores a verified Gateway. If the helper also dies, `openclaw update repair` can recover promptly and restart the Gateway the update left stopped. Operator stops, lost ownership, named data risk, and unverifiable runtime identity still prevent automatic restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

The live Linux reproduction exposed two related ownership gaps. The helper only armed restoration when it parked the service through the foreground protocol; the normal native updater stops systemd itself (`update-command-service-maintenance.ts:618`). Its SIGKILL therefore reached the old “no verified recovery result” branch. Standalone repair also only recognized the helper's `service-stop` step. Dead handoff owners could additionally retain the 45-minute recovery grace.

Both recovery paths now consume `findUpdateGatewayStop` in `src/infra/update-run-gateway-stop.ts`. It recognizes the helper's stop, or a managed handoff followed by activation with the service currently stopped. The existing completed `managed-service update handoff` receipt is written by both Gateway `update.run` (`src/gateway/server-methods/update.ts:546`) and automatic updates (`src/infra/update-startup-auto-run.ts:379`), so it remains usable after target selection changes `installationMethod` to `npm-global`. The initial `update.run` running snapshot is not a restart receipt. Later incoming running observations after activation persist the existing `service-running` receipt; those receipts, replacement boot/settled verification, completed managed restarts, and newer settled runs retire the stop. These receipts survive ledger compaction. No new stop protocol, ledger schema, or updater-side stop receipt is needed.

The helper uses its staged runtime to retain bookkeeping while the installed tree is missing. It cancels untouched publication preparation; once displacement begins it completes publication forward through the sealed publication owner, runs the installed post-core finalizer as this run's continuation, then uses `gateway restart --preserve-definition --json` and verifies readiness/version/build identity. Updater-stopped recovery does not require the helper-only parked systemd generation. History records rollback, success with recovery, or failure with repair/deep-status guidance.

Repair reclaims promptly only when the recorded owners are proven dead; live/unknown owners and descendant/runtime-holder fences remain. After finalization, it uses the same stop evidence to start and verify an update-stopped service while preserving later operator stops.

Rejected alternatives: treating a signal as an unrecoverable result; inferring restart permission solely from an inactive unit; requiring a new native-stop receipt from an older installed driver; importing bookkeeping from the package while it is being swapped; and adding a second helper/repair stop policy. The combined change retains one publication owner and one stop-evidence reader.

LOC against base `4daeb9252ce`: production +800/−235; tests/support +764/−73; docs +76/−12; total +1640/−320 across 39 files. The required growth covers sealed crash recovery, standalone service restoration, and their boundary proof. Simplification removed the repair-only stop inference and reuses existing durable handoff evidence.

## Evidence

- **Focused tests:** 364 tests across 16 files passed, including all nine SIGKILL/publication cases, native-stop group-death repair, operator-stop negatives, data-risk refusals, systemd/launchd recovery, lifecycle/terminal outcomes, and ledger receipt/interruption coverage. The full run initially found seven stale termination-harness source lookups; removing the duplicate lookup and rerunning that file passed all seven. Production was unchanged for that rerun.
- **Red/green:** with production temporarily reverted to pre-follow-up merge `cc34e4ae6ea`, five helper regressions, two repair regressions, and two compaction regressions failed. Native-stop fixtures include the real entry point's initial `serviceRunning: true` snapshot. The base reproduced the old no-verified-result branch and the missing installed-runtime failure during publication. Production was restored with SHA-256 verification; all corresponding tests pass on this change. A separate interim run also proved that the initial running snapshot suppressed recovery before its fix (three helper and two repair failures).
- **Build/checks:** packaged runtime build passed (2m22s), including CLI bootstrap and Doctor closure checks. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- **Typecheck limitation:** the requested `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` stops before source checking with `Declaration input escapes checkout` for `tsrs` in the prescribed external pnpm virtual store. The checkout containment guard was preserved; this is not a passing typecheck.
- **Autoreview:** Codex local review of the complete combined diff against `4daeb9252ce` finished `scoped-clean` (P0–P2), with no accepted/actionable findings. A fresh final pass included the termination-harness fix.

<details>
<summary>Focused test command</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-interrupted.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-service.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-run-ledger.compaction.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-command.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize-refusal.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-recovery.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-lifecycle.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-recovery-systemd.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-recovery-launchd.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-triage.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-terminal-result.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-termination.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-command.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-run-ledger.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-run-capture-receipts.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-run-interruption.worker.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

The termination file was rerun with the same runner after fixing its stale lookup. The existing manager/lifecycle suites exercise process startup, publication, cancellation, and lease custody and take longer than unit-only tests.

</details>

The helper boundary uses real SIGKILL children, package publication journals, ledger writes, and native lease custody, with synthetic native-manager/readiness/finalizer I/O. The repair boundary runs the registered CLI with real ledger and dead-handoff reclamation. This is not a fresh live Linux/systemd upgrade result; the AWS reproduction still needs to be rerun against this head.

prs.title: refactor: resume running sessions after graceful restarts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Graceful Gateway restarts can wait on busy agent work for tens of seconds, then reconstruct execution through competing recovery owners and hold new user input behind recovered runs.

The motivating incident had 15 restarts in one day, each draining roughly 170–185 operations including about 20 agent runs. Restart recovery occupied approximately 290 non-test files / 57k lines across a dozen owners, following roughly 200 restart-fix commits in 30 days. One new prompt waited 14m15s in admission behind recovered work. Shutdown also failed on retained plugin resources and stalled for about 80 seconds in lifetime sidecar cleanup.

## User Impact

A graceful restart records which root sessions are running, promptly aborts their work, then sends each one ordinary input asking it to inspect current state and continue. Captured queued user messages follow in FIFO order under each sender's current authority. New messages use ordinary steering and queueing. The Control UI shows the conversation and normal composer, without recovery banners, interrupted-input notices, or bulk dismissal.

**Accepted loss:** a crash or SIGKILL records no shutdown marker, so nothing automatically resumes. The transcript remains available and a new user message works. Background processes do not survive a replacement process. When the shutdown snapshot saw running background exec, the same single resume input also says exactly: “Background exec processes were stopped; rerun them if still needed.” There is no exactly-once guarantee for external effects, child task adoption, or startup orphan reconstruction.

Refused or unavailable stores are skipped and logged, so one refused agent cannot hold healthy agents’ chat admission closed. If inventory discovery itself fails, automatic resume is skipped with a warning and fresh input remains available for healthy sessions.

Markers are cleared before admission. A crash or admission failure in that startup window can lose the automatic resume; no effect or input exactly-once machinery is added. The transcript and a fresh user input remain the recovery path.

Old recovery fields and inference-only queued rows remain readable but inert. Their text is preserved; normal retention may reclaim data previously pinned only by dead recovery state. There is no schema migration, Doctor migration, new config option, dependency change, or protocol version bump. `sessions.recover` is retired: repository-wide client inspection found only Control UI callers, with no shipped native client contract to preserve.

## Why This Change Was Made

Peter's direction:

> for restart recovery, can we redesign this? IMO this should be WAY easier. if a session runs (meaning, agent loop OR subagent OR process running) the resume just sends a "system restarted, resume your work" and that's it. this should not be so complicated!

> we should grossly simplify restart recovery. session should have some indicator if it runs [agent loop OR subagent OR process running], and if it's slightly lossy that's okay. we usually can rely on gateway being properly shut down, so suspend has a chance to write that state, don't paranoid write it all the time. delete a lot of code

> and yes we need e2e test for that.

One new owner, `src/gateway/session-restart-resume.ts`, snapshots the existing live run, subagent requester ancestry, and background-process owners after admission closes and before aborting them. It stores `resumeAfterRestart: { queuedInputIds, hadBackgroundExec?: true }` in the existing `session_nodes.entry_json`, with one replacement batch per physical session store. Nothing is checkpointed per turn or tool for restart recovery. Startup clears each marker and admits the standard resume input through the existing session-event path, preserving current admission, tool authority, routing, and reply delivery.

Short cleanup cutoffs apply only to existing `exitAfterClose:true` process hosts; embedded `GatewayServer.close()` joins owned cleanup. Startup rollback receives no inferred intent. The shutdown/supervisor owner `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop-cleanup.ts` owns bounded cleanup joins and exit classification. Bounded-grace leftovers are logged; lifecycle sets `process.exitCode` and returns naturally. Retained resources prohibit reusing the runtime for an in-process restart. The already-armed native hard-exit watchdog is the sole backstop for leaked handles; a watchdog signal/nonzero exit in that case is accepted. Real required-write/finalizer failures remain failures. Healthy global retirement measured 2327ms, so resource cleanup gets 5s headroom; required persistence has a 3s bound. The existing owned-process supervisor receives its normal 5s TERM policy plus 1s extinction headroom before shared-state retirement. No line-cap or test-budget limits were raised.

The coordinated cutover decisions are:

1. Resolve the recorded owner principal's current authority and session access; refuse revoked, inaccessible, archived/deleted, or foreign sessions. Current Gateway-owner authority applies only to that same owner profile; role-bearing profiles receive current role scopes. Never decode saved requester/operator authority for restart. Sessions without a human profile use ordinary system-event authority, whose missing capabilities are an accepted limitation.
2. Mark root sessions only. Running children lead to their top-level requester; shutdown terminates them quietly without completion announcements. The parent's resume input covers inspecting/replacing child work.
3. Retire the Control-UI-only `sessions.recover` method, schema, validators, and manual recovery UI.
4. Preserve reversible suspend/freeze semantics. Drain preparation waits for persistence, not agent idleness; only committed stop/restart snapshots and aborts work.
5. Keep the required persistence bounds. Apply short cleanup cutoffs only when existing `exitAfterClose:true` is set; embedded close joins owned cleanup. Log leftover sidecars/plugin resources and exit rather than reuse an unsafe runtime. Bounded leftovers alone set exit code 0 and return naturally; leaked handles may require the existing native watchdog. Never reuse a retained runtime in-process.
6. Exclude cron occurrences and ACP/external-harness sessions; their existing owners retain scheduling/catch-up and harness lifecycle.
7. Remove remote provisioning turn/claim reconstruction. Preserve lease/resource release, staged results, file/move journals, and orphan integrity cleanup. Cancel in-flight provisioning and let the resumed turn request it again.
8. Keep outbound delivery of already-produced bytes/media and the passive update-outcome notice. Delete queue/sentinel paths launching model turns. Legacy inference rows stay inert.
9. Admit exactly one new standard resume input per marker. Later provider requests may contain that input in history.
10. Leave legacy interrupted/ownerless rows inert, out of active counts/notices/history pins, without deleting their text. Normal retention applies.
11. Capture exact queued input IDs in the shutdown marker. After the resume admission, process only those IDs FIFO using each recorded sender's current authority. An unresolvable sender receives one ordinary failed-send state. Crash-left rows are not swept into later resume work.

Live agent-tool caller context is preserved through resumed gateway tools and forced preflight compaction. Ordinary dispatch-error persistence, explicit completion reply obligations, quiet child completion, automation yield, and live FIFO reservation release from related fixes are retained. Restart reconstruction versions of those paths are deleted.

## Evidence and current CI

**Ready for coordinator admin merge** at tested head `921837281c640928bda5f15cfb9af233fd88cdba`, integrated main `e85b3c8ddf64f463bf12b5abed67e55253f6a739`. The coordinator owns landing; no merge attempt, new CI wait, or all-green CI claim.


All requested 55 gateway/agent files reached assertions (775 passed / 2 RPC-timeout failures). Both timeout files pass final-head proof; the earlier failures remain investigated intermittent observations, not proven fixed/inherited. Exact current-main comparison reproduces only the 9 listed UI failures. No assertion loosening or timeout/retry/budget increase.

Acceptance is one isolated real Gateway with a mock provider and parallel sessions: running stream/tool/root-child/background work; idle exclusion; current authority and active caller context; gateway-backed tool and forced preflight compaction; ordinary steering; exact shutdown-captured FIFO and crash-left exclusion; final replies/history; graceful managed/SIGTERM shutdown and documented SIGKILL loss. All final assertions reached. Explicit PR e2e routing is retained.

Original installed base proof was semantically red: resume count 0/no final reply; SIGTERM20,542/20,543ms against unchanged10,000ms. Steering/FIFO passed on base and are not claimed red. Earlier slow Darwin shutdown and RPC observations remain unresolved; passing replays do not diagnose them.

Core, gateway-server, UI and UI-e2e-chat targeted types, matching type-aware lint, format, line-cap ratchet and diff checks pass. Gateway-other/UI-components proof is reused with unchanged inputs. Fresh isolated Codex P1 repair and conflict reviews are scoped-clean; author pr-simplify completed. 65 of 67 rebased patches are identical; remaining differences are retained main import context and combined UI readiness fences. Dependencies unchanged.

Original run 40486652848's 70 failed jobs were classified/repaired in prior batches (retired symbols, static cycle, lint, fixtures, ordinary FIFO/delivery/cleanup/current authority). Baseline changes only shrink retired entries. This new repair deletes no test. Main matching signatures for UI inheritance are independently reproduced with the native runner on the exact integrated main, rather than inferred from job names.

Commands use repository wrappers, nice -n5 / maxWorkers=8 and separate module caches. Full per-invocation results and exact commands are in the coordinator report. No live Gateway, production state, real channels/providers, deployment, release or version/config/dependency change.

## Change size

`1452 files changed, 19667 insertions(+), 124765 deletions(-)`; net **-105,098 LOC**.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse archive carriers during maintenance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automatic session maintenance started a fresh archive worker for each transcript-materialization batch, even though the following publication step already used the reusable archive carrier.

## User Impact

Maintenance does less worker startup work. Archived content, pruning decisions, FIFO ordering, idle expiry, native custody, and crash cleanup remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run maintenance materialization through the existing scoped archive owner. It closes native handles and removes staging files before handing execution to another operation. Reclamation continues to retain its database lease; snapshot embedding continues to wait for its dedicated worker's native exit. Maintenance sizing remains a separate one-shot path. Cold preparation/restoration and archive reads already use `ArchiveSession` with five-minute idle expiry and per-request handle closure. Reclamation already retains one carrier per physical database (30-minute Gateway idle expiry). Startup validation already uses a bounded two-carrier pool; runtime validation uses reclamation. The residual fixed here is the unscoped materialization call in maintenance finalization. Failed or uncertain native cleanup still retires and joins the carrier before custody is released.

## Evidence

- The existing automatic-maintenance regression fails on main after its archive-byte and deletion checks: materialization plus publication starts two carriers. The candidate removes the one-shot materialization start.
- Focused maintenance, archive-session custody, and maintenance-close tests: 66 passed. The revised maintenance file also passed all 33 tests, including a real directory-alias regression.
- Strict script/root-test typechecks and sessions-test typecheck passed; focused lint/format and test-line ratchet passed. Final test-line count is 6,311,634 versus the unchanged 6,311,700 ceiling (66 lines slack). CI exposed benchmark inference annotations and a computed-launch recognizer mismatch; both are repaired, independently reviewed, and covered by the focused 28-test dead-code-checker file. Exact-head CI is tracked in [run 40779078129](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40779078129).
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): provider preflight refused a configuration mismatch. The review found an alias-path regression; the fix consumes the prepared plan’s native path, and independent re-review has no remaining findings.
- Synthetic 10,000-session owner comparison, identical prebuilt archive worker, counterbalanced host-source baseline/candidate: all archive-byte, deletion, and restore assertions passed in every counted run. No live production access or load.
- Whole-Gateway load not run under the task's fast-path exception for reuse of an existing carrier without pool, scheduling, protocol, TTL, or connection-lifetime changes. No whole-Gateway CPU, latency, or memory claim.

Production LOC command (excluding tests/docs): +102 lines, comprising +8 runtime and +94 benchmark/checker tooling. Runtime growth supplies the existing owner’s captured database scope, including the native locator for aliases. No new cache, pool, protocol, or timer. Two adjacent checker destructuring expressions were rewritten equivalently to satisfy its existing lint rules.

## Measurement

Measured source revisions: base `76f483876f86`, candidate `c0b06c5fa71428c67a8a69e5b376810a827cce1a`. The subsequent rebase and benchmark-only CI repairs leave the runtime change identical. Five counterbalanced timing pairs, six finalizations/sample (30 operations/arm; 25 steady operations/arm). Allocation uses two separate counterbalanced pairs, six operations/sample (12/arm). All operations use one synthetic 10,000-session store. Seed/verification are outside timing; the first operation's source-host cold setup is reported separately rather than included in steady results.

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Archive-worker starts / six operations | 14 | 8 | −6 |
| Steady starts / operation | 2 | 1 | −50% |
| Process CPU / steady operation | 1,113.1 ms | 707.6 ms | −36.4% |
| Main-thread CPU / steady operation | 17.23 ms | 14.79 ms | −14.2% |
| Wall time / steady operation | 929.9 ms | 603.2 ms | −35.1% |
| Archive-worker V8 allocation / operation | 537.15 MiB | 363.34 MiB | −32.4% |
| Sampled main-thread allocation / operation | 7.63 MiB | 7.45 MiB | −2.4% |
| Instrumented archive-worker GC / operation | 30.13 ms | 21.33 ms | −8.80 ms |
| Process RSS after timed window | 1,622.99 MiB | 1,635.88 MiB | +12.89 MiB (+0.8%) |
| Process peak RSS | 1,637.84 MiB | 1,647.73 MiB | +9.89 MiB (+0.6%) |
| Main heap after timed window (not post-GC) | 143.34 MiB | 144.40 MiB | +1.06 MiB |
| Mean run event-loop p99 | 14.77 ms | 15.80 ms | +1.03 ms (+7.0%) |
| Cold first-operation process CPU | 16,638.8 ms | 16,888.9 ms | +250.1 ms (+1.5%) |

The loop-tail differences have mixed signs, and none are treated as a whole-Gateway verdict. Host-load and timing evidence per pair:

| Pair/order | CPU ms/op base → candidate | Loop p99 ms base → candidate (samples) | Host load1 base → candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 (AB) | 1529.0 → 851.0 | 20.07 → 24.30 (2972/2866) | 31.05 → 32.18 |
| 2 (BA) | 1015.7 → 622.5 | 12.99 → 12.98 (1859/1782) | 21.26 → 23.83 |
| 3 (AB) | 992.5 → 597.6 | 12.94 → 12.57 (1932/1723) | 21.49 → 17.46 |
| 4 (BA) | 930.0 → 720.0 | 14.00 → 15.73 (2086/2017) | 18.22 → 22.82 |
| 5 (AB) | 1098.5 → 746.9 | 13.85 → 13.43 (1968/2073) | 16.31 → 16.28 |

Allocation pair worker totals were 538.12 → 362.93 and 536.17 → 363.75 MiB/op; host load1 was 18.81 → 27.21 and 18.39 → 20.56. Worker GC totals cover 553 baseline and 340 candidate collections across the two profiling samples. GC is instrumented context, not an untraced acceptance gate; per-kind tails/maxima were not collected. Native allocation and loader/preload prelude are excluded from the worker V8 counter. Main allocation is Inspector sampling at 4 KiB, reported separately rather than added to exact worker totals.

Across 12 baseline materialization workers, first reply averaged 291.3 ms wall, 283.9 ms worker CPU, and 173.0 MiB V8 allocation. This includes module evaluation and the first archive operation, not pure isolate boot alone.

At a simulated cadence of one operation/minute (within the existing five-minute idle expiry), the measured work counts project **122 → 62 starts/hour**, including the two initial retained carriers. This is a count extrapolation, not a one-hour run or a forecast of production traffic. The remaining per-operation start is the unchanged `maintenance-size` path. Separately, snapshot embedding still retains its dedicated native-exit requirement. No idle policy is extended.

Reproduce with the existing harness and an owned, already-built worker generation:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/archive-worker-churn-measure.ts \
  --operation maintenance --stores 1 --sessions 10000 --iterations 6 \
  --entry <built-archive-worker.js> --output <fresh-task-directory>
```

Baseline adds `--owner-dir <overlay-containing-base-maintenance.ts>`; allocation passes add `--allocations`. Both arms use the same built worker. Five AB/BA/AB/BA/AB timing pairs and two AB/BA allocation pairs were counted without trimming. Earlier setup attempts with a wrong fixture archive directory failed correctness assertions and were fixed before this series. A previous completed timing pair was excluded in advance when rebasing, and replaced by this pinned series.

Scope gap: no ten-minute whole-Gateway load, sessions.list/server-handler latency, main-thread GC rate, or live production validation. The task's fast-path exception applies to this call-site reuse of an unchanged existing carrier; these owner results do not claim a whole-Gateway improvement.

Current PR head: `f0d25f468d54eeaab5b051dcf1cf5d2b8218b2b3`.

prs.title: perf(plugins): omit delivery snapshots from Reef peer reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reef peer lookups resend the entire retained outbound-delivery namespace to the SQLite worker, even though those operations only read peer state. Periodic friend reconciliation repeats this for every active peer.

## User Impact

Less worker traffic and main-thread CPU during Reef peer reconciliation when delivery history is retained. Trust checks, delivery recovery, TTLs, stored data, and the Plugin SDK contract are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared operation declared both stores, so the SDK included both namespace snapshots. Peer-only snapshot/list/observe reads now retain a peer-only operation; rejection and overdue-delivery scans retain the two-store operation and their existing receipt invalidation.

Runtime production delta: **+6 lines** (8 added, 2 removed). The extra handle preserves operation reuse while keeping the two required scopes separate. The committed measurement harness adds 266 lines; the wire-budget regression adds 35. No general-purpose cache, hash, write suppression, or schema change.

## Evidence

Acceptance set before measurement: identical results and complete stored rows/metadata, fewer serialized request bytes, and lower main-thread CPU or sampled allocation. Five serial counterbalanced pairs per instrumentation mode; 2,000 operations per arm, allocation sampled separately from timing.

Synthetic workload: eight peers, 1,600 retained outbound deliveries, and 43 inert namespace scopes. Each modeled 30-second cycle reads eight peers and scans rejections/overdue deliveries. Rates are synthetic, not production attribution. Workboard, team-reports, and knowledge use dedicated stores; their inert fixture names are not claimed as plugin-state traffic. All measured persisted rows remain unchanged.

| Owner metric (median of five runs) | Base | Candidate | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Main-thread CPU / 2000 operations (ms) | 4,121.72 | 2,374.57 | -42.4% |
| Wall time / 2000 operations (ms) | 8,722.36 | 5,013.27 | -42.5% |
| Sampled allocation / 2000 operations (MB) | 385.16 | 360.55 | -6.4% |
| Serialized request MB / simulated minute | 13.80688 | 2.821968 | −79.6% |

Per-namespace standalone serialized snapshot sizes (not additive shares of the V8 wire encoding):

| Namespace | Base MB/min (sends) | Candidate MB/min (sends) |
|---|---:|---:|
| `["reef","peer-state"]` | 0.060940 (20) | 0.060940 (20) |
| `["reef","outbound-deliveries"]` | 13.822920 (20) | 2.764584 (4) |

All five paired CPU and allocation deltas improve. Mean paired CPU delta: −1,712 ms (−39.3%); mean paired allocation delta: −25.89 MB (−6.7%). Timing CPU ranges: base 3,824–4,846 ms; candidate 2,109–3,214 ms. Wall time is noisier (one pair slower); use CPU and exact byte counts for the owner claim. The one-minute host load ranged 30.6–49.5. Timing-arm end RSS medians: 733 → 670 MB; heap-used medians: 86 → 90 MB (end-of-run samples, not retained/post-GC claims).

Measured baseline: `70bf5121704c7a7173722c2bd7e360362e5da165` plus this candidate patch. Final rebase onto `a53e9583dfbf` changed none of the affected Reef or plugin-state owners. Test-lines ratchet after rebase: 6,311,515 / 6,311,700, with 185 lines of slack; ceiling untouched by this PR.

Commands:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/reef-state-request-bytes.ts --iterations 2000 --owner .local/trust-store-base.ts
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/reef-state-request-bytes.ts --iterations 2000
# Repeat with --allocations; save the baseline trust-store.ts before editing.
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/reef/src/trust-store.test.ts extensions/reef/src/friends.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The regression fails on main with a 32,776-byte peer request against a 16,384-byte budget (128 retained deliveries). Candidate: 56 focused tests passed, including the byte budget, authority revocation, delivery recovery, and friend reconciliation. Combined wall time 92.78 s including worker-artifact preparation; new regression 0.97 s. Export-name collision guard and 38 import-closure checks passed. Changed-file format/lint, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` passed.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. Autoreview refused its provider/config mismatch before inference; configuration was not changed.

This follows the narrow duplicate-work fast path: an owner benchmark and real SQLite transport proof, not a whole-Gateway stress measurement. No whole-Gateway CPU, GC, event-loop, or sessions.list latency claim is made. Live plugin/namespace attribution remains unverified.
