prs.title: fix(sessions): context token count stays stale for the whole of a long agent turn
prs.body:
Related: #164550

## What Problem This Solves

The session's context count (`totalTokens`) can stay at its pre-turn value throughout a long embedded agent turn. This publishes the latest settled model call's prompt context while the turn is running. Turn completion still writes the final accounting result.

The writer serializes and coalesces writes, fences them to the admitted session/run, closes before final accounting, and drains before settlement returns. Detached and incognito attempts, and follow-ups that preserve user-facing session state, do not use it. This covers the embedded runner; mid-turn reporting for the separate Codex app-server and CLI backends is not established.

## Current revision

Head: [`170809258591d0b12f65f2054404e906e87ac2b3`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/170809258591d0b12f65f2054404e906e87ac2b3)
Tree: `f3f4f7519c047e58dbe45da651e001dfc68ba769`

This merges previous head `633860da372bfa96638235cde41244f853357115` with pinned main `4a2a1962d9caaf965c0432c7c9a84e5a40290f7d`, preserving both parents. The session-store conflict resolution keeps main's removal of the retired recovery API and the PR's final-context override after snapshot projection. It also retains upstream's fork-boundary and cron writer contract changes. No duplicate repair for the upstream PostgreSQL setup fixture was added.

The exact 20-path delta received an independent source review with no actionable finding. This does not settle the Goal-budget policy decision below.

## Evidence

A bounded Linux x64 runner validated the complete tree above with Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`, Vitest 5.0.5 and frozen dependencies. Lockfile SHA-256: `01c02f06984feaa8090c17b45e80e83e1f0842f38eed2f9ab37b113f0a4627fc`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Database-worker registry | 12 cases passed |
| Selected agent context, subscription, settlement, finalization and session-store groups | 81 cases passed |
| Cron final-context fixture | 2 cases passed |
| Test types: agents-root, agents-other, commands, services-cron | All four passed |
| Canonical scoped source/registry lint, format, whitespace | Passed |
| Remove only `onModelCallSettled: contextTotalTokensWriter.offer` from subscription preparation | Exactly the intended one-case failure: “publishes a tool-use call's context total from the real subscription”, at the expected 12,000-token assertion; no unhandled errors |
| Restore the callback and rerun that regression | 1/1 passed; exact candidate tree restored |

The positive total is **95 distinct cases**. The restored confirmation repeats one of those cases; it is not counted again. The first supervised agent attempt stopped on a stale disk-monitor sample without a runtime verdict. Its failure is retained; the successful continuation above used the same exact source tree. All owned validation processes exited.

Reproduction, using the repository's pinned runtime and frozen dependencies:

```sh
export OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK=1 OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK_MODE=throttled
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/database-worker-registry.test.ts --run --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-context-total-tokens.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-prepare.context-total.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-settle.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-finalize.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.model-state.test.ts \
  src/agents/command/session-store.context-total.test.ts \
  src/agents/command/session-store.test.ts \
  src/agents/command/session-store.snooze.test.ts --run --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts \
  src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.context-total.test.ts --run --maxWorkers=1
for leaf in agents-root agents-other commands services-cron; do
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p "test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.$leaf.json" --incremental
done
```

Run the repository's `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` for the 19 scoped source/test paths and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json` for `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`; run `CI=1 node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on all 20 paths and `git diff --check 4a2a1962d9caaf965c0432c7c9a84e5a40290f7d...HEAD`.

Final validation receipt SHA-256: `14d3b6419fc9636f9acb2efa67a81cdb3560ccdbfaa2cd268ae784b425c35fd2`.
Negative-control log: `66b6a86559e40a4774eed44db5ceece677c8593b1074683fcb3e729732e30ac6`.
Restored-control log: `4cbda836d36c9611ecbf87b9bd214198f85e826b56c64a037e8d88b0e61393ba`.

## Hosted CI and prior failure

[Fresh CI 40792556489](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792556489) is **not green**. At 00:29 UTC on October 29, 54 jobs had passed, 27 were skipped, two had failed, and all three PostgreSQL shards were still running. The aggregate gate is pending. [Security and dependency review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792548544) and the corrected [description check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40793505041) passed. No gate has been waived or rerun requested.

CI checks merge `d4f5d6eace1d7c5cbc55bf5a004a082bc2abde88` against main `3163d58b31e3d99a1ad11ae9289e252d22a126fe`. The complete comparison with the published head contains 144 upstream-changed paths, with no overlap with this PR's 20 paths. This newer merge is distinct from the pinned tree tested above.

- [Mock-export ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792556489/job/123181649499): 14 findings in `server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `server.spawn-broker.test.ts`. The [exact main base](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792463841/job/123181561334) executes the scanner and reports the same 14 findings. Both files are byte-identical between base and merge. This is an inherited failure; no baseline exemption or duplicate repair was added.
- [Subagent registry test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792556489/job/123181650718): “does not restore a superseded lifecycle after a successor is released” fails at `subagent-registry.native-termination.test-support.ts:59`, expecting a positive `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount()` but receiving 0. That fixture is unchanged between base and merge. Upstream [#187090](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187090) removed independent root-work admission around termination cleanup while retaining the caller's join; the old assertion still expects that admission. This explains a source-level contract mismatch. The exact base skipped runtime lanes, and the upstream PR's failed logs did not execute this case, so an exact-base runtime control and a verified fixture repair remain outstanding. No production rollback or test weakening was applied.

The API reports this revision mergeable; broad CI and the Goal-budget maintainer decision still gate it.

The previous head's [CI 40139208391](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139208391) failed seven interactive-setup cases because the fixture omitted `runtime/standalone-runtime-profile.mjs`. Its 60 scoped context-accounting cases passed. [Main CI 40138789542](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138789542/job/121006161355) had the same seven startup failures. The exact old tested base skipped that lane, so it was not an executed exact-base control.

Upstream [#182990](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182990) repaired the fixture and [its PostgreSQL shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40140365971/job/121010977081) passed all eight setup cases. [#183037](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183037) then derived copied root modules from the package manifest. Both are in this integration base. The pinned base's [CI 40786288337](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40786288337) skipped PostgreSQL and the other broad lanes; its successful aggregate is not an executed PostgreSQL control. Fresh PR CI remains the current hosted check.

## Goal budget decision and proof limits

Goal accounting retains the existing peak-usage policy. The store-backed regression starts a Goal with a 50,000-token budget and publishes 40,000, 60,000, then 30,000 tokens. Current context finishes at 30,000; Goal usage remains 60,000 and `budget_limited`. The lower snapshot goes through the real writer and store; the test does not execute the compactor.

Publishing intermediate observations can expose a peak that turn-end accounting alone would not have seen. Whether those intermediate peaks should count toward Goal budgets remains a maintainer decision. My recommendation is to preserve the existing peak reducer. Explicit resume starts a fresh budget window at the current context and resets `tokensUsed` to 0. Automatically crediting the Goal after compaction would change budget semantics; this PR does not do that.

The earlier real-provider `agent --local` measurements and [successful October 20 CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630) remain historical, tied to `a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33` and its recorded merge checkout. This validation adds no shipped Gateway, channel, compactor or live-provider execution of the current head.

prs.title: fix(msteams): allowlisted Teams senders and channels are ignored after an unrelated config reload
prs.body:
Closes #186333

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Microsoft Teams stops applying the allowlists it resolved at startup after any config reload that does not restart the Teams channel (for example `agents.defaults.userTimezone`), until the channel restarts.

## User Impact

User impact: senders listed as `user:<aad-object-id>` or `msteams:user:<aad-object-id>`, and `teams` entries that startup resolved from names to IDs, keep working after unrelated config reloads. Editing `channels.msteams` behaves as before: with the default hot reload it applies right away and restarts the Teams channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

At startup the monitor projects `allowFrom`, `groupAllowFrom` and `teams` to stable IDs (provider prefixes stripped, names resolved through Graph, unresolvable lists matching nothing since #184989) and hands that projection to the handler. The handler config reader (`monitor-handler/config.ts`, from #112811) follows the runtime config so allowlist edits apply before a restart, but after any reload it returned the raw configuration for these fields.

The reader now reuses the startup projection while the account's allowlist inputs (`allowFrom`, `groupAllowFrom`, `teams`, `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching`) are unchanged. When one of them changes it returns the live configuration exactly as before; with config hot reload in its default `hybrid` mode that edit also restarts the Teams channel (its reload prefix is `channels.msteams`), which resolves the lists again. Accepted edge, not coded around: between an allowlist edit and that restart, the edited values apply as written, as on main today.

This is the reload path #184989 described under "Boundary decisions requested" (2): a name-keyed team beside `"*"` no longer falls through to `"*"` after a reload. With `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching`, behavior after a reload now matches startup: names that resolved stay IDs, and display names are not matched again while the four allowlist inputs stay unchanged.

Production change: one file, +30/-2; tests +176. The access-control bullet on startup name resolution now matches the code (user names resolve only with `dangerouslyAllowNameMatching`; names that do not resolve are not used for routing) and says when the mapping is refreshed.

## Evidence

- **RED / GREEN at the owning boundary** (`monitor.lifecycle.test.ts`, real monitor startup with Graph resolution mocked): on base `9a0458cf695` the new cases fail at the intended assertions (after the reload the handler gets `user:40a1…`, `msteams:user:50a1…`, the `Product` / `Roadmap` name keys and `"Alice"` instead of the startup IDs): 4 failed / 34 passed. With the fix: 38 passed. The cases cover the default account, a named account and a named account inheriting root lists, and check that an edit to `allowFrom`, `groupAllowFrom`, `teams` or the name-matching flag applies before the restart; a mutant that drops any one input from the comparison, compares the raw account entry instead of the merged one, or skips the removed-section guard fails them.
- **Real Gateway, main twice vs this branch twice** (`pnpm openclaw qa msteams`: bundled Teams plugin, loopback Bot Framework connector, mock model). Each scenario sets the allowlist, gets a reply, applies an `agents.defaults.userTimezone` patch, then sends again:

| After the `agents.defaults.userTimezone` hot reload | main `9a0458cf695`, runs 1 / 2 | this branch, runs 1 / 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DM sender listed as `user:<aad-object-id>` | no reply / no reply | `QA-MSTEAMS-RELOAD-AFTER-OK` / same |
| Group-chat sender listed as `msteams:user:<aad-object-id>` (`groupPolicy: "allowlist"`) | no reply / no reply | `QA-MSTEAMS-GROUP-RELOAD-AFTER-OK` / same |

On main every run answers the probe before the reload and times out after it (`timed out after 60000ms`). The main Gateway log shows the allowlist patch restarting the Teams channel (`restarting msteams channel`, `starting account (reason: config-reload)`) and the timezone patch applied as `config hot reload applied (agents.defaults.userTimezone)` without a Teams restart. The two scenario files are local QA flows, not part of this PR.

- **Rejections after the reload, and an allowlist edit while a message is pending** (same harness, main twice vs this branch twice; "no dispatch" counts `message dispatch completed` per conversation in each run's Gateway log, "no reply" is a 25 s window with no outbound activity):

| Scenario | main `9a0458cf695`, runs 1 / 2 | this branch, runs 1 / 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DM sender not in `allowFrom` (it lists `user:<other-aad-object-id>`); group-chat sender listed as `msteams:user:<aad-object-id>` | unlisted DM: no reply and no dispatch before and after the reload; listed group sender: answered before, no reply after / same | unlisted DM: no reply and no dispatch before and after; listed group sender: answered before and after / same |
| Group-chat sender not in `groupAllowFrom` (it lists `msteams:user:<other-aad-object-id>`); DM sender listed as `user:<aad-object-id>` | unlisted group sender: no reply and no dispatch before and after; listed DM sender: answered before, no reply after / same | unlisted group sender: no reply and no dispatch before and after; listed DM sender: answered before and after / same |
| A listed DM sender's second DM waits in a 15 s inbound debounce; an `allowFrom` edit that keeps the sender lands before it flushes | pending DM answered after the Teams channel restart / same | same / same |
| Same, but the edit removes the sender | pending DM: no reply for 45 s, no model request; a listed group sender is still answered / same | same / same |

The two pending-DM rows are identical on main and this branch: an allowlist edit uses the live configuration exactly as before, and the kept-sender row shows the restart does not drop the pending message, so the removed-sender row is the edit taking effect.

- **Removal during message preparation** (`message-handler.authz.test.ts`, two new cases): the handler is wired like the monitor (raw configuration plus the account-scoped startup projection), an unrelated reload comes first so admission uses the retained startup allowlists, the Graph thread fetch is held, and the team or the channel is removed from `teams` before it resolves. The message is dropped (`dropping message (dispatch-time account authorization changed)`) and nothing is dispatched. The file passes 36/36; a mutant that keeps the startup allowlists after an edit fails exactly these two cases.

- **Upgrade from 2026.10.8, the latest stable release (dist-swap proxy).** 2026.10.8 predates this regression: its handler keeps the allowlists projected at startup for the life of the channel (the reader from #112811 first shipped in 2026.10.10-beta.1). The published `openclaw` package does not bundle Teams (its `files` list excludes `dist/extensions/msteams/**`); Teams runs from the installed `@openclaw/msteams` npm plugin, so a 2026.10.8 install gets this fix through the plugin update that ships with the release. Each run (twice, Linux x86_64): install `openclaw@2026.10.8` and `@openclaw/msteams@2026.10.8`, store Teams settings (`dmPolicy` / `groupPolicy: "allowlist"`, `allowFrom: ["user:<aad-object-id>"]`, `groupAllowFrom: ["msteams:user:<aad-object-id>"]`, `teams` with a `19:...@thread.tacv2` team and channel, a name key and `"*"`), validate, start the Gateway, stop it. Then replace the installed plugin package's files with this branch's `@openclaw/msteams` packed by the release tooling (`scripts/lib/plugin-npm-build-and-pack.mts`), keeping its install record, installed dependencies, configuration and state; start this branch's core from its `npm pack` file list (version set to 2026.10.10 locally so it accepts the 2026.10.8 state) on the same state; set `agents.defaults.userTimezone`.

Both runs, copied from the run output (sha256 prefixes; `<id>` redacted):

```text
openclaw.json sha256 after 2026.10.8 / after the plugin swap / after this branch's Gateway start: b1b6a08782092b8e x3 (run 1), 9c0c482331b37ee1 x3 (run 2)
plugins list, this branch's core: msteams origin=global trust=trusted-official status=loaded rootDir=<state>/npm/projects/openclaw-msteams-<id>/node_modules/@openclaw/msteams
Gateway module loads (Node module.registerHooks load hook): 19 msteams files, all from the Gateway's copy of the installed package, 19/19 byte-identical to the packed branch plugin
[msteams] starting provider account default (Gateway route /api/messages)
[reload] config hot reload applied (agents.defaults.userTimezone)
msteams channel: running, connected, lastError null; lastStartAt unchanged across the reload
config keys changed since 2026.10.8: agents.defaults.userTimezone, meta.lastTouchedVersion; channels.msteams identical
```

This is a proxy for the plugin update a release ships, not a published release. The upgraded Gateway receives no Teams traffic (the loopback Bot Framework connector exists only inside `pnpm openclaw qa msteams`), so the allow / deny behavior after the reload is the scenarios above.

- **Suites:** `pnpm test extensions/msteams` (16 + 91 files, 156 + 929 tests), `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files pass. The lifecycle file's test time is under 1 s (23.7 s wall, almost all transform; unchanged by this PR). Unit runs: macOS arm64, Node 24.22.1; Gateway legs: Linux x86_64. Test-lines ceiling: main at `b0961419e46` is already 343 lines over its ceiling (6291661 vs 6291318); this PR adds 176 test lines and raises the ceiling to the tree total, 6291837 (the branch merges current main for that line).
- **Not tested end to end:** Graph-resolved team and user names (the QA connector has no Graph); the lifecycle cases cover them with a mocked resolution. Which Teams monitor drops a message pending across an allowlist edit (the stopping one or the restarted one) is not visible in the Gateway log; the handler cases above cover the dispatch-time check.

prs.title: fix: restore gateways left stopped by interrupted updates during repair
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update repair` can wait 45 minutes after both managed-update owners have died, then finish successfully while leaving the Gateway that the interrupted update stopped offline.

Refs #164800 (repair backstop, items 3 and 4).

## User Impact

Repair can reclaim a handoff immediately when every recorded owner is positively dead. After successful finalization, it starts and verifies the managed Gateway only when the recovered update recorded stopping it without a later successful start. Operator-stopped Gateways stay stopped; named data risks, lost ownership, and live or unverified descendants still prevent unsafe recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The grace check in `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-cleanup.ts:93` used elapsed time even after reclamation had established owner death. It now distinguishes positively dead owners from unknown custody while retaining the descendant census and transactional ownership checks. The separate reboot flag retains its existing census meaning.

Standalone finalization previously always returned `restart: false` (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize.ts:526` on the base). Repair now consumes the existing `service-stop` step and restart/verification facts, finalizes first, then restores through the existing installation executor, native service lock/start, and readiness machinery. It records health in both the recovered run and repair run and reports the result in human and JSON output. Failures direct operators to `openclaw gateway status --deep`.

No new stop-time fact or schema is needed. Repair records completed `service-start` or `service-running` steps in the active repair run before awaiting readiness. These retained facts survive thrown errors and later stopped health snapshots; ordinary step writes cannot mutate terminal original runs. Later repair retries readiness on a running service and leaves a subsequently stopped Gateway stopped. A blanket restart of every stopped service was rejected because it would override operator intent. Treating positively dead parents as the reboot flag was rejected because that would weaken descendant inspection. Keeping the grace for proven-dead owners would preserve the original outage.

## Evidence

- Red proof against the unchanged base: all four selected regressions failed as expected (three grace refusals and finalization without Gateway start/verification).
- Green proof: 156 tests passed across handoff recovery, repair service, repair handoff, repair command, repair history, finalization refusal, and finalization lifecycle suites. Commands use `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with `--maxWorkers=1`.
- The first six-file run passed 128/129; its one failure was an existing test that expected fresh, proven-dead custody to remain blocked by grace. The fixture now uses an unverified descendant, and its targeted rerun passes. The separately selected lifecycle suite passed 20/20.
- Additional review regressions reproduced lost readiness settlement and a repeated native start after a thrown readiness wait; both were red before their fixes. The final service suite covers all 15 service/retry cases.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` passed for `tsconfig.core.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.cli-update.json`. Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, docs MDX sanity, and `git diff --check` passed.

The CLI regressions invoke registered repair, real finalization, and the SQLite ledger, with synthetic host service/readiness responses and the existing Doctor/plugin fixture. The live Linux/systemd SIGKILL reproduction has not been rerun here; combined-lane validation remains necessary.

Final isolated Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**. Accepted review findings about readiness retries, thrown probes, and overwritten liveness evidence were fixed and covered by repair-boundary tests. Startup evidence is retained in the active repair run rather than attempting to append ordinary steps to a terminal original run.

Diff against the base: production **+283/-7** (net +276), tests/harness **+339/-25** (net +314), docs **+38/-11** (net +27). The production growth is the missing restart orchestration; it reuses existing ownership, service, readiness, and ledger owners rather than adding a persistence mechanism. The simplification pass kept one history-based restoration decision, reused the existing fences, and replaced the obsolete grace expectations.

prs.title: fix(matrix): gallery messages reach the agent without their images
prs.body:
Closes #162499

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when you pick several photos at once in Element X, the agent only gets the caption. With no caption it gets nothing at all.

## User Impact

User impact: everything in a Matrix gallery (photos, video, audio, files) now reaches the agent in the order it was sent. Same trigger and mention rules as any other message. Single media works like before, and there are no config changes.

A few limits:

- Only the first 20 items get downloaded, same as the image tool's default.
- Anything past 20, anything that fails to download, and entries with a bad type or URL get rolled into one marker: `[matrix gallery: K of N attachments unavailable]`. If they were all over the size limit it says `too large` instead.
- A gallery with no caption shows up as `[matrix gallery: N attachments]`.
- `mediaMaxMb` is per item, so one gallery can pull down up to 20x that.
- Not covered here: gallery edits, quoting a gallery in a reply or thread root, and sending galleries.

## Why This Change Was Made

Element X sends a multi-photo pick as one message (MSC4274, msgtype `dm.filament.gallery`) with the attachments in a list inside the event. The Matrix plugin only looked for a single top-level attachment, so it found nothing.

Now it reads that list (the stable `m.gallery` too) and downloads each item through the existing `downloadMatrixMedia`, so size limits and decryption work the same as for single media. One bad item doesn't take the others down with it. The cap is there because the event size limit doesn't really bound how many entries a gallery can have.

Audio inside a gallery skips the Matrix audio preflight. In a room with history on, an unmentioned gallery goes into history as text only and nothing gets downloaded.

## Evidence

- 10 new tests in `handler.gallery.test.ts`: order with and without a caption, partial and total failures, too large and encrypted items through the real downloader, skipped entries, the cap (22 entries give 20 downloads and `2 of 22`), room history, and the single-image path.
- With the source changes reverted, 9 of 10 fail. The single-image one still passes, which is the point of it.
- Green: `pnpm test:extension matrix`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm docs:check-links`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes except the dead-export scan, which flags 2 files this PR doesn't touch (`extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-catalog.ts`, `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-archive-types.ts`).

I also ran it live on 2026.10.8 with a local vision model and sent galleries from Element X on iOS:

| Sent | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 photos with a caption | caption only | all 3, described in order |
| 4 photos, no caption | no reply | all 4, described in order |
| 3 photos, no caption | no reply | all 3, described in order |
| single photo | worked | still works |

<details>
<summary>Gateway logs and session trace (redacted)</summary>

Same Matrix room, 2026-10-27, times UTC. Room and thread ids replaced with `<thread>`, file name suffixes trimmed.

**Before (2026.10.7), 3-photo gallery with a caption.** No images staged for the turn. The agent went looking for one with `exec` and opened an older photo with `view_image` (the one resized image below is that old file):

```
16:52:03Z session.started  <thread>
16:52:12Z tool.call        <thread> exec
16:52:16Z tool.call        <thread> view_image
16:52:17Z log              Image resized to fit limits: 2048x1536px 928.4KB -> 303.6KB (-67.3%)
16:52:37Z session.ended    <thread> success
```

**After (this change on 2026.10.8), 3 photos with a caption, same thread.** 3 staged, 3 sent to the model, no tool calls:

```
20:52:58Z staged           media/inbound/IMG_9313….jpg, IMG_9314….jpg, IMG_9315….jpg
20:53:04Z session.started  <thread>
20:53:04Z log              Image resized to fit limits: 2048x1536px 720.3KB -> 255.3KB (-64.6%)
20:53:04Z log              Image resized to fit limits: 2048x1536px 532.1KB -> 189.4KB (-64.4%)
20:53:04Z log              Image resized to fit limits: 2048x1536px 832.0KB -> 295.3KB (-64.5%)
20:53:34Z session.ended    <thread> success
```

**After, 4 screenshots with no caption** (new thread). Before this change it was dropped:

```
21:12:36Z staged           media/inbound/IMG_9217….png, IMG_9218….png, IMG_9220….png, IMG_9221….png
21:12:40Z session.started  <thread>
21:12:40Z log              Image resized to fit limits: 945x2048px (x4)
21:13:03Z session.ended    <thread> success
```

**After, 3 screenshots with no caption** (same thread):

```
21:13:20Z staged           media/inbound/IMG_9210….png, IMG_9211….png, IMG_9214….png
21:13:22Z session.started  <thread>
21:13:22Z log              Image resized to fit limits: 945x2048px (x3)
21:13:46Z session.ended    <thread> success
```

</details>

To try it yourself:

1. Run a Gateway on this branch with Matrix set up and a vision-capable model.
2. In Element X, pick a few photos, add a caption and send. The agent should describe each one.
3. Do it again without a caption. You should get a reply instead of silence.

prs.title: fix(plugins): scheduled command turns ignore the requester's tool policy
prs.body:
Closes #186281

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: occurrences of requester-scheduled plugin commands resolve tool policy like a live turn with no sender, so the guest `toolsBySender["*"]` entry applies to them (with a subagent deny there, every occurrence fails), and the requester account's current tool policy and the removed-account refusal are skipped.

## User Impact

User impact: scheduled command turns resolve tool policy the way capped automations do. Guest wildcard sender entries no longer apply to them, each occurrence uses the requester account's current group/channel tool policy, and an occurrence whose requester account its channel no longer lists is refused before it runs, naming the account. As for capped automations, sender-specific `toolsBySender` entries, including `"*"`, no longer apply to occurrences, and a later change to the requester's own entry does not reach existing schedules. Plugin schedules now share the capped-automation account check, so open reports of false refusals there (#156895, #186008) would affect them too until that check is fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each occurrence now resolves the job's stored scheduled tool policy once, as capped automations do, and passes it to both admission and native tool preparation (before, preparation never received it). Command schedules record no creator origin, so the schedule's own channel (captured from the live command and checked against the stored job on every occurrence) stands in for it; schedules created from a direct chat on a named account keep working, where a capped automation without a recorded origin would refuse them. The account check runs right after the source check, before the occurrence accepts any input. The background-work docs now say how scheduled command turns resolve tool policy.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway (built `dist`, isolated state, WebChat operator over `chat.send`, local stub provider, a plugin with requester-command scheduled turns, `tools.toolsBySender["*"]` denying `sessions_spawn` / `agents_wait`), schedule created then the occurrence forced with `cron.run`:

  | build | runs | occurrence | command ran | model requests |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `main` `eb78444932f` | 3/3 | `error`: Scheduled command requires current native subagent eligibility. | no | 0 |
  | this fix | 3/3 | `ok` | yes, with native subagents | 0 |

- Existing `test/plugin-command-scheduled-restart.e2e.test.ts` passes on the fix.
- `commands-plugin.scheduled-turns.test.ts` (repo fixture: real plugin loader, cron service, channel ingress): on `main` the wildcard case and the account case fail at their assertions (the child loses `read`; a later deny for the requester's account is not applied), the direct-chat case passes; with the fix all three pass, together with the existing scheduled-turns, scheduled-turns-restart, `plugin-command-scheduled-run` and `operator-authority` tests (114/114 on the final code). The new cases take 2.3-2.5 s each; the whole file runs in 92 s alone (`--maxWorkers=1`, 31 tests), so they add about 8% to an existing fixture-heavy suite. The fixture now loads a minimal Discord channel that lists the configured accounts and resolves conversation tool policy like the Discord plugin; without a loaded channel, any configured-account check refuses every fixture occurrence.
- `tsgo:core`, core test shards, oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, line-cap and max-lines ratchets: clean.
- Test-line ratchet: `main` at `b0961419e46` is already 343 lines over its ceiling (6291661 vs 6291318); the new tests add 125 net test lines, so the last commit raises `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` to the tree total, 6291786.
- Named account, real Gateway (built `dist`, isolated state, fake Telegram Bot API, named account `team`, supergroup requester whose sender is linked to an admin profile with `users.linkChannelIdentity`, local stub provider, the same plugin), occurrences forced with `cron.run`. Phase A: an allowed child reads a sentinel file. Phase B: two children with `tools.swarm.maxConcurrent: 1`, the first held at the provider so the second is queued, then the change. Phase C: the first occurrence after the change. Two runs per build and change:

  | build | change (`config.patch` on account `team`) | runs | A: allowed child | B: queued child | C: first occurrence after the change |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `main` `198b761c325` | account removed | 2/2 | reads the file | runs before the change applies, reads the file | `ok`; its child has `read` and reads the file |
  | this branch | account removed | 2/2 | reads the file | same | `error`: Scheduled account "team" is unavailable. Re-add it to the channel configuration, or recreate this automation from the intended account. No command ran, no child |
  | `main` `198b761c325` | `groups["*"].tools.deny: ["read"]` | 2/2 | reads the file | same | `ok`; its child has `read` and reads the file |
  | this branch | `groups["*"].tools.deny: ["read"]` | 2/2 | reads the file | same | `ok`; its child has no `read` |

  Both changes need a Telegram channel reload, which waits for running work (`deferring until ... complete`), so the queued child runs under the old configuration on both builds; only phase C differs. (This branch was measured at `3aea9294fac`; the later merge with `main` changes none of this PR's files.)

- Registry used by the account check: the occurrence's source check compares the Gateway's current plugin registry with the one it captured on entry, and the account check runs right after it with no `await` in between, so the process-root registry it reads is that captured registry. Instrumented builds of `main` and this branch on the named-account setup above (reload or config change while the occurrence waits for its parent session's turn) recorded the same object for the scheduled runner's scoped registry, the published registry and the process root at every point read: the account check, child tool policy, command runtime and execution admission. A registry published during the wait, including by a plugin that declares `reload.turnHandover` and is replaced mid-turn, makes the occurrence refuse at its next check with `Scheduled plugin command source changed or expired.` before any input, on `main` and on this branch alike; channel configuration changes wait for the running occurrence. On this setup the job carries no cron-level operator source, so its launch does not wait for the parent session; a wait at launch was not exercised.

prs.title: perf(gateway): release obsolete catalog planning rosters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completed session catalog pages kept entire obsolete planning rosters alive after session metadata changed.

## User Impact

Lower retained Gateway memory while catalog pages remain cached. Catalog response content, viewer authorization, and stale-adoption rejection are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retained page's adoption identity was also the weak-cache key for the full planning roster. Reuse the existing detached planning revision for adoption identity instead, so a page can retain its slim adoption facts without retaining the roster. No new cache, invalidation listener, or option. Production diff: +4/-3 lines, net +1 (the ownership comment); executable LOC is unchanged. The reproducible benchmark adds 92 net lines and the regression adds 46; the non-test diff including benchmark tooling is +93 lines.

## Evidence

Acceptance: obsolete catalog arrays and wrappers must collect immediately after a row publication, even with old page instance maps retained and no subsequent catalog request. Preserve unchanged-snapshot reuse, exact responses, and stale-adoption rejection. CPU/allocation per call should remain neutral.

Synthetic owner workload: 40 agents × 112 immutable entries (4,480 rows), 65 retained completed-page instance maps across selection revisions. Empty pages isolate the token edge without a returned session retaining the roster. The committed benchmark executes the actual owner source, with selection imports replaced at the boundary; this is not a whole-Gateway measurement.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained obsolete catalog arrays | 65 | 0 |
| Post-GC retained heap delta | 17,789,184 B | 95,816 B |
| Cold main-thread CPU/call | 0.141256 ms | 0.143566 ms |
| Cold allocation/call | 411,848 B | 411,707 B |
| Warm main-thread CPU/call | 0.0005926 ms | 0.0006180 ms |
| Warm allocation/call | 1,364.54 B | 1,369.45 B |

Retained heap falls 16.87 MiB (99.46%). CPU/allocation are neutral: cold CPU +2.31 µs/call and warm CPU +25 ns/call. Timing and allocation each used five counterbalanced samples of 3,000 calls per side, separately. Cold CPU ranges: base 0.140344–0.141677 ms, candidate 0.141469–0.144393 ms. Host load was recorded per arm; retention pair load1 was 20.25 on both arms. Retention endpoint RSS was 77,030,784 → 60,431,992 B; RSS is contextual and includes allocator behavior. Forced GC ran outside timing.

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-catalog-entry-snapshot-measure.ts --mode retention --entries-per-agent 112 --expect-retained-catalogs 0`; add `--owner-file <baseline-source>` for base. The assertion fails on main (65 !== 0), passes with this fix. Use `--mode timing|allocation --workload cold|warm --iterations 3000 --entries-per-agent 112` for the per-call measurements.

Validation:
- New real-projection collection regression fails on main because the old catalog array remains reachable; passes with the fix, including stale adoption rejection after session-key reuse. Retention file: 3 tests passed, 1.56 s test time / 32.16 s Vitest wall time including compiler preparation.
- Existing catalog snapshot and privacy tests passed (18 tests), including interleaved callers, permission changes, and unchanged planning reuse.
- Changed-file oxfmt/oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, matching gateway-root test typecheck, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Test-lines ratchet: 6,243,085 / 6,320,000; ceiling unchanged.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean, no actionable findings. Configured autoreview refused before inference because the requested route did not match operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

No live deployment or live-server load was performed. This direct retention-edge fix uses focused owner/collection proof; full Gateway handler CPU, allocation/GC rates, event-loop/list p99, and worker round trips are not measured here. PR CI supplies broad validation. Ready for maintainer review; do not auto-merge.

### CI result

Exact-head [CI run 40792205683](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792205683) is **not green**: `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` fails its mock-export scanner on 14 pre-existing factories in `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` (13) and `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts` (1), making `openclaw/ci-gate` fail. [Failure log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40792205683/job/123180564954).

Attribution was checked rather than relying on job names: the two files are byte-identical between CI's main parent `4f4d241683ee9f2bd32178a4c643b2f14e5808ac` and tested merge `6e8d19a48ef7dfd4cb184b5e7855acfafc64d42f`. Their blob IDs are respectively `6cb171387ddd1b818ee48bf77475d32c924661f4` and `e9417547d4c600190ff2c1d4b221a7db24134b41`. A focused replay of the production `scanClosedMockFactories` scanner, import resolver, fingerprint calculation, and CI-base baseline ledger against just those two files reports the identical 14 violations on both revisions. The scanner/resolve code is also unchanged. The automatic failure report labeled the job new because its main job passed without comparing selected scope; the source and focused replay establish this failure is inherited.

No CI rerun, unrelated source changes, or merge performed. The PR remains open for maintainer disposition of the inherited failure. Automatic GitHub Codex review also completed with no findings on this head.

prs.title: fix(node): start managed nodes when descriptor reception is blocked
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes managed node startup under process sandboxes that deny descriptor reception, including Strands Box. Node IPC uses `recvmsg` even though the launcher exchanges only JSON control messages.

## User Impact

Node.js on macOS and Linux can bootstrap, report readiness, and restart managed nodes without granting descriptor import. Bun, Windows, and installed packages without the new capability retain their existing native IPC path. The Box qualification uses Node.js; this does not claim Bun support under Box's descriptor-reception denial.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launcher owns executable selection and this parent/child channel. It selects `byte-pipe-v1` from the selected package manifest and uses length-prefixed JSON on a private inherited stream. Frames are limited to 1 MiB; queued writes to 256 messages and 4 MiB. Invalid frames close the channel, and a child stops if its supervisor disconnects.

Keeping transport selection in the launcher preserves mixed-version updates without an OCE preload duplicating launcher lifecycle or monkey-patching `process.send`. Executable selection, restart authorization, pairing, and sandbox policy remain unchanged. The necessary growth is the bounded transport, narrow client wiring, two real-child regressions, and one existing legacy-runtime case.

Bun retains native IPC because the repository's pinned Bun 1.4.4 does not consume inherited socket data through `net.Socket({ fd })` in a minimal ping/pong reproduction. Selecting the byte transport there regressed existing startup tests; retaining native IPC restores them. The same socket reproduction works with Node 24.22.1.

## Evidence

Current branch, macOS ARM64:

- Native launcher suite with Node 24.22.1: **14/14 passed**. Vitest wall time 25.02 s, test time 4.77 s. Includes 80 KiB bootstrap data, byte-only operation, invalid-frame termination, readiness, restart, rollback, and mixed-version transport.
- Same suite with pinned Bun 1.4.4: **13 passed, 1 inapplicable byte-transport test skipped**; 7.47 s wall, 2.31 s tests. Existing Bun startup passes on the original base as well.
- Regression control on original launcher/client at `d884222b50d0c48ed44846da920b99ebb5807c47`: the new bootstrap case fails because it observes native IPC; the fixed Node case observes no native IPC. Payload delivery itself succeeds in both, so this is not a setup failure.
- Repository focused typecheck, lint wrapper, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. No dependency-version or lockfile changes. CI time and broad/platform CI remain pending.

Separate installed integration evidence: the backport on pinned OpenClaw `f8386bc7df0a6c9eda7a28ae81943c5c06a414ff` passed 33/33 native OCE cases and actual VM stop/start recovery on Linux ARM64, including remote Harness, files, skills, local semantic memory, and code mode. Runtime digest: `sha256:8829c6bf6230d4c0ab4aa3a55b5c9822ce245149fc749607239609d954c63d08`. The image build passed 32 pinned-source launcher cases; descriptor reception stayed denied. These results qualify that pinned backport, not a full installed E2E of this main-branch port. Windows has not been runtime-tested locally.

Draft for review. Independent autoreview is unavailable with the installed CLI/account model combination. The author approved a draft-only waiver; independent review still blocks merge. No merge or readiness promotion is requested.

prs.title: chore(codex): test warm claim settlement and scope revocation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Tests-only regression coverage; no runtime source change or production fix in this PR.** The proof target here is that a failed owner leaves no orphan native-thread claim and a later attempt can reuse that thread.

A Codex-backed conversation can reject the next turn as “claimed by active work” after failed ownership settlement, even though the failed attempt is no longer running. The existing cleanup lacks targeted coverage at the warm-claim cleanup and monitor-setup revocation seams.

Related: karmaterminal/openclaw#1431 (the queue-behind-*genuinely active* work request is separate and remains open).

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. These tests protect the existing claim-release behavior against regressions that could strand subsequent Codex attempts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inject a lease-settlement failure after proving warm claim transfer (without a cold resume), and separately revoke session binding authority during monitor setup. Assert cleanup clears each claim and the same native thread can be claimed by a follow-up attempt. The latter is **scope revocation, not a simulated binding-store lease expiry**. The tests complement the existing lifecycle cleanup; they do not implement queueing behind active work.

## Evidence

- Based on upstream `main` `6ba6ad224ae` (2026-10-25); two Codex app-server test files only.
- Focused Codex app-server suites: 2 files, 21/21 tests passed on upstream base.
- Exact PR head 14bf56f9ea33: [GitHub Actions changed-extensions-config](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121349722824) ran both changed test files, 21/21 passed. Its log includes the warm lifecycle injected-failure test and the monitor-failure binding-scope revocation test; the latter asserts a completed follow-up turn on the same native thread with the claim cleared. [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121351049271) passed. These are fixture-driven in-repo assertions, **not** a shipped Gateway/CLI lease-loss trace.
- Extension test typecheck, targeted format and lint pass; line-cap ratchet passes against `upstream/main` for the two changed files. (The default local ratchet base is `origin/main`, a divergent fork, and falsely flags unrelated upstream files.)
- No live service change or end-to-end field reproduction claimed.

**Follow-up proof correction (2026-10-27):** A Claude source review found the monitor case calls `releaseBindingAuthority()` (binding scope, not simulated lease expiry); the warm case now asserts ownership is held at the injected settlement fault and no cold `thread/resume` occurs before it. Updated head `71d416664521dc5f51bf3e6ac2a435786f91f07c`: focused Vitest 21/21, extension-test tsgo, targeted oxfmt/oxlint and diff check passed locally. Hosted CI is pending; no live lease-expiry or production fix is claimed.

Anthropic API requests fail after API-key setup when the key requires an explicit provider workspace.

## User Impact

Interactive API-key setup accepts a Claude Console workspace ID. Workspace-scoped keys can leave it blank, and existing provider or request headers, including SecretRefs, are preserved.

The workspace setting applies to all requests through the configured Anthropic provider. Accounts requiring different workspaces should use workspace-scoped keys or separate provider configurations. Non-interactive setup continues to use the existing provider-header configuration.

prs.title: feat(ios): steer queued chat messages into the running reply
prs.body:
Related: #168604

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on iPhone, a message sent with **Queue next** while a reply is running goes straight into the Gateway's queue, so it can't be steered into that reply the way Control UI's queued messages can.

## User Impact

User impact: while a reply runs, a **Queue next** message stays in the chat as **Queued**. Touch and hold it and choose **Steer** to send it into the running reply now, or press Command-Return with an empty draft on a hardware keyboard to steer the oldest queued message (Command-Return with a typed draft sends it). If you do nothing, queued messages send in order when the reply finishes.

Behavior change to note: **Queue next** messages now wait on the device instead of in the Gateway queue. If the app is closed or backgrounded before the reply finishes, they send the next time the app is active. Switching to another chat, or a run this view can't see, hands them to the Gateway queue as before. Tapping **Send** and **Steer now** are unchanged. The macOS app shares this chat code, so it gets the same hold and the **Steer** menu item, but not the shortcut. Easy to revert (two-way door): no schema change, no new Gateway request, and rows already queued keep working either way.

## Why This Change Was Made

Control UI holds queued messages on the client until the run is idle and steers one by re-sending it with `chat.send` `queueMode: "steer"`. The iOS durable outbox now does the same, reusing the existing `queue_mode` column and `chat.send` request:

```diff
 flush outbox
-  claim oldest queued row
+  claim oldest queued row, skipping Queue next rows of the visible running session
+    (watch run activity; when it settles, flush again → held rows send FIFO)
   chat.send(queueMode: row.queueMode)

+Steer (message menu, Command-Return)
+  queued followup row → steer   (only while still queued)
+  flush → steered row passes older held rows → chat.send(queueMode: steer)
```

Steering a message the Gateway has already queued still isn't possible from iOS; #160275 / #160593 propose a `chat.steer` request for that.

## Evidence

- **Not run locally: Swift build and tests.** No macOS host was available (the shared chat UI needs SwiftUI/UIKit). PR CI's macOS lanes run them. New and updated tests:
  - `ChatViewModelBusySendTests` › `queue next waits for the visible reply then keeps FIFO` (replaces the old busy-followup FIFO test, which expected **Queue next** to go to the Gateway right away): the row stays queued and steerable during the run, then sends as `followup`, in order, once the run settles.
  - `ChatViewModelBusySendTests` › `steering a queued message sends it into the running reply ahead of older queued messages`: the menu path sends the newer row as `steer` while the older one stays queued, then the keyboard path steers the older one.
  - `ChatCommandOutboxStoreTests` › `held queue next rows let later rows pass and steer only while queued`: claim skips only the held session's followups, and the steer update is refused once a row has been claimed.
  - `ChatComposerTextViewIOSTests` › `command return routes to send or steer outside text composition`: Command-Return/Enter route to the handler, other modifiers and IME composition don't, and an unhandled key falls back to UIKit.
- SwiftFormat 0.63.1 `--lint --config config/swiftformat` on the 10 changed Swift files: 0 need formatting. Changed Swift lines stay within the 120-column limit.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify`: pass (one new source entry, `Steer`; translations are left to the locale refresh workflow). Docs: `oxfmt --check` and `docs:check-mdx` pass, no spellcheck hits in `docs/platforms/ios.md`, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Local review: openclaw/agent-skills autoreview (`2882b90`, source-sha256 `4cf7f15a…`), branch mode, base `dadf9122058`, head `594e4ae5cb6`, P0–P2, Claude engine (Codex CLI isn't logged in on any host available to me). Result: **scoped-clean**, no findings. I checked the three things the reviewer couldn't confirm: every input to run activity is observation-tracked (`liveRunStateByRunID` registers access and mutation by hand), a session switch resets all of them so held rows get released, and the only outbox conformers are the SQLite store and the test double.
- pr-simplify pass: every hunk serves the feature. I dropped an unused accessibility identifier and a `@discardableResult`. The change is +255/−9 against the merge base: about 150 production lines (no new types, no migration) and 112 test lines.
- **Screenshots pending:** send enabled during a run, the queued **Queue next** message, and its menu showing **Steer**. They need a macOS host with the iOS simulator and a seeded fixture Gateway. This PR stays a draft until they're added.

prs.title: fix: restore sidebar rail alignment checks for fresh preferences
prs.body:
Closes #187091

## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar rail alignment checks time out for both desktop and touch when fresh preferences contain no personal sections. The tests wait for the removed empty sections wrapper, so they never reach their remaining vertical-spacing assertions.

## User Impact

This restores the two browser checks without changing the sidebar. Both 1280×800 scenarios retain their existing session fixtures, All-owner selection, loaded-row checks, 0.5px centering tolerances, icon-ink comparison, and timeouts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current renderer intentionally omits personal sections when none are saved. The test now measures the session region that is actually rendered and verifies that its first row starts at the region's top. This preserves exact vertical-spacing protection without introducing a saved section or restoring removed DOM.

Measurements in both variants show the toolbar ending at 44px and the session region and first row starting at 48px. The assertions therefore retain the 4px toolbar gap and check a 0px row inset. Touch rows remain 44px tall while desktop rows remain 30px tall.

## Evidence

The unchanged complete file failed both cases at the absent-wrapper locator. With the correction, both complete cases pass against the bundled Control UI in Chromium. The related session-projection and sidebar-footer layout files also pass all 21 cases.

Targeted formatting, lint, i18n, and the affected UI E2E type graph pass. The complete test-line check passes at 6,312,402 lines against the unchanged 6,320,000 ceiling; this change removes one net test line. The corrected E2E plan took 20.96s including its harness preparation, and the related UI plan took 8.21s. The hosted [Chromium job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40789770184/job/123172511229) also passes both cases in 4.74s; its full selected batch passes all 13 cases. The CI merge composition passes the complete test-line check at 6,243,011 lines against the same ceiling.

[CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40789770184) retains one unrelated failure: the mock-export ratchet reports 14 violations in two Gateway test files. The same leaf reproduces the identical violations on unmodified CI base `4e42bc1825bd962c4ac3a9552d6939f08c21cdc0`. This PR changes no mock, ledger, or scanner input; all other selected checks pass.

prs.title: perf(state): skip redundant maintenance after acknowledged activity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary session activity acknowledged while a maintenance result is delivered changes the scheduling generation and forces another empty planning pass, even when the owner already knows that capacity and age maintenance are not due.

## User Impact

Automatic session maintenance makes fewer worker requests during concurrent activity. Retention policy, capacity thresholds, protected sessions, failure retry cadence, database schemas, lease custody, and FIFO ordering are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Write-triggered scheduling already trusts the owner's published age and entry-count facts. Successful completion now uses that same predicate before scheduling a quiet-window retry. Invalidated facts, changed policy, capacity pressure, and due deadlines still resume planning. Failed passes retain the existing retry behavior.

Runtime production delta is **+17 lines**: the scheduler shrinks by two lines, while the existing age-fact module gains the shared predicate. This keeps one decision for both scheduling entry points, with no new cache or stored state. Measurement tooling adds 285 lines; tests add 20 net lines. The requested non-test/non-doc diff is +302 lines including tooling.

## Evidence

The new `young-activity` case fails on baseline with **2 planning passes instead of 1**, then passes with this change. Independent review found an error-path immediate-retry issue in the first candidate; its regression reproduced **102 passes instead of 2** over a 100 ms fake-clock window. The final candidate preserves the periodic failure cadence and passes both regressions.

Owner measurement: 10,000 synthetic session rows (100 live, 9,900 archived), one acknowledged activity write during each result delivery, 2,000 rounds per arm. The script accelerates only the private quiet retry from 1 second to 1 ms; wall time is harness throughput, not production latency. Base owner: `f25b36e95b0161b324ad772127264fb0021c4d6c`.

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Preparation requests / 2,000 rounds | 4,000 | 2,000 | −50% |
| Requests / simulated minute at 12 rounds/min | 24 | 12 | −50% |
| Final-code main-thread CPU, ms/round, mean of two AB/BA pairs | 1.6982 | 1.2492 | −26.4% |
| Sampled allocation, bytes/round, mean of two AB/BA pairs | 841,944 | 504,267 | −40.1% |
| Final-code untraced GC, ms/round, mean of two pairs | 0.05073 | 0.03228 | −36.4% |
| Final-code maximum GC pause, ms, pairs 1 / 2 | 5.242 / 6.871 | 5.509 / 5.062 | no material increase |
| Final-code GC collections, both pairs | 156 | 94 | −39.7% |
| Final-code pair 1 end RSS, decimal MB | 969.416 | 969.318 | −0.098 MB |
| Final-code pair 1 end heap used, decimal MB | 158.969 | 163.525 | +4.556 MB |

Each timing and allocation arm ran 2,000 rounds, totaling 4,000 rounds per side per metric. Final timing pairs measured CPU 1.8883→1.4278 and 1.5082→1.0707 ms/round. Pair 1 host load was 12.61→11.82 base and 13.47→15.91 candidate; pair 2 was 17.42→16.34 base and 21.35→21.35 candidate. Pair 2 end RSS was 1,248.84→1,161.91 MB, heap used 135.75→152.72 MB. Memory snapshots are uncollected context, not retained-memory claims.

Four identical-code A/A pairs (2,000 rounds/arm) showed CPU differences of −22.4%, +14.2%, +5.5%, and −27.8%; CPU improvement is an observed result with substantial process spread. Their maximum pauses were 5.63→4.58, 4.96→6.02, 7.83→5.86, and 12.94→5.26 ms (44–48 collections/arm). Earlier timing pairs measured CPU 3.435→1.669 and 2.159→2.153 ms/round; the second had a 4.10→68.40 ms maximum pause. Neither two earlier A/A pairs nor the four final controls reproduced that spike; its cause remains unresolved, not established as noise. Final A/B pairs above did not reproduce it. GC by-kind was not recorded; no GC or latency percentile is claimed.

The strongest evidence is exact halving of preparation requests and consistent allocation savings: 842,048→501,810 and 841,841→506,723 bytes/round. Allocation runs preceded the error-only guard; their successful-path workload is unchanged.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-maintenance-kick-measure.mjs --output .local/maintenance-candidate --iterations 2000 --instrument timing`; add `--revision <base-sha>` for baseline, or `--instrument allocation` for the separate allocation pass. Use fresh output directories. This follows the scoped owner-proof fast path; no whole-Gateway stress or live-service load was run, so no sessions.list, handler, or event-loop latency claim is made.

Validation: 26 maintenance-kick tests, 60 cadence/worker tests, and 38 closure tests passed. The changed owner file took 8.81 seconds of test execution in its final local run (41.7 seconds including compiler preparation). Targeted agents/sessions test typecheck, root test typecheck, changed-file lint/format, export-collision guard, and diff checks passed. Test-lines ratchet: 6,242,740 / 6,320,000; baseline unchanged. Exact-head [CI run 40789275986](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40789275986) completed successfully for `664d4c3bd57c437a51eb7a034b418360e03334e2`; the final check snapshot has 70 passed, 66 skipped, zero failed, and zero pending checks. No CI reruns were requested.

Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**, scoped through P2. Autoreview refused the requested provider/config mismatch before inference; operator configuration was left intact. The accepted error-path finding was fixed and independently re-reviewed with no remaining actionable findings. Maintainer merge is intentionally left to the coordinating session.

## What Problem This Solves

Android store and Internal release builds spend several minutes compiling and optimizing phone/Wear bundles on hosted Ubuntu.

## User Impact

No app behavior change. Release operators get faster builds at additional Blacksmith compute cost: the selected 32-class lists at $0.064 per runner-minute, while standard hosted compute is free for this public repository.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the shared build/upload job to the measured Blacksmith class that delivered eight usable CPUs. Keep the existing release process and hosted qualification. The temporary diagnostic runner change stays outside this PR.

## Evidence

- [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40789557341) passed on `a0aa0b42ce64a85e9b684723f8bd7c550d1bffd0`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.

- [Six cold signed build comparisons](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40777243961), three fresh VMs per arm: median signing preflight plus phone/Wear bundles **620.702s → 217.310s (65% less time)**; complete diagnostic jobs **766s → 324s**. All bundles passed signature verification. Blacksmith samples cost an estimated **$1.216 total** before discounts. Images and Java 17 launcher patches differed; source, Node pin, pinned Gradle Java 21 runtime, and cache policy matched.
- [Secretless phone/Wear screenshot qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40788513643) passed on the selected runner. Canonical capture took **5m06s**; KVM was usable; phone/Wear boots took **28s/24s**. Inspected all eight JPEGs and both successful manifests. Android, toolchain, and screenshot owners are identical between the profiled source and this PR base.
- **24 focused tests passed** in 19.74s wall time. The changed routing file took 422ms; its negative control rejects the previous runner. The changed routing file took **323ms in PR CI**.
- Targeted type checking, lint, workflow checks (actionlint/zizmor), MDX, formatting, and diff checks passed. Local AutoReview completed a P0/P1 review of the final local snapshot against `386510139adaf2f7cef620de6f8ad4468fbd9294`, with no actionable findings. That identical patch is committed as `a0aa0b42ce64a85e9b684723f8bd7c550d1bffd0`.
- No builds published. Ruby/Fastlane installation, real credentials, and uploads were not exercised on the new runner.

<details>
<summary>Unrelated documentation anchor audit failures</summary>

The full anchor audit found five failures in untouched pages: duplicate `#agent-process-environment` in `/tools/acp-agents-setup`; missing fragments in `gateway/config-tools.md:60`, `gateway/troubleshooting.md:87`, `providers/ollama.md:128`, and `releases/2026.10.1.md:849`. Neither edited CI page had an anchor error. ClawHub fragments remain unverified because its separate source checkout is unavailable.

</details>

prs.title: perf(update): batch retained runtime hash requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Retaining the installed updater inventories and hashes every runtime file before the update can proceed. Large dependency trees currently dispatch one worker request for every file after the first 1,023 local hashes.

## User Impact

This is a measured performance experiment. Update integrity and output remain unchanged; a speedup is unproven until the acceptance rule below passes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This experiment batches up to 32 sibling files per request at the existing inventory owner, preserving the resource-aware maximum of four hash workers and all pinned-file integrity checks.

Directory-leaf scheduling explicitly admits at most four batches. On failure it stops new admissions, drains accepted batches, and joins worker retirement before returning. Each worker hashes its batch sequentially. The bounded metadata window grows from four to at most 128 files; already accepted peers may finish read-only hashes after another batch fails. Graph discovery/progress publication stays in directory listing order. No partial inventory is published. The single-file private request path is replaced, with no cache, retry, schema change, or trust shortcut.

## Acceptance rule — registered before A/B timing

Flow: the real private runtime-retention helper and its actual worker transport, driven by `scripts/perf/update-retention.mts`. Synthetic installed tree: 312 packages × 512 1-KiB payload files, plus manifests and entrypoints (160,370 regular files). Source and retained destination share one filesystem: APFS for the local experiment, or the allocated Linux filesystem for a remote experiment. Both arms use the same host, filesystem and Node version; remote results are labeled Linux and do not establish macOS wall time. No user state is accessed.

Timing excludes the frozen SQL observer and per-call filesystem instrumentation. A separate count run must show at least 90% fewer hash request envelopes, with identical files, inventory visits, hash bytes, links/copies and integrity outcomes. Time five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs on the same platform after a separate warmup pair; fresh helper process and retained destination each run. These are warm-filesystem measurements: no cache eviction or cold-filesystem claim. Keep any later cold native-update samples separate.

Record retention-step wall time, total process user+system CPU, and main-thread user+system CPU, with medians, nearest-rank p95, and min–max. Exit-only CPU accounting covers the helper lifetime, including startup and retirement. The timing lock is held and load1 must be below 24 before every sample. **Merge only if retention wall or total process CPU median improves by at least 10%.** All other measured user-facing cells must hold or improve; a 20% adverse change stops the experiment. A request-count reduction alone does not qualify.

## Evidence

Experiment stopped without merging: the required observer-free performance floor is unproven. Focused source replacement, byte/ownership integrity, resource refusal, stop/drain/retire, actual worker, and retained-tree cases pass. The existing metadata-drain fixture was enlarged across batch boundaries and passed on rerun. Two isolated Codex reviews of the production change are clean; the additional test-only trim review is also clean. Production grows by 35 lines to represent batching explicitly; net test-line growth is zero. An initial 4,114-file count reproduction reduces hash requests from 3,091 to 103 while preserving 4,195,073 hash bytes and all counted source filesystem operations. The full-size inventory reproduces 159,347 → 5,271 requests (−96.69%), identical 160,370 files / 161,309 entries / 163,603,928 hashed bytes, identical inventory fingerprint, and identical counted source filesystem calls. The existing real-worker regression fails on the baseline in both native-copy modes (expected 5 requests, received 129); candidate cases pass. No qualified observer-free timing sample started: the host stayed above the registered load threshold throughout the 60-minute wait.

If the floor passes, the matched full update proof must patch the installed driver as well as the candidate, followed by exact-head CI including all three PostgreSQL shards. The edited worker also serves database modes, but their handlers and SQL are unchanged; the batched branch performs filesystem hashing only.

The full-tree instrumented capture exceeded its diagnostic timeout during unchanged materialization under severe host I/O load and is excluded from performance evidence. Full-size work counting targets the exact retention inventory owner with identical roots and real worker transport; the uninstrumented timing workload still includes inventory and materialization. Small full-retention counts cover unchanged materialization operations.

Local typecheck was refused before compilation because the required external dependency-store layout fails the checker's declaration-containment gate. This environment limitation is recorded; no guard was bypassed. Broad static checks remain pending until the performance floor is established.

Open-PR overlap: the shared index reports #144699 at `3414787f83d03b1ef3efadb6cb40221b188038f0`. Paired base-only and base-plus-candidate `git merge-tree` checks produce the same conflict set; the touched tree owner has ten inherited conflict blocks in each. No new merge conflicts are introduced.

## Resumed timing experiment

The draft remains unmergeable until observer-free timing qualifies. One immediately granted Blacksmith Testbox allocation will be attempted, without queueing or provider escalation. If unavailable, the local runner retries under the timing lock and load1 < 24, with at most six hours of cumulative lock/load waiting including the initial 3,600.525 seconds. A separate warmup pair precedes five measured alternating pairs. A measured failure of the 10% floor closes this draft; expiry without qualified samples leaves the floor unproven.

## Initial experiment decision

Do not merge this experiment. The timing runner waited 3,600.525 seconds under the timing lock; all 120 load observations were above the required 24 (range 33.793–88.522). Zero warmup or measured samples started. Qualified wall-time, total-process CPU and main-thread CPU medians/p95 are unavailable. The ≥90% envelope reduction passes, but the ≥10% wall-time or total-process-CPU gain is unproven. Count-instrumented CPU captures are excluded from the decision because instrumentation may flatter batching. No speedup or regression is claimed.

The runner restored the committed candidate source and released the lock. Matched installed-driver native proof and broad CI/PG gates were not pursued after this measurement limit. This remains a draft and nothing has landed.

## Larger levers — design only

A held directory with descriptor-relative, no-follow leaf admission could remove repeated parent checks while preserving per-file identity and hash stability. A cached pathname is insufficient against external replacement; pinned-directory rename semantics need an explicit contract. Rough experiment target: 10–25% of retention cost.

Independent APFS clones would prevent later writes through the source inode from changing retained bytes. Removing content hashes still requires an admitted-capture authority design, dependency/symlink validation and portable fallback; clone plus unchanged hashing adds work. Rough target if the hash walk is removed: 30–60%.

Clone-based retention now belongs to a separate design effort. Directory admission remains deferred to its filesystem dependency owner. Previous-retention reuse is dropped because its expected average hit rate is near zero. These estimates are unmeasured and are not implementation approval.
