prs.title: fix(macos): prevent duplicate voice sends and false sent feedback
prs.body:
Related: #127557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: manual Send and an already-queued auto-send can submit one voice transcript twice, and an RPC rejection can appear successfully sent.

## User Impact

One coordinator-owned attempt submits each active transcript. Pending sends show progress; only Gateway acceptance produces sent feedback. Rejection preserves editable text for explicit retry.

**Ready for maintainer review.** The conflict repair and Anmol's native compile fixes are published at d6c006bed106d1cb0c58be150d9d902e8f95b881, refreshed onto main dad7cbe17463dd9040f723d69f2826cf8e931fdf. GitHub reports the branch mergeable (no source conflicts). The earlier publication refusal came from a stale upstream Android release workflow in the older prepared base; the supported base refresh incorporated live main's definition. No permission change or guard bypass was needed. Exact-head focused native gates and real rejection/retry proof are now supplied by Anmol below. Ready status was requested by Anmol; no merge has been requested or performed. Skipped native CI jobs are not counted as passing.

There are no authored config, schema, durability, public protocol, dependency, or permission changes. This is not a durable outbox or exactly-once delivery guarantee; cancellation cannot retract an already-submitted RPC.

Contributor credit: @anmol0b requested this fix and supplied native verification, resolution choices, and follow-up compile fixes.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @anmol0b](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f10d7d72-7d35-44c9-858b-62fbb32bf32f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5eee3800-f321-48db-9daf-2f35ae11bae2)

## Why This Change Was Made

The coordinator claims a token before route lookup, retains one task, consumes the result, and retires work at replacement or dismissal start. Identical full payload and resolved route reuse the invocation key; edits or route changes get a fresh key. Queued auto callbacks cannot retry failures. The unowned coordinator forward and unconditional sent timer are removed.

Wake cleanup dismisses only its capture token, preserving pending PTT sends during ordinary lease release. Manual send, immediate/delayed auto-send, and PTT share the owner; the no-overlay wake fallback plays its chime only after acceptance.

The published repair preserves main's removed trace logging, source-free session API, context-free token/chime APIs, single state-bound action owner, canonical routeEntries lookup, and event-based lifecycle waits. It applies Anmol's fixes for mutually inferred lazy fixture types, the routeEntries fixture argument, and the long Forward typealias.

Risk is bounded to native voice submission and overlay lifecycle, with no stored-state migration. Exact-head focused native validation is documented below; no broad native CI pass is claimed. The published delta remains the same 16 task files relative to the refreshed main base.

## Evidence

### Native proof supplied by Anmol — exact published head

[Published-head native gates and live rejection/retry proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186271#issuecomment-6464391677), supplied by @anmol0b for d6c006bed106d1cb0c58be150d9d902e8f95b881 **as-is, with no local changes**, on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Xcode 27.1 / Swift 6.4:

- Native app build and test build both exited 0 (the supplied capture reports 3m13.470s combined wall time).
- All 47 tests in the six focused voice suites passed in 0.307s; the suites then passed 10/10 repetitions.
- SwiftFormat 0.63.1: 0/33 files require formatting, exit 0. SwiftLint 0.65.1 reports no violations in this PR's files; the reported whole-run finding remains the preexisting, untouched DashboardManager.swift file-length error (1505 > 1500). This is not labeled an all-green global lint run.
- Localization verification passed on this exact head: entries=4545 changed=false, exit 0.
- The author audited the focused suites' injected Gateway/microphone/defaults/Keychain boundaries, then ran them under sandbox-exec with private HOME/state and restrictions on operator state, preferences, and the live Gateway port. These are author-provided native results, not execution performed by the Linux implementation agent.

![Native gates on the exact published head d6c006b](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1f58385-4869-4b05-801e-fc405af2dea9)

**Live RPC rejection → visible retry UI → explicit retry accepted, on the same published head:** the packaged app used its own profile and an isolated Gateway at 127.0.0.1:19271 with separate state/config. The test Gateway was suspended while the app connection stayed open, producing a real UNAVAILABLE admission response rather than a transport disconnect.

1. A real PTT send was rejected at 13:54:11.630 (242ms). The overlay retained the transcript and Send button, displayed “Send failed. Click Send to retry.”, and neither showed sent feedback nor dismissed.
2. Admission reopened when the suspension lease expired at 13:54:35.449. No automatic agent request occurred before the explicit click.
3. Clicking Send produced one retry request at 13:54:41.667, accepted at 13:54:41.746 (80ms). The overlay progressed through retry/sent feedback and closed. Captures show the retained failure state, the retry, and the dismissed overlay.
4. The same app connection was used throughout: exactly one rejected request followed by one accepted explicit retry, without duplicate or automatic sends.

![Real rejection, retained retry UI, explicit retry and accepted dismissal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d8b653c-a9c9-4496-871e-47865a302178)

The later agent-run 401 at 13:54:52 reflects the isolated Gateway's missing model credentials after submission acceptance; it does not claim successful model execution or external delivery. The earlier [baseline red/green probe and outage proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186271#issuecomment-6460923071) remain supporting history: an outage keeps transport retry pending, whereas an RPC error response surfaces manual retry UI. The new evidence directly addresses the exact-head native and live-rejection gaps in ClawSweeper revision 2. Both new captures were inspected.

### Conflict-repair checks

- Inspected and simplified complete delta: 16 files, +483/−132; production Swift +213/−126, tests/fixtures +262/−2, docs +7/−4, generated inventory +1/−0. No new submission owner or compatibility wrapper was added. The two continuation-gated regressions retain duplicate/rejection/retry identity and late-settlement coverage; the PTT lifecycle regression holds preparation across wake-lease release.
- Independent Auto Review completed all eight passes at P0–P3 with no actionable findings (OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol), against the prior refreshed base 6311376. The later disjoint main refresh preserved the voice repair; its review remains applicable to the unchanged authored logic, not a claim that all incoming main changes were independently reviewed here. Restart-interrupted attempts are not counted. This is static review, not native execution.
- Linux checks passed on Node 26.12.1 and frozen pnpm 12.15.0 tooling: conflict markers, attribution/Doctor/export/duplicate/coercion guards, dependency pins/patches, native state schema guard, localization verification (4521 unchanged before the final base refresh; 4545 unchanged after it), docs links (16,080 checked, zero broken), docs/JSON formatting, and git diff --check. The formatter used its supported one-thread option; this does not claim Swift formatting on Linux.
- **Not green:** pnpm test:macos:ci exited 1 after 76.566s. Three failures in unchanged src/skills/runtime/discovery.integration.test.ts: two live-watch version waits did not advance, and replacement-workspace observation saw four watch registrations instead of one. Its temporary skill roots and Node discovery/watcher owners are disjoint from the Swift voice delta and match the refreshed base. No separate baseline replay is claimed; the chained remainder did not complete. No unrelated watcher fix or test exception is included.
- Swift/AppKit execution was not performed on the Linux implementation host. Exact-published-head native and live UI results are now supplied by Anmol above. Native CI jobs were skipped, so no native CI seconds or broad CI success is claimed. Original defect-introducing commit attribution remains unverified.

### Review scope

The new evidence is tied to the unchanged published head d6c006b and closes the two validation gaps named in revision 2 for another ClawSweeper assessment. Sent means Gateway acceptance, not eventual model-run success. The PR is ready for review and remains unmerged; global lint/earlier Linux tooling failures and skipped native CI are disclosed rather than converted to green.

## Worked on by

- @anmol0b

prs.title: perf(ui): preserve unchanged dashboard report content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Updating one saved dashboard report makes unchanged reports repeat content work because the full snapshot gives them fresh objects.

## User Impact

Unchanged reports retain their prepared content while the changed report and all layout or metadata changes still appear. No user action or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway Board provider preserves an unticketed native report when its name, instance, revision and envelope are unchanged. Changed envelopes still publish every incoming field while retaining the unchanged content reference. Explicit refreshes, replacements, missing identities, and ticketed or framed reports retain their existing refresh behavior. Key enumeration avoids creating a pair array for every compared field.

The Gateway remains authoritative. Content puts advance the report revision; layout operations do not. The provider still reads and scans the full snapshot in O(N); this is not a delta-only update path. The base already contains fixed-report viewport activation and CSS containment; this change addresses the remaining snapshot identity work rather than introducing another rendering or caching owner.

The benchmark keeps distinct labels for the supported 48-report workload, a staged 1,000-report stress workload, and the legacy 1,000-report workload. Staged cases install the synthetic reply before timing, then measure event delivery, the full board.get request/response, reconciliation, visible metric 2 and settling. The legacy case retains fixture installation inside its original interval. None is a live-Gateway or actual-network measurement, and the 1,000-report fixture exceeds the current 48-widget new-write cap.

## Evidence

Final source head: `d00844549bf23b2db19ca4ab13a5ccb991c97e02`. Completed renderer proof uses the frozen assets below. Exact-head PR CI completed with the inherited failures listed below. prs.title: fix(macos): New Thread exhausts memory during session creation
prs.body:
Closes #186215

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native macOS New Thread hanging and allocating unbounded memory when creating a conversation.

## User Impact

Native Mac users can create a thread through the sidebar or keyboard shortcut without entering recursive session creation. A missing or retired Gateway connection is rejected rather than silently retargeted. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mac transport now routes ordinary creation through its existing captured new-session lease. This replaces the recursive default-dispatch path without introducing another request builder or changing generic transports and iOS.

## Evidence

This is a draft proof head, not a readiness claim.

- Finite native base-red: [fork run 40568043055](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40568043055), Intel macOS 26, proof commit `cd45388962cfa007d6bf3052dbee8ada9d3e8c3b` on upstream base `1b50ce5a6835798634c4d98ac87891f4e5290120`. The exact explicit-options regression ran once and failed with the expected unsupported-options error after its captured-lease control. The test is unchanged in this fix.
- Added sibling coverage for plain and legacy existential creation, disconnected and retired/replaced sockets, recovery, and a mismatched window Gateway pin.
- Normal staged Git hook and native localization inventory passed; private-key scan and whitespace check passed. No lockfile or generated-source changes.
- Independent Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, P0–P2) reviewed the complete two-file candidate against `c4c345af4e8842219a880c13a1788a560878dc84`: scoped clean. Static review is not native test proof.

prs.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): gateway stalls after every model call when content capture is on
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Content capture repeatedly redacts whole model, tool and log payloads while searching for a value that fits the export budget. On large calls this can stall the Gateway and every channel sharing its event loop. This PR bounds that work in diagnostics-otel and reuses serialization for mirrored GenAI attributes. Fixes #158116.

The plugin keeps capture budgets; core keeps secret matching and the registered-value owner. Configured redaction patterns retain whole-value handling. With the default rules, clipped values use bounded lookahead, incomplete-secret detection and a bounded retry. This changes capture completeness for some large values; maintainer acceptance remains required.

## October 28 repair

Current head: `e84c7301e2da9588fe7404d02166ae81f064a433`. Final tree: `89d47a8422baeebf04ff347bb916aa32c29d3c24`. Parents: prior published `45eab5ab306e15546a661148a1cec2819d9802d8` and main `0ded0ed7a8cae4867a3a201e32cccbfbfe9bde70`.

Preserved the exact upstream [#187030 / `0ded0ed7a8ca`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0ded0ed7a8cae4867a3a201e32cccbfbfe9bde70) test-line ceiling of 6,320,000. That baseline file is unchanged from main and is no longer in this PR's diff. Counting the base Git blobs gives 6,311,694 test lines; this PR adds 977 required lines: normalization 772, open-secret 66, registry 31, registered-secret consumer 63, service-capture 36 and config 9. The combined 6,312,671 lines fit the upstream ceiling. These cases exercise boundary masking, emitted diagnostic content and bounded work; every assertion remains.

The integration also includes upstream [#187003 / `bf9709250b87`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bf9709250b87bec4a26637046096092ee68d3366), which observes idle-module evaluation before starting the existing render counter. Its render limits and selected-title/viewer controls remain. This is the upstream test correction, separate from the telemetry repair below.

- Fixed an additional registered-secret boundary case. Earlier masks can shorten the prefix enough to move a partially observed registered value inside the exported text. The open-secret fallback previously marked that result settled. It now leaves it unsettled while registered values exist, allowing the existing retry and retained-lookahead rules to mask the complete value. Whole-input redaction and the no-registry fallback are unchanged.
- Added the failing registered/unregistered pair and a service-level regression through the real diagnostic event, SDK lifecycle and stdout JSONL exporter. The fixture contains synthetic values only.

## Evidence

The original positive, mutation and static results in this section are bound to tree `d17cab788da1a6be4df015f28bb44a82841172ed`; original-source and base controls identify their deliberate variations. The later tree-specific replays are recorded separately below. The isolated Linux x86_64 run used Node `24.22.1`, pnpm `12.15.0` and repository-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`. The unchanged package-manager integrity, lockfile and 240 dependency-input blobs were checked. Raw blob and mode verification covered 61,095 tracked paths. Tests used the canonical wrapper with source freshness enabled, one worker and synthetic state.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file> --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=json --outputFile=<report>
```

| File | Passed | Failed / skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service-content-normalization.test.ts` | 102 | 0 / 0 |
| `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.content-capture.test.ts` | 9 | 0 / 0 |
| `src/logging/config.test.ts` | 10 | 0 / 0 |
| `src/logging/secret-redaction-registry.test.ts` | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| `src/logging/redact.test.ts` | 50 | 0 / 0 |
| `src/logging/redact-open-secret.test.ts` | 22 | 0 / 0 |
| `test/diagnostics-otel-registered-secret.test.ts` | 4 | 0 / 0 |

The original normalization file recorded 5.013 seconds of test-file runtime; service capture recorded 0.063 seconds and the root registered-secret consumer 0.058 seconds. Canonical wrapper wall times were 91.94, 84.98 and 79.76 seconds respectively, including source/runtime preparation. Those setup costs are retained in the measurements.

That is 198 distinct cases, not a sum of repeated executions. The cases cover ordinary-content preservation, quoted assignments, long registered values, JWT/Atlassian/form/URL-password boundaries, configured patterns, export-size limits and redaction-input work bounds.

Negative controls:

- Restoring the original normalizer while keeping the new registered/unregistered pair gives 1 passed and 1 named assertion failure. The fixed pair passes; the complete root file passes all 4 cases.
- Restoring the original normalizer for the new emitted-body case gives a named assertion failure in the serialized diagnostic record. The fixed complete service-capture file passes all 9 cases.
- Making the initial redaction window consume the whole log body fails the named work-bound assertion; restoring the candidate passes it.
- Replacing registered-secret lookahead with the fixed 4,096-character minimum fails the named masking assertion on all 5 export paths; restoring the candidate passes all 5.

Each control reached its intended assertion after setup. The candidate source was restored and verified after mutations. The emitted-body case proves stdout JSONL and the shared pre-transport log body, not OTLP network delivery or wire encoding.

At tree `d17cab788da1a6be4df015f28bb44a82841172ed`, format checking all 19 changed paths, the test-line ratchet, core/plugin types, logging-test/root-test types and all touched core/plugin/script/root-test lint checks pass. The commands use `run-format.mts`, `run-tsgo.mjs` and `run-oxlint.mjs`; the ratchet uses `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 39b3d94413ba1400822dc644743fe3045acb8a64 --no-merge-base`.

Plugin declarations were prepared with the repository's selected-extension route:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts.mts '--extensions=["diagnostics-otel"]'
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/diagnostics-otel/tsconfig.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile=<temporary-path>
```

That route discovered 11 SDK roots and emitted 12,377 files, including transitive declaration dependencies. The normal type-aware lint wrapper consumed those same-source artifacts; only its duplicate full-SDK preparation was skipped, following the existing parent-preparation convention. Source/toolchain freshness remained enabled. Preparation plus the remaining four type/lint checks finished in 344.88 seconds, with sampled aggregate RSS peaking at 6,070,042,624 bytes under the unchanged 6 GiB stop threshold. No owned process remained after cleanup.

Earlier full-SDK preparation attempts hit that resource threshold; a retry also encountered the dead task's artifact lock before compilation. Those attempts are retained as incomplete/setup results, not passes. The supported selected-extension route above completed without raising the memory bound or changing source/check semantics.

The SDK surface check remains red with an executed exact-main control:

| Tree | Public entrypoints / budget | Exports / budget | Callable exports / budget |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main `39b3d94413ba` | 160 / 158 | 3,840 / 3,822 | 2,225 / 2,214 |
| This candidate | 160 / 158 | 3,843 / 3,825 | 2,228 / 2,217 |

This exact-base comparison applies to the earlier `d17cab` qualification, not to a fresh execution on the current tree. Both exceed their own budgets by 2 entrypoints, 18 exports and 11 callables. The PR's existing three-function addition accounts for its +3 exports/callables and matching +3 budgets. No SDK surface ceiling was raised to hide that excess. This does not grant acceptance of the three SDK additions.

An independent source review inspected the original integration diff and then the three-file repair, found the registered-prefix defect above, and found no unresolved P1/P2 issue in the repaired scope. Its audit checked the actual before/after report hashes. This was an independent source/evidence review, not a formal approval. The current published tree and hosted checks are verified separately.

## Qualification and current CI

At behavioral-test tree `7b0e0d5cd879f427cccce76255dae5b3f19ca272`, the focused qualification recorded **25 passed, 0 failed and 0 skipped: 9 service-capture, 4 root registered-secret and 12 UI cases**:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.content-capture.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/diagnostics-otel-registered-secret.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_UI_E2E_SKIP_REAL_GATEWAY=1 OPENCLAW_UI_E2E_SKIP_PRODUCTION_ARTIFACT=0 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner --maxWorkers=1 ui/src/e2e/chat-background-invalidation.e2e.test.ts ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e-readiness.e2e.test.ts
```

The actual invocations also emitted JSON reports. The canonical UI setup built its production bundle from the current source; the run used Playwright `1.64.1` and Chromium `156.0.8078.4`. All 61,124 tracked raw blobs/modes and the 240 unchanged dependency inputs were verified before/after qualification. The 25-case run finished in 388.726 seconds; sampled aggregate RSS peaked at 4,828,749,824 bytes under the unchanged 6 GiB stop threshold. Cleanup left no owned process.

Main then changed only its baseline file in `0ded0ed7a8ca`. The final tree `89d47a8422baeebf04ff347bb916aa32c29d3c24` preserves that file exactly. All other 61,123 raw tracked paths, including every code and test blob/mode, are identical to the 25-case-tested tree. Those cases were not repeated for this baseline-only integration.

Final-tree qualification uses:

```sh
pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 0ded0ed7a8cae4867a3a201e32cccbfbfe9bde70 --no-merge-base
```

Its positive, temporary over-ceiling negative and restored runs exit **0, 1 and 0**. The actual 6,312,671 lines pass; adding 7,330 temporary comment lines reaches 6,320,001 and fails against the unchanged 6,320,000 upstream ceiling. Restoration is verified by raw blob/mode identity. Formatting all 19 changed paths and `git diff --cached --check` pass. Final qualification took 17.584 seconds, peaked at 363,339,776 bytes sampled aggregate RSS and left no owned process.

The earlier 198-case mutation/static qualification and the 235-case replay at tree `ca87a7dfed7574e41c4da1f7b50be8ff183bd2a4` remain scoped to their recorded trees. No new full-suite, full-shard, type/lint-suite or live-runtime pass is claimed by the focused integration runs above.

The previous published head `45eab5ab306e15546a661148a1cec2819d9802d8` finished [run 40763826859](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40763826859) with **66 successful jobs, 3 failed and 26 skipped**. GitHub tested merge `ac6d728ec2409fe4eb2796c9d57f262149d8d226` against actual base `b9c6e9c0163f51f2d4b74ded87393c45f1d13769`.

- [UI job 123106877760](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40763826859/job/123106877760) recorded 533 passed and 1 failed: the unchanged-conversation render test observed `3` renders against an expected limit of `<= 1` at line 173. Reconstructing the complete raw trees for actual base `b9c6e9c0163f51f2d4b74ded87393c45f1d13769` and merge `ac6d728ec2409fe4eb2796c9d57f262149d8d226`, then running the same two focused UI files in the same environment, produced 11 passed, 1 failed and 0 skipped on each. Both failed the same complete test name and assertion. That independently reproduces the symptom without the telemetry patch. Upstream `bf9709250b87`, now integrated, changes this test's startup observation.
- [UI job 123106877768](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40763826859/job/123106877768) recorded 546 passed and 1 failed: the readiness case with `offline: false` expected `terminalActivationReady: true`, got `false`. All 11 readiness cases passed in both focused controls, including `offline: false` and `offline: true`. The hosted failure remains unexplained under its broader ordering/concurrency; the focused passes do not prove it fixed or inherited.
- [Aggregate job 123114866310](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40763826859/job/123114866310) failed for those selected lanes. The actual-base CI run was cancelled with zero jobs, so the local exact-tree comparison above is the executed base control. Older scheduled jobs with the same job names are not substituted for that base.

The focused UI controls used one worker and two files. Hosted shards used four workers and much larger selected scopes; no full-shard equivalence is claimed. Their initial browser setup attempt ran zero assertions because a temporary socket path was too long. After correcting only that task-local path, both exact-tree comparisons completed with the results above. No assertion, render limit or timeout was weakened.

Automatic [CI run 40782721694](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40782721694) on `e84c7301e2da9588fe7404d02166ae81f064a433` finished with **65 successful jobs, 4 failed and 26 skipped**. The checkout logs identify merge `9644c2d96cde8a9e53fc35022f6114be022bca9d` against actual base `61f44e6ec5ce7bd9075356188254a4568e891d06`. Selected baseline-ratchet and type/lint jobs passed, along with UI shards 1/7, 3/7, 5/7 and 7/7. This head is not qualified for landing.

| Failed job | Executed result |
| --- | --- |
| [UI 2/7, job 123148927380](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40782721694/job/123148927380) | 503 passed, 1 failed. `chat-session-diff.e2e.test.ts` reports a non-Element `getComputedStyle` argument error. The hosted failed-name and line suffixes are redacted; the public token/parent color comparison at lines 499-500 is a source lead, not an unredacted trace. |
| [UI 4/7, job 123148927518](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40782721694/job/123148927518) | 512 passed, 8 failed. Six session-ownership cases time out waiting for `.personal-session-groups__heading`; sidebar interactions also time out during hover and fail to reach the requested agent route. |
| [UI 6/7, job 123148927379](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40782721694/job/123148927379) | 486 passed, 2 failed. Both rail-alignment variants time out waiting for `.sidebar-sessions > .personal-session-groups` at line 101. |
| [Aggregate gate, job 123154528468](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40782721694/job/123154528468) | Rejects the failed selected UI E2E lanes. |

The [exact-base CI run 40782479746](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40782479746) succeeded with its UI E2E jobs skipped. It supplies no executed control for these failures. The complete [base-to-merge diff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/61f44e6ec5ce7bd9075356188254a4568e891d06...9644c2d96cde8a9e53fc35022f6114be022bca9d) contains the 19 telemetry/docs/test changes and no UI, browser-harness or dependency changes. That source comparison does not establish runtime causality. Matched controls on those exact source trees are now complete; no assertion, timeout or security gate was weakened.

The four files were run sequentially on the same isolated Linux x86_64 builder, using the same pinned Node/pnpm/Bun, Playwright and Chromium environment:

```sh
OPENCLAW_UI_E2E_SKIP_REAL_GATEWAY=1 OPENCLAW_UI_E2E_SKIP_PRODUCTION_ARTIFACT=0 \
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts \
  --configLoader runner --maxWorkers=1 \
  ui/src/e2e/chat-session-diff.e2e.test.ts \
  ui/src/e2e/session-ownership.e2e.test.ts \
  ui/src/e2e/sidebar-interactions.e2e.test.ts \
  ui/src/e2e/sidebar-rail-alignment.e2e.test.ts \
  --reporter=json --outputFile=<report>
```

| Source target | Full Git tree | Passed / failed / skipped | Wall time | Peak sampled aggregate RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base `61f44e6ec5ce7bd9075356188254a4568e891d06` | `259d6bef5d9bbb8b31b1e59e2849734802fb8176` | 24 / 9 / 0 | 502.233 s | 4,770,869,248 bytes |
| CI merge `9644c2d96cde8a9e53fc35022f6114be022bca9d` | `b41a242831fc867f040d2047187cc6bcd7ef9513` | 24 / 9 / 0 | 479.819 s | 4,934,770,688 bytes |

All 33 local case identities and statuses match between the two controls. Both reproduce six waits for `.personal-session-groups__heading`, two waits for the optional `.personal-session-groups` wrapper, and the native-link hover blocked by a `.kbd__text` element in the sidebar rail. The hover target exists: the hosted trace shows a `+` glyph intercepting it; both local traces show `Ctrl`. The six hosted ownership case names remain redacted, so their association is by file, count and timeout signature. No hidden names were reconstructed.

All eight chat-diff cases and the named agent-settings keyboard case pass on both trees. Their additional hosted failures remain unreproduced and unexplained under the larger shard ordering/concurrency. These focused passes do not prove them fixed or inherited.

Raw blob/mode inventories cover 61,120 paths for the base and 61,126 for the merge, before and after execution. Independent reconstruction of those inventories gives the exact Git trees above. The 240 dependency-input fingerprint and toolchain hashes match. The staging checkout's historical `HEAD` remained `39b3d94413ba`; the tested source is identified by the complete reconstructed tree, not that staging ref. The original candidate tree `89d47a8422baeebf04ff347bb916aa32c29d3c24` was restored after each run. Both controls exited 1 for their recorded test failures, without a resource stop; cleanup left no owned process. Runs used two CPUs and a sampled 6 GiB aggregate-RSS stop, not a kernel hard memory cap.

Retained JSON report SHA256 values: base `54be0d9c24f60cb583f6d76fa0308b7c350d81c03e534997ee671d34267843a1`; merge `8802a5b67ba15cb45f2d189d60a814ad5af9b896f6499e69eedc90b18bfbfbdb`. These are 33 distinct cases repeated on two trees, not 66 distinct cases or complete hosted shards. Real-Gateway stages were excluded by the mocked-Gateway control envelope; production bundles and source freshness checks remained enabled.

Upstream has source corrections for the heading expectation in [#187070 / `4a2a1962d9ca`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4a2a1962d9caaf965c0432c7c9a84e5a40290f7d) and the tooltip interception in [#186360 / `a919e5ecc4f6`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a919e5ecc4f6c579e16ab21499ccda3acaa1fb07). Neither newer revision was executed in these original-tree controls. The rail fixture still expects a wrapper that the empty-group renderer omits; that is separate from the telemetry change.

Head remains `e84c7301e2da9588fe7404d02166ae81f064a433`. Per the repository's [test-failure policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a919e5ecc4f6c579e16ab21499ccda3acaa1fb07/.agents/skills/openclaw-testing/SKILL.md#test-failure-policy), the original failures, bounded attempts and remaining uncertainty are retained here. No source push or CI rerun was made merely to chase green.

Security-sensitive approval remains separate: a maintainer must approve the actual published revision through the normal repository gate. Capture-completeness and SDK-surface decisions below remain open.

## Review disposition and maintainer decisions

The 21 retained discussion/review items were reconciled before publication. The old quoted-assignment finding is addressed in core's incomplete-secret matchers and the current regressions; its inline thread is already resolved/outdated. Historical author replies and measurements remain historical evidence. The latest hosted source review at `6f8053117fe3750c77010510be39036ca39d1f6d` reported no actionable code finding and explicitly left these decisions open:

1. Accept reduced capture completeness and the documented omissions for large values, or require a different bounded-redaction contract.
2. Accept `findTruncatedSecret()`, `getLongestRegisteredSecretLength()` and `hasConfiguredRedactPatterns()` in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/logging-core`.
3. Complete security-sensitive review for the new published head.

No owner acceptance, live-host recovery or merge readiness is inferred from the passing synthetic tests. Earlier Gateway/OTLP measurements in this discussion were supplied by the author at older heads and were not repeated for this revision.

## Capture and security limits

- Whole-value handling covers JSON up to 4x the attribute budget, and eligible open-secret cases above it within the existing 8x redaction-work budget. Other larger values can be truncated even when their fully masked content would fit. That is the work/completeness tradeoff requiring maintainer acceptance.
- The bounded retry can export less text while registered values exist, including when a registration is unrelated to the open-secret match. A longer registered value increases lookahead and reduces the number of captured items that fit the work cap. A window larger than the cap produces the `max_redaction_work` summary.
- Configured patterns retain whole-value work and can still block on very large captures. The shared configured-pattern implementation processes long strings in 16,384-character chunks without overlap; matches across chunk boundaries remain a pre-existing limitation, including the 131,072-character tool-call cut.
- Incomplete quoted values, private keys, JWT bodies, URL passwords, Atlassian tokens, first-pair form values and registered secrets have explicit boundary handling. Identifier prefixes in `SG.` keys, Slack webhook URLs, Telegram bot tokens and `FlyV1 fm<digits>_` would need to exceed lookahead before their secret part is reached; that case is not covered. A JWT header longer than lookahead can still export header parameters up to the cut; claims and signature are distinct parts.
- Conservative URL handling can drop a database port/path that runs to the window end without whitespace or `@`, and a web URL port that ends there without `/`, whitespace or `@`. Main can retain those values.
- Plugins are trusted in-process code. The new SDK helpers return positions, lengths or configuration presence, not registered secret values. The registry remains a security-reviewed owner; this PR does not replace that approval with tests.

No private transcript, credential file, live operational log, runtime installation or service restart was used for this repair's evidence.

prs.title: fix(discord): voice autoJoin flaps in and out when joining keeps failing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Discord bot with `voice.autoJoin[].whenOccupied` flaps in and out of the voice channel about once a second when joining keeps failing (for example, the realtime provider is down or the bot lost access to the channel).

## User Impact

User impact: when an occupied auto-join fails, the bot stays out of the channel and retries after a growing wait (5 seconds, doubling up to 10 minutes) instead of rejoining on every voice-state change. Discord `Missing Access`/`Missing Permissions` failures stop auto-join for that channel with one warning that says to restore the bot's View Channel and Connect permissions, then run `/vc join` or reload the config. A successful `/vc join` or a config reload clears the wait.

## Why This Change Was Made

Occupied auto-join reconciles on every guild voice-state update, including the bot's own leave after a failed start. Only credential-like errors were suppressed, so any other failure rejoined immediately and the bot's own leave scheduled the next attempt. In the reported incident this produced 119 join/leave cycles in under three minutes, then 140+ `Missing Access` lookups, and a voice-state queue backlog of 30–45 seconds per event.

The auto-join owner in `voice-runtime.ts` now keeps one failure record per guild/channel: fatal failures (the existing credential set plus Discord access errors) stay suppressed until a successful join or manager rebuild; other failures get bounded exponential backoff. Voice-state events during the wait return early without a join attempt, and a one-shot scheduler job rechecks the room when the wait expires so an idle room still recovers. Each failure logs one warning naming the next retry; skipped events log nothing. Cancelled joins and shutdown are not counted as failures.

Not changed here: GPT-Live error redaction (separate follow-up), and plain (non-`whenOccupied`) auto-join still retries only on gateway Ready/Resumed, now subject to the same backoff.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `extensions/discord/src/voice/voice-auto-join.test.ts` use fake timers through the plugin scheduler:
  - transient realtime startup failure: the bot's own leave and another member's update do not rejoin; retry happens at exactly 5 s, then 10 s, and the third attempt connects.
  - Discord `Missing Access` on channel lookup: no further lookups across voice-state updates and an hour of time; an explicit `join` afterwards succeeds.
- Red on base `364c0d4` (runtime file reverted, tests kept): both new tests fail (`joinVoiceChannel` called 3 times instead of 1; `fetchChannel` called 3 times instead of once).
- Green with the fix: `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/voice/voice-auto-join.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 10/10 passed; wall time 41 s cold (Vitest duration 38.1 s, mostly transform; tests themselves ~20 ms), 9 s warm.
- Sibling voice/autoJoin consumers: `manager.ready-listener`, `transcripts-capture`, `transcripts-readiness`, `transcripts-target`, `voice-following`, `voice-receive`, `voice-runtime.e2e`, `voice-runtime.secret-owner.e2e`, `voice-session.lifecycle`, `voice-session.promotion`, `voice-occupancy`, `monitor/provider.lifecycle` → 12 files, 217 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `tsgo -p extensions/discord/tsconfig.json` reports no errors in changed files (its only error is an existing test-support import outside that config's scope); `run-oxlint` on both changed files clean, `oxfmt --check` on all changed files clean.
- Local autoreview (helper `source-sha256:d2b2d03f…`, default Codex engine), branch mode `origin/main` `364c0d4` → `f6afb3d`, max priority P1, with `voice-runtime.ts`, `listeners.ts`, and the scheduler sources as context: scoped-clean, no findings. The reviewer did not execute tests.
- Not run: live Discord e2e against a real guild. The live Team Gateway and its config were intentionally left untouched; the incident timeline above comes from its logs.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7f538e07-7436-4691-aa09-77db4d1d11f9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/eef0742d-1019-47a6-b670-e6f8990c6b99)

## Worked on by

- @jalehman

prs.title: feat(telegram): roll Telegram's native dice from the message tool
prs.body:
Closes #137110

## What Problem This Solves

An OpenClaw bot cannot take part in a Telegram dice roll. Sending 🎲 as text posts a static
emoji: no animation, no roll, no value. Telegram's `sendDice` is the only way for a bot to
trigger the real thing, and it was unreachable — the message tool exposed no action for it.

The distinction matters because Telegram picks the outcome server-side. Nobody in the chat,
agent or operator, can influence or fake it, so a roll everyone watches land is credible in a
way a number the agent typed is not.

## Why This Change Was Made

`dice` joins the core action vocabulary with target mode `to` and no conversation read — it
is an outbound send to an explicit target. That vocabulary is closed by design ("Plugins add
names through a core PR; runtime registration is intentionally unsupported",
`src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts`), so a third-party plugin cannot add this and
the core entry is the intended path.

Scoped tool schemas prune parameters the selected actions do not use and merge the surviving
groups into one flat object. Dice therefore gets its own `diceEmoji` key rather than reusing
the reaction group's `emoji`: sharing that name would retitle the reaction parameter for
`react` whenever both actions are enabled. The group is also part of the full schema, so the
six faces are advertised in both scoped and unscoped tool surfaces.

The Telegram runtime wraps `sendDice` and returns `messageId`, `chatId`, `emoji` and the
rolled `value` in the same tool result, so the agent learns the outcome without a second
round-trip. Input is validated against Telegram's documented allowlist before the API call,
after stripping the emoji presentation selector (⚽️ vs ⚽) the same way the plugin's reaction
path does — that form is what most keyboards and models emit.

No new configuration key. Dice rides the existing `sendMessage` gate: permission to post in a
chat already governs it, and a roll is an ordinary outbound message to a chat the bot may
already post in, so a dedicated toggle would guard nothing. `sticker` is gated because it also
enables `sticker-search`, which reads external sticker packs; dice has no such surface, which
puts it with `edit`, `delete`, `reactions` and `topic-create` — all enabled without a toggle.
Disabling `channels.telegram.actions.sendMessage` withdraws dice too, and a test asserts that.

Accepted tradeoff: the returned `emoji` echoes the validated request rather than
`result.dice.emoji`. Telegram's contract returns the requested face, and reading it back
would add a branch for a state the API does not produce; the rolled `value`, which the API
alone decides, is read from the response.

Inbound dice are a separate defect and ship in their own PR (#137112); this one is outbound
only.

Opened so the product decision on #137110 has a concrete diff to judge rather than a
description. The gate shape here follows the recommendation in that issue's review — dice under
the existing send gate, no new configuration key. If maintainers decide against the capability,
closing this costs nothing.
`sticker` and `poll` have `openclaw message` subcommands and `dice` does not; CLI parity
is a small follow-up rather than part of this change, since most action names have no
subcommand either.

## User Impact

Telegram operators can have their agent roll Telegram's native animated dice — 🎲 🎯 🏀 ⚽ 🎳 🎰 —
and act on the result in the same turn, with no configuration to discover or enable. Operators
who have disabled Telegram sending are unaffected: dice is withdrawn along with `send`.

## Evidence

- **Live**: run on a live gateway against a real Telegram bot.
  `{"action":"dice","diceEmoji":"🎲"}` returned
  `{"ok":true,"messageId":"944","emoji":"🎲","value":6}`, a real animated roll landed in the
  chat, and the agent reported the value in the same turn with no chat re-read between the
  call and the reply. The model picked the `diceEmoji` key unprompted, from the schema
  description alone. That run predates the gate change below; the send-gate coupling is
  covered by a test rather than by that session.
- **Live**: ⚽ with the presentation selector (`U+26BD U+FE0F`) was accepted and reached
  `sendDice` as the bare face, returning `{"emoji":"⚽","value":1}`. That form was rejected
  before this change.
- **Live**: the stale-key case behaves as documented — `{"action":"dice","emoji":"🎯"}` with
  no `diceEmoji` rolls 🎲, since `emoji` remains a legal key belonging to reactions in the
  same flattened object. This is why the separate key is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
- **Live, earlier revision**: an earlier form of this action ran for a week on a live
  instance before the rename and the selector handling.
- `pnpm check:changed` — exit 0 (oxlint 0 errors, `tsgo:all`, assertion/max-lines ratchets,
  Knip dead-export scan, import cycles, plugin boundaries, generated-metadata check).
- `pnpm test:extension telegram` — exit 0.
- `pnpm test:contracts:channels` — 13 files, 32 tests passed.
- Focused: dice send tests (default face, all six faces, presentation selector, rejection
  before the API call, missing dice payload) and schema-scoping tests, including a regression
  test that `emoji` keeps its reaction description when `react` and `dice` are both in scope.
- Gate coupling: `ties dice availability to the send gate` asserts dice is offered under an
  ordinary config and withdrawn when `channels.telegram.actions.sendMessage` is `false`.
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — exit 0 as its own job, confirming the generated bundled
  channel metadata matches the schemas now that no dice key exists.
- `autoreview` (skill) — `scoped-clean`, no accepted findings.

Note on the telegram lane: three cases in `bot/body-helpers.inbound.test.ts` (inline-code
whitespace normalization) fail on this branch, and they fail identically on a clean
`upstream/main` checkout with the file byte-identical to upstream. They are unrelated to dice —
not Node-version specific (same on 24.20.0 and 26.8.1) and not locale specific (same under
`C.UTF-8`). Nothing in this PR touches that file or its subject.




## v2

Rebased onto current `main` first: `annotateSourceDelivery` was refactored there after the
review, which absorbed part of the second repair and made the rest smaller.

- `dice` is declared `GUARDED_ACTION` in `CHANNEL_MESSAGE_ACTION_DEFINITIONS`
  (`src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts`), so a roll addressed by `to` clears the same
  cross-context check as every other recipient-visible send. As a plain targeted action it
  carried no `crossContext` fact, and the guard returns early for such actions, which is why the
  gap was silent rather than a build error. Deliberately not `"marker"`: that decoration writes
  into `params.message`, which dice never sends.
- A successful roll now sets `messageToolOnlySourceReplyDelivered`. The fact was neither
  produced nor trusted, so the repair has two halves:
  - Produced: `source-reply-mirror.ts` carried the "which actions address their conversation by
    target" rule twice — once inside `isCurrentSourceConversation`, once in the `default` arm of
    `isDeliveredCurrentSourceReply`, where it compared `params.action` raw while the switch head
    compared it normalized. Both now read one `TARGET_ADDRESSED_ACTION_NAMES` set that includes
    `dice`, since a roll addresses its conversation by target exactly like a send. Net zero
    production lines in that file (+11/-11), one duplicate policy gone. Transcript mirroring
    shares the predicate and needs no second gate: a roll carries no text or media, so it drops
    out on the existing empty-payload check.
  - Trusted: `isDeliveredMessageToolOnlySourceReplyResult`
    (`src/agents/embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.ts`) re-derived eligibility from an
    action-name list (`["reply", "thread-reply", "poll"]` plus the send names) even when the
    producer had already recorded the route, so it still rejected dice after the marking landed.
    It now reads the recorded fact. This is more permissive in exactly one direction: a result
    the producer stamped `current-source` is trusted regardless of action name, and only results
    that passed the target comparison carry that stamp — nothing that did not deliver visible
    content to this conversation can reach it. The `allowExplicitSourceRoute` path, where no such
    stamp exists, still requires the name list.
- Mirrorable payload eligibility is now separate from current-source delivery classification.
  The message tool's argument object is flat, so `{action: "dice", message: "You rolled a six"}`
  passes validation; Telegram ignores `message`, but `mirrorDeliveredSourceReplyToTranscript`
  reads text and media straight out of `actionParams` and would have recorded assistant text no
  recipient ever saw. A `MIRRORABLE_SOURCE_ACTION_NAMES` set (currently `send` alone) gates the
  mirror, while `TARGET_ADDRESSED_ACTION_NAMES` keeps covering delivery classification. The same
  hole already existed for `poll` — its params can carry `message` too — so the regressions cover
  dice text, dice media and poll text; all three fail without the gate.
  Both halves are in core rather than in `extensions/telegram/src/channel-actions.ts` where the
  finding was reported: a channel plugin cannot classify itself into a core delivery decision,
  and the classification has to hold for any channel that grows an equivalent send.
- `silent` is read in the dice handler and forwarded to `sendDiceTelegram`, matching the schema
  the action already advertises.

Named follow-up, not changed here: `sticker` is likewise absent from `MESSAGE_TOOL_SEND_ACTIONS`
and the reply-name list, so it does not set `messageToolOnlySourceReplyDelivered` either. Whether
that is the same gap or deliberate — a sticker may not answer the question, so the fallback reply
is wanted — is a product call this PR does not make. Stickers behave exactly as before.

### Dependency contract

The review recorded that it could not inspect the `sendDice` contract (dependency sources absent,
DNS blocked). From the installed tree:

- `grammy@1.46.0`, `node_modules/grammy/out/core/api.d.ts:470` —
  `sendDice(chat_id: number | string, emoji: … | "🎲" | "🎯" | "🏀" | "⚽" | "🎳" | "🎰", other?, signal?): Promise<Message.DiceMessage>`.
- `@grammyjs/types@5.0.0`, `methods.d.ts:927-935` — payload is `chat_id`, `message_thread_id?`,
  `emoji?` restricted to the same six faces, and `disable_notification?`, which is what `silent`
  maps to. This is the upstream source of both the allowlist and the silent option.
- `@grammyjs/types@5.0.0`, `message.d.ts:878-883` — `Dice` is `{ emoji: string; value: number }`,
  with value ranges documented as 1-6 for 🎲 🎯 🎳, 1-5 for 🏀 ⚽ and 1-64 for 🎰. The roll is
  server-decided, which is why `value` is read from the response while `emoji` echoes the
  validated request.

### v2 evidence

- Regressions, each verified by reverting its own fix and rerunning:
  - cross-context denial for `dice` (`src/infra/outbound/outbound-policy.test.ts`) — without the
    policy entry: `expected [Function run] to throw an error`.
  - current-source marking for a target-addressed send
    (`src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.reply-action.test.ts`, plus the negative case
    for another conversation) — without the set entry:
    `expected { ok: true, …(2) } to match object { sourceReplyRoute: 'current-source' }`.
  - the classifier accepting a recorded route it does not enumerate by name
    (`src/agents/embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.test.ts`, plus the unconfirmed negative)
    — without the fix: `expected false to be true`.
  - `silent` forwarded to `sendDiceTelegram` (`extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.test.ts`)
    — without the fix: `expected undefined to be true`.
- `pnpm check:changed` — exit 0.
- `pnpm tsgo` — exit 0.
- Vitest over `src/infra/outbound`, `src/agents/tools`, both source-reply suites,
  `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts` and `extensions/telegram` — the only failures are
  the three pre-existing `body-helpers.inbound.test.ts` whitespace cases noted above. Both that
  test and the module it covers are byte-identical to `upstream/main` on this branch.
- `autoreview` (skill) — `scoped-clean`, no accepted findings.

Repair commit alone: production +20/-9 (net +11), tests and test support +114/-3. The
`source-reply-mirror.ts` half is net-neutral (+11/-7 replacing a duplicated action list with one
set). Whole branch versus `main`: production +181/-10, tests +274/-3, docs +16/-1.

The branch is a linear series of six commits on current `main`, with no merge commits; each
rebase is recorded in the PR conversation with its conflicts and checks.

### Live proof

Captured against a real Telegram bot on `dfa0fb6`, an earlier head of this branch. Later
revisions rebased and compressed it without changing the behaviour on the proven paths. The run used a gateway built from this
branch, agent model `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`. Chat identifiers are redacted as `<chat-a>` (the
conversation the run is bound to) and `<chat-b>` (a different configured chat).

**Cross-context egress.** With `tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinProvider: false`, a
direct message-tool call from the session bound to `<chat-a>`:

```
toolCall   message {"action":"dice","target":"telegram:<chat-b>","diceEmoji":"🎲"}
toolResult Cross-context messaging denied: action=dice target="telegram:<chat-b>"
           while bound to "telegram:<chat-a>" (channel=telegram).
```

Nothing reached `<chat-b>`. Before this change `dice` carried no `crossContext` fact, so the
guard returned before it ever compared targets.

**Terminal delivery.** With `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, a roll in the bound
conversation:

```
toolCall   message {"action":"dice","diceEmoji":"🎲","final":true}
toolResult {"ok":true,"messageId":"…","emoji":"🎲","value":4,
            "sourceReplyRoute":"current-source"}
```

`sourceReplyRoute: "current-source"` is the marking this PR adds; the operator observed
exactly one message in the chat — the animated roll — with no fallback text after it.

**Silent.** The call carried the option and the roll was delivered:

```
toolCall   message {"action":"dice","diceEmoji":"🎲","silent":true}
```

The forwarding is covered by the sender-boundary regression above and by
`extensions/telegram/src/send-special.ts:183`, which maps `silent` to the
`disable_notification` field `@grammyjs/types` declares for `sendDice`.

An earlier attempt at the cross-context case did not exercise the guard: the model routed
around it with `sessions_send`, asking the session already bound to `<chat-b>` to roll in its
own conversation, where no cross-context target exists. The proof above is the direct call.

prs.title: fix: dashboard handoff stops after one document timeout
prs.body:
Closes #183682

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: first-run onboarding abandons the dashboard when one local document request times out, even though the Gateway is already running.

## User Impact

User impact: a transient two-second dashboard timeout is retried before onboarding gives up. If the dashboard still does not respond, the Gateway stays up and the printed dashboard URL remains the way to open it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared document check treated a thrown request error as final. The reported Windows log showed one fetch timeout after Gateway ready, then "The browser handoff did not finish." Timeout errors now get two more attempts. Other request failures still stop immediately, and a timeout that keeps happening still fails instead of waiting out the asset-build deadline.

## Evidence

- On current main, a `TimeoutError` followed by HTTP 200 `text/html` returned not ready with "request timed out". The same case passes after this change.
- `pnpm test src/commands/control-ui-handoff.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed, 14 tests, about 62s wall on this host. Most of that was worker startup; the new cases were a few milliseconds.
- Onboarding, dashboard, and wizard callers of the same check passed: `pnpm test src/commands/onboard-browser-handoff.test.ts src/commands/onboard-quickstart-host.test.ts src/commands/dashboard.test.ts src/commands/dashboard/json.test.ts src/wizard/setup.finalize.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (3 shards, about 44s).
- A hanging local server, fetched through the real document probe, threw `TimeoutError` with message "request timed out".
- Changed-file format, lint, and core typecheck passed. `pnpm check:changed` later failed an existing unused-export scan in files this PR does not change.
- Native Windows foreground onboarding was not rerun.

prs.title: fix(compaction): preserve active request provenance
prs.body:
## Problem

Compaction could replace the active human request with a later internal observation, or revive completed human work during an independent internal run. The first revision also rejected a second recovery after the production semantic-window reader archived the original admitted request.

## Solution

- Carry the admitted request boundary from the runtime through AgentSession into core compaction, with explicit unresolved/none/legacy-inference selection.
- Centralize recorded-source attribution for summary input, preserved excerpts, and token accounting. Clear stale generated pending asks without rewriting unrelated summary sections.
- When a **processed** request is outside the current semantic window, reuse the existing bounded checkpoint request. Newer human steering wins; internal updates preserve that request or authoritative none. Missing **unprocessed** admitted input still rejects.
- Reuse the existing compaction checkpoint; no new persisted state, configuration, or schema. Replace the redundant in-memory mapping test with persisted, repeated-recovery coverage.

This is an independent remediation related to #178477, with credit to @dmitryvostryakov for the original report and implementation. Request provenance remains separate from general model-quality concerns.

## Verification

- **Base red:** all three repeated-recovery cases fail at `a085f281e904` with `invalid_session: Compaction cannot find the admitted request.` on the second recovery.
- **Candidate green:** 76 tests across core request scope/provenance, registered safeguard, AgentSession small-context and persisted boundary recovery, runtime/session-rotation recovery, and stable tool prefixes.
- New persisted boundary cases reopen through production `SessionManager.openAsync(..., { compaction: true })`, verify the original request is absent, and complete a second automatic compaction: human request survives internal updates; internal selection remains none; newer human steering supersedes the old request. Missing pending input still rejects.
- Focused batch: 223.38s including cold compilation. New three-case test bodies: 3.25s total; CI duration pending.

prs.title: fix: queued messages stay pending after a Gateway crash
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accepted queued messages remaining pending forever after the Gateway is forcibly killed. Their text stayed in storage, but history hid them and their receipts never reported a terminal outcome.

## User Impact

Startup exposes these messages through the existing cancelled-send recovery notice, retaining their text so users can review and resend them. Crash input is not resumed automatically. No schema, index, configuration, or UI surface changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing startup owner discovers orphan candidates once per physical store through the pending-input worker. One Kysely query returns distinct current `(sessionKey, sessionId)` pairs with unconsumed queued input from an earlier lifecycle, excluding the exact queued IDs already held by graceful-restart markers. Only those pairs enter the existing withdrawal writer; empty sessions never cause a settlement round-trip. Discovery targets are deduplicated using the inventory's physical database path.

The withdrawal writer rereads the current marker in its transaction and rechecks lifecycle/state predicates before setting the existing cancelled state. Current-lifecycle input and exact graceful marker inputs retain custody. Repeated startup leaves cancelled input unchanged; consumed input is excluded. Per-session failures warn without preventing settlement of other candidates.

This keeps reconciliation out of ordinary history reads and reuses existing history, receipt, and recovery presentation contracts. Legacy interrupted rows remain inert. Settlement failures preserve stored text for a later startup.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: for 20 sessions without pending input plus one session with a crashed queued input, startup performs one store discovery and settles only the crashed-input session; repeating startup performs another single discovery and zero additional settlements. Counts are the performance metric; no production startup latency claim is made.

| Work | Previous PR head | Updated head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First-startup settlement calls | 21 | 1 |
| Settlement calls for the 20 empty sessions | 20 | 0 |
| Discovery calls per startup | — | 1 |
| Additional settlements on repeated startup | not measured | 0 |

The work-count assertion failed on previous head `19a8ae40c290844fe103eb4055586770c094f5e8`: expected 1 settlement call, received 21. The original visible-outcome regression was red on base because the crashed input receipt lacked `cancelled: true`.

`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the canonical in-memory SQLite schema, with and without marker exclusions:

```text
SCAN pending USING INDEX idx_agent_session_pending_inputs_session
SEARCH node USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_session_nodes_1 (session_key=?)
```

The query scans the existing pending-input index once; it does not scan all session nodes or issue per-session queries. Marker exclusions use the existing bound string-set helper. No new index is needed.

Final local proof on the tree committed as `537dc7577d1c689b5a5a8efa38f8856817f3c0ba`:

- `nice -n 5 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-restart-resume.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-pending-input-history.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-pending-input-withdrawal.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-pending-input-dismissal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **25 passed**, two shards in **87.77 seconds wall** including compilation. Startup file: 5 passed, 52.60 seconds wall, about 17 seconds test execution on a loaded host; config shard: 20 passed, 29.79 seconds wall. CI seconds pending.
- `nice -n 5 node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --incremental`: passed.
- `nice -n 5 node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-root.json --incremental`: passed.
- Focused `run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`, `pnpm exec oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent local Codex autoreview of the coordinator repair at P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Original visible-outcome change also passed independent review.
- Lint initially found the new dispatch branch would exceed the transcript worker's line cap (707/700); the operation now uses the existing history-read dispatcher alongside other pending-input reads. No limit or baseline changed.

Simplification: removed the per-session startup sweep; retained one pending-input discovery operation and the existing settlement owner. The complete PR is production **+177**, tests **-1**, docs **+1**; **11 files, 270 insertions, 93 deletions**, net **+177**. This follow-up alone is production **+124**, tests **+14**, net **+138**. The test-line ceiling remains net negative.

The regression exercises real startup discovery and worker-backed storage with synthetic state. No fresh real-model SIGKILL campaign, live Gateway, browser campaign, or large-history startup benchmark was run. The earlier native preparation belongs to the previous head; no updated native merge attempt or auto-merge was armed. Coordinator owns the final admin merge.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

**Before reclaim — worker is Attached**

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

**After reclaim — worker moved to Recent worker history as Destroyed**

![Systems sidebar showing the reclaimed worker as destroyed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee681765-dd7b-4cad-adf6-0708837275eb)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).
  - `pnpm test:changed`: 20,926 pass / 3 skip; one unrelated `shell-viewport.test.ts` RAF-coalescing assertion failed under the full parallel lane, then passed 3/3 isolated reruns (11/11 each).
  - Upstream `control-ui-performance`: pass. The local check showed a nondeterministic gzip edge 24–30 B over the 373,454 B startup limit while raw startup JS stayed exactly 1,208,683 B with and without the Systems reconciliation helper, confirming this patch does not change the startup asset set.
  - Repo autoreview helper was attempted but unavailable because its local Codex credential returned HTTP 401; no review verdict was produced.

The two older `Destroying` rows visible in the screenshots predate this worker and are a separate provider-history cleanup issue.

prs.title: fix(gateway): release the account start gate after minimal startup
prs.body:
Fixes #187073.

## What Problem This Solves

`server-runtime-state-prepare.ts` always gives the channel manager `deferStartupAccountStartsUntil: startupAccountStarts.promise`, and every explicit account start waits on it. The only release is `onChannelsStarted`, which `server-startup-finish.ts` passes to the post-attach sidecar startup. **Minimal test Gateways** (`OPENCLAW_TEST_MINIMAL_GATEWAY=1`) skip those sidecars, so the gate never opens. An explicit `channels.start` then reports a hand-off while the provider never starts and never receives the Gateway approval runtime. The startup-order gate came from #186857.

## User Impact

This affects test infrastructure only; production startup is unchanged. The real-Gateway fixtures for manual account recovery and approval forwarding work again in minimal mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Successful minimal startup now releases the existing gate. The release sits in the same `if (minimalTestGateway)` branch that already resolves `databasePreparationReady`.
- Full startup keeps its preparation boundary, because there the gate is still released only by `onChannelsStarted`.
- Cancellation and close still prevent provider startup. After the gate, `server-channels.ts` waits with the start's abort signal (`waitForDeferredAccountStart(…, abort.signal)`) and re-checks `startCancelled()` before invoking the provider.
- The account manager's shared wait is not bypassed, as ClawSweeper recommended, so the #186857 ordering protection stays intact.

## Evidence

The reported fixtures are the regression tests, so this PR adds no test lines. Each one starts a real minimal Gateway and explicitly starts configured accounts with `channels.start`.

![test run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/187073/proof-187073.png)

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server.approval-forwarding.test.ts src/gateway/server.channels-start-outcomes.test.ts` (Windows 11, Node 26.12.1):

| case | main `4a2a1962d9c` | this branch `bfd67ecbbb4` |
|---|---|---|
| starts config-backed accounts manually while breaker suppression remains active | **fail** (21.7 s) | pass (5.7 s) |
| reports skips and in-flight ownership while manual recovery bypasses the breaker | **fail** (125 s, timed out) | pass (4.4 s) |
| uses the owning native runtime and destination account for approval forwarding | **fail** (25.7 s) | pass (12.8 s) |

This matches the issue's native remote run: all three cases failed on main. oxlint, core `tsgo` and `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` are clean.

The sibling suites `server-startup*.test.ts`, `server.channels*.test.ts` and `server-channels*.test.ts` (42 files) were also run on this branch: 314 passed, 1 skipped, and 2 failed. The 2 failures, `server-startup-config.secrets.test.ts` ("uses the activation env when publishing persisted startup auth") and `server-startup-post-ready.test.ts` ("holds post-ready maintenance until deferred startup settles"), fail identically on main with this change reverted, so they are already failing on Windows. One more file reported a file-level failure with no failing test; my filtered output did not name it, so it is not attributed here.

prs.body:
## Why

A successful `sessions_yield` can render as **Interrupted** and lose its public acknowledgment when a plugin appends text after the yield receipt. Separately, the resume label relied on `uppercase`/`capitalize` CSS. That CSS turned duration units like `9m 32s` into `9M 32S` and also changed the casing of localized units.

## What changed

- The private `readYieldReceipt` helper now treats a structured status as authoritative. If there is no structured status, only a valid leading JSON object counts as the receipt. A JSON example later in the appended text is ignored.
- Confirmation and the public acknowledgment now use the same selected receipt, so they can't disagree.
- The English resume label now gets its title case from the copy in three keys, not from CSS transforms. Localized duration units keep their native casing.

## Scope

- Private-context filtering, genuine aborts and the GitHub handoff work as before.
- After integrating upstream, paused-child behavior is unchanged: child count, order, links, the quiet note and actual navigation.
- CI repair integrates the already-landed idle-render measurement fix (#187003) and moves the pointer off the previous sidebar control before approaching the next header, so a lingering shortcut tooltip cannot intercept it. The whole-file sidebar audit also adds complete agent-row and Show all outcome assertions.
- No settings, Gateway, API, dependency or permission changes.

## Tradeoffs

Until the normal post-merge locale refresh, other locales show English for the three changed keys. This PR does not modify translated locale files.

## Blast Radius

This only affects how yielded and resumed turns render: the Interrupted state, the public acknowledgment and the resume label.

## Verification

The published CI-repair head is `27f732c`. Its independent exact-commit review is complete, and native preparation and publication passed. Fresh CI run [40788332022](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40788332022) passed on that exact head, including production and test types, all planned UI E2E shards and security-fast. After strengthening the sidebar assertions, that complete five-case file passed again: 8.815s test time, 56.54s harness time, 98.419s command wall time, including a 17.79s build. Real browser interaction is required for native tab gestures, pointer hit-testing, keyboard focus and menu navigation.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes shutdowns that remain blocked in native wrapper cleanup after the bounded Gateway close has finished, and maintenance handoffs that can expire before the native service stop.

## User Impact

Process-owned shutdown respects its existing cleanup deadline and identifies retained sidecar owners. Embedded hosts still join cleanup fully. Subagent termination finishes its internal cleanup after admission closes, and the deployment controller commits shutdown before stopping the service.

## Why This Change Was Made

The wrapper now bounds read-only-worker and Linux admission/broker cleanup with the process owner's existing deadline, while the underlying ordered cleanup continues. Fatal core close errors survive an additional cleanup timeout. Existing shutdown tracing supplies sidecar names; no new shutdown subsystem, configuration, dependencies, or persisted shapes are introduced.

The controller uses the existing `commit: true` handoff after its live custody checks, including READY suspensions, and stops polling the retired reversible lease. The public armed-only RPC contract remains supported. Native watchdog budgets are unchanged: the 90-second supervisor case reserves five seconds and adds a two-second watchdog grace, targeting 87 seconds after accepted signal handling. Worker startup latency remains an unproven source of drift; this change does not promise native handle extinction.

## Evidence

- Base-red regressions: wrapper close remained pending past the injected deadline; held sidecar errors omitted the owner; closed admission skipped synthetic attachment cleanup; controller handoffs omitted commitment or rejected committed acknowledgement.
- Node focused tests: wrapper 9/9; shutdown diagnostics/runtime 4/4; subagent worker 21/21. Wrapper's last run took 39.86s wall (mostly compiled native fixtures); subagent/shutdown test time stayed below five seconds per file.
- Controller custody 27/27; focused handoff/source-stop ordering 7/7. Linux/root-only controller cases were skipped on macOS; full installed-controller activation was unavailable in this isolated environment.
- `test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts`: PASS, 63.07s test time. Busy SIGTERM shutdown 475ms; committed maintenance shutdown 583ms. Proves graceful resume, FIFO delivery, and intentionally lossy SIGKILL handling through isolated Gateway processes and a synthetic provider.
