## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session menu rows render taller and wider-inset than designed (33 px rows, 13 px insets, icons and labels out of line with their neighbors) in the chat header menu, the browser-tab card menu, sidebar session submenus such as Move to group, Snooze, and Advanced, and the Systems filter menu.

## User Impact

Session menus use their compact 28 px rows with 8 px insets again on every route, so icons, labels, chevrons, and shortcut badges line up the way they did on chat routes before 2026-10-25. Plain menus keep the default overlay padding, and the performance budgets are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`.session-menu__item` (startup stylesheet) and the overlay primitive's `.oc-menu-item` (a later boot chunk) set `padding` at equal specificity, so whichever sheet loaded last won. Chat routes used to win only because a duplicate copy of `session-menu.css` rode in the chat chunk. #183909 removed that duplicate for the CSS budget, and from then on the overlay default won everywhere except direct children of `.session-menu__panel`, which had their own higher-specificity patch.

The overlay now reads its padding from `--oc-menu-item-padding-block` / `--oc-menu-item-padding-inline` (the inline variable already positioned its check and submenu icons), and session-menu rows set those variables. The tie now resolves to the same value whichever sheet loads last, so load order no longer matters and the panel-only patch is gone. Caller overrides that already beat the overlay, such as the side panel type menu's `9px 8px`, are untouched, because nothing gained specificity.

Accepted, unchanged from current `main`: hover background (`--surface-hover`), disabled opacity (0.5), and `text-align: start` on these rows still come from the overlay. Before #183909 the chat-route copy also overrode those (`--bg-hover`, 0.42, `left`); `main` has used the overlay values on every route since then, and this PR keeps them.

## Evidence

**Before (`main`) / after (this PR)**, production builds, mock Gateway, dark theme:

| | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat header session menu | ![chat header menu on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/305e14e7-80eb-4d19-b4c4-50d6fac0810d) | ![chat header menu with fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/290844d7-c90e-4f12-930e-0d11bceef05b) |
| Browser-tab card menu | ![browser tab menu on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66121997-b7e5-45ed-935a-81c9c3134ce0) | ![browser tab menu with fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20f8d74d-3e5b-4c21-9194-1cf0da886e96) |
| Sidebar row menu on `/new` (non-chat route), Move to group open | ![sidebar row menu on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c3192db-6e84-4f18-a991-529ab49b1f59) | ![sidebar row menu with fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21118142-b0a0-41df-b28c-626b78fbb9c7) |
| Systems filter menu (`.sidebar-session-sort-menu__item` rows) | ![systems filter menu on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b1fe96a-b74e-49c8-8b90-d6e01063bf69) | ![systems filter menu with fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/429bb7a6-cea9-4e9a-9187-635987e104c2) |

- **Computed-style parity:** three production builds served by `startBuiltControlUiE2eServer` with an identical mock Gateway: `main`, this PR, and `main` with the two #183909 imports restored (the pre-10-25 chat look). Each build gets a full `getComputedStyle` of every light-DOM element across 20 states: `/new` idle, sidebar row menu, row submenu, and Filter & sort; chat idle, browser-tab menu, row menu and submenu, header menu and submenu, and Filter & sort; the Systems filter menu; plus hover states. A `main` vs `main` run shows 0 diffs.
  - This PR vs the pre-10-25 chat look: no geometry differences in any chat state, and the browser-tab menu and row submenu crops are pixel-identical. The only remaining diffs are the new custom property and the three overlay-owned values listed above, which match `main`.
  - This PR vs `main`: the only changed declarations are padding, plus the row and menu sizes that follow from it, on `oc-menu-item` elements that also carry `session-menu__item` or `sidebar-session-sort-menu__item` (13px → 8px inline, 6.5px → 0 block). `/new` idle and both Filter & sort states show 0 diffs.
- **Regression test:** `overlay-style.browser.test.tsx` loads `session-menu.css` before the overlay, matching production order. It fails on `main` (`6.5px 13px`) and passes here. It also checks that plain menu rows keep `0.5em 1em`.
- **Budgets:** `pnpm ui:check-performance:base cf77199afb2d…` passes with no violations and no budget changes: total CSS gzip 308,098 → 308,111 B (+13 B, fixed ceiling 308,298 B), raw +45 B, startup CSS +3 B, Chat and New boot CSS +13 B each, request counts unchanged. The duplicate-import deletion itself already landed in #183909.
- `oxfmt`, `stylelint`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` are clean. Browser suites pass: `overlay-style` (11), `menu-native-contract`, `menu-surface`, `shortcut-badges`, and `cursor-policy` (4 files, 55 tests), plus both `browser-tab-card` suites (46).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI runs through OpenClaw use up the Claude subscription 5-hour window about 1.8x faster than needed, because `claude -p` identifies as `sdk-cli` (anthropics/claude-code#97074). Weekly limits are not affected.

## User Impact

User impact: the same Claude CLI work uses about 45% less of the 5-hour window.

## Why This Change Was Made

`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` was cleared from the child env, so the CLI fell back to `sdk-cli`. This sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=openclaw` in the `claude-cli` backend `env` and removes it from `CLAUDE_CLI_CLEAR_ENV`, so the backend value is not filtered out. Two small edits: `extensions/anthropic/cli-backend.ts`, `extensions/anthropic/cli-constants.ts`.

## Evidence

Same prompts, no prompt cache, alternating order, `claude-opus-5-5`, Claude Code 2.1.310, Claude Max 20x subscription:

| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` | Calls that fit in 1% of the 5-hour window |
|---|---|
| unset (`sdk-cli` / `sdk-ts`, current) | 14–15 |
| any other label (here `t3-code`) | 25–27 (about 1.8x) |

I did not measure the interactive `cli` entrypoint myself; reports in #97074 put it at the same rate as a custom label. Other users reproduced the effect with their own benchmarks (links below). The same change is open in T3 Code: pingdotgg/t3code#25597. I read the env path in `src/agents/cli-runner/execution-env.ts` but did not run the tests or the CLI through OpenClaw, so please check the node-host path (`CLAUDE_NODE_CLEAR_ENV`), which I left unchanged.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reuse sidebar row UTF-8 sizes
prs.body:
Related: #186840

## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing sidebar pages still rescans unchanged packed row JSON for UTF-8 sizing after the row prefix has already been prepared. For conditional replies, that can flatten large strings for full rows that are never sent.

## User Impact

Reduces allocation while preparing session-list replies during sidebar churn. Response bytes, viewer authorization, redaction, and row revisions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the immutable JSON prefix and its UTF-8 size with the existing one-layout-per-row packing record. Only numeric shared-fact indexes change between equal layouts, so their ASCII suffix supplies the remaining byte count. The row serialization owner carries that size into array registration, removing repeated byte scans. Prefixes retire with their row/layout and their backing-string bytes are included in the existing retention budget.

This is a residual after #186840, which is present in the profiled build. No additional viewer cache or authorization shortcut is introduced. Runtime code grows by 33 lines to carry exact sizes and preserve conservative retention accounting. The non-test diff is +45 lines including the benchmark (+12); tests add 31 net lines.

## Evidence

Acceptance declared before measurement: exact packed JSON digest and expanded row equivalence; lower allocation or CPU; no material controlled regression. Synthetic workload: 10,000 immutable session rows, 500-row pages, 66 interleaved page slots, one changed row per page. Five alternating AB/BA pairs, 3,000 iterations per arm, separate untraced timing and sampled-allocation passes. Full-transmission control included.

| Owner workload (per 500-row page) | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prepare: sampled total allocation | 766,651 B | 578,418 B | −24.6% |
| Prepare: sampled owner allocation | 761,374 B | 573,191 B | −24.7% |
| Prepare: main-thread CPU | 0.854 ms | 0.483 ms | −43.4% |
| Full transmission: total allocation | 989,993 B | 994,829 B | +0.5% |
| Full transmission: main-thread CPU | 0.851 ms | 0.798 ms | −6.2% |

Each cell is the mean of five matched arms (15,000 calls per side per mode). Preparation owner allocation per presented row: 1,523 → 1,146 B. All 40 runs produced the same packed JSON digest. The full-send control shows that most allocation savings apply when full rows are reserved but not transmitted; sending still materializes their bytes.

Untraced GC per page: preparation 0.325 → 0.034 ms; full transmission 0.345 → 0.261 ms. Mean owner latency p99 (3,000 samples/arm): preparation 2.104 → 0.641 ms, full transmission 0.994 → 0.983 ms. Mean event-loop p99: 5.892 → 2.717 ms and 6.283 → 2.534 ms respectively (1,217–2,101 samples/arm). These are owner-process metrics, not RPC latency. Minor/major GC time per page: prepare 0.102/0.222 → 0.034/0.000 ms; wire 0.148/0.196 → 0.041/0.219 ms. Preparation CPU medians were 0.787 → 0.482 ms; full-send medians were 0.859 → 0.806 ms.

Memory tradeoff: warmed post-GC heap was 240.0 → 233.9 MiB for preparation and 231.6 → 237.9 MiB for full transmission. End-of-run RSS was 1,304 → 1,345 MiB and 1,118 → 1,108 MiB; these terminal RSS values were not forced-GC measurements. The full-send warmed heap increases 6.3 MiB to retain the reusable prefix facts; the existing cache budget includes their backing strings.

<details>
<summary>GC controls, per-arm host load and reproduction</summary>

Maximum GC pauses (base → candidate, ms), paired in launch order:

| Pair | Preparation | Full transmission | Host load, preparation | Host load, full transmission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 688.7 → 2.2 | 353.8 → 345.7 | 15.8 → 14.2 | 10.6 → 10.7 |
| 2 | 597.4 → 7.9 | 152.2 → 170.7 | 13.6 → 15.0 | 10.3 → 11.4 |
| 3 | 615.6 → 2.3 | 350.9 → 330.7 | 12.7 → 11.8 | 9.5 → 8.5 |
| 4 | 729.0 → 1.9 | 147.6 → 346.3 | 13.3 → 11.1 | 7.7 → 8.1 |
| 5 | 706.8 → 2.3 | 342.9 → 167.3 | 16.5 → 14.8 | 7.6 → 7.3 |

Four additional identical-source A/A controls produced maximum pauses of 161.5→378.2, 154.4→426.0, 175.4→401.9, and 389.4→416.1 ms. Three controls trip the 2× max-pause signal on identical code: this short-window max-pause metric is inconclusive, not evidence of candidate harm. No pauses were trimmed. Major collections are context-only: preparation had 1→0/arm; full transmission had 4→4/arm. Minor collection counts were 108–112→62–67 and 100–104→102/arm.

Run the committed `scripts/perf/sidebar-fact-sharing-measure.ts` with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`, `--iterations 3000`, and `--output <result.json>`. Add `--allocations` for the separate sampled pass; add `--transmit` for full replies. Pin base source from `9cd97293eb93e0d445481a08ccbe94d5ae52ce63` with `--owner-file <base-session-row-presentation.ts>` and three `--source-file` options for `session-list-view-cache.ts`, `session-row-serialization.ts`, and `serialized-json.ts`. Basenames must be preserved. Base and candidate alternate AB/BA across five pairs. Node 26.12.1; isolated local synthetic fixtures; no production access.

</details>

The work-count regression interleaves owner/viewer pages and changing fact indexes, including a reused Unicode prefix. It fails on main with 12 redundant UTF-8 scans and passes with zero. Existing tests cover changing viewer roles, row modes, exact serialized frames, delta application, eviction, and collection of replaced rows.

Focused validation: 34 tests across five presentation/serialization/delta/retention files passed; four cache-accounting tests passed. Root test typechecks and gateway-root test typecheck passed. The final serialization file passed all 10 tests (3 seconds of test work; 39 seconds including compiled fixture setup); the two required import-closure files passed 38 tests. Changed-file lint/format, export collision guard, and test-lines ratchet passed (ceiling unchanged, 7,648 lines of headroom). An initial local fixture build was interrupted by the source-change guard during editing; the completed runs above passed.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean, including the final Unicode regression and benchmark loader correction. The autoreview helper refused its provider-route preflight; no configuration was changed.

Scope: owner measurements, not a whole-Gateway or production claim. This uses the requested FAST PATH for removal of duplicate work; no production load was run. Whole-Gateway CPU, allocation rate, GC s/min, sessions.list latency, and event-loop p99 remain unmeasured for this change.

prs.title: fix(ios): stop dropping photos from multi-photo requests
prs.body:
Closes #186001

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: requesting several recent iPhone photos silently returns fewer photos when their combined size exceeds the old 340 KiB reply budget.

## User Impact

Users can receive the requested batch of up to 20 photos. The existing per-photo size limit and Photos permission checks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the outdated shared budget. The existing limits already keep a batch below 6 MiB of base64 data, leaving room below the native 16 MiB and Gateway 25 MiB transport limits. No new settings, response fields, or pagination.

## Evidence

- **Before/after native regression:** the committed test uses real PhotoKit and synthetic images on a disposable iOS 27.1 simulator. On base `b4c0b92a2fc7`, both requests return 1 photo instead of 2 and 20. With the fix, the test passes in **7.944 seconds**, with no skipped tests. It also checks that the encoded payload stays below 16 MiB.
- **Real CLI/Gateway proof:** an isolated, authenticated Gateway from the same base, the production photo service, and the shared native `GatewayNodeSession` transport. Before: `photos.latest` requests for 2 and 20 both return 1. After: requests for 1, 2, 20, and 99 return **1, 2, 20, and 20**. The 20-photo reply contains 4,734,640 base64 characters; every photo remains below 300 KiB. Gateway health/readiness remain healthy afterward. No model call or real user data was used.
- **Checks:** focused native build/typecheck and XCTest passed; pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and SwiftLint 0.65.1 passed on both changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- **Independent local review:** AutoReview against `b4c0b92a2fc7`, covering the final local change through priority P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

**Proof limits:** native execution used a focused test host compiling the production photo service with the real shared SDK, not the full iOS app UI or a physical iPhone. The integration test is opt-in (`TEST_RUNNER_OPENCLAW_IOS_PHOTOS_INTEGRATION=1`, selector `OpenClawTests/PhotoLibraryServiceTests`); it requires an owned disposable simulator with Photos access granted to the host. Delete that simulator afterward. [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40554488870), including iOS screenshot capture and its evidence check; those CI jobs do not replace the photo-service regression.

Scope: production +3/-9 lines; one 59-line native regression. No unrelated code, dependency, or configuration changes.

<details>
<summary>Captured before/after test and CLI/Gateway output</summary>

Base: `b4c0b92a2fc7a2b4db4b19c33013961b7a77a0c8`. Reviewed fix: `ea695094352dd4312d0cda12215cdf4965899dfb`.

Native test invocation used the focused host described above, the committed test file, and the production photo service:

```sh
TEST_RUNNER_OPENCLAW_IOS_PHOTOS_INTEGRATION=1 xcodebuild test \
  -scheme OpenClaw -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=<owned-simulator>' \
  -parallel-testing-enabled NO \
  -only-testing:OpenClawTests/PhotoLibraryServiceTests
```

Selected execution output (local source paths removed):

```text
BASE
Test Case '-[OpenClawTests.PhotoLibraryServiceTests testLatestReturnsRequestedPhotosBeyondTheOldBatchBudget]' started.
XCTAssertEqual failed: ("1") is not equal to ("2")
XCTAssertEqual failed: ("1") is not equal to ("20")
Test Case '-[OpenClawTests.PhotoLibraryServiceTests testLatestReturnsRequestedPhotosBeyondTheOldBatchBudget]' failed (16.529 seconds).
Executed 1 test, with 4 failures (0 unexpected) in 16.529 (16.551) seconds
** TEST FAILED **

FIXED
Test Case '-[OpenClawTests.PhotoLibraryServiceTests testLatestReturnsRequestedPhotosBeyondTheOldBatchBudget]' passed (7.944 seconds).
Executed 1 test, with 0 failures (0 unexpected) in 7.944 (7.950) seconds
** TEST SUCCEEDED **
```

The CLI commands ran against the isolated authenticated Gateway and the native node. Node identity and the owned simulator identity are replaced with placeholders; no credentials, endpoints, or image contents are included:

```sh
pnpm openclaw nodes invoke --node <paired-node> --command photos.latest \
  --params '{"limit":2,"maxWidth":1600,"quality":0.8}' --invoke-timeout 60000 --json
pnpm openclaw nodes invoke --node <paired-node> --command photos.latest \
  --params '{"limit":20,"maxWidth":1600,"quality":0.8}' --invoke-timeout 60000 --json
# Fixed revision also checked limit=1 and limit=99 with otherwise identical options.
```

Captured CLI JSON responses, summarized without image contents. `rpcOk` is taken from each saved response; all returned images also passed strict base64 decoding and JPEG header/end-marker checks:

```jsonl
{"revision":"base","requested":2,"rpcOk":true,"returned":1,"base64Chars":236732,"maxPhotoChars":236732,"validJpegs":1}
{"revision":"base","requested":20,"rpcOk":true,"returned":1,"base64Chars":236732,"maxPhotoChars":236732,"validJpegs":1}
{"revision":"fixed","requested":1,"rpcOk":true,"returned":1,"base64Chars":236732,"maxPhotoChars":236732,"validJpegs":1}
{"revision":"fixed","requested":2,"rpcOk":true,"returned":2,"base64Chars":473464,"maxPhotoChars":236732,"validJpegs":2}
{"revision":"fixed","requested":20,"rpcOk":true,"returned":20,"base64Chars":4734640,"maxPhotoChars":236732,"validJpegs":20}
{"revision":"fixed","requested":99,"rpcOk":true,"returned":20,"base64Chars":4734640,"maxPhotoChars":236732,"validJpegs":20}
```

Matching successful Gateway transport log samples, with connection/request identifiers removed:

```text
BASE
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ node.invoke 1662ms bytes=483556
FIXED
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ node.invoke 2606ms bytes=9666408
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ node.invoke 2429ms bytes=9666408
```

The two full-batch responses were each under the native 16 MiB limit, including the Gateway response envelope. Gateway `/healthz` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`; `/readyz` returned `ready=true`, `coreReady=true`, and an empty `failing` list. Both checks used only the task-owned Gateway.

</details>

prs.title: improve(ui): copy selected text out of the Browser panel
prs.body:
<!-- Related: none -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: text cannot be copied out of the Control UI Browser panel. The remote page is drawn as a screenshot, Ctrl/Cmd+C was never handled, a native copy copied the panel's empty input and left the clipboard unchanged, and the actions menu only offered "Copy URL". Text the agent selected, or that a page selected itself, could not reach the user's clipboard.

## User Impact

User impact: press Ctrl/Cmd+C with the page focused, use the browser's Copy, or choose **Copy selection** in the Browser actions menu to put the remote page's selected text on your local clipboard; a "Copied!" notice confirms it. An empty selection, a disconnected panel, disabled page scripting (`browser.evaluateEnabled=false`) or a clipboard failure each show a notice naming the next step, and the menu entry is disabled with a reason when there is nothing to copy. Password fields and cross-origin frames are never copied. Mac tabs still copy natively with ⌘C. Known gap: the panel cannot yet create a selection in the remote page (no drag-select, no Ctrl/Cmd+A), so copy works on selections that already exist; the notices tell users to ask the agent to select text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel already runs page functions through the existing `act:evaluate` route, so a small page script reads the selection back (input/textarea ranges, open shadow roots, same-origin frames, capped at 1,000,000 characters). No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool change is needed. The clipboard write needs a live user gesture but the text only arrives after a round trip, so `copyToClipboard` now accepts a pending promise (`ClipboardItem`, then `writeText`, then `execCommand`). The tab and connection are rechecked right before the write so a stale result from another tab is dropped, a read that finishes after a newer copy never overwrites it, and selected text never reaches logs, errors, the local textarea, chat or panel state. Forwarding the key to the remote browser's clipboard was rejected because the Gateway cannot read that clipboard.

## Evidence

- Before/after screenshots (Copied toast, Copy selection menu entry, disabled state) are in the first comment.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/components/browser src/lib/clipboard.test.ts src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts` in `ui/`: 28 files, 328 tests pass; 23 of the 24 new tests fail without the production change (the chord guard passes trivially on the base).
- Earlier head of this PR: throwaway real-Chrome e2e against the repo's mock Gateway (deleted afterwards): Ctrl+C puts the selected text on the local clipboard with the toast, the menu entry copies, and an empty Ctrl+C shows a toast and leaves the clipboard untouched. Existing browser e2e files (panel width, route handoff, stream startup, tab preview URLs): 17 tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, oxfmt check and `git diff --check`: clean. `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passes on this head merged with current main. oxlint reports one warning at `browser-panel-toolbar.tsx:220`, the existing Copy URL handler, also flagged before this change.
- Not observed: a real managed browser over CDP, Safari/Firefox clipboard behavior, the native bridge, `contenteditable` selections (jsdom lacks them). Screenshots come from the mock-Gateway harness.

prs.title: fix: Windows installer setup does not start after the npm shim is installed
prs.body:
Related: #183680

## What Problem This Solves

Windows setup can fail to start after installation, leaving users without clear recovery instructions. This change also fixes an earlier PR regression that rejected valid launcher paths.

## User Impact

Batch launchers in paths containing spaces, `&`, `!`, and literal `%PATH%` can receive the onboarding command. A process-creation failure prints a manual setup command; child failures preserve their exit status.

The original reported silent handoff failure remains unexplained. The original report's cause is not established; this evidence stops before provider authentication and does not establish Codex activation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows batch shims launch through System32 `cmd.exe` using the existing attached `Start-Process` owner. A temporary environment value preserves the literal launcher path and is restored after success or failure. Behavioral fixtures exercise the handoff and recovery rather than only checking a constructed command string.

The branch incorporates main at `bb9b2fd4fcbb732371de08a71da8bf317f3965c1`, resolving the test-file conflict while keeping both the upstream conflicted-pull regression and the handoff tests.

## Evidence

- **Fresh installer and interactive input, native Windows:** On Windows 10 / Windows PowerShell 5.1.19041.6456, the unmodified installer from `f1bf6180b2d646fbd41bec93585d921d3daf1fce` (SHA256 `bb1834fe5f16ef64f5d47c4f7a0338e007536ccfa772a1c283595eecf6a91d9d`) installed OpenClaw 2026.10.8 into a new isolated npm prefix in a real SSH ConPTY. Both console input and output reported `IsRedirected=False`. Without manually running `openclaw onboard`, the installer printed `Starting setup...` and opened the wizard. prs.title: fix(exec): dollar amounts in agent messages are corrupted when exec text uses $<digit> in double quotes
prs.body:
Closes #179890

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dollar amounts in agent-sent messages are silently corrupted ("$900" becomes "00") when an `exec` command passes the text in double quotes.

## User Impact

User impact: exec commands that would deliver a corrupted dollar amount are refused before they run. The refusal shows the text as written next to what the shell would deliver, and how to fix it (single quotes, `\$`, or a quoted heredoc), so the agent retries correctly instead of sending the wrong amount to a customer. It can be disabled with `OPENCLAW_EXEC_DOLLAR_GUARD=off`.

**Open question for maintainers:** this is default-on and uses an environment switch. If you'd prefer it opt-in, or shipped as a plugin on the existing `before_tool_call` hook instead of in core, I'm happy to rework it that way. Tell me which shape you want.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBeforeToolCallHook` checks `exec` command text for a `$<digit>` that the shell would expand, before any plugin or approval policy runs. Codex-native shell commands reach the same policy through the PreToolUse native hook relay. Relay planning now counts the guard as a before-tool-call policy and keeps `exec` in the PreToolUse matcher, so native commands are covered even with no other policy installed.

The scanner is deliberately conservative. It only flags an expansion it can show would be empty:
- It honours single quotes, `\$`, `$'...'`, quoted heredoc delimiters, `${...}`, `$((...))` and comments.
- It recurses into `$(...)`, including substitutions inside unquoted heredoc bodies, with their own quoting.
- It ignores `$0` (the shell or script name) unless it reads as money (`$0.50`).
- It stays out of commands that define functions or set positional parameters (`set --`, `shift`, `getopts`), where `$1.00` may be intended.
- It fails open on anything it cannot parse.

Code-mode `exec` (JavaScript) is excluded.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/shell-dollar-expansion-guard.test.ts` (35 tests): the hazard shapes, every safe quoting form, `$0`, populated positional parameters, heredoc command substitution, `bash -lc` unwrapping, fail-open, and the `runBeforeToolCallHook` veto, allow and disable cases. The `$0`, positional-parameter and heredoc-substitution cases fail on the previous revision and pass now.
- `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.dollar-guard.test.ts` (6 tests): Codex `Bash` and `exec_command` are denied and single-quoted amounts pass. Relay planning enables PreToolUse for `exec` with no other policy and keeps it in a relay scoped to other tools; these planning cases fail without the relay change.
- The existing `agent-tools.before-tool-call*` and `native-hook-relay*` unit suites pass. `native-hook-relay.participants` and `native-hook-relay.remote-http` fail identically on `main` without this change in my environment.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Replayed against 391 unique `$`-bearing exec commands from a production deployment: 18 were flagged, all genuine expansion bugs, with no false positives.
- Still to add: a gateway trace of a real agent refusing and retrying. I'll attach it before asking for re-review.

prs.title: fix(backup): redact bundled plugin credentials from Git exports
prs.body:
## Summary

Secret-redacted Git backups retain credentials embedded in bundled plugin state. Filter the identified credential scopes before SQLite serialization and PostgreSQL image materialization while preserving unrelated plugin records and blobs. This extends the backup redaction policy introduced in #122485 and shared across engines in #174698.

## What Problem This Solves

1. `src/state/secret-state-tables.ts` and `src/snapshot/git-backup-sanitizer.ts` now classify bundled account credentials, identity keys, callback signing secrets, hosted-media bearer records, and Discord Activity token stores. Their opaque values and token keys previously reached Git history even with `--exclude-secrets`.
2. Discord thread bindings contain webhook credentials alongside routing data. Remove only `webhookToken` from those JSON records, preserving routing fields. Unreadable records in that credential scope are omitted.

Redacted exports withhold these credentials while retaining allowlists, spending counters, memory settings, widget records, relay grants, registration identities, and unrelated durable blobs.

## Why this design

- Keep the existing export sanitizer as the policy owner for both engines.
- Match plugin IDs, credential namespaces, account variants, and individual keys in mixed namespaces; cover retained namespaces without dropping entire plugin tables.
- Preserve full-fidelity backups and existing user configuration, schemas, SDK signatures, and manifest formats.
- Document reauthentication and registration after redacted restores. Custom opaque plugin payloads require their own credential classification; these rules cover the identified bundled scopes.

## Why this does not conflict with #122485 and #174698

| PR | Governed layer | Relation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #122485 | Git snapshots and secret-redaction policy | Extends the existing policy to credentials inside plugin records. |
| #174698 | PostgreSQL export redaction | Reuses its shared row-transform seam before portable image materialization. |

Both changes are already in the base. The plugin tables remain present; selected rows or fields are redacted.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path and mode | Before | After / observed proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SQLite create, commit, push to isolated bare remote; `excludeSecrets=true` | Synthetic credential JSON and blob values present in remote history; regression failed at the leak assertion. | Identified credential values and Discord bearer keys absent; nonsecret state survives export and restore. |
| Same path; `excludeSecrets=false` | Full-fidelity control passes. | Credentials, nonsecret records, and blobs remain intact. |
| Discord thread bindings, including retained records | Webhook token survives redacted export and restore. | Token removed; routing fields preserved. Dedicated regression reproduced the failure before the repair. |
| Product CLI: SQLite create/push/verify/restore, redacted and full modes | Baseline integration reproduced the credential leak. | Actual `pnpm openclaw` commands passed with synthetic state and bare remotes: identified JSON/blob credentials absent only in redacted history; source credentials, allowlist, spend, memory settings, routing fields and ordinary blob preserved. |
| PostgreSQL 17.11 portable image and fresh server restore | On original base `903394cceb1`, both state cases fail: seven plugin rows instead of four, credential bytes and webhook token still present. The two agent controls pass. | Four real-server conformance cases passed. Redacted state image/restores retain four nonsecret/mixed plugin rows and one ordinary blob; full mode retains seven rows and both blobs. Raw redacted image bytes contain no secret marker. Normal and generic identities cover export; normal identities cover actual fresh PostgreSQL namespace restore. |
| `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/snapshot/git-backup-plugin-secrets.test.ts src/snapshot/git-backup.test.ts src/snapshot/git-backup-codec.test.ts src/state/secret-state-tables.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | New regression failed on the original code; full-fidelity control passed. | 29 tests passed; one Windows-only case skipped on Linux. Following the Discord repairs, the changed regression and registry suites passed again: five tests. |

Integration and CLI assertions inspect committed JSONL in the bare remote and query restored SQLite data. The PostgreSQL test inspects portable-image bytes and queries fresh restored server namespaces, including spending counters, memory-disable settings, relay grants and field-redacted Discord bindings.

CLI proof used isolated synthetic state with `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. `$REPO`, `$REMOTE` and `$TARGET` below name fresh task-owned temporary paths:

```bash
pnpm openclaw backup git init --repository "$REPO" --remote "$REMOTE" --json
pnpm openclaw backup git create --repository "$REPO" --global --exclude-secrets --push --json
pnpm openclaw backup git verify --repository "$REPO" --global --json
pnpm openclaw backup git restore --repository "$REPO" --global --target "$TARGET" --json
```

The full-fidelity control ran the same commands without `--exclude-secrets`. Real PostgreSQL proof used the repository-pinned pgvector image with PostgreSQL 17.11 and this supported wrapper:

```bash
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$OPENCLAW_DATABASE_DSN" -- src/infra/database-engine/git-backup-secrets.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The PostgreSQL harness substitutes worker dispatch/custody around real database handlers; client/server data operations, image verification and namespace restoration are real. The separate product CLI proof uses the actual CLI dispatch and backup runtime.

prs.title: perf(workspace): trim redundant writer request payloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local sandbox workspace admission and checkpoint settlement resend expanded inventories to the SQLite writer after their content is already prepared.

## User Impact

No storage format or reconciliation behavior changes. Workspace writes send less data between the host and writer; full checkpoint documents remain durable for recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The workspace store now sends only the manifest root publication fields consumed by the writer. A checkpoint also contains recovery documents and build-input arrays, which previously crossed this boundary because its structural type fits the mutation interface. Source-path creation and updates send the existing `[]` storage placeholder after content-addressed preparation, while the original mutation retains the complete JSON for host publication and lost-reply recovery.

No schema, durability, FIFO ordering, authorization, revision, or lease checks change. Production delta: **+25 lines** (31 added, 6 removed). The added projection preserves the separate contracts: full host receipt reconstruction and compact writer input; it adds no cache or alternate persistence path.

## Evidence

The new real-store regression fails on main `9cd97293eb93e0d445481a08ccbe94d5ae52ce63`: create **48,009 B**, settlement **53,824 B**, both over the **2,048 B** request budget. It passes with this change and verifies exact durable readback and retained checkpoint content.

Synthetic workload: 16 retained workspace rows, 1,000 admitted build-input paths, prepared roots differing in one file, source admission, checkpoint reservation, settlement, and cleanup through the real store and SQLite broker. Byte measurements use 32 cycles; MB/min below uses a declared **30 cycles/minute**, not benchmark throughput or a claim about production operation mix.

| Writer operation | Base MB/min | Candidate MB/min |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Source preparation | 0.025065 | 0.025065 |
| Source admission | 1.420620 | 0.012030 |
| Checkpoint reservation | 1.463790 | 1.463790 |
| Settlement | 1.428540 | 0.019260 |
| Cleanup | 0.010620 | 0.010620 |
| **Total** | **4.348635** | **1.530765** |

**64.8% fewer request bytes**. Source-admission mutation: 47,354 → 401 B/request. Settlement: 47,618 → 642 B/request. Create setup: 48,086 → 1,138 B/request. Content preparation and saved checkpoint traffic are unchanged.

Rerun instructions are in `scripts/perf/local-workspace-request-bytes-measure.ts`. `--revision <base-sha>` substitutes only the old store owner. Byte-count instrumentation is disabled during timing and allocation measurements.

Owner measurements use 2,048 cycles per arm, AB/BA order, with timing and allocation collected separately. Mixed-sign initial CPU pairs triggered one predeclared extra untraced pair.

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Untraced main-thread CPU, three pairs | 4,796.10 µs/cycle | 4,948.31 µs/cycle | +152.21 µs (+3.17%) |
| Sampled main-thread V8 allocation, two pairs | 1,056,370 B/cycle | 1,058,317 B/cycle | +1,947 B (+0.184%) |
| Elapsed per 2,048-cycle arm, three pairs | 27.802 s | 32.778 s | +17.90% |

This demonstrates a request-byte reduction, **not a CPU or V8-heap allocation win**. CPU pair differences were −110.28, +441.78, and +125.14 µs/cycle. Wall-time differences were +5.32%, +44.48%, and +1.89%; host/runtime drift was large. No rejection is inferred from these mixed measurements. The main-thread heap sampler does not account for all external serialization backing buffers or worker allocations.

<details>

Validation: `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, the matching Gateway test typecheck, changed-file lint/format, export collision guard, and diff whitespace checks passed. Store, manifest-scan, and projection files passed **83 tests**, with two environment-dependent skips (required Podman and invalid-UTF-8 filesystem support). Wall time 156 seconds including worker compilation; regression test time is under one second. Test-lines ratchet passed: 6,312,380 / 6,320,000. The two required import/source-closure files passed 38 tests (57 seconds). prs.title: feat(sessions): include stored categories in JSON output
prs.body:
Closes #133108.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions --json` omitted the canonical stored session category even though adjacent metadata such as color was already projected. Offline scripts could not group the same sessions as Gateway and Control UI consumers without reading private state directly.

## User Impact

JSON session rows now include `category` when it is stored. Unset or cleared categories remain omitted, and the human-readable table is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change extends the existing `toSessionDisplayRow` ownership boundary by one optional field, with focused coverage for present and cleared values and a CLI documentation update.

## Real Behavior Proof

The proof used this PR head with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. A session was written through the production session accessor, then read through the shipped CLI entry point:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated-state> node --import tsx src/index.ts sessions --json
{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "key": "agent:main:proof",
      "sessionId": "proof-session",
      "label": "category-proof",
      "category": "Research",
      "visibility": "shared"
    }
  ]
}
```

The same stored row was then cleared through `patchSessionEntryCore` and read through the same CLI command:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated-state> node --import tsx src/index.ts sessions --json
{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "key": "agent:main:proof",
      "sessionId": "proof-session",
      "label": "category-proof",
      "visibility": "shared"
    }
  ]
}
```

Observed result: the stored category is emitted as `"category": "Research"`; after clearing it, the `category` property is absent rather than serialized as null or an empty value. The proof state contained only synthetic identifiers and was removed after capture.

## Evidence

- Base-red focused test failed only because the expected `category` field was absent.
- Focused regression: 1 passed.
- Full `src/commands/sessions.test.ts`: 17/17 passed (Vitest duration 83.04s).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: passed.
- Scoped oxfmt, oxlint, and `git diff --check`: passed.

prs.title: fix(telegram): preserve reset-aware conversation naming lifecycle
prs.body:
Related: #183368 (one-shot refinement follow-up), #174317 (landed Dashboard refinement).

## What Problem This Solves

Reset and control-only turns can rename a Telegram DM topic (and its mirrored WebUI session title) from the command text itself: after `/reset` or a model switch, the "first turn after reset" path arms automatic naming from the service-command body, so a long-running topic like "YouGile" silently becomes a description of the model change before any substantive message arrives. The naming lifecycle also conflated one-shot in-conversation refinement with reset/new lifecycle transitions, and stale inference could overwrite an observed manual rename.

## User Impact

- `/reset`, `/model` and other service commands never arm or produce an automatic rename; the topic keeps its current name.
- After a reset, a substantive message re-checks the previous name: if the conversation continues the same task (e.g. YouGile/CRM), the old name is preserved; only a real topic change gets a new generated name.
- `/new` signals a new-topic intent but still requires substantive content before any naming.
- Manually set names (Telegram side or WebUI side) keep priority over automatic inference across reset/new transitions and both sync directions.
- A generated creation title keeps a skip-next marker only for new generated names; captionless media turns count with current media facts instead of hijacking the name.

## Implementation and Scope

- Telegram: non-command guard on the reset-aware first-turn path (`prepareTopicLabelTurn` with lifecycle revisions), refinement store keyed per lifecycle revision, topic-name cache hardening, captionless-media naming, and recovery from failed state-writes.
- Core: `session-title-refinement-state` (new, 123 lines) carries refinement lifecycle state; session rollover/preemption preserve the reset-aware presentation; session-entry projection/public-patch expose the preserved selection without new configurable thresholds.
- Config: `autoTopicLabel` refinement config (opt-in `refine`, defaults clamped), schema labels/help updates, regenerated baselines.
- UI: new-session create/draft params keep generated-title provenance consistent with the server-side skip-next marker.
- SDK surface: two helpers plus state type through the existing `reply-dispatch-runtime` subpath (`advanceConversationLabelRefinement`, `readConversationLabelRefinementSource`); no new subpath or RPC.

Remaining feature diff: 67 files, +4095/-262 (including regenerated config baselines and docs). Branch `reset-aware-topic-naming-20261026`, head `34b63f5cee6f0bd13bdf519ff6f730fbd3f0bde6`, rebased onto current `main` (`c824dc97`).

## Evidence

- 53 focused naming cases pass (topic-label refinement, topic-name cache, media naming, recovery, config precedence), plus infra and Telegram database/recovery shards (~120 tests total) under Node 24.22.1.
- Canonical full build completed (8m 42s) and a self-contained package tarball passed `check-openclaw-package-tarball` integrity, import-graph and declaration screening.
- The packaged runtime was deployed to an isolated test gateway (non-production, mock-LLM): health, control UI bootstrap, and build-info `2026.10.6-b7c0c041` verified live.
- One follow-up test (`retains a later refinement after foreground dispatch settles` in the media refinement suite) still fails: the deferred-dispatch fixture selects the "initial" lifecycle where "refine" is required; fix in progress in the fixture, not in product code.

## Live Proof Still Pending

No live Telegram refinement verdict or screenshot is claimed yet; mocked transport/model tests plus the isolated test-gateway deployment do not replace live evidence. No production deployment or merge is requested.

prs.title: improve(ui): acknowledge Browser panel clicks locally and stop queuing clicks behind each other
prs.body:
<!-- Related: none; complements #187032 (queued text, wheel, refresh delay, resize), which does not touch the click path -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking in the Control UI Browser panel (for example filling a captcha whose tiles appear and disappear) gives no immediate feedback, and rapid clicks lag. The first sign a click registered is the remote page's next frame (about 70-100 ms on loopback, plus a full round trip on a real link), and each click waited for the previous click's reply, which the server holds for about 250 ms. Two clicks 50 ms apart reached the page 250-290 ms apart.

## User Impact

User impact: a click shows a local press ring in 1.5-3.6 ms instead of nothing for 70-100 ms or more (a cue only; it does not claim the remote click landed). Rapid clicks are sent at once: the second of two clicks 50 ms apart reaches the page in about 28 ms instead of about 255 ms, and the gap between them on the page matches how the user clicked (about 52-59 ms instead of about 285 ms). Not fixed: a single click's remote round trip (about 285 ms per action), and typing, which still waits per key. No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Measured against a real Gateway built from this checkout, a real managed Chrome and the real built Control UI. Nearly all of the per-action wait is a deliberate 250 ms post-action navigation grace in the browser extension's SSRF guard (`extensions/browser/src/browser/act-policy.ts:32`), shared with the model-facing tool. That needs the browser/security owner, so this PR leaves it alone and proposes a follow-up: let panel input kinds return at dispatch while the guard completes in the background. What the UI can own is shown here: acknowledge the press locally (a transparent ring animated on opacity/transform only, ends by itself after 500 ms, reduced-motion fade, touch and pen only after a tap becomes a click so scrolling shows nothing), and stop chaining a click behind the previous click's reply. A click still waits for text typed before it, and text after a click still waits for every click and for the latest one to succeed.

Known risk: concurrent `/act` requests carry no server ordering guarantee, so pipelined clicks rely on dispatch order. Stress on the real stack (20 bursts of 9 clicks at 15 ms and 3 ms gaps) kept every click in order with none lost.

## Evidence

Real stack, loopback, same machine, interleaved main/branch, 20 clicks and 20 double clicks per cell, medians (p95 in the audit). Loopback means every stage is a lower bound.

| metric | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| local acknowledgement after pointerdown | none (first sign at 70-99 ms) | 1.5-3.6 ms |
| 2nd of two clicks 50 ms apart, UI to remote page | 251-263 ms | 27-29 ms |
| gap between the two clicks on the page | 284-292 ms | 52-59 ms |
| single click to change visible (stream) | about 50-80 ms | unchanged within noise |
| screenshot fallback, click to change visible | about 1004 ms | unchanged |
| 10 keys typed 70 ms apart, last key arrives after | about 1950 ms | unchanged (see #187032) |

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/components/browser` in `ui/`: 24 files, 276 tests pass; 5 new or changed tests fail without the production change.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm lint:ui:styles`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, oxfmt check, `git diff --check`: clean. oxlint reports one existing warning in toolbar code this PR does not touch.
- Not run: headful Chrome screencast, a non-loopback Gateway, the native WKWebView path (unchanged), Safari/Firefox. The existing browser UI e2e files were not re-run by me after the final edit.
- Overlap with #187032: a textual conflict is possible around `pendingText`/`pendingClick` in `handleStageClick`.

prs.title: fix(browser): preserve native CORS preflights
prs.body:
## Summary

Browser navigation guards used Playwright catch-all page routing, which made Chromium treat intercepted CORS preflights as permissive and could send a cross-origin request the destination rejected. This change moves guard handling into document-only CDP interception, preserves native CORS, and explicitly cancels a committed timed-out page opening while retiring successful committed document ownership without canceling healthy response bodies or child loads. It preserves the invocation-scoped navigation policy introduced by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104254 and does not depend on the unmerged policy-removal proposal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167703.

## What Problem This Solves

1. In `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-navigation.ts`, guarded actions and guarded `goto` used catch-all Playwright routing. Playwright could synthesize a successful CORS preflight, so a rejecting destination received the non-simple `PUT`.
2. In `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session-navigation-fence.ts`, the existing operation-owned fence tracked document redirects and out-of-process frames but did not own the route handler or limit Fetch interception to documents.
3. The first document-only implementation waited for a terminal Network event after a committed streamed document timed out. Chromium does not consistently emit that event after `Page.stopLoading`, so cleanup could replace the original Playwright `TimeoutError` and close a usable committed tab.
4. A successful action could also return before delayed response headers committed streaming main-frame HTML. Cleanup sampled commitment once, then waited 20 seconds even after the later commit, failed, and retained interception until page close, so later navigation on the otherwise usable tab was aborted.

5. Successful action cleanup also used page-wide stopLoading after main-frame commit, truncating healthy delayed finite HTML and simultaneous child loads. Ownership now retires independently at each document commit; failure and cancellation still stop loading.

The net effect was excess page-script network authority before this fix plus committed-page recovery and successful-load regressions in its first revisions.

## Why this design

- Intercept only `Document` resources through the operation-owned CDP session; leave preflights and subresources on Chromium's native network path.
- Keep top-level/subframe checks, redirect/OOPIF ownership, and live invocation authority in one fence.
- Establish a same-target protocol barrier before cleanup so a queued document cannot escape interception.
- On navigation failure, acknowledge `Page.stopLoading`, settle the fence's owned document state, and preserve the original navigation error.
- Retire each document at its own frame commit, including OOPIF sessions: committed responses cannot redirect, so their bodies can continue while uncommitted redirect chains and policy work remain fenced. Reserve page-wide stopLoading for failure or cancellation.
- Disable Fetch before detaching and retain interception when cancellation cannot be confirmed.
- Add no setting, dependency, public API, or migration surface.

## Why this does not conflict with related browser-navigation work

| PR | Governed layer | Relation to this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104254 | Invocation-scoped document policy for browser actions | The base includes it. This PR preserves its policy and changes only the interception mechanism and cleanup. |
| https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167703 | Unmerged proposal to retire native navigation-policy enforcement | This PR keeps the current contract and does not depend on that proposal. |

The shared navigation files compose with the existing policy: this branch narrows interception and repairs cleanup without redefining the allowed destinations.

## Evidence

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Loading saved Code Mode results allocates a full host object and another JSON string even though the result store already owns the normalized JSON needed by the worker.

## User Impact

Code Mode programs that reuse large saved results spend less main-thread CPU and allocate less garbage. Guest values, error visibility, network provenance, and transcript output remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The result store now returns its existing JSON to the bridge. The inbox remains the single owner of capacity admission, cancellation and delivery release, with a normalized-JSON entry point shared by ordinary value settlement. The guest still decodes each load into a detached object. Session-store envelopes retain their existing missing-value behavior.

Production change: 22 added / 11 removed lines, **+11 net**. This small growth exposes the existing inbox admission boundary without duplicating it; it deletes both full-payload operations from every saved-result load. No cache or retained representation is added. The reproducible benchmark adds 160 tooling lines plus one exact Knip entry.

## Evidence

Baseline: `9cd97293eb93e0d445481a08ccbe94d5ae52ce63`. The new real-worker regression fails there with two host parses, then passes with zero while verifying that mutating the first guest load does not affect the second.

The committed `scripts/perf/code-mode-result-load-measure.ts` invokes the real result store, bridge and inbox with synthetic data and verifies exact delivered JSON. Each side has five samples of 2,000 loads for CPU, plus a separate 10,000-load allocation pass (4 KiB sampling, including collected objects). CPU is main-thread CPU; GC is from the untraced pass.

| Workload / metric | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 81,198-byte result: sampled bytes/load | 192,368 | 5,149 | −97.3% |
| Main-thread CPU/load | 96.75 µs | 7.66 µs | −92.1% |
| GC time / 10,000 loads | 28.779 ms (78 collections) | 0.374 ms (1 collection) | −28.405 ms |
| 41-byte control: sampled bytes/load | 5,042 | 5,207 | +3.3% |
| Control main-thread CPU/load | 2.161 µs | 1.924 µs | −11.0% |
| Control GC time / 10,000 loads | 0.463 ms (1 collection) | 0.518 ms (1 collection) | +0.055 ms |

Allocation stacks attribute about 106 KB/load to the host parse and 81 KB/load to `stringifyCodeModeJsonSafe`; both disappear. The small control exposes the extra inbox-method cost rather than hiding it. Large-result arm load averages were 22.35 baseline / 16.63 candidate; CPU samples were 191.8–197.2 ms / 14.9–15.9 ms per 2,000 loads. End-run RSS was 613.1 / 587.4 MiB and heap used 149.6 / 163.2 MiB; these are context, not retained-heap claims, since collection counts differ.

- Exact-head CI is green at `251a50544d092e99dad41f7856cc3353aea2be0f`: 64 passing checks, 55 skipped, zero pending/failing; [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40784992138). Runtime/benchmark bytes are unchanged by the rebase from the measured baseline.

prs.title: fix(update): treat PostgreSQL anchors as anchors through update Doctor, Gateway startup and repair
prs.body:
Fixes #187006. Thanks @etzelm for the report and reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes dev updates, subsequent Gateway startup, and `openclaw update repair` failing when PostgreSQL-backed families retain local SQLite identity anchors.

## User Impact

PostgreSQL-backed installations can complete update Doctor's existing forward migrations and start the Gateway without treating identity anchors as SQLite application databases. No database schema, dependencies, configuration options, or CLI options change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delegated update Doctor bypassed normal CLI engine selection, so SQLite migration attribution compared a PostgreSQL capture fingerprint with the untouched local anchor. Configured-agent ownership inspection also opened an old PostgreSQL schema as a runtime store before maintenance could migrate it. Manual `doctor --fix` already selects engines during CLI boot and begins maintenance before its current-state preflight, which explains why it could recover the installation.

Initialize the existing engine selection before Doctor inspection, read ownership through the existing matched PostgreSQL metadata path, and reuse the main updater's engine-selection scope for repair/finalization ledger reads. Transcript detection uses the selected engine's catalog; SQLite reclamation reuses the canonical anchor recognizer and leaves PostgreSQL anchors alone. Gateway runtime admission continues to require a completed migration. The extracted updater scope replaces its former private implementation; there is no second recognizer or parallel migration owner.

## Evidence

- Real task-owned PostgreSQL 17 proof: captured update Doctor completed the existing agent migration **27 → 38**; state schema remained **36**. Both anchors retained `user_version=0`, **8,192 bytes**, and unchanged modification times. Regression tests additionally assert exact anchor bytes and retained rows/search/trigger behavior.
- Actual public `pnpm dev update repair --yes --no-restart --channel dev --json` exited **0** (`coreUpdate: completed`, Doctor lint exit 0). Actual `pnpm dev gateway run --port 19847` reached `/readyz` **HTTP 200**, `ready=true`, `coreReady=true`, `failing=[]`, then shut down cleanly. All HOME/state paths and the PostgreSQL container were task-owned.
- Red-before/green-after regressions cover the captured-generation refusal, configured-agent migration custody, repair/finalization schema-role refusal, PostgreSQL transcript catalog reads, and SQLite reclamation of retained anchors. No mock factory loses real exports.
- Rebased owner files: PostgreSQL state/agent/update admission **26/26 passed**, SQLite reclamation **9/9 passed**; **35/35 across all four touched test files**, 274.35 s wrapper time. Required import-consumer results are recorded below.
- Core typecheck plus affected `cli-update`, `commands-doctor`, `infra`, and `state-logging` test projects passed. Touched production lint, formatting, docs MDX, `git diff --check`, and Madge (**0 cycles**) passed. The mock-export ratchet passed. Full `check:changed` was omitted under the campaign's SQLite-inventory time budget; PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Fresh Codex autoreview of the local patch against `0661e52a19d166bec1ef3956844fd230e5d5a8f5` was attempted at P2 coverage but returned **HTTP 401** without a completed assessment. This is recorded as unavailable under the campaign's explicit exception; lead review remains necessary.
- Production **+99/−54 (net +45)** lines, tests/test support **+126/−129 (net −3)**, docs **+7**. Existing fixture cleanup and search-schema helpers replace duplicated test setup while preserving behavioral coverage.

### Five-run comparison of the two earlier intermittent CLI failures

Ran each case five times on the patched tree and five times in a separate, unmodified detached `origin/main` worktree pinned to `70bf5121704c7a7173722c2bd7e360362e5da165`. The comparison worktree was removed afterwards. Runtime and arguments matched the original failed run: Node **26.12.1**, pnpm **12.15.0**, Vitest **5.0.5**, and the repository-selected Bun **1.4.4**, revision **1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1**. Test/fixture sources, assertions, mocks, and deadlines were unchanged.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli.test.ts \
  -t 'routes package updates for explicit beta from Git|uses the installed Git CLI when service env refresh cannot complete' \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Each invocation used isolated HOME/state, the same temporary-directory parent, its own checkout's persistent module cache, and `OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1`.

prs.title: fix: restore sidebar alignment browser coverage
prs.body:
Fixes #187063

## What Problem This Solves

The six existing sidebar status/alignment browser cases stop at a 30-second timeout after the Sections UI removed its global heading. Each case reads that heading before reaching the assertions that protect status/title alignment, hover and keyboard-focus stability, child controls, and pinning, so the failure obscures the checks those cases are meant to perform.

## User Impact

This restores supporting browser coverage for the current sidebar. It changes no product code or visible layout: Sections keep their icon-based presentation, and the existing desktop/mobile grouping behavior and geometry tolerances remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first Person row now sits directly below the owner picker, as the sidebar's existing layout rule specifies. The test originally measured that boundary before the personal heading was introduced. It now measures the owner picker's bottom edge again, only inside the Person-spacing assertion where the value is used, and retains the existing maximum 12px gap.

All six combinations of None, Custom groups, and Person at 1200px and 390px remain. The legacy-owner, running, unread, artwork, Draft, hover/focus, parent/child, and pinned-row checks are preserved. No fixture, timeout, production seam, or tolerance is added or relaxed.

## Evidence

On unmodified source `0ded0ed7a8cae4867a3a201e32cccbfbfe9bde70`, the existing `aligns None left status at 1200 px` case failed after 31.354 seconds waiting for `.personal-session-groups__heading`. The same selector failure affects all six cases in [CI run 40780389933](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40780389933/job/123141113621). Relevant sidebar, fixture, test, and dependency inputs are unchanged at this branch's `61f44e6ec5ce7bd9075356188254a4568e891d06` base.

The complete `ui/src/e2e/session-ownership.e2e.test.ts` file passes: **18/18 cases, including all six grouping/width combinations**, with no skips. The native browser invocation took 64.28s (Vitest reported 61.70s, including its bundled UI setup); these cases require a browser to measure actual layout and interaction behavior. Changed-file format/lint and the affected `core-test-ui-e2e` type graph also pass on the same tree.

Production delta: 0 lines. Test delta: +5/−4, with no added test case. Exact-head [CI run 40783875369](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40783875369) completed successfully in 10m25s wall time. The selected Chromium browser job passed in 144s; all three selected UI unit rows and the selected lint, types, boundary, baseline-ratchet, Node, and security checks passed. Independent review and canonical AutoReview found no actionable defects. [ClawSweeper’s exact-head report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187070#issuecomment-6482972065) likewise reports no findings.

prs.body:
## Superseded for the Cron unread scope

Current main `b9c6e9c0163f51f2d4b74ded87393c45f1d13769` already covers the scheduled persistent-session behavior through the existing conversation-result owner. [#182262](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182262) merged as `721cdadccb93b9c185d367f0e8082b2338553c81` on2026-10-24T20:42:23Z. A settled visible result, including delivery `none`, is committed through `commitCronConversationResult` and `commitBackgroundResultToSession`; the accepted append advances `lastInteractionAt`. `deriveSessionUnread` intentionally compares the maximum of that field and `lastActivityAt` against `lastReadAt`.

The original extra lifecycle visibility stamp is therefore unnecessary for this Cron scope. Its old requirement that specifically `lastActivityAt` must increase is narrower than the current unread contract. The unshipped conflict integration is preserved locally and has not been pushed. This is a supersession assessment, **not a merge of this PR or verified adoption/credit of my implementation**. The canonical commit carries its existing authorship; no alkor2000 coauthor credit is claimed.

### Current-main owner verification

A canonical-production control extends the existing shared-session regression with a persisted read acknowledgment. It runs the real `runCronSessionTurn`, controller, tool and private SQLite owners; only model I/O decisions are synthetic. The sole product file changed by this proposal, isolated `run.ts`, is replaced with exact main bytes during the control; the retained test support stays explicit. This is not a checkout of main or a Gateway/RPC, Codex runtime, vendor, release or deployed-adoption proof.

Three selected cases **pass** (5 unselected):

- The original structured-progress control with delivery `none` retains its result, visible-row and no-channel-send assertions.
- A plain visible report with **no `record_result` call** and delivery `none` changes an acknowledged row from read to unread, with one committed visible report and zero channel sends. `lastInteractionAt` advances while `lastActivityAt` stays unchanged.
- A structured `no_change` check with delivery `none` keeps the row read, both activity fields unchanged, no visible result and zero channel sends.

The native wrapper completes in209.22s; working bytes, file modes and shared index are restored exactly. A first diagnostic attempt remains **1 failure /1 pass,441.47s**: both unread checks succeeded, but the new no-record case incorrectly reused a summary assertion promised by `record_result`. The corrected diagnostic scopes only that assertion to recorded results and retains the original six scenarios and their assertions. Its model/history/read-state controls are unchanged. No product behavior, timeout, baseline or old Gateway quiet assertion is changed.

The original general-Codex report in #142002 remains open; these Cron-specific checks do not establish that its entire scope is fixed. The old first-NO_REPLY missing-answer failure, RPC readiness timeout and narrow fixed-head permissions below retain their original scopes. They are not reclassified or declared repaired by this owner verification.

<details>
<summary>Original proposal and historical validation (superseded implementation)</summary>

Related: #142002. Reported by @lakemike; @DarkJuanFra supplied the scheduled-session reproduction.

## Problem and change

Visible scheduled reports can leave an acknowledged conversation marked read. Record actual terminal-output visibility on the original active run claim before its existing lifecycle event; the canonical lifecycle projection remains the activity writer. Silence, empty/error/reasoning-only output and heartbeat acknowledgments keep read state; structured media remains visible. Admission, identity, delivery and settlement retain their current owners.

Current head: `bcce26217e6285b7db35ef6931d7790341a0c73e`. The initial integration was `88ac5a2084f90f2a1a5ec55904765065bcb47b23`, a normal merge with official main `698a6f83b46beae08b9e63dc06138c5fccfb66b1`. The follow-up removes exactly one retired `agents.defaults.heartbeat` line from the retained Gateway fixture. No product configuration option, schema, protocol or dependency is added.

## Approved fixed-head Gateway diagnostic (2026-10-23)

<!-- openclawpr-fixed26644-diagnostic-20261023 -->
With explicit authorization, the retained isolated Gateway test ran once on local `26644d415b2f1ba3a3a0704778e649e520e78f63`, a direct child of `bcce` adding only the case/run-record assertion message. This diagnostic commit has not been pushed. The unchanged test fails: **1 file / 1 case, 153.431 s wrapper / 145.41 s Vitest**.

The visible-report and ordinary blocker-report model/history/unread assertions complete. The **first `NO_REPLY` control** then records `status: error`, `completionStatus: failed`, with the host message “No answer was returned. Ask again if you still need one.” The loopback provider accepted the fixture requests; the failure is the completed run's missing-answer outcome. The empty, `HEARTBEAT_OK` and detached controls were not reached. The original CI lacked a case label, so this does not retroactively identify its exact failed response.

The effective terminal reply expectation and its source still need tracing before deciding whether the route or fixture contradicts the intended silence contract. No status/unread assertion was relaxed and no production repair is claimed from this diagnostic. Native cleanup completed: no remaining test worker and no before/after listener difference. This used private test state and a synthetic loopback model, with no operator Gateway, real credential/provider or paid service.

### Follow-up authorized diagnostic at local c691 (2026-10-23)

<!-- openclawpr-fixedc691-diagnostic-20261023 -->
A second, separately authorized single execution used local `c6913293431babb6688ae56de4725999f800f957`, a child of `26644` that only observes the real reply-expectation resolvers while preserving their results and every original assertion. It remains unpushed. **1 file / 1 case failed, 288.316 s total command / 286.45 s native wrapper / 269.73 s Vitest.**

This attempt stopped earlier: `beforeEach` timed out waiting for the public `cron.status` RPC, before the model, history, unread or quiet-control assertions. It produced no effective reply-policy observation. The timeout's cause is unknown; neither the resolver wrapper nor compilation delay is established as its cause. It does not replace or explain the earlier first-`NO_REPLY` missing-answer failure. No timeout, assertion or production policy was changed, and the one-time execution was not retried. Cleanup left no test worker or listener difference.

Static tracing also distinguishes the two execution routes: the isolated Cron prompt executor already explicitly passes `terminalReplyExpectation: "optional"`; persistent shared-session scheduling goes through `runCronSessionTurn` and ordinary session-event reply admission. The latter's effective policy still needs runtime evidence. The next investigation must first explain the precondition timeout and confirm the actual policy owner, rather than weakening internal result-required rules or the quiet controls.

## Validation and remaining CI evidence

<!-- openclawpr-ci-39795018833-qualified -->
**Latest natural CI: failure onbcce.** [Run39795018833](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39795018833) tested merge6b3bb95db39a66d02182d224bcf150fa55ab07a3 against official base3cd9bddb36d93d43b50595dfd0d5b18a4478a0c9.

- [Gateway job119880968704](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39795018833/job/119880968704) gets past config validation and the visible/blocker model, history and unread assertions, then fails at the quiet-loop completion-status assertion: expected `ok`, received `error`. The log does not identify which quiet response or include the run's error. That quiet case's unread/activity assertions and the later detached control are not reached. This is partial actual Gateway evidence, **not a passing complete flow**. It remains an author investigation; no assertion is weakened and no speculative producer repair is claimed.
- [Types job119881631017](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39795018833/job/119881631017) reports missing Twitch test helpers `expectTarget`/`expectTargetError`. Exact official base3cd9 contains those calls; this PR does not change Twitch. Official [271329fd32df15f9347099872d1c35e756597cad](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/271329fd32df15f9347099872d1c35e756597cad), whose parent is3cd9, replaces them with real outbound-adapter assertions. This is source attribution and an official repair, not a local reproduction or a CI waiver for this head.
- The prior WebChat timeout is not listed among this run's failures; different selected shards and a nonfailure do not establish a root-cause fix. The local fixed26644 diagnostic above now identifies a first-NO_REPLY missing-answer failure; the earlier145 owner cases still cannot stand in for the unexecuted Gateway controls.

- Initial production-owner negative control: exact main698a gives three intended unread failures and six passing quiet controls. The repaired owner passes **145 cases across seven complete files**, using real Cron admission/start/event and canonical lifecycle projection/unread rules with a controlled provider. These are owner integration results, not a running Gateway/DB/RPC proof.
- Those 145 cases ran on88ac. Their executed test files and production inputs are unchanged inbcce, so they are reused by input qualification; this is **not a fresh145-case replay**. Original production/consumer types, lint, format, mock-export ratchet, line-cap, assertion, documentation and whitespace gates pass, with a scoped-clean independent review of the seven-file proposal.
- [Initial integration CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39773871725/job/119808526957) failed before the retained Gateway fixture could start: its config writer rejected the retired heartbeat key. Official #179387 intentionally removed that runtime setting. Removing the single legacy line makes the complete fixture config pass the current strict production config validator (before: rejected; after: accepted). No Gateway/model/server was started for this check. Fresh targeted consumer types, affected-file type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace and independent review pass forbcce.
- The same CI job also recorded a separate `session-message-events.exec-completion.test.ts` WebChat timeout. Its cause remains **unknown**: no matching main job or current/main Gateway reproduction establishes attribution, and the shared Cron mock change could not be ruled out. The heartbeat config correction does not claim to fix that timeout. Natural CI onbcce is tracked separately; no manual workflow rerun is requested.

**Proof boundary:** the retained fixture was typechecked; its fixed26644 and c691 diagnostic descendants have been executed with the distinct failures above. The latest review on88ac asks for current Gateway persistence/public-RPC/quiet-control proof. Earlier f9d Gateway results and permissions remain tied to their original head. Node24.22.1/pnpm12.15.0 satisfy the current branch manifest. No operator Gateway, real provider/data, paid resource, upstream merge or release is involved.

<details>
<summary>Initial integration and earlier exact-head evidence (historical)</summary>

Related: #142002. Reported by @lakemike; @DarkJuanFra supplied the scheduled-session reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled report can be saved after a conversation was acknowledged as read while that conversation still appears read.

## User Impact

Visible scheduled reports restore unread activity, including delivery mode `none`. Empty, silent, heartbeat-only and reasoning-only output keep read state; media remains visible even with a silent text reply. Diagnostic content capture and delivery success do not decide unread status. No configuration, protocol, schema or dependency change is required. The current merged-runtime Gateway/SQLite/RPC path has not been rerun locally; earlier Gateway evidence below remains tied to its original head.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run owner records actual output visibility on its original active claim before publishing the existing terminal event. Broadcast routing defaults missing visibility to true, but the durable lifecycle projection requires an explicit true flag before advancing activity. Current terminal-reply facts and the shared presentation classifier supply that fact; admission, run identity, delivery and lifecycle settlement keep their existing owners.

## Evidence

Current head: `88ac5a2084f90f2a1a5ec55904765065bcb47b23`, a normal merge of `f9ddf58f4d004e87eb616af8236dc8bf379723bd` and official main `698a6f83b46beae08b9e63dc06138c5fccfb66b1`. Actual Node24.22.1 / pnpm12.15.0 meet the manifest; package, lock and workspace inputs match the previously qualified installation. The whole seven-file proposal has production net+36 lines, tests/fixtures net+551, docs+2 and one removed obsolete mock exception.

- **Before:** with the production run owner set to exact main698a, the real Cron entry, prepared admission, runner-start callback and terminal event feed the canonical lifecycle projection and unread rule. Visible report, silent-with-media and capture-disabled report all incorrectly stay read: **3 intended failures /6 passing quiet controls /4 filtered cases**,283.631s wrapper/266.58s Vitest. This is a controlled-provider owner integration, not a standalone Gateway or durable unread DB/RPC run.
- **After:** **145 cases across seven complete files pass**,610.043s wrapper. Native groups:50 cases/1 file253.06s,52 cases/2 files44.88s,43 cases/4 files264.60s. All nine visibility controls pass,869–1228ms each, covering actual event→projection→unread behavior, exact silence, structured media, empty/error/reasoning/draft/heartbeat output and content-capture independence. Existing fallback, restart, unstarted-run, claim/event and lifecycle consumer controls also pass. Cold worker compilation is included in these local durations; no performance or hosted-CI timing claim is made.
- **Current ownership:** preserve `sessionPreparationEffect`, the captured terminal, `resolveUnstartedTerminalMetadata()` third emit argument, original claim token/generation, prompt settlement and continuation cleanup. Main #170534 deliberately removed raw-text/terminal-kind reconstruction; it stays removed. Fixtures now use current namespace harnesses, actual prepared admission/start callbacks and producer terminal-reply facts. The Cron facade preserves its exports and the shared mock uses the real function contract; the ratchet only drops the old closed-factory exception.
- **Checks:** production types78.735s,67-root targeted consumer types71.851s (including60 Gateway/Cron test files without executing them), five-file type-aware lint145.796s, formatting7.784s, line-cap3.612s, assertion safety85.472s, mock exports59.962s, targeted canonical MDX1.350s and whitespace all pass. An initial nonexistent docs script alias never executed a check; the supported `scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs` invocation is the passing documentation result. No timeout, assertion, baseline or ignore is weakened. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of all seven changed-file hunks has no actionable findings; metadata-only passes are not source proof. Reviewed/index/committed blobs match.

<details>
<summary>Current focused test command</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
```
