**Proof boundary:** the retained421-line Gateway/HTTP-model/WebSocket test is byte-identical to the original f9d test and is typechecked, but was not executed locally against this merged runtime. The provider/store harness and canonical projection prove the owner contract; they do not prove current Gateway persistence, RPC history or installed-service behavior. Old f9d hosted Gateway results and any earlier permission remain historical. Current natural CI, maintainer/security review and any required current-runtime Gateway proof remain separate; no workflow dispatch/rerun, paid resource, operator Gateway or upstream merge was used.

<details>
<summary>Retained prior-head Gateway proof, CI failures and qualifications</summary>

Related: #142002. Reported by @lakemike; @DarkJuanFra supplied the fresh scheduled-session reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled agent report can be saved to a persistent conversation after its last read acknowledgment while the Control UI still shows that conversation as read.

## User Impact

Visible scheduled reports restore the conversation's unread indicator, including with delivery mode `none`. Assistant-written blocker reports count without implying scheduler execution failure; empty results, text-only silent replies and heartbeat acknowledgments preserve read state. Detached runs with no source delivery preserve their source conversation’s read state; source delivery keeps its existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the completed output's visibility on the original live run claim before its existing terminal event is emitted. The existing lifecycle owner remains the activity writer; execution timing, transcript identity, delivery and access checks stay with their owners. Shared reply/payload classifiers preserve silent and structured-output semantics. Gateway test doubles now use the real Cron function contract and preserve the facade's exports, so the regression reaches actual execution. The canonical mock-export prune removes one obsolete closed-factory entry from the ratchet; it adds no exception.

## Evidence

<!-- exact-head-complete-gateway-proof-f9dd -->
Natural broad [CI run 38812626406](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38812626406) on exact head `f9ddf58f4d004e87eb616af8236dc8bf379723bd` completed **successfully**. Its [Gateway job 116690071869](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38812626406/job/116690071869) tests merge `7a3b49a1c60be46e77127e6eae02074969493f98` against official base `b4fb60242fef5a39ba2db40225072762e6a08200`. The complete `server.cron.unread-activity.test.ts` case passes in **62.240 seconds**.

This is the actual isolated Gateway flow with a synthetic loopback model: stored-account admission, model response, chat/cron history equivalence and visible-report unread; ordinary blocker report with status `ok`, persisted text and unread; all three `NO_REPLY`/empty/`HEARTBEAT_OK` quiet controls; and detached session identity/history with the source staying read. The unconditional test body reaches its final detached assertions. This resolves the earlier account and obsolete text-protocol fixture failures; it does not claim provider/runtime-error reports, installed production services, power-loss or real vendor proof. No local Gateway operation or CI rerun was used.

Current head: `f9ddf58f4d004e87eb616af8236dc8bf379723bd`. The latest one-file correction migrates the retained Gateway fixture to official main's accepted blocker-report contract; product code and persisted-account setup remain unchanged from `412cd9cff58245156d507c47c606df80622d4975`.

Current-parent natural [CI run 38808499872, job 116676475840](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38808499872/job/116676475840) tested merge `50040983d8acf35b33fbec89f4618c0ff4bf180a` against base `d9fa5ac1303a1fc85e82363d5aad6d2f8f573923`. The stored-profile correction passes `cron.add`, the first actual model request, both public histories, last-activity advancement and the unread assertion. It then fails at the old `status: "error"` expectation for an HTTP-200 assistant report; subsequent blocker history, quiet and detached checks were not reached. This is a recorded failing job, not an overall passing Gateway flow.

Official [#170267](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170267), commit `0ae42f07a6537dab50cb6788d66e1c92aaef91d5`, intentionally removed the `AUTOMATION_FAILED` prose protocol. The current unattended-run docs and canonical `cron-blocked-outcome` QA require ordinary task-blocker prose to finish with status `ok`; runtime/provider failures remain structured errors. This fixture now uses `OWNED_BLOCKER_REPORT`, names its variables accordingly, and expects `ok` while preserving actual model execution, public report history, lastActivityAt and unread-positive assertions, along with every quiet and detached control. It does not change production error classification or replace a visible assistant report with a synthesized provider error. It is **not Gateway runtime-error proof**.

- Two existing real Cron outcome-owner controls, distinguishing ordinary output from structured errors while keeping delivery-target failure separate, pass: **2 passed / 7 unselected**, **95.987 seconds wrapper / 87.42 seconds Vitest**. They use the existing isolated orchestration harness and do not boot a Gateway; they are not execution of the corrected Gateway fixture.
- Final relevant test-consumer types pass in **22.947 seconds**, type-aware core lint in **26.585 seconds**; formatting, diff and the one-file native staged line-cap check pass. No new tests, sleeps, timeout changes, skips, mocks, permissions, schema or dependency changes are introduced.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the one-file correction plus its full fixture and accepted contract is scoped-clean; the committed fixture hash matches reviewed bytes. prs.title: feat: remove saved personal model accounts from Profile and CLI
prs.body:
Related: #178803

## Current revision and validation

Head: `a4ca426863b8d0096e5086a37415fbe130b388c3`. Integrated upstream main `b0e550ecc50d391f19d7f84c17c11d4e75111ff2` while preserving the account-removal changes. The removal entry point is now internal rather than a new member of the public connect-service contract. The returned affected-chat count describes completed cleanup, not a pre-removal preview.

Local validation on this revision: **174/174 focused tests**, plus **1/1 stable upgrade/removal/restart test** from v2026.10.8 (`dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`); strict plugin-SDK build checked **160 public subpaths**; core/UI types, changed-file lint and formatting passed. Independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. These are isolated synthetic checks, not live-provider or deployment acceptance; hosted CI is reported separately.

Submitted as ready for review. Maintainer acceptance of the bounded removal lifecycle and deferral of affected-chat preview remains open. No merge approval or new bot score is claimed. Earlier evidence and screenshots below retain their original revision and coverage limits.

## Earlier execution evidence — 2026-10-24

Evidence revision: `9d970f3ce72690064c72632ef345a18da2713a54`. Final authority rerun after lint-only cleanup: **6/6 passed**. Changed-file lint and Gateway-method test types passed.

This update supersedes the earlier CLI end-to-end coverage gap below. The registered production CLI parser removed a synthetic owned account over a real local TLS/WebSocket Gateway. The subsequent `chat.send` turn reached a local synthetic Anthropic-compatible endpoint with the configured default credential, completed, and placed `CHAT_AFTER_REMOVAL_OK` in the assistant history. The CLI runs in-process, not as a spawned installed binary. This next-turn proof covers a **durable** chat, not an incognito next turn or every provider/runtime. Existing screenshots below remain mocked-transport UI evidence, not screenshots of this integration run.

Combined local run: **4 files, 15 tests passed**, Node 26.12.1. It includes seven remaining worker cases (incognito memory-only cleanup, partial/retry included), six authority cases, stable upgrade/restart and CLI-to-chat. These are synthetic credentials and isolated local endpoints; no live account was removed or provider revoked.

```sh
B1_UPGRADE_SOURCE_CHECKOUT=/path/to/clean/stable-checkout B1_UPGRADE_SOURCE_COMMIT=fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/model-account-removal.worker.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/model-account-removal.authority.integration.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/model-account-removal.upgrade.integration.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/model-account-removal.cli-chat.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

<details>
<summary>Sanitized observed execution trace (selected lines; not a proposed result)</summary>

```text
[b1-upgrade] state generated by stable checkout fe06181dc5ec (credential values never printed)
[b1-upgrade] doctor --fix completed on stable-generated state
[b1-upgrade] stable state loads on PR build: 2 owner accounts over transport
[b1-upgrade] one account removed: kept+foreign rows, unrelated settings, kept pin, and rollback metadata preserved
[b1-upgrade] restart on PR build: removal, selections, and unrelated state survive reopen
[b1-removal-authority] owner transport removal: removed=true sessionCleanup=complete
[b1-removal-authority] storage after: removed credential row deleted; kept+foreign rows intact; pinned session override and rollback pin cleared; kept session byte-identical
[b1-removal-authority] admin transport denial (explicit owner target): code=FORBIDDEN
[b1-removal-authority] storage after denials: unchanged rows, unchanged session pin
[b1-removal-authority] revocation issued over transport: users.setRole owner -> revoked
[b1-removal-authority] storage after revoked fence: credential row, link row, and session pins unchanged
[b1-removal-authority] owner socket closed during preparation hold
[b1-removal-authority] storage after disconnected fence: credential row, link row, and session pins unchanged
[b1-removal-authority] deletion committed before authority loss (committed effect, no rollback claimed)
[b1-removal-authority] post-commit revoked: credential row stays deleted; session pins stay untouched
[b1-removal-authority] post-commit disconnected: credential row stays deleted; session pins stay untouched
[b1-cli-chat] registered CLI removed credential; current and rollback pins cleared
[b1-cli-chat] next Gateway chat completed; synthetic default selected; assistant confirmation present in history
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests  15 passed (15)
```

The upgrade source is the clean stable `v2026.10.6` checkout, pinned to the full commit above. Authority tests use deterministic holds around the real state operation; disconnected-client cases now wait for server-side operation settlement before asserting final stored effects. A committed deletion is **not** claimed to roll back after subsequent authority loss.
</details>

Simplification: removed the weaker in-process handler/auth-selection test and its imports (77 deleted lines, plus one corrected proof comment), now covered by the CLI/transport/next-turn scenario. Consolidated repeated mutation-hold setup. Production functionality and unique incognito, partial/retry, ownership and UI cases are retained. New runtime proof adds more lines than these deletions; this is not a claim of net PR shrinkage.

An independent source review of this delta found no actionable P0–P2 findings; it did not execute tests and lacked unchanged helper contracts. Local execution evidence is separate. No new rating is self-assigned.

**Remaining product decisions:** affected-chat preview and broader/incognito next-turn coverage remain open. The explicit [maintainer and SDK contract question](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181657#issuecomment-6379380750) is awaiting a decision; tests and bot ratings do not substitute for it.

## What Problem This Solves

Saved personal model accounts cannot be removed through Profile, the CLI or a supported Gateway operation, leaving duplicate or obsolete credentials in the account list.

## User Impact

Owners can explicitly remove their own saved account from this Gateway through Profile or `openclaw models accounts remove <account-id>`. This deletes the local credential record, not access at the provider. `clear-default` still keeps credentials.

This is a **implementation submitted for product review**, not a claim that the proposed lifecycle contract has been accepted. It does not yet show the number of affected chats before confirmation. Live incognito current/rollback pin cleanup now has focused native-worker coverage. Fallback behavior across every runtime remains unverified.

### Known gaps and product decisions

- **Pinned-chat count:** confirmation explains what removal does, but does not count or list affected chats. The reporter requested that count; it is not implemented here.
- **Incognito:** this update covers existing live memory owners, including agents without a durable session store, current/rollback pins, no durable persistence, and truthful partial cleanup/retry. This is bounded native-worker proof, not a claim about every runtime or provider.
- **Fallback coverage:** the native runtime resolves Gateway credentials in the tested synthetic scenario. No claim is made that every runtime behaves identically. Product acceptance of this lifecycle contract is still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removal uses the existing admitted credential transaction and retirement publication. It clears exact current and rollback account pins across discovered agent session stores without changing unrelated accounts or model choices. An already-open account picker refreshes instead of retaining a deleted row.

Credential deletion can succeed while chat cleanup fails. In that case, Profile offers a cleanup retry and the CLI reports partial completion with a nonzero exit status. Retrying the same account ID never restores its credential. Administrators cannot use this operation to delete another person's account, and shared credentials are outside its scope.

There is no provider-side revoke, schema migration or new background service.

Pre-publication overlap check: no PR referencing #178803 or implementing `users.removeModelAccount` was found. The merged #157745 handles existing credential-removal cleanup/recovery, and #174904 changes provider/shared-account controls; neither adds this personal-account removal operation. This change reuses the existing cleanup owner rather than replacing those flows.

## Evidence

### Incognito and transport/upgrade follow-up (2026-10-24)

- Incognito cleanup uses the existing memory session owner; it neither creates a new owner nor persists incognito sessions. Unrelated account/model selections and rollback metadata are retained.
- Independently rerun local checks: state removal 7/7; incognito/worker suite 8/8; real local Gateway transport and stable-upgrade suites 7/7; targeted gateway-methods types, changed-file lint and format checks passed. These are local synthetic results, not hosted CI or production acceptance.
- Regression negative control: omitting the incognito cleanup call makes the live-incognito test fail at the retained account pin; restoring the implementation passes. No mutation is retained.
- Transport coverage includes owner removal, foreign-admin denial, revoked writer and disconnected-client scenarios before/after credential commit. The transport is real local TLS/WebSocket with deterministic operation holds; no real provider or real account is used.
- Upgrade input is generated by the clean stable checkout pinned to `fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc`; the test requires that exact supplied commit and rejects a dirty source checkout. It exercises Doctor, removal and restart while checking unrelated state preservation.
- Independent autoreview of the follow-up delta against `999bfccdb7d522398876697a3e106c33bd9b8512` returned `scoped-clean` at P0–P2. It reviewed source, did not execute the project, and explicitly lacked unchanged implementation contracts. Local runtime checks above are separate evidence; this is not a new ClawSweeper rank.

Reproduce the follow-up with Node 26.12.1 and the repository test runner:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/model-account-removal.worker.test.ts src/state/user-model-account-removal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
B1_UPGRADE_SOURCE_CHECKOUT=/path/to/clean/stable-checkout B1_UPGRADE_SOURCE_COMMIT=fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/model-account-removal.authority.integration.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/model-account-removal.upgrade.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json --incremental
```

At that earlier revision, pinned-chat count, broad fallback coverage, client-to-Gateway end-to-end coverage and lifecycle acceptance remained open. The latest evidence above adds the bounded durable CLI-to-chat scenario; the other limits remain. The PR was draft at that revision; it is now submitted for review.

### Original candidate evidence (commit 999bfccd)

- Native SQLite: 33 tests passed, covering existing account behavior and seven removal cases. The foreign-owner guard was deliberately removed: its regression failed; restoring the guard passed.
- Gateway worker/handler: four tests passed, including retained-authority retirement, current and rollback pins across two agents, preservation of unrelated accounts, partial cleanup and retry. An existing synthetic chat resolved Gateway credentials after removal through the real RPC handler and native storage path.
- Profile/picker: 37 tests passed. CLI: 16 tests passed. The browser scenario covers cancel, confirmed removal, partial cleanup, retry and preservation of the other account.
- Production and selected test types, protocol registry/generation/native contracts, changed-file formatting/lint, and an independent final-diff review were checked locally. Hosted CI is reported separately in the PR checks; these local results are not a claim that hosted CI is green.

Local evidence is for commit `999bfccdb7d522398876697a3e106c33bd9b8512`, based on `4a5eef31765e801a2425afe35e5c9b05d57d5216`. The independent full-diff review reported no actionable P0–P2 findings; a separate fresh-context review covered the final equivalent exact-link loop simplification. Review was source-based, not an additional runtime test. No new manager, schema, background service, dependency or provider-revocation mechanism was introduced; the additional code wires the existing credential owner into Profile, CLI and RPC consumers and tests those boundaries.

<details>
<summary>Reproducible local commands and observed results</summary>

Run from the repository root in an isolated, dependency-installed checkout, with Node 24.20.0 and `CI=true OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`. Tests use synthetic identities and credentials.

```sh
# Native storage: 33/33 (26 existing cases + seven removal cases).
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts --configLoader runner src/state/user-model-account-removal.test.ts src/state/user-model-accounts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

# Gateway worker/handler: 4/4; final run 106.41 seconds.
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-database-workers.config.ts --configLoader runner src/gateway/model-account-removal.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

# Browser flow: 1/1; final run 39.96 seconds, including setup/build.
OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1 PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/model-account-removal.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

# Final affected canonical type graphs after file extraction: all four passed.
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core","core-test-gateway-root","core-test-state-logging","core-test-ui-e2e"]'
```

Additional focused suites: `ui/src/pages/profile/model-accounts.test.tsx` plus `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-controls.test.tsx` — 37/37; `src/commands/models/accounts.test.ts` — 16/16. These counts include existing regressions, not only new tests.

Ownership negative control: temporarily removing the exact credential-owner guard caused the foreign-owner/shared-ID regression to fail (`expected function to throw`). Restoring it passed all seven removal cases. No weakened guard remains. The final loop-only simplification was subsequently covered by those seven native tests, lint and the separate review; the type result above predates that equivalent simplification.

The native path exercises committed credential retirement, exact current and rollback pins across two agents, an unreadable-store partial result, and same-ID retry. The browser flow exercises cancel → no removal; confirm → credential removed, cleanup pending; retry → complete, with the other account preserved.

</details>

The browser capture uses the built Control UI and a **mocked Gateway with synthetic accounts**. The native handler test uses real state workers and SQLite, but is not a WebSocket/full-Gateway or real-provider test. No real account or provider token was removed or revoked. These are bounded WIP proofs, not production acceptance.

### Before and after the removal action

These inspected captures show the **candidate UI**, not a base-versus-patch visual comparison. Built Control UI in Chromium 156, mocked Gateway, two synthetic accounts. No private account or desktop content is shown.

Before confirmation — both saved accounts remain:

![Candidate UI before removal: two synthetic saved accounts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e894c93-4e34-4f83-80da-7477a8601a9f)

After removal and successful cleanup retry — only the unrelated account remains:

![Candidate UI after removal: the other account remains and completion is explicit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/799d6b10-4fb6-4bd6-aafb-6e7e3b759eaf)

<details>
<summary>Confirmation and truthful partial-completion state</summary>

![Confirmation separates local credential deletion from provider revocation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df5336db-d224-4e26-8594-91ccb0e7a941)

![Credential already removed, with a retry for pending chat cleanup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1948f16b-73a0-4e5b-894f-83065b6575b8)

prs.title: fix(update): update repair refuses PostgreSQL installations with "schema role missing" on the state anchor
prs.body:
Related: #187006 (the `openclaw update repair` refusal; the activation Doctor and Gateway-start symptoms in that issue are not changed here). #186328 and #186341 also edit `update-repair-command.ts`; they change the body of `repairUpdate`, this change wraps the `updateRepairCommand` entry point, so only the import block is adjacent.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update repair` refuses to run on an installation whose `state` family lives in PostgreSQL, failing in its preflight with "OpenClaw state database …/state/openclaw.sqlite has schema role missing; expected global", so the documented recovery after a failed update is unusable exactly when it is needed.

## User Impact

User impact: operators on PostgreSQL families can run `openclaw update repair` to finish or reconcile an update again. SQLite-only installations see no change. No new options, dependencies, or schemas.

## Why This Change Was Made

Updater-owned commands skip the CLI's boot-time database-engine selection (`update *` is in the owned list), so each updater entry point has to scope the authored `database.families` choice itself. `openclaw update` does this through `withUpdateDatabaseEngine` (added with PostgreSQL Gateway support in #174786); `openclaw update repair` never did. Without a scoped selection, the repair preflight falls through to the SQLite path and opens the 8 KiB PostgreSQL anchor as a SQLite state database, which has no `schema_meta` row and is refused.

The fix exports the existing wrapper and runs the whole repair inside it. No new module, option, dependency or schema; production delta +7/−2 lines in two files.

<details><summary>pr-simplify</summary>

An earlier revision moved the wrapper into a new `update-command-database-engine.ts` with its own unit tests. Those tested unchanged code, so they were dropped: the wrapper stays where it is and only gains `export`. The remaining test names the actual defect (repair not entering the wrapper). Whole-change delta against main: production +7/−2, tests +30 (one regression test; the mock factory spreads the real module exports as the mock-exports ratchet requires).
</details>

## Evidence

Base: main `08e08b72049`; fix commit `85adada5051` (production change), followed by `cb0a3452b71` (test-only: mock pass-through and the test-line ceiling). Installation: Git checkout on `dev`, macOS 15 arm64, Node 24, PostgreSQL 17, `database.families` = state/agent/workboard on `postgres`, 11 agents with SQLite anchors.

**Before (installed main `1b356b487d8e`, same code path), gateway healthy:**
```
$ OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external openclaw update repair --yes --no-restart --channel dev
[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:preflight","status":"failed","detail":"OpenClaw state database [redacted-path]", … "code":"finalization-failed"}
OpenClaw state database /Users/openclaw/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite has schema role missing; expected global. Run openclaw doctor --fix to inspect and repair its ownership.
```

**After (this branch built from source and run against the same installation):**
$ node /Users/openclaw/scratch/pr-187006/openclaw.mjs --version   # this branch, built with pnpm build
OpenClaw 2026.10.8
$ OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external node …/openclaw.mjs update repair --yes --no-restart --channel dev
[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:preflight","status":"in_progress",…}
[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:preflight","status":"completed",…}
[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:targetConfigValidation","status":"completed",…}
[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:configSnapshot","status":"completed",…}
[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:doctor","status":"skipped","detail":"Doctor could not enter maintenance. GatewayStateOwnerContentionError: OpenClaw state database is busy at [redacted-path]",…}
Doctor and plugin maintenance remain pending. Stop the Gateway through its service owner (`openclaw gateway stop --force` for the managed service), stop other OpenClaw processes using this state, then rerun `openclaw update repair`.
exit=2
The preflight that refused the anchor now completes; repair reaches its ordinary "Gateway still serving" decision and asks for a stop, which is the correct answer with a live Gateway (holder pid 29423, lease renewed seconds earlier). Output above is from the exact PR head (`85adada5051`), rebuilt with `pnpm build`; an earlier revision of the branch behaved identically. I did not run the stopped-Gateway continuation from this build against the live installation because the branch is 8 commits ahead of the serving build and its Doctor could migrate live PostgreSQL schemas past the serving Gateway (#186971 territory).
```

**Focused tests** (`pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-command.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`):
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  56 passed (56)
 ✓ update repair ledger recovery › scopes the configured database-engine selection around the whole repair
 (plus the 55 pre-existing repair tests)
```
- "scopes the configured database-engine selection around the whole repair": fails on base (the wrapper is never entered), passes on this branch; it also pins the order select → ownership check → finalize → release.

Typecheck (`pnpm tsgo:prod`: core, ui, extensions): ok. Baseline ratchets (`pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`): all ok after the second commit; `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` is raised by exactly the 30 test lines this PR adds (6,311,372 on `main` → 6,311,402), with no extra allowance. Lint (`scripts/run-lint.mts --base origin/main`): no findings in the changed files; the run reports 19 pre-existing `eslint(max-lines)` errors in untouched files that are already over the limit on `main`. Format: `pnpm format` clean.

Gaps: no PostgreSQL-backed automated test for repair (the repair harness mocks the state owner and finalize; a disposable-PostgreSQL run of the full repair, including the stopped-Gateway Doctor continuation, is the remaining proof). The two other refusals in #187006 (activation Doctor "migration source changed after update capture" on the state anchor; new Gateway refusing the agent anchors before the deferred migration ran) are in the delegated Doctor path, which #186971 is reshaping, and are left for that work.

prs.title: perf(ui): load session and account copy with its consumers
prs.body:
> **Current-head proof pending; auto-merge is not armed.** Current head `2d988d90d0c775eba1d607ea05e32ee98dbd48f4` integrates main `c2243320434e1c1ae99105f4b070e1a3a4d24479`. Current strict comparison: startup 281,415 → 280,862 raw B / 90,333 → 90,230 gzip B; Chat 4,017,365 → 4,009,720 raw B / 1,255,017 → 1,252,459 gzip B. Request counts unchanged. Production Knip and UI typecheck pass. Fresh paired coverage/readiness/CPU proof will replace the historical measurements below before merge. All older measurements below belong only to their named prior heads and must not be attributed to the current head.

## What Problem This Solves

Cold Chat loads the full English session-management and account-settings catalogs when its resident controls need only a small set of labels.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Chat downloads 19,336 fewer raw JavaScript bytes (5,109 fewer encoded bytes) in the measured cold load, with the same 62 JavaScript requests. Translation text, active locale, and existing UI behavior stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

The personal-session list and Chat account control now register small catalogs containing their required labels. Full session-management and account-settings copy remains with the existing lazy consumers. The full catalogs reuse the same string definitions in their existing property order, and registration still updates the existing namespace objects in place.

The slim catalogs stay in the measured shared boot chunk; the full catalogs have separate deferred chunks. This avoids adding a request to first-screen rendering. No new loader, state owner, dependency, or feature boundary is introduced.

## Evidence

Candidate: `71bb42bfde04bcdf73ccda15b989c9bb27a17623` against base `0e38bda9526bdde3c4287a5163ddbb6b47c7fe98`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Focused optional-English tests | 2 passed. The consumer-demand test fails on the base: it receives `Search groups` before the management catalog is requested. |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed. |
| `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` / `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` | Passed; translation content and full-catalog ordering preserved. |
| Production Knip | Same findings on base and head: `scheduleLine` and `runPrompt` in `extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-catalog.ts`; `SessionColdOversized` in `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-archive-types.ts`. No new findings. |
| Source review | Scoped review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; checked in-place namespace registration, preserved copy/order, and lazy full-catalog consumers. |
| UI build and strict performance check | Both sides built on the same machine; no strict-check violations. |
| Exact-build coverage | Final clean-head and base bundle identities verified by opening and closing censuses; all four coverage captures use the same frozen harness and Chromium. |
| Local / 100 ms RTT readiness, CPU, and long tasks | 20 base/base/head triplets per profile; readiness within the stated band. Byte-reduction claim only; adverse tails and A/A noise disclosed below. |

The focused test also checks that deferred registration preserves the active German locale and existing namespace object identities, and that a cold roster metadata failure remains readable. No markup or styling changes are intended.

### Actual cold-load bytes and V8 coverage

One diagnostic base/head pair per profile, desktop Chat, cold HTTP/browser cache, synthetic data. The RTT profile uses 100 ms latency and 10,000 kbps download. Coverage captures are separate from untraced timing.

| Profile / version | V8 loaded raw B | V8 executed raw B | V8 unused raw B | HTTP raw B | HTTP encoded B | JS requests |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Local / base | 4,158,683 | 1,938,911 | 2,219,772 | 4,566,057 | 1,256,770 | 62 |
| Local / head | 4,139,301 | 1,919,866 | 2,219,435 | 4,546,721 | 1,251,661 | 62 |
| 100 ms RTT / base | 4,158,683 | 1,937,435 | 2,221,248 | 4,566,057 | 1,256,770 | 62 |
| 100 ms RTT / head | 4,139,301 | 1,918,306 | 2,220,995 | 4,546,721 | 1,251,661 | 62 |

HTTP raw/encoded savings are **19,336 / 5,109 B** in both profiles. V8 loaded raw bytes fall by **19,382 B**. V8 marks most catalog initialization as executed, so unused-at-boot bytes fall by only **337 B locally and 253 B at 100 ms RTT**. This is a download/evaluation reduction; it is not a 19 KB reduction in V8-unused code, and coverage counts do not establish a CPU speedup.

### Strict bundle accounting

These are the checker's static route closures, distinct from the complete HTTP capture above.

| Surface | Raw JS B, base → head | Gzip JS B, base → head | JS requests, base → head |

| Startup | 281,104 → 281,104 | 90,299 → 90,301 | 3 → 3 |

Startup CSS remains **1 request, 32,745 B gzip**. The 2 B startup gzip difference is within the checker's 64 B build-variance allowance; startup raw bytes and requests are unchanged. Chat and New Session CSS are unchanged. No budget is raised.

### Timing and CPU

Twenty serial base/base/head triplets per profile (120 untraced cold loads total), with one frozen harness and no sample exclusions. Values below are median / nearest-rank p95; CPU/time values are milliseconds. The A/A column repeats the unchanged base. Host one-minute load was 13.20–18.83 locally and 9.10–14.41 at 100 ms RTT.

prs.title: fix: Shift-selection skips pinned sessions across sections
prs.body:
Related: #186229

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Shift-selection skips intervening pinned sessions and selects later section members when a range crosses Pinned and Sections.

## User Impact

Users can select a contiguous visible range from Pinned into Sections or ordinary sessions, in either direction. Duplicate appearances still produce one batch target; collapsed and archived section members remain excluded. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Selection now consumes appearances in the same Pinned → Sections → ordinary-session order that the sidebar renders. This is a one-line production ordering repair using the existing selection owner, with no new state or flags.

## Worked on by

- @shakkernerd

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @shakkernerd](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2209f173-3c22-4586-853c-8e8a45b2e90a)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/015f154e-dec5-4e54-ba56-3f08e95ae95f)

## Evidence

- Real Chromium UI against the canonical synthetic mock Gateway: the extended existing browser regression failed on base `bb6c6a5a27637228a5c5d8c161821e5d926b205d`, selecting `first/last/middle` instead of `first/middle/release`. It passes with this repair in both directions and verifies exact selected keys and unique batch targets.
- The complete affected browser file passed all 8 tests (42.63 s test time; 62.23 s invocation wall time including production build and capture). This file covers complete section editing/navigation flows that cheaper helper tests do not exercise. Final regression after mechanical lint fixes passed (2.75 s test time, 16.31 s wall time).
- Selection-owner sibling suite: 31 tests passed (2.24 s invocation). UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Broader checks are delegated to PR CI; no live Gateway or user state was used.
- Fresh local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, complete local diff against the base above): scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The reviewer disclosed that unchanged source context and runtime execution were not included; independent browser and sibling proof above supplies runtime evidence. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its existing checkout was dirty; [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187060#issuecomment-6482760081) of this exact head found no actionable issues.
- Tested commit `4de69429f50ccf315c30aebb6dcd5b0b3965663d` and published head `fe33b90da6108280012887d725c5553744b0d76b` have identical tree `4d4985c40f3a22a5c041d0a207460c98309e1906`.
- The two public screenshot assets were byte-for-byte verified against the inspected local PNGs and visually inspected in the actual rendered PR body (both 1280 × 900).
- Broad [CI run 40781747793](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40781747793) completed **failed**, with 10 older sidebar-test failures in two E2E shards. An isolated, unmodified checkout of its exact main parent `9cb54474` reproduces the missing section-heading selector, obsolete direct-child selector, and rail-tooltip interception. The remaining agent-menu focus failure did not reproduce locally; its inputs are unchanged and it has no personal groups, so this ordering swap has identical output there. These failures are retained, not relabeled green; landing uses the repository’s attributed-inherited-failure path. No unrelated UI/test cleanup or CI rerun was performed.
- Simplification: production +1/−1 line, test +60/−14 lines; existing browser regression extended rather than adding a parallel owner or test-only seam.

The same Alt-click on the first pin followed by Shift-click on the middle section row, with synthetic data at 1280 × 900:

### Before

The intervening second pin is skipped and the later section row is incorrectly selected.

![Before: Shift-selection skips the second pin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa339a5e-11fb-45dd-be3b-1c23caef3428)

### After

The range includes the intervening pin and stops at the clicked section row. Repeated appearances of the same selected session remain highlighted together.

![After: Shift-selection follows visible sidebar order](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8efce7cb-01b1-47da-a5d1-f6f944492d13)

prs.title: fix(gateway): reject stale exact-run cancellation after session replacement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: API clients cannot bind an exact-run Stop request to the physical conversation they observed, leaving them without a stale-session guard when that conversation is replaced.

## User Impact

Clients can pass `sessionId` alongside `runId` to reject cancellation against a replaced session or a mismatched local or worker run. Existing callers that omit the fence retain their current Stop behavior. There are no configuration changes or migrations; the fence does not grant additional cancellation permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cancellation authorization owner now resolves the optional physical-session restriction alongside scoped-caller and queued-input restrictions. Exact-run selection applies it before cancellation, while retaining the current source-capture, ownership, sibling-run, and incognito behavior. The protocol schema and generated validator accept the new optional field.

Contributor credit: Adapted from Galin Iliev (@galiniliev)'s reviewed cancellation changes in `fa6b7bc1fb5db71d8a1ef2e0883c01971608ee4e` at his request; unrelated changes from that commit are excluded.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d0705165-5352-4f6e-955d-99ab0c2be386)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/3656f067-4801-4570-9b95-c36851d2338e)

## Evidence

- Published test consolidation `906f40233625b933d8511892eb59b3f78e12b932` reuses the surviving old local/worker owners after exact current-worker Stop, then proves unreadable fenced refusal and unfenced best effort. Production is unchanged. The two worker scenarios become one; the separate local-owner/sibling scenario remains. Ping/pong barriers and incremental terminal identities/outcomes remain explicit. The file shrinks from 334 to 315 lines (net −19), with no removed helper, import, production seam, or test contract.
- Consolidation validation: all 84 tests pass across the six RPC-fence, authorization, read-error, source-withdrawal, incarnation, and agent-scope files (114.81 seconds command wall time). The changed file also passes alone: 2 tests, 13.24 seconds Vitest / 48.32 seconds command wall time. Baseline: 3 tests, 68.99 seconds Vitest / 73.09 seconds command wall time; compiler-cache/fixture startup differed, so these single observations are not a causal speedup measurement. The worker phase itself changes from two observed runs of 0.804 and 0.798 seconds to one of 1.024 seconds. Published head `c05a3ff7da47f74845ec622a0d7318a9dd969e25` has the same complete tree as this tested candidate; current-head CI completed successfully (details below). Targeted types, lint, formatting, staged diff checks, and canonical test-line accounting pass: 6,301,924 / 6,310,000, slack 8,076; no baseline modification.
- Fresh independent consolidation review: local autoreview (Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P2) reviewed the final local delta against `3a3dcc16a5510dec20b545a5d9b97fa2ead15e8c`, committed unchanged as `906f40233625b933d8511892eb59b3f78e12b932`: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Source/diff review only; the reviewer did not execute the validation commands. The cause of the prior-head Android timeout remains unresolved; its history is retained below.

prs.title: improve(ui): cut Browser panel input and refresh latency
prs.body:
<!-- Related: none -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI Browser panel feels laggy. Typing or pasting faster than the Gateway round trip sends one request per chunk and queues them, so characters land hundreds of milliseconds late. A wheel scroll waits a full interval before the first movement. When the panel falls back to screenshots, every action waits a fixed 350 ms refresh timer on top of the action's own round trip.

## User Impact

User impact: in the screenshot-fallback path and for fast typing or paste, the page reflects input sooner (numbers below). A live screencast is unchanged for clicks, slow typing, panel open and tab switch. Costs: a wheel burst sends slightly more scroll requests (the first delta goes out immediately instead of after an interval), and a slow resize drag now waits 150 ms of quiet before the sharp frame (about 44 ms later in the measurement) but no longer restarts mid-drag at a stale width. No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delays stay where they protect against races; waste is removed:
- Text queued behind an in-flight request is joined into one `insertText` (ordering with clicks and keys is preserved: a click or key starts a new batch).
- The wheel throttles instead of debouncing: the first delta scrolls at once, later deltas coalesce for one interval.
- The post-action refresh subtracts the time the action already took from the 350 ms settle delay. If a capture is still pending, retries stay 350 ms apart.
- The stream resize restart waits for the layout to stop changing for 150 ms instead of a fixed 500 ms deadline.

## Evidence

Measured in real Chrome against the repo's mock-Gateway UI e2e harness with injected latency (40 ms RTT, 150 ms screenshot, 100 ms frame cadence), 20 runs per version per mode, order before/after/after/before. **Real CDP and real network latency were not measured.** Medians (taken before the parallel page-geometry read was dropped; it showed no gain):

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| typing 20 chars @15 ms/char, last char reaches page (stream) | 675 ms, 20 requests | 55 ms, 8 requests |
| typing 20 chars @15 ms/char, last-char frame visible (fallback) | 1072 ms | 285 ms |
| typing @70 ms/char, frame visible (fallback) | 485 ms | 288 ms |
| click to updated frame (fallback) | 613 ms | 571 ms |
| wheel burst, first movement (stream) | 135 ms, 5 scroll requests | 78 ms, 7 scroll requests |
| wheel burst, first movement (fallback) | 769 ms | 567 ms |
| click, panel open, tab switch (stream) | unchanged within noise | |
| slow resize drag, last change to sharp frame (stream) | 242 ms (3 of 20 runs never sharp) | 286 ms (20 of 20 sharp) |

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/components/browser` in `ui/`: 24 files, 274 tests pass; 10 new or changed tests fail without the production change.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, oxfmt check, oxlint on the changed files: clean. `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passes on this head merged with current main.
- Not run: the existing browser e2e files were not re-run after the final edit, and the harness itself is not part of this PR.
- The stream-mode click and typing @70 differences of +6 and +16 ms are within noise (overlapping ranges).
- Not observed: a real managed browser over CDP, the native bridge.

prs.title: perf(gateway): trim placement retirement inventory replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Placement retirement repeatedly transfers complete placement records after session or environment invalidation, although its discovery pass only uses session ID, agent ID, and session key.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Retirement discovery allocates and transfers less data. No schema, stored-shape, configuration, retention, or FIFO changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ordered placement worker now selects the three consumed identity columns. The host adds memory-only local identities from the existing placement owner, including released local claims. Absent-session cleanup still reads the complete current placement before retirement or environment teardown and retains the existing generation, claim, and ownership checks.

Full-record inventory remains for startup/recovery consumers that need it; retirement no longer uses it. This adds a narrow projection rather than a new cache or revision protocol. Runtime production code is +36 lines: the narrow SQL projection, its registry entry, and the local-only identity overlay are required to preserve discovery semantics. Benchmark/Knip/inventory tooling is +130 lines; the requested non-test/non-doc diff is +166 lines in total.

## Evidence

Acceptance declared before measurement: fewer reply bytes and allocated bytes without a consistent CPU regression, with unchanged identity selection and retirement safeguards. The committed owner benchmark uses real placement SQL, V8 reply serialization, and host deserialization on 10,000 synthetic placements across 40 agent identities. Five counterbalanced AB/BA pairs, 40 scans per arm per pair: 200 scans/arm for timing and another 200/arm for allocation (2 million row visits/arm/pass). CPU is untraced; allocation is separately sampled at 32 KiB including collected objects. Host one-minute load was 38.5–55.1.

| Owner metric | Full records | Identity projection | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Reply bytes/scan | 4,375,009 | 1,115,009 | −74.5% |
| CPU ms/scan, paired mean | 38.79 | 9.56 | −75.4% |
| Sampled allocated MB/scan, paired mean | 28.31 | 7.58 | −73.2% |
| Synthetic reply MB/min at one invalidated scan/min | 4.375 | 1.115 | −74.5% |
| Inventory calls/min at that cadence | 1 | 1 | unchanged |

Command: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/placement-retirement-replies.mjs --rows 10000 --iterations 40 --pairs 5`.

The recurring census is eligible on a 60-second reconciliation cadence after full invalidation; unchanged idle reconciliation does not scan. Keyed reads already use the placement replica, active recovery uses the separate `workers` request class, and metadata snapshots already return a narrow projection. Read-only production counters before deployment showed 1.630 MB/min of `workerPlacements` replies, with 1.105 writer requests/min and 0.100 state-reader requests/min. Request-class counters alone do not identify the exact production suboperation mix, so these are synthetic per-census savings, not a measured post-deployment production rate.

This is the lane's projection-only fast path: no whole-Gateway stress run or claim about Gateway main-thread CPU, GC, latency tails, or RSS. Those remain deployment/load-test measurements.

Validation: 102 tests passed across the retirement, evidence, placement-read, session-event/recovery consumers and the two source-closure guard files (354 s including compiled-worker preparation). The final retirement file passed all 8 tests again after consolidating a redundant assertion (15 s wrapper wall time, under 1 s total test execution). The committed byte-budget regression fails on pre-fix main `70bf5121704c7a7173722c2bd7e360362e5da165` at 1,726 bytes against a <1,024-byte budget and passes on the candidate; it also proves detached identities, active/released local-only claims, and refusal to retire owned requests.

`pnpm tsgo:test:root` and both affected Gateway test configs passed. Changed-file lint/format, `git diff --check`, and export-name collision guard passed. After the final rebase: test-line ratchet 6,311,699 / 6,320,000, no baseline edit in this PR. The rebase only required preserving adjacent benchmark entries in the Knip index; the measured placement owners are unchanged on the new base. The benchmark has an exact Knip entry; a full-tree unused-file scan was not run under this lane's local compute restriction.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): fresh-context Codex review of the frozen diff and complete owner/publication/registry context, P0–P2 clean with no actionable findings. Autoreview preflight refused a provider-route mismatch; operator configuration was unchanged. Review confirmed identity ordering, local-only inclusion, replica publication/invalidation freshness, post-await admission, and retained retirement/teardown checks. Subsequent edits only removed a redundant test assertion, registered the benchmark entrypoint, and ensured its scratch parent exists.

Initial CI caught a missed scripts-side consumer in `placement-session-evidence-measure.ts`: its in-memory retirement fixture still exposed `listAsync`. The follow-up now prepares and supplies three-field identities through `listSessionIdentitiesAsync`. Script typecheck, strict root-test typechecks, changed-script lint, and its 10-iteration smoke passed (11 evidence passes, 11,000 subjects, one inventory read). Independent follow-up review is P0–P2 clean. No runtime change was needed.

CI also caught the new query missing from the existing exact-operation database-worker inventory. Caller tracing confirms its sole runtime caller is `placement-lifecycle.worker.ts`; the other caller is the isolated benchmark. Added that exact symbol and worker-caller evidence, with no broader reclassification. The focused actual-source inventory probe returns W; script and strict root-test typechecks, changed-script lint/format, and independent review passed. Runtime owners are unchanged by the final rebase.

Final exact-head CI: [`40780691453`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40780691453) passed on `2dcefb997f3bf1ffb5d667929051d32a30f9ca71`, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, strict test types, baseline ratchets, and the aggregate CI gate. Applicable security review passed. PR left ready and unmerged for the coordinating maintainer.

prs.title: chore(installer): add Windows Git selector reproduction fixture
prs.body:
Related: #127352

## What Problem This Solves

The Windows Git installer accepts an explicit `-Tag` but can reach dependency installation on its current branch instead of the requested ref. This PR records a standalone reproduction; it does not fix the installer.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. This is a manually invoked diagnostic fixture, not an always-on CI test. It is being submitted for review as reproduction tooling only. Omitted `-Tag`, explicit `latest`, and `-NoGitUpdate` policy remain undecided.

**Decision for Dallin — undecided:** For existing Git checkouts, should omitted `-Tag` preserve the current branch, should explicit `latest` select the published stable release, and how should explicit selectors interact with `-NoGitUpdate`? No default policy is selected by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture uses distinguishable commits in a disposable local Git remote, loads the complete installer through its public parameters, and re-enters the real `Main` dispatcher. It records the selected HEAD at `Ensure-Pnpm` and stops before dependencies, build, wrapper publication, Doctor, or service operations. Clone, pull, checkout validation, and selector decisions remain production code. Only explicit main/tag/missing selectors with updates enabled have contract assertions.

Only `test/scripts/install-git-selector.ps1` is added: +196 test lines and zero production lines. A one-line correction selects the first Git `ApplicationInfo`, preserving discovery order while producing a single executable path. Without it, a PATH containing both `/usr/bin` and `/bin` returned two Git applications and the fixture attempted to invoke their combined paths as one command. Production installer behavior, recovery/worktree behavior, and CI configuration remain unchanged; no extra abstraction or policy was added.

## Evidence

### Corrected candidate: Linux PowerShell 7.6.9

The original discussion session executed the following bounded proof in a task-owned Docker environment; this publishing session verified the integrated and published hashes, one-line delta, full tree, and whitespace. This is Linux proof, not native Windows or a full installation.

- Corrected fixture SHA-256: `b630598930e90c05bbfcde860b92ac2cbf6e4cc5f8716673dce18d06e51ef8eb`. The pinned installer from `e135fce9d7b2daeaebb26998b133523563e9509f` is unchanged, SHA-256 `7cd362c179c34825842406c5efe8e07e575b70e7ae57e3f240a5c93a47cf1203`. Integration base remains `5bab0c1454827e1819ca670ac476903483229dc5`.
- Before correction, all 20 cases failed during setup when Git was discovered at both `/usr/bin` and `/bin`; none emitted a `RESULT:`. These are fixture failures, not selector-defect proof.
- After correction, all 20 fresh/existing × five selectors × Git-update-on/off observations completed the real `Main`/Git path to `Ensure-Pnpm`. Six explicit-update contracts were evaluated: five correctly expose the still-unfixed selector defect, while fresh/main succeeds by default-branch coincidence. The other 14 combinations remain observation-only; this is not 20 passing product contracts.
- Three additional existing-checkout main/tag/missing runs with `-AssertExplicitContract` emitted wrong-working-HEAD receipts and exited 1 as expected.
- All four existing worktree scenarios (valid, missing HEAD, broken gitfile, subdirectory) and the unchanged pull-conflict fixture passed. The latter verified a rebase-abort reflog, restored HEAD/status, and no active rebase.
- PowerShell parsed five inputs with zero errors: installer, old and corrected selector fixtures, and existing worktree/pull fixtures. Total corrected-candidate proof time: 14.064 seconds. Fixture roots were removed; no package installation, build, wrapper publication, Doctor, service, or onboarding operation ran.
- The portable official Linux x64 PowerShell 7.6.9 archive was verified against its API asset digest and official hashes file: SHA-256 `1da6d6d6035d651f20e70ddee7c4c15ac6ab8b9fb40ee92240d91263f28a884b`. It was task-local; no shared-host installation or PATH/service change.
- Fresh independent source-only review (P0–P2) of the full corrected fixture found no actionable findings. The reviewer did not execute code or independently hash supplied bytes; the execution owner and this integration bind the reviewed/tested candidate by the SHA-256 above. This is a narrative independent review, not an Auto Review-helper result.

**Remaining gaps:** The corrected candidate has not run under native Windows PowerShell 5.1/7. PSScriptAnalyzer, Vitest, and a full installer run remain unrun. Parser success is not a lint pass, and CI on the prior head is not CI proof for the corrected head. The fixture is not wired into always-on CI.

### Historical evidence and review (2026-10-28)

- The original fixture SHA-256 was `3187a3b895831909b1fa5ca980642fb710f31b0b7904ad3158a42d6ba360611c`. Historical Codex-reported native Windows runs used PowerShell 7.6.9 and Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9444: existing-clean-checkout main/tag/missing with updates enabled, three of twenty combinations per engine. All six reached the pre-build boundary at working-remote and failed the explicit-selector contract (exit 1).
- Those six runs used installer source `5962ce779a8a425d1ffc9e1279b6242154c467e9`, SHA-256 `d8c1395e4e463c2e8faef8898fe5b6ac073df021581496851cfa26f3abd5096d`. They do not establish native Windows execution of the corrected fixture or the newer pinned installer.
- Before initial draft publication, local Auto Review terminated with exit 143 after allocator diagnostics exceeded its output limit; no validated review report was produced. Mert explicitly authorized that initial reproduction-only draft publication without a completed review, with the failure and then-unrun tests disclosed. That attempt remains a failed review, not a clean helper result.
- [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187029#issuecomment-6481435031) found no actionable findings on prior head `e135fce9d7b2daeaebb26998b133523563e9509f`, executed no target code, and retained the Windows execution gap. It predates this one-line correction.

<details>
<summary>Manual reproduction</summary>

Run in a new PowerShell process with Git and Node already available. Use a new disposable fixture directory; the fixture removes only the root it creates. For example:

```powershell
pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File test/scripts/install-git-selector.ps1 -InstallerPath scripts/install.ps1 -FixtureRoot "$PWD/selector-repro-main" -Checkout existing -Selector main -AssertExplicitContract
```

Repeat with `-Selector tag` and `-Selector missing`, each using a new root. The Linux PowerShell runs against the pinned installer produced a `RESULT:` record with `contractSatisfied:false`, followed by exit 1, for these three existing-checkout assertions. A nonzero exit alone is not reproduction proof: verify that setup succeeded and inspect `buildBoundaryReached`, the selected HEAD, and `outcome`.

Omit `-AssertExplicitContract` to collect observations without failing for the known selector defect. Omitted/latest selectors and `-DisableGitUpdate` combinations remain observations, not selected policy.

</details>

## Contributor credit

Reproduction work contributed by @MertBasar0.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @MertBasar0](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0dd07137-b2dd-4aa4-b9c4-7a682d78f174)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/eb84f3c4-d1b8-40b3-a360-a01e348be8c8)

The original discussion owns the supplied fixture, historical Windows evidence, corrected-candidate Linux execution, and independent review coordination; the second session owns correction integration and publication verification.

prs.title: fix(telegram): sibling bot's deleted stream previews corrupt group history
prs.body:
Closes #164958

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in a group running two OpenClaw bots, one bot's streamed reasoning preview (the 🧠 draft) is recorded into the other bot's persistent message cache as an ordinary message. Telegram never delivers message deletions to other bots, so when the streaming side deletes the superseded preview, every sibling cache keeps its copy. From then on, each group turn's history window carries that foreign reasoning text, and Anthropic rejects the whole turn with `reasoning_extraction`. The issue's live capture shows the orphaned preview surviving in cache long after it disappeared from Telegram.

## User Impact

User impact: multi-bot Telegram groups stop breaking on streamed reasoning previews. Once a preview is confirmed deleted, every account's history cache drops it, so later turns no longer inherit dead draft text from a sibling bot. No config change or migration is needed. The fix handles deletions observed after deployment and does not claim to clean up pre-existing orphans.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix tracks previews precisely instead of classifying by content, which is the direction the review discussion on the issue called for. The draft stream is the one component that knows the exact message id of a superseded preview, and it already waits for Telegram to confirm the delete. It now reports that id through a new `onPreviewRetired` callback, and the dispatch layer fans the retirement out to every configured account's message cache, including the sender's own (its cache recorded the preview too). Each cache drops the entry from the live map and the persisted store: retained group history through a compare-and-delete loop, bounded private-chat history through a map delete plus store delete. Nothing keys on message text, prefixes, or usernames, so ordinary bot messages are never misclassified. If Telegram rejects or never confirms the delete, nothing is retired, because the preview may still be visible and its history copies are then still honest.

## Evidence

- New `preview-retirement.test.ts`: two accounts each holding the same preview id in group (retained) and private (bounded) history, fan-out retires it from both and keeps neighboring messages; a single-account config with no `channels.telegram` section still covers the implicit default account.
- New cache tests: `retireMessage` evicts from the live map and the persisted store, a reopened bucket does not resurrect the entry, repeat retirement returns false, non-native ids are rejected, and other chats with the same message id are untouched.
- New draft-stream tests: `onPreviewRetired` fires exactly once after a confirmed supersede delete, and never fires when the delete is rejected or returns unconfirmed.
- Review round 4 follow-ups (head 8e35a3e79d5, rebased onto current main a134038ad7f): retirement fan-out now keys on the Bot API chat type carried from the inbound message instead of the `-100` id prefix, so a basic group whose id was recycled into the supergroup space stays account-local; `record()` and `retireMessage` serialize per cache key through a writer chain shared across all cache instances over the same bucket, so a record in flight while retirement lands from a separate fan-out handle can no longer write the preview back; the persisted tombstone settles before retirement reports done, keeping the fence across restarts. New regression tests cover the recycled-id basic group, channel fan-out, unknown chat type staying local, and both store paths racing retirement mid-write.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/preview-retirement.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.retained.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed. The same command over `message-cache.test.ts` and `draft-stream.test.ts`: 64 passed. oxfmt and oxlint passed on the five touched files.
- Earlier head `c3677719ea19cfb0f1c7461c70a535153adb4634` had green CI. Current head `e5a3c6a5ae3a7f9c981ef41f861353624649fa66` includes the lint and persisted-retirement follow-ups, with fresh CI required.

- New cross-instance regression in `message-cache.retained.test.ts`: two cache handles over the same bucket, one recording and one retiring the same key. The retire from the second handle completes its fence and delete before the first handle's compare commits; without the shared writer queue the stale observation resurrects the preview. This test fails on the previous per-instance chains and passes after moving `keyWriteChains` onto the shared bucket.
- New persisted-eviction regression: 3,000 rows are seeded with message 1 and preview 2. Reading message 1 makes it newest in memory, then row 3001 evicts preview 2 from the memory LRU while SQLite evicts message 1 by creation order. Retirement previously returned false and left preview 2 persisted; it now deletes the persisted key independently of memory membership and the reopened cache stays empty. Current verification across `message-cache.test.ts`, `message-cache.retained.test.ts`, `preview-retirement.test.ts`, and `draft-stream.test.ts`: 79 passed. oxfmt and type-aware oxlint pass on the changed files.

Gap I want to be explicit about: I could not stage the live two-bot Anthropic reproduction locally, so the end-to-end proof rides on the issue's live capture for the failure side and on the cache/draft-layer tests above for the fix side. The retirement path itself is covered at every layer it touches; a maintainer with two bots can confirm in one group turn by watching the sibling's cache stay empty after the preview is deleted. Latest-stable upgrade evidence with existing history and settings is also still open.

prs.title: perf(agents): defer unused tool-schema canonical fingerprints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tool-schema publication eagerly canonicalizes and hashes provider-normalized variants even though their consumers only need the published schema. Repeated publication therefore allocates sorted JSON strings that are never used.

## User Impact

Lower CPU and allocation during tool-schema preparation, with unchanged provider request bytes, prompt-cache digests, schema validation, and source-mutation isolation. No configuration or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compute the canonical fingerprint on its first read and memoize it in the existing immutable publication. The publication owner already detaches and recursively freezes the schema; its WeakMap lifetime bounds the memo, and every replacement publication gets a new fingerprint. The wire-order fingerprint remains unchanged.

The remaining cost is visible after #170610 and #185132: finalization prewarms provider schemas, and the normalization owner publishes those variants separately. Prompt comparison and diagnostics consume source canonical fingerprints; provider variants do not. This removes unused work without adding cross-session or content-keyed schema caches. Runtime production delta: **+4 lines** (benchmark tooling +65; total non-test delta +69); the getter and its local memo preserve the existing read-only property contract. Test delta: **-1 line**, with the work-count regression folded into existing provider coverage. Benchmark usage stays in the existing script header.

## Evidence

Acceptance: unchanged request bytes and canonical digests, lower canonical work, and non-adverse owner CPU/allocation. Synthetic owner workload: 80 synthetic tools (the tool-count scale of two tools × 40 plugins), fresh publications followed by real strict OpenAI conversion, including consumption of every source fingerprint. Five counterbalanced AB/BA pairs, 40 turns per arm per pair: **200 turns / 16,000 tools / 32,000 first publications per revision**. CPU is untraced; allocations include collected objects in a separate 4 KiB sampling pass. No own test or typecheck ran during the paired campaign. Baseline: `d840d4bab300`, with the same measurement script applied.

| Per 80-tool turn | Base mean | Candidate mean | Paired mean change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| First publications | 160 | 160 | unchanged |
| Canonical serializations | 160 | 80 | -50% |
| Canonical JSON bytes serialized | 89,760 | 44,880 | -50% |
| Process CPU | 7.699 ms | 7.079 ms | -8.10% (-0.620 ms) |
| Wall time | 6.040 ms | 5.373 ms | -11.05% (-0.667 ms) |
| Sampled allocation | 11,275,417 B | 9,180,076 B | -18.58% (-2,095,341 B) |

Every pair improved both CPU and allocation. CPU ranges: base 7.476–7.993 ms, candidate 6.792–7.876 ms; allocation ranges: base 11.251–11.325 MB, candidate 9.127–9.221 MB. Host one-minute load per pair: 32.52, 30.95, 29.43, 28.36, 27.69 (same sampled load for both arms within each pair). Each process completed in under 3 seconds. Five samples are insufficient for a tail-latency claim.

Both revisions produced the same 54,631-byte provider payload with SHA-256 `6003569e7a8003306379d4246889f80ee4ee041f6af7a3d8fb3a3f6b59ad3085` and the same source canonical digest. Canonical byte work comes from precise function counts multiplied by the verified equal JSON length of source and normalized fixture schemas.

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/tool-schema-request-admission-measure.ts \
  --tools 80 --iterations 40 --samples 1 --mode publication --strict
```

The provider-variant work-count regression fails on base with five eager canonical serializations and passes with the fix. Existing owner and updated consumer tests together cover real provider conversion, first-read work, repeated-read reuse, reordered keys, source mutation, and restored transcript pins. Provider payload bytes are also checked by the benchmark.

Focused proof: all 96 tests across `openai-tool-schema-reuse`, `anthropic-tool-projection`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, `session-prompt-state`, and `prompt-cache-observability` pass. Local focused runs include cold compiler preparation; the initial focused run took 182 s and the first consumer rerun took 62 s. Changed-file formatting/lint, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, package-test and agent-other test typechecks, and a strict root-test-config check including the benchmark passed. Test-lines ratchet after consolidation passed at 6,311,693 / 6,311,700. The final rebase inherited main’s newer ceiling: 6,312,177 / 6,320,000, 7,823 lines slack. This PR does not edit the ceiling. The first CI attempt passed tests/lint but failed this ratchet after the pre-push rebase picked up 64 test lines from main. Consolidating the new regression and simplifying touched test cleanup changed this PR from +35 to -1 test line; no coverage or ceiling exception was needed.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): fresh-context P0–P2 review of the complete local diff and relevant owners/consumers found no actionable findings. The configured autoreview helper refused its provider route because it did not match the operator configuration; configuration was not changed. The independent reviewer also reviewed the consolidated test proof and found no actionable findings. Rebase preserved the reviewed patch exactly. Reviewed head: `6e0da9f891be7a84cb991fb71f18d317bf0676f1`. Exact-head [CI run 40781717070](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40781717070) completed successfully: 61 checks passed, 56 intentionally skipped, none failed or pending. Current-head hosted Codex review also completed with no findings. ClawSweeper’s sole P2 reviewed the prior head’s +35 test-line failure; the net -1 consolidation, inherited main update, and green exact-head ratchet resolve it.

Scope of measurements: owner preparation only. Under the requested redundant-work fast path, no ten-minute Gateway stress or A/A campaign was run; no whole-Gateway CPU, GC, event-loop/list latency, or RSS/heap improvement is claimed. No live deployment was accessed or changed.

prs.title: fix(agents): channel owner's subagent keeps native runtime access after the owner is removed
prs.body:
Related: #185597, #185476

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a subagent spawned by a channel owner (for example a Telegram owner in `commands.ownerAllowFrom`) keeps running on its native runtime, such as Muse, after that person stops being an owner.

## User Impact

An owner's subagent keeps remembered native runtime consent (`nativeRuntimeConsent`) only while the spawner is still an owner. When an operator removes the owner, the child stops before its next native dispatch. Children spawned by non-owners still get refused, and owner-spawned children still dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

#185597 made remembered consent cover an owner's own turns. A child run already gets its owner fact from the spawner's live requester check (`prepareCommandOwnerAuthority`), not from the stored `spawnedBySenderIsOwner` receipt. But that check ran only while the Gateway admitted the child. After that, nothing checked it again, so removing the owner did not stop the child.

This change adds the same check to the child run's source assertion. A channel owner's own turn already uses this pattern (`captureCommandOwnerAssertion` in the run's `assertSourceCurrent`). The harness host checks that assertion just before native dispatch. If the check fails, it stays failed for the rest of the run.

## Evidence

Regression test (in-process): production-boundary test `fences remembered native consent for a child spawned by a channel %s`. It runs the real `sessions_spawn` tool, then the in-process Gateway `agent` admission, then the child's run parameters. The parent turn is a Telegram sender. The agent config has `nativeRuntimeConsent: ["native-fixture"]` and the child session modes are unset. The model-facing `senderIsOwner` receipt is `true` in both rows.

- Owner (`telegram:456`): the child gets `senderIsOwner: true` and `assertAgentHarnessExecutionEnvironment` returns consent. When the owner is removed after admission, the captured admitted-run assertion (the one the harness host checks before `runAttempt`) throws.
- Guest (`telegram:789`): the child gets `senderIsOwner: false` and consent is refused, even with an owner receipt.
- Negative control: without the production change, the owner row fails because nothing stops the child after revocation.

Also ran:
- The full spawn production-boundary file (106 tests), `agent.test.ts` and `agent.followup-owner.test.ts` (414 tests), and `execution-environment.test.ts`: all pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and `git diff --check`: clean.


### Live proof: Telegram Test Server + real Muse

Isolated Gateway with a leased Telegram Test Server bot and user. The parent agent is a deterministic mock model that issues a real `sessions_spawn`. Children run on the real Muse runtime (`meta/muse-spark-1.3`, Muse Code 1.4.11). Config: `nativeRuntimeConsent: ["muse"]`, `agents.defaults.subagents.model: meta/muse-spark-1.3`, `subagents.maxConcurrent: 1`. The tester is made an owner through `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, then removed by editing the config file while child A runs on Muse.

A Gateway detail controls the timing: it defers an owner-removal config reload until active runs end, or until its 300 s timeout. Child A runs a 330 s shell `sleep` on Muse, so the removal takes effect while A is still running.

| Step | `main` (`32f9477bf4`) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Owner's child A dispatches to Muse | Yes: Muse replies (`muse-spark-1.3`) | Yes: Muse replies (`muse-spark-1.3`) |
| Owner removed; reload applies after 300 s timeout | Applied | Applied |
| Child A's next native dispatch | **Continues**: `FIRST_CHILD_DONE` is delivered to Telegram | **Stopped**: "Requester owner authority changed; send a new request." |
| Queued child B (admitted before removal) | Refused, no Muse turn | Refused, no Muse turn |
| Guest's child (tester not an owner) | — | Refused before Muse I/O: "Muse Code cannot enforce this conversation's tool policy." No Muse assistant turn. |

So the discriminating case is a child that is already running when the removal applies. A queued child was already refused on `main`.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. The change writes no state and does not change config or protocol, so a revert undoes it fully. Blast radius: only child runs whose owner fact comes from a channel requester (`requesterOwner`). If the owner is removed while such a child runs, the child now stops instead of finishing. Operator, admin-scope and non-owner children do not change. Restart replay of a final reply keeps its current behavior.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): loading status no longer adds dividers or shifts views
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Knowledge Recent, Browse and Scribes views carry an always-on empty status row with a divider line, which adds about 30px of loose space under the controls.

## User Impact

Knowledge views sit tighter under their search box, tabs and table controls. Loading text appears as a small label at the top right of the view and never moves the content. A failed load still shows its error and Retry button above the content.

## Why This Change Was Made

The status row kept a fixed 30px height and a bottom border so loading text would not shift the layout. It now floats over the top of the view's data with no net height and no divider. It stays in the accessibility tree while empty. A terminal error, which needs the user's attention, joins the normal flow and wraps so Retry stays visible.

## Evidence

All captures come from the live Knowledge Control UI at 1280×900, with the CSS applied to the same page. In each image, the top half is before and the bottom half is after.

**Recent:** the line above the date heading and the empty row are gone.

![Recent before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ecdc6168-7d2d-48c4-a4df-ec3b21149b97)

**Scribes:** the line and empty band under the tabs are gone.

![Scribes before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dbbe33d9-af68-4fdb-9a84-e98506d4f454)

**Browse:** the empty strip between the table controls and the column header is gone.

![Browse before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d10ef69-79d3-4629-bcdd-9f0496a79af7)

**Loading:** the label floats over the view. Below are a Recent initial load and a Browse reload over previous results.

![Recent loading](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b882271f-59c3-4b39-bcf8-de8ec466d636)

![Browse loading](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4010147d-81c1-4cc3-a260-e5ec9a9e9aa6)

Measured in the live UI:
- **Real reload:** the top of the Browse data stayed at 233px before, during and after a reload triggered by a facet click. The top of the Recent data stayed at 246px during and after loading.
- **Idle:** the empty status has opacity 0 and visibility visible, so it stays in the accessibility tree and takes no net height.
- **Long loading text in a narrow pane:** the label ends in an ellipsis and keeps a 9px inset on both sides.
- **Error containing an unbroken path:** the row wraps, Retry stays inside the box, and the content moves down below it.
- **Hot reload:** the built plugin was reloaded into a running Gateway and checked in the browser.

**Gaps:** no automated tests cover this CSS and none were changed. I didn't run CI locally.
