prs.title: fix: keep Draft selection when creation is disabled
prs.body: Fixes #186918. ## What Problem This Solves A pending New Session form could silently lose its explicitly selected Draft audience when an administrator disabled Draft creation. The message and attachments remained, but a subsequent Start sent no visibility preference and created a Shared conversation. The same substitution also existed in the submission path when the Draft chooser became unavailable before the form refreshed. ## User Impact The open form now keeps the selected Draft, message, and attachments. When the authenticated Gateway policy disables new Draft creation, it displays an explanation and prevents a fresh submission. The active Draft control remains available in the desktop, mobile, and attachment-menu presentations so the user can explicitly turn Draft off to create Shared work. Ordinary fresh Shared defaults, existing logical Draft conversations, and Incognito rules are preserved. This changes the retained form's behavior; it does not add a persisted audience preference or change what a fresh document restores from browser storage. ## Why This Change Was Made Gateway capability refresh previously rewrote the form's selected audience, and submission independently converted an unavailable Draft to normal visibility. Both substitutions are removed. The existing request builder already represents explicit Draft intent correctly, so it stays unchanged. The existing submit-reason owner presents the current disabled policy without replacing server authorization. Requests prepared against stale policy retain their explicit Draft visibility for the Gateway to evaluate. Accepted-session and placement recovery continue through their existing owners; the new-form check does not reclassify an already-created conversation as a fresh Draft. A refused creation restores the existing form. Its display check now uses the existing presentation scope across transport reconnects, while changed identity still retires the form. Creation and navigation continue to require current authenticated authority. ## Evidence The original real Control UI flow silently created Shared work after a policy refresh. On exact UI head `1c11197bb969dd74888213262127569da7a518c5`, the same refreshed form keeps Draft, its message and attachment, shows disabled-creation guidance, disables Start, and sends zero creation requests on Enter. The stale-policy control sends explicit `visibility: draft` to the real Gateway, which refuses it without creating a session. A subsequent same-document reconnect keeps Draft and all input; Enter sends no additional request. Explicitly turning Draft off then creates exactly one intended Shared session with the retained input. Its real model turn completes, with no active run or processes. The administrator setting was restored after settlement. Remote validation passed formatting, lint, localization, affected compiler graphs, and 812 initially affected cases. The recovery correction then passed 80 owner cases and 35 browser cases, including principal/Gateway changes, Incognito rollback, accepted first-turn authority, and explicit Shared choice. The new owner and browser regressions fail on the earlier code at the observed behavior boundary. The correction browser batch took 57.72 seconds including production UI setup; the hosted browser lane took 203 seconds including setup and other selected cases. Independent engineering review and canonical AutoReview are clean for the unchanged patch. Current hosted checks pass every selected job except the browser row described below and its aggregate gate, including all three Bun UI rows. The earlier run failed the test-line ratchet at 6,310,599 lines against its then-current 6,310,000 ceiling. Main now has an effective 6,320,000 ceiling. The shared native composition includes this exact 82-line regression contribution and passes that policy. No assertions or existing coverage were removed; the integrated candidate passes that ratchet. The remaining browser failure is inherited: six existing sidebar alignment cases wait for `.personal-session-groups__heading`, which the upstream Sections UI removed. Running one of those unchanged cases on unmodified target `0ded0ed7` reproduces the same 30-second timeout. The shared case block and executable fixture setup are identical on the target and this PR; the three changed Draft cases pass in the same hosted row. The test adaptation is tracked separately from this runtime repair. The recordings use the exact UI head with the retained Gateway build `a334bd75`; the relevant creation and policy owners are unchanged. Current candidate `0671ba63e986d280da9b39f65ad582fb9a86c650` includes the accepted policy from main; all 16 files in this change are identical to the captured UI revision. Current server refusal adds guidance, so the earlier recording does not claim its new exact wording or wrapping. This is not a full current-backend execution claim. Fresh-document audience persistence remains unchanged. The earlier recovery-before screenshot was read after policy restoration while its client retained the disabled-policy hello; no second submission was made in that failure case. ## Visual evidence ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | New Session after policy refresh | ![Draft choice disappeared while the prompt and attachment remained and Start was enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85bf17b4-b29e-450f-b9fa-df2614694995) | ![Corrected head retains Draft, prompt and attachment with clear policy guidance and disabled Start](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01b2d398-a478-4ad3-bc78-158eca1ebefa) | | Refused Draft after reconnect \(before: ab14e182\) | ![Earlier recovery path loses Draft selection after refusal and reconnect while retaining input](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11af272a-274e-4857-9ce2-5653357e38a8) | ![Corrected recovery retains selected Draft, prompt and attachment and blocks a new submission](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5bb7d3f9-a57d-4512-b335-dd0e577987c1) | ### Before and corrected after: policy refresh, refused Draft recovery, and explicit Shared choice https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e6d37ba-cfa8-416c-ab75-5d4eb336d081 ### Visual verification - Baseline: a334bd753a2bba08e63d56a17b5d3b60b20660ad - Exact head: `1c11197bb969dd74888213262127569da7a518c5` - Scenario: Select Draft with a message and attachment; disable new Draft creation through the administrator owner\. Exercise direct policy refresh and stale\-policy refusal followed by reconnect\. Press Enter while Draft remains selected, then explicitly turn Draft off to create Shared work\. - Runtime/build: Control UI 1c11197b; retained Gateway a334bd75; same authenticated synthetic guest and Gateway boot\. - Refreshed pending Draft: Zero creation requests;84\-character prompt and one attachment retained - Refused Draft after reconnect: One refused Draft request; no session and no additional request after Enter;68\-character prompt and attachment retained - Explicit Shared choice: One accepted Shared task only after Draft\-off; completed with no active run or processes - Actual Control UI and native Gateway configuration; no mocked policy or creation responses - Committed after head and served runtime source maps verified before capture - Same1440×1000 viewport, light theme and authenticated identity; matching input for each paired scenario - Historical baseline a334bd75 for policy refresh;ab14e182 for refused\-create recovery - Earlier recovery screenshot was read after policy restoration while retaining the false hello; no second submission was made - Current\-head assertions completed while policy remained false; L1 restored original config only after successful settled handback - Original recordings retained; four source clips are identified by captions; no replayed product interactions

prs.title: fix: prevent queued agent failures after the sending turn ends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An accepted, queued agent message can fail required context compaction after the sending turn ends, even though the recipient still has a valid running task.

## User Impact

The recipient can prepare its context and continue under its own run authority. Existing source/operator and Gateway checks remain in force. No configuration change or data migration is required.

**Real-model Gateway sequence recorded; settlement limitation remains:** [The audited 28 October built-CLI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177296#issuecomment-6482568096) exercises this exact head with a real OpenRouter model: accepted queued send, normal sender completion, required native token compaction, successful recipient execution and a persisted assistant response in the original source session. Two explicitly disclosed in-memory timing/logging transforms instrument the build; the changed dispatch module is untransformed. The driver reports `passed:true`, but cleanup interrupts still-active work, logs a reply-flow failure and escalates to SIGKILL. Original-return terminal settlement and graceful teardown are **not** proved. The earlier credential-launch blocker is superseded. [ClawSweeper revision 4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177296#issuecomment-6266910403), reviewed 28 October at 22:48 UTC on this exact head, rates the changed-handoff proof sufficient and reports no findings or remaining contributor-facing before-merge items. It expressly retains the return-settlement/teardown limitation. The PR is ready for human maintainer review; automated proof acceptance is not human authority-boundary approval or merge acceptance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The asynchronous handoff already detaches the sender's transcript and operator-tool context, but carries its temporary Gateway caller identity into the recipient. A plugin can capture that expired identity during required compaction before the recipient establishes its own identity.

Use the existing caller-context reset at that same handoff, after validating the caller and retaining the source/operator guards. Other methods, including `agent.wait`, retain their caller context. This is one small production change with three regressions; it adds no retry, authority owner or lifetime extension.

## Evidence

- **Before/after at the dispatch boundary:** host-close and admission-close cases fail before the fix with `agent tool caller authority is no longer active`. Afterward, all 125 tests in eight focused suites pass; expired entry remains rejected and `agent.wait` stays scoped. Targeted types, ordinary lint and formatting pass. Turn-service acceptance/settlement is a fixture; caller admission, lifetime and authority assertions are native.
- **Published head:** `cacfa20bc2d430bdbbc38c67f4d55153c5e3fb55`; [the code CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39247956740/job/118053866938). The published production/test files match the tested inputs.
- **Separate 2026.10.5 source flow:** with the equivalent one-file fix, an actually accepted and queued `sessions_send` survives normal sender completion, performs required compaction, completes the recipient and returns the original result. Committed role revocation or Gateway retirement instead produces zero recipient model calls, compactions, new transcript entries or original return runs. Cancelled/interrupted pending-input bookkeeping remains. [Redacted output and persisted readbacks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177296#issuecomment-6267500396).

The previously published release-source authority-control flow uses synthetic model transport. It is not a full-flow test of the PR head, installed-package/live-provider proof, a different-selected-person case, later revocation during model I/O or external-channel delivery. The original incident's exact first invalidator is not uniquely reconstructed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction details, validation limits and related work</summary>

The full flow ran in official 2026.10.5 source `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8` with locked dependencies. Recorded usage was 120000/128000 tokens and history was below the 4 MiB byte threshold, forcing token preflight. A real selected local plugin captured the expired sender identity; the earlier personal-selection guard threw `This turn has ended; ask again in a new turn.` The unchanged and repaired flows isolate the stale-context cause; separate native dispatch cases prove the exact caller-error guard.

The initial type-aware lint wrapper stopped during declaration preparation before lint and is not a passed check. Separate targeted types and supported ordinary lint passed. Prior P0-scoped Autoreview found no actionable findings on the unchanged production/test inputs.

Related: #158070. Merged #159353 fixes deferred post-turn maintenance; this PR fixes the earlier foreground handoff. #173026 handles the requester's progress and result return, a separate stage from this recipient-preflight failure. Maintainer review of the authority boundary remains required.

</details>

prs.title: perf(cron): skip redundant completion maintenance and publication scans
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron still rebuilds unchanged job snapshots and diffs the entire inventory for small runtime updates. Explicit runs also request a second schedule-maintenance write after the finalization worker has already repaired the completed job.

## User Impact

Less allocation on the Gateway main thread and fewer SQLite writer requests. Job definitions, scheduling, receipt/history durability, authority checks, notification order, and stored formats remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing committed row delta into definition-change comparison. Preserve the resident jobs and revision map for an empty delta; retain wake-event publication. Replace the resident-ID set and intermediate inventory arrays with one pass that keeps resident order and appends imported jobs. No cache or stored state is added.

Finalization now uses the existing maintenance-needed predicate for explicit runs too. Manual preflight and worker finalization retain their normalization, and an unrelated job missing its next deadline still triggers maintenance.

The earlier full-store revision-hashing improvement (#186397) is already in the measured baseline. This change measures and removes residual work after it.

## Evidence

Measured baseline: d840d4bab300ab27703bdfc05b0a077ebdc04100. Synthetic data only, local owner workloads; no production load. Acceptance was unchanged notifications/durable schedules and lower owner CPU/allocation or writer counts. The requested fast-path protocol applies: these changes remove duplicate work; no whole-Gateway p99 or RSS improvement is claimed.

Five counterbalanced timing pairs and five separate allocation pairs, 5,000 iterations per arm per pair, 200 jobs. Values are medians per publication; cloning/IPC is outside the publication microbenchmark. Durable wake publication remains included. Single-row calls alternate detached snapshots, so each call observes a different row identity.

| Runtime publication | Base CPU | Candidate CPU | Base allocation | Candidate allocation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Empty delta | 35.03 µs | 11.63 µs (-66.8%) | 122,818 B | 29,825 B (-75.7%) |
| One changed row | 60.18 µs | 43.60 µs (-27.6%) | 151,930 B | 100,987 B (-33.5%) |

Commands: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/cron-definition-publication-measure.ts --runtime-only --iterations 5000` and a separate `--allocations` pass; baseline uses `--owner-dir` with the original owner files. Host load per arm is recorded in the JSON output.

The real cron request/queue/receipt/finalization workload uses 40 jobs and 80 explicit runs per arm, with a stubbed job executor. Five counterbalanced pairs gave identical producer counts and persisted schedule digests in every arm:

| Writer producer | Base requests | Candidate requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Schedule maintenance | 160 | 80 |
| Request admission | 80 | 80 |
| Finalization | 80 | 80 |
| Queue drain | 20 | 20 |
| Scheduler refresh | 40 | 40 |
| Total | 380 | 300 (-21.1%) |
| At 20 synthetic explicit runs/minute | 95/min | 75/min |

This removes one post-finalization maintenance request per explicit run. Scheduled runs already used the repair predicate. These rates describe the synthetic mix, not a measured production producer breakdown. One-minute host load per timing arm was base [15.70, 15.78, 14.23, 11.86, 13.71], candidate [17.78, 16.89, 12.78, 11.91, 12.82].

Reproduce the producer census with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/cron-refresh-measure.ts --workload runs --iterations 20 --count-commands --output .local/cron-census.json` on each revision. Census CPU/allocation values include diagnostic deserialization and are excluded from performance claims. The counter is now opt-in, preserving clean timing/allocation modes; both modes were smoke-tested after that correction.

Regression proof: both new work-count/identity regressions fail on unchanged baseline source (two expected failures), while the stale-sibling repair control passes. Candidate: 45 focused tests across runtime store, list snapshot guards, receipt finalization, and batch finalization pass. The expanded runtime-store observer test also passes for exactly one import/removal notification. Focused wrapper wall time was 51.6 s; the final six-test runtime-store rerun was 58.3 s including worker compilation. PR CI supplies broad validation.

`pnpm tsgo:test:root`, the services-cron strict test typecheck, changed-file oxlint/oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Test-line ratchet passes without modifying its ceiling.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): fresh context, complete diff and relevant owners, P0–P2, no remaining actionable findings. The requested autoreview provider route was refused before inference because it differed from the operator configuration; configuration was left unchanged. The review's benchmark-instrumentation finding was fixed and re-reviewed.

Production delta: +22 lines across two owners. The explicit delta pass replaces compact allocating array pipelines while preserving resident/import order, deletion precedence, complete revision publication, and callback ordering; no cache, configuration option, schema, or stored-shape change. No whole-Gateway stress, model/tool transport, or live-state measurement is claimed.

prs.body:
Related: #185955

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the config CI shard times out when its archive-retirement fixture waits for a raw transcript read to start cold restoration.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The existing regression again exercises idle archive retirement and cold restoration without hanging the shard. No configuration, schema, migration, or timeout changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Raw hydration intentionally reads verified cold archives without restoring them after #185955. Request restoration explicitly, then perform the original read. Preserve both open-scope variants and every existing worker-exit, replacement, lease, snapshot, and cleanup assertion.

## Evidence

- Original failure: [main run 40532514201, attempt 1, job 122289584880](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40532514201/job/122289584880), head `c168d2b0b7fb11f4cd463191a4f508c6775fbc9b`. The native case reaches its 120-second test and 180-second hook timeouts before the later 300-second no-output termination.
- Recovered and replayed the original four-group job input with frozen dependencies and the pinned Bun fork. The same case and watchdog failure reproduced. Passive diagnostics confirmed the history read completes without entering restoration or the mutation gate. The full-job replay used Node 26 orchestration; subsequent focused proof used CI Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+807211511`.
- Corrected complete archive-session file: **22/22 pass**, including both scope variants, with one worker and unchanged ordinary test/hook lifetimes and no-output watchdog. Wrapper wall time: **86.55 seconds**, including **36.12 seconds** preparing compiled workers; native Vitest duration: **82.89 seconds**. CI job cost is not yet available.
- Targeted agents-sessions typecheck, typed lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Reversing only the import and restoration-trigger changes reconstructs the original file byte-for-byte, including all assertions and `finally` blocks.
- Local ClawSweeper is unavailable. Context-complete local autoreview using Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, reviewed the complete candidate against `c168d2b0b7fb11f4cd463191a4f508c6775fbc9b` with the full fixture and relevant owners: no actionable findings. Runtime results were author-supplied evidence, not independently executed by the reviewer. A separate read-only source check independently confirmed the intentional read-contract change and the explicit-restoration correction.
- Tested commit `6ba9861ba12a4111be09c8224d2ade180389fe04` and managed-worktree commit `abc57855ad1ebf14ce0ff1f258c58d81713d6281` have the identical complete tree `a1c4df6897d9753e0d66fdfe35a46098d71d0fc3`. Registered-worktree history was preserved without a reset; only this fixture differs from the verified failing head.
- Required unused-file scan: production **0 entries**; full-tree scan remains failed on **six unchanged performance scripts**. This is not an aggregate pass. The broad local replay also exposed one unrelated conversation-registry wall-clock assertion and three live-dist fixture refusals caused by a retained host artifact lock; those were not repaired or hidden, and no lock was removed.
- Direct main submission was rejected as non-fast-forward; no force push or retry was used.

Requested and co-authored by @vincentkoc.

prs.title: feat(tavily): expose search controls and correct request attribution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tavily’s dedicated Search and Extract tools cannot select several useful current API options, and requests put the integration name in the transport attribution field.

## User Impact

Users can choose faster Search depths, domain preference, language and date filters, safe search, exact matching, and credit usage, plus Extract text format, favicon and usage metadata. Search still defaults to five results; existing content limits and the generic `web_search` interface remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The options flow through the existing client and cache, with distinct cache entries for each request shape. Direct requests send `X-Client-Name: openclaw` and `X-Client-Source: api`. Optional response metadata is limited to finite numeric credit usage and validated, bounded HTTP(S) favicon URLs.

The added fields stay with the existing schema, request and cache owners; no new tool, state layer or runtime dependency is needed. Date descriptions reflect Tavily’s best-estimate published or last-updated dates.

Live validation rejected `max_results=0` even though the public reference permits it. The tool schema and documentation therefore retain their original 1–20 range. Direct programmatic calls still forward explicit zero unchanged and expose the provider error; no silent clamping is introduced.

## Evidence

- All 60 Tavily tests pass at the corrected head. The focused regression failed before the schema correction and now checks the advertised range, default five results, literal-zero forwarding and provider-error propagation.
- Thirteen synthetic HTTP checks passed through the actual registered tools, generic provider and HTTP implementation. They cover defaults, optional controls, partial results, output bounds, caching, authentication/rate-limit/server faults, malformed JSON, cancellation and attribution.
- Eight real Tavily HTTP attempts returned seven HTTP 200 responses and one HTTP 400 for the zero-result request. Default Search, added controls, Extract, focused extraction and generic search were exercised. The zero-result conflict remains a failed boundary expectation, not a passing capability claim.
- One default-Extract assertion expected a fixed page heading; the API returned one useful extraction with different text. The original failed assertion is retained as a test expectation issue; no repeat API call or retroactive pass is claimed.
- All eight observed outgoing requests carried the intended name/source headers. No server-side analytics ingestion was checked. Date/language request acceptance does not establish ranking or filter accuracy.
- Targeted lint, formatting, docs assertions and whitespace checks pass for the correction. The initial patch also passed targeted TypeScript and 13 tool-definition stability tests; these were not rerun for the schema/prose-only follow-up.

The API checks used minimal registration capture, not a Gateway session or hosted-platform workflow. No model or Research calls were made for this integration. Broader repository coverage remains for PR CI.

prs.title: perf(agents): share run identity across trajectory append batches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Trajectory persistence repeats a recorder's unchanged run ID in every event wrapper sent to its SQLite worker.

## User Impact

A small reduction in trajectory transport bytes and allocation, with no user-visible behavior change. Stored JSON, schema, ordering, durability, retention attribution, and authorization remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each production recorder owns one captured run ID. Carry it once on the append batch and consume it for SQLite `run_id` and incognito retention attribution. Remove the per-event copy from both queues. Direct fixtures and benchmark callers use the same contract; mixed-run fixtures retain their order and atomic fixture transaction.

The runtime change is +7 net lines, needed to pass the shared fact through both storage backends; no cache, fallback, compression stage, or JSON parsing is added. Benchmark instrumentation is separate (+119 lines). Existing settlement and encoding-budget tests are consolidated without reducing their cases; net test/support growth is zero and the test-line ceiling is untouched.

## Evidence

Base: `70bf5121704c7a7173722c2bd7e360362e5da165`. Acceptance: identical persisted event bytes and run attribution, fewer request bytes, no adverse transport CPU/allocation.

The real recorder/worker/SQLite workload uses 40 tools, retained conversation context, tool results, lifecycle metadata, and five synthetic sessions. Two base/candidate pairs ran in candidate/base then base/candidate order. Each arm persisted 50 measured events plus warmup; normalized persisted JSONL was byte-identical in all four runs. Timing replays actual captured commands through V8 serialization/deserialization: five passes × 2,000 appends per arm per pair (20,000 appends per revision). Allocation uses separate sampled passes, 2,000 appends per arm per pair (4,000 per revision).

| Owner transport metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Steady 10-event append bytes | 127,584 | 127,368 (−216 B, −0.17%) |
| CPU µs/append, paired mean | 29.487 | 26.953 |
| Sampled JS allocation B/append | 128,092 | 127,616 (−0.37%) |

CPU is **inconclusive**, not a claimed speedup: the pairs were 30.843→25.002 and 28.131→28.904 µs/append. Allocation pairs were 128,010→127,602 and 128,175→127,631 B/append; these are sampled estimates, not total native allocation. Host 1-minute loads were 60.77/42.32 for candidate/base and 36.18/43.91 for base/candidate. This is a small deterministic byte saving, not a whole-Gateway latency claim.

Per-event serialized wrapper bytes (six captured events/type including warmup, except 12 tool results; rounded). Request-level shared fields are counted only in the full append totals above.

| Event type | Base B/event | Candidate B/event |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| session.started | 521 | 497 |
| trace.metadata | 11,602 | 11,578 |
| context.compiled | 48,489 | 48,465 |
| prompt.submitted | 32,105 | 32,081 |
| tool.call | 675 | 651 |
| tool.result | 4,292 | 4,268 |
| model.completed | 24,179 | 24,155 |
| trace.artifacts | 808 | 784 |
| session.ended | 502 | 478 |

Reproduce with the header in `scripts/perf/trajectory-request-bytes-preload.mjs` and `trajectory-persistence.ts`, using fresh state directories and `--compare-golden` across revisions. The larger repeated prompt/tool-result payloads remain intact because removing them would change persisted diagnostic content.

Validation:

- Node regression on main: the existing eight-event writer test fails the byte budget (436,601 B versus a 435,887 B limit). It exercises the actual sink, worker dispatch, and persistence. Bun's more compact serializer already passed that budget on main.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root`: all four shards passed. Matching core test configurations (`other`, `agents-sessions`, `gateway-server`, `gateway-methods`) passed.
- Changed-file formatting/lint, export collision guard, and test-line ratchet passed (6,311,630 lines; ceiling 6,311,700 after rebasing).
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): fresh source review of the complete staged patch, P0/P1/P2, no actionable findings. Autoreview preflight refused the requested provider/config mismatch; no operator configuration was changed. The benchmark-only CI correction also received a clean independent review.

The seven affected focused test files passed: 92 tests, 299.27 seconds wall time including worker preparation and three test configurations. Native persistence/retention and real Gateway-close cases retain their full transaction, settlement, and cleanup coverage. The Node candidate regression passed (16.71 seconds wall); the two source-closure guard files passed (38 tests, 102.95 seconds wall). Rebased without conflicts onto `bb6c6a5a2763`; the reviewed patch ID is unchanged. The first CI run caught an async EventEmitter callback in the new benchmark under the stricter scripts lint configuration. Fixed with an explicit promise-error handler; the exact scripts lint, all root type shards, and a real persistence/probe smoke passed. No production code or measurement body changed. Exact-head PR CI passed on `683bcada04d7aef10b86c759d25927fa6bae5057`: [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40778885436), with 76 passing and 52 skipped checks. [Hosted Codex review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187047#issuecomment-6481830081) and [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187047#issuecomment-6482441058) reported no findings on this head. Large Boards still allocate offscreen report chrome and body renderers, and native report cells subscribe to foreign-frame work they do not use. Visiting and returning to tabs republishes that work across hundreds of retained cells.

## User Impact

Large Boards open and switch tabs faster while preserving card geometry, keyboard focus, report identity, current hidden updates, and foreign-widget teardown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing report-entry latch for fixed-report chrome, and admit its body once. Retain admitted bodies across hidden height-mode changes and MCP retirement. Move the existing content-visibility rule to the fixed card while retaining strict body containment. Native cells avoid foreign-frame reactive inputs and the HTML-only exact-height calculation; loading-covered native readiness remains observed.

The Board data/live-update owner is unchanged. One memo is added; no new observer, cache, dependency, or eager import. Cell LOC is 717 → 725; stylesheet 893 → 895. Signals 6 → 6, effects 2 → 2, cleanup registrations 2 → 2, memos 6 → 7. Tests add zero net lines across the PR.

prs.title: fix(browser): isolate extension tab discovery from stalled renderers
prs.body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

With the extension in **All tabs**, a renderer that stops responding can make Playwright's cold `connectOverCDP` wait for every Page initializer. Browser status succeeds, but listing or using unrelated healthy tabs times out.

This revision separates native target inventory from individual Page initialization on lifecycle-registered extension relays. Healthy tabs remain usable. Selecting the stalled tab returns a bounded, target-specific readiness error; after it responds, the same native target recovers without restarting the Browser or losing healthy-tab snapshot references.

The relay's public auto-attach barrier, native debugger ownership, generation checks, access policy, quarantine rules, and transient inventory errors remain enforced. Only the private Playwright adapter defers its initial Page barrier. Failed initializers can publish dummy Pages with an empty main-frame URL, so selected-target recovery detaches and reattaches only that logical session through the existing relay.

## Complete-product before/after proof

Isolated Proxmox Debian 13 amd64; Node 24.22.1; Chrome for Testing **156.0.8078.73** under Xvfb. Fresh synthetic Chrome profile and Gateway state. Canonical built Gateway daemon and browser CLI; **unmodified shipped extension 2.3.0**, paired through its normal Settings page in **All tabs** mode.

Fixture: one healthy HTTP page with a button, one HTTP parent embedding a foreign-extension iframe, and another HTTP page whose renderer runs a bounded 45-second JavaScript loop. No native API overrides, injected Chrome errors, in-memory socket adapter, buffered detach events, or inspector breakpoints.

- Before: previous PR head `b3cee431843234274a1d06c793715749832b3a00`. Status passes; tabs fails in **8,068 ms** with a cold-connection timeout naming the real stalled target.
- After: clean source/build head **`991200f72de9e75b78d3f6fa22beecea6368df10`**, tree `28dd6b0d4ed43a57080c9a85727cd1b8544e3780`. The canonical build stamp records the same head and `inputsClean: true`.

| Final candidate operation | CLI wall time | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Status | 3,952 ms | Success |
| List tabs while renderer stalls | 4,029 ms | Healthy and busy native target IDs listed; Chrome-refused neighbour skipped |
| Evaluate healthy tab | 4,306 ms | `Healthy tab` |
| Interactive snapshot / click | 3,660 / 4,359 ms | Button reference works while neighbour stalls |
| Select busy tab | 8,591 ms | Target-specific `did not become ready` error; includes CLI startup, readiness budget remains 5 s |
| Reuse original healthy snapshot reference | 3,857 ms | Success after busy-tab error |
| Verify button click count | 3,982 ms | Exactly 2 |
| Evaluate same busy target after loop ends | 2,835 ms | `Busy tab`; no Browser/Gateway restart |

All healthy actions completed during the busy interval. The final test explicitly asserts native target identity, retained healthy snapshot references, target-specific failure, and recovery of the same busy target.

Reproduction uses normal `browser --browser-profile chrome status/tabs/evaluate/snapshot/click --json` commands against the isolated Gateway. The busy fixture schedules `setTimeout(() => { const until = Date.now() + 45000; while (Date.now() < until) {} }, 0)` before the first cold tabs call.

## Validation

- 104 focused owner/sibling tests passed across six browser suites.
- After the final lint-only test adjustment and refusal-classifier extraction, both changed suites passed again: 62 tests.
- Production and focused test typechecks, targeted Oxlint, formatting, commit hooks, and diff checks passed.
- Independent read-only review found no actionable issue in the new transport/readiness/recovery implementation.
- Tested head `991200f72` had an exact test-line recount of **6,312,189**, ceiling **6,312,189**, zero slack. The recovery follow-up adds 243 justified regression lines. Counting rules and assertions are unchanged. The refusal classifier moved to a coherent sibling module to respect the bridge's line-cap ratchet.
- Published head **`6d02a663132e911e3b94d0bf70094aa7a0315135`** merges current main `67a7001050ff57c67f73123713670e3e0af234ad` to resolve the new budget-only conflict. All browser source/tests are byte-identical to tested `991200f72` (`git diff 991200f72 HEAD -- extensions/browser` is empty). The merge retains main's existing **6,320,000** ceiling unchanged. The full native proof was not redundantly rerun for this mechanical merge.
- Broad checks are delegated to PR CI for this pushed head; older green CI is not claimed for this revision.

## Additional agent/model attempt

A separate run used an actual isolated Gateway agent and a local Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0 model. Status and tabs CLI passed while the renderer stalled, but the model returned prose without calling the browser tool. Transcript inspection confirmed no actual browser-tool call. This attempt **does not pass agent/model acceptance** and is not counted as browser-tool proof. No paid API, operator state, or production Gateway was used. The complete Gateway + extension + CLI before/after proof above passed independently.

## Proof boundaries

This is a newly isolated **renderer-initialization failure**, not proof that the original wrapped-refusal inventory race occurs through the complete product. The [independent NO-REPRO investigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186674#issuecomment-6466831554) remains valid. The earlier wrapped permanent-refusal classifier is retained with its native-boundary and transient-error controls, but its complete-product before/after acceptance remains open.

The operator's exact offending tab has not been identified. This proves the reproduced timeout mechanism and fix, not that every reported timeout has that cause. No claim is made that this repairs the separate Windows native Chrome/PC crash. The operator's normal Chrome and production Gateway were not operated or modified for these tests.

Related: #156749, #156890, #162110.

## What Problem This Solves

The maintained unused-export check reports `OVERSIZED_WORKSPACE_FILE_ERROR_PREFIX` in both production and full-tree scans. The constant is still needed to construct and recognize oversized workspace-file errors, but its module export has no remaining consumer.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. The exact single-file and aggregate error messages, workspace size limits, recovery guidance, and file-preservation behavior remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier recovery change moved external callers to `workspaceSizeRecoveryPaths`, leaving the single-file prefix's export behind. This removes only that `export` keyword and keeps the constant and all uses in the same owner.

The aggregate prefix stays exported because `local-workspace-recovery.ts` consumes it. The reconciliation barrel and computed-import benchmark use other exports; the package's public export map does not expose this module.

## Evidence

On the PR source based on `a53e9583dfbf6d93e994d494b3c76d4e576c72dd`, the unchanged `pnpm deadcode:exports` command completed all three passes before and after the change. Production findings decreased from 5 to 4 and full-tree findings from 9 to 8; script findings stayed at 4. The single-file prefix was the only removed finding, and every other finding was identical. Both aggregate commands exited 1 because those unrelated findings remain.

Changed-file formatting, formatter parity, lint, and all selected compiler groups passed. The five existing reconciliation, projection/recovery, generated-path, managed-skill, and hash-memo test files passed: **100 tests passed, 1 existing opt-in Podman test skipped**. This includes the exact single-file error, ordinary and cross-device recovery, aggregate overflow, and preserved-file controls. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40779886497) passed on `4ba5a0b14505f87141169ea6933188a68d5e0c80`. The unrelated native scan findings above remain recorded as failures.

prs.title: feat(backup): recover local Gateway state with PostgreSQL agents
prs.body:
Related: #178971

## What Problem This Solves

Recover a replacement Gateway's local identity and PostgreSQL store pointers while its agent history remains in the existing central stores.

## User Impact

Proposes `openclaw backup local create --output <archive> --json` and `openclaw backup local restore <archive> --json`. The private archive contains the SQLite global database, its matched device/client credentials and configured PostgreSQL anchors. It excludes PostgreSQL records, configuration, workspaces and provider secrets managed through external SecretRefs.

Restore requires a stopped Gateway, original configured paths and fresh database targets. This remains a **draft awaiting maintainer acceptance of the storage/public CLI design in #178971**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing full backups export PostgreSQL history and restore fresh namespaces. Replacing a Gateway that will reconnect to the same central stores needs its native global/client pair and original UUID/schema pointers instead. A global-only snapshot cannot restore that pair.

This reuses native updater capture/restore, custody and matched-client receipt owners. The local profile applies the existing global snapshot sanitizer, including removal of pending outbound delivery intent: an older checkpoint must not resend messages acknowledged after capture. Ordinary full-backup rollback behavior is unchanged.

Restore reads configuration without observing or initializing database targets. Under native custody, it validates images, the global/client pair and anchor identities, creates missing private parent directories durably, then prepares and publishes images. A genuinely empty replacement state root is covered.

The archive is a per-database recovery point, not a distributed atomic snapshot. Anchors created after capture require a newer checkpoint; this does not discover namespaces after every local pointer is lost.

## Evidence

Current upstream head: `3426d311496` merges `origin/main` at `0ded0ed7a8c` to clear the `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` conflict; it changes none of this PR's files. The live proof below ran on the previous head `d553602eda5a5887ba1c5f326e0a34a7db63cb42` (merge of `origin/main` plus the ratchet fixes; `openclaw --version` of that full build reports `2026.10.8 (d553602)`), whose PR-owned sources are identical to the current head.

Live proof on this exact head, run with the built CLI against real PostgreSQL 16 and a real model provider:

1. **Source Gateway with a PostgreSQL agent store** completes a real model turn (`TANGERINE-4471` stored; reply `OK`). The agent namespace `proof_agent_c285…` holds 48 tables; the local tree holds the SQLite global/client pair and the agent anchor.
2. **Pending outbound delivery present at capture**: one `delivery_queue_entries` row is enqueued through the runtime's own storage owner before `backup local create` runs against the live Gateway (3 images, 206 KiB archive).
3. **Refusals before publication**: restore while the source Gateway still owns the state, and restore over existing database targets, both fail with `Local checkpoint restore requires fresh database targets: …` and change nothing.
4. **Replacement root**: the departed state directory is moved aside, an empty directory is created at the original path with the host-managed config kept outside it, and `backup local restore` publishes exactly the global, client and anchor databases.
5. **No delivery replay**: the departed global database still holds its 1 pending row (source acknowledges after capture); the restored global database holds 0; the replacement Gateway log has no delivery recovery activity.
6. **Same PostgreSQL identity**: the restored anchor row is byte-identical (`store_id c285d948-…`, schema `proof_agent_c285d94839f24786`); no new namespace is created. Doctor reports `Agent data: … effective=postgres (configured); observed=postgres`.
7. **Recovery turn**: the replacement Gateway lists the prior session from PostgreSQL and answers the recall turn with `TANGERINE-4471`.
8. **Data-model compatibility**: the released `openclaw@2026.10.8` (dc2523e) creates an all-SQLite installation and runs a turn (`MARIGOLD-2287`); this head refuses to serve its schema 25 until `doctor --fix` upgrades it to 38 with pre-migration backups, then serves it and answers the recall turn with `MARIGOLD-2287`. The released CLI does not accept the `database` key, so no released installation can hold PostgreSQL agent anchors; this head refuses `backup local create` on that layout with the documented message.

Native regressions: `src/infra/local-checkpoint.proof.test.ts` (capture with a pending delivery, source acknowledgement, cold-root restore, recovery without a second send, forged paths and anchor mismatch), `src/infra/sqlite-snapshot.prepared-volume.test.ts`, the no-replace copy cases in `src/infra/sqlite-file-copy.test.ts`, and the `backup local` dispatch rows in `src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts` pass on this head, as do core types, test types, and the test-lines, assertion-safety and mock-exports ratchets against `origin/main`.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal transcript of the live proof</summary>

Run on 2026-10-28 (macOS host, Node 24.22.1). The shipped CLI is the full `pnpm build` of the head
(`openclaw --version` reports `2026.10.8 (d553602)`). PostgreSQL 16.15 runs in a local container with
`unaccent` and `pg_trgm` installed; the Gateway reaches it through an env SecretRef DSN. Model turns use
a real provider (OpenAI Responses API, `gpt-5.4-mini`) through an env SecretRef key. Redactions:
`<proof-root>`, `<head-checkout>`, `<pg-host>:<pg-port>`, `<gateway-token>`, `<provider-key>`.

Host-managed config for the source and replacement Gateway (outside the state directory):

```json
{ "database": { "engine": "sqlite", "families": { "agent": { "engine": "postgres" } },
  "postgres": { "connection": { "source": "env", "provider": "default", "id": "OPENCLAW_DATABASE_DSN" }, "schemaPrefix": "proof" } } }
```

### A. Source Gateway → local checkpoint → refusals → empty replacement root → recovery turn

```text
=== head: d553602eda5a5887ba1c5f326e0a34a7db63cb42
$ node --version
v24.22.1
[exit 0]
$ <head-checkout>/openclaw.mjs --version
OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (d553602)
```

prs.title: fix(macos): app quits with "Client credentials unavailable" after an in-place update while the previous Gateway service is running
prs.body:
Related: #156712

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app quits at launch with "Another OpenClaw process is using your data" / "Client credentials unavailable. Run openclaw doctor --fix before reopening the app." when it is updated in place (reproduced from the latest stable, 2026.10.8, and from 2026.10.7) while the previous build's app-managed Gateway LaunchAgent service is still running.

## User Impact

User impact: after an in-place update, the app now starts normally. The Gateway service moves to the new build's runtime, client credentials are migrated, and existing config and cron jobs are kept. Users no longer have to run `openclaw doctor --fix` by hand. Normal launches, where the installed service already matches this build, are unchanged.

Operators who chose their Gateway version keep it: with `update.channel = extended-stable` or a channel install policy (`stable`, `beta`, `dev`), startup does not replace the service. This is the same gate setup and post-update repair already use. In that case startup behaves as it does today: the credential step can still fail while the old Gateway runs, and replacing the operator-pinned Gateway without consent would be worse. This is an accepted edge case.

## Why This Change Was Made

At launch, the app prepares client credentials before anything that replaces the service (`ConnectionModeCoordinator.apply`, `PostUpdateController`). Stable builds up to and including 2026.10.8 have no `client/credentials.sqlite`, so preparation is `required`. `doctor --client-credentials` deliberately does not control services: it calls `beginDoctorMaintenance({ root: null })`, so the stop branch gated on `params.root` never runs. Its state acquire then runs into the old Gateway's state-ownership lease and throws `GatewayStateOwnerContentionError`. The app then terminates, so the post-update replacement never runs.

The CLI's own refusals force the order:
- While the old Gateway runs, both the credential migration and `gateway install` refuse.
- After a stop, `gateway install` still refuses until credentials are migrated ("Client credentials require backed-up migration custody").

At startup the app now detects an app-managed service pinned to a different build's runtime, provided `CLIInstallPrompter.managedRepairGatesOpen` allows a managed repair. It then:
1. stops that service with this build's CLI;
2. prepares credentials;
3. installs the service on this build's runtime.

Stop, restore and install all carry the service custody captured at detection (`expectedServiceAuthority`) and recheck `serviceUpdateAuthorityError` before dispatch. So a service the operator reassigns while this build seeds its runtime or migrates credentials is refused instead of stopped or overwritten.

If credential preparation fails, the app restarts the previous service and the error surfaces as before. If the install fails, the failure is logged and startup continues, because credentials are valid and `PostUpdateController` still owns the retry. The CLI is unchanged.

Stopping only, without the install, was tried and rejected. Credentials migrated, but the app then kept retrying "gateway ensuring launchd" through the stale stable CLI, and the Gateway stayed down.

## Evidence

**Reproduction from the latest stable (isolated profile `p178719`; never the live `ai.openclaw.gateway` or `~/.openclaw`).**
- Start: the official notarized `OpenClaw-2026.10.8-arm64.dmg` (sha256 `7974be75…a3e899`), with its app-managed service seeded with a custom timezone and a cron job.
- Replace the `.app` bundle in place with the candidate build and launch it, with no manual steps.
- Both candidates are ad-hoc packaged from this branch merged with current `main` (2026.10.8). The control build has the four changed files reverted.

Before the fix (`main`, 2026.10.8), red:
```
## before (stable 2026.10.8)
service bun: ~/.openclaw-p178719/runtime/2026.10.8-release-5413218d77df-2026-10-27T20-43-42.000Z/bin/bun
client credentials db: absent
timezone: Asia/Kolkata
proof cron: 1
stable Gateway still listening: pid 47099

## after replacing the bundle in place (180s)
service bun: ~/.openclaw-p178719/runtime/2026.10.8-release-5413218d77df-2026-10-27T20-43-42.000Z/bin/bun
listener pid: 47099
runtime dir: 2026.10.8-release-5413218d77df-2026-10-27T20-43-42.000Z current
client credentials db: absent
app log (credentials):
  credentials: Credential startup failed: Could not prepare local client credentials. [openclaw] The CLI command failed.
  [openclaw] Another OpenClaw process is using your data. Wait for it to finish before trying again.
  credentials: Client credentials unavailable. Run openclaw doctor --fix before reopening the app.
```

After the fix, green (first run at 396f68ca0a72; rerun at 3f4cc925 with detection-time custody, same result: service moved in 20 s, credentials present, timezone and cron kept, control channel connected):
```
## before (stable 2026.10.8)
service bun: ~/.openclaw-p178719/runtime/2026.10.8-release-5413218d77df-2026-10-27T20-43-42.000Z/bin/bun
client credentials db: absent
timezone: Asia/Kolkata
proof cron: 1
stable Gateway still listening: pid 19672

## after replacing the bundle in place (21s)
service bun: ~/.openclaw-p178719/runtime/2026.10.8-396f68ca0a72-2026-10-28T21-27-38.000Z/bin/bun
listener pid: 20188
app running: 19977
client credentials db: present
timezone: Asia/Kolkata
proof cron: 1
app log (credentials, control channel):
  credentials: Replacing the previous build's Gateway service before credential preparation
  control: control channel state -> degraded: Cannot reach gateway at localhost:29871 (old service stopped, new one starting)
  control: control channel state -> connected
  control: control channel recovery finished
  control: control channel state -> connected
```

The same flow starting from stable 2026.10.7 was also red on `main` (443530a55b7e) and green with the first commit, twice: the service moved to the new runtime in 20 s, and the timezone and cron job survived.

**Tests:** `swift test --filter "stale service replacement keeps|StaleGatewayServiceReplacementTests|ClientCredentialStartupTests|UpdateOrchestrationTests"` passes (35 tests, at 3f4cc925). The new tests pin:
- a service reassigned after detection being refused before dispatch (`The Gateway service changed before dispatch; retry.`, no daemon command recorded), while an unchanged service gets exactly `stop --force`. This test fails without the captured authority: the reassigned service receives the stop;
- the order stop → credentials → install;
- a credential failure leading to restore instead of install;
- a refused stop skipping credential preparation;
- detection admitting the default and `exact` policies, and rejecting `extended-stable`, `beta` and `stable`.

**Not covered:**
- The restore path (credential preparation failing after the stop) is unit-tested only.
- Remote mode with a local companion Gateway is excluded by the `.local` gate and was not exercised.
- The policy rejection was unit-tested through detection, not run end to end.
- Local packaging needed a temporary, uncommitted change that skips Finder `.DS_Store` files in `src/infra/package-dist-inventory.ts`. A stray `dist/.DS_Store` otherwise breaks the inventory/tarball check. This touches build tooling only, not the app code under test.

prs.title: fix: Knowledge row type fails the unused-export check
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The unused-export check rejects Knowledge’s conversation row type even though the settings page consumes only the enclosing `GrantSessions` type. This is one of the existing CI findings reported in #186992.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change. Conversation labels, archived-state handling, the grant picker, and access enforcement retain their existing behavior. The row fields and the exported `GrantSessions` structure stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`GrantSession` is a private plugin implementation type used only by `GrantSessions.rows` in the same module. Keeping the alias module-local removes the unnecessary export while preserving its definition and the actual settings consumer. No scanner configuration, ignore, dependency, or runtime code changes.

## Evidence

The complete, unchanged `pnpm deadcode:exports` command ran before and after the change. Production findings dropped from 5 to 4 and full-tree findings from 9 to 8, with only `GrantSession` removed. The scripts pass retained its 4 findings; all unrelated findings and aggregate exit 1 remain unchanged.

Changed-file formatting, lint, and the selected i18n check passed. The native affected `extensions` type graph also passed, including the real settings consumer of `GrantSessions`.

prs.title: fix: guide recovery for unsupported generated attachments
prs.body: Fixes #186633 ## What Problem This Solves WebChat tells users to retry a generated file after managed attachment preparation has rejected its detected format. For a valid gzip file, sending the same bytes again cannot resolve that rejection. The original may still be saved and downloadable, but the failure card does not explain the supported recovery path. ## User Impact Unsupported generated attachments receive format-specific guidance. When the original is saved in the session, users can download it from Files or ask for a ZIP containing the original file. Supported sibling attachments remain available, and recovery preserves the saved bytes. The managed format allowlist, byte verification, session/read authority, cancellation, and file cleanup rules are unchanged. Other preparation failures retain their existing handling. The guidance is conditional because a failure card alone does not establish that an original file is saved or currently readable. Existing stored generic failures keep their recorded outcome; their discarded causes cannot be reconstructed safely. ## Why This Change Was Made The managed preparation owner already knows when a successfully ingested file fails its MIME admission check. It now carries that existing `unsupported-format` outcome into the failure card instead of discarding the distinction. The code is scoped to each attachment and still rechecks current authority before returning any failure card. Strict callers retain their sanitized exception and rollback behavior. The existing UI reason text and WebChat documentation explain Files/ZIP recovery. prs.title: fix: follow destination changes for published PRs
prs.body: Fixes #186611 ## What Problem This Solves Refreshing a conversation’s published PR can report the old base as current after someone retargets that PR on GitHub. ## User Impact Explicit refresh follows the original PR’s current destination, and subsequent publication continues the same PR and head branch. The existing integration workflow preserves saved work, history, and conflict handling. Imported PRs retain their verified-author checks; personal and first publication retain their existing selection rules. ## Why This Change Was Made The publication target owner now uses the current conversation’s completed receipt to select and verify its original PR before resolving the destination branch. Repository, head branch, publisher, and current requester checks still govern continuation. Valid mixed-case repository remotes resolve the canonical PR. Recovery verifies the recorded commit’s tree, parent, and request marker before settling uncertain effects. It observes a PR created by the current request before consulting an older receipt, preserving recovery when an earlier PR closed and a later request created another one. Historical receipts remain unchanged. The change adds no persistent binding, configuration, migration, or public API. ## Evidence The stale-base result was reproduced through the native tool/RPC/workspace path with real Git, and separately in a live conversation after its own draft PR was retargeted and the destination advanced. Saved edits and history were preserved in the live baseline. Remote regressions exercise destination refresh and same-PR publication, interruption followed by retargeting or closure, new publication after closure, revoked authority, foreign head repositories, same-publisher credential rotation, and mixed-case remotes. Related caller checks, formatting/lint, and affected production/test type checks passed. Closed-PR fixtures use metadata behavior independently observed on GitHub. The integrated revision passed 274 tests across eleven affected files, plus selected formatting, lint, and production/test type checks. The runtime suite's 23 conditional PostgreSQL cases were skipped. Independent engineering review, automated engineering review, and exact-head hosted CI passed. On the final head, the original live conversation saved a new checklist edit and refreshed the same PR after its review branch advanced again. The native receipt selected the current review branch and integrated the new destination note; all five existing file hashes and guest history were preserved. Subsequent publication kept the same draft PR, author, title, body, branch, and destination. Its initial reply was unconfirmed; existing automatic recovery settled the same request and reported published in the original conversation without another publication request or permission change. Guest status, the stored receipt, and independent GitHub readback agree on head `234479c7`, its tree, and parent. The initial observation failure is not attributed to a specific cause. Authority evidence exercises the real requester, session, receipt, and Git transaction owners with external process I/O controlled. [Registered Gateway dispatch cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/634dec29d7a165599f206b7b47dbc2defbbe25ab/src/gateway/github-publication-session-access.test.ts#L266) reject foreign and non-publishing targets before execution; their authority path is unchanged. [Current-head revocation cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/634dec29d7a165599f206b7b47dbc2defbbe25ab/src/gateway/github-publication-requester.test.ts#L357) revoke the role after a real local ref/index transaction and verify no external writes. The transport harness leaves the [final pre-push authority check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/634dec29d7a165599f206b7b47dbc2defbbe25ab/src/gateway/github-publication-executor.ts#L578) intact. Current-head retargeted and closed-PR recovery cases settle the original result after revocation without adding write calls. The live evidence separately establishes actual GitHub continuation and settlement; no live forbidden-write attempt is claimed. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![The original conversation still selects main after its PR was retargeted\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/880714cd-3148-428f-83f8-b5051b03daf3) | ![The original conversation refreshes from the current review destination, preserving its saved checklist and history\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ac0f723-45a5-448d-b602-abb90ca35443) | ### Exact\-head refresh: loading and native checks are shown at 4× https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2afa89e7-bf88-4f1b-b1c8-0be5eebfe023 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 1b6532ba471c3e86304c89f9dfbbc379a81f816f - Exact head: `634dec29d7a165599f206b7b47dbc2defbbe25ab` - Scenario: Refresh the existing conversation after its original draft PR is retargeted, preserving the saved checklist and history\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.8; build 2026\.10\.8\-634dec29d7a1\-2026\-10\-28T17\-16\-15\.630Z - Native destination before: main in the historical baseline; current review branch remains selected for continuation - Native destination after: r30\-20261028\-review; 5ae1515e - Saved work: All five existing file hashes preserved; guest HEAD and history unchanged - PR during refresh: Same open draft \#13; remote metadata unchanged - Subsequent publication: Same draft PR \#13 updated to 234479c7; native receipt and automatic completion report agree - Same original conversation, draft PR, natural refresh request, viewport and theme\. - The retained failing baseline predates the fix\. The exact\-head rerun advances the same review destination again and saves a new checklist edit; it preserves the previously accepted contribution\. - Native refresh receipt names review/5ae1515e and destination\-follow\-up\.md; independent branch and workspace readbacks agree\. - All five existing file hashes remain unchanged through refresh; the canonical merge retains its previous head and the new destination as ancestors\. - Guest HEAD remains 82ca614; the native review base advances to 5ae1515e\. - No motion or frame\-level performance claim\. - Publication initially returned unconfirmed; existing automatic recovery settled the same request and reported it in the original conversation\. No second publish or permission change\. The initial observation failure is not attributed to a specific cause\. ### Subsequent publication confirmation The initial unconfirmed reply and the later native completion report remain visible in the original conversation. ![Native same-PR publication completion](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f9e3310-4814-4e13-ba11-8f012aff92f1)

prs.title: feat(agents): preserve stores during controlled Gateway handoff
prs.body:
Related: #178748

## What Problem This Solves

An agent's identity and history should survive a change in where it runs. An operator may start an agent on a shared Gateway, then move it to a dedicated Gateway for capacity or isolation. Today there is no supported per-agent removal operation for that handoff: `agents.delete({ agentId, deleteFiles: false })` still requests session-store purging. Keeping files does not preserve sessions.

With PostgreSQL, the durable agent data can already stay in the same database. The missing operation releases the source Gateway's use of that store without deleting its contents.

## User Impact

An administrator can:

1. Stop routing new work to the source and wait for `agents.detach({ agentId })` to succeed.
2. Transfer the closed original anchor and required workspace files, keeping the agent ID and PostgreSQL namespace.
3. Use existing `agents.create` on the destination, verify retained identity/history, restore destination settings, then switch routing.

This enables planned capacity changes and maintenance without resetting the agent's history or copying its PostgreSQL rows. Workspace files remain a separate transfer responsibility. This is a new operator capability, with no claim of a current outage or regression.

## Why This Change Was Made

Changing `agents.delete` would weaken its cleanup contract. Editing the roster or copying an anchor alone bypasses admission closure, draining and restart recovery. Detach makes retention explicit while reusing those lifecycle owners.

The implementation records durable detach intent, drains work, closes database owners and retains the store/files. Recovery and destructive retries cannot convert a pending detach into deletion; offline CLI deletion refuses a pending detach, and `openclaw agents detach <id> --force --json` runs the same journaled lifecycle while the Gateway is stopped.

Core supplies the local lifecycle primitive; a controller or plugin orchestrates placement and routing. There is no database schema-version change, new adoption RPC or distributed ownership manager. Three unchanged session-policy constants move out of the method table to meet the repository's file limit.

## Scope and Compatibility

This is administrator-controlled sequential handoff. The controller owns exclusive assignment, routing, database permissions and file transfer. Source tombstones refuse ordinary writes after restart, but cannot prevent explicit source recreation or duplicate adoption.

Detach removes Gateway-local bindings, execution approvals and provenance; restore required destination settings explicitly. It retains cron jobs; the detached agent cannot execute them. Existing restrictions on the sole configured agent and shared/inherited credential owners remain. Local shared state and anchors can remain SQLite.

The new journal phases are a compatibility commitment: binaries without this change reject retained detach journals, including completed records, at the journal read sites (agent re-creation, deletion, recovery) while still starting and serving the remaining agents. Keep a compatible runtime while those records remain.

**Held-scheduler caveat (undecided).** The integration test's `held: true` and `held: offline CLI` cases, and one sentence in `docs/gateway/postgresql.md`, refer to a `cron.migration` RPC (hold / export / resume phases). That RPC exists only in a downstream scheduler-custody overlay, not in upstream OpenClaw, so those two cases fail on upstream with `unknown method: cron.migration`. The unheld path is what this PR proves. Whether to drop the held cases and that doc sentence, or to upstream a scheduler hold first, is an open decision for the author and maintainers; nothing in this revision changes code to paper over it.

## Evidence (exact head)

Head: `fcc6e8302b862be09ab72de1dfe0f8ffe9347318` (PR branch merged with upstream `main` `0661e52a19d`; the reviewed commits are unchanged, conflicts were resolved in the merge commit).

### Live two-Gateway handoff on this head (redacted transcript)

Setup: two real Gateway processes started from this head's source (`startGatewayServer` with a managed restart owner, as under the CLI supervisor), each with its own `HOME`, state directory, config, token and port; one PostgreSQL 16 database (`unaccent`, `pg_trgm`) shared through `database.families.agent.engine = "postgres"` with one schema prefix; SQLite shared state and anchors stay local. Every RPC is a separate client process; the scopes it requests are printed with each call. A third process is an upstream `main` checkout without this change (`54afe289085`), used as the no-PR build. Paths, tokens, the database password and the user name are redacted; nothing else is edited.

What the transcript shows, in order:

1. Source Gateway A creates `traveler` (PostgreSQL store, anchor records store UUID and namespace), a session and one transcript message.
2. Destination Gateway B's state directory is created and written by the no-PR build, then opened by this head: the pre-existing session and message load (existing-data check).
3. An `operator.write`-only caller is refused `agents.detach` (`FORBIDDEN`, missing `operator.admin`); roster and journal are untouched.
4. An administrator's `agents.detach` succeeds (`ok: true`, hot reload applied, no recovery restart). The roster drops `traveler`; the journal records `detach-retiring`, `deleteFiles: false`, `cleanupCompleted: true`; the anchor file, workspace file and PostgreSQL namespace are all still present.
5. Before restart the source refuses a `traveler` write; `keeper` is still listed and readable.
6. After restarting A, `sessions.create` for `traveler` is refused (`Unknown agent id`) and a write into the old session is refused (`deletion is in progress; new work is unavailable`); `keeper` still writes.
7. The closed anchor and workspace are copied to B (same agent id, same namespace recorded in the anchor).
8. B's `agents.create` admits the existing anchor; `chat.history` on B returns the **same session id and message** created on A; a new write on B lands (2 messages). The source still refuses `traveler` afterwards.
9. Offline CLI on the stopped source: a journal left in `detach-retiring` is completed by `openclaw agents detach --force --json` (`detached: true, storePreserved: true`; roster entry removed, workspace and state directories retained); a journal in `retiring` (pending destructive deletion) is **not** converted (`has a pending deletion; finish agents.delete before detaching`); with the Gateway running, the offline command refuses with `requires exclusive offline state ownership`, no mutation.
10. The no-PR build against the source state: its Gateway starts and lists `keeper`, but `agents.create traveler` and `agents.delete traveler` are refused with `Invalid agent deletion journal phase.`, and its journal reader reports the same error.

Not exercised live here: a replaced deletion lease racing a detach between two processes (covered at the journal-authority level by `src/state/agent-deletion-journal.fence.test.ts`, `changed before recovery`), the held-scheduler cases (see caveat), and a packaged v2026.10.5 upgrade.
