prs.title: fix(gateway): config.patch hangs after a superseded reload until another config change lands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A persisted `config.patch` / `config.apply` can leave its RPC waiting indefinitely after an in-process Gateway restart. Retained reload candidates were not always rescheduled. Real Gateway verification also exposed a second cause: the effective-unchanged path compared a resolved secrets snapshot with an unresolved SecretRef candidate, classified the permanent mismatch as supersession, and kept retrying it.

## User Impact

Provisioning and other source-equivalent config writes receive their application acknowledgment without an unrelated follow-up edit. Existing credential activation, publication ownership, and rollback checks remain in force. No config option, schema, dependency, or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Schedule another attempt whenever a superseded write candidate is retained, including candidates retained by either inner catch.
- The second cause this PR originally repaired, a resolved-snapshot versus unresolved-SecretRef comparison that classified an unchanged write as superseded, is fixed upstream by #183964 (merged October 27). This PR's guard for it and its two regression cases were dropped on October 28; `server-reload-managed-secrets.ts` and its test are now identical to `main`.

The complete PR now changes one production line in `config-reload.ts` and adds one focused regression file, reusing the existing retry owner rather than introducing a second resolver, state, or weaker guards.

## Evidence

### October 28 refresh: exact-head real Gateway run on `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`

<!-- pr177823-oct28-refresh -->

Upstream `main` moved past the reviewed head `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625`, and the branch picked up test-path and test-line-ceiling conflicts. The branch now carries merge commits of upstream `main` (latest `56eba2fae26`) plus two ceiling-only commits; the reviewed commits are untouched and the production diff against `main` is still the same two files, nine net lines. Everything below ran on the exact pushed head `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`, built from source (`dist/build-info.json` commit `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`, OpenClaw 2026.10.8), host Node v24.19.0, Gateway native runtime Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64, isolated `--profile` state, token auth, distinct free loopback ports.

#### Executed workload

Identical to the October 19 workload: full `gateway run --verbose`, real `SIGUSR2` **in-process restart**, `config.get`, one source-equivalent `config.patch` (`response:"summary"`) that rewrites the disabled Mattermost account's `baseUrl` to the `${PR177823_MATTERMOST_URL}` placeholder, then, right after the `config.patch write` log line, rotate the file-backed `proof/proof` provider key A→B and call `secrets.reload`, wait 2.5 s, restore B→A and call `secrets.reload` again, no further config write, 30 s RPC deadline, clean shutdown. The client is one process built on the repository's own `callGateway` owner (`src/gateway/call.ts`, CLI client mode), so the rotation reaches the Gateway about 40 ms after the write log line.

| Source | Same restart + file-credential-refresh workload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Merge parent `953eba4bbeec1c8cf7b255cce1c8c3f1496aaf3b` (current upstream `main` without this PR) | Identical | Original patch answered successfully in **270 ms server / 280.7 ms client**, zero supersessions, clean shutdown. **PASS** |
| Final head `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9` | Identical | Original patch answered successfully in **420 ms server / 433.2 ms client**, zero supersessions, clean shutdown. **PASS** |

Redacted exact-head Gateway log, **October 28, 2026, UTC−07:00**:

```text
2026-10-28T15:00:42.439-07:00 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
2026-10-28T15:00:42.845-07:00 [gateway] restart mode: in-process restart (unmanaged: use in-process restart to keep custom supervisor PID tracking stable)
2026-10-28T15:01:06.966-07:00 [gateway] config.patch write changedPaths=channels.mattermost.accounts.proof.baseUrl restartReason=config.patch
2026-10-28T15:01:07.196-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 174ms
2026-10-28T15:01:07.298-07:00 [reload] config source revision 1 accepted (write)
2026-10-28T15:01:07.367-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ config.patch 420ms
2026-10-28T15:01:09.852-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 127ms
2026-10-28T15:01:10.503-07:00 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 553ms
```

Raw trace SHA-256 values: final-head Gateway log `ff77f2dd59dd24ba308e09d8f5e5d47af91672bc440ae5ec23b27baac1ad3e26`, final-head client event trace `1fb2d2fb88aaaf73400895f5acea84d45bf221ca0949a97622bb37af374d0cf8`, merge-parent Gateway log `8ea5b86083fef455e0a92d24a318486415e7989ff56d9cb4996e09065952f238`.

#### Exact-head rerun after the guard removal: `c3efb3da9a340c5957702cfbe783b8976593d52b`

Same build procedure, same workload, same client. Original patch answered successfully in **265 ms server / 274.4 ms client**, zero supersessions, clean shutdown. Redacted Gateway log, **October 28, 2026, UTC−07:00**:

```text
2026-10-28T15:21:07.167-07:00 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
2026-10-28T15:21:07.626-07:00 [gateway] restart mode: in-process restart (unmanaged: use in-process restart to keep custom supervisor PID tracking stable)
2026-10-28T15:21:15.624-07:00 [gateway] config.patch write changedPaths=channels.mattermost.accounts.proof.baseUrl restartReason=config.patch
2026-10-28T15:21:15.769-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 110ms
2026-10-28T15:21:15.820-07:00 [reload] config source revision 1 accepted (write)
2026-10-28T15:21:15.873-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ config.patch 265ms
2026-10-28T15:21:18.368-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 83ms
2026-10-28T15:21:18.544-07:00 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 127ms
```

Raw trace SHA-256 values: Gateway log `cda9311452c3a1c967099bd028e9355bb010e6618b097c457a29158af51c4b59`, client event trace `26e14af67145e907356902a48622f308792b534a1217b19cbe629f8896e52941`.

#### What changed upstream, and what this PR still fixes

The merge-parent control **no longer fails** this workload. Upstream [#183964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183964) (merged October 27) changed the unchanged-write handler in `server-reload-managed-secrets.ts` so an unchanged candidate whose secrets-source form equals the running snapshot's is accepted instead of being reported as superseded. That is the second cause this PR targeted, so the real-Gateway run no longer discriminates between `main` and this head. This PR's `server-reload-managed-secrets.ts` guard sat on top of an equivalent upstream guard (its stable-key and rotated-key regression cases pass on the merge parent without it), so the guard and those two cases were **dropped**: both files are now byte-identical to `main`.

The first cause is still present on `main`: a retained superseded write candidate is not rescheduled. `config-reload.superseded-retry.test.ts` fails on the merge parent (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 3 times, but got 1 times`) and passes at this head with the two-line `config-reload.ts` change. Two attempts to force a genuine supersession on a real current-`main` Gateway (a second concurrent `config.patch`; an external on-disk save of `openclaw.json` inside the first write's apply window) were refused before apply by the base-hash guard (`config base hash required…`, `config changed since last load…`), so no live-supersession trace is claimed for the new head; the scheduler repair remains proven by the focused regression, as stated below.

#### Checks at the final head

- `config-reload.superseded-retry.test.ts` (1) and `server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts` (19): **20 passed** at `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`; the same two files on the merge parent: 19 passed, superseded-retry failed. After the guard removal (head `c3efb3da9a340c5957702cfbe783b8976593d52b`), superseded-retry, upstream's managed-secrets suite and `config-reload.test.ts` pass together.
- Gateway test-path list, test-projects routing and CI node test plan checks: 284 passed on the first merge commit of this refresh.
- Test-line ceiling: `main` keeps `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` at zero slack; this PR adds exactly 118 test lines, so each merge admits the measured total with no future allowance. `main` raised its own zero-slack ceiling twice more while this refresh was running (ceiling-only merges `d9bc85d1ff74122e2188028ddb72876ecf0f366b` and `1b9faf2d32354ceb3d0d93ef68c4da23cc0a1667`). After the guard removal the PR adds 60 test lines, which fit under `main`'s current ceiling, so `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` is back to `main`'s file.
- The merge commits require fresh maintainer security approval on the final head; none is claimed.

### Exact-head real Gateway recovery: `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625`

<!-- pr177823-real-gateway-repair-b8c13e0 -->

The previously stalling workload now completes on the final fixed full Gateway: **437 ms server / 439 ms client**, after a real SIGUSR2 in-process restart and concurrent synthetic credential refresh, with **no later config edit**.

Important distinction: this final run logged **zero supersessions**. The repair prevents the permanent resolved-value/SecretRef mismatch that produced them on the older head. This is not presented as a new-head trace that throws a supersession and then succeeds.

#### Comparable real-runtime controls

| Source | Same restart + file-credential-refresh workload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct parent `08d04a9d7b97e50849ba089c3837d2e1c3c4f7fd` | One supersession, credential restored, no additional config write | Original patch still pending at the 30 s client deadline. It answered UNAVAILABLE only during shutdown, at 50,016 ms. **FAIL** |
| Initial PR head `ebfffd5599a7ee7c6d793718b96f923107b27691` | Eight supersessions before credential restoration; retries continued afterward | Original patch still pending at 30 s; 482 supersessions were recorded before task-owned forced cleanup. **FAIL** |
| First repair `c337231afc47e7cf137f0273a9051daab79b71ae` | Identical public-RPC/file workload | Original patch answered in **308 ms**, but broader CI exposed a restart-reapply regression. This is prior-head runtime evidence, not the final candidate. |
| Final head `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625` | Identical public-RPC/file workload | Original patch answered successfully in **439 ms**, before the credential-restoration step. Clean Gateway shutdown. **PASS** |

All runs used OpenClaw 2026.10.5, Node v26.8.1, macOS arm64, independently owned dependencies, isolated synthetic HOME/state/config/workspace, and distinct free loopback ports between control families. The final build and runtime-postbuild stamps both identify exact `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625` with `inputsClean:true`.

No mocked hot-reload callback, injected exception, fake clock, manually settled receipt, inference call, live Mattermost traffic, operator Gateway change, or TEST/PROD mutation was used in these real Gateway runs.

#### Executed workload

1. Start the full maintained Gateway with `node scripts/run-node.mjs --profile pr177823proof gateway run --port <isolated-port> --verbose`; wait for readiness.
2. Send SIGUSR2 only to that fixture's own Gateway PID; verify **in-process restart** and readiness again.
3. Connect through the real token-authenticated Gateway WebSocket protocol (v4). Read `config.get` for the base hash.
4. Submit one `config.patch` with `response:"summary"`:
   ```json
   {"channels":{"mattermost":{"accounts":{"proof":{"baseUrl":"${PR177823_MATTERMOST_URL}"}}}}}
   ```
   The environment placeholder resolves to the existing synthetic URL; the Mattermost account is disabled.
5. After the actual `config.patch write` log, rotate a task-owned JSON file's synthetic provider key A→B and call the real `secrets.reload {}` RPC. The provider is a custom `proof/proof` model pointing at an unused loopback endpoint; no model turn is sent. Its config uses:
   ```json
   {"apiKey":{"source":"file","provider":"proof","id":"/apiKey"}}
   ```
6. Observe for 2.5 s, restore that **credential file** B→A, and call `secrets.reload {}` again. Do not edit config or send another config-write RPC. The RPC deadline stays 30 s.
7. Join Gateway shutdown. On the fixed head, the original patch had already completed before step 6.

Redacted actual fixed Gateway log; **October 19, 2026, UTC−07:00**:

```text
18:27:43.065 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
18:27:43.192 [gateway] restart mode: in-process restart
18:27:49.708 [gateway] config.patch write ... changedPaths=channels.mattermost.accounts.proof.baseUrl
18:27:49.971 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 242ms id=proof-4
18:27:50.068 [reload] config source revision 2 accepted (write)
18:27:50.082 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ config.patch 437ms id=proof-3
18:27:52.511 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 33ms id=proof-5
18:27:52.595 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 77ms
```

The original patch response was `ok:true`, with the expected changed path, `sentinel.persisted:true`, and `requiresRestart:false`. The raw trace contains one config write for the scenario and no later config write. The client observed settlement before the restoration RPC.

Raw local trace SHA-256 values (the redacted excerpt above is the submitted public evidence):

These are isolated production-path controls, not a claim that the original tenant's entire environment was replayed. An earlier setup attempt expired while the source launcher was still rebuilding, before any config RPC; it is a setup failure, not a Gateway behavior verdict. The final clean-head run completed normally.

### Focused behavioral regression and checks

- The stable-key and rotated-key cases once added to `server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts` were dropped on October 28 together with the guard they covered; upstream #183964 carries an equivalent case ("settles an unchanged activation write whose secrets are still unresolved").
- Existing `config-reload.superseded-retry.test.ts` still proves two retained supersessions followed by automatic application. Its hot-reload failures are mocked; this remains focused scheduler proof, not real-Gateway evidence.
- Maintained focused runs: **271 tests passed across 4 affected files**: config-reload plus superseded-retry (134), the complete restart/reload-handler suite (118), and managed secrets (19). After narrowing the guard, the combined run passed the first 252 but exposed the secrets fixture's identity stub; replacing that stub with production's existing `restoreCanonicalSecretRefs` helper made all 19 secrets tests pass (18.05 s wrapper / 12.12 s shard). No assertions, timeouts, or baselines changed. No full Bun/CI pass on the final head is claimed.
- Core typecheck and the canonical Gateway-server test typecheck passed.
- Targeted oxlint, formatter check, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap ratchet passed.

- The broad changed-test typecheck selector encountered pre-existing advisory root-budget excesses in unrelated graph inventories; the relevant canonical Gateway-server graph was typechecked directly and passed. No inventory, budget, assertion, or baseline was weakened.

### CI and review status

The final repair remains at exact `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625`. Its [pull-request CI run 39353612934](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39353612934) completed successfully, including the CI workflow's `openclaw/ci-gate`. The separately enforced aggregate status is still **failing**, because the [security review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39356909084/job/118413751307) explicitly reports “awaiting maintainer approval.” A successful policy-workflow execution is not a security approval, and no merge clearance is claimed.

The first repair's [CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39351516553/job/118396992531) timed out both existing `revalidates restart secrets after held promotion and an explicit reapply` cases at 120 s. The maintained CI classifier returned unknown/no comparable main job; the exact job log and a bounded local comparison established this as PR-caused, not inherited: both cases passed on initial `ebfffd5`, while `c337231` locally reproduced the first timeout (the second was interrupted after the same CI failure was established). The broad mismatch guard had incorrectly entered hot publication inside restart-owned reapplication. The final canonicalization comparison retains the restart owner; both cases and the full 118-test handler suite pass without changing those tests.

Prior-head dependency review passed. The [prior security-sensitive review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39351510133/job/118396555176) reports **awaiting maintainer approval** for the credential-owner change. Final-head security approval is still required; it is not bypassed or described as passing.

The local independent-review helper for this repair returned `reviewer_unavailable` without producing a report. The author explicitly approved publication for ClawSweeper review without that local review; that history is unchanged. [ClawSweeper's latest exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177823#issuecomment-6279684646), refreshed October 20 after this evidence update, rated **readiness 5/6, proof 5/6, patch quality 5/6**, with zero actionable findings on final `b8c13e0`. Its remaining checklist item is maintainer security approval. The later successful local review of a downstream integration is not relabeled as an independent review of this PR.

### October 20 refresh integration check

<!-- pr177823-oct20-refresh -->

The complete patch is retained in the downstream [refreshed native source `10f31e19e8a7b5d882c7078c1701bc8a7d3daa9b`](https://github.com/ceckert/openclaw/commit/10f31e19e8a7b5d882c7078c1701bc8a7d3daa9b), integrated with selected upstream main `2d03d5632a69d04181844f85b05d5509240dcc14`.

- The exact-head parent/fixed Gateway controls above remain the primary behavioral proof. No later deployment, live-provider result, merged security approval, or new-head real supersession trace is inferred from today's build.

The original pre-fix incident remains a failure: after an in-process restart, a source-equivalent Mattermost URL write logged supersession and timed out after 130 s; an unrelated heartbeat edit later released the parked request at 198,627 ms.

prs.title: feat(mattermost): acknowledgement reactions, channel events and compact tool progress
prs.body: Related: #184712 ## What Problem This Solves Mattermost users get a thinner experience than Telegram, Discord and Slack users: no acknowledgement reaction while the agent works, repeated `Exec` rows crowding the progress preview, no awareness of edits, deletions or members joining a channel, no introduction when the bot is added to a channel, every reaction in a busy channel forwarded to the agent, and voice messages that cannot wake a mention-gated channel. ## User Impact User impact: Mattermost chats now ack an inbound post with an emoji (`messages.ackReactionScope`, `channels.mattermost.ackReaction`) and swap it for ❌ when the agent run fails, count repeated tool calls into one row in `progress` previews (`🛠️ Exec ×12`, as Telegram does since #184712), forward post edits, deletions and member joins/leaves as system events, post a join introduction when the bot is added to a channel (`joinIntro: true`, opt-in for Mattermost; admission is re-checked from the live configuration while the introduction's context loads and right before the model turn), can limit forwarded reactions to the bot's own posts (`reactionNotifications: all | own | off`), and admit a media-only voice message in a mention-gated channel when the transcript names the agent (the preflight transcription honors `tools.media.audio.scope` with private and group rooms counted as `group`, and transcript echoes happen only for admitted posts). No behavior change on upgrade: `reactionNotifications` defaults to `all`, so existing deployments keep forwarding every allowed reaction (`own`, the Telegram/Discord/Slack default, and `off` are opt-ins); the join introduction stays off until `joinIntro: true` is set at channel or account level. Existing configs load unchanged: every new key is optional and the bundled channel metadata is regenerated. The one visible addition for an existing config is the acknowledgement reaction where `messages.ackReactionScope` already applies. ## Why This Change Was Made Each feature reuses the shared runtime the other channels already use (`ack-reactions`, `StatusReactionController`, `createChannelPreflightAudio`, `reportChannelRoomJoin`, `compactToolRuns` on the progress compositor) and wires it to Mattermost's websocket events and reaction API, so Mattermost stops being the odd channel out without new core behavior. The Mattermost emoji map gains the status-reaction glyphs the controller emits. ## Evidence - `pnpm vitest run extensions/mattermost`: 57 files / 557 tests pass; the one failure, `slash-http.boundary.test.ts` ("reserves authenticated capacity…"), fails identically on a clean `main` checkout and is unrelated to this change. - New or extended tests: compaction with `status` vs `raw` command text (`monitor.preview-delivery.test-support.ts`), ack reaction through a run and the ❌ swap on a failed run outcome (`monitor.feedback.test-support.ts`), spoken-mention admission and no double download (`monitor.feedback.test-support.ts`, `preflight-audio.test.ts`), `reactionNotifications` modes incl. the `all` default (`monitor.reaction-thread-session.test.ts`), websocket dispatch of edit/delete/membership events (`monitor-websocket.test.ts`), system-event forwarding, join introduction with channel purpose and recent posts, and the join-intro authority skips (policy disabled at start, revoked after start, account disabled after start) resolved by the real `reportChannelRoomJoin` owner with no Mattermost request (`monitor-system-events.test.ts`). Each exercises production code that does not exist on `main`. - `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `format:docs`, `config:channels:gen`/`check`, the assertion-safety, mock-exports, line-cap and max-lines ratchets, and `git diff --check` are clean. The mock-exports baseline shrinks by two lines (two retired `vi.mock` factories). - Branch merged with `main` (merge commit, no conflicts). - Test-lines ratchet: the branch adds net +214 test lines after consolidation and the review-driven additions (shared loopback monitor fixture in `monitor.loopback.test-support.ts`, `it.each` tables for system events, feedback and websocket dispatch, and twelve duplicated or mock-argument tests removed where a sibling already proves the behavior at the owning boundary; each removal and its surviving test is listed in commit `6bcebf6e154`). The check is still red: after merging `main` the tree measures 6,311,016 against the 6,310,783 ceiling, and `main` itself is 19 lines over it, so no PR that adds a test line can pass until the ceiling moves; the ceiling was not raised here. - Channel config docs budget 4001 → 4007: three new documented Mattermost options (`joinIntro`, `reactionNotifications`, `ackReaction`), regenerated with `config:docs:gen` (same precedent as `allowBots` in da579df307a). - Docs: `docs/channels/mattermost.md` (reactions, acknowledgement and status reactions, channel events and join introduction, voice admission, compaction note) and `docs/concepts/streaming.md`. ### Live proof on a disposable gateway and Mattermost server Setup, all local: Mattermost Team Edition 11 in Docker (fresh Postgres), a bot account `@octo` with a personal access token, two human users, and an isolated OpenClaw gateway started from this branch with its own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (`gateway run --verbose`, `streaming.mode: progress`, `progress.toolProgress: true`, `messages.ackReactionScope: "all"`, `reactionNotifications: "own"`). The model is a scripted OpenAI-compatible provider that answers "please run twelve steps" with twelve real `exec` tool calls (`sleep 1; printf step-N`) and a final text, so the gateway runs real tools; a driver script posts as the human and reads the Mattermost REST API every 250 ms. **Compact tool progress.** One preview post (`6tbem8oj`) edited in place, then finalized in place; no counted-row cap: | t (ms) | post | preview text | | ---: | --- | --- | | 267 | `6tbem8oj` | `Working · · 🛠️ Exec: running` | | 1582 | `6tbem8oj` | `Working · · 🛠️ Exec ×2: running` | | 2638 | `6tbem8oj` | `Working · · 🛠️ Exec ×3: running` | | 3960 | `6tbem8oj` | `Working · · 🛠️ Exec ×4: running` | | 5252 | `6tbem8oj` | `Working · · 🛠️ Exec ×5: running` | | 6298 | `6tbem8oj` | `Working · · 🛠️ Exec ×6: running` | | 7598 | `6tbem8oj` | `Working · · 🛠️ Exec ×7: running` | | 8914 | `6tbem8oj` | `Working · · 🛠️ Exec ×9: running` | | 9967 | `6tbem8oj` | `Working · · 🛠️ Exec ×10: running` | | 11280 | `6tbem8oj` | `Working · · 🛠️ Exec ×11: running` | | 12589 | `6tbem8oj` | `Working · · 🛠️ Exec ×12: running` | | 13111 | `6tbem8oj` | `Ran 12 steps. Last tool output: step-12` | **Acknowledgement reaction.** Every human post in the channel received the bot's `:eyes:` reaction within the poll window (`GET /posts//reactions` → `[{"user":"bot","emoji":"eyes"}]` on the hello, twelve-steps and fail-one-step posts). **Channel events and reaction filtering** (gateway debug log, same run): ```text 16:53:59.751Z mattermost system event: Mattermost message edited by @alice in #deploys-mvscrt64 (post ff5o6rbpa3bi8emh8cehyyxzah). 16:54:01.262Z mattermost: drop reaction (reactionNotifications=own post=ff5o6rbpa3bi8emh8cehyyxzah author=brno58g953bapxu9s3jqf4ewbr) 16:54:02.289Z mattermost reaction: added :thumbsup: by alice on gy88u9gbdi8zjg3wpayjd9akho 16:54:03.808Z mattermost system event: Mattermost message deleted by @alice in #deploys-mvscrt64 (post ff5o6rbpa3bi8emh8cehyyxzah). 16:54:22.438Z mattermost system event: Mattermost: @bob joined #ops-mvsctkf5. 16:54:28.980Z mattermost system event: Mattermost: @alice left #ops-mvsctkf5. ``` The next model turn in that channel carried the events (captured from the provider request): `System: [..] Mattermost message edited by @alice in #deploys-mvscrt64 (post ff5o6…)`, `Mattermost reaction added: :thumbsup: by @alice on post gy88u…`, `Mattermost message deleted by @alice …`; alice's `:tada:` on her own post was not forwarded. In `#ops`, `Mattermost: @bob joined #ops-mvsctkf5.` reached the turn after bob was added. **Join introduction.** Adding `@octo` to a fresh `#ops` channel (purpose "Keep the lights on", two prior posts by alice) produced one bot post: "Hi, I'm Octo. I read this channel's purpose and recent posts, and I'll help with deploys here." The intro prompt the model received included the channel purpose and the two prior messages. **Spoken-mention admission** (second round, head `94316e8`, same setup with `chatmode: oncall`, `messages.groupChat.mentionPatterns: ["\\bocto\\b"]`, and `tools.media.models` pointing audio transcription at the scripted provider, which answers every `/audio/transcriptions` call with "hey octo can you check the deploy window for me"): | post by alice | result | | --- | --- | | plain text, no mention | dropped: `mattermost: drop no mention target=417c1ga…`, 0 model calls | | `@octo are you there?` | answered | | media-only `voice-note.wav` (`audio/x-wav`, no text) | admitted: the preflight downloaded the file, transcribed it, matched the mention (`mattermost: audio transcript mentioned the bot channel=417c1ga… post=hkdbpx8g…`), the turn's prompt carried `[Audio] Transcript: hey octo can you check the deploy window for me`, the bot answered within 2 s and acked the post with 👀 | The provider log shows two transcription requests for the admitted voice note (preflight admission, then the shared media pipeline for the agent) and one chat completion. **Mid-load revocation with real effects** (third round, live): the gateway was routed through a logging proxy that holds every `GET /channels//posts` response for 12 s, with `joinIntro: true`. Control join: the bot was added, the context request was held, then released, the model was called once and the introduction was posted (`POST /posts 201`). Revocation join: the bot was added to a fresh channel and, while the context request was held, `channels.mattermost.groupPolicy` was set to `disabled` in the config file. Result: 0 model calls, no `POST /posts`, and the owner logged `channel room join introduction settled {kind: skipped, reason: room-not-allowed}` the moment the held context arrived (proxy log: `GET /channels/`, `GET /channels/`, `GET /channels//posts 200 delayed 12000ms`, nothing else). **Audio scope** (third round, `preflight-audio.test.ts`, real `transcribeFirstAudio` with a stub provider and `tools.media.audio.scope.rules: [{ action: "deny", match: { chatType: "group" } }]`): a captionless voice post in a private room (`P` → `group`) is denied before any provider request (0 transcriber calls; red on the previous head which reached the provider), while the same post in a public channel is transcribed once with `echoTranscript` forced off for the preflight (red on the previous head which left the echo on). **Audio scope and echoes, live** (fourth round; same setup with `chatmode: oncall`, `tools.media.audio.echoTranscript: true`, the scripted transcription provider, and a logging proxy recording every Mattermost write): | case | provider requests | Mattermost writes by the bot | outcome | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | public room, voice note that names the bot (control) | transcription (preflight), transcription (admitted pass), chat | `POST /reactions`, `POST /posts` (one 📝 echo), `POST /posts` (reply) | admitted, one echo | | public room, voice note "just a note to myself about lunch" | transcription (preflight) | none | dropped (`drop no mention`), no echo | | private room (`P`), rule `deny chatType: group` present at start | none | none | `audio understanding disabled by scope policy`, dropped | | private room, same rule added by config reload after start, head `6eee2c6` | transcription (preflight) | reactions, typing, reply | **defect**: the preflight used the monitor's startup config snapshot while the admitted pass honored the new rule | | private room, same rule added by config reload, head `2ae49b1` | none | none | `disabled by scope policy`, dropped | The last row is the fix in `ada4e61`: the preflight now reads `config.current()` like the join introduction does; the harness case asserts the live scope reaches it (red on the previous handler). In every case the bot's only Mattermost read was `GET /files/` (the download that precedes admission); the scope decision runs before any provider request. **Join introduction authority, second round** (`94316e8`; vitest verbose, loopback server, real `reportChannelRoomJoin` owner): ```text ✓ skips the introduction without reading or posting when introductions were never enabled ✓ skips the introduction without reading or posting when the group policy is disabled ✓ skips the introduction without reading or posting when the group policy was disabled after the monitor started ✓ skips the introduction without reading or posting when the account was disabled after the monitor started ✓ stops the introduction when the group policy is disabled while the room context loads ✓ reportChannelRoomJoin > stops a join whose room admission is revoked while its context loads and leaves its claim available Tests 26 passed (26) ``` Red run with both owner re-checks (after context resolution and before the isolated turn) disabled: ```text × stops the introduction when the group policy is disabled while the room context loads → expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times (the isolated agent turn started) ``` **Upgrade from the latest stable** (`openclaw@2026.10.8` from npm in an isolated prefix): the stable gateway ran with a config that has only today's keys (no `reactionNotifications`, `joinIntro` or `ackReaction`), converged by the stable `doctor --fix`, and answered one post. The same state dir and config opened with this branch: `config validate` → `Config valid`; `doctor --fix` ran the schema admission and database migrations (agent database schema 25 → 38, pre-migration SQLite backups saved); the gateway booted, connected, answered the next post in the same channel, the stable-era message was present in the upgraded turn's prompt (same session), and the config file was left unchanged. **Join-introduction authority and failed-run reaction** (second run on the review-fix head `f15242c`, same setup; driver `drive-join-gate.mjs`, evidence `proof-evidence-join-gate.json`): | step | what happened | | --- | --- | | allowed room, `groupPolicy: open` | bot added to a fresh channel → one intro post, 1 model call, log `channel room join introduction settled … kind: posted` | | failed agent run | the scripted provider answered HTTP 500 on every attempt; the run retried 6× over ~70 s, posted "⚠️ The AI service is having trouble…", and the ack went 👀 → ❌ (held 2.5 s) → 👀 | | policy revoked at runtime | `groupPolicy` set to `disabled` in the config file; the gateway deferred the channel reload until the in-flight run settled (`[reload] config change requires channel reload (mattermost) — deferring until … 1 admitted agent run(s) complete`), then applied it (`config hot reload applied (channels.mattermost.groupPolicy)`) | | room joined after revocation | bot added to a fresh channel → no bot post, 0 model calls, log `channel room join introduction settled … kind: skipped, reason: room-not-allowed`; a human post in that room got no ack, no reply, 0 model calls | A room joined while the reload was still deferred (the old policy still live) was introduced, which is the deferred-reload contract, not a bypass: the introduction reads `config.current()` at event time and the shared owner returns `room-not-allowed` before dedupe, context reads or the model call. **Screenshots** (same run, Mattermost web UI as alice): Mid-run preview with the counted row, edited in place while the bot is still typing: The channel afterwards: 👀 acks on every human post, the preview finalized in place, the failing-step turn, alice's 👍 on a bot post: Join introduction in a fresh channel right after the bot was added: ### ClawSweeper review: what changed - Ack feedback now finishes from the agent-run outcome (`readAgentRunTerminalOutcome`, as Slack does) combined with final-delivery failures, so a run that delivers its own error notice still gets ❌; harness test red on the previous code. - `reactionNotifications` default kept at `all` (compatibility): existing deployments keep today's forwarding; `own` and `off` are opt-ins. Config UI hint, docs and bundled metadata regenerated. - Docs now state the real default ack scope: `group-mentions` acks mentioned channel posts only; DMs need `direct` or `all`. - The test-only `createMattermostPreflightAudio` injection factory is gone; one module-level adapter remains and the skip cases prove the transcriber is not called. - Join introduction authorization moved to the effect boundary: the handler passes a closure that re-resolves the account and group policy from `config.current()`, and the shared owner evaluates it before the context read, again after the context resolves, and again right before the isolated agent turn (`roomAllowed: boolean | (() => boolean)`, other channels keep passing a boolean). Unit cases red without the re-checks; live revocation runs above. - Second round, per the reviewer's recommendation: Mattermost introductions are opt-in (`enabledByDefault: false` passed to the shared owner; `joinIntro: true` enables them per channel or account); docs and config hints updated. - Second round proof: live spoken-mention admission, the mid-load revocation traces, and the stable 2026.10.8 upgrade run are above. - Fourth round: live audio traces above found that a scope rule added by config reload did not reach the preflight (startup snapshot); fixed by reading the live configuration (`ada4e61`), harness case red first. - Third round: the audio preflight passes the room's real kind (`direct`/`group`/`channel`) so `tools.media.audio.scope` deny rules apply before provider I/O, and uses the shared helper's default echo suppression so only admitted processing echoes; the extension test no longer mocks a core module (`lint:plugins:no-extension-test-core-imports` clean, the revocation case still red on the pre-fix owner through its `room-not-allowed` outcome); the branch is merged with `main`; live mid-load revocation with real provider and Mattermost effects is above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(qa): isolate legacy node recovery from finalization load
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The node-worker launch proof also runs independent legacy-capability recovery inside its fixed load-test deadline. A timeout can therefore mix capability recovery with the workspace finalization contract.

## User Impact

No user-visible or production behavior changes. This separates the existing QA contracts without changing either test deadline or reducing the 4,096-file, twelve-session load coverage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move legacy capability negotiation into its own case in the existing warm lifecycle suite. It keeps an independent modern witness and legacy host, the visible unsupported error and no-launch assertion, same-device reconnect, successful reply, no invoke errors, exactly one reply marker, and no bundle prewarm.

The case owns a subscribed operator and refreshes placement state before cleanup; a read-only turn does not have to change its content-addressed workspace manifest. The load case gains phase markers after reply completion and workspace settlement. Production delta: 0; test delta: +19 lines.

## Evidence

- Root and independent source reviews: clean after the two reviewed corrections.
- Pinned formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Runtime, targeted type/lint, and full two-file validation in original order: pending ordinary exact-head CI. The original failure ran under Bun; no local Node or same-Bun reproduction is claimed.
- Failure context: [node-worker launch CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40533093742/job/122292005154).

Follow-up: existing paired-node fixture temp-root custody after rejected or unconfirmed host shutdown remains a separate lifecycle issue. This change preserves aggregate cleanup and makes no physical-closure claim for that failure path.

prs.title: fix(matrix): forget cached credentials when an account is removed
prs.body:
Related: #186011. This PR covers its account-removal half. The cached-token recovery half is in #186135, which does not touch account removal.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw channels remove --channel matrix --account <id> --delete` removes the Matrix account from config but leaves that account's cached login (`plugin_state_entries`, `plugin_id=matrix`, `namespace=credentials`, `entry_key=account:<id>`). When the account is re-added with the same id, startup finds the matching cached credential and reuses the old access token instead of logging in with the newly supplied password. If that token was revoked, which is the reason most people remove and re-add, the account cannot recover without editing `openclaw.sqlite` by hand.

## User Impact

Removing a Matrix account now forgets its cached login. Re-adding the same account id with a password performs a fresh `m.login.password` login (a new device) instead of resurrecting the removed token. Accounts that are not removed are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel account-removal flow already calls the plugin's `lifecycle.onAccountRemoved` hook after the config change (`src/channels/plugins/account-config-mutation.ts`). Telegram uses it to drop its per-account update offset and bot-info cache. Matrix had no lifecycle hook, and `clearMatrixCredentials` (in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/credentials-read.ts`), which writes a durable revocation record so Doctor cannot resurrect the entry from a legacy file, had no production caller.

The Matrix plugin base (`extensions/matrix/src/channel.setup.ts`) now declares `lifecycle.onAccountRemoved`, which lazily loads the credentials module and calls `clearMatrixCredentials(process.env, accountId)`. It lives on the shared base because `channels remove` resolves Matrix through its setup entry (`matrixSetupPlugin`); the runtime plugin spreads the same base. Encrypted stores, recovery keys and other accounts' credentials are not touched.

**Stored-data compatibility:** there is no schema or format change. The hook writes the existing `kind: "revoked"` record that `clearMatrixCredentials` already defines, which `loadMatrixCredentials` and Doctor already read as "no credentials". Cached logins of accounts that are not removed are untouched, and the regression checks a sibling account. In the live run below, the cache written before the removal is the existing format, read unchanged by both builds.

## Evidence

### Tests

`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/credentials.test.ts` (already in the database-worker suite) has a renamed case, "clears only the account removed through channels remove". It stores credentials for `default` and `ops` in the real plugin state store and runs `matrixSetupPlugin.lifecycle.onAccountRemoved` for `ops`. It then expects `ops` to read as no credentials, with a `revoked` record, and `default` to keep its credentials.

- It fails on main, which has no hook, and passes on this branch.
- The file passes 12/12, including when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` points at an unusable path, because the test pins its own state dir.
- The first CI failure (`Shared-state admission requires the host broker`) came from a standalone test outside the database-worker list. That file is removed, which also keeps the test-lines ratchet within budget: the net diff is +18 lines.

Checks run locally: oxfmt, oxlint and `git diff --check` are clean.

### Live run (Windows 11, Node 26.12.1)

This is the real `openclaw gateway run` and `openclaw channels remove --channel matrix --account default --delete`, with an isolated state dir per build, each rebuilt before its run. A Matrix homeserver stand-in runs on loopback: `/login` issues `first-token` and later `fresh-token`, and once the bot's devices are "deleted" it answers `first-token` with `401 M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN`. The cache is the `plugin_state_entries` row (matrix / credentials / `account:default`) read from `openclaw.sqlite`.

![live run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/186011/proof-186011.png)

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| cache after `channels remove --delete` | **`accessToken=first-token` (kept)** | revoked marker |
| re-added account (same id and password) on start | **reuses revoked `first-token`** (5 requests), 0 logins | 1 fresh `POST /login`, then requests with `fresh-token` |
| cache afterwards | `first-token` / `DEVICE1` | `fresh-token` / `DEVICE2` |

### Upgrade from a released version (stored-data compatibility, changed plugin selected)

These are real released packages from npm, `openclaw@2026.9.35` (extended-stable) with `@openclaw/matrix@2026.9.35`, run against the same homeserver stand-in with two accounts, `default` and `ops`. The released Gateway logs both accounts in and writes their cached logins. This branch then runs the upgrade steps on the same state:

1. `gateway recover-lock` (the stable Gateway was hard-stopped);
2. `doctor --fix` (schema migration);
3. updates the installed official Matrix plugin to **this branch's release package**: `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack extensions/matrix` builds `@openclaw/matrix-2026.10.7.tgz`, then `plugins install <tgz> --force --accept-capabilities` installs it, as a matching `@openclaw/matrix` release would;
4. `channels remove --account ops --delete`;
5. a Gateway start.

![upgrade run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/186011/proof-186011-upgrade-v2.png)

| | result |
|---|---|
| `doctor --fix` on the 2026.9.35 state | exit 0 (migrated) |
| plugin update to this branch's package | `Installed plugin: matrix` (2026.10.7). `channels.matrix.accounts` is still `default, ops` |
| `channels remove --account ops --delete` | **`ops`: revoked marker**; `default`: its 2026.9.35 login is unchanged |
| Gateway start | `default` **loads and uses the 2026.9.35-written login** (9 requests, 0 new logins); no requests with `ops`'s old token |

Notes:

- The plugin shows `provenance-invalid` only because the archive was built locally and is unsigned.
- Matrix encrypted-state directories are not touched by the hook, which only writes the credentials row.
- `openclaw@latest` (2026.10.8) could not be used as the upgrade source. It was cut with a newer state schema than current `main` (still 2026.10.7), so a main-based build, with or without this PR, refuses that state ("schema migration pending", "Failed to open the plugin state database"). A 2026.10.8 run did confirm that `@openclaw/matrix@2026.10.8` writes the same cached-credential row format.
- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` fails on the repo-wide test-lines ceiling ("over by: 535; net delta: +8"). This PR adds 8 lines, so the base is already over before it.

prs.title: fix(codex): duplicate final reply after a resumed parent waits for a native child
prs.body:
## Status: blocked on correctness, not ready to merge

[Follow-up investigation and failing owner-boundary regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186128#issuecomment-6458850513). The current head can falsely settle an unconsumed result. Neither turn completion nor proxy-observed provider completion proves native sampling completion. The new local regression reports 28 passed / 1 failed; it simulates the native schedule, not an end-to-end native reproduction. No production repair has been pushed, and the hosted test-line ratchet remains red.

The proposed direction is to expose native sampling completion after resume and consume that signal in the existing receipt owner. The original implementation description and historical evidence below are preserved for review, not a recommendation to merge. In particular, the earlier turn-completion composition advice is superseded by this finding.

---

Related: #156070

## What Problem This Solves

After a Gateway restart, a Codex parent can receive a native child's result through `wait_agent` and answer it. A separate automatic `announce:codex-native:…:succeeded` run then gives the same answer again.

## User Impact

On providers that native Codex treats as OpenAI (OpenAI API key and Codex/ChatGPT login), a resumed conversation that waits for a native child and answers it in a turn that completes normally no longer gets a second automatic answer for that result. In the tested yield/unconsumed scenarios, results the parent did not sample are still delivered automatically. No configuration change or migration is needed.

**Known correctness limitation:** a native compaction-setup failure after a preempted or mailbox-failed request can cause a result to be marked consumed without a completed sampling. The detailed condition is below; this edge has not been reproduced end to end.

Not changed, so an extra reply can still happen (nothing is dropped in these cases):

- **Other provider names.** Native removes the per-item metadata this fix reads unless the provider is named exactly `OpenAI`. That covers OpenClaw's subscription-sharing route and custom Responses providers. Routes that do not use the inference proxy are not covered either.
- **WebSocket incremental requests.** On the covered routes native can use WebSocket `response.create`, which sends only new input. If the parent makes another model request in the same turn after the one that carried the result, that later request no longer carries it and the result stays pending. The end-to-end runs below used HTTP.
- **Uncertain samplings.** The result stays pending if the parent's turn fails or is interrupted, or if a later model request in the turn no longer carries the result. It also stays pending if context compaction or a hook other than `Stop` runs after the request that carried it, or if the foreground owner is released or yields before native reports the turn completed.

"Consumed" here means native completed a parent sampling that carried the result. That is neither a durable native acknowledgement nor channel delivery. Recovering a pending child result across Gateway replacement is not tested.

The native contract below was checked against the managed Codex 0.164.0. Older or newer external app-server overrides were not validated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex streams raw item events only to threads started with `experimentalRawEvents`, and `thread/resume` has no such option. V2 `wait` items carry no receiver status, and after resume the alternative raw envelope events are also absent, so OpenClaw records no receipt and the completion owner delivers the already-consumed result again.

#130503 tried to fix this on the native side by renewing the raw-event opt-in on resume. It was withdrawn to keep completion handling in OpenClaw without a Codex protocol change, and Codex 0.164.0 still has no resume opt-in. This change stays in OpenClaw. #166349 tracks the broader parent-wake and restart semantics; this PR fixes only the duplicate.

The receipt still reaches OpenClaw: native sends the child's `FINAL_ANSWER` envelope as current-turn input in the parent's next model request, which the plugin already authorizes. The parent's receipt tracker holds the receipts carried by the turn's latest ordinary model request, and hands them to the existing tracker when native reports that turn `completed`, unless compaction or a non-`Stop` hook ran in between.

<details><summary>Settlement rules and native contract</summary>

Resumed threads get no per-sampling completion notification (`rawResponse/completed` is a raw event). `thread/tokenUsage/updated` is also emitted after a context-window error, on rate-limit headers and around compaction, so it does not prove that a sampling succeeded. The change therefore uses this evidence:

1. The parent's receipt tracker holds only the receipts carried by the parent turn's **latest** model request. Each later request replaces them. A request that is not an ordinary sampling, such as compaction or review, carries none.
2. Native `contextCompaction` items, and `hook/started` for any hook other than `Stop`, discard what is held for that turn. These are how native can complete a turn without another sampling after a preempted or interrupted stream: a hook that blocks steered input, or a session-start hook after compaction. `Stop` hooks run only after a final sampling completed.
3. When native reports that same turn `completed`, the held receipts go to the existing tracker. This happens behind the existing owner gate (bound, not yielded, not settled) and before the turn observer marks the owner's model execution settled.

Native's contract, as checked in source: a turn is `completed` when no turn-affecting error was recorded. Retries rebuild the prompt from the current recorded history. Same-turn preemption can drop a streaming request and continue the turn. Compaction or a token-budget rollover can then remove `FINAL_ANSWER` items before the next sampling. A blocking input hook can also end the loop without another sampling. Capture always precedes forwarding, so it is ordered before the turn's completion.

One native path is not covered: if setting up a mid-turn compaction fails before the compaction task starts, native reports the turn `completed` with neither a `contextCompaction` item nor an error. A result could be marked consumed only if, in the same step, the request carrying it was also preempted or hit a mailbox stream error and a compaction was due. The underlying `completed` status there looks like a native status issue. This remains an unresolved correctness limitation for maintainer consideration, not a demonstrated no-drop guarantee.

Held receipts are foreground-only. They are discarded when an owner releases its turn, when the last owner releases, and when a parent retires or the monitor is disposed. Matching, alias, predecessor/successor and custody state stay in the existing tracker. Fresh threads keep their raw-event receipts unchanged.

Checked in openai/codex rust-v0.164.0:

- `ThreadResumeParams` has no raw-event option. The resumed listener is attached with raw events disabled (`app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs`). `rawResponseItem/completed` and `rawResponse/completed` are dropped for listeners without the opt-in (`app-server/src/request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs`).
- `handle_turn_complete` reports `Failed` only when a turn-affecting error was recorded, otherwise `Completed`; aborts report `Interrupted` (`app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs`).
- Sampling retries rebuild from recorded history. Preemption and mailbox stream errors return a follow-up without `response.completed`. Mid-turn compaction or rollover can run before the next sampling, and a blocking input hook can end the loop (`core/src/session/turn.rs`). Remote compaction excludes `FINAL_ANSWER` items (`core/src/compact_remote_v2.rs`). Compaction tasks emit a `contextCompaction` item (`compact.rs`, `compact_remote_v2*.rs`, `compact_token_budget.rs`).
- Token-count notifications are also emitted after `ContextWindowExceeded`, on rate-limit events and during compaction (`core/src/session/turn.rs`, `compact*.rs`).
- Non-OpenAI providers have `internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough` cleared before the request is sent (`core/src/client.rs`, `model-provider-info/src/lib.rs`).
- Hook notifications are emitted for synchronous, non-built-in hooks (`core/src/hook_runtime.rs`).
</details>

**Composition with #149490** (open; rewrites the same tracker): #149490 holds raw receipts until a later non-compaction `rawResponse/completed`. That is a raw event, so it does not fire on resumed threads. If both land, the input receipts held here should keep settling on `turn/completed` and should not be routed through #149490's "wait for a later response" gate, which never fires after the turn ends. The two changes touch overlapping lines in `native-subagent-delivery-receipts.ts` and the monitor wiring, so whichever lands second needs a manual merge.

## Evidence

[Inspectable original-head terminal results and test boundaries](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186128#issuecomment-6448741684), including the restart/wait case, unconsumed-result control and failing baseline. These are retained runs, not proof of a later repair.

The reproduction and test results below come from the prepared source-build investigation. The publication review inspected the retained logs and exact patch, but did not rerun those tests.

Base `ba1828c8fb5554b752e11cdba0306fa2d1d4c634` (`main`), head `d7ca03a8938a66809aa7334a67daa2c273b7c7d7`; native Codex 0.164.0 from the lockfile. The change was first developed on `89bc6de`; none of its nine files changed between the two bases, and the commit is patch-identical.

**Freshness check (2026-10-27).** Upstream main had advanced to `5cf6a7fd4ebaebb9f1fee12a1d33f2ab291e3f86`; all nine patch-target files have identical Git blob IDs to the tested base `ba1828c8`. This is a source-drift check, not a rerun of tests on that newer main. #156070 remains open; #149490 remains open and unmerged at `9d4bc16a`.

**Real Gateway scenarios** (isolated state, real native app-server with V2 multi-agent, scripted loopback Responses provider over HTTP, synthetic credentials, provider named `OpenAI`). The steps follow the issue: an ordinary turn, then a real Gateway restart. The parent spawns a child, calls `wait_agent` and answers. After an ordinary turn, a fresh request re-tasks the same child and waits again.

| Scenario | Base | This change |
|---|---|---|
| Restart, parent consumes the result via `wait_agent` | **Fails**: the parent answers, then a separate `announce:codex-native:…:succeeded` run answers again (every base run) | Passes: one answer per result, no automatic run, same child reused, session idle |
| Restart, parent yields instead (result never sampled) | — | Result delivered automatically exactly once |
| Restart, terminal provider error on the request carrying the result (turn fails) | — | Result stays pending and is delivered once; one answer |
| Restart, one-shot provider 503 on that request (native retries) | — | One answer, no automatic run |
| Restart, one-shot OpenClaw request-preparation failure on that request | — | One answer, no automatic run |
| No restart (fresh thread) | — | One answer per result, no automatic run |

The first row was rerun on both the base and head above; the second row was rerun on the head only. The other rows ran with the same patch on the earlier base `89bc6de`.

The preemption, compaction and hook-stop paths could not be driven by a scripted provider alone; they are covered by the owner-boundary tests below.

**Tests**

- `native-subagent-monitor.completion-delivery.test.ts` (owning monitor boundary, real tracker and delivery owner):
  - With the production change reverted, 5 cases fail: the duplicate (with and without a following `Stop` hook), both reused-child cases, and the release-lifetime case.
  - Against the previous revision of this change, 4 cases fail: a later request without the result, compaction after it, a non-`Stop` hook after it, and held evidence surviving release.
  - With this change, all 28 pass. The remaining new cases keep failed, interrupted and earlier-turn results pending.
- `inference-routing.test.ts`: only ordinary `/responses` turn input is offered for receipt capture. All 49 pass; with the production change reverted, that case fails.
- `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: 12 s and 11 s wall when warm (46 s and 23 s on a cold transform cache, over 80% transform). Each file runs under 2 s of test time. The 11 new monitor cases total 18 ms, and the 2 routing cases 2 ms.
- `pnpm test:extension codex` (438 files): 5,319 passed, 17 skipped, 2 failed. The 2 failures are in `transport-startup.test.ts` (`ProcessInspectionError`, from the local sandbox's process-inspection permission) and fail identically on base.
- `pnpm check:changed` against the base: 31 of 32 lanes pass, including extension and extension-test typecheck, changed-file lint and format, and the line-cap and other ratchets. The dead-export scan is red with 20 entries that are identical on base, none in the changed files. `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` reports 14 entries, also identical on base and none in the changed files. The monitor shrinks by 2 lines.
- The change does not alter provider request bytes; `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` passes.
- Local review: canonical autoreview was not run in the preparation lane because model-service access was outside that lane's authorization; only its P0–P2 dry run succeeded. No completed canonical-autoreview result is claimed for this submission.
- Actual review evidence: independent Astra and Opus AI source reviews examined the r2 patch/tree on base `89bc6de4583cb2b3fd70a6bb52dd1a5e1db202c9`, supplied head `42a1336656637c2df8829ce3d69ac1af8af665b6`. Both returned **approve-with-changes**, with no P0/P1 findings; required P2 scope disclosures (native version and WebSocket efficacy) are included above. The reviewed patch and final submission have the same stable patch ID, `4a7dea7442e030a81a3aaf94f634c156c9c7b1d6`. A separate native Codex handoff review inspected the exact final patch (`ba1828c8` → `d7ca03a8`) for correctness, ownership and loss paths and found no new actionable P0–P2 production-code finding; a separate evidence review checked retained logs and corrected count/scope wording. Those publishing-lane reviews did not rerun tests. The compaction-setup loss edge remains explicitly unresolved, not waived by these reviews.

Not covered: a real-native run of the preemption, compaction or hook-stop paths; WebSocket transport; external app-server versions other than 0.164.0; a pending child result surviving Gateway replacement; channel delivery. The reporter's `queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming` warning did not appear on the tested `main` snapshots, although the duplicate `announce:codex-native:…:succeeded` run did.

prs.title: feat(ui): clear failed session alerts from the Subagents panel and session hovercard
prs.body:
Related: #185192, #185054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when several child sessions fail or time out, the parent's sidebar row stays red ("Child session X failed: reason") and each failure can only be cleared by opening that child, one at a time; the Subagents panel lists the failures but cannot acknowledge them.

## User Impact

User impact: failure alerts can be cleared in place. In the Subagents panel each unread failure has a **Mark {name} as read** control and the Failed heading has **Mark all as read** (two or more), on desktop and mobile. The session hovercard shows **Dismiss** under a failure, including a child failure folded into its parent row. Acknowledging clears the sidebar alert and hovercard notice on every surface and device, survives reload, and a later failure of the same session alerts again. Panel grouping does not change: failed runs stay listed under Failed, exactly as on main after you open them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already decides whether a failure is still an alert: a failed session alerts until its read time passes its failure time, and opening the session writes that read time. These controls send the same conditional `sessions.patch { unread: false }` (fenced by `expectedSessionId` and `expectedMarkedUnreadAt`), so there is one acknowledgement shared by every surface, tab and device, and no new state, option or API.

- Controls appear only where the viewer can patch the failed session. For a child failure folded into a parent row, the hovercard uses that child's own sharing role and manual-unread marker, so a session-scoped owner gets Dismiss and a manually unread child is acknowledged instead of rejected as stale.
- The alert stays until the Gateway row reports the read. If the Gateway rejects the write, an error toast says so with the Gateway's reason ("Couldn't mark as read. Try again. ..."), and the alert and its control stay, so the same click retries; the next successful acknowledgement replaces that toast with "Marked as read". It is a toast rather than an inline line because the hovercard can close before the reply arrives (session deletion reports its failures the same way).
- Focus: on desktop it moves to the next failure's control, then to the acknowledged row; on mobile it stays on the row. The hovercard keeps its existing focus restoration.
- Known limits: the acknowledgement is fenced to the session, not a run, so a newer failure that lands between render and click is acknowledged too (opening the session behaves the same today). While the parent conversation is open, main's existing hidden-run read for subagents can acknowledge a child whose retry fails immediately; this PR does not change that path.

## Decision for the area owner

The open question is only whether the Subagents panel and the session hovercard should offer these acknowledgement controls (per row, Mark all as read for two or more, Dismiss in the hovercard). They add no state, option, setting or API: each control sends the same conditional read receipt the Control UI already sends when you open a failed session, so the Gateway stays the single owner of "is this failure still an alert", grouping stays by run outcome exactly as on main, and declining the direction means simply not merging. Approving it on this PR is enough; nothing else depends on it.

#185054 (open, another contributor) makes the same choice for the composer failure cards that #185192 has since removed from main; this PR covers the surfaces that remain.

<details><summary>Surface inventory</summary>

| Surface | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel, desktop Failed group | Lists failures, no acknowledgement | Per-row Mark as read, Mark all as read (2+); rows stay in Failed |
| Subagents panel, mobile Finished list | Failed rows with red indicator, no acknowledgement | Same controls; rows keep their Failed indicator |
| Sidebar row failure indicator (own or folded child) | Own failure via row menu Mark as read; folded child only by opening it | Cleared by any acknowledgement of the failed session |
| Session hovercard failure section | No action | Dismiss, acknowledging the failing child when folded |
| Background session toast, sidebar issues inbox, chat details tally, native roster | Unchanged | Unchanged (transient, no session failures, or counts only) |

</details>

<details><summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `isUnacknowledgedSessionFailure` (`ui/src/lib/session-attention.ts`) is the single failure-alert rule; `sessionRowAttention` and the chat pane's read acknowledgement use it instead of two copies.
- Error attention carries the failed session's `sourceSessionId`, `sourceMarkedUnreadAt` and `sourceSharingRole`, so the hovercard targets the failed session with its own fence and role.
- `canDismissSessionFailure` / `dismissSessionFailures` (`ui/src/lib/sessions/session-failure-dismissal.ts`) own the access check, the conditional write and its rejection feedback (the shared `showToast` owner with `severity: "error"`).
- The hovercard error section moved to `session-hovercard-error.tsx` to keep `session-hovercard-solid.tsx` under the file line cap.
- New copy: `chat.subagentsPanel.markFailureRead` ("Mark {name} as read") and `chat.subagentsPanel.markAllFailuresRead` ("Mark all as read"). `sessionsView.markFailureReadFailed` ("Couldn't mark as read. Try again. {error}") and `sessionsView.markFailureReadDone` ("Marked as read"). The hovercard reuses `common.dismiss`.

</details>

## Evidence

### Real Gateway, real failed subagents (Chromium 156 and WebKit 27.2)

An isolated Gateway built from this branch (`dist/` plus `dist/control-ui`, served bundle hash checked against the build) on loopback with a synthetic config. A parent turn spawns four real subagents through `sessions_spawn`; only the loopback model provider is scripted, and it rejects every child request with HTTP 400, so each child run fails through the real runtime (`status: "failed"`, `lastRunError: "LLM request rejected: Synthetic provider rejected the request | synthetic_rejection"`). No WebSocket interception; frames are observed passively. Two browser contexts are paired as two devices.

| | Before (main) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel with four real failures | ![main: Failed 4, no controls, parent row red](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-before-panel.png) | ![branch: Mark as read per row and Mark all as read](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-after-panel-controls.png) |

| Same child fails again | | ![device B sidebar alert returns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-refail-sidebar-device-b.png) ![device B panel offers Mark as read again (WebKit)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/rg-refail-panel-device-b-webkit.png) |

Sequence asserted in both browsers (all pass):

1. Main build: Failed 4, zero acknowledgement controls in the panel and hovercard, still 4 after reload.
2. Branch build: the hovercard on the parent row names one failed child. That child is also marked unread by hand (`sessions.patch { unread: true }`); Dismiss then sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt` equal to its marker and the Gateway advances `lastReadAt`.
3. Mark as read on one row, then Mark all as read on the remaining two: controls go, all four rows stay in Failed, the parent row's red indicator clears.
4. Reload: still acknowledged. A second paired device: no controls, no red row.
5. The operator asks the parent to retry one child; the parent's real `sessions_send` runs it again and it fails again. Both devices show the red parent row with "Child session ... failed" and that one row's Mark as read control.

| Child | Sent | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| folded child, manually unread | `{ unread: false, expectedSessionId, expectedMarkedUnreadAt: <its marker> }` | ok, `lastReadAt` set |
| row control | `{ unread: false, expectedSessionId, expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null }` | ok, `lastReadAt` set |
| Mark all as read (2) | same shape, one per child | ok, `lastReadAt` set |

Real-seam red for the hovercard fence: the same harness against the previous head of this PR sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null` for the manually unread child; the Gateway answers ok with the entry unchanged (no `lastReadAt`) and the alert stays.

### Rejected acknowledgement and retry (mocked Gateway, Playwright Chromium and WebKit 27.2)

The mock Gateway holds the first `sessions.patch` and answers it with `UNAVAILABLE: Session store unavailable`; the second click goes through. Asserted in both engines: the error toast text, the alert and control still present and enabled, a second `sessions.patch` on the same control, the alert cleared, and the error toast replaced by "Marked as read".

| | Rejected | Retried |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subagents panel (WebKit) | ![error toast, Mark as read control still on the failed row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/webkit-panel-mark-read-rejected.png) | ![Marked as read toast, control gone, row still in Failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2d5dcf1e9bfb8adfbd5b5b3065fdff84142fbcf1/dismiss-failed-alerts-r3/webkit-panel-mark-read-retried.png) |

A rejection was not forced on the real Gateway: the session store would have to be broken under a running Gateway, or the row changed between render and click, which races the live row update. The retry sends the same request as the real-Gateway acknowledgements above.

### Mobile (mocked Gateway, 390px)

![mobile before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/mobile-before.png) ![mobile after marking one read: control gone, Failed indicator kept](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/5ce409da568ada2cbacc658d577aa36032e2c9a7/dismiss-failed-alerts-r2/mobile-after-one-read.png)

### Tests (macOS arm64)

Red = the new tests on the previous head's production code; green = this branch.

- `ui/src/components/session-progress-hovercard-target.test.ts`, new: Dismiss on a folded child failure under `operator.sessions.write` sends that child's `expectedMarkedUnreadAt` and `expectedSessionId`. Red: Dismiss is absent (child role dropped); with broad `operator.write` it sends `expectedMarkedUnreadAt: null`. Green: pass.
- `ui/src/lib/session-attention.test.ts`: failure stays an alert until read and alerts again later; error attention carries the source session id, marker and role. Red: source facts missing. Green: pass.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-subagents-panel.test.ts`, 2 cases: desktop controls only on unread failures the viewer can patch, exact conditional params, rows stay in Failed, focus to the next control then to the row; mobile acknowledged in place with its Failed indicator and focus on the row. Red: fail. Green: pass.

Red on the previous head: 3 fail (no toast; the rejection was swallowed). Green: pass.

prs.title: test(perf): add real-Gateway flaky network proof for Control UI recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reconnect and offline changes to the Control UI have no real-Gateway regression check for airplane-grade links. The rig that measured openclaw/openclaw#186325, openclaw/openclaw#186342 and openclaw/openclaw#186316 lived only in an ignored scratch folder.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Maintainers can run one opt-in command that starts an isolated Gateway behind a simulated airplane link and reports pass/fail for the key recovery behaviors. It is not part of CI.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/perf/flaky-network-proof.ts` reuses the warm-reload proof owners: the synthetic Team-shaped fixture, the QA Lab mock provider, and the signed-in trusted-proxy admission. A new TCP fault proxy (`flaky-network-proxy.ts`) becomes the browser-visible origin and shapes the byte stream: 700 ms RTT, jitter, 190/50 KB/s, silent blackholes with permanently dead NAT flows, and refused/reset connections. That means HTTP, service-worker fetches and WebSockets all share one link.

`startWarmReloadAdmission` gains an optional `publicPort` instead of being forked. The free proof-port helper moves from `warm-reload-proof.ts` into the admission module, so both tools share one copy (a pure move; warm-reload behavior is unchanged). Ports stay in 19600–19699 and state stays under `.local/`.

Three scenarios carry explicit thresholds, set between the base and fixed values measured for openclaw/openclaw#186325:

- `blackout`: a 45 s silent blackout with a send into the still-open socket. A hung opening attempt must exist at restore (precondition). Send → visible connection status ≤ 22 s; restore → first `hello-ok` ≤ 10 s; the message lands exactly once in the Gateway transcript and on screen.
- `offline-reload`: reload with every connection refused. Cached transcript ≤ 3 s; visible connection status ≤ 10 s; the composer keeps the cached agent name; restore → `hello-ok` ≤ 10 s.
- `queue-reload`: a send queued offline survives an offline reload and is delivered exactly once.

Restore ends at a post-restore handshake rather than the phase flag, and delivery is read from the Gateway's `chat.history`, not the optimistic bubble. Both rules came from runs where the phase flag or the bubble alone would have produced a false pass (details below). A failed threshold is `fail`; `invalid` is reserved for a pass whose precondition did not hold. The tool writes `events.json`, `timeline.txt` and `summary.json`, and stops its browser, proxies, mock provider and Gateway, with a listening-port backstop for the detached Gateway re-exec.

## Evidence

All runs are on this Mac with `dist` built from `bf6a97a1761e` and synthetic data only.

| Run | blackout | offline-reload | queue-reload |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main, final code | pass: send→status 15.3 s, restore→hello 7.2 s, 1 copy | **fail**: no cached rows or status for 15 s (see below); restore 3.9 s | pass: restore 2.4 s, 1 copy |
| main, earlier full run (45 s) | pass: 15.1 s, 7.5 s | pass: rows + status 0.35 s, restore 3.7 s | pass: 2.9 s |
| main, 30 s blackout | pass: 15.6 s, 3.4 s | pass: 0.35 s, restore 3.5 s | pass: 3.1 s |
| UI with openclaw/openclaw#186325 reverted, same Gateway | **fail**: send→status 29.8 s, restore→hello 22.1 s | not rerun | not rerun |

So the rig goes red when the #186325 fix is removed and is green on main in most runs. Two blackout-only reruns on main gave 7.4 s / 7.3 s, but one of them lost the message (below).

Developing the rig surfaced three intermittent behaviors on current main. They are reported as follow-ups and are not changed here:

1. **Silent send loss** (1 of 5 blackout runs): a message sent into the dead socket showed "1 queued" while reconnecting. After the reconnect it was neither queued nor delivered, and it is absent from the agent database. This is why delivery is read from the Gateway transcript: a DOM queue check had passed in that run.
2. **Offline reload without the cached transcript** (1 of 4): after the blackout scenario, an offline reload showed only skeletons with no connection status for 15 s.
3. **Health-probe replacement after longer blackouts**: at 45 s, the hung opening attempt ended at its own 30 s timeout (≈7.4 s to reconnect), not by `/healthz` replacement (≈3.4 s at 30 s). The proxy's flow labels show several NAT-dead idle keep-alive sockets at restore, which the 1.5 s probe likely lands on. This is unverified.

Checks: `tsconfig.scripts.json` typecheck, oxlint on touched files, format check, `check:script-erasability`, and `git diff --check` all pass. `deadcode:unused-files` is red only on pre-existing unrelated `scripts/perf` entries; the new entry is registered and does not appear. An independent review is clean through P2. No tests were added: the tool is opt-in, and its behavior proof is the real-Gateway runs above (green on main, red on the reverted base).

Simplification: dropped scratch scenarios without a threshold (cold/warm/stall/flap/switch), the unused `stall` fault, and the separate summarizer. The admission is extended rather than copied, and the free-port helper now has one owner. The change is +1051/−49, about 880 lines of tooling plus a 112-line guide. That is comparable to the scratch rig it replaces; no smaller stage would still prove the airplane metrics.
