prs.title: feat(control-ui): show where to edit read-only Gateway configuration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway administrators currently have to attempt a config edit to discover that the Gateway treats its configuration as read-only.

## User Impact

The Control UI shows **Gateway configuration is read-only** and tells administrators where to make changes. A deployment can supply its own instructions and a documentation link with `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY_NOTICE`. [Paired OCE change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/3981)

## Why This Change Was Made

The serving Gateway reports the same policy its config writer enforces, including Nix mode. The banner uses generic guidance by default. Custom guidance comes from the Gateway's startup environment and only appears while the active connection points to that read-only Gateway.

## Evidence

| Before, read-only Gateway | After, same settings with default guidance |
| --- | --- |
| ![Settings before the change, with no indication that the Gateway configuration is read-only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57d264e1-6b6a-4e76-8d46-75ed474709a7) | ![Settings with the generic read-only banner above the page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9124e21e-5e10-4f28-bdbe-49d1019c87b6) |

**After, with deployment-supplied guidance**

![Settings with the OCE draft and deploy instructions and a Learn more link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62f2ab1f-7c1c-4f07-9cdc-2168deb4b942)

<details>
<summary>Mobile view and verification</summary>

![The same OCE guidance on a mobile viewport](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86b42a61-85ba-4691-97ae-aca5fd749f50)

Chromium opened Settings on three real OpenClaw 2026.10.8 Gateways. The default notice appeared on a read-only Gateway. With the OCE message, **Learn more** requested the [published guide](https://docs-enterprise.openclaw.org/reference/agents/gateway-managed-mode/). The browser intercepted the response. A writable Gateway given the same message and terminal/job restrictions hid the notice. The mobile banner fits a 390 px viewport and the desktop banner clears the collapsed sidebar.

The before capture used `60b52d9`. The refreshed captures use the production UI sources at `4f6840f` and the Gateway built at `e5de95e`, which has the same bootstrap implementation. The local UI build used the rc.18 Solid JS wrapper with the rc.16 native compiler. The paired OCE change covers the handoff from an OCE deployment to the Gateway.

**Service installation and upgrade.** On Debian systemd, a fresh install passed the notice to the running Gateway. We also upgraded the published 2026.10.8 CLI (`dc2523e`) to `e5de95e`, repaired it with `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, and regenerated the service with the new notice. A second regeneration with both read-only variables omitted preserved the notice, read-only enforcement and an unrelated service setting. Authenticated bootstrap returned the notice and a refused `config.patch` left the config bytes unchanged.

**Regression coverage.** The startup environment inventory adds the one deployment-owned setting. The existing test-line budget accommodates all 64 net lines covering bootstrap policy, serving-Gateway identity, default and custom guidance, and service environment preservation. The 11 Gateway presentation and 20 shell tests passed locally, along with the Gateway TypeScript graph. The [hosted performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40773450584/job/123117219226) passed on the captured UI. Its release build used 308,490 gzip bytes of CSS against the 308,526-byte limit. The subsequent merge of main at `be66c2c` kept the banner implementation and tests identical and retained main’s test-line budget.

**Base comparison.** With just the two new test files overlaid on clean main (`a53e9583`), all 27 existing tests passed. The shell assertion received no banner, and the three new Gateway assertions received no read-only policy fields. All 31 passed on `be66c2c`.

**CI on the reviewed head.** Security, UI performance, budgets, types and the tests for the banner passed. Two browser shards keep the aggregate red. Nine sidebar cases reproduced on clean main, including the missing personal-group heading, the absent empty group and a shortcut intercepting a hover. The widget assertion intermittently received **Ready** after a click expected to produce **Updated**. The same assertion failed in GitHub Actions on October 26, before this change, and passed in isolation on both current heads. [Sidebar and widget job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40775788095/job/123125297967) · [Rail-alignment job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40775788095/job/123125297892) · [Earlier widget failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40259970480/job/121370429808)
</details>

prs.title: fix: unblock scripts lint for cache lock deadlines
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The scripts lint gate rejects the dependency-cache metadata-lock retry deadline, so otherwise unrelated changes that select scripts lint cannot complete validation. The reported conversion is necessary at runtime: the original clock produces BigInt nanoseconds, while `Atomics.wait` consumes a numeric timeout in milliseconds.

## User Impact

This restores validation of the existing PR tooling without changing its cache ownership or lifecycle behavior. Metadata-lock acquisition still uses a one-second monotonic retry budget and waits for at most 10 ms at a time. Namespace checks, initialization, retained crash state, ledger contents, permissions, and cleanup remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lock now uses Node's `performance.now()` clock to express the deadline and remaining budget directly in milliseconds. This removes the need for the conversion that native lint misclassifies, with no rule suppression, type assertion, new timer, or configuration change. The existing persistent-contention test also checks the one-second lower bound alongside its finite upper bound and lock-retention assertions.

## Evidence

The frozen baseline at 79a4b37034ca9dd5f7006405a79660f5d03b295e reproduces `typescript(no-unnecessary-type-conversion)` at the metadata-lock wait through `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --files-json '["scripts/pr-lib/cache-lifetime.mjs"]'`.

The same lint command passes on the candidate. Remote changed-file formatting/lint and the native affected type plan passed. Existing dependency-cache tests passed all 43 cases, including overlapping initialization, real metadata handoff, persistent contention, crashed initialization, replaced ownership, and retained cleanup state. The existing wrapper, operation-lock, and eager-import suites passed 201 tests with three existing capability-dependent skips.

The changed test file took 16.26 seconds in Vitest with one worker (19.40 seconds including its native runner). It reuses the existing contention wait and adds no timer or fixture cost. The independent review is clean, and the initial hosted PR tooling Darwin job passed. The initial hosted run failed the then-current test-line ceiling at 6,310,170 / 6,310,000. The unchanged repair now incorporates accepted main with its 6,311,490 ceiling; source-bound count evidence qualifies the resulting 6,311,470 test lines. Refreshed hosted CI, including the test-line ratchet and PR tooling Darwin job, passed on this head.

prs.title: fix: recognize live PR cache imports in export checks
prs.body:
Fixes #187031

## What Problem This Solves

The export audit reports four PR-wrapper cache helpers as unused even though `scripts/pr` imports and calls them. These false positives fail the scripts and full-tree checks; removing the exports would break the wrapper's dependency preparation.

## User Impact

The audit now recognizes those live consumers while continuing to report genuinely unused exports. PR execution, cache ownership, cleanup safeguards, and the exported helpers keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The wrapper supplies a module path to a Node heredoc and imports named bindings through `process.argv`. The existing dynamic-consumer projection now connects that argument to the import in the same heredoc. Its names come from the live destructuring, so removing a binding, import, path argument, or launch removes the corresponding edge.

The configured-compiler suite covers these cases. Its repeated source-fixture setup is consolidated without removing existing assertions, keeping the test corpus two lines smaller overall.

## Evidence

The unchanged maintained `pnpm deadcode:exports` command ran before and after the fix on Linux with Knip 6.40.0:

| Scan | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 5 | 5 |
| Full tree | 9 | 5 |
| Scripts | 4 | 0 |

Exactly the four cache findings disappear. The unrelated findings are identical, so the aggregate command still exits 1.

The new regression first failed on the missing live bindings while all 27 existing tests passed. With the fix, all 28 tests pass through the configured compiler. The focused run took 43.01 seconds, including 35.16 seconds of existing worker preparation. Selected formatting, lint and type checks passed, as did the maintained test-line ratchet with a net change of −2. The exact-head hosted CI and aggregate gate are green. Independent calibrated review and automated review completed without findings. The maintained unused-file check reports 0 production and 8 full-tree findings, all existing standalone commands addressed separately by #187027.

prs.title: improve(auto-reply): name each failed model in the fallback notice
prs.body:
Related: #187011

## What Problem This Solves

When several fallback candidates fail before one answers, the fallback notice names only the first failure and hides the rest behind "(+N more attempts)".

## User Impact

User impact: the fallback notice names each failed model with its reason, up to three, so users can see which models failed and why without opening logs. A single failed model reads exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw already formats a per-attempt summary (`attemptSummaries`) for the lifecycle `fallback` event. When two or more attempts failed, the visible notice and the persisted reason now use that same formatter, capped at three hops plus the existing "(+N more attempts)" tail. Each model reference gets its own 40-character budget, shortened in the middle, so a long reference (a Bedrock inference-profile ARN runs past 100 characters) cannot push the reason out of the 80-character hop. References of 40 characters or fewer read as before, on the event too. Zero or one failed attempt keeps today's text.

The second and third failed models show the same error preview the first one already shows.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/fallback-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 22 passed. Against unchanged `main`, the 4 new behavior cases fail (names every hop, caps at three, keeps the reason for a long model reference, truncates each long reason) and the 2 regression guards pass (single-attempt notice unchanged, no repeated notice for the same chain).
- The same-chain repetition test stays, though ClawSweeper suggested removing it: it is the only test that pins the persisted multi-hop reason. Persisting only the first attempt's reason while the notice shows the chain (`reason: buildFallbackReasonSummary(params.attempts.slice(0, 1))` in `resolveFallbackTransition`) fails that test alone; the other 21 pass.
- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1`: passed (typecheck core and all 27 core test graphs, lint and format of the changed files, every guard). The dead-export scan, run on its own, reports 7 exports in 4 files this change does not touch (`scripts/pr-lib/cache-lifetime.mjs`, `extensions/knowledge/src/conversation-access-view.ts`, `src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-manifest-comparison.ts`, `src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-cleanup.ts`); this change adds no exports.
- Live, real providers: an isolated Gateway built from `main` and from this branch, the TUI as the client. The chain's first two candidates are the real OpenAI and xAI endpoints given an invalid key (both answer 401), and the third is Claude Haiku through the `claude-cli` backend, which answered. Text-only change, so a terminal capture rather than a screenshot:

  ```text

  branch: ↪️ Model Fallback: claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5 (selected openai-direct/gpt-5-mini; openai-direct/gpt-5-mini auth; xai-direct/grok-4-fast auth)
  ```

- Live, scripted transient failures (a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, since real providers cannot be made to rate-limit on demand): the first candidate returns 429 (retried, then abandoned), the second 402, the third answers:

prs.title: fix(cron): keep a channel chat's origin when its owner edits an automation
prs.body:
## Summary

An automation created from a channel chat on a named (non-default) account is stored as account-scoped, with an external caller origin (`{kind: "external", channel}`). Editing it from the same chat goes through the cron management grant. `withCronManagementGrant` forwarded only `local` origins, so `reconcileCronChannelRequesterAuthority` re-stamped the job's origin as `unknown`. Every later run then failed in ~50 ms with `Scheduled account "<id>" is unavailable`, although the account was still configured and connected.

This change carries the admitted turn's known origin (`local` or `external`) through the management operation, instead of only `local`.

- The origin is still the server-authenticated one from the admitted turn. `unknown` stays unknown.
- `hasCronCreatorGrantProvenance` is not touched, so requester proof is not widened.
- Who may manage a job is unchanged: the grant is still minted only for an admitted owner/admin turn, and the continuation check still runs before the mutation commits.
- The run-time account check still runs against the channel's configured accounts.

Default-account chats lose the origin the same way, but nothing shows because default accounts skip the account check.

Related: #156895, #161735, #162087 (same error string; this PR fixes the "edited from a channel chat" path only, not the pre-9.7 migration gap described in #162087).

## Changes

- `src/gateway/cron-creator-authority-grant.ts`: `withCronManagementGrant` forwards `entry.scope.callerOrigin` whenever it is not `unknown`.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.test.ts`: an owner edits an account-scoped job through management. The persisted origin stays external, and unknown still persists unknown.
  - Base red / head green: with `cron-creator-authority-grant.ts` from main, the external case fails and the unknown case passes. With this PR, both pass.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** an account-scoped automation created from a Telegram chat on a named account stops running after its owner edits it from the same chat (`Scheduled account "proof" is unavailable`). Round 2 also checks the authority boundary and upgrade compatibility, as asked in review.
- **Real environment tested:**
  - Clean Multipass Ubuntu 24.04 VMs, one per round.
  - Baseline: published `openclaw@2026.10.8` (dc2523e5a5c7) from npm.
  - Candidate: this branch, packed and applied to the same install with `openclaw update --tag file:<tgz> --yes`. Gateway state is kept across the update.
    - Round 1 used `cd869e539660`. Round 2 used `d2871aec847d`, the current head; `build-info` commit `d2871aec847d74be587a63cf1ac12a178f60fa53`, tgz sha256 `404d9131…0fe39`.
    - `cd869e53966` is this PR's fix commit before a rebase onto main. `git patch-id --stable` is identical for `cd869e53966` and `495b7f34be0`: `201a07afd1b8…`. `d2871aec847` adds only the test-file change above.
  - The gateway has a real Telegram bot as the named account `proof` (polling, `dmPolicy=allowlist`). The owner is allowed through `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, and the messages come from the owner's Telegram app.
  - The model is `scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs` with scripted `automations` tool calls (`add` / `update`), so the steps are deterministic and no provider key is used.
  - In round 2, a pass-through recorder in front of the Bot API counts Telegram methods per run, recording only the method name and status.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  - **Round 1:** create a job from the owner DM, edit it from the same DM, then `openclaw cron run <id> --wait`, on baseline and then on the candidate.
  - **Round 2,** on a single install whose state carries across the update:
    1. On the baseline, the owner DM creates J1, which is never edited. It then creates J2 and edits it, so J2 becomes `unknown`.
    2. Update to the candidate. Run `cron show` on J1 and J2, then force-run J1 and force-run J2.
    3. The owner DM edits J1 on the candidate, then force-run J1.
    4. **Non-owner caller:** remove the user from `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, keeping the channel `allowFrom` so the DM is still admitted as an ordinary sender. That user then asks to edit J1. Restore the owner.
    5. **Owner revoked mid-edit:** the owner DM asks to edit J1. The mock holds the model's tool-call answer, so the turn is admitted with owner authority but has not reached `cron.update`. While it is held, the owner is removed from `commands.ownerAllowFrom`.
    6. **Account removed:** remove `channels.telegram.accounts.proof`, then force-run J1.
- **Evidence after fix:**

  Round 1, a job edited by its owner:

  | | Baseline 2026.10.8 | Candidate |
  |---|---|---|
  | origin after create | `{kind: external, channel: telegram}` | `{kind: external, channel: telegram}` |
  | origin after owner edit | `{kind: unknown}` | `{kind: external, channel: telegram}` |
  | `cron run` | `status=error`, `Scheduled account "proof" is unavailable. Re-add it to the channel configuration, or recreate this automation from the intended account.`, 0 model calls | `status=ok`, `deliveryStatus=delivered`, 1 model call |

  Round 2, candidate `d2871aec847`:

  | Scenario | Persisted job after | Forced run |
  |---|---|---|
  | J1 created on baseline, carried across the update | loads; origin `external/telegram` | `ok`, `delivered`, 1 model call, 1 `sendMessage` to the owner |
  | J2 created and edited on baseline (already `unknown`), carried across the update | loads; origin `unknown` | `error` `Scheduled account "proof" is unavailable`, 0 model calls, 0 `sendMessage` |
  | Owner edits J1 on the candidate | payload updated; origin stays `external/telegram` | `ok`, `delivered`, 1 model call, 1 `sendMessage` |
  | Non-owner asks to edit J1 | unchanged (same `updatedAt`) | n/a |
  | Owner revoked while the edit turn was held | unchanged (same `updatedAt`) | n/a |
  | Account `proof` removed | n/a | `error` `Scheduled account "proof" is unavailable`, 0 model calls, 0 Bot API calls of any kind |

  The scheduled policy stayed `mode=account`, `ownerAccountId=proof` throughout, with announce delivery through `telegram` on account `proof`.

  Non-owner edit, `automations` tool result returned to the model:
  ```
  automations needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner. Do not retry automations.
  ```

  Owner revoked mid-edit, gateway log (the held turn never reached the tool; the job's `updatedAt` is unchanged):
  ```
  22:46:55 [reload] config change requires channel reload (telegram) — deferring until ... 1 admitted agent run(s) complete
  22:51:55 [reload] channel reload timeout after 300239ms with ... 1 admitted agent run(s) still active; reloading channels anyway
  22:51:55 [reload] config hot reload applied (commands.ownerAllowFrom)
  22:51:55 [telegram] [proof] starting account (reason: config-reload)
  ```

  Round 1: the owner's Telegram chat showed `PROOF_RUN_DELIVERED: scheduled reminder from the proof automation.` after the candidate run, and nothing after the baseline run.
- **Observed result after fix:**
  - An owner's edit from a channel chat keeps the chat's external origin. The edited job then runs on its named account and delivers.
  - Jobs persisted by the published release still load and run after the upgrade.
  - The patch does not widen who can edit: a non-owner sender is refused by the tool and nothing is persisted.
  - An owner revoked while the edit turn is in flight does not get the edit persisted.
  - A job whose named account is removed fails closed before any model or Bot API call.
  - This prevents the loss but does not repair jobs that an older build already re-stamped `unknown` (J2): they keep failing until the automation is recreated.
- **What was not tested:**
  - **Revocation inside `cron.update`'s awaited validation.** Live, the gateway defers the `ownerAllowFrom` channel reload until admitted runs finish, for up to 300 s. Revocation can therefore only land live after that deferral, which is what scenario 5 shows. The narrower window, between admission and the commit inside `cron.update`, is covered by the existing unit tests: `cron-caller-scope.test.ts` (revoked before dispatch, nothing persisted) and `cron-creator-authority-grant.test.ts` (channel owner revoked).
  - Other channels (WhatsApp, Signal, Discord) with named accounts. The code path is channel-agnostic.
  - Edits from the Control UI or the CLI (local origin; behavior unchanged).
  - A real provider model.
  - The pre-9.7 carry-over case from #162087.

## Tests

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/cron-creator-authority-grant.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.test.ts`: 37/37.
- Broad cron and gateway suites: 2510 of 2511 pass. The one failure, `isolated-agent.session-identity.test.ts`, is unrelated to this change: a macOS `/var` vs `/private/var` path difference in the test's temp directory.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint on `src/gateway/`.

prs.title: fix(imessage): report Automation failures after Gateway updates
prs.body:
Related: #178719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Messages Automation send failures leave the iMessage account green, with no recovery guidance, when a Gateway reply uses AppleScript text, attachment delivery, or the auto fallback.

## User Impact

Failed sends report the affected account and Messages Automation recovery steps. A successful send clears that warning; a successful read probe does not. Delivery error identity and classification are preserved.

**Limitations:** This does not preserve TCC grants across upgrades. Signed macOS upgrade testing was not available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary sends and native attachment actions now share the existing account-warning publisher. The RPC-only publication and duplicated RPC error-message augmentation were removed. Successful ordinary and native message completion clear only a matching Automation warning, not unrelated watcher errors. No options, permissions, runtime identities, or automatic resend behavior changed.

## Evidence

**Fault-injected imsg on Linux:** real shipped Gateway, real iMessage plugin, and real process spawn. The executable emits the exact imsg v0.17.0 Automation diagnostic and exits non-zero. This is not real Messages/TCC testing. RED and GREEN used fresh isolated HOME/state/config paths, separate free ports, and identical stand-in/media bytes. The live Gateway was not touched.

Server and client entry points (targets, paths, ports, and hosts redacted):

```sh
pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> gateway run --bind loopback --port <isolated-port>
pnpm --silent openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> gateway call send --port <isolated-port> --expect-url <isolated-url> --params '{"channel":"imessage","accountId":"proof","to":"chat_guid:[redacted]","message":"synthetic Automation proof","idempotencyKey":"[case-key]"}' --timeout 20000 --json
# Attachment case: message="", mediaUrl="<isolated-workspace>/proof.pdf"; sendTransport=applescript.
pnpm --silent openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> gateway call channels.status --port <isolated-port> --expect-url <isolated-url> --params '{"probe":true,"timeoutMs":2000}' --timeout 20000 --json
```

The following are recorded account-status projections from CLI JSON; `probeOk` is the returned probe's `ok` field. Long recovery text is explicitly truncated after the System Settings destination. Full captured responses remain in the proof folders.

Captured recovery guidance (identical on both GREEN paths):

```text
Messages automation failed with AppleScript error -1712. Messages timed out; check for an unresponsive Messages.app or a hidden permission prompt. On the Messages Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation and allow Messages for the process running imsg. For an app-managed background Gateway, check the current Gateway runtime (bun), not Terminal or the previous node/bun runtime. An app update can change this permission identity. After granting access, verify delivery and queued replies before retrying from the Gateway.
```

### RED — f9c2f84b693bcb36759b2bfe89a9bd767bb0cb31

```text
rpc failed send: exit 1
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":"Messages automation failed with AppleScript error -1712. Messages timed out; check for an unresponsive Messages.app or a hidden permission prompt. On the Messages Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation [truncated]"}
rpc successful read probe: exit 0
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":"Messages automation failed with AppleScript error -1712. Messages timed out; check for an unresponsive Messages.app or a hidden permission prompt. On the Messages Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation [truncated]","probeOk":true}
rpc next successful send: exit 0
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null,"statusIssues":[]}

attachment failed send: exit 1
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null,"statusIssues":[]}
attachment successful read probe: exit 0
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null,"probeOk":true,"statusIssues":[]}
attachment next successful send: exit 0
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null,"statusIssues":[]}

```

The baseline preserves the already-working RPC warning; its attachment failure reproduces the green/no-warning defect.

### GREEN — 3d0c4db063e0201fa9c4634faae2ae45017d74ad

```text
rpc failed send: exit 1
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":"Messages automation failed with AppleScript error -1712. Messages timed out; check for an unresponsive Messages.app or a hidden permission prompt. On the Messages Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation [truncated]"}
rpc successful read probe: exit 0
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":"Messages automation failed with AppleScript error -1712. Messages timed out; check for an unresponsive Messages.app or a hidden permission prompt. On the Messages Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation [truncated]","probeOk":true}
rpc next successful send: exit 0
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null,"statusIssues":[]}

attachment failed send: exit 1
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":"Messages automation failed with AppleScript error -1712. Messages timed out; check for an unresponsive Messages.app or a hidden permission prompt. On the Messages Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation [truncated]"}
attachment successful read probe: exit 0
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":"Messages automation failed with AppleScript error -1712. Messages timed out; check for an unresponsive Messages.app or a hidden permission prompt. On the Messages Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation [truncated]","probeOk":true}
attachment next successful send: exit 0
{"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null,"statusIssues":[]}

```

### Successful-send control

```text
RED control before: {"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null,"statusIssues":[]}
RED control send: exit 0
RED control after: {"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null,"statusIssues":[]}
GREEN control before: {"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null,"statusIssues":[]}
GREEN control send: exit 0
GREEN control after: {"accountId":"proof","running":true,"connected":true,"lastError":null,"statusIssues":[]}
```

Both heads returned these same failure classifications:

```json
{
  "rpc": {
    "exit": 1,
    "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
    "deliveryCode": "OUTBOUND_DELIVERY_QUEUED",
    "retryable": false,
    "nativeDisposition": "not_started",
    "nativeRetrySafe": true
  },
  "attachment": {
    "exit": 1,
    "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
    "deliveryCode": "OUTBOUND_DELIVERY_QUEUED",
    "retryable": false,
    "nativeDisposition": null,
    "nativeRetrySafe": null
  }
}
```

### Tests and gates

- Real-CLI regression RED on `f9c2f84`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "reports .* Automation errors"` — **2 failed / 36 skipped**, both on the absent account-warning patch. Exact baseline production blobs were replayed with the committed regression; candidate bytes were restored and hash-verified. Both cases retained the original Error class/text before the warning assertion.
- Regression GREEN: the same `send.test.ts` suite without the name filter — **38 passed**, including applescript and auto local attachment subprocesses, normalized account ID `work`, unchanged CLI rejection, exact native arguments, and no RPC fallback; 83.60 s Vitest wall time.
- `pnpm test:extension imessage --maxWorkers=1` — **823 passed in 59 files**, 305.52 s Vitest wall time. The final assertion/cleanup refinements were then covered by the 38-test send-suite rerun above.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .openclaw/tmp/tsconfig.imessage.json --incremental` — passed. The scoped config extends `extensions/tsconfig.json` and includes all iMessage production/test/support files and canonical ambient declarations.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json <7 changed TypeScript files>` and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check <same files>` — passed.
- `node scripts/lib/plugin-npm-runtime-build.mjs extensions/imessage` — **13 runtime entries built**, passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base a0a998b8 --no-merge-base` — passed: 6,285,650 test lines, ceiling 6,285,000, **net delta 0**. Existing ceiling pressure is 650 lines; this PR no longer adds to it. No ceiling/baseline changes.
- `git diff --check a0a998b8f4748489e041e14f95917b1f46e94b64 HEAD` — passed.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the whole PR diff — **no findings**. The reviewer inspected source and evidence; it did not independently execute the tests.
- Earlier `d30362d` CI failed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: 6,286,277 / ceiling 6,285,587, including 570 lines of base pressure plus this PR's +120. The consolidation above repairs the PR growth instead of raising the ceiling. Final-head CI results are separate from these local gates.

Production delta **+107/-7**; test delta **+53/-53**; documentation **+11/-0**, against `a0a998b8`. The shared account-warning publisher replaces RPC-only publication and duplicate RPC message decoration. Added mock-Gateway scaffolding was removed in favor of shipped-Gateway proof; the existing real-CLI rejection regression now covers both transports. Original boundary assertions remain or are strengthened to exactly-once-with-arguments assertions.

Proof captures: `.openclaw/tmp/p178719/red/` and `.openclaw/tmp/p178719/green-final/`; raw CLI responses are in each `capture/`, with `observations.json`, `binding.json`, and cleanup receipts. Config/state credentials are not published.

**Merge risk:** account-status reporting only; delivery and retry classifications remain unchanged. The proof boundary is fault-injected imsg, not macOS permission continuity.

Contributor credit: @anmol0b.

prs.title: fix(macos): iMessage replies stop after app updates until Automation is re-granted
prs.body:
Closes #178719

Related: #186117 reports Automation failures on the iMessage account; this PR keeps the grant across app updates.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: outbound iMessage stops after an OpenClaw.app update when the Gateway runs as the app-managed background service. Every send fails with AppleScript -1712 until Messages Automation is granted again by hand, while `channels status` stays green.

## User Impact

The Messages Automation grant given to the background Gateway carries over to later app updates. The first move onto the new path (including Node to Bun) still needs one approval, and when Automation is missing the send error now says which grant and which process to check instead of a bare AppleScript code.

## Why This Change Was Made

`BundledRuntime` keeps owning the runtime layout. App-managed services now pin `<state>/runtime/service/bun`, a clone of the selected build's Bun; the package and SQLite library still load from the concrete build. `matchesBundledRuntime` accepts the stable path only when it is byte-identical to that build's Bun, so the "one matching build" rule from #161709 holds.

- Installs stage the clone with an atomic rename. After a failed install the staged Bun follows the installed service: it stays when the service now runs this build, the previous clone comes back otherwise, and a first clone is never deleted.
- Runtime collection also checks the arguments of a process running the stable Bun, so it never removes a build that process still loads.
- Restoration keeps the retained executable: hosting-change recovery resolves the build from its package entrypoint, and installed-service custody binds the expected command and runtime pin to the executable the service actually runs.
- A paused service updated by the app keeps the stable Bun in its resume command, and Resume stages the new build there first. Operator-pinned runtimes keep their own path.
- iMessage: AppleScript -1712 and -1743 send failures now append guidance naming the Automation grant, the local Gateway runtime path (or the SSH host for remote Messages), and the one-time re-grant after a runtime move. Other errors and `bridge_v2` failures are unchanged.

<details><summary>Root cause</summary>

`installArguments` passed `--runtime-path runtime.bun.path` (`<state>/runtime/<buildId>/bin/bun`), and each app update reinstalled the service onto the new build's path. tccd attributes the Gateway's Apple events to that path (`responsible_path=…/runtime/<buildId>/bin/bun` in the report), so each update created a new TCC client. A `runtime/current` symlink does not help: the kernel records the resolved path (see Evidence).

</details>

## Evidence

### macOS keeps the Automation grant on the path

Bun copies on macOS 27.0.1, signed with a test certificate (hardened runtime, production Bun entitlements; certificate removed afterwards) or ad hoc. A LaunchAgent runs `<profile>/runtime/service/bun probe.js`; the probe asks Messages for `count of accounts`, an Apple event that needs Automation and sends nothing.

- Step 1: Bun A on the stable path prompts once; allowed.
- Step 2: Bun B (different bytes, same signing requirement) renamed over the same path: no prompt, still allowed.
- Step 3: Bun B re-signed ad hoc (new identifier and cdhash) at the same path: no prompt, still allowed.
- Step 4: the step 2 binary, unchanged, at a second profile's path: tccd prompts again and creates a new grant with `identifier_type=Path`.
- Step 5: an ad-hoc Bun on a third profile's never-granted path: prompt, Don't Allow, the Apple event fails with -1743 and Messages never answers.
- Step 6: a different ad-hoc Bun renamed over that denied path: no prompt, still -1743.

So the decision is keyed by the executable path, in both directions: moving the same signed binary to a new path costs a new approval, which is what every update did before this PR, and replacing the binary at a fixed path keeps whatever the user decided there, Allow or Don't Allow. A stable path does not let a new build inherit a grant the user refused.

I tried a packaged paused-update run at `6fc72514bc9` → `e9d4d67c89d` and it did not complete: pausing build 1 removed the LaunchAgent and recorded a resume command on `runtime/service/bun` with build 1's package, but I set the pause through the profile's preference instead of the menu, build 2 never ran its post-update step, and after unpausing build 2 stayed idle without starting a Gateway. I could not tell whether that comes from the emulated pause or the app, so this PR claims only the unit-level proof for paused updates.

### Tests (red on the broken behavior, green with the fix)

| Behavior | Without the fix | With the fix |
|---|---|---|
| New installs pin `runtime/service/bun` | fails, 2 issues at `GatewayServiceRuntimeTests.swift:100` with the old `--runtime-path` line restored | passes |
| A failed first install keeps the published service's Bun | fails, 3 issues at `BundledRuntimeTests.swift:568,571,572` with the old delete-on-failure cleanup | passes |
| Paused update then Resume stays on the stable Bun | fails, 3 issues at `GatewayProcessManagerTests.swift:993,995,996` (resume prefix, `--runtime-path`, staged Bun) | passes, including the operator-runtime case |
| Restored service pin matches its own executable | the previous head rejected a restored per-build service's own pin (its test asserted that) | accepts the matching executable on either path; mismatches, operator paths and non-Bun pins rejected |
| Collection keeps a build a stable-path process still loads | new path | passes against a real running process |
| iMessage -1712/-1743 errors carry Automation guidance | with the guidance call removed, the -1712 and -1743 rows fail and the unrelated AppleScript row passes | `client.test.ts` passes 22/22; `bridge_v2` stalls get no Automation guidance |

<details><summary>Red/green: install-argument regression test</summary>

```
## RED: fix line reverted (installArguments pins runtime.bun.path)
✔ Test "missing pin exception still rejects conflicting recorded intent" passed
✘ Test "fresh and replacement installs pin the selected bundled runtime" recorded an issue at GatewayServiceRuntimeTests.swift:100:13: Expectation failed: arguments == expected
✘ Test "fresh and replacement installs pin the selected bundled runtime" recorded an issue at GatewayServiceRuntimeTests.swift:100:13: Expectation failed: arguments == expected
✔ Test "service Bun keeps one real path across builds and restores it after a failed install" passed
✔ Test "healthy collection retains a build a stable service Bun still runs" passed
✘ Test run with 4 tests in 3 suites failed with 2 issues.

## GREEN: fix restored
✔ Test "fresh and replacement installs pin the selected bundled runtime" passed
✔ Test "missing pin exception still rejects conflicting recorded intent" passed
✔ Test "service Bun keeps one real path across builds and restores it after a failed install" passed
✔ Test "healthy collection retains a build a stable service Bun still runs" passed
✔ Test run with 4 tests in 3 suites passed.
```

</details>

### Checks on head `e76bcc919e3`

- PR CI on this head: 60 checks pass, none fail (type, lint and test shards included).
- Since `e9d4d67c89d`, the only changes are the `serviceBun` doc comment and `docs/platforms/mac/bundled-gateway.md`.
- iMessage: `client.test.ts` passes 22/22 locally at `e9d4d67c89d`; `extensions/imessage` has no changes since.
- Swift focused tests: 5 tests in 4 suites pass (6 cases), run at `ba63f8265ff`; since then `apps/macos` has changed only in the `serviceBun` doc comment.
- Affected native suites (185 tests, 7 suites, default and named profile, isolated HOME/state): the same environment failures as on `upstream/main`. Two named-profile tests swap between runs; each passes 3/3 when run alone, so they are order-dependent, not regressions.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`: 0 files need formatting. `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: one violation, `DashboardManager.swift` file_length, unchanged from `upstream/main`.
- Test-line ratchet: within main's ceiling, baseline file unchanged.
- `git diff --check` clean.

### Not shown

- A real iMessage send across an app update. The probe above uses a read-only Apple event to the same Automation target, so nothing is sent.
- Revoking an existing grant. The System Settings Automation toggle for a bare `bun` client reverted on this Mac and `tccutil reset AppleEvents <path>` only accepts bundle IDs, so the only revocation is resetting Automation for every app. Steps 5–6 show the same path-keyed record enforcing a Don't Allow decision across a binary swap.

An ad-hoc Bun granted at the stable path read `chat.db`; a different ad-hoc Bun renamed over it got `EPERM` while System Settings still showed `bun` enabled. Access did not come back in that session after restoring the original bytes or re-adding a signed Bun (the test certificate had already been removed from the keychain, which may explain the last part). prs.title: fix(update): give platform-correct stop guidance and do not block when the Gateway is verifiably stopped
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An already-current npm update could require a Gateway stop when native service inspection was unavailable, despite replacing no core files. It could also reject the installed runtime against the unused registry artifact's older schema limits. The reported Linux refusal named Windows Task Scheduler.

Refs #186995. Thanks @BFG508 for the report.

## User Impact

Same-version registry updates can complete while a foreground Gateway keeps serving. Replacement failures name systemd user/system units on Linux, launchd on macOS, or Task Scheduler on Windows and include `openclaw gateway status --deep --json` as the next diagnostic command.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing target classifier already identifies registry no-ops. Carry that fact through service/schema admission and already-current finalization, so replacement-only shutdown and registry-schema checks apply when core files will actually change. Explicit artifacts and installation rebinding retain their replacement checks. Native inspection continues to own its fallback routes and specific failure reasons; canonical Gateway lock inspection already admits stopped Gateways and protects live or unverifiable owners.

Production: +22/−4 lines (net +18). Tests: +73/−73 (net 0), extending existing tables and retaining real exports in mock factories. No new options, dependencies, or database schemas.

## Evidence

- Regression on the original base: 9 failures/11 passes in the service suite, including both already-current live-owner cases and platform guidance. The additional schema case failed before its fix (`undefined` admission rather than success).
- Final focused/consumer run: 134 tests across 13 files passed, 3 shards, 164.10 seconds wall time. This includes every direct test consumer and the execution barrel's consumers. No individual test exceeded 30 seconds; compiler preparation took 30.24 seconds.
- Core and CLI-update test `tsgo`, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge (0 cycles) passed. Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Codex autoreview of the working diff against `0661e52a19d166bec1ef3956844fd230e5d5a8f5`, with target classification, publication, and schema context: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The final test parameter's optional type annotation was then checked by typecheck and lint. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its runner checkout contained unrelated edits; the ready PR's hosted review is requested.

Live proof used the local-container provider (`upd-l1948-live`, removed after use), Node 24.22.1 on Linux arm64, an isolated built npm-layout package fixture, isolated HOME/state, and port 18998. Dependencies came from a frozen pnpm install in that container; no remote lease was used. Commands through the built package CLI:

```text
openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured --auth none --bind loopback --port 18998
openclaw gateway status --deep --json
openclaw update --json --yes --no-restart --tag 2026.10.8
```

Native status reported `service-manager-unavailable` while the foreground Gateway owned state and listened on the port. Before the schema fix, the real update refused schema 36 versus registry target 20. Afterward it exited 0 with `status=skipped`, `reason=already-current`, `mode=npm`, and before/after version 2026.10.8. The same Gateway process remained alive, its port remained open, and the package manifest hash stayed unchanged. The task-owned Gateway shut down cleanly afterward. Linux x64 was not exercised.

Reporter follow-up remains necessary to identify the original native inspection failure: Gateway launch method and actual unit/profile, SSH/container context and service account; sanitized `openclaw gateway status --deep --json`; `systemctl --user is-system-running`; availability of `systemctl`/`busctl` and whether `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is set; the stalled check/timeout or permission error; and whether an owner-controlled stop clears the refusal. Confirm the exact update command and whether an artifact override or intentional reinstall/repair was involved. Missing user bus, missing tools/no manager, permission denial, and timeout are distinct existing diagnostics, not a confirmed diagnosis of this report.

prs.title: fix: skip final-tag scans when no marker is present
prs.body:
Closes #186093

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: reasoning-only assistant text and direct sanitizer callers still scan every tag-shaped span, and lowercase each candidate, when no `<final>` marker exists.

## User Impact

User impact: reasoning-only and direct-call text no longer pays for a full final-tag scan while streaming or rendering. Fully marker-free Control UI text already skips through the existing probe; this hardens the shared scanner for the paths that still reach it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`findFinalTagMatches` currently runs `text.matchAll(/<[^<>]*>/g)` before it knows a final marker can exist. A cheap case-insensitive probe now returns early when the marker is absent. All existing parsing, attribute validation, code-region handling, and stripping behavior is unchanged for text that can contain a marker.

This is an owner-level guard for the direct callers that remain after #174833. #174833 added `createTagNameProbe` to the Gateway conditional projectors; it does not remove the shared `findFinalTagMatches` scan used by reasoning-only UI extraction or `stream-rendering.ts`.

## Evidence


### Patched Control UI browser proof

Served the patched Control UI from this head (`da7970`) with the repository's Vite source server and drove the real UI in Playwright WebKit 27.2. The mock Gateway transcript was `<thinking>hidden</thinking>Answer` followed by 2,000 HTML rows; it contained no `<final>` marker.

Temporary instrumentation (not in the diff): a counter in `findFinalTagMatches` plus a wrapper around `String.prototype.matchAll`. Both were removed before the final commit.

| Source | `findFinalTagMatches` calls | `matchAll` calls for `/<[^<>]*>/g` | Rendered body text | `Answer` visible | `hidden` visible |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| base, no probe | 5 | 5 | 48,188 chars | yes | no |
| patched | 5 | **0** | 48,188 chars | yes | no |

Base and patched runs produce the same rendered body (48,188 chars). The patched run reaches the scanner five times but skips candidate enumeration entirely.

```json
{"allMatchAll":5,"finalScanMatchAll":5,"finalTagCalls":5,"bodyLen":48188,"hasAnswer":true,"hasHidden":false}
{"allMatchAll":0,"finalScanMatchAll":0,"finalTagCalls":5,"bodyLen":48188,"hasAnswer":true,"hasHidden":false}
```

No IPs, API keys, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints are present in this synthetic proof.

### Production Control UI build proof

Built `dist/control-ui` from the PR head tree and loaded it in Playwright WebKit 27.2 with a mocked Gateway. Scenario: `<thinking>hidden</thinking>Answer` + 2,000 HTML rows, no `<final>` marker.

Temporary instrumentation (not in the diff): a counter in `findFinalTagMatches` plus a wrapper around `String.prototype.matchAll`. Both were removed before the final commit.

| Build | `findFinalTagMatches` calls | `matchAll` calls for `/<[^<>]*>/g` | Rendered body text | `Answer` visible | `hidden` visible |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| base, no probe | 7 | 7 | 48,117 chars | yes | no |
| patched | 7 | **0** | 48,117 chars | yes | no |

Base and patched runs produce the same rendered body (48,117 chars). The patched production build reaches the scanner seven times but skips candidate enumeration entirely.

![Base production proof](https://github.com/Acache/openclaw/releases/download/proof-186098/proof-production-base.png)
![Patched production proof](https://github.com/Acache/openclaw/releases/download/proof-186098/proof-production-patched.png)

The screenshots contain synthetic `Proof 186098` UI data only; no user data, credentials, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints. The composer model label is a mock fixture value; no real provider or model was called.

- Current Control UI extraction reaches `stripReasoningTagsFromText`, which passes reasoning-only text to the final scanner even without a `<final>` marker.
- Real Safari instrumentation on 2026.10.7 captured the client-side stack `it` → `ct` → `Ge` with `re=/<[^<>]*>/g` on a heavy session.
- A reasoning-only regression asserts `<think>hidden</think>Answer` does not call `matchAll` and still returns `Answer`.
- A combined 100 KB HTML-like text and 20 KB single-tag payload asserts `stripFinalTags` does **not** call `matchAll`.
- Focused `final-tags` + `reasoning-tags` tests: 49 passed.
- Test additions are net-zero under the repository test-lines ratchet.
- The no-marker tests fail on the parent commit because `matchAll` is called, and pass with the probe.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and a targeted `tsc -p` passed for the changed files.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice-only sessions never get the daily session reset
prs.body:
Closes #185942

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `session.reset` set to `daily` (or `idle`), a session used only by voice never resets, so every voice consult re-sends days of old history to the model.

## User Impact

User impact: after the configured reset boundary, voice consults (browser Talk, meetings, voice calls) and new Talk calls start the new conversation, the same as a typed message. Sessions without an automatic reset policy are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Voice consults reused whatever session existed and never ran the reset-freshness check that typed turns run. Before a consult claims its session, it now checks freshness with the shared check (`resolveSessionEntryResetFreshnessAsync`). If the session is stale, the consult rolls it over in place through the same reset lifecycle the agent command uses (`resetSessionEntryLifecycle`): the session id stays the same, the transcript gets a `preserve-tail` reset boundary with reason `daily` or `idle`, and old run metadata and runtime state are cleared.

The rollover runs before the consult's session admission, because rollover cleanup interrupts work bound to the old incarnation. It first applies the existing work-start policy (`resolveSessionWorkStartError`), on the read entry and again on the row it replaces, so archived, restart-tombstoned or provider-paused sessions keep their state and admission still rejects them with the specific reason. Sessions with a locked model selection are skipped, as in the agent command.

All four consult callers (browser Talk, meeting bot, voice-call, FaceTime) share this runtime, so they all get the reset. The reset clears the old incarnation's queued system events and prompt state but keeps queued controller inputs: browser Talk reserves its input before calling the consult runtime and passes that input's signal to the consult, so clearing the mailbox would cancel the very request that triggered the reset (`clearCommittedSessionResetRuntimeState` gains an optional `preserveControllerInputs`; other callers are unchanged). Accepted edge case: any other input already queued when a consult resets the session also continues, into the new conversation. After a day or an idle period without use such a queue is rare, and it holds the user's own requests.

A Talk call also quotes the session's history to the realtime provider and to every consult when it starts, before any consult runs, so a stale session would still replay old context that way. When the reset is due, `readTalkRealtimeInitialItems` now quotes no history; the call's first consult then resets the session in place. The call start itself writes nothing: the Gateway pins the call's session target before the handler reads history, and changing the session there fails `talk.client.create` with "session changed". One read-only check, `resolveDueVoiceSessionReset` (`src/talk/voice-session-reset.ts`), decides for both the call start and the consult. Accepted difference from a typed reset: such a call starts with no quoted history rather than the 6-message continuity tail.

A call that starts before the boundary and keeps running past it holds the history it quoted at start and passes it as every consult's transcript. Consults now take an optional `onSessionReset` callback: when a consult resets the session, the browser Talk and Gateway-relay call owner (`createTalkClientAgentConsultRunner`) clears that snapshot, so the resetting consult and every later one quote none of it. Meeting, voice-call and FaceTime transcripts are live call content and do not use the callback.

Both new consult callbacks (`onSessionReset` above and `assertSourceCurrent` below) belong to the Gateway's own Talk call owner, so the plugin SDK does not expose them: `openclaw/plugin-sdk/realtime-voice` keeps exporting `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` with its existing parameters, and plugins (voice-call, FaceTime, meetings) get the reset with no contract change.

The reset commits under the caller's live authority, not only its cancellation signal: consults accept an owner-held `assertSourceCurrent`, which the Talk call owner builds from its current-call check and the run authority's `assertCurrent()` (operator and device). The reset's final `commitGuard` runs it, so a caller revoked while the consult prepares cannot reset the session; the run's own authority checks still follow.

Because idle expiry now applies to them too, each consult that reuses a session also records `lastInteractionAt`; before, only browser Talk recorded voice activity, so continuous meeting or call use would otherwise have idled out.

## Evidence

- New regressions in `agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts`, with a real session store and the clock pinned to midday:
  - Daily: a voice session started two days ago with one earlier answer in its transcript, `session.reset: { mode: "daily", atHour: 4 }`, then a consult. On `main` the consult's model history still contains the earlier answer (fails). With the fix the history starts fresh, the session id is unchanged and the lifecycle revision is new; a second consult continues that session without resetting again. Control: a session started one minute earlier keeps its history and revision.
  - Blocked: the same stale session, archived. The consult is rejected with "is archived", no run starts and the session is not reset. Fails if the work-start check is removed.
  - Browser reservation: a controller input reserved the way `client-gateway-control.ts` reserves a Talk tool call, its signal passed as the consult's. The consult answers, the input is not aborted and the session is reset. Without `preserveControllerInputs` it rejects with "Session mailbox cleared".
  - Cancelled: the caller aborts while the consult is still preparing. No run starts and the session is not reset; the reset commit checks the caller's signal through `resetSessionEntryLifecycle`'s `commitGuard`. Fails without that guard.
  - Call start (`session-transcript-preview.hydration.test.ts`): a stale session whose first of ten messages holds a code word; a Talk call's starting history is empty and the session's lifecycle revision is unchanged. Control: a same-day session quotes all ten. Fails on `main`.
  - Call crossing the boundary: a caller-supplied transcript of pre-reset history is replaced through `onSessionReset` in the prompt of the consult that resets (`agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts`), and the call owner drops it for the triggering and following consults (`client-gateway-control.agent-consult.test.ts`). Each fails if its half is removed; the owner test fails on `main`.
  - Caller authority: see "Caller-revocation proof" below (real Talk call owner, run authority and device-revocation owner).
  - Idle: `idleMinutes: 5`, a consult every four minutes for twelve minutes keeps the session; the next consult after ten quiet minutes resets it. Fails if consults stop recording `lastInteractionAt`.
- On a Linux bench, on this head: all of `src/gateway/talk`, the Talk consult, session-reset cleanup, session fork, config override, session actor memory, call-start history and prompt-prefix stability suites pass (576 tests) except three `talk.client.create handler` cases in `src/gateway/talk/handlers/index.test.ts` that fail the same way on unchanged `main` d79a7b6c371 (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepareSessionEntryPatch')`); on unchanged `main` the new daily, browser-reservation, idle, call-start, call-snapshot and caller-authority regressions fail.
- Changed-file core test typecheck and `tsconfig.core.json` typecheck clean; oxfmt and oxlint clean on the changed files.
- `pnpm check:changed` on the bench: everything passes except the dead-export scan, which reports three unused exports already present on `main` (`extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-catalog.ts`, `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-archive-types.ts`; this branch does not touch them). The wider `src/talk`, `src/gateway/talk` and auto-reply session suites pass (1,094 tests).
- Test cost (`--maxWorkers=1`, local): `agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts` 16.7 s of test time (23.5 s wall), above the 5 s target because each new reset case runs a consult against a real session store with its transcript and reset boundary, the layer where the defect lives; `client-gateway-control.agent-consult.test.ts` 3.3 s; `session-transcript-preview.hydration.test.ts` 4.4 s. Net test lines: +217 (the new cases share fixtures and tables; no case or assertion dropped from the +315 first version).
- Test-line ceiling raised to 6,303,000: `main` moved to 6,301,952 of its 6,302,000 ceiling while this PR was in CI, and this PR's 217 lines of base-red voice-reset regressions (consolidated from +315) put the tree at 6,302,169, 169 over (CI run 40687369551). Rounded to the next 1,000, as main's own last raise did.
- `server.sessions.patch-expected-identity.test.ts` failed once in an earlier CI run with "state database still has active native borrowers" (session-patch code this branch does not touch) and passed on the next run.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/session.md` now names voice consults for both idle activity and automatic reset.
- Stored data: no new fields or migrations; the rollover writes the existing session row fields and the existing transcript reset boundary.

## Real Gateway runs (upgrade from 2026.10.8, real models)

Bench container per run, `session.reset: { mode: "daily", atHour: 4 }`, agent model `gpt-4.1-mini` through a local forwarder that records request bodies (never headers or keys).

1. Day one on the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.10.8` from npm: a real Gateway and a Control UI dashboard session, five typed turns. The first says "Please remember this code word for later: PELICAN-DAY1"; the other four are fillers, so the session holds more than the 6-message tail a reset keeps.
2. A copy of that state per run, then the tree's `openclaw doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive` (the upgrade step), and a Gateway from the tree with the clock two days ahead.
3. Browser Talk: a real Gateway-controlled call (`talk.client.create` with `gateway-control-v1`, `gpt-realtime-2.1`). Headless Chrome posts the WebRTC offer the way the Control UI does, and its microphone plays a recorded question: "Please ask the OpenClaw agent: what code word did I ask you to remember earlier in this conversation? If there is none, the answer is none." The realtime model calls the agent tool, and the Gateway runs the consult through its reservation path.
4. A call crossing the boundary (from a second day-one recording on 2026.10.8): same call, but the Gateway clock starts at 03:58 the day after day one (session still fresh, so the call quotes the old history at start) and moves to 04:01 once the WebRTC answer is applied, before the question is spoken (it begins after 6 s of silence).
5. Plugin route: one consult through a small proof plugin that calls the plugin SDK's `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent`, the same call voice-call and FaceTime make.

```text
browser Talk call            agent request   code word in request   daily reset   spoken answer
main (d79a7b6c371)           15 messages     yes                    0             "The code word is PELICAN-DAY1."
this PR (main + 83fe843)      7 messages     no                     1             "none"

call started 03:58, asked 04:01   agent request   code word in request   daily reset   spoken answer
main (d79a7b6c371)                15 messages     yes                    0             "The code word is PELICAN-DAY1."
this PR (main + 83fe843)           7 messages     no                     1             "None."

plugin-route consult         agent request   code word in request                 reply
main (d79a7b6c371)           13 messages     yes                                  "... is PELICAN-DAY1."
this PR (main + 83fe843)      9 messages     no                                   "NONE"

Doctor on the 2026.10.8 state: ok on every run; talk.client.create succeeds on the stale session
```

The 6 kept day-one messages in the consult are the same continuity tail a typed message gets after a daily reset (`DEFAULT_REPLAY_MAX_MESSAGES`); the realtime call itself quotes none of them. In the crossing run the agent prompt is stamped 04:01 on both trees, so the consult ran after the boundary; on this PR it resets the session and its prompt no longer carries the history the call quoted at 03:58. The consult after that is covered by the call-owner regression above, not by a live run.

## Caller-revocation proof

`client-permission-parity.test.ts` drives the real Talk call owner (`createTalkClientAgentConsultRunner`), its run authority (`retainTalkClientRunAuthority`) and the Gateway device-revocation owner against a real session store; only inference is stubbed. The consult is paused between its reset-freshness check and the reset write, and the revocation is the real owner event (`invalidateGatewayDeviceRevocation`).

```text
stale session (lifecycle revision "before-reset"), daily reset due     session after    run started   error
allowed caller                                          this PR        reset (new revision)  yes      -
revoked during preparation                              this PR        "before-reset"        no       "Talk caller source authority is no longer active"
revoked during preparation, reset authority guard removed              reset (new revision)  no       "Gateway caller authority is no longer active" (later run check)
revoked during preparation, at the previous head 4df25a8               reset (new revision)  no       (same)
```

Follow-up worth considering: the in-place rollover sequence (clear rotated metadata, new lifecycle revision, reset boundary, runtime cleanup) now appears in both the agent command and the consult runtime; a shared helper could serve both.

prs.title: fix(tlon): unlisted citations stay opaque when auto-discovery is off [AI]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tlon could use the bot ship's authenticated session to fetch a cited post from a channel the operator did not list while auto-discovery was off, then prepend that content to the agent input.

## User Impact

With auto-discovery off, Tlon now expands citations only from channels in `groupChannels`, including channels added through the settings store. Citations to other channels remain opaque references.

With auto-discovery on, citations continue to expand from any channel the bot ship can read, including Notebook and Gallery channels in joined groups. Tlon still listens and replies only in auto-discovered chat channels. Cross-channel citations within this operator-selected scope continue to work.

The owner's verified 1:1 DMs continue to expand citations from any channel the bot ship can read. This exemption does not apply to channel messages or group DMs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Citation resolution now receives a predicate that reads the live channel configuration before constructing or fetching a post path. Explicit-list mode requires the cited channel to be in the watched set; auto-discovery mode permits ship-readable citations because that setting selects joined groups as a whole. The DM path additionally permits the verified 1:1 owner case. Owner authority is rechecked from live settings before each citation read, so reassignment revokes the exemption even while a multi-citation message is being processed.

Sender admission still happens before citation expansion, and approval replay remains unexpanded.

This pull request was prepared with AI assistance.

## Evidence

- Red/green boundary proof:
  - Against base `8014c48bb9f`, the explicit-list table failed because an admitted citation to unlisted `chat/~private/leadership` was fetched.
  - Against previous PR head `3ac509b8f3f`, the auto-discovery regression failed because a Notebook citation made zero authenticated reads.
  - Against previous PR head `9fd3c54b525`, the configuration-transition regression failed because a removed settings-store channel was still fetched from the cumulative watch set.
  - At current head `c5b04d749fd`, the focused command passed all 45 tests in 4 files (41.24 s wall time), including settings-helper coverage.
- Per changed test file with one worker: `cites.test.ts` passed 6 tests in 96.30 s, `index.thread-mentions.test.ts` passed 19 tests in 38.53 s, and `index.club-sender.test.ts` passed 15 tests in 31.29 s. Compiler preparation dominated the first wall time.
- A temporary production-monitor fixture used the real authenticated Urbit client against a synthetic local endpoint. With auto-discovery enabled, Notebook and Gallery citations each made exactly one authenticated post fetch. The test passed in 226 ms (90.96 s wall time including cold compiler preparation); the fixture was deleted after capture.
- The explicit-list production capture remains valid: same-channel and DM-to-listed citations fetched once; channel-to-unlisted, channel-to-Notebook, and non-owner-DM-to-unlisted citations made no post request. The owner-DM exemption fetched once.
- The test-lines ratchet passed locally at 6,310,538 lines against a ceiling of 6,310,560 (22 lines slack), with the PR's test delta consolidated to exactly zero. The branch merged `main` because the named baseline gate exceeded the former ceiling; this PR did not raise the baseline. Line-cap and max-lines ratchets, changed-file formatting, extension production/test typechecks, targeted lint, documentation checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The full Tlon run passed all 261 assertions across 33 files, but Vitest exited 1 after the unchanged `write ECONNRESET` teardown error in `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/channel-ops.transport.test.ts`. This is the same unrelated error reproduced and documented on the prior head.
- Required local agentic review was run. Suggestions to add per-sender or club restrictions were rejected because those are membership hardening outside the operator-selected channel boundary; its documentation wording concern was incorporated. ClawSweeper's later finding that monitoring history retained removed channels was reproduced and fixed by deriving explicit citation scope from live file and settings-store configuration.
- Known gaps: no live Urbit ship was used, and the agent's generated reply was not exercised.
- Accepted edge case: if `session.dmScope` is not per-peer, other DM senders share the session and can see content the owner cited in a DM. The monitor already warns about that configuration.

### Sanitized production-path capture

Cookie values and the loopback port are omitted.

```text
[explicit-list-citation-boundary]
sameChannel.authenticatedFetches=1
dmToListed.authenticatedFetches=1
ownerDmToUnlisted.authenticatedFetches=1
channelToUnlisted.postFetches=0
channelToNotebook.postFetches=0
nonOwnerDmToUnlisted.postFetches=0

[auto-discovery-citation-boundary]
notebook.authenticatedFetches=1
gallery.authenticatedFetches=1
PASS index.citation-transport.test.ts (1 test, 226 ms; 90.96 s wall time including cold compiler preparation)
```

The earlier owner-reassignment fixture also remains valid: the first owner citation fetched once, a settings update reassigned `ownerShip`, the former owner's second citation made no post request, and the dispatched role was `user`.

prs.title: perf(knowledge): Knowledge page header jumps and flickers on first load
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Knowledge page's header, tabs and search box jump around while the page first loads.
- The agent/store row wraps when the tab counts arrive.
- Placeholder text and "Connecting…" flash before the real content appears.
- The tab counts appear one at a time.

## User Impact

The page settles in one step. The header and search box no longer move, the tab counts appear together, and startup is faster. Going back to a tab shows its last results while they refresh. That last part needs #186994 (keeps plugin pages mounted when their params change) to take effect.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Header:** the agent/store row stays on one fixed-height line, shortening text with an ellipsis instead of wrapping. Its placeholder is the same height.
- **Tab counts:** both tabs reserve a count slot. The Scribes count loads with the page total, and both are applied together.
- **Copy:** text that depends on the agent stays hidden, with its space kept, until the agent is known. "Connecting…" shows only when the page is actually offline or a refresh fails.
- **Startup:** store info and status load in parallel when routing can't depend on the store info. Tab counts load alongside the view, and Browse waits only for the type list it needs.
- **Failures:** a failed count never fails the page.
- **Returning to a tab:** the last few views are kept and shown again, dimmed, while they reload. They are cleared when the agent or store changes.

## Evidence

**Layout measurements** on an isolated Gateway built from this branch, sampling element positions every animation frame. Same click sequence, with Knowledge reads answered by synthetic data after 350 ms:

| | tab-row moves | header moves | search-box moves |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before, 1440px | 11 | 7 | 3 |
| After, 1440px | 1 (3px) | 0 | 0 |
| Before, 1180px | 11 | 10 | 4 |
| After, 1180px | 1 | 0 | 0 |

**Tests:**
- New `control-ui.test.ts` covers: parallel startup, the hidden copy, both counts landing together, the kept view on return, a failed vocabulary load not failing the page, and Browse receiving its types before the Scribes count. The first three fail on `main`; the Browse case guards an ordering this PR introduces and failed on its first revision.
- The Scribes view and state tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` and oxlint are clean.

**Review:** an independent review raised two P2 defects, both fixed with regression tests:
- the vocabulary was applied late, so Browse could show "Loading types…";
- a failed vocabulary load flashed an error.

It also raised several P3s, all fixed:
- empty count slots stayed when the page opened offline;
- status could be read for the wrong agent after a default-agent change;
- the Scribes list loaded twice on the Scribes tab;
- kept views could survive an agent switch;
- a long agent name could crowd out the store warning.

**Screenshots** (isolated Gateway at 1180px, captured with this PR and #186994 applied, before the review follow-ups; synthetic data):

Header area during first load, before (left) and after (right):

![Knowledge header during first load, before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc49942a-1984-4ad4-971c-4d1327383f50)

150 ms after returning to Recent, before (placeholders) and after (last view kept while it refreshes):

![Returning to Recent, before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c30c7f9-073f-47d6-b636-dcd50ec3f238)

Full click sequence (open, Browse, Scribes, back to Recent), before:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27b1cde1-f051-46d6-babc-5095986e186d

After:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e64a2fb-2d56-4694-8605-09e26038668a



## Test-line budget

This PR raises `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` to 6,311,700 (same file content in #186993 and #186994, so they merge cleanly in either order).
- `main` at 52e1c75e measured 6,311,485 test lines against a zero-slack ceiling of 6,311,490; the ratchet then rejects any PR that adds test lines.
- These two PRs add 131 net lines of regression coverage (Knowledge 119, plugin-page navigation 12), after compacting both suites (from 176 and 43).
- 6,311,485 + 131 = 6,311,616, plus 84 lines (~0.0013%) so main advancing during exact-head CI does not fail the check again.
- Counting and CI rules are unchanged. I looked for offsets first: memory-core has no skipped, duplicate or dead tests; the only savings are shared-fixture consolidations (~100 lines) unrelated to these changes, so they are left for a separate cleanup.

prs.title: fix(ui): plugin pages remount when they change their own params
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a native plugin page is torn down and mounted again whenever it navigates to new page params (for example, switching its own tabs through `host.navigation.openPage`).

## User Impact

Plugin pages keep their state across their own navigation. Params reach the mounted view through `update()`, so pages no longer replay their whole loading sequence on every tab click. The Knowledge page's tab switches were the visible example (related: #186993).

## Why This Change Was Made

The `/plugin` route keys its match on `p.*` params, and the router outlet replaced the rendered route while the next match was pending. The route now declares a `renderOwnerKey`, the same mechanism the Settings route uses, so the outlet keeps the mounted `PluginPage` while the next plugin location loads. Switching to a different plugin or tab still remounts through `PluginPage`'s own contribution keys. Frame and bundled plugin pages don't read page params, so they are unaffected.

## Evidence

- The existing `native-plugin-navigation` e2e flow now has the native page navigate its own params: it must keep one mount and receive the new params through `update()`. On `main` it fails (the page reports a second mount); here it passes.
- `native-plugin-navigation`, `plugin-tab-slugs` and `native-plugin-ui` e2e suites pass.
- `plugin-page`, `tab-slugs` and `router-outlet` unit tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` and the ui-e2e test typecheck are clean.
- Live check on an isolated Gateway: the Knowledge page element now survives tab clicks. Before this change, every click created a new page.
- An independent review found no P0–P2 issues. Its P3 notes were the intended shared-owner behaviour and a counter that would also reset if the plugin were activated again; neither needs a change.



**Live proof** (isolated Gateway at 1180px, Knowledge page, synthetic data). Before this PR, returning to a Knowledge tab rebuilt the page and showed placeholders; with it (and #186993), the mounted page keeps its last view while it refreshes, 150 ms after the click:

![Returning to Recent, before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c30c7f9-073f-47d6-b636-dcd50ec3f238)

Full click sequence, after:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e64a2fb-2d56-4694-8605-09e26038668a



## Test-line budget

This PR raises `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` to 6,311,700 (same file content in #186993 and #186994, so they merge cleanly in either order).
- `main` at 52e1c75e measured 6,311,485 test lines against a zero-slack ceiling of 6,311,490; the ratchet then rejects any PR that adds test lines.
- These two PRs add 131 net lines of regression coverage (Knowledge 119, plugin-page navigation 12), after compacting both suites (from 176 and 43).
- 6,311,485 + 131 = 6,311,616, plus 84 lines (~0.0013%) so main advancing during exact-head CI does not fail the check again.
- Counting and CI rules are unchanged. I looked for offsets first: memory-core has no skipped, duplicate or dead tests; the only savings are shared-fixture consolidations (~100 lines) unrelated to these changes, so they are left for a separate cleanup.
