prs.title: perf(anthropic): avoid rescanning unchanged inline images
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Anthropic requests repeatedly scan the base64 of unchanged inline images in frozen conversation history. The message projection cache deliberately excludes image-bearing messages to preserve request-wide image budgets, and tool-result conversion also rebuilt each image block before normalization.

## User Impact

Repeated image-bearing Anthropic turns spend less CPU preparing requests. Wire bytes, mutable-input validation, MIME detection/conversion, and per-image/aggregate safety limits are unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve tool-image identity and use the existing weak frozen-plain-data projection helper for the byte-only canonicalization result. Mutable or accessor-bearing inputs are not memoized. Image decoding, MIME policy, conversion retries, and request budgets retain their existing owners and still run per request. The cached fact dies with the source image.

This addresses the image case left outside #186872. Production delta: **13 added / 15 removed, net −2 lines**. The two affected image suites have **net −1 test line** after consolidation; the existing owner benchmark gains an image workload. No shared perf README changes and no baseline allowance, ceiling, or budget is raised. The repaired image-converter mock removes one obsolete baseline entry.

## Evidence

Acceptance, declared in the benchmark header before measurement: identical wire hashes; lower CPU/allocation per request; no controlled material GC regression. Workload: 48 messages, 12 frozen 64 KiB synthetic PNG images split between user messages and tool results, changing tail and max_tokens, observer payload hook. Mac, serial counterbalanced runs. Both final arms use the same sparse source-overlay loader; baseline production files are from `953eba4bbeec`.

Five untraced full-path pairs, 1,000 measured requests per arm after 1,000 warmup requests. Full path includes build, payload hook, serialization, and the contiguous body copy used before fetch. Allocation uses two separate counterbalanced sampling pairs (4 KiB sampling, including collected objects).

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Main-thread CPU/request, mean | 7.172 ms | 4.286 ms | **−40.2%**; every pair improves 37–44% |
| Sampled JS allocation/request, mean | 5,824,151 B | 5,817,573 B | −0.11%; effectively unchanged |
| GC/request, mean | 0.1047 ms | 0.1215 ms | +0.0168 ms; below the 1 ms/op materiality threshold |
| Post-GC heap, mean | 33.07 MiB | 33.04 MiB | unchanged |
| Post-GC RSS, mean | 439.9 MiB | 455.5 MiB | +3.5%, mixed per-pair signs; no memory-saving claim |
| Serialized body | 1,291,170 B | 1,291,170 B | identical SHA-256 |

Wire SHA-256: `2e21ba8c8d4179be63cd8aad96c9718b4db6654e9852898c2719be08157a4131`. All six additional scenario hashes also match: initial history, tool call, tool result, moved cache boundary, hook edit, and hook replacement.

<details>
<summary>Untraced full-path pairs and measurement limits</summary>

Each row represents 1,000 requests. GC totals below include all natural collections; no pauses or windows were removed. GC counts are 142–145 per arm, so no GC tail-percentile claim is made. Major-GC samples are insufficient for an independent major-tail claim.

| Pair | CPU ms/request B→C | GC ms B→C | GC count B→C | Max pause ms B→C | RSS MiB B→C | Host load B→C |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 7.149→4.376 | 97.94→100.77 | 143→143 | 9.09→1.55 | 465.8→436.3 | 16.2→15.1 |
| 2 | 6.907→3.849 | 103.10→117.04 | 143→145 | 1.82→1.62 | 457.4→489.6 | 22.0→23.4 |
| 3 | 6.987→4.371 | 101.89→104.62 | 145→142 | 4.34→4.31 | 443.0→463.3 | 19.7→18.4 |
| 4 | 7.693→4.651 | 101.14→120.79 | 143→143 | 2.24→4.38 | 421.7→454.8 | 16.6→17.5 |
| 5 | 7.123→4.183 | 119.43→164.52 | 143→145 | 1.86→5.57 | 411.6→433.5 | 16.6→17.1 |

Across all five arms, GC by kind (count / total ms / maximum ms): base Scavenge 655 / 460.01 / 9.09, IncrementalMarking 31 / 6.55 / 2.24, MarkSweepCompact 31 / 56.94 / 4.34; candidate Scavenge 654 / 539.79 / 1.79, IncrementalMarking 32 / 4.65 / 0.20, MarkSweepCompact 32 / 63.30 / 5.57.

Earlier build-only runs (five arms, 2,000 requests each) showed CPU 5.714→2.497 ms/request (−56.3%), but higher candidate RSS (~258→315 MiB) despite equal retained heap. Matching the overlay loader did not remove that build-only RSS difference. The full-path comparison above was added to include serialization/body-copy lifetime and is the landing measurement. Allocation-instrumented RSS also behaves differently, so it is not used to gate timing or infer retained-memory savings. No adverse classification or rejection is based on the shorter build-only experiment.

Reproduce with both revisions' two production files in separate sparse source overlays:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/anthropic-request-construction.ts \
  --images --iterations 1000 --baseline-dir /absolute/source-overlay
# Separate allocation pass: add --allocation.
# Canonicalization-focused owner pass: add --mode build --iterations 2000.
```

No live service was touched. No whole-Gateway load campaign was run under the requested duplicate-recomputation fast-path exception; these are owner/request-construction measurements, not a whole-Gateway latency claim.

</details>

Regression: both provider and transport profiles fail on base (six canonicalization calls across two requests instead of four: frozen user/tool images once, mutable image per request), then pass on candidate. Covers frozen user/tool reuse and changed mutable bytes. Existing malformed input, conversion, per-image/aggregate limits, replay/cache behavior, and prefix-stability tests remain green.

Focused validation: **149 tests across six files**, 78.03 s wall time. After test consolidation, **21 tests across the two affected image suites** passed in 10.85 s; the updated media file runs 18 tests in 7.19 s. The revised regression was also rerun on base: both profiles fail with six calls instead of four. Changed-file oxfmt, core/script lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Production files remain byte-identical to the measured candidate.

Initial CI run [40759234972](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40759234972) passed tests, lint, security, and all other checks, but the test-line ratchet failed: the base was already 59 lines over its ceiling and this PR added 50 more. Consolidated the MIME/conversion/size-limit cases and reused fixture setup, preserving coverage while reducing the patch to net −1 test line. The targeted ratchet now passes; **no baseline allowance, ceiling, or budget was raised**. CI [40764598902](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40764598902) subsequently completed on `8ba28f85c6649e2f54b8253dddbbe6c95470a04b`: all selected checks passed except the mock-export ratchet (and its aggregate CI gate). The test-line ratchet passed with net −1. The changed image-converter mock needed real-module export preservation; it now uses `importOriginal` while overriding only the two converters. The owner’s prune command removed exactly its obsolete baseline entry (6553→6552). The affected file’s 18 tests, export ratchet, test-line ratchet, formatting, and lint pass. Independent review of this repair found no actionable P0–P2 issue. Production files remain byte-identical to the measured candidate.

The repair is pushed at `cb618cbfec0a5eccb75d00c83293d5ac04a36ebe` after a clean rebase on current main. Exact-head CI [40772671290](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40772671290) completed successfully. The repository watcher returned **GREEN**, with zero pending checks and ten superseded checks excluded. No job was rerun and no shared CI settings were changed.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), fresh context, P0–P2: **no actionable findings**. Autoreview preflight refused a configured-provider mismatch; no operator configuration was changed. The reviewer received the patch and complete relevant owners/callers, without implementation conversation.

A fresh independent review of the final consolidated patch also found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The hosted Codex review of the preceding head `8ba28f85c6649e2f54b8253dddbbe6c95470a04b` completed without findings. ClawSweeper’s earlier-head test-line finding is addressed by the consolidation above.

prs.title: fix(ios): session drawer downloads the full session list on every session event
prs.body: Closes #167729 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the iOS drawer downloads the full session roster for every session event, even when the event already contains the changed row. ## User Impact User impact: drawer rows stay current while downloading **46.9% less session-roster data** in the real-Gateway simulator run: **476,148 → 252,997 bytes** for the same event sequence. ## Why This Change Was Made Known, identified, active-scope rows use the shared row updater. Missing, deleted, archived, malformed, or stale rows request a coalesced roster refresh. The drawer and shared sidebar queries use the same refresh coordinator. Known child lifecycle and subagent-status events still request a coalesced authoritative refresh: child-only deltas cannot clear omitted activity flags on ancestors. Ordinary label patches remain local. The original shared session-change projection is preserved: partial event rows merge field by field; omitted fields retain loaded metadata, explicit null clears a field, and supplied arrays replace it. This preserves model selection and thinking capabilities when Gateway lifecycle events omit them. A model, provider, or runtime change invalidates stale thinking capabilities; a new session incarnation replaces retained state. Complete roster snapshots remain authoritative. Event encoding preserves omission and explicit null through replay. Row changes received during a load accumulate the projected row so a later partial lifecycle event cannot erase an earlier model update. They are replayed without resurrecting rows invalidated afterward. Newer held metadata and matching observer receipts survive older roster snapshots; foreign global observer receipts are cleared. Connection, pull, and sequence-gap refreshes remain immediate. ## Evidence ### Partial-event metadata regression - The new regression fails with the pre-fix row replacement: 17 assertion issues across 7 tests. - Patched focused run: **161 tests in 7 suites passed**, including omitted thinking/model metadata, explicit null clearing, event replay, model/provider/runtime changes, session replacement, sidebar queries, refresh coordination, Gateway decoding, and reasoning visibility. - SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint pass on all six changed Swift files: **0 violations**. ### In-flight roster replay regression (ae3267c84fb) The iPhone 17 simulator on iOS 26.5 runs the same nine `RootSidebarModelSessionEventsTests` against the old partial-event buffer and the cumulative projection fix. A model-selection update is followed by a lifecycle update omitting the model while a roster response is held. - Red, reverting only the buffer fix: **1 test fails, 8 pass**, exit 65. The held-load regression reports `Expectation failed: (model.sessions.first?.model → nil) == "new-model"`. - Green, restoring the fix: **9 tests in 1 suite pass**, exit 0 (`** TEST SUCCEEDED **`). The selected model survives both updates and the older roster response, without another fetch. - All six tested source-file SHA-256 hashes match the submitted files. The shared **161 tests in 7 suites** and strict six-file lint pass on those same sources. ### Known helper completion regression (current revision) - Red control uses the exact reviewed `ae3267c84fb` drawer source with the new tests. Both `lifecycle` and `subagent-status` cases fail: `hasActiveSubagentRun → true` remains set and `loads.rosters → 0` instead of 1; xcodebuild exits 65. - Green: **11 tests in 2 suites pass** on an isolated iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 simulator (including both parameterized completion cases), exit 0, **TEST SUCCEEDED**. Eight child events coalesce to one roster load, the parent's helper flag clears, and ordinary label updates still perform zero roster loads. The 20-event burst still requires only one load. - Shared native validation: **300 tests in 24 suites pass**, including the existing finished-helper lifecycle/subagent-status regression and `ChatSessionSidebar` tests. This result is reused only under matching source hashes. - SwiftFormat, strict SwiftLint on all six Swift files, and docs formatting pass. All seven submitted source/doc hashes match the tested tree. - The client contract now documents identified nested wire rows as partial deltas; authoritative roster snapshots retain replacement semantics. ### Real Gateway: rendered drawer and measured traffic The iPhone 17 Pro simulator on iOS 26.5 runs base `fddee787e37` and head `e001c9d8447` through the normal iOS Gateway adapter. Each run starts with six sessions, performs 16 label patches, creates two sessions, and deletes two sessions. Both deliver **22 `sessions.changed` events**. Initial connection and roster loads are excluded. Counts and payload bytes come from the Gateway response log for the app operator connection, independently matched to passively captured WebSocket frames. | Measured result | Base | Fixed | |---|---:|---:| | Delivered session events | 22 | 22 | | Drawer roster responses during 16 label patches | 16 | 0 | | Drawer roster responses, whole sequence | 22 | 3 | | All session-roster responses on app connection | 40 | 21 | | Session-roster response payload bytes | 476,148 | 252,997 | **223,151 bytes saved (46.9%)**. Both UI runs pass: four renamed rows and two newly created rows appear; both deleted rows disappear. prs.title: fix(ui): align reactions with opposite message edges

Fixes #186082

## What Problem This Solves

Reaction chips sit on the sender-facing side of Control UI messages instead of the opposite edge of each bubble.

## User Impact

The viewer's own messages show reactions below the left edge. Agent replies and other participants' messages show them below the right edge, including short messages and grouped conversations. Counts, reaction controls, and message actions remain available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the transcript's registered message elements and pooled resize observer to align the existing footer without inserting a new footer row or changing message data. Visible reactions wrap when needed; the add button cannot create an empty wrapped line.

## Evidence

- 44 existing message/reaction tests and both existing reaction E2E scenarios pass.
- UI build, focused chat typecheck, lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Real Control UI with a mock Gateway: desktop and 390px touch, one or many reactions, short/long/grouped messages, bubble mode with an image, keyboard picker operation, and a new message advancing the group's footer.
- Matching before/after captures and a recording verify that revealing message actions preserves the surrounding message layout.
- Autoreview P0–P2: scoped-clean on the complete diff based on `43dc38e6c137`, committed unchanged as `192cb1f9a55b`.

The broader `ui/tsconfig.json` check reports diagnostics in native-desktop Gateway E2E declarations and the quota-reset diagnostic fixture, outside this diff. The focused chat configuration passes.

## Risk and coverage

Presentation only; no transcript, reaction protocol, permission, or persistence changes. No new permanent visual assertions were added.

## Visual evidence

Before: `43dc38e6c137`. After: `192cb1f9a55b`. Both use the Control UI with mock Gateway data.

prs.title: fix(cli): prevent missing-cache errors after state uninstall (#112625)
prs.body:
Closes #112625

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a new shell reports a missing completion script after `openclaw uninstall --state` deletes the cache but leaves its source registration behind.

## User Impact

State uninstall removes registrations for the completion caches it deletes, without removing another profile's registration, user-managed portable hooks, unrelated shell settings, or shared PATH entries. Separately installed CLI files remain under their installation owner's removal flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Summary

Retire selected-state completion registrations before deleting their caches.

### Root Cause

`uninstallCommand` delegates state deletion to `removeStateAndLinkedPaths`, which removes the completion cache with the state tree but previously never asked the completion owner to update shell profiles. Legacy unguarded `source` lines then fail every time a new shell reads the profile.

### Changes

- Reuse the completion owner's literal source formats, profile paths, encoding handling, and atomic publication.
- Remove only exact registrations for the selected lexical/canonical state paths. Preserve orphan markers, compound user commands, other-state registrations, and portable HOME hooks.
- Scan both Bash startup files and both Windows PowerShell profile directories, following existing profile symlinks without replacing them.
- Perform edits only after Gateway and native SQLite cleanup admission, using the existing atomic mutation fence immediately before replacement, after staging and fsync. A profile-write failure stops cache deletion.
- Preserve unrelated locale/ANSI bytes without a lossy round trip, and reject observed changes to the profile binding, identity, content, or permissions before replacement.
- Keep `reset` behavior unchanged and preview profile changes without writes in `--dry-run`.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

Ran the supported development CLI against isolated real HOME/config/state directories on macOS arm64, using Node 24.22.1 as the launcher and the repository-pinned development runtime. The resolver, profile I/O, state deletion, and fresh Bash process were not mocked.

After-fix capture head: `eae7b026fae96cdeabf227afbe583110430b65ef`, including main parent `dfe4488d7b74e6205738ecddb7bd15cab6c87132`. The ordinary flow and the combined ancestor-workspace/non-UTF-8 flow were rerun on this committed head.

Command: `pnpm openclaw uninstall --state --yes --non-interactive`.

| Observation | Reproduced main `443530a55b7e` | Fixed head `eae7b026fae9` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI exit | 0 | 0 |
| Selected completion cache | Deleted | Deleted |
| Selected legacy source registration | Still present | Removed |
| Fresh Bash stderr | `openclaw.bash: No such file or directory` | Empty |
| Other-state cache and registration | Preserved | Preserved |
| Unrelated profile bytes and file mode | Preserved | Preserved |

The fixture includes an other-state registration, an orphan marker followed by a user setting, a guarded user-managed hook, shared PATH settings, and mixed line endings. After removal, the entire profile equals its original bytes minus only the selected owned block.

```text
dryRunProfileAndCacheUnchanged=true
profileWriteFailureExit=1
profileWriteFailureRetainsCacheAndProfiles=true
cliExit=0
selectedCacheExists=false
selectedHookRemains=false
otherStatePreserved=true
profileModePreserved=true
shellExit=0
shellStdout=user=preserved other=preserved last=preserved
shellStderr=""
```

The additional real-CLI refusal uses a task-owned read-only profile directory: publication returns EACCES, the CLI exits 1, and both the cached script and original profiles remain intact. Permissions are restored during fixture cleanup. No operator Gateway or state is used.

Repeated the full acceptance flow with HOME explicitly configured as the retained workspace, an ancestor of the selected state directory. Dry-run and denied publication still preserve all bytes; successful uninstall deletes the selected cache and its hook while retaining the workspace and other-state registration.

The non-UTF-8 case includes a raw `0xE9` byte in a user comment. The same byte-for-byte assertions pass, and fresh Bash starts without stderr after removal. This is an actual CLI run, not a mocked codec check.

### Latest-stable profile upgrade compatibility

Resolved npm `latest` and the GitHub latest non-prerelease on October 27, 2026: both select OpenClaw `2026.10.8` (published CLI build `dc2523e`). Used that exact published CLI in a temporary prefix, with dependency lifecycle scripts disabled, and isolated HOME/config/state directories. This is persisted-profile compatibility proof, not qualification of the package updater or installer.

The published CLI itself ran `config set agents.entries.main.workspace <fixture-workspace>` and `completion --shell bash --write-state --install --yes`. It generated a real completion cache and this actual guarded profile registration:

```sh
# OpenClaw Completion
[ -f '<fixture-home>/.openclaw/completions/openclaw.bash' ] && source '<fixture-home>/.openclaw/completions/openclaw.bash'
```

A fresh Bash loaded that generated completion (`complete -p openclaw` succeeded). Added a separate other-state registration and a raw non-UTF-8 user-comment byte to the stored profile, then set its mode to `0640`.

Switched the executable to candidate `eae7b026fae9` while retaining those exact directories and files. Candidate `config get agents.entries.main.workspace` loaded the stable-written value without rewriting its config bytes. Candidate dry-run preserved the profile and cache. Actual uninstall then removed the selected stable registration/cache, and the profile exactly equaled its pre-uninstall bytes minus that one owned block:

```text
stableVersion=OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (dc2523e)
candidateHead=eae7b026fae96cdeabf227afbe583110430b65ef
stableGeneratedCacheAndRegistration=true
stableFreshShell=completion=0 user=preserved other=preserved last=preserved
candidateLoadsStableConfigWithoutRewriting=true
candidateDryRunPreservesStableProfileAndCache=true
selectedStableCacheRemoved=true
selectedStableRegistrationRemoved=true
unrelatedBytesAndRawCommentPreserved=true
otherStateHookAndCachePreserved=true
profileModePreserved=0640
candidateFreshShell=completion=1 user=preserved other=preserved last=preserved
candidateFreshShellStderr=""
VERDICT=LATEST_STABLE_PROFILE_UPGRADE_COMPATIBLE
```

Here `completion=0` means the selected completion was registered before uninstall; `completion=1` means the fresh post-uninstall shell no longer has it. Both shell processes exit 0, retain the user/other-state settings, and have empty stderr. No shell-profile or filesystem calls were mocked.

### Test

- Red first: the real live-state-owner regression failed on unmodified main because the legacy hook remained after successful uninstall.
- Focused completion, cleanup, and current terminal-text sibling suites on the integrated candidate: 91 passed, 4 native Windows cases skipped on macOS.
- Coverage includes selected-state preservation, both Bash files, symlink aliases and traversal, literal POSIX paths containing newlines, dry-run no mutation, staged publication failure, ownership invalidation, and reset preservation.
- Windows-native coverage also checks both PowerShell directories and UTF-8/UTF-16 BOM preservation; native PowerShell execution is not claimed on this macOS host.
- Consolidated existing completion fixtures retain their previous assertions with a net reduction of 1 test line. The exact global test-line ratchet passes without changing its ceiling.
- Production types, all 29 core-test type graphs, typed lint, formatting, import-cycle and cleanup-related boundary checks pass. The two changed documentation pages pass MDX validation.
- The initial `pnpm check:changed --base 443530a55b7e670863cbe85d78a5a85b92e4b949` run exits 1 only in the repository-wide Knip unused-export scan. That exact scan on a separate clean checkout of the same main reports the same 9 distinct unchanged exports in Matrix QA, session recovery, workspace inventory, UI, and a session-share fixture. The follow-ups reran the focused checks above; the full global scan was not rerun locally. No check is disabled or baseline weakened, and unrelated findings stay out of this repair.
- Native branch reviews identified four P2 boundary defects. All were reproduced red and repaired: effective ancestor preservation, late authority fencing, non-UTF-8 byte preservation, and concurrent profile edits. The frozen final-candidate Codex re-review through P3 reports no actionable findings. Final `codex review --base origin/main` also completed with no actionable findings.
- A fresh independent P0-P3 review of the entire staged candidate against main parent `dfe4488d7b7`, including the actual current `terminalText` API as context, also completed with no actionable findings.

### CI follow-up

The initial published head's run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40530463360 exposed a semantic automatic-merge failure: main migrated the completion owner to `terminalText` and removed its former sanitizer import, leaving this PR's added error message with an undefined `sanitizeTerminalText` reference in the merged tree. The integration commit retains published history, merges main, and migrates the three new path-bearing messages to `terminalText`.

The exact formerly failing extension package-boundary compile now passes locally for all 138 plugins, and its negative canary passes. Core types, all 29 core-test type graphs, typed lint, formatting, and test/source ratchets pass on the integrated candidate. The test-line ceiling is unchanged relative to the incoming main parent and this PR remains net -1 test line; main itself is 496 lines over its current ceiling.

Completed current-head CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40539199085 passes baseline ratchets, documentation, extension package-boundary compilation, production/test types, and lint. It fails two updater test shards and the aggregating `openclaw/ci-gate`:

| Shard | Failing case | Assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-large-29` | `src/cli/update-cli.plugin-convergence.test.ts`: `fails unexpected post-core npm update exceptions` | `src/cli/update-cli.plugin-convergence.test.ts:440` |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-large-2` | `src/cli/update-cli.fresh-doctor.test.ts`: `preserves foreground failure 2 without granting handoff undefined authority` | `src/cli/update-cli/update-cli-failure-recovery.test-support.ts:87` |

Both results contain an additional `recovery-artifact-cleanup` step beyond their expected step arrays.

Reproduced that exact test independently on candidate `eae7b026fae9` and on a separate, clean detached checkout of its unchanged main parent `dfe4488d7b7`, each with its own pinned dependency installation:

```sh
pnpm test src/cli/update-cli.plugin-convergence.test.ts -t "fails unexpected post-core npm update exceptions"
```

Both runs exit 1 with the same unexpected step and the same local diagnostic, `Recovery cleanup removed 1 files (1436994 logical bytes); protected recovery artifacts were retained.` Each reports 1 failed and 12 skipped tests. `git diff --exit-code dfe4488d7b7 HEAD -- src/cli/update-cli.plugin-convergence.test.ts src/cli/update-cli` passes; the entire update implementation subtree and the failing test have identical Git object IDs in both trees. This is an existing updater/test-contract failure on the incoming main parent. The required check remains red; this PR does not weaken its assertion or change the unrelated cleanup path.

Also ran the second exact failing case on a clean detached `dfe4488d7b7` checkout with its own pinned installation:

```sh
pnpm test src/cli/update-cli.fresh-doctor.test.ts -t "preserves foreground failure 2 without granting handoff undefined authority"
```

It likewise exits 1 (1 failed, 11 skipped) with the same unexpected cleanup step and `1436994`-byte local diagnostic. The second failing test and its assertion helper are unchanged from that parent. Both CI failures are therefore reproduced on the unchanged main parent, rather than dismissed as flakes or inferred from similar file names.

## Risk

Compatibility: the matcher owns complete literal cache commands, not generic `openclaw completion` invocations or arbitrary similarly named completion directories. Profile symlinks, remaining bytes, modes, and supported PowerShell encodings are retained.

Availability: exclusive cleanup admission precedes profile edits; failed publication prevents cache deletion. Already-running shells may retain in-memory completion definitions until restarted.

## Changelog

Release-note context: state uninstall no longer leaves stale cached-completion registrations that produce missing-file errors in new shells. The release-owned changelog file is not edited.

## Notes

AI-assisted: yes. Real CLI before/after proof and supporting test coverage are recorded above. Native PowerShell proof remains a platform gap.

Previous #119722 and #112631 are closed without merge. #136241 repaired literal-path installation rather than selected-state uninstall cleanup. This PR follows the maintainer's invitation to reopen a current-main repair only after reproducing the leftover-hook defect.

## What Problem This Solves

Stopping a chat before an accepted message starts adds a redundant cancellation notice and Dismiss button.

## User Impact

Direct Stop keeps the canceled message without an extra notice or empty row. Older records with no known Stop origin, external cancellations, and interruptions keep their notices. Stop scope and manual-resend behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record explicit chat Stop intent with the existing pending input and filter only its cancellation notice. Incognito inputs also finish recording cancellation after execution admission ends, while retaining exact input custody and the existing execution gates. No database migration is needed.

## Evidence

- Browser history-state validators now match the canonical Stop metadata schema. ACK ownership, input cleanup, history-tool output, and prompt-prefix checks pass. All 10 focused browser cases pass. The earlier sidebar roster timeout was not reproduced locally and remains unclassified.

- Focused UI, Gateway, and termination tests pass; the updated cleanup argument assertion passed in a focused rerun. Core/UI typechecks, scoped lint/format, generated validators, and Swift/Kotlin protocol checks pass.

- Focused browser scenario: 8.8 seconds; browser command including build: 17.8 seconds. UI unit command: 10.2 seconds. Gateway/storage command including preparation: 53.2 seconds. PR CI provides the broader validation.

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep progress and final replies after delegation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram can lose its progress card and final reply after an agent delegates work. A later user message can suppress an already accepted result, and retained cards can show an outdated plan. A yielded requester can also incorrectly treat consumed child input as fulfillment of its own final answer.

## User Impact

The conversation keeps one progress card while delegated work runs and the requester processes its results. A requester that yields while it still owes an answer must deliver its own final or a visible failure outcome. Ordinary child completion events can remain quiet, as intended by [#185388](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185388). Plan changes replace outdated steps; finished work disappears and explicit failures remain visible. Meaningful acknowledgments and streaming preferences are preserved.

Use `sessions_yield` with an acknowledgment for a waiting update when a final is still owed. A normal final “started” acknowledgment alone does not register a pending final. Progress remains process-local and is not restored after Gateway restart. Stop/reset and revoked authority prevent follow-up delivery; private child input is not automatically forwarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair follows the existing completion and delivery owners:

- Accepted results retain their original caller, conversation and session. A new message retires old automation privileges without discarding a still-authorized result or borrowing the new turn's privileges.
- Progress follows the pending result through waiting and requester processing. Updated plans replace old steps; closed owners retire their rows.
- Telegram confirms initial card delivery before taking it over. The additive `adoptProgressDraftWithReply` contract preserves a normal reply alongside the card; optional `updatePlan` keeps retained cards accurate.
- A yielded requester's final obligation remains until its own visible-final receipt is recorded. Silent/empty settled output uses the existing bounded tool-free finalizer; exhausted recovery uses the existing missing-answer notice. Completed actions are not replayed. Ordinary quiet child processing and Peter's later [visible-unsent fallback coverage (#185840)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185840) are both preserved.

No new queue, job store, polling loop, permission model or generic blocked-notice producer is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Conflict resolution and correlation diagnostics ([8acf8a32bb61](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8acf8a32bb61893328dec71e4b782192cd065fdf)):** Integrated pinned main `ac0ca14148a7a30ff700e41b9d90b4b33a57f85f` after a confirmed conflict. Only the test-line ceiling required manual resolution; incoming test routing retains the existing PR route. All 81 other previous PR-owned files, including the eight final-answer runtime files, remain byte-identical to `5c990c`. Main measures 6,301,523 test lines; the combined tree measures 6,303,336, comprising the existing +1,770 coverage and 43 lines of bounded diagnostics. prs.title: fix(ui): keep chat actions and timestamps with their message
prs.body:
Fixes #186014

## What Problem This Solves

Hovering or focusing a chat message could reveal actions on neighboring messages. Consecutive user messages also shared the first message's timestamp in the closing group footer, so hovering an earlier message showed its actions and a timestamp underneath a different bubble.

## User Impact

Each message reveals its own actions and timestamp together. Moving into its toolbar keeps them available. Existing message grouping, bubble positions, sender identity, saved reactions, and touch access are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use per-message disclosure for actions and metadata. Earlier desktop user messages show their timestamp in their existing action row; the closing user footer reads the last message's timestamp. Assistant run metadata retains its existing ownership.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the timestamp defect in a real Gateway session with three messages sent as steering during a live agent response.
- Replayed hover, movement into the toolbar, and keyboard focus for all three persisted messages. Each exposes only its own actions and recorded timestamp; bubble positions remain unchanged.
- Reply on the middle message quotes that message. Adding a reaction targets its persisted message ID, and the reaction stays on that message after moving the pointer away.
- Extended the existing grouped-reaction E2E test to check timestamp ownership. Two bundled E2E tests passed in 10.87 seconds; 42 existing rendering tests passed in 3.58 seconds.
- Existing attributed-identity E2E also verifies touch disclosure and footer geometry at narrow widths; it passed together with the hover regression in 12.84 seconds.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, and independent code review passed.
- Live proof uses the candidate Control UI connected to an existing isolated Gateway. The Gateway and its configuration were not replaced or restarted.

## Visual evidence

Real Gateway conversation. Both screenshots hover the middle message; the after capture also shows the reaction added during verification. Before: `8237bbaee32f`. After: `39be6843a8b0`.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The middle message reveals a timestamp below the last bubble](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3876af3-c3fb-42f8-a01a-84ac7044cd00) | ![The middle message keeps its timestamp and actions together](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ab84623-5837-4acf-ab2c-ec0948e6e5db) |

The recording runs at normal speed for 15.2 seconds. Arrows identify the hovered message; the final pause shows the saved reaction with the transient controls hidden.

prs.title: feat(ui): switch command palette between Search and Compose
prs.body:
Fixes #186024

## What Problem This Solves

The command palette mixes search with background-session creation and switches views automatically when text becomes long or multiline.

## User Impact

Search and Compose now have small tabs above the existing palette. Tab switches from the main input, the inactive tab shows the shortcut, and reopening retains the last selected mode. New session opens Compose; background creation and its settings live there. Text, mentions, attachments, foreground drafts, and the palette's top/width anchor are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

One explicit mode replaces the text-length heuristic. The first-open loading view uses the same tabs and passes its selected mode through the existing input handoff. Shift+Tab retains normal focus navigation, and mention selection keeps its Tab shortcut.

## Evidence

- Regenerated the canonical boot manifest from cold and warm New Session/Chat captures to include the shared-tab dependency graph; the production UI build passed.

- Regression fails on the base: long/multiline search unexpectedly enters prompt mode.
- CI repair verified: 126 palette, shared-tabs, and architecture tests passed (5.12 s); 14 affected bundled browser scenarios passed (27.48 s excluding build), including Tab switching, remembered choice, arrow-key focus, background creation, recovery, and cold handoff. Lifecycle and icon-reuse cases retain their assertions and select modes explicitly; the shared-control guard is unchanged.
- Per-frame geometry assertions at desktop and phone widths, with dark/light and normal/reduced motion.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint/style checks, translation-key verification, controller guard, formatting, and independent review.


## Risk and coverage

Mode retention is in memory for the current application lifetime. Gateway behavior is covered through the existing mock-Gateway browser fixture; no live provider calls were made. The change removes the automatic prompt-length policy and reuses the existing draft/submission owners. Against the base, production changes are +222/-48 lines and test changes are +110/-67; no new test files. CI timing is pending.

## Visual evidence

The same 1280 × 900 palette and search text after pressing Tab. Previously Tab focused New session in the combined view; now it switches to Compose.

After media was captured at `4394100`. The final `fe7e4d` commit changes only generated boot-module metadata; the UI source tree is identical.

prs.title: feat(mattermost): message actions and multi-file sends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Mattermost message tool only offers `send`, `react` and `read`, while Slack and Discord let the agent edit, delete and pin posts, search, look up members and channels, list custom emoji and move files. A Mattermost send also rejects more than one attachment, so the agent has to split multi-file replies into separate posts.

## User Impact

User impact: agents on Mattermost can now `edit`, `delete`, `pin`, `unpin`, `list-pins`, `search`, `member-info`, `channel-info`, `emoji-list`, `download-file` and `upload-file`, and a send with several files lands as one post carrying all of them (beyond Mattermost's 10-file cap the rest continue as a reply in the same thread, with the receipts of every post that landed reported if a later one fails).

Gates (`channels.mattermost.actions`, per account under `accounts.<id>.actions`):

| Gate | Default | Actions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reactions` | `true` | `react`, `emoji-list` |
| `messages` | `false` | `read` (unchanged meaning) |
| `messageWrites` | `false` | `edit`, `delete`, `upload-file` |
| `fileDownloads` | `false` | `download-file` |
| `pins` | `false` | `pin`, `unpin`, `list-pins` |
| `search` | `false` | `search` |
| `memberInfo` | `false` | `member-info`, `channel-info` |

No behavior change on upgrade except one read-only addition: because `reactions` is on by default, an unchanged config that leaves `reactions` unset (or `true`) also advertises `emoji-list` (custom emoji names). `messages: true` keeps meaning history reads only, and writes, file transfer, pins, search and member/channel information are separate opt-ins. Existing configs load unchanged (all keys optional, bundled channel metadata regenerated).

## Why This Change Was Made

Delegated writes reuse the reaction action's conversation authorization (a post must belong to the authorized channel or DM) and recheck the calling run's authority (`assertDirectAdapterHandoff`) before every provider request, including the file-body request of `download-file` (passed as `assertCurrent` into the shared media owner, which runs it right before `GET /files/<id>` as Slack does); delegated reads reuse the existing `read` admission, and `search`, `member-info`, `emoji-list` and `download-file` are additionally bound to the account that owns the current conversation. Delegated `search` is pinned to the authorized channel: the query gets `in:<channel>`, caller `in:` operators are rejected, and results from other channels are dropped. The discovery gate table lives in a dependency-free module so channel discovery does not import the execution path; the actions adapter and shared loader move out of `channel.ts` into sibling modules, bringing that file under the line cap.

## Evidence

- `pnpm vitest run extensions/mattermost`: 56 files / 550 tests pass; the one failure, `slash-http.boundary.test.ts` ("reserves authenticated capacity…"), fails identically on a clean `main` checkout and is unrelated.
- Tests (each red on `main` production code): `mattermost/actions.test.ts` (every write action against a loopback server incl. cross-conversation refusal, revoked caller rejected before any request for edit/delete/pin/unpin/upload-file, foreign-account rejection for member-info/emoji-list/channel-info/download-file, non-member `member-info` rejected, channel-scoped search with result filtering and `in:` operator rejection, upload through the real send path with target authorization, a real `saveRemoteMedia` download that writes the file and a caller revoked after the `/files/<id>/info` lookup that never reaches `GET /files/<id>`), `send.test.ts` (several files in one post, overflow threaded under the first post, partial-delivery receipts when an overflow post fails), `channel.test.ts` (discovery per gate incl. the default set `send`/`react`/`emoji-list` and `messages: true` → `read` only, multi-attachment presentation, the `sendPayloadGroupsMedia` contract core keys on), `read.test.ts` (denied channels make no request).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `format:docs`, `config:channels:gen`/`check`, `check:import-cycles`, assertion-safety, mock-exports, max-lines, line-cap ratchets and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Channel config docs budget 4001 → 4011: five new documented gates (`messageWrites`, `fileDownloads`, `pins`, `search`, `memberInfo`) at the channel and per-account level, regenerated with `config:docs:gen` (same precedent as `allowBots` in da579df307a).
- Branch merged with `main` (merge commit, no conflicts; generated metadata and docs baseline unchanged after regeneration).
- Test-lines ratchet: this branch adds net +460 test lines after consolidation (`actions.test.ts` 419 → 323 lines, merged `send.test.ts` cases, two client-level cursor tests folded into the action-boundary test that already proves them). The check is still red: after merging `main` the tree measures 6,311,262 against the 6,310,783 ceiling, and `main` itself is 19 lines over it, so no PR that adds a test line can pass until the ceiling moves; the ceiling was not raised here.
- Docs: "Message actions (message tool)" section with the gate table, upgrade semantics, scoping rules and `channelId` search example; attachment paragraph documents overflow threading and partial-delivery reporting; `docs/cli/message.md` support table lists Mattermost for edit, delete, pin/unpin, pins and search with their gates and the `--channel-id` requirement.

### Live proof on a disposable gateway and Mattermost server

Setup, all local: Mattermost Team Edition 11 in Docker (fresh Postgres), bot `@octo`, human users `alice` and `carol` (team member, not a channel member), an isolated gateway started from this branch (`gateway run --verbose`, all seven gates on, `groupPolicy: open`, `tools.profile: full`), a logging HTTP proxy between the gateway and Mattermost that records every request the bot makes, and a scripted OpenAI-compatible provider that answers each of alice's `proof <step>` posts with the corresponding `message` tool calls. A driver posts as alice, waits for the turn, and records the tool calls, the tool results returned to the model, the REST state and the proxied requests (`proof-evidence-actions.json`, `proof-evidence-multifile.json`).

| step | result |
| --- | --- |
| `send` with two workspace files | one bot post with both `file_ids` (`proof-01.png`, `proof-02.png`); one file-carrying `POST /posts` |
| `send` with twelve files | a 10-file post and a 2-file post with `root_id` = the first post; `proof-11/12` in the overflow |
| `react`, `pin`, `list-pins`, `unpin` on alice's post | ✅ reaction; `is_pinned` true; `list-pins` returns it; false after `unpin` |
| `edit` then `delete` the bot's own post | `edit_at` set with the new text, then `delete_at` set (`PUT /posts/<id>/patch`, `DELETE /posts/<id>`) |
| `search` (plain query) | rewritten to `in:actions-<run> <word>`; 1 hit from the authorized channel, 0 of the 2 same-keyword posts in the other channel |
| `search` with `in:town-square` | rejected: "Mattermost delegated search is scoped to the authorized channel; remove in: operators from query." |
| `member-info` alice / carol | alice returned; carol rejected after `GET /channels/<id>/members/<carol>` → 404 ("limited to members of the current conversation") |
| `channel-info`, `emoji-list` | returned (custom emoji list empty on a fresh server, with the note) |
| `upload-file`, `download-file` | upload posted `proof-upload.png` with its caption into the channel; download saved alice's 76-byte attachment to `media/inbound/` with matching size |
| `edit`/`delete`/`pin` on a post from the other channel | all three "Mattermost <action> post belongs to a different conversation."; that post unchanged (`edit_at` 0, `delete_at` 0, not pinned); proxy shows only `GET /posts/<id>` ×3, no PUT/DELETE/pin |

**Authority traces** (vitest verbose on `00847b1`, loopback Mattermost server; each test asserts the exact request log):

```text
✓ edit stops at a revoked caller before any provider request
✓ delete stops at a revoked caller before any provider request
✓ pin stops at a revoked caller before any provider request
✓ unpin stops at a revoked caller before any provider request
✓ upload-file stops at a revoked caller before any provider request
✓ download-file stops at a revoked caller before any provider request
✓ member-info refuses a delegated caller from another account before any request
✓ emoji-list refuses a delegated caller from another account before any request
✓ channel-info refuses a delegated caller from another account before any request
✓ download-file refuses a delegated caller from another account before any request
✓ saves a downloaded file and never fetches its bytes for a caller revoked after the info lookup
Tests  20 passed (20)
```

Red run of the last case with the `assertCurrent` handoff removed from `download-file` (the bytes were fetched):

```text
× saves a downloaded file and never fetches its bytes for a caller revoked after the info lookup
  → promise resolved "{ content: [ { …(2) } ], …(1) }" instead of rejecting
  expect(requestKeys(requests)).toEqual(["GET /api/v4/files/file-1/info"])
```

**Upgrade from the latest stable** (`openclaw@2026.10.8` installed from npm into an isolated prefix, fresh state dir): the stable gateway ran with an operator config that only has today's keys (`actions: { reactions, messages }`, `groupPolicy`, `streaming`, …), converged by the stable `doctor --fix`, and answered one post. The same state dir and config were then opened with this branch: `config validate` → `Config valid`; `doctor --fix` ran the schema admission and database migrations (agent database schema 25 → 38, pre-migration SQLite backups saved); the gateway booted, connected, answered the next post in the same channel, and the stable-era message was present in the upgraded turn's prompt (same session). The config file was left unchanged (`actions` still `{ reactions, messages }`, no new keys written), so no new action was granted by the upgrade.

**CLI output** (third round): `list-pins` returns the `pins` envelope and every `read`/`list-pins`/`search` post carries `content`, `user` (username resolved with one `POST /users/ids` per call, falling back to the id) and `timestamp` next to the raw Mattermost fields, so the shared `openclaw message` formatter prints them. The table below was rendered by the shared `formatMessageCliText` over the branch's loopback results while developing the change (red before the change: both printed the `Key/Value` object summary with `messages: 2 items`); `actions.test.ts` asserts the `pins`/`messages` envelopes and the exact `id`/`user`/`content`/`timestamp` cells the formatter reads, without importing core (`lint:plugins:no-extension-test-core-imports` is clean):

```text
Pinned messages
┌──────────────────────────┬───────────┬───────┬────────┐
│ Time                     │ Author    │ Text  │ Id     │
├──────────────────────────┼───────────┼───────┼────────┤
│ 2024-04-24T23:06:41.000Z │ user-gone │ newer │ post-2 │
│ 2024-04-24T23:06:40.000Z │ bob       │ older │ post-1 │
└──────────────────────────┴───────────┴───────┴────────┘
```

`docs/cli/message.md` now lists Mattermost for react, read, edit, delete, pin/unpin, pins, search and member info with their gates. Output from the shipped `openclaw message` CLI against the disposable server has not been captured yet; the rendered table above comes from the shared formatter over the branch's loopback results.

The first run of this proof found a real gap: plain multi-file sends fanned out into one post per file because the outbound adapter never declared `sendPayloadGroupsMedia`, so core split the files before `sendPayload` ran. Fixed in `a2501ff` (capability declared, contract test added) and re-proved above. Screenshots are in the comment below.

### ClawSweeper review: what changed

- Search is pinned to the authorized channel (query prefix, operator rejection, result filtering); member-info, emoji-list, channel-info and download-file require same-provider/same-account admission and member-info is limited to members of the current conversation.
- Caller authority (`assertDirectAdapterHandoff`) is asserted before any effect and rechecked by the client before every request for edit/delete/pin/unpin/upload-file, react and read.
- Overflow posts thread under the first post when there is no `replyToId`, and an overflow failure raises the shared partial-delivery error with the receipts that landed.
- Gate constants moved to a dependency-free module; `actions.ts` is reached only through `channel.runtime.ts`; `check:import-cycles` is clean.
- Config semantics (second round, per the reviewer's recommendation): `messages` stays read-only; `messageWrites`, `fileDownloads`, `pins`, `search` and `memberInfo` all default off, so only `reactions` is on without an explicit choice.
- Third round: `list-pins` returns `pins`; `read`/`list-pins`/`search` posts carry `content`/`user`/`timestamp` for the CLI formatter (CLI-boundary tests red first); CLI support table covers react/read/member info too; the upgrade claim names the `emoji-list` exception.
- Second round: caller authority now reaches the file-body download request through the media owner's `assertCurrent` (real-boundary test, red without the handoff); the CLI support table lists Mattermost; authority traces and the stable-upgrade run are above.
- Docs use `channelId` for search; the low-value upload test was replaced by a real-send-path test with target authorization; the `saveRemoteMedia` mock returns the full `SavedRemoteMedia`.
- Live proof through the shipped `message` tool entry point incl. forbidden conversation, non-member and revoked-caller rejection, multi-file delivery, and unchanged-config loading.

## What Problem This Solves

Project observations and task suggestions can indirectly expose sessions omitted from a guest's session list.

## User Impact

Project and task projections use the same membership-aware session inventory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry canonical projection membership into the existing project/session selectors.

Stack step **9/17**, based on [fix/guest-access-06-http-resources-20261026](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/tree/fix%2Fguest-access-06-http-resources-20261026). Review and merge in order; each upper PR contains only its own slice against its predecessor.

Previous: [guard HTTP resources and session tickets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184506).

Next: [filter usage, cron and approval lookups](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184509).

Stack order: [complete stack](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184515#stack-order).

## Evidence

### Current-head qualification — 2026-10-28

Current head: `e412ec29549386ffa524387d96d31fc21f938bf2`, based on main `08e08b7204951b7d4f6b0760a814241fa7c17bf1`. Only this slice was rebased. The sole conflict was `config/test-lines-baseline.txt`; range-diff confirms the production patch and both regressions are unchanged from `a3d934b580f2482740f9f80d2ff59f6fd575e37f`.

- **69/69 scoped tests passed** across five project/task suites. Both new regressions were red on the original pinned main base and remain green.
- Core typecheck, five-file typed lint, format and diff checks passed on this exact head.
- Test-line ceiling: exactly **6,311,490**, **zero slack**. The combined tree was measured again to retain the invited-summary regressions without deleting tests or reserving allowance.

The [exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184508#issuecomment-6414253713) is clean, with no findings or before-merge items. Prior-head CI is historical evidence only.

### Authorized AWS proof carry-over

The AWS execution below tested head `a3d934b580f2482740f9f80d2ff59f6fd575e37f` against main `f22f675dbcb352c4875c1a848b4f3fc1e23c77be`. It is **carried over, not rerun**, for this mechanical rebase under the stack owner's instruction.

- Incorporated-main range: `f22f675dbcb352c4875c1a848b4f3fc1e23c77be..08e08b7204951b7d4f6b0760a814241fa7c17bf1`.
- Changed project/task-summary, sharing, membership, session-selection/profile, project-discovery/worktree and invited-schema paths in that range: **`[]`**.
- The authored production and regression patch is unchanged; its only rebase adjustment is the baseline ceiling. No AWS instance was allocated for this carry-over.
- The 72-case paired proof, 48 unchanged view/none comparisons, three main-red/head-green rows, exact local enum diff, source restoration and verified lease release below remain the runtime evidence. In that section, “final head” means the AWS-tested `a3d934b5`, not a claim of a new execution on `e412ec29`.

### AWS integration plan and expected versus actual

A fresh AWS `openclaw-check` lease, `cbx_52442bad4867`, ran on an observed **c7a.2xlarge, 8 CPUs / 15.2 GiB RAM**. Hardware and no-IAM-role admission ran before bootstrap installation; public networking, no Tailscale and the supported Crabbox doctor were verified. [The final-head run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_23da2f7462c8779b641e1f3311d0a7ef) built the pinned main base and final head separately with `pnpm build` and booted isolated real Gateways through the normal `pnpm openclaw` CLI.

Plan: create distinct synthetic A/B/C profiles and three real Git repositories/sessions (`shared`, `uninvited`, `draft`); authenticate certificate-verified TLS/WebSocket clients without administrator scope; read project and task summaries under `view`, `none` and test-enabled `invited`; A invites B to shared and draft, then removes B from shared. B’s first project read and next task read after the acknowledged removal use the same retained connection, with no sleep, reconnect, cache helper or state edit. C never receives membership.

This table applies to both global project and task summaries. Public project/task fields and source identities were independently checked; disposable checkout roots and times were normalized for comparison.

| Case | Expected | Main actual | Final-head actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A, all policies/stages | draft + shared + uninvited | same | same |
| B/C, view, all stages | shared + uninvited | same | same |
| B/C, none, all stages | empty | empty | empty |
| B, invited, before invitation | empty | empty | empty |
| B, invited, after invitation | shared only | empty — reproduced omission | shared only |
| C, invited, all stages | empty | empty | empty |
| B, invited, first reads after removal | empty | empty | empty |
| B, invited, keyed shared task list while a member | shared only | empty — reproduced omission | shared only |

**72 paired cases completed; all 72 final-head policy assertions passed, all 48 view/none pairs were unchanged, and exactly three main-red/head-green cases were observed** (member project list, global task list and keyed shared task list). Membership on `draft` never disclosed it to B. Hidden keyed task sources retained their exact not-found/no-payload contract. Positive cold project discovery used bounded ordinary RPC readiness reads; the first post-removal reads were not retried. No authorization helper was mocked, and no model inference or model credential was needed.

Both variants reported complete execution, zero unexpected failures, settled Gateway process groups, removed isolated state and restored source bytes. The only local runtime-schema edit enabled the invited enum. Generated documentation counts/hashes also reflect the fixture’s disabled bundled plugins. None of these test-only files was committed or pushed. The exact diff was identical on both revisions (SHA-256 `dbbf9c2b14e5697057acd18f3b9a6524aab832d6505a370ddf1309706767c4b4`), checked against the tested source and restored afterward:

prs.title: fix: dashboard reports success when link preparation fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`dashboard --no-open` with a stopped Gateway and closed stdin prints a failure and no URL but returns exit 0. Shell callers receive false success. Other readiness/listener/pairing preparation failures can omit nonzero status too.

## User Impact

Failed preparation now exits 1, matching the existing JSON path. Explicit interactive recovery decline still cancels successfully with exit 0. This intentionally changes failed noninteractive shell invocations; browser/clipboard fallback after URL issuance remains nonfatal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the private distinction between an actual interactive decline and inability to recover, then set the existing runtime failure status at failure returns. No new option, schema, default, credential/link issuance rule, target-selection rule, browser fallback or recovery/start policy.

## Evidence

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171753#issuecomment-6480529565

Normal built Linux CLI + real built Control UI on **Node 24.22.1** Docker. Main `f25827c78da2d4ca564918675c5e7436e006aa79` versus product head `dc0104e30f6ff63046ba1919617c2315be1a35c4`, **main twice and candidate twice**, 16 dashboard calls with isolated profile/HOME/state/config:

- Closed stdin/stopped target: main exits **0** despite diagnosis/no URL; candidate exits **1** with the same diagnosis/no URL. TCP listener remains closed before/after; no service files or config changes.
- JSON stopped-target control exits **1** and emits valid failure JSON on both versions.
- Running-Gateway control uses four actual owned foreground Gateways and matching built UI (**HTTP 200 text/html, 39,078 bytes**). Both versions print a Dashboard URL and exit **0**; `--no-open` keeps browsers closed, and clipboard fallback remains nonfatal.
- **Maintainer-approved interactive-control limit:** real Linux PTY attempts cannot reach the recovery prompt on isolated profiles. Selected-URL overrides/non-default identity classify the native service diagnostic-only, so diagnosis returns before any question. No decline is claimed from that PTY run. The existing qualified-native-service/TTY branch test explicitly declines and verifies no error exit; it is the accepted explicit-decline control. No fake service or target-policy change.
- Focused suites **21/21**, 5.57s; lint and formatter parity pass. Committed readiness regression fails on main because exit(1) is absent (**1 failed, 14 unselected**, 4.75s).
- Additional unchanged real-socket consumer cleanup fails identically on main and candidate in native child lifecycle teardown; full case/stack attribution is in the evidence comment. No supervisor, assertion, timeout or baseline was relaxed.

Final head `fdf56526d50b7874df8c5b42176e91d44c6ce91a` retains the contributor commit and changes tests only after the measured product build. Shared failure assertions remove duplicate setup while retaining failure/side-effect observations. **Production +6, tests −1**, no baseline change.

Initial runtime/UI identity mismatch was corrected with normal matching builds before the successful running controls. No models, live accounts/state, native Windows/macOS, browser GUI, service installation/recovery or release upgrade is claimed.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: revert restores prior exit-status behavior, without changing persisted data or config. Blast radius is shell automation interpreting dashboard preparation failures; explicit decline and successful URL/browser/clipboard fallback retain their existing contracts. Credential issuance and recovery authority are unchanged.

issues.title: Matrix: add groupPolicyOverrides (per-room group policy, parity with Napcat)
issues.body:
## Problem

`groupPolicy` is channel-wide on Matrix (one of `open`, `mention`, `allowlist` applies to **every** group room). Only DMs (≤2 members) bypass it (`_should_process_message`, `nanobot/channels/matrix/runtime.py`, v0.3.5).

A deployment with many rooms usually wants different behavior per room:

| Room type | Desired policy | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Topic/project rooms | `open` — respond to every message | Bot is the copilot there |
| Shared / busy room | `mention` — respond only when @mentioned or replied to | Unprompted replies are noise, and the room will also host another bot |

This cannot be expressed today: `open` everywhere is noisy in the shared room, `mention` everywhere silences the topic rooms.

## Existing precedent in the codebase

The Napcat channel already ships this exact mechanism — the ask is a small parity port to Matrix:

- `nanobot/channels/napcat/manifest.py`: `"groupPolicyOverrides": field("json", default={})`
- `nanobot/channels/napcat/runtime.py`:
  ```python
  group_policy_overrides: dict[str, GroupPolicy] = Field(default_factory=dict)
  policy = self.config.group_policy_overrides.get(str(group_id), self.config.group_policy)
  ```

Related Telegram-side RFCs with the same gap: #3309, #5972.

## Proposed config

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "matrix": {
      "groupPolicy": "open",
      "groupPolicyOverrides": {
        "!aaaa...:example.org": "mention"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- **Keys:** Matrix room IDs. **Values:** the same vocabulary as Matrix's `groupPolicy` — `"open" | "mention" | "allowlist"` (Napcat additionally accepts a probability float; not required here).
- **Precedence:** per-room override → channel `groupPolicy`. Rooms not listed behave exactly as today, so existing configs are unaffected.
- An `"allowlist"` override would reuse the existing channel-wide `groupAllowFrom` list for that room (minimal change; per-room allow lists could come later).
- `allowRoomMentions` semantics unchanged.

## Implementation

Single lookup change at the existing policy-resolution point in `nanobot/channels/matrix/runtime.py`, `_should_process_message()` (~L1136–1149 in v0.3.5):

```diff
-        policy = self.config.group_policy
+        policy = self.config.group_policy_overrides.get(room.room_id, self.config.group_policy)
```

plus the matching `field("json", default={})` declaration in `channels/matrix/manifest.py`, mirroring Napcat.

Happy to attempt the PR if this is wanted.

issues.title: PermissionError [WinError 5] when rewriting the gateway client lease on Windows
issues.body:
# `PermissionError: [WinError 5]` when the gateway client lease is rewritten on Windows

## Summary

On Windows, rewriting `~/.nanobot/run/gateway.clients.json` intermittently fails with
`PermissionError: [WinError 5] 拒绝访问 (Access is denied)`.

The file is the on-demand gateway client lease (`{"auto_stop": ..., "clients": {...}}`).
It is written with a temp-file + `os.replace()` pattern, and Windows refuses the rename
whenever any other handle has the target open without `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, or when a
real-time scanner is briefly holding the temp file.

Because Python's `Path.read_text()` (used by the same class to read the lease) does not
grant delete sharing, a reader on the other side of the race is enough to make the write
fail. The failure is not retried, so it escapes as an exception to the calling client.

Related: a failed write also means the client is *not* registered in the lease, which is
the data structure that decides whether an on-demand gateway may auto-stop.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Windows 11 (AMD64) |
| Python | 3.14.9 |
| nanobot | 0.4.0 |
| Commit | `4a14faa47e9af06a66968cb59f5b5d46754dc6fe` |
| Install | source checkout, `python -m nanobot gateway --foreground --port 18790` |
| Data home | `%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot` |
| File system | local NTFS, not a network drive, not OneDrive-synced |

## Actual behaviour

```
PermissionError: [WinError 5] 拒绝访问。:
  '%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot\run\gateway.clients.json.d8y0i3t6.tmp'
  -> '%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot\run\gateway.clients.json'
```

Observed while a single gateway service was running (one launcher process plus its
worker child, the worker owning ports 8765 and 18790). The run directory was writable —
`run/gateway.json` was being written successfully in the same time window — so this is
not a directory ACL problem, and the lease file was not marked read-only. No `.tmp`
leftovers remained, i.e. the `finally: temporary.unlink()` cleanup ran each time.

## Expected behaviour

The lease write should tolerate a transient sharing violation, since the file is
short-lived state that is read roughly once per second by
`monitor_gateway_clients()`.

## Root cause

`nanobot/gateway/runtime.py`:

- write path — `GatewayClientLease._write_state()` (lines 782–798):

  ```python
  fd, temporary_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
      prefix=f"{self.state_path.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=self.state_path.parent
  )
  temporary = Path(temporary_name)
  try:
      with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
          json.dump(state, handle, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
          ...
          os.fsync(handle.fileno())
      temporary.replace(self.state_path)      # <-- single attempt, no retry
  finally:
      temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
  ```

- read path — `GatewayClientLease._read_state()` (lines 766–773):

  ```python
  payload: object = json.loads(self.state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
  ```

- poller — `monitor_gateway_clients()` (lines 801–815) calls
  `lease.begin_orphan_shutdown()` every `poll_interval_s` (default `1.0`), and
  `begin_orphan_shutdown()` (lines 622–637) reads *and* writes the lease.

On POSIX, `os.replace()` over a file that another process has open simply succeeds.
On Windows it maps to `MoveFileExW(..., MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)`, which returns
`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (5) when the destination has an open handle that did not specify
`FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, or when the destination is read-only.

Python's `open()` / `Path.read_text()` on Windows requests read+write sharing but **not**
delete sharing, so any concurrent `_read_state()` — in the gateway process, in a second
client process, or in a status/UI reader — is enough to make the replace fail.

Note that `begin_orphan_shutdown()` does take `transition_lock` before touching the file,
so the *application-level* readers and writers it controls are serialised. The remaining
windows are:

1. external handles that do not participate in the app-level lock (real-time antivirus /
   Defender scanning the freshly written `.tmp`, Windows Search indexer, backup agents,
   an editor with the file open), and
2. any future/third-party reader of the lease that calls `_read_state()` outside the
   transition lock.

Either way the mitigation is the same: don't let a transient share lock turn into a
hard failure.

## Minimal reproduction of the underlying Windows behaviour

```python
import os
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

d = Path(os.environ["TEMP"]) / "share-lock"
d.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
target = d / "gateway.clients.json"
target.write_text('{"old": 1}', encoding="utf-8")

handle = open(target, "r", encoding="utf-8")   # same sharing as Path.read_text()
tmp = d / "new.tmp"
tmp.write_text('{"new": 2}', encoding="utf-8")


def replace():
    try:
        os.replace(tmp, target)                 # nanobot line 796
        print("ok")
    except PermissionError as exc:
        print("failed:", exc)                   # -> [WinError 5]


thread = threading.Thread(target=replace)
thread.start()
time.sleep(0.01)
handle.close()
thread.join()
```

A single `os.replace()` fails here; a short bounded retry succeeds as soon as the reader
closes.

## Proposed fix

Retry the replace with a bounded, short backoff. The whole function is state that is
rewritten immediately afterwards anyway, so a few milliseconds of patience is harmless,
and it keeps a scanner/reader blip from raising into the client.

```diff
--- a/nanobot/gateway/runtime.py
+++ b/nanobot/gateway/runtime.py
@@ -793,7 +793,7 @@ class GatewayClientLease:
                 handle.write("\n")
                 handle.flush()
                 os.fsync(handle.fileno())
-            temporary.replace(self.state_path)
+            _replace_with_sharing_retry(temporary, self.state_path)
         finally:
             temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
@@ -820,3 +820,20 @@ def _instance_suffix(*, workspace: str | None, config_path: str | None) -> str |
     if not raw:
         return None
     return hashlib.sha1(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
+
+
+def _replace_with_sharing_retry(source: Path, target: Path, *, attempts: int = 10) -> None:
+    """Atomically replace ``target`` with ``source``, retrying Windows share locks.
+
+    Windows reports a concurrent reader of ``target`` (or a scanner briefly
+    holding ``source``) as ``ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED``; the window is short, so a
+    bounded retry clears it where a single ``os.replace`` would fail.
+    """
+    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
+        try:
+            os.replace(source, target)
+            return
+        except PermissionError:
+            if attempt == attempts:
+                raise
+            time.sleep(0.005 * attempt)
```

`time` is already imported in this module. Worst case adds ~0.23 s before the original
`PermissionError` is re-raised, so a permanently locked file still fails loudly instead
of hanging.

Verified locally against both cases:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Reader holds the file briefly, then closes | replace succeeds, new content visible |
| Reader never closes the file | `PermissionError` still raised, after ~0.23 s |

## Possible follow-ups for maintainers

- If `_read_state()` should never block a writer, the read could be done through a
  handle opened with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` (ctypes `CreateFileW`) so `os.replace()`
  succeeds even while a read is in flight. The retry above makes that optional.
- Consider logging a warning plus retry-scheduling instead of propagating, so a client
  attach never fails because of lease bookkeeping.

## Workaround for users (no code change)

- Add `%USERPROFILE%\.nanobot` to antivirus exclusions.
- Make sure only one gateway service runs (`nanobot gateway status` / one `gateway start`).
- The error is transient: the next lease write succeeds, and the client can usually
  attach again.

issues.title: [channels/matrix] v0.4.0 attaches m.in_reply_to to every non-threaded bot reply — no config toggle, quote noise in Element
issues.body:
## Environment
- nanobot v0.4.0 (Docker deploy)
- Clients: Element Web + Element X
- Unencrypted rooms, long-polling sync

## Behavior since v0.4.0

Every bot reply in a room now renders with a quote block of the user's message above it (Element's rendering of a plain `m.in_reply_to` relation).

Observable cause (verified in the installed v0.4.0 source): `MatrixChannel._build_outbound_relates_to()` in `channels/matrix/runtime.py` attaches a plain `m.in_reply_to` relation to every non-threaded outbound message — introduced by #5292 (implementing #5274):

```python
reply_to = metadata.get("message_id") or metadata.get("event_id")
if not isinstance(reply_to, str) or not reply_to:
    return None
return {"m.in_reply_to": {"event_id": reply_to}}
```

## Why this is noisy

The linking is useful for command-style flows, but in normal conversational rooms every single bot message now carries a quote block of the triggering message. In an active back-and-forth the quote adds visual noise without adding context — the user just sent the message the bot is replying to.

## Request

A config toggle on the Matrix channel (e.g. `replyToUser` or similar) so deployments can choose whether non-threaded replies carry the `m.in_reply_to` relation. Thread relations (`m.thread`) should be unaffected either way.

## Workaround

Local boot patch that makes `_build_outbound_relates_to()` return `None` for the plain reply fallback (thread relations preserved). Happy to turn this into a PR with the config toggle if that approach works for maintainers.
