issues.title: Matrix: "listen" group policy — observe the room, reply only on mention
issues.body:
## Problem

Under Matrix's `mention` policy, messages that fail the policy check are dropped outright in `_on_message` (`nanobot/channels/matrix/runtime.py`) — the bot never ingests them. So in a busy group, when someone finally @mentions the bot, it has no knowledge of the conversation that happened since its last reply. Under `open` it replies to everything. There is no way to get "aware but quiet": read the room, respond only when addressed.

## Request

Add a third group policy value, **`"listen"`** (usable as the channel-wide `groupPolicy` and, with #6286 / PR #6287, per-room via `groupPolicyOverrides`):

- Every message from an allowed sender in a listen room is ingested.
- The bot replies only when mentioned (same `m.mentions` / `allowRoomMentions` semantics as `"mention"`).
- When a mention-triggered turn fires, the recently heard room chatter is attached as context for that turn, so the reply reflects the intervening conversation.

## Proposed v1 (channel-contained, no agent-core changes)

- A bounded per-room transcript buffer (oldest-dropped, hard caps on entries and characters) is filled at ingest time for unmentioned messages.
- On a mention-triggered turn the buffer is attached via the **existing trusted channel seam** `_runtime_context_blocks` (`nanobot/runtime_context.py`, `RUNTIME_CONTEXT_INPUT_META`) — blocks are appended to the turn's user content and persisted with a display-time-removal marker, and the buffer is cleared once consumed.
- No LLM cost for unheard messages; bounded memory; delimiters and caps per the `RuntimeContextBlock` docstring's "bound and delimit content obtained from untrusted sources" requirement.

## Future option (separate discussion if there's interest)

Fully persisting unheard room chatter into the session transcript *without* an agent turn would need an append-only admission path in the loop — today every non-user inbound becomes a `TurnKind.SYSTEM` turn, which runs the LLM. That interacts with auto-compaction/token burn, so it needs maintainer design review; v1 above needs none.

issues.title: WebUI: allow changing an existing chat's project directory (picker is unreachable after the first message)
issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

In the WebUI a chat's project (working directory) can only be chosen while the chat is still empty. Once the chat has one user message, the directory control disappears from the composer, so moving an existing topic to another folder is impossible from the UI — the only workaround is to start a new chat and lose its title and history.

I keep ~15 topics grouped by project in the sidebar. Re-organizing them, or fixing a topic that was created before I picked the right folder, currently has no path at all.

### What I checked on `main` @ b07b3ea (2026-10-27)

1. **Front-end gate.** `projectPickerAvailable` in `webui/src/components/thread/ThreadComposer.tsx:1199` is now `!workspaceProjectLocked && ...` (before #6256 it was `isHero`, i.e. new-chat only). The picker is rendered in exactly one place, the composer (`ThreadComposer.tsx:2435`), so an existing thread falls back to showing only the permission menu.
2. **Lock source.** `webui/src/components/thread/ThreadShell.tsx:796` computes

   ```ts
   const projectLocked = session?.projectLocked === true
     || (session?.projectLocked === undefined && displayMessages.some((message) => message.role === "user" && ...));
   ```

   `webui/src/lib/api.ts:209,231` reads `project_locked` from `GET /api/sessions`, but no gateway code ever emits that field (grep `project_locked` under `nanobot/` → 0 hits). The fallback therefore keeps **every existing chat locked**.
3. **The gateway already accepts the change.** `set_workspace_scope` (`nanobot/webui/inbound_commands.py:428`) → `WebUIWorkspaceController.scope_for_set_request` (`nanobot/webui/workspaces.py:412`) only refuses while the chat is running (`chat_running`, 409). There is already a test for the set-request path: `tests/utils/test_webui_workspaces.py::test_remote_existing_chat_can_reduce_its_workspace_access`.

So the gap looks like a missing marker in the sessions payload plus a missing affordance, not a missing capability.

### Proposed Solution

- Emit `project_locked` in the `/api/sessions` payload — for example `false` for an idle, non-temporary session and `true` for temporary chats — or simply show the picker for existing chats and let `set_workspace_scope` stay the authority.
- Keep the existing guards: 409 while a turn is running, temporary chats stay locked, and the next turn must re-derive runtime context / system prompt from the new scope.
- Optional: a sidebar affordance (topic context menu → "Change directory", like the existing "New chat in project") so re-organizing many topics does not require opening each chat.

### Alternatives Considered

- Create a new chat in the target folder and restate the task. That is today's workaround, and it drops the topic title and history.
- Hand-editing session metadata under `~/.nanobot/`. Undocumented and error-prone.
- Dragging the topic into another sidebar project group. Drag-and-drop in `webui/src/components/ChatList.tsx` only moves tabs/panes; it does not change project membership.

### Related Component

Other (WebUI)

### Additional Context

- Environment: nanobot 0.3.5 installed from `main` @ d617b72, Windows 11, Edge, WebUI served at `127.0.0.1:8765`.
- #6256 states "The existing project-lock behavior is not redesigned here" and lists the directory lock as a known limitation, so I am filing this as a follow-up rather than a regression. If locking a topic's folder after its first message is intentional (to keep memory/context bound to one project), a documented way to relocate a topic would also solve the problem — happy to adjust this request to whatever direction fits the design.
- Unrelated to #1302 (per-session isolation for non-WebUI channels).

## Summary

- Add a complete Langfuse setup dialog under Settings → System → Tracing, with installation, enable/disable, service URL, masked credentials, and draft connection testing.
- Persist an optional `observability.langfuse` block. An explicit block takes precedence as a whole; omitted configuration keeps the existing environment-variable setup and `${VAR}` references.
- Keep saved settings separate from the running tracing state. Apply changes after restarting the owning process, including OpenAI-compatible and Codex calls.
- Add a named optional WebUI capability, credential-safe authenticated mutations, guarded connection checks, translations for all supported locales, and updated setup documentation.

## Behavior and limits

Connection tests use the current draft and check the Langfuse public API without saving, activating tracing, or sending conversation content. Private self-hosted endpoints must be allowed through the existing SSRF whitelist. Tracing uploads model inputs and outputs; the dialog makes this visible. A separately running API server must also be restarted to apply changes.

No tracing dashboard or advanced SDK tuning controls are added. SDK resources use the public Langfuse API; WebUI saves/tests do not mutate process environment or initialize a tracing client.

- Passed local `git diff --check`, changed-Python syntax inspection, and JSON source parsing.

prs.title: fix(gateway): reduce lease writes and use Windows-safe I/O
prs.body:
## Why

Gateway status queries and the local-client monitor currently rewrite the lease JSON even when nothing changes, performing unnecessary file synchronization and atomic replacement. Necessary lease I/O also bypasses the Windows-safe atomic file helpers already used by gateway process records.

## What changed

- Keep lease snapshots read-only while still reporting only live clients, including PID-reuse detection.
- Persist monitor cleanup only when client records change; continue committing orphan shutdown under the existing lifecycle locks.
- Reuse `read_atomic_bytes()` and `replace_atomic()` for lease I/O, preserving UTF-8 decoding and allowing existing snapshot readers to retain the previous file during replacement on supported Windows filesystems.

## Scope

Keep the existing JSON format, cross-process locks, and lifecycle behavior. No database or retry policy is added. External handles that deny the required sharing can still block writes; this does not claim to resolve every cause of #6514. Process-record cleanup outside the lease is unchanged.

Related to #6514. Thanks to @BBTAN-bot for the report, and @balabommablock-cpu (B Rishabh Rao) for the Windows-safe I/O proposal and [patch](https://github.com/balabommablock-cpu/nanobot/commit/8d671457935e44579f37ceffe6dbaf61b36b00be), adapted here with a real snapshot-replacement regression test. Both contributors are credited in the commit history.

Resolves NAN-385

## Tradeoffs

Status queries filter stale clients in memory rather than cleaning the lease on disk. The monitor and lifecycle mutations remain responsible for persisted cleanup.

## Blast Radius

Local TUI/WebUI gateway status and lease monitoring on all platforms. Registration, release, and shutdown coordination retain their existing lock order. Windows uses the shared atomic-file implementation; POSIX continues to use ordinary reads and `os.replace()`.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Regression coverage checks unchanged lease bytes/mtime during queries and steady polling, stale-client cleanup, and explicit versus on-demand lifetimes; existing lifecycle-race tests retained.
- Added a deterministic test that opens a real snapshot through the lease read path, performs an actual replacement before closing it, and verifies that the old reader sees the old state while a subsequent reader sees the new state. This test is included in the existing Windows and Linux Python CI suites.
- Local lint, type checking, and tests were not run; validation of the updated head is delegated to this PR's GitHub Actions.

prs.title: feat(matrix): per-room group policy overrides (groupPolicyOverrides)
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds `groupPolicyOverrides` to the Matrix channel — a per-room policy map that overrides the channel-wide `groupPolicy`, mirroring the mechanism the Napcat channel already ships (#6286).

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "matrix": {
      "groupPolicy": "open",
      "groupPolicyOverrides": {
        "!abc123:matrix.org": "mention"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Behavior

| Room | Global `groupPolicy` | `groupPolicyOverrides` entry | Resulting policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `!abc123:matrix.org` | `open` | `"mention"` | `mention` |
| `!def456:matrix.org` | `open` | — | `open` (fallback) |
| Any DM (≤2 members) | any | any | Unaffected — DMs bypass group policy as before |

Resolution is a single lookup in `_should_process_message`:

```python
policy = self.config.group_policy_overrides.get(room.room_id, self.config.group_policy)
```

- Values share the `groupPolicy` vocabulary (`"open"`, `"mention"`, `"allowlist"`); an `"allowlist"` override checks the existing channel-wide `groupAllowFrom` (no per-room allow-list surface added).
- Rooms not listed behave exactly as before — existing configs need no changes, zero migration.
- `allowRoomMentions` and `groupAllowFrom` semantics unchanged.

## Why room IDs (not aliases) as keys

Keys are Matrix room IDs (`!local:server`) exactly as reported in sync — the same identifier `_should_process_message` already compares for the `allowlist` policy. This is homeserver-agnostic: Synapse, Conduit/Conduwuity/Continuwuity, and Dendrite all emit spec-compliant room IDs, and a room keeps its ID regardless of which server implementation serves it, so a config keyed by room ID works identically across backends. Alias keys (`#name:server`) would need lookup calls at startup and stop matching when aliases move; room IDs are stable and opaque.

## Related

- **Fixes #6286**
- Same pattern as the Napcat channel: `groupPolicyOverrides` manifest field + runtime lookup (`nanobot/channels/napcat/manifest.py`, `nanobot/channels/napcat/runtime.py`)
- Telegram counterparts: #3309, #5972

## Tests

Five new behavioral tests in `nanobot/channels/matrix/tests/test_matrix_channel.py`:

1. An override of `"mention"` beats a global `"open"` and the room falls silent without `m.mentions`, while a non-overridden room still follows the global policy.
2. `m.mentions` user mentions are still accepted in an overridden-mention room.
3. An override of `"open"` opens a room under a global `"mention"` policy.
4. An `"allowlist"` override is checked against `groupAllowFrom` (allowlisted room handled, non-allowlisted overridden room blocked).
5. Direct rooms (≤2 members) bypass overrides, as with the global policy.

Contract checks covered by the existing suite: `test_every_runtime_channel_field_has_a_webui_contract` and `test_channel_locales_cover_authoritative_setup_contracts` — locale copy added for all 10 languages (en, es, fr, id, ja, ko, pt-BR, vi, zh-CN, zh-TW), matching how Napcat localizes its override field.

Verified locally: 125 matrix-channel tests pass, 152 channel-contract tests pass, `ruff check nanobot tests` clean, `basedpyright` clean (0 errors) on the touched files.

prs.title: fix(mcp): propagate resource and prompt failures as structured tool errors
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix MCP resource reads and prompt calls being reported as successful tool executions when they fail.

## Root Cause

`MCPResourceWrapper` and `MCPPromptWrapper` returned caught failures as plain strings. The harness recognizes failures through `ToolResult.is_error`, so these responses triggered success hooks and `status="ok"` events and skipped the existing recovery hint.

`MCPToolWrapper` already uses structured error results for these failure paths.

## Changes

- Wrap nine terminal failure returns in ToolResult.error(...), preserving their existing messages.
- Strengthen timeout, exception, retry exhaustion, and recovery assertions.
- Add regression coverage for SDK cancellation, external cancellation, and resource/prompt execution through the tool registry and executor.
- Verify that successful content beginning with "Error:" still follows the success lifecycle.

## Result

Failed resource reads and prompt calls trigger error hooks and `status="error"` events. Their original failure details receive the existing recovery hint.

Successful responses, retry and reconnect behavior, and external cancellation propagation remain unchanged.

## Test

- Red/green verification: 14 regression cases failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- Related MCP, registry, execution, runner error, and logging suites: 240 passed.
- Real MCP SDK 1.28.1 client/server verification over in-memory transport: six scenarios passed, covering protocol errors, timeouts, and successful responses.
- Ruff on changed files: passed.
- BasedPyright on nanobot/agent/tools/mcp.py: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Import boundary checks and git diff --check: passed.

prs.title: fix(providers): retry/fallback fixes for local-backend (Ollama/vLLM) errors
prs.body:
## Summary

Two small, independent retry/fallback fixes for self-hosted backends (Ollama / vLLM), found while running nanobot against a local Ollama instance in production:

- **Local-backend congestion fails over instead of retrying in place.** Ollama/vLLM report their own queue congestion as `"server is busy"` / `"queue is full"` rather than an HTTP rate-limit response, so none of the existing `_FALLBACK_ERROR_TOKENS` matched — a congested backend just kept getting retried on itself instead of failing over to the next chain entry, making the congestion worse.
- **Ollama cold-start errors get a realistic retry pace.** Ollama returns a malformed empty body while paging a model back into memory, surfacing as `Expecting value: line 1 column 1`. The default `_CHAT_RETRY_DELAYS=(1, 2, 4)` exhausts all attempts well before a ~30s model load finishes. Added a separate `_COLD_START_RETRY_DELAYS=(5, 15, 30)` table, selected only when that specific error is detected — `Retry-After` still takes priority, and both tables are the same length, so attempt-count/exhaustion semantics are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `test_chat_with_retry_uses_cold_start_delays_for_ollama_loading_error`, matching this file's existing `ScriptedProvider` + sleep-recording monkeypatch pattern.
- [x] Added `test_should_fallback_on_local_backend_congestion` (parametrized), matching this file's existing style.
- [x] Full retry/fallback suite: `test_provider_retry.py`, `test_provider_retry_after_hints.py`, `test_provider_sdk_retry_defaults.py`, `test_runner_fallback.py`, `test_mcp_transient_retry.py`, `test_interactive_retry_wait.py` — 196/196 passing.
- [x] `ruff check` clean on all touched files.

## Note

Writing the cold-start test caught a real gap in the first draft of this fix: `is_transient_response()` — the gate deciding whether a response is retried *at all* — didn't check the new cold-start marker, only the delay-selection code did, so a cold-start response was classified non-transient and returned immediately without ever reaching the delay override. Fixed by checking `_is_cold_start_error()` directly inside `is_transient_response()` too.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: feat(mcp): add opt-in self-contained Apps hosting in WebUI
prs.body:
Nanobot currently reduces MCP results to model-facing text/image artifacts and exposes app-only tools to the model. This adds an opt-in MCP Apps host: structured results stay outside model context, while self-contained HTML Apps can render in the WebUI and call approved tools on their originating MCP connection.

Refs #5251. The earlier #5386 was withdrawn; this is an independent implementation. Enable with `channels.websocket.mcpAppsEnabled: true` and restart the gateway. It defaults to false, preserves WebUI protocol 1, and advertises the optional `webui.mcp-apps.v1` capability only when enabled.

The implementation spans the complete path:

- Preserve bounded, detached MCP rich results in `ToolResult.data`, including source identity, metadata, schemas and result fields. Error guidance retains this data; model observation normalization strips it before messages/checkpoints are built.
- Honor model/App visibility independently of `enabledTools`. Bind each App to its original connection and declared `ui://` resource, with URI/MIME/UTF-8 validation and connection-close revocation.
- Negotiate `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` for enabled gateway MCP connections. Carry only ephemeral App handles in ordinary progress attachments; rich UI data is fetched through authenticated WebUI mutations.
- Use the official AppBridge in an opaque-origin iframe with restrictive CSP. Every tool call requires host-owned approval outside the iframe, then consumes a single-use receipt bound to the exact recorded arguments and chat. Requests cannot reach another server or bypass its allowlist. Cancellation before approval removes the prompt and prevents dispatch.
- Load AppBridge on demand, reject stale loads after host/session switches, retain text fallbacks, localize controls in all ten locales, and document configuration, architecture and limits.

The current revision merges main through `3c022ada`. It preserves shared proxy configuration in MCP connection/reload/reconnect, all current update capabilities and translations, and the current ThreadShell structure. The real MCPProvider regression covers initial negotiation and reload with Apps both enabled and disabled; old App objects lose access after reload or shutdown. The channel-schema inventory now includes the internal WebSocket `mcpAppsEnabled` option.

This initial host supports **self-contained Apps**. It blocks external assets/fetches and does not grant requested browser/device permissions. Temporary-chat rendering, durable App recovery, external-domain policy and host-side App installation are outside this change. HTML is capped at 1 MiB; rich messages at 64 KiB/depth 16/4096 values; at most 32 handles are retained for 15 minutes. The bridge does not retry possibly committed tool actions or claim exactly-once execution. CSP is not a general network firewall against iframe navigation.

Current revision: `f7aa239acc12dce4feaf3d9340d5b84b6865e26f`. It adds the missing npm lockfile entries required by the Docker build and npm consistency check. Application source and the Bun lock are identical to functional merge `96b7382f`; the checks below retain their original identity where carried forward.

Validation:

- Windows Python 3.11 regression selection: 4,909 passed, 84 platform skips and one missing channel-schema inventory entry. After correcting that expectation, all 58 affected channel-contract/MCP Apps/client-contract tests passed. The broader selection covered tools, WebUI, channels, agent, gateway, config, security and architecture; its totals are not added to the follow-up.
- Complete WebUI: **3,298 passed across 186 files** with Bun 1.3.13 and two workers. The initial default-concurrency run timed out in four files; all 146 tests in those files and then the full suite passed at reduced concurrency without changing timeouts or assertions.
- All channel dependencies and package consistency, full CI Ruff selection, strict BasedPyright for the complete production tree, Python/client import boundaries, 42 import-checker tests, application/browser TypeScript, ESLint and production build passed. All ten merged locale files were compared against the fixed upstream and feature commits.
- Real in-memory MCP sessions exercise provider negotiation/reload, source/visibility/allowlist restrictions and revocation. The wider Python selection includes live authenticated WebSocket approval dispatch and identical-request replay without a second tool execution.
- Chrome 155 checks on the actual AppBridge/card fixture passed initialization, structured weather data, blocked parent access/fetches, rejection with zero executions, one approved call/result, forged message-source rejection, cancellation before approval, and a 390px viewport. The fixture is `/browser/mcp-apps.html`; it uses synthetic host transport rather than a model or external provider.
- On `f7aa239a`, `npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run` and the actual Dockerfile's `webui-builder` stage passed clean npm installation and production build.

[The upstream workflow](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40080996868) awaits maintainer approval. [The fork Test Suite](https://github.com/Aschenbath/nanobot/actions/runs/40080993400) completed on the exact current head. Docker, WebUI checks/build/browser, both TUI jobs, all Python jobs and Linux native acceptance passed. Linux Python 3.11/3.14 each passed 10,956 main tests (79 skipped) and 252 serial tests (one skipped). Windows Python passed 81 isolated update tests (five skipped), 10,658 main tests (135 skipped) and 244 serial tests (nine skipped); the previous supervisor timeout did not recur. Windows installer compatibility passed 80 tests with one skip.

The sole failing test job is native Windows acceptance, so aggregate CI remains failed. A clean, unchanged `3c022ada` build reproduces its executable-size error: 157,286,912 bytes, 512 bytes over the 150 MiB ceiling. The builder, TUI sources and verifier are unchanged by this feature. Independent #6428 addresses this upstream size limit and passes both native acceptance jobs on its own head; this PR does not include that change or count the failed native acceptance as a pass.

Implemented and tested with AI assistance. No live model credentials or external MCP deployments were used.

prs.title: fix(retry): prevent replay amplification and isolate backoff (NAN-313)
prs.body:
## Why

Nested retry owners multiply physical requests, replay already-delivered Telegram prefixes, and let failing destinations hold every outbound send slot while sleeping. Keep replay decisions with the domain owner, release resources before backoff, and remove duplicated recovery mechanics without adding a retry framework or dependency.

Fixes [NAN-313](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-313)

## What changed

- Hold outbound permits only for an adapter invocation, retaining bounded admission, destination FIFO, scheduled claim ordering, and pre-submission deadlines; add equal jitter to local manager/LLM backoff without changing server-hint rules.
- Prevent Telegram whole-message replay after per-part failures, disable nested SDK retries for internally created Bedrock clients, and close StepFun SSE response contexts before retry waits.
- Share request-only recovery across MCP wrappers and keep LLM stream/image/persistent recovery in an explicit domain loop; consolidate regression coverage into existing fixtures. No Tenacity dependency remains.

## Scope

Python outbound delivery, model-request retries, MCP wrapper recovery, and StepFun transcription resource lifetime. Preserve configured admission, scheduled unknown-result handling, provider continuation, cancellation, and public return shapes. Persistent-task recovery, other adapters' delivery policies, UI, configuration schemas, and dependency versions are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Removing nested retry budgets intentionally reaches exhaustion sooner; it does not promise equal success probability for every external fault sequence. Adapter-internal waits still occupy one invocation permit, and Telegram transport retries do not provide exactly-once delivery. Local jitter uses `[base / 2, base]`; provider/server Retry-After buffer and cap rules remain intact.

The final diff is production -77 lines and tests +668 lines, net +591. The proposed library adaptation was withdrawn because it added callbacks/state and maintenance cost without sufficient simplification.

## Blast Radius

ChannelManager scheduling affects ordinary outbound sends; Telegram and internally created Bedrock clients have intentional retry-policy changes. MCP tools/resources/prompts share one recovery owner, while rendering remains outside the replay boundary. Review focus: partial delivery, independent recovery budgets, active-permit release, cancellation, and response closure before sleep.

## Verification

Local checks ran on the exact published source delta against base `73a55e0b2fac17ae70641f028448201c4a0cb710`; commit preparation changes no source content. The current target branch is newer, so these local results are not merge-result CI results.

- **FAIL:** CI-scope Windows Python suite, isolated HOME, `-n 2 --dist loadfile`, the existing three CLI/native/WSL files excluded for serial execution, and `--cov=nanobot`: **9989 passed, 130 skipped, 5 failed; coverage 85.43%** (75% threshold unchanged). Four failures reproduce on the baseline environment: copied Scoop rg shim companion, Windows symlink permission, and two missing-USERNAME cases. The fifth is an unchanged shell-test marker-write race: normal focused runs pass on both snapshots; exposing the existing non-atomic marker window reproduces the same empty-content assertion on both. The full run remains FAIL.
- **PASS:** excluded serial CLI/native/WSL files: **222 passed, 1 skipped**. Ruff, import boundaries, dependency consistency, `git diff --check HEAD`, and strict typechecking of affected production files pass.
- **FAIL:** full-project BasedPyright retains the same two baseline `setproctitle` diagnostics; no affected-production diagnostics.
- **PASS:** real FastMCP stdio/connect/registry/reconnect/timeout/cancel/aclose comparison; five balanced fresh-process loopback SDK/MessageBus pairs preserve work/error/result counts; real unread-response SSE closure and cancellation regressions. These use deterministic local services, not production accounts or public models.

Performance evidence distinguishes the policy comparison from the final simplification rerun: before/after retry-policy probes measured Telegram 9→3 HTTP requests, successful-prefix submissions 3→1, and Bedrock continuous-503 requests 20→4. Final-source reruns preserve the reduced counts. An equal-work public-MessageBus fixture (65 sends, 33 completed destinations) reduces healthy-destination queueing under 32 sleeping retries from about 1009ms to 0.1ms. These are fault-isolation/request-count results, not general model throughput claims.

Seven new original-base/final bookkeeping pairs show transient→success p50 16.4→16.1µs, p99 31.7→33.5µs, and worst-run p99 37.7→43.1µs; provider-import medians are 101.7→107.5ms with overlapping ranges. No general speedup or zero-tail-regression claim. The issue records scope, acceptance criteria, measurements, and local evidence identifiers; raw local logs remain outside tracked source.

prs.title: refactor(channels): move tool hint rendering out of core
prs.body:
## Why

Tool activity should describe what happened, not decide how every chat platform must display it. The runner currently generates both structured events and a universal shortened hint; this change moves that presentation decision to each channel while preserving existing delivery behavior.

## What changed

- Core hooks publish tool start/end/error facts with call IDs, arguments and results, without generating hint text; remove the presentation-length plumbing from the agent loop and hook assembly.
- Add channel-owned `prepare_tool_events()` before queueing. Plain-text channels reuse the shared formatter, while WebSocket, Linear and Weixin's native progress path consume structured events directly. Project once so retries retain the same envelope and multipart delivery cursor.
- Migrate both classic CLI paths and document the channel/callback contract. WebUI and TUI keep their existing grouping and rendering.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Core: structured tool facts] --> B[Target channel]
    B --> C[Native activity / WebSocket events]
    B --> D[Optional shared text formatter]
    C --> E[Platform-specific presentation]
    D --> E
```

## Scope

Preserves the current wire/storage formats, per-channel visibility defaults and overrides, tool start versus terminal visibility policy, hint-length setting, thread metadata and FIFO/retry handling. No execution, model-context, WebUI layout or file-list UX redesign.

## Tradeoffs

Reuse `ProgressEvent` rather than adding a second tool-event protocol. Third-party channels inheriting the default text projection retain readable starts; native consumers opt out of that projection. Direct `on_progress` consumers must accept `tool_events` to display tool activity instead of relying on core-generated text.

## Blast Radius

The change touches tool progress for local and provider-hosted calls, channel adapters, and classic CLI output. Regression coverage retains Telegram quotes, Feishu cards, Slack text, Linear actions, Weixin native/legacy delivery, Email suppression, and same-envelope WhatsApp multipart retries.

## Verification

- Final head `0216b1cc292938ab6415161c9a40f5095c628dc3`: [GitHub Test Suite](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40706269848) passed all 15 selected jobs, including Python 3.11, Python 3.14 with coverage, Windows Python 3.14, strict BasedPyright, WebUI checks/build/browser, TUI on Linux and Windows, native package acceptance on both platforms, Docker, and the required aggregate gate.
- Local focused regressions: 1,041 passed, 3 optional-channel dependency skips. A separate serial CLI process matched CI's test grouping: 254 passed, 1 Windows-only skip. Full Ruff and Python import-boundary checks passed locally; the shared local environment did not provide a clean full BasedPyright run, so complete strict typing is established by the fresh CI environment.
- The CI follow-up fixes an overlooked privacy-test expectation: tool starts now carry empty core text rather than a core-rendered hint. Exact visible-text and final-response assertions still protect against internal reasoning leaking into progress. No tests were disabled and no CI gates were relaxed.
- Incorporated `main` at `55210eb9f1217bcddb53b8987bcd74ecadd975af` with an ordinary merge, preserving the centralized WebUI outbound owner and WebSocket's structured-event opt-out. Kept wire/transcript/history regression coverage and did not restore the removed socket-side projector.
- No live third-party IM credential tests were performed. The PR remains Draft; this update does not approve, merge, or deploy it.

Contributes to NAN-375

prs.title: feat(web-search): add Serply (Google Search API) provider
prs.body:
## What

Adds [Serply](https://serply.io) as a web search provider, following the same pattern as the existing Serper provider (#4406). Serply is a Google SERP API; selecting it routes the `web_search` tool through `https://api.serply.io/v1/search/` with the user's own API key.

## Why

Gives users another API-key-backed Google search option alongside Serper, useful when they already hold a Serply key or want an alternative to avoid rate limits on free backends. Like every other keyed provider, it falls back to DuckDuckGo when no key is configured.

## Notes

- Serply support is optional, and behavior is unchanged when `SERPLY_API_KEY` is unset. The provider falls back to DuckDuckGo without a key, matching Serper and the other keyed providers.
- Follows the existing provider pattern in `nanobot/agent/tools/web.py`: an entry in `SEARCH_PROVIDER_OPTIONS` (which feeds the WebUI settings picker and CLI onboarding), a branch in `_effective_provider`, and a `_search_serply` method mirroring `_search_serper`. The request sends an explicit `User-Agent` because Serply sits behind Cloudflare, which rejects requests without one.
- Tests added in `tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`, mirroring the six Serper tests: keyless concurrency fallback, mocked search (URL, headers, params, formatting), env key resolution, DuckDuckGo fallback, HTTP error, and rate limiting. Network is mocked.
- Docs updated in `docs/configuration.md`: provider table row, config example, and the provider enum. See the [Serply documentation](https://serply.io/docs) for the response fields used (`results[].title/link/description`).

## Testing

- `uv run python -m pytest tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py -q`: 51 passed (45 existing plus 6 new).
- `uv run ruff check nanobot/agent/tools/web.py tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`: all checks passed.
- `uv run basedpyright nanobot/agent/tools/web.py`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Live-tested against the real Serply API with a valid key: `execute(query="retrieval augmented generation", count=3)` returned three normalized results in the shared plaintext format, and `_effective_provider()` resolved to `serply` with a key and `duckduckgo` without one.

Disclosure: I work with Serply. Happy to adjust scope, naming, or drop this
entirely if it isn't a direction you want for the project.

prs.title: feat(matrix): add "listen" group policy (observe room, reply on mention)
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a third Matrix group policy value — **`"listen"`** — for rooms where the bot should read the whole conversation but reply only when mentioned (#6288).

Under `mention`, messages that fail the policy check are dropped outright (`_on_message`), so the bot has no knowledge of the conversation when it's finally mentioned. Under `open` it replies to everything. `listen` closes that gap:

- Every message from an **allowed sender** in a listen room is ingested into a bounded per-room buffer.
- The bot replies **only when mentioned** — same `m.mentions` / `allowRoomMentions` semantics as `mention`.
- On a mention-triggered turn, the buffered chatter rides along as **trusted runtime context** so the answer reflects the intervening conversation.

## How context is attached

Uses the existing trusted channel seam `RUNTIME_CONTEXT_INPUT_META` (`nanobot/runtime_context.py`) — this is the first channel producer of `_runtime_context_blocks`, whose docstring describes exactly this: *"trusted, channel-produced context blocks"* read from inbound metadata. Blocks are appended to the turn's user content and persisted with a display-time-removal marker, so the LLM retains the context in subsequent turns while users never see the injected block as chat output.

Bounds per the `RuntimeContextBlock` docstring's requirement ("callers must bound and delimit content obtained from untrusted sources"): 30 messages / 6,000 chars per room, 500 chars per line, header-delimited block, buffer cleared once consumed. No LLM calls for unheard messages; no agent-core changes.

## Behavior details

- Deny-listed senders are never buffered.
- Direct rooms (≤2 members) bypass the policy entirely, as today.
- Media messages buffer a caption or `[attachment]` note — downloads/transcription are not triggered for unheard messages.
- Composes with per-room `groupPolicyOverrides` from #6287 once that lands (a trivial rebase in `_should_process_message`).

## Fixes #6288

## Tests

Seven new tests in `nanobot/channels/matrix/tests/test_matrix_channel.py`:

1. `"listen"` accepted via attribute and camelCase config; unknown policy values still rejected.
2. Buffer bounds: oldest-dropped at 30 entries, 6,000-char budget, 500-char line truncation.
3. Unmentioned messages buffered with no reply/typing; the next mention triggers one turn carrying a bounded `matrix_room_transcript` block containing the buffered line; buffer cleared (subsequent mention carries no block).
4. Denied senders neither replied to nor buffered.
5. Direct rooms unaffected (no buffering, normal DM path).
6. `open` policy rooms never buffer (regression guard).
7. Media captions buffered as notes.

Verified locally: 127 matrix-channel tests pass, 152 channel-contract tests pass, `ruff check nanobot tests` clean, import-boundary check passes, `basedpyright` clean (0 errors) on touched files. WebUI locale copy added for all 10 languages (en, es, fr, id, ja, ko, pt-BR, vi, zh-CN, zh-TW).

> Note: this branch is based on current `main` without #6287. If #6287 merges first, expect small conflicts in `_should_process_message` (adjacent lines) and the docs table — happy to rebase.

prs.body:
## Why Users need to correct a sent message without creating another sidebar topic. This implements the approved in-place edit: keep the prefix before the selected user message, replace that message and its entire suffix, and generate a new reply in the same session. Related to [NAN-92](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92/webui-支持编辑并重新发送已发送的用户消息). ## What changed - Add **Edit message** beside Copy in the existing desktop/mobile message actions, using the existing `EditIcon`. Edit directly inside the native user-message bubble with its own draft, Cancel/Resend controls, actionable errors and translations in all 10 locales. Composer drafts, quotes, attachments and waiting input remain separate. - Commit the replacement model records and display facts in one session-owner SQLite transaction. Preserve session identity and settings, rotate the history generation, invalidate obsolete summaries/provider continuation, and record retry identity so an accepted input executes once. Both histories now live in the same database; there is no file-backed replacement journal. - Reuse ordinary latest-thread reads for the source snapshot. Confirming the edit is the only mutation. Validate one page-independent source revision and stable message identity inside the transaction, rather than maintaining a separate prepare protocol and an eight-field anchor. - Share prefix retention between in-place replacement and the existing **New conversation** fork. Keep idle admission, the normal execution queue, cancellation safety, and generation fences across drafts, streams, HTTP pages, trace details, navigation caches and late subagent results. - The historical cleanup removed 106 net production lines without moving the implementation into a replacement framework. Original message text is used for the current source check, not retained in the retry receipt. - Retain two Windows PowerShell installer regressions for unrelated uv/pipx modules; main now supplies the equivalent no-auto-import implementation. - Keep a native touch input round attached to its original target across lazy Markdown replacement, including move/end/cancel and listener cleanup. - Admit supported Windows baseline TUI builds with a bounded 160 MiB executable budget; retain the download, required-file, checksum/source/license and oversize guards. ## Scope The first version supports persisted ordinary user text in saved WebUI sessions. Attachments, quotes, session/CLI/MCP mentions, slash/shell commands and special/system deliveries are explicitly rejected rather than resent with lost metadata. Temporary Chat has no persisted edit target; shared history cannot be edited from an individual conversation. The WebUI and gateway ship together, without an edit-specific compatibility gate or older-gateway fallback. Resend is the only destructive authorization, with no second modal. The URL, session ID, handle, title, creation identity, workspace, permissions and model settings remain unchanged. There is no backup topic, hidden persistent fork or version tree. Previously executed file/Shell effects are not rolled back. ## Tradeoffs Model history and display facts remain separate projections, but replacement is atomic in the existing SQLite store. A pre-acceptance failure preserves the previous effective history and editable draft. A model failure after acceptance keeps the new failed turn instead of restoring the discarded suffix. A changed source is rejected rather than guessed from a page-local index. ## Blast Radius This touches session admission/persistence, WebUI transcript reads and WebSocket delivery, frontend history reconciliation, and subagent result ownership. The main risks are cross-client races, stale events restoring a removed suffix, and retry/crash behavior. Existing new-fork behavior is covered separately; this does not redesign subagent cancellation or external-effect rollback. ## Verification ### Current CI follow-up Current published source: `d06d326ad2fe6c7c85ab86eae1aa129584ed0a5c`. Historical real-gateway/provider acceptance below was not rerun for this test-only repair. ### Historical verification Cleanup snapshot: `cc083aaf269bd6f92a70ddb863162c25ea5543ad`, an ordinary commit on `95463f90389354244b0973c25d34ea0757a7e55b`. Its committed tree matches the tested cleanup candidate exactly. Historical CI-verified source: `36c5adc9d305f567f026d81291331af1b410398b`. The requested rebase, two ordinary CI repairs and a test-only timeout diagnostic preserve the feature semantics. The final CI tests merge `373554240816c48e5b5155ce72becdf43b48bd7a` against target `0254bf121736bf02bbcd9e988a2c1b3fc265f8d9`. The editor-specific 54/133/10-case results retain their original snapshot identity. | Check | Actual result | | --- | --- | | Cleanup snapshot: Python white-box regressions | **54 passed**: edit/fork identity, source revisions, stale/busy rejection, SQLite rollback and real process exits around commit, cancellation/admission and retained model context | | Cleanup snapshot: full ThreadShell and editor component files | **133 passed**, including source-read failure, cancellation, independent drafts and one confirmed request | | Cleanup snapshot: full-project Ruff, strict BasedPyright and Python import boundaries | **PASS**, including 0 BasedPyright errors/warnings/notes | | Cleanup snapshot: full-project WebUI typecheck, lint and import checks | **PASS**; prs.title: feat(webui): sync unread activity across devices
prs.body:
Linear: [NAN-367](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-367) ## Why A result completed on one WebUI device currently leaves its activity indicator in that browser only. Store shared reading progress in the Gateway so viewing a result on a phone clears the indicator on the desktop too, including after reconnects or browser-storage loss. ## What changed - Persist generation-bound latest-result/read positions in the existing SQLite history header. Advance the result position in the completion transaction and acknowledge only an observed cursor; late receipts cannot consume newer results. - Publish small authenticated `session_read_state` updates instead of refetching every device's session list. Duplicate receipts do not update rows or broadcast, and reading does not change model history, transcript revision/ETag, or activity ordering. - Replace browser-local activity ownership with server state. Confirm only a foreground, visible live tail after the result is installed; recover missing final content after a delivery gap, and do not confirm a conversation covered by a narrow-screen file preview. ## Scope Shared reading progress for authorized WebUI clients of the same Gateway. Temporary chats stay connection-private; browser notification permissions and sounds stay device-local. This does not add TUI reading acknowledgements, cross-Gateway/cloud sync, an account system, or a notification center. ## Tradeoffs SQLite schema v3 baselines pre-existing, imported, and fork-copied history as read. Existing browser-local unread indicators can reset once during upgrade; their old chat-ID sets cannot reconstruct exact cross-device reading positions. The feature adds a small metadata cost rather than claiming zero-overhead synchronization. ## Blast Radius Session storage/migration, session-list and transcript projections, authenticated WebUI mutations/events, and viewport reading observations. No AgentLoop/Runner or provider changes. A generation mismatch is reconciled from a fresh authoritative snapshot instead of guessing the order of opaque generations. ## Verification - Related Python suites: **785 passed**, including real loopback HTTP and two authenticated WebSocket clients, persistence, migration, old-generation rejection, and late-receipt behavior. - Nine related WebUI suites: **676 passed**; TypeScript, ESLint, client/Python import-boundary checks, focused strict BasedPyright/Ruff, and the production build passed. Build output includes a >500 kB chunk-size warning; no threshold was raised. - Chromium 156 with two isolated browser contexts: cross-device clearing without a peer list refetch, recovery after clearing browser storage, no premature confirmation before final-body recovery, and 390px preview occlusion/close behavior. Browser fixtures used synthetic history and injected completion timing with real Gateway HTTP/ACK/broadcast; no real model was called. - Primary performance result: the full HTTP session-list round trip was **4.64 → 5.23 ms median** for 64 sessions × 128 turns, five interleaved trials per side on local loopback. This is about **+0.59 ms**, not a speedup. [Measurement details and limitations](#performance-evidence). Remote CI passed for `9999ce097fd1d1c0d0f1436a367091112997eb11`: [Test Suite, attempt 2](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40352694937/attempts/2) (**15/15 jobs successful**). The Windows installer job passed after one diagnostic failed-jobs rerun following a 90-second PowerShell timeout; its cause remains unconfirmed, and no installer code, concurrency, or timeout was changed. Local tests and loopback measurements do not establish Windows, public-network, or mobile-device performance.
Performance evidence: methods, ranges, and write/fan-out checks Measurements used Python 3.12.10 on Linux/WSL, synthetic sessions, actual WAL and `synchronous=FULL` connections, identical Python dependencies, fresh isolated fixture directories, and baseline source archived from `f23a6d1485572e1485a7892abe17fc8d6a3b46bf`. Seeding, warmups, trace audits, and separate profiler runs were excluded. Both storage experiments interleaved baseline/candidate for five trials per side with 20 measured samples per operation after three warmups. Their 4,800 formal samples had zero failures and unchanged candidate source fingerprints. The table reports the median of trial medians, with the range of those five medians. Storage values use the eager runtime API-call phase, excluding subsequent correctness-consumer overhead; outputs were still consumed and checked inside the enclosing verified measurement. | Path | Baseline ms | Candidate ms | | --- | --- | --- | | Runtime metadata list: 64 sessions × 8 turns | 0.5652 (0.5546–0.5711) | 0.6263 (0.5755–0.6429) | | Runtime metadata list: 64 sessions × 512 turns | 0.5493 (0.5282–0.5609) | 0.5913 (0.5625–0.6362) | | Runtime metadata list: 1,000 sessions × 20 turns | 6.7788 (6.2535–6.8731) | 7.8386 (7.7030–7.9964) | | Completion commit: 64 sessions × 512 turns | 4.4890 (4.2584–7.2770) | 4.6526 (4.4934–7.0866) | | Advancing read receipt, same dataset | — | 4.4992 (4.2858–6.9285) | | Duplicate receipt, same dataset | — | 0.1487 (0.1239–0.1616) | At fixed session count, longer stored conversation text did not produce a proportional cost increase in these measurements. There is a measurable metadata cost; the completion-commit ranges overlap, so the small difference is not evidence of a reliable speedup or regression. Separate worker profiling identified SQLite commit as the main write-path cost; durability was not relaxed to reduce latency. The network experiment used 64 sessions × 128 turns, five interleaved trials per side, 30 measured HTTP requests after two warmups, and 20 measured WS batches per case after two warmups. Eight real authenticated WebSocket receivers stayed connected, with 1/4/8 clients acknowledging the same result concurrently. All expected replies/state frames were consumed and verified; there were zero failures. | Network path | Baseline ms | Candidate ms | | --- | --- | --- | | Full `GET /api/sessions` | 4.6445 (4.5542–4.6576) | 5.2293 (5.1452–5.2522) | | One advancing receipt, broadcast to eight receivers | — | 5.5881 (5.5095–5.6467) | | One duplicate receipt, no broadcast | — | 0.6937 (0.6608–0.7339) | | Four simultaneous receipts, replies and one state update/receiver | — | 7.8135 (7.6993–7.9386) | | Eight simultaneous receipts, replies and one state update/receiver | — | 10.8497 (10.7429–10.9767) | | Eight duplicate receipts, no broadcast | — | 5.2376 (5.1923–5.3800) | The decoded HTTP JSON body was 64,442 → 70,458 bytes for 64 sessions (+6,016 bytes); that is not compressed wire traffic. Write audits confirmed one changed row for an advancing receipt, and zero SQL DML/row changes or WAL-content/data-version change for duplicate/zero receipts. Concurrent acknowledgements of the same result produced only one advance and one state event per receiver. The browser check separately verified that observing on B did not add a `/api/sessions` request on A. These are warm-cache synthetic storage and loopback protocol measurements on a shared host, not cold-start/migration, public-network, browser-throughput, long-duration stress, or mobile-power measurements. Storage producer counts are not network-client counts; the network results above come from separate real sockets. Detailed scripts, raw samples, dependency/source fingerprints, and profiles are retained with the local verification artifacts, not embedded in this PR.

prs.title: refactor(webui): centralize outbound delivery (NAN-365)
prs.body:
## Why

Adding a WebUI event or changing history behavior still requires editing the WebSocket channel's business-specific send paths. Centralize outbound presentation, stream state, durability policy and delivery-turn completion so those changes no longer spread into connection transport code.

Tracks [NAN-365](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-365), which contains the **before/after Mermaid architecture diagrams**, ownership changes and acceptance boundaries. This follows the completed [NAN-102](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-102) wire-encoding extraction rather than reopening it.

## What changed

- Replace the old projector with one `WebUIOutboundDelivery` owner for ordinary messages, text/reasoning streams, file-edit events and the existing hydration/discard/session-refresh hooks.
- Reduce its transport contract to recipient snapshots and raw-frame enqueue. Move feature-specific payload construction, transcript policy, stream buffers, pairing projection and WebUI delivery completion out of the socket channel; retain the existing connection queues and drain behavior.
- Complete public payload types, tighten import boundaries and migrate tests to emitted frames/durable history, including a subscriber joining while history persistence is awaiting.

## Scope

Preserve public wire fields, history schemas, BaseChannel streaming entry points, temporary-chat/restart-control policy, offline persistence, incomplete recovery, audience isolation and late-owner handling. `SessionState` remains the persistent authority; the moved completion logic is the WebUI delivery projection, not Agent execution ownership.

No frontend, AgentLoop/runner, database migration, WS-to-HTTP mutation redesign, admission-receipt change, new event bus or deployment is included. Existing command-router changes only reconnect its outbound hooks to their owner.

## Tradeoffs

Evolve the existing projector into a single delivery owner instead of adding a coordinator/effect-plan layer. Keep read-only connection identity snapshots at this adapter edge rather than introducing opaque-recipient wrappers; the owner never performs socket I/O. Each send captures its recipients before the persistence await, while subsequent broadcasts take their own snapshots.

## Blast Radius

WebUI and TUI outbound delivery share this path. The principal regression risks are stream ordering/merging, history failures clearing a turn too early, audience selection and slow-client isolation. The channel retains ready ordering, writer budgets, timeouts, retirement and in-flight drain accounting.

## Verification

All verification below is bound to `8acf73a1975e689a467a6d9c4c50bcff8544513d`; no product or test source changed during this readiness pass.

- **Fresh white-box regression: 1694 passed**, 0 failed/errors/skipped, in 73.38s: all colocated WebSocket tests and WebUI Python tests, selected session history/recovery, bus, channel-manager streaming/reasoning/compaction/concurrency, turn helpers, response-source and architecture tests.
- Strict BasedPyright **1.39.0** for all `nanobot/webui` and `nanobot/channels/websocket/runtime.py`: **0 errors, warnings or notes**. Ruff on all 11 changed Python files, import boundaries (13 rules / 217 files), production imports and diff whitespace: passed.
- **Public black-box acceptance passed** against a real isolated CLI gateway and a local deterministic OpenAI-compatible model fixture: authentication rejection/acceptance; ordinary command and literal-shell delivery/replay; all-connection session refresh; text/reasoning streaming; a second client attaching to a live turn; actual file-edit tool activity and durable replay; all clients disconnecting before completion; and process restart restoring the completed result without replaying the model.
- **Built WebUI browser acceptance passed** without route mocks: real access-secret login, normal composer send, streamed fixture-model answer, terminal event, durable refresh and narrow-viewport reachability. Bun **1.3.6**, Playwright **1.64.1**, Chromium **156.0.8078.4**; no page errors or unexpected HTTP failures. The existing empty-draft 404-to-null behavior is preserved, not counted as a product failure.
- Owned gateways, local model server and browser were closed; all three temporary listening ports were checked closed and temporary runtime state removed. Daily/handed-off services and real user sessions/configuration were not used or changed.
- [Exact-head CI, run 40358925261, attempt 1](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40358925261): **15/15 jobs successful**, including Python 3.11/3.14, Windows, installer/process compatibility, WebUI checks/browser, TUI on both platforms, native package acceptance, Docker and required gates.

Test selection:

```bash
python -m pytest -q nanobot/channels/websocket/tests tests/webui tests/session/test_display_history.py tests/session/test_recovery.py tests/bus tests/channels/test_websocket_application_boundary.py tests/channels/test_channel_manager_delta_coalescing.py tests/channels/test_channel_manager_reasoning.py tests/channels/test_channel_manager_compaction_notices.py tests/channels/test_channel_manager_concurrency.py tests/utils/test_webui_turn_helpers.py tests/agent/test_response_source.py tests/architecture/test_import_boundaries.py
basedpyright --pythonpath <test-environment-python> nanobot/webui nanobot/channels/websocket/runtime.py
python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries
```

Local white-box environment: Linux, Python **3.12.10**, websockets **16.0**, pytest **9.1.1**. Packaging fixtures used hatchling **1.32.4** only through an isolated test dependency directory; shared runtime dependencies were not changed. An initial long temporary path exceeded the existing SSH control-socket limit; the full same suite passed after correcting the harness path. Browser harness assumptions about intentionally hidden `/model` responses and topic-dependent composer labels were corrected before the final complete pass. Failed-attempt inputs/results were retained; no tests were skipped or product source patched to make verification pass.

Black-box verification used fresh isolated state and a local model fixture, not a commercial/real-account model; external tokenizer download was blocked and the gateway used its existing UTF-8 byte estimates. This is affected-contract verification rather than a claim of universal compatibility or absence of risk. The PR is Ready for review; formal review/approval is still required. prs.title: fix(webui): keep saved topics bound to their project
prs.body:
## Why

Saved topics can show the directory picker again when their loaded history contains only assistant or automation output. The gateway also accepts directory changes while those topics are idle, allowing old context to be reused in another execution scope.

Follow the project-binding direction agreed in #6505, using persisted-session existence as the boundary rather than inspecting message history.

## What changed

- Report saved sessions as project-locked and keep the picker available only for unpersisted new-topic drafts, including when connecting to hosts without the marker.
- Reject project changes both in explicit scope updates and message envelopes, rechecking the stored directory inside the metadata write transaction. Keep same-project access-mode changes available while idle.
- Refresh clients when a draft is persisted, document the boundary, and cover empty saved sessions, admission races, deleted project directories, and draft-to-saved UI state.

## Scope

No session schema changes, history scans, or additional persistent binding markers. Saved forks follow the same rule. This does not enable moving an existing topic to another project; start a new topic instead. Temporary-chat restrictions remain unchanged.

CI follow-up adjusts Cron rearm tests to await the owned timer task instead of putting synchronous disk writes under a two-second deadline. All operation, cancellation, persistence and schedule assertions remain. Goal shutdown uses the existing failure-stack diagnostic with its unchanged five-second deadline.

## Blast Radius

WebUI and TUI clients share gateway scope validation. Older clients may still display the picker, but the updated gateway rejects a directory change. New clients also hide the picker for saved sessions on older hosts; gateway enforcement requires updating the host.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Local tests, lint, typecheck, and builds were not run; validation ran in remote CI.
- [Final-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40663844741), attempt 2: all selected jobs passed, including Python 3.11/3.14, Windows Python, WebUI unit/build and browser checks, Linux/Windows TUI, Docker, and the required gate. Native package and Windows installer acceptance were not selected for this diff.
- The final-head first attempt passed Python and WebUI unit/build checks but failed dependency downloads (Bun tarball integrity checks and npm `ECONNRESET`). One failed-job rerun passed without changing dependency locks or integrity verification.
- The original Windows goal-test shutdown timeout did not recur. Its cause remains unconfirmed; the added stack diagnostics are not a claimed runtime fix.

Related to #6505.
Contributes to NAN-380.

Thanks to @Xiaoyu-hub for identifying and investigating the gateway/UI mismatch in #6505. Their contribution is credited with a `Co-authored-by` trailer in the fix commit; please retain it when merging.

prs.title: feat(webui): keep delegated work within reach
prs.body:
## Summary

Long replies push running delegated work out of reach, while keeping every finished task above the composer creates another backlog. This change gives active work and saved results different homes.

- Attach a slightly inset drawer flush above the rounded composer. Its full header strip is the handle: default collapsed, no automatic opening, click/keyboard support, and mouse/touch dragging that follows the held pointer before snapping on release. Cancel restores the initial state. The drawer is non-modal, the composer stays editable, and the height-bounded task list scrolls independently.
- Keep queued/running/stopping tasks reachable across parent completion and later inputs. Preserve displayed rows and their order while reading; append newly active work. Closing prunes terminal rows. After all work ends, a truthful four-second completion/failure receipt retires, paused by hover, focus or details; cold reload does not resurrect old receipts.
- Archive terminal results as compact, default-collapsed groups at their originating prompt. Temporarily unmatched results appear under **Other tasks**, then relocate when the source history loads, retaining detail and focus handoff.
- Render complete successful-result Markdown in the drawer without character slicing or a two-line clamp. Keep full task conversations, revision ordering, reconnect recovery, scope boundaries and per-task stopping.
- Use one running ring per task header and static tool-activity marks. Success removes the ring without replacing it with a green check or another badge; an empty icon slot preserves alignment. Non-success states remain visible. Share archive columns, keep whole-row detail access, and retain accessible progress and 44px mobile controls.
- Keep details to a single-line title/control header, without repeating the elapsed duration already shown in outer rows. Long titles retain their complete accessible name and tooltip.

## Tracking and scope

[NAN-361 — 改进子任务可达性：贴附输入框的可拖动抽屉与结果归档](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-361)

Frontend presentation and interaction only: no Gateway execution authority, authentication, task persistence, protocol or cancellation contract changes; no global task-monitoring page. Rebased onto main `4701218719eb8a9206f0447006d7914f15590876`, observed at the authorized rebase checkpoint. Both the appearance and loaded-session-search fixtures were retained when resolving the fixture entry import conflict.

## Archive heading refinement — `f35ea30814777c62b9cc3d7d132f7946fba71c8f`

- Reuse the bundled nanobot SVG mark in task-result summaries. Keep the mark, title, completion count and disclosure on one row on mobile, while preserving task-label width and shared elapsed-time alignment.
- This snapshot: **50 focused unit tests** and **4 focused browser scenarios** passed, together with application/browser TypeScript, ESLint, import boundaries, production build and `git diff --check`. Browser checks preserve archive columns, disclosure/detail focus, light/dark appearance and narrow long-title controls. Built-Gateway checks at 1440/390/320px confirmed a single-row heading with browser-only synthetic completed-task input.
- New-head CI is pending at publication. Earlier verification below remains bound to its original snapshots, including the recorded local touch-test limitation.

## Compact running control — `8db8fccb79230c7320da1e76ea4fbd5bf03232fe`

- Reuse the Composer's existing `ComposerActionIcon` for the running task's circular Stop control, without a separate visible Running label or ring. Keep the localized running description accessible to screen readers, queued/non-success status feedback, and existing cancellation/error/retry behavior.
- This snapshot: **50 focused unit tests** and **4 focused browser scenarios** passed, together with application/browser TypeScript, ESLint, import boundaries, production build and `git diff --check`. Built-Gateway header alignment, mobile control size and focus checks passed at 1440/390/320px with browser-only synthetic task/history inputs.
- New-head CI is not yet complete at publication. The earlier full-unit, full-browser and CI results below retain their original snapshots.

## Review fixes — `c9896c5a195f9a85f140c19ddaabd69911098076`

- Keep Composer slash/session-mention palettes reachable above the drawer. Recognize React-owned result portals as part of its interaction boundary so image zoom does not dismiss the viewer and drawer.
- Move the single-task Stop action into the detail header beside its status and close controls. Preserve pending/disabled state, cancellation, failure/retry feedback, focus handoff and 44px mobile targets.
- Final local Windows checks: **3440 tests across 192 files**, application/browser TypeScript, ESLint, import boundaries, production build and `git diff --check` passed. **7 focused browser scenarios** passed, including desktop/narrow palette selection, image zoom and header Stop controls. Built-Gateway header checks at 1440/390/320px passed with browser-only synthetic task/history responses.
- Known local limitation: an earlier full drawer browser run had **25 passed / 1 failed** in the existing CDP-touch reopening case, which also failed on the unmodified PR head. That failure remains unresolved; timeouts, retries and assertions were not relaxed.
- New-head CI is pending at publication. Earlier CI and coverage results below retain their original snapshot.

## Earlier verification — `c903cfe999f6899dfe9598aa6d7dc9ac81a18c7e`

- Final-head [Test Suite #40213348743](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40213348743): **SUCCESS**. WebUI checks/build, **385 full browser tests**, Docker, `webui` and `CI required` passed. CI's unit suite passed **3440 tests in 192 files** with statements/lines **94.27%**, branches **89.05%**, functions **91.8%**. Python/Windows/TUI/native jobs were skipped by scope, not counted as executed platform acceptance.
- Local complete WebUI coverage: **3438 tests in 192 files**, same **94.27 / 89.05 / 91.8 / 94.27%** totals, original coverage thresholds retained. Relevant Python task/control/lifecycle/persistence and real-Gateway smoke contracts: **128 passed**.
- Task drawer, history-boundary, loaded-session-search and appearance browser checks: **54 cases repeated twice with two workers, 108 passing executions**, no retries. Coverage includes held mouse/CDP-touch positions, cancellation and rebound, composing Escape, editable input, independent scrolling, full Markdown, details/focus, reading retention, four-second retirement, archives, pane/session/portal boundaries, reduced motion, both themes and short/narrow viewports.
- Import boundaries; **41 import-checker tests, one Windows directory-casing skip on Linux**; application/browser TypeScript; ESLint; frozen install/lockfile checks; independent production build; and `git diff --check` passed. The existing large-chunk build advisory remains. Local Bun was **1.3.6**, while CI used **1.3.13**; actual local dependencies were Playwright 1.64.1, Vitest 2.1.9, Vite 5.4.21, React 18.3.1 and Pele 1.9.0.
- Independent authenticated Gateway + built WebUI + controlled local model, with new empty data: actual `stopping → cancelled` while parent output and siblings continue; success/failure while the parent remains active; a child surviving parent completion and later input; indistinguishable wrong-owner/missing 404 and unauthenticated 401; actual WebSocket close and missed-completion/new-task recovery; fresh-context active-only restoration; and terminal state/result persistence across an owned Gateway restart with no task re-execution. No paid model calls, real credentials or user history were used.
- Real paginated history: delay an older HTTP read while details are open, load the actual originating prompt, verify one relocated archive, retained details and replacement-row focus; the same reading prompt moved **0.25px**. Screenshots of the held drag, complete results, narrow archive and retained reading position were inspected. No page runtime errors in the real-task sequence.
- All new verification processes and temporary runtime directories were cleaned up. The handed-off user preview was not restarted/stopped/replaced, and all **554** existing `nanobot/web/dist` file hashes remain unchanged. New builds used a separate ignored output directory.

The readiness pass corrected a stale default-expanded integration expectation and browser sampling before animation/Markdown settlement, without relaxing held-position, non-overlap, cancellation, scroll-isolation or <1px reading assertions. Read-only white-box checks found no confirmed reachable blocker; the final follow-up commit is tests-only. Browser acceptance is headless Chromium on Linux with mobile emulation/CDP touch, not physical iOS/Android, Safari, native IME or assistive-technology certification. Offline mode alone did not close an existing Chromium socket, so recovery proof additionally closed the recorded native transport while offline; no fixture task events substituted for real Gateway state. This verification is not formal review approval or a merge.

- Remove CSS whose DOM/state/animation consumer no longer exists; keep the active queue entrance animation, reduced-motion handling and message virtualization.
- Remove 730 unused translation-path instances across 40 JSON files and ten languages. All retained values, interpolation tokens and object order are unchanged, including the new appearance and attachment strings.

## Scope

This is the first, conservative batch from the repository-wide audit: 105 files, +209/-1284, including the focused CI test repair. Public/compatibility API retirement, production fixed-mode narrowing, security-guard removal and 224 uncertain translation candidates are deliberately excluded. Previously suspected history-fixture methods were kept after current-base WebSocket consumers were found. No dependencies, lockfiles, configuration or CI definitions change.

## Blast Radius

Affected consumers include channel callback/queue plumbing, session/history and dev-server helpers, QR connection flows, composer attachments and TUI footer rendering. SDK callback signatures, client-owned authentication, MIME sniff/whitelist/size budgets, real dev/browser URLs, recovery checks and resource ownership remain intact. prs.body:
## Why

When a completed subtask has a long result, reading it scrolls the only detail-opening control out of view. The remaining result looks like part of the task row but is ordinary selectable Markdown, so clicking it does not open the task conversation.

Tracks [NAN-364 — 保持子任务长结果中的详情入口可见](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-364). The user explicitly narrowed the report to an already-open task list, not the drawer handle.

## What changed

- Keep each task header visible within its own result while the drawer scrolls, with an opaque surface above result controls. The following task naturally replaces it at the task boundary.
- Preserve the existing detail button, stop action, native Markdown selection, links, code copying and image controls; no new click handler or duplicated selection state.
- Extend desktop/narrow browser coverage for hit testing over a scrolled code-copy control, detail access near the end of a long result, native selection, exact reading-position/focus restoration and opening the next task.

## Scope

One production layout change plus the existing browser scenario and fixture. No Gateway, protocol, persistence, task execution, drawer gesture or shared-instance changes.

## Tradeoffs

The current task's existing 36px desktop / 44px narrow header remains visible while reading its result. This keeps an explicit, keyboard-accessible detail entry without turning selectable Markdown into a large nested button or intercepting links and image viewers.

## Verification

- Regression first: the desktop and narrow long-result scenarios both failed on the unchanged production source because the detail row had zero visible viewport intersection; both pass with the fix.
- A second controlled hit test exposed a code-copy control intercepting the first sticky-header version. Raising the task header above result controls passes that test at both widths.
- Final `bun run typecheck`, `lint`, `check:imports`, `test:imports` (**42 tests**), `build`, and `test:coverage` (**3442 tests in 192 files**) passed. Coverage: statements/lines **94.26%**, branches **89.06%**, functions **91.81%**. The existing large-chunk build advisory remains.
- `bun run test:browser subagent-dock.spec.ts`: **26 passed**, including the changed regression, touch dragging, detail focus, cancellation, palettes, image viewers and archives.
- Final full `bun run test:browser`: **394 passed / 1 failed**. `history-boundary.spec.ts` → “archived task results stay with the retained boundary when earlier messages load” fails its 48px held-anchor assertion. A bounded five-run comparison reproduced the same assertion on the unchanged parent (**1 passed / 4 failed**) and this head (**4 passed / 1 failed**). That fixture renders the archive, not `SubagentTaskDock`. The full command remains FAIL; this PR does not change history physics or weaken its assertion. Publishing as Draft with this limitation recorded.
- Full App + actual Workbench/portaled Composer, using browser-local synthetic API/WebSocket task data: desktop mouse and 390px emulated-touch detail open/close passed. After reading a long result, closing details retained scrollTop exactly (1885→1885 desktop, 6199→6199 narrow). This is frontend acceptance, not real task execution or physical-device certification.

An earlier concurrent local verification run failed three unit cases and two import-check subprocess cases; unchanged isolated full reruns passed, followed by the successful final full commands above. No timeout, retry count, assertions or production behavior was relaxed to obtain a passing result. CI is not yet complete at publication.

prs.title: fix(webui): retain history touch gestures across message replacement
prs.body:
## Why

A history pull can lose its remaining touch events when React replaces the message node under the finger, such as when a lazy Markdown renderer replaces its fallback. The viewport then never receives the move, release, or cancellation: a short pull can remain at 22.6775px, or a longer pull can fail to reach the loading threshold.

## What changed

- Keep the originating touch target observed for the lifetime of the viewport-owned gesture. Forward events to the existing handlers only when their DOM path no longer reaches the viewport, so connected events are not processed twice.
- Release the target listeners on touch end/cancel, effect cleanup, and conversation changes; cancel an active pull when another finger is added.
- Add real Chromium touch regressions that gate the actual Markdown renderer and replace the target before movement, release, or cancellation, plus multi-touch and conversation-switch checks.

## Scope

Only the WebUI history touch lifecycle and its browser tests. Existing spring physics, pull thresholds, wheel/keyboard scrolling, request ownership, backend, persistence, worker counts, retries, and timeouts are unchanged. No diagnostic instrumentation is included.

## Verification

- Before the fix, the controlled browser regressions reproduced both observed values: long-pull displacement 0 instead of at least 56px, and short-release displacement 22.6775px instead of 0. They pass with the fix, including cancellation followed by a new pull.
- The full history-boundary spec passed all 25 cases; history-spring unit tests passed all 7 cases.
- Lockfile/import checks, lint, full WebUI and browser TypeScript checks, build, and the full unit/coverage suite passed (3,490 tests).
- **Full browser verification is not green, so this PR remains Draft.** The first candidate run had 395 passed / 1 failed: a blank chat-failure fixture. A fixed, isolated full baseline/candidate diagnostic pair then had 390 passed / 1 failed on the baseline (Dock touch reopening) and 394 passed / 2 failed on the candidate (the same Dock assertion and a blank compaction-reasons fixture). The page-blank failures have not been causally attributed; the original chat-failure blank was not reproduced. No assertions or timings were relaxed and these failures are not counted as fixed.
- The controlled target-replacement path is confirmed. The exact event interleavings in the earlier CI failures were not captured, and physical-device acceptance has not been performed.

Contributes to NAN-374

prs.title: fix(webui): keep Dock taps working after touch drags
prs.body:
## Why

A fast touch drag can leave Chromium with an internal fling even though the subtask Dock handle uses `touch-action: none`. The next tap stops that fling instead of producing a DOM click, leaving the closed Dock unable to reopen.

## What changed

- Cancel native handle touch movement only after the existing tap slop is crossed, using a nonpassive listener. Normal taps keep their native click, while the task list keeps its independent scrolling.
- Attach and clean up the listener with the visible handle, including when completion feedback disappears and later work restores the Dock.
- Add a controlled fast-release regression that verifies one-tap reopening and native click delivery, while retaining the existing drag, cancellation, mouse, keyboard and list-scroll coverage.

## Scope

Only Dock handle touch ownership changes. This does not change history gestures or add waits, retries, extra taps, or synthetic click fallbacks.

## Verification

- The new regression failed on the unchanged Dock at the reopening tap (0 tasks instead of 23), then passed with the fix. The unchanged touch-drag/list-scroll scenario also passed.
- A Chromium input trace of the fixed regression recorded no native fling starts or tap suppression; the next native tap generated a trusted click and reopened all 23 tasks.
- Windows, Bun 1.3.13: lockfile validation, import boundaries/checker tests, lint, full application/unit and browser TypeScript checks, production build, and full unit/coverage suite passed (3,490 tests).
- Full browser suite passed: 393 tests, two workers, zero retries. The tracked source snapshot remained unchanged throughout verification.

Touch verification used Playwright/CDP with Chromium 156 on Windows; physical touchscreen hardware was not exercised.
