prs.title: fix(websocket): abort disconnected HTTP handshakes before sending
prs.body:
## Why

A browser or HTTP client can disconnect while a WebUI HTTP route is awaiting work. With websockets 15/16, the handshake then tries to send the stale response and hits `assert not self.eof_sent`, producing repeated internal-error logs. Allowing 17.x alone leaves Feishu installations on the affected 15.x resolution.

## What changed

* Register one synchronous `process_response` hook on TCP and Unix listeners. Immediately before sending, terminate only an already-disconnected connection's handshake task. The request callback has already finished; callback failures remain visible in the existing server logs.
* Keep `websockets>=15.0,<17.0` and Feishu SDK requirements unchanged. This replaces the earlier dependency-ceiling approach.
* Cover full-close and TCP half-close through the real channel and binary HTTP bridge, followed by normal HTTP and WebSocket traffic. Cover connected and disconnected callback failures separately.
* Run focused transport regressions before optional channel installation in CI, then exercise Feishu's older compatible resolution in the all-channel suite. These regressions do not skip on websockets 15/16.
* Isolate Settings and HTTP-route tests from the user's configuration.

## Scope and tradeoffs

The production change remains 18 added lines in the WebSocket channel. There is no SDK fork, global monkeypatch, handshake-method copy, new log filter, transport replacement or dependency upgrade. The response hook must stay synchronous so it cannot yield between checking connection state and sending. Request callbacks are allowed to finish; their effects are not rolled back.

Rebased onto main `219c8bb2`. Conflicting ripgrep and attachment-boundary test fixes, plus duplicate account-fixture patches, were resolved by keeping main's existing implementations. The final PR delta is five files; the three-commit sequence and author metadata are retained.

## Verification

Rebased head `1f08c9a4`, Windows / Python 3.14.6, isolated worktree and private non-input desktop:

* Default websockets **16.1.1** transport selection: **12 passed / 4 Unix-only skips**.
* Actual channel installation selected **lark-oapi 1.7.5 / websockets 15.0.1**; affected listener, HTTP, Settings, Feishu and retained Windows fixture regressions: **549 passed / 8 skipped**. Dependency consistency passed.
* Current Windows CI main group with two local workers: **10,783 passed / 148 skipped**; serial CLI group **244 passed / 9 skipped**; serial native-process group **59 passed**; coordination selection **20 passed / 5 skipped**. Heavy installer and isolated-update matrices are left to their existing remote CI jobs. These counts are separate selections, not an aggregate full-suite claim.
* Full Ruff, strict BasedPyright and Python import boundaries passed.
* Full WebUI import checks, lint, typecheck, coverage tests and production build passed. A fresh real headless-Chrome `/help` exchange and refresh passed; its disposable gateway was stopped and ports released.
* The real Feishu SDK established a loopback WebSocket connection, sent its binary ping and stopped. Bootstrap/identity calls were stubbed; no real account or external platform was used.

A pre-rebase full run recorded one SQLite `disk I/O error`; its cause remains unconfirmed. Original/candidate targeted probes, the subsequent pre-rebase private-desktop full run and the rebased CI main group passed. No SQLite workaround, retry, delay, assertion weakening or new skip was added; the earlier failure is not claimed fixed.

Current-head remote verification is running in [Test Suite](<https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40484147705>). Linux/Python 3.11, Unix-socket and remaining installer/update acceptance belong to remote CI. The daily instance was unchanged.

Contributes to NAN-362

prs.title: fix(api): release idle session locks
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #4883.

Completed API requests with distinct `session_id` values currently leave their locks in the application's registry indefinitely. Store these locks in a `WeakValueDictionary` so idle entries can be collected, while the existing request handlers and streaming tasks keep strong references to locks that are held or awaited.

The production change updates the registry's typed `AppKey`, local annotation, and initialization. It does not introduce expiration tasks or a new lock helper.

## Tests

- Exercise completed requests with 20 distinct session IDs through the real HTTP endpoint, for both streaming and non-streaming responses.
- Extend the existing serialization test to cover default and custom sessions in both response modes, including garbage collection while one request holds the lock and another waits.
- Synchronize request arrival with an event instead of relying on a scheduler yield.

## Related work

PR #4890 uses the same weak-reference approach and is currently open with merge conflicts. This proposal is based on current main, preserves its typed application keys, and adds streaming coverage to the API regression tests.

## Validation

- The new cleanup tests fail on unmodified main (`30e43aec822bdd1d6d770db43a3b27a08667ed53`) because both response modes retain 20 idle locks. After the repair, the API and AgentLoop lock-lifecycle suites pass: **34 passed**.
- Repository Ruff checks, Python import boundaries, and strict BasedPyright pass (**0 errors, 0 warnings**).
- Serial CLI tests: **159 passed, 1 skipped**. Windows process compatibility tests: **55 passed**.
- Initial broader Windows/Python 3.13.6 run: **9,256 passed, 120 skipped, 9 failed**. All nine failing test identities and causes reproduce on an unmodified checkout of the base commit. Six pass on both base and this branch with UTF-8 mode and uv on PATH; three cannot create symlinks on this host (`WinError 1314`). No test exclusions or workflow changes are committed.
- Broader rerun with the corrected local environment, excluding only those three symlink-privilege cases: **9,262 passed, 120 skipped**. Including the separate CLI and Windows process suites, **9,476 tests passed and 121 were skipped**.

Original reports retain da965 source and manifest `e4e82f8627919bdb6e366a68aa655452ba511ce75106382ddeda604dd3a59736`; they do not certify the final 74cffe bytes. The old upload command remains withdrawn until the new exact six-file set is accepted.
- #6508 removes the obsolete bundled wizard without modifying user-workspace skills or the current updater. Local skill-loader/CI checks: 102 passed; focused WebUI skill-ranking test: one passed, 195 unselected. Website 0.4.0 contains no obsolete wizard instructions, so its unchanged ten-language evidence is retained.
- Release notes and the private article include the Windows polling fix and preserve live identity/PID-reuse checks, handle cleanup and both contributors' attribution.

## Historical b4 verification — superseded upload set

The following results belong to `b4c3f8f5e85485806c016f1387f6886db7c4f6e4`, before #6507. They remain useful historical evidence, not current-head acceptance or permission to upload those files.

- [b4 PR CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40565642306) passed all 15 jobs, including Python 3.11/3.14, Windows Python/installers/process compatibility, WebUI/browser, TUI, Docker and Linux/Windows native recovery.
- [b4 exact candidate acceptance](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40565872061) passed all five platforms and **Candidate required**: macOS arm64/x64, Linux arm64/x64 and Windows x64. Each exact manifest-bound wheel passed clean installed startup, 388 WebUI assets, five terminal input/resize/exit samples, Chinese C4 rendering and render-worker restart, plus nine update/recovery scenarios with fifteen journeys. Configuration, authenticated canonical/display history, SQLite/outbox, continued writes, second start and cleanup passed. The Windows job explicitly set and checked `LongPathsEnabled=0`.
- Historical b4 candidate/source; manifest SHA-256 is `c9214b0e451751ae451857519ce394fbcdb9c852a93021436a909eecb0c5e7e7`. Accepted artifact `installable-candidate-12-1` and its matching bytes/source are retained locally beyond CI expiry. An independent `--no-local` clone, `git fsck --full`, the complete repository candidate verifier, archive/RECORD/tag/content audit and Twine 7.0.0 `check --strict` passed. No public package was uploaded.
- The historical b4 PyPI set is five platform wheels plus one sdist. Wheels are 33.74–52.80 MiB, 10.05–17.08% larger than actual PyPI 0.3.5; sdist is 6.78 MiB, 57.15% larger. Windows/Linux x64 uncompressed TUI binaries are 128.18/122.88 MiB, below the 135 MiB budget; other targets are below 150 MiB. The growth is measured, not assumed unchanged. No intermediate universal wheel, test environment, private configuration or database is in the upload set.
- Earlier failed candidates remain failed historical evidence, not retroactive passes. They exposed macOS 15's private PingFang faces, the missing Linux CJK fixture prerequisite and Windows test synchronization. Those causes were fixed without weakening glyph, batching, ordering or data-preservation assertions; the final exact native execution above confirms the affected paths.
- Website PR #35 at `b9169498eeaa51f7371a27d659a72424ae4a8cfd` completes all ten 55-page manuals. Full local build, documentation/route/site/SEO/AI audits, TypeScript, 22 Bun/six Node tests, mobile/desktop browser samples and Lighthouse mobile pass. [Current remote CI](https://github.com/Re-bin/nanobot-web/actions/runs/40563408993) passed; deployment was skipped. It remains unmerged and undeployed.
- Full source evidence at `9ed984294…`: 8,915 Python tests passed / 53 platform or environment skips; channels 2,208 / 2; CLI 252 / 1; installer suite 80 / 1; dependency-impact checks 428 passed; strict Python types passed. Subsequent affected build checks passed 21 / 1. These retain their actual source identities under `.agent/workflow.md`.
- Earlier frontend evidence: TUI 310 tests / 1,986 assertions, native rendering 19 / 127, WebUI lint/types/build and dependency audit. These retain their original identities; current native package execution is separately recorded above.

## Upgrade and data-preservation evidence

The exact CI-produced f43 macOS arm64 wheel has SHA-256 `8ecc5bc425a43f8f3a31da5bcbee33d2dae2fbe5eb91f7d3ed7ce8f022b5b66c`.

- Genuine public 0.3.5 installations through pip, uv tool and pipx upgraded through their original owners to f43. Configuration and retained legacy bytes, authenticated canonical/display history, continued writes, second start and cleanup passed. This is not a one-click claim for 0.3.5, which lacks the new updater.
- A genuine tagged 0.3.5 source installation upgraded in the same clone through the fixed build hook. The same preservation and second-start checks passed. The actual baseline commit is `1bb712d3488915ca4ed9ccc1a93067ff722f5ab9`, not its annotated tag object.
- Genuine retained Preview packages, pre-SQLite 1902 and SQLite-v1 2102, each passed three scenarios/five journeys against f43: normal upgrade; backup failure with service recovery and subsequent upgrade; installed-target import failure with automatic old-program/service restoration and subsequent upgrade. Actual old dependencies were resolved. Protected data, Dock process lifecycle and cleanup passed. These are private historical packages and a controlled feed, not public signature/catalogue validation.
- A real isolated source-installed WebUI/Gateway passed check-update feedback, stable/Preview preference persistence, refusal to downgrade an ahead-of-stable candidate, real restart/reconnect, retained authentication, migrated test conversation and exact unsent draft. No intercepted API or daily data was used. This is restart UI coverage, not a browser-driven package replacement.
- The five-platform 6407 candidate previously passed nine recovery scenarios/fifteen journeys per platform, with Windows `LongPathsEnabled=0`. It predates the new terminal/font gate and does not override its failure. Prepared artifacts and independent source handoffs retain their original hashes.

Historical b4 Docker acceptance used test-merge `4ee9d0c28c5266477e7f9bb007fd1c7f6b7699a8`, whose parents are main b07 and b4 and whose tree equals b4. The actual 0.3.5 baseline image was replaced on the same isolated volume by target image SHA-256 `ad12e47dfe632be4f251ce8bceb05695a74e7ebd828bf5c2dea8d17f971ff2dd`. Configuration/legacy bytes, authenticated canonical/display history, continued writes, second start, non-root operation and cleanup passed without external network. This is deployment-owner image replacement, **not** in-container updating or automatic Docker rollback. Report artifact: `docker-upgrade-40565642306-1`.

Installed-startup reports deliberately retain `interactive_ui_e2e=false`; Windows records process cleanup but `gateway_graceful_shutdown=false`. They are not browser interaction or Windows graceful-stop proofs. Genuine old-package and browser evidence above is inherited for their unchanged macOS/Linux and data/browser contracts. The #6507 delta affects Windows process identity, so Windows lifecycle and recovery need fresh exact-package evidence. Native fault-injection fixtures are not relabelled as previously published packages.

Both f43 source-installed and native-wheel runtime audits examined 110 distributions with no reported advisories; only unpublished nanobot-ai 0.4.0 could not be looked up on PyPI. This does not guarantee absence of vulnerabilities. Unchanged evidence is inherited with its original identity; it is never relabelled as a new package run.

## Remaining pre-merge gates

- [x] Fix and verify macOS 15 packaged font/rendering failure on both architectures; full current-candidate update/recovery is a separate gate below.
- [x] Finish the post-#6507/#6508 current-head CI and all five exact-byte native acceptance reports; preserve accepted new bytes and source before CI artifact expiry.
- [x] Complete website translations, full local build/audits/rendered review and current remote CI in website PR #35. Final-source reconciliation remains required; do not deploy early.
- [x] Recheck new package/license/source contents and replace the hash-locked manual PyPI instructions after acceptance. The Release article is updated in the previous release's style, including #6507/#6508 and their contributors; final merged range and tag links must be reconciled at publication.
- [ ] Obtain independent review and the maintainer's merge/publication decision. Current GitHub review decision remains `REVIEW_REQUIRED`; no unresolved review threads were present at the final check.

## Publication gates — require a later command

1. Merge the reviewed preparation only after explicit approval. Compare the actual merge result to the accepted candidate and rebuild/rebind/reverify changed source or package identity. Do not tag an unchecked later main tip.
2. Confirm the maintainer's at-least-three-year corresponding-source retention commitment and required signing/protected-environment approvals.
3. With publication authorization, tag the exact verified commit, publish complete immutable GitHub assets before PyPI, and verify actual public downloads.
4. Validate release signatures and complete public stable/Preview catalogue assets before advancing the update feed. The public Preview catalogue returned HTTP 404 during preparation; private controlled-feed tests do not prove public updates are available.
5. Merge/deploy the verified website and publish announcements when the promised downloads and links are live.

`docs/releasing.md` remains authoritative. Legacy goal-history collisions are not repaired by preventing new collisions; release notes retain that limitation. Daily checkouts, configuration and conversations remain untouched.

prs.title: fix(runtime): stop Windows identity polling memory leak
prs.body:
## Why

On Windows with Python versions before 3.14, each process identity query created a new `FileTime` structure and pointer type retained by ctypes' global pointer cache. Idle WebUI launcher and gateway client polling repeatedly called this path, causing unbounded memory growth. Reuse the native types and bindings rather than reducing polling or caching process identities.

Fixes #6506
Resolves NAN-378

## What changed

- Share the `FileTime` structure and pointer type, and cache the kernel32 function bindings.
- Keep each PID identity query live, preserving HANDLE signatures, exit-state checks, and `CloseHandle` cleanup.
- Add one native Windows regression that checks a stable process identity without creating new pointer types after warmup. It detects the original allocation pattern even on Python 3.14, whose ctypes cache no longer retains these types globally.

## Scope

This fixes the shared Windows process identity helper used by WebUI launcher status and gateway client monitoring. It does not change polling intervals, process lifetime policy, or non-Windows identity behavior.

## Verification

- Native Windows regression on Python 3.13.7: **failed before the fix, passed after the fix** (`tests/gateway/test_runtime.py::test_windows_identity_polling_reuses_pointer_types`).
- Earlier isolated Windows/Python 3.12.10 diagnosis: 10,000 real identity queries followed by GC grew Private Working Set by 58.3 MiB and Private Bytes by 58.8 MiB, retaining 10,000 extra pointer-cache entries. The reporter's proposed shared-type/cached-binding correction eliminated that growth in the controlled comparison.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- The complete test suite is delegated to GitHub Actions; it was not run locally. An overnight WebUI run was not performed.

## Credit

Thanks to @snailak for the report, diagnosis, and suggested patch in #6506. The fix commit includes their `Co-authored-by` trailer; please retain it when merging.

releases.name: v0.4.0
releases.body:
🐈 **nanobot `v0.4.0`** makes everyday work easier to continue — with durable conversation history, a more capable workbench, and a clearer path to the next update.

**Keep moving.** The gateway now stores model history and browser transcripts in SQLite, imports existing conversations, and coordinates updates around saved state. Stable and opt-in Preview releases share one update flow, with explicit confirmation before installation and restart.

The browser workbench is easier to navigate and connect: complete prompt-history navigation, remote instances, clearer delegated-task details, richer attachments, and more consistent mobile controls. The terminal gains Mermaid diagram viewing and target-specific native bundles. Both clients continue to use the same Python gateway.

This release also makes installation ownership explicit. Supported managed installations can update and recover the program through the app; other installations receive instructions for their original package manager or deployment. Recovery does not mean restoring an old copy of your chats. Please read the upgrade notes before replacing an existing installation.

## Highlights

- **One update flow, with your confirmation** — Check releases in Settings → About, choose whether to receive Preview updates, review the exact version, and confirm installation and restart. Supported official-installer and POSIX uv environments can use the in-app flow once the public release has verified approval proof.
- **Recovery that protects current data** — Installer-managed updates can attempt repair and, when safe, restore the original program and service. Configuration and conversations are not automatically replaced with an older backup. Installation owners outside that flow keep their own repair route.
- **Durable conversation history** — SQLite brings model history and WebUI display history under gateway ownership. Existing JSONL history is imported with source backups retained. Paging, live-output reconciliation, queued follow-ups and goal continuation receive reliability fixes.
- **A clearer browser workbench** — Navigate the full prompt history with bounded loading, search loaded messages and session handles, rename topics inline, and archive topics in batches. Delegated tasks have clearer run state and detail views.
- **Your workbench, on the right host** — Connect to existing remote instances with explicit host identity, pairing and reconnect feedback. Update instructions identify the gateway computer, rather than assuming it is the device displaying the page.
- **Richer files and a better small-screen experience** — Local-file and video attachments, image thumbnails, file cards, Markdown source views, reading-size controls, and touch and theme improvements. External websites open in the browser instead of an arbitrary embedded preview.
- **Diagrams in the terminal** — View, zoom, pan and copy Mermaid diagrams without leaving the conversation. Platform wheels contain the matching native TUI and built WebUI; supported wheel installations need neither Bun nor a first-launch TUI download.
- **More control over models and integrations** — Searchable providers, explicit API choices, per-preset request overrides, shared proxy choices, Linear and WhatsApp Agent Platform channels, QQ QR setup, and DeepSeek Search. Scheduled jobs can be edited, enabled and disabled in place, with recent runs available for inspection.
- **A fix for Windows idle memory growth** — Process-status polling now reuses native type and API bindings on Python versions before 3.14, while keeping live process checks and handle cleanup.

## Upgrade Notes

- **Distribution availability.** The verified v0.4.0 packages are available in this GitHub Release and on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/nanobot-ai/0.4.0/). In-app automatic installation is not enabled for this release yet: it requires verified release approval proof and the applicable public release sources. Publishing these files does not enroll users in Preview or start an update.
- **Upgrade v0.3.5 through its original installation method first.** That release does not contain this new in-app updater. Run the installer, package manager or container replacement on the gateway computer under its original OS account. Existing installations are not silently converted into official-installer environments. Follow the [installation-owner instructions](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/docs/updating.md#installation-owners), including recorded extras, constraints and custom options.
- **Stop shared writers and back up the complete instance.** Finish active work, stop all nanobot processes using the environment or data, and back up the selected configuration directory and workspace together. Include authentication, sessions and WebUI state. Do not copy only a live SQLite database file. After upgrading, use the original launcher, check the running version, open older conversations, write a new message and verify another restart.
- **SQLite changes the downgrade procedure.** JSONL import remains available throughout 0.4.x; older JSONL-only installations must pass through an import-capable release before 0.5.0. Keep imported source backups and the old WebUI directory. Older versions cannot read new SQLite display history. A downgrade requires a stopped-writer backup-restoration procedure that accounts for messages created since the backup; it is not an automatic data rollback. See [Session Storage](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/docs/cli-reference.md#session-storage).
- **An update can restart the gateway.** Confirming installation can interrupt running tasks. Turning Preview off saves the subscription but does not downgrade an installed Preview. Recovery cannot guarantee service restoration after permanent storage damage, incompatible data writes, or loss of both recovery processes. Missing or unverifiable public assets must not be treated as a successful install. See [Updating nanobot](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/docs/updating.md).
- **Fresh official-installer instances stay in the background.** Their normal WebUI launcher starts a persistent instance. Closing the terminal or browser does not stop it; use `nanobot gateway stop` with the same configuration and workspace selectors. Existing unrecorded installations retain their original lifecycle. Local macOS WebUI sessions can show a Dock icon; `--no-dock` suppresses it.
- **Review migrated configuration before saving.** Legacy proxy conversion remains supported in 0.4.x. The old OpenAI `apiType` / `api_type` selector is converted to `api` in 0.4.0 and the immediately following release; save the current format during that window. See [Configuration](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/docs/configuration.md).
- **Platform requirements remain explicit.** Python 3.11+ is required. Native wheels target macOS 13+ arm64/x64, glibc 2.17+ Linux arm64/x64, and Windows x64; x64 requires SSE4.2. Windows ARM64 and musl Linux do not have native wheels. Chinese terminal diagrams require suitable installed fonts: Heiti SC on macOS, Noto Sans CJK on Linux, or Microsoft YaHei on Windows. Diagram source remains accessible if rendering is unavailable.
- **Keep container data volumes and reconnect clients.** Replace the container through its deployment owner; do not upgrade packages inside a running container. Reconnect or reload WebUI/TUI clients after upgrading the intended gateway, and follow any client/host compatibility guidance shown.

## Community

Thank you to everyone who contributed code, reviewed changes, reported problems, supplied reproductions and tested nanobot in everyday use. Clear bug reports and useful use cases remain important contributions. We want the agent to stay small and inspectable while becoming easier to rely on for daily work.

issues.title: Vision probes can't resolve `catalog_provider` for named custom providers (routed as `custom`)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: tool/vision
labels.description: Vision analysis and image generation

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Description
With `catalog_provider: openrouter` on a named custom provider, `get_model_capabilities` correctly resolves the catalog (including `modalities.input`), so vision routing should work without per-model overrides. It doesn't in real turns: named custom providers are canonicalized to provider name `custom`, and the vision probes see only that name.

## Reproduction
```yaml
model: {default: z-ai/glm-5.3-flash, provider: openrouter-fast}
providers:
  openrouter-fast:
    api: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
    key_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
    catalog_provider: openrouter
agent: {image_input_mode: auto}
```

```python
_models_dev_id('openrouter-fast', config=cfg)   # 'openrouter' — works, supports_vision True
# in a real turn the probe receives 'custom':
_models_dev_id('custom')                        # None → probe chain None → mode 'text'
```

## Root cause
`_probe_models_dev` calls `get_model_capabilities(provider, model, allow_network=True)` without config or the `requested_provider` identity, so `_configured_catalog_provider()` can't match `providers.openrouter-fast` under the canonicalized name. The override lane handles this (`_supports_vision_override` retries the requested name); the catalog probe lane doesn't.

## Expected
`catalog_provider` should make per-model `supports_vision` overrides unnecessary for catalogued models on named custom providers.

**Related:** #112649, #83666, #41036

prs.title: Office and PDF helpers stop dropping content on read, restructure and flatten (salvage #82724)
prs.body:
Office and PDF helpers no longer drop content: Word reads include nested tables and every header/footer variant, Excel restructures shift whole-row/column references and remove fully deleted artifacts, PowerPoint keeps explicit titles on layouts with no title placeholder, and `pdf_fill_form.py --flatten` actually removes form interactivity without losing fields the JSON leaves out.

Salvage of #82724 by @fangliquanflq (cherry-picked with authorship; git's rename detection carried it onto the new `microsoft-office` skill paths). Fixes #82722.

## Infographic

![Office edits stop dropping content](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab04801/5K4JDtjlrhv20LRC35JiR_8QsZ6HX5.png)

## What changes

| Helper | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `docx_read.py --text` | skips tables nested in table cells and first-page/even-page headers and footers | reads all of them, without duplicating linked header/footer parts |
| `xlsx_restructure.py` | `A:A` / `3:3` style references and fully deleted row dimensions, validations and tables stay stale | whole-axis refs shift; fully deleted artifacts are removed |
| `pptx_create.py`, `pptx_from_template.py` | a slide with `"title"` on a layout with no title placeholder (e.g. blank) silently loses the title | a visible title box is added |
| `pdf_fill_form.py --flatten` | only marks fields read-only; the form stays interactive | appearances are merged into the page, widgets and `/AcroForm` are removed, other annotations (links) kept |

**Our fix on top (second commit):** @yuzilongleif-collab found on #82724 that `--flatten` with a partial JSON deleted prefilled fields: pypdf bakes only the fields it is handed, and every widget is removed afterwards. Flattening now passes every field with its current value, with the JSON values on top.

## Verification

All of these run the real helper CLIs as subprocesses on real files (pinned python-docx 1.2.0, python-pptx 1.0.2, openpyxl 3.1.5, pypdf 6.21.2):

- **Red on main:** the six new regression tests from #82724 fail against main's scripts (nested-table/header read, two blank-layout title cases, whole-axis refs, deleted artifacts, flatten).
- **Red on the PR head:** the new partial-flatten test (`test_form_fill_flatten_keeps_fields_left_out_of_the_json`) fails on #82724's version of `pdf_fill_form.py`.
- **Green:** `microsoft-office/tests` + `pdf/tests`, 90 passed. Ruff is clean and `audit_pr_attribution.py` says every contributor email is mapped.

**Not included:** the second XLSX follow-up posted on #82724 (literal `=` strings treated as formulas, column-dimension `min`/`max` shifts). Those are separate bugs and outside this PR.

prs.title: feat(catalog): add mediarag entry
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/mediarag.yaml`. MediaRAG is multimodal local search over documents and
media — pdf, office files, notes, images, audio and subtitles in one SQLite corpus, queried by
meaning from any MCP-capable agent. Hybrid retrieval (semantic vectors fused with an FTS5/BM25
keyword lane), documents and media level in the same index.

One-file diff. Owner submission (`dyiapanis` owns `dyiapanis/mediarag`). Pinned at
`6c3bba2b6a21e48ffdae1992638d2e4e6c3358e3` (main after the `v0.1.4` promotion; CI green at that
SHA on both Linux and Windows).

## Rule-13 disclosures

**Network egress.** None by default, and none on any local-search path. Opt-in only:
`add_source` with an `http(s)://` URL fetches that URL with `curl` (`--proto`/`--proto-redir`
restricted to http/https, `--max-time 120`, `--max-filesize 268435456`); the optional
`raindrop://` adapter calls `api.raindrop.io` and only when invoked. `pcloud://`, `obsidian://`
and `rclone://` read the local mount or the user's own configured rclone remote through that
tool's own credentials — the plugin holds no remote credentials of its own.

**First-run download.** ~480MB of embedding weights, and only when the operator runs
`python scripts/fetch_model.py` explicitly — nothing is downloaded on startup. The sharded
Hugging Face cache is materialized once into `~/.cache/mediarag/onnx-real` (real files, because
onnxruntime will not load external-data blobs), after which the process runs with
`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.

**Local data boundaries.** Reads only the paths passed to it, plus the corpus root
(`mediarag-config.yaml` `root:` > `MEDIARAG_ROOT` > `~/.mediarag`). Writes: the corpus at
`<root>/.corpus/store.db`, the model materialization under `~/.cache/mediarag/`, `rclone` copies
under `~/.cache/mediarag/rclone`, and http fetches under `~/.cache/mediarag/_url`. No writes
outside those.

**Credentials.** `RAINDROP_API_TOKEN`, optional, only for the Raindrop adapter. Inside Hermes it
is read through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret("RAINDROP_API_TOKEN")` and **fails closed** — any
exception there returns no token rather than reaching for the environment. The environment read
happens solely when the `agent` package is absent (standalone MCP lane, where the client injects
the env per the Agent Plugins v1 lifecycle). The adapter is invoked with a scrubbed environment:
the token is removed when it does not resolve.

**Subprocess use, all bounded.** `pdftotext` (120s), `pandoc` (120s), `ffmpeg` (1200s), `curl`
(120s request / 130s process), adapters (1800s). Adapters are executables from the corpus's
`sources.d/` and the package's own `adapters/` — two directories, no PATH or `$HOME` lookup.

**Session-prompt registrations.** None. The plugin registers no hooks, no middleware and no
prompt sections; it registers five tools (`mediarag_search`, `mediarag_add_note`,
`mediarag_ingest_dir`, `mediarag_add_source`, `mediarag_status`) and declares a stdio MCP server
in `mcp.json`.

**License.** MIT.

## Capability declarations

`provides_tools` lists exactly the five tools `register(ctx)` calls; hooks, middleware and
`requires_env` are empty because nothing of those kinds is registered and nothing is required
(`RAINDROP_API_TOKEN` is optional).

`hermes plugins validate` reports one warning at the pin — *"declares mediarag_add_note, …
but register() did not register them"*. That is the isolation probe running without the engine
dependencies: `register()` refuses to register rather than advertise tools that cannot work,
because the processor chain needs torch and torchvision. On any host with `requirements.txt`
installed the five tools register (the Linux CI lane runs the full suite, and the Windows lane
installs the declared dependency set and passes). This warning direction is the benign one
(declared-but-unregistered); the pinned tree declares nothing it does not register.

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins validate <clone>` at `6c3bba2` → `ok: true` (one engine-probe warning as above).
2. `pip install -r requirements.txt && python scripts/fetch_model.py && python tests/test_parity_slices.py` → all parity checks pass.
3. `python tests/test_contract.py` (28 checks), `tests/test_ingest_units.py` (25), `tests/test_engine_deref.py` (9) → all pass.

## Validation receipt (at `6c3bba2`, without `--install-deps`)

```
✓ manifest — plugin.yaml parses
✓ manifest fields — name, version, description present
✓ loadable — entry: __init__.py, plugin.json
✓ python dependencies — 8 requirements from manifest
✓ capability probe — register() ran in isolation
✓ declared tools — matches registrations
✓ declared hooks — matches registrations
✓ declared middleware — matches registrations
✓ built-in tool collisions — no collisions
✓ security scan — safe
✓ no core override — no runtime rebinds of Hermes core
⚠ provides_tools declares … but register() did not register them   (engine probe, see above)
Validation passed.
```

`--install-deps` was not run here on purpose: it installs into the invoking Hermes venv, and this
entry's dependency set includes a CPU torch build (~200MB). CI at the pin does install and
exercise the full dependency set (`pip install -r requirements.txt` on both runners).

## Checklist

- [x] Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`feat(catalog): add mediarag entry`)
- [x] Searched for existing PRs — none; an earlier unfiled branch existed on the fork and is superseded by this one
- [x] PR contains only `plugin-catalog/mediarag.yaml`
- [ ] `pytest tests/ -q` — N/A: data-only entry, no code in this repo changes
- [ ] `python scripts/check` — N/A for the same reason
- [x] Entry validated at the pinned SHA (receipt above)
- [x] Tested on: Linux (Debian, Python 3.14) and Windows (`windows-latest`, Python 3.12) via the plugin repo's CI
- [x] Docs: entry carries `docs_url`; the plugin README is rendered from the pin

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add withhuman
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/withhuman.yaml`, a community entry for the withHuman plugin. It pins [`withHumanAI/withHuman`](https://github.com/withHumanAI/withHuman) at `a88bfd7358bfbf15508117f8158fbc48acdc5705` with `subdir: plugins/hermes/withhuman`, version `1.5.2`.

I own the plugin repository: withHumanAI is my company's GitHub organization (rule 5).

withHuman is a central approval layer for AI agents. It lets you:

- Write rules for which tool calls run automatically and which need a person, such as "refunds up to $20 run, larger ones go to support".
- Use one set of rules for every agent you run: Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw and your own.
- Send each approval to the right people, by team, with escalation levels and working hours.
- Approve or deny from the web app, Slack, Discord, email or the iPhone and Android apps.
- See every call, and who approved it, in an audit log.

This plugin connects Hermes to withHuman, so users can let Hermes tool calls wait for human approval if needed.

### Hermes surfaces used

- `ctx.register_hook("pre_tool_call", ...)`: returns `modify` with the approved arguments, or `block` with the reason. It never approves on Hermes's behalf: it adds a check before the call and leaves Hermes's own approval system alone.
- `ctx.register_cli_command`: `hermes withhuman setup` and `hermes withhuman test`.
- `ctx.get_config` / `ctx.set_config` for the withHuman address.
- A `secret` in `config_schema` (`WITHHUMAN_AGENT_TOKEN`), read with `agent.secret_scope.get_secret`.
- `plugins.plugin_storage.plugin_data_dir` for the downloaded CLI.
- `after-install.md`, which tells the user to run setup.

### Disclosures (rule 13)

The same list is in the plugin's README, section "Security and footprint".

- **Network calls.** Each tool call's name and arguments go to the withHuman address set up for the profile (`https://app.withhuman.ai` by default, or a self-hosted one). Setup also calls that address to sign in or to check a pasted key. No telemetry.
- **Waiting for a person (rule 12).** A call the user's rules send to a person waits until someone decides, up to a week. That includes cron and messaging-gateway runs, because holding the call is what the user installed the plugin for. Interrupting the turn withdraws the request. A call that gets no decision is blocked, never run.
- **Hook timeout.** Human approvals can often take longer than Hermes's 30-second hook limit, so setup sets `plugins.hook_callback_timeout` to `0` for the profile. Setup says so before it does it, and notes that the setting applies to every plugin's hooks. The plugin keeps its own one-week ceiling.
- **Shell commands.** The hook runs the withHuman CLI (`withhuman hook hermes`) once per tool call. Setup also runs `withhuman version` to check the installed CLI, and sends its test request through the same hook command.
- **Download (rule 17).** When no withHuman CLI is installed, or an older one is, setup downloads a pinned CLI release from `downloads.withhuman.ai`, our official release host. It checks the file against SHA-256 sums in `connect.py` before saving it to `plugin-data/withhuman/bin`. When a plugin update pins a newer CLI release, the plugin replaces that copy the same way, in a background thread on load. A CLI the user installed themselves is never touched. The plugin never fetches or replaces its own files (rule 3).
- **Credentials (rule 11).** The agent key is saved as `WITHHUMAN_AGENT_TOKEN` in the profile's secrets and read with `get_secret`. The plugin keeps no credential store and reads no `.env` or other tool's login.
- **Other changes setup makes.** On hosted withHuman it adds a `withhuman-gateway` remote MCP server whose `Authorization` header references `${WITHHUMAN_AGENT_TOKEN}`. It offers to install the `withhuman` and `withhuman-pipelines` skills from withhuman.ai through Hermes's own skill installer.
- **Removal.** `hermes plugins remove withhuman` leaves the timeout setting, the MCP server and the skills. The README lists the command to remove each.
- **Private core imports (rule 9).** `hermes plugins validate` warns about three: `tools.interrupt.is_interrupted` (to withdraw the request when the turn is interrupted), `hermes_cli.mcp_config._save_mcp_server` and `hermes_cli.skills_hub.do_install` (setup adding the MCP server and the skills). None rebinds anything. I'm happy to open issues asking for public seams for these.

## Related Issue

None. This is a new catalog entry.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/withhuman.yaml` (new, and the only file changed): pins `withHumanAI/withHuman` at `a88bfd7358bfbf15508117f8158fbc48acdc5705`, `subdir: plugins/hermes/withhuman`, version `1.5.2`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.5"`, `platforms: [linux, macos]`, one `pre_tool_call` hook.

## How to Test

1. Clone `withHumanAI/withHuman`, check out the pinned SHA and run `hermes plugins validate plugins/hermes/withhuman --install-deps`.
2. Run `hermes plugins install withhuman --enable`, then `hermes withhuman setup`. Setup asks for the withHuman address, signs in through the browser (a free account at app.withhuman.ai works), and sends a test request.
3. Approve the test request in withHuman. Then ask Hermes to do something, and approve or deny the call in withHuman.

What I ran, on macOS 26.6 arm64 with Python 3.14.3 and Hermes main at `9fc982ecd0a4`:

- `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` at the pin: passed, security scan `safe`, with the three private-import warnings above.
- `hermes plugins doctor --ci` at the pin: passed (1 hook, 0 tools).
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/`: `OK: 863 file(s) valid`.
- `scripts/scan_plugin_payloads.py` on the pinned plugin directory: exit 0.
- `hermes plugins install withhuman --enable` into a throwaway `HERMES_HOME`, with this entry added to the cached live catalog: cloned the pin, showed `after-install.md`, enabled the plugin, and registered `hermes withhuman setup|test`. `hermes plugins search` finds it for "approval", "human approval", "human in the loop" and "guardrails".
- The catalog CI lane, `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the 33 files from `scripts/ci/catalog_test_files.py`: 389 passed, 0 failed.
- `python scripts/check`: 13 checks, ok.
- The plugin's own tests (29, in `plugins/hermes/tests`) against Hermes 0.21.5, 0.21.6 and 0.22.5: all pass. They load the plugin in Hermes and cover approval, denial, the callback timeout, interrupts and setup. On 0.21.4 the plugin is refused by its `requires_hermes` floor.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the plugin-catalog admission rules
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry
- [x] I've run the catalog CI lane (`scripts/run_tests.sh` over `scripts/ci/catalog_test_files.py`): 389 passed, 0 failed. The full suite isn't green on my machine only in suites that need extras I don't have installed (ACP and others), which a data-only entry doesn't touch.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (13 checks)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes: N/A, data-only entry. The plugin's own tests live in its repository.
- [x] Tested on my platform: macOS 26.6 arm64

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation: N/A (the entry's README renders from the pinned SHA)
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact: `platforms: [linux, macos]`, because setup downloads the CLI only for those
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A, no tools

## Notes for the reviewer

- `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.5"` is the first release that knows the `secret` config type the agent key uses.
- `tier: community`.

prs.title: chore(catalog): add OpenCode Session Sync plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Owner submission of the separate **OpenCode Session Sync** community plugin: https://github.com/cryptobredda/hermes-opencode-sync

- Registers manual `hermes opencode-sync` with dry-run, exact directory, literal session ID and source-path filters.
- Reads OpenCode history from a consistent read-only SQLite snapshot; an authorizer denies credential/account table access.
- Uses the active profile's authenticated native owner API for guarded import-owned upserts. Stable IDs, deterministic message UIDs and linked long-history segments allow repeat runs without duplicate unchanged messages.
- Preserves Hermes-side continuations/edits as conflicts, and operator titles, flags and model choices. Busy leases and retired/deleted identities are not bypassed. Backups and verification accompany writes.
- Exact source pin: `6fcc8284e1f4b573565e23b55f34d4feaaee9fd9`, version `1.0.0`, manifest/catalog floor `>=0.22.5`, community tier.

## Important: internal API dependency / requested supported seam

`hermes plugins validate` passes but warns about undocumented imports in the native ticket, owner mutation/lease, import-binding, row-serialization and local-lineage helpers. They are disclosed in the pinned README and entry's known issues. There are **no runtime core rebinds, monkeypatches or core/TUI file modifications**.

A public incremental imported-history update API is requested in #145451. Please hold/decline this listing if it must wait for that seam; this submission does not claim an exception to catalog rule 9. This build deliberately refuses isolated/secondary backend owners and needs the gateway primary profile with `plugins.isolation: in_process` rather than opening a competing database writer.

## Disclosure

Reads the selected source history and relevant imported Hermes transcripts; stores source-digest/checkpoint state, pre-update compressed transcript backups, inline attachment/large-output artifacts and run reports privately under the active Hermes home's `imports/opencode-sync/`. Chat content/backups can contain incidental secrets a user pasted; these files must not be published. Does not read `.env`, auth/login files, account tables, browser data or credential stores. Uses a same-user native owner ticket from Hermes' control socket, not a provider token. Makes loopback owner API calls only. Starting an absent normal gateway is delegated to Hermes runtime discovery. No external network requests by the plugin, model generations, historical tool/shell execution, cron, automatic sync, telemetry, updater or registration-time work. No external attachment downloads.

## Validation

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` against a clean upstream Hermes checkout: **19 passed** (codec/source permissions, append/repeat idempotency, independently edited Hermes history refusal, running leases, long-segment routing, malformed/forged identities, preserved operator state, partial-run recovery and a fresh-profile dry run).
- `hermes plugins validate . --install-deps`: passed; security scan safe; no core override; private-core-import warnings explicitly acknowledged above.
- Public repository CI passed (codec and real Hermes compatibility jobs): https://github.com/cryptobredda/hermes-opencode-sync/actions/runs/40479426355. The compatibility job uses the pinned Hermes release's own locked PM setup rather than plain pip, honoring its declared Pillow/browser dependency override.

This is a request for maintainer review, not an approved/endorsed marketplace listing. No unrelated core changes.

prs.title: catalog: novel-reader — read local .txt/.md novels beside the conversation
prs.body:
## What it does

**Novel Reader** — read a local novel beside the conversation while the agent works.

- **Chapters** from CJK (`第3章`, `第十二回`) and latin headings (`Chapter 7`), with a leading table-of-contents trimmed so the TOC itself is not a chapter.
- **Encoding**: UTF-8 / GBK / GB18030 sniffing (a big share of Chinese `.txt` novels are GBK), BOM handling, and a 512 KB+ read path that does not truncate mid-book.
- **Progress**: one mark per book in plugin storage; reopening resumes at the same scroll position, chapter and percentage.
- **Typography**: serif / sans / mono, size, line height, theme follow.

## Surfaces used (Desktop SDK only)

| Surface | What it is |
|---|---|
| `panes` | contributed layout pane, docked to the workspace |
| `routes` | `/novel` full-page reader |
| `sidebarNav` | sidebar row that opens it |
| `statusBar.right` | chip showing book + percentage, navigates to the page |
| `titleBar.right` | book button → floating panel over the chat, or the docked column |
| `palette` | two commands (open reader, choose folder) |

No agent tools, hooks, middleware, provider profiles or env vars. `desktop/plugin.js` imports only `@hermes/plugin-sdk`, `react` and `react/jsx-runtime`; no `eval`, no dynamic import, no app-markup queries (panel geometry is measured from the plugin's own title-bar button, and the status-bar height is a constant).

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Reads only files the user picks**: a folder granted through the Hermes file door (`ctx.files`, when the host exposes it) or individual `.txt`/`.md` files chosen in the OS dialog via the desktop bridge. No directory walking outside those, no other disk reads.
- **Storage**: the shelf (absolute path + file name), typography settings and one progress mark per book, in Hermes plugin storage only.
- **No network**: no telemetry, no update checks, no remote fonts or images.
- No self-updating code — updates reach users through a SHA-bump PR here, per rule 3.

## Validation

```
hermes plugins validate .
✓ manifest — plugin.yaml parses
✓ requires_hermes — spec '>=0.22.0' parses
✓ loadable — entry: desktop/plugin.js
✓ security scan — safe
✓ no core override — no runtime rebinds of Hermes core
✓ desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface
◆ Isolation — portable plugin (no Python): runs anywhere
Validation passed.
```

The repo also has 21 unit tests over the pure functions (chapter splitting, encoding, progress maths) plus an artifact test asserting the built file's import allowlist, run in CI on every push.

## Screenshots

Floating panel beside the conversation:

![Reading panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bingochen87/hermes-novel-reader/d62369430251232c764373f8253784937d3295b7/assets/panel.png)

Full-page reader (`/novel`):

![Full page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bingochen87/hermes-novel-reader/d62369430251232c764373f8253784937d3295b7/assets/page.png)

## Entry

One file: `plugin-catalog/novel-reader.yaml`, pinned to `d62369430251232c764373f8253784937d3295b7` (CI green on that commit: https://github.com/bingochen87/hermes-novel-reader/actions).

Published by the repository owner (`bingochen87`).

prs.body:
Bumps `plugin-catalog/hermetic.yaml` from 1.2.0 (d0f3077) to 1.3.0 (e03fc0c). Submitted by the repository owner.

## Changes

- Costs: plan limits for every provider Hermes has an account report for (OpenRouter usage and limits, Anthropic and OpenAI Codex usage windows, Nous credits), through `fetch_account_usage` and Hermes' Nous portal helpers.
- Costs: each chat's cost is spread over the days it ran, so a long chat still counts today.
- Costs: pricing fixes (Fireworks model ids, provider-named models at that provider's rate, Hopscotch-billed models priced from hopscotchlabs.ai's public model pages), and the routing premium uses the same profiles as the headline.
- Costs: offers Hermes' own `compression.proactive_prune_tokens` as a fix only when the session history shows it would save more than the cache resets it causes.
- AAI: until the judge is checked against the user's ratings and trusted, automatic revert ignores its verdicts. The check now also requires it to fail most replies the user corrected, using the same prompt those tests are graded with; 3-star ratings no longer count as agreement; Settings shows which model the judge runs on and warns when it is the agent's own model family.
- HDR: code that names a sensitive place counts as a read only when every line naming it is a read-only command (`ls`, `cat`, `stat`...) and nothing in the code writes anywhere; otherwise it still counts as a write. Sensitive places are one row per path; a row opens to the line that ran (typed secrets masked), the chat, and what the guard does there, and reads can be marked expected for a scheduled job or chat (a write, or a read from elsewhere, still shows). LaunchAgents are counted as startup items instead of keys and logins. The first HDR load after a restart is faster (no per-path regex compiles), and AAI and HDR show a quiet skeleton while their first copy loads.
- Catalog entry: `title` (lowercase "hermetic", matching the plugin name) and an `image` banner.
- README: banner, badges, links, a demo video, and a shorter rewrite of the AAI and HDR sections.

Full range: https://github.com/forefy/hermetic/compare/d0f30770b4a3531f19830699def0f7ba3b5cc457...e03fc0cb6b8a6405da18722f51c0931644507953

## Disclosures

Two additions, both in the entry's description and in the README under "What it does on your machine":

- Costs reads hopscotchlabs.ai's public model page (no key, once a day per model), only for models a profile is billed for through Hopscotch.
- The account report Costs asks Hermes for (at most once a minute) now covers the profile's provider, not only OpenRouter: Anthropic and OpenAI Codex usage windows and Nous credits. Hermes looks up the credential; Hermetic only receives the report.

Guard behaviour change: at Ask, code that only lists or reads a startup folder no longer waits for an answer (it shares the read/write rule above). Writes to startup folders and reads of keys are guarded as before.

## Validation

- `hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` at e03fc0c: passed.
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` on the new entry: OK.
- Tests in `tests/`: all pass. Installed from a clean `HERMES_HOME`.

prs.body:
Adds MariaDB's official Hermes packages from [mariadb/ai-plugins](https://github.com/mariadb/ai-plugins), all pinned at the 26.10.6 release (`c188e6417f2b667db4d3107c8a33e5d98cc29fea`). Submitted by a maintainer of that repository (MariaDB plc).

| Entry | Subdir | Kind | Hermes surfaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mariadb-dev` | `hermes/dev-plugin` | Agent Plugins v1 (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) | 85 skills, one stdio MCP server |
| `mariadb-sql` | `hermes/sql-plugin` | Agent Plugins v1 (plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/) | 47 skills (a subset), the same MCP server |
| `mariadb-guard` | `hermes/guard-plugin` | Python plugin (plugin.yaml + `__init__.py`) | `pre_tool_call` hook, one system-prompt section |

Users pick `mariadb-dev` or `mariadb-sql`, and the README recommends adding `mariadb-guard` alongside. The guard is a separate package because Hermes runs hooks only from a Python plugin.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes for all three at the pinned sha, against hermes-agent `8acb7f6`: security scan `safe` for each. The guard's declared hooks, tools and middleware match its registrations, and there is no core override. `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes too.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

**mariadb-dev / mariadb-sql**
- The MCP server is the local `mariadb-shell` binary, started by `scripts/mariadb-mcp-launcher.sh`. Nothing is bundled: the package holds no binaries.
- **Downloads at first start.** If no `mariadb-shell` of at least the required version is on `PATH` or in `~/.local/bin`, the launcher fetches the official installer from `github.com/mariadb-corporation/mariadb-shell` (our own upstream). That installer installs the newest release into `~/.local/share/mariadb-shell` and links it into `~/.local/bin`, verifying it against the release's `SHA256SUMS`. The `mariadb-shell` binary, and therefore the MCP tool set, is not covered by the pinned sha. The launcher never touches the plugin's own files.
- Tools run SQL against the databases the user registered with `mariadb-shell` (`mariadb-shell -- mcp setup`). Their passwords stay in mariadb-shell's own OS secret store. The plugin never reads them, and they never pass through the agent.
- The sandbox tools download MariaDB server releases and run local server instances, as long-running processes, until the user stops them.
- No telemetry.

**mariadb-guard**
- Pure Python, no dependencies, no network or file access. It blocks `mariadb`/`mysql`-style command-line clients so database passwords never land on a command line. Setting `MARIADB_PLUGIN_ALLOW_CLI=1` disables it.

## Tier

Entered as `community`. MariaDB plc makes MariaDB and maintains these packages, so if `verified` applies, we would be glad to have it.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add hermes-plexus (vault graph, file tree and editor for Desktop)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a catalog entry for **Plexus** (`hermes-plexus`), a Desktop plugin that opens a local markdown vault (Obsidian-style `[[wikilinks]]`) as one workspace tab: a collapsible file tree, a force-directed graph of the notes, and a tabbed editor behind a divider that can collapse either side. Owner submission (rule 5): I own https://github.com/mr-september/hermes-plexus.

Pinned to `7a0ee944917b265892a456975ed957258a94191d` (tag `v0.1.0`, `plugin.yaml` version `0.1.0`). Entry points: `desktop/plugin.js` (a committed, unminified esbuild bundle of `src/`; CI checks that it matches a fresh build). MIT licensed.

**Surfaces it uses** (Desktop SDK only): `host.openWorkspace` for the tab, palette and keybind (`Ctrl/⌘+Shift+G`), a status-bar item, `ctx.registerSettingsPage`, a transcript directive (`::vault{note="…"}`, which opens a note from chat and never creates files), `ctx.storage`, `ctx.i18n`, and `host.composer.insertText` for "Add to chat". No agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars (`capabilities` are all empty).

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- **Reads outside the plugin's own data:** it reads and writes markdown files (and reads images for previews) in the vault folder the user picks. Deleting moves a note to the OS trash. Saves are check-then-write and refused when the file changed on disk.
- **How it reaches the disk:** through the Electron file bridge the app already exposes to the renderer (`window.hermesDesktop.readDir / readFileText / writeTextFile / renamePath / trashPath / readFileDataUrl / selectPaths`). The Desktop SDK has no file-access door today, and `hermes plugins validate` passes (`desktop surface: stays inside the plugin SDK surface`), but I want to say plainly that this is the one place the plugin steps beyond the SDK's own calls. If you would rather have an SDK door for local files, I will move to it.
- **No** network calls, shell commands, background processes, telemetry, stored credentials, or self-updating code (rule 3).
- **Build-time rewrite:** the bundled CodeMirror (`@codemirror/language`) extends its own class with `Object.defineProperty(EditorState.prototype, "tree", …)`, which the static `desktop surface` lint matches literally. `scripts/build.mjs` rewrites that one call to `Reflect.defineProperty` (same effect) and fails the build if the library line ever changes. Documented in the README ("Build notes").
- **Platforms:** developed and tested on native Windows 11 only. macOS and Linux are untested (the plugin uses only the cross-platform file bridge).

## Related Issue

None.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality): a new catalog entry, no changes to Hermes itself

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/hermes-plexus.yaml`: new entry (one file).

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins validate <checkout of mr-september/hermes-plexus at 7a0ee94>`: all checks pass, `security scan` is `safe`.
2. `hermes plugins install mr-september/hermes-plexus --ref 7a0ee944917b265892a456975ed957258a94191d`, open Hermes Desktop, press `Ctrl/⌘+Shift+G` (or the status-bar **Vault** button), and choose `demo/vault` from the repo as the vault folder.
3. The repo's CI (typecheck, 77 tests, bundle-is-current, and this repo's own `desktop_surface_findings` lint) is green on `main`.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs (no other `plexus` entry; there are other vault-style plugins in the catalog, `vault-view`, `brain-graph` and `obsidian-memory`, which differ by transport and layout: this one needs no Unix shell or Python backend, works on native Windows, and puts graph, tree and editor in one workspace tab)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 (Hermes Desktop v0.22.2 local build)
- [ ] `pytest` / `python scripts/check`: not run, since this PR adds only a YAML entry; catalog CI runs `hermes plugins validate` at the pinned commit
- N/A: tests for Hermes itself (the plugin's own tests live in its repo)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation: the plugin's README at the pinned commit documents usage, limits and the disclosures above (note that the catalog docs page drops raw HTML, so the centred hero in that README will not render there; the `screenshots:` gallery will)
- N/A: `cli-config.yaml.example`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`, tool schemas, new skills

## Screenshots / Logs

Rendered from the plugin's fictional demo vault with the real plugin components in a headless-browser harness (the surrounding Hermes chrome is simulated, so these are representative rather than literal captures):

![overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mr-september/hermes-plexus/7a0ee944917b265892a456975ed957258a94191d/docs/screenshots/overview-dark.png)

prs.title: catalog: add webmint (community)
prs.body:
Adds `plugin-catalog/webmint.yaml`, pinning `DECRUX9812/webmint` at `1a0aa249b5d51c162d6e2cba46ff34e843606094` (tag `v0.1.1`).

**Owner submission** — I own and maintain https://github.com/DECRUX9812/webmint.

## What it does

A website becomes a tool instead of a repeated browsing task: a real browser captures the page
once, the host's own model writes a declarative extraction spec, two runs must agree before the
tool is saved, and every later call executes that spec with no model in the loop.

Five tools: `webmint_setup`, `webmint_mint`, `webmint_run`, `webmint_list`, `webmint_remove`.

Two properties that matter for admission:

- **Model-agnostic by construction.** It calls the host's `ctx.llm`; there is no vendor SDK, no
  API key of its own, and no bundled client. Whatever provider the profile runs is what mints.
- **Verification is the gate.** A mint is persisted only if two runs return the same field set,
  both return rows, and every declared field is populated in at least half the rows. A spec that
  returns 25 rows of `null` is rejected and re-minted, not shipped. (That case is in the README.)

## Disclosure

- Needs Node >= 18 and Playwright. On first mint the plugin installs Playwright + Chromium into
  its own directory (~120 MB, one time); `WEBMINT_NO_AUTO_SETUP=1` disables that and
  `webmint_setup` reports readiness explicitly. Node and Playwright are discovered, not assumed.
- **Read-only.** It reads pages. It does not submit forms, log in, or write anywhere.
- Headless Chromium is refused by some bot-protected sites (2 of 8 in the README's sample). That
  limitation is stated up front rather than discovered by users.

## Gates run locally, at the pinned SHA

```
$ git clone https://github.com/DECRUX9812/webmint /tmp/webmint-pin
$ git -C /tmp/webmint-pin checkout --detach 1a0aa249b5d51c162d6e2cba46ff34e843606094
$ hermes plugins validate /tmp/webmint-pin
✓ manifest — plugin.yaml parses

✓ requires_hermes — spec '>=0.22' parses
✓ config schema — not declared
✓ requires_env — all entries UPPER_SNAKE

✓ loadable — entry: __init__.py
✓ python dependencies — none declared
✓ capability probe — register() ran in isolation
✓ declared tools — matches registrations
✓ declared hooks — matches registrations
✓ declared middleware — matches registrations

✓ security scan — safe
✓ no core override — no runtime rebinds of Hermes core
Validation passed.

$ python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py <entry>
OK: 1 file(s) valid
```

The diff is exactly one added file. No self-updating code: the plugin never fetches, downloads or
replaces its own files; its only network access is the host's model call at mint time and the
site it is asked to capture.

## Repo age

The repository was created today, so it is inside any maturity window you apply to young repos. I
am happy to re-pin after a period, or to wait before this merges — a SHA bump is a one-line PR
under rule 4.

Note on CI: fork PRs need a maintainer to approve the workflow run before checks appear. The local

## What this plugin does

`muse-harness` starts a local `muse serve` process and speaks Muse Session Protocol (newline JSON-RPC) so a Hermes tool can run one turn inside Muse Code. Wonder Full stays inside the official harness. The tool can attach session MCP servers, which is how that turn calls something like Unreal mid-run.

It does not mint a Muse Code subscription key, does not read Muse credential files, and does not call `api.meta.ai` itself.

- Default approval mode is `denyUnmatched`. `allowAll` is only used when the tool call sets it. No `--yolo`, no sandbox disable.
- Unattended runs hit `timeout_s` (default 600, max 1200) instead of waiting on a browser login.
- No telemetry. No self-updater. No bundled binaries.

## What this plugin does

GameForge is an offline-by-default game-development toolkit for Hermes Agent. One prompt builds a real game: procedural SFX (22 sfxr-compatible presets), mood-based music loops with MIDI + stems, NPC voices (Animalese babble, Edge/Hermes neural TTS + character FX), pixel-art sprite sheets (16x16 RPG, 4-dir walk/idle, TexturePacker/Phaser/Godot export), seamless Wang autotiling tilesets with Godot TileSet + collision, low-poly and AI 3D models (.glb + turntables), 4 playable web genres (topdown, platformer, arena, roguelike), Godot 4 / Unity scaffolds, headless Blender + Unreal pipelines, an automated playtester (explorer/monkey/vision-LLM agent, 40x Godot bot-play, crash/stuck/boredom verdicts with HTML/JSON/MD reports), and one-click export (PWA, itch.io, single-HTML, Capacitor, butler push).

Settings live in the standard surface only: Desktop Settings → Plugins → GameForge (config_schema in plugin.yaml), no custom preferences UI.

## Surfaces used

- Tools (9): forge_sfx, forge_music, forge_voice, forge_sprite, forge_tileset, forge_model3d, forge_engine, forge_playtest, forge_export
- Hooks: none
- Middleware: none
- Env (optional secrets only): FAL_KEY, MESHY_API_KEY, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY
- CLI: `hermes gameforge demo`
- Skills (10): gameforge:game-studio, playtesting, godot-dev, unity-dev, blender-pipeline, game-audio, pixel-art-pipeline, 3d-asset-pipeline, ship-it, game-reverse-engineering

## Validation

```
hermes plugins validate ~/Code/hermes-plugin-gameforge --install-deps --json
# ok: true, 15/15 checks green, 0 warnings (manifest, requires_hermes, config schema,
# requires_env UPPER_SNAKE, loadable, capability probe, declared tools/hooks/middleware
# match registrations, no built-in collisions, security scan safe, no core override)
```

Entry pins full 40-hex SHA `d88bdd1dd0fbc4c684dbe5361f330cf478b0a7e3` (v1.1.0, HEAD of DECRUX9812/hermes-plugin-gameforge). No `subdir` (plugin at repo root). Category `tools`, tier `community`.

## Disclosure (admission rules 9-13)

- No destructive or irreversible default: everything writes inside the game project dir (+ throwaway browser profile). No `rm -rf`, no system writes, no auto-publish.
- No exfiltration: offline by default (pure Python + Pillow). Network only on explicit opt-in calls: fal.ai / Meshy (prompt+image for 3D), ElevenLabs (SFX prompt), Edge TTS (dialogue text, if installed), GitHub (~1 GB Godot export templates, only `forge_export target=godot_templates`), itch.io via butler (only `target=itch` with explicit `itch_target`).

- Env vars are secrets only (FAL_KEY / MESHY_API_KEY / ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, stored in .env); paths (`godot_path`, `unity_path`, `blender_path`, `unreal_path`, `browser_path`, `default_project`) live in config_schema, not requires_env.
- No core override, no install scripts, no telemetry. Description carries the Disclosure block verbatim.

prs.title: catalog: add agent-reel
prs.body:
Adds `agent-reel` to the catalog at pinned commit `1005afe2249f76d109f55f29621278fa82a51297`. One plugin, one file, one entry.

**What it does.** Reads your own Hermes history read-only, finds a story with a problem/struggle/result, writes a chapter script where every line and caption carries the ids of the messages that state it (a claim the cited messages do not support is refused rather than printed), then draws the episode through your own image route and letters it. A series ledger carries one open thread into the next chapter and refuses repeats; an idea deck of 16.9 billion frames varies world/villain/genre per chapter; 55 art styles.

**Registration.** One CLI command (`hermes reel`). No tools, no hooks, no middleware. `kind: standalone`.

**Checks at the pinned commit**
- `hermes plugins validate` → passed (manifest v2, `requires_hermes >=0.21.5`, `pillow>=10.0,<14` with an upper bound, declared `requires_env`).
- `hermes plugins doctor --ci` → runtime discovery, manifest parsing, import and registration passed.
- Validated against a clean clone of upstream `NousResearch/hermes-agent` with its own venv: `doctor_plugin` → ok, zero findings.
- Suite: 662 tests.

**Rule 11 (credentials).** API keys for the optional paid image routes are read through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret` with the environment only as a CLI fallback; no key is needed for the `host` or `comfyui` routes. Declared in `requires_env` and in the entry's capabilities.

**Disclosure (rule 13).** The entry description carries it: reads history read-only (strace proof in `scripts/readonly_proof.sh`), sends redacted text to Hermes's own model and panel prompts to the chosen image route, stores plans/renders/ledger/kits in the plugin data directory, no telemetry, no auto-posting.

**What the entry declares as `known_issues`.** All 55 styles render (`--strict-styles` limits a run to the styles with a recorded bake-off); images are drawn by the route you choose, roughly 3-20p per panel on paid APIs and free on a local GPU, with `--budget` capping new images; a line with no pocket in the art is recorded as unplaced and reported rather than given invented space; public mode refuses any real person without a consent record.

prs.body:
Adds `plugin-catalog/revamp.yaml` for REVamp, a community Winamp-style music, audiobook, and radio player for Hermes Desktop.

Pinned source: https://github.com/KeyArgo/hermes-revamp @ `a882c1e499622b8652a39c04e2a13f9487f93a83` (`1.0.0-alpha.4`). This is an alpha listing.

## Validation

- `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passed at the pinned source.
- Manifest/capability probe passed: 4 tools and 6 observer-only hooks.
- Security scan passed; no core overrides; desktop surface stays within the plugin SDK.
- Public-source CI is green on Linux, Windows, and macOS.

## Disclosures

- Runs a token-protected loopback server on `127.0.0.1` while Hermes runs.
- Reads the user’s configured music/book folders, media tags/art, and Hermes configuration; stores state, a token, optional skins, and private backups in its own data directories.
- Contacts Radio Browser, user-selected radio streams and favicon hosts, LRCLIB, and the Webamp Skin Museum.
- May invoke `ffprobe` when installed and optionally opens a local Chrome-family pop-out.
- Has no accounts, telemetry, stored passwords, or self-updater.

The entry follows the established Adolanium catalog-entry layout and uses an exact 40-character SHA pin.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: bump hermes-vcc-engine to 0.4.3
prs.body:
Re-pins `hermes-vcc-engine` from `31ee4fe` (0.4.1) to `ddc3a1d` (0.4.3, tag `v0.4.3`). It started as a 0.4.2 bump. 0.4.3 adds one opt-in option on top, so the PR moved to it instead of opening a second one.

**Commit range:** https://github.com/danbiocchi/hermes-vcc-engine/compare/31ee4fe7ef3e3f6c67dadfd45ebc1a3cb9773f95...ddc3a1db37cd27c626d29c8395e5538e59b74ec8

**What changed upstream:** fixes for the problems found in a public review of 0.4.1, plus the ones found while checking them. The summary text changes. Full notes: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/danbiocchi/hermes-vcc-engine/blob/ddc3a1db37cd27c626d29c8395e5538e59b74ec8/docs/CHANGELOG.md).
- **Web, browser and MCP results are classified by their content.** Hermes wraps these results in `<untrusted_tool_result>` with a fixed preamble, which stopped the engine from parsing the JSON inside. On a corpus of 163 wrapped results, 4 successes were marked failed and 8 failures were marked ok. The engine now removes Hermes's own envelope before classifying the result, and all 163 match their success flag.
- **A failure fixed after a compaction leaves Blocked**, instead of staying there while Commands Run said it succeeded.
- **A failed file action is no longer listed as done** (`write failed (not written)` instead of `written`).
- **Successful MCP results keep their payload** (`result` / `structuredContent`), and so do core tools that return only a `message`.
- **`memory_context` from a memory provider's `on_pre_compress` is kept** in its own section, treated as data and capped.
- **`compression.proactive_prune_*` settings reach the engine**, with Hermes's own parsing and floors.
- **The compaction trigger leaves room for the model's output, as the stock compressor does.** Plugin engines don't receive `max_tokens` (see #115522), so the engine asks `_compressor_max_tokens` for the same value on its first `update_model`. This only matters for providers with a reservation, such as native Gemini.
- **The budget fit no longer overshoots by its own "lines omitted" note.** That overshoot caused a hard cut on 4 of 22 real windows; now on none.
- Offline `bench/` scripts were added and updated. Hermes doesn't load them.
- **0.4.3: new option `context.vcc.only_local_models`** (default `false`, so behavior is unchanged unless it is set). When it is on, each compaction checks the chat model's endpoint with Hermes's own `agent.model_metadata.is_local_endpoint`. A local model gets the vcc summary. A hosted model gets Hermes's stock LLM summary, and the summariser's context window caps the trigger as it does for the built-in compressor.

**Entry changes:** `sha` (also in the `image:` and `screenshots:` URLs) and `version` bumped together. The description and disclosure are unchanged.

**Disclosure (rule 13), unchanged from the listed version:**
- **Network:** none of its own. No model call on the normal path. If a projection raises and `context.vcc.fallback_to_llm` is on (the default), that pass uses Hermes's own stock summary call to the model Hermes is configured with.
- **Files:** reads only Hermes's `config.yaml`, through `hermes_cli.config.load_config_readonly()`. Writes no files.
- **Not used:** shell commands, subprocesses, credentials, environment variables, background processes, telemetry and self-update. Standard library only.
- **Internals:** subclasses `ContextCompressor` and relies on its private methods. A startup check falls back to the stock compressor if any is missing. New in this version: calls to `agent.agent_init._compressor_max_tokens` and `agent.model_metadata.is_local_endpoint`. If either is missing, the engine behaves as before (no reservation, and the summary is always written by vcc).

**Compatibility (rule 14):** `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.7"` stays. All 114 tests pass against Hermes v0.21.7, v0.22.2 and v0.22.4.

**Checks:**
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/hermes-vcc-engine.yaml` → OK
- `hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` on the new sha → passed. It reports the same private-import warnings (rule 9) as before, plus the ones above.
- Upstream CI is green (Python 3.11–3.14)
- `bench/proofs.py` on real sessions: 821 / 821 log lines verified against their source messages, 11 / 11 planted fabrications caught, 467 / 467 `[#N]` links opened the right message
- The image and screenshot URLs at the new sha return 200
