prs.title: plugin-catalog: add dynamic-memory
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one plugin-catalog entry: `plugin-catalog/dynamic-memory.yaml`.

`dynamic-memory` is a keyword-index memory pattern for Hermes. A small resident index of `keyword,keyword → file.md` routing lines stays in the system prompt; verbose topic files stay on disk and enter context only when the conversation touches their keywords. Retrieval is the model reading a literal index — no embeddings, no vector store, no retrieval service.

It is not a memory provider and registers no backend. It is a `pre_tool_call` hook plus a `tool_execution` middleware that keeps the index well-formed, which is why it is submitted here as a standalone plugin rather than under `plugins/memory/` (CONTRIBUTING: that lane is closed to new providers).

## Related Issue

Not applicable — this adds a catalog listing, no code change. Two open issues propose *core* variants of the idea (#22612 indexed memory routing, #59576/#60462 progressive-disclosure tiers); this is the standalone-plugin path for the same problem, with no core patch and no changes to existing behavior.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

Catalog entry (metadata only) — none of the boxes above describe it accurately, so none are checked.

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/dynamic-memory.yaml` — new entry, `tier: community`, `category: memory`, pinned to `bd0dd6eef7659fe95f6fcb604116f3d62ee13c16`, `subdir: plugin/memory-shaper`.

Submitted by the repository owner (`ockentap`), per admission rule 5.

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins validate <checkout>/plugin/memory-shaper` at the pinned commit — passes:
   ```
   ✓ manifest / ✓ loadable / ✓ capability probe / ✓ declared hooks
   ✓ declared middleware — matches registrations
   ✓ security scan — safe / ✓ no core override
   Validation passed.
   ```
   Run against a **fresh clone at the pinned SHA**, not a local working tree.
2. After a catalog install, `hermes plugins list` shows `memory-shaper` enabled with the `pre_tool_call` hook and `tool_execution` middleware registered.
3. Behavioral check: write a malformed index line through the memory tool → refused with a fix message; `cat ~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md` → still allowed.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- **Writes:** refuses other tools' writes to `~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md` (`write_file`, `patch`, shell redirects, `tee`, `sed -i`). Refuses malformed index lines with a fix message instead of silently correcting them. Read-only commands always pass so the agent can audit the file it maintains.
- **Escape hatch:** a scripted wholesale rewrite is permitted when `$HERMES_HOME/state/.memory_shaper_rewrite_approved` exists. Documented in the plugin README; no other path bypasses the guard.
- **Reads:** only `$HERMES_HOME/memories/`.
- **Network:** none. **Shell:** none. **Background processes:** none. **Self-updater:** none. **Credentials:** none read or stored.

## Benchmark claim, stated with its limits

The repo compares against native memory on six complex memories (30 detail probes): native 11/30, this pattern 30/30, with method and limitations in `docs/complexity.md`. The live-corpus routing figure (28/30 to the right file on the first try, 7,140 prompt tokens vs 171,091 for the full corpus) was measured on a deliberately weak flash-tier model and should be read as a floor, not a capability claim. Reproducible without API keys: `python3 benchmarks/scripts/run_complexity.py --verify-only`.

## Checklist

No code, tests, docs or config keys in this repository change — only a catalog metadata file. The repo-wide gates therefore do not apply to this diff; the catalog gate (`hermes plugins validate`) is the one that does, and it passes at the pin.

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit message follows Conventional Commits (`plugin-catalog: add dynamic-memory`)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs and catalog entries — no `dynamic-memory` or `memory-shaper` entry exists, and no open PR adds one
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this entry (one file)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04 / arm64, Hermes v0.22.5+14.g7bc40cb
- [ ] `pytest tests/ -q` and `python scripts/check` — not run, no code in this repo is touched (N/A)
- [ ] Tests added — N/A, metadata only
- [ ] Docs updated — N/A

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add BriefNest desktop news dashboard
prs.body:
## Summary

Please add **BriefNest · 讯集** (formerly Intelligence Feed) as a `community` / `desktop` plugin. I own the upstream plugin repository (`bit-RGB/briefnest`). The internal plugin ID and catalog key remain `intelligence-feed` for compatibility with existing installations, routes and stored reading/bookmark data.

- Repository: https://github.com/bit-RGB/briefnest
- Release: https://github.com/bit-RGB/briefnest/releases/tag/v0.1.0
- Exact pin: `98a347c8c2b52d74a9feb294e40366f2a50c3649` (branding-only follow-up to the original v0.1.0 release commit; the existing release tag was not rewritten)
- Version: `0.1.0`
- License: MIT

A multi-channel news dashboard for Hermes Desktop: semiconductor, AI, automotive, music, Weibo hot topics, and bookmarks. It supports title search, read/unread filters, source enable/disable controls, and an embedded webpage preview with persistent zoom settings.

## Hermes surfaces

- Native `plugin.yaml`, a no-op `register(ctx)` entrypoint, `dashboard/manifest.json` / FastAPI backend, and `desktop/plugin.js`.
- Desktop uses `@hermes/plugin-sdk`, React, scoped backend requests, and plugin-local settings storage.
- No tools, hooks, or middleware are registered; the corresponding catalog capabilities are empty.
- No self-updater, core runtime overrides, renderer prototype patches, telemetry, or bundled native executables/model weights.

## Behaviour / risk disclosures

- Makes HTTPS requests to third-party news sites configured in `config/sources.json`. Sources include Chinese news portals, official AI/company blogs, Nature and Weibo. Opening a preview or an external article also connects to the original website.
- Persists collected titles, links, source settings, reading state and bookmarks in local SQLite. The Windows default is `%LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/data/intelligence-feed`; `INTELLIGENCE_FEED_DATA_DIR` overrides it. The default data directory is shared rather than physically isolated by Hermes profile.
- The webpage preview uses an Electron `webview`. It executes a small fixed script in the third-party guest page to install zoom shortcut listeners and adjust horizontal overflow; only `in`, `out`, and `reset` messages on a per-navigation channel are accepted. Guest-provided text is not evaluated in the host, and Node/preload permissions are not added.
- Optional local title translation lazily imports `ctranslate2` / `sentencepiece` and loads a user-provided Marian model. No model is bundled or automatically downloaded. Missing translation support does not prevent news collection.
- No LLM API key is required. Default sources require no credentials. The generic legacy source adapter supports an `api_key_env` option via `os.environ`, but no configured source uses it; please flag any needed change to that unused compatibility path under the current secret-scope policy.
- Installation does not create cron jobs or background collection services. Manual collection scripts are included. The Windows legacy cron launcher assumes the default install path.
- No shell subprocesses are launched by the plugin during normal operation.

## Validation

Against a clean archive of the exact pinned commit:

- Executed the installed Hermes `hermes_cli.plugin_validate.validate_plugin_dir` admission routine directly: **all 16 checks pass, zero warnings**, security scan `safe`, desktop SDK surface passes, capability probe passes, no core override.
- The routine was invoked directly to avoid the local Hermes launcher's unrelated automatic dependency synchronization. This is not a claim that `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` was completed; catalog CI should verify the dependency installation seam under its own core constraints.
- `python -m pytest tests/ -q`: **268 passed** (one upstream Starlette/httpx deprecation warning).
- `node --test tests/test_desktop_navigation.mjs tests/test_desktop_preview.mjs`: **5 passed**.
- No claim of a fresh end-to-end install on other operating systems or live availability of every news source.

## Known limitations / review notes

- Current UI and README are Chinese. Only Windows is listed as tested/supported for this submission.
- No guessed `requires_hermes` floor is declared; the required Desktop SDK/dashboard API surface is documented in the upstream README. Please advise if a verified SemVer floor is required before admission.
- A fresh live Desktop screenshot is not attached to this initial submission; it can be supplied during review. The screenshot limitation is not being represented as completed UI acceptance testing.
- News titles/articles and third-party trademarks are not covered by the code's MIT license.

This PR adds only `plugin-catalog/intelligence-feed.yaml`; it does not change Hermes core.

## What does this PR do?

Bumps the **crew** plugin-catalog entry to 0.10.5 and re-pins it to the release commit: [macd2/Crew](https://github.com/macd2/Crew) `998fd9d` -> `b1cfccd` (tag `v0.10.5`).

What changed from 0.10.1 to 0.10.5 (four releases):

- **0.10.5, one card link (#18, #22, #23):** a card has one shareable address, `<dashboard>/crew?card=<id>`, that opens it on the standalone page, in the Hermes web dashboard's Crew tab and in Desktop; the ticket id in a Desktop chat message is that link and a click opens the card in-app (only a link to this dashboard that reads as the id). Crew's Windows steps start Hermes from the checkout's own launcher. Rescope questions show what changed in a long proof command, and endings say how far the card got. Ideas from @phuongvm.
- **0.10.4, lighter polling (#20, #21):** the board and card pages are polled every 2 s and each poll rebuilt the whole graph with a database connection per query (64 for the board, 108-118 for a card). prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add ankle (ANKLE OS)
prs.body:
Adds `plugin-catalog/ankle.yaml`: **ANKLE OS**, a portable Agent Plugins v1 package (no executable code), pinned to `aleqth/ankle-hermes-plugin@f7ce94105e3410bfe30f436369f7b25ec435c435`.

## What it is
`plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + `skills/ankle/SKILL.md`. The MCP server is ANKLE OS's hosted endpoint (Streamable HTTP, `https://aleqth.com/api/mcp`). With it, a Hermes agent can list and found Worlds, create private website drafts, read and patch them with revision checks, search the SURF cultural archive, transcribe references into DADA objects, and leave proposals for World owners.

## Disclosures
- **Hosted connector.** Tool arguments (search queries, World names, authored HTML for drafts and patches) are sent to `https://aleqth.com/api/mcp`, and only when an `ankle` tool is invoked. No telemetry; no background calls.
- **Authentication is required for every call**, including discovery. Either set a scoped agent key (`ANKLE_AGENT_KEY`, minted at https://aleqth.com/developers; the bundled `mcp.json` sends it as `Authorization: Bearer ${ANKLE_AGENT_KEY}`), or use OAuth 2.1 with the device flow (`hermes mcp add ankle --url https://aleqth.com/api/mcp --auth oauth`, then `hermes mcp login ankle --flow device`). Unauthenticated requests get HTTP 401, and grants are revocable at https://aleqth.com/developers.
- **Least privilege by scope.** New pages are private drafts; publishing requires an explicitly granted publish scope. No wallet, signing, trading or spending tools are exposed.
- `capabilities`: no tools, hooks or middleware provided by plugin code; `requires_env: [ANKLE_AGENT_KEY]` for the key path.

## Testing done (2026-10-25)
- `hermes plugins validate .` at the pinned commit: portable manifest parses (Agent Plugins v1), manifest fields present, security scan **safe**, isolation: portable (no Python).
- Key path: with `ANKLE_AGENT_KEY` unset, Hermes refuses to connect (`${ANKLE_AGENT_KEY} ... is not set`) and sends no unauthenticated request.
- OAuth path, end to end in an isolated `HERMES_HOME`: `hermes mcp login ankle --flow device` → approved at https://aleqth.com/oauth/device → `hermes mcp test ankle`: connected in about 1.6 s, **10 tools discovered** with the default scopes (`worlds_list`, `builder_list`, `builder_create`, `builder_get`, `builder_patch`, `surf_search`, `dada_transcribe`, `world_describe`, `world_read`, `world_propose`). The test grant was then revoked via `/oauth/revoke` and confirmed refused (401 `agent key revoked`).

Maintainer: @aleqth (ANKLE LLC). Docs: https://ankle.md/SKILL.md

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: feat(catalog): add laya-oneshot
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds the community **laya-oneshot** plugin to the Hermes Plugin Catalog.

The plugin exposes one tool, `laya_decide`: it asks typed questions about a piece of text
(yes/no, pick one of N, score on a scale) and returns probabilities from an open
[Laya](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya) checkpoint in about a second. The model is loaded
for that one call and the process exits — no server, no port, no resident memory, no API key.

Pinned plugin source:

- repo: `gergeisabo/laya-oneshot`
- commit: `0251efbaa1dc530760fe790ff1e6fa2cd8e8b2d4`
- plugin version: `0.1.0`

### Safety / disclosure

- Registers **one tool**; no hooks, no middleware, no desktop surface.
- **No credentials.** `requires_env: []`, no config schema, no OAuth.
- **No Python dependencies** declared: the plugin shells out to the `laya-oneshot` CLI, which the
  user installs themselves (`external_dependencies` documents the exact command). This keeps
  Hermes's managed environment untouched and avoids adding a package to its solve.
- **No self-updater**, no network calls of its own, no compiled binaries.
- Raw text being decided about is sent to the model host: either this machine, or an ssh host the
  user configures. No third party is called.
- The model is a ~400M-parameter encoder, not a language model. It is a fast filter in front of an
  expensive call; the README says plainly where not to use it (multi-step reasoning, long inputs,
  any label you would not train on your own data first).

## Changes Made

- Added `plugin-catalog/laya-oneshot.yaml`.

## Validation

At the pinned commit `0251efb`:

- `hermes plugins validate .` — **PASS** (manifest, loadable entry, capability probe, declared
  tools match registrations, built-in tool collisions none, security scan safe, no core override).
- `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/laya-oneshot.yaml` — **OK: 1 file(s) valid**.
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_validate_plugin_catalog.py tests/website/test_catalog_rules_mirror.py -q`
  — **40 passed**.
- End to end: `hermes plugins install gergeisabo/laya-oneshot --ref 0251efba…` cloned, installed and
  appeared in `hermes plugins list` as `git pinned@0251efba` (removed afterwards).
- The same repo also carries `skills/laya-oneshot/SKILL.md`, verified with
  `hermes skills install gergeisabo/laya-oneshot/skills/laya-oneshot` — so the functionality is
  reachable without the plugin, for anyone who would rather not add a tool schema.

Not run: the full suite — this diff only adds one catalog YAML.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The catalog already has **local-system-one-hermes**, which also uses Laya, but as a loopback HTTP
  sidecar wired into `pre_llm_call` and `llm_request`. This is the opposite trade-off: one tool, no
  sidecar, no hook, and a cold start instead of residency. Not a duplicate — worth a look if you
  would rather see one Laya entry than two.
- `python_dependencies` is deliberately empty rather than `laya-oneshot==0.1.0`: the CLI is not on
  PyPI, and pulling a CLI tool into Hermes's env for one tool call is the heavier option.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add squad-hub (Hermes Agent Squads Hub)
prs.body:
Adds `plugin-catalog/squad-hub.yaml`: **Hermes Agent Squads Hub**, a community Desktop plugin for people who run
[Hermes Agent Squads](https://github.com/PuntoyComaTech/hermes-agent-squads) (a manager bot per squad, workers on a
Kanban board). Submitted by the repository owner.

## What it does

- **One list, no profile switch.** A Desktop pane lists bot → project → folder → main checkout or worktree → chat.
  Each chat opens as a tab under its own bot, so several bots stay open at once and the window never reloads.
- **Squads at work.** A manager's row shows its Kanban board's count. A read-only **timeline** draws each bot's runs
  (6 h to 7 days) next to a **What went wrong** list (crashes, timeouts, retries, blocks).
- **The bell** lists what waits on you across bots (approvals, clarify questions, blocked cards). A card opens with the
  question it asks and a button that drafts the answer in a chat with the manager.
- **PR and dirty chips per worktree**, read through Desktop's git review surface.
- **Live Kanban cards in chat** (`::squad-task{...}` directive). **Managers ask with buttons**: the agent half adds a
  prompt section telling squad managers to ask through `clarify` with suggested answers.
- **The empty chat names the squad** in the official `chat.empty` slot with the SDK `Wordmark`, plus the project and
  folder the chat works in.

## Hermes surfaces used

- Desktop plugin SDK only: pane, status-bar and title-bar slots, `chat.empty`, a markdown directive, a route, settings,
  `host.requestProfile` / `rpc` (`session.active_list`, `plugins.manage` settings), the Kanban plugin's REST routes with
  GET only, git review, `ctx.os.notify`. `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes, including the `desktop
  surface` and `no core override` checks; security scan: safe.
- Agent half: `register_system_prompt_section`, hooks `post_tool_call` (`kanban_create` only, to remember filed cards)
  and `transform_llm_output` (adds up to three card lines, Desktop platform only, and only when the Desktop half has set
  the plugin's own `desktop_cards` setting). Fail-open; it does nothing in cron, subagents or workers.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- No network calls of its own and no telemetry. PR chips come from Desktop's own git review surface; the plugin never
  calls GitHub itself.
- Reads other profiles' session lists and Kanban boards through Hermes' own RPC and REST routes. It asks only backends
  that are already running and never wakes a sleeping bot.
- Writes only its own `desktop_cards` setting on manager profiles (through `plugins.manage`), clearing it on dispose,
  plus Desktop plugin storage for its preferences.
- Never reads `.env` or credentials. "Edit .env" opens the file in the system editor.
- Theme and layout presets are opt-in buttons; nothing is applied on install. Native notifications are opt-in.
- No self-updater. Squad workers never get the plugin.

## Screenshots (invented data)

![Empty chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PuntoyComaTech/hermes-agent-squads/2695b14754f5dc186e431dc27a2d870664031321/squads/_plugins/squad-hub/docs/empty-chat.png)
![Timeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PuntoyComaTech/hermes-agent-squads/2695b14754f5dc186e431dc27a2d870664031321/squads/_plugins/squad-hub/docs/timeline.png)
![Bell](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PuntoyComaTech/hermes-agent-squads/2695b14754f5dc186e431dc27a2d870664031321/squads/_plugins/squad-hub/docs/bell.png)

(Hermes 0.22.2).

prs.title: feat(catalog): add model-fallback-heuristic plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds **`model-fallback-heuristic`** (*Fallback — Model Switching Heuristics*) to the official Hermes Plugin Catalog (`plugin-catalog/model-fallback-heuristic.yaml`).

- **Repository:** https://github.com/tomkubik/hermes-fallback
- **Pinned Commit SHA:** `10e91c4c199c3272e7a3b8086660133d2101e248` (`v0.2.0`)
- **Category:** `models`
- **Tier:** `community`
- **Requires Hermes:** `>=0.19`

### What It Does
- **Multi-Provider Heuristic Model Fallback & Orchestrator Failover:** Dynamically discovers and ranks concrete fallback models across all configured/authenticated providers (`openrouter`, `nous`, `gemini`, `zai`, `kimi-coding`, `minimax`, `huggingface`, `opencode-zen`, `nvidia`, `openai-codex`, `anthropic`, etc.) using configurable ranking strategies (`largest_parameter_count`, `greatest_context`, `latest`, `latest_flash`, `smallest`, `provider_preference`) and filters (`free_only`, `require_tools`, `flash_only`, `min_context`/`max_context`, `min_params`/`max_params`, `vendor`, `name_filter`, `reasoning_effort`).
- **Zero-LLM-Call Recovery:** Works both automatically via orchestrator hooks/middleware (`on_session_start`, `pre_llm_call`, `api_request_error`, `llm_request`, `llm_execution`) and deterministically without an LLM call via CLI (`hermes fallback-heuristic ...`) and slash commands (`/fallback ...`) when the user's primary model is rate-limited or offline.

### Capabilities
- **`provides_tools`**: `fallback_heuristic_resolve`, `fallback_heuristic_switch`, `fallback_heuristic_configure`, `fallback_heuristic_providers`
- **`provides_hooks`**: `on_session_start`, `pre_llm_call`, `api_request_error`
- **`provides_middleware`**: `llm_request`, `llm_execution`
- **`requires_env`**: `[]`

### Disclosure (Catalog Rule 13)
- Reads and updates `fallback_providers` and `plugins.model-fallback-heuristic` settings in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
- Queries public model catalog endpoints (`https://models.dev/api.json`, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`, and `https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1/portal/models`) to enrich model parameter counts, context windows, and free-tier availability.
- Optional interactive CLI onboarding (`hermes fallback-heuristic free-setup`) can save user-entered provider API keys to `~/.hermes/.env` when explicitly requested by the user in an interactive terminal.

### Verification
- `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/model-fallback-heuristic.yaml` -> `OK: 1 file(s) valid`
- `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` -> `Validation passed` (all 15 checks pass)
- `python3 scripts/scan_plugin_payloads.py` -> pass (0 findings)
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_catalog.py tests/scripts/test_validate_plugin_catalog.py` -> 53 passed

prs.title: plugin-catalog: bump telesec to 0.17.0
prs.body:
## Summary

Bump **Telesec** from 0.16.1 to **0.17.0**, pinned to `74d2d97ad4023aefcd49b287cd9778659111ddf0` ([release v0.17.0](https://github.com/neoromantic/telesec/releases/tag/v0.17.0)). I own the plugin repository. This PR changes one file, `plugin-catalog/telesec.yaml`: `sha` and `version` together, the image URLs pinned to the same commit, and the disclosure. Telesec is not affiliated with Nous Research.

Commit range to review: [b23cd63...74d2d97](https://github.com/neoromantic/telesec/compare/b23cd63358e1a66518106c485402a9033f6b31d9...74d2d97ad4023aefcd49b287cd9778659111ddf0) (code changes in neoromantic/telesec#108 and neoromantic/telesec#109; the rest is CI and docs).

## What changed in 0.17.0

- **Raw-first transcripts.** The transcript is posted as soon as STT returns. When cleanup changes the text, the bot edits that same caption or reply in place (`editMessageCaption` / `editMessageText` with the `business_connection_id`). It never posts a second transcript.
- **Deletion alerts.** With history on, when a contact deletes a message that no later message explains, the bot sends a short alert to the owner's private chat with the bot, with **Show text** and **Chat panel** buttons. The alert holds no message text; on the owner's tap, the bot edits it to add the deleted text from local history. On by default once history is on; switched in Settings, in a chat's panel, or with `hermes telesec settings set alerts` / `hermes telesec chat set <chat> --alerts`. Nothing goes into the Business chat.
- **Compact switches** in Settings and the owner panel (new screenshots).
- **Usage stats** (see the disclosure below).

## Disclosure changes

- **Usage stats (new, opt-out).** The plugin sends usage stats over HTTPS to `https://usage.sergeybaus.com`, which passes them to PostHog: `app_installed`, `app_started`, `feature_used` with a name from a fixed list, and `error_occurred` with an error type or code only. Each event goes at most once a UTC day, with the plugin version, OS, architecture, Python version, and a random install ID stored in `HERMES_HOME/data/telesec/`. Never sent: message content, transcripts, names, chat/user/connection IDs, paths, settings values, keys, or error text. **Nothing is sent before the owner has seen a notice** that the gateway sends once to the owner's private chat with the bot, with a **Turn off usage stats** button; sending starts at the next gateway start. Off switches: **Don't share** in Settings (`/telesec`), `hermes telesec telemetry off`, `TELESEC_TELEMETRY=0`, or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`. It is also off in CI, tests, and development versions. The client is the stdlib-only `telemetry.py` (a daemon thread per request, 3-second timeout, one attempt). The catalog policy asks for opt-in telemetry; this one is on by default after the notice, so the entry states it plainly.
- **Bot API, edits in place:** cleanup edits the posted transcript (above).
- **Bot API, deletion alerts:** messages and edits only in the owner's private chat with the bot (above).
- **Bot API, `/stats`:** for the owner's `/stats`, the bot edits that command into a stats card the contact sees (`editMessageText` with a rich message). If the edit fails, it sends the card (`sendRichMessage`, else plain text) or a short notice into the same Business chat and deletes the command and the notice (`deleteBusinessMessages`). Added to the entry next to the existing `/dossier` line.
- **Direct model calls (unchanged since 0.16, now spelled out in the entry):** two optional dossier steps, both off by default, call a model directly over HTTPS with the standard library: a message check (TypeSafe Jev through Vercel AI Gateway, zero data retention) and fact extraction (Cloudflare Workers AI). They read `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` through the Hermes secret scope, never from credential files, and never store or log them. `requires_env` stays empty because both steps are optional.
- **Dossier model:** if the `telesec_dossier` task fails, Hermes may retry with the task's fallback chain and then the main model; the plugin cannot turn this off.
- **Background work:** the dossier thread starts on adapter connect even while dossiers are off and only checks the stored switch every minute; model calls happen only after the owner turns dossiers on.
- **Settings:** transcription, history, retention, dossiers, deletion alerts, and usage stats are switched in Telegram (`/telesec` and the Manage Bot panel) or with `hermes telesec settings`, with no restart. The Desktop form keeps only `cleanup_style` and `agent_enable`; it has no setting for usage stats.
- The `description` line now says "opt-out usage stats ...; no self-updater" instead of "no telemetry".

Unchanged: no tools, no middleware, no core overrides; one hook (`pre_gateway_dispatch`); no Python dependencies; no binaries or JS; `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.6"`; the one private STT import (`tools.transcription_tools.transcribe_audio`, tracked in #142505).

## Validation

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/`: OK, no warnings for this entry.
- Every image URL returns 200 at the pinned SHA.
- Plugin CI at the pinned commit: pytest on Python 3.11–3.14 and ruff pass (the latest run is green).
- The release runs on the maintainer's Hermes gateway, with a live smoke recorded in the plugin's `docs/VERIFY.md`.

## Screenshots

Real Telegram screenshots over made-up data, pinned to the same commit. `settings.png` is new and shows the usage stats switch; `stats-panel-en.png` and `dossier-panel-en.png` replace the `@2x` files.

![owner panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neoromantic/telesec/74d2d97ad4023aefcd49b287cd9778659111ddf0/docs/images/owner-panel.png)

![settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neoromantic/telesec/74d2d97ad4023aefcd49b287cd9778659111ddf0/docs/images/settings.png)

prs.title: feat(catalog): add Hermes-iOS-sim community plugin
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one community catalog entry for **Hermes-iOS-sim**, submitted by its repository owner. It builds, installs and launches an authorized Xcode app target and connects its Simulator preview to Hermes Browser through localhost. Optional Desktop controls provide target discovery, prerequisite checks, status and owned-runtime controls.

- Repository: https://github.com/akinduroifedayo/Hermes-iOS-sim
- Release: https://github.com/akinduroifedayo/Hermes-iOS-sim/releases/tag/v1.0.0
- Exact pin: `7f48cf060e76eae29a2bdef77c2969ba6ca9898f`, subdirectory `plugin`.
- macOS only. No minimum compatible Hermes version is asserted; the manifest and entry both omit `requires_hermes` rather than inventing a supported floor.

## Related Issue

None. Searched existing issues and PRs for the exact project name and found no existing catalog submission.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature: community catalog listing only.

## Changes Made

Adds only `plugin-catalog/hermes-ios.yaml`. No Hermes core, bundled plugin, dependency lock or runtime code changes.

The entry declares the manifest's two tools (`ios_iteration`, `ios_setup`), two hooks (`pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call`), `tool_execution` middleware, and no required secret environment variables. The Python half uses registration, hooks, middleware, skill registration and lifecycle subscription. The Desktop bundle imports the plugin SDK and React; optional controls use `host.openWorkspace`. Browser preview and image inspection remain host-tool operations.

### Rule 13 disclosures and reviewer attention

- **Native execution and reads:** runs Xcode, `simctl`, Git and process/port-inspection commands on the local Mac. Builds can execute scripts and dependencies from the selected checkout. Reads the authorized checkout, Xcode/Simulator metadata, process state, and host configuration needed for lifecycle selection. Build-input fingerprints are partial, not a sandbox.
- **Network and downloaded code:** approved setup downloads official npm registry artifacts for locked `serve-sim 0.1.48`, with locked integrity checks. This includes JavaScript and upstream native payloads. No downloaded native binary is bundled in the pinned plugin tree. The plugin does not self-update or replace its own files.
- **Background processes and retained state:** runs a localhost preview server and supervision processes; stores coordination state and receipts in profile-scoped plugin data. Closing Browser does not necessarily stop the server. Explicit Stop can terminate the coordinator-owned app as well as its preview, but does not uninstall or erase it.
- **Known dependency security issue:** `serve-sim 0.1.48` lacks Host validation and has unauthenticated Simulator stream/control routes. The execution token is disclosed by the preview page. Localhost is not an authorization boundary and does not eliminate malicious-browser risk. Remediation is deferred with plugin-maintainer acceptance, not claimed fixed. This is disclosed in the README, security audit and entry's `known_issues`; catalog maintainers must make their own admission decision. This PR does not claim that a passing scanner clears that issue.
- **Undocumented host import:** validation warns about `host_compat.py:37`, `agent.safe_worker_policy.worker_config_snapshot`. This is a read-only lifecycle-selection dependency, not a runtime override. There are no core rebinds. It can break across host versions and is disclosed in `known_issues`. If admission requires a public replacement, please identify the supported seam; this submission does not assert an exemption from catalog policy.
- **Credentials and approvals:** no credential store or OAuth tokens are read or maintained by the plugin, and no API key is required. Native mutations and dependency provisioning use normal host approval. No approval bypass or telemetry is introduced.

Full scope and limitations: [security audit](https://github.com/akinduroifedayo/Hermes-iOS-sim/blob/7f48cf060e76eae29a2bdef77c2969ba6ca9898f/docs/security-audit.md), [release status](https://github.com/akinduroifedayo/Hermes-iOS-sim/blob/7f48cf060e76eae29a2bdef77c2969ba6ca9898f/plugin/RELEASE-STATUS.md).

## How to Test

1. Clone the public plugin repository and check out `7f48cf060e76eae29a2bdef77c2969ba6ca9898f`.
2. Run `hermes plugins validate ./plugin --install-deps --json`.
3. On a suitably provisioned Mac, follow the pinned README to install, enable and select an authorized app target. Do not expose or tunnel the preview port.

Local admission validation ran in an isolated HOME/HERMES_HOME and returned `ok: true`. All 16 checks passed, including capability matching, security scan (`safe`), no core override, and Desktop SDK surface. The private-core-import warning above remains visible.

Public-URL installation at the exact pin also passed in an isolated home. Plugin Doctor reported two tools and three hooks including host registration behavior; all 40 installed package files matched the release manifest. This was not a new live-device or independent-Mac test. Prior local product verification passed 758 Python cases with 63 skips and 36 JavaScript cases with six skips. The published revision changes documentation only from that tested preparation. Hosted catalog CI has not yet run at submission time.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contribution guide and current catalog submission/admission rules.
- [x] Conventional commit and one-file catalog-only change.
- [x] Searched existing submissions for duplicates.
- [x] Ran the documented catalog admission validator with `--install-deps`.
- [x] Tested local validation and isolated public installation on macOS.
- [x] Declared capabilities, platform limits, known issues, and third-party/native execution.
- [x] Documentation and config changes in Hermes core are not applicable.
- [ ] Full Hermes core test suite and `python scripts/check` were not run for this catalog-only entry; catalog CI and maintainer review remain pending.

## Screenshots / Logs

![Hermes-iOS-sim Desktop controls](https://github.com/akinduroifedayo/Hermes-iOS-sim/releases/download/v1.0.0/desktop-controls.png)

Privacy-cropped screenshot from the earlier isolated Desktop lifecycle exercise, showing the idle controls. Its Desktop bundle is byte-identical to this pin (`SHA-256 41d877925d7fb35109e2ebe8cddb57bad3a297d0ddf1aa9d9652a7b291534821`). This is UI illustration, not a claim of a new live native-device run.

Release assets include package manifests, checksums and isolated-install verification. No private screenshots, machine paths or raw session logs are included in this PR.

prs.body:
Owner-submitted SHA bump for hermes-whatsapp-voice (live WhatsApp voice calls with Hermes): `e472a47` (0.1.12) → [`ef3b8be4a79651b6c11a720f20a95b9e2939c92e`](https://github.com/ashwanthbalakrishnan5/hermes-whatsapp-voice/tree/ef3b8be4a79651b6c11a720f20a95b9e2939c92e) (0.2.1).

## What does this PR do?

Updates the catalog entry to 0.2.1. Commit range for review (rule 4): [e472a47...ef3b8be](https://github.com/ashwanthbalakrishnan5/hermes-whatsapp-voice/compare/e472a47dda4e9986ca44f0ad62cb1b71c893bec0...ef3b8be4a79651b6c11a720f20a95b9e2939c92e).

What changed in the plugin:
- **Fix:** after Gemini's `goAway` the old socket stayed open, so the resume was refused and calls lost their voice mid-call.
- **Optional chat-session mode** (`context_mode: core_session`, off by default): the call becomes part of the owner's WhatsApp DM session with Hermes. While such a call is active, a `pre_gateway_dispatch` hook routes the owner's DM texts into the call instead of a second text reply.
- **Every call behaviour is a setting** (main spoken language, pause before reply, goodbye grace, Hermes timeout, tools before speaking, recording of the owner's side, Live endpoint), editable in the dashboard tab.
- **Per-call metrics** (time to first audio, reply delays, longest silence, tokens, who ended the call) and a `hermes whatsapp-voice calls` command.
- **Tests:** a call simulator runs whole calls against fake WhatsApp, Gemini and Hermes in CI, plus opt-in real-model tests.

Entry changes: `sha`, `version`, `capabilities.provides_hooks: [pre_gateway_dispatch]`, and disclosure lines for the new behaviour. `requires_hermes` stays `>=0.21.6` (the first release with `pre_gateway_dispatch`), now also declared in `plugin.yaml`.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate --install-deps` at the pinned commit (Hermes 0.22.5): **Validation passed**. Declared tools and hooks match registrations, security scan `safe`, no core overrides, no Python dependencies.

Warnings for review: **private core imports** (rule 9 warns, does not fail). All come from the opt-in chat-session mode (`core_session.py`, plus `hermes_yaml.safe_load` in the dashboard backend). The full list and what each is used for is in the repo's [`CORE_PATCHES.md`](https://github.com/ashwanthbalakrishnan5/hermes-whatsapp-voice/blob/ef3b8be4a79651b6c11a720f20a95b9e2939c92e/CORE_PATCHES.md). It reads the owner's DM session through `SessionDB`, runs tools through the agent the way a gateway turn does, and asks for approvals through `tools.approval`. Nothing is patched or rebound. If an internal changes, a call falls back to the default mode, which uses none of them. If you'd prefer, I'm happy to propose public seams for these in a Hermes issue.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

Unchanged from the current entry (sidecar process, attested binary download, WhatsApp linked device, Gemini Live, local api_server, dashboard backend commands, no telemetry), plus:
- **Hook:** `pre_gateway_dispatch` returns `skip` only for the owner's WhatsApp DM text messages while a chat-session call is active. Slash commands, media, groups and other platforms are untouched.
- **Chat-session mode (opt-in):** a loopback service (bearer token, loopback-only) inside Hermes's process. It reads the owner's DM session (system prompt, recent history up to `history_chars`, tool schemas of `voice_tools`) and sends it to Gemini. It runs the voice's tool calls through Hermes in that session under Hermes's approval flow, and writes the call into that session.
- **Recording (opt-in, `record_calls`):** the owner's side of each call is saved as WAV in the plugin's data directory. Never uploaded.
- **`voice_api_url` (advanced):** if changed from Gemini's endpoint, that endpoint receives the Gemini key and call audio.

## Provenance (rule 17)

The binaries are built by the repo's release workflow and attested to the `v0.2.1` tag's commit (`9256a39`). The pinned commit is that tag plus one commit that only adds their checksums (`sidecar/release-checksums.txt`). To verify: `gh attestation verify <binary> --repo ashwanthbalakrishnan5/hermes-whatsapp-voice --source-ref refs/tags/v0.2.1`. No binaries are committed.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

prs.title: chore(plugin-catalog): bump kiwi to v1.2.3 (kiwi@0.12.7)
prs.body:
## What

SHA bump for the existing `kiwi` community entry: the pinned buyer runtime moves from `@harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.5` to `@harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.7`.

| Field | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin-catalog/kiwi.yaml` → `sha` | `5d23517308bf9e5d75b62dcda63a19dd03ab0491` | `6703b4f6187f9a2ec0826959f0c87ccc2d0f14fe` |
| `version` | `"1.2.2"` | `"1.2.3"` |
| `mcp.json` runtime pin | `@harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.5` | `@harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.7` |

- Plugin repo: <https://github.com/harrylabsj/hermes-plugin-kiwi> (public) — commit `6703b4f`, tag `v1.2.3`, release note: *pin the buyer runtime to @harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.7*.
- Engine: `@harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.7` on the public npm registry (`dist-tags.latest = "0.12.7"`), published from the open-source A2A commerce runtime <https://github.com/harrylabsj/kiwi> (Apache-2.0).
- tier: `community` · category: `tools` · `capabilities`: all four keys empty — this is a portable manifest-only package (`plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + `skills/`), there is no host `__init__.py`/`register()` to probe. The tool surface is disclosed in `description`.
- Entry diff is exactly three lines (`sha`, `version`, the pin version inside `description`); `repo`, `maintainer`, `docs_url`, `platforms`, `capabilities` unchanged.

## What changed upstream (0.12.5 → 0.12.7)

Release notes: <https://github.com/harrylabsj/kiwi/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md> (v0.12.7 section). Buyer-facing, enforcement-side changes:

- **Delegation limits are now actually enforced on accept** (`max_total_price` / `max_unit_price` / `max_quantity` / `allowed_merchants` / `allowed_currencies`), with fail-closed rejection when a price cannot be parsed as a structured amount. Previously these limits were declared but not applied on the accept path.
- **ASK approvals are bound to `task_id` + candidate digest and are single-use** (consumed once accept/handoff lands).
- `GetExtendedAgentCard` now requires an authenticated identity (anonymous calls are rejected with `authentication_required`); `message/send` anonymous T0 inquiries are unchanged.
- Optional buyer-side A2A request signing (`a2aSigningKeyDir`, Ed25519 / RFC 9421) — unset keeps the previous anonymous-T0 behaviour.
- Merchant listings may now carry a platform product page (JD / Taobao / Tmall) surfaced to buyers as an `external_checkout_url` handoff destination; Kiwi still neither orders nor pays.
- Buyer HTTP surface (`kiwi buyer-api serve`) now fails closed without a bearer token; loopback is not exempt.

No buyer tool was added, removed or re-parameterised — the MCP tool surface is unchanged (see evidence below), so the bundled `kiwi-buyer` skill text needs no behavioural edit for this bump.

## Verification (run locally for this revision)

1. **Consumer path, neutral directory** (no `package.json` in cwd, `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8`): `npx -y @harrylabsj/kiwi@0.12.7 mcp serve` with JSON-RPC `initialize` → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/list` → **13 tools**, `serverInfo: kiwi-buyer-mcp 0.1.0`, every description ASCII/English.
2. **Tool surface unchanged**: full `tools/list` JSON dumped for `0.12.5` and `0.12.7` and compared — **byte-identical** (same 13 tool names, schemas and descriptions), so no bundled-skill drift.
3. **Pinned-source segment**: `git clone https://github.com/harrylabsj/hermes-plugin-kiwi` → `git checkout --detach 6703b4f6187f9a2ec0826959f0c87ccc2d0f14fe` → `hermes plugins validate .` → `Validation passed.` The only message is a pre-existing warning (`skill:kiwi-buyer: metadata must map string keys to string values`) that also shows up on the currently catalogued `5d23517` commit; it is not introduced by this bump.
4. **Structural segment**: `uv run --with ruamel.yaml==0.18.17 python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog` at upstream `main` (`dc39239`) with this change applied → `OK: 861 file(s) valid`, exit 0.
5. **No self-update logic** in the pinned tree (grep for update-fetch / self-replace patterns: no hits). Updating the runtime pin is exactly this SHA-bump PR.

## Checklist

- [x] `sha` is a 40-character commit that is pushed and publicly reachable in the plugin repo
- [x] `version` matches the plugin repo's release tag (`v1.2.3`)
- [x] No self-update / fetch-and-replace logic in the package
- [x] Bundled `SKILL.md` is English-first (`SKILL.zh-CN.md` ships as the translation)
- [x] `capabilities` left empty (portable package, no host code to probe)
- [x] `platforms` unchanged (`[]` — pure npx/Node, no OS-specific dependency)

prs.body:
Bumps the LoreConvo catalog entry from 0.10.19 to 0.10.20.

- `sha`: `4ea667e9` -> `99114bdc` (labyrinth-analytics/loreconvo main, tag `v0.10.20`; `integrations/hermes/plugin.yaml` and `pyproject.toml` pin `loreconvo==0.10.20`)
- `version`: `0.10.19` -> `0.10.20`

**Provider change:** the provider now exposes the full LoreConvo tool set (42 tools) under the same names as the LoreConvo MCP server, instead of the three `loreconvo_*` tools. Schemas are generated from the MCP server registry at build time, so Hermes and MCP stay in sync. `capabilities.provides_tools` is updated to match what `get_tool_schemas()` returns.

- Renamed: `loreconvo_search_sessions` -> `search_sessions`, `loreconvo_get_context` -> `get_context_for`, `loreconvo_save_memory` -> `save_memory_item`.
- `inject_agent_context` and `configure_tools` are listed but return a clear "available via the LoreConvo MCP server or CLI" error in Hermes-native dispatch.
- Pro-only tools return an upgrade message on the free tier.
- New optional env var `LORECONVO_PRO` (Pro license key), added to `requires_env`. When unset, the provider falls back to the license already stored on disk by LoreConvo.

Also fixed in this release: the Hermes wheel now ships its tool-schema file, so an installed provider registers all its tools instead of none.

**Dependencies:** no packages added or removed. `fastembed` 0.9.1 (was 0.8.0) and an explicit `pillow==13.0.0` pin (previously pulled in by fastembed) to pick up security fixes; LoreConvo now requires Python >= 3.11.

prs.title: catalog: add Nostr VPN skill plugin
prs.body:
Adds Nostr VPN 0.1.1 to the community tools catalog, pinned to `ffc8a77d342dd8db5e680fef92921a9706adf9f8`. Publisher: Sirius Business Ltd.

This is a portable Agent Plugins v1 package containing one workflow skill. It registers no tools, hooks, middleware, servers, or required environment variables. It contains no executable code, bundled binaries, updater, telemetry, or automatic installation of the separate CLI.

Disclosure: The skill invokes the separately installed nvpn CLI on request. It uses private config/key sidecars, connects to relays and peers, and starts a persistent daemon. A tunnel requires elevated host networking permissions; the plugin does not grant them. Joining devices keep separate identities and require administrator approval. CLI approval and JSON join-request output are currently source-only; the skill documents the released CLI/native admin app fallback. No tunnel or privileged networking was started for validation.

Validation against Hermes `9b904dcc22c23fe8b82834339bbdd96495072e59`, using the exact pinned plugin files:

- `hermes plugins validate <plugin> --install-deps`: passed; security verdict `safe`, no admission warnings.
- `hermes plugins doctor <plugin> --ci`: passed real runtime discovery and registration.
- Installed the exact package through the documented manual plugin-directory route, then `hermes plugins enable nostr-vpn`; native `skills_list` and `skill_view` loaded `nostr-vpn:nostr-vpn` with the exact canonical skill content. Installed file hashes matched the pinned package.
- Catalog structural validator: passed.

Hermes ran only in a non-root Docker container with fresh profiles and no host credentials mounted. Setup downloads used an allowlist proxy; validation and skill loading ran with all container networks disconnected. The external application workflows have separate project validation; this submission check verifies Hermes packaging and loading, without invoking an LLM or making public writes.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add hermesvault
prs.body:
xf## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/hermesvault.yaml`, a catalog entry for **hermesvault**: a secret-source plugin that keeps secrets out of plaintext `.env` files.

It resolves `secrets.hermesvault.env` entries (`ENV_VAR: hv:<item>[:field]`) at startup from a local [FloorVault](https://github.com/Guerilla-ops/floorvault) store (AES-256-SIV, context-bound records). It also adds a `hermes hvault` CLI to add, update, show, list and remove items.

The plugin lives in the FloorVault repository under `plugins/hermesvault`, pinned at `1fcb5988225b981fd0b28320c02a9ae607e7ab11`. This entry is submitted by the repository owner.

**Hermes surfaces used:**
- `ctx.register_secret_source()`, using `SecretSource` from `agent.secret_sources.base`.
  - Mapped shape, scheme `hv`.
  - The fetch never raises and never prompts.
  - The bootstrap key is read through `get_source_environment()` and declared via `token_env_key`, so it is protected from being overwritten.
- `ctx.register_cli_command()` for `hermes hvault`. The hermes hvault CLI command is skipped under plugins.isolation: host. The secret source works there as of NousResearch/hermes-agent#144430: before that fix a hosted fetch() result crossed the plugin-host wire as a generic record and apply_all applied nothing. That case was found by the maintainer during this review, not by my testing, which ran the source in-process.
- No tools, hooks, middleware or core overrides.

**Disclosure (rule 13):**
- **Reads and writes** an encrypted store under `<HERMES_HOME>/agent-vault`, or `secrets.hermesvault.dir`.
- **Reads its own master key** from the OS key store (macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service or Windows DPAPI; service `floor-vault`), or from the environment variable named by `token_env` (default `HERMES_VAULT_KEY`).
  - It reads only its own key entry; it never reads `.env`, `auth.json`, or other tools' credentials.
  - The listed `hermes-wincred` and `hermes-dpapi-secrets` sources read the OS key store in the same way.
- **Resolved values** become environment variables of the Hermes process and its children, like `.env` entries.
- **Installs** `floorvault>=0.2.1,<0.3` from PyPI, plus `secretstorage` on Linux and `pyobjc-framework-Security` on macOS. Every dependency has an upper bound. `floorvault`'s runtime dependency is `cryptography>=50.0.0`, which is compatible with Hermes' pin `cryptography==50.0.1`.
- No network calls, no subprocesses, no telemetry, no self-update. The plugin directory (5 text files) contains no binaries or bytecode.
- **Interactive input:** `hermes hvault put` prompts for a value with `getpass`. That is an interactive CLI command; the startup fetch path never prompts.
- **Protection** is at rest (backups, sync, copied files), not against code already running as the same user.

## Related Issue

None. This is a catalog submission.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/hermesvault.yaml`: new entry. `tier: community`, `category: tools`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.2"`, `version: "0.2.0"`, with a 2:1 banner image pinned to the same commit.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` prints `OK` for every file, including this one.
2. At the pinned commit, `hermes plugins validate plugins/hermesvault --install-deps` passes, including `security scan — safe` and `no core override`. Dependencies resolve from PyPI.
3. End to end, on a scratch `HERMES_HOME`:
   1. `hermes plugins install Guerilla-ops/floorvault/plugins/hermesvault`
   2. `hermes plugins enable hermesvault`
   3. `printf 'value=test\n' | hermes hvault add "Test" --id vault_test --stdin`
   4. Map `OPENROUTER_API_KEY: hv:vault_test` under `secrets.hermesvault.env`.
   5. `hermes status` should print `FloorVault: applied 1 secret`.

Results in the submitter's runs:
- **Catalog checks:** the catalog validator and `scan_plugin_payloads.py` pass.
- **Conformance:** Hermes' `SecretSourceConformance` kit passes (10/10) against releases 0.21.2, 0.21.3, 0.21.4 and 0.21.5, and against main `fab9b01`.
- **End to end:** the steps above pass on main `fab9b01`, with `floorvault` 0.2.1 installed from PyPI.
- **Not tested end to end:** Keychain, Secret Service and DPAPI custody, which need a desktop session. The `token_env` path was exercised.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Submitting to the Plugin Catalog](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/plugins/catalog-submission)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass: N/A (catalog-only change; catalog validator run instead)
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes: N/A (no code)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (Ubuntu container), Hermes main `fab9b01` and releases 0.21.2–0.21.5

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation: N/A (the plugin README renders on the catalog page)
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact: the plugin supports Linux, macOS and Windows; only Linux was tested end to end
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A (no tools)

prs.title: fix(kanban): a host-side stall must not spend the card's retry budget
prs.body:
## Problem

A Kanban submitter whose profile owner never answered died as a counted crash. Three real outage shapes all landed in the dispatcher's plain-failure booking (`_record_task_failure` → `consecutive_failures += 1` → breaker at 2):

* the owner stayed silent past `OWNER_WAIT_S` — never admitted, or admitted then stalled;
* `prompt.receipt` settled `unknown` and the submitter immediately raised `GatewayClientError('Kanban execution unknown; retained by owner')` — which, being a `ValueError` subclass, fell into `_submit()`'s `except (KeyError, ValueError, OSError)` and printed **"Kanban owner refused"** — a mislabel: the owner never refused, it never answered;
* either shape exited **1**, indistinguishable from a genuine card failure.

Measured on `main` (an e2e run of the *new* test against unmodified sources proves it): submitter exits **1** for the never-answered owner; `detect_crashed_workers` books `crashed`, `consecutive_failures` reaches **1**, and the second identical outage books **2** → `gave_up` + `blocked` (`effective_limit = 2` = `DEFAULT_FAILURE_LIMIT`). Three identical deaths in one tick are systemic-blocked (`is_systemic`, `failure_limit=1`). Exit **75** remains the only host-shaped code that costs nothing (the quota wall). During a fleet outage this parked healthy cards one tick after another — none of them did anything wrong.

## Fix (narrow, three parts)

1. **`KANBAN_INFRASTRUCTURE_EXIT_CODE = 74`** (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`) — BSD `EX_IOERR`, deliberately the *same* code **#140272** chose for the persistence/host-I/O family, so the fleet does not grow two competing host sentinels. The dispatcher classifies it as `infrastructure_failure` and funnels the death through the **existing infrastructure seam of #114720** — `_record_task_failure(..., infrastructure=True)` — the same path `RestartSafeScopeUnavailable` uses: the counter move and every trip decision become no-ops. The run closes as a `crashed` booking carrying `"infrastructure": true` + `exit_kind` in its metadata/event (observability: `hermes kanban runs` and `last_failure_error` still show the card was host-blocked), and `check_respawn_guard` now extends the `infrastructure_cooldown` it already applies to `spawn_failed` refusals to `crashed` runs with that marker — the outage retries forever, spaced, never counted, like the #114720 condition it is.
2. **F3 — reconcile the board before blaming the worker**: on `unknown`, the submitter now reads this run's own `worker_result` through a new gated reader (`worker_result_for_claim`: the claim-lock gate of `worker_result` **and** the `worker_bound` pid gate of `_bound_worker_matches`, the same invariant that let the result be written). Match → the REAL exit code is reported (a completed run is no longer punished for a lost settlement, and a genuinely failed run still books as failed). Missing / foreign-claim / foreign-pid → the old raise stands, now exiting 74: **an ambiguous receipt never synthesizes success.**
3. **The "never admitted" marker already exists and is reused**: the `owner_admitted` board write and the `kanban.run` answer commit together, so the submitter's own view (`claim.session_id`) names the never-admitted case in the error text (`"… silent for 183s"` vs `"… silent for 183s after admission"`) — no new flag is defined.

The four give-up assertions in `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_worker_socket_recovery.py` are updated to the new exception class — they test exactly the death whose verdict this PR changes. The one new source file beyond the three kanban modules is `gateway/session_kanban.py`: the reconcile reader composes `worker_result` + `_bound_worker_matches`, and board-schema knowledge belongs where those live; replicating it in the submitter would duplicate the schema.

## Deliberately excluded (measured, with reasons)

* **Reconnect/resume by `admission_id` with jittered redial** — already on `main` (`kanban_worker_client.py` redial loop + `_Claim`); porting a second copy would conflict.
* **Deriving `OWNER_WAIT_S` from `TimeoutStopSec`** — host-unit configuration, not an upstream defect (our unit runs 210 s; upstream default `resolve_systemd_timeout_stop_sec(0, 30)` is 70 s).
* **A gateway-unavailable streak ceiling** — a follow-up: neutrality alone means an *up-but-broken* gateway is re-probed forever, spaced. This PR keeps the seam's existing "retries forever, spaced" policy and its breaker honest; a ceiling should be designed and env-gated separately.
* A `gateway_unavailable` outcome label with its own DispatchResult counter — rejected in favour of routing through #114720's seam: one mechanism, one cooldown class, minimal surface.

## Tests

* New `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_infrastructure_exit.py` (15 tests, real boards in tmp homes): exit 74 → `consecutive_failures` **0** and card **not blocked** (events show no `gave_up`/`blocked`); plain exit 1 still counts (control); `unknown` + matching board result → real code returned, no raise; `unknown` + no result / foreign claim lock / foreign pid → raises, exits 74 with its trailer; three systemic identical 74-deaths → never trips; cooldown holds while fresh and releases after; classify registry.
* New `tests/e2e/core/kanban/test_kanban_host_stall.py` (1 test): real claimed card, real bound submitter process running `kanban_worker_client.main()` against a stalled owner → exit **74** + `[kanban-worker-exit] rc=74` trailer + `Kanban host unavailable` label (and no `Kanban owner refused` mislabel), booked by a real `hermes kanban dispatch` tick → released to `ready`, `consecutive_failures == 0`, run metadata carries `infrastructure: true`, archived after.
* A/B on a clean base: the e2e test **fails** on unmodified sources (`submitter exited 1`), proving the measured red; the whole-suite red set (`-k kanban`, 63 pre-existing environment-conditioned failures in this sandbox) is **byte-identical** with and without this change — zero new breakage.
* `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_worker_owner_wait.py` (2), `test_kanban_worker_socket_recovery.py` (25), `test_kanban_worker_admission_wait.py`/`test_kanban_managed_result_pid.py` (4): all pass. `tests/e2e/core/kanban/` directory: 9 passed, 9 pre-existing xfailed, 0 failed. `ruff check` on all changed files: clean.

Addresses #139612

prs.title: catalog: add hermes-pr-studio 0.3.0 (community)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one community catalog entry, `plugin-catalog/hermes-pr-studio.yaml`, for **PR Studio**, a Hermes Desktop plugin for reviewing GitHub pull requests without leaving Hermes. Submitted by the repository owner (rule 5).

- **Repo:** https://github.com/Murali-lns/hermes-pr-studio (MIT)
- **Pin:** `b9ba1c6bb567a8aeeff60fb4cfd17abebc0fa95f` (`version: "0.3.0"`, matches `plugin.yaml`)
- **requires_hermes:** `>=0.22.1` (same floor in `plugin.yaml`)

### What it does
- Inbox of the user's open PRs across GitHub (needs review / authored / involved), a repository picker, and per-repo Open/Merged/Closed lists.
- PR conversation rendered from GitHub's HTML, including private-repo images fetched through the user's `gh` login, plus an in-app image viewer.
- Unified/split diffs with existing review threads on the correct lines; line comments, replies, and Comment / Approve / Request changes reviews (always confirmed before submitting).
- **Send to Hermes** on any comment, thread or PR: sends a structured prompt (repo, branch, `file:line`, hunk, comment) to the active chat. *Review in new chat* uses the composer's model picker.
- Watched PRs: polls for new commits, CI, reviews and comments, then notifies.

### Hermes surfaces used
- `desktop/plugin.js`: Desktop plugin SDK only (tile, status-bar item, command-palette entries, plugin storage, `rest` to its own backend). Passes the `desktop surface` check.
- `dashboard/plugin_api.py`: a FastAPI router served at `/api/plugins/hermes-pr-studio/…` through the plugin host.
- `__init__.py`: registers no tools, hooks or middleware (`capabilities` all empty, which matches the probe).

### Lineage (rule 16)
This is an independent codebase, not a fork or derivative of `githermes`. The UI was inspired by the T3 Code PR workflow. What it adds over the listed GitHub plugin: a cross-repo inbox, private-repo image rendering through `gh`, queued multi-comment reviews, Send-to-Hermes prompts with diff context, and PR watching with notifications.

### Disclosure (rule 13)
- **Shell commands:** runs the user's logged-in `gh` CLI (`gh api`, `gh api graphql`, `gh repo list`) and `git remote get-url origin` in the open project folder. Argument lists only, no shell, 30–40 s timeouts.
- **Network:** only through `gh` to the GitHub API. Public images and avatars load from GitHub's CDN.
- **GitHub writes:** only on an explicit click (comment, line comment, reply, review). Review submissions are confirmed first.
- **Credentials:** none stored or read. `gh` attaches its own auth, and the plugin never touches the token.
- **Background work:** while Desktop is open, watched PRs are polled every 60 s (one GraphQL call) and open PR views refresh every 60–90 s. No other background processes.
- **Local data:** UI state, watch list and pending review comments in Desktop plugin storage.
- **HTML:** GitHub-rendered HTML is re-sanitised by a backend allowlist (no scripts, styles, iframes, event handlers or non-http links).
- **No telemetry. No self-updater.** It does contain a "Restart Hermes service" button, shown only when the backend route is stale after an update. It calls the SDK's `host.restartGateway()` and does not fetch or replace any files.

## Type of Change
- [x] ✨ New feature (catalog entry)

## Changes Made
- `plugin-catalog/hermes-pr-studio.yaml` (new; this is the only file changed)

## How to Test
1. `git clone https://github.com/Murali-lns/hermes-pr-studio && cd hermes-pr-studio && git checkout b9ba1c6bb567a8aeeff60fb4cfd17abebc0fa95f`
2. `hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` passes all checks: manifest, loadable, capability probe, declared tools/hooks/middleware, security scan `safe`, no core override, desktop surface. I ran this on a fresh public clone at the pinned SHA.
3. `hermes plugins install hermes-pr-studio --enable`, then enable the Desktop half under Capabilities → Plugins and open it from ⌘K → *PR Studio*. This needs `gh auth status` to be signed in.

## Checklist
- [x] I searched existing PRs; this isn't a duplicate
- [x] Only one file changed
- [x] Tested on Omarchy (Arch Linux), Hermes Desktop v0.22.5. The backend has 19 tests, and it loaded live PR lists, details, checks, files and a private-repo image from a real account.
- N/A: core code, config keys, tool schemas

## Screenshots / Logs
I don't have gallery screenshots on a public repo yet. I'll add them in a follow-up `screenshots:` bump if reviewers want them.

prs.title: feat(catalog): add Hermes Handoff
prs.body:
## Add Hermes Handoff (community)

Adds only `plugin-catalog/hermes-handoff.yaml`: Linux, version `0.3.0`, maintainer `yuzushi-dev`, conservative floor `>=0.22.5` in both catalog and native manifest. Pin: `2bab6cf77a436544f58f5b528cd0d838e6d60309`. Derived from [yuzushi-dev/session-handoff](https://github.com/yuzushi-dev/session-handoff) (MIT); this is its native Hermes edition, not the Claude Code/Codex npm package.

Creates immutable, profile-bound semantic handoffs and opens a new CLI/Desktop session without closing the source. Destination A and optional summary-writer B are independent. `resume_verified` remains false: reading a handoff is not proof of successful continuation. The destination is instructed to inspect real project files and wait for confirmation; this instruction is not a sandbox or obedience guarantee.

Surfaces: `hermes_handoff` tool, `pre_api_request` hook, `/hh`, `handoff-open` CLI command, bundled skill; Desktop SDK route/sidebar, state atoms, `ctx.rest`, session creation/submission/opening; dashboard `POST /opening`. LLM trust requests are `llm.model_override` and `llm.provider_override`, distinct from catalog tool/hook declarations. No self-updater, runtime core rebind, remote executable loader, prototype patch or core DOM manipulation was identified.

## Rule 13 disclosure

- Reads outside plugin data: read-only originating-profile `state.db` queries scoped to the exact host session, bounded persisted message/tool evidence including labelled compacted history; not parent history, attachments or hidden/in-flight client context. Reads host configuration through `load_config()` for tool-policy preflight and filesystem/Git workspace identity.
- Subprocesses: local `git -C <workspace> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` without a shell, timeout 3 seconds; installed Hermes foreground CLI without a shell for destination opening. No plugin-owned background daemon, dependency installer or download path. Interactive foreground Hermes has no global lifetime timeout.
- Writes: private handoffs, bindings, indexes and opening/writer routing/receipt sidecars under the originating profile's `handoffs/data` and `handoffs/state`; Desktop preparation receipts in plugin storage. These can contain sensitive context despite redaction: inspect before sharing. Route observation stores session/model/provider identifiers, not request payloads.
- Network/cost: optional writer B sends bounded, already-redacted persisted evidence via `ctx.llm.complete`, not the full conversation. Preparation and destination opening request host-owned chat turns using configured providers and may incur inference charges. Redaction is imperfect. No direct third-party HTTP client, telemetry or usage reporting was identified.
- Credentials: no plugin-owned store or direct `.env`, `auth.json`, vendor-login/browser/keychain reads, OAuth refresh or rotation was identified. Hermes owns provider authentication. The CLI child inherits the selected host environment after session/worker/approval-bypass flags are removed; it is not an OS capability sandbox and may inherit credential-bearing variables.
- Approvals/unattended: explicit B requires user-owned override consent, never automatic enablement. CLI opening requires real stdin/stdout TTYs and strips inherited YOLO/noninteractive and worker/session/toolset flags without overriding profile approval settings. Writer timeout 60 seconds, SDK REST 10 seconds, RPC 15 seconds. Preparation adds a source turn. Uncertain launches/submissions are not automatically retried; another explicit preparation may incur another charge.

## Local checks and limits

The previous pin (`fc95cff80965a988880082cb75ee203ca9720e50`) passed `hermes plugins validate` on official stable `v0.22.5` (`bf0203a794a07aac3ff764972ab9087baa4e4f4e`): exit 0, 16/16 checks, security `safe`, stderr empty. The current pin passed the installed Hermes validator: exit 0, 15/15 checks, security `safe`; the four private-import warnings remain. The `v0.22.5` SDK exports `usePluginI18n` and scoped plugin-locale registration. Desktop/i18n and CLI fixtures, JS/Python syntax checks, and diff check also exit 0. No live installation, paid inference or Desktop E2E was performed.

Earlier full-catalog validation at upstream base `3440aa5212284308e9ef7ee56c501c967ad5f706` passed the official structural validator and payload scanner, including the committed PNG. At current PR base `850efff14f0d2a6de205eb1363c35dac35906763`, the official structural validator reports `ok: true` with no errors or warnings for this entry; the exact pinned source passes the payload scanner. Existing full-catalog warnings from the earlier run were: unknown `homepage_url` in `agent_memory_es.yaml` and `stack.yaml`, `provides_commands` in `skill-integrity.yaml`, and `requires_env` in `vornik-companion.yaml`.

Validator warning (not suppressed), all in `server/handoff_open.py`:
- line 65 `agent.coding_context.coding_selection`
- line 67 `toolsets.resolve_toolset`
- line 73 `hermes_cli.tools_config._get_platform_tools`
- line 78 `agent.skill_utils.parse_config_string_list`

These imports preserve fail-closed tool-policy preflight and remain release-coupled; no public-API-only claim. The floor is an admission-tested support boundary, not the oldest working version or full CLI/Desktop certification. Named-profile/bot workflows through another profile socket and non-Linux platforms are not certified. Host-isolation audit notes buffered dashboard responses and skipped CLI registration: `host_ready` does not certify `handoff-open` in plugin-host mode. Desktop strings now default to English, with Italian retained as a plugin-scoped SDK translation; CLI launch messages are English. GitHub Actions for this fork PR are `action_required` pending maintainer approval, so no GitHub CI pass is claimed.

## Historical UI evidence

![Historical handoff configuration controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuzushi-dev/hermes-handoff/850c13db71f6c8ed3fbbbb1075b8b729eee4a6e3/assets/hermes-handoff-ui-controls.png)

Historical configuration-controls crop from a synthetic policy-rejection scenario (opening rejected with HTTP409); not a fresh end-to-end run.

Real historical Electron capture, crop only, no reconstructed pixels: shows A/B controls, not successful opening. Recorded attempt stayed `prepared`, destination null, `resume_verified=false`; HTTP409 was the expected policy refusal. Host paths and identifiers are outside the crop. This historical screenshot predates the English-first change and still shows Italian controls; current code adds English-default Desktop strings, an Italian plugin locale bundle and English CLI launch messages. Promotional artwork is not substituted for functional UI evidence.

prs.body:
Adds **netplane 0.3.0** — Headscale control-plane tools and a Desktop pane — as an owner-submitted community/tools entry.

- Repository: https://github.com/lEWFkRAD/netplane
- Exact pin: `ca432caaa18cc681c967b1fee915125643ab28f4`
- Requires Hermes `>=0.21.6`.
- Review delta from Tek's base: https://github.com/lEWFkRAD/netplane/compare/b7e86700...ca432caaa18cc681c967b1fee915125643ab28f4

## Review fixes

- All handlers accept Hermes's `handler(args, **kwargs)` contract, covered by dispatch tests. `create: false` only lists key metadata.
- Join-key creation requests approval through `pre_tool_call`, defaults to single-use, and enforces a 1–168-hour expiry in both tools and the dashboard API. Lists omit stored join secrets.
- Settings are read per key at call time; API credentials come only through the active Hermes secret scope. No environment/file credential fallbacks remain.
- The dashboard imports the same package module. Desktop no longer hardcodes a user and confirms node expiration.
- Stubs were regenerated with `grpcio-tools==1.81.1` / `protobuf==6.33.5`, matching bounded runtime floors `grpcio>=1.81.1,<2` and `protobuf>=6.33.5,<7` under Hermes's constraints.
- Non-loopback gRPC always uses certificate-verified TLS; loopback TLS is also supported for Headscale's TLS listener.

## Optional setup feature

`netplane_setup` defaults to a preview. Explicitly approved installation supports fresh Debian 12+/Ubuntu 22.04+ systemd hosts (amd64/arm64), verifies the official Headscale 0.29.6 DEB checksum, configures and starts the service, creates its first user, and saves a 90-day bootstrap API key plus connection settings through Hermes's active-profile APIs. The API key is never returned in tool output. Existing deployments or profile credentials are not overwritten; partial installations are preserved for repair. Desktop provides preview and confirmation for the same flow.

## Verification

At the final pin: **85 tests pass, 16/16 Hermes admission checks pass, host ready**. Admission reports one expected caution for network listeners and sudo usage; it is not represented as an unqualified security-safe scan. Catalog structural validation reports no errors or warnings for this entry.

A fresh isolated Ubuntu 24.04 KVM guest installed official Hermes `1f91da2a277093c6909542d8c725c0c52fae4628` and Netplane `10b6bff5cf5bb521d39e4443d9d33ee6768fbb23` through the real plugin CLI. Real Hermes dispatch verified setup preview, denied/approved installation, Headscale 0.29.6 service setup, owner-only profile-secret persistence, management RPCs, denied/approved single-use join keys, secret-free listings, expiry/deletion, repeat-install refusal without another API key, and bootstrap-key revocation. The final pin adds only the harness/tests, documentation and attribution/license notices to that VM-tested runtime.

Separately configured guest nginx with a disposable test certificate passed certificate-verified HTTPS health before and after reboot. Headscale/nginx remained enabled and active. Test credentials were revoked and the VM is shut down; no production fleet/tailnet configuration was changed.

Limits: no public DNS/ACME issuance, real Tailscale node enrollment, peer traffic, or interactive Desktop UI test. The VM exercised root installation; noninteractive sudo is unit-tested. The plugin does not claim an unverified public endpoint is ready.

## Risk and network disclosure

Approved setup runs on the Hermes host with root or noninteractive sudo. It invokes APT/dpkg, systemctl, runuser and Headscale; downloads the checksum-pinned official package from GitHub and may contact configured APT repositories. It writes system configuration/data and enables a persistent service. Depending on mode, the preview discloses public HTTPS/ACME and embedded DERP/STUN listeners; management gRPC and metrics remain loopback. Let's Encrypt receives the chosen domain/email in ACME mode. Public DNS/firewall changes, reverse-proxy installation, upgrades and device migration are excluded.

Management sends the API credential only to the configured Headscale gRPC endpoint. Status also probes the configured HTTPS endpoint and runs best-effort `systemctl is-active headscale` / `tailscale serve status`. Join-key creation and confirmed node expiration mutate the control plane. No telemetry, self-updater or Hermes core override. Desktop stays within the SDK surface. `requires_env: []` allows setup before an API key exists; management still needs `NETPLANE_APIKEY`.

## Credits

Jeff Watts / @lEWFkRAD owns and maintains the project. Qwen 3.8 wrote the original implementation under Jeff's direction; @teknium1 supplied the security/integration review; OpenAI Codex performed the follow-up audit, hardening, setup and tests under Jeff's direction. README also credits Nous/Hermes, Headscale/Tailscale, Google APIs, gRPC and Protocol Buffers contributors. Exact pinned upstream license texts and source provenance are preserved under `LICENSES/`; these notices do not assign a license to Netplane's original code.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add kubernetes
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds kubernetes, a way to approve one namespace in cluster.json and then read it with four operations: list pods, get one pod, list events, and read logs. The pinned server is kubernetes-mcp-server 0.0.68, started with uvx, and this plugin does not modify that package. Helm is not offered. Kubernetes is a registered trademark of The Linux Foundation.

Pinned commit: efd99f3afca5054c7f15b37e39261402827f3cda

## Changes Made

- Four tools: `pods_list_in_namespace`, `pods_get`, `events_list`, and `pods_log`. Each has readOnlyHint set to true, so Hermes does not show an approval card. A tool outside those four is refused and nothing is sent.
- `read_only` stays true, toolsets stay `core`, and Secret, ConfigMap, and ServiceAccount are denied. `configuration_view` is not listed.
- The namespace in cluster.json is injected into every call. A different namespace is refused. A context argument is refused.
- A prod, production, live, or prd name is refused unless `allow_production` is true. A public or link-local API host is refused even then. DNS is not resolved.
- The kubeconfig path is passed to the pinned server. The token is not written into `server.toml` and is not placed on the command line. HTTP proxy variables are not passed to the child.
- A password-like env value is replaced with `[redacted]`. The kubectl last-applied-configuration annotation is replaced with `[redacted]`.
- requires_hermes is >=0.21.4. Hermes 0.21.4 installed, enabled, and validated this package. The manifest is plugin.json. There is no plugin.yaml. The plugin does not use MCP trust. This plugin does not create a cron job.

## Disclosure

Disclosure — the kubeconfig token is sent only to the API host in that file. Plain http sends it without encryption. An HTTP proxy is not used. Status, events, and logs reach the model. Anyone allowed on an enabled gateway can call these tools with that kubeconfig. Stop the plugin with `hermes plugins disable kubernetes`. Turn the toolset off with `hermes tools disable mcp-kubernetes`.

## How to Test

Install with `hermes plugins install --no-enable file:///absolute/path/to/hermes-plugin-kubernetes`, then `hermes plugins enable kubernetes`. Create `$HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/agent-plugin-kubernetes-94abcb2d/work` and write `cluster.json` next to `work`. Four steps, then ask what is down in the namespace. Then list pods and their status. Then ask why one pod is restarting and quote the phase, the waiting reason, the restart count, the event reason, and the log.

Checked against rancher/k3s v1.31.4-k3s1. Namespace shop. The account could get and list pods, pods/log, and events. `pods_get` quoted phase Running, reasons ContainersNotReady, Error, and CrashLoopBackOff, and restartCount 1. `events_list` quoted Scheduled, Pulling, Pulled, Created, Started, and BackOff. `pods_log` quoted boom. The pod was still named broken. A direct GET of the Secret with that account returned 403. The pinned server, with an admin kubeconfig and the same denied resources, returned `resource not allowed` for Secret, ConfigMap, and ServiceAccount. `configuration_view` was refused and nothing was sent.

Unit tests inject the upstream reply and do not open a socket.

## What was not verified

- No model session was run.
- A gateway was not started. Hermes printed `hermes gateway restart` after install.
- A cluster whose context name is production was not started. That refusal is covered by unit tests.
- Helm was not called. It is not listed.
