prs.title: plugin-catalog: add Session Relay (hand-off to a fresh session before compaction)
prs.body:
## Plugin

**Session Relay** — https://github.com/ikuro4kin-dev/hermes-session-relay, pinned to `b65ebe9c2995f71c325f42a98914e6aca46809b6`.

Hands a long-running conversation over to a fresh session before the context window fills up:

- a ⚡ chip in the status bar shows live context usage;
- at the threshold (45% by default — below the ~50% point where Hermes compacts) the agent writes a hand-off note and calls `start_chat`; the new chat is named after the current one with the number incremented (`Title-6` → `Title-7`);
- the gateway half injects a prepared hand-off as the first message of the new session after `/new` on Telegram and other messaging platforms.

Nothing is deleted: the previous session keeps the full record. The relay runs only when the session is idle.

## Checks at the pinned commit

- `hermes plugins validate` — all checks pass, including `security scan — safe`, `desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface`, `no core override`, `declared hooks — matches registrations`.
- `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` — passes; no Python dependencies.
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/session-relay.yaml` — `OK: 1 file(s) valid`.
- `image` and `screenshots` are pinned to the same SHA and return 200.

## Disclosure

- Each relay submits one hidden service message to the agent — that is one extra agent turn, so model tokens are spent.
- The desktop half stores two keys in its own plugin storage: `prefs` (settings) and `relayed` (session ids already relayed, pruned after 30 days).
- The gateway half writes `pending.json` inside its own folder (hand-off text, platform name) and deletes it after the message is injected; entries older than 24 hours are ignored.
- No network calls, no telemetry, no shell access, no reads outside the plugin's own folder.

## Author

Owner of the plugin repository.

prs.title: Optional deep-researcher skill: evidence-ledger research that batches searches in code
prs.body:
Adds `deep-researcher` as an official optional research skill with a persisted claim/evidence ledger, native Hermes retrieval, report auditing, and resumable archives. The original contribution and human authorship are preserved; follow-up fixes remain in the optional skill, tests, and documentation.

## Behavior and reliability

- Persist search budgets and receipts, including empty and failed searches. Batch discovery through native Hermes tools while retaining original retrieval URLs and complete cached text for passage selection.
- Record sources and claims atomically with source keys, avoiding hard-coded ledger IDs and silent evidence misattachment. Validate individual claims before writing them.
- Preserve meaningful URL query parameters, parse balanced Markdown links, distinguish calendar years from citations, and count extracted sources for question coverage. References appear last in the dossier template.
- Require a current four-part critique covering finality, independence, named entities, and numbers. The reviewer checks retained passages and writes concise notes; report or ledger changes invalidate that review. This records an attestation, not proof of factual correctness.
- Gate completion and archiving on required artifacts, citation/evidence checks, resolved search receipts, and the current critique. Preserve readable reports and verify registered artifacts before optional pruning.
- Refactor the validators to meet the complexity limits without vendored-code waivers. No new core tools, dependencies, or per-session configuration changes.

## Validation

The selected skill, workflow, URL/audit, authoring, and documentation suites passed: **1,577 tests**, with one platform-specific skip. All **13 `scripts/check` gates** passed. Regression cases cover shifted source IDs, URL identity, citation parsing, failed-source coverage, atomic writes, stale reviews, and archive integrity.

Live Qwen testing exposed a performance regression: the completed full research run took **30m35s**, compared with **12m06s** for the earlier baseline on the same heat-pump question. It passed structural checks but still contained factual mistakes. Those results motivated replacing repeated approval records with a concise four-part critique; they do not establish a speed or quality improvement for the final workflow.

The full repository test suite and full Docusaurus build were not run. macOS and Windows execution remain unverified. Deterministic checks establish structural contracts; they cannot establish source truth, independence, or research quality.

## Infographic

![deep-researcher search-as-code](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0236d/Fnt6gQy8KzXvfnhhddqtT_GBAVZa2w.png)

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add token-rate and catalogo-it
prs.body:
Adds two community catalog entries, both from
[`Lazzdaycod/hermes-lang-it`](https://github.com/Lazzdaycod/hermes-lang-it),
pinned at `7bb28ed61954004053232e9532e659173343a78d`. Both live under `plugins/`
next to the Italian language pack that repo also ships. One commit, two added
files, nothing else touched.

## `token-rate` — live tokens/sec for a local llama.cpp model

Status-bar chip with the real output/input tokens-per-second of the local
llama.cpp server. Hermes itself reads the server's log
(`$HERMES_HOME/logs/llama-server.log`, last 200 lines) and serves it at
`/api/plugins/token-rate/`; the chip polls that route once a second. The counter
starts **off** — click the chip, or run the palette entry *Token Rate:
start/stop the tok/s counter* — to start it. It also registers the
`get_token_rate` agent tool so the model can read its own speed.

**Disclosure:** reads one local file (the llama.cpp log) and nothing else — no
network calls, no external process, no extra port, no API key, no credentials,
no telemetry. It never talks to the local server over HTTP either. The only file
it writes is its own on/off flag (`$HERMES_HOME/cache/token-rate-state.json`).

## `catalogo-it` — the Hermes plugin catalog, in Italian

Native page (sidebar entry, route `/catalogo`, plus a palette entry) listing the
official catalog with an Italian interface and on-the-fly Italian descriptions,
plus a search field, category/tier filters and a detail panel with Hermes' own
install button.

**Disclosure:** fetches the public catalog feed
(`hermes-agent.nousresearch.com`), `translate.googleapis.com` and
`api.mymemory.translated.net`; sends a plugin description to the **local** model
endpoint only as the last translation fallback. That endpoint comes from Hermes'
own config (`model.base_url`) and the key is the one Hermes generated for the
local server (`$HERMES_HOME/runtimes/llamacpp/.api_key`), read through the
plugin's own backend route — no credential is stored or sent anywhere else.
Translation runs when an entry is opened, not for the whole catalog. No
telemetry.

## Review notes

- `hermes plugins validate` at the pinned commit, run here: every check passes —
  `security scan — safe`, `no core override`, `desktop surface — stays inside the
  plugin SDK surface`, and declared tools/hooks/middleware match registrations.
- Both are unified packages (`plugin.yaml` + `__init__.py` +
  `dashboard/plugin_api.py` + `dashboard/manifest.json` + `desktop/plugin.js`),
  each with its own README carrying the disclosure.
- No Python dependencies, no `requires_env`, no binaries, no committed bytecode
  (`.gitignore` keeps `__pycache__` out), no self-updater.
- Desktop code imports only `@hermes/plugin-sdk` and `react`/`react/jsx-runtime`;
  no prototype patching, no `eval`, no dynamic `import()`, no queries into core
  markup.
- UI is English-first with an Italian bundle (`ctx.i18n.register({ en, it })`),
  so the chip/page follow the app locale.
- `catalogo-it` does not hardcode the local server port or model name: it reads
  `model.base_url` from Hermes' config and takes the model from the endpoint's
  `/v1/models`, falling back to the configured one.
- `category: desktop` for both; `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.6"` (unified packages
  with a `dashboard/plugin_api.py`).

I maintain `Lazzdaycod/hermes-lang-it` (rule 5) and will open the SHA-bump PRs
for future changes myself.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add hermes-finance 0.2.5
prs.body:
Adds `hermes-finance` 0.2.5 to the plugin catalog, pinned to the v0.2.5 release commit `9c5a10562aaa9f625240d9a59e197cd01187fec5` of https://github.com/arspesk/hermes-finance (`subdir: hermes_plugin`). I own the repository.

The plugin answers money questions from a local hermes-finance database through 16 tools, and registers one `pre_tool_call` hook that puts the four write tools behind Hermes approval. It also adds a usage skill and the `hermes finance` CLI command (report-job setup and shell completion) through `register_cli_command`.

## Disclosure

- **Reads outside the plugin directory.** The tools open the SQLite database of a separate app checkout (`HERMES_FINANCE_APP_DIR`, prepared with Python 3.12 and `uv sync`). The plugin installs no Python dependencies into Hermes.
- **Writes.** `finance_set_category`, `finance_add_rule`, `finance_set_cap` and `finance_track_bill` change that database only after the user approves each call. The hook blocks them under cron, the gateway's unattended platforms and single-query runs, and returns `block` (never `approve`) if it can't ask.
- **Network.** `finance_sync` runs the app's bank sync, which calls Plaid with the user's optional Plaid keys. The opt-in report jobs also call Plaid and, with a live read-only key, Alpaca. The read tools make no network calls.
- **Credentials (rule 11).** The six optional Plaid and Alpaca keys are declared as `config_schema` secrets and read with `agent.secret_scope.get_secret` at call time. In plugin mode the app opens no `.env`, `secrets.env` or key file, and it has no fallback to one. Tests plant marker key files and check the values never appear in output, logs or error messages.
- **Shell and scheduled jobs.** `hermes finance crons plan` / `apply` are explicit commands. They write profile-owned entry scripts and schedule the app through Hermes cron. Installing starts no server, sync or job.
- **No telemetry and no update check.** Updates arrive only through a SHA-bump PR here.

## Validation

- `hermes plugins validate hermes_plugin` at the pinned commit, in a throwaway `HERMES_HOME` on Hermes v0.22.0: passed. Tools, hooks and middleware match the registrations, the security scan is `safe`, and the no-core-override check passed.
- It warns under rule 9 about four imports: `gateway.session_context.get_session_env` and `tools.approval._UNATTENDED_APPROVAL_PLATFORMS` (used to keep writes blocked in unattended runs) and `cron.jobs` / `cron.scheduler` (used by the opt-in report jobs). The plugin patches no core function. If public seams exist for these I'll switch; otherwise I'm happy to open an issue for them. Both are listed in `known_issues`.
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/`: OK. `scripts/scan_plugin_payloads.py` on the plugin directory: clean.
- The image (1200×600) and both screenshots are raw URLs pinned to the same commit and return 200. The screenshots come from the README and show synthetic demo data.
- The app's own CI is green on the pinned commit.

`readme: false` because `hermes_plugin/` has no README. `docs_url` points to the install section of the root README at the pinned commit.

issues.title: Proposal: low-dependency Plazmi MCP/CLI example for persistent agent sessions
issues.body:
PicoClaw's MCP CLI and heartbeat capabilities look like a useful home for a small persistent-world example. [Plazmi](https://plazmi.gg) provides homes, gardens and neighbour interactions on real UTC time, plus `pulse`/`digest` for returning agents. Its community shell client is one Python file with no third-party dependencies.

I can supply an optional example using your existing HTTP MCP transport and a separate read-only heartbeat. Installation would inspect the public schema and preview onboarding first; attaching a resident and enabling a heartbeat would remain explicit operator steps. It would not add a new built-in skill or create accounts by default.

Acceptance proposal: the documented MCP add/test path works, the configured resident resumes through the same key, a rejected domain result remains a failure, and heartbeat work is bounded to status reads. I have validated the Plazmi surface and portable wrapper, not a complete PicoClaw deployment. Interested in a documentation/example collaboration?

issues.title: Model identifier validation suggests lowercasing unknown provider prefixes, breaking case-sensitive upstream model IDs
issues.body:
## Summary

In the model edit sheet, entering a model identifier whose prefix is **not** a picoclaw provider but is an upstream model namespace (for example `ACME/gpt-4o-mini`, where the upstream API is case-sensitive) shows a warning:

> "ACME" should use "acme" — Fix

Clicking **Fix** rewrites the model to `acme/gpt-4o-mini`. With case-sensitive upstream routing this breaks a previously working configuration (401 / provider not found).

## Steps to reproduce

1. WebUI → Models → Edit (or Add) a model.
2. Provider = OpenAI, API Base = an OpenAI-compatible gateway, Model identifier = `ACME/gpt-4o-mini` (the prefix is an upstream namespace, not a picoclaw provider key).
3. The form shows the warning `"ACME" should use "acme"` with a Fix button.
4. Click Fix → the field becomes `acme/gpt-4o-mini`; saving it makes the upstream reject the request because its provider namespace is case-sensitive.

## Expected

- No "should use" suggestion unless the prefix actually maps to a known provider/alias in the provider catalog.
- When a Provider is selected and the field is documented as a full model ID (the field hint says a slash-containing value is kept as a full ID and not re-split), provider-prefix validation should be skipped.
- At minimum, do not offer a destructive one-click "fix" that lowercases an unknown prefix.

## Root cause (v0.3.1, git 2cf030d2)

- `web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts:26-28` — `normalizeProvider()` lowercases the input.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts:76-82` — `getCanonicalProviderKey()` returns `aliasMap[normalized] ?? normalized`; for an **unknown** prefix it falls back to the lowercased input instead of returning empty.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts:85-91` — the validator treats that fallback as a real alias and emits `models.validation.shouldUse` with `fix: ${alias}/${model}`.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/edit-model-sheet.tsx:268-269` — the Fix button applies `modelValidation.fix` to the input.

## Proposed patch

```diff
--- a/web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts
+++ b/web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts
@@ -79,7 +79,7 @@ export function getCanonicalProviderKey(
   const normalized = normalizeProvider(provider)
   if (!normalized) return ""
-  return getProviderAliasMap(backendOptions)[normalized] ?? normalized
+  return getProviderAliasMap(backendOptions)[normalized] ?? ""
 }

--- a/web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts
+++ b/web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts
@@ -64,6 +64,17 @@ export function validateModelField(
   const provider = trimmed.slice(0, slashIdx)
   const model = trimmed.slice(slashIdx + 1)
   if (!model) {
     return { level: "error", messageKey: "models.validation.emptyModel" }
   }
 
+  // When a provider is explicitly selected, a slash-containing identifier is
+  // documented as a full model ID for that provider (see modelIdHint) — do not
+  // re-interpret its first segment as a provider prefix.
+  if (selectedProvider) {
+    return {
+      level: "success",
+      messageKey: "models.validation.parsed",
+      messageParams: { provider: selectedProvider, model: trimmed },
+    }
+  }
+
   if (!knownProviderKeys.has(provider)) {
```

Add a regression test with an uppercase upstream namespace (e.g. `ACME/model`) and a lowercase provider alias in the catalog, asserting that no `shouldUse` warning is produced.

## Impact

One click can silently change a working model ID to a different, invalid one; the UI appears to be helping but breaks the configuration. This is more than a cosmetic warning.

## Environment

- picoclaw v0.3.1 (git 2cf030d2), Linux, WebUI

issues.title: WebUI falsely reports "restart required" after gateway hot-reload has already applied the config
issues.body:
## Summary

With `gateway.hot_reload: true`, changing the default model in the WebUI is applied by the gateway within ~2 seconds (confirmed in the gateway log), but the WebUI still shows the "restart required" toast, and `gateway_restart_required` in the gateway status stays `true` until the launcher/gateway is restarted.

This makes operators think the change did not take effect and repeatedly restart the service, interrupting active chats.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set `"gateway": {"hot_reload": true}` in `~/.picoclaw/config.json` (default is `false`) and restart `picoclaw-launcher.service` once so the watcher is enabled.
2. In the WebUI, change the default model (or edit a model setting) and save.
3. With `gateway.log_level: info`, `~/.picoclaw/logs/gateway.log` shows:
   ```
   🔄 Config file changed, reloading...
    New model is '<new-alias>', recreating provider...
   Provider and config reloaded successfully
     ✓ Provider, configuration, and services reloaded successfully (thread-safe)
   ```
   The gateway PID does not change, and the new model is actually used.
4. The save toast still says "restart required", and `GET /api/gateway/status` returns `gateway_restart_required: true`.

## Expected

- When hot reload has successfully applied the change, the WebUI should not ask for a restart.
- If a change genuinely requires a process restart, the prompt should only appear in that case.

## Actual

The flag stays `true` after every config save, even though `handleConfigReload` already applied the new provider/config in-process.

## Root cause (v0.3.1, git 2cf030d2)

- The flag is computed by the launcher backend, not the gateway:
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:807-814` — `gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(bootSignature, currentSignature, gatewayStatus)`.
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:864-868` — `attachToGatewayProcessLocked()` records `gateway.bootConfigSignature` when the launcher attaches.
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:1086` — the launcher records it when it starts the gateway.
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:1471-1477` — status compares the recorded signature with the current config signature.
- Hot reload happens inside the gateway process (`pkg/gateway/gateway.go:257` starts the polling watcher; `pkg/gateway/gateway.go:586-660` `handleConfigReload` recreates the provider and restarts services). There is no callback to the launcher, so `bootConfigSignature` is never refreshed.
- The WebUI consumes `gateway.restartRequired` directly (`web/frontend/src/components/models/edit-model-sheet.tsx:395-399`, `web/frontend/src/lib/restart-required.ts`).
- `computeConfigSignature()` only covers model/default/streaming, tool enablement and channel settings — all of which `handleConfigReload` applies. It does not include process-level fields such as `gateway.host`/`gateway.port`, so the current flag is effectively only ever about hot-reloadable config.

## Proposed patch

```diff
--- a/web/backend/api/gateway.go
+++ b/web/backend/api/gateway.go
@@ -804,14 +804,20 @@
-func gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(bootSignature, currentSignature, gatewayStatus string) bool {
+func gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(bootSignature, currentSignature, gatewayStatus string, hotReload bool) bool {
 	if gatewayStatus != "running" {
 		return false
 	}
 	if bootSignature == "" || currentSignature == "" {
 		return false
 	}
+	// With hot reload enabled, the gateway watcher applies every field covered
+	// by computeConfigSignature (model/tools/channels) in-process. A launcher-
+	// side restart is not required for these changes.
+	// Process-level settings (host/port) are not part of this signature.
+	if hotReload {
+		return false
+	}
 	return bootSignature != currentSignature
 }
@@ -1468,9 +1474,12 @@
 	gatewayStatus, _ := data["gateway_status"].(string)
 	currentConfigSignature := computeConfigSignature(cfg)
+	hotReload := cfg != nil && cfg.Gateway.HotReload
 	gateway.mu.Lock()
 	bootConfigSignature := gateway.bootConfigSignature
 	gateway.mu.Unlock()
 	data["gateway_restart_required"] = gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(
 		bootConfigSignature,
 		currentConfigSignature,
 		gatewayStatus,
+		hotReload,
 	)
```

Alternative (more robust long-term): have the gateway publish an "applied config signature" (pid file field or health endpoint), update it on every successful `handleConfigReload`, and have the launcher compare the current config against that value instead of its boot-time value.

## Verification after patch

1. Enable `hot_reload`, restart once.
2. Change the default model in the WebUI and save.
3. The toast should be the normal "saved" success message; `gateway_restart_required` should be `false`.
4. Switch back and repeat.

## Environment

- picoclaw v0.3.1 (git 2cf030d2), Linux, WebUI
- `gateway.hot_reload: true`

prs.title: fix(cron): agent response not sent to channel after cron job
prs.body:
## Description

Cron-triggered agent replies were silently discarded and never delivered to any channel (e.g. Telegram).

`ExecuteJob` calls `ProcessDirectWithChannel`, which bypasses the `AgentLoop` bus and invokes `processMessage` directly. The `Run()` loop's `PublishOutbound` — which is responsible for dispatching the response to the channel — never fires in this code path. The returned response was discarded with `_ = response`.

**Before:**
```go
_ = response // Will be sent by AgentLoop  ← never is
```

**After:**
```go
if response != "" {
    t.msgBus.PublishOutbound(bus.OutboundMessage{
        Channel: channel,
        ChatID:  chatID,
        Content: response,
    })
}
```

This is consistent with the `deliver=true` and command execution paths in the same function.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## 🤖 AI Code Generation

- [x] 🤖 Fully AI-generated — AI (Claude) identified the root cause and wrote the fix; contributor reviewed and validated it

## Related Issue

N/A — identified from production logs showing agent response generated but not received on Telegram.

## Technical Context

Call chain: `CronTool.ExecuteJob` → `ProcessDirectWithChannel` → `processMessage` → `runAgentLoop` → returns `string`. The `Run()` loop that normally calls `PublishOutbound` is never involved when `ProcessDirectWithChannel` is used directly.

## 🧪 Test Environment
- **Hardware:** PC
- **OS:** Debian 13.02
- **Model/Provider:** Claude Sonnet 4.6
- **Channels:** Telegram

## Evidence

```
2026/02/25 10:10:32 [INFO] agent: Response: ... {agent_id=main, session_key=agent:main:main, iterations=1, final_length=369}
# → message never received on Telegram
```

- [x] `make check` passes locally
- [x] My change is focused and does not bundle unrelated changes
- [x] I have disclosed AI involvement above

prs.title: fix(anthropic): make claude-haiku-5-5 (thinking-always models) work with token credentials
prs.body:
## Problem

Every token-based Anthropic call to a thinking-always model (e.g. `claude-haiku-5-5`) fails with:

```
status=400 invalid_request_error: "temperature" is deprecated for this model
```

Repro: model entry with `provider: anthropic`, `auth_method: token` (API key stored in `auth.json`), any Claude 5 model. Reproduced on picoclaw 0.3.1 / Termux armv7; current `main` has the same code path.

## Root cause

Two separate bugs on the token path (`oauth.ClaudeProvider`):

1. The wrapper does not implement `ThinkingCapable`, so `applyTurnThinkingOptions` treats the provider as not thinking-capable, **never injects `thinking_level`**, and the inner SDK provider then always sends an explicit `temperature`. Claude 5 family models reject an explicit `temperature` with 400.
2. `buildParams` sends `temperature` unconditionally, so even when thinking injection is fixed or absent, thinking-always models still get a `temperature` they reject.

## Fix

- `pkg/providers/oauth/claude_provider.go`: delegate `SupportsThinking()` to the inner SDK provider so `thinking_level` is honored for token/OAuth credentials as well.
- `pkg/providers/anthropic/provider.go`: omit `temperature` for models that have thinking enabled by default and reject an explicit one (`haiku-5`, `sonnet-5`, `opus-5`, `opus-4-5`, `sonnet-4-5`).

## Verification

- On-device (Termux armv7, picoclaw 0.3.1 + these patches): `picoclaw agent -m ...` against `claude-haiku-5-5` with `thinking_level: adaptive` now succeeds (verified with a real API round-trip).
- `go test ./pkg/providers/... ./pkg/agent/...` passes with tags `goolm,stdjson,whatsapp_native`.

Note: Claude 5 models only accept `thinking.type: "adaptive"` (not `enabled` + `budget_tokens`); that is a config-side concern and unaffected by this change — with the wrapper fix in place, `thinking_level: adaptive` now actually reaches the API.

## AI assistance disclosure

The patches were written by an AI coding agent (Hermes Agent) on the contributor's machine, tested on-device (Termux armv7) and with the project test suite, and reviewed, submitted and taken responsibility for by the human contributor (sebbY82).

issues.title: Signal channel: image/PDF attachments unreachable from agent container

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## Bug

Images and PDFs sent over Signal arrive at the host but the agent inside the container can't open them.

## Reproduce

1. Install Signal via `/add-signal` on a v2 install.
2. From your phone, send a DM with an image attached (e.g. `archetype.png`).
3. Ask the agent \"can you see this image?\".

Agent responds with something like *\"I see that an image came through (the path is showing) but I can't access the file from my container — the Signal attachments folder isn't mounted into my workspace\".*

Same behaviour for PDFs (`application/pdf`), except PDFs are dropped silently — there's no handler for them at all in `src/channels/signal.ts`.

## Root cause

`src/channels/signal.ts` (upstream/channels) builds the inbound message's structured `attachments` array as `{path: <host-path>, contentType}` and also emits a `[Image: <host-path>]` line in the text body. The host path points into `~/.local/share/signal-cli/attachments/<id>`, which is **never mounted into the agent container** — `src/container-runner.ts:buildMounts` only mounts `/workspace`, `/workspace/agent`, `/workspace/global`, `/app/CLAUDE.md`, `/app/src`, `/app/skills`, `/home/node/.claude`, plus any `additionalMounts` the operator configures per-group.

So the agent receives a path that doesn't resolve inside its filesystem. Vision-capable models never see images; PDFs are silently dropped.

## Fix

The host already has a complete pipeline for this: `src/session-manager.ts:extractAttachmentFiles` saves any `attachments[].data` base64 to `<sessionDir>/inbox/<msgId>/<filename>` and rewrites the entry as `localPath`. The container formatter renders `[image|document: <name> — saved to /workspace/inbox/.../...]`. The agent can then `Read` the file.

signal.ts just needs to read each image/PDF file off disk and inline it as base64 in the `attachments` array. No host changes, no new mount, no new dependency.

PR with the fix (image + PDF, refactored into a shared helper, tests updated): #2529 — will edit this issue with the link after creating it.

## Verified

Fix is running live on a downstream install since 2026-05-17. Images now render through to the agent; PDFs work end-to-end with original filename preserved.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(scheduling): start a scheduled run at its due time, not on the next sweep tick
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Starts a scheduled task at its due time instead of on the next 60s sweep tick.

- **Problem**: due tasks only wake on the resync tick (`SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000`), so a run due at `:00` starts anywhere up to a minute late. `ncl tasks run` inserts a row that is due now and then waits for the same tick.
- **Fix**: each reconcile reports the session's next due time through a new `InboundMailbox.nextDueAt()`. A due-time wake feed (`src/due-wake.ts`) keeps one timer per session and enqueues a reconcile just after that instant. `ncl tasks create`, `ncl tasks run`, and an update that moves `--process-after` enqueue a reconcile right away, so the timer is armed without waiting for a tick.
- **Why it is safe**: the feed is additive, like the mail-write and runtime feeds. The reconcile re-reads truth, so wake, cap and claim rules are unchanged. A stale timer costs one no-op reconcile, a lost one costs one tick, and the resync tick stays the floor.
- **Bounded**: only due times within 5 minutes are armed (later ones are re-reported by a later reconcile), which also keeps every delay far below `setTimeout`'s 2^31 ms ceiling. `stopHostSweep` clears the timers.
- **Who needs this**: anyone with a frequent schedule (`*/5`, `*/30`) or a task that reports at a fixed minute: today its start time drifts by up to a minute every run, and an operator who runs `ncl tasks run` to test a task waits up to a minute for it to start.

## Related work

No issue. Touches the same files as #3921, #3932 (task envelope fields) and #3903 (scheduler admission), but different hunks: none of them changes when a session is reconciled.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/due-wake.test.ts src/mailbox/sqlite/next-due-at.test.ts` -> 8/8 pass (timer fires just after the due time, not before; ignores null/past/beyond-horizon; one timer per session; `nextDueAt` skips past, paused and non-triggering rows and returns ISO UTC for a naive SQLite timestamp).
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/cli/resources/tasks.test.ts` -> 32/32 pass, including a new test that create, run and a moved due time enqueue a reconcile, and a prompt-only edit does not.
- `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint` (0 errors), `pnpm run format:check` -> clean.
- `pnpm test` -> 4244 pass. One unrelated `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts` case timed out under the full parallel run and passes alone (29/29).

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Scheduled tasks now start at their due time instead of up to a minute late, and `ncl tasks run` starts the run immediately.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. No new input, permission or credential path. The timers only enqueue the existing reconcile.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: fix(delivery): back off rate-limited and transient sends instead of dropping them
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops delivery from dropping a reply when a channel rate-limits it or the network blips.

- **Problem**: every failed send counts toward one cap of 3 attempts, retried on the next polls, so a few seconds apart. A Teams 429 with no Retry-After fails all three tries within seconds, and the reply is marked failed for good. `delivery_attempts.next_attempt_at` exists for this, but it is always written as null and nothing reads it.
- **Fix**: transient failures (Chat SDK `RATE_LIMITED`, HTTP 408/429/5xx, network errors) write `next_attempt_at`. The wait is the adapter's Retry-After when it gives one (capped at 5 min); otherwise it is 2 s, doubling to 60 s. The attempt count and its deadline go into one write, so a crash cannot keep one without the other. The give-up is an attempt cap: the 35th failure fails the message. With the default backoff that is about 30 minutes; with long Retry-After values it can stretch to about 170 minutes. The drain skips a row that is not due yet; it never sleeps and never holds a poll.
- **Order**: a held message holds its destination (channel + conversation) for its own session. That session's later messages to the conversation wait behind it, so they arrive in order. Other conversations and other sessions are not delayed. Another session sending to the same conversation (for example a per-thread session) is not held; order across sessions is not guaranteed, as on `main` today.
- **Split replies**: a channel that splits long text (Telegram, Discord) posts the chunks one by one, and a retry posts the sent chunks again. When a chunk after the first fails, the bridge marks the error (`PARTIAL_SEND`), and that send stays on the cap of 3: still backed off and still holding its conversation, but the first chunk is posted at most 3 times, as on `main`. Resuming from the failed chunk would need per-message chunk state; that is out of scope.
- **Durable**: the backoff lives in `delivery_attempts`, so a restart keeps it. The failure that reaches the cap stores no retry deadline, and the drain marks a stored give-up failed before it would send. A restart between storing the last failure and marking it failed therefore cannot send once more.
- **Permanent errors are unchanged**: they are still retried on the next polls and fail after 3, and they never hold the destination. Unknown errors count as permanent, so a deterministic failure cannot wedge a conversation. An HTTP status anywhere in the cause chain is checked before the error's name, because the Teams adapter wraps a 400 in a `NetworkError`. The walk detects loops, and a chain longer than 32 links counts as permanent.
- **Out of scope**: telling the agent that a message failed (#2423), and ordering across sessions that share a conversation.

<details>
<summary>Why the core change is over 30 lines</summary>

`src/delivery.ts` gains about 140 lines, `src/db/coordination.ts` about 10, and `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts` about 8 (the split-reply mark). Most of the new lines are the error classifier, the network-code list and the constants. The drain itself changes by about 25 lines: one read of due rows per drain with pending messages, a skip, and one new branch in the existing catch. There is no new table and no migration. The schedule fits in the existing `attempts` and `next_attempt_at` columns.

</details>

## Related work

Closes #3058. Refs #2423.

This builds on the classifier and the 30-minute horizon from #3059 (thanks @mashkovtsevlx). It differs in three ways:
- it keeps the schedule in `delivery_attempts` rather than an in-memory map, so a restart keeps it;
- it holds the destination, so order is kept;
- it recognises the Chat SDK's `AdapterRateLimitError` / `RateLimitError` (code `RATE_LIMITED`) and their Retry-After.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/delivery-transient-backoff.test.ts`: 20 passed. Before the fix, 9 of the first 12 failed and the 3 permanent-error guards passed.
  - A Teams-style 429 with no Retry-After is retried at 2 s, 6 s and 14 s, then delivered. Before the fix it was marked failed on the third poll.
  - The adapter's Retry-After (30 s) is honoured.
  - Order is kept for one conversation: a1 throttled, b1 delivered, a2 waits, then a1 and a2 go out in order.
  - A held conversation does not delay a neighbour session in the same poll.
  - A backoff row from before a restart is not retried early.
  - Horizon: the 34th transient failure is still held, and the 35th gives up as `failed`.
  - A plain error still fails after 3 attempts and does not hold later messages.
  - A Teams `NetworkError` that wraps an HTTP 400 is permanent.
  - 5xx and `ECONNRESET` are transient.
  - The first `delivery_attempts` write already carries the deadline, so a crash right after it keeps the backoff. A separate fault-injection run kills the process right after that write; on restart nothing is sent before the 300 s Retry-After.
  - A 400 five links down a chain of `NetworkError`s is permanent; a looping chain is read once; a 100-link chain is permanent.
  - Split reply, through the real Chat SDK bridge (`maxTextLength` 40, three chunks) and the real drain: with the second chunk always refused with a Telegram-shaped `RATE_LIMITED` (`retryAfter` 3), the first chunk is posted 3 times and the message fails (it was 35 times before this mark).
  - Split reply refused twice, then accepted: each retry waits the 3 s Retry-After, the next message to the chat waits behind it, and the whole reply then goes out in order.
  - A give-up that a restart cut short (3 failures stored, never marked failed) is marked failed with no further send, and the failure that reaches the cap stores no deadline. A separate crash run kills the process right after the third failure is stored; on restart the first chunk stays at 3 posts (it was 4).
  - Each of these breaks fails a test: no Retry-After cap (a 3600 s Retry-After is held 5 min), 408 made permanent, the Teams status read only from `innerHttpError.statusCode` dropped, and system and agent rows classified as transient (they keep 3 attempts and no backoff).
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `pnpm test` (full host suite): 304 files passed and every delivery test passed. Four files fail the same way on an unchanged `main` checkout on this machine (`scripts/q.test.ts`, `scripts/update/service.test.ts`, `setup/gateways/selection.test.ts`, `setup/gateways/onecli-detection.test.ts`). Three slow script files timed out under load and pass when run alone.
- Not covered: a live Teams conversation actually throttling a send. The tests use the error shape the Teams adapter throws.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Replies that hit a channel rate limit or a network blip are now retried with backoff for up to about 30 minutes, in order, instead of being dropped after three quick tries.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. No new inputs. The classifier reads only fields on errors that adapters throw.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

<!-- Required. -->
- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: feat(providers): add Obscurify.ai as an OpenAI-compatible provider
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds Obscurify.ai as an OpenAI-compatible provider. It follows the same pattern as #990 (Eden AI).

Obscurify.ai is a privacy-focused gateway. Accounts are a random 16-digit account number with no email, and prompts and responses are not stored on the server. Disclosure: I run it.

Usage:

```json
"models": { "providers": { "obscurify-ai": { "api_key": "sk-obs1_..." } } }
```

Or set `OBSCURIFY_API_KEY` (`OBSCURIFY_AI_API_KEY` also works). Model ids keep the lab prefix, e.g. `obscurify-ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`. Keys come from https://obscurify.ai/account, API docs are at https://obscurify.ai/api-docs, and the model list is public at https://obscurify.ai/v1/models.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- `src/providers/factory.zig`: `compat_providers` entry, base URL `https://obscurify.ai/v1`, plus test asserts.
- `src/providers/api_key.zig`: env candidates `OBSCURIFY_API_KEY`, `OBSCURIFY_AI_API_KEY`, plus a test.
- `src/provider_names.zig`: aliases `obscurifyai` and `obscurify_ai`, plus test asserts.
- `src/onboard.zig`: `known_providers` entry, default model `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`.
- `src/model_refs.zig`: known provider namespace.
- `src/integrations.zig`: integrations list entry.
- `README.md`, `config.example.json`, `docs/en` and `docs/zh` `configuration.md`: config example.

No `models_dev_providers` row, because the provider isn't on models.dev, so onboarding falls back to the default model.

</details>

## Validation

- `zig fmt --check src/`: pass.
- `git diff --check`: pass.
- `zig build test --summary all` (Zig 0.16.0): 7493/7508 passed, 14 skipped, 1 failed. The one failure is `workspace audit staged diff finds raw token in added line`, and it fails the same way on unmodified `main` on my machine, so it isn't related to this change. I built with `-Dtarget=x86_64-linux-gnu.2.38` because my distro's glibc `crt1.o` has `.sframe` relocations that the Zig 0.16 linker rejects.
- Live check: with only `OBSCURIFY_API_KEY` set and `"obscurify-ai": {}` in config, `nullclaw agent -m "Reply with exactly: pong"` using `obscurify-ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` streamed back `pong`.
- Tool call: `nullclaw agent --provider obscurifyai --model moonshotai/kimi-k2-0905 -m "Use the file_read tool to read note.txt and tell me the secret word only."` (with `max_tokens: 500`). The model called `file_read`, and nullclaw ran it and answered with the word from the file. This also checks that the `obscurifyai` alias resolves.

## Notes

- No new dependencies.
- No behavior change for other providers.

issues.title: Would you accept Obscurify.ai as a named provider?
issues.body:
Would you accept Obscurify.ai as a named provider in `providers.json`? I saw the Novita PR (#1115) closed because the list shouldn't grow to include every provider, so I'm asking before opening a PR.

Disclosure: I run it.

Why I think it fits: the registry already has privacy-focused entries (Tinfoil, Venice). Obscurify.ai is in the same space. Accounts are a random 16-digit account number with no email, prompts and responses are not stored on the server, and requests only use zero-data-retention routes. It's OpenAI-compatible (chat completions with streaming and tools), and one key covers 200+ models. Docs: https://obscurify.ai/api-docs

Today users can already reach it with `openai_compatible` and a base URL. A named entry would add it to `ironclaw onboard` and `ironclaw models list` with a key link and a default model.

Proposed entry (after `venice`):

```json
{
  "id": "obscurify_ai",
  "aliases": [
    "obscurify-ai",
    "obscurifyai"
  ],
  "protocol": "open_ai_completions",
  "default_base_url": "https://obscurify.ai/v1",
  "api_key_env": "OBSCURIFY_API_KEY",
  "api_key_required": true,
  "model_env": "OBSCURIFY_MODEL",
  "default_model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash",
  "description": "Obscurify.ai privacy-focused inference (no-email accounts, prompts not stored)",
  "setup": {
    "kind": "api_key",
    "secret_name": "llm_obscurify_ai_api_key",
    "key_url": "https://obscurify.ai/account?utm_source=ironclaw",
    "display_name": "Obscurify.ai",
    "can_list_models": true
  }
}
```

`can_list_models` is true because `GET https://obscurify.ai/v1/models` is public and returns the model list with context lengths.

I tested this on a branch off current `main` (the JSON entry, plus a row in `docs/capabilities/llm-providers.md` and `OBSCURIFY_API_KEY`/`OBSCURIFY_MODEL` added to the env-mask list in the onboarding credential tests):

- `ironclaw models list` with `LLM_BACKEND=obscurify_ai`: shows `obscurify_ai` as active with default `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`.
- `ironclaw run -m "Reply with exactly: pong"` (isolated `HOME` and `IRONCLAW_REBORN_HOME`, key from `OBSCURIFY_API_KEY`): replied `pong`.
- `ironclaw run -m "Use a tool to read the file note.txt in the current directory and tell me only the secret word."`: the agent read the file with a tool and answered with the word that was in it.
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_llm --lib`: 1023 passed. `cargo test -p ironclaw llm_credentials`: 19 passed. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- I built with `SKIP_FRONTEND_BUILD=1` because my machine has no corepack, so the web UI path wasn't exercised.

If you're open to it, I'll send the PR from that branch and link it here. If you'd rather keep the list as it is, that's fine too, and I'll close this.

prs.title: feat(media): erase from a close-up and blend it back into the source
prs.body:
## Summary

Improves image Erase quality. Previously the full source and full mask were sent to the image model, so small marks were easy to miss and the model re-rendered unmarked areas too.

- Compute the marked area's bounds from the mask and send the model a close-up around it (3x the mark, min side 512, aspect ratio ≤ 2; falls back to the full image when the close-up would cover ≥ 60% of it). Private copies of the cropped source/mask are recorded in the new `ImageEditRequest.eraseCrop`.
- Blend the model output back into the immutable source locally (`imageEditingErase.ts`): the mask is grown and feathered, the patch's color drift is measured on preserved pixels and removed, and every pixel outside the feather stays untouched.
- Erase now shares the local-compose flow with background removal via `composesImageEditLocally()` (raw output downloaded privately, only the composed result is published).
- Erase uses its fixed prompt and ignores the conversation model's extra prompt; the conversation-model context tells it not to inspect the mask or guess the marked object.
- Media generation logs now record the prompt actually sent, plus the edit operation and crop rect.
- Requests staged before this change (no `eraseCrop`) fall back to the full image.

## Electron behavior changes

Main process only; no IPC channel, storage schema, or OpenClaw config changes. New private files `*-erase-source.png` / `*-erase-mask.png` are written alongside existing edit guides, and erase results are saved as `image-erase-*.png`.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/main/libs/imageEditing src/main/libs/agentEngine/openclawRuntimeAdapter.test.ts` — passed
- New unit tests in `src/main/libs/imageEditingErase.test.ts`
- `tsc -p electron-tsconfig.json` — no errors
- ESLint clean on touched image-editing files
- Manually verified erase results in the app

prs.body:
## Summary
Opening a task no longer reads every detected image artifact as a base64 data URL over IPC and keeps it in Redux. The conversation already shows these images from their files, so the full read only cost memory and time on entry. Image artifacts on disk now load from the file, versioned by its mtime.

## Changes Made
- `loadDetectedFileArtifact`: image artifacts with a file path only get an existence check (`statFile`), keep empty `content`, and use the file's `mtimeMs` as `contentVersion`. Reopening a task reuses the decoded image; a file changed on disk is fetched again.

- Artifact panel refresh handles images like HTML: it bumps `contentVersion` instead of re-reading the file as a data URL.
- `ImageEditor` reloads when `contentVersion` changes; its failure fallback renders the artifact directly.

prs.title: fix(signal): decode event stream across chunk boundaries
prs.body:
## Summary

The Signal event loop decoded each network chunk from the signal-cli SSE stream with `String::from_utf8_lossy` before parsing. A chunk boundary can fall inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character such as an emoji. Lossy decoding then turns both halves into `U+FFFD`, corrupting the message before it reaches the agent.

`SseParser` now buffers raw bytes and decodes only complete lines. A `\n` byte never appears inside a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence, so splitting on it is always safe. The buffer is also drained once per chunk instead of once per line.

## Context

Part of a small series of Signal fixes, each standalone. Next: skip data messages with no content (incoming reactions currently reach the agent as empty messages).

## Validation

### Completed

- [x] `cargo test -p moltis-signal`: 17 passed, 4 new tests in `sse.rs`
  - emoji split across two chunks
  - one-byte chunks with CRLF line endings
  - invalid UTF-8 still yields the event, with the bad bytes replaced by `U+FFFD`
  - trailing unterminated line flushed by `finish()`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p moltis-signal --all-targets -- -D warnings`: zero warnings

### Remaining

- [ ] `./scripts/local-validate.sh <PR_NUMBER>`
- [ ] Upstream CI (fork workflows need maintainer approval)

## Manual QA

1. Run `signal-cli daemon --http 127.0.0.1:8080` and connect a Signal account in Moltis.
2. From an allowlisted contact, send a DM with several emoji and accented characters, e.g. `héllo 👍🏽🎉`.
3. Confirm the agent receives the text unchanged, with no `�` replacement characters.

issues.title: [Bug]: Feishu 入站图文混发（post 内嵌图片）被静默丢弃——仅解析文字、不下载图片、无任何警告（inbound，与 #2792 出站方向相反）
issues.body:
## Summary (English)

Incoming Feishu **rich-text (`post`) messages that contain both text and images** are only partially parsed by the Feishu channel: the **text is delivered to the agent, but the embedded images are silently dropped** — no media file is downloaded and no warning is logged. Images sent as a **standalone `type=image` message always work**. This is the **inbound direction**; outbound mixed-content handling is tracked in #2792.

## 环境 / Environment

- QwenPaw version: **2.2.2b4** (QwenPaw Desktop, `qwenpaw-backend` packaged exe)
- OS: Windows 10 (AMD64)
- Channel: **Feishu**
- Model: unrelated (pure channel-layer issue)

## 复现步骤 / Steps to Reproduce

1. 在飞书里给机器人发**一条同时包含文字和图片的消息**（文字＋图片合并在同一条消息里，飞书会打包成富文本 `post`）。
2. 观察 QwenPaw 日志：只有一条 `type=post` 的 recv 记录，**没有**对应的 `type=image` recv，`media` 目录也没有新文件落盘。
3. Agent 只收到文字，图片内容永久丢失，**日志中没有任何 WARNING/ERROR**（静默失效）。

对照组（均正常）：
- a) 单独发纯文字 → 正常；
- b) **单独发一张图片（不带文字）→ `type=image` → 下载落盘 → 正常**（实测 3/3 成功）。

## 实际结果 / Actual Behavior

日志实录（chat id 已脱敏）：

```
2026-10-09 12:07:00 | INFO | qwenpaw\app\channels\feishu\channel.py:901 | feishu recv from=unknown#c130 chat=oc_**** msg_id=om_x100b63b2cb35 type=post text_len=43
（同一消息中的 2 张图片：无任何 recv/下载记录，media 目录无落盘）

2026-10-09 12:09:32 | INFO | ... type=image text_len=0   ← 单独发的图片，正常收到
2026-10-09 12:10:01 | INFO | ... type=image text_len=0   ← 单独发的图片，正常收到
```

即：**图文混发 → 图片被静默丢弃；图单独发 → 正常**。用户侧表现为“发了图但 AI 说没看到/图老是收不到”。

## 期望结果 / Expected Behavior

1. 解析 `post` 消息载荷中的 `{"tag":"img","image_key":...}` 元素（飞书富文本文档：一条 post 可含多段落，图片元素需独立段落），按 `image_key` 走图片下载接口，把图片作为媒体附加上下文交给 Agent；
2. 多张图片全部提取，顺序保留；
3. **至少**：当消息含图片但未被处理时打一条 `WARNING`（标注丢弃了几张），避免静默失效——排查这类问题目前只能靠人工比对 recv 日志与用户描述。

## 备注 / Additional Context

- 相关但方向相反：#2792 是**出站**（Agent→飞书）图文同发丢图，本 issue 是**入站**（飞书→Agent），建议分别修复。
- 与 #7817 的区别：#7817 问题 2 是 **file/media/audio 独立事件**因缺 `im:resource` 权限被服务端过滤；本 issue 中**独立 `type=image` 消息完全正常（3/3 实测）**，丢的是**打包在 `post` 载荷内嵌的 img 元素**——是 channel 对 post payload 的解析缺口，不是事件推送/权限问题。
- 当前用户侧规避：图片单独一条消息发、一张一张发（实测有效）。
- 猜测修复点：`qwenpaw/app/channels/feishu/channel.py` 中处理 `type=post` 的分支（recv 日志所在 ~L901 附近），目前只取了 text 部分。

issues.title: [Feature]: Add environment variable to set default language for initial Docker setup

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

Allow setting the default language for QwenPaw's initial setup via an environment variable (e.g. `QWENPAW_LANGUAGE`), so deployments can default to English (or any supported language) without manual config edits.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [x] Scripts / Deploy
- [ ] CI/CD

## Problem / Motivation

The default language is hardcoded to `"zh"` in multiple places (`AgentsConfig.language`, `AgentProfileConfig.language`, bootstrap hook, prompt/memory defaults). On a fresh Docker startup, even if a user pre-seeds `config.json` with `{"agents":{"language":"en"}}`, migration and first-run agent creation can reset it to `"zh"`, and the generated `.md` files remain Chinese. There is no environment variable to control this, so non-Chinese deployments require manual post-startup edits.

## Proposed Solution

Introduce an env var (e.g. `QWENPAW_LANGUAGE` / `QWENPAW_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE`) that overrides the default language used by:
- `AgentsConfig` and `AgentProfileConfig` defaults
- Migration and first-run agent creation (`_do_ensure_default_agent`, `_do_ensure_qa_agent`)
- MD file copying (`copy_md_files`) and `installed_md_files_language` seeding
- Prompt / memory / bootstrap language defaults

When unset, keep current behavior (`"zh"`).

## Alternatives Considered

- Pre-seeding `config.json` — doesn't work reliably because migration overwrites `config.agents.language` from the existing agent config.
- Patching the installed package defaults — works but is fragile and lost on upgrade.
- A CLI flag on `qwenpaw init` — helps for manual setup but not for unattended Docker first boot.

## Additional Context

Affected files (installed package): `config/config.py`, `app/migration.py`, `agents/hooks/bootstrap.py`, `agents/prompt.py`, `agents/memory/prompts.py`, `agents/memory/base_memory_manager.py`, `agents/utils/setup_utils.py`, `cli/init_cmd.py`.

## Willing to Contribute

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).
p.s I am not familiar with this project code base and my contribution would rely heavily on QwenPaw coding agent.

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [x] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [x] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

QwenPaw's bundled Office skills are based on Anthropic's skills. The upstream Office skills have since been updated with template-format support and changes to document editing, validation, and spreadsheet recalculation.

Synchronizing the bundled copies would make those improvements available to QwenPaw users and provide a clear upstream reference for future maintenance.

## Proposed Solution

Synchronize the English and Chinese variants of the DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX skills with [[anthropics/skills@fa0fa64](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/commit/fa0fa64bdc967915dc8399e803be67759e1e62b8)](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/commit/fa0fa64bdc967915dc8399e803be67759e1e62b8):

- Update skill instructions and scripts, including support for `.dotx`, `.potx`, and `.xltx` templates.
- Retain QwenPaw-specific platform adaptations and instructions for running bundled scripts.
- Update the built-in skill version metadata and English and Chinese skill documentation.
- Preserve the existing skill license files and record the upstream commit.
- Add focused tests and address compatibility issues identified during review.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep the current bundled versions and update individual fixes as needed.
- Submit separate synchronization PRs for DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX to make each change easier to review.

Maintainer guidance on whether to use one coordinated PR or separate PRs would be appreciated.

## Additional Context

A proposed implementation is available on [[the feat/sync-office-skills branch](https://github.com/nanxu0124/QwenPaw/tree/feat/sync-office-skills)](https://github.com/nanxu0124/QwenPaw/tree/feat/sync-office-skills), with one commit per format. The combined change touches 108 files, including shared helper copies and both language variants.

Initial validation included Python syntax checks, skill metadata and script-path checks, a DOCX comment example, and a PPTX slide-duplication example. `pre-commit run --all-files` passed locally.

A full local unit-test run on macOS produced **18,587 passed, 24 skipped, and 1 failed**. The failure concerns the existing macOS runtime-isolation test and Homebrew SQLite/OpenSSL library access; the affected code was not changed by this branch.
