prs.title: fix(history): avoid per-request FTS scans with a workspace-owned store
prs.body:
## Description

Each conversation request currently opens a new `HistoryStore` and runs an FTS integrity check over the accumulated history. Consequently, a large history database delays even a new, empty conversation.

This change makes the store a reusable Workspace service and injects it into request-local scroll contexts. Requests retain their own context/deduplication state and no longer close borrowed connections. Standalone callers retain their existing ownership behavior. Reload reuse checks the backend, context strategy, database path and file identity; deferred FTS checks can retry, and reported corruption schedules another check.

Workspace shutdown rejects new requests and cancels/awaits its own tracked requests before closing services. This preserves cancellation-time history writes, including when a stop caller is cancelled, without interrupting requests owned by a replacement Workspace. Closed contexts/stores return persistence failure so compaction cannot evict unwritten history.

**Related Issue:** None.

**Security Considerations:** Existing database path validation and SQLite locking are retained. No database schema or configuration format migration is introduced.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep a failing import-cache refresh from taking out the plugin system
prs.body:
## Description

Every backend plugin failed to load on hosts whose interpreter is CPython 3.11.9+ but whose `importlib.metadata` is older (Debian 12 ships 3.11.2): `importlib.invalidate_caches()` raises `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'`, and the call was unguarded in `PluginNamespaceFinder.register()`, which runs once per backend plugin during startup. One raising stdlib call took out the whole plugin system instead of one plugin.

This change makes the import-cache refresh best effort: the failure is logged at debug level and the caller continues.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8473

**Security Considerations:** None. The refresh is a cache invalidation; failing to refresh it can only make an import resolve to a stale entry for the rest of the process, which is what the call was already trying to avoid.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Why the call can fail

Since CPython 3.11.9 the frozen `PathFinder.invalidate_caches()` ends with:

```python
from importlib.metadata import MetadataPathFinder
MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches()
```

`MetadataPathFinder` is resolved through `sys.path`. When an older distro stdlib sits ahead of the bundled one, that name resolves to a plain function without `@classmethod`, so the call raises `TypeError`.

Reproduced on CPython 3.12.15 by replacing `MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches` with a plain function, which is the shape the pre-3.11.9 stdlib has:

```
bundled MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches: classmethod
importlib.invalidate_caches() -> TypeError: plain_invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'
```

## The change

`src/qwenpaw/plugins/module_isolation.py` gains `_invalidate_import_caches()`, which calls `importlib.invalidate_caches()` inside a `try`/`except` and logs the failure at debug level. Both call sites in the module — `PluginNamespaceFinder.register()` and `clear_plugin_bytecode()` — go through it.

This covers the startup path of #8473. The install path of #8265 is a different call site; #8345 and #8107 are open against it, and this change does not touch `loader.py`.

prs.title: fix(channels): keep control-command routing on the user's own text in quoted replies
prs.body:
## Description

Replying to a message with a control command such as `/stop` in Feishu, QQ, WeChat, WeCom, DingTalk, OneBot or Yuanbao never routed as a command. These channels prepend the quoted (replied-to) message before the user's own text, so the inbound text becomes:

```
[quoted message: Alice: quarterly report]
/stop
```

Three shared consumers classify or dispatch on that first text block:

- `manager.enqueue` -> `CommandRegistry.get_priority_level`: `/stop` received normal priority 20 instead of critical 0.
- `BaseChannel._consume_one_request` -> `CommandRegistry.is_control_command`: the reply took the normal tracked-message branch instead of the control branch.
- `Runtime.run` -> `SlashCommandRegistry.dispatch`: even when routed fast, the command was not resolved and reached the agent as plain chat text.

Root cause in all three: they must look at the user's own text, but see the quote-first rendering (source probes in #8342).

### Fix

Add one shared recognizer, `strip_quote_context_prefix()` (`src/qwenpaw/utils/quote_context.py`), that removes leading `[quoted ...]` context blocks (some channels stack more than one, e.g. `[quoted media: download failed]` before `[quoted message: ...]`), and apply it at the two extraction points those consumers share:

- `BaseChannel._extract_query_from_payload`: command classification, queue priority, and the ACL "first message" record now see the user's own text, for both dict and `AgentRequest` payloads.
- `Runtime.run` slash-command dispatch text.

Behavior contract (pinned by tests):

- Quote + own `/stop` -> classified and dispatched as the command.
- Command only inside the quoted text -> not a command (unchanged).
- Quote-only reply (no new text) -> no command.
- Normal quoted chat -> unchanged; quote-first input still reaches the model, and text without the prefix is extracted byte-identically.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8342

**Security Considerations:** None. Quoted content is not modified; only the text used for routing and classification is stripped. The full quoted message still reaches the model.

## Type of Change

- [ ] New feature

prs.body:
issues #8307 featrue
Implement the on_streaming_start/on_streaming_delta/on_streaming_end hooks
for the QQ channel using the official stream messages API
(POST /v2/users/{user_openid}/stream_messages), gated behind the existing
streaming_enabled flag (QQ_STREAMING_ENABLED env or the channel config),
mirroring the Feishu channel streaming behavior.

- replace-mode slices carry the full accumulated text; the first slice

  normal completed-message path
- any stream API failure falls back to the normal send path; media parts
  are still delivered after a successful finalize

[stream messages API](https://bot.q.qq.com/wiki/develop/api-v2/autogen/api/v2_users_user_openid_stream_messages.post.html),
closing the parity gap with the Feishu channel's streaming experience.

**Related Issue:**​ Fixes #8307

existing QQ access-token flow (`_get_access_token_async`); `streaming_enabled`
is read from the existing channel config / `QQ_STREAMING_ENABLED` env var the

prs.title: perf(skills): install a staged pool skill by renaming it in place (#8013)
prs.body:
## Description

Item 4 of #8013: a pool download copies a skill twice — pool → staging directory, then staging → workspace. When both live on one volume, that second hop is a plain directory rename, so it should not be a full tree copy.

This adds:

- `same_volume(path_a, path_b)` in `skill_system/store.py`. It compares `st_dev` and, for a path that does not exist yet, probes through its nearest existing ancestor — the callers ask this question before creating the target.
- `install_staged_skill_dir(staged_dir, target_dir)`, which renames the already-scanned staged tree into place. It falls back to the existing `copy_skill_dir` when the volumes differ or the filesystem refuses the rename, so behaviour there is unchanged.
- The rollback snapshot gets the same treatment: when the workspace shares a volume with the skill directory, the backup is created beside the workspace instead of in system temp, so restoring it renames it back instead of copying every file again. Cross-volume workspaces keep the old temp-dir backup and the copy-based restore.

Staging itself is untouched: it still carries atomicity and scan isolation, and cross-volume installs still go through both copies.

Two things worth calling out for review:

1. `install_staged_skill_dir` installs the staged tree **as it stands**, so it is only equivalent to `copy_skill_dir` when the stage was produced by it — that copy filters OS artifacts and dereferences symlinks, which a rename cannot do. The pool download builds its stage that way, and the docstring now states the prerequisite.
2. The backup lives inside the workspace directory while a download runs, so it becomes visible to anything that lists the workspace root. It is removed by `_restore_workspace_skill` and by the download route's `finally` in both the success and the failure path.

## Evidence

Targeted tests (`tests/unit/agents/skill_system/test_staged_install.py`, plus the two touched router test modules):

```
182 passed in 11.06s
```

Neighbouring package (`tests/unit/agents/skill_system`, 810 tests):

```
810 passed, 1 warning in 16.14s
```

Pre-commit on every touched file — `check-ast`, `check-yaml`, `check-toml`, `check-json`, `docstring-first`, `fix-encoding-pragma`, `detect-private-key`, `trailing-whitespace`, `add-trailing-comma`, `mypy`, `black`, `flake8`, `pylint`: all Passed.

Covered by the new tests: the volume probe (siblings, and a path that does not exist yet), the rename path installing without calling `copy_skill_dir`, replacement of a pre-existing target that still holds stale files, the fallback when `os.rename` raises, the cross-volume path still copying, cancellation touching nothing, the download actually installing the stage instead of copying it, and the rollback renaming a same-volume backup back.

Not measured: no wall-clock benchmark is included. The change removes a full tree copy, but this PR does not claim a number.

Environment note: this worktree is Windows, so the same-volume path is exercised there; the cross-volume behaviour is covered by monkeypatching `same_volume` to return `False` rather than by a real second volume.

prs.body:
…g control (#8439)

feat(jobs): add thinking_level to JobRuntimeSpec for per-job reasoning control  Close #8439

## Description

Adds per-job reasoning control to cron jobs by introducing `thinking_level` (and optional `thinking_budget`) on `JobRuntimeSpec`.

Today every cron job inherits the agent-level thinking configuration. Users running many pipeline-style jobs (data collection, report generation, format conversion) must create a separate lightweight agent for every job just to turn reasoning off, which is error-prone and hard to maintain. This change lets each job choose:

- `inherit` (default): keep the existing agent/session behavior.
- `off`: disable reasoning for this job.
- `minimal` / `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`: force an effort level for this job.
- `budget`: use an explicit token budget via `thinking_budget`.

The value uses the existing `ThinkingLevel` enum instead of inventing a new `enabled` string. `CronExecutor` passes it through `request_context`, and `AgentBuilder` applies it to a request-scoped copy of `agent_config` after session-level thinking resolution and before model construction. It is never persisted to the shared chat/session.

Backward compatibility:
- New jobs default to `inherit`.
- Existing `jobs.json` files without the new fields load as `inherit`.
- Replacement requests from older clients that omit the fields preserve the stored values.
- `inherit` adds no `request_context` keys and leaves the agent config unchanged.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8439

**Security Considerations:** No authentication, channel, or secret-handling changes. The override is request-scoped and never written to the shared session or persisted agent config, so `share_session=True` cannot leak per-job reasoning settings into another conversation. `runtime` is authoritative in `CronExecutor`; stale or hand-written `cron_thinking_*` keys in the passthrough payload are removed. Invalid hand-written `request_context` overrides are ignored with a warning rather than reaching model construction. `off` remains best-effort, matching existing agent-level behavior: models without a disable control keep their defaults. `thinking_budget` is clamped by the existing model-card resolver.

prs.title: feat(memory): add reranker model center with service test, multi-query precision history and auto-verify
prs.body:
## Description

**What this PR does:** Adds a reranker model center to the reranker settings (Runtime Config → Memory & Retrieval), mirroring the existing Embedding model center, and upgrades the ranking-precision verification from a single binary smoke test into a multi-query, persisted, and optionally scheduled metric.

**Why:** A misconfigured reranker is currently invisible until retrieval quality degrades. The new center surfaces configuration status, current model, service verification (connectivity + latency) and a meaningful ranking-precision figure (`correct/total`, 10-run rolling average, sparkline) so a bad model is visible at a glance and its trend can be tracked across restarts.

The overview shows four slots: configuration status, current model, service verification and ranking precision.

### Changes

- **Reranker model center**: `RerankerModelCenter` overview on the same 4-column grid and status styles as the embedding card; session-scoped `rerankerVerificationStore` keyed by agent + service fingerprint, invalidated when the service config changes or the agent switches.
- **Service verification**: `POST /workspace/reranker/test` sends a real rerank request with sample documents (one clearly relevant plus two distractors) and returns latency, relevance scores mapped back to request order, and whether the expected most-relevant document ranked first. The outbound call runs under a hard `asyncio.wait_for` deadline, upstream HTML error pages are stripped to plain text, and the API key is masked in returned messages.
- **Multi-query precision**: runs a 5-case multi-domain suite (password / checkout / unit conversion / planet / subscription) and reports `total`, `correct_count`, `precision` and per-case `scores`/`correct`, instead of a single boolean.
- **Persistent history**: new `reranker_history.py` appends each verification to `WORKING_DIR/reranker_history.json`, keyed by a service fingerprint; new endpoint `GET /workspace/reranker/history?fingerprint=`.
- **Trend UI**: the precision slot shows `correct/total = NN%`, a 10-run rolling average and a mini SVG sparkline; history survives restarts and refreshes.
- **Scheduled auto-verification**: `RerankerConfig.auto_verify_interval_hours` (0 = off) plus a background sweep task in the app lifespan that probes due services.
- **i18n**: strings for the overview, verification and precision slots across all 7 locales.

prs.title: feat(models): run local Blink with bidirectional candidate scoring
prs.body:
## Description

Allow downloaded Blink models to supply QwenPaw's native Jev decisions for automatic tool review and ReMe context compaction. Blink uses bidirectional prompt attention and candidate-token scoring, so a causal Chat Completions adapter cannot reproduce its trained inference behavior.

- Reuse AgentScope's Jev question/answer mapping and call the managed llama.cpp runtime's native `/v1/systemone` endpoint, with request compression disabled. Read candidate-token probabilities instead of generating probability JSON.
- Preserve the existing Download → Start → default Decision model flow and the separate automatic-review and decision-compaction switches. Starting Blink does not enable either feature or change another provider's chat selection.
- Group the local selector into independently scrollable **Chat models** and **Decision models** sections, with Chinese labels **对话模型** and **决策模型**. Remove the redundant Local Models heading, Blink purpose subtitle, and blue repository links. Keep a single managed runtime.
- Use current `agentscope-ai` Hugging Face repositories for QwenPaw-Flash recommendations; preserve stored IDs for existing downloads and their lifecycle actions.
- Recommend separate `agentscope-ai/Blink-{4,9,27}B-Q8_0` repositories, following QwenPaw-Flash's quantization suffix convention. Preserve the decision role after download, restart, and API activation. Download GGUF/runtime metadata only.
- Launch Blink with a complete-prompt budget, one slot, no prompt cache, and no context shifting. Reject runtimes that report Blink as a text-generation model.
- Include a focused companion llama.cpp patch and build instructions in `docs/local-blink.md`. Ordinary Ollama Chat Completions is not enabled for this contract.

The companion patch targets llama.cpp `f4d8af608a6b39946406f9439edfb6e83ca6a923`. It adds Blink metadata and the checkpoint's exact `flex_twice` layout to the existing native SystemOne implementation. Full-attention layers use bidirectional prompt attention; linear-attention layers keep their native computation. Candidate softmax at temperature 1 is equivalent to renormalizing the candidate token log probabilities. No answer tokens are generated.

**Related work:** Reuses the decision configuration and review integration in #8205 and #8360.

**Security considerations:** Existing approval thresholds, human-confirmation fallback, context recovery, and opt-in switches remain in control. Candidate probabilities are model outputs, not a calibration or safety guarantee.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Refactoring
- [ ] Breaking change

## Components

Local model lifecycle and catalog, provider adapter, Console capability detection, English model guide, and tests. No workflow files are changed.

- Changed Python hooks passed: AST, encoding, private-key scan, whitespace, trailing commas, mypy, Black, flake8, and pylint. Changed Console/docs passed Prettier. The full-repository pre-commit run is not claimed as passing; unrelated formatter/actionlint bootstrap and full CI remain outstanding.
- Companion runtime: 49 server-component tests / 191 assertions passed. The patch applies cleanly to the pinned upstream source.
- Exact C++ versus checkpoint-tokenizer comparison: 33 cases across three tokenizers, 78 prompt rows, including 255 options, ordered scores, Chinese, special tokens, and non-repeated long prompts.
- Complete original 4B, 9B, and 27B checkpoints ran in the Transformers reference. BF16 and Q8 GGUFs were compared on four smoke questions per size. Q8 maximum absolute candidate probability differences were approximately 0.00564 / 0.00286 / 0.00298, with matching top choices.

An earlier startup SIGKILL did not reproduce on retry; its cause remains unestablished.

prs.body:
## Description

After a conversation switches from model M1 to M2, standalone `/compact` still builds its temporary agent from M1's persisted agent defaults. Normal messages resolve the conversation override through `AgentBuilder`, but slash-command dispatch bypasses that builder.

This change shares model-override parsing, conversation selection, and model-owned thinking resolution across the affected paths:

- Scroll and native `/compact` use the conversation/request model and share one resolved configuration snapshot with their system prompt.
- `/history` context limits, chat titles, `/model` display, and model-list active markers follow the same selection. Explicit request overrides are resolved before model validation and thinking lookup.
- Media capability checks and probes read the executing model, including its active fallback. The model context is isolated per task and reset before stream events are yielded, including cancellation and cross-task stream closure.
- Token-recording wrappers expose the same `model_key` identity as retry wrappers, including Hub models. Invalid override values are sanitized before logging.
- Spawned subagents resolve parent conversation settings using the carried parent owner and channel, including when submitted through Console. Explicit subagent models retain their own model-specific thinking preference; ordinary requests keep their own conversation identity.
- `/model` switching/resetting continues to update agent defaults and explains when a conversation override remains active.
- English and Chinese command, Console, and context-management documentation describe model scope, precedence, compaction, titles, and media capabilities.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8464

**Security Considerations:** Compaction and title generation now honor the selected conversation/request provider instead of silently using the agent-default provider. Conversation settings do not mutate agent defaults, and media model context is isolated across concurrent requests.

prs.title: fix(memory): stop leaking auto-memory-recall payload to channels
prs.body:
## Description

The auto-memory-recall pipeline injected a synthetic `memory_search` tool interaction (`ToolCallBlock` + `ToolResultBlock`) into the LLM context. Two problems followed from that:

- models that observe a tool interaction in their own context tend to imitate it out loud in the next user-facing reply ("I'll check memory for relevant context…"), which leaks the internal recall flow to the user and to outbound channels;
- the payload had to be kept off the wire with a dedicated `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_BLOCK_HIDDEN_KEY` metadata flag plus a channel-renderer guard and a console tool-card guard — three cooperating layers, none of which was actually connected (see *Root cause*).

This PR carries the recall payload in a single `HintBlock` instead. Every provider formatter (OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / DashScope / Ollama) turns a hint into a separate `role="user"` message, so the request never ends with an assistant turn; and the console / PawApp history converter skips hint blocks entirely, so the payload never reaches a transcript. Because the block type already covers both concerns, the hidden flag and the two guards are gone. The middleware recognises the message through the pre-existing `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_BLOCK_IDS_KEY`, which the block-cleanup path already uses, so the transient injection and cleanup behaviour are unchanged.

The branch is rebased onto the latest `main`.

## Root cause

Two independent issues, both reproduced against the real converter and the real formatters before the change:

1. **Assistant prefill.** With the payload in a `TextBlock`, the Anthropic formatter emitted the recall as an assistant turn, so the request ended with `role="assistant"`. Anthropic reads a trailing assistant turn as a prefill continuation, which Claude 4.6+ rejects.
2. **The hiding logic was not connected.** `agentscope_msg_to_message()` nests the original metadata under `message.metadata["metadata"]`, while the renderer guard only checked the top level, so `_is_auto_memory_recall_message()` never fired and the recall text was rendered to the channel as an ordinary assistant message. The console guard did not help either: it lived on the tool-card path, which the payload no longer used, and the tool-card adapter did not forward the metadata the guard checked.

## Evidence

The two issues above were reproduced against the real converter and the real provider formatters before the change, and the same paths were re-checked after it. The payload never appears in an outbound message, and the model request never ends with an assistant turn.

### Before / after, against the real converter and formatters

Request tail, Anthropic:

```
before: [{"role": "user",     "content": [...]},
         {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "<auto_memory_recall>..."}]}]   # assistant tail -> prefill
after:  [{"role": "user",     "content": [...]},
         {"role": "user",     "content": [{"text": "<auto_memory_recall>..."}]}]   # no assistant turn
```

History conversion:

```
before: agentscope_msg_to_message([recall]) -> 1 message containing the payload
after:  agentscope_msg_to_message([recall]) -> 0 messages
```

The renderer guard before the change:

```
message.metadata = {"original_id": ..., "original_name": "memory_search",
                    "metadata": {"auto_memory_search_hidden": true, ...}, ...}
                                   ^ nested here
guard checks:    message.metadata.get("auto_memory_search_hidden")   # top level -> misses
=> rendered parts: 1  (full recall payload sent to the channel)
```

### Formatter coverage

The request ends with a `user` turn and contains no `assistant` turn for: Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini, DashScope, Ollama (and DeepSeek / MiniMax, which share the OpenAI base formatter).

### Local verification evidence

- `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_base_memory_manager.py` + `tests/unit/agents/test_memory_middleware.py` + `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` + `tests/unit/app/chats/test_utils.py`: **132 passed**
- `black --line-length=79`, `flake8 --extend-ignore=E203`, `pylint` (repository pre-commit arguments): clean, **10.00/10**

### Regression tests added

`tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` — four test functions, nine execution cases:

- `test_final_request_carries_the_recall_as_a_user_turn` (parametrized over Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini, DashScope and Ollama): the request ends with a `user` turn carrying the recall, and contains no `assistant` turn;
- `test_recall_is_injected_and_reused_from_the_cache`: the recall is injected right after the user turn without touching the agent context, and the same turn then reuses the serialized cache instead of searching again — the reloaded message still carries its hint block and block id;
- `test_recall_is_omitted_from_the_converted_transcript`: the real conversion path (`agentscope_msg_to_message`) drops the recall from a mixed transcript while the user message and the normal reply survive;
- `test_next_user_turn_replaces_the_cached_recall`: a new user turn replaces the cached recall instead of reusing it.

## Changes

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/base_memory_manager.py` | carry the recall payload in a `HintBlock` instead of a text/thinking/tool_call/tool_result quartet |
| `src/qwenpaw/agents/middlewares.py` | `_is_auto_memory_recall_msg` helper; memory-extraction filter accepts the recall message |
| `src/qwenpaw/constant.py` | remove the now unused `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_TEXT` / `_THINKING_PREFIX` |
| `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` | new regression tests (final request, conversion path, middleware injection path) |

4 files, +334 / -62 lines. No new metadata flag and no renderer or frontend guard: the block type handles both, so the payload cannot reach a transcript even if a future channel renders messages directly.

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass

prs.title: fix(console): persist market install provenance so 'Update All' covers third-party plugins (#8176)
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8176.

When a plugin is installed from the AgentScope plugin market, the install URL is discarded after download. The console later re-derives the market identity by string-matching the local `author` field against the market `owner`/`developer` logins. Real plugin.json `author` strings frequently differ from the market owner login (the issue's reporter has owner `onesix` but author `onesixth`), so third-party plugins never match, never enter the `updates` map, and the `Update All` button silently skips them.

Changes:

- Stamp a small `.qwenpaw-market.json` marker with the scoped market id (e.g. `@onesix/qwenpaw-plugin-tool-wait_agent_task`) into the freshly extracted plugin tree before the loader copies it into the install directory. The marker rides through install, gets overwritten on update, and is removed with the plugin on uninstall.
- Expose `market_id` on every entry in `GET /api/plugins`, in both the loader path and the pre-loader disk-scan fallback.
- `marketPluginMatches` treats a recorded `market_id` as authoritative; the existing author heuristic is the fallback for legacy installs that have no provenance yet.

Non-market install sources (local paths, third-party hosts, uploads) are untouched — the marker is only written for official-market archive URLs that match `{host}/plugins/{owner}/{name}/archive/zip/{ref}`.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8176

**Security Considerations:** None. The marker is derived from the install URL after the hostname is verified to match the official market; no user-supplied path or query is persisted. Local-path and third-party-host installs do not write the marker.

prs.title: fix(memory): inject automatic recall as reference context
prs.body:
## Description

Automatic memory recall was represented as an assistant-authored thinking/tool-call/tool-result sequence. Models could imitate that synthetic trajectory and call `memory_search` again in the same turn.

This change represents automatic recall as transient, untrusted system reference context instead. When a request already has a system message, the evidence is merged into a copy of that leading message so provider message-order requirements remain valid. Explicit model-initiated `memory_search` calls are unchanged.

The original user query is not copied into the system evidence, avoiding both duplicated context and elevation of untrusted user instructions.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8361

**Security Considerations:** Retrieved memory is explicitly labeled as untrusted reference data. The wrapper tells the model not to follow instructions found in the retrieved content, and raw user query text is never promoted into the system evidence.

## What Problem This Solves

With Automatic Memory Search enabled, the injected context looked like a tool call the assistant had just made. Some models continued that synthetic trajectory by repeatedly calling `memory_search`; after the duplicate-call guard stopped the loop, they could still fail to produce a usable text response. The model now receives the retrieved content without a tool-call example to imitate.

prs.title: fix(desktop): handle Windows installer preparation failures
prs.body:
## Description

Fix two locally reproduced causes of Windows installer preparation failure and make preparation errors visible:

- Keep the original `powershell.exe` invocation first. Only when nsExec reports `error`, retry through `$SYSDIR\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`. Share this behavior across preparation, launcher restoration, and CLI PATH updates. Numeric script exit codes do not trigger a retry. This fixes missing-PATH failures while preserving working custom lookups even if the system executable is missing or cannot start.
- Check for empty native-host launcher/backup contents before calling `Contains()` or `ToLowerInvariant()`. `Get-Content -Raw` returns no content for empty files, causing preparation or restoration to throw.
- Replace the blanket file-contention message with a preparation-failure message, showing the return result and existing script output. Explicitly identify failures to start Windows PowerShell. Update the six existing installer translations.

Existing process selection, launcher restoration, and cancellation behavior are preserved.

**Related Issue:** User-reported Windows desktop installation failure; the exact trigger on the reporter's machine remains unconfirmed.

**Security Considerations:** Uses NSIS's system-directory resolution with the existing arguments and architecture behavior. Process termination scope is unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, deleting a Creator project fails with `503 STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR` / `WinError 5` once that project's `creator.log` has been opened. `delete_project` renamed the project directory via `atomic_replace_path` / `os.replace` **before** releasing the per-project log handler (`close_creator_project_logging`) and the poller. prs.title: feat(skills): make skill-pool downloads cancellable jobs (#8126)
prs.body:
## Description

Downloading a skill from the skill pool is currently a blocking request:
`POST /skills/pool/download` only answers when the whole install finished.
For a large pool, or a slow connection, that can take minutes with no way to
stop it from the Console, and the server keeps installing even after the user
walks away.

This PR turns the download into a cancellable job, following the design note
that was reviewed and approved on the tracking issue
(https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8126#issuecomment-6210083224 —
"Thanks for the plan. (a) is good.").

What it does:

- Adds `POST /skills/pool/downloads`, which returns `202` with an opaque job id
  instead of blocking.
- Adds `GET /skills/pool/downloads/{job_id}` and
  `DELETE /skills/pool/downloads/{job_id}`. Job states are `running`,
  `cancelling`, `completed`, `failed` and `cancelled`.
- Leaves the existing blocking endpoint untouched, so current callers keep
  working.
- Moves the per-workspace lock from the request handler to the job, so the lock
  is released at a safe point when a job is cancelled instead of being held for
  the lifetime of an HTTP request.
- Reuses the existing failure rollback for cancellation: a cancelled job never
  leaves a partially installed skill behind, and never deletes the skill that
  was already installed, nor its settings.
- Drives the Console broadcast preview through the job, shows `Cancelling`
  until cleanup has finished, keeps its own polling interval with no fixed
  timeout, and never exposes the job id in the UI. A completed install still
  wins over a concurrent cancel.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8126

**Security Considerations:** No new authentication or authorization surface.
The endpoint keeps the existing workspace/session checks, and job ids are
generated server-side, opaque, and not surfaced to the user.

prs.title: fix(creator): keep review decisions publishable on long Windows paths
prs.body:
## Description

On Windows with a long runtime data root, deciding any Review in the `qwenpaw-creator` plugin fails permanently, and the first failed attempt makes it unrecoverable (report: #8163).

Two defects combine:

1. **The journal publish needs a longer path than the journal itself.** `runtime_files/atomic_store.py` staged every write as `.<name>.<8 random>.tmp`, about 14 characters longer than the target record. With Windows long paths disabled, a `journal.json` whose final path fits under the legacy `MAX_PATH` limit still failed in `mkstemp` (259 -> 273 characters) and left the `decision-<hash>` directory created just before it behind, empty.
2. **That empty leftover then blocks every retry.** `project_files/review.py::_assert_no_other_active_decision` read each other `decision-*` directory with `read()` instead of `read_or_none()`, so a directory without a `journal.json` raised `ReviewDecisionConflict` ("Review decision journal set is inconsistent"). Each attempt uses a new `decisionId`, so the stale directory always counted as "another" decision and the API returned a retryable 409 that could never succeed.

The fix:

- Stage the temp file with a short, fixed 12-character name (`.tmp` plus the 8-character random suffix) so the decision journal's staged path no longer exceeds its target (273 -> 259 characters).
- Treat a `decision-*` directory with no `journal.json` as the leftover of an unpublished attempt: log and skip it instead of failing. A journal that exists but cannot be read still fails closed, and a non-finalized active journal still blocks a concurrent decision.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8163

**Security Considerations:** None. This is local storage path-length handling; no auth, config or network surface is touched.

prs.title: fix(memory): require non-empty api_key for ReMe reranker enablement (#8276)
prs.body:
## Description

Resolves two related issues in `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_reranker.py`:

1. **Enablement requires non-empty credential:** `load_reranker_config()` previously evaluated enablement from `config.enabled and config.model_name` alone. Since `RerankerConfig.api_key` defaults to `""`, a configuration without an API key was accepted as enabled, causing memory searches to over-fetch `max_results * candidate_multiplier` candidates for a rerank call that cannot succeed. This aligns the reranker enablement rule with the existing embedding path (`src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_config.py:717`), requiring `bool(config.api_key and config.api_key.strip())`.

2. **Pre-flight guard for missing API key:** `call_reranker_api()` previously checked `base_url` but not `api_key`. An empty or whitespace-only API key resulted in an invalid `Authorization: Bearer ` header, which failed serialization in HTTP transport and was caught as an opaque `[rerank] unexpected error`. A pre-flight check now logs `[rerank] api_key not configured` and returns `None` early, matching the `base_url` error reporting pattern.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8276

**Security Considerations:** None. The API key is validated for presence/non-emptiness and is never logged.

prs.title: feat(memory): support PowerContext prepared context and Artifact APIs
prs.body:
## Description

Update the optional PowerContext memory backend for PowerContext v1.4.1 and expose its prepared-context and Artifact APIs. QwenPaw can reuse profiles, topic memories, atomic memories, and experiences when preparing a turn, and explicitly read or write supported Artifact families.

- Use Atomic Memory writes and preserve exact artifact/source references on recall. Resolve a stable Scope for each installation and agent.
- Recover startup Scope binding on the same manager after transport or HTTP 5xx failures, using exponential delays from 1 to 30 seconds. A temporary 503 no longer leaves the manager permanently disabled. Keep tools and automatic memory disabled until binding succeeds; report permanent errors explicitly and cancel retries on shutdown. Recovery applies to future turns without backfilling skipped turns.
- Make `prepare` the default recall mode, with ordered Profile, Topic Memory, Memory, and Experience sections and a UTF-8 byte budget. Keep explicit `memory` mode for older servers.
- Register `prepare_context` and seven Artifact tools alongside `memory_search` and `memory_remember`: schema discovery, search, list, get, history, create, and conditional replacement. Cover atomic memory, topic memory, experience, skill, profile, prompt, and handoff; search is available for the four searchable families.
- Preserve returned records, pagination cursors, exact revisions, and ETags. Update the bilingual configuration UI and documentation.
- Run the non-integration plugin suite in the existing Python 3.11/3.13 CI unit-test matrix, including plugin-only changes in workflow path filters.

The plugin version is **1.2.0**; the recommended PowerContext server version for new databases is **1.4.1**. These are independent version numbers. Existing users of the PowerContext v0.2 server must explicitly select `memory` mode; prepared context and Artifact tools require their corresponding server endpoints.

**Database compatibility:** The [PowerContext 1.4.1 release notes](https://github.com/oceanbase/powercontext/releases/tag/powercontext-v1.4.1) state that upgrade acceptance was skipped: this release supports new databases only, and upgrades of existing databases are unsupported. The quick-start example uses a separate `POWERCONTEXT_HOME`. This PR validates a fresh SQLite database and does not upgrade the deployed demo.

**Related Issue:** Follow-up to #7080.

**Security Considerations:** Retrieved context remains explicitly marked as untrusted historical data. Network read/write tools retain host governance metadata, and Artifact replacements require the ETag returned by the read path. Deployment credentials, private infrastructure configuration, and acceptance logs are not included.

## Type of Change

prs.title: fix(mail): do not append domain when account name is already a full address
prs.body:
## Description

The mail monitor and the QwenPawMail driver env built the IMAP/SMTP login as `f"{credential.name}@{credential.domain}"`. Mailboxes configured with the full address in `name` (for example `name="user@qq.com"`, `domain="qq.com"`) therefore logged in as `user@qq.com@qq.com`, and the provider rejected it with `[AUTHENTICATIONFAILED]` even though the auth code was valid (#8425).

This PR adds `mail_login_address(name, domain)` in `app/mail/driver_config.py`:

- if `name` already contains `@`, it is used as-is;
- otherwise the login is `name@domain`, as before.

It is used for `QWENPAWMAIL_EMAIL` in `build_qwenpawmail_env()` and for `MailMonitorService.email_address`, so both login paths agree. Configs that store only the local part keep the exact same behaviour.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8425

**Security Considerations:** No change to how credentials are stored or sent. Only the login name string is built differently when `name` is already a full address.

prs.title: fix(providers): honor declared thinking disable wire
prs.body:
## Description

The internal `disable_thinking=True` flag previously injected both known OpenAI-compatible disable shapes into every request. Strict endpoints can understand one shape while rejecting the other, causing compaction summaries and governance generalization to fail before generation.

This change resolves the neutral flag through each model's declared `ThinkingControl` mapping. It also prevents the internal `disable_thinking` marker from reaching the OpenAI SDK, including the configured `gpt-5.2` path identified in review. OpenAI, OpenRouter, and Ollama models now receive their declared disable wire parameters; unknown controls add no guessed parameter.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8417

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This overlaps with #8358 in thinking-control selection. #8358 makes declared native controls authoritative; combined with this PR, `gpt-5.2` maps thinking-off to `reasoning_effort="none"`. This PR independently enforces the transport boundary so the neutral `disable_thinking` marker can never reach `client.chat.completions.create()`.

issues.title: [Bug]: Tool enable/disable buttons auto-save while at the same time enabling save button

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Affected component

web dashboard

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

In config/tools if you enable or disable a tool using the upper right toggle button, the ui currently autosaves the setting. However, at the same time the ui state becomes dirty and the save button buttom right becomes enabled, even though the state is already saved. An unfortunate further side effect is, the internal representation of the config state is not toggled by the enable/disable button, it only saves the changed state. The result is that if you use the save button, the untoggled state is saved back to config, reversing the toggle you just made.

### Expected behavior

I would expect that all widgets either autosave or requires using the save button to save the state. Having some buttons auto save and others require manual saving is inconsistent and is a trap to inconsistent behaviour such as what is seen here.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
You are in the web dashboard.

1. Click the config sprocket icon in the sidebar.
```

issues.title: [Feature]: Keep non-durable consolidation updates out of Core with a durability label and a user quote
issues.body:
### Summary

An opt-in `memory.consolidation_evidence_gate`: the consolidation model labels each `memory_update` durable or transient and quotes the user's own words for it, and only durable updates backed by a matching quote are written to Core; everything else is kept in Daily.

### Problem statement

`consolidate_turn` writes every non-empty `memory_update` to Core (subject only to the policy gate and the opt-in `dedup_on_write`), and Core is permanent, undecayed at recall and has the highest base importance (details in #11657). The model is asked for "new facts, preferences, decisions, or commitments worth remembering long-term", but nothing checks that an update is durable or that the user said it.

mov-xound-glitch's numbers in #11657 show what that does on a real install: 244 auto-extracted Core rows (of 269 in Core) in seven weeks, a fair share of them task state such as "a test email is still pending because of a provider error".

To measure it, I ran a small local eval: 65 made-up turns (three of them long ones built around the 4000-byte input cut): 35 that state a durable fact, 28 that don't, and two scored separately. Each was run three times through `consolidate_turn`. With today's prompt, more than half of the non-durable turns were written to Core, for example:

- transient state: "I'm at the store right now", "my build is failing right now", "I'm really tired today", "on vacation this week";
- the assistant's guesses or suggestions, stored as facts about the user: "Since you like jazz, …", "You should learn Rust";
- one-off requests and refusals: "Don't use bullet points in this one, I'm pasting it into a letter", "Not interested in that recipe";
- sarcasm, questions and tentative plans: "Oh yeah, I just love Mondays", "Do you think I should switch to vim?", "I might move to Lisbon next year, not sure yet".

### Proposed solution

Behind a new `memory.consolidation_evidence_gate` (default off), only when the plain consolidation prompt is used:

1. The consolidation prompt also asks for `durability` ("durable" if the update will still be true and useful weeks from now; "transient" for current state, today's plans, one-off requests or a single refusal) and `evidence`, the exact clause of the user's message that states the update. It tells the model not to store the assistant's claims, guesses or suggestions as facts about the user, and to write the update in the third person ("User …") in the language of the user's sentence.
2. The update goes to Core only if it is labelled durable and a quote passes three checks: it appears word for word in the part of the user's message the model was sent, ignoring case, punctuation and lines quoted with `>`; it has at least 2 words and 8 letters unless it is the whole message; and it shares a content word with the update, so a real quote is harder to attach to an unrelated update.
3. Anything else is stored in Daily, so it is kept for the history but not treated as a lasting fact.
4. The labels are read separately from `ConsolidationResult` and leniently, so an odd value never breaks parsing, and with the switch off the prompt, parsing and writes are unchanged.
5. Config load rejects the switch together with `memory.types.enabled` or `memory.consolidation_extract_facts`, because the typed prompt has no durability or evidence fields; per-fact labels for typed facts would be a follow-up.

The idea of a per-item `durability` field is mov-xound-glitch's, from #11657.

Results from the local eval (three runs per case; today's prompt is unchanged master from an earlier run of the same cases; one gated run was dropped after a provider timeout):

| | Today's prompt | With the gate |
|---|---|---|
| Durable-fact turns with a Core write | 105 of 105 (100%) | 103 of 105 (98%) |
| Non-durable turns written to Core | 47 of 84 (56%) | 2 of 83 (2%) |
| Replies that failed to parse | 1 | 0 |

Notes on the results:

- Only whether a Core write happened is scored, not whether it states the fact correctly.
- All of the improvement comes from the new prompt: the model labelled non-durable turns transient or returned no update, and the quote check did not hold back any non-durable turn.
- The quote check held back 3 replies the model had labelled durable, and all 3 were real facts: "Call me Sam" twice (the name case added after the comparison run, not in the table; a 3-letter name is never a shared content word) and a German turn once (the model wrote that update in English). In these cases it caught nothing that should have been kept out, so its value as a backstop is not measured here.
- The two leaks were sarcasm ("Oh yeah, I just love Mondays") and a durable-labelled "User has a sister who occasionally stays with them; currently her sister is visiting until Sunday, …" from "My sister is staying with us until Sunday, so plan dinners for three." The two missed facts were "Any tips for my sourdough?" and the German turn above.
- The gated prompt was revised twice after earlier runs on these same cases, so these are in-sample numbers from one model; a held-out set and other models are not tested.
- The cases are made up; the model was Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (IQ4_NL GGUF) through llama.cpp's OpenAI-compatible server at temperature 0.7.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Not a security boundary. Consolidation can't tell the user's own words from text a channel adds to the message: link previews (`[Link: …]`), Slack thread context (including the bot's own replies), Matrix thread roots and forwarded text all reach the quote check as if the user wrote them. A trustworthy version needs channels to pass the user's own text separately from the context they add. A turn-origin signal like the one in PR #10007 would only cover turns no person authored.
- Not per-fact gating for `consolidation_extract_facts` or typed memory.
- No change to the default behaviour.

### Alternatives considered

- A per-install target category (#11657). Simpler, but it moves durable facts out of Core along with the noise; the two can coexist, with the gate deciding per update and the category deciding where non-durable updates go.
- Schema-validated consolidation (#6998). Complementary: it makes the reply's shape reliable, and the durability and evidence fields would fit its schema.
- The existing `memory.dedup_on_write` (off by default). It catches near-identical text but not task state or assistant claims.

### Acceptance criteria

- The switch is off by default and, when off, consolidation behaves exactly as today.
- With the switch on, a non-empty `memory_update` reaches Core only when labelled durable and backed by a matching quote; otherwise it is stored in Daily.
- The switch is rejected at config load together with typed memory.
- Unit tests cover the quote rules and the routing.

### Architecture impact

`crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/consolidation.rs` (prompt, label parsing, routing) and `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs` (the switch and its validation). One new config key; no trait or storage change.

### Risk and rollback

Off by default; turning it off restores today's behaviour. Known limits if it is turned on:

- One matching quote clears the whole update, so a detail the assistant added can ride along with a real fact. In the eval, a request to set up a nightly backup was stored with the assistant's "2am" in all three runs, and "Yes, let's do that plan" was stored as a commitment in all three runs, twice with the assistant's "3-day split", although the prompt says agreeing with the assistant is not stating.
- One shared content word is enough to tie a quote to an update.
- Content words need 4 or more letters, so a short name ("Sam") or word ("cat") can never be the shared word, and the update is held back.
- An update written in a different language from the user's sentence often shares no content word with it and is then held back, even when the model was asked to keep the language.
- Updates held back are stored in Daily as plain text, and Daily entries are recalled into later prompts.
- Facts the user states about other people (for example a friend's allergy) are stored like any other fact.
- The content-word check and the stopword list work best for English and other space-separated languages.

### Expected routing

Needs maintainer design assessment

### Next decision surface

This issue: whether per-update durability with a quote check is a shape maintainers want, and how it should sequence with #11657, #6998 and #10007, under the persistent-memory tracker #8891. Related: #10755 and the closed RFC #9048.

I have this working locally behind the switch, with unit tests, an eval harness and the eval cases, and can open a PR if maintainers want this shape.

### Breaking change?

No

- [x] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [x] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

issues.body:
## Problem

Memory consolidation currently asks the model for JSON in a prompt, parses the text with `serde_json`, and falls back to a raw-turn summary when parsing fails.

That path is fragile across providers and models. Output may contain Markdown fences, extra prose, missing fields, or invalid field types. Consolidation must not silently treat malformed model output as schema-valid memory.

The original RFC generalized this problem into a reusable Schema-Guided Reasoning subsystem. ZeroClaw currently has one concrete consumer, so the accepted decision should prove the behavior inside memory consolidation before introducing a public cross-runtime abstraction.

## Decision

### Add schema-validated extraction to memory consolidation

Implement the first slice inside the existing `zeroclaw-memory` consolidation boundary.

The consolidation path requests a flat structured result matching the existing history-entry, memory-update, fact, trend, and kind semantics. It validates candidate output against a real JSON Schema before any extracted value is stored.

One canonical flat JSON Schema, using an explicitly pinned dialect, is the runtime-validation authority and the source for the internal tool definition. Provider-compatible tool schemas must be mechanically derived from that canonical schema rather than maintained as separate handwritten contracts. A native provider path may use only a derived projection it demonstrably accepts; every returned candidate is still validated against the complete canonical schema before decoding. `ConsolidationResult` is decoded only after that schema accepts the candidate, and contract fixtures must fail if the Rust type, derived tool schema, or validator behavior drifts. The schema sets `additionalProperties: false`, requires a nonblank `history_entry`, limits `facts` to at most five nonblank strings, restricts `kind` to `preference`, `fact`, `decision`, `entity`, or `null`, and requires `kind` to be `null` when `memory_update` is `null`. It also declares the exact numeric maximum length for every string field; the implementation PR must expose those limits for review. Excess facts, unknown kinds, blank required values, and over-limit strings are validation failures rather than values silently truncated, discarded, or coerced before storage.

This work reuses the existing `ModelProvider`, `ProviderDispatch`, tool payload, prompt-guided, and parsing machinery. It does not add another agent loop, provider stack, public runtime service, or new crate.

### Use a bounded provider ladder

The memory-specific extraction path uses this order:

1. Select one extraction mode for the request. Use native tool calling only where the selected provider path demonstrably supports both forcing the one extraction tool and accepting its derived tool schema; otherwise use the existing prompt-guided tool path.
2. Use one flat internal extraction tool for the complete consolidation result. The tool is a structured-output envelope and is never executed as an ordinary agent action.
3. Require exactly one unambiguous candidate. In native mode, one forced extraction-tool call supplies its arguments as the candidate; zero or multiple extraction calls are invalid. In prompt-guided mode, preserve fenced, prefixed, or plain JSON extraction only when it yields exactly one object candidate; zero or multiple candidate objects are invalid. Validate the single candidate against the complete canonical schema.
4. Allow at most two model calls total: the initial extraction and one repair retry containing bounded schema feedback. Do not cascade from native to prompt-guided to text modes with a separate retry budget for each.
5. Retry feedback identifies only bounded schema keywords and field paths. It does not echo candidate values into logs or diagnostics.
6. On provider failure, missing output, second validation failure, or retry exhaustion, use the existing safe consolidation fallback rather than storing a partial candidate or failing the whole user turn.

Unsupported force behavior must be explicit. If `TOOL_CHOICE_OVERRIDE` is not wired and tested for a provider path, the implementation must not claim that provider supports forced native extraction.

No malformed candidate may be stored merely because it parsed as JSON.

### Keep the schema flat

The first schema uses flat scalar and short-array fields. It avoids nested reasoning objects and broad routing unions that are difficult for smaller or prompt-guided models to satisfy.

The first slice uses one flat extraction tool so history, memory update, kind, facts, and trend form one candidate with one validation and retry outcome. Multiple extraction tools remain deferred because they would require partial-result, duplicate-call, ordering, and aggregation semantics that this consumer does not need.

### Defer the generic abstraction

This revision does not ratify a public `structured_call` API or an SGR subsystem.

After a second concrete consumer needs the same forcing, validation, retry, and fallback semantics, extract the shared behavior at the narrowest dependency boundary supported by both consumers. That follow-up must identify the owning crate, public API, error contract, provider support matrix, and relationship to model capability metadata.

## Current implementation state

Current `master` still uses prompt-constrained JSON in `zeroclaw-memory::consolidation` and falls back through `parse_consolidation_response` when deserialization fails.

The repository already has native and prompt-guided tool paths, lenient tool-call parsing, provider dispatch, and a task-local `TOOL_CHOICE_OVERRIDE`, but forcing is not uniformly wired across providers. The first implementation must verify each claimed provider path and preserve the existing fallback behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- Memory consolidation validates extracted model output against a real JSON Schema before storing it.
- The schema remains flat and preserves the existing consolidation result semantics.
- One canonical JSON Schema uses a pinned dialect, owns runtime validation, and mechanically derives any provider-compatible tool-schema projection; contract fixtures detect drift with the Rust result type.
- Extraction accepts exactly one unambiguous candidate and treats zero or multiple native calls or JSON objects as validation failures.
- The implementation PR exposes the schema's exact numeric string limits for review.
- The first slice uses one non-executed internal extraction tool and has no partial multi-tool aggregation state.
- The extraction path makes at most two model calls total and does not multiply retries across fallback modes.
- Schema validation rejects unknown fields, unknown kinds, blank required values, more than five facts, and over-limit strings rather than silently coercing or truncating them.
- Retry diagnostics contain bounded schema keywords and field paths without candidate values.
- Native tool forcing is used only on provider paths where it is wired and tested.
- Prompt-guided extraction remains available when native tools are unavailable.
- Validation errors drive a bounded retry with concrete feedback.
- Retry exhaustion uses the existing safe consolidation fallback rather than storing malformed structure or failing the whole user turn.
- The implementation stays inside the existing memory/provider boundaries and does not create a second agent loop or provider stack.
- No public generic `structured_call` or SGR subsystem is added in this slice.
- Tests cover native-tool success, prompt-guided fallback, fenced or prefixed JSON, zero and duplicate candidates, schema mismatch, bounded retry, retry exhaustion, unsupported forcing or tool-schema projection, and safe fallback.

## Non-goals

- Adding a public cross-runtime structured-output API.
- Creating an SGR crate, framework, or configuration block.
- Shipping cascade, routing, or cycle pattern helpers.
- Adding provider-native constrained-decoding request fields such as `response_format`, `responseSchema`, or Ollama `format`.
- Activating SOP `StepSchema`.
- Adding token-level grammar decoding.
- Claiming every provider or model can force native tools.
- Changing memory storage, retention, deduplication, conflict resolution, or policy gates.

## Compatibility and rollback

The structured extraction path preserves the existing consolidation fallback. Validation or provider-forcing failure must not make an otherwise successful user turn fail.

Rollback restores the current prompt-and-parse extraction path. No persisted schema or data migration is required.

## Durable follow-through and revisit surface

The first implementation should update memory-consolidation and provider/tool behavior documentation.

Revisit the generic abstraction only when a second concrete consumer exists. That proposal must identify the common semantics and owning dependency boundary rather than generalizing from memory alone.

## Data hygiene checks

- [x] I removed personal or sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [x] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

issues.body:
### Problem

On a single `zeroclaw daemon` process, every configured `stdio`-transport MCP server gets connected (and, for stdio, spawned as a child process) **three times on every boot**, not once — even though nothing later re-triggers it, and real inbound messages don't cause additional reconnects.

Traced this on a host running multiple `zeroclaw` instances that each configure the same local stdio MCP servers. Log evidence for one boot: each of 3 configured servers logged `MCP server \`<name>\` connected` exactly 3 times, all within ~2 seconds of `ZeroClaw daemon started`. No further reconnect events appear later — a real inbound channel message processed ~16s later goes straight to `starting LLM call` with no additional `Initializing MCP client` line, so the cost is a fixed one-time boot cost that scales with server count, not a leak or a per-message cost.

Root cause: `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/scoped.rs:89-98` documents the intended contract on `ScopedAssembly.mcp_registry` — a caller-supplied `Arc<McpRegistry>` **must** be reused; `None` "preserves the legacy per-call connect path (CLI / one-shot / process_message), which is correct for callers that have no cross-turn reuse contract." The fallback logs `"Initializing MCP client - {} server(s) granted via mcp_bundles"` (`scoped.rs:297`) and calls `McpRegistry::connect_all` fresh (`scoped.rs:311`), guarded by the comment at `scoped.rs:302-306` that names the heartbeat worker as the one caller that already does this correctly.

That's the catch: **only the heartbeat worker does it correctly.** `connect_heartbeat_mcp_registry` builds one registry per worker and reuses it for the worker's lifetime — proven by the existing regression test `heartbeat_worker_reuses_shared_mcp_registry_across_n_ticks` (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/daemon/mod.rs:4385`). But within the *same daemon process*, at least two other boot-time consumers never pass a shared registry into `scoped.rs`'s assembly and each independently fall through to the legacy per-call path: the gateway's dashboard-agent channel-binding warm-up, and the channels orchestrator's own startup registry build. Each of those, plus the heartbeat worker's own connect, account for the 3× we measured — three independent, non-communicating registries for the lifetime of one process.

This is easy to miss on a lightweight setup (an HTTP-transport MCP server just eats a few extra cheap reconnects), but it's very visible once a `stdio` MCP server does real work on startup — e.g. a server that performs a live OAuth/session handshake against a third-party API. There, "3× per boot" means 3× the login/session-refresh cost and 3× the process-spawn overhead, every single restart, for zero functional benefit.

### Proposal

Extend the registry-sharing mechanism that `AgentRunOverrides::mcp_registry` already gives the heartbeat worker to the other boot-time consumers in the same process — the gateway's dashboard-agent assembly and the channels orchestrator's own startup assembly — so a single daemon process builds each agent's MCP registry once at boot and threads it through every internal consumer that needs one, instead of each consumer independently falling back to `scoped.rs`'s legacy per-call path.

This is additive to an existing, already-tested mechanism (`ScopedAssembly.mcp_registry` / `overrides_mcp_registry`), not a new one — the shape of the fix already exists and is proven correct for one caller.

### Design sketch

Affected surfaces:
- `crates/zeroclaw-gateway` — wherever it registers the dashboard-agent channel bindings and assembles its own tool registry.
- `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs` — its own boot-time registry construction, prior to activating channel bindings.
- `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/scoped.rs` — no change needed to the contract itself; `mcp_registry`/`overrides_mcp_registry` already does the right thing when populated.

Proposed phases:
1. Have the daemon boot sequence (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/daemon/mod.rs`, where the supervised `gateway`/`channels`/`heartbeat` components are spawned) construct one `Arc<McpRegistry>` per granted-agent (reusing `Config::mcp_servers_for_agent`, matching what `connect_heartbeat_mcp_registry` already does), before spawning gateway/channels.
2. Pass it into both the gateway's and channels' own startup paths the same way `AgentRunOverrides::mcp_registry` already reaches the heartbeat worker.
3. Regression test mirroring `heartbeat_worker_reuses_shared_mcp_registry_across_n_ticks`, but asserting a single boot spawns each configured stdio server's child process exactly once across gateway + channels + heartbeat combined.

I haven't opened a PR for this — happy to attempt one, but wanted to raise it as an RFC first per the architecture map's guidance, since it crosses `zeroclaw-gateway`, `zeroclaw-channels`, and `zeroclaw-runtime`.

### Alternatives considered

- **Do nothing, document the workaround instead**: for a `stdio` MCP server, wrap it as a persistent server behind an HTTP transport (`transport = "http"` pointing at a long-lived process) instead of letting the daemon spawn it. This sidesteps the cost (an HTTP reconnect is cheap even done 3×) without touching daemon internals, and it's what we did locally. It doesn't fix the underlying gap for anyone still using `stdio` transport, though, and doesn't help servers that only support stdio.
- **Make `McpRegistry::connect_all` itself dedupe/cache globally** (e.g. a process-wide cache keyed by server config) instead of threading a registry through each caller explicitly. Simpler call sites, but a global cache is a bigger behavioral change (lifetime/ownership questions, harder to reason about who's responsible for closing a server) than reusing the existing per-caller-supplied-registry pattern.

### Non-goals

- Not proposing anything about sharing MCP servers **across separate daemon processes** (e.g. multiple `zeroclaw daemon` instances on one host each with their own config) — that's a different, larger problem (would need an out-of-process broker) and out of scope here. This issue is scoped to redundant connects *within one daemon process*.
- Not proposing changes to the `stdio` vs `http` transport contract itself.

### Risks and mitigations

- **Stale/dead server handling**: `missing_or_dead_servers` (`daemon/mod.rs`, used by the heartbeat path) already has logic for "only reconnect what's missing or unhealthy" — reuse that exact function for gateway/channels instead of writing new logic, so failure/health-check behavior stays consistent across all three consumers.
- **Fail-open requirement**: the heartbeat path is documented as fail-open (an unreachable granted MCP server must not crash the worker). Any shared boot-time registry construction for gateway/channels needs the same fail-open behavior — a bad MCP server config shouldn't take down the whole daemon.
- **Ownership/shutdown**: today each consumer's registry lifetime is tied to that consumer. Sharing one registry across gateway + channels + heartbeat means its shutdown/drop timing needs to outlive all three, not just one — needs care so a stdio child isn't killed while another consumer still expects it alive.

### Breaking change?

No — this only changes internal boot sequencing/reuse, not any public config schema, API, or default behavior. Should be observable only as fewer child-process spawns and log lines.

### Decision and revisit surface

This issue — happy to expand into a linked proposal PR (draft/WIP) once there's agreement on the direction, or to hand it off if a maintainer wants to take it from here.

issues.title: [Bug]: A web chat receives no cron results or pushed session messages until its first reply
issues.body:
### Affected component

gateway/api

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

A dashboard chat that has just been opened shows no live events, such as `cron_result` or a `message` pushed into an existing session through `POST /api/sessions/{id}/messages` (the API added in #6671 for #6659; for example a reopened conversation, since a session that has never had a frame returns 404 from that API), until the user has sent a message in it and the reply has finished. Events published before then are never shown live. Pushed messages do appear after a reload, because they are saved to the transcript; cron results are not saved there.

`handle_socket` sends `session_start` and then waits for the client's first frame, either the optional `{"type":"connect"}` frame or a chat message ([`ws.rs` L584](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/ee2f5f58f7d760456cf6a61f531784b7f7696a7c/crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/ws.rs#L584)). Only after that does it build the agent, run the first message's turn if the frame was a chat message, and then subscribe to the shared event channel ([L890](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/ee2f5f58f7d760456cf6a61f531784b7f7696a7c/crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/ws.rs#L890)), whose events it forwards at [L1075](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/ee2f5f58f7d760456cf6a61f531784b7f7696a7c/crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/ws.rs#L1075).

The web chat never sends the connect frame. It passes `session_id` and `agent` in the URL and sends nothing when the socket opens ([`web/src/lib/ws.ts` L84](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/ee2f5f58f7d760456cf6a61f531784b7f7696a7c/web/src/lib/ws.ts#L84), [`AgentContext.tsx` L672](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/ee2f5f58f7d760456cf6a61f531784b7f7696a7c/web/src/contexts/AgentContext.tsx#L672)). So the socket subscribes only once the reply to its first message has finished, and a broadcast receiver gets nothing sent before it subscribed. A reconnected socket starts in the same state, and since #11431 every gateway reload reconnects all open chats.

### Expected behavior

An open chat receives these events from the time it connects, without the user sending anything first.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# 1. With the daemon and gateway running, add an agent job that replies every minute:
zeroclaw cron add-every --agent <alias> --prompt 60000 'Reply with the current time.'
# 2. In the dashboard, open an agent's chat and send nothing. Wait a few minutes: no results appear.
# 3. Send any message. Results appear from the first run that finishes after the reply; the earlier runs are never shown.
# 4. Remove the job afterwards (zeroclaw cron remove <id>); it makes a model call every minute.
```

### Impact

Affected users: dashboard users relying on cron results or on messages pushed into a session.
Frequency: always, until the first reply in each opened or reconnected chat.
Consequence: live notifications are missed in a chat that has not had a reply since it last (re)connected.

Possible fixes:

- Gateway: subscribe once at the start of `handle_socket`, use that receiver in a new arm of the first-frame `select!` to forward matching events while waiting, and keep it for the main loop, so events published while the agent is built and the first turn runs are queued rather than lost. Queuing is best-effort: the channel holds 256 events shared with log and observer frames, so a long first turn can overflow it, and the chat arm ignores `Lagged` ([L1076](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/ee2f5f58f7d760456cf6a61f531784b7f7696a7c/crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/ws.rs#L1076)), losing the overwritten events.
- Web chat: send `{"type":"connect"}` when the socket opens. A small change, but every opened or reconnected chat would then build its agent straight away, and an agent that fails to build or is refused would close the socket on open, putting the chat into a reconnect loop of error messages (the same applies to the onboarding and cwd errors). Today that only happens once the user sends a message. Every opened chat would also create a session record even if it is never used.

This should land after, or together with, #11916: otherwise every chat that is open but not yet used would also start showing quiet `NO_REPLY` cron results.

### ZeroClaw version

v0.8.6 plus unrelated local patches; ws.rs changed in #11431 since then, but the subscription order is the same on master `ee2f5f58f` (line numbers above are master's)

### Rust version

1.98.0

### Operating system

Debian Linux

### Regression?

Unknown
